10.1126/science.adt3444.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
10.1126/science.adt3444.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli-electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.
authors: Jiasen Niu, Maialen Ortego Larrazabal, Thomas Gozlinski, Yudai Sato, Koen M. Bastiaans, Tjerk Benschop, Jian-Feng Ge, Yaroslav M. Blanter, Genda Gu, Ingmar Swart, Milan P. Allan

10.1126/science.adt7185.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
10.1126/science.adt7185.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch-based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction-based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.
authors: Clinton H. Hansen, Mark Lipstein, Sarah C. Erlandson, Tobias Schwalbe, Sylvie G. Bernier, Peter Gmeiner, Andrew C. Kruse, Wesley P. Wong

10.1126/science.aea3046.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
10.1126/science.aea3046.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis-associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell-dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1-positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.
authors: Qiang Pan, Xuege Wang, Yaqi Li, Ni Li, Ying Han, Guoying Zhang, Jiacheng Guo, Le Zhang, Aoyuan Cui, Yongqiang Gu, Yannan Lian, Wei Zhang, Naiheng Lin, Beitao Xu, Zige Jin, Xin Zeng, Lan Wang, Yu Li, Junjie Peng, Xiaoming Wang, Zhengquan Yu, Gui-Hua Wang, Wei Lu, Jun Qin

10.1126/science.aed4270.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
10.1126/science.aed4270.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades-or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

10.1126/science.aed8952.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
10.1126/science.aed8952.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.
authors: Xinyu Qi, Hong Chen, Qixing Nie, Hongyu Niu, Yong Ding, Xi Luo, Manfei Si, Shuqi Wu, Xianglei Xiong, Meng Li, Bangjian Dong, Haohan Ma, Chenghao Guo, Yicun Wang, Xiaoyu Long, Jianhuai Zheng, Kai Wang, Shaoping Nie, Changtao Jiang, Yanli Pang, Jie Qiao

10.1126/science.aeg3800.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
10.1126/science.aeg3800.abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.
authors: Gino Caspari, Timur Sadykov, Daria Fomicheva, Jegor Blochin, Dominic Armbruster, Oliver Happel, Natalia Ryabogina, Kseniia Boxleitner, Robert Spengler

10.1126/science.aeg7301.title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
10.1126/science.aeg7301.abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.
authors: Fumiaki Tomita, Tianhaozhe Sun, Motoyuki Kido, Takeshi Iinuma, Naoki Uchida, Yusaku Ohta, Ryota Hino, Jiangheng He, Kelin Wang

10.1126/science.aeh9311.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
10.1126/science.aeh9311.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.
authors: Hadas Raviv, Arkadii Tsyhanov, Kira Gousios, Aja Altenhof, Haocheng Wang, Berlin Chen, Ofri Raviv, Tal Rosenwein, Casey Lew-Williams, Liat Hasenfratz, Uri Hasson

10.1126/science.aej1765.title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
10.1126/science.aej1765.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.
authors: Badih Ghazi, Pritish Kamath, Ravi Kumar, Pasin Manurangsi, Adam Sealfon*

10.1126/science.adv1247.title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
10.1126/science.adv1247.abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.
authors: Jirayu Mongkolkiattichai, Liyu Liu, Sohail Dasgupta, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Peter Schauss

10.1126/science.adu9593.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
10.1126/science.adu9593.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.
authors: Hansjoerg P. Kunc and Rouven Schmidt

10.1126/science.aeh7074.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
10.1126/science.aeh7074.abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer-enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >10 8 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

10.1126/science.aee9044.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
10.1126/science.aee9044.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

10.1126/science.aek9987.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
10.1126/science.aek9987.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.
authors: Stina Börchers, Giulia Mazzini, Henrik Zetterberg, Christoffer Clemmensen

10.1126/science.aej1120.title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
10.1126/science.aej1120.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

10.1126/science.aen6314.title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
10.1126/science.aen6314.abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

10.1126/science.aea5324.title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space
10.1126/science.aea5324.abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 10 4 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of 9.7 − 2.7 + 3.2 pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

10.1126/science.aed9286.title: RAD51 stabilizes neutrophil extracellular traps to compartmentalize inflammation
10.1126/science.aed9286.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) feature a branched chromatin architecture whose origin and function remain unknown. We found that NET branching is mediated by RAD51, a protein generating DNA junctions during DNA recombination repair. Pharmacological inhibition, RAD51 knockdown, or GEN1 and RuvC resolvase treatment reduced branching and destabilized NETs, whereas RAD51 up-regulation by different stimuli generated NETs with variable stability. RAD51 inhibition during murine pulmonary Aspergillus fumigatus infection dismantled NETs and reduced lung cytokines. However, the increased accumulation of NET components in the circulation led to interleukin-6 (IL-6) induction in circulating monocytes that exacerbated type 2 inflammation and asthma. Extracellular plasma DNA correlated with IL-6 and eotaxin in human aspergillosis. By structurally stabilizing NETs, RAD51 compartmentalizes inflammation to thwart aberrant systemic immune activation, linking DNA repair to inflammation.

10.1126/science.aei2836.title: Conformal oxides decouple chemical stability and energetics at NiO x /perovskite interfaces
10.1126/science.aei2836.abstract: Nickel oxide (NiO x ) is a common hole transport layer (HTL) in perovskite photovoltaics, but the chemical reactivity of NiOx surfaces accelerates degradation when contacting perovskites. We developed an ultrathin, conformal tin oxide (SnO x ) interlayer to suppress interfacial reactivity between NiO x and perovskite. SnO x is typically an electron transport layer, but we show that the energy alignment can be modified for hole extraction using molecules with dipoles. This synergy yielded high efficiency in perovskite photovoltaic devices and showed an ~10x improvement in T 90 lifetime in open-circuit conditions under AM1.5G at 65°C. This structure also improves resilience to thermomechanical durability, as minimodules retained 95.7% of their initial performance after 1000 thermal cycles (−65° to 85°C), highlighting the importance of interfaces for robust perovskite photovoltaic modules.

10.1126/science.aeh5267.title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
10.1126/science.aeh5267.abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method - microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells - to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

10.1126/science.adw0855.title: Spatially resolved single-cell atlas reveals the macroevolutionary trajectory of animal hearts
10.1126/science.adw0855.abstract: Animal hearts display diverse anatomical structures during adaptive evolution. Here, we present a multiomics atlas of adult hearts from 27 species across chordates, arthropods, and mollusks. Joint analysis indicates that Bilateria hearts share a core gene repertoire, taking a stepwise “add-on” approach as a universal evolutionary strategy. The “proto-heart” is populated by key cell types, including cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and neural cells, which maintained core signatures while evolving with shifts in living environments and corresponding adaptations in the cardiovascular system. Additionally, we reveal an evolutionarily conserved cardiomyocyte state dynamic potentially linked to cardiac development and stress responses. Finally, we identify a common molecular program underpinning chamber evolution from a ventricular foundation. This work establishes a resource for understanding the intrinsic mechanisms of heart evolution.

10.1126/science.aed6452.title: Longitudinal dynamics of gene expression and metabolomics in an aging population cohort
10.1126/science.aed6452.abstract: Multiomic profiling provides a comprehensive physiological overview at the molecular level, but understanding of its spatiotemporal dynamics remains limited in human populations. We profiled longitudinal whole-blood gene expression and metabolite levels in 335 females over 8 years. Levels of 5061 genes and 181 metabolites changed over time, with individual trajectories often diverging from population-level trends. Longitudinally variable genes showed cell type specificity and enrichment for aging-relevant pathways, including cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative disorders. Longitudinal trajectories were further shaped by genetics, circadian rhythm, seasonality, and environmental pollutant exposures. Integrative analyses revealed extensive static and time-variable cross-omic connectivity. Longitudinal profiling offers insight into the temporal evolution of age-related conditions at the molecular level, and understanding individual variation within these longitudinal patterns will be essential for future precision medicine approaches.

10.1038/s41467-026-78271-9.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
10.1038/s41467-026-78271-9.abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0 Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7 Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4 In this study, the authors develop a computational framework, Scellmate, that curates and analyzes large-scale microbial single-cell datasets from complex environments, and show that this helps to reveal microbial diversity and infer microbe-plasmid and microbe-phage associations in sewage.

10.1038/s41467-026-78169-6.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
10.1038/s41467-026-78169-6.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode-skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78378-z.title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
10.1038/s41467-026-78378-z.abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78137-0.title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
10.1038/s41467-026-78137-0.abstract: Abstract Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0-90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon-climate feedbacks.

10.1038/s41467-026-77097-9.title: Evaluating the consequences of childhood adiposity on the human plasma proteome at four timepoints across the lifecourse
10.1038/s41467-026-77097-9.abstract: Abstract Applying a lifecourse approach using human genetic data, we evaluate the effect of childhood adiposity on the circulating proteome using measurements taken at four key life stages. Using lifecourse Mendelian randomization, we find genetically predicted childhood adiposity to have an effect on 8 proteins measured during childhood (mean age: 9.9 years) including increased circulating TNFSF11 which is involved in T cell-dependent immune responses. Using a mediation framework, we demonstrate that TNFSF11 confers risk of childhood-onset asthma (colocalization posterior probability =88.6%) but not adult-onset asthma (colocalization posterior probability =0.2%), highlighting its putative role as a causal intermediate between adiposity and asthma risk specific to early stages in the lifecourse. Additionally, we find that genetically predicted childhood adiposity has an independent effect on 24 proteins measured during midlife after accounting for adulthood adiposity. Of particular interest is the effect of childhood adiposity on CST6 and NOTCH3 levels in adulthood, which have been found previously to play a role in breast cancer susceptibility.

10.1038/s41467-026-77511-2.title: Decoding the genomic repertoire of fosfomycin resistance genes in staphylococci
10.1038/s41467-026-77511-2.abstract: Abstract Fosfomycin is regaining clinical relevance for multidrug-resistant staphylococcal infections, yet the diversity, evolutionary origin and nomenclature of staphylococcal fosfomycin resistance genes remain inconsistently defined. We surveyed 17,024 publicly available genomes representing 14 clinically common Staphylococcus species to curate a catalogue of fosfomycin-modifying fos homologues. By integrating amino-acid identity, phylogenetic topology, genomic context and population-level distribution, we established a reproducible classification framework that resolved species- or lineage-associated intrinsic genes, including fosSA , fosSE , fosSC , fosSCp and fosSL , from acquired determinants, including fosB , fosD , fosY and ten prophage-associated families designated fosSΦA-J . Intrinsic genes showed conserved local contexts, whereas prophage-borne determinants occupied diverse insertion sites, supporting distinct evolutionary trajectories. Functional assays showed variable effects on fosfomycin susceptibility. Deleting fosSA in MRSA reduced the fosfomycin MIC 16-fold, and complementation restored resistance. This study provides a unified nomenclature and evolutionary framework for staphylococcal fos genes and highlights the need to monitor both lineage-associated and mobile fos determinants.

10.1038/s41467-026-77602-0.title: A programmable organosulfate platform for concurrent molecular sequence and topology control
10.1038/s41467-026-77602-0.abstract: Abstract Metal-organic frameworks achieve structural complexity without deterministic sequence control. Conversely, biological macromolecules encode molecular information with extraordinary precision, yet provide limited access to discrete void-bearing topological complexity. Bridging these paradigms requires a programmable strategy capable of simultaneously defining molecular sequence and topology within a unified synthetic framework. Here we introduce a programmable platform that achieves this dual control. Iterative SuFEx-based homologation, coupled with controlled annulation, enables precise sequence definition and topological specification. Incorporation of a trifunctional scaffold permits access to bicyclic and cage-like molecular architectures with defined connectivities. Physicochemical analyses reveal that encoded sequence and topology dictate thermal stability and hydrodynamic behavior. Extension to polysulfate networks further demonstrates topology-dependent gelation, establishing programmable organosulfates as a versatile platform for constructing information-rich molecular systems and functional soft matter.

10.1038/s41467-026-77706-7.title: Visible light suppresses carbon formation on Ni/CeO2 catalyst in methane dry reforming reaction

10.1038/s41467-026-77696-6.title: Mapping high resolution, multidimensional phase diagrams of near-physiological protein condensates
10.1038/s41467-026-77696-6.abstract: Abstract Biomolecular condensates are membraneless compartments, crucial for organising and regulating diverse cellular processes. Current approaches to study condensate biology either use simplified recombinant protein systems with limited physiological relevance, or complex live-cell models with restricted experimental control and scalability. Here, we present ExVivo PhaseScan, a droplet microfluidics platform that couples mammalian lysate-based reconstitution with scalable analysis to generate high-resolution phase diagrams of compositionally complex protein condensates. We apply this approach to study two multicomponent condensate systems, stress granules and nucleoli, and dissect the physicochemical interactions that influence their stability. We further developed a machine learning pipeline to analyse condensate morphology which we use to reveal how mutations in the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-linked protein Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) remodels condensate properties. We identify liquid-to-solid transitions of mutant FUS within stress granules and nucleoli, and show that these transitions can be reversed by RNA aptamer-based interventions. Together, these findings establish ExVivo PhaseScan as a versatile tool for dissecting the physicochemical and pathological regulation of condensates, with potential to inform therapeutic strategies for diseases driven by aberrant phase transitions.

10.1038/s41467-026-77402-6.title: Rapid changes in risk attitudes originate from Bayesian inference on parietal magnitude representations
10.1038/s41467-026-77402-6.abstract: Abstract Risk attitudes-the willingness to accept uncertainty for larger potential rewards-are often treated as a stable individual trait, yet people’s risky choices change markedly across contexts and even across repetitions of identical decisions. Here we show, using modelling and neuroimaging, that such rapid changes emerge from Bayesian inference on noisy magnitude representations in parietal cortex. Participants underwent fMRI while choosing between safe and risky options that are either held in working memory or shown on screen. Options held in working memory are noisier and more prone to central-tendency biases, so relatively small payoffs are overestimated and large payoffs underestimated, shifting choices between risk-seeking and risk aversion. A computational model of payoff perception captures these effects mechanistically. Numerical population-receptive-field modelling shows that when intraparietal payoff representations are noisier, choices are less consistent and less risk-neutral. Thus, risk attitudes and their contextual variability can be rooted in perceptual inference on parietal magnitude representations.

10.1038/s41467-026-76880-y.title: Potential sublimating exocomets around the young star PDS 70
10.1038/s41467-026-76880-y.abstract: Abstract Recent observations by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have indicated the presence of water in the inner regions of the disc around the young protostar PDS 70, but the origin of this water remains unclear. Here we report the discovery of variable absorption lines of neutral sodium in archival High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher (HARPS) spectra of PDS 70. These lines vary strongly and stochastically on a daily basis, in amplitude, number, and radial velocity. Our measurements indicate that this gas tends to be optically thick, and partially cover the stellar disc, meaning this fast-moving gas is often spatially confined. We explore several hypotheses for the origin of these lines, and conclude that a likely source of the observed sodium is sublimation of planetesimals that transit the star on highly elliptical orbits, reminiscent of the exocomet phenomenon seen in other seen in other extrasolar systems. These sublimating exocomets could play a role in sourcing the previously observed water in the inner, terrestrial-planet forming region of the PDS 70 system.

10.1038/s41467-026-78461-5.title: Multi-model collaborative early warning for battery systems with integrated fiber optic sensors
10.1038/s41467-026-78461-5.abstract: Abstract The safety assessment of battery systems is constrained by sparse temperature measurements and monolithic diagnostic frameworks in conventional battery management systems (BMS). To address this, we propose a multi-model collaborative thermal-runaway early-warning framework using distributed temperature sensing. An integrated sensing scheme increases temperature sensing points within the battery pack from 32 to 540 with minimal wiring complexity and is validated in real-world vehicle operation. We establish a functional relationship between temperature Shannon entropy (SE) and average temperature variation to derive a dynamic warning boundary incorporating error tolerance. Integrating this boundary with thresholds for temperature, temperature change rate, and SE change rate enables collaborative early warning. Compared with conventional BMS warning benchmarks, the framework provides maximum warning lead times of 706 s in laboratory modules and 554 s in real-world vehicle operation. These findings demonstrate the potential of distributed sensing and collaborative diagnostics for proactive thermal-runaway risk identification.

10.1038/s41467-026-76850-4.title: Creating locally enriched single-atom catalysts via bio-inspired internalization process for interference-resistant NO2 detection in complex environments
10.1038/s41467-026-76850-4.abstract: Abstract Intelligent gas-sensing technology that accurately and stably identifies gas categories in complex atmospheres is critical for protecting public safety and environment. However, competing interactions among different gases on sensing surfaces can trigger interference even poison of sensors. Here, we present a bio-inspired atomic internalization process that produces locally enriched single Pt species, enabling highly selective and interference-resistant gas detection. By engineering Sn/C precursors as homologous receptors, Pt 3 Sn alloys are two-step redistributed into high-density single Pt species within regionalized SnO 2 surface. This structure constitutionally alters the distribution patterns of NO 2 molecules and thus delivers accurate NO 2 monitoring in multicomponent atmospheres and stable detection for over 550 days, surpassing state-of-the-art commercial devices. Further integrating characteristic-specific sensors into arrays, the resulting device further achieves 100% classification accuracy for single and mixed gases at ultralow cost. Moreover, we demonstrate an autonomous “cruise-monitoring” system by equipping the sensor on a robot to detect and identify NO 2 in real time. Our findings thus guide the accurate analysis and interference-resistant detection in complex gas mixtures.

10.1038/s41467-026-77620-y.title: RAISE quantifies RNA binding protein activity via transcriptomic profiling

10.1038/s41467-026-77720-9.title: The hijacking of a wheat Exo70-like protein by a fungal pathogen triggers disease
10.1038/s41467-026-77720-9.abstract: Abstract Tan spot is an economically important fungal disease of wheat that occurs globally. In this necrotrophic pathosystem, pathogen effectors are recognized by wheat genes in an inverse gene-for-gene manner, leading to the hijacking of host defense mechanisms and ultimately disease susceptibility. Here, we identified the tan spot susceptibility gene Tsc2 through positional cloning, mutagenesis, and transgenic complementation. Tsc2 encodes a diverged form of the exocyst subunit Exo70FX15 that localizes to the nucleus and cytoplasm and does not interact directly with the fungal effector. A 21-nucleotide deletion in Tsc2 occurred in durum wheat more than a century ago and subsequently spread to common wheat through breeding practices, which allowed recognition of the pathogen effector and subsequent hijacking of the host immune system. We demonstrate that elimination of Tsc2 through conventional breeding using a diagnostic marker or disruption of Tsc2 by gene editing can be used to improve tan spot resistance in wheat.

10.1038/s41467-026-77609-7.title: Cardiac fibroblast deletion of PTBP1 modulates the profibrotic response by alternative splicing

10.1038/s41467-026-77264-y.title: Thermal conductivity and optical phonon scattering of CMOS compatible aluminum nitride based ferroelectric thin films

10.1038/s41467-026-77113-y.title: LGR5-positive fibroblasts orchestrate skin mechanoadaptation through JAK1 modulation
10.1038/s41467-026-77113-y.abstract: Abstract Mechanical adaptation is a fundamental yet poorly understood process in stromal tissue biology. Here, we identify a population of LGR5 + mechanically induced regulatory fibroblasts (LGR5 + MIRFs) in mouse and human dermis, whose induction requires a YAP/AP-1-dependent transcriptional program. LGR5 + MIRFs channel mechanical input toward adaptive tissue remodeling by coordinating extracellular matrix reorganization while restraining inflammation. Their ablation or fibroblast-specific deletion of Lgr5 converts adaptive stretching into pathological fibro-inflammation, while dermal Lgr5 overexpression enhances tissue extensibility. Mechanistically, we uncover a non-canonical LGR5-JAK1 interaction that suppresses JAK-STAT signaling, directly coupling mechanosensing to kinase pathway activity. Topical JAK1 inhibition recapitulates the pro-remodeling effects of LGR5 + MIRFs, suggesting a translatable therapeutic strategy for optimizing skin expansion, treating striae, and mitigating fibrotic disorders. Our work redefines LGR5 as a conserved stromal mechanoresponder and provides a new conceptual framework for understanding adaptive tissue plasticity under mechanical stress.

10.1038/s41467-026-77711-w.title: Broad-scale shift in dominance of arbuscular mycorrhizal trees along the Japanese archipelago associated with tree diseases and climate warming
10.1038/s41467-026-77711-w.abstract: Abstract Distribution shifts of mycorrhizal tree symbioses are predicted to alter the nutrient cycling in temperate forests worldwide. Yet, our understanding of the drivers and specific impacts of such shifts remains limited. Here, we assign mycorrhizal types to trees at the species and genus level in >13,000 forest plots to assess the dominance of arbuscular mycorrhizal trees based on basal area proportions along the Japanese archipelago in temperate East Asia. We show a significant increase in arbuscular mycorrhizal tree dominance within 15 years associated with climate warming and the spread of tree diseases, contributing to a more important role of arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis in forest ecosystems than previously predicted. Arbuscular mycorrhizal tree dominance is negatively related to the ratio of soil carbon and nitrogen stocks, suggesting that tree symbiosis shifts will affect soil nitrogen availability and retention. In light of the global surge of biotic forest disturbance, our results stress the importance of forest pest and disease control to decelerate tree symbiosis shifts and their impact on ecosystem functioning.

10.1038/s41467-026-77635-5.title: Reinterpreting precipitation isotope records from Asian monsoon region through the hidden role of atmospheric updraft
10.1038/s41467-026-77635-5.abstract: Abstract Speleothem oxygen isotope records (δ 18 O s ) from the Asian monsoon region provide valuable insights into past hydroclimate variability, yet their interpretation relies on understanding the controls on modern precipitation isotopes (δ 18 O p ). Although numerous explanations for the spatiotemporal variability of δ 18 O p across this region have been proposed, the primary controls remain unresolved. Here we propose a hypothesis to explain δ 18 O p variability from δ 18 O p records at 46 sites along a transect spanning the Asian monsoon region. Our results show that seasonally low δ 18 O p values migrate gradually westward along the east-west transect. We further demonstrate that the corresponding westward migration of atmospheric updraft, particularly convection, controls δ 18 O p variations along the transect. In contrast to previous interpretations emphasizing monsoon moisture advection, our findings highlight atmospheric updraft as an important control on δ 18 O p variations across the Asian monsoon region. These findings provide an alternative perspective on interpreting the climate signals preserved in Asian δ 18 O s records.
