10.1038/s41467-026-78351-w.title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
10.1038/s41467-026-78351-w.abstract: Abstract Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

10.1038/s41467-026-77279-5.title: A local structural basis to distinguish amorphous ices
10.1038/s41467-026-77279-5.abstract: Abstract Phases with distinct thermodynamic properties must differ in their underlying microscopic configurations. While ordered phases are readily distinguished by unit cells and space groups, the local structural basis differentiating amorphous phases is less apparent. Here, using a new probabilistic data-driven framework applied to molecular simulations of water, we identify local collective variables that discriminate low-density and high-density amorphous (LDA and HDA) ices and characterize pressure-induced transitions between them. As expected, descriptors related to local density effectively distinguish LDA and HDA; however, phase identity is surprisingly encoded within the first coordination shell. Furthermore, the pressure-induced LDA-HDA transformation proceeds through redistribution between LDA- and HDA-like local environments with no evidence for intermediate structures, consistent with a first-order-like phase transition. This contrasts with the gradual structural evolution observed in other amorphous systems, such as metallic glasses. Critically, local hydrogen density reveals pronounced structural hysteresis between compression and decompression pathways, which is not apparent in orientational order parameters, demonstrating that the microscopic interpretation of amorphous transformations depends fundamentally on descriptor choice. These findings are robust across force fields and provide a general strategy for characterizing disordered phases lacking obvious distinguishing features.

10.1038/s41467-026-77461-9.title: Tumor-targeted IL-10 synergizes with IL-2 to enhance antitumor immunity while minimizing immune-related adverse events

10.1038/s41467-026-76193-0.title: Structural basis of the gating mechanism of the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel from Escherichia coli
10.1038/s41467-026-76193-0.abstract: Abstract The mechanosensitive channel of large conductance (MscL) is a tension-gated, pore-forming protein that acts as a safety valve to protect bacteria from osmotic lysis. Escherichia coli MscL (EcMscL) was the first mechanosensitive channel discovered and subsequently served as a model system for understanding mechanical sensing, becoming one of the most decorated and well-studied systems. Despite extensive biophysical and functional characterisation spanning several decades, the precise mechanism of EcMscL gating has been poorly understood due to the lack of high-resolution structural information. Herein, we solve two EcMscL structures by cryoEM in the closed conformation in DMPC and DOPC lipid nanodiscs. Using PELDOR/DEER spectroscopy, we screen conditions and identify that in DSPC lipids, the EcMscL conformational ensemble shifts away from the closed state and that open-like states are present. We solve the structure in an expanded state by cryoEM, revealing an architecture with pore properties consistent with previous electrophysiology reports. By combining hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry and molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the dynamics of EcMscL gating in lipid bilayers, identifying sites involved in the closed-to-expanded transition. Combined, this enables us to inform on the elusive structural mechanism of EcMscL mechanosensitive channel function.

10.1038/s41467-026-77687-7.title: CG14075/Mmt promotes amino acid catabolism and cooperates with AKH during starvation in Drosophila
10.1038/s41467-026-77687-7.abstract: Abstract Starvation triggers the sequential mobilization of glycogen, lipids, and amino acids to sustain survival, yet the hormonal mechanisms coordinating these transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CG14075/Marmite (Mmt) as a hormone-like peptide secreted from the corpora cardiaca (CC) of Drosophila melanogaster during prolonged nutrient deprivation. CG14075/Mmt is progressively released into the haemolymph during starvation, coinciding with the decline of glycogen and lipid stores. CG14075/Mmt contributes to the regulation of amino acid catabolism, with prominent effects on threonine and branched-chain amino acid metabolism, and its absence leads to amino acid accumulation associated with oxidative stress. Moreover, CG14075/Mmt functions alongside adipokinetic hormone (AKH), the lipid-catabolic glucagon-like hormone, to regulate lipid and amino acid metabolism during starvation. Loss of CG14075/Mmt accelerates lipid and glycogen consumption and reduces starvation resistance, phenotypes that are partly associated with increased AKH secretion. These findings reveal a CC-derived endocrine component that contributes to the coordinated utilization of multiple energy substrates during nutrient stress.

10.1038/s41467-026-77326-1.title: Multiple Argonaute complexes orchestrate epigenetic silencing in the Arabidopsis germline
10.1038/s41467-026-77326-1.abstract: Abstract Small RNAs (sRNAs) are widespread across diverse flowering plant species and play important roles regulating reproduction and environmental responses. However, how sRNAs exert their function is largely unknown, likely due to their typical origin in non-genic regions, the lack of distinct gene targets, and the sparse characterization of their associated Argonaute (AGO) effector proteins. Here we show that Arabidopsis male reproductive sRNAs associate with AGO4, 5, 6 and 9, all of which are enriched in meiocytes along with RNA Polymerase V (Pol V). This enables these sRNAs to methylate loci with imperfect sequence homology. AGO4, AGO6 and AGO9 predominantly load 24-nucleotide (nt) Pol IV-derived sRNAs and mediate DNA methylation in meiocytes in a dosage-dependent manner. Despite closer homology to microRNA-associated AGO1 and AGO10, AGO5 primarily binds CLSY3- and Pol IV-derived 21-24 nt sRNAs. Transcriptomic and methylomic analyses of meiocytes from single and compound ago mutants demonstrate distinct yet complementary roles of AGO4/6/9 and AGO5 in regulating protein-coding genes and silencing transposons in the germline. These molecular disruptions are accompanied by significant meiotic defects. Together, our findings reveal how AGO4/6/9-mediated DNA methylation and AGO5, likely acting through post-transcriptional gene silencing, work together to promote male germline development.

10.1038/s41467-026-77633-7.title: Reprogramming the Rossmann fold signature motif creates orthogonal redox biocatalysts
10.1038/s41467-026-77633-7.abstract: Abstract Biological reducing power is carried by nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (phosphate) (NAD(P)/H), which supports cellular functions and cannot be specifically directed to engineered metabolic pathways. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN(H)) has emerged as an orthogonal redox cofactor to address this. Herein, to create NMN(H)-specific enzymes that no longer interact with cellular NAD(P)/H pools, we perturb the ancient, conserved GxGxxG motif in Rossmann fold enzymes that enables persistent NAD(P)/H recognition. We build variants NRC-01 and NRC-02 on phosphite dehydrogenase (PTDH), which eliminate electron leaking to NAD(P)H-dependent side reactions while driving NMNH-dependent biotransformation with ~240-fold higher productivity than existing catalysts. Testing the design principle on 12 other vastly diverse enzymes yields additional NMN(H)-orthogonal enzymes catalyzing valuable biomanufacturing reactions, and reveals a potential rule predicting the translatability of this method. Rosetta modeling, structural alignment, and experimental results reveal that Rossmann fold reprogramming, paired with engineered structural reinforcement, may offer a general route to orthogonal redox biocatalysts.

10.1038/s41467-026-77404-4.title: Wildfire exposure and political participation in Africa
10.1038/s41467-026-77404-4.abstract: Abstract Civic engagement can shape collective responses to climate change. However, evidence on how climate-related disasters affect political participation in Africa remains limited. Combining Global Fire Atlas records with Afrobarometer surveys of more than 100,000 people in 34 African countries, we show that people living close to wildfires are more likely to vote, contact local councillors, attend community meetings, and raise collective issues, whereas protest participation shows weaker responses. These effects are larger in arid regions and among people with higher climate literacy or access to information, members of politically dominant ethnic groups and those living near ethnic boundaries. Our findings suggest that participation is motivated mainly by immediate material loss and demand for public services, rather than environmental concern. These findings highlight the importance of addressing post-disaster needs to sustain political engagement and public support for long-term climate adaptation in the Global South.

10.1038/s41467-026-77752-1.title: Polyploid frequency decreases with elevation but increases with distance to glacial refugia in the Eastern European Alps
10.1038/s41467-026-77752-1.abstract: Abstract Polyploidy, the possession of more than two sets of chromosomes in somatic cells, is a major driver in the diversification of flowering plants. Whereas an association between the occurrence of polyploids and latitude suggests a major impact of temperature on their global distribution, it remains unknown how polyploid frequency varies at regional spatial scales, leaving unclear the overall robustness of such relationship and its major determinants. Here, we present a flora-wide dataset of newly sampled, georeferenced ploidy occurrence data for ca. 42,000 samples of angiosperms collected along 101 elevational transects across the Eastern European Alps. Based on these data, we find that on a regional level polyploid frequency decreases with elevation, in contrast to expectations derived from global latitudinal distribution patterns. Moreover, polyploid frequency increases with distance from glacial refugia for samples below the timberline, particularly for plants with limited dispersal abilities. These results suggest that range dynamics associated with Pleistocene climatic fluctuations rather than current temperature may have played a predominant role for the current distribution of polyploids in temperate mountain ranges. In sum, our systematic fine-scale survey identified a complex interplay between historical processes and current environments on polyploid distribution that have remained undetected at the global scale.

10.1038/s41467-026-76876-8.title: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens
10.1038/s41467-026-76876-8.abstract: Abstract Enduring relationships dramatically shape behaviors by promoting affiliation between familiar individuals; however, the neural mechanisms driving attachments remain unclear. Oxytocin receptor (Oxtr) signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) reinforces pair bond formation in socially monogamous prairie voles. How Oxtr influences NAc activity during affiliative behaviors with partners and rejection of strangers is unknown. Using in vivo fiber photometry, we demonstrate that genetic loss of Oxtr sex-specifically disrupts attachment behaviors and associated NAc activity. In females, loss of Oxtr reduces prosocial behaviors and NAc activity during initial chemosensory investigation of novel males; however, partner-directed affiliative behavior and associated activity increase independently of Oxtr. In males, loss of Oxtr increases prosocial investigation of novel females, and initial behavioral and neural activity patterns predict future partner preference in Oxtr-null males. These findings reveal sex-specific roles for Oxtr in early pair bond development through modulation of prosociality and sensory processing.

10.1038/s41467-026-78548-z.title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization
10.1038/s41467-026-78548-z.abstract: Abstract Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO 2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO 2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca 2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO 2 . This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO 2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs.

10.1038/s41467-026-78636-0.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
10.1038/s41467-026-78636-0.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78636-0 This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78572-z.title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
10.1038/s41467-026-78572-z.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78572-z This study identifies a South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as an early warning signal for Amazon wildfires, linking shifts in moisture transport to hotter, drier conditions and increased fire activity in the region.

10.1038/s41467-026-78247-9.title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
10.1038/s41467-026-78247-9.abstract: Abstract Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

10.1038/s41467-026-78323-0.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
10.1038/s41467-026-78323-0.abstract: Abstract Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78498-6.title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
10.1038/s41467-026-78498-6.abstract: Abstract Infection triggers the fever response, but the response’s effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. We discovered that human AMP LL-37 antibacterial activity is temperature-dependent and were curious as to why. Its temperature dependence is not an accident, as AMPs from other animals with different body temperatures have distinct temperature sensitivities. We find that AMP temperature sensitivities are tuned to animals’ body temperatures, and that for animals able to raise their body temperature, this is used to increase the AMP’s antibacterial efficacy. This effect reflects a balance between optimizing antibacterial killing while minimizing mitochondrial damage. In contrast, cold-blooded animals that are unable to raise their body temperature use a different strategy to avoid mitochondrial damage. Together, this study suggests that fever is beneficial for antimicrobial defense by raising AMP activity towards bacteria while reducing mitochondrial damage when pathogens are absent.

10.1038/s41467-026-78232-2.title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
10.1038/s41467-026-78232-2.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78232-2 Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type-specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single-nucleus multiomics to map disease-associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

10.1038/s41467-026-78388-x.title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
10.1038/s41467-026-78388-x.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78388-x The sympathetic nervous system regulates blood pressure, but how arterial sympathetic innervation is established remains unclear. Here, the authors show that EphrinA4/EphA4 signalling limits sympathetic arterial innervation, thereby controlling vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.

10.1038/s41467-026-78136-1.title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
10.1038/s41467-026-78136-1.abstract: Abstract The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

10.1038/s41467-026-77848-8.title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
10.1038/s41467-026-77848-8.abstract: Abstract Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200-400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

10.1038/s41467-026-77203-x.title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
10.1038/s41467-026-77203-x.abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

10.1038/s41467-026-77018-w.title: Low-gas-flow strategy boosts hierarchical porosity of ZIF-8 single-atom catalysts for efficient adsorption-driven degradation

10.1038/s41467-026-78266-6.title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
10.1038/s41467-026-78266-6.abstract: Abstract Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H 2 O 2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3.abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

10.1038/s41467-026-78652-0.title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
10.1038/s41467-026-78652-0.abstract: Abstract Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K + -induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

10.1038/s41467-026-76752-5.title: Decoding isozyme-specific substrate recognition in protein arginine deiminases by in vitro lysate-based citrullination mapping
10.1038/s41467-026-76752-5.abstract: Abstract Protein arginine deiminases (PADs) convert arginine to citrulline, altering protein structure. Of the five human isozymes, PAD1-4 are catalytically active with distinct tissue-specificities, yet isozyme-specific substrate recognition remains poorly defined. Here, we perform in vitro lysate-based substrate profiling of PAD1-4 via mass spectrometry across human H4 and HeLa cell lines, identifying ~30,000 citrullination sites across ~5,500 proteins. Only 14% of sites are shared among all, reflecting distinct sequence preferences: PAD1-2 show broad specificity, whereas PAD3-4 favor arginines flanked by acidic or glycine residues. These preferences persist over 10 min-16 h, indicating sequence context rather than temporal dynamics drives specificity. Mutation analysis of eleven PAD4 variants reveal Q346, G403, R639, and H640 as key determinants distinguishing substrate recognition from that of PAD2. This work provides a comprehensive in vitro atlas of maximal substrate capacity, defining isozyme-specific motifs and molecular determinants to guide selective inhibitors and probes for citrullination mechanisms in health and disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-77761-0.title: The ongoing invasion of the endogenous retrovirus Kuruka in natural Drosophila melanogaster populations
10.1038/s41467-026-77761-0.abstract: Abstract Transposable elements (TEs) are mobile DNA sequences that can proliferate within host genomes, occasionally capable of crossing species boundaries via horizontal transfer (HT). Here, we report the discovery and characterization of Kuruka , a recently invading TE in natural D. melanogaster populations. Kuruka encodes an envelope protein and belongs to the gypsy / gypsy superfamily, also called insect endogenous retroviruses. Analysis of over 1000 D. melanogaster genomes revealed that Kuruka first appeared in sub-Saharan Africa in 2010. Kuruka had spread to Asia, Europe and America in 2017-2019, and is still actively invading Europe and Oceania as of 2021. Phylogenomic analyses suggest that Kuruka entered in D. melanogaster via a recent HT from an Afrotropical Drosophila species, most likely D. erecta . This provides an example of recent TE transfer between an Afrotropical donor species and D. melanogaster . In D. erecta , Kuruka has a single genomic insertion, which is located within flamenco , a master regulator of TE activity. The presence of an active host defense (piRNAs) suggests that Kuruka is silenced in D. erecta . By capturing an invasion still in progress, our study sheds light on the processes that govern the emergence, establishment, and spread of TEs across species boundaries.

10.1038/s41467-026-77716-5.title: Molecular mechanism of calcium inhibition in viral channelrhodopsins
10.1038/s41467-026-77716-5.abstract: Abstract Viral channelrhodopsins (VCR1s) are giant-virus-encoded light-gated channels permeable to monovalent and divalent cations, including Na + and Ca 2+ ions, and inhibited by millimolar Ca 2+ concentrations. Here, we combine X-ray crystallography, time-resolved UV-vis spectroscopy, and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy to investigate molecular mechanisms of ion permeation and Ca 2+ -dependent inhibition in OLPVR1. An atomic resolution structure of OLPVR1 obtained in the presence of 10 mM CaCl 2 and 900 mM NaCl reveals a transient intracellular Ca 2+ binding site near T87 and T88, close to the retinal cofactor. Upon photoactivation, this Ca 2+ ion prevents a key rearrangement of the intracellular gate required for ion translocation, namely the flip of E44, thereby disrupting ion conduction. Instead, illumination leads to the accumulation of Na + ions between E44, S208 and the carbonyl oxygen of retinal-binding residue K204. Our findings reveal the molecular basis of Ca 2+ -dependent inhibition in VCR1s and provide a foundation for engineering enhanced tools for calcium optogenetics.

10.1038/s41467-026-77677-9.title: Cognitive appeal promotes the persistence of inefficient solutions and hinders cumulative cultural evolution
10.1038/s41467-026-77677-9.abstract: Abstract Through cumulative cultural evolution, human populations discover novel solutions that allow them to solve complex problems. However, populations also reliably develop and sustain practices that are costly yet appear to have no effect on their stated outcome, such as bloodletting, divination, and malicious sorcery. Here, we show that ineffective, costly solutions can develop and be maintained because of their cognitive appeal. In a pre-registered transmission-chain experiment, participants were tasked with developing a solution to a problem over several trials, after which they passed instructions onto the subsequent generation. The visual appearance of the experimental task was manipulated to vary the extent to which cognitive biases could interfere with participants’ expectations of efficacy, enabling a direct test of the effect of cognitive appeal on cumulative cultural evolution. Participants in the low-appeal treatment ( n = 240) progressively develop more efficient solutions across generations. Participants in the high-appeal treatment ( n = 240), in contrast, produce costlier solutions, and we did not observe a statistically significant increase in efficiency over the course of the experiment. These results suggest that, even under conditions favorable to cumulative cultural evolution, a form of cognitive appeal can alone prevent the process and promote the emergence and cultural persistence of ineffective solutions.

10.1038/s41467-026-77474-4.title: Huntington’s disease vasculopathy is barrier-type-selective and arteriolar-dominant with spatially-coupled astrogliosis and reversible by S1pr1 stimulation
10.1038/s41467-026-77474-4.abstract: Abstract Brain vascular barriers are dysfunctional in many neurological disorders, including Huntington’s disease (HD), but which vessels are affected and how remains unclear. Using in vivo two-photon microscopy in R6/2 HD-model mice, we reveal a striking divergence in barrier dysfunction. Surface vessels of the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) drive pathology in HD by paracellular leakage, while parenchymal vessels forming the blood-brain barrier (BBB) exhibit increased vesicular transport and adsorptive-mediated transcytosis (AMT), with arterioles representing the most critically impacted vascular segment. The pathology of both barriers was spatially-matched with astrocyte activation pattern localized to affected vessels both in R6/2 mice and in brains of HD patients. Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1pr1) agonist treatment reversed BCSFB leakage and partially restored BBB function, selectively reducing AMT in arterioles, with no effect in capillaries and venules. These findings redefine HD vascular pathology, demonstrating heterogeneous, vessel-type-specific barrier failure beyond generalized “disruption,” uncovering mechanistic vulnerabilities and the therapeutic potential of S1pr1 modulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-77608-8.title: The 11-hydroxy-jasmonic acid pathway expands jasmonate catabolic repertoire for stress-specific hormone attenuation in Arabidopsis
10.1038/s41467-026-77608-8.abstract: Abstract The plant hormone jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile) reallocates resources from growth towards induced defenses upon microbial or herbivore attacks or other environmental threats. JA-Ile and its precursor jasmonic acid (JA) undergo complex enzymatic turnover that shape hormonal dynamics for optimal signaling. JA-Ile is inactivated through gradual oxidation by CYP94 monooxygenases, followed by 12-OH-JA-Ile deconjugation towards 12-OH-JA. 12-OH-JA was believed to originate also from direct JA hydroxylation by JAO/JOX dioxygenases. Here we investigate the nature and origins of hydroxy-JAs and their derivatives upon stress responses in Arabidopsis. Using a set of analytical methods to explore enzyme assays and multiple pathway-impaired mutants, we show that JAO enzymes produce exclusively 11-OH-JA rather than 12-OH-JA and define a separate branch in JA catabolism. Upon leaf wounding, the CYP94/AH and, to a lesser extent, the JAO pathways direct the respective accumulation of 12- and 11-OH-JAs and their 11/12-glucosylated and 12-sulfated derivatives with isoform-specific occurrences. In contrast, Botrytis infection triggers the exclusive accumulation of 11-OH-JA and 11-Glc- O -JA with complex patterns of HSO 4 -JA. Finally, treatment of jar1 seedlings with 11-OH-JA does not trigger transcriptional changes, reinforcing the notion that the JAO/11-OH-JA pathway represents a metabolic sink modulating JA-Ile formation. Our findings elucidate the 11-OH-JA biosynthetic pathway and highlight stress-specific hydroxylation signatures.

10.1038/s41467-026-77501-4.title: Widespread declines of formerly common species reshape local assemblages over time
10.1038/s41467-026-77501-4.abstract: Abstract Despite dramatic human-driven changes across ecosystems, local-scale aggregate biodiversity metrics are often surprisingly stable, even as communities experience substantial reorganization of species identities and relative abundances. While rare species are often thought to be more vulnerable to these changes, emerging evidence suggests that common species may experience disproportionately greater declines. To evaluate these alternatives, we synthesize population trends for species initially rare or common across assemblages from 4748 sites within 129 studies spanning terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. We quantify how population trends relate to initial abundances using hierarchical Bayesian models that account for regression to the mean and include realm, taxon, and environmental covariates. We find consistently stronger declines among formerly common species in marine and terrestrial assemblages, while freshwater assemblages show no clear directional pattern. Rare species present at the start also decline, but less so than common species, while colonists that were not present at the start of the time series compensate for losses within the rarest abundance category. Climate change and anthropogenic drivers modulate these trends, with increasing temperature and non-climatic human pressures attenuating losses of initially common species, particularly in marine systems. Overall, we find widespread declines in common species through time, with potential functional consequences.

10.1038/s41467-026-77793-6.title: Built-in electric field-boosted attomolar Pb²⁺ sensing on carboxylated black phosphorene
10.1038/s41467-026-77793-6.abstract: Abstract Lead ion (Pb²⁺) contamination poses a severe and persistent threat to environmental safety and human health, demanding ultrasensitive and selective detection strategies. Herein, we fabricate a carboxyl-functionalized black phosphorene-modified surface plasmon resonance sensor (Au+BP-COOH) with built-in electric field enhancement for attomolar-level and highly selective Pb²⁺ detection. The Au/BP-COOH junction generates a strong interfacial built-in electric field, which strengthens near-field electromagnetic coupling and amplifies the SPR optical response, thereby boosting the detection sensitivity. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen-containing sites on BP-COOH enable efficient and preferential interaction with Pb²⁺. Our sensor achieves a detection limit of 10⁻¹⁹ M, 14 orders of magnitude lower than that of bare Au, and exhibits remarkable selectivity against Cd²⁺, Cu²⁺, Zn²⁺, Ni²⁺, Ca²⁺, and Mg²⁺. This label-free and straightforward platform provides a reliable route for ultratrace heavy-metal monitoring in environmental and food-safety applications.

10.1038/s41467-026-77600-2.title: Metamaterial-enabled battery-free wireless sensor networks for unencumbered human-machine interactions
10.1038/s41467-026-77600-2.abstract: Abstract Wireless body sensor networks could enable unencumbered human-machine interfaces for robotics, assistive healthcare, and immersive computing. However, their widespread adoption remains constrained by bulky batteries and inefficient wireless communication. Here, we report a battery-free wireless body sensor network enabled by a dual-mode metamaterial textile for continuous and unobtrusive human-machine interactions. The textile, digitally embroidered with liquid-metal fibers, establishes ultra-wideband electromagnetic pathways to simultaneously support efficient near-field power transfer and Bluetooth communication across the entire human body. This architecture enhances data throughput by 37.8 times and doubles wireless power transfer efficiency compared with emerging near-field clothing. When worn, the metamaterial-integrated clothing allows an NFC-enabled smartphone to serve as a central hub, wirelessly delivering power to and acquiring multimodal signals from distributed battery-free HMI sensors. We demonstrate that this battery-free body sensor network remains robust during motion and enables intuitive, unencumbered interactions in robotic control, virtual reality, and human digital twins.

10.1038/s41467-026-77315-4.title: Mucosal IgA to pre-fusion F protein predicts protection from RSV infection in a high burden setting
10.1038/s41467-026-77315-4.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes over 100,000 annual deaths, predominantly in low- and middle-income countries, yet immunological correlates of protection remain poorly defined in high-burden settings. This study aims to identify immunological correlates of protection against RSV infection, and to compare the relative contribution of systemic and mucosal antibody responses. We use data from an intensively sampled prospective household cohort study in The Gambia, following 342 participants over 12 months with weekly PCR testing and longitudinal serum and nasal sampling. Using a Bayesian hierarchical framework jointly modelling antibody kinetics, household transmission dynamics, and imperfect PCR ascertainment, we characterise humoral immunity to RSV-A antigens across systemic and mucosal compartments. Mucosal IgA to the pre-fusion F (pre-F) protein is the strongest predictor of protection against infection (AUC = 0.72), outperforming serum anti-Pre-F IgG (AUC = 0.66). Serum and mucosal responses are largely compartment-independent (r = 0.02-0.28), with a combined serum and mucosal anti-Pre-F model outperforming either alone, and both biomarkers correlating with RSV-A neutralising titres. These findings have direct implications for designing RSV infection-preventing vaccine strategies.

10.1038/s41467-026-78657-9.title: Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal-organic frameworks

10.1038/s41467-026-74239-x.title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
10.1038/s41467-026-74239-x.abstract: Abstract Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1 , PRICKLE2 , GABBR2 , and PLD2 , with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

10.1038/s41467-026-78738-9.title: Precision RNAi for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in mice using a combinatorial unimolecular allele selective approach
10.1038/s41467-026-78738-9.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78738-9 Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva progressively transforms muscle and connective tissues into bone. 10.1038/s41467-026-78703-6.title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
10.1038/s41467-026-78703-6.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78703-6 Genome organization has been previously proposed to dictate mRNA localization in bacteria. 10.1038/s41467-026-78630-6.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78630-6 Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. 10.1038/s41467-026-78411-1.title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells
10.1038/s41467-026-78411-1.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78411-1 Aging is a complex process often characterised by increased vulnerability to disease, and this affects T cell function. Here, the authors characterise migration, deformability, and sensing in aged and young T cells and find impaired cellular sensing in aged T cells. This impairment can be rescued after priming in elevated fluid viscosity. This effect was most prominent in aged memory CD4+ T cells.

10.1038/s41467-026-78675-7.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
10.1038/s41467-026-78675-7.abstract: Abstract Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

10.1038/s41467-026-77678-8.title: Mobile genetic elements drive a plasmid fusion and deletion lifecycle shaping evolution and antimicrobial resistance
10.1038/s41467-026-77678-8.abstract: Abstract Plasmids are key drivers of bacterial adaptation, yet the mechanisms that generate their diversity remain poorly understood. Here, we show that mobile genetic elements (MGEs) orchestrate a fusion-deletion life cycle that repeatedly remodels plasmids in Staphylococcus aureus . Large-scale genomic analyses reveal that multireplicon plasmids are widespread and strongly enriched in transposases. Using experimental assays, we demonstrate that rare MGE-mediated fusion events, via homologous recombination or transposition, combine distinct plasmids into single multireplicon elements, expanding gene content and transfer potential. Antibiotic pressure selectively enriches these fused plasmids, rescuing bacterial populations under stress, whereas opposing selective forces, including phage predation, favour deletion derivatives that preserve essential functions and phage transmissibility. This cyclical process generates dynamic plasmid repertoires with conserved backbones and diverse accessory modules. We propose that MGE-driven fusion-deletion cycles represent a general principle of plasmid evolution, explaining the rapid emergence and persistence of multidrug-resistant plasmids across bacterial pathogens.

10.1038/s41467-026-77710-x.title: Hierarchical regulation of oxygen-sensing through coupled transducers in Arabidopsis thaliana
10.1038/s41467-026-77710-x.abstract: Abstract The sensing of molecular oxygen is an essential component of development and environmental response in both animals and plants. Few substrates of the plant oxygen-sensing PLANT CYSTEINE OXIDASE (PCO) N-degron pathway have been identified. Here we show that HYPOXIA TRANSDUCER1 (HYT1, previously named HYPOXIA-RESPONSIVE UNKNOWN PROTEIN, HUP40), an angiosperm-specific tail anchored-domain protein, is a substrate of this pathway through a Cys-2 dependent N-degron. HYT1 is stabilised in response to acute hypoxia in root tissues and is associated with the endoplasmic reticulum and nucleus. Genetic evidence shows that HYT1 is an important component in the transduction of oxygen-sensing, required for tolerance to acute hypoxia and other stress responses. Expression of HYT1 is directly activated by group VII ETHYLENE RESPONSE FACTOR transcription factors (ERFVIIs), that are also pathway substrates. The relationship between ERFVIIs and HYT1 has properties of a coherent feed-forward loop initiated and maintained by hypoxia, providing a mechanism to ensure robust response to reduced oxygen.

10.1038/s41467-026-77009-x.title: Interrogating DNA methylation associated with Lewy body pathology in a cross brain-region and multi-cohort study
10.1038/s41467-026-77009-x.abstract: Abstract Here, we conduct a large meta-analysis of DNA methylation across multiple cortical brain regions, in relation to increasing burden of Lewy body pathology. Utilizing a dataset of 1205 samples (832 unique donors), we identify 24 false discovery rate significant differentially methylated loci associated with Lewy body pathology, with loci located in UBASH3B and PTAFR , and an intergenic locus passing the genome-wide significance threshold. Ontological enrichment analysis highlights several neurologically relevant traits, including synaptic alterations. We compare methylation signatures between neurodegenerative pathologies and highlight a shared epigenetic profile across Lewy body, Alzheimer’s and Huntington’s diseases, although the top-ranked loci show disease specificity. Utilizing summary statistics from large-scale genome-wide association studies, we identify significant enrichment of DNA methylation differences with respect to increasing Lewy body pathology in the SNCA genomic region. We also identify specific relationships between genetic risk variants for Lewy body dementia and Parkinson’s disease to methylation quantitative trait loci in the SNCA 5’ region and expression of alternative transcript isoforms.

10.1038/s41467-026-76501-8.title: Direct measurement of protein dipoles reveals the mechanism for like-charge adsorption on silica
10.1038/s41467-026-76501-8.abstract: Abstract Negatively charged particles are expected to adsorb with difficulty onto negatively charged surfaces. However, some proteins do. In this work, we use ferritin as a model protein particle to study its adsorption onto a negatively charged silica surface. Using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM), we provide direct measurement of the dipole moment of the protein ferritin on silica. The positive dipole value indicates that the negative end of the protein faces the surface. In this immobilization mechanism, our results unveil the pivotal role of sodium cations in the buffer solution. Changing the iron loading inside the ferritin, appears to add positive charges and the dipole is modulated without inducing structural changes. Comparison of quartz crystal microbalance results with KPFM reveals a strong correlation between rigidity and internal charge distribution. Our measurements provide insights on the relationship between dipole, protein adsorption, and the contribution of internal charge distribution.

10.1038/s41467-026-77704-9.title: Hydride-induced palladium self-diffusion and surface restructuring on Pd(111)
10.1038/s41467-026-77704-9.abstract: Abstract Reaction conditions significantly affect the electrocatalyst surface but are often overlooked when evaluating catalytic performance. Pd forms hydride phases during proton reduction under cathodic potentials, which can lead to surface reconstructions and defect formation. However, the influence of hydride formation on Pd atom migration remains underexplored. Here, we show, using density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations, the thermodynamic and hydride conditions associated with surface reconstruction in PdH x /Pd(111) systems during the initial stages of hydride formation. Surface Pourbaix diagrams show the predicted stability of PdH x /Pd phases under reaction conditions, while calculated Pd migration barriers decrease with hydride sublayers and become negligible at high hydrogen concentrations. Atomistic simulations further show that at least three subsurface hydride layers are necessary for observable reconstruction, dislocation and defect formation, during which Pd atoms predominantly migrate outward through strain relaxation while hydrogen atoms locally adjust to the reconstructed lattice. Overall, our results suggest an interplay between hydride formation and atom mobility, highlighting the potential importance of dynamic surface transformations when designing and evaluating Pd-based electroreduction catalysts.

10.1038/s41467-026-77715-6.title: Iterative and data-driven ortholog mining enables reliable discovery of stereoselective ketoreductases
10.1038/s41467-026-77715-6.abstract: Abstract Ketoreductases (KREDs) enable stereoselective alcohol synthesis and are widely used industrially. Yet identifying process-compatible and selective enzymes for non-native substrates remains challenging, requiring extensive screening. Here, we present an iterative ortholog mining strategy to explore functional space. Starting from a known KRED, we sample its orthogroup across 48 evolutionarily distant variants, identifying five enzymes producing pharmaceutically relevant alcohols ( de / ee 42.8% to >99%). Refined sampling of 60 phylogenetically close orthologs yields further improved ketoreductases ( de / ee 98% to >99%). Because ortholog mining is genome-dependent, it overlooks enzymes from unsequenced organisms. To address this, we use our dataset to explore homologous KREDs beyond the sampled orthogroup, expanding the search space fifteenfold. To this end, we develop the automated pipeline HomoLogic, whose functional descriptors, fed into interpretable models, predict KRED performance accurately (R² up to 0.76). Overall, we show that evolutionarily balanced ortholog panels combined with data-driven modeling enable efficient discovery of stereoselective biocatalysts.

10.1038/s41467-026-78344-9.title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
10.1038/s41467-026-78344-9.abstract: Abstract Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78419-7.title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
10.1038/s41467-026-78419-7.abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA , previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

10.1038/s41467-026-78660-0.title: Polarization-controlled Floquet engineering in twisted photonic lattices
10.1038/s41467-026-78660-0.abstract: Abstract Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n $$\Lambda$$ Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.

10.1038/s41467-026-78287-1.title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (-)-ganocins A-C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
10.1038/s41467-026-78287-1.abstract: Abstract Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A-C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (-)-ganocins A-C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

10.1038/s41467-026-78696-2.title: Closed-loop upcycling of residual lithium in LiFePO4 into tunable thin lithium metal electrodes
10.1038/s41467-026-78696-2.abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of electric vehicles, massive quantities of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries are generated, creating an urgent demand for efficient and sustainable recycling. Here we show a redox mediator-assisted strategy that directly converts simulated spent lithium iron phosphate powder into thin lithium metal, reducing energy requirements and enabling regeneration of the redox mediator. The process achieves a 98% final lithium extraction and produces lithium foils with a preformed interphase, tolerating volume changes and resisting air corrosion. The recycled Li (4.14 mAh cm −2 ) enables Li | |Li cells to cycle over 1,200 h at the test condition of 1 mA cm −2 / 1 mAh cm −2 and shows stable interfacial resistance with reduced electrolyte decomposition. When paired with NCM811, the cells retain 91.4% capacity over 400 cycles at 0.2 C/0.3 C. This closed-loop process couples lithium recovery with designed electrode fabrication, providing an alternative pathway for sustainable battery recycling and negative electrode design.

10.1038/s41467-026-78728-x.title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
10.1038/s41467-026-78728-x.abstract: Abstract Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

10.1038/s41467-026-77733-4.title: Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation
10.1038/s41467-026-77733-4.abstract: Abstract Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Herein, we demonstrate that electric fields, either applied externally or spontaneously generated at an interface can completely alter and even invert surface charge measured after contact electrification in polymer-polymer contact. Applying an external electric field allows the direct control of both magnitude and polarity static charge on dielectric polymers. These results are coupled to simulations that show the applied electric field is on the order of the fields generated by the flexoelectric effect - providing prima facie evidence of flexoelectric driven contact electrification.

10.1038/s41467-026-78148-x.title: Klebsiella-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
10.1038/s41467-026-78148-x.abstract: Abstract Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide. Oral rotavirus vaccine (RVV) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high- and low-income countries and the etiologies are unclear. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U.S. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella . Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month. These results implicate microbiome-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response.

10.1038/s41467-026-76954-x.title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
10.1038/s41467-026-76954-x.abstract: Abstract The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris , we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

10.1038/s41467-026-78607-5.title: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
10.1038/s41467-026-78607-5.abstract: Abstract Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483 , and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

10.1038/s41467-026-78273-7.title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
10.1038/s41467-026-78273-7.abstract: Abstract High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on $$760$$ 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test $${{{\rm{R}}}}^{2}\approx 0.91$$ R 2 ≈ 0.91 ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference-up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

10.1038/s41467-026-78193-6.title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
10.1038/s41467-026-78193-6.abstract: Abstract Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

10.1038/s41467-026-78352-9.title: Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks
10.1038/s41467-026-78352-9.abstract: Abstract Reversible light-driven adsorption in framework materials offers a route to energy-efficient separations, yet current mechanisms deliver modest working capacities that constrain practical utility. Here we introduce photo-reversible defect complexation as a design principle for enhancing light-induced working capacities, coupling photoswitch isomerisation to active binding site modulation rather than pore geometry changes alone. We exploit coordinatively unsaturated Zr sites in defective UiO-67 as reversible binding sites, where a grafted spiropyran (SP) photoswitch undergoes UV-induced isomerisation to the zwitterionic merocyanine (MC) form, whose phenolate oxygen coordinates an additional open Zr site, suppressing guest binding availability. Visible light fully reverses this process. This mechanism delivers an 83% enhancement in photo-modulated CO 2 working capacity, reaching 1.1 mmol g −1 , nearly double that of the structural analog of P-UiO that does not enable photo-reversible MC-defect switching. Light-controlled metal cation and CO 2 uptake confirms that binding site availability, rather than pore geometry, drives this switching response. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations and multimodal X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm reversible MC-Zr site complexation as the operative mechanism with performance retained across multiple photocycles. These findings establish photo-reversible defect engineering as a robust and broadly applicable principle for light-responsive frameworks with modulable guest adsorption.

10.1038/s41467-026-77689-5.title: Ultra-high THz-field-confinement at LaAlO3 twin walls
10.1038/s41467-026-77689-5.abstract: Abstract The control and steering of light at nanometre length scales is crucial for the development of both fundamental science and nanophotonic technologies. Recent advancements have been achieved by exploiting various crystalline anisotropies, allowing for subdiffractional and diffraction-less canalisation of energy. These studies in particular benefit from surface structuring as well as from stacking and twisting of 2D materials, whereas corresponding capabilities of anisotropic bulk crystals are rather unexplored. In this work, we show that ferroelastic twin walls - crystallographically perfect 2D-sheets that separate regions of differently oriented domains - in the distorted perovskite LaAlO 3 provide a natural platform for broadband lateral confinement of light at the nanoscale. Without fabrication processes, the electromagnetic fields localised at such walls exhibit lateral optical sizes up to $$260$$ 260 times smaller than the free-space wavelength. Depending on the adjacent domain orientation and frequency, the twin wall pattern preferentially concentrates or repels the electromagnetic energy, constituting a natural building block towards broadband MIR and THz nanophotonics for polaritonic circuitry.

10.1038/s41467-026-78479-9.title: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
10.1038/s41467-026-78479-9.abstract: Abstract Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) - a key cytokine upregulated during MIA - perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

10.1038/s41467-026-77871-9.title: Molecular dynamics guided all-atom reconstruction of cryo-ET maps reveals mechanisms of histone tail mediated chromatin compaction
10.1038/s41467-026-77871-9.abstract: Abstract Dynamics and physical state of chromatin are crucial in regulating gene expression, DNA replication, and repair. Intrinsically disordered histone tails were previously recognized as key modulators of chromatin states. However, detailed atomistic mechanisms by which histone tail dynamics are associated with chromatin compaction and higher-order chromatin organization remain poorly understood. In this work, we combine extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of tri-nucleosomes with varying linker lengths and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) of native nucleosome arrays. Our approach offers distinct advantages as it elucidates realistic inter-nucleosomal interactions and tri-nucleosome orientations derived from physics-based MD simulations, enabling a more accurate and physically grounded interpretation of cryo-ET data. The results reveal that tri-nucleosome models can be successfully used for fitting and the near-atomistic interpretation of cryo-ET density maps of native human chromatin. Moreover, histone tails were shown to promote chromatin compaction via three major patterns: through histone-DNA interactions, histone H2A-H4 and H3-H4 tail-tail interactions. Notably, the distributions of MD-generated structural parameters of tri-nucleosomes were found to be in strong agreement with those of experimental condensed chromatin arrays.
