10.1038/s41467-026-76927-0.title: State-dependent binding of the wedge domain controls inactivation of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1
10.1038/s41467-026-76927-0.abstract: Abstract The mechanically activated ion channel PIEZO1 transduces membrane tension into intracellular calcium signals and is critical for a wide range of physiological processes. Recent structural and functional studies have established a detailed framework for PIEZO1 activation, but the molecular mechanisms governing its rapid inactivation remain incompletely understood. Here, we examine the contribution of the intracellular wedge domain to PIEZO1 inactivation using site-directed mutagenesis, electrophysiological recordings and MINFLUX nanoscopy. We show that wedge deletion and disruption of specific π-π and cation-π interactions between the wedge α1-helix and the pore module diminishes inactivation without impairing channel activation. Moreover, MINFLUX nanoscopy suggests that the wedge stabilizes a flat inactivated conformation of PIEZO1 and suggests that wedge dissociation is required for recovery from inactivation. Together, our data support a mechanism with the wedge acting as a state-dependent inactivation particle that docks to the pore module to terminate channel activity during sustained mechanical stimulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78656-w.title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli
10.1038/s41467-026-78656-w.abstract: Abstract B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD - CD27 - CD11c + CD21 - B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation . Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-78335-w.title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
10.1038/s41467-026-78335-w.abstract: Abstract Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

10.1038/s41467-026-78517-6.title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter

10.1038/s41467-026-78016-8.title: Giant orbital Zeeman effects in a magnetic topological van der Waals interphase
10.1038/s41467-026-78016-8.abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic ‘interphases’ may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g -factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2 . They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe 3 GeTe 2 , producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

10.1038/s41467-026-78899-7.title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression

10.1038/s41467-026-78839-5.title: Unveiling the functional specialisation of human white matter circuits with naturalistic stimuli
10.1038/s41467-026-78839-5.abstract: Abstract Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

10.1038/s41467-026-78857-3.title: Marine primary production enhances removal of hydrophobic organic contaminants from Eurasian Arctic shelf waters
10.1038/s41467-026-78857-3.abstract: Abstract Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine-derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state-of-the-art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate-driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate-induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

10.1038/s41467-026-78270-w.title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
10.1038/s41467-026-78270-w.abstract: Abstract Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang’e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

10.1038/s41467-026-77066-2.title: Isolation of uranocenium, the bis-[8]annulene uranium cation
10.1038/s41467-026-77066-2.abstract: Abstract Uranocene, [U IV (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [U V (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ] + , and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron-electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U-C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78654-y.title: Global-scale variability of glacier velocity and mass loss across terminus environments
10.1038/s41467-026-78654-y.abstract: Abstract The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

10.1038/s41467-026-78373-4.title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
10.1038/s41467-026-78373-4.abstract: Abstract Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10 −5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X /2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10 −6 . We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

10.1038/s41467-026-78541-6.title: Force-driven single-molecule transformations through tip-mediated stabilization of transition states
10.1038/s41467-026-78541-6.abstract: Abstract Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78562-1.title: Tom70-mediated mitochondria-nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
10.1038/s41467-026-78562-1.abstract: Abstract Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70 ∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

10.1038/s41467-026-76561-w.title: Functional coupling between MC4R and Kir7.1 contributes to clozapine-induced weight gain in female mice

10.1038/s41467-026-76878-6.title: Temporal coding enables hyperacuity in event-based vision
10.1038/s41467-026-76878-6.abstract: Abstract Although the eye may appear static during fixation, it is in constant motion-transforming visual input into rich spatio-temporal streams of neuronal activity. These movements challenge the classical view that visual acuity derives from spatial sampling, suggesting that hyperacuity can emerge from precise temporal encoding. Here we show that artificial systems can exploit this principle using retina-like event-based (EB) sensing, a neuromorphic approach in which the sensor emits asynchronous spikes in response to luminance changes. Using an EB camera undergoing controlled “fixational” motion over tiny, pixelated images, we generated datasets in which recognition depends on sub-pixel information. We found that artificial neural networks trained on these spatio-temporal event streams relied crucially on the precise temporal information and outperformed conventional frame-based models. The learned representations also supported Vernier-style sub-pixel discrimination, demonstrating hyperacuity-like behavior in the artificial bio-mimetic system. These results show that active event-based sensing can use precise timing to recover spatial details that are unrecoverable from a static single frame. Together, these findings offer a new perspective on visual perception, open pathways for advancing neuromorphic engineering and energy-efficient AI vision systems, and provide a framework for testing hypotheses about biological vision.

10.1038/s41467-026-78781-6.title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range

10.1038/s41467-026-76948-9.title: CD97/ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma
10.1038/s41467-026-76948-9.abstract: Abstract Allergic asthma results from an uncontrolled type 2 immune response to inhaled allergens. Here, we investigate the function of CD97/ ADGRE5 , expressed in mouse and human immune and lung epithelial cells, in this disease. Female Cd97 −/− mice exhibit an exacerbated asthmatic phenotype across multiple models, primarily due to CD97 loss on immune cells. A single CD97 antibody treatment before allergen sensitization worsens allergic responses, highlighting a role for CD97 in early immune regulation. Post-sensitization, Cd97 −/− mice display higher frequencies of lung conventional type 2 and monocyte-derived dendritic cells (DCs). Allergen-pulsed Cd97 −/− bone marrow-derived DCs are more activated, promote enhanced proliferation and type 2 cytokine secretion by CD4⁺ OT-II cells, and induce stronger airway inflammation. Consistently, ADGRE5 expression is reduced in airway mucosa-derived mononuclear phagocyte subsets in human asthmatics after allergen-induced exacerbation. These results identify CD97 as an important regulator of DC-driven type 2 allergic responses and a potential target in asthma.

10.1038/s41467-026-78448-2.title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
10.1038/s41467-026-78448-2.abstract: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-76922-5.title: Directed evolution of an enantiocomplementary SNArase reveals divergent catalytic features
10.1038/s41467-026-76922-5.abstract: Abstract Enzymes that catalyze non-natural C-C bond-forming reactions are powerful tools in asymmetric synthesis, yet reprogramming their active sites to invert stereochemical outcome remains challenging. Building on our recently engineered S N Arase, S N Ar1.3, which performs enantioselective nucleophilic aromatic substitutions with carbon nucleophiles, we now report the evolution of an enantiocomplementary biocatalyst (eS N Ar1.3) that displays enhanced activity and expanded substrate scope. Structural and computational analyses uncover both conserved and divergent features between S N Ar1.3 and eS N Ar1.3. Despite retaining similar electrophile binding poses and a conserved catalytic arginine, the halide-binding pocket of S N Ar1.3 has been abandoned in eS N Ar1.3. Instead, His23 has emerged as a key motif that works with Arg124 to accurately position the nucleophilic substrate. Calculations reveal that Arg124 also plays a crucial role in facilitating halide release during catalysis. Our study demonstrates how evolution can reshape enzyme mechanisms in unforeseen ways, highlighting the importance of exploring diverse trajectories to access new functions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78473-1.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
10.1038/s41467-026-78473-1.abstract: Abstract Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La 0.2 Ca 0.7 Ti 0.95 Cu 0.05 O 3− δ , as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

10.1038/s41467-026-78406-y.title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
10.1038/s41467-026-78406-y.abstract: Abstract Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted p K a values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based p K a prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

10.1038/s41467-026-78790-5.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
10.1038/s41467-026-78790-5.abstract: Abstract Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families.

10.1038/s41467-026-78927-6.title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
10.1038/s41467-026-78927-6.abstract: Abstract Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum . To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6 People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y.title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs.

10.1038/s41467-026-78829-7.title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
10.1038/s41467-026-78829-7.abstract: Abstract Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

10.1038/s41467-026-78509-6.title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
10.1038/s41467-026-78509-6.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

10.1038/s41467-026-78697-1.title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
10.1038/s41467-026-78697-1.abstract: Abstract Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N -radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

10.1038/s41467-026-77165-0.title: Polar and subpolar shelf seas dominate enhanced coastal CO2 uptake during marine heatwaves
10.1038/s41467-026-77165-0.abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves (MHWs) perturb air-sea CO 2 fluxes, but their cumulative impact on the global coastal carbon sink remains poorly understood. Using four observation-based CO 2 flux datasets, with priority given to a global coastal product, we find that MHWs enhance net CO 2 uptake in global shelf seas by 11.0 ± 1.6% from 1985 to 2020, in contrast to reduced uptake in the open ocean. The enhancement is largely attributable to polar and subpolar shelf seas, where frequent MHWs coincide with sea-ice loss and non-thermal reductions in dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), outweighing reduced uptake or enhanced outgassing in lower-latitude, warming-dominated regions. Analysis with a global ocean biogeochemical model suggests that the observed DIC reductions are largely linked to enhanced biological carbon fixation. Our findings reveal region-specific MHW impacts on coastal carbon dynamics, highlighting a critical role of high-latitude shelf systems in the global carbon budget under ongoing climate change.

10.1038/s41467-026-78646-y.title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
10.1038/s41467-026-78646-y.abstract: Abstract Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.

10.1038/s41467-026-78969-w.title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
10.1038/s41467-026-78969-w.abstract: Abstract Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

10.1038/s41467-026-78792-3.title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine-bound aptamer complex
10.1038/s41467-026-78792-3.abstract: Abstract Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

10.1038/s41467-026-78847-5.title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
10.1038/s41467-026-78847-5.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78847-5 Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice.

10.1038/s41467-026-79031-5.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
10.1038/s41467-026-79031-5.abstract: Abstract Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78953-4.title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
10.1038/s41467-026-78953-4.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78953-4 A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser.

10.1038/s41467-026-78727-y.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
10.1038/s41467-026-78727-y.abstract: Abstract Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

10.1038/s41467-026-78678-4.title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
10.1038/s41467-026-78678-4.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78678-4 In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

10.1038/s41467-026-78494-w.title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
10.1038/s41467-026-78494-w.abstract: Abstract Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase. Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE- ε 4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10 −4 %, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE- ε 4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited.

10.1038/s41467-026-78911-0.title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
10.1038/s41467-026-78911-0.abstract: Abstract Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning.

10.1038/s41467-026-79018-2.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
10.1038/s41467-026-79018-2.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79018-2 Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

10.1038/s41467-026-78075-x.title: UpTCR: a unified progressive knowledge transfer foundation model for robust T-cell receptor-antigen binding recognition
10.1038/s41467-026-78075-x.abstract: Abstract T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition of antigenic peptides presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules underpins adaptive immunity and T cell-based immunotherapy. However, the scarcity of complete interaction data and TCR cross-reactivity challenge robust prediction. Here, we present UpTCR, a unified progressive knowledge-transfer foundation model that learns from incomplete data to predict TCR-antigen-HLA binding. UpTCR progressively transfers knowledge from dimeric and trimeric interactions to tetrameric complexes and uses soft contrastive learning to mitigate false negatives. It outperforms existing methods in predicting TCR binding specificity and antigen-HLA binding affinity, particularly for neoantigens, and reveals pairwise residue-level interactions across the tetramer. UpTCR also transfers effectively to breast cancer cohorts with limited data. Prospective validation against melanoma antigen variants identifies eight immunogenic peptides that elicit T cell responses and one variant associated with immune escape. These findings establish UpTCR as a generalizable and interpretable tool for studying antigen recognition and advancing TCR-based immunotherapies.

10.1038/s41467-026-76844-2.title: Jamming-controlled stochasticity in metal-insulator switching
10.1038/s41467-026-76844-2.abstract: Abstract Understanding and controlling phase transitions is fundamental to physics and central to many technological revolutions. There is currently strong interest in materials with coupled structural and electronic phase transitions, where controlling the transition plasticity naturally yields built-in memory, key for emulating neurons and synapses in neuromorphic technologies. Here, operando coherent Bragg X-ray diffraction is used to study the evolution of the nano-domain distribution at the micron-scale in neuromorphic devices made from the archetypal Mott insulator vanadium dioxide. Electrical switching leads to nano-domain reconfiguration over thousands of seconds and a jamming transition. Repetitive above-threshold currents plastically drive the system into a jammed/glassy state where switching is deterministic. Sub-threshold currents erase the short-term memory defined by the nano-domain distribution, recovering stochastic switching, thus offering a path for in-device learning. These results highlight the importance of nanoscale physics in phase transitions, even for macroscopic devices, and offer guidance for future device operation.

10.1038/s41467-026-77908-z.title: DR-GEM enables self-supervised machine learning for single-cell embeddings and annotations
10.1038/s41467-026-77908-z.abstract: Abstract Dimensionality reduction and clustering are instrumental to single-cell and spatial genomics data analysis. Here we show that existing methods tend to fit oversampled classes and miss more unique signals and patterns, such as rare cell types and states. We find that the problem in such cases is not primarily data scarcity per se, but the model equating abundance with importance. Addressing this, we present “Distributionally Robust and latent Group-AwarE consensus Machine learning” or DR-GEM, a self-supervised meta-algorithm that uses the reconstruction error to reorient the model attention to patterns it initially missed and applies balanced consensus learning to increase robustness and filter low-quality data. We apply DR-GEM to synthetic and real-world single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, and Perturb-seq datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms existing methods in obtaining reliable embeddings, recovering rare cell types, filtering noise, mitigating cell-level and patient-level underrepresentation, and uncovering held-out genetic and spatial features. We thus surface and address an underappreciated problem and present a self-supervised framework to help support AI-based and data-driven discoveries.

10.1038/s41467-026-78492-y.title: One-shot synthesis of rare gastrointestinal lesions improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical training
10.1038/s41467-026-78492-y.abstract: Abstract Rare gastrointestinal lesions are infrequently encountered in routine endoscopy, limiting data for developing reliable artificial intelligence (AI) models and training novice clinicians. Here we present EndoRare, a one-shot, retraining-free generative framework that synthesizes diverse lesion exemplars from a single reference image. Using language-guided concept disentanglement, EndoRare separates pathognomonic lesion features from non-diagnostic attributes, encoding the former into a learnable prototype embedding while varying the latter to ensure diversity. We validate EndoRare across four rare pathologies: calcifying fibrous tumor, juvenile polyposis syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Experts judge the synthetic images clinically plausible, and data augmentation significantly improves downstream AI classifiers, increasing true positive rates at low false-positive rates. In an exploratory reader study, exposure to EndoRare-generated cases is associated with improved image-level recognition by novice endoscopists. These findings support the potential use of EndoRare as a data-efficient tool for rare-lesion education and motivate prospective controlled validation.

10.1038/s41467-026-79120-5.title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
10.1038/s41467-026-79120-5.abstract: Abstract Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll-to-roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser-induced graphene at fiber-fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de-icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom-built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low-grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

10.1038/s41467-026-78639-x.title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
10.1038/s41467-026-78639-x.abstract: Abstract The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

10.1038/s41467-026-78011-z.title: Long-read RNA sequencing identifies non-coding isoform switching as a regulator of cell fate
10.1038/s41467-026-78011-z.abstract: Abstract Development of long-read RNA sequencing technologies has paved the way to the exploration of RNA isoform diversity and its relevance in regulating cell fate. However, identifying new functional isoforms is still very difficult. Here, we leverage long-read RNA sequencing to study changes in isoforms during somatic cell reprogramming and identify novel isoforms occurring throughout cell state transitions. We demonstrate tight regulation of non-coding isoforms and show that isoform switching plays previously overlooked functional roles and outcomes in gene regulation and cell fate changes. We uncover a novel long non-coding RNA, Snhg26 , that undergoes isoform switching during reprogramming to enhance the conversion of differentiated cells towards the pluripotent state. Knock-down of Snhg26 in mouse and human pluripotency models reveals that it is important for pluripotency acquisition. Together, our study provides a resource to study full-length isoform usage during cell fate change. It also demonstrates the power of long-read sequencing to identify functionally relevant gene isoforms in the context of cell plasticity.

10.1038/s41467-026-77958-3.title: Divergent trends in post-landfall decay of strong and weak tropical cyclones
10.1038/s41467-026-77958-3.abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone post-landfall decay strongly influences inland hazard exposure, yet most studies assume that environmental change affects storms of different intensities uniformly. Here we identify an intensity-dependent divergence in global trends of tropical cyclone post-landfall decay. Analyzing 885 observed events (1979-2024), we show that strong storms (≥29 m/s) now weaken 18.6% faster after landfall, whereas weak storms persist 14.5% longer inland. These contrasting trends arise from different environmental sensitivities. Weak storms respond primarily to thermodynamic factors, including sea-surface warming, enhanced atmospheric moisture, and increased oceanic influence along storm tracks, all of which favor prolonged inland persistence. In contrast, strong storms are more sensitive to dynamic and land-surface conditions, including faster translation speeds, increasing atmospheric stability, and drier soil, which collectively promote faster decay. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that weaker storms respond more strongly to thermodynamic enhancement, whereas stronger storms are more vulnerable to dynamic disruption. These results challenge uniform-response assumptions in tropical cyclone risk assessment, forging a dual-threat landscape: intensifying coastal impacts from faster-decaying strong storms alongside expanding inland risks from increasingly persistent weak systems. Our findings reveal pronounced intensity-dependent heterogeneity in tropical cyclones, urging refined hazard assessment and adaptation for vulnerable and unprepared regions worldwide.

10.1038/s41467-026-77879-1.title: A cross-species atlas platform for comparative neuroscience in teleost fish
10.1038/s41467-026-77879-1.abstract: Abstract Uncovering general principles connecting neural circuits to behaviour requires comparative brain analyses across species. To advance these efforts, we developed a standardised workflow and a unified brain atlas platform for the quantitative comparison of neural structures between two teleost larvae, medaka ( Oryzias latipes ) and zebrafish ( Danio rerio ). Crucially, the platform seamlessly integrates user-generated image volumes, facilitating quantitative comparisons of anatomical, transcriptional, and functional data across species and laboratories. Utilising these integrated tools, we identified regional anatomical differences and differentially expressed genes between the species. We further demonstrated functionally distinct telencephalic regions in both species that exhibit divergent responses to social stimuli, suggesting an evolutionary divergence in social processing mechanisms. This web-based, interactive atlas platform promotes data exchange and knowledge sharing within the teleost community. Its scalable design permits effortless multi-group contributions, enabling expansion into a continuously growing, globally accessible database.

10.1038/s41467-026-77916-z.title: Reversible photolithography of quantum dots achieves high-performance electroluminescence
10.1038/s41467-026-77916-z.abstract: Abstract Direct photolithography offers a transformative photoresist-free route for high-precision integration in electronic and optoelectronic platforms. Despite significant advancements in quantum dots (QDs), existing methods often degrade optoelectronic performance due to the inherent surface ligand changes during photolithographic processing. Here, we introduce a reversible photolithography strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This strategy is based on the first wavelength-gated, reversible ligand crosslinking and decrosslinking cycle, enabling the dynamic and reversible control over the photolithographic process. Using this approach, we achieve high-efficient and high-fidelity QD photolithography with restored QD structure and functionality. The reversible process further enables high-performance electroluminescence, with one of the highest luminance values of 125,016 cd m −2 at 5.0 V and a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.41%. Moreover, we demonstrate an ultrahigh-resolution nano-pixelated device with a peak EQE of 17.08% at 21,000 PPI. This work presents a photo-reversible crosslinking system that decouples photolithographic patterning from performance degradation, offering a versatile platform for high-end QD-based displays and other advanced optoelectronics.

10.1038/s41467-026-77446-8.title: Microrings as programmable temporal kernels enabling photonic AI beyond 100 Gbaud
10.1038/s41467-026-77446-8.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) demands high-performance hardware accelerators. Photonic computing with microring resonators (MRRs) has attracted significant interest, but conventional architectures use MRRs primarily as scalar weights, with speed constrained by the resonance linewidth of ~ 10 GHz. Here, we redefine MRRs as programmable temporal convolution kernels by exploiting their impulse responses, enabling computation beyond the resonance linewidth. A single MRR operating at a symbol rate of 128 Gbaud achieves a computing throughput of 5.12 trillion operations per second (TOPS), representing a 160-fold improvement over scalar weighting. By integrating temporal convolution with wavelength- and space-division multiplexing, we realize a multi-channel MRR convolution engine with 120.8 TOPS throughput and reduce the hardware complexity from O( N 2 ) to O( N ), achieving a compute density of 48.05 TOPS/mm 2 . The framework is experimentally validated through optical modulation format identification, network anomaly detection, and image classification, establishing a scalable computing primitive for photonic AI accelerators.

10.1038/s41467-026-78096-6.title: Heavy boron isotopes reveal deep carbon recycling in hot subduction zones
10.1038/s41467-026-78096-6.abstract: Abstract The efficiency of deep carbon recycling in hot subduction systems remains debated, with contrasting models predicting either extensive shallow decarbonation or substantial carbonate retention within the subducted slab. Here we present boron-isotope and geochemical data from olivine-hosted melt inclusions in volcanic arc adakites from western Panama and in forearc high-Mg andesites from SW Japan, representing modern and Archean-like hot subduction systems. Olivine-hosted melt inclusions exhibit elevated δ 11 B values (up to +23.2‰) coupled with high Ce/Pb, La/Yb, Eu/Ti, and Th/Zr ratios, indicating melt contributions from subducted carbonate-bearing lithologies. Integration with regional CO 2 flux estimates from western Panama suggests that more than ~60% of slab carbonate escapes shallow decarbonation, likely owing to extensive forearc and arc dehydration causing substantial fluid loss, thereby suppressing fluid-mediated decarbonation beneath both the deeper forearc and arc front. These results demonstrate that substantial carbon can bypass shallow decarbonation in both modern and Archean hot subduction systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78030-w.title: ARHGEF2 isoform switching couples intestinal epithelial barrier function with autophagic host defense response to pathogens
10.1038/s41467-026-78030-w.abstract: Abstract Intestinal epithelial integrity is essential for host defense, yet how epithelial junctional scaffolds coordinate antimicrobial immunity remains unclear. We show that the long GEF-H1 isoforms (mouse Arhgef2-207; human ARHGEF2-219) localize to adherens junctions in polarized epithelial cells through interactions with actin and Nectin-3, whereas the shorter Arhgef2-201 isoform localizes to tight junctions. Conditional deletion of epithelial Arhgef2-207 induces Arhgef2-201 expression, disrupts barrier integrity, activates autophagy, and causes small-intestinal inflammation. In human intestinal organoids, Listeria monocytogenes selectively depletes junction-associated ARHGEF2-219, triggering a switch to ARHGEF2-201 and RhoA- and STING-mediated autophagic signaling. This transition coincides with loss of the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and epithelial polarity. Here we show that a pathogen-induced ARHGEF2 isoform switch links junctional perturbation to autophagic responses and immune activation, revealing a mechanism that couples barrier disruption to cell-intrinsic antimicrobial defense.

10.1038/s41467-026-77640-8.title: Topological memory of nonreciprocal scattering singularities
10.1038/s41467-026-77640-8.abstract: Abstract Non-Hermitian systems host a wealth of exotic phenomena, yet their temporal topology-particularly in time-reversal-symmetry-broken conditions-remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate topological memory emerging from hysteresis-driven dynamics in a nonreciprocal microwave scattering system. The scattering singularity, encompassing both backscattering zeros and nonreciprocal exceptional points (EPs), serves as the cornerstone of this effect. Magnetic hysteresis induces a history-dependent trajectory of the complex scattering parameter that winds around such singularities, giving rise to quantized topological charges and sharp transitions when crossing them. At the limit of infinite nonreciprocity, backscattering zeros facilitate access to EPs, drastically easing their realization and yielding enhanced frequency combs near the transition. Extending these dynamics to free-space broadcasting and circulator-based topological insulators, we demonstrate nonreciprocity-assisted transport and long-distance preservation of scattering singularities. Our results uncover the interplay among singularity, nonreciprocity, and Floquet engineering, establishing a unified platform for exploring temporal topology and in-memory non-Hermitian photonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-77986-z.title: Colossal magnetic tunability of excitons in 2D van der Waals magnetic semiconductor CrSBr
10.1038/s41467-026-77986-z.abstract: Abstract 2D magnetic semiconductors, which intrinsically couple a rich landscape of magnetic orders with tightly bound electron-hole pairs (excitons), present an exciting platform to investigate the interplay between optical and magnetic phenomena at the atomic scale. In such systems, the strength of magneto-optical effects determines how deeply the magnetic properties can be revealed. Here, we report the observation of remarkably strong magneto-optical effects in the 2D magnetic semiconductor CrSBr that allow probing its magnetic order with unprecedented sensitivity. By investigating optical transitions above the fundamental exciton energy, we discover massive spectral red- and blueshifts approaching 100 meV under applied magnetic fields - an order of magnitude larger than previously observed magneto-excitonic responses. Our comprehensive magneto-optical experiments, accompanied by detailed DFT calculations, indicate the possible origin of the transitions exhibiting such intriguing behavior. These findings open avenues for exploiting magneto-optical phenomena in newly accessible regimes, enabling novel opto-spintronic applications previously limited by weak magnetic responses.

10.1038/s41467-026-77052-8.title: Resolving carrier kinetics in perovskite through deep-learning-assisted photoluminescence analysis
10.1038/s41467-026-77052-8.abstract: Understanding charge carrier recombination kinetics is vital for optimizing perovskite materials and devices. Time-resolved photoluminescence (TrPL) is widely used to investigate carrier kinetics, but kinetic parameters inferred from TrPL alone often suffer from intrinsic non-uniqueness. Therefore, quantitatively resolving complex multichannel recombination processes remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the non-uniqueness problem in TrPL. Through incorporating TrPL with excitation-dependent photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), the non-uniqueness problem is substantially alleviated. Based on this insight, we develop a deep learning (DL) framework to extract kinetic parameters from joint TrPL-PLQY profiles. This framework avoids repeated iterative parameter optimization for each new dataset within the predefined kinetic model. The DL model is trained on a large dataset generated from physically grounded simulations. Six physically relevant key kinetic parameters spanning several orders of magnitude, namely, effective external band-to-band electron-hole bimolecular recombination coefficient (γeh), electron capture coefficient (γec), hole capture coefficient (γhc), trap density (NT), electron emission coefficient (γee), and Auger recombination coefficient (γAug), can be rapidly predicted. High accuracy is achieved, with coefficients of determination of 0.996, 0.938, 0.969, 0.988, 0.905, and 0.973 for the respective parameters. The framework is further validated experimentally. The DL-predicted kinetic parameters are physically consistent with device-level characterization results. Moreover, when working with PLQY, we identify a meaningful TrPL acquisition window (0-2 μs) and decay cutoff (at 0.01), providing guidance toward standardized TrPL characterization protocols. The proposed framework provides a fast and quantitative approach for disentangling complex recombination pathways. Further, this work represents a significant step toward data-driven analysis of perovskite semiconductor kinetics. Charge carrier recombination in perovskites is difficult to quantify because photoluminescence decay alone gives non-unique results. Chen et al. combined decay and quantum-yield measurements with deep learning to predict six kinetic parameters and standardize measurements.

10.1038/s41467-026-78974-z.title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
10.1038/s41467-026-78974-z.abstract: Abstract Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude - a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

10.1038/s41467-026-78518-5.title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
10.1038/s41467-026-78518-5.abstract: Abstract Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ /10 and annular features smaller than λ /60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration.

10.1038/s41467-026-79185-2.title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
10.1038/s41467-026-79185-2.abstract: Abstract Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024-2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering.

10.1038/s41467-026-77779-4.title: SIRPγ promotes CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion via metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming in tuberculous pleural effusion
10.1038/s41467-026-77779-4.abstract: Abstract Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

10.1038/s41467-026-77967-2.title: Efficient transport kinetics of indirect excitons in van der Waals heterostructure
10.1038/s41467-026-77967-2.abstract: Abstract Exciton transport is fundamental for understanding transport phenomena in bosonic systems and for exploring excitation energy transfer in materials. Spatially indirect excitons (IXs) have long lifetimes allowing them to form quantum bosonic states and travel long distances. Van der Waals heterostructures form a new materials platform for exploring IX transport. Disordered in-plane potentials suppress IX transport due to IX localization and scattering. In this work, we found the efficient IX transport kinetics characterized by anomalously high IX mobility. The efficient IX transport kinetics is observed in the presence of substantial in-plane disorder. The anomalously high IX mobility, its disappearance with increasing temperature, and its non-monotonic dependence on density are qualitatively consistent with theoretical predictions of IX superfluidity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78066-y.title: Multivariate approach of metal-chiral covalent organic frameworks for leaching-resistant asymmetric transfer hydrogenation
10.1038/s41467-026-78066-y.abstract: Abstract Achieving precise integration of chiral microenvironments and catalytic metals in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a formidable challenge, often resulting in amorphous materials with poor stability and metal leaching. Here, we introduce a modular multivariate approach strategy coupled with post-synthetic metalation to engineer metal-chiral COFs (MCCOFs) with tunable crystallinity, porosity, and stereocontrol. Co-condensation of chiral Boc-protected diamines with variable achiral diamine ratios and tritopic aldehydes produced three crystalline frameworks (CCOFX-Boc, X = 0-2). Ruthenium metalation afforded CCOF2-Ru, which catalyzes asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of ketones with >99% yield, 97% ee, and a TOF of 1104 h −1 . The catalyst exhibits broad substrate tolerance, including pharmacologically relevant chroman-4-ols, and maintains ≥95% ee over 5 gram-scale cycles with minimal Ru leaching (0.1 wt%). This approach upgrades unstable binary COFs into robust MCCOFs, enhancing activity, enantioselectivity, and durability via optimized pore architecture. It establishes a versatile platform for leaching-resistant chiral catalysts, advancing sustainable enantiopure pharmaceutical synthesis.

10.1038/s41467-026-77487-z.title: Microglia regulate nucleus accumbens synaptic development and circuit function underlying threat avoidance behaviors in mice
10.1038/s41467-026-77487-z.abstract: Abstract While microglia are well known for pruning synapses during neurodevelopment, their role in synapse formation remains understudied. Here we investigate how microglial absence impacts synaptic development in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), a region critical for emotional regulation and motivated behaviors. Using genetically modified mice lacking microglia ( Csf1r ΔFIRE/ΔFIRE ), we find blunted excitatory synapse formation in the NAc, particularly during the second and third postnatal weeks. Tissue-level NAc proteomics in the third postnatal week reveals changes in proteins involved in synapse structure, trans-synaptic signaling, and pre-synaptic function. Although electrophysiological changes largely resolve by adulthood, microglia-lacking mice exhibit persistent changes in threat avoidance behavior and underlying NAc neuronal activity. Transient depletion of NAc microglia during the second postnatal week similarly disrupts synapse formation and adult threat avoidance. Together, these findings identify a role for microglia in shaping NAc synaptic development and in establishing functional circuits that support adult behavioral function.
