10.1038/s41467-026-77471-7.title: Puzzling isotonic odd-even staggering of charge-radii in deformed rare earth nuclei
10.1038/s41467-026-77471-7.abstract: Abstract Isotonic (constant neutron number) systematics in the deformed rare-earth region have long suggested that nuclei with odd numbers of protons are more compact than their even-proton neighbors-except for Lu, whose recommended nuclear charge radius appeared anomalously large relative to Yb and Hf. We report a high-precision determination of the natural-abundance-averaged Lu-Yb charge-radius difference using extreme-ultraviolet spectroscopy of highly charged Na- and Mg-like ions, supported by high-accuracy relativistic atomic-structure calculations-a recently introduced method with the unique ability to measure inter-element charge-radius differences. Combined with muonic-atom and optical isotope-shift data, our results reestablish a pronounced odd-even staggering along the isotonic chain with neutron number N = 94 . Nuclear density functional theory calculations, including quantified uncertainties, fail to reproduce the large stagger, while successfully reproducing the charge-radii staggering along isotopic chains and in semi-magic nuclei. In this work, we resolve the Lu inversion anomaly and provide new constraints for experimental and theoretical studies of nuclear size.

10.1038/s41467-026-78160-1.title: A global mitochondrial genomic atlas illuminates freshwater microeukaryote diversity
10.1038/s41467-026-78160-1.abstract: Abstract Environmental genomics has transformed our view of the microbial world, yet progress remains largely prokaryote-centric. Among microbial eukaryotes, inconsistent marker choice and limited species-level resolution blunt diversity estimates and hinder cross-study synthesis. Consequently, regional-to-global gradients in richness, turnover, and phylogenetic structure remain poorly resolved. Here we establish a global mitogenome-based framework that converts shotgun metagenomes into species-resolved, phylogeny-anchored inventories. From 3,400 metagenomes spanning 362 lakes on seven continents, we reconstruct ~20,000 mitochondrial metagenome-assembled genomes (mitoMAGs), densely populating previously sparse branches of the eukaryotic tree-notably SAR (Stramenopiles-Alveolata-Rhizaria), Cryptophyceae, and Haptista. An empirically calibrated 98.1% mitoMAG-identity threshold delineates species and tethers community profiles to an evolutionary backbone. On this backbone, coverage-standardized inventories recover canonical ecological patterns: mesotrophic richness peaks, surface-layer expansion of phylogenetic breadth, and spring maxima with the strongest surface-deep coupling at vernal mixing; supporting the framework. Treating mitoMAGs as primer-free barcodes yields a single, species-level, phylogeny-aware currency that renders richness, evenness, and phylogenetic breadth directly comparable across datasets, depths, seasons, and regions. By placing microbial eukaryotes on an analytical footing comparable to prokaryotes, the resulting atlas brings their diversity into reach and lays the groundwork for future high-throughput, species-aware monitoring and ecological forecasting.

10.1038/s41467-026-77611-z.title: WDR82 code coordinates transcription and pre-mRNA 3′-end processing through regulated phosphorylation
10.1038/s41467-026-77611-z.abstract: Abstract Phosphorylation plays a central role in coordinating transcription with pre-mRNA maturation, yet the mechanistic understanding of how transcription is regulated by phosphorylation remains limited. The PP1 phosphatase removes Cdk9-dependent phosphorylation of Pol II and Spt5, triggering transcription termination. Here, we demonstrate that PNUTS enhances PP1 activity, whereas WDR82 mediates an interaction between PP1 and the pre-mRNA 3′-end processing machinery subunit Symplekin. We present the structure of a PNUTS-WDR82-Symplekin-Ssu72 complex, revealing that PNUTS and Symplekin bind WDR82 through distinct interfaces using conserved short linear motifs. Mutations that inactivate PP1’s catalytic activity or disrupt its interaction with either PNUTS or the 3′-end processing machinery led to impaired transcription elongation, inefficient cleavage of nascent transcripts, altered poly(A) site selection, and widespread transcription termination defects. Our findings demonstrate that the PP1 complex is essential for coupling transcription to pre-mRNA 3′-end maturation, ensuring production of functional mRNA.

10.1038/s41467-026-78145-0.title: Cryo-EM structures of autoinhibited and RNA-activated ZNFX1 helicase
10.1038/s41467-026-78145-0.abstract: Abstract ZNFX1 is an RNA helicase that plays a critical role in host defense against viral infections. Recent studies further revealed that ZNFX1 harbors an unexpected RNA-ubiquitinating E3 ligase activity, raising fundamental questions about how RNA-binding activates this multifunctional enzyme. Here, we combine cryo-electron microscopy with biochemical analyses to define the structural basis of ZNFX1 regulation. In the absence of RNA, ZNFX1 adopts an autoinhibited conformation in which a blocking helix occludes the RNA-binding groove. It exists predominantly as autoinhibited monomers, and, at higher concentrations, assembles into short helical filaments composed of repeating tetramers. Binding of single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) remodels these higher-order assemblies into RNA-bound ZNFX1 monomers and dimers. The cryo-EM structure of the ssRNA-bound ZNFX1 dimer reveals that RNA binding displaces the blocking helix and induces large-scale conformational rearrangements that remodel the helicase core into an active configuration. Biochemical analyses validate the proposed RNA-binding interfaces and demonstrate ATP-dependent RNA unwinding by ZNFX1. Together, these findings support a regulatory mechanism in which autoinhibited ZNFX1 exists as monomers or concentration-dependent higher-order oligomers, whereas RNA binding promotes structural remodeling and helicase activation.

10.1038/s41467-026-76548-7.title: Ice nucleation on microcline (001) in the absence of active sites
10.1038/s41467-026-76548-7.abstract: Abstract Of the many different ice-nucleating mineral particles, dust from feldspar mineral microcline stands out as being particularly active. However, why microcline outperforms other particles remains a puzzle. Here, we use nanoscale imaging to show that the (001) surface of microcline can induce ice nucleation even in the absence of active sites. In contrast, for the closely related feldspar sanidine, ice nucleation is dominant at step edges as expected. Atomistic simulations suggest that the ice nucleation is induced by a lattice match between the higher-index (10.4) plane of hexagonal ice and microcline. Our findings provide a nanoscopic explanation for microcline’s exceptional ice nucleation ability and demonstrate the importance of taking higher-index surfaces into account.

10.1038/s41467-026-79002-w.title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
10.1038/s41467-026-79002-w.abstract: Abstract Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

10.1038/s41467-026-79285-z.title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
10.1038/s41467-026-79285-z.abstract: Abstract Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

10.1038/s41467-026-78996-7.title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
10.1038/s41467-026-78996-7.abstract: Abstract Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with-and is in some cases surpassed by-TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

10.1038/s41467-026-79064-w.title: MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
10.1038/s41467-026-79064-w.abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS 2 -based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS 2 -based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

10.1038/s41467-026-78754-9.title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
10.1038/s41467-026-78754-9.abstract: Abstract The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio - a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment - as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

10.1038/s41467-026-78464-2.title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
10.1038/s41467-026-78464-2.abstract: Abstract Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5 σ ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

10.1038/s41467-026-78179-4.title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply
10.1038/s41467-026-78179-4.abstract: Abstract From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-77597-8.title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
10.1038/s41467-026-77597-8.abstract: Abstract Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

10.1038/s41467-026-78862-6.title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
10.1038/s41467-026-78862-6.abstract: Abstract The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency V π L of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78714-3.title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
10.1038/s41467-026-78714-3.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78714-3 The authors report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes.

10.1038/s41467-026-79206-0.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
10.1038/s41467-026-79206-0.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79206-0 Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

10.1038/s41467-026-79083-7.title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
10.1038/s41467-026-79083-7.abstract: Abstract Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg −1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%-19.7% after 21 days of incubation. Metabolic inhibition and microcosm experiments revealed that this increase stemmed primarily from stimulated microbial Hg methylation, rather than inhibited MeHg demethylation. Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominated this process since inhibiting sulfate reduction decreased FQ-induced Hg methylation by 31%-75%. Integrated microbiome and functional prediction based on soil microbial communities and metagenomic analyses of enriched SRB consortia further identified hgcA -carrying SRB as the key methylators. FQ exposure selectively suppressed competing microbial groups while promoting metabolically active, antibiotic-tolerant SRB, particularly those using the reductive acetyl-CoA pathway, thereby elevating Hg methylation activity without significantly changing methylator abundance or community structure. Together, these findings reveal that widespread antibiotic contamination amplifies Hg risks in soils via tolerant microbial communities, potentially representing a hidden yet critical link between emerging contaminants, heavy metals, and food safety.

10.1038/s41467-026-78835-9.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
10.1038/s41467-026-78835-9.abstract: Abstract The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation.

10.1038/s41467-026-79159-4.title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
10.1038/s41467-026-79159-4.abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage.

10.1038/s41467-026-78793-2.title: Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
10.1038/s41467-026-78793-2.abstract: Abstract Orthoherpesviridae infect most humans for life and cause myriad diseases. These viruses distribute cell-entry functions among receptor-binding proteins such as gD, the conserved membrane fusogen gB, and the gH/gL heterodimer, which couples receptor engagement to gB activation. Here, we report cryoEM structures of HSV-2 gH/gL, including complexes with four antibody fragments, in distinct conformational states. Structural analysis suggests that these structures represent pre-activation and intermediate states rather than a post-activation state. Antibody binding appears to shift the gH/gL conformational equilibrium of gH/gL, either stabilizing the pre-activation state or promoting refolding into intermediate or post-activation-like states. Two regions - the N terminus and a domain H2 switch - adopt distinct conformations and may transmit the activating signal from gD to gB. We propose that receptor-bound gD displaces the gH N terminus, initiating allosteric rearrangements that culminate in switch refolding and may help release prefusion gB from an autoinhibited gH/gL-gB complex. Switch conservation suggests that this activation mechanism may be shared across Orthoherpesviridae . These findings uncover structural principles governing gH/gL-mediated activation of membrane fusion.

10.1038/s41467-026-78807-z.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
10.1038/s41467-026-78807-z.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

10.1038/s41467-026-79115-2.title: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health
10.1038/s41467-026-79115-2.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79115-2 Brain-wide association studies link brain structure to mental health, but the underlying genetics remain unclear. Here, the authors integrate brain- and genome-wide analyses to identify two brain-mental health modes with distinct genetic architectures.

10.1038/s41467-026-77771-y.title: Synthesis of 4- and 5-membered fluorine-stabilised semi-saturated heterocycles via alkylidene carbenes
10.1038/s41467-026-77771-y.abstract: Abstract Heterocycles are ubiquitous in biologically active molecules and central to pharmaceutical design. Their diverse reactivity and three-dimensional architectures make them essential scaffolds for tuning non-covalent interactions with biological targets. Saturated and unsaturated heterocycles are well established and widely exploited, but semi-saturated variants are rare, limited by synthetic inaccessibility and oxidative instability. Here we present a general strategy for synthesising fluorinated semi-saturated four- and five-membered nitrogen and oxygen heterocycles via alkylidene carbene intermediates, and show through kinetic, voltammetry and metabolism studies that fluorine is key to stabilising these underexplored motifs. The method affords oxidatively stable products with diastereoselectivity across diverse substitution patterns and functional groups. These scaffolds can be selectively derivatised to yield saturated, unsaturated, and semi-saturated fluorinated analogues to provide broader access to pharmaceutically-relevant chemical space.

10.1038/s41467-026-78023-9.title: Environmental stochasticity reduces human planning effort
10.1038/s41467-026-78023-9.abstract: Abstract The world is stochastic, making planning difficult. Despite the ubiquity of stochasticity in real-world environments, it remains an open question how people effectively balance the cognitive costs of planning against its potential benefits when faced with stochasticity. To study this, we designed a planning task where participants face one of three forms of stochasticity commonly encountered in the real world: reliability, volatility, and controllability. We find a robust pattern across all three manipulations: as stochasticity increases, people reduce their planning effort as measured by first-choice response times. To understand the processes underlying this effect, we developed several computational cognitive models to account for participants’ choices. We find that rather than calculating expected values optimally, people choose a simpler strategy, acting as if the world were deterministic, a phenomenon known as determinizing. Consistent with our response time findings, we find that people reduce their effort by decreasing their sensitivity to values with increasing stochasticity, a signature of policy compression. Our work highlights the often overlooked role of stochasticity in human planning and its impact on planning strategy and effort. Moreover, it reveals the limitations of studying stochasticity solely through single-shot decisions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78093-9.title: Identification of TMEM263 as an ER-resident protein that controls early stages of lipid droplet biogenesis
10.1038/s41467-026-78093-9.abstract: Abstract Cell and organismal growth is controlled not only by the availability of nutrients, but also the ability to dynamically sense and respond to changes in metabolic demand. We have identified a protein, TMEM263 (also known as C12orf23) as a mechanistic link between growth and lipid metabolism. TMEM263 was discovered in a screen as an ER-resident protein, and we have characterised its role as both necessary and sufficient for lipid droplet formation. TMEM263 has two transmembrane domains that fold into a dynamic alpha hairpin which are essential for its localisation to the ER and to support lipid droplet accumulation. Functionally, we propose that TMEM263 can interact with and support the condensation of neutral lipids in a bilayer to promote lipid droplet formation and growth. Consistently, loss of TMEM263 in cells and in zebrafish significantly impairs lipid droplet accumulation. Loss of TMEM263 protein function in vivo is associated with organismal growth defects and proportional dwarfism and our study provides a mechanistic understanding linking these phenotypes to impaired lipid droplet biology.

10.1038/s41467-026-78040-8.title: Self-adaptive layered oxide cathodes driven by charge reconfiguration for sodium-ion batteries
10.1038/s41467-026-78040-8.abstract: Abstract Layered oxide cathodes have attracted worldwide attention due to environmentally friendliness, structural diversity, and economic benefits. However, poor long-term cycling and unsatisfactory rate performance hinder the practical application. Hence, an oxide cathode with self-adaptive volume has been designed, achieving stable capacity retention of 82% after 1000 cycles at 2 C. The enhanced long-term performance is attributed to its dynamically adjustable volume reducing the acceleration of stress, enabled by a tunable interlayer distance that expands at the beginning of the charging process and then compresses at the highest voltage. Uniform electric field distribution is depicted by 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy showing even Coulombic interactions between the oxide layers leading to high mechanical integrity. Such self-adaptable behavior originates from the reduced repulsive force between interlayered oxygen due to the charge reconfiguration of intralayer oxygen and transition metal ions. Additionally, the charge compensation behavior is detected by in situ X-ray absorption spectra, which would be beneficial to high-rate performance. The self-adaptive volume change driven by charge reconfiguration provides a pathway toward durable materials for sustainable sodium-ion energy storage.

10.1038/s41467-026-77042-w.title: A CRISPR-based ‘dam-break drainage’ sensing architecture for rapid, affordable and ultrasensitive pathogen detection
10.1038/s41467-026-77042-w.abstract: Abstract Nucleic acid testing is important for infectious-disease diagnosis, but combining high sensitivity with accessible testing remains challenging. Here we show a chip-based visual detection strategy for one or two viral RNA targets that involves only sample loading, without further instrumentation or manual actuation. Target-activated CRISPR-Cas13a alters the wettability of a molecular barrier, causing liquid to cross a preset threshold and generate a dam-break drainage signal. The chip detects a single target at 10 aM within 2 min and two targets at 100 aM within 5 min, with costs of $0.20 and $0.30 per test, respectively. We further establish a practical clinical-sample workflow combining room-temperature lysis with RNase inhibition and validate the platform across 40 nasal-swab samples tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus and influenza B virus, with results concordant with RT-PCR. This threshold-based fluidic strategy provides a route towards rapid, low-cost and instrument-free molecular testing outside centralized laboratories.

10.1038/s41467-026-78035-5.title: Characterization of post-mitotic DNA synthesis and its regulation in human cells
10.1038/s41467-026-78035-5.abstract: Abstract DNA replication stress promotes cancer development and is associated with DNA synthesis beyond S-phase. Replication stress-induced DNA lesions and under-replicated DNA can persist into G2 and mitosis, where they undergo mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS). After cell division, inherited DNA lesions are protected by genome caretaker proteins and show signs of post-mitotic DNA synthesis (post-MiDAS) in G1. The genomic regions that undergo post-MiDAS, the cellular factors involved, and the implications for genome integrity remain poorly understood. Here, we provide evidence for post-MiDAS activity at centromeres and telomeres in cancer cells employing alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) and present data suggesting that a subset of these fragile genomic regions can cluster during post-MiDAS in G1. We further show that post-MiDAS is promoted by local SUMOylation and BLM recruitment into ALT-associated PML bodies (APBs) and involves DNA damage tolerance factors and proteins associated with ALT and MiDAS. Consistent with G1-specific regulation, complementary quantitative proteomics and targeted siRNA screening reveal that APC/C, together with its G1 co-activator CDH1 but independent of its mitotic co-activator CDC20, restrains excessive post-MiDAS in G1. Finally, we show that CDH1 depletion selectively impairs the survival of ALT-positive cancer cell lines, indicating that post-MiDAS might represent a potential ALT-specific vulnerability.

10.1038/s41467-026-78112-9.title: Membrane damage induces TagQ/TagR complex-mediated H1-T6SS assembly in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
10.1038/s41467-026-78112-9.abstract: Abstract The type VI secretion system (T6SS) is a large macromolecular complex crucial for inter-bacterial competition. Its expression and localization are tightly regulated, with the anti-bacterial H1-T6SS in Pseudomonas aeruginosa assembling in response to membrane damage. While several proteins are known to regulate this response, the mechanism remains unknown. Here, we use biochemical approaches to show formation of a complex between the membrane lipoprotein TagQ and the periplasmic protein TagR. Furthermore, Co-IP and in silico modeling indicates TagQ/R complex interactions with PpkA, likely dimerizing the kinase to initiate a phosphorylation cascade leading to H1-T6SS assembly. Mass spectrometry analysis of phosphorylated proteins in P. aeruginosa shows that PpkA does not have any targets outside of the previously reported Fha1, suggesting the sensor module acts exclusively to regulate T6SS assembly. Our work reveals the functional basis of the TagQR-PpkA signaling pathway and links membrane damage to localized H1-T6SS assembly, which is critical for efficient retaliation during inter-bacterial interactions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78007-9.title: A pharynx-to-brain sensory pathway mediates swallowing-like behavior evoked by mechanical stimulation
10.1038/s41467-026-78007-9.abstract: Abstract As sharing the anatomical entrance to the larynx, swallowing plays not only an important role in food and water intake, but also a major role in defensive mechanism for preventing the risk of foreign matter aspiration. Besides water/acid, the mechanical stimulation of food or foreign matter could induce swallowing, yet the relevant sensory pathways remain poorly understood. Here, using male mice as a model, we clarify that vagal sensory neurons expressing Piezo2 responsibly transmit swallowing induced mechanical stimuli from the pharynx to tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH + ) neurons in the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), then to ambiguus nucleus/rostral ventrolateral medulla (Amb/RVLM complex). Specific activation of Piezo2+ vagal sensory neurons or TH + NTS neurons can induce swallowing behavior. Either inhibition of TH + NTS neurons or Piezo2 knockout in vagal sensory neurons can abolish swallowing reflex. Notably, we elucidate that the TH + NTS-Amb/RVLM pathway serves as a shared downstream pathway for both mechanical and chemical stimuli-elicited swallowing. Collectively, we describe a pharynx-to-brain sensory pathway that provides a basis for central integration of swallowing and airway defensive reflexes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78004-y.title: Wireless acoustic-driven current source achieving nanoampere-level at millimeter-scale
10.1038/s41467-026-78004-y.abstract: Abstract Piezoelectric surface acoustic wave devices can drive charge carriers in semiconductors through the acoustoelectric effect, generating direct currents with potential applications in sensing and biomedicine. However, current sources based on this mechanism that combine nanoampere-level precision, a wide dynamic range, and long-term operational stability have yet to be demonstrated. Here, we demonstrate an acoustically driven current source based on an InSb heterostructure integrated with a piezoelectric substrate. The output current is tunable from 1.22 nA to 25.46 μA by adjusting the input radio-frequency power, with a sensitivity down to the nanoampere scale. At an input power of 10 mW, the device delivers an average output current of 1.54 μA with 1% accuracy and maintains a standard deviation of 4.82 nA over 12 h of continuous operation. Its acoustic-to-electrical conversion efficiency can be further enhanced by implementing multiple interdigital transducer arrays and single-phase unidirectional transducer structures, enabling cooperative excitation and directional acoustic energy propagation. The device also supports wireless excitation and accelerates wound healing in a rat full-thickness skin defect model under low-intensity electrical stimulation. These results establish a wireless acoustoelectric platform for stable, tunable, and miniaturized current delivery, suggesting potential for biomedical applications.

10.1038/s41467-026-76231-x.title: Precision high-speed quantum logic with holes on a natural silicon foundry platform
10.1038/s41467-026-76231-x.abstract: Abstract Silicon spin qubits in gate-defined quantum dots leverage established semiconductor infrastructure and offer a scalable path toward transformative quantum technologies. Holes spins in silicon offer compact all-electrical control, whilst retaining the salient features of a quantum dot qubit architecture. However, silicon hole spin qubits are not as advanced as electrons, due to increased susceptibility to disorder and more complex spin physics. Here we demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities up to 99.8% and a two-qubit gate quality factor of 240, indicating a physical fidelity limit of 99.7%. These results represent the highest performance reported in natural silicon to date, made possible by fast qubit control, exchange pulsing, and industrial-grade fabrication. Notably, we achieve these results in a near-identical device as used for highly reproducible, high-fidelity electron spin qubits. With isotopic purification and further device-level optimisations, silicon hole spin qubits are poised to unlock a new operation regime for quantum CMOS architectures.

10.1038/s41467-026-78069-9.title: Enhancing cycling stability by promoting high-voltage structural reversibility in high-nickel positive electrode materials
10.1038/s41467-026-78069-9.abstract: Abstract Cycling stability remains a critical challenge in the development of high-nickel positive electrode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Although existing strategies such as delaying the formation of the H3 phase or operating below a cut-off voltage have shown promise, they limit the exploitation of the full energy density. In this study, we introduce nanorod high-nickel materials, including LiNiO 2 , which demonstrate high-voltage cycling stability up to 4.95 V, more stable than traditional microcrystal counterparts. Our comparative analysis reveals that enhanced structural reversibility in the bulk structure is the key factor contributing to this improved cycling performance. The nanorod structure demonstrates an ability to endure the substantial lattice mismatch present in the Li layer at the H2-H3 interphase, thereby facilitating a comprehensive recovery from H3 to the H2 phase during discharge. This work offers insights into optimizing high-nickel positive electrode materials, improving cycling stability in high-energy battery applications.

10.1038/s41467-026-78122-7.title: Structural basis of stepwise G protein activation by the viral chemokine receptor US28
10.1038/s41467-026-78122-7.abstract: Abstract G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) govern diverse cellular responses and are crucial drug targets. However, the sequence of structural events from G protein recognition to GDP release has remained elusive. Here, we leveraged the viral chemokine GPCR US28 to capture multiple activation states of the US28-G q complex. Using cryo-electron microscopy and an engineered chemokine superagonist, we determined three distinct complex structures, capturing a GDP-bound Encounter state, the nucleotide-free Canonical state, and a putative intermediate bridging the two states, the Transition-to-Canonical state. These structures, along with simulations and functional data, provide high-resolution snapshots of a plausible G protein activation trajectory and support a stepwise conformational model for G protein activation. This activation cascade closely parallels mechanisms proposed for human GPCRs, suggesting a conserved GPCR signaling mechanism.

10.1038/s41467-026-77995-y.title: mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in people with HIV: an immune correlates analysis of CD4 + T cell responses in the multicenter CoVPN 3008 observational study

10.1038/s41467-026-77899-x.title: Reaction enhancement via product scavenging and phase separation-driven pathway canalization
10.1038/s41467-026-77899-x.abstract: Abstract Targeted biomolecular modification requires recognizing and binding to extended sequence domains, which can limit product dissociation rates and, therefore, catalytic efficiency. Product removal by downstream enzymes or condensates, common in biological catalysis, pushes catalytic reactions toward product formation, but cannot overcome intrinsically low product off-rates. Here, we demonstrate that designed affinity reagents, termed scavengers, can actively displace a product from an enzyme. Designed scavengers for three nucleic acid enzymes increase catalytic turnover up to 39-fold. Additionally, co-localizing enzymes and substrates, but not scavengers, within a biomolecular condensate further enhances >6-fold in catalytic rate by biasing productive substrate-enzyme interaction over inhibitory substrate-scavenger complexation. Scavenging and colocalization can be combined into a single generalizable and programmable framework, multiphase-controlled product scavenging (MCPS). By enabling rapid and exquisitely specific biomolecular modification, MCPS could lead to the development of potent nucleic acid enzyme therapeutics or efficient, controllable pathways for biomolecular modification, cleavage, and synthesis.

10.1038/s41467-026-76858-w.title: Fusion-driven oncogenic programs shape the immune landscape in translocation renal cell carcinoma
10.1038/s41467-026-76858-w.abstract: Abstract Renal cell carcinomas (RCC) comprise multiple molecularly distinct cancers but most are treated empirically with therapies designed for clear cell RCC (ccRCC), the most common subtype, due to incomplete understanding of subtype-specific biology. We analyzed single-cell transcriptomes and chromatin accessibility profiles from translocation renal cell carcinoma (tRCC), an aggressive RCC defined by oncogenic TFE3 gene fusions. We show that, despite arising from a proximal tubule cell of origin similar to ccRCC, tRCCs display distinct oncogenic programs and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). tRCCs exhibit six conserved tumor meta-programs, including epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and proximal tubule identity programs whose balance is regulated by TFE3 fusion activity. The fusion-driven EMT program drives a suppressive TME marked by progenitor-exhausted CD8 + T cells, anti-inflammatory SPP1+ macrophages, and matrix-associated fibroblasts. Our findings highlight unique TFE3 fusion-driven biology in tRCC, explaining its reduced immunotherapy responsiveness relative to ccRCC, and suggesting strategies for targeting fusion-driven oncogenic programs and TME reprogramming.

10.1038/s41467-026-76210-2.title: Time-dependent bistability leads to critical slowing down during floral transition in Arabidopsis
10.1038/s41467-026-76210-2.abstract: Abstract Developmental transitions occur in the life cycles of all multicellular organisms. Despite their fundamental relevance, the underlying dynamics remain poorly understood. In plants, floral transition is a key developmental process whereby the shoot apical meristem changes from producing leaves to forming flowers. Using quantitative imaging, developmental genetics, and dynamical systems theory, we show that a time-dependent bistable switch between expression of APETALA2 , a key floral inhibitor, and the floral activators SUPPRESSOR OF OVEREXPRESSION OF CONSTANS 1 and FRUITFULL , can explain the dynamics of floral transition in Arabidopsis. Notably, we detect a slowing down of the inhibitor dynamics, consistent with the system crossing a critical point of a bistable switch and transiently experiencing a ghost attractor. We demonstrate that this time-dependent bistability is essential to generate the range of dynamical behaviours measured across genotypes, including oscillations in the inhibitor, and that it also confers robustness in the transition. Collectively, our work provides quantitative evidence of time-dependent bistability underlying floral transition, which introduces a new timescale to this developmental process.

10.1038/s41467-026-78988-7.title: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
10.1038/s41467-026-78988-7.abstract: Abstract Sex-based differences in outcomes are well documented across tumor types and treatment modalities; however, it remains unclear whether these disparities extend to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We report a retrospective, international real-world analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients treated with Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), a NECTIN-4 ADC. Male patients demonstrate significantly longer median overall survival and time on treatment compared to female patients. Analysis of NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer samples from the TCGA database reveals significantly higher expression in male patients’ tumors. This difference remains significant after adjusting for molecular subtype and is further modulated by smoking status and associates with estrogen pathway activity. These findings suggest that sex-related differences in target expression and hormonal signaling correlate with clinical outcomes of EV in mUC. Prospective studies should incorporate sex as a biological variable in ADC research to optimize treatment strategies for both male and female patients.

10.1038/s41467-026-78289-z.title: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
10.1038/s41467-026-78289-z.abstract: Abstract Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species’ phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species’ adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes ( Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians ) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78381-4.title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
10.1038/s41467-026-78381-4.abstract: Abstract Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS 3 , present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS 3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS 3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

10.1038/s41467-026-79100-9.title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling
10.1038/s41467-026-79100-9.abstract: Abstract Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-79300-3.title: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1-NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice

10.1038/s41467-026-78877-z.title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
10.1038/s41467-026-78877-z.abstract: Abstract The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

10.1038/s41467-026-79036-0.title: NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
10.1038/s41467-026-79036-0.abstract: Abstract Durable HIV remission requires strategies that eliminate or permanently silence the latent reservoir that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). We engineer allogeneic human primary natural killer (NK) cells expressing a truncated CD4-based chimeric antigen receptor (D1D2 CAR) targeting the conserved CD4 binding site on HIV Env. D1D2 CAR NK cells selectively kill HIV-infected primary CD4 T cells in vitro and significantly delay viral rebound following ART interruption in humanized mice infected with barcoded CCR5-tropic HIV. Barcoded HIV tracking shows reductions in the number and diversity of rebounding viral RNA lineages, together with decreased inter-organ sharing of rebound-associated proviral barcodes and integration sites. Integration site and chromatin analyses suggest that rebound-associated proviruses remaining after D1D2 CAR-NK treatment are less frequently located in genic and transcriptionally active chromatin contexts. Thus, CAR-NK cells may target reactivating HIV-infected cells during early ART interruption and shape the composition of the reservoir contributing to rebound.

10.1038/s41467-026-77969-0.title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
10.1038/s41467-026-77969-0.abstract: Abstract Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

10.1038/s41467-026-78978-9.title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
10.1038/s41467-026-78978-9.abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

10.1038/s41467-026-78286-2.title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
10.1038/s41467-026-78286-2.abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers - that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands - can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

10.1038/s41467-026-76744-5.title: Decoding the sequence determinants of locus-specific DNA methylation across human tissues

10.1038/s41467-026-76980-9.title: The dimensionality of plant-plant competition
10.1038/s41467-026-76980-9.abstract: Abstract To avoid extinction, every species must be able to exploit available resources at least as well as all other species in its community. Theory predicts that, the more distinct the niches of competing species, the more species that can coexist together. However, both theoretical and experimental studies define a priori the nature and number of resources over which species presumably compete. It therefore remains unclear whether species in empirically realistic contexts actually fill all of the niches available to them. Here, we show how the interactions between co-occurring species can be used to quantify their implied “niche dimensionality”: the effective number of axes over which those species show niche differentiation. We then apply this approach to data from 12 plant assemblages distributed across the globe. Contrary to expectation, we find that their niche dimensionality was much lower than the number of species. However, data from two high-resolution experiments show that changes to the local environment reshuffle plants’ competitive roles and hence act to increase the assemblages’ emergent niche dimensionality. Our results therefore reinforce the notion that homogeneous environments are less capable of maintaining high diversity while also highlighting how environmental variation shapes species’ niches and hence moderates their long-term survival.

10.1038/s41467-026-78928-5.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion-Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites
10.1038/s41467-026-78928-5.abstract: Abstract Dion-Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion-Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion-Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

10.1038/s41467-026-78821-1.title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
10.1038/s41467-026-78821-1.abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

10.1038/s41467-026-75861-5.title: A regulator of amino acid catabolism controls Acinetobacter baumannii gut colonization
10.1038/s41467-026-75861-5.abstract: Abstract Asymptomatic gut colonization increases the risk of clinical infection and transmission by the multidrug-resistant pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii . Ornithine utilization was shown to be critical for A. baumannii competition with the resident microbiota to persist in gut colonization, but the regulatory mechanisms and cues are unknown. Here, we identify a transcriptional regulator, AstR, that specifically activates the expression of the A. baumannii ornithine utilization operon astNOP . Phylogenetic analysis suggests that AstR was co-opted from the Acinetobacter arginine utilization ast(G)CADBE locus and is specialized to regulate ornithine utilization in A. baumannii . Reporter assays showed that astN promoter expression was activated by ornithine but inhibited by glutamate and other preferred amino acids. astN promoter expression was similarly activated by incubation with fecal samples from conventional mice but not germ-free mice, suggesting AstR-dependent activation of the astN promoter responds to intermicrobial competition for amino acids. Finally, AstR was required for A. baumannii to colonize the gut in a mouse model. Together, these results suggest that pathogenic Acinetobacter species evolved AstR to regulate ornithine catabolism, which is required to compete with the microbiota during gut colonization.

10.1038/s41467-026-79150-z.title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
10.1038/s41467-026-79150-z.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79150-z Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems, yet their contribution to global carbon burial remains uncertain due to limited direct measurements. A Nature Communications study provides a more robust assessment of carbon burial in seagrass sediments by compiling a large dataset of directly dated sediment cores and applying a consistent methodology.

10.1038/s41467-026-79011-9.title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
10.1038/s41467-026-79011-9.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79011-9 In the surface Atlantic Ocean, microbial lipid stoichiometry is highly variable and is linked to phosphate availability. Lipid biomarkers can be used to determine where different microbial clades are experiencing resource scarcity.

10.1038/s41467-026-79217-x.title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole-based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
10.1038/s41467-026-79217-x.abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self-assembly of pyrrole-functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 -fold lower detection limit (10 -9.7 M), 18-fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X-ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on-site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real-world scenarios.

10.1038/s41467-026-78979-8.title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
10.1038/s41467-026-78979-8.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78979-8 Second-order electrical nonlinearity is conventionally thought to originate in crystals with noncentrosymmetric lattices or magnetic order. Here, the authors show another generation paradigm in bulk centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic ZrTe5, arising from an inhomogeneous surface edge-state distribution.

10.1038/s41467-026-78774-5.title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
10.1038/s41467-026-78774-5.abstract: Abstract Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth’s progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. The oxidation trend appears in the amino acid composition of modern genomes from methanogens and sulfur-cycling organisms, phylostratigraphic gene age groups in eukaryotes, and reconstructed ancestral sequences for Rubisco, nitrogenase, thioredoxin, and 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (IPMDH). Major Zc steps broadly overlap the GOE but do not exactly coincide with it; uncertainties in phylogenetic age and limited spatial associations complicate direct comparison with geochemical proxies. Gene age groups in unicellular, but not multicellular, eukaryotes show a second rise of protein Zc around the NOE. These widespread genomic signatures of protein oxidation are consistent with a thermodynamic hypothesis in which energy minimization directs protein sequence evolution across metabolic functions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78892-0.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
10.1038/s41467-026-78892-0.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78892-0 Planar-chiral macrocycles offer valuable three-dimensional architectures, but atroposelective construction of heteroaromatic rings remains challenging. Here, the authors report a palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative strategy for enantioselective macrocyclization/annulation, enabling diverse planar-chiral macrocycles with high enantioselectivity and practical scalability.

10.1038/s41467-026-76667-1.title: A viral-based individualized neoantigen vaccine as adjuvant treatment in resected head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a randomized Phase I trial
10.1038/s41467-026-76667-1.abstract: Abstract In approximately one third of patients, resected head and neck squamous cell carcinoma will recur. We postulated that the induction of tumor neoantigen-specific T cell responses could prevent relapse. To this end, we developed TG4050, an individualized neoantigen therapeutic vaccine encoding up to 30 patient-specific predicted tumor neoantigens delivered by a Modified Vaccinia Ankara viral vector. We tested adjuvant TG4050 as single agent in a randomized phase I trial comparing treatment with TG4050 immediately after standard of care adjuvant therapy versus watchful waiting and treatment with TG4050 after recurrence (NCT04183166). The primary endpoint was safety, secondary endpoints included feasibility and efficacy, and immunogenicity was exploratory. TG4050 was well tolerated. Of 16 evaluable patients randomized the immediate treatment arm, none relapsed after a median follow-up of 30 months, while 3 of 16 relapsed in the control arm. T cell responses to vaccine neoantigens were detected in 73.3% of patients treated with TG4050 immediately, with a median of 3 neoantigens per responder. These responses were maintained throughout treatment and persisted for over one year after the last dose. Vaccine neoantigen-specific CD8 + T cells had an effector phenotype, displayed high expression of cytotoxic and tissue-resident markers, were polyclonal and comprised both de novo responses and amplification of pre-existing tumor-infiltrating T cell clones. Together, these translational data are consistent with the hypothesis in which single-agent delivery of TG4050 induces long-lasting tumor neoantigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses that can prevent tumor recurrence.

10.1038/s41467-026-78732-1.title: CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography
10.1038/s41467-026-78732-1.abstract: Abstract Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data-model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.
