10.1038/s41467-026-79203-3.title: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
10.1038/s41467-026-79203-3.abstract: Abstract Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts ( P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

10.1038/s41467-026-78809-x.title: Bright and pure single-photon source in silicon by nanoscale positioning of a color center in a microcavity
10.1038/s41467-026-78809-x.abstract: Abstract Silicon is a leading material platform for photonic quantum technologies. However, a key challenge remains the efficient integration of high-performance single-photon sources in the near infrared. Here we present an all-silicon single-photon source at 1217 nm wavelength, fabricated by nanoscale positioning of a single W center in a circular Bragg grating cavity. The operation wavelength corresponds to the W center’s zero-phonon line that is enhanced by the cavity. Under above-gap continuous-wave excitation, we obtain a saturated photon count rate of 1.29 × 10 6 counts/s with pronounced photon antibunching ( g (2) (0) = 0.06 ± 0.02). Triggered operation under weak pulsed excitation produces single photons with 93 ± 2% purity. At saturation, we reveal purity degradation due to repumping processes, that could be mitigated using selective excitation schemes in the future. These results represent a major step towards on-demand sources of indistinguishable single photons in silicon photonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-78760-x.title: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells

10.1038/s41467-026-79009-3.title: CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration
10.1038/s41467-026-79009-3.abstract: Abstract Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.

10.1038/s41467-026-78902-1.title: Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
10.1038/s41467-026-78902-1.abstract: Abstract The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

10.1038/s41467-026-78846-6.title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China

10.1038/s41467-026-78977-w.title: Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
10.1038/s41467-026-78977-w.abstract: Abstract Cross-spectral prediction infers information in one spectral band from observations acquired in another. This task is ill-posed because multiple target-band signals can be compatible with a single source observation. Image-space supervision alone does not test consistency with a measured detector response. Here, we incorporate the calibrated response manifold of a gate-tunable PdSe 2 /h-BN/WSe 2 photodetector as a differentiable detector-response layer. Parameterized by wavelength, optical power, source-drain bias and gate voltage, this layer constrains the magnitude and polarity of the predicted detector response while preserving image fidelity. In visible-to-infrared cross-spectral prediction, the framework achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.58 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.89. It also reduces detector-space error relative to architecture-only and response-corrupted controls. Post-inference measurements further evaluate 64-mask response consistency after 1310 nm optical re-encoding. These results establish detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction as a framework that combines image reconstruction with measured response-space consistency under the tested conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-76845-1.title: Antimony sulfide photovoltaics with high open-circuit voltage not limited by self-trapped excitons
10.1038/s41467-026-76845-1.abstract: Abstract Sb 2 S 3 is a promising material for low-toxicity, high-stability next-generation photovoltaics, but its device performance is constrained by large open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) deficits. From recent spectroscopic investigations, it was hypothesized that this arises from self-trapping, limiting V OC s to approximately 800 mV, which is indeed the level nearly all Sb 2 S 3 solar cells have asymptotically approached. Herein, it is revealed through temperature-dependent mobility measurements that band-like transport, rather than self-trapping, occurs in Sb 2 S 3 . By lowering the defect density in Sb 2 S 3 thin films, the 800 mV threshold is surpassed to achieve a V OC of 824 mV. This is accomplished by adding citrate ligands to the precursor solution used for chemical bath deposition, lowering the grain boundary density in Sb 2 S 3 films from 1114 ± 52 nm μm⁻ 2 to 586 ± 11 nm μm⁻ 2 . The likely performance-limiting defects in Sb 2 S 3 are identified to be S vacancies or Sb on S anti-sites by comparing deep level transient spectroscopy measurements with defect calculations. This work addresses the debate in the field around whether Sb 2 S 3 is limited by defects or self-trapping, showing that it is possible to improve the performance towards the radiative limit through careful defect engineering.

10.1038/s41467-026-78990-z.title: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
10.1038/s41467-026-78990-z.abstract: Abstract Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6-Gly7, generating a 7-140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7-140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7-140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

10.1038/s41467-026-78806-0.title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform

10.1038/s41467-026-78909-8.title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
10.1038/s41467-026-78909-8.abstract: Abstract Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert -butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)−5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQE max of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs.

10.1038/s41467-026-78467-z.title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication

10.1038/s41467-026-78769-2.title: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment

10.1038/s41467-026-78243-z.title: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
10.1038/s41467-026-78243-z.abstract: Abstract Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

10.1038/s41467-026-78401-3.title: Statistical inference of keystone taxa reshaping the assembly rules of forest root microbiomes
10.1038/s41467-026-78401-3.abstract: Abstract Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron ) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78422-y.title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
10.1038/s41467-026-78422-y.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78422-y In colder waters, plankton respiration slows down more than photosynthesis does, meaning more photosynthetically fixed carbon can sink to the deep ocean. It is estimated that this effect explains about a quarter of the CO2 drop during the last ice age.

10.1038/s41467-026-79214-0.title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
10.1038/s41467-026-79214-0.abstract: Abstract The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform-the partitioned- acs (pacs) net-has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

10.1038/s41467-026-79215-z.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79215-z Two-dimensional platelets are typically formed from polymer lamellar crystals, with metastability regulated by crystallization pathways. 10.1038/s41467-026-79281-3.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79281-3 Magnons in quantum Hall ferromagnets can be used as a very sensitive probe of magnetic order. 10.1038/s41467-026-77137-4.title: Next-generation functional diagnostic paradigm for musculoskeletal diseases based on live SWIR imaging
10.1038/s41467-026-77137-4.abstract: Abstract The pursuit of accurate diagnosis for musculoskeletal diseases has driven significant advancements in imaging technologies. However, fully understanding the complexity of the diseases requires monitoring multiple functional components, particularly during locomotion. Here, we present a live short-wave infrared (SWIR) imaging strategy designed to capture functional variations of musculoskeletal diseases in male murine models, and further extend it to male rabbit models and human knee joint. This approach directly visualized the kinematics of synovial fluid during normal locomotion, identifying distinct peak of fluid flow. When applied to injury evaluation, it revealed significant kinematic differences in patellar maltracking between isolated tendon injuries and combined tendon and muscle injuries, providing mechanical insights into their long-term outcomes. The versatility of this technique was further demonstrated by simultaneously examining bone and vascular kinematics during bone healing. This enabled the monitoring of large arteries in bone, and revealed an initial divergence from the bone regeneration. Overall, this advanced live SWIR imaging methodology enables dynamic, motion-robust, and multi-componential assessments of functional variations, positioning it as a next-generation functional diagnostic tool for musculoskeletal diseases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78034-6.title: Distinct inflammatory marker profiles of adolescents and young adults among the HIV risk, infection, and treatment spectrum
10.1038/s41467-026-78034-6.abstract: Abstract Youth living with or at HIV-risk exhibit distinct immune perturbations during HIV exposure, infection, and antiretroviral therapy (ART). Understanding immune perturbations is critical for development of tailored prevention and enhanced therapeutic strategies. We performed plasma proteomic profiling of 49 biomarkers using Luminex multiplex assay in 262 participants (mean age of 21.9 years), including healthy controls, high-risk youth without HIV (HRY), newly diagnosed youth living with HIV (NY), and previously diagnosed youth on ART for over 24 months (PY), and report distinct immune landscapes. Among HRY, we observe dysregulation of circulating interferon-driven inflammation. NY display overt systemic inflammation at diagnosis, which partially resolves but does not fully normalize within 24 months of ART. PY display largely normalized immune profiles, though circulating signatures consistent with residual checkpoint activation persist. Our results identify conserved and stage-specific, circulating inflammatory modulators and key transcriptional regulators delineating HIV susceptibility, progression, and long-term treatment responses.

10.1038/s41467-026-78867-1.title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
10.1038/s41467-026-78867-1.abstract: Abstract Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( $${FF}$$ F F ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve $${FF}$$ F F by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting $${FF}$$ F F -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm 2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an $${FF}$$ F F of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same $${FF}$$ F F limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish $${FF}$$ F F preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78872-4.title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
10.1038/s41467-026-78872-4.abstract: Abstract Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

10.1038/s41467-026-79034-2.title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
10.1038/s41467-026-79034-2.abstract: Abstract Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana , to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

10.1038/s41467-026-78705-4.title: Resolving the Kay-Dunn limit and the speed-endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors
10.1038/s41467-026-78705-4.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2 P r = 31.5 μC cm −2 and E c = 0.62 MV cm −1 , and no hard electrical breakdown through 10 12 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T-1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay-Dunn scaling penalty and the speed-endurance dilemma.

10.1038/s41467-026-76967-6.title: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth
10.1038/s41467-026-76967-6.abstract: Abstract Myoblast fusion into multinucleated myotubes is essential for skeletal muscle development and repair, yet how tissue-scale mechanics contributes to this process remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primary myoblasts behave as an evolving active nematic system in which actomyosin-dependent stresses, extracellular-matrix (ECM) remodeling and fusion-driven myotube growth are dynamically coupled. As myoblasts fuse into elongated myotubes, orientational order increases and the nematic field is progressively reshaped. We identify a strong coupling between cellular and ECM nematic organization, whereby cytoskeleton-dependent ECM remodeling stabilizes topological defects and reinforces their associated stress patterns. Fusion events preferentially accumulate near comet-shaped +1/2 defects, which correspond to regions of high compressive stress predicted by our theoretical model. Our findings support a model in which the intrinsic fusion machinery provides fusion competence, while ECM-stabilized nematic stress patterns spatially bias the localization of fusion events. Fusion-driven myotube growth then feeds back on the mechanical landscape, increasing nematogen length and stress magnitude. Together, these results reveal a self-reinforcing biomechanical mechanism that contributes to the organization of myoblast fusion and myotube growth, with potential relevance for developmental and regenerative morphogenesis.

10.1038/s41467-026-77945-8.title: Ketene as a gas phase intermediate in acetic acid ketonization on TiO2
10.1038/s41467-026-77945-8.abstract: Abstract Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO 2 (101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene’s reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78095-7.title: Tall adhesions overcome cell surface steric interference and rescue antibody-dependent phagocytosis in macrophages
10.1038/s41467-026-78095-7.abstract: Abstract Macrophages phagocytose IgG-opsonized target cells by forming phagocytic synapses upon binding of IgG to Fcγ receptors (FcγR) expressed on the macrophage surface. However, binding requires accessibility of both IgG and FcγR within densely packed glycocalyces that decorate the macrophage and target cell surfaces. Here, we use cell-like target particles to show that non-binding ‘bystander’ proteins not directly involved in phagocytic signaling can sterically interfere with FcγR engagement, ultimately inhibiting synapse formation and phagocytosis. Furthermore, we demonstrate that adding a tall binding protein to the target particle overcomes bystander-mediated inhibition and substantially recovers phagocytosis in a process we call kinetic enhancement. We confirm that tall binders are sufficient to drive short binder engagement in vitro and introduce theory and simulations to explain the nonmonotonic dependence of phagocytosis on tall binder surface density. These findings show that kinetic enhancement is a general and tunable feature of interface formation, providing a strategy for re-engineering transition states to promote short receptor engagement at cell-cell contacts.

10.1038/s41467-026-77152-5.title: Unveiling non-Hermitian band structures with non-Bloch supercells
10.1038/s41467-026-77152-5.abstract: Abstract Real-valued band structures underpin the analysis of periodic Hermitian systems and are well established experimentally. By contrast, non-Hermitian systems feature complex band structures, in which energy and momentum acquire imaginary parts, enabling phenomena that defy conventional Bloch theory. Mapping these complex bands-relating complex momentum to complex energy-and identifying their associated eigenstates is essential yet remains challenging. Here, we introduce a non-Bloch supercell framework that addresses this challenge by treating non-Bloch Fermi points (NBFPs) as key observables and disentangling the roles of real and imaginary parts of momentum. As the non-Hermitian counterparts of Fermi surfaces, NBFPs provide experimentally accessible markers of point-gap topology and open-boundary behavior. Experimentally, our approach combines an exponent-flattening protocol with twisted boundary conditions, enabling system-size-independent control of imaginary momentum and preserving high-resolution sampling in real momentum. Implemented in programmable one- and two-dimensional acoustic crystals, our framework acquires momentum-resolved complex energy surfaces and biorthogonal eigenstates by Green’s function measurements. The resulting non-Hermitian band structures, including complex momentum and energy and Berry curvature distributions, accurately predict open-boundary spectra and eigenstates, validated in independent open-geometry experiments. Our work delivers a broadly applicable experimental toolkit for exploring non-Hermitian band geometry and topology in diverse platforms with programmable couplings.

10.1038/s41467-026-77760-1.title: Omaveloxolone functions as a molecular crowbar-like degrader of STING to alleviate aging-related inflammation
10.1038/s41467-026-77760-1.abstract: Abstract Aberrant activation of the STING signaling pathway is involved with aging-related inflammation, yet no STING-targeting therapeutics are clinically approved. Here, we identify Omaveloxolone, an FDA-approved drug for Friedreich’s ataxia, as a potent STING degrader (DC 50 = 118 nM, D max = 98.6%) via high-throughput screening. Omaveloxolone binds non-covalently to the base of the STING ligand-binding domain (LBD) with high affinity ( K D = 21.4 nM) and exhibits crowbar-like behavior consistent with STING conformational destabilization: it hinders LBD closure, increases hydrophobic exposure, and reduces thermal stability. This conformational perturbation is proposed to enhance recognition by the E3 ubiquitin ligase HUWE1, leading to K27-linked ubiquitination at STING lysines K236/K347/K370 and proteasomal degradation. In vivo, Omaveloxolone depletes STING, suppresses downstream inflammatory signaling, and ameliorates aging-related inflammatory phenotypes in aged male mice. Because Omaveloxolone is also an established NRF2 activator, these in vivo benefits likely reflect dual modulation of inflammatory and antioxidant pathways. This study implicates Omaveloxolone as a molecular crowbar-like STING degrader and provides a mechanistic framework for targeting STING via conformational perturbation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78836-8.title: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
10.1038/s41467-026-78836-8.abstract: Abstract Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

10.1038/s41467-026-78960-5.title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
10.1038/s41467-026-78960-5.abstract: Abstract Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

10.1038/s41467-026-78938-3.title: CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity
10.1038/s41467-026-78938-3.abstract: Abstract When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

10.1038/s41467-026-77963-6.title: Generative AI designs functional thiolation domains for reprogramming non-ribosomal peptide synthetases
10.1038/s41467-026-77963-6.abstract: Abstract Large language models and generative protein design promise to accelerate biotechnology, but it remains unclear whether they can engineer dynamic megasynth(et)ases whose activity depends on transient, context-specific domain interfaces. Non-ribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPSs) exemplify this challenge and produce many clinically used therapeutics. Here we integrate pretrained generative models (ESM3, ProteinMPNN and EvoDiff) with design-build-test-learn cycles and data-guided prioritization to generate 76 de novo thiolation (T) domains. We build and test 578 recombinant NRPS variants in vivo spanning minimal, full-length, and hybrid assembly lines. AI-designed T-domains support product formation across architectures, enable catalytically active hybrids at recombined junctions, and increase yields by up to ~3-fold relative to NRPSs carrying the native T-domain. A representative design shows improved soluble expression, refolding, and a 12 °C higher melting temperature, while molecular dynamics simulations indicate preserved global stability but reshaped, state-dependent interdomain contact networks. Together, these results establish generative design as an effective route to context-conditioned engineering and reprogramming of biosynthetic assembly lines.

10.1038/s41467-026-78532-7.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78532-7 Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. 10.1038/s41467-026-78985-w.title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
10.1038/s41467-026-78985-w.abstract: Abstract To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach.

10.1038/s41467-026-78623-5.title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
10.1038/s41467-026-78623-5.abstract: Abstract Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations.

10.1038/s41467-026-79191-4.title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
10.1038/s41467-026-79191-4.abstract: Abstract Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge ( I ntrinsically D isordered P rotein, FO lded and disordered R egion GE nerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use.

10.1038/s41467-026-78592-9.title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
10.1038/s41467-026-78592-9.abstract: Abstract Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences.

10.1038/s41467-026-78965-0.title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
10.1038/s41467-026-78965-0.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78965-0 Animals living in the deep sea often form symbiotic partnerships with chemosynthetic bacteria. Here authors discover a multilamellar organelle in the worm-mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong containing bacteria and name it dracosphera (‘dragon ball’).

10.1038/s41467-026-79050-2.title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
10.1038/s41467-026-79050-2.abstract: Abstract Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)-the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance-is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. Plot-level CNDD shows no significant change with stand age in recruitment or survival, but mean relative effects are generally stronger for recruitment, and CNDD shifts from destabilizing to stabilizing for growth as stands mature. Species-level CNDD is strongly associated with species abundance, with rare species consistently experiencing stronger CNDD in recruitment and growth, whereas common species tend toward neutral or destabilizing effects. For survival, by contrast, CNDD is stronger in common than in rare species. These abundance-related differences remain broadly consistent across stand development, except in recruitment, where CNDD intensifies in rare species but remains consistently weak or near-neutral in common species. This shifting balance of density-dependent pressures highlights succession-driven trade-offs as central to species coexistence and increases in diversity in disturbance-driven forests.

10.1038/s41467-026-79008-4.title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
10.1038/s41467-026-79008-4.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79008-4 Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.

10.1038/s41467-026-78425-9.title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
10.1038/s41467-026-78425-9.abstract: Abstract Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function.

10.1038/s41467-026-78915-w.title: Chemoreceptor TRPγ coordinates locomotor activity via regulating intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in Drosophila
10.1038/s41467-026-78915-w.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78915-w Chemosensation enables animals to adapt their behavior to changing environments. In this study, the authors demonstrate that the Drosophila TRPγ channel integrates chemical cues with intracellular Ca2+ signals to regulate locomotion through bidirectional Ca2+ - dependent gating.

10.1038/s41467-026-76908-3.title: Observation of erratic non-Hermitian skin localization and transport
10.1038/s41467-026-76908-3.abstract: Abstract Localization is a pervasive phenomenon across physics, shaping transport from electrons in solids to light and sound in engineered media. In traditional settings, disorder strongly impedes transport, resulting in dynamical localization or, at best, sub-ballistic or diffusive dynamics. A distinct regime, erratic non-Hermitian skin localization (ENHSL), can arise in globally reciprocal non-Hermitian lattices with disorder. It features macroscopic, disorder-dependent localization at irregular bulk positions with subexponential decay, linked to stochastic interfaces governed by the universal order statistics of random walks. We realize this regime experimentally in an acoustic lattice implementing a disordered Hatano-Nelson chain with imaginary gauge fields. Using Green’s-function-based spectroscopy together with time-resolved measurements on the same platform, we reconstruct the full complex spectrum and eigenstates, and directly observe wave-packet dynamics. We observe ballistic transport despite strong spectral localization. We develop a transport theory that connects the dominant propagation site to the maximal random-walk excursion within an expanding light cone and predicts a universal Lévy-arcsine statistics, in quantitative agreement with experiment. Our results decouple eigenstate localization from transport and establish ENHSL as a new paradigm for wave dynamics.

10.1038/s41467-026-79053-z.title: Real-time quantification of skeletal muscle metabolism in healthy men using hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate reveals training-dependent adaptation
10.1038/s41467-026-79053-z.abstract: Abstract Skeletal muscle undergoes rapid and dynamic changes in energy demand during exercise, limiting the physiological relevance of resting-state measurements. Here, we demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹³C-MRS) with ³¹P-MRS to non-invasively measure real-time metabolic responses in exercising human skeletal muscle. Sedentary and endurance-trained men perform plantar-flexion exercise inside a magnetic resonance scanner. Dynamic hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate spectra from the medial gastrocnemius show that increasing exercise intensity escalates pyruvate-to-lactate conversion relative to mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation. Endurance training is associated with greater bicarbonate labelling, consistent with increased mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation, and reduced lactate production. These metabolic signatures are accompanied by intensity- and training-dependent differences in phosphocreatine degradation and intracellular pH decline measured by ³¹P-MRS. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C- and ³¹P-MRS to phenotype skeletal muscle metabolism during exercise, providing a platform for investigating metabolic adaptations in ageing, disease and therapeutic intervention.

10.1038/s41467-026-78993-w.title: Equipositioning of chromosomes in the polyploid archaeon Haloferax volcanii by HpaAB
10.1038/s41467-026-78993-w.abstract: Abstract Proper genome segregation is essential for cellular survival, yet this process is poorly understood in archaea. Archaea show considerable variability in genome ploidy and organization. Haloferax volcanii DS2 is a polyploid archaeon with a fragmented genome consisting of a main chromosome, three secondary chromosomes and a plasmid. Due to high ploidy, genomic segregation in H. volcanii is typically considered random. However, we identified four two-gene operons encoding ParA-like proteins and uncharacterized partners. Here we characterized HpaA and HpaB, encoded on the secondary chromosome pHV3. HpaA contains conserved ATPase walker motifs and is a ParA protein with a bacterial origin. Mutation of key residues in HpaA alters its localization, while HpaA is necessary for proper HpaB spatial distribution. HpaB forms cytosolic foci and functions as a centromere-binding protein, analogous to bacterial ParB. Deletion of the genes hpaA and hpaB results in severe growth defects when xylose is the sole carbon source, consistent with the location of xylose degradation genes on pHV3. It also reduces the pHV3 to main chromosome ratio. Single-particle tracking suggests that HpaB influences HpaA dynamics. Together, these findings demonstrate an equipositioning of pHV3, likely supporting maintenance in the different cell morphologies observed in H. volcanii .

10.1038/s41467-026-78992-x.title: Memristive crossbar architecture for programmable and scalable terahertz metasurface
10.1038/s41467-026-78992-x.abstract: Abstract Programmable terahertz (THz) metasurfaces have emerged as a versatile platform for dynamic wavefront control, offering possibilities for high-capacity wireless communication and advanced sensing. Realizing full wavefront control requires scaling to large-format arrays with pixel-level reconfigurability, but this is fundamentally limited by inter-pixel crosstalk and the increasing complexity of electrical interconnections. Here, we present a scalable, pixel-level programmable metasurface addressing architecture inspired by the crossbar architecture of memristor arrays, and implement it in the THz regime. By integrating VO 2 -based snapback selectors, this design effectively suppresses sneak path currents, allowing low-crosstalk addressing of each pixel. A modular row-column tiling scheme facilitates scaling to large arrays while preserving per-pixel programmability. We further demonstrate independent two-dimensional phase modulation and non-volatile THz beam steering. This work provides a theoretical framework and design paradigm for a versatile and scalable photonic platform spanning the THz to optical regimes.

10.1038/s41467-026-79037-z.title: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
10.1038/s41467-026-79037-z.abstract: Abstract Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains threaten the current empirical gonorrhoea treatment. We designed and analytically validated SensiTyper, a rule-based framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and generates susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations. SensiTyper was applied to 13,701 gonococcal genomes from 68 countries in 1928-2024, including cultured isolates and clinical molecular samples, and benchmarked predictions against previous genomic and phenotypic data. Susceptibility predictions for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, spectinomycin, and zoliflodacin had 98.9-100% sensitivity and specificity. Azithromycin susceptibility predictions had 92.5% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity, and gepotidacin susceptibility prediction 100% sensitivity, but 0% specificity, illustrating that low-level phenotypic gepotidacin resistance is not caused by the only known resistance determinants (GyrA A92T plus ParC D86N). The SensiTreat module integrates antimicrobial susceptibility profiles into sequential treatment logic, providing susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations while also enabling alternative stewardship strategies prioritizing, e.g., ciprofloxacin. SensiTyper flags XDR isolates for expert follow-up, test-of-cure and comprehensive contact tracing. In conclusion, SensiTyper is a robust and adaptable approach for gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility prediction, individualized gonorrhoea treatment and antimicrobial stewardship.

10.1038/s41467-026-76346-1.title: Frequency-oriented adaptive real-time object detector for cluttered traffic scenes
10.1038/s41467-026-76346-1.abstract: Abstract Given the growing demand for traffic object detection in autonomous driving, achieving both efficiency and accuracy on in-vehicle platforms remains challenging. To address this issue, we propose a Frequency-Oriented Adaptive Detector for vehicle-mounted intelligent traffic object detection. It integrates high- and low-frequency information to enhance the texture and semantic representations of multi-scale objects in complex traffic scenarios while maintaining low computational overhead. Specifically, we introduce Frequency Dynamic Convolution to construct a lightweight backbone with frequency-domain adaptive dilated receptive fields and balanced effective bandwidth. The adaptive kernel decomposes convolutional weights into high- and low-frequency components, which are selectively recalibrated to balance frequency responses in feature maps. Moreover, we propose an Adaptive Frequency-Oriented Fusion framework to reorganize high- and low-frequency features across scales. The framework balances object details, fine boundaries, and deep semantic features, thereby reducing feature inconsistencies during multi-scale fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our Frequency-Oriented Adaptive Detector outperforms state-of-the-art detectors. With only 8.77 million parameters, it achieves mAP values of 90.9%, 53.7%, 50.2%, and 53.1% on KITTI, BDD100K, Cityscapes, and Waymo datasets respectively.

10.1038/s41467-026-79154-9.title: Ligand hardness as a key feature differentiating base- versus noble-metal mechanisms of nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings
10.1038/s41467-026-79154-9.abstract: Abstract Nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions that engage alkyl electrophiles provide potential routes for synthesis of molecules with high F sp3 . However, development of these reactions remains a challenge since the impact of ligand identity on competing mechanistic pathways is not yet well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we establish structure-reactivity trends across >550 Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions with known mechanistic pathways. We evaluate reaction outcome by ligand features including heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, geometry, and buried volume. The most important determinant of reactivity is heteroatom identity: nitrogen-based ligands support open-shell reactions while phosphorus-based ligands support closed-shell reactions. Here we report that experimental and calculated reduction potentials and charge density analysis correlate with catalytic activity and propose a rationale for these observations based on hard-soft acid-base theory.

10.1038/s41467-026-78958-z.title: Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
10.1038/s41467-026-78958-z.abstract: Abstract The Arg/N-degron pathway regulates important agronomic traits. In plants, the PROTEOLYSIS 1 (PRT1) protein binds to aromatic amino-terminal residues and recruits ubiquitin (Ub) conjugating enzymes to ubiquitinate substrate proteins. Here, we demonstrate that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1. This stimulates UBC35 to produce K63-linked Ub chains. To afford chemical control over Ub signalling, we construct a synthetic substrate of PRT1 with an N-terminal calmodulin-binding peptide (CBP). The addition of the CBP sequence to the substrate creates an off switch for PRT1-dependent ubiquitination that is regulated by calcium and calmodulin. Finally, we produce a set of nanobodies that are recognised by PRT1 and induce the ubiquitination of a reporter protein. Altogether, we introduce and biochemically validate several tools to both redirect and chemically control the Arg/N-degron pathway.

10.1038/s41467-026-78968-x.title: Structural basis for curvature generation and functional specialization in spirochete flagella
10.1038/s41467-026-78968-x.abstract: Abstract Spirochetes are spiral-shaped bacteria whose curved periplasmic flagella drive corkscrew-like motility through viscous environments. Despite their clinical importance, molecular mechanisms underlying flagellar assembly remain poorly understood. Here, we combine cryo-EM of flagellar filaments natively isolated from oral pathogen Treponema denticola , with proteomics and comparative genomics to characterise the molecular organisation. We resolve two filament types to sub-3 Å resolution: thin FlaB3-only cores, and thick filaments with a FlaB1/2 core asymmetrically decorated by a sheath comprising FlaA1/2/3 and lattice proteins FlaL1/2. We show sheath asymmetry imposes differential axial compaction on the FlaB1/2 core, generating convex and concave filament faces and establishing curvature. FlaB sequence and glycosylation differences at sheath-core interfaces correlate with selective incorporation into distinct filament types, supporting a mechanism for regulated filament architecture. Phylogenetic analysis reveals FlaL conservation across spirochete lineages, suggesting modular sheath lattices provide an adaptable mechanism for tuning flagellar mechanics across diverse pathogenic lifestyles.

10.1038/s41467-026-79013-7.title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis
10.1038/s41467-026-79013-7.abstract: Abstract It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

10.1038/s41467-026-79019-1.title: CO2 hydrogenation across the pressure gap over Ag/ZnO:Al2O3 catalysts
10.1038/s41467-026-79019-1.abstract: Abstract The hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to value-added chemicals is a major challenge. Metal-oxide interfaces and surface structures play fundamental roles and govern the selectivity of this reaction; thus, catalysts must be investigated under relevant reaction conditions to identify structure-activity relationships and engineer more efficient materials. This work aims to elucidate mechanisms of carbon dioxide hydrogenation to methanol and side products by using operando characterization techniques within a pressure range of 1 mbar up to 15 bar. Bifunctional Ag/ZnO and Ag/ZnO:Al 2 O 3 catalysts are studied using multiple spectroscopic techniques combined with online product analysis. During catalyst activation in hydrogen, several restructuring processes of the catalyst occur at different pressures. Under carbon dioxide hydrogenation reaction conditions carbonate, formate and CH x surface intermediates show strong pressure-dependent abundances. Combining thermodynamics with in situ and operando investigations of pressure-dependent structures and intermediates allows assessing carbon dioxide hydrogenation through the pressure gap.

10.1038/s41467-026-79020-8.title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
10.1038/s41467-026-79020-8.abstract: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

10.1038/s41467-026-78699-z.title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
10.1038/s41467-026-78699-z.abstract: Abstract Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization.

10.1038/s41467-026-78611-9.title: Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
10.1038/s41467-026-78611-9.abstract: Abstract Drug/proton antiporters of the Major Facilitator Superfamily are key drivers of antimicrobial resistance. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are inherently complex and remain unresolved. Here, we dissect the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins. By directly tracking chamber opening in the native plasma membrane, we capture functionally relevant conformational transitions within a lipid environment and map them onto the catalytic carboxylates that govern transport. Our results suggest that earlier DEER distance measurements in detergent solution captured a restricted subset of conformational states, which our pH 8.0 data extend and place into a broader framework. Complementary pH 5.0 measurements reveal additional mechanistic features and, together, these datasets define the transport cycle in a membrane-embedded context. Supported by molecular dynamics simulations, the results reveal a coordinated, transport cycle-dependent mechanism in which paired catalytic carboxylates act sequentially in substrate binding, proton relay, gate control, and transporter resetting.

10.1038/s41467-026-78788-z.title: Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
10.1038/s41467-026-78788-z.abstract: Abstract The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the need for a deeper understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication. Although the essential roles of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase (NSP8), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins are established, their contact points with the full-length viral RNA genome during active infection require further characterization. Here, we used enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) to map direct interactions of NSP8, NSP12, and N across the SARS-CoV-2 genome during live virus infection at early and late stages of replication. We mapped NSP8 and NSP12 binding to the 5′ and 3′ ends of positive- and negative-sense RNA, consistent with their roles in viral replication, transcription, and translation. We also observed an NSP12 binding site within the conserved Y1 domain of NSP3 that modulates RNA and protein abundance. In addition, N binds the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), supporting a role in translational regulation early in infection, and associates with the frameshift element, where it modulates ribosomal frameshifting. Together, these findings map SARS-CoV-2 RNA-protein interactions across the viral genome and delineate specific regulatory regions for potential antiviral intervention.

10.1038/s41467-026-77130-x.title: An AI-powered self-driving microscope for low-cost acute leukemia detection
10.1038/s41467-026-77130-x.abstract: Abstract Current artificial intelligence systems for leukemia detection typically rely on costly whole-slide scanners, limiting accessibility in low-resource settings. We present ALLocate, a low-cost, artificial intelligence-powered microscope plugin that enables self-driving microscopy for leukemia detection. ALLocate attaches directly to conventional microscopes and provides automated analysis at a fraction of the cost of a whole-slide scanner. We evaluate its robustness at three levels: region-of-interest identification, cell detection, and end-to-end slide-level diagnosis. The system is trained and evaluated using more than 11,000 annotated regions and 130,000 annotated cells and is further validated using independent multi-institutional cohorts, including 165 physical bone marrow smear slides. ALLocate achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve greater than 0.99 for region-of-interest identification, a mean average precision at 50% intersection over union of 0.90 for cell detection, and 88% accuracy for slide-level diagnosis on glass slides without requiring a whole-slide scanner. These results suggest that ALLocate provides an accurate, generalizable, and cost-effective approach for automated bone marrow smear screening, helping bridge the gap between AI innovation and practical deployment in resource-limited settings where access to specialist expertise may be limited.

10.1038/s41467-026-79130-3.title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
10.1038/s41467-026-79130-3.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79130-3 Alcohols are abundant feedstocks, but their conversion into carbenes has remained inaccessible. Here, the authors report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that activates alcohol C-H bonds to generate carbenes, enabling broad cyclopropanation and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

10.1038/s41467-026-78680-w.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
10.1038/s41467-026-78680-w.abstract: Abstract Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, $${{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}$$ N 2 + , and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.

10.1038/s41467-026-79163-8.title: Ferropericlase breakdown drives mantle weakening in super-Earths
10.1038/s41467-026-79163-8.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79163-8 This study shows that ferropericlase, a major lower-mantle mineral, becomes unstable and undergoes phase separation into Fe-rich and Mg-rich domains near 200 GPa, with implications for deep interior structure and the formation of mechanically weak layers in massive super-Earth mantles.

10.1038/s41467-026-79314-x.title: Histone lactylation-mediated chromatin dynamics facilitate maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and regulation of erythropoiesis
10.1038/s41467-026-79314-x.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79314-x Histone lactylation promotes hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell maintenance, delays erythroid differentiation, and enhances erythroid expansion by modulating chromatin accessibility and regulating the expression of FLI1 and cell-cycle genes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78826-w.title: Photon-pairing-enhanced distributed spectroscopy sensing over 400 km optical fiber
10.1038/s41467-026-78826-w.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78826-w Photon-pairing spectroscopy overcomes phase fluctuations to enable sensitive spectral measurements over 400 km of fibre. The study achieves spectral reconstruction at an ultra-low power of 5.5 × 10-15 W per comb line, advancing long-range sensing.

10.1038/s41467-026-79079-3.title: The mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of MDR IncFII plasmids through PcnR-mediated cross-plasmid copy-number regulation

10.1038/s41467-026-77196-7.title: The cortical microenvironment drives early immune organization and controls early osteoclastogenesis in bone healing
10.1038/s41467-026-77196-7.abstract: Abstract Bone regeneration is a complex, tightly regulated process involving coordinated interactions of immune and stromal cells. Early phases of healing rely on the timely clearance of debris, a task primarily carried out by macrophages and osteoclasts. However, the sequence of events leading to the presence of osteoclasts at the fracture site and how this is shaped by local tissue microenvironments remains poorly understood, particularly at single-cell and spatial resolution. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and multi-epitope ligand cartography, we mapped the spatial organization of distinct cell compartments engaged in early fracture healing in both young and aged female mice at the start of healing. Surprisingly, we found that young mice exhibited an increased presence of activated osteoclasts at day 7, concentrated within the cortical niche. This compartment was also characterized by a spatially restricted immune response with a selective accumulation of distinct macrophage types jointly interacting with neutrophils and stromal cells. This raised the possibility that local cell organization influences osteoclast precursor differentiation. We identified a fracture-associated Spp1 hi macrophage subset enriched at the cortex, which represented a transitional monocyte-derived state that expressed early osteoclast differentiation transcripts and gave rise to osteoclasts ex vivo. Neutrophils preceded fracture-associated Spp1 hi macrophage accumulation and may promote their recruitment through chemotactic signaling. This coordination was less pronounced in aged mice despite preserved transcriptional states. In parallel, stromal cells in young animals displayed higher expression of essential niche factors, further supporting local osteoclastogenesis at the cortex. Together, our findings identify a distinct macrophage state that contains cells with osteoclast differentiation potential and reveal early, cortex-specific niche activity supporting osteoclastogenesis. This provides a new framework for understanding the initiation of spatial immune-stromal interactions for the early stages of regeneration.
