10.1038/s41467-026-79258-2.title: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
10.1038/s41467-026-79258-2.abstract: Abstract How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1 -deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-76873-x.title: NASA’s ECOSTRESS satellite reveals widespread midday depression in ecosystem evapotranspiration
10.1038/s41467-026-76873-x.abstract: Abstract Plants often exhibit a midday depression in water use (i.e., transpiration), reflecting a constraint on their ability to sustain maximum water transport, which may occur at the cost of reduced photosynthesis. Eddy covariance observations and geostationary satellites cannot quantify this widespread phenomenon globally while resolving fine-scale spatial variability. Using evapotranspiration measurements from the ECOsystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station (ECOSTRESS) and machine learning, we quantify the global distribution of midday depression in evapotranspiration. Midday depression primarily occurs during peak-growing seasons in temperate zones and dry periods in the tropics, with a morning shift of the peak evapotranspiration time by > 0.5 h. Droughts and heatwaves intensify midday depression, with peak evapotranspiration time shifting earlier, typically by 0.5 to 1.5 h and approaching 2 h during local extremes. By contrast, the coarse resolution upscaled flux products and hourly meteorological reanalysis datasets cannot capture this phenomenon. Midday depression of evapotranspiration detected using ECOSTRESS and machine learning is strongly associated with plant water stress, and helps us better understand how plants use water during drought and heatwaves.

10.1038/s41467-026-76076-4.abstract: Abstract Foundational artificial intelligence models are gaining traction in various applications, including medical fields like radiology. However, medical foundation models are often tested on limited tasks, leaving their generalisability and biases unexplored. Here we introduce RayDINO, a large-scale self-supervised visual encoder for chest X-rays trained on 840,000 images and evaluated on 82,000 images sourced from 12 publicly available datasets. We compare RayDINO to previous state-of-the-art models across nine radiology tasks, from classification and dense segmentation to text generation, and provide an in-depth analysis of population, age and sex biases of our model. Our findings suggest that self-supervision enables patient-centric analysis useful in clinical workflows, allowing for a more holistic interpretation of X-rays. With RayDINO and small task-specific adapters, we reach state-of-the-art results and improve generalization to unseen populations while mitigating bias, illustrating the versatility and robustness of foundation models.

10.1038/s41467-026-79231-z.title: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
10.1038/s41467-026-79231-z.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for alkene functionalization, yet its application to sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remains severely underdeveloped. Here, we report an Ir(III)-catalyzed nitrene-triggered aziridination-rearrangement cascade that enables the efficient conversion of cyclic-substituted tetrasubstituted alkenes into cycloalkane-fused δ-lactams. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with excellent yields and uniformly high diastereoselectivities and exhibits broad compatibility with carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-based nucleophiles, including structurally complex and biologically relevant substrates. Combined experimental and computational studies support a concerted aziridination by an Ir-nitrenoid to generate a strained tricyclic intermediate, which undergoes a strain-release-driven aza-semipinacol rearrangement to furnish a bicyclic azacarbocation. Divergent nucleophilic interception or elimination of this intermediate provides rapid access to structurally diverse fused δ-lactam architectures. These findings establish a nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement manifold for the functionalization of tetrasubstituted alkenes and expand the synthetic potential of transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer.

10.1038/s41467-026-79225-x.title: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
10.1038/s41467-026-79225-x.abstract: Abstract Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7 . Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression.

10.1038/s41467-026-76854-0.title: Soft microgel networks stabilize and extend nozzle-free water jets
10.1038/s41467-026-76854-0.abstract: Abstract The stability of high-speed liquid jets is crucial for applications ranging from precision printing to needle-free drug delivery, yet it is fundamentally limited by capillary-driven breakup. We find that tuning the nanoscale softness of Poly( N -Isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) microgels provides a robust, biocompatible strategy to overcome this limitation. Soft, low-cross-linker-density microgels form elastic interfacial networks at the air-water interface that suppress surface tension recovery, delay Rayleigh-Plateau instabilities, and extend Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW)-driven jet lengths by up to 44%. In contrast, stiffer microgels lose network cohesion under strain, leading to rapid jet breakup. To gain molecular-level insights, we perform dissipative particle dynamics simulations, which reveal that polymer bridges in soft microgels remain entangled during elongation, maintaining a reduced effective surface tension. Finally, a simple scaling analysis, balancing the SAW-driven kinetic energy imparted to the droplet against the surface energy required to form a jet, quantitatively predicts the observed length enhancement.

10.1038/s41467-026-76856-y.title: Asian summer monsoon orbital variability directly paced by CO2 and precession, not eccentricity
10.1038/s41467-026-76856-y.abstract: Abstract The pacing and intensity of the Asian summer monsoon have long been debated. Geological records indicate either a dominant precession or eccentricity variability, while modelling studies have largely emphasised monsoon intensity rather than its temporal pacing. Here, we investigate both the temporal variability and changes in intensity of the Asian summer monsoon using a unique set of four series of full-complexity climate model equilibrium simulations spanning the last 800 kyr at 4-kyr resolution. The simulations have differing insolation, greenhouse gases, and ice sheet forcing. Here, we show that variations in greenhouse gases exert the dominant control on the 100-kyr variability via the thermal forcing of the Asian summer monsoon circulation, while precession directly impacts the 20-kyr variability. In contrast, the direct contributions of eccentricity forcing and ice sheet variability are smaller. Spatial heterogeneity in monsoon dynamics reveals different sensitivities to imposed forcings, which may help reconcile conflicting proxy records.

10.1038/s41467-026-77305-6.title: An FGF21-IGFBP1 tumor-liver relay drives musculoskeletal defects in colorectal cancer cachexia
10.1038/s41467-026-77305-6.abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) is frequently accompanied by cachexia, a wasting syndrome characterized by progressive loss of muscle and bone that worsens physical function and survival. Although liver dysfunction is increasingly recognized in cachexia, whether tumor-induced liver signaling contributes directly to musculoskeletal decline remains unclear. Here we show that CRC establishes a tumor-liver endocrine relay in which tumor-derived fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) stimulates hepatic production of the hepatokine insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 (IGFBP1). IGFBP1 is consistently elevated in patients with CRC and in multiple mouse models, where it promotes osteoclast differentiation, muscle atrophy, and bone loss. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of IGFBP1 preserves muscle and bone despite persistent tumor burden, whereas deletion of tumor-derived FGF21 suppresses hepatic IGFBP1 production and mitigates musculoskeletal wasting. These findings identify a tumor-liver signaling axis that drives CRC-associated cachexia and highlight the FGF21-IGFBP1 pathway as a therapeutic target to preserve musculoskeletal health.

10.1038/s41467-026-77818-0.title: Spatial control of karyopherin binding avidity within NPC mimics revealed by designer FG-nucleoporins
10.1038/s41467-026-77818-0.abstract: Abstract Nucleocytoplasmic transport occurs via nuclear pore complexes (NPCs), ~40-60 nm wide pores lined with intrinsically disordered proteins that are rich in Phe-Gly motifs (FG-Nups) that form a selective barrier. Molecules larger than ~50 kDa are increasingly blocked for transport unless they are bound to a nuclear transport receptor such as the karyopherin (Kap) family of proteins. How the amino acid sequence of FG-Nups contributes to this selectivity is not fully understood. Here, we present de novo designed artificial FG-Nups with a systematically varied FG-repeat spacing and charge-to-hydrophobicity ratio (C/H). Starting from a reference sequence termed NupY (with the average properties of yeast GLFG-Nups), we design, synthesize, and experimentally test a library of NupY variants using quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring and phase separation assays. We find that the spacing between FG-motifs governs Kap95 absorption into the FG-Nup phase, while increasing C/H results in higher avidity for Kap95 due to an increased accessibility of FG-motifs. Molecular dynamics simulations of transport through NupY-coated pores show a reduced barrier function for noncohesive variants and the highest transport selectivity for designs close to native GLFG-Nups. We postulate that a balance between steric hindrance and enthalpic gain from multivalent Kap-FG-Nup interactions drives the spatial and temporal partitioning of Kaps in the NPC.

10.1038/s41467-026-79168-3.title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
10.1038/s41467-026-79168-3.abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700-366,400 km 2 ), global burial scales to 6-15 Tg C yr −1 . Although one-fourth of earlier benchmarks, seagrasses account for 3-4% to 3-6% of total oceanic OC burial despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor. Combined with mangroves and tidal marshes, vegetated coastal ecosystems contribute 8-13% of oceanic OC burial.

10.1038/s41467-026-79058-8.title: In vitro-reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
10.1038/s41467-026-79058-8.abstract: Abstract The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

10.1038/s41467-026-77767-8.title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
10.1038/s41467-026-77767-8.abstract: Abstract Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

10.1038/s41467-026-78784-3.title: Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
10.1038/s41467-026-78784-3.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78784-3 Entanglements among long-chain macromolecules dictate the mechanical performance of polymeric materials and are described with the tube model but the validity of this model has been questioned for nonlinear extension. Here the authors reveal the key mechanism that governs the mechanical response during extension by elucidating the evolution of entanglements using computer simulations and theoretical analysis.

10.1038/s41467-026-79306-x.title: Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host-pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
10.1038/s41467-026-79306-x.abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host-pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

10.1038/s41467-026-78828-8.title: Engineering filamentous myosins for optical control of contractility
10.1038/s41467-026-78828-8.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78828-8 Zemsky and colleagues employ protein engineering to create filamentous myosins controlled by light. These optogenetic motors enable spatiotemporal control of contractility in vitro and in cells, providing a tool for probing contractile actomyosin systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78946-3.title: Energy-guided combinatorial co-optimization of antibody affinity and stability
10.1038/s41467-026-78946-3.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78946-3 Here, Tennenhouse et al. develop LAffAb, a structure-based method for designing CDR mutations to improve affinity and developability. By filtering mutations predicted to disrupt stability and foldability, LAffAb enables accurate, one-shot design.

10.1038/s41467-026-79170-9.title: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
10.1038/s41467-026-79170-9.abstract: Abstract Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. However, how striatal subregions contribute to stress vulnerability versus resilience remains unclear. Here, we show dissociable roles of the nucleus accumbens (NAC) and dorsal caudate (dCA) and their associated brain networks in shaping stress responses. We identify neural stability (NS)-capturing stress-induced changes in state-switching frequency over the course of stress responses-as a marker: task-state NS correlates positively with stress-related NAC activity, whereas resting-state NS correlates inversely with stress-related dCA activity. NAC-mediated networks and associated NS further predict faster cortisol recovery. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D 2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Together, these findings reveal striatal subregional heterogeneity in stress coping and characterize resilience as a multisystem homeostatic process integrating neural, endocrine, and molecular layers.

10.1038/s41467-026-78880-4.title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
10.1038/s41467-026-78880-4.abstract: Abstract X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability - both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.

10.1038/s41467-026-79280-4.title: The modular evolution of chitinases is governed by coevolution of auxiliary and catalytic domains
10.1038/s41467-026-79280-4.abstract: Abstract The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments.

10.1038/s41467-026-79005-7.title: Strong hydrogels through precisely oriented crystallization regulation
10.1038/s41467-026-79005-7.abstract: Abstract Achieving high mechanical strength and environmental stability is critical for hydrogels in demanding engineering scenarios. Crystalline hydrogels hold promise because their crystallites act as physical crosslinks and energy dissipators; however, precise control over crystalline architecture remains underexplored. Inspired by industrial thermoplastic processing, we report an ASGS strategy for crystalline hydrogels that integrates alkali-induced chain activation (A), ultra-stretching-driven orientation (S), and glycerol-seawater-mediated densification (GS). Alkali treatment yields moderate initial crystallinity with refined nascent crystallites. Ultra-stretching establishes a highly oriented chain network, and subsequent densification achieves maximum crystallinity and highly oriented crystallites. The resultant hydrogels, in the fully hydrated state, combine a tensile strength of 160.0 MPa, a modulus of 746.0 MPa, and a fracture energy of 26.4 kJ·m⁻². The corresponding plastic reaches 414.2 MPa tensile strength while retaining flexibility. This thermoplastic-inspired crystallization engineering provides a scalable paradigm for fabricating strong and stable crystalline hydrogels, promising for load-bearing and harsh underwater engineering applications.

10.1038/s41467-026-79025-3.title: Electrolyte-dependent physico-chemical interfacial kinetics shape degradation pathways and lifetime in lithium-ion batteries
10.1038/s41467-026-79025-3.abstract: Abstract Electrolyte-dependent lifetime variability remains a major obstacle to sustainable deployment of lithium-ion batteries, contributing to premature retirement, increased material demand and uncertainty in lifecycle assessment. However, most continuum degradation models represent the electrolyte through bulk transport, without capturing its role in interfacial degradation. Here, we use customised multi-layer pouch cells with varied ethylene carbonate:dimethyl carbonate ratio, lithium hexafluorophosphate concentration and electrolyte amount to examine how electrolyte conditions shape degradation trajectories under accelerated degradation. Within this formulation framework, changing the solvent ratio leads to distinct lifetime trajectories across otherwise comparable cells. Electrochemical diagnostics, gas analysis and post-mortem interfacial characterisation show that this divergence is associated with electrolyte-sensitive interphase growth, parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous surface degradation. We incorporate electrolyte-dependent transport and thermodynamic properties into a physics-based degradation model. A transport-only implementation does not reproduce the observed separation in capacity-retention trajectories. Introducing a minimal electrolyte-sensitive refinement through an effective interphase transport parameter improves agreement in the ethylene-carbonate-rich case. These results identify electrolyte-sensitive interfacial degradation as a necessary modelling dimension for reliable lifetime prediction.

10.1038/s41467-026-79143-y.title: Pulsed photoelectrocatalysis enables efficient urea synthesis over Cu(salen)-COF
10.1038/s41467-026-79143-y.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from carbon dioxide and nitrate under ambient conditions offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process. However, its efficiency is constrained by the spatiotemporal mismatch of key carbon and nitrogen intermediates at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we address this limitation through interfacial microenvironment optimization combining ionic liquid modification of copper-salen covalent organic framework, pulsed electrolysis, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling. The ionic liquid modification enriches carbon dioxide and facilitates interfacial charge transfer, pulsed electrolysis promotes the dynamic matching of carbon and nitrogen intermediates, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling boosts interfacial electron accumulation. The integrated system achieves a urea yield rate of 69.2 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 56.7% in an H-type cell and 82.5% in a flow cell. In this work, we establish a generalizable strategy for efficient urea electrosynthesis via hierarchical interfacial control and highlight the potential of pulsed photoelectrocatalysis.

10.1038/s41467-026-76809-5.title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
10.1038/s41467-026-76809-5.abstract: Abstract In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves. Should the Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement not be implemented, in most regions a concerningly large proportion of projected heatwaves exceeds all analyzed heatwave characteristics at once. Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

10.1038/s41467-026-79252-8.title: Two distinct α2β1 integrin glycan interactions mediate cell entry of a picornavirus
10.1038/s41467-026-79252-8.abstract: Abstract Equine rhinitis A virus (ERAV), a picornavirus closely related to foot-and-mouth disease virus, causes respiratory infections in horses. We performed a HEK293T CRISPRi screen and identified integrin α2β1 as a protein receptor for ERAV. Using knock-out cells and pretreating cells with an antibody or soluble receptor, we confirmed the importance of this integrin for infection of multiple cell types, including equine fibroblasts. Cryo-EM and glycoproteomics analyses revealed that ERAV binds integrin α2β1 in its closed conformation by attaching to the β-propeller of the α2 chain, independent of divalent cations, as well as to a high-mannose glycan on α2 N112 and a sialylated glycan on β1 N269. Using glycan knockout and knock-in cells and by reconstituting integrin α2β1-depleted cells with mutant receptors, we demonstrated the importance of these glycans for virus entry. Our results identify a hitherto unseen combination of protein and glycan interactions between a virus and its receptor.

10.1038/s41467-026-79266-2.title: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions
10.1038/s41467-026-79266-2.abstract: Abstract Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus-a core lexico-semantic region-was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain’s capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.

10.1038/s41467-026-78204-6.title: Chemokine and opioid peptide scavenging through constitutive and ligand-induced release of ACKR3-bearing extracellular vesicles
10.1038/s41467-026-78204-6.abstract: Abstract Atypical chemokine receptors (ACKRs) are non-signaling GPCRs that regulate ligand availability, with ACKR3 functioning as a dual scavenger of chemokines and opioid peptides. Here, we demonstrate that following ligand stimulation, besides the canonical internalization, ACKR3 is released on extracellular vesicles (EVs). ACKR3 was also found on EVs released under basal conditions, although to a lesser extent. These observations were confirmed across multiple cellular contexts, including endogenous systems. Mechanistically, basal and ligand-induced EV release are independent of GRKs and β-arrestin but each relies on different trafficking routes and C-terminal determinants. Ligand-induced EV release is associated with plasma membrane localization and receptor recycling pathways. In contrast, basal EV release is governed by intracellular sorting processes and influenced by receptor ubiquitination and RAMP3. Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. We also show that the release on EVs, in particular under basal conditions, is observed for other receptors such as KOR, CXCR4 and several ACKRs. Collectively, these findings establish EVs as regulators in chemokine and opioid systems and as a distinct dimension of ACKR3 and more broadly GPCR biology.

10.1038/s41467-026-78875-1.title: Mannitol-stimulated Copeptin for diagnosing Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency: a randomized controlled proof of concept and a single-arm pilot study
10.1038/s41467-026-78875-1.abstract: Abstract Differentiating arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency from primary polydipsia is challenging. The most accurate test, hypertonic saline-stimulated copeptin, requires intensive monitoring. Intravenous mannitol stimulates AVP release and may provide a simpler alternative. In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, 22 healthy adults received mannitol and placebo in random order, of whom 21 were included in the primary analysis. In a pilot study, 10 patients with AVP deficiency and 10 with primary polydipsia received mannitol. The primary outcome was copeptin after mannitol infusion. Mannitol resulted in a 2.29-fold higher copeptin at 90 minutes (+6.4 pmol/L (95% CI: +5.2, +7.7; p <0.001)) than after placebo at mean baseline copeptin levels in healthy adults. In patients, copeptin after 30 minutes was 11.7 pmol/L (95% CI: 6.5, 17.0) higher in primary polydipsia than in AVP deficiency. Mannitol infusion shows promise as a new diagnostic approach. Larger confirmatory studies are required to validate both the optimal diagnostic cut-off and patient safety. Trial Registration number: NCT06542198 .

10.1038/s41467-026-77460-w.title: Cell type-selective targeting by heterobifunctional protein binders via in-cell enrichment
10.1038/s41467-026-77460-w.abstract: Abstract Non-catalytic heterobifunctional protein binders promise to expand the range of therapeutic options by establishing complexes between key target proteins and accessory presenter proteins equipped with additional properties. Here, we systematically investigate the rational design of such molecules, explore the biochemical basis of complex formation and determine how they achieve cellular efficacy using the endogenously expressed immunophilin FKBP12 as presenter protein and the transcriptional regulator BRD4 as target protein. We present classes of bifunctional molecules that enable selective, FKBP12-dependent killing of specific cell types at subnanomolar concentrations and allow to differentiate between closely related bromodomains of the BET family. We propose that the strongly potentiated efficacy of these bifunctional compounds is based on cellular enrichment through binding to the highly abundant presenter protein FKBP12, a mechanism we term “CellTrap”. Our findings substantiate the concept that highly expressed, non-essential proteins can be repurposed as selective recruiters to expand therapeutic windows of existing small-molecule inhibitors, opening new avenues for designing targeted drugs with improved cell-type specificity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78805-1.title: Conveyor-mode electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe
10.1038/s41467-026-78805-1.abstract: Abstract Conveyor-mode shuttling in gated Si/SiGe devices enables adiabatic transfer of single electrons, electron patterns and spin qubits confined in quantum dots across several microns with a scalable number of signal lines. To realize their full potential, linear shuttle lanes must connect into a two-dimensional grid with controllable routing. We introduce a T-junction device linking two independently driven shuttle lanes. Electron routing across the junction requires no extra control lines beyond the four channels per conveyor belt. We measure an inter-lane charge transfer fidelity of $$F={100.0000000}_{-9\times 1{0}^{-7}}^{+0}\,\%$$ F = 100.0000000 − 9 × 1 0 − 7 + 0 % at an instantaneous electron velocity of 270 mm s −1 . The filling of 54 quantum dots is controlled by simple atomic pulses, allowing us to swap electron patterns, laying the groundwork for a native spin-qubit SWAP gate. This T-junction establishes a path towards scalable, two-dimensional quantum computing architectures with flexible spin qubit routing for quantum error correction.

10.1038/s41467-026-78851-9.title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
10.1038/s41467-026-78851-9.abstract: Abstract The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

10.1038/s41467-026-79247-5.title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
10.1038/s41467-026-79247-5.abstract: Abstract Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3-15% CO 2 , and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO 2 -starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni-N-C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO 2 reduction under dilute CO 2 . By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni-N x sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO 2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO 2 adduct that enhances local CO 2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption-re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO 2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni-N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO 2 reduction catalysts under CO 2 -limited conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-79187-0.title: Toward Ternary Computing Enabled by Origami-Inspired Modular Architectures
10.1038/s41467-026-79187-0.abstract: Abstract Modern mechanical computing, being envisioned as a pathway toward structure- and material-level processing, holds potential for intelligent metamaterials and robotics in extreme environments. However, current computing architectures remain constrained by binary paradigms. Here, we introduce an origami-inspired modular architecture that encodes logical mappings into its inherent kinematic responses under an input-output decoupled paradigm, enabling both binary and ternary mechanical computing. Within this emerging paradigm, the multi-stable states of two Kresling origami configurations serve as physical carriers for generating discrete signals, while torsional transitions among these states ensure signal switching, supporting operations from logic gates to advanced arithmetic. Based on this mechanical architecture, we systematically demonstrate seven common logic gates and modular arithmetic half- and full-adders in both binary and ternary systems, revealing challenges and opportunities in advancing multi-valued logic through comparative analysis. The physical platform, along with its accompanying response-programming strategy, represents a simplified and generalized paradigm that supports migration to higher-level mechanical computing mechanisms.

10.1038/s41467-026-79010-w.title: Bistable origami robot for adaptive multimodal motion actuated by nonuniform magnetic fields
10.1038/s41467-026-79010-w.abstract: Abstract Conventional magnetically controlled mini-robots require operation within highly uniform and high-precision magnetic fields, which are impractical for large space applications. In this work, the bistable origami robot offloads these requirements onto the pre-programmed geometry of its mechanical architecture. These structures exhibit distinct deformation modes at each stable state when subjected to small-amplitude magnetic perturbations. Moreover, transitions between stable states-triggered by large-amplitude impulsive magnetic inputs-enable impulsive motions such as grasping. Correspondingly, a large-workspace magnetic actuation system is developed to generate low-uniform magnetic fields, and it is capable of controlling the bistable origami structure for desired multimodal locomotion and manipulation. We demonstrate capabilities including self-grasping, object capture, and adaptive locomotion modes such as crawling, turning, tumbling, scampering, jumping, and rolling at two different stable configurations. Our findings offer an approach for designing multi-functional and wireless mini/microrobots in large spaces, which is validated through analytical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental testing.

Here, McKenna et al. show that the two types of serovars use opposing pre-invasion strategies to sense and invade human intestinal epithelium.

10.1038/s41467-026-79298-8.title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
10.1038/s41467-026-79298-8.abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T 50 ) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. Here, we demonstrate stable green PeLEDs with a T 50 lifetime of 1350 h at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m −2 (nits), a maximum energy-conversion efficiency of 28.0%, and a peak external quantum efficiency of 24.5%. The exceptional performance is enabled by the insertion of a fluorinated self-assembled monolayer between the metal oxide and polymeric hole-transport layers. This molecular interlayer leads to Ohmic-like characteristics for charge injection, lowering the operating voltage at ~1000 nits to sub-bandgap levels (~2.1 V) where ion migration is suppressed. The accumulated photon output of our PeLEDs over the course of their T 50 lifespan is found to sharply increase as the driving voltage drops to sub-bandgap values, highlighting the critical role of employing low-voltage device architectures in reaching the 1350-h/1000-nit stability milestone. Finally, a flexible active-matrix PeLED display prototype is developed, showing the potential of the devices for wearable optoelectronics.

10.1038/s41467-026-79060-0.title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C-H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
10.1038/s41467-026-79060-0.abstract: Abstract Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing α-amino C-H bonds. Here we show a photoredox/cobalt dual-catalytic strategy for N-methyl-selective α-C-H vinylation of unactivated tertiary alkylamines with internal alkynes. This redox-neutral method provides trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or external oxidants, with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and site-selectivity under mild conditions. The reaction accommodates diverse amines and alkynes, including electronically unbiased dialkyl alkynes, and enables gram-scale synthesis, preparation of the fungicide fenpropidin and late-stage functionalization of structurally complex pharmaceuticals. Some drug analogues show enhanced apparent human histamine H1 receptor binding affinity. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a reasonable reaction pathway involving α-amino carbon radical generation via photoredox catalysis, followed by aminomethyl-cobalt I -mediated alkyne migratory insertion and protonolysis. This work provides a practical strategy for selective trialkylamines editing and late-stage diversification.

10.1038/s41467-026-79331-w.title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
10.1038/s41467-026-79331-w.abstract: Abstract The role of the hippocampus in resolving memory interference has been greatly elucidated by considering the relationship between the similarity of visual stimuli (input) and corresponding similarity of hippocampal activity patterns (output). However, these input-output functions can take surprisingly different forms. Here, we reconcile seemingly conflicting findings by considering the possibility that the hippocampus prioritizes different dimensions of visual similarity across different stages of learning. First, we generated a set of natural scene images from two visual categories and rigorously characterized visual similarity using a wide array of methods: neural networks, artificial intelligence models, and human perceptual and memory decisions. We then identified two orthogonal dimensions of visual similarity that each predicted memory interference, but that did so at distinct stages of learning. Using high-resolution fMRI, we then tested for dimension-specific input-output functions within the hippocampus. Within CA3 and dentate gyrus (CA3/DG), we show that dimensions of visual similarity were inverted (repulsion) at stages of learning when they contributed to memory interference. In contrast, CA3/DG preserved similarity when dimensions did not contribute to interference. These findings reveal that hippocampal representations of visually-similar stimuli are highly dynamic and critically depend on the dimensions of similarity that currently contribute to memory interference.

10.1038/s41467-026-78710-7.title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
10.1038/s41467-026-78710-7.abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

10.1038/s41467-026-79006-6.title: CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
10.1038/s41467-026-79006-6.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79006-6 Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. 10.1038/s41467-026-76178-z.title: Altered bone marrow niche forms central innate immune memory driving cardiac dysfunction
10.1038/s41467-026-76178-z.abstract: Abstract We previously showed that heart failure induces innate immune memory in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, which contributes to recurrence of heart failure and impaired stress responses in multiple organs. While the bone marrow microenvironment maintains blood cell formation, its role in this memory remains poorly understood. Here we show that bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells expressing the leptin receptor influence hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells to promote cardiac pathology. Transplanting these stromal cells from mice with heart failure together with healthy hematopoietic cells caused inflammatory macrophages to accumulate in the heart and worsened cardiac remodeling. Mechanistically, heart failure reduced a stromal subpopulation producing heparin-binding epidermal growth factor and suppressed growth factor signaling in hematopoietic cells. Heart failure also activated a fat-forming program in stromal cells. Notably, an equivalent stromal subpopulation exists in human bone marrow, and heart failure was associated with increased bone marrow fat in humans, identifying the bone marrow microenvironment as a regulator of innate immune memory.

10.1038/s41467-026-78777-2.title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
10.1038/s41467-026-78777-2.abstract: Abstract Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory-Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Overall, this work establishes redundancy maximization as a design principle for associative memories and opens pathways for new associative memory models based on information-theoretic goals.

10.1038/s41467-026-79319-6.title: Phospholipase D1 activates NAD kinase fuelling neutrophil extracellular trap formation
10.1038/s41467-026-79319-6.abstract: Abstract Neutrophil extracellular trap formation is a central innate immune defence mechanism that depends on NADPH oxidase-driven reactive oxygen species production. How NADP⁺ availability is regulated during neutrophil activation remains unclear. Using integrated lipidomic, biochemical and functional analyses in human neutrophils, we identify NAD kinase, the sole enzyme responsible for NADP⁺ synthesis, as a direct lipid-regulated effector downstream of phospholipase D1. Neutrophil activation induces rapid, phospholipase D1-dependent production of phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate, which bind and activate NAD kinase. The resulting cytosolic NADP⁺ is reduced to NADPH by the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and consumed by NADPH oxidase during neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Pharmacological or genetic disruption of phospholipase D1 suppresses NAD kinase activity, depletes NADP⁺ and impairs neutrophil extracellular trap formation independently of direct NADPH oxidase inhibition. These findings define a lipid-metabolic axis coupling phospholipase D1-driven membrane remodelling to NADP⁺ availability and innate immune function.

10.1038/s41467-026-78980-1.title: [18F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
10.1038/s41467-026-78980-1.abstract: Abstract Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([ 18 F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [ 18 F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [ 18 F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

10.1038/s41467-026-78948-1.title: A topographic video model predicts the spatio-functional organization of the human visual system
10.1038/s41467-026-78948-1.abstract: Abstract The human brain organizes visual processing into spatially structured functional clusters. Recent topographic neural networks model category-selective clusters but are limited to static images and ventral cortex. In this work, we model the topographic organization of dynamic visual representations across high-level visual cortex. We introduce a general method that spatially arranges and transforms units from a neural network onto a simulated cortical sheet. Applied to a pretrained video foundation model, the method produces spatially structured response correlations while preserving task performance and brain alignment. It captures ventral and dorsal clusters, including face-, body-, and motion-selective patches, and reflects system-level selectivity distributions for animacy, object size, and static versus dynamic content. Functional selectivity varies smoothly across both model and human tissue, suggesting predominantly general-purpose cortical processing with continuous transitions into local functional clusters. Taken together, we provide a computational framework for understanding the spatial and functional organization of high-level visual cortex.

10.1038/s41467-026-77762-z.title: Payoff selectivity drives collective intelligence during dynamic resource tracking in humans
10.1038/s41467-026-77762-z.abstract: Abstract Humans’ abilities for complex social learning and collective adaptation stand out across species. Yet it is largely unknown how people integrate dynamically changing personal and social cues in realistic environments, resulting in collective intelligence or maladaptive behavior. Here, we report an online 3D immersive-reality experiment in which participants ( n = 621) search for and track a mobile resource under realistic visual-spatial constraints. Participants complete the task either alone or in groups of five with different types of social information and resource speeds. Contrasting earlier work, participants in groups outperform solitary individuals, but only when payoff information was available. High-resolution visual field data and movement trajectories reveal that payoff visibility prompts adaptive recalibration of visual information flow, thereby enabling flexible adaptation. Computational models of fine-grained movement decisions and agent-based simulations show that payoff information lets participants dynamically identify and selectively respond to reliable social cues, thus unlocking the group’s collective potential.

10.1038/s41467-026-79127-y.title: Continuous directed evolution using engineered human B cell lines
10.1038/s41467-026-79127-y.abstract: Abstract The B cells of the human immune system have evolved somatic hypermutation (SHM) mechanisms that introduce mutations at the immunoglobulin genomic loci at a significantly higher frequency than the rest of the genome thereby allowing them to evolve antibody sequences without compromising fitness due to genome-wide mutations. Inspired by these observations, here we develop a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the SHM mechanisms to a stable, non-immunoglobulin genomic locus of the human B cell lines to continuously evolve cytosolic and surface displayed proteins with a broad mutational spectrum comprising of substitutions, deletions and insertions. Using our human B cell surface display platform and CODE-HB, we evolve neutralizing antibodies targeting avian influenza and escape variants of influenza. Given the modularity and simplicity of CODE-HB, we anticipate that this platform can be used for rapidly evolving biotechnologically relevant biomolecules directly in human cells.

10.1038/s41467-026-78489-7.title: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
10.1038/s41467-026-78489-7.abstract: Abstract A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them - such as global vegetation - are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. Here, we introduce a method to account for non-stationarity in estimating the resilience of diverse synthetic and real-world systems via a regression-based formulation of the Langevin equation. Our method does not require extensive data pre-processing, is robust to gaps in the data record, and does not require regular time sampling. We further show that our method can incorporate time-varying data uncertainties, derive uncertainty bounds for stability estimates, and can be natively extended to examine spatial systems. Our method is a drop-in replacement for widely-used autocorrelation-based resilience estimates, and can be applied across diverse Earth system components.

10.1038/s41467-026-77617-7.title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
10.1038/s41467-026-77617-7.abstract: Abstract The role of phonons in cuprates remains controversial, with their complex lattice structure complicating the investigation. Here, we identify phonon modes originating from charge reservoir and superconducting layers of Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ using sub-unit-cell resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy in a scanning transmission electron microscope. We reveal several phonon modes exhibiting layer-specific localization: ~78 meV in-plane modes localized in the CuO 2 planes, ~42 meV hybrid (in-plane and out-of-plane) modes in the CuO 2 planes, and ~38 meV hybrid modes in the BiO layers. We also observe a periodic modulation of phonon frequencies induced by the superstructure, spatially correlating with the superconducting gap variation. Our findings offer new insights into the lattice dynamics in cuprates, fostering deeper exploration of the microscopic linkage between structural modulation, electronic inhomogeneity, and electron-phonon coupling.

10.1038/s41467-026-79118-z.title: Propofol induces sustained suppression of alcohol drinking via habenular activation in mice
10.1038/s41467-026-79118-z.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79118-z The lateral habenula is known to regulate alcohol drinking behaviors in mice. Here, the authors show that a single dose of propofol reduces voluntary alcohol drinking in mice via hyperactivity of neurons in the lateral habenula, and through propofol interaction with the 5-HT2C receptor.

10.1038/s41467-026-79077-5.title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
10.1038/s41467-026-79077-5.abstract: Abstract Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

10.1038/s41467-026-79432-6.title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
10.1038/s41467-026-79432-6.abstract: Abstract Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP-c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

10.1038/s41467-026-78713-4.title: Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
10.1038/s41467-026-78713-4.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78713-4 Recovering polymerization-grade monomers from waste textiles remains challenging. Here the authors report that the depolymerization of PET from thermally treated mixed textiles via methanolysis can be achieved in a rapid yet highly selective manner under mild conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-79376-x.title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
10.1038/s41467-026-79376-x.abstract: Abstract Exploiting thin Li foils ≤ 20 μm is required for high-energy-density and long-cycling-lifespan battery, but is severely hindered by the poor processability of Li, as well as its inhomogeneous plating behaviors and resulting low Coulombic efficiency. Herein, an approach balancing Li supply and consumption is fulfilled by designing thin molten-salt-derived, nanocomposite Li@LiX metal negative electrodes. Benefitting from the formation of nanofluid due to the spontaneous reaction of inorganic nanoparticles in molten Li, the bonding states at both Li surface and Li|Cu interface are effectively regulated, displaying an enhanced wetting behaviour of Li on Cu. This approach enables the fabrication of an 800-nm-thick Li-based negative electrode foil as well as the formation of an inorganic-rich interphase upon cycling, which suppresses Li consumption by reducing corrosion susceptibility. As a result, practical pouch cells composed of 10-μm-thick Li@lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) and LiFePO 4 offer stable cycling over 250 cycles, while those composed of 20-μm-thick Li@LiFSI and LiNi 0.92 Co 0.03 Mn 0.05 O 2 with an areal capacity of 4.6 mAh cm −2 achieve 100 cycles, yielding specific energy of 498 Wh kg −1 and energy density of 1,142 Wh L −1 , indicating that this design strategy is applicable to lithium metal batteries.

10.1038/s41467-026-78009-7.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78009-7 Marine pressure monitoring helps reveal ocean dynamics and assess human impacts. This work reports a self-contained low-power flexible marine temperature depth (FMTD) sensor featuring wide range, high precision and restrained temperature drift.

10.1038/s41467-026-79065-9.title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
10.1038/s41467-026-79065-9.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79065-9 How actin regulates late phagosomal maturation and microbial killing in neutrophils remains unclear. The authors here show that WASH drives actin-dependent lysosomal dynamics and STX19 recruitment to phagosomes, enabling lysosome fusion and bacterial killing.

10.1038/s41467-026-79393-w.title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries

10.1038/s41467-026-78325-y.title: Ultra-high precision speckle spectrometer enabling radio-frequency scale resolution of atomic spectra
10.1038/s41467-026-78325-y.abstract: Abstract Laser speckle, the granular intensity pattern arising from random optical interference, provides a high-dimensional encoding of spectral information that can be exploited for precision metrology. Speckle-based spectrometers have advanced rapidly owing to their compact footprint, mechanical robustness and alignment agnostic nature, yet their spectral resolution has remained limited to the picometre scale. In this work, we break this limit by employing an integrating sphere as a multiply scattering cavity with access to a high range of path lengths to enhance spectral sensitivity. At 780 nm, the resulting device achieves a resolution of 6 fm, corresponding to a resolving power of 1.3 × 10 8 , representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previous implementations. This ultra-high resolution enables clear discrimination of laser sidebands generated by an electro-optical modulator, with extracted sideband powers agreeing with expected values to within 1%. It further permits a direct speckle-based measurement of the hyperfine structure of the D 2 transition in 85 Rb, with transmission spectra differing by no more than 3.7% from independent wavemeter-referenced measurements. These results establish speckle as a platform for ultra-high precision spectroscopy, radio-frequency spectrometry, and microwave photonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-78804-2.title: Insular motor and error encoding supports self-correcting intracranial brain-computer interface
10.1038/s41467-026-78804-2.abstract: Abstract Error recognition is fundamental to adaptive behavior, enabling rapid compensatory action when outcomes deviate from expectations. Central to this function are neural circuits for performance monitoring, encoding cognitive signals that could support more reliable neural interfaces. Here, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) in epilepsy patients to enable a motor brain-computer interface (BCI) while sampling error-related activity across a distributed network. Our work reveals high-frequency population dynamics emerging in the anterior insula and propagating to the prefrontal cortex as the interface fails to follow the user’s intention. We identify spatially organized insular responses to error processing and movement feedback, highlighting it as a heterogeneous hub linking action and outcome. Frontoinsular recording sites were found to preferentially encode error-related activity, while centroparietal responses were intermixed with compensatory motor signals, making the former a compelling target for real-time error correction. Together, our findings demonstrate a human intracranial BCI harnessing insular brain activity, integrating cognitive processes directly into device control.

10.1038/s41467-026-76521-4.title: Optotagging in primate cortex uncovers excitatory and inhibitory neuron specializations in form vision
10.1038/s41467-026-76521-4.abstract: Abstract The perception of complex visual shapes is a hallmark of primates and a foundation for many of their decisions and actions. The neural mechanisms of this visual function are best studied in macaques, but progress in this animal model has been hampered by the inability to dissect the contributions of distinct neuronal cell types. Here, we developed and applied an optogenetic approach for identifying the responses of individual excitatory and inhibitory neurons in the macaque visual cortex with light. Using this optotagging approach in male macaques, we uncovered clear functional differences between the two neuronal cell types. Excitatory and inhibitory neurons showed moderate differences in their extracellular spike waveforms and considerable differences in their visual response properties. Inhibitory neurons signaled simple visual forms almost exclusively, whereas excitatory neurons signaled both simple and complex forms and were more visually responsive than inhibitory neurons. Excitatory neurons had protracted response dynamics and developed their selectivity for complex forms gradually over time. These findings reveal a dominant role for excitatory neurons in visual shape processing, advancing a deeper mechanistic understanding of high-level vision. Beyond these insights, this work establishes a blueprint for elucidating the cell type-specific circuit logic underlying higher brain functions in primates.
