10.1126/sciadv.aec7590.title: Carbon ion irradiation at a clinically used dose rewires super-enhancers to drive necroptosis and systemic immunity
10.1126/sciadv.aec7590.abstract: Radiotherapy augments immunotherapy, yet conventional 2 Gy x-ray fractions largely induce apoptosis, whereas robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) is more commonly associated with higher-dose irradiation regimens. Here, we reveal a dose-independent, high-LET-specific paradigm: a physical dose of 2 Gy of carbon ions provokes antitumor immunity. Carbon ions redirect death wiring to MLKL-dependent necroptosis and trigger an NF-κB-driven inflammatory cascade (IL1A/B, CXCL1/2/3), surpassing 8 Gy x-rays in immunogenicity despite lower direct tumor cell-killing capacity. Multi-omics analyses identify clustered DNA damage-driven super-enhancer remodeling as an epigenetic switch that suppresses cIAP1/2-caspase-8-mediated apoptosis while licensing inflammatory necroptosis. Pharmacologic inhibition of MLKL abolishes these responses to carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT). In vivo, 2 Gy CIRT drives abscopal response with increased CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. Together, these findings establish CIRT as a feasible, immune-stimulatory radiotherapy converting local exposure into systemic control via super-enhancer-mediated reprogramming of death and inflammation, providing a mechanistic rationale to integrate carbon ions into next-generation radio-immunotherapy.

10.1126/sciadv.aed9129.title: Ultrasensitive chiral detection by nonlinear chiroptics in spiral plasmonic metastructures surpasses linear limits
10.1126/sciadv.aed9129.abstract: Chiral sensing is vital in pharmaceuticals and biomedicine but is hindered by the inherently weak chiroptic signals of molecules. Conventional methods rely on tedious chromatographic techniques with expensive chiral columns. This work introduces a breakthrough in ultrasensitive chiral detection by combining nonlinear optics and tailored chiral plasmonics. We fabricate spiral gold metastructures that provide strong enhancements of both electric and superchiral near fields, which simultaneously optimize both the nonlinear conversion efficiency and dissymmetry factor, thereby generating a prominent nonlinear chiroptic response to chiral molecules. The resulting change of circularly polarized second-harmonic generation (ΔCP SHG ) demonstrates remarkable sensitivity to chiral adsorbates, achieving a record-low detection limit of ∼11 picomolars and an outstanding figure of merit of 3260 per micromolar. A key advantage is the ability to selectively detect specific enantiomers directly within racemic mixtures, thereby dispensing with the need for preliminary chromatographic separation. This platform opens promising avenues for chiral analysis, pushing the boundaries of sensitivity, selectivity, and miniaturization for next-generation biochemical assays.

10.1126/sciadv.aea7469.title: Jomon genomics reveal cold adaptation in Upper Paleolithic hunter-gatherers of eastern Eurasia
10.1126/sciadv.aea7469.abstract: How did Homo sapiens thrive in extreme environments during their dispersal across Eurasia? Unraveling adaptations that enabled human survival during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) remains critical. Here, we analyze 42 genomes from Holocene hunter-gatherers (Jomon) in the Japanese archipelago, revealing their deep ancestry from an isolated Upper Paleolithic (UP) East Eurasian lineage. We detect gene flow from northern UP Siberians into Jomon, reconciling long-standing debates between bioanthropology and archaeology regarding East Asian peopling. We find no Jomon-specific Denisovan ancestry, suggesting shared introgression before their LGM divergence from mainlanders. Furthermore, we find evidence consistent with cold adaptation in Jomon UP ancestry, highlighting diverse physiological pathways. Our study provides one of the first paleogenomic frameworks for investigating ancient adaptations in UP East Eurasians, revealing an evolutionary legacy from a colder past in present-day humans.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg3223.title: The extreme diversity of retinal amacrine cells has deep evolutionary roots
10.1126/sciadv.aeg3223.abstract: Amacrine cells (ACs) comprise a heterogeneous class of inhibitory neurons in the vertebrate retina, exhibiting morphological and functional complexity rivaling that of cortical interneurons. Here, we integrate single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic atlases from 24 vertebrate species to reconstruct the evolutionary origins of this extreme diversity. We identify 42 orthologous AC types, most of which exhibit a one-to-one correspondence across amniotes and, in many cases, across vertebrates. While core molecular identities are conserved, AC types vary in abundance and gene expression across species, likely reflecting adaptations to distinct visual ecologies. AC diversity scales with that of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), indicative of coevolution. Last, we suggest that ACs arose from an AC-RGC hybrid precursor, with glycinergic ACs diverging early in vertebrate evolution, followed by a bifurcation between RGCs and GABAergic ACs. Together, these findings establish a unified evolutionary framework for understanding the diversity, development, and function of a class of inhibitory neurons across vertebrates.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh9625.title: A biomimetic, ultralow-power edge-AI-empowered and self-sustaining gait analysis system
10.1126/sciadv.aeh9625.abstract: Smart digital health has reshaped patient monitoring, but it faces a fundamental trade-off between device intelligence and continuous, energy-efficient monitoring. Inspired by self-sustaining intelligent biospecies, we develop a biomimetic, battery-free, and high-precision edge-AI system through a harvested-energy-constrained holistic co-design that couples ultralow-power edge-AI-empowered sensor hardware with biomechanical energy harvesting and cold-start power management. Our edge-AI-empowered motion sensor performs instantaneous, context-aware on-device inference and timely result updating from raw sensor data while consuming only 86 μW. A high-output energy harvester and tailored high-efficiency power management circuitry sustain energy levels exceeding system requirements, eliminating downtime associated with charging and enabling true 24/7, hassle-free monitoring. This breakthrough establishes a paradigm for system-level, edge-AI-empowered, and self-sustaining sensing, demonstrating that intelligence and energy autonomy can coexist within a single wearable platform and pointing to next-generation always-on, personalized digital health systems.

10.1126/sciadv.aec6015.title: Distinct types of dendritic Ca 2+ spikes in CA3 pyramidal neurons associated with neuronal activity changes during navigation
10.1126/sciadv.aec6015.abstract: Active dendrites enrich single-neuron computations by performing nonlinear input integration, including generation of dendritic spikes. Diverse dendritic spike types have been found in various cortical neuron classes in vitro; however, their in vivo prevalence and roles remained elusive. We measured calcium activity in apical dendrites and soma of pyramidal cells in the hippocampal area CA3 (CA3PCs) during virtual navigation in mice. Although dendritic activity was generally synchronous with the soma, their correlation decreased with dendritic distance. We identified two types of regenerative dendritic activities: slow, large-amplitude global Ca 2+ events representing putative Ca 2+ plateaus and fast Ca 2+ events with large dendrite-to-soma attenuation, representing putative dendritically initiated Ca 2+ spikes. Ca 2+ plateaus contributed to spatially tuned activity but only occasionally induced new place fields, suggesting conditional induction of synaptic plasticity. In contrast, fast Ca 2+ spikes were often followed by transient increase in somatic activity without spatial tuning, suggesting increased excitatory inputs or excitability. Our results unveil previously unidentified mechanisms whereby dendritic activity shapes output of CA3PCs in vivo.

10.1126/sciadv.aef6109.title: Lignin-degrading-inspired dehydrogenative photocatalysis via reductive quenching of donor-acceptor covalent organic framework
10.1126/sciadv.aef6109.abstract: Achieving a photocatalytic reductive quenching cycle that enables direct oxidation of the photocatalyst radical anion by H(I) species, without requiring stoichiometric oxidants or cocatalysts, remains a long-standing challenge in artificial photoredox catalysis. Here we report a bioinspired approach based on the lignin-degrading-mediated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process, implemented through a perylene-based covalent organic framework (NPy-Per-COF) with precisely engineered donor-acceptor characteristics. This heterogeneous photocatalyst sustains a reductive quenching cycle in which controlled radical generation, catalyst regeneration and hydrogen evolution are intrinsically coupled. The system enables dehydrogenative radical cascade reactions between lignin-inspired precursors and structurally diverse unsaturated partners, providing access to a broad range of functionalized aromatic architectures. Further synthetic modifications and in silico analyses confirm the biological relevance and medicinal potential of the synthesized scaffolds. Beyond model substrates, the photocatalytic system can be extended to lignin-derived motifs, highlighting its potential relevance to complex biomass-related chemical space. Mechanistic investigations support the view that donor-acceptor polarization within the COF promotes efficient charge separation, stabilizes the photocatalyst radical anion and facilitates a PCET-initiated reductive quenching cycle. By abstracting and translating key elements of enzymatic redox control into a fully artificial, heterogeneous photocatalytic framework, this work establishes mechanistically informed design guideline for photocatalytic reductive quenching cycle and advances the development of bioinspired systems for controlled dehydrogenative transformations.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg7753.title: Multiple quantum 19 F electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) for distance measurements with multifluorinated spin probes
10.1126/sciadv.aeg7753.abstract: Mims electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) spectroscopy with 19 F spin labels is emerging as a powerful tool to access molecular distances in the 5 to 20 Å range. A time domain (TD) version of the experiment allows to manipulate nuclear spin coherences, similarly to NMR, and thus to increase distance resolution. Nevertheless, Mims ENDOR sensitivity strongly decays with the inter spin distance r , and measurements of longer distances benefit from labels with multiple 19 F nuclei, such as CF 3 probes. Here, we demonstrate that TD Mims ENDOR with two or three 19 F nuclei reveals multiple-quantum effects and homonuclear dipolar couplings. We present a general theoretical framework for TD Mims ENDOR with multiple like nuclei (i.e., 19 F), enabling analysis of spin evolution and the controlled experimental generation of single- and multiple-quantum nuclear coherences. Our results directly report not only on electron-nuclear distances but also on measurements and correlation of internuclear distances. Overall, TD ENDOR potentially offers a toolbox for molecular structure investigations.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg0958.title: CaMKIIα holoenzymes self-organize into chain-like mesoscale clusters
10.1126/sciadv.aeg0958.abstract: Calcium- and calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) is highly enriched in dendritic spines at concentrations comparable to those of cytoskeletal proteins and plays a central role in synaptic plasticity. During long-term potentiation, CaMKIIα further accumulates in spines. However, the mechanisms governing its higher-order organization remain poorly understood. Here, we use high-speed atomic force microscopy to visualize interholoenzyme interaction of CaMKIIα at mesoscopic scales (5 to 500 nanometers). Under freely diffusible conditions, CaMKIIα holoenzymes do not form stable clusters. In contrast, when spatially confined, they assemble into chain-like clusters mediated by kinase-domain interactions. These clusters expand upon activation, concomitant with the dissociation of the regulatory segment. Notably, the CaMKIIα Pro 212 →Leu (P212L) mutant associated with neurodevelopmental disorders forms extensive clusters even in the basal state. Together, our findings demonstrate that CaMKIIα-CaMKIIα interactions drive mesoscale cluster formation and that precise regulation of cluster size and activation-dependent growth might be critical for synaptic signaling.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3751.title: Light-tunable charge dynamics enable ultralow-power bidirectional lead-free perovskite synapses for intelligent vision
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3751.abstract: Advanced vision systems for autonomous robotics require high efficiency, ultralow power consumption, and real-time decision-making. However, conventional vision sensors that rely on single-mode optical excitation fundamentally constrain their versatility. Here, we report a fully light-tunable optoelectronic synaptic device based on perovskite PEA 2 SnI 4 /C 60 heterostructures that uniquely supports dual-mode bidirectional synaptic behaviour with potentiation under visible light and depression under near-infrared illumination, enabled by a synergistic mechanism of sub-bandgap absorption and interfacial carrier trapping-detrapping for wavelength-selective control. The heterostructure device features long-lasting synaptic plasticity, with excitatory and inhibitory retention times of 350 s and over 8000 s, respectively, and an ultralow energy consumption of ∼1 fJ per event. These exceptional characteristics enable unprecedented performance in neuromorphic vision tasks, including attention-enhanced traffic sign recognition, physical reservoir computing, and dynamic target detection using a 7 × 7 array device, which establishes a powerful and energy-efficient platform for next-generation robotic eyes and advances all-optical neuromorphic perceptions toward intelligent autonomy.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh5234.title: Ultrawide-FOV full-color waveguides free of rainbow and fishbone artifacts via physics-constrained generative metagrating design
10.1126/sciadv.aeh5234.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) displays are gaining prominence in consumer and industrial applications due to two-dimensional pupil-expanding waveguides, which achieve the essential dual requirements of compact form factors and large eyebox through innovative dual-axis beam replication technology. Nevertheless, these systems face an intrinsic trilemma compromising three critical parameters-efficiency, angular uniformity, and chromatic dispersion-with all three limitations becoming particularly pronounced at wide angles (>50°) across the visible spectrum, manifesting as fishbone artifacts (periodic non-uniformity patterns) and rainbow effects. To overcome these fundamental limitations, we present a physics-constrained generative adversarial network (PC-GAN) that systematically resolves the trilemma by incorporating two key physical principles: dilated pupil restraint ratio (DPRR) for uniformity control and periodic constraint theory (PCT) for dispersion management. This framework enables high-throughput discovery of metagrating designs while ensuring high-quality imaging performance in single-layer waveguides across the full visible spectrum and ultrawide field of view. Notably, the PC-GAN demonstrates its unique capability by autonomously discovering optimized snowflake-like metagrating (SLMG) geometries - fractal structures that provide breakthrough solutions for pupil expansion uniformity through their hierarchical light manipulation properties. Experimental realization of PC-GAN-optimized metagratings in disparate material systems (polymer and SiC) consistently delivered wide-angle, full-color operation in single-layer waveguides, while eliminating the characteristic fishbone artifacts and rainbow effects of conventional diffractive designs. This physics-constrained generative framework unlocks transformative potential for complex photonic systems beyond AR, enabling advanced designs ranging from ultrathin VR displays to multi-physics-optimized quantum optical devices.

10.1126/sciadv.aed4055.title: Photonic time crystals assisted by quasi-bound states in the continuum
10.1126/sciadv.aed4055.abstract: Photonic time crystals (PTCs) are characterized by the rapid modulation of the material properties in time, causing a momentum bandgap for light. However, the observation of these bandgaps at optical frequencies remains elusive as the necessary temporal modulation amplitudes to show notable momentum bandgaps are relatively high, inaccessible with available materials. While it has been known that structuring PTCs at the subwavelength scale can improve the bandgap size, we push this concept to the extreme by leveraging the nanophotonic toolbox. Specifically, we demonstrate that structures composed of scatterers supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum can substantially reduce the required modulation amplitudes by enhancing the interaction time between light and time-varying matter. This allows us to observe noticeable momentum bandgaps despite the weak temporal modulation. Our approach bridges the concepts of bound states in the continuum and time-varying metamaterials, paving the way toward realizable PTCs at optical frequencies.

10.1126/sciadv.aed3650.title: Truthful visualizations for mass spectrometry imaging enable high-spatial-resolution interactive m/z mapping and exploration
10.1126/sciadv.aed3650.abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) produces high-dimensional molecular data, but practical interpretation remains limited by visualizations that incompletely preserve global structure. We present MSI-VISUAL, an open-source framework for interactive MSI analysis that integrates truthful dimensionality reduction visualizations with region-of-interest selection, statistical comparison, and direct mass/charge ratio ( m/z ) mapping. MSI-VISUAL introduces four visualization strategies: SALO and SPEAR (optimization-based methods designed to improve global structure preservation across distance metrics) and TOP3 and PR3D (lightweight approaches for memory-efficient, rapid visualization of large datasets). Across benchmarks and lipidomics case studies, including mouse brain and kidney pathology examples, the proposed methods outperform commonly used alternatives in our benchmarks, improve detection of subtle tissue differences, and reveal fine molecular-anatomical patterns that support biological insights. These results establish MSI-VISUAL as a scalable framework for discovery-oriented and diagnostic MSI workflows.

10.1126/sciadv.aei7742.title: Fentanyl purity and overdose decline: A reexamination of geographic trends
10.1126/sciadv.aei7742.abstract: Drug overdose deaths in the United States reached record levels during the unregulated (“illicit”) fentanyl era before recently declining. A plausible hypothesis is that a sudden drop in fentanyl purity (“supply shock”) beginning in 2023 caused the downturn. We evaluated this hypothesis by replicating a published analysis with regional overdose data, using transfer function models accounting for time trends and autocorrelation; negative controls tested for spurious correlation. Replicating the original paper, we extracted fentanyl purity data from a Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) figure; overdose mortality used standard vital statistics sources. We found rising national fentanyl purity did not track fatal fentanyl overdose rates in most United States regions, showing only modest association in the West. When both purity and mortality later declined, the observed associations were also seen with unrelated macroeconomic indicators that shared the same time pattern, raising concerns about spurious correlation in the original study. Canadian analyses also revealed variation in both strength and direction of association between fentanyl purity and overdose deaths at subprovince level. Differential selection bias in law enforcement purity assessment may have compromised longitudinal and geographic generalizability of DEA data, notably stimulated reporting for higher-purity wholesale samples in 2023-2024. National fentanyl purity alone does not provide sufficient explanation for the recent decline in overdose deaths. Reductions in localized purity may influence localized overdose decreases, but alternative causes must be considered nationally, including drug supply changes, public health interventions, demographic shifts, behavior changes, post-pandemic recovery, cartel dynamics, and fewer initiates to illicit opioid use.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh8129.title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
10.1126/sciadv.aeh8129.abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.
authors: Aharon G. Fleury, Casey C. O’Hara, Jason D. Everett, Benjamin S. Halpern, Carissa J. Klein, Anthony J. Richardson, Daniel C. Dunn

10.1126/sciadv.aec2023.title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
10.1126/sciadv.aec2023.abstract: The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning-based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector Anopheles coluzzii in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the orco and IR76b chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between An. coluzzii and Aedes aegypti linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.
authors: Joanna K. Konopka, Danny Poinapen, Shivam S. Chitnis, Carmen M. Morrow, Gwyneth M. Card, Christopher J. Potter

10.1126/sciadv.aec2045.title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
10.1126/sciadv.aec2045.abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: K p ,glycine = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; K p ,alanine = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.
authors: Jihua Hao, Can Liu, Feixiang Liu, Chengtao Zhang, Javed Akhter Mondal, Christopher R. Glein, Herve Cardon, Gilles Montagnac, Xiaobin Cao, Isabelle Daniel

10.1126/sciadv.aed5357.title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
10.1126/sciadv.aed5357.abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm-over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

10.1126/sciadv.aee1955.title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
10.1126/sciadv.aee1955.abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.
authors: Sushrut Thorat, Adrien Doerig, Alexander Kroner, Carmen Amme, Tim C. Kietzmann

10.1126/sciadv.aee9266.title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence-assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
10.1126/sciadv.aee9266.abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human-machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)-enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.
authors: Chunyu Yang, Qi Wang, Chen Wang, Antonia Akoto-Yeboah, Shaoru Cheng, Billings Amoah, Yizhen Jia, Shulin Chen, Akhil Canumalla, Kai Zhao, Christopher Simons, Jinghua Li

10.1126/sciadv.aef0666.title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
10.1126/sciadv.aef0666.abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional-printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.
authors: Oscar Demeulenaere, Nikita Ustimenko, Athanasios G. Athanassiadis, Lovish Gulati, Carsten Rockstuhl, Peer Fischer

10.1126/sciadv.aef4365.title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
10.1126/sciadv.aef4365.abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo-electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C-DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.
authors: Yuji Sakai, Mariko Ariyoshi, Yasuhiro Hirano, Yutaka Mahana, Aussie Suzuki, Toru Hirota, Masashi Tachikawa, Tatsuo Fukagawa

10.1126/sciadv.aef7070.title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses
10.1126/sciadv.aef7070.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved sasF gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when S. aureus colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for S. aureus resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of sasF are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper S. aureus surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.
authors: Timothy J. Enroth, Eunjeong Lee, Elan Z. Eisenmesser, Alexander R. Horswill

10.1126/sciadv.aef7786.title: p75NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
10.1126/sciadv.aef7786.abstract: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75 NTR ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis. p75 NTR loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-p75 NTR axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced p75 NTR expression levels. Together, these data establish p75 NTR as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75 NTR axis as a potential therapeutic target.
authors: Chiho Kadota-Watanabe, Jinsook Suh, Eric Yin, Byron Zhao, Jey Kim, Yan Zhang, In-Won Chang, Sowmya Ramesh, Yuna Lee, Joshua Chen, Maulik Ahuja, Sara Jahangiri, Isabelle Lao-Ngo, Ursula Eisinger, Kate Lindsey, Haihui Zhang, Fatemeh Momen-Heravi, Juan Du, James M. Gardner, Rebeka Silva, Sumit Yadav, Chelsea S. Bahney, Aaron W. James, Reuben H. Kim, Ophir D. Klein, Christine Hong

10.1126/sciadv.aef7931.title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
10.1126/sciadv.aef7931.abstract: Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away-mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys 526 (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.
authors: Xiao-Jie Zhang, Cheng-Jie Zhou, Chun-Ru Song, Meng-Lei Feng, Fang-Rui Xue, Dui Sun, Qi Yang, Kang Ding, Zhao-Yu Jiang, Cheng-Guang Liang

10.1126/sciadv.aef9265.title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
10.1126/sciadv.aef9265.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10 7 per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10 8 per milliliter in soils, and 10 9 per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.
authors: Jacopo Marchi, Chadiga Khalek, Abir George, Joshua S. Weitz, Remy Chait

10.1126/sciadv.aeg5289.title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
10.1126/sciadv.aeg5289.abstract: Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ p = 10.42 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , μ n = 30.23 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml −1 for Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.
authors: Yang Yue, Junhong Zhao, Xuejun Wang, Yanan Tang, Yunqi Liu, Dacheng Wei

10.1126/sciadv.aeg7106.title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
10.1126/sciadv.aeg7106.abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh0254.title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
10.1126/sciadv.aeh0254.abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust-like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.
authors: Zaicong Wang, Xiang Wang, Haijin Xu, Junbo Zhang, Frances Elaine Jenner, Stephen Foley, Liang Ma, Kang Chen, Jiyao Sun, Keqing Zong, Yongsheng Liu, Jianwei Li, Junfeng Zhang, Zhaochu Hu

10.1126/sciadv.aeh0887.title: Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO2
10.1126/sciadv.aeh0887.abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide-a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.
authors: Di Cheng, Ao Wu, Hui Pan, Yu-Peng Zhu, Shizhuo Luo, King Yau Yip, Wei Zhang, Ariando Ariando, Chang Liu, Jian-Sheng Wang, Xinwei Li

10.1126/sciadv.aeh1087.title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits
10.1126/sciadv.aeh1087.abstract: The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice, Dmrt1 −/− females are fertile, although they show a reduction of Stra8 expression. Using our DMRT1 mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation when DMRT1 expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development, DMRT1 −/− gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.
authors: Emilie Dujardin, Francis Poulat, Ivan Barberá Aura, Aurélie Dewaele, Marjolaine André, Jennifer McKey, Stéphanie Le Gras, Anne Frambourg, Luc Jouneau, Darío G. Lupiáñez, Béatrice Mandon-Pépin, Eric Pailhoux

10.1126/sciadv.aeh1582.title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe2
10.1126/sciadv.aeh1582.abstract: Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices-ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors-have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe 2 /LiAl 2 Fe 3 O 8 (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe 2 /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe 2 . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field-temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe 2 . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.
authors: Meng Yang, Xiaolong Yin, Jingjing Liu, Yifeng Chen, Qinwu Gao, Hongxing Zhu, Danni Huang, Lang Chen, Shuo-Ying Yang, Junxue Li

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3401.title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3401.abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo-electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3885.title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3885.abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization-selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.
authors: Yang Zhang, Chenggang Chen, Xindong Song, Yueqi Guo, Xiaoqin Wang

10.1126/sciadv.aeh4436.title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4+ T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
10.1126/sciadv.aeh4436.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4 + responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4 + response was strongly T helper 1 (T H 1)-polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor-α and minimal T H 2 cytokines. Both CD4 + and CD8 + T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F-specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.
authors: Anthony DiPiazza, Emily Marcisak, Wen-Han Yu, Daniel Makrinos, Hsiao-Hsuan Kuo, Jenna Landy, Shannon McGrath, Xiaolin Chang, Maria Cavallaro, Christopher Wu, Adam Essene, Haining Lin, Laura Walker, Andrea Carfi, Jaap Oostendorp, Robert Paris, Yanbo Sun

10.1126/sciadv.aeh7206.title: Physical confinement modulates the rate-limiting transition in the release of phosphate from actin filaments
10.1126/sciadv.aeh7206.abstract: The nucleotide state and rates of transitions between states regulate the dynamics of ATPases. Slow inorganic phosphate (P i ) release following ATP hydrolysis is often rate limiting and associated with key conformational changes. Actin filaments offer a unique opportunity to understand the fundamentals of P i release because identical subunits at filament ends and the interior release P i at markedly different rates. The molecular origin of this difference is debated, so we used extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize P i release from different subunits within an actin filament. The calculated dissociation rates of P i from ADP-Mg 2+ in the active site correlate with experimentally measured P i release rates and scale inversely with the numbers of water molecules in the cavity surrounding the γ-phosphate. Simulations show that egress of P i through the protein channels, including through the N111-R177 backdoor, is not rate limiting and that subunits at the filament ends use alternative egress pathways.
authors: Kristina M. Herman, Sahithya Sridharan Iyer, Yihang Wang, Thomas D. Pollard, Gregory A. Voth

10.1126/sciadv.aeh8187.title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
10.1126/sciadv.aeh8187.abstract: Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3: K d = 13.3 ± 3.2 μM, τ = 447 ± 31 seconds; Cy5: K d = 24.0 ± 3.3 μM, τ = 537 ± 22 seconds) and cortisol (Cy3: K d = 36.6 ± 3.9 μM, τ = 205 ± 7 seconds; Cy5: K d = 30.7 ± 5.5 μM, τ = 259 ± 4 seconds) in buffer, serum, and artificial cerebrospinal fluid. Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.
authors: Albert Zehan Li, Sean W. Stewart, Conrad H. T. Belzberg, Amani A. Hariri

10.1126/sciadv.aei3178.title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
10.1126/sciadv.aei3178.abstract: All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10 4 at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.
authors: Sehyun Kim, Minji Kim, Haechan Park, Kihyun Sim, Jihyeon Jang, Yerin Kim, Jinyeong Park, Donghyung Shin, Myeonghyeon Na, Kyoseung Sim

10.1126/sciadv.aei3465.title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N2O5 hydrolysis
10.1126/sciadv.aei3465.abstract: Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N 2 O 5 hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.
authors: Abigail S. Williams, Lynn M. Russell, Sanghee Han, Veronica Z. Berta, Jeramy L. Dedrick, Teresa Campos, Lauren T. Robinson, Rachel Y.-W. Chang, Ryan N. Farley, Allison C. Aiken, Cynthia H. Twohy, Michael J. Wheeler, Jeremy J. B. Wentzell, John Liggio

10.1126/sciadv.aei4624.title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
10.1126/sciadv.aei4624.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.
authors: Jihai Dong, Wenjin Sun, Baylor Fox-Kemper, Zhiyou Jing, Changming Dong

10.1126/sciadv.aei5171.title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model
10.1126/sciadv.aei5171.abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.
authors: Amberlyn Simmons, Sierra F. Wilferd, Sofia Campagnuolo, Veronica Pena, Heather Bimonte-Nelson, Jason Newbern, Rachael W. Sirianni, Christopher L. Plaisier, Sarah E. Stabenfeldt

10.1126/sciadv.aej4153.title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
10.1126/sciadv.aej4153.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How E. faecalis evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how E. faecalis biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that E. faecalis biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of E. faecalis , which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis . We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid-independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.
authors: Haris Antypas, Ronni Anderson Gonçalves da Silva, Geneve Kang Xin Wong, Cui Liang, Logeshwari Muthualagu Natarajan, Rachel Jing Wen Tan, Cheryl Jia Yi Neo, Siu Ling Wong, Kimberly A. Kline

10.1126/sciadv.aej4603.title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
10.1126/sciadv.aej4603.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.
authors: Somnath Shee, Meixiang Huang, Meghraj Singh Baghel, Yuxin Zheng, Shichun Lun, Santosh K. Yadav, Nirbhay N. Yadav, Carlos E. Ruiz-Gonzalez, Sandeep Tyagi, Eric Nuermberger, Sanjay K. Jain, Zaver M. Bhujwalla, Barbara S. Slusher, Philip C. Wong, William Bishai

10.1126/sciadv.aej6501.title: Interpreting the Hall effect of highly doped conducting polymers
10.1126/sciadv.aej6501.abstract: Accurate determination of carrier density and mobility is fundamental to understanding the transport physics of conducting polymers and optimizing their performance. However, Hall effect measurements, widely used for determining carrier concentrations in other materials, have been of limited use for conducting polymers. Applying the conventional Hall coefficient expression ( R H = [ n H q ] − 1 ) consistently yields unphysically high carrier densities in heavily doped polymers. Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi-one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.
authors: Yingqiao Ma, Xinglong Ren, Juncheng Fan, Sebastiaan Hoek, Henning Sirringhaus

10.1126/sciadv.aej9484.title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
10.1126/sciadv.aej9484.abstract: A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations-bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons-is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops below T N ≈ 0.53 kelvin. A c -axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface above μ 0 H c ≈ 3 T , evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. Approaching H c from above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.
authors: Suguru Hosoi, Sejun Park, Michihiro Hirata, Minseong Lee, Adam P. Dioguardi, Joe D. Thompson, Filip Ronning, Allen O. Scheie, Kumpei Imamura, Kenichiro Hashimoto, Takasada Shibauchi, Bishnu P. Belbase, Arjun Unnikrishnan, Johannes Knolle, Arnab Banerjee, Yuji Matsuda

10.1126/sciadv.aek0125.title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
10.1126/sciadv.aek0125.abstract: Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in Betula platyphylla (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the BpMYB123 promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator BpMYB123 , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as BpRD29B . Disrupting BpGAPDH or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.
authors: Zihang He, Zhibo Wang, Caiqiu Gao, Xiaoyu Ji, Yucheng Wang

10.1126/sciadv.ady6777.title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
10.1126/sciadv.ady6777.abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.
authors: Sandy Grégorio, Jonathan M. Lauderdale, Louis-Philippe Nadeau, Raffaele Ferrari

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3417.title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3417.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax ( P. vivax ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.
authors: Jeremy Salvador, Lucas Guselli, Romminea Yeat, Sokchea Lay, Titsophantharoth Thol, Nisa Ya, Lionel Brice Feufack-Donfack, Sievleang Heng, Candice Bohaud, Agnes Orban, Léa Baldor, Baura Tat, Chetan E. Chitnis, Tineke Cantaert, Jean Popovici

10.1126/sciadv.aeg5357.title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
10.1126/sciadv.aeg5357.abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.
