10.1126/sciadv.aed1177.title: Oxygen-dependent constraint of glycolysis through the mitochondrial electron transport chain
10.1126/sciadv.aed1177.abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are constitutively active in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cells. Here, we investigated whether these cells could still respond to hypoxia independently of canonical HIF activation. We found that hypoxia provokes a NADH reductive stress that attenuates lactate release when the supply of extracellular pyruvate becomes limited, a response that was restored by the ectopic expression of the cytosolic and mitochondria-targeted NADH oxidase ( Lb NOX). Suppression of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mtETC) alone is sufficient to attenuate glycolytic flux when extracellular pyruvate is limited, a situation consistent with metabolomic data from human ccRCCs. Furthermore, this response can be mimicked by pharmacological or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) activity and restored by the mitochondrial-targeted alternative oxidase (AOX). Therefore, our data suggest that cells can respond to low oxygen tension through a mitochondrial-dependent elevation of NADH/NAD + , resulting in the suppression of glycolysis when pyruvate availability is compromised.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh9736.title: GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive Treg differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
10.1126/sciadv.aeh9736.abstract: Regulatory T cell (T reg ) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating T reg lineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin + stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote T reg differentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183 + T reg infiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4 + T cells or T reg cells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet-induced T reg expansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8 + T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC-GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced T reg expansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC-GPR183-AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.
authors: Yang Qu, Yihan Xu, Jingchao Bai, Yuhan Zhang, Ning Ji, Xinxin Li, Hui Li

10.1126/sciadv.aeg4737.title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions
10.1126/sciadv.aeg4737.abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure-with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions-supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.
authors: Felix Schoeller, Marc Santolini, Dana Xiadani, Mickael Eskinazi, Ashwin Murali, David Esselman, Wyatt Houtz, Wesley Bellanca, Joshua White

10.1126/sciadv.aeh7099.title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
10.1126/sciadv.aeh7099.abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.
authors: Zhiqing Guo, Thomas J. Roper-Smith, James W. Clark, Jordi Paps, Ruolin Wu, Davide Pisani, Philip C. J. Donoghue

10.1126/sciadv.aeh7105.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
10.1126/sciadv.aeh7105.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti-lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody-functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10 3 -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10 3 -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh8618.title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping
10.1126/sciadv.aeh8618.abstract: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R 2 = 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform’s versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.
authors: Donho Lee, Hyeonseok Han, Chankyu Han, Seungtaek Jang, Changjoon Lee, Chang-yeon Gu, Jiwon Moon, Jihyeon Ahn, Junseong Ahn, Ji-Hwan Ha, Seokjoo Cho, Byeongmin Kang, Yong Suk Oh, Jungrak Choi, Inkyu Park

10.1126/sciadv.aei8832.title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
10.1126/sciadv.aei8832.abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform-Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.
authors: Yang Wu, Gang Huang, Songlin Zhuang, Xinghu Yu, Wenqi Jia, Zhitai Liu, Zhan Li, Mingsi Tong, Li Zhang, Huijun Gao

10.1126/sciadv.ael4020.title: Coarse climate model grids underestimate coastal humid-heat extremes
10.1126/sciadv.ael4020.abstract: Humid-heat extremes reach intensities close to the limit of human survivability around the Arabian Peninsula. Here, we analyze fully coupled kilometer-scale Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) and Integrated Forecasting System-FinitevolumE Sea ice-Ocean Model (IFS-FESOM) simulations from the nextGEMS project, with original resolutions of around 9 kilometers, and compare them with station observations, ERA5, and CMIP6 projections. IFS-FESOM reproduces well the observed upper-tail wet-bulb temperature (TW) and lies near the high end of the CMIP6 distribution over coastal regions, while ICON simulates weaker extremes. Spatial smoothing suppresses localized coastal maxima, reducing daily-maximum TW extremes by up to 8°C and lowering exceedance frequencies across multiple thresholds. Native resolution fields also show stronger mid-century increases in exposure under SSP3-7.0 than their coarse-gridded counterparts. These results suggest that conventional coarse resolution projections may underestimate localized coastal humid-heat risk, although the magnitude of this effect remains model dependent.
authors: Cosimo E. Carniel, Jonathan D. Wille, Lukas Brunner, Diana Francis, Erich M. Fischer

10.1126/sciadv.aef8069.title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
10.1126/sciadv.aef8069.abstract: Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plus FGF21 -encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.
authors: Zhengtai Chen, Hanxiao Sun, Yuanyang Zheng, Xuan Jiang, Yan He, Kai Ye, Yufan Zhang, Zhengwei Mao, Ziyi Zhou, Xiaoxi Lin, Chenggang Yi, Wei Wang

10.1126/sciadv.aek5197.title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage
10.1126/sciadv.aek5197.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of Lactobacillus plantarum -derived extracellular vesicles ( L. plantarum EVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment with L. plantarum EVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.
authors: Ga-eun Go, Seungju Han, Minjae Kang, Sangoh Choi, Soo-eun Lee, Uidon Jeong, Sang-Hee Lee, Ki-Nam Gu, Hanji Kim, Bo Kyoung Hwang, Yunkwan Kim, Euitaek Jeong, Nae-Gyu Kang, Doory Kim

10.1126/sciadv.aeg6228.title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
10.1126/sciadv.aeg6228.abstract: Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O 2 consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O 2 demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O 2 demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O 2 inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (C soft ) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O 2 inventory and C soft decrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O 2 and C.
authors: Shlomit Sharoni, Keisuke Inomura, Stephanie Dutkiewicz, Oliver Jahn, Gregory L. Britten, Michael J. Follows

10.1126/sciadv.aeg5364.title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
10.1126/sciadv.aeg5364.abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.
authors: John Soukar, Kayli Jones, Natalie M. Garza, Valeria Duran Salas, Shounak Roy, Vishal M. Gohil, Akhilesh K. Gaharwar

10.1126/sciadv.aem8494.title: Erratum for the Research Article “Aptamer-functionalized Apoptotic Vesicles Ameliorate Osteoarthritis via Resuming Mitochondria OXPHOS of Chondrocytes”

10.1126/sciadv.aef4658.title: Boron-assisted synthesis of compositionally complex amorphous oxides via short-range-order-constrained generative design
10.1126/sciadv.aef4658.abstract: Engineering short-range atomic order offers a promising route to design amorphous solids. Here, we establish a boron-assisted amorphization strategy using ApolloX, a theory-guided, short-range-order-constrained generative framework for identifying low-energy configurations in compositionally complex multielement systems. Using FeCoNiMoBO x as a model platform, ApolloX generates candidate amorphous structures across varied boron contents. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal that increasing the boron content suppresses atomic diffusion and crystallization, accompanied by the stabilization of BO 3 -centered local motifs that favor amorphous structure formation. Guided by these predictions, we synthesize three FeCoNiMoBO x compositions with distinct boron contents and use synchrotron scattering and electron microscopy to confirm their compositional fidelity, structural homogeneity, and targeted amorphous characteristics, thereby validating the predicted boron-dependent structural evolution. We further extend this strategy to a broader library of multimetal BO x compositions spanning diverse metal combinations and boron loadings. These results identify boron incorporation as an effective and generalizable means of enhancing amorphization and establish a theory-guided framework for the discovery of compositionally complex amorphous materials.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg3333.title: A ciliated intravascular soft millirobot for multimodal in-flow collective manipulation
10.1126/sciadv.aeg3333.abstract: The laminar nature of blood flow and the resulting boundary layer pose substantial challenges for transverse mass transport in blood vessels, limiting intravascular biomedical applications such as targeted delivery, thrombolysis and biomarker enrichment. Herein, we develop a ciliated intravascular millirobot, CiliaVine, for active manipulation of particle and cell collectives through flow regulation. Actuated by tailored magnetic fields, soft cilia on the robot oscillate in different modes, generating desired flow patterns for flow regulation. CiliaVine enhances the transverse transport that is otherwise suppressed under laminar flow, driving circulating collectives from the vessel center toward the vessel wall for drug penetration, or reversing transport for thrombus residue clearance. Flow regulation is investigated in a vascular model using fluorescent tracer particles. Enhanced targeted drug delivery and accelerated thrombolysis enabled by the robot are validated. Circulating tumor cell (CTC) enrichment is evaluated using cancer patient blood and in tumor-bearing rabbits, revealing its effectiveness in physiological environments and its potential for intravascular rare-cell enrichment.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg5529.title: Shedding light on the formation mechanisms of Islamic polychrome lusters: A Cu, Fe, Ag micro XANES study
10.1126/sciadv.aeg5529.abstract: Islamic luster is a ceramic glaze decoration exploiting the quantum-confined optical response of noble metallic nanoparticles to produce a colorful metallic and iridescent appearance. Upon firing, silver and copper initially present in an overpaint diffuse into the glaze and are reduced to Ag 0 and Cu 0 nanoparticles. This study examines the relationship between luster colors and paint composition. The six analyzed shards are 9th century Abbasid polychrome lusters exhibiting green, red, ochre, and brown colors. Key chemical factors are revealed by imaging 16 luster cross sections with different micro- and nanoanalytical methods, including UV-Vis spectroscopy, Ag L 3 -, Cu-, and Fe K-edge micro x-ray absorption spectroscopy (μ-XAS), micro x-ray diffraction (μ-XRD), and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FIB-FE-SEM). These factors connect together (i) the Cu/Ag ratio; (ii) the Cu, Ag, and Fe speciation; (iii) the nature, size, and concentration of metallic nanoparticles; and (iv) the luster color. Notably, the Cu/Ag ratio balances the competitive reactions between Ag + reduction and Cu + disproportionation.

10.1126/sciadv.aec0398.title: Cooperative and collective quantum light emission from perovskite superball superstructures
10.1126/sciadv.aec0398.abstract: Superfluorescence (SF), the coherent light burst from synchronized quantum emitters, has been demonstrated in perovskite quantum dot superlattices. However, limited control over self-assembly, heterogeneity and emitter properties has hindered systematic exploration of cooperative emission and its transition to collective emission regimes such as amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) and lasing. Here, we present emulsion-templated perovskite superballs (SBs) as a robust, tunable platform for investigating collective light-matter phenomena. This strategy enables versatile control over perovskite nanocrystal (PNC) size, packing density, ligand chemistry, optical cavity structure, etc. We identify a critical packing density (∼0.34) for triggering SF in PNC ensembles, in agreement with theoretical calculations. Larger SBs function as self-assembled microcavities, supporting low-threshold lasing with high quality factors. Tunable excitation fluence induces a crossover between the SF and lasing regimes, while high-density SB films also support ASE. These findings establish perovskite SBs as a versatile platform for studying cooperative and collective emission dynamics crucial for advancing scalable quantum photonic technologies.

10.1126/sciadv.aef3043.title: Realizing long-cycling silicon-based all-solid-state batteries with near-zero-stress variation
10.1126/sciadv.aef3043.abstract: Silicon anodes present a compelling alternative to lithium metal for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), offering high capacity without dendrite risks. However, their application is hindered by incomplete understanding of electro-chemo-mechanical (ECM) failure mechanisms in all-solid-state configurations. Through multiple in situ characterizations combining optical microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and pressure monitoring, this work uncovers fundamental stress-mediated degradation pathways in silicon-based ASSBs. Stress evolution-particularly in-plane strain mismatch and out-of-plane mechanical constraints-governs the dominant failure criterion, superseding traditional volume change metrics. This stress-dominated mechanism arises from the interplay between volume and modulus in constrained all-solid-state systems. Guided by these insights, complementary mitigation strategies were developed, including electrode/electrolyte modulus engineering to reduce interfacial stresses and elastic constraint design to accommodate mechanical fluctuations. The synergistic implementation achieves near-zero stress variation and breakthrough cycling stability (90.1% capacity retention after 5000 cycles). This work establishes a paradigm for high-energy-density batteries, shifting the design focus from volume accommodation to comprehensive stress management in all-solid-state systems.

10.1126/sciadv.aed8456.title: A full-range sweat rate sensor with superhydrophobic heterophase shunt for psychology, skin health and body dehydration evaluating
10.1126/sciadv.aed8456.abstract: Sweat secretion provides insights into physiological and psychological states. However, the current single detection method is not compatible with the simultaneous monitoring of gaseous and liquid sweat, which restricts its application for exploring dynamic physiological processes. Herein, a fully integrated sweat sensor with a heterophase shunt for full-range sweat rate monitoring is reported. Through non-interfering integration of epidermal microfluidic conductivity sensing and humidity detection, continuous measurement across 0.182 ∼ 10 μL/(min·cm 2 ) is achieved. The LiCl-doped UiO-66-NH 2 enables a highly sensitive and fast-responding humidity sensor. The biomimetic heterophase shunt, composed of a polydimethylsiloxane and polymethyl methacrylate co-electrospun membrane, exhibits superhydrophobicity (151.9°), gas-permeable [58.07 g/(H·m 2 )], and water pressure tolerance (1.1 kPa). Heterophase shunt effectively integrates sweat detection modes while providing protection for humidity sensor against sweat corrosion and skin contact-induced damage. Integrated with a specialized weak-signal processing module, the sensor allows applications in psychology, skin health and body dehydration evaluating.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh4592.title: Wafer-scale 2D semimetal heterostructures enabling mid-infrared motion tracking with in-sensor perceptual compression
10.1126/sciadv.aeh4592.abstract: Accurate motion detection and trajectory tracking are crucial for scientific and technological applications, but current techniques rely on high-pixel-density imaging arrays that demand extensive hardware and computational resources. Here, we demonstrate high-performance motion detection and tracking sensors based on in situ monolithically integrated wafer-scale telluride semimetals and germanium. Interfacial engineering enhances carrier transport while minimizing interfacial recombination, enabling room-temperature infrared detection up to 10.6 micrometers with a peak sensitivity of 91.6 millivolts per millimeter, a low nonlinearity of 5.1%, and a specific detectivity exceeding 10 10 centimeter-square root hertz per watt in the mid-infrared range. These advancements facilitate real-time infrared position sensing and trajectory tracking with a resolution of 9.7 micrometers. With in-sensor compression, which achieves a 400× reduction by condensing data from 100 × 100 pixels to 5 × 5 elements, a sparse position-sensitive detector array achieves 95% accuracy in simultaneously identifying and tracking multiple dynamic targets. Our monolithically integrated semimetal sensors open avenues toward resource-efficient, precise motion analytics and perception.

10.1126/sciadv.aef8713.title: Ethylene-regulated dimeric ETR1 kinase reveals multi-site EIN2 docking targeted by peptides that delay climacteric ripening
10.1126/sciadv.aef8713.abstract: Ethylene receptors are ER membrane histidine kinases that repress ethylene responses, and the central transducer ETHYLENE INSENSITIVE 2 (EIN2) docks to receptors through its C-terminal tail. Here we express full-length Arabidopsis ETR1 in Pichia pastoris and show that ethylene selectively suppresses the autokinase activity of the dimer, establishing a ligand-responsive receptor preparation. Bio-layer interferometry shows that EIN2-C binds both full-length ETR1 and an isolated transmembrane-GAF module with low-micromolar affinity. NMR mapping of EIN2-C titrated with ETR1-GAF identifies three discrete docking segments, including the known NOP-1 octapeptide and two additional peptides (DP1 and DP2). Synthetic peptides engage ETR1-GAF with distinct kinetics and affinities, and docking models place DP2 in a hydrophobic pocket at the GAF dimer interface. When applied as surface coatings to tomato and mango, these peptides delay ripening in proportion to binding strength. Multi-site competitive inhibition at the EIN2-ETR1 interface thus provides a tunable strategy to modulate ethylene signaling and extend climacteric fruit shelf life.

10.1126/sciadv.aee5160.title: Aqueous lignin adhesive for high-performance wood bonding
10.1126/sciadv.aee5160.abstract: Developing formaldehyde-free and high-performance wood adhesives is imperative for sustainable wood utilization. To overcome performance trade-offs in lignin adhesives, we developed a formaldehyde-free aqueous adhesive formulation via reactive cysteine-functionalized lignin, achieving high performance with an unprecedentedly low lignin loading (20 wt %), which is sprayable and injectable and exhibits excellent fluidity (1.96 mPa·s, 10 3 s −1 ). It undergoes self-curing via forming amide bond, achieving robust bonding performance under simple hot-pressing conditions. The solvent-free lignin adhesive for plywood outperforms commercial resins, demonstrating exceptional dry strength (4.0 MPa), high wet-strength retention (83.7%), and superior durability against extreme temperatures (−196° to 190°C), humid heat aging, and solvents. Cysteine substitution enhances fracture toughness eightfold (reaching 11.06 kJ/m 2 ) by forming dual covalent/noncovalent networks that facilitate the polarity-enabled adhesion and crosslinking-induced toughening. This work establishes an environmentally friendly and scalable strategy for constructing full bio-based adhesives with exceptional processability and durability, providing a paradigm for lignin valorization within lignin-first biorefinery frameworks.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg3567.title: Antenna photosystem I remodeling in the iron stress-induced complex from Anabaena sp. PCC 7120
10.1126/sciadv.aeg3567.abstract: The structure and oligomeric states of the photosystem I-iron stress-induced protein A (PSI-IsiA) supercomplex from several species have been investigated using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and atomic force microscopy. The cryo-EM structure of the PSI-IsiA complex from cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 (7120) has been published previously. However, not all IsiA and PSI subunits were identified. In this work, we have structurally and spectroscopically characterized the PSI-IsiA supercomplex from 7120 using single-particle cryo-EM at a resolution of 2.2 angstroms. The data resolved all individual IsiA and PSI subunits, highlighting features that distinguish the 7120 PSI-IsiA from other complexes, including additional IsiA and a unique PsaK subunit specific for PSI-IsiA. Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy showed tight energetic coupling of IsiA to PSI, which may play a role in lowering antenna fluorescence yield and increasing the efficiency of energy transfer. This work extends the scope of PSI cellular remodeling in response to different stress conditions.

10.1126/sciadv.adz6665.title: Multilocus basis of incipient reproductive isolation in hybridizing populations is revealed by pangenomic and epigenetic divergence
10.1126/sciadv.adz6665.abstract: Incipient reproductive isolation in the presence of gene flow has traditionally been attributed to a small number of major-effect loci under strong selection. Here, using the Heliconius erato adaptive radiation, we apply a pangenome framework to examine how mutational divergence, regulatory variation, and structural variants contribute to genome-wide divergence. In contrast to earlier studies, our high-resolution analyses reveal widespread divergence across the genome, consistent with a multilocus barrier to gene flow. Our findings support a model in which selection acts on regulatory phenotypes under migration-selection balance, with genetic differentiation becoming more pronounced as gene flow declines. By integrating population-level sampling, we show that apparent population-specific structural and regulatory variation inferred from single-reference genomes is overestimated, reflecting pervasive reference bias. While structural variants contribute to genomic variation, in our system, most are shared or polymorphic rather than fixed differences between populations. Together, our results show that the genomic landscape of H. erato divergence reflects the combined contributions of regulatory variation and mutational change, while highlighting the importance of accounting for reference bias when interpreting structural and regulatory divergence. This multilocus framework provides a more accurate view of how reproductive barriers emerge and strengthen under ongoing gene flow.

10.1126/sciadv.aee3092.title: Metal-free redox active covalent organic frameworks for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction
10.1126/sciadv.aee3092.abstract: Designing efficient, metal-free covalent organic framework (COF) electrocatalysts is a promising strategy for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their structural tunability and stability. Herein, we report two redox-active donor-acceptor COFs, TAPA-DHTD and TTT-DHTD, incorporating a thiophene-based dithiophenedione (DHTD) unit. Among them, TTT-DHTD exhibits superior ORR performance with a half-wave potential (E 1/2 ) of 0.82 V vs RHE, approaching that of 20% Pt/C (0.85 V) and surpassing most reported metal-free COFs. It also demonstrates excellent methanol tolerance and long-term durability, maintaining activity over 120 hours. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the donor-acceptor framework optimizes the p -band center, enhances charge separation, and improves adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, thereby accelerating ORR kinetics. This work provides a rational strategy for designing durable, high-performance metal-free electrocatalysts for sustainable energy applications.

10.1126/sciadv.aek3138.title: Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, stratigraphic integrity, and confirming early inland dispersal: Evaluating peopling of the Americas modeling
10.1126/sciadv.aek3138.abstract: Statistical models shape debates over the timing and geography of the initial peopling of the Americas, but their value depends on testing their assumptions against archaeological evidence. We examine the Apparent Stratigraphic Integrity Index (ASI), used to infer postdepositional mixing at Late Pleistocene sites and support a relatively late occupation of temperate North America. ASI describes vertical discontinuity in binned artifact-frequency profiles; it does not directly measure artifact movement or stratigraphic integrity. At Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, Idaho, the 5-centimeter absolute-elevation bins used to calculate ASI do not reflect the actual stratigraphic positions of artifacts across the irregular LU2 surface on which LU3 loess accumulated. The resulting ASI value cannot support claims of large-scale vertical mixing. Independent chronological, stratigraphic, pedogenic, archaeological, and excavation evidence supports the integrity of the ∼16,000-calibrated-years-before-the-present occupation. Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe provides early inland evidence expected under coastal-migration models, showing that models should be evaluated against archaeological evidence rather than used to override it.
authors: Loren G. Davis and David B. Madsen

10.1126/sciadv.aeb9422.title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
10.1126/sciadv.aeb9422.abstract: Mars is reputed to lack ongoing volcanic activity. However, marsquakes were revealed recently, and clues to volcanism younger than tens of million years have accumulated. While sulfur dioxide, so far undetected, could testify to ongoing eruptive activity, evidence of active magma chambers may be better identified by seepage of halogen gases, such as hydrogen chloride (HCl). Observations by Atmospheric Chemistry Suite led to the widespread observations of HCl at part-per-billion levels in the atmosphere of Mars during the warm perihelion period, attributed to aerosol-atmospheric sources. Here, we report HCl detections during the cold aphelion season that are isolated in the Alba Mons region. We also identify fresh and narrow (<1 meter) fissures in this area, which we interpret to be potential HCl pathways rooted into magmatic bodies at depth. Our results are best explained by ongoing igneous processes in the Martian interior.

10.1126/sciadv.aec2297.title: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression
10.1126/sciadv.aec2297.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. Suppression of METTL3, either genetically or pharmacologically, and depletion of its binding partner METTL14 impair ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, we show that METTL3-mediated m 6 A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), the primary maintenance DNA methyltransferase responsible for preserving genome-wide methylation patterns and silencing tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacological inhibition of DNMT1 induces widespread DNA hypomethylation and up-regulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 suppression reduces DNMT1 abundance and derepresses TNFAIP3 and FBXO32 expression. Knockdown and rescue studies further reveal that DNMT1 primarily mediates METTL3-dependent regulation of cell migration, whereas the antiproliferative effects of METTL3 suppression are likely driven by additional downstream targets. Collectively, these findings identify the m 6 A-METTL3-DNMT1 axis as a mechanistic link between RNA and DNA methylation pathways and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HGSOC.

10.1126/sciadv.aed4599.title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
10.1126/sciadv.aed4599.abstract: Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. Some corals exhibited stochastic divergence, whereas others showed deterministic shifts in symbiont community composition. Heat stress generally reduced symbiont diversity and promoted predictable restructuring, consistent with deterministic adaptation to moderate thermal stress but stochastic accumulation of diversity under extreme conditions. We propose that adaptive and stochastic responses represent endpoints along a continuum of host-orchestrated symbiont sorting. This study bridges coral reef ecology with broader host-microbiome theory, offering an integrated perspective on how symbiotic systems may respond to environmental change.
authors: Mariana Rocha de Souza, Janaya Bruce, Annick Cros, Christopher P. Jury, Crawford Drury, Robert J. Toonen

10.1126/sciadv.aed9351.title: A functional connectome identifies vulnerability to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease progression
10.1126/sciadv.aed9351.abstract: Identifying the neurobiological basis of cognitive vulnerability is essential for preventing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We derived the Alzheimer’s Resilience-Vulnerability Connectome (ARC) by contrasting SuperAgers (SA), an extreme phenotype of preserved late-life memory, with AD using resting-state fMRI. ARC distinguished SA from AD in a discovery cohort ( N = 290; AUC = 0.85) and replicated independently ( N = 143), involving prefrontal, temporal, and insular networks and associating with brain age. Applied to cognitively unimpaired adults (discovery: N = 818; replication: N = 497), ARC-based subtyping revealed SA-like and AD-like subgroups with comparable baseline cognition but divergent longitudinal trajectories. AD-like individuals exhibited faster cognitive decline, greater amyloid-β accumulation, and higher AD conversion risk. Exploratory GWAS nominated CLYBL and FRMD6 as candidate novel loci associated with the subtype difference. These findings suggest that ARC captures a continuous connectomic dimension of cognitive aging spanning SA, cognitively typical aging, and AD, highlighting the potential of functional connectomic variation for early risk stratification in AD.
authors: Kanhao Zhao, Hua Xie, Gregory A. Fonzo, Nancy B. Carlisle, Tovia Jacobs, Ricardo S. Osorio, Arpana Church, Feng Vankee Lin, Yu Zhang, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative

10.1126/sciadv.aee6166.title: Local translational program at the muscle-tendon junction endows domain identity in muscle syncytia
10.1126/sciadv.aee6166.abstract: How cells establish specialized subdomains is a fundamental question in cell and tissue biology. Skeletal muscle fibers, among the largest cells in the body, are multinucleated and form distinct regions such as the neuromuscular and myotendinous junctions (MTJs), the latter forming a critical interface between muscle and tendon that transmits contractile force. While transcriptional heterogeneity among myonuclei has been described, whether local translation contributes to domain identity remains unknown, largely due to the lack of tools for domain-specific manipulation. Here, we introduce MTJ-AAV, a viral system that enables selective genetic targeting of MTJ myonuclei. This approach allowed MTJ-specific ribosome tagging and revealed extensive translational regulation underlying MTJ biology and its remodeling during exercise. Untranslated regions of these transcripts were sufficient to control regionalized translation. Notably, the Krüpper-like factor-family transcription factors emerged as translationally up-regulated targets at the MTJ, where they drive local gene expression. Our findings establish local translation as a key layer of subcellular specialization and provide a versatile toolkit for dissecting spatial molecular regulation within muscle syncytia.
authors: Nour El Khazen, Juliana de Carvalho Neves, Vedran Franke, Coalesco Smith, Sakulrat Mankhong, Edgar Jauliac, Laura Yedigaryan, Elise Lefebvre, Altuna Akalin, Pascal Maire, Minchul Kim

10.1126/sciadv.aee7712.title: Clinically derived micro- and nanoplastic uptake drives spatiotemporally confined metabolic stress revealed by bond-selective imaging
10.1126/sciadv.aee7712.abstract: Although microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants, our understanding of cellular toxicity remains incomplete, as adverse effects are often attributed to long-term intracellular accumulation, while the spatiotemporal onset of cellular damage remains poorly defined. Here, we use chemical bond-selective stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy and cell models that decouple continuous exposure from intracellular retention to directly visualize clinically derived MP/NP-cell interactions. Cellular stress occurs primarily during MP/NP exposure, accompanied by alterations in lipid droplet (LD) composition. In contrast, following extracellular removal, intracellularly retained MP/NP become largely inert, with recovery of lipid metabolism and cellular functions. Lipidomics identifies arachidonic acid (AA) as a key dysregulated metabolite, and SRS imaging further reveals transient, spatially confined AA enrichment in MP/NP-proximal LDs during uptake. Phospholipid coating of MP/NP attenuates LD alterations and cytotoxicity while preserving particle internalization, establishing uptake-driven metabolic stress, rather than long-term intracellular retention, as a primary source of MP/NP-induced damage.
authors: Jingyuan Li, Nian Liu, Delong Zhang, Hyeon Jeong Lee

10.1126/sciadv.aee7886.title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
10.1126/sciadv.aee7886.abstract: The stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major uncertainty in projections of future climate. However, direct evidence for AMOC tipping behavior on orbital timescales remains scarce. Here, we reconstruct the strength of Iceland-Scotland Overflow Water, a key lower branch of the deep Atlantic circulation, over the past 800,000 years by combining 12 current-speed records from North Atlantic sediment cores with a data-driven hybrid model. The resulting reconstruction reveals persistent alternation between weak (glacial) and strong (interglacial) circulation modes, pervasive millennial-scale variability within both regimes, and systematic asymmetry between weak-to-strong recoveries and strong-to-weak collapses. Threshold and phase-space analyses show that regime shifts occur within a narrow window of atmospheric carbon dioxide and sea level and often follow hysteresis-like loops. Although bistability persists throughout the last 800,000 years, its sensitivity and timing evolve through time. These findings provide long-term, high-resolution, data-driven constraints on the bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters and its implications for AMOC resilience in a warming world.
authors: Nathan Stevenard, Aline Govin, Catherine Kissel, Didier Swingedouw, Samuel Toucanne, Nathaëlle Bouttes

10.1126/sciadv.aef3222.title: On-going retinal neuronal degeneration despite clinical stability in glaucoma
10.1126/sciadv.aef3222.abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, involves progressive retinal ganglion cell loss. Early detection of this neurodegeneration is critical, yet current clinical methods often identify disease only after substantial damage has occurred. This preliminary study used high-resolution adaptive optics-optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to track individual retinal ganglion cells in patients and healthy volunteers over 3 to 5 years. Results revealed higher neurodegeneration in glaucoma compared to normal aging. We observed 4.16 to 6.86% annual decrease in cell density in glaucoma, far exceeding the 0.27% cell loss rate observed in the healthy volunteer group. Critically, AO-OCT detected progression significantly earlier, identifying cell loss 0.74 years before conventional OCT and 1.49 years before visual field testing. These findings demonstrate AO-OCT as a more sensitive tool capable of monitoring glaucomatous damage with superior precision, potentially representing a major advancement over current clinical imaging.
authors: Achyut J. Raghavendra, Kenaan Elbash, Marlon Diaz, Osamah J. Saeedi, Zhuolin Liu, Daniel X. Hammer

10.1126/sciadv.aef9661.title: Oxygen-mediated projection microstereolithography for sub-100-μm zirconia dental veneers
10.1126/sciadv.aef9661.abstract: High-resolution vat photopolymerization of ceramics is constrained by light scattering, which broadens cured features, and by shallow penetration, which limits interlayer bonding. This trade-off is particularly damaging for microscale structures such as no-preparation dental veneers. We introduce an oxygen-mediated projection microstereolithography strategy in which an oxygen-permeable release film creates an interfacial inhibition field in high-solid-loading zirconia slurry. Rather than uniformly reducing curing, oxygen preferentially filters low-dose scattered light at pattern edges while preserving curing in the projected core. This anisotropic inhibition reshapes the accuracy-depth trade-off, enabling optimized multilayer printing of thin-wall zirconia. The process enabled reproducible fabrication of ∼80-micrometer zirconia veneers with high trueness, improved marginal adaptation, and handling-related strength comparable to substantially thicker milled veneers. The approach provides the potential for minimally invasive dental restoration and a general strategy for high-resolution additive manufacturing of strongly scattering ceramic suspensions.
authors: Yanru Shen, Xiang Wang, Chen Yang, Ying Jiang, Feng Wang, Zhankun Pan, Jinhua Li, Nicholas X. Fang, Yuchun Sun

10.1126/sciadv.aeg0571.title: BCLAF1 links RNA splicing to ATF4-dependent metabolic adaptation in acute myeloid leukemia
10.1126/sciadv.aeg0571.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by genetic alterations and non-mutational mechanisms that disrupt normal hematopoiesis and support leukemic cell survival. While the mutational landscape of AML is well characterized, the non-genetic processes sustaining leukemic maintenance remain less understood. Using human AML cells and murine models, we identify BCL2-associated transcription factor 1 (BCLAF1) as a key regulator of leukemic progression through control of mRNA processing. BCLAF1 physically associates with core spliceosome components and regulates alternative splicing programs in leukemic cells. Mechanistically, BCLAF1 is required for productive splicing of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) mRNA, thereby sustaining ATF4 protein levels and downstream metabolic gene expression programs. Loss of BCLAF1 reduces ATF4 levels, leading to impaired de novo amino acid biosynthesis and increased sensitivity to venetoclax. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism linking RNA splicing control to metabolic adaptation in AML, identifying BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg2088.title: Hoxa10 governs lifelong skeletal stem cell maintenance and bone repair
10.1126/sciadv.aeg2088.abstract: Skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) sustain bone homeostasis and regeneration throughout life, yet the transcriptional programs that preserve their identity remain poorly defined. Here we identify the distal Hox gene Hoxa10 as a cell-autonomous regulator of skeletal stem cell maintenance. Using inducible genetic deletion, lineage tracing, single-cell transcriptomics, and injury models, we show that loss of Hoxa10 leads to progressive depletion of SSPCs, impaired bone regeneration, and defective matrix organization. Mechanistically, Hoxa10 maintains the undifferentiated state of skeletal stem cells by restraining premature osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic commitment, while promoting collagen III production and collagen fiber alignment within regenerative niches. Hoxa10 -dependent regulation of extracellular matrix composition is restricted to primitive progenitors and is uncoupled from osteoblast differentiation. Notably, transient depletion of distal Hox genes in primary human SSPCs recapitulates the murine defects in proliferation, self-renewal, and differentiation restraint. Together, these findings define a conserved Hox-dependent program that preserves skeletal stem cell identity and regenerative competence, revealing how developmental transcription factors are repurposed to sustain the adult skeleton across the life span.
authors: Kevin Leclerc, Margaux Sambon, Raven Weng, Vincentius Jeremy Suhardi, Malissa Ramsukh, Rohan Phadke, Gabrielle Pack, Matthew Rytel, Jack Zhong, Benjamin Schaffler, Sergio Butron, Sophie M. Morgani, Philipp Leucht

10.1126/sciadv.aeg2342.title: Ultrasound neural interface enabling acute spinal cord monitoring and blood flow modulation
10.1126/sciadv.aeg2342.abstract: The days following decompression surgery for acute spinal cord injury (SCI) are a critical period for postoperative monitoring. After wound closure, clinicians lack on-demand access to local spinal cord morphology and hemodynamics, and care therefore remains guided largely by systemic surrogates rather than direct postoperative insight into the injured cord. We present the Multimodal Ultrasound System for Injury Care (MUSIC), a temporary epidural ultrasound neural interface placed during standard decompression surgery to enable postoperative brightness-mode imaging, Doppler-derived hemodynamic monitoring, and future device-integrated ultrasound actuation. Across simulations, benchtop, human cadaveric, and porcine studies, MUSIC enabled on-demand visualization of cord structure, hematoma tracking, detection and longitudinal tracking of localized Doppler flow signatures attributable to the sulcal artery region, and, in healthy pigs, proof-of-concept focused ultrasound modulation of blood-flow velocity. MUSIC establishes a temporary postoperative acoustic interface that provides spinal cord information to inform monitoring, future management, and localized intervention strategies after SCI.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg3486.title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer’s disease
10.1126/sciadv.aeg3486.abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. Common transcriptional changes in mitochondrial and ribosomal genes are observed in all different cell types. In addition, hibernation triggers an inflammatory-like response in microglia that in part resembles cell states observed in Alzheimer’s disease, but here in the absence of Aβ-accumulation and neurodegeneration. These findings reveal brain transformations that might help preserve vital functions under extreme conditions and they suggest that early cellular changes in AD may be a natural adaptive process.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg4687.title: Genetic dissection of cell type-specific congenital heart disease variants reveals ETS1 control of vascular smooth muscle cell fate
10.1126/sciadv.aeg4687.abstract: Numerous congenital heart disease (CHD) risk variants lie in cis-regulatory elements, yet the impact of variants in repressed and bivalent chromatin on cell type-specific heart development is unclear. Here, we generated a single-cell multiomic atlas of human cardiac differentiation by jointly profiling H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K4me3, and transcriptomes in individual cells, classifying cis-regulatory elements into six chromatin states, enabling prioritization of 610 CHD-associated noncoding variants enriched in lineage- and state-specific regulatory elements, including repressive and bivalent regions. CRISPR knockin of selected variants perturbed nearby gene expression and impaired cardiac differentiation. Dissection of a Polycomb-marked variant near ETS1 (ETS proto-oncogene 1) revealed local H3K27me3 loss, H3K27ac gain, and ETS1 up-regulation, which redirects differentiation toward second-heart-field progenitors with epithelial characteristics at early stages and, ultimately, highly migratory ETS1 + vascular smooth muscle cells. Together, our work establishes a single-cell chromatin-state framework for interpreting noncoding CHD risk variants and uncovers an ETS1-driven program linking Polycomb-deregulated noncoding variation to aberrant vascular smooth muscle fate commitment during human cardiogenesis.
authors: Xin Li, Mingzhu Fu, Shengtao Jia, Zhenwei Wu, Long Pang, Ke Xiong, Yujun Wang, Wen Li, Aibin He, Shanshan Ai

10.1126/sciadv.aeg4834.title: Unveiling the underlying spin mechanism in quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing
10.1126/sciadv.aeg4834.abstract: Spin-polarized lasers hold great potential in integrated photonic devices for secure communication, optical interconnections, and advanced optical devices, offering excellent properties superior to those of conventional lasers. Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites are promising candidates for spin-polarized lasers, because their potential structural inversion asymmetry will result in strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) facilitating spin injection and hence spin splitting of electronic bands. However, strong SOC involves a trade-off between spin injection and spin lifetimes. How to prolong spin lifetimes in the lasing regime while maintaining the optical gain make it challenging to sustain spin polarization for lasing. Here, we unveil the underlying spin mechanism and successfully realize quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing by suppressing fast spin relaxation through triplet exciton regulation using organic cations of phenylethylammonium (PEA) and 1-naphthylmethylamine (NMA). We identify the Bir-Aronov-Pikus (BAP) mechanism is the dominant spin relaxation mechanism preventing the achievement of spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites. By modulating the reverse intersystem crossing of triplet excitons, the D’yakonov-Perel’ (DP) mechanism becomes to play a key role and results in a new-emerged prolonged spin lifetime of 35.4 ps at 77 K, which is ∼5 times that of the BAP-induced one. Consequently, spin-polarized lasing is realized below 200 K, and the threshold is 30.2% lower than that for linearly polarized excitation. This work underscores the potential of PEA-based quasi-2D perovskites in spin-polarized lasing and contributes to the rapid advancements in perovskite spintronic devices.
authors: Qian Li, Zhiping Hu, Hongzhi Zhou, Zhengzheng Liu, Sihao Huang, Hao Wang, Zijun Zhan, Baihui Nie, Zeyu Zhang, Jiajun Luo, Yuxin Leng, Juan Du

10.1126/sciadv.aeg5744.title: Self-charged toothbrush facilitates tooth healthcare maintenance
10.1126/sciadv.aeg5744.abstract: Toothbrushes have undergone no substantive improvements beyond their mechanical function for about 1118 years to date. Conventional toothbrushes often fail to establish an antibacterial environment on the tooth surface, allowing bacteria to recover and recolonize. Here, we developed an innovative self-charged toothbrush that integrates daily tooth brushing with piezoelectric functionality, synergizing both optimal mechanical properties and stable electrical activity. The self-charged toothbrushes can generate reactive oxygen species to disrupt bacterial membrane integrity and diminish bacterial adhesion by combining static antibacterial inhibition through surface potential with dynamic piezoelectric stimulation. Clinical evaluation revealed that the localized piezoelectric stimulation of self-charged toothbrushes can mitigate plaque formation and gingival inflammation. Mechanistic studies further revealed that the self-charged toothbrushes induced oxidative damage to the oral pathogenic bacterial membranes, thereby impairing the ATP-binding cassette transporter pathway. Hence, this study developed a concept of piezoelectric PVDF toothbrushes that combine physical cleaning with sustained antibacterial effect, thus highlighting the potential of self-charged materials in advancing oral healthcare.
authors: Yanhui Lu, Jia Song, Xiaopei Chi, Wenjing Li, Liping Wu, Yusi Guo, Qun Cui, Xiaona Zheng, Yunyang Bai, Boon Chin Heng, Xiaoyu Han, Xuehui Zhang, Xuliang Deng

10.1126/sciadv.aeg6518.title: Thermalization of quantum light induced by classical nonlinear wave dynamics
10.1126/sciadv.aeg6518.abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum systems is an intriguing phenomenon at the forefront of contemporary physics. In this work, we demonstrate that nonlinear multimode optical platforms can be harnessed to induce effective quantum interactions between photons. Through numerical experiments, we reveal the thermalization of quantum light, specifically single- and two-photon states, propagating alongside classical light within multimode nonlinear optical systems. This thermalization is clearly manifested by the emergence of Rayleigh-Jeans and Boltzmann statistical distributions. Beyond providing a deeper understanding of how classical nonlinearities can be used to investigate quantum many-body dynamics, our findings enable the exploration of a broader range of complex quantum phenomena, including aspects of quantum phase transitions, within readily accessible classical optical settings.
authors: Fouad Chahrour, Şahin K. Özdemir, Kurt Busch, Ramy El-Ganainy, Armando Perez-Leija

10.1126/sciadv.aeg8317.title: N6-methyladenosine-dependent ARv7 translation couples lactate metabolism with enzalutamide resistance in prostate cancer
10.1126/sciadv.aeg8317.abstract: Enzalutamide (Enz)-resistant prostate cancer (PCa) is a lethal disease that affects a broad population of elderly men. Experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that androgen receptor variant 7 (ARv7) plays a critical role in Enz-resistant (EnzR) PCa by functioning as a constitutively active transcription factor driving disease progression. However, the predictive value of the ARv7 transcript has not been fully recognized due to its low frequency in castration-resistant PCa. In this study, we identified ARv7 mRNA as an N 6-methyladenosine (m 6 A)-modified transcript. Enz treatment increases METTL3-dependent m 6 A methylation of ARv7 mRNA at the A1177 site, which is subsequently recognized by the reader protein YTHDC2, leading to enhanced translation efficiency of ARv7. Furthermore, EnzR PCa exhibited elevated lactate metabolism, which regulated AR transcription through promoter-mediated epigenetic modifications at H3K9 and H3K14. Reactivated AR exhibited enhanced phase separation to transcriptionally up-regulate YTHDC2 expression. In vivo experiments demonstrated that targeting the METTL3-YTHDC2-ARv7 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to suppress EnzR PCa progression. Moreover, the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 synergized with Enz to inhibit tumor growth without observable toxicity. Collectively, our findings suggest that the clinical utility of ARv7 may need to be reconsidered in light of its m 6 A-dependent translational regulation.
authors: Meng Zhang, Bo Cheng, Man Jia, Xiang Li, Yingying Huang, Boyang Li, Xulin Wang, Jiawei Shao, Qinyue Deng, Wenjun Yu, Mingyu Li, Zhao Yang, Chaozhao Liang, Tian Li, Rongyang Dai, Ronghao Wang

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3280.title: Toxic mercury, aquatic ecosystem collapse, and the ancient Lowland Maya
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3280.abstract: Environmental impacts endured by the Lowland Maya during the Classic Period (250 to 920 CE) included droughts, deforestation, and soil erosion. Recent studies on mercury (Hg) pollution and cyanotoxins suggest that degraded water quality was also a stressor for the Pre-Columbian Maya. Hg in the Maya region is related to use of both elemental mercury and mineral cinnabar (HgS), the latter used as a red pigment. Questions, however, remain concerning the toxicity of Hg or the consequences of prehistoric Hg exposure on ecosystem and human health. Here, we show that Classic Period Hg concentrations in sediment cores from two lakes on the Yucatán Peninsula exceeded modern sediment Hg toxicity thresholds by orders of magnitude for centuries during ancient Maya occupation. Sediments also have evidence of aquatic food web collapse (algae, bacteria, cyanobacteria, ostracods, snails, and nonbiting midges), coincident with the time of high Hg concentrations, confirming that Hg toxicity was an additional environmental stressor for Classic Maya populations.
authors: Matthew Neal Waters, Savanna Lee Wooten, Ashley Mark Abrook, Mark Brenner, Jason Hilleary Curtis, Peter Guy Langdon, Roger Manuel Medina-Gonzalez, Savvas Paradeisis-Stathis, Richard Scott Vachula

10.1126/sciadv.aeh5487.title: Independent origin of genomic imprinting in placental fish
10.1126/sciadv.aeh5487.abstract: Genomic imprinting results in biased expression of one parental allele. Such non-Mendelian expression occurs in angiosperms and placental mammals, which share having an active paternal genome during maternal offspring provisioning. It is hypothesized that imprinting modulates conflict between maternal control of resource allocation and paternal control of resource acquisition. If true, then imprinting should evolve in any organism that evolves a placenta. Here, we demonstrate genomic imprinting in a placental poeciliid fish, Poeciliopsis prolifica . Using transcriptomes from reciprocal crosses between two inbred strains, we identified 84 protein-coding genes with robust evidence of imprinting in P. prolifica placenta. These include the teleost ortholog of mammalian imprinted gene, grb10 , and a pair of adjacent genes, dpp4 and gcga , with opposing effects on glucose metabolism that are oppositely imprinted in a fashion that potentially resolves parental conflict. Significantly elevated allelic DNA methylation on the promoters of two focal imprinted genes suggests epigenetic mechanisms of imprinting similar to those in mammals. We also discovered the convergent recruitment of a gene network associated with nutrient transport in mammals. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of genomic imprinting in a non-mammalian vertebrate and supports the potential role of imprinting in resolving parental conflict.
authors: Ying Zhang, Polly Campbell, Alec Kingsley, Yuridia Reynoso, Yuan Kang, Chen-Che Jeff Huang, John H. Werren, David Reznick, Xu Wang

10.1126/sciadv.aeh7786.title: Cytoplasmic crowding drives intracellular viscoelastic increase during epithelial maturation
10.1126/sciadv.aeh7786.abstract: The cytoplasm is a crowded, active medium whose mechanical properties underpin essential cellular functions, yet how intracellular rheology adapts during tissue maturation remains unclear. Here, we examine the evolution of cytoplasmic viscoelasticity in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial monolayers as cell density increases. Using magnetic rotational spectroscopy, an active microrheology technique, we quantify zero-shear viscosity and elastic modulus throughout monolayer maturation. We uncover a substantial enhancement of intracellular viscoelasticity correlated with increasing cell density and a concomitant rise in cellular dry mass concentration. Hyperosmotic perturbations on subconfluent monolayers reproduce this effect, confirming cytoplasmic crowding as a driver of rheological changes. Notably, intracellular viscoelasticity scales linearly with dry mass concentration, suggesting a direct coupling between internal mechanics and cytoplasmic concentration during epithelial maturation. These findings establish a link between tissue-level organization and intracellular mechanics, highlighting cytoplasmic crowding as a regulator of epithelial homeostasis and providing a framework to connect rheology with tissue behavior.
authors: Gregory Arkowitz, Olivier Destrian, Anis Aggoun, Marc-Antoine Fardin, Pascal Berto, Gilles Tessier, René-Marc Mège, Jean-François Berret, Benoit Ladoux

10.1126/sciadv.aei0181.title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8+ T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases
10.1126/sciadv.aei0181.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)-high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-I high contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8 + T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8 + T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor- and chimeric antigen receptor-based immunotherapies in IFN-I high tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-I high / IFNAR1 low axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.
