10.1002/adma.75504.title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu-Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C-C Coupling for Selective CO2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
10.1002/adma.75504.abstract: ABSTRACT The abundant Cu 0 /Cu δ+ interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C-C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO x . The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO 2 reduction to ethylene at −1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm −2 in a flow cell. In-situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cu δ+ (0<δ<1) sites at multimetallic interfaces is effectively regulated by other metals, inducing electronic heterogeneity and an asymmetric charge distribution on the Cu sites that facilitates asymmetric *CO-*CHO coupling. This work establishes the design principles for Cu-based multimetallic alloy with atomic-level customisation, demonstrating that the precise structural design and electronic structure of Cu δ+ sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.
authors: Yupeng Li, Xinrui Liu, Shu Liu, Haiping Li, Xiuling Jiao, Yuguo Xia, Dairong Chen

10.1002/adma.75482.title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low-Cost Solar Fuels
10.1002/adma.75482.abstract: ABSTRACT Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field-scale NP typically operates at sub-percent solar-to-biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double-digit solar-to-fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar-to-chemical conversion.

10.1002/adma.75495.title: Anti-Poisoning Tin Single-Atom Unlocks High-Activity Ruthenium Catalysts for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
10.1002/adma.75495.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) is constrained by the lack of efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), primarily due tothe sluggishVolmer step and inefficient intermediate desorption. While Ru-based catalysts exhibit promising *H binding energy, their practical performance is compromised by poor water dissociation kinetics and susceptibility to active-site blockage by adsorbed species. Herein, we report a Sn-doped RuO 2 @Ru catalyst supported on carbon black, wherein atomically dispersed Sn modulates the electronic structure of RuO 2 via Sn─O bonds, simultaneously facilitating water dissociation, optimizing *H adsorption, and preventing *OH poisoning. The catalyst achieves exceptional performance with an overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , positioning it among the most active HER catalysts reported to date. When integrated into a full AEMWE, it operates at 1.85 V and 1000 mA cm −2 with stability exceeding 300 h. Mechanistic studies suggest that Sn doping fine-tunes the *OH and *H binding energies, addressing the kinetic imbalance inherent in conventional Ru catalysts. This work highlights the effectiveness of atomic-level electronic engineering via an anti-poisoning strategy for designing efficient, stable alkaline HER electrocatalysts toward industrial hydrogen production.
authors: Yiqing Sun, Fangkun Fan, Liang Wu, Yapeng Li, Tao Gan, Lingyou Zeng, Chunhui Xiao, Dingsheng Wang, Shujiang Ding, Shenghua Chen

10.1002/adma.75489.title: Engineering Thermoelectric-Electrocatalytic Coupling in RuO 2 /PrCoO 3 Heterointerface for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
10.1002/adma.75489.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is pivotal for diverse electrochemical energy conversion systems; however, it has so far been plagued by sluggish kinetics and excessive energy consumption. In this study, we proposed an innovative thermoelectric-electrocatalytic coupling strategy to enhance OER efficiency by constructing an Ohmic heterointerface through uniform integration of RuO 2 with thermoelectric oxide (PrCoO 3 ). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the thermoelectric potential generated by PrCoO 3 selectively activates the intrinsically inert (101) facet of RuO 2 by lowering *OOH formation barrier, thereby substantially boosting the overall OER performance. Consequently, the RuO 2 /PrCoO 3 heterointerface delivered exceptional OER performance under a mild temperature gradient (Δ T ) of 175°C, achieving dramatic reduction in overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 from 300 mV (Δ T = 0°C) to 178 mV, 4 300% increase in current density, and negligible potential loss over 1,000 h. When the catalyst was assembled into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the cell driven by spontaneous heating reached a low voltage of 2.18 V at a current density of 2.0 A cm −2 , with stable operation for 600 h. These insights into harnessing thermal gradient via integrated electrocatalytic system are crucial for the recovery of industrial waste heat and its conversion into high-value chemicals.

10.1002/adma.75118.title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration
10.1002/adma.75118.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep-seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug-resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self-propelled Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic-gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3-guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo-responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature-dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail-safe thermal self-destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface-engineered (DSS) 6 peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone-homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo-immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next-generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro-engineering to address complex clinical challenges.
authors: Yang Lan, Xuemin Liu, Zhifeng Shi, Yuanlong Li, Ani Chi, Jiaqian Zheng, Tan Ye, Chuang Xiao, Rui Zheng, Yifan Yang, Xuetao Shi, Xufeng Zhu, Muyuan Chai, Shengtao Yan

10.1002/adma.75512.title: Lewis-Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries
10.1002/adma.75512.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline all-iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low-cost grid-scale energy storage using Earth-abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer-sphere electron-transfer kinetics of Fe-chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)-region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis-basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe-chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide-assisted outer-sphere electron-transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni 3 S 4 -modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm −2 and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm −2 , compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm −2 for the pristine cell. The Ni 3 S 4 -based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm −2 . This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis-basic interface engineering as a strategy for high-power and low-cost long-duration energy storage.
authors: Wendong Yang, Xue Long, Hua Jiang, Shuangbin Zhang, Linfeng Wang, Pei Liu, Zuoxuan Gan, Xuan Cai, Yilin Zeng, Huaiyu Ke, Jiabao Sun, Bin Luo, Jiangjiang Duan

10.1002/adma.75429.title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large-Area Tin-based Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75429.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p-type small molecule, 4,4'-(5,6-bis(2-methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole-4,7-diyl)bis(2,5-difluoro-N,N-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic-angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H- 1 H double-quantum-single-quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning-rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high-quality Sn-based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap-assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG-PEDOT:PSS-based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1-cm 2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04-cm 2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N 2 atmosphere.
authors: Wenqi Zhang, Tianpeng Li, Xiaozhen Huang, Duanfei Zhang, Zuoming Jin, Peilin Wang, Junyu Nie, Siyuan Lin, Wangqiang Cao, Yi Wang, Yang Wang, Zhi Li, Yao Fu, Mingwei An, Jia Liang

10.1002/adma.75517.title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard-Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion-Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
10.1002/adma.75517.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard-carbon anode design lacks a precursor-level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed-pore formation. Here we establish a precursor-level cohesion-solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene-fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke-like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard-carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect-engineered carbon galleries. The solvent-selected AHC-80-1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide-temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10-kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC-80-1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg −1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle-to-gate life-cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC-80-1400 production reduces climate-change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor-stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.
authors: Yuhan Liu, Hao Yang, Qianxun Li, Zhenghe Xu, Chao Yang

10.1002/adma.75487.title: Stabilizing Ru Sites via Lattice Oxygen Locking of Nb-Ru/RuO2 to Break the Activity-Stability Trade-Off for Acidic Oxygen Evolution
10.1002/adma.75487.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly active and stable Ru-based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru-based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb-doped Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site-Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen-intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb-Ru/RuO 2 delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm −2 with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm −2 . This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low-cost PEMWE hydrogen production.
authors: Xiaodan Wen, Shuanglong Tang, Xia Sheng, Yuqi Yan, Dongyue Xin, Jiannan Du, Yanbin Ning, Chunyu Ru, Guokang Han, Jinli Qiao, Shuaifeng Lou

10.1002/adma.75522.title: A Glycan Key Unlocks Microglia Targeting and Reprogramming to Promote Functional Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury
10.1002/adma.75522.abstract: ABSTRACT Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers uncontrolled neuroinflammation driven by dysfunctional microglia and pro-inflammatory-biased reprogramming, yet precise therapeutic strategies remain limited. Here, we report a novel glycan-targeted nanoparticle system (ICT@APD) designed to enhance the microglia-reprogramming potential of icaritin (ICT) while overcoming its inherent narrow therapeutic window. By functionalizing nanoparticles with 2,5-anhydro-D-mannitol (2,5-AM), a high-affinity ligand for the microglia-specific transporter GLUT5, ICT@APD achieves selective microglial uptake and amplifies the capacity of ICT to reprogram microglia toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. The targeted reprogramming consequently creates a positive microenvironment that promotes axon regeneration, neuronal survival, and synaptic reconstruction, leading to significantly improved locomotor recovery after SCI. Our findings establish a novel glycan-mediated microglial targeting and reprogramming strategy for SCI repair, which may extend to other central nervous system disorders and provide a referenceable platform for the delivery of other therapeutic agents with a narrow therapeutic window.
authors: Ting Liu, Liangchao Du, Wanrong Ma, Ge Long, Dingyang Liu, Xing Li

10.1002/adma.75496.title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal-Organic Network for CO2 Conversion
10.1002/adma.75496.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous-phase synthesis of a woven metal-organic superstructure assembled from Cu 2+ and 2,4,6-trinitrobenzene-1,3,5-triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu 2+ yields charged one-dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two-dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu 2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π-conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox-active Cu 2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu-TNPG network was evaluated for visible-light-driven CO 2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu-TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre-activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H 2 , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.
authors: Shayan Karak, Soubhik Khata, Subhajit Chakraborty, Maitrayee Biswas, Poulami Paul, Biswarup Pathak, Dinesh Shetty, Srabanti Ghosh, Sebastian C. Peter, Rahul Banerjee

10.1002/adma.74365.title: Establishing Atomic Coherence in Twisted Oxide Membranes Containing Volatile Elements
authors: Young-Hoon Kim, Reza Ghanbari, Min-Hyoung Jung, Yang Zhang, Young-Min Kim, Ruijuan Xu, Miaofang Chi

10.1002/adma.75539.title: Threo-Chiral Cation Additive Enables Ordered Lattice Adsorption and Enhanced Operational Stability of Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75539.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral molecular engineering is an effective strategy to modulate crystallization and mitigate nonradiative defects in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, unconstrained bond rotation often leads to spatial mismatch between chiral molecules and the perovskite lattice, hindering effective defect coordination. Herein, we introduce threo-chiral cation additive of (2 S ,3 R )-2-amino-3-hydroxybutanamide hydrochloride (ThrA) to achieve precise perovskite lattice regulation. Benefiting from methyl-induced steric hindrance originating from its dual chiral-center threo-configuration, ThrA acquires a conformationally locked rigid stereostructure and further facilitates thermodynamically-favored parallel-to-lattice multi-site synergistic adsorption via hydrogen bonding and Pb coordination. Such stereoselective “lock-and-key” interaction reduces lattice surface energy, guides preferential (100) crystal growth, and simultaneously suppresses lattice distortion and ion migration. Consequently, the ThrA-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 26.68% (certified 26.31%), while 65 cm 2 large-area module delivers a promising PCE of 22.78% (certified 22.12%), representing one of the outstanding certification efficiencies for perovskite modules of comparable size. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS-D-2) and maintain 92% performance after 2000 h continuous maximum power point tracking (ISOS-L-2). This work demonstrates that the stereostructure of additive is decisive for precise perovskite crystallization modulation, providing advanced stereochemical strategy toward high-efficiency and ultra-stable perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Yilin Gao, Guozhen Liu, Bingying Xu, Yinjuan Zhang, Muge Xu, Ruikun Cao, Zheng Lv, Qingshun Dong, Haiying Zheng, Zhiyong Wang, Guohao Dai, Guanghao Zhou, Lin Yang, Bo Xu, Yifan Huang, Wenming Tian, Jiming Bian, Jijun Qiu, Yantao Shi

10.1002/adma.75493.title: Monolithically 3D-Printed Spectral-Spatial Meta-Authenticators
10.1002/adma.75493.abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurface holography can encode multiple independent images in a single flat element, yet simultaneous operation at several visible wavelengths has typically relied on geometric-phase elements, which require a prescribed circular polarization and bulky polarization optics, and on high-index dielectrics that can suffer from visible-band absorption. Here, we demonstrate a monolithically 3D-printed, low-index, height-coded metasurface that performs polarization-insensitive, broadband holography across spectral (wavelength) and spatial (near- and far-field) channels. The propagation phase accumulated by each resin pillar is set by its height, so a single height map fixes the phase response at every wavelength at once and acts as a multi-wavelength phase library. The symmetric pillar cross-section removes the dependence on input polarization, and the transparent resin keeps the response low-loss across the visible band. A fabrication-aware optimization folds the discrete height levels imposed by two-photon-lithography slicing directly into the loss, so the design is printed as optimized in a single continuous step, without post-optimization rounding. Experimentally, the device reconstructs a far-field image that is read directly as a public key together with wavelength- and distance-selective near-field images that act as locked passwords, realizing a compact, dual-credential optical authentication scheme under unpolarized illumination without polarization optics.
authors: Cherry Park, Shiqi Hu, Youngsun Jeon, Junsuk Rho

10.1002/adma.75456.title: Spin-State Modulation of Octahedral Co Sites for Enhancing Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion
10.1002/adma.75456.abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon-free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber-Bosch process is energy-intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. Herein, we report a metal-organic framework (MOF)-derived Co 3 O 4 electrocatalyst (MD-Co 3 O 4 ) prepared by controlled pyrolysis of Co-MOF-74, which achieved a high Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% and excellent stability for the electrosynthesis of NH 3 from nitrate, along with robust activity over a wide pH and nitrate concentration range. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the oxygen vacancies generated during MOF pyrolysis induce coordination distortion of octahedral Co sites, leading to a high-spin state transition with an electron-rich configuration that synergistically enhances nitrate adsorption and interfacial electron transfer, thereby boosting the intrinsic activity. Moreover, this MOF-based strategy is applicable to other M 1 Co 2 O 4 spinels, which provides an effective approach for spin engineering at the atomic scale and sustainable ammonia synthesis.
authors: Jiawei Kang, Wenyu Yang, Chunyang Pu, Runan Xiang, Haixin Sun, Qinghua Liu, Yanglong Hou, Guangqin Li

10.1002/adma.75516.title: Heterointerfacial Bonding Governs Service Stability in Flexible Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75516.abstract: ABSTRACT The service stability of flexible perovskite solar module (FPSM) is contingent upon the bonding strength and stress-response behavior at heterointerfaces. However, the fullerene-based layer mainly relies on weak non-covalent interactions. This makes it difficult for the FPSM to tackle the challenges posed by the coupling of multiple stresses in the actual service environment. Through the blending strategy of the polyamide curing agent and fullerene derivatives, we constructed an active energy-dissipating multi-bond network featuring covalent bond anchoring and hydrogen bond dissipation, which significantly enhanced the interfacial bonding and energy dissipation capabilities. Based on this strategy, a 100 cm 2 FPSM achieves a recorded power conversion efficiency of 22.33% (certified 21.5%). More importantly, for the first time, we developed an in situ bending electroluminescence experiment for FPSM under ultraviolet irradiation. After 5000 consecutive bending cycles, there was no significant decline in the module's performance, which verified its service stability under multi-field coupling.
authors: Junliang Li, Zhaoyang Chu, Yihuan Xie, Baojin Fan, Yaling Luo, Jiaju Gao, Yongkang Wang, Zongyi Gu, Zhi Xing, Xiangchuan Meng, Xiaotian Hu, Yiwang Chen

10.1002/adma.75526.title: Activation-Free and Strain-Resilient Island-Bridge Liquid Metal Inks for Machine-Learning-Enabled Epidermal Electromyography
10.1002/adma.75526.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid metal particle-based inks offer a scalable route toward stretchable electronics, yet their practical implementation is hindered by activation-dependent conductivity and poor electrical stability under deformation. Herein, we report an intrinsically conductive and strain-resilient liquid metal ink with a rationally engineered island-bridge micro-architecture, in which Cu-decorated carbon nanotubes (CuCNTs) bridge adjacent liquid metal particles (LMPs) through initial hydrogen-bonding/coordination-assisted attachment to the native gallium-oxide shell, followed by local Cu-Ga alloying at the CuCNTs/LMPs interface. Enabled by solvent-mediated dispersion and interfacial hybridization, the strain-resilient composite ink supports high-resolution (100 µm) screen printing and deformable circuit integration. The dynamically reconfigurable island-bridge network retains a sheet resistance of 1.3 × 10 −1 Ω sq −1 at 300% strain, together with stable resistance during prolonged cyclic stretching and bending. When printed into a compact 12-channel array on breathable fibrous substrates, the resulting electrode array exhibits low skin-electrode impedance and superior high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) performance compared with commercial gel electrodes. Combined with machine-learning-assisted analysis, the electromyography arrays enable training-state recognition, individualized load assessment, and continuous monitoring of fatigue-associated exercise states during dynamic exercise. This work provides a scalable strategy for intrinsically conductive liquid metal electronics and advances their application in intelligent wearable biointerfaces and soft electronic systems.
authors: Yidong Peng, Yanqing Gu, Haoxuan Zhu, Lingqi Liu, Haoran Liu, Haitao Huang, Biao Zhou, Jiancheng Dong, Yunpeng Huang

10.1002/adma.75499.title: Adaptive Supramolecular Interactions Govern Redox-Active Molecules in Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries
10.1002/adma.75499.abstract: ABSTRACT Weak noncovalent interactions critically govern molecular behavior in solution, yet how they shape redox processes in aqueous electrochemical environments remains underexplored. Here, we demonstrate control over the solubility and redox stability of aromatic redox-active molecules in aqueous redox flow batteries (RFBs). Zwitterionic substitution of naphthalene diimide (NDI) bearing quaternary ammonium and sulfonate groups shows weak π-π cohesion through steric and electrostatic effects, rendering otherwise insoluble NDIs responsive to external anions. Hydrophobic and weakly hydrated anions such as iodide and bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide disrupt residual stacking through anion-π interactions, enabling dissolution to concentrations approaching 1.3 M. Upon electrochemical reduction, these anions dissociate, and the reduced NDI species are instead stabilized through spin pairing and cation-mediated intermolecular interactions, which suppress irreversible aggregation, slow self-discharge, and enable rapid redox reactions. Operando Raman spectroscopy, 1 H NMR, and EPR elucidate the redox-state-dependent evolution of these supramolecular assemblies. Together, these results establish zwitterionic molecular design for adaptive supramolecular redox chemistry in aqueous RFBs.

10.1002/adma.75515.title: Time-Encoded Ligand Presentation via a Magnetically Actuated Hydrogel Mitigates T Cell Exhaustion
10.1002/adma.75515.abstract: ABSTRACT Adoptive T cell therapy (ACT) requires ex vivo expansion of tumor-reactive CD8 + T cells, yet prolonged antigenic stimulation frequently induces exhaustion, limiting persistence and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we present a magnetically actuated, extracellular matrix-mimetic hydrogel that enables reversible control of T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation timing. By embedding αCD3ε/αCD28-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles within a soft hyaluronic acid matrix, external magnetic fields dynamically expose or conceal stimulatory ligands, allowing programmable alternation between activation and rest. Continuous ligand presentation sustains TCR signaling and drives inhibitory receptor expression and functional exhaustion. In contrast, alternating activation-rest cycles periodically attenuate proximal TCR signaling, reduce exhaustion-associated marker expression, and bias differentiation toward central memory-like states while preserving cytokine production and recall capacity. T cells expanded under intermittent stimulation exhibit enhanced antigen-specific cytotoxicity, reduced dependence on PD-1 blockade, and superior tumor control in vivo, together with increased CD8 + T cell abundance across analyzed tissues. These results identify temporal control of mechanochemical signaling as a materials-encoded regulator of T cell fate and provide a non-genetic strategy for generating functionally competent T cell products with reduced exhaustion-associated dysfunction and improved antitumor activity.
authors: Xuemei Wang, Runyao Wang, Guangli Xiang, Xueyou Zhang, Luyang Wang, Wai Ki Wong, Yingrui Deng, Yongkang Yang, Jiwon Oh, Xian Xie, Zhinan Yang, Nathanael Chun Him Lai, Bohan Yin, Kunyu Zhang, Liming Bian, Siu Hong Dexter Wong

10.1002/adma.75497.title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali-Ion Batteries Through Two-Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering
10.1002/adma.75497.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon-based anode materials offer compelling advantages for rechargeable ion batteries, and particularly fullerene C 60 has a higher theoretical capacity of 446 mAh g −1 than the traditional graphite anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, its zero-dimensional cage structure tends to spontaneously aggregate, and its alkali-metal intercalated intermediate (fulleride) facilely dissolves in organic electrolytes, severely limiting its practical anode capacity and deteriorating recyclability. Herein, for the first time, we apply metal-free two-dimensional C 60 covalent network (2D-C 60 ) with distinct bonding patterns, including tetragonal phase (TP-2D-C 60 ) and hexagonal phase (HP-2D-C 60 ) nanosheets, as novel anode materials for LIBs, achieving high anode capacity, breaking the theoretical limit of C 60 molecule. TP-2D-C 60 delivers a specific capacity of 522.0 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , outperforming HP-2D-C 60 (408.6 mAh g −1 ) and pristine C 60 (3.4 mAh g −1 ). This phenomenon is rationalized by DFT calculations, revealing that TP-2D-C 60 exhibits a higher density of Li-ion binding sites and a lower Li-ion migration barrier than HP-2D-C 60 . To assess its universality across ion-battery chemistries, we further demonstrate the application of TP-2D-C 60 as an anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), achieving a high discharge capacity of 309.9 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 .
authors: Rongyao Lv, Jialong Shen, Xuan Wu, Zhihao Chen, Yalin Lu, Wenhua Zhang, Yan Yu, Shangfeng Yang

10.1002/adma.75465.title: A Synergistic Hydrogel Strategy for the Treatment of Candida Vaginitis Through Pathogen Clearance and Microecosystem Restoration
10.1002/adma.75465.abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for Candida vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment-degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@Lab PC , which self-assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular-weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection-dysbiosis-recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.
authors: Dong Yang, Limeng Zhu, Jiayuan Chen, Huike Zhao, Yongping Chen, Shuang Pan, Na Li, Dazhi Chen

10.1002/adma.75491.title: Magnetically-Gated Haptic Locomotion Display Enabled by Motion-Coupled Light Emission
10.1002/adma.75491.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic actuation is a powerful strategy in robotics for tactile feedback, navigation, and biomedical applications and can be extended to interactive displays by coupling mechanical motion with optical emission. Here, we present a magnetically-gated haptic locomotion display (MHLD) that integrates a flexible alternating-current (AC)-driven quantum-dot light-emitting diode (QLED) with a magnetoresponsive elastomeric soft actuator. Under external magnetic fields, the soft actuator deforms and modulates its contact with the AC display, triggering electroluminescence (EL) whose emission area and intensity are directly coupled to mechanical displacement. A maximum luminance of 396 cd m - 2 was achieved, with emission area and intensity varying with deformation. The device maintains stable output under repeated actuation, with directional motion programmable via magnetization profiles. Demonstrations include a 3 × 3 haptic feedback array visualizing pixel displacement and a maze-navigating locomotive display with path-dependent emission. Finite element simulations support the contact-mediated formation of the vertical electric field underlying motion-coupled light emission.
authors: Jioh Yoo, Jihye Jang, Wei Jiang, Woojoong Kim, Jong Woong Park, Seonju Lee, Kyuho Lee, Cheolmin Park

10.1002/adma.75078.title: Record-High Capacitive Energy Density in Polyimide Dielectrics at 300°C via Conformational-Vibrational Engineering
10.1002/adma.75078.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer dielectrics are crucial for capacitors in various applications, including electric vehicles, geothermal instrumentation, and aerospace systems. However, polymers tend to exhibit strongly nonlinear conduction at high temperatures and under high electric fields, leading to a rapid increase in leakage current and typically limiting the stable operating temperature to around 250°C. Here, we report a coupled conformational and vibrational engineering strategy in polyimide (PI) dielectrics that weakens electronic coupling and suppresses specific molecular vibrations governing thermally assisted charge transport. This dual-action design effectively delays the onset of high-field nonlinear conduction and suppresses leakage current at extreme temperatures. Consequently, the resulting PI dielectric films achieve a maximum discharged energy density of 5.9 J cm −3 at 300°C and maintain 2.8 J cm −3 with 90% efficiency, while sustaining over 10 5 charge-discharge cycles at 300°C, surpassing state-of-the-art polymer dielectrics in operating temperature and cycling reliability. This strategy provides a fundamentally different route from conventional bandgap engineering approaches for high energy density polymer dielectrics operating at 300°C.
authors: Guanghu He, Wenhan Xu, Jiajun Peng, Hang Luo, Zhifang Zhou, Xiaona Li, Yuting Wan, Dou Zhang

10.1002/adma.74949.title: Laser-Printing of Dynamic Colorful-Patterns Activated by Pure-Water
10.1002/adma.74949.abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional printing technologies rely heavily on chemical dyes and organic reagents, posing significant environmental risks and resource sustainability challenges. Although bio-inspired structural colors offer a promising alternative, efficiently and conveniently achieving high-resolution, reversible, and eco-friendly patterning of dynamic optical content remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a scalable and sustainable color-printing strategy that employs pure water to activate dynamic patterns within laser-programmed cholesteric liquid crystal networks (CLCNs). By leveraging laser direct-writing technology, a highly temporal-spatial resolution complex optical information with a highly customizable printing ecosystem has been constructed. This strategy relies on adjusting the spatial distribution anisotropy of internal cross-link density to program the swelling behavior of the helical-structures, which generating structural-color can cover across the full visible spectrum. We demonstrate the versatility of this high-throughput fabrication platform through multidimensional information encryption, self-adaptive QR codes, and smart architectural coatings. The presented new printing ecosystem, due to its characteristics such as easily accessible raw materials, simple process, high economic applicability, and environmental friendliness, is bound to have a broader development space and will not be confined to laboratory manufacturing.
authors: Jiale Liu, Jianying Zhang, Xinzhao Xia, Bo Yang, Yunxiao Ren, Jiajun Chen, Jiaxing Zhang, Tao Dong, Yinuo Yu, Wenting Xie, Wei Hu, Huai Yang

10.1002/adma.74946.title: Versatile Sb2S3 Interlayer for Back-Interface Carrier Management in Narrow-Bandgap Sb2(Sx,Se1−x)3 Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.74946.abstract: ABSTRACT Severe carrier recombination at the back interface, exacerbated by valence-band misalignment arising from the tunable S/Se composition in Sb 2 (S x ,Se 1−x ) 3 (0 ≤ x < 1) absorbers, remains a critical bottleneck in these solar cells. Here, we address this issue by inserting an Sb 2 S 3 interlayer between the narrow-bandgap Sb 2 (S x ,Se 1−x ) 3 absorber and the PbS hole transport layer (HTL). KPFM and GIWAXS measurements reveal that this Sb 2 S 3 interlayer reduces surface defect density and improves the crystalline quality of the film surface. Moreover, leveraging the complete mutual solubility between Sb 2 S 3 and Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 , TOF-SIMS confirms the formation of a compositionally graded heterojunction from the Se-rich bulk to the S-rich back surface during annealing, creating a continuous energy staircase. Consequently, the hole-extraction barrier is eliminated, the built-in electric field is enhanced, and the depletion region is broadened, accelerating hole collection. This strategy delivers the following performance: for Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 -derived devices, efficiency increases from 6.88% to 9.76%; when extended to the Sb 2 Se 3 -derived case, efficiency rises from 7.77% to 10.03%. These results set new benchmarks for all-inorganic Sb 2 (S x ,Se 1−x ) 3 thin-film solar cells, especially for carbon-electrode devices, and establish a back-interface engineering strategy for Sb 2 (S x ,Se 1−x ) 3 solar cells.
authors: Lingjie Liu, Juncai Zhang, Hu Li, Jinrui Cai, Limei Lin, Shuiyuan Chen, Guilin Chen

10.1002/adma.74867.title: Synergistic Catalysis of Single-Atom Alloys and Ordered Indium Clusters in Aluminum Sheet for Enhanced Hydrogen Production
10.1002/adma.74867.abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrolysis of aluminum (Al) in pure water is regarded as a greatly promising strategy for on-demand hydrogen supply due to the high energy density of Al and the operational simplicity of the process. However, its precise reaction mechanism remains poorly understood. Here, we report an efficient smelting method to fabricate AlGaIn alloy sheet and elucidate the atomic-scale reaction pathways of the hydrolysis process. Spherical aberration correction electron microscopy, X-ray absorption fine structure, and in situ scanning electron microscopy reveal that AlGaIn alloy sheet shows a typical layered structure with rich grain boundaries and is composed of a uniform reactive surface AlGa film, AlGa 1 single-atom alloys, and highly ordered In atom clusters. An optimized AlGaIn alloy sheet demonstrates excellent hydrolysis performance at room temperature when directly immersed in pure water without prior pulverization. Ambient-pressure x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the hydrolysis reaction is initiated at the active sites on the reactive AlGa film and is further accelerated by a cooperative catalytic effect of AlGa 1 single-atom alloys and highly ordered In atom clusters. In particular, In clusters mainly facilitate water dissociation, while AlGa 1 single-atom alloys are responsible for enhancing *H combination and Al spillover.
authors: Xiaoxuan Wang, Xiaodong Li, Lixiang Zhu, Jin Wang, Shuo Wang, Xueqiang Zhang, Tinglu Song, Fenghao Yang, Zhengxu Cai, Shubo Tian, Youqi Zhu, Meishuai Zou

10.1002/adma.74787.title: Fast Hydrogel Micro-Actuators Driven by Electric Fields
10.1002/adma.74787.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrically-driven hydrogels are crosslinked, charged polymer networks that can deform in an electric field, prompted by osmotic pressure changes. To date, such actuators generally suffer from sluggish response time, with equilibrium actuation times ranging from minutes to hours in aqueous electrolytes, and lack sophisticated design, due to established manufacturing protocols. Herein, these limitations are overcome through the fabrication of polyelectrolyte hydrogel microstructures via two-photon polymerization (2PP). This approach allows for the realization of microscale electrically-driven actuators exhibiting fast actuation (∼200 ms equilibrium time). The work highlights three photoresist formulations for poly(anionic) and poly(cationic) hydrogel networks and their fabrication via 2PP to produce micro-electro-actuators with sub-micron features. The electrically-driven actuation performance is investigated by varying the hydrogel composition, actuator geometry, along with electric field strength and direction, and local environment (pH and electrolyte concentration) during actuation. It was determined that micro-cantilevers of 80 × 20 × 10 µm 3 reached equilibrium bending of up to 44.9 ± 7.8°, in ∼ 200 ms, in response to electric fields of 6 V mm −1 . This pioneering work marks the first integration of 2PP with electrically actuated gelatin-based hydrogels, showcasing micro-electro-actuators with rapid and programmable 4D motion.
authors: Annaël Sort-Montenegro, Jason M. Delente, Žiga Roblek, Yekaterina Tskhe, Luke Dowling, Colm Delaney, Larisa Florea

10.1002/adma.74936.title: Ultramicropore-Matched Molecular Transport in Low-Loading Mixed-Matrix Membranes via Trace-Oxygen-Mediated Thermal Reorganization
10.1002/adma.74936.abstract: ABSTRACT The complementary structural tunability of polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIMs) and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) redefines the design space for engineering precise transport channels in mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). Herein, we present that trace-oxygen-mediated thermal reorganization (TOTR) of PIM-1 micropores enables MOF-dominated gas transport in MMMs without requiring high filler loading. Spectroscopic analyses and molecular simulations reveal trace-oxygen-mediated radical processes that induce the PIM-1 backbone rearrangement, together with triazine crosslinking and partial π-conjugation extension, resulting in a contracted and homogenized ultramicropore distribution. Meanwhile, the dual-interface design establishes a covalently coupled MOF-polymer interface, where the interfacial carboxylated PIM-1 (cPIM-1) layer co-reorganizes with the polymer matrix to form an integrated microporous environment with suppressed defects and enhanced mechanical robustness. This coupled pore-and-interface regulation integrates PIM-1 ultramicropores and MOF micropores into pore-matched transport channels, enabling effective expression of MOF sieving capability at an ultralow filler loading of 2 wt.%. The resulting MMMs deliver approximately threefold enhancement in CO 2 /CH 4 and CO 2 /N 2 selectivity compared with PIM-1 membranes, while maintaining high CO 2 permeability and improved resistance to physical aging and plasticization. This study may broaden the design concepts for advanced MMMs toward challenging molecular separations.
authors: Lei Wang, Jingxian Hua, Yizheng Tao, Jing Huang, Benxin Li, Yurong Luo, Yawei Gu, Lixiong Zhang, Weihong Xing, Yichang Pan

10.1002/adma.74790.title: Lattice Strain and Built-In Field Synergistically Boost Urea Oxidation via Dynamic NiOOH Mediation at Multiphase Heterointerfaces
10.1002/adma.74790.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of nickel-based heterojunction electrocatalysts for the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) is impeded by insufficient active sites and sluggish multi-step reaction kinetics. Herein, a sulfur-doped lignin-derived carbon encapsulated Ni-NiO-MoO 2 micro-nano array (Ni-NiO-MoO 2 @SC) is fabricated to tackle these issues. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that the multiphase heterointerfaces spontaneously generate a built-in electric field due to the distinct work function and electronic structure of each component, and simultaneously induce lattice strain, which synergistically optimizes the electronic structure and accelerates the dynamic formation of active NiOOH species. In-situ electrochemical characterizations and density functional theory calculations further confirm that the engineered interface promotes urea adsorption, facilitates N─N coupling and C─N bond cleavage, expedites *COOH intermediate desorption, and avoids excessive accumulation of NiOOH. Consequently, Ni-NiO-MoO 2 @SC delivers superior UOR activity with low potentials of 1.34/1.40 V at 10/500 mA cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, the sulfur-doped carbon encapsulation and micro-nano array architecture endow the catalyst with excellent corrosion resistance and mass transport capability, realizing long-term stability (500 mA cm −2 at 1.53 V for 500 h) in membrane electrode assemblies. This work provides a versatile interface engineering and encapsulation strategy for high-performance nickel-based electrocatalysts toward urea electrolysis and beyond.

10.1002/adma.74815.title: Bioengineered Interfaces for Peripheral Nerve Sensory Restoration
10.1002/adma.74815.abstract: ABSTRACT Peripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) severely impair motor and sensory function, diminishing patient independence and quality of life. Despite decades of research, rehabilitation has prioritized motor recovery and residual function over the sensory restoration essential for embodiment, intuitive control, and natural movement. This lack of feedback drives poor prosthetic integration, high cognitive demand, and high abandonment rates. This review organizes the field along the translational pathway from injury to functional recovery: the biology of what is lost, strategies that restore the native substrate, the interfaces required when it cannot be rebuilt, and how these strategies are integrated and embodied. Approaches are compared by biological target, sensory function restored, invasiveness, clinical maturity, and limitation, emphasizing how interface properties such as modulus mismatch, charge injection capacity, and foreign body response govern long-term stability and naturalness. Proprioception, the hardest and least measurable sensation to restore, is examined in depth, as are biomimetic, neuromorphic, biohybrid, and machine-learning approaches toward adaptive, closed-loop communication, weighed against their limits to adoption. The review closes with design principles and the challenges they face, from power and scalability to regulatory and ethical hurdles. The future lies in patient-centered interfaces that let individuals not only move, but feel again.
authors: Sydney Swedick, Salim El Hadwe, Kesi Liang, George G. Malliaras, Damiano G. Barone

10.1002/adma.74940.title: Tailoring the d-Band Center via Multi-Metal-Phosphorus d-p Orbital Hybridization in a High-Entropy Metal Phosphide to Enable Accelerated Sulfur Redox Kinetics
10.1002/adma.74940.abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish lithium polysulfide (LiPS) reduction kinetics and the shuttle effect lead to low active mass utilization and poor cycling stability, thereby seriously hampering the commercial application of Li-S batteries. Herein, a theoretically guided high-entropy phosphide (Fe 0.74 Co 0.64 Ni 0.61 Cu 0.32 Mo 0.24 P, FCNCMP-HEMP) nanoparticle is designed to enhance LiPS conversion. The electronic interaction among the S 3 p orbitals of S x 2- in LiPSs, the metal d orbitals, and the P 3p orbitals in FCNCMP-HEMP enables favorable catalytic activity for LiPS conversion. Impressively, FCNCMP-HEMP/C exhibits a higher electron transfer number and lower activation energy in solid-liquid-solid LiPS reduction reactions, indicating enhanced LiPS conversion kinetics. Specifically, Li-S cells with FCNCMP-HEMP/C@S cathodes deliver a high discharge capacity of 744 mAh g - 1 and an ultralow capacity decay of 0.014% per cycle over 2000 cycles at 5 C. Moreover, the assembled pouch cell with the FCNCMP-HEMP/C@S cathode shows a high energy density of 456 Wh kg - 1 . This work opens a new pathway for designing high-entropy metal phosphides for high-performance Li-S batteries.
authors: Manchuan Guo, Jianhong Jiang, Fengxing Liang, Yanqiu Zhu, Jinliang Zhu
