10.1002/adma.74835.title: Plasmon-Free Surface-Enhanced Raman Sensing Enabled by Phase-Engineered Two-Dimensional Mo2C-Based Heterostructures
10.1002/adma.74835.abstract: ABSTRACT Plasmon-free surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) based on two-dimensional materials is a promising approach for nondestructive analysis. However, the smooth surfaces commonly formed during chemical vapor deposition (CVD) limit the generation of localized high electromagnetic fields and reduce chemical interactions with adsorbed molecules, even in metallic 2D materials. In this study, 2D Mo 2 C was synthesized by CVD, and MoOx/Mo 2 C, MoS 2 /Mo 2 C, and MoSe 2 /Mo 2 C heterostructures were fabricated through thermal oxidation, plasma-assisted sulfurization, and selenization, respectively. The MoS 2 and MoSe 2 top layers were phase-engineered into 1T-rich and 2H-rich structures at 350°C and 550°C, respectively, under the same plasma power of 150 W. The heterostructures exhibit improved SERS activity, mainly due to chemical enhancement (CM) arising from increased surface roughness, defect/edge-rich nanostructures, and heterointerfaces that provide abundant localized chemically active sites for molecular adsorption and interfacial charge transfer. The 1T-rich MoS 2 /Mo 2 C shows a detection limit of up to 10 −10 M and a Raman enhancement factor of 9.1 × 10 4 , while the 1T-rich MoSe 2 /Mo 2 C displays a detection limit of up to 10 −9 M and a Raman enhancement factor of 8.9 × 10 4 for rhodamine B (RhB), attributed to the presence of a high density of states and localized chemically active sites on the 1T-rich MoS 2 and MoSe 2 surfaces.
authors: K. M. M. D. K. Kimbulapitiya, Bushra Rehman, Sumayah Shakil Wani, Chia-Chen Chung, Po-Chien La, Tzu-Hsuan Lin, Sujith Lakshan Cooray, Tzu-Wen Kuo, Yu-Qi Huang, R. J. G. L. R. Kumara, Feng-Chuan Chuang, Yu-Lun Chueh

10.1002/adma.74297.title: Thickness-Gated Water and Electron Transport in Near-Critical Ultrathin Polyethylene Membrane Electrodes
10.1002/adma.74297.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical systems are constrained by a materials paradox: chemically robust porous separators are typically hydrophobic and electronically insulating, forcing bulky, carbon-rich interfaces to couple mass transport and electrical contact. Here we show that pushing freestanding porous polyethylene into a near-critical ultrathin regime turns thickness into a geometric gate, enabling these functions to be switched without chemical modification. Near an inferred lower bound (∼10 nm), a 60 nm membrane already enters this regime: liquid-entry pressure collapses into a sub-bar window, enabling aqueous-electrolyte permeation, while the electrical threshold shifts to sub-volt soft dielectric breakdown, yielding persistent through-plane conductivity. The same scaffold enhances nanowire-matrix coupling via high conformability and real contact area, enabling a binder- and carbon-free ∼300 nm ultrathin membrane electrode. As a stringent liquid-phase electrochemical validation, this membrane electrode drives selective nitrate-to-ammonia electroreduction in flowing alkaline electrolytes with sustained performance. Near-critical ultrathinness thus emerges as a gateable design dimension for re-imagining commodity plastics as transmembrane-active platforms.
authors: Runlai Li, He Zhang, Chuyue Lu, Zirui Wang, Jia Liu, Qin Zhang, Kian Ping Loh, Zhongxin Chen, Qiang Fu

10.1002/adma.74957.title: Volumetrically Accessible Ion-Electron Transduction for High-Fidelity Bioelectronics
10.1002/adma.74957.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable bioelectronics are essential for continuous health monitoring and rehabilitation, yet existing soft electrodes often lose signal fidelity during prolonged dynamic wear because surface-confined ion-electron transduction offers limited electrochemically addressable volume and charge-buffering capacity. Here, we report a mixed ionic-electronic transduction layer (PGWL) that addresses these limitations through volumetric charge compensation. By maintaining ionic accessibility and electronic continuity within the mixed-conducting network, PGWL supports a stable bulk-engaged ion-electron transduction mode, thereby lowering interfacial impedance while enhancing charge-buffering capability against perturbations. Integrated with a body-temperature-activated biogel for adaptive viscoelastic adhesion and a breathable nanofibrous substrate, the electrode preserves signal integrity under sweat and mechanical interference, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 30-36 dB with signal variations within 5%. We demonstrate high-fidelity surface electromyography for monitoring weak neuromuscular signals during post-stroke rehabilitation and long-term electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, establishing PGWL as a modular transduction layer for functionally integrated, high-fidelity wearable bioelectronics.
authors: Jinbin Xu, Xiaoliang Chen, Yujiao Wang, Yizhuo Luo, Yahui Chen, Xingliao Zhou, Juan He, Qi Chen, Xiaohao Ma, Jian Lv, Chunhui Wang, Hongmiao Tian, Xiangming Li, Jinyou Shao

10.1002/adma.74879.title: Bioprinting of Biomimetic Periosteum-Bone Integrated Scaffolds
10.1002/adma.74879.abstract: ABSTRACT Bone is composed of periosteum, cortical bone, and cancellous bone. The development of tissue engineering scaffolds mimicking these three parts of bone tissue and enabling synergistic functional performance remains a significant challenge. Herein, a biomimetic periosteum-bone integrated scaffold was successfully fabricated by assembling the outer engineered periosteum with the inner Haversian bone module, achieving structural and functional biomimicry of natural bone tissue. The engineered periosteum constructed with periosteal cells (PCs) with zinc silicate nanorods (ZS) spontaneously recapitulated the diverse bioactivities of natural periosteum, thus facilitating the synergistic osteogenesis when co-cultured with bone marrow related cells in vitro. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations revealed that surface curvature of ZS affected membrane bending-energy landscape and particle reorientation during endocytosis, thereby regulating PCs’ function via altered intracellular ion accumulation kinetics. Notably, in a segmental bone defect, the engineered periosteum and Haversian-bone module exhibited the superior synergistic effect on integrative bone regeneration in vivo. More importantly, the engineered periosteum was found to functionally replace natural periosteum with the mechanism of ZS activating a specific fibrogenic sub-cluster with potent chondrogenesis and neurovascular communication. This biomimetic periosteum-bone integrated scaffold offers a fresh perspective for the design of full structure and function-mimicking bone tissue engineering materials.
authors: Lin Du, Xin Ye, Ruihan Hou, Jianmin Xue, Wenping Ma, Hongjian Zhang, Hongxu Lu, Hongshi Ma, Jinglei Hu, Mengfei Yu, Chengtie Wu

10.1002/adma.74912.title: Aromatic Heterocycle Ligands for Perovskite Photovoltaics: Balancing Defect Passivation and Heterostructure Formation
10.1002/adma.74912.abstract: ABSTRACT Inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) possess great potential for improving efficiency and operating stability, but parasitic charge recombination at the interfaces still limits their performance. As additives and surface treatment agents, ammonium ligands have been reported to form either two/three-dimensional (2D/3D) heterojunctions or passivation layers. In this work, we first conduct a comprehensive, large language model (LLM)-enabled literature mining to systematically enumerate ligand molecules reported over the past decade, through which we identify a pronounced knowledge gap concerning thiazole-based ligands. Then, in a comparative case study, perovskite films are treated with two thiazole- and thiophen-based ligands, which are small rigid aromatic heterocycles with similar molecular conformation. Thiophen-2-ylmethanamine hydrochloride (TPMA) induces 2D phase formation within 3D perovskite films. In comparison, 1,3-thiazol-2-ylmethanamine hydrochloride (TMA), with enhanced charge-transfer interactions associated with the S ions on the aromatic rings, demonstrates a stronger defect passivation capability. Overall, the TMA-based counterpart exhibits lower defect density, extended carrier lifetime, and a more favorable band offset. With the thiazole-based ligand, the resulting inverted PSC achieves an efficiency of 26.81% (certified 26.43%) and retains 96.4% of its initial performance after 1000 h tracking under continuous illumination at the maximum power point.
authors: Yulan Huang, Muchen Li, Qingbin Cai, Zhuoqiong Zhang, Qiang Weng, Xicheng Tang, Bingzhe Wang, Fei Wang, Tanghao Liu, Jiafeng Zhang, Yuhan Guo, Xianfang Zhou, Xinjiang Wang, Xiaoyu Wang, Yunfan Wang, Mingzhu Long, Shu Kong So, Sai-Wing Tsang, Hanlin Hu, Guichuan Xing, Lijun Zhang, Tom Wu

10.1002/adma.74958.title: Superlattice Engineering Stabilizes Bulk-to-Surface Microenvironment in Single-Crystalline Ultrahigh-Ni Cathodes
10.1002/adma.74958.abstract: ABSTRACT Single-crystalline ultrahigh-Ni cathodes hold great promise for high-energy Li-ion batteries, but their practical adoption is hindered by sluggish delithiation kinetics and severe structural degradation. Although superlattice engineering has been established as an effective strategy to stabilize lattice oxygen and enhance Li-ion diffusion in polycrystalline counterparts, realizing ordered Li/Ni anti-site superlattices in micro-sized single-crystalline materials remains challenging, as their formation is largely restricted to the near-surface region. Herein, we report for the first time the construction of a bulk-locally-pinned and surface-even-distributed ordered Li/Ni anti-site superlattice structure in single-crystalline ultrahigh-Ni LiNi 0.93 Co 0.02 Mn 0.03 Al 0.02 O 2 cathodes via Mo-induced local microenvironment regulation during high-temperature lithiation. The resulting cathodes exhibit a 32% reduction in Li-ion diffusion energy barrier, a 23% decrease in lattice oxygen loss, and a 26% suppression of c-axis lattice contraction at 90% state of charge. Consequently, these improvements effectively alleviate stress concentration and substantially accelerate delithiation kinetics. The optimized cathode delivers an ultrahigh reversible capacity of 230 mAh g −1 at 0.1C and achieves a cycle life exceeding 4500 cycles in Ah-level pouch-type full cells.
authors: Liyun Yao, Haifeng Yu, Jiajun Cai, Haoran Bian, Ling Chen, Hao Jiang, Chunzhong Li

10.1002/adma.74914.title: Spatially Synergistic Dual-Confinement Enables Underwater-Stable Room-Temperature Phosphorescent Hydrogels
10.1002/adma.74914.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic room-temperature phosphorescent (RTP) hydrogels are attractive as flexible luminescent materials for optoelectronic and biomedical applications, but their water-rich and mechanically compliant nature makes it difficult to create microenvironments that simultaneously suppress nonradiative decay, resist external quenching, and maintain structural robustness. Here, we report an amphiphilic polymer chain-driven in situ curing strategy that generates rigid luminescent epoxy microspheres uniformly within a PVA hydrogel matrix. Combined with annealing-reswelling-induced matrix densification, this process creates a spatially synergistic dual-confinement system, in which the inner epoxy domains immobilize phosphors while the outer dense PVA network helps impede the ingress of water and oxygen. The resulting hydrogels exhibit tunable multicolor RTP, an ultralong phosphorescence lifetime of up to 4342 ms, a daylight-visible afterglow luminance of 87.9 cd m −2 , a time-gated delayed-emission quantum yield of 55.49%, and a tensile strength exceeding 10 MPa. Notably, the hydrogels retain a phosphorescence lifetime of 3172 ms after 170 days of water immersion. This work identifies spatially synergistic dual confinement as an effective route to jointly optimize phosphorescence efficiency, mechanical robustness, and long-term underwater stability in soft luminescent hydrogels.
authors: Lei Liu, Chunyin Lu, Chuanyong Yan, Wanjuan Huang, Shikun Wen, Junjun Wang, Yujie Wu, Chaolong Yang

10.1002/adma.74874.title: Self-Assembling Copolymers Encapsulating Single Endothelial Cells Induce Endogenous ECM Deposition and Vascular Regeneration
10.1002/adma.74874.abstract: ABSTRACT Cell therapy combined with biomimetic polymer engineering offers a promising strategy for cardiovascular regeneration. Compartmentalizing single cells in hydrogels creates three-dimensional (3D) micro-niches that enhance bio-responsiveness and the therapeutic efficacy of cell therapy. A non-microfluidic strategy for single-cell encapsulation using a stimuli-responsive amphiphilic copolymer, gelatin-poly(glycerol sebacate)-methacrylate (GPM) is developed. When incubated with cells at room temperature, GPM self-assembled into single-cell vesicles via ligand-receptor-mediated interactions, creating a nanoscale matrix around each cell with near 100% encapsulation efficiency. The presence of bioactive moieties, dynamic mechanical properties, and matrix metalloproteinase mediated degradability enabled reciprocal, cell-matrix interactions. Consequently, 3D cultures of GPM vesicles encapsulating single endothelial cell (GPM/EC vesicles) promoted deposition of thread-like extracellular matrix (ECM), which facilitated cell migration and served as a guidance scaffold for vessel-like network formation. For enhanced in vivo distribution and immunoprotection, GPM/reprogrammed EC vesicles were assembled into injectable microspheres, termed mGPM-rEC. Upon injection into a mouse hindlimb ischemia model, mGPM-rEC demonstrated robust cell survival and intramuscular migration with the deposition of dense ECM. This ECM functioned as a reservoir for growth factors and signaling molecules, recruiting host vasculature to promote neovascularization and providing structural and mechanical support for implanted cells to form de novo blood vessels.
authors: Viola B. Morris, Sangho Lee, Kalp Soni, Simon He, Matthew Huang, Dandan Chen, Dae Hoon Lee, Kyung Hee Kim, Seonggeon Cho, Laura Pencea, Divit Jain, Young-Sup Yoon

10.1002/adma.74837.title: Inducing Bulk Polarization in Nonpolar Photocatalysts by Interstitial Li and Charge Compensator Codoping
10.1002/adma.74837.abstract: ABSTRACT Establishing a bulk-penetrating built-in electric field is crucial for enhancing charge separation efficiency in nonpolar photocatalysts. Compared with most existing approaches relying on widening surface space charge layers, inducing bulk polarization via doping is more effective. However, this relies on an ordered spatial distribution of dopants throughout nonpolar photocatalysts, requiring a new mechanism enabling spontaneous alignment of spatially separated dopants. Herein, for interstitial Li-doped anatase TiO 2 , we reveal that a specific reduction in local symmetry around interstitial Li atoms achieved under an ordered Li spatial distribution leads to a strong s-d hybridization. This promotes the localization of excess electrons donated by interstitial Li atoms, thereby lowering the total energy and rendering the ordered Li spatial distribution the most stable. Combined theoretical and experimental results confirm that the ordered Li spatial distribution, coupled with charge-compensated N-codoping, induces bulk polarization of 2.36 and 3.47 µC/cm 2 along the [100] and [001] directions, respectively, at 5 at.% doping level. This leads to a 440% improvement in the photocurrent density of Li/N-codoped anatase TiO 2 compared to the pristine one at 1.23 V versus SHE. Moreover, the mechanism has also been generalized to Y 2 Ti 2 O 5 S 2 and SrTaO 2 N, demonstrating its universality for inducing bulk polarization in nonpolar photocatalysts.
authors: Kangyu Zhang, Guoqiang Deng, Lichang Yin, Lianzhou Wang, Gang Liu

10.1002/adma.74797.title: Spatial-Compatibility-Assisted Molecular Intercalation in MXenes
10.1002/adma.74797.abstract: ABSTRACT MXenes have emerged as versatile platforms for electrochemical energy storage, stimuli-responsive systems, and nanofluidic technologies, owing to their compositionally tunable surfaces and diverse intercalation chemistries. Although ion intercalation in aqueous or organic media is widely employed to modulate the interlayer structure and electronic state of MXenes, the identification of compatible intercalants remains largely empirical. A generally accepted quantitative framework for evaluating the feasibility of guest incorporation into MXene hosts has not yet been established. Here, we propose a general steric-compatibility criterion, in which intercalation becomes geometrically feasible when the effective 3D size of an intercalant molecule, as defined from its molecular crystal structure (i.e., considering a single molecule in the crystalline state), is comparable to or smaller than the interlayer spacing (Δd) created by Al extraction in the parent MAX phase. Guided by this principle, a series of sterically compatible small molecules can be screened, and their intercalation/etching behavior can be rationalized. This study establishes a universal geometry-based guideline for evaluating guest-host compatibility in 2D MXene systems and lays the foundation for predictive design of MXene intercalation chemistries.
authors: Minhao Sheng, Xiaoqing Bin, Xiangyang Liu, Yingji Zhao, Wenxiu Que, Yusuke Asakura, Yusuke Yamauchi

10.1002/adma.74875.title: Proton Environment Optimization Enhanced Asymmetric C1-C2 Intermediate Coupling for CO2 Reduction to n-Propanol
10.1002/adma.74875.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical conversion of CO 2 into value-added n-propanol (n-PrOH) product is pivotal for establishing a sustainable carbon cycle. However, the process is severely hindered by the kinetically sluggish and uncontrolled asymmetric C 1 -C 2 coupling step. Here, we develop a proton modulation strategy to optimize the CO 2 -to-C 3 pathway. Structural engineering of the gas diffusion electrode modulates the H 2 O network environment at the triphasic interface, establishing a gradient H + concentration environment that avoids the direct hydrogenation of *C 2 intermediates. The Faradaic efficiency (FE) for n-PrOH reaches 21% at a partial current density of 167.5 mA cm −2 in a flow cell. In the membrane electrode assembly, the FE n-PrOH remains 19% at a partial current density of 132.9 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic investigations identify *OCH 2 CH 3 as the pivotal intermediate in n-PrOH formation. The simultaneous reduction of the formation energy barriers for both the C 1 -C 1 and C 1 -C 2 coupling rate-determining steps drives C 3 product formation. This work highlights the significant role of proton environment engineering as a crucial parameter in the selection of the C 3 product pathway.
authors: Xi Cao, Xinyang Li, Chengyang Zhu, Rui Yu, Jiaojiao Fang, Junjie Mao

10.1002/adma.74756.title: Polar Wurtzite NbAlN: A Transition-Metal Nitride Alloy for Polarization-Engineered GaN Heterostructures
10.1002/adma.74756.abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of ferroelectric ScAlN sparked a search for new polar wurtzite alloys; however, incorporating transition metals remains a formidable challenge. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of wurtzite-phase NbAlN, a polar transition-metal nitride alloy that is highly compatible with GaN-based heterostructures. Despite the strong metallic character of elemental Nb, we achieved coherent epitaxial NbAlN films that preserve the wurtzite crystal structure and metal polarity of the underlying GaN, as directly visualized by annular bright-field scanning transmission electron microscopy. Nb incorporation induces a monotonic lattice expansion and produces coherent Nb-enriched nanoscale regions that are accommodated within the continuous wurtzite framework. Functionally, NbAlN barriers induce a substantial enhancement in the two-dimensional electron gas density at the AlN/GaN heterointerface, consistent with polarization-related carrier modulation by the metal-polar NbAlN barrier. This study demonstrates that d -electron transition metals can be integrated into polar nitride systems without compromising their functional asymmetry, making NbAlN a promising building block for polar nitride heterostructures and carrier-density-engineered GaN electronics.
authors: Atsushi Kobayashi, Souta Kurogi, Tomoya Okuda, Riku Kikuchi, Yusuke Wakamoto, Kouei Kubota, Hikaru Sasaki, Kazuhisa Ikeda, Kanako Shojiki, Takahiro Kawamura, Toru Akiyama, Takehito Seki, Takuya Maeda

10.1002/adma.74915.title: Steering pH-Dependent Pathways on Unconventional Phase Alloy Nanostructures for Universal Nitrate Electroreduction
10.1002/adma.74915.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) to ammonia has been regarded as a sustainable strategy for industrial wastewater denitrification and fertilizer manufacturing toward green nitrogen circulation. However, complex pH conditions of practical nitrate wastewater result in poor catalyst universality, severely hindering their long-term deployment. Furthermore, the underlying reaction mechanisms in different pH scenarios remain ambiguous, obstructing the rational design of pH-universal electrocatalysts. Here we propose a crystal phase engineering approach to enhance the NO 3 RR performance in complex pH scenarios. The as-designed unconventional face-centered cubic (fcc) RuW nanoflowers exhibit excellent ammonia Faradaic efficiency (FE) above 91.0% over a wide pH range of 1-14, with the largest yield rate of 40.1 mg h −1 mg cat −1 . Mechanism studies indicate that fcc RuW nanoflowers adaptively steer reaction pathways toward diverse pH environments. Based on the long-term durability test at an industrial-level current density of 300 mA cm −2 for 200 h in flow reactors, techno-economic analysis with the optimized process further demonstrates promising application potential. This study not only provides a fundamental insight into the pH-dependent mechanisms of nitrate electroreduction, but also offers a robust catalyst design approach toward complex practical conditions.
authors: Fengkun Hao, Liang Guo, Yunhao Wang, Xinyi Li, Jingwen Zhou, Fu Liu, Juan Wang, Peng Chen, Yuecheng Xiong, Chaohui Wang, Yangbo Ma, Xiang Meng, Guozhi Wang, Qingbo Wa, Mingzheng Shao, Xintao Ma, Yunming Zhong, Miao Wang, Fangren Qian, Xiuyun Zhang, Chenliang Ye, Chongyi Ling, Xiao Zhao, Zhanxi Fan

10.1002/adma.74952.title: Bio-Inspired Rigid-Flexible Integrated Materials With Gradient Interphases for Superior Energy Dissipation
10.1002/adma.74952.abstract: ABSTRACT Bio-inspired rigid-flexible integrated architectures effectively mitigate the intrinsic trade-off between strength and toughness. However, conventional rigid-flexible architectures assembled by adhesives or non-covalent interactions typically suffer from weak interfacial bonding and modulus-mismatch-induced stress concentration, thereby causing delamination. Here, we report a facile strategy combining monomer diffusion with network reconfiguration to construct rigid-flexible multilayered materials with continuous modulus gradient interphases. The optimized 7-layer gradient material (7L-G), comprising rigid polydicyclopentadiene and its flexible copolymers, exhibits a high tensile strength of 51.7 MPa and an elongation at break of 261.0%. Real-time fluorescence tracking using aggregation-induced emission molecules and quantum dots reveals the monomer diffusion kinetics, while nanoindentation confirms a ∼60 µm-thick gradient transition interphase. Both quasi-static tensile and split Hopkinson tension bar (SHTB) tests demonstrate that the 7L-G sample displays significantly superior energy dissipation to its non-gradient counterparts. This enhancement is attributed to the efficient stress delocalization and coordinated plastic deformation enabled by the gradient interphases. Ballistic impact tests and numerical simulations demonstrate the exceptional ballistic resistance performance of the 7L-G sample. This study confirms the effectiveness of modulus gradient interphases in enhancing the interfacial integrity and energy dissipation of rigid-flexible materials, and provides a versatile strategy for developing high-performance impact-resistant polymer materials.
authors: Chenhui Cui, Li Ma, Huiwen Luo, Haoqing Teng, Kexiang Chen, Yinzhou Guo, Menglong Li, Yilong Cheng, Zhishen Ge, Yanfeng Zhang

10.1002/adma.74876.title: Low-Temperature Perovskite Crystallization Suppresses Interfacial Thermal Stress for Robust and High-Resolution Flat-Panel X-Ray Imaging
10.1002/adma.74876.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial thermal stress is a common issue limiting the performance of perovskite optoelectronics, particularly x-ray detectors. This challenge originates from thermomechanical incompatibility: conventional high-temperature perovskite crystallization induces severe interfacial thermal stress upon cooling, triggering film delamination and cracking. Herein, through solvent engineering and intermediate design, we demonstrate, for the first time, the low-temperature formation of perovskite thick films, mitigating this issue at its origin. This is achieved by a new perovskite ink formulation containing highly volatile 2-methoxyethanol (2-ME) and monodentate coordinating 1-cyclohexyl-2-pyrrolidone (CHP). This combination yields a new intermediate, (CHP) 2 Pb 3 I 6 , that largely decouples nucleation from growth and lowers the crystallization temperature from 135 to 75°C. This reduction, along with an improved wettability, decreases the interfacial thermal stress by ∼75% and doubles the interfacial adhesion strength. Consequently, robust integration of perovskite thick films with an indium-gallium-zinc-oxide (IGZO) thin-film transistor (TFT) backplane is achieved. The resulting flat-panel imager delivers a spatial resolution of 4.73 lp mm −1 (0.59 lp pix −1 ) when the modulation transfer function (MTF) reaches 0.2, outperforming commercial amorphous selenium (α-Se) and previous perovskite-based imagers. This work elucidates intermediate-regulated crystallization thermodynamics and opens avenue for integrating monolithic perovskite optoelectronics onto temperature-sensitive substrates.
authors: Yulong Wang, Yunjie He, Zhen Cheng, Yi Zhang, Wenhang Yan, Da Xu, Shujuan Liu, Qiang Zhao, Xiuwen Xu

10.1002/adma.74953.title: Interfacial Gap Switching in MXene Ti3C2Tx MoS2 Memristors
10.1002/adma.74953.abstract: ABSTRACT Resistive-switching devices are essential building blocks for advanced multifunctional integrated circuits (ICs), with four major switching mechanisms (ion migration, phase change, magnetization orientation, and ferroelectric polarization) having been extensively studied, each facing inherent limitations for practical applications. Herein, we disclose an interfacial gap switching mechanism in a two-terminal Ti 3 C 2 T x /MoS 2 device, fundamentally distinct from those conventional mechanisms. The switching mechanism relies on the interfacial gap modulation between the metallic MXene Ti 3 C 2 T x layer and semiconducting MoS 2 layer under applied bias, leading to reversible switching between low resistance state and high resistance state. The gap modulation phenomenon was further observed in three-terminal transistor devices. The working principle takes advantage of MXene Ti 3 C 2 T x with high concentration of negative charges, electrostatically interacting with MoS 2 triggered by bias or gating dynamically. Further optimization of memristor device exhibited ultra-low cycle-to-cycle variation, with a set voltage standard deviation of 40 mV and coefficient of variation of 2.31%, outperforming most reported 2D memristors. This discovery of gap modulation provides new insights into memristor device physics and offers a unique idea to build 2D memristor architecture for non-volatile memory related applications.
authors: Xiangming Xu, Sebastian Pazos, Dekang Zhu, Yue Ping, Ning Chu, Mario Lanza, Husam N. Alshareef

10.1002/adma.74910.title: Dynamic Active-Hydrogen-Buffering Interfaces Enable Fluctuation-Resilient Selective Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation
10.1002/adma.74910.abstract: ABSTRACT Renewable-electricity-driven electrocatalysis is difficult to maintain under steady-state operation because of the intermittent, variable, and stochastic nature of renewable power. This challenge is particularly critical for selective electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH), such as phenol-to-cyclohexanone conversion in acidic media, where fluctuating operation can induce transient accumulation of active hydrogen intermediates, compromising product selectivity and energy efficiency. In this study, we develop a dynamic active-hydrogen-buffering interface strategy to construct fluctuation-resistant electrocatalysts using the short-chain surfactant butyltrimethylammonium bromide (BTAB). Under simulated power fluctuations in a flow cell, the BTAB-modified catalyst maintains near-steady-state performance, achieving 90.1% cyclohexanone selectivity and 83.6% Faradaic efficiency (FE), and outperforms the unmodified system by 1.69-fold in cyclohexanone FE under more drastic fluctuations. Mechanistic studies reveal that the BTAB layer weakens the interfacial hydrogen-bond network and attenuates Grotthuss-type proton relay, thereby regulating proton flux and buffering active hydrogen accumulation during current fluctuations. This suppresses competing hydrogen evolution and overhydrogenation to cyclohexanol while preserving phenol hydrogenation kinetics. Combined with techno-economic analysis, this work establishes active-hydrogen buffering as an interfacial strategy for maintaining selective electrosynthesis under dynamic operating conditions.
authors: Yan Du, Jian Shang, Zichao Xi, Jinxiao Wu, Longji Yuan, Huimin Yu, Huanyu Jin, Hui-Ming Cheng

10.1002/adma.74916.title: High-Performance Stretchable Field-Effect Transistors Based on Intrinsically Flexible n-Type Partially Conjugated Polymers Synthesized via Aldol Polycondensation
10.1002/adma.74916.abstract: ABSTRACT Two intrinsically flexible conjugated polymers, PBT-90 and PFBT-90 , were designed and synthesized via aldol polycondensation. Both polymers incorporate a novel double-flexible-node unit, 5,5'-bis(1,1,2,2-tetrafluoro-2-(thiophen-2-yl)ethyl)-2,2'-bithiophene, which can reduce brittleness and enhance recoverability in both bulk polymers and processed films. Both polymers displayed n -type charge transport in transistors fabricated on a polyethylene terephthalate substrate, achieving high electron mobilities ( µ e ) of 3.85 and 4.56 cm 2 V −1 s −1 for PBT-90 and PFBT-90 , respectively, only slightly inferior to 5.44 and 6.37 cm 2 V −1 s −1 of their fully conjugated analogues, PBT-100 and PFBT-100 . Utilizing a self-developed PET/CYTOP/AlO x three-layer thin film transfer process, combined with orthogonal solvent design and interlayer protection strategies, we fabricated high-performance stretchable transistors. The PFBT-90 -based devices exhibited a record-high µ e of 3.51 cm 2 V −1 s −1 in the pristine state. Under 100% strain, they retained a µ e > 2.86 cm 2 V −1 s −1 (>80% retention). The remarkable device performance originates from its suitable frontier molecular orbitals structure, low backbone glass transition temperature, and well-balanced finitely conjugated backbone, where rigid conjugated segments ensure highly efficient charge carrier transport and flexible nonconjugated segments dissipate stress. Our findings offer a pivotal molecular design strategy and a versatile fabrication process for advanced stretchable organic electronics.
authors: Qian Che, Weifeng Zhang, Jiadi Chen, Chang Cui, Zhihui Chen, Liping Wang, Gui Yu

10.1002/adma.74882.title: Wavelength- and Helicity-Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Optical Diodes Enabled by Molecular Photoswitches
10.1002/adma.74882.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving nonreciprocal transmission of circularly polarized light (CPL) is critical for chiral photonics and spin-selective optical communication, yet existing optical diodes typically operate at fixed wavelengths. Here, we report an all-optical, photoswitchable diode-type device for tunable nonreciprocal (asymmetric) transmission of CPL across a broad spectrum of light using molecular motor (photoswitch)-doped cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs) sandwiched between polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and polydopamine (PDA)-PVA composite layers. Under ultraviolet irradiation, the photoswitches continuously modulate the helical twisting power of the CLC, enabling reversible tuning of the photonic bandgap (PBG) and, at higher irradiation levels, helix inversion with opposite handedness. Thus, we demonstrate dynamic switching of both the operating wavelength and the isolated CPL helicity within a single device architecture. The asymmetric PDA@PVA photothermal interface enables forward photothermal activation of the cholesteric-isotropic transition while maintaining spin-selective Bragg reflection under backward incidence. This mechanism enables wavelength-tunable and chirality-adaptive nonreciprocal transmission for both right- and left-handed CPL. The device achieves isolation ratios exceeding 15.10 dB at all tested wavelengths, with a maximum value of 15.80 dB at 980 nm, while maintaining insertion losses below 2.89 dB, reaching as low as 1.05 dB. Furthermore, the operating thresholds and thermal tolerance can be tailored through liquid-crystal composition.
authors: Chaoguang Ye, Ming Yuan, Jiaxin Liu, Wei Zhou, Changsheng Wu, Zhenyu Zhou, Chaoying Zhu, Xiao-Fang Jiang, Jiawen Chen, Lakshminarayana Polavarapu, Guofu Zhou, Xiaowen Hu

10.1002/adma.74917.title: Electron-Extracting Pd Single Atoms Arrest Solar Photooxidative Upcycling of Waste Polyesters at Glycolaldehyde
10.1002/adma.74917.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective solar oxidation of ethylene glycol (EG) derived from waste poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) to glycolaldehyde (GAld) is hindered by the high reactivity of the aldehyde intermediate, which readily undergoes overoxidation and C─C cleavage. Here, we report an exfoliated polymeric carbon nitride (PCN) photocatalyst with atomically dispersed Pd sites (Pd SA /PCN) that arrests EG photooxidation at the C 2 aldehyde stage. In PET hydrolysate, optimized Pd SA /PCN achieves a GAld formation rate of 2479 µmol g cat −1 h −1 with 92.8% selectivity; in gram-scale upgrading of real PET waste, the selectivity reaches 95.9%. Mechanistic studies suggest that Pd single atoms function as electron-extraction centers, removing electrons from long-lived, low-energy localized states in PCN and increasing surface-accessible holes for selective alcohol dehydrogenation. Meanwhile, Pd sites strengthen EG adsorption and lower the barrier for initial O─H activation, favouring alkoxy intermediates while limiting ·OH-type overoxidation and C─C scission. The catalyst converts diverse real polyester wastes under fluctuating natural sunlight while maintaining >90% GAld selectivity. Coupled techno-economic and geospatial analyses identify priority deployment regions with a median annual net profit of US$5.95 million, highlighting the potential of single-atom materials for solar plastic upcycling to C 2 platform molecules.
authors: Guanqi Yu, Kaizhou Kong, Xiangkun Jia, Feifei Fan, Yingying Zhao, Chunli Wang, Wei Liu, Pengfei Wang, Sihui Zhan

10.1002/adma.74719.title: Functional Complementation of Sn/La Diatomic Sites Over V2O5 Cathodes Resolves the Capacity-Stability Trade-Off of Aqueous Potassium Ion Battery
10.1002/adma.74719.abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic trade-off between high specific capacity and structural stability severely limits the development of high-capacity K + cathodes. Herein, we address this limitation through a strategic pairing of f / p -block elements for constructing isolated heteronuclear diatomic sites (La/Sn) on carbon substrate. This pairing drives the reconstruction of V 2 O 5 into hydrated layered phase, forming a dual-function interface where La acts as a structural anchor and Sn as a kinetics promoter. The strongly Lewis acidic La center stabilizes the host framework by suppressing vanadium dissolution, whereas Sn, with energetically accessible p -orbitals, facilitates interfacial charge transfer. The resulting interface couples K + intercalation with interfacial proton storage, forming a highly reversible hybrid reaction pathway that reconciles capacity and stability. As a result, C/Sn/La-V 2 O 5 electrode achieves a high specific capacity of 350 mAh g −1 , exceptional rate capability, and outstanding cycling stability (95.5% retention after 10 000 cycles). Operando spectroscopic analyses support the existence of this dual-ion coupling pathway governs the reversible charge-storage process, with the exceptional electrochemical performance originating from the functional complementarity of the Sn/La dual-atomic sites. This work establishes f / p -block element pairing as a promising design strategy for engineering atomic interfaces that integrate complementary charge-storage mechanisms, with preliminary generality supported by additional element pairs.

10.1002/adma.74883.title: Topological Spin-Texture Transitions in van der Waals Magnets Revealed by X-Ray Fourier Transform Holography
10.1002/adma.74883.abstract: ABSTRACT Nontrivial topological spin-textures, such as skyrmions, merons, bimerons, and skyrmioniums, are envisioned as robust building blocks for future memory and logic devices. Controllable transformations between these states require a quantum-mechanical description of electronic degrees of freedom and atomic-scale insight beyond existing phenomenological models. Here, we report an atomic-scale investigation of topological phase transitions and their protection in the two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2 (FGT) using a combined experimental-theoretical approach. Synchrotron-based Fourier transform holography directly images labyrinth domains, isolated skyrmions, mixed labyrinth-skyrmion phases, and skyrmion bags with high spatial resolution. We compare these observations to simulations based on an electronic lattice Hamiltonian that captures both metallicity and relativistic spin-orbit coupling in FGT. By systematically exploring a broad range of temperatures and magnetic fields, we map the mechanisms governing topological transitions and their stability. This sequential-integrated experimental-theoretical framework advances understanding of spin-texture interactions and enables precise control of external tuning parameters. Our results establish a platform for creating, stabilizing, and manipulating topological states, paving the way for engineered spin-texture transitions in next-generation spintronic technologies.

10.1002/adma.74880.title: Mixed-Dimensional 1D/2D Ternary CMOS for High-Performance Integrated Circuits
10.1002/adma.74880.abstract: ABSTRACT Ternary logic offers a path to higher information density and lower power consumption beyond the limits of binary CMOS, yet its progress has been limited by the absence of high-performance ternary transistors and scalable circuit technologies. Here we report a mixed-dimensional ternary CMOS (T-CMOS) platform that monolithically integrates aligned carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and monolayer MoS 2 within silicon backend-of-line processes. The resulting CNT-MoS 2 heterojunction transistors exhibit more than an order-of-magnitude performance improvement in output current and negative differential transconductance over previous ternary devices, enabling robust three-level switching with large noise margins. By co-fabricating CNT p-FETs and MoS 2 n-FETs into heterojunction devices, we realize CMOS-compatible standard, positive and negative ternary inverters, as well as NMIN and NMAX logic gates. A fully functional ternary 2-to-9 decoder, the most complex low-dimensional ternary circuit to date, is also demonstrated. Dynamic measurements and calibrated simulations confirm the scalability, cascade capability, and robustness of the T-CMOS architecture, providing a viable pathway toward large-scale ternary integrated circuits beyond binary limits.

10.1002/adma.75550.title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster-Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature
10.1002/adma.75550.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three-dimensional cuprous iodide cluster-based covalent organic framework (CuI-MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI-MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti-interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density-functional theory calculations reveal that the imine-linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption-desorption sites, while the electron-rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on-chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti-interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high-performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster-based COFs in gas sensing.

10.1002/adma.75405.title: Bacteria-Trained, MnO2-Armored Dendritic Cells for Immunotherapy
10.1002/adma.75405.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over the phenotypic state of immune cells is critical for overcoming the limitations of on-target off-tumor toxicity and inefficient tumor infiltration in cell-based cancer immunotherapy. Here, we developed an engineered DC platform-trained with inactivated bacteria and armored with MnO 2 nanoparticles (designated MnArmL-trDCs)-endowed with immune reconfigurability and mechano-transformable characteristics to boost tumor penetration and remodel immune microenvironment. In circulation, the MnO 2 armor enforces a stiff mechanical state and globally masks surface immunological ligands (such as CD80, CD86, MHC-II, and CCR7), rendering the DCs biologically silent and resistant to premature immune recognition or hepatic clearance. These engineered cells integrate selectively into lesion sites, enabling restoration of the deformability of dendritic cells and targeted intratumoral immune activation triggered by local pH and hydrogen peroxide. This transformation enables deep tumor penetration, robust activation of TLR, NLR, and cGAS-STING pathways, and efficient trafficking to tumor-draining lymph nodes. In vivo, MnArmL-trDCs induce a pro-inflammatory immune landscape, promote cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration, reverse immunosuppression, and synergize with anti-PD-1 therapy to achieve sustained tumor regression. This nano-engineering cell armor-based strategy could also be possibly expanded to different cell types in other types of immunotherapies.

10.1002/adma.75505.title: In Situ Polymerization of Covalent Organic Frameworks Networks for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75505.abstract: ABSTRACT The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong π-π stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF-based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre-synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS-treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long-term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.
authors: Tianhong Huang, Yu Yuan, Zhihui Chen, Shuai Yang, Wei Huang, Kaifeng Quan, Chang Cui, Jiadi Chen, Weifeng Zhang, Jizheng Wang, Gui Yu

10.1002/adma.75527.title: Photothermal Catalytic Dry Reforming of Methane With 1000-Hour Stability via Redox Shuttle of Metal Vanadate
10.1002/adma.75527.abstract: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalytic dry reforming of methane (DRM) mediated by lattice oxygen (O l ) is promising for converting two major greenhouse gases into syngas. However, conventional oxide supports possess strong metal-oxygen bonds that restrict O l migration, compromising stability, typically less than 200 h. Herein, we design a Rh/Mg 2 V 1.33 O 4 catalyst with Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + interfacial sites ( n = 3 or 4). The defective spinel vanadate support exhibits quasi-metallic properties, enabling efficient solar harvesting and photothermal conversion. Under 4 W cm −2 light irradiation without external heating, the redox flexibility of V species enables an interfacial redox shuttle (Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + ⇌ Rh δ + ─O l ─V ( n +1)+ ), which endows the catalyst with effective O l migration and regeneration ability in the DRM reaction. This property steers the reaction along a coking-resistant CH 3 O* pathway and guarantees structural stability. As a result, the catalyst delivers long-term stability for 1000 h, outperforming state-of-the-art photothermal catalysts. It also achieves high syngas generation rates of 16.1 and 18.6 mol g Rh −1 h −1 for H 2 and CO, respectively, along with a light-to-chemical energy efficiency of ∼20.9%. This work establishes quasi-metallic, redox-active vanadate supports as a transformative platform for durable O l -mediated photothermal catalysis.
authors: Yueyue Dong, Zhiyong Ouyang, Zhongliao Wang, Wei Ma, Hailong Xiong, Tingting Kong, Ran Long, Yujie Xiong

10.1002/adma.75520.title: Processing Window Expansion Enables Uniform Crystallization in Scalable Ambient-Fabricated Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75520.abstract: ABSTRACT Slot-die coating is a promising scalable deposition technique for perovskite devices due to its high material utilization and inherent compatibility with continuous manufacturing. However, a narrow deposition-to-annealing time window and inhomogeneous ink distribution limit the device performance. Herein, we report a combined additive (CA) strategy that simultaneously regulates nucleation kinetics and phase evolution, broadening the processing window for slot-die coating in the ambient. By synergistically introducing rubidium thiocyanate (RbSCN) and formamidinium thiocyanate (FASCN), an in situ coordination mechanism is established that lowers the energy barrier for the δ-to-α phase transition while suppressing non-photoactive phase formation. This leads to uniform crystallization over an extended time window exceeding 100 s, yielding dense large-grained α-FAPbI 3 films with minimized vertical compositional gradient and reduced residual strain. The resulting films exhibit suppressed defects, prolonged carrier lifetime, and optimized energy-level alignment, enabling efficient charge extraction and reduced nonradiative recombination. The CA strategy enables highly uniform large-area deposition to deliver an efficiency of 22.70% for perovskite solar modules. Meanwhile, the unencapsulated devices maintain 97.76% of the initial efficiency under ISOS-L-3 for 1300 h. This CA strategy establishes a generalizable pathway for decoupling crystallization kinetics from processing constraints, providing a robust method for scalable high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Lianjie Duan, Ruixia Yang, Dongqi Yu, Shaoan Yang, Jieqiong Liu, Shengzhong (Frank) Liu, Zhihua Zhang, Xuejie Zhu, Dong Yang

10.1002/adma.75502.title: Nanocatalytic Inhibition of ROS-Dependent GSDMD Palmitoylation Mitigates Sepsis Progression
10.1002/adma.75502.abstract: ABSTRACT Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by multiple organ dysfunction, high morbidity, and mortality. Gasdermin D (GSDMD)-mediated pyroptosis constitutes a key pathogenic mechanism. Here, we discovered that GSDMD in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from septic patients undergoes enhanced palmitoylation, driven by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mediated by ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 transferases. Targeting this new mechanism, we designed and screened vanadium oxide hydroxide nanosheets (VOOH NSs) as catalytic ROS scavengers and GSDMD palmitoylation inhibitor. Crucially, we investigated and optimized the exposure patterns of specific lattice planes to maximize their ROS-eliminating capability. This intervention measure prevents GSDMD palmitoylation, inhibits both canonical and non-canonical pyroptosis, alleviates inflammatory damage, and demonstrates potent therapeutic effects in two sepsis animal models. Validation in GSDMD-knockout mice further confirms this palmitoylation pathway as the key therapeutic target. These results demonstrate that targeting ROS-mediated GSDMD palmitoylation is a key therapeutic strategy for treating sepsis.
authors: Chenglong Zhu, Renqi Yao, Wuyang Wei, Jiaojiao Feng, Lindong Cheng, Tian Zhou, Ruoyu Jiang, Wangzheqi Zhang, Yaohua Yu, Meiqi Chang, Yu Chen, Zui Zou

10.1002/adma.75007.title: Ultrafast All-Solid-State Electrochromic Devices for Multicolor Displays
10.1002/adma.75007.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state electrochromic devices (ASSECDs) hold tremendous potential for emerging display technologies. However, achieving sufficiently fast switching for modern display applications remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report an interfacial engineering strategy that synergistically optimizes both electron transfer and ion compensation processes to realize ultrafast-response ASSECDs. Through surface immobilization of rationally designed dual-chromophore extended viologen derivative 2BTB-2POH on TiO 2 -modified electrodes combined with a succinonitrile-based solid-state electrolyte, the device achieves unprecedented response times of 0.16 s for coloration and 0.40 s for bleaching, representing the fastest switching speeds reported to date for all-solid-state electrochromic systems. Furthermore, the device demonstrates a high optical contrast (Δ T = 65.1%), an exceptionally high coloration efficiency (708.9 cm 2 /C), and robust cycling stability (>10,000 cycles with 91.1% retention). By rationally tuning the chromophore structure of viologens ( 2BBAr-2POH and 2BTD-2POH ), we extend this strategy to multicolor systems covering a red-green-blue (RGB) primary-color demonstration, and successfully fabricate patterned display prototypes with dynamic display demonstrations. This work establishes a viable pathway toward high-performance ASSECDs for next-generation display applications.
authors: Fangyuan Sun, Yanan He, Miao Li, Haibo Wu, Delai Kong, Chengwei Jiang, Ziyan Yu, Yu Feng, Dake Dong, Guanquan Wang, Fengyu Su, Yanqing Tian, Yan Jun Liu

10.1002/adma.75519.title: Closed-Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy
10.1002/adma.75519.abstract: ABSTRACT Closed-loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed-schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real-time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed-loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed-loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof-of-concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next-generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.
authors: Narlawar Sagar Shrikrishna, Drishya Prakashan, Sonu Gandhi

10.1002/adma.75547.title: Electromigration-Biased Carbon Transport and Isotope Fractionation in High-Carbon-Solubility Metals
10.1002/adma.75547.abstract: ABSTRACT Electromigration, usually studied as a failure mechanism can also guide materials formation. We demonstrate that direct current drives interstitial carbon transport in solid cobalt and nickel leading to graphite precipitation, isotope fractionation, and distinct thermal properties of the recovered phase. Carbon supplied centrally accumulates as graphite 8-10 mm away on the cathode side, whereas alternating-current control experiments under comparable heating produce only thin deposits near the source. Raman mapping and ToF-SIMS profiling reveal 12 C enrichment across source compositions from natural abundance to ∼88 at% 13 C, with Raman-derived enrichment factors of 1.29-1.62. The composition dependence of these factors, with increased enrichment toward the 13 C-rich end, supports isotope-sensitive transport coupled to localized precipitation. Finite-bias calculations demonstrate directional migration-barrier asymmetry, while isotope-dependent hopping and a concentration-threshold model predict preferential 12 C enrichment in both hosts. Frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) measurements of both thermal conductivity components reveal a pronounced in-plane and a weaker out-of-plane composition dependence. These results show current-directed graphite formation in solid metals accompanied by isotope fractionation and composition-dependent thermal properties. This approach may extend to other mobile interstitial solutes in suitable metal hosts.
authors: Alisher Sultangaziyev, Yongchul Kim, Yongqiang Meng, Liyuan Zhang, Sun Hwa Lee, Rodney S. Ruoff, Won Kyung Seong

10.1002/adma.75541.title: 4f-Electron-Regulated Dual-Periodic Bonding Evolution Across the Lanthanide Series
10.1002/adma.75541.abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide-based catalysts have attracted increasing attention due to their unique electronic structures, yet the relationship between 4f electron evolution and catalytic behavior remains unclear. Here, using structurally uniform lanthanide single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we systematically investigate the influence of 4f electron filling on bonding evolution across the lanthanide series. We reveal a dual-periodic trend in lanthanide-support binding energies and adsorbate bonding energies, which increases from La to Eu and from Gd to Yb. This behavior originates from progressive electron redistribution between 5d and 4f orbitals, which modulates the electron population of bonding orbitals. The half-filled 4f 7 configuration induces an abrupt transition between Eu and Gd. Furthermore, similar crystal-field splitting enables robust linear relationships between binding and bonding energies across diverse coordination environments. More importantly, the persistence of these electronic characteristics across diverse coordination environments demonstrates that the dual-periodic evolution represents an intrinsic feature of lanthanide chemistry rather than a system-specific phenomenon. These findings establish a 4f-electron-regulated bonding framework for understanding lanthanide reactivity and guiding catalyst design.
authors: Yaxiong Yao, Yaxin Cheng, Xinyu Ye, Jiamin Zhu, Yiwei You, Zirui Wang, Yaowei Xiang, Ting Wang, Li An, Pinxian Xi, Yuanmiao Sun

10.1002/adma.75514.title: Copper Surface Engineering Enables Uniform Zn Plating in Zn Batteries at Unity N/P Ratio
10.1002/adma.75514.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc (Zn) metal plating is notoriously sensitive to interfacial inefficiencies under Zn-limited conditions, where small losses of active Zn rapidly lead to premature cell failure. Here, we demonstrate a surface reconstruction strategy for copper (Cu) current collectors that enables exceptional performance at a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.0. By chemically etching Cu to create a sacrificial cuprous chloride (γ-CuCl) interface, we obtained a micro-textured Cu substrate with increased electrochemical surface area (ECSA). Upon initial electrochemical reduction, γ-CuCl converts to metallic Cu while releasing Cl − ions into the local interfacial region of the electrolyte. Density functional theory calculations indicate that localized Cl − ions favorably regulate Zn 2+ adsorption energy while suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. Benefitting from the synergistic combination of enhanced ECSA and dynamic Cl − mediated interfacial engineering, Zn//Cu cells achieve stable plating/stripping cycling for 1654 h (69 days). Notably, Zn//MnO 2 full cells using 3D-printed etched Cu substrate assembled under a nominal N/P ratio of 1.0 (determined by a reversible capacity at 10 mA cm −2 ) deliver a remarkable device volumetric capacity of 53.5 mAh cm −3 . Under high-rate cycling (80 mA cm −2 ), the cell retains 70% of initial capacity over 500 cycles. This performance represents a benchmark for Zn reversibility under extreme material-limited conditions.
authors: Xinzhe Xue, Mykyta Motin, Marisa Hertzog, Calvin D. Quilty, Igor I. Bezsonov, Karim Aljamal, Nathan Delaney, Samuel Eisenberg, Cassidy Tran, Swetha Chandrasekaran, Xiao Wang, Marcus A. Worsley, Cheng Zhu, Timothy N. Lambert, Yat Li

10.1002/adma.75548.title: Mechanically-Driven Reconstruction of Lithium Metal for Stable All-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/adma.75548.abstract: ABSTRACT Dendrite growth at lithium-metal anode remains a critical bottleneck in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Current approaches often rely on alloy anodes that compromise energy density or artificial interlayers, introducing additional processing complexity. Herein, we show that accumulated deformation imposed by repeated folding and rolling mechanically reconstructs commercial Li from surface to bulk, replacing a rough carbonate-rich surface and mixed texture with a refined oxide-passivated surface and a strongly Li(200)-preferred texture. At low and medium folding degrees, surface refinement and renewal of the native passivation layer improve solid-solid contact and interfacial Li-ion transport, but remain insufficient to prevent short circuiting, whereas high-degree reconstruction drives texture homogenization, reduces spatial variations in local interfacial response, and synchronizes Li recession and advancement across the rigid Li | solid-state electrolyte interface. The synchronous interface motion suppresses differential recession and void formation during stripping, while mitigating dendritic Li growth during plating. As a result, Li | LPSCl 1.5 | NMC811 full cells achieve 79.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at C/2 rate, support 7.4 mA h cm −2 operation with 0.05% decay per cycle, and cycle stably below 0.5 MPa. These findings establish mechanical reconstruction as a direct materials-level strategy for stabilizing Li metal in sulfide-based ASSBs.

10.1002/adma.75553.title: In Situ Lab-on-Fiber Platform: A Versatile Tool for Dual-Mode Optoelectronic Tracking Photocorrosion Dynamics of Cadmium Sulfide
10.1002/adma.75553.abstract: ABSTRACT As versatile catalysts, metal sulfides (MSs) unlock new possibilities for photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, driving innovations in clean energy production. However, they are prone to photocorrosion under illumination, which severely impairs their catalytic efficiency and recyclability, thus fundamentally compromising the stability of the catalytic reaction system. Therefore, critical to this effort is the elucidation of photocorrosion for the practical application of high-performance catalysts and long-lasting reactors. Herein, a lab-on-fiber sensing platform is developed for in situ, real-time monitoring of the photocorrosion of cadmium sulfide (CdS). Anchored by a tapered seven-core optical fiber, the platform facilitates dual-mode sensing by correlating transmission spectrum evolution with photocurrent dynamics, revealing that CdS photocorrosion exhibits a nonlinear dependence on light intensity. The photocorrosion rate is minimized at 0.8 mW∙cm −2 UV light and is further suppressed by applying a 0.4 V bias. Furthermore, the platform uncovers a protective, dynamic sulfur cycle enabled by sacrificial agents on the catalyst surface. Crucially, key structure-activity relationships of the CdS undergoing photocorrosion are established, enabling the optimization of catalysts and reactors. Beyond catalytic systems, the platform is applicable to the operando exploration of interfacial dynamic behaviors and mechanisms in various nanomaterials, thereby underpinning the design of micro-nano material interfaces and reaction systems.

10.1002/adma.75549.title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto-Viscoelastic Patches
10.1002/adma.75549.abstract: ABSTRACT We report a machine learning (ML)-augmented magnetic sensing system for real-time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″-Fe 16 N 2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML-based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical-grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real-time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

10.1002/adma.75501.title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
10.1002/adma.75501.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum-based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic-anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni-Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high-surface-area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface-limited deposition. The resulting Al-alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge-transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric-cell operation and long-duration full-cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low-cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm −2 . When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm −2 with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni-assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al-containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

10.1002/adma.75552.title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75552.abstract: ABSTRACT Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet-sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor-iridium coordination polymer (BTP-N-Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet-triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long-lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra-moiety excited (i-EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet-exciton transfer pathway with the i-EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

10.1002/adma.75525.title: Ultra-Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy
10.1002/adma.75525.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non-ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe-Co-Ni-Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m 2 ) into the ferromagnetic face-centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non-magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am 2 /kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe-Si and Fe-Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high-performance soft magnetic alloys.
authors: Shang Zhao, Mingliang Wang, Huan Wang, Liuliu Han, Xiaoyi Du, Yiping Lu

10.1002/adma.74903.title: Powering Skin Repair: Piezoelectric Biomaterials-Driven Wound Healing
10.1002/adma.74903.abstract: ABSTRACT Over the past decade, piezoelectric biomaterials have emerged as powerful platforms for tissue repair and regeneration by enabling self-generated, minimally invasive bioelectric stimulation. Among them, skin wound healing has become a prominent area of research due to the tissue's accessibility and clinical relevance. Specifically, the microcurrents powered by piezoelectric biomaterials closely mimic the endogenous electrical cues present in healthy skin. These bioelectrical signals regulate multiple stages of wound healing, including cell migration and proliferation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix formation, and immune modulation. This review will provide a comprehensive overview of piezoelectric biomaterials for skin wound healing and examine the physiological and biochemical roles of the naturally occurring electric fields in healthy skin and injured skin. By integrating these perspectives, we highlight how piezoelectric scaffolds can power skin tissue repair by recapitulating native bioelectric signaling. We further discuss current challenges, translational opportunities, and future directions toward the development of next-generation electroactive wound dressings for the treatment of acute and chronic wounds.

10.1002/adma.75542.title: Biointerface-Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria-Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
10.1002/adma.75542.abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune-beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface-customized nanomodulator (C/C-HP@M2M-TPP), developed through a biointerface-engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria-specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria-directed subcellular localization. Co-delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface-customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

10.1002/adma.75561.title: Entropy Stabilized Li-Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High-Voltage Cathodes
10.1002/adma.75561.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small-particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser-induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high-entropy doped Li-rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high-voltage performances. The direct bottom-up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li-rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic-resolution imaging, operando x-ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut-off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition-metal framework in the high-entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5-4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high-voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high-voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next-generation energy storage research.

10.1002/adma.75524.title: Ionic-Ligand-Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg−1 Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75524.abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic-ligand-assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI − anions, creating anion-rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li + hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm −1 ) and an exceptional Li + transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li-metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid-state Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high-energy-density (515 Wh kg −1 ) solid-state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high-loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm −2 ) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic-ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high-performance and high-safety solid-state batteries.
