10.1002/adma.75523.title: In-Situ Self-Evolving µ-Sn10Bi Cross-Interlocked Structure and Three-in-One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low-Temperature Sodium Storage Performance
10.1002/adma.75523.abstract: ABSTRACT Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low-voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high-energy-density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long-term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three-in-one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ-Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ-Bi. Interestingly, µ-Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross-linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long-term structural stability of µ-Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in-situ formed further accelerate e − /Na + transfer. As a result, the prepared µ-Sn 10 Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure-activity relationship of µ-Sn 10 Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low-cost, high-capacity, structurally stable, fast-charging anode with wide-temperature adaptability for HSIBs.
authors: Ying-Ying Wang, Yi-Heng Peng, Hao-Jie Wang, Le Zhang, Zhen-Yi Gu, Ben-Jian Xin, Jia-Hui Ren, Xing-Long Wu, Bao-Hua Hou

10.1002/adma.75569.title: Wafer-Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c-Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
10.1002/adma.75569.abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non-uniformity, and the need for post-growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2-inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp 2 -hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long-range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate-tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

10.1002/adma.75478.title: Synthesis of Ti2B2Clx MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
10.1002/adma.75478.abstract: ABSTRACT The unique properties and application possibilities of two-dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti 2 InB 2 with ZnCl 2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 < x < 1.4. Further, in situ x-ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti 2 InB 2 to ml-MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml-MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A-element substitution into the 3D Ti 2 ZnB 2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li-ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.
authors: Rodrigo M. Ronchi, Emile Defoy, Andrejs Petruhins, Justinas Palisaitis, Leiqiang Qin, Joseph Halim, Lianghao Yu, Lan Tang, Solenn Reguer, Dominique Thiaudière, Ningjun Chen, Durga Sankar Vavilapalli, David Portehault, Jonas Björk, Per O. Å. Persson, Johanna Rosen

10.1002/adma.75545.title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
10.1002/adma.75545.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system-level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure-property relationships across p-type, n-type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte-channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all-gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant-bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT-native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed-loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near-term direction for the field.
authors: Meera Stephen, Mingyu Zhang, Yingjun Chen, Wei Lin Leong

10.1002/adma.75540.title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen-Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer-Macrocycle-Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
10.1002/adma.75540.abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of high-performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption-active motifs into higher-order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen-bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif-conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non-additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I 3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100-fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif-level host-guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid-state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.
authors: Xirui Wang, Zhonglin Ma, Xinnan Chen, Weiyi Xiong, Yimin Cai, Long Chen, Wen Feng, Lihua Yuan, Xiaowei Li

10.1002/adma.75452.title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro-Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer
10.1002/adma.75452.abstract: ABSTRACT The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology-enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β-blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time-of-flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro-immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer-associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.
authors: Shi-Jie Hao, Xiejunhao Zheng, Shun-Yu Wu, Zitong Wang, Tiange Wu, Yanli An, Han Guan, Zihao Wang, Shen Zhang, Wei Yang, Gao-Jun Teng, Bin Xu, Fu-Gen Wu

10.1002/adma.75546.title: Autonomous Discovery of Multi-Material Metamaterials With Programmable Multimodal Thermal Responses via Reinforcement Learning
10.1002/adma.75546.abstract: ABSTRACT Inverse design deep learning models have significantly accelerated materials discovery through mapping complex structure-property relationships. However, they remain constrained by prohibitive data demands and are limited to in-distribution interpolation designs. Efficient out-of-distribution inverse design under sparse data constraints remains a critical bottleneck. Here we present an inverse design framework integrating Transformer encoder with reinforcement learning (RL) agent. By combining adaptable structural parameterization and hybrid iterative optimization, this framework efficiently navigates the complex, high-dimensional multi-material design landscape with extremely low data dependency (<10 3 samples). The inverse design framework leverages reward-driven mechanism to autonomously evolves multi-material architectures that achieve unseen target thermal deformation behaviors while strictly adhering to manufacturing requirements. Uniquely, the versatility of this framework is demonstrated through the realization of multiple thermal deformation targets, including near-zero, negative, and highly anisotropic thermal expansion, as well as complex multimodal deformations. Experimental validation of fabricated structures further confirms the efficacy of our framework for accelerated on-demand design of multi-material functional architectures.
authors: Chenxi Lu, Kewen Pan, Xingran Li, Zhaohui Qiu, Nianyao Chai, Xuehao Gao, Muhammad Aziz, Lin Li, Chao Wei

10.1002/adma.75544.title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host-Guest Oxygen Reduction
10.1002/adma.75544.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high-performance metal-free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host-guest chemistry strategy based on metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular-level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O 2 . A series of fluorene-based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half-wave potential ( E 1/2 , vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal-free COF-based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host-guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O 2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host-guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high-efficiency metal-free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.
authors: Genfu Zhao, Xiaoxiao Zou, Lebin Cai, Zhemin Gong, Yongjiang Sun, Kai Qi, Bao Yu Xia, Hong Guo

10.1002/adma.75484.title: Scalable and Lithography-Free Fabrication of High-Aspect-Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
10.1002/adma.75484.abstract: ABSTRACT The scalable integration of low-dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography-free top-down etching approach to produce densely distributed high-aspect-ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single-crystal (SCD), and boron-doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2-inch wafer. By correlating time-dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag-initiated, redeposition-sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self-assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen-vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire-assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30-fold increase in electrochemical double-layer capacitance (C dl )-derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5-fold enhancement in pollutant-degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

10.1002/adma.75485.title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single-Atom-Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
10.1002/adma.75485.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite-free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single-atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single-atom-nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination-mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non-equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co-species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d -band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption-energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high-loading Li||LiFePO 4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic-structure regulation in practical LMAs.
authors: Jun Zhang, Yu Dong, Zhenyu Wang, Tongxiang Chen, Xudong Sun, Jing Li, Chenming Zhou, Kai Li, Gang Huang, Zhaolin Na

10.1002/adma.75464.title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
10.1002/adma.75464.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting-edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.
authors: Boyu Zhu, Qian Wang, Licheng Han, Yanfang Wang, Xinwei Wei, Zhen Gu

10.1002/adma.74765.title: From Growth to Performance: Emerging Frontiers in Diamond Materials for High-Performance Devices
10.1002/adma.74765.abstract: ABSTRACT Diamond's ultra-wide bandgap, high carrier mobility, extreme thermal conductivity, and chemical robustness make it a promising platform for next-generation optoelectronic, electronic, photonic, and thermal technologies. This potential is increasingly unlocked by rapid advances in chemical vapor deposition, enabling precise material synthesis and integration. This review adopts a “growth-to-performance” perspective to evaluate emerging frontiers in diamond research. We first highlight critical progress in diamond synthesis, including large-area single crystal and polycrystalline diamond growth, heteroepitaxy, low-temperature deposition, and advanced doping strategies. We then examine how these upstream material advancements directly dictate downstream performance across three core technological pillars. In optoelectronics and electronics, these material breakthroughs enable diamond photodetectors, high-voltage p - n diodes, Schottky barrier diodes, and field-effect transistors based on both p - and n -type diamond channels. In photonics, advances in nanofabrication and heterogeneous integration are expanding diamond's role in nonlinear optics, integrated photonics, and quantum technologies. In thermal management, diamond heat spreaders integrated with wide-bandgap semiconductors, coupled with advances in thermal metrology and phonon-transport modeling, enable superior heat dissipation and reliability. By connecting synthesis with emerging applications, this review outlines the critical pathways through which diamond is poised to play a transformative role in high-performance technologies across electronics, photonics, and thermal management.
authors: Xiang Zhang, Jiangwei Liu, Shuo Sun, Janghan Park, Dongyeon Daniel Kang, Xun Li, Tia Gray, Haolin Zhu, Diego Terrones, Kinfung Ngan, Robert Vajtai, Li Shi, Pulickel M. Ajayan

10.1002/adma.75535.title: “Activation-Resistance Elimination” Regulation by Lanthanide/Transition Metal Ion-Coordinated Nanostructures Intensifies Cuproptosis and Tumor Immunotherapy
10.1002/adma.75535.abstract: ABSTRACT The therapeutic efficacy of cuproptosis is constrained by its insufficient activation and resistance mechanisms. Here, a lanthanide/transition metal ion-coordinated nanoparticle, La-Cu@Lap/IWR-1, with optimized coordination, has been proven to achieve remarkable results in realizing comprehensive resistance-eliminating cuproptosis activation. La 3+ not only enhances Cu 2+ -mediated multiple enzyme-mimetic activities via coordination to amplify oxidative stress but also disrupts lysosomal acidification to improve copper ion availability. Moreover, combined with lapatinib (Lap), it alleviates the shielding effect of mediator of cell motility 1 (MEMO1) on Cu 2+ , significantly strengthening the cuproptosis activation efficacy. Meanwhile, the released Wnt inhibitor IWR-1 can not only inhibit the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway that is concomitantly activated during cuproptosis induction to weaken the oxidative stress tolerance of tumor cells but also synergize with Lap to downregulate hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) expression, thereby effectively eliminating cuproptosis resistance. This comprehensive cuproptosis not only triggers significant immunogenic cell death but also synchronously inhibits key steps of tumor metastasis, such as epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix remodeling. This work proposes a therapeutic strategy for achieving comprehensive resistance-eliminating cuproptosis activation using lanthanide/transition metal ion coordination nanomaterials, providing a new entry point for tumor therapy.
authors: Junrong Wang, Mengqian Xu, Huaping Zhao, Yulin Xie, Guoqing Zhu, Haoze Li, Qianqian Sun, Yong Lei, Chunxia Li

10.1002/adma.75565.title: Nb5+-Induced-CeO2 Lattice Strain for Robust and Scalable Solar-Driven Ammonia Synthesis
10.1002/adma.75565.abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia (NH 3 ) underpins fertilizer production and is emerging as a renewable-energy carrier. Solar-driven gas-phase N 2 /H 2 conversion requires catalysts that couple efficient light utilization with structural stability under H 2 -rich conditions. Here, Nb 5+ incorporation into CeO 2 contracts the lattice and induces compressive microstrain, suppressing excessive oxygen-sublattice reduction and preserving Ru dispersion. In situ NAP-XPS and computational results show that Nb-CeO 2 maintains an electron-enriched Ru working state under reaction conditions, which is further promoted by illumination. Accordingly, 5 wt% Ru/Nb-CeO 2 achieves an NH 3 synthesis rate of 7.4 mmol g −1 h −1 at 350°C and 0.1 MPa and remains stable for 144 h. Kinetic analyses and in situ DRIFTS indicate that the electronically promoted Ru state alleviates N 2 -activation limitations and facilitates subsequent *NH x hydrogenation and NH 3 desorption. Scale-up synthesis affords a 3 wt% Ru/Nb-CeO 2 -L catalyst stable for 480 h and operable under outdoor concentrated sunlight. A screening-level analysis estimates a catalyst-and-feedstock cost of 286-322 USD t NH3 −1 under the lower-bound electricity scenario, 42%-51% below the selected Cs-Ru/MgO benchmark within the same framework. These results identify lattice strain as a promising strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the oxygen sublattice and electronically promoting Ru for efficient solar-driven ammonia synthesis.

10.1002/adma.75574.title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair
10.1002/adma.75574.abstract: ABSTRACT Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre-programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow-degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell-instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non-degrading or fast-degrading hydrogels. Slow-degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long-term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.
authors: Zhiyuan Chen, Tuba Marjan, Xinyue Lu, Nicole E. Mertens, Keira Vesy, Dean E. Stornello, James F. Markworth, Taimoor H. Qazi

10.1002/adma.75562.title: A Magnetic Robotic Platform for Enhanced Stem-Cell-Based Tendon Repair
10.1002/adma.75562.abstract: ABSTRACT Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D-MRI with real-time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering-precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF-mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC-based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.

10.1002/adma.75518.title: Ion-Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All-Solid-State Li-S Batteries
10.1002/adma.75518.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active-material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li 2 S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface-bound ion-electron convergent interphases on the Li 2 S surface that reconstruct localized triple-phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li 2 FeS 2 is identified to form a robust surface-bound interphase with Li 2 S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li 2 S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm −2 while delivering a loading-insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm −2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface-bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion-electron transfer (CIET) in all-solid-state batteries.

10.1002/adma.75566.title: Life-Cycle-Sustainable Capacitive Deionization Enabled by Organic Molecular Engineering for Selective Ammonium Capture
10.1002/adma.75566.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective ammonium (NH 4 + ) recovery from complex wastewater streams remains a pivotal challenge in sustainable nitrogen management. Capacitive deionization (CDI) offers an energy-efficient electrochemical route for ion separation, yet its practical application is constrained by the inherent trade-off between NH 4 + adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we circumvent this fundamental limitation through the rational molecular engineering of an organic electroactive material, 1,4-bis(1H-imidazo[4,5-b]phenazin-2-yl)benzene (IPB), which features extended electron delocalization and abundant C═N moieties for NH 4 + -specific redox-coupled capture. The resulting IPB-based CDI prototype delivers a high NH 4 + adsorption capacity of 267.23 mg g −1 and a fast rate of 62.51 mg g −1 min −1 , while sustaining remarkable selectivity in complex multi-ion matrices, thereby effectively surpassing the conventional capacity-selectivity trade-off. Notably, CDI adsorption reduces wastewater NH 4 + levels to below 3 mg L −1 and achieves 82.3% direct recovery as liquid fertilizer during CDI desorption, as demonstrated by isotope tracing experiments. The CDI process exhibits a low carbon footprint of only 4.66 × 10 −2 t CO 2 -equivalent per tonne of NH 4 + treated, underscoring its superior life-cycle sustainability. Therefore, this work proposes a molecularly engineered organic electrode material for high-performance wastewater remediation and circular nutrient recovery, paving the way toward carbon-neutral electrochemical water treatment technologies.

10.1002/adma.74414.title: Continuous-Conductivity-Gradient All-Organic Aerogels with Machine-Learning-Assisted Design toward Ultrabroadband, Ultralow-Reflection Electromagnetic Shielding
10.1002/adma.74414.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultralow-reflection electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding across broad frequency ranges remains elusive as low reflection and low transmission are rarely achieved simultaneously, particularly in lightweight aerogels amenable to scalable manufacturing. Here, a continuous-conductivity-gradient (CCG) aerogel with machine-learning (ML)-assisted optimization is developed via diffusion-controlled in situ oxidative polymerization of pyrrole within an as-prepared, mechanically resilient porous aramid nanofiber scaffold, followed by an energy-efficient, scalable ambient-pressure-drying strategy. The resulting CCG aerogel integrates a continuous through-thickness gradient of polypyrrole (PPy) with a highly porous architecture, enabling a smooth impedance transition and progressive bulk microwave attenuation for ultrabroadband, ultralow-reflection EMI shielding. The optimized CCG aerogel delivers an effective absorption-dominated frequency bandwidth of 29.76 GHz spanning 10.24-40 GHz, with an EMW reflectivity below 0.1, while maintaining an EMI shielding effectiveness above 40 dB across the ultrabroadband frequency range of 8.2-40 GHz, surpassing the shielding performance of existing EMI shielding materials. Mechanistic analyses reveal that the continuous gradient couples efficient front-surface impedance matching with progressive internal dissipation, thereby circumventing the impedance discontinuities inherent to discrete multilayers. Overall, this ML-assisted strategy integrates novel electromagnetic and structural design with robust, scalable all-organic aerogel manufacturing, offering a general platform for ultrabroadband, ultrahigh-absorption, ultralow-reflection EMI shielding across diverse material systems.

10.1002/adma.75558.title: Supramolecular Stabilization of Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Durable Perovskite-Organic Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75558.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite-organic tandem solar cells (PO-TSCs) offer a compelling platform for flexible photovoltaics by combining wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells with mechanically compliant organic rear cells. However, their long-term stability is critically limited by the intrinsic instability of WBG mixed-halide perovskites. Here, through systematic ageing and mechanistic analyses, we identify halide phase segregation in the WBG perovskite sub-cell under photothermal stress as the dominant degradation pathway that dictates the operational stability of the PO-TSC investigated here. To address this challenge, we develop a halogenated cyclodextrin-based supramolecular strategy that enables precise regulation of perovskite crystallization, defect passivation and halide distribution. Synergistic host-guest, hydrogen-bonding, halogen-bonding and coordination interactions simultaneously regulate crystallization and suppress ion migration to result in stabilized halide homogeneity. Consequently, 1.80-eV WBG devices achieve 20.60% efficiency with improved operational stability. Integrated PO-TSCs deliver an efficiency of 27.17% (certified 26.3%) together with T 80 lifetimes of 1100 h under maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation and T 85 lifetimes of 1128 h under thermal stress of 85°C, while flexible PO-TSCs reach an efficiency of 24.00%. This work defines a general supramolecular design paradigm for efficient, durable and flexible tandem photovoltaics.

10.1002/adma.75534.title: Fundamental Inhibition of Polyiodide Formation by a Site-Separated Binder for Highly Stable Aqueous Zinc-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/adma.75534.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Zn-I 2 batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage systems, yet their practical performance is severely limited by the formation and shuttling of polyiodide intermediates. Here, we report a site separation strategy to block the generation paths of polyiodides and address the related issues from the source. This is realized with a site-separated polymer (SSP) binder that strongly and selectively confines I 2 and I − at varied functional groups on different side chains. It disrupts their coupling to generate polyiodides chemically. Meanwhile, these effective interactions regulate the thermodynamic features of iodine species, which disfavors the formation of polyiodide intermediates and promotes direct I 2 /I − conversion during electrochemical reactions. The binder also reinforces cathode integrity at different iodine loadings. Therefore, the I 2 /SSP cathode delivers 212 mAh g −1 capacity at 0.2 A g −1 and retains 102 mAh g −1 at 50 A g −1 , superior to 172 mAh g −1 /11 mAh g −1 with the conventional polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. I 2 /SSP also realizes 97.1% capacity retention over 31000 cycles at 20 A g −1 , again far exceeding 46.8% after 20000 cycles for I 2 /PVDF. Under a high iodine loading of 50 mg cm −2 , the I 2 /SSP cathode further achieves 10.1 mAh cm −2 capacity with 97.9% retention over 400 cycles.
authors: Guoli Zhang, Haoren Zheng, Xinkai Liang, Ping Lu, Xiao-Xia Liu, Xiaoqi Sun

10.1002/adma.75019.title: Thermo-Optically Engineered Radiative Cooling Materials With Tailored Thermal Conduction
10.1002/adma.75019.abstract: ABSTRACT Radiative cooling, featuring zero-energy operation and compatibility with global decarbonization, is a promising route for passive thermal management. Despite major progress over the past few years, advances in radiative cooling have mainly focused on spectral modulation, while the role of thermal conduction in determining practical cooling performance remains far less systematically understood. In fact, different thermal conduction modes can influence radiative cooling in distinct ways by either limiting parasitic heat gain from the environment or enabling heat dissipation from internal sources. Accordingly, radiative cooling materials need to be systematically examined through the lens of tailored thermal conduction. Here, we first analyze the coupling mechanisms between radiative cooling and three different thermal-conduction modes, namely thermal insulation, enhanced heat conduction, and thermal rectification, and further quantitatively clarify the effects of thermal conduction under different operating conditions, together with the distinct roles of in-plane and through-plane thermal transport and system-level thermal resistance. Building on these mechanisms, we survey recent developments in thermo-optically engineered radiative cooling materials and their implementation. We further discuss the potential of these different coupling mechanisms in diverse applications. Finally, we identify unresolved challenges and promising research directions for advancing radiative cooling technologies with tailored thermal conduction.

10.1002/adma.74945.title: Ultrafast Charge Transfer Driven by Strong Adsorption: An Efficient Interfacial Strategy for Photocatalysis
10.1002/adma.74945.abstract: ABSTRACT In practical photocatalysis, the strong interaction between surface adsorbates and the cocatalyst is unavoidable, which inevitably triggers a reconfiguration of its electronic structure. However, how this strong adsorption-induced electronic state reconfiguration (SA-ESR) affects the ultrafast charge transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. To fill this gap, we deliberately introduced thiocyanate ions (SCN − ) as a model adsorbate, which selectively adsorb onto the Au nanoparticles deposited on CdZnS, thereby establishing a well-defined strong-adsorption system to probe how such SA-ESR effect governs the ultrafast charge transfer kinetics during photocatalytic H 2 evolution. Comprehensive investigations reveal that the strongly adsorbed SCN − effectively withdraws electrons from Au, inducing an electronic state reconfiguration to form electron-deficient Au δ+ . Such SA-ESR effect efficiently promotes ultrafast photoelectron transfer from CdZnS to the Au cocatalysts, thereby accelerating the overall charge transfer kinetics and ultimately boosting the photocatalytic H 2 -evolution performance. Consequently, the optimized CdZnS/Au-S system (0.05 mM SCN − , pH = 2) achieves an outstanding H 2 -production rate of 8.33 mmol g −1 h −1 with visible hydrogen bubble evolution. This work clarifies the deterministic role of strong surface adsorption in driving ultrafast charge kinetics, providing practical insights for the precision design of highly efficient photocatalytic architectures.
authors: Pinsi Deng, Duoduo Gao, Jianjun Zhang, Chuanbiao Bie, Bei Cheng, Jiaguo Yu, Huogen Yu

10.1002/adma.75132.title: 120-Channel High-Fidelity Optical Multiplexing Using a Minimal Meta-Atom Set
10.1002/adma.75132.abstract: ABSTRACT High-capacity optical multiplexing is crucial for next-generation intelligent information systems, spanning high-speed communications, optical computing, and immersive displays. A fundamental challenge is to maximize the number of independent channels while maintaining high fidelity, compact footprint, and low structural complexity, constraints that severely limit existing diffractive optical elements. Here, we overcome these long-standing trade-offs by introducing a multi-dimensional reconfigurable diffractive neural network (MRDNN) that enables high-capacity, high-fidelity optical multiplexing within an exceptionally compact and simple architecture through the co-design of predictive neural optimization and multi-physical-dimension multiplexing. Experimentally, a dual-layer MRDNN realizes 24 independent channels for distinct functionalities, including focusing, beam steering, and holographic image reconstruction. Owing to its excellent scalability, only four metasurface layers comprising a minimal library of 200 2 meta-atoms achieve 120 distinct optical channels with low crosstalk and high fidelity (measured mean structural similarity index measure of over 0.8), representing a record experimental multiplexing capacity with one of the smallest normalized footprints and simplest structural configurations in a metasurface-enabled system. This work establishes a scalable and efficient paradigm for extreme optical multiplexing in multifunctional and reconfigurable photonics systems.
authors: Zhiyu Tan, Xiaofei Zang, Zhe Gao, Jianshu Miao, Alexander P. Shkurinov, Fei Ding, Yiming Zhu, Songlin Zhuang

10.1002/adma.75551.title: Multi-Hydrogen Adsorption as a Dynamic Electronic Gate for Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer
10.1002/adma.75551.abstract: ABSTRACT Reactive materials operate under dynamically evolving adsorption environments, yet how cooperative adsorbates reshape interfacial electronic structure and charge-transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. Here we show that multi-hydrogen adsorption can function as a dynamic electronic gate that reprograms interfacial charge-transfer energetics. Using a sulfur-rich amorphous CoReS 2+x cocatalyst as a model system, we demonstrate that abundant unsaturated sulfur sites enable cooperative multi-hydrogen adsorption, which induces spontaneous electron delocalization and generates an electron-deficient interfacial state. This adsorption-driven electronic redistribution reverses the thermodynamic directionality of electron injection from CdZnS, converting an originally endothermic process into a spontaneous one. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals that the gated interface accelerates interfacial electron transfer to the ultrafast regime, in agreement with first-principles calculations. The resulting a-CoReS 2+x /CdZnS system achieves highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from biomass-derived formic acid with an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.8%. More broadly, these findings establish multi-adsorbate-induced electronic gating as a general mechanism for dynamically programming interfacial charge transfer in catalytic and energy-conversion materials operating under realistic reactive environments.
authors: Duoduo Gao, Pinsi Deng, Chuanbiao Bie, Jianjun Zhang, Weilai Yu, Huogen Yu

10.1002/adma.75335.title: Engineering Li+ Transport in Ni-Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization
10.1002/adma.75335.abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel-rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next-generation lithium-ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg −1 , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li + transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li + transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo-mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li + transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport-centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross-scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport-centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next-generation high-energy-density cathode materials.
authors: Lili Lin, Min Du, Jiatao Lou, Ziqiang Wang

10.1002/adma.75500.title: Kirigami-Inspired Stretchable Silicon Solar Cell Modules as Portable Power Sources
10.1002/adma.75500.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of photovoltaic modules into wearable electronic devices represents a pivotal advancement for enhancing portability and sustainability. Despite their high efficiency and stability, traditional silicon solar modules are brittle, preventing their applications in mechanically flexible and impact-resistant wearable devices. Herein, we present a novel approach to deformable silicon solar cell modules of different sizes utilizing flexible kirigami-structured substrates integrating commercial silicon cells, enabling durability against continuous deformations caused by body movements. For instance, our Module-14-7S2P, consisting of 14 silicon solar cells, exhibits a power output of 37.50 mW while maintaining > 95% power retention of its original power output after 5000 deformation cycles and > 94% power retention after 120 h of water immersion. Furthermore, upon deformation to a 13% strain, this module retains ∼80% of the initial power output, data supported by FEA simulations. Our study provides new possibilities for employing silicon solar cells in wearable applications, accelerating the adoption of sustainable and portable wearable electronic devices powered by solar energy.
authors: Yusheng Zhang, Chenyi Zhang, Pei Wang, Yetai Cheng, Qi Liang, Yonghuan Li, Zhengdong Wei, Huanyu Zhou, Xinyi Kong, Minghua Li, Yifan Wang, Zhishan Bo, Yuqiang Liu, Antonio Facchetti

10.1002/adma.75533.title: Fundamental Design Principles and Engineering Strategies of Liquid-Phase Electrolytes for Highly Durable Rechargeable Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75533.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal has emerged as the premier anode candidate in next-generation high-energy-density batteries due to its ultrahigh theoretical capacity and ultralow electrochemical potential. However, critical technical barriers persist in Li metal anode implementation, such as uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and persistent interfacial side reactions. Acting as the mediating agent between cathodes and anodes, electrolytes critically determine battery overall performance. Taking solvent-salt-additive components as the entry point, adopting liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies to optimize electrolyte composition and regulate solvation structure can not only address the inherent issues of Li metal anodes, but also endow Li metal batteries with desired performances, including high safety, high-voltage tolerance, fast-charging capability, and wide-temperature operation. In this review, the design principles of reliable liquid-phase electrolytes for Li metal batteries are discussed in detail. The essential liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies, including designing new-type salt/solvent molecular architectures, restructuring salt-solvent combination systems, incorporating electrolyte additives with various functions, utilizing (localized) high-concentration electrolytes, and developing brand-new electrolyte formulations for adapting to different temperature ranges, are comprehensively summarized. Moreover, emerging design strategies, future design considerations, and remaining challenges in electrolyte engineering are highlighted, with the aim of pointing out potential opportunities to propel the practical development of Li metal batteries.

10.1002/adma.75513.title: Near-Infrared Imaging of H2O2 in Plants With Nanosensors Under Environmentally Changing Conditions
10.1002/adma.75513.abstract: ABSTRACT Optical sensors are powerful tools to monitor biological systems. However, their practical deployment is often limited by environmental interferences such as autofluorescence, mechanical motion, and fluctuating illumination. These challenges are particularly pronounced in plants because they require and use light, which has impaired the use of (fluorescent) sensors for plant stress signals such as H 2 O 2 . Here, we present a ratiometric sensing platform that overcomes these limitations by integrating three spectrally distinct components: 1) an H 2 O 2 sensor based on aptamer modified near infrared (NIR) fluorescent single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs, ∼1000 nm), 2) a stable NIR reference based on polyethyleneglycol modified Egyptian Blue nanosheets (EB-NS, 900-955 nm) and 3) a visible (VIS) signal (∼641 nm) to correct for the NIR autofluorescence tail of plants (>835 nm). This ratiometric approach enables robust signal correction under relevant perturbations, including leaf rotation and wind-induced motion. Furthermore, it allows continuous H 2 O 2 monitoring under dynamically varying illumination conditions (>300%), resulting in a 75% enhancement in signal contrast compared to single-channel detection. By spectrally resolving nanosensor signals and endogenous plant autofluorescence, this strategy enables in vivo monitoring of stress-induced H 2 O 2 under realistic environmental conditions. It establishes interference-resistant optical sensing and advances field-deployable nanosensor technologies for precision agriculture.
authors: Jiaqi Li, Bjoern F. Hill, Chen Ma, Juliana Gretz, Tanuja Kistwal, Janus A. C. Wartmann, Justus T. Metternich, Juan Pablo Giraldo, Sebastian Kruss

10.1002/adma.74989.title: Dynamic Disentanglement Enables Highly Crystalline Fluorinated Polyimide Films Featuring Superior Dielectric Property and Intrinsic Thermal Conductivity
10.1002/adma.74989.abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of high-frequency communication and miniaturized electronics necessitates dielectric materials that combine high intrinsic thermal conductivity ( λ ) with low dielectric loss ( D f ) to mitigate signal delay and thermal accumulation. Conventional strategies, particularly nanocomposite approaches, often struggle to simultaneously achieve high λ and low D f without compromising processability or mechanical integrity. Herein, a semicrystalline polyimide (TAHQ/TFMB) architecture is initially established by circumventing the amorphous nature of fluorinated systems via rigid-rod backbone design and programmed thermal processing. Subsequently, minor dynamically exchangeable siloxane segments (≤ 1 mol%) act as molecular disentanglement switches, triggering topological rearrangement that promotes the formation of widely distributed crystal nuclei and enables the subsequent development of large-scale crystalline domains, ultimately yielding an enhanced crystallinity exceeding 50%. The optimally designed film with merely 0.25 mol% siloxane exhibits an enhanced in-plane λ of 2.33 W·m −1 ·K −1 and an ultralow D f of 0.00142 at 10 GHz. This synergy facilitates the first realization of a broadband thermoacoustic generator featuring an all-organic substrate and a flexible hairpin bandpass filter with excellent signal transmission performance. Furthermore, the DBPI-0.25 film exhibits excellent thermal stability ( T d5% = 478.3°C), superior moisture resistance (water uptake of 0.41%), and good mechanical flexibility, rendering it highly suitable for advanced microelectronics.
authors: Zhuang Nie, Xin Wang, Xiaodi Dong, Hongxiang Li, Gehong Su, Zhihui Xie, Yue Zhang, Xiaoyu Mu, Longbo Luo, Junwei Zha, Yi Zhang, Xiangyang Liu, Xu Wang

10.1002/adma.74996.title: Gradient Gyroid Aerogels With Programmable Multiscale Pore Architectures and Fibrillated Loss Networks for Electromagnetic, Thermal/Fire, and Mechanical Protection
10.1002/adma.74996.abstract: ABSTRACT Airborne electronic systems operating in extreme environments require lightweight protective materials that combine efficient electromagnetic attenuation, thermal protection, and mechanical robustness. However, conventional aerogel absorbers typically rely on pore engineering at a single length scale, making it difficult to simultaneously optimize these properties. Herein, we develop a decoupled multiscale structural engineering strategy based on a custom-built freeze-printing platform, in which pore structures at different length scales are regulated through distinct mechanisms and subsequently integrated into a hierarchical Gyroid architecture spanning from the nanoscale to the millimeter scale. Notably, the amino-functionalized metal-organic framework employed for nanopore regulation can also intercalate between MXene nanosheets through interactions between its amino groups and the polar surface terminations of MXene, thereby suppressing nanosheet restacking, generating abundant MX@MOF heterointerfaces, and realizing the coupling of structural regulation and functionality. Building on these heterointerfaces, trypan blue directs PPy growth from discrete particles into fibrillar bridges, linking MX@MOF units into continuous conductive pathways enriched with electromagnetic-loss sites. As a result, the optimized CS-4 aerogel achieved a minimum reflection loss of −71.5 dB at only 2.45 mm and an effective absorption bandwidth of 6.26 GHz, while maintaining excellent thermal insulation, compressive strength, flame retardancy, and smoke suppression.
authors: Xiuhong Sun, Kangkang Gao, Jinhu Hu, Zhaolu Qin, Tao Lin, Mingliang Ma, Jiacheng Ma, Fan Wu, Wenhuan Huang, Ye-Tang Pan

10.1002/adma.75597.title: Waveguided, Self-Sensing Sheath-Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
10.1002/adma.75597.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard-to-access environments, while providing integrated self-sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next-generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath-core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near-infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load-bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real-time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self-sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

10.1002/adma.75579.title: Air-Stable Radical Additives Modulate Spin-Dependent Recombination in High-Efficiency Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75579.abstract: ABSTRACT Triplet-associated recombination remains a potential loss channel in high-efficiency nonfullerene organic solar cells, particularly when separated charges re-encounter to form spin-correlated charge-transfer or polaron-pair states. Here, we introduce the air-stable organic radical TTM-1Cz as an additive to manipulate the triplet formation by the single electron-occupied doublet state characteristic of radicals. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurements confirm that the radical character of TTM-1Cz is retained after solution processing. Grazing-incidence wide-angle x-ray scattering measurements show that TTM-1Cz and its structurally related closed-shell analogue α HTTM-1Cz induce comparable, modest increases in crystalline coherence, indicating a structural contribution associated with the common molecular framework. In contrast, charge-separated-state-normalized transient absorption spectroscopy reveals a pronounced reduction in the late-time triplet-associated signal only in the TTM-1Cz-containing blend. Together with magneto-photocurrent measurements and local molecular-complex calculations, these observations are consistent with an additional, radical-specific perturbation of spin-dependent charge-transfer recombination. The optimized D18:L8-BO:TTM-1Cz device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.63%, with a certified efficiency of 20.45%. These results reveal a design principle for radical additives in organic solar cells, in which molecular-packing effects and spin-active modulation of recombination act as distinct but complementary contributions.

10.1002/adma.75585.title: Dynamic Molecular Scaffold Enables Thermomechanical Stress Regulation and Adaptive Defect Healing for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75585.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermally induced stress accumulation is a major origin of lattice disorder, defect evolution, and ion migration in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), limiting their long-term operational stability. We develop a dynamic molecular scaffold strategy based on the adduct of α-lipoic acid and N-hydroxysuccinimide ester to mitigate thermomechanical degradation through simultaneous thermomechanical stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing. During film formation, DL-α-lipoic acid-N-hydroxysuccinimide ester (LA-NHS) undergoes in situ polymerization to establish a crosslinked polydisulfide scaffold at grain boundaries. The dynamic scaffold accommodates thermally induced lattice expansion and contraction, dissipates accumulated stress, anchors the perovskite lattice, and continuously passivates stress-generated defects through reversible disulfide-bond exchange, thereby preserving lattice ordering and improving the thermal durability. Consequently, the optimized PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.19%. The devices retain 91.71% of their initial efficiency after 150 thermal cycles between 15°C and 100°C, and 85.72% after 1500 h at 85°C. The strategy is successfully translated to large-area PSCs (25.02% for 1 cm 2 and 22.06% for 10 × 10 cm 2 ). This work establishes a dynamic molecularscaffold framework for managing thermomechanical degradation through stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing, providing a route toward efficient, durable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

10.1002/adma.75571.title: Maleimide-Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic-Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adma.75571.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals. The regulation of biotic-abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide-functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI-gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio-interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis , resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23-fold increase in electron transfer and a 6-fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis . Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non-covalent group, yielding a 2-fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2-fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI-gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio-interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic-abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk-adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular-level interface engineering.

10.1002/adma.75568.title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt-Free Ultrahigh-Ni Cathodes
10.1002/adma.75568.abstract: ABSTRACT Eliminating Co from ultrahigh-Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li + transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics-guided defect-engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt-free ultrahigh-Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high-valence dopants reveals that Te 6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi 0.948 Al 0.045 Te 0.007 O 2 containing coherent local antisite-ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2-H3 phase separation and c -axis contraction, and preserve low-barrier Li + migration pathways. Local Te-O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen-loss-induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g −1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability-transport trade-off in cobalt-free ultrahigh-Ni layered cathodes.

10.1002/adma.75594.title: Layered Precursor-Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In2O3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
10.1002/adma.75594.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor-guided synthesis of atom-thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance-voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 . We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement-mode transistors with sub-3 nm channels, featuring near-zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate-stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high-performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next-generation nanoelectronics.

10.1002/adma.75601.title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming
10.1002/adma.75601.abstract: ABSTRACT Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten-salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI-K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano-derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole-polaron absorption and extends the average exciton-associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap-assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI-K photoreforms alkaline-pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target-product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H 2 evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g −1 h −1 , with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two-electron oxidation of surface-bound α-hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

10.1002/adma.75554.title: Water-Heat Synergistic Regulation to Optimize Water State and Enhance Thermal Effect in Solar Interfacial Evaporation
10.1002/adma.75554.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar-driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This work proposes a strategy to synergistically enhance the heat and mass transport of solar interfacial evaporators by balancing water transport capacity and water activity and reverse heat compensation. A higher proportion of loosely bound intermediate water (IW) with low enthalpy of vaporization is induced by in situ construction of a hydrophilic micron-to-submicron hierarchical pore structure within the wood-based biomass framework, while maintaining its water pumping capacity. Simultaneously, a biomimetic thermal compensation mechanism significantly enhances the thermal effect of the wood-based biomass evaporation interface (temperature up to 50.7°C). This synergistic design enables a record evaporation rate of 5.12 kg m −2 h −1 in wood-based evaporators. Furthermore, the vertically distributed hierarchical pore structure and surface polar groups endow it with excellent salt repellency and antifouling capabilities. This reported water-heat management strategy provides a scalable, low-cost, and environmentally friendly approach to highly efficient solar interfacial evaporation.
authors: Jian Li, Yang Wang, Ling Wang, Pengcheng Lin, Yimeng Du, Ying Chen

10.1002/adma.75538.title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti-Ambipolar Characteristics in n-Type Organic Mixed-Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons
10.1002/adma.75538.abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio-realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long-term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti-ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti-ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF-ON-OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC electronics strategy to improve device performance and enable tunability, yet unexplored for improving anti-ambipolar stability in non-ladder-type anti-ambipolar materials. Here, the n-type OMIEC, P(gNDI-gT2), is blended with the insulating polymer, PMMA, yielding stable anti-ambipolar characteristics. The miscibility in solution forms a mechanically stabilizing and ion-permeable framework in the solid state that considerably reduces swelling-induced structural damage, thus preventing dramatic failure after the first operation cycles without compromising the conductive polymer's electronic pathways. Modulating the polymer blend ratio enables low-power, fast-spiking Hodgkin-Huxley neurons with tunable and programmable dynamics, without optimized device geometries, demonstrating frequency deconvolution and reservoir computing. These two computing primitive building blocks are essential for designing efficient spiking neural networks.

10.1002/adma.75576.title: Bottom-Cell Engineering as the Key to Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75576.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have emerged as a highly promising thin-film photovoltaic architecture, combining the exceptional efficiency potential of perovskites with the industrial maturity of CIGS technology. Despite rapid advances in perovskite top cells, overall tandem performance remains fundamentally constrained by the CIGS bottom cell, which critically governs bandgap matching, voltage losses, and interfacial recombination. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent progress in CIGS absorber and interface engineering for tandem applications. We highlight key strategies including Ga-gradient bandgap engineering, alkali post-deposition treatment, Ag alloying for low-temperature growth and bifacial operation, as well as buffer-layer and intermediate recombination layer optimization. We further discuss how surface morphology and defect chemistry collectively dictate carrier recombination dynamics and interfacial stability in monolithic device architectures. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward the commercialization of perovskite/CIGS tandem photovoltaics. By linking materials-level engineering with device-level constraints, this review establishes a unified framework to guide the development of high-efficiency, scalable, and industrially viable tandem solar technologies.
authors: Ming Yang, Yue Zhou, Qi Henry Chen, Junbo Gong, Dongxu Lin, Weimin Li, Yaohua Mai, Pengfei Huang, Qi Chen, Yan Jiang

10.1002/adma.75578.title: From Water Vapor Transmission Rate (WVTR) to Intrinsic Water Vapor Permeability (WVP)
10.1002/adma.75578.abstract: ABSTRACT Water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) is widely used to assess breathability in skin-interfaced electronics. In gravimetric wet-cup tests, however, the measured flux depends on transport through both the membrane and the apparatus. Apparatus resistance can dominate measurements of highly permeable membranes. Evaporation, headspace transport, membrane permeation, and external vapor spreading are modeled as resistances in series under a common chemical-potential driving force. The apparatus coefficients are calibrated using open-cup measurements in the same setup, independently of the reference permeability. For poly(dimethylsiloxane) membranes, where membrane resistance dominates, both a literature air-gap correction and the calibrated model reduce deviations from the reference. For a highly permeable anion-exchange membrane (AEM), the air-gap correction becomes unstable. Relative to a dynamic sweep-cell reference, the calibrated model reduces mean absolute relative deviation from 49.8% for classical conversion to 6.2%. It also provides model-based criteria for geometry selection and measurement duration, together with a procedure for converting WVTR to water vapor permeability (WVP).

10.1002/adma.74519.title: Multifunctional Electrode/Neural Integration Interface Enabling Chronic High-Fidelity Neural Recording and an Order-of-Magnitude Neuromodulation Quality
10.1002/adma.74519.abstract: ABSTRACT Neural electrodes face persistent challenges, including inflammation, biofouling, and impedance, which compromise long-term recording and stimulation quality. Here, we introduced a multifunctional polyamino acid interface that enhances neural interfacing by combining biocompatibility, antimicrobial activity, and antifouling properties. Applied to flexible electrodes, this coating reduces foreign body reaction and preserves neuronal proximity, ensuring stable integration with brain tissue. In chronic rodent models, functionalized electrodes achieve high-fidelity single-unit recordings for over 300 days with significantly higher spike amplitudes and yield than bare controls. Notably, the interface enables an order-of-magnitude improvement in neuromodulation efficiency, evoking robust motor responses at only 2 µA compared to 100 µA for uncoated probes. Multi-omics analysis reveals a molecularly profound alteration in the host tissue response, transitioning from a pro-inflammatory injury signature to an attenuated inflammatory state with improved tissue homeostasis. Furthermore, the interface's resistance to biological “cementing” facilitates damage-free electrode removal and recovery, preserving the neural architecture and enabling the possibility of chronic replacement. This universal platform offers a promising and practical strategy for the next generation of stable, clinically viable neural-computer interfaces.

10.1002/adma.75590.title: Re(I)-Based Molecular Actuator-Equipped Nanomotors for Integrated Photodynamic and Photomechanical Therapy of Solid Tumor
10.1002/adma.75590.abstract: ABSTRACT The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen-dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through molecular engineering, we develop a Janus nanomotor ( Re1@NMs ) that integrates a three-dimensional rhenium(I)-based molecular actuator ( Re1 ) with glucose oxidase (GOx)-powered propulsion. Owing to the Janus structure, asymmetric GOx-catalyzed glucose consumption generates local chemical gradients that fuel autonomous motility, thereby enhancing intratumoral distribution. Upon light activation, the engineered Re1 , screened from six Re(I) complexes, functions both as a dual Type I/II photosensitizer generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) to induce oxidative stress and as a molecular actuator whose Y -axis motif undergoes E / Z photoisomerization and torsional deformation, thereby contributing to membrane permeabilization. The resulting integrated mechano-photodynamic action coordinately activates ferroptosis and pyroptosis. In a murine tumor model, Re1@NMs -mediated phototherapy achieves superior tumor suppression with excellent biosafety and further elicits robust antitumor immunity, as evidenced by enhanced dendritic cell maturation, increased tumor-infiltrating T cells, elevated effector cytokine expression, and damage-associated molecular pattern release. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first integration of a deliberately engineered metal-complex-based three-dimensional molecular actuator with a tumor-microenvironment-adaptive nanomotor, establishing a new paradigm for overcoming tumor barriers.

10.1002/adma.75600.title: Realizing Reversible Photo-Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS 2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo-Rechargeable Batteries
10.1002/adma.75600.abstract: ABSTRACT Photo-rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo-batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo-assisted charging, whereas light-only photo-charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo-charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo-charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo-charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS 2 by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS 2 . Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self-discharge current and the photo-charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn 2+ photo-batteries that can be reversibly photo-charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo-rechargeable batteries could realize a photo-charging capacity ratio of 100% by 2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest-conversion-storage mini-system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.

10.1002/adma.75592.title: Submolecular Selenium Enables Low-Pressure and Recyclable All-Solid-State Li-Se Batteries
10.1002/adma.75592.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium-selenium (Li-Se) batteries offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their practical deployment is hindered by sluggish solid-state redox kinetics, large volume fluctuations, and unstable solid-solid interfaces, particularly under low stack pressure. Here we report a submolecular Se x cathode by converting crystalline cyclo-Se 8 into amorphous single-atom and short-chain Se (Se x , x < 4) species anchored on graphene (Se x @G), which increases the electronic conductivity from 6.3 × 10 −5 to 13 S cm −1 and Li + diffusivity from 1.7 × 10 −14 to 2.0 × 10 −11 cm 2 s −1 . Meanwhile, a Li 2 O-nanoshell-modified sulfide solid electrolyte is designed to stabilize the interface against both Li metal and Se cathode. As a result, all-solid-state Li-Se batteries deliver the theoretical capacity of 673 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retain 86% capacity over 2800 cycles at 3 C under 8 MPa, with stable operation down to −30°C. All-solid-state Li-Se pouch cells further achieve an energy density of 420 Wh kg −1 and 94% capacity retention after 300 cycles under 2.5 MPa. Post-mortem analysis reveals that the submolecular Se x species are not only structurally preserved but also recyclable after electrochemical cycling within the solid-state reaction environment. This work establishes submolecular chalcogen chemistry as a new design paradigm for low-pressure, recyclable, and high-energy all-solid-state batteries.
