10.1002/adma.75595.title: Underlying Mechanisms of Helicobacter pylori in Caries Progression and the Corresponding Dual-Responsive Hydrogel-Based Intervention
10.1002/adma.75595.abstract: ABSTRACT Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infects nearly half of the global population. Given that H. pylori is considered poorly adapted to the oral environment, previous studies have mainly focused on gastric infection. By contrast, how H. pylori persists in the oral cavity and relates to oral diseases remains unclear. This study investigates the role of H. pylori in caries progression. The results show that H. pylori is retained within Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ) biofilms, and its presence is associated with transcriptional remodeling in S. mutans , alongside increased overall cariogenic potential of the mixed biofilm. In a rat caries model, H. pylori co-colonization aggravates caries progression and oral microbiota dysbiosis. To address this pathological niche, a multifunctional hydrogel, termed GPAM, is designed by integrating a Cu 2 O@Pt heterojunction (MCP) with amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP). Under activation by yellow light and ultrasound, MCP generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) to disrupt S. mutans-H. pylori mixed biofilms. Meanwhile, released Cu 2+ reduces H. pylori urease activity, and ACP promotes tooth remineralization. GPAM also shows microbiota-modulating potential. Together, these findings provide insight into H. pylori -associated caries progression and support GPAM as a multifunctional therapeutic strategy for mixed biofilms and caries-related damage.

10.1002/adma.73801.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Polarization-Lattice Decoupling Enables Ultrahigh Energy Storage in Lead-Free Dielectric Ceramics
10.1002/adma.73801.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving ultrahigh energy storage in lead-free dielectric ceramics is fundamentally constrained by the intrinsic trade-off between large polarization and high dielectric breakdown strength. Here, we establish an interpretable machine-learning-guided design framework that quantitatively links ionic descriptors with polarization behavior in ABO 3 -based dielectric matrices, enabling the rational identification of compositions with intrinsically high polarization potential. Guided by this strategy, a (Bi 0.275 Na 0.2255 K 0.0495 Ba 0.3 )(Ti 0.985 Hf 0.015 )O 3 -0.15(La 0.5 Sm 0.5 ) 2 Ti 2 O 7 (BNBT-3) composition is discovered that exhibits an exceptional maximum polarization of 50.19 µC cm −2 . When processed via a viscous polymer process, the resulting BNBT-3-VPP capacitors achieve an ultrahigh breakdown strength of 1400 kV cm −1 and a recoverable energy density of 25.1 J cm −3 with high efficiency, placing them among the best-performing lead-free dielectric ceramics reported to date. Structural characterization combined with phase-field simulations reveals that the outstanding performance originates from polarization-lattice decoupling, where nanoscale polarization clusters and multiphase coexistence suppress long-range ferroelectric order while enabling reversible polarization rotation. This work establishes a generalizable strategy that integrates interpretable machine learning with physically grounded materials design, providing a powerful route for discovering high-performance dielectric energy storage materials.

10.1002/adma.75521.title: Lignin-Based Supramolecular Dynamic Networks: A General Platform for Energy Harvesting and Sensing
10.1002/adma.75521.abstract: ABSTRACT Lignin- based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio-based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. The ionogel exhibits an elongation at break of 1564%, underwater adhesion strength of 488.3 kPa on steel, and near complete self-healing at room temperature. It further functions as a strain sensor with a gauge factor of 2.83 and stable signal output over 350 stretching cycles. When assembled into a triboelectric nanogenerator, the ionogel delivers a stable voltage output of 75 V under deformation. This work establishes a lignin derived dynamic ionogel platform that integrates robustness, adaptability, sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting for sustainable flexible electronics.

10.1002/adma.75616.title: Selective Hydrogen Transport Through Polymeric Fullerene Nanosheet Membranes
10.1002/adma.75616.abstract: ABSTRACT Lamellar membranes, assembled from two-dimensional (2D) nanosheets, have attracted intensive attention for molecular and ion sieving due to their tunable interlayer channels and ultrathin selective layers. However, molecular transport in conventional lamellar membranes usually occurs through interlayer galleries whose dimensions vary with stacking, limiting ångström-scale control over selectivity. Therefore, developing a novel lamellar membrane with ångström-scale in-plane pores is highly desirable. In an idealized qTP lattice, four-directionally connected fullerene cages define periodically distributed apertures that converge from an approximately 5.87 Å entrance to a 3.11 Å waist. Upon assembly, the constriction regions can discriminate by size, while their converging entrances and the intersheet galleries govern molecular access and transport resistance through the in-plane apertures. The resulting polymeric fullerene nanosheet membrane exhibits an H 2 permeance of 3896 ± 107 GPU and an H 2 /CO 2 separation factor of 88.5 ± 5.9 for the separation of an equimolar H 2 /CO 2 mixture at 303.15 K and a total feed pressure of 100 kPa. The separation performance remains stable over 200 h of operation. This study establishes topology-encoded pore geometry as a design principle for integrating short selective pathways with ångström-scale molecular discrimination in lamellar membranes.

10.1002/adma.75613.title: Dichlorobenzodithiophene-4-8-dione Derived Polymer Donor Enables Efficient Thin-Film/Thick-Film Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75613.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer donors with electron-withdrawing benzodithiophene-4-8-dione (BDD) unit play an important role in improving power-conversion-efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs), although these achievements rely on high-cost electron-donating fluorinated thienyl-benzodithiophene (BDTT) moiety. Herein, a dichlorobenzodithiophene-4-8-dione (BDD2Cl) unit is developed to design fluorine-free BDTT- alt -BDD2Cl-structured cost-effective polymer donor (PBDTT-BDD2Cl). Compared to its halogen-free BDTT- alt -BDD-structured control (PBDB-T), PBDTT-BDD2Cl shows deep-shifted energy levels, improved solubility, crystallinity, and packing, tending to suppress energy loss, manipulate film-forming kinetics, and improve charge transport properties. Accordingly, the PBDTT-BDD2Cl:L8-BO device demonstrates dramatically higher photovoltage (0.947 V) and lower non-radiative energy loss (0.182 eV) and compared to the PBDB-T:L8-BO device (0.735 and 0.369 eV), while it achieves decreased PCE. When incorporating it into D18:L8-BO host, ternary D18:PBDTT-BDD2Cl:L8-BO shows optimized donor/acceptor miscibility, delayed material nucleation, and prolonged molecular ordered packing duration, leading to boosted charge dynamics and favorable morphology. Thereby, thin-film (100 nm) OSC achieves a superior PCE (21.1%, certified as 20.6%, ranking among the highest values) than the D18:PBDB-T:L8-BO control (19.3%), while its thick-film (500 nm) device also obtains a top-high PCE (17.3%) among these reported thick-films (≥500 nm). This work highlights that BDD2Cl is an ideal candidate for developing cost-effective polymer donors toward efficient thin-film/thick-film OSCs.

10.1002/adma.75583.title: Homojunction Back Contacts Enable Efficient Cu2O Photocathodes
10.1002/adma.75583.abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing carrier separation and extraction is crucial to achieve efficient metal oxide photoelectrodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Here, we report a highly efficient Cu 2 O photocathode based on p + /p back-contact homojunction. The homojunction significantly enhances hole-selective extraction while suppressing electron backflow at the back-contact interface, leading to marked improvements in PEC performance. The optimized photocathode delivers a hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) onset potential of 1.1 V and a saturated photocurrent density of ∼8.0 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the p + /p back homojunction design enables the fabrication of a semi-transparent Cu 2 O photocathode, which, when integrated with a perovskite solar cell in a tandem configuration, achieves a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 7.31%. This work demonstrates a viable strategy for advancing metal oxide photoelectrodes via homojunction engineering.

10.1002/adma.75614.title: High-Mobility p-Type TexSe1-x Films With Yb-Enabled Oxidation Suppression for Short-Wave Infrared Imaging Detection
10.1002/adma.75614.abstract: ABSTRACT Scalable high-mobility p-type semiconductor films hold considerable promise for advancing the performance of both photoelectronic devices and complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technologies. Currently, tellurium (Te)-based semiconductors exhibit high intrinsic hole mobility and compatibility with low-temperature processing, making them promising candidates for cost-effective p-type materials. However, owing to their low Gibbs free energy, they are prone to oxidation into TeO 2 , which introduces deep-level defects and severely degrades hole transport, thereby hindering practical applications. Here, we present an effective antioxidant strategy based on ytterbium (Yb) doping, wherein the strong Te-Yb bonding and high oxygen affinity of Yb effectively suppress the oxidation of Te to TeO 2 , fundamentally stabilizing Te x Se 1- x alloys. The resulting Te 0.7 Se 0.3 :Yb films exhibit a remarkable hole mobility of 177.5 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Furthermore, ZnO/Te 0.7 Se 0.3 :Yb photodetectors achieve a high responsivity of 0.21 A/W at 1300 nm, enabling multispectral imaging for precise target discrimination. These results demonstrate the Yb-enabled oxidation suppression for Te-based semiconductor, making a crucial stride toward the establishment of commercially viable high-mobility p-type semiconductor technology and short-wavelength infrared photoelectronics.

10.1002/adma.75621.title: Cross-System Recycling of Spent Layered Oxides Boosts Synergistic Optimization of Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathodes via Site-Selective Ni/Mn Co-Doping
10.1002/adma.75621.abstract: ABSTRACT To address the economic inviability of recycling spent sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) and the intrinsic drawbacks of Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) cathodes, a “cross-system recycling” strategy is proposed to transform the waste layered oxides cathodes (NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 , NFM) into high-performance polyanionic cathodes (Na 4 Fe 2.9 Ni 0.05 Mn 0.05 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 , NFNMPP). Nickel and manganese in the waste NFM that degrades due to “sodium deficiency” and irreversible phase transitions are leached out and doped into the NFNMPP lattice. Benefiting from the synergistic optimization of NFNMPP via site-selective Ni/Mn co-doping, the impurities and [P 2 O 7 ] distortion are suppressed, while the conductivity and Na + diffusion kinetics are enhanced. Consequently, the high-purity NFNMPP (91.2%) exhibits an ideal initial coulombic efficiency of 92.84%, remarkable rate capability (75.21 mAh g −1 at 50 C), and excellent cycling stability (86.74% capacity retention after 12 000 cycles at 20 C). Furthermore, paired with hard carbon (HC) anode, NFNMPP//HC pouch cells exhibit high safety, a record-long cycling life of 5557 cycles, 82.37% capacity retention at 30 C, and a wide operating temperature range (−40°C to 55°C), demonstrating great potential for energy storage applications and powering low-speed electric vehicles. This study presents a viable pathway for optimizing cathode materials by recycling spent SIBs, and facilitates its practical applications validated by Ah-level pouch cells.

10.1002/adma.75610.title: Quasi-Continuous Multimodal Sensing of Urinary Oxalate Dynamics for Home-Based Metabolic Monitoring
10.1002/adma.75610.abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous at-home monitoring of urinary oxalate dynamics is vital for the comprehensive management of hyperoxaluria and thus reduces the risk of kidney stone formation. However, home-based devices for capturing dynamic oxalate profiles remain elusive, as urine is challenging to sample and unstable for subsequent biochemical testing. Here we report a remote multimodal sensing platform for achieving such urine monitoring during daily sequential urination through seamless embedding into a standard urine collection bucket. This platform integrates electrochemical oxalate sensing with simultaneous pH and urine-volume measurements to correct the matrix drift in oxalate quantification. We achieve quasi-continuous monitoring of 24 h urinary physicochemical dynamics under diet-induced transient hyperoxaluria. By decoupling oxalate concentration from multimodal signals per urination, we reveal distinct metabolic response profiles under different dietary oxalate loads, providing new real-time insights into oxalate metabolism and its associated risk of kidney stones. Our all-in-one sampling-and-testing platform could revolutionize clinical urine analysis for hyperoxaluria, shifting from a one-time, multi-day turnaround assay into a paradigm of quasi-continuous monitoring with immediate feedback. This work represents a practical route toward personalized management of hyperoxaluria and a decentralized metabolic monitoring strategy for urology.

10.1002/adma.75609.title: Attribution Fingerprinting by Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Category-Specific Additive Design Rules for Zinc Anodes
10.1002/adma.75609.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte additives are one of the most direct remedy for interfacial instability in aqueous zinc-ion batteries, yet their development remains empirical. Existing machine-learning (ML) screening strategies presume a single global structure-property relationship shared by all additives. Here, an interpretable ML framework predicts cycle life from molecular descriptors and test conditions, and molecule-specific SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) profiles serve as attribution fingerprints. Unsupervised clustering resolves the additives into three attribution-based categories, governed respectively by adsorption energetics, charge-transfer gap and hydrogen-bond-network regulation, indicating that one universal descriptor set may not hold across chemically distinct additives. Representative additives from each category, none present in the training set, agree with experiment to within 11%. Category I screening identifies 2-fluoropyridine-5-carbaldehyde (2FPD), predicted at 3218 h, and Zn//Zn cells deliver 3010 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 , within 6.5% of prediction. Structural controls trace the improvement to the aldehyde: retaining it alone gives 900 h against an 89 h baseline, whereas fluorine alone gives 90 h. 2FPD constructs a graded organic-inorganic interphase that limits water access to the zinc surface and accelerates Zn 2+ desolvation, and Zn//MnO 2 full cells retain 96% capacity over 4000 cycles. This workflow offers a route towards interpretability-guided additive design.

10.1002/adma.75625.title: Sub-10 nm Confined Channels in Edge-Closed MXene Nanoribbons Boost Proton Transport for Efficient Single-Atom Electrocatalysts
10.1002/adma.75625.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoribbons from atomic layers such as graphene, carbides, and nitrides (MXenes) have attracted considerable interest owing to their distinct quantum confinement effects and high surface activity. However, the controlled synthesis of MXene nanoribbons remains challenging due to their random fragmentation and poor stability. Here, an efficient stiffness-mediated strategy is developed to fabricate unique edge-closed MXene nanoribbons, featuring a large aspect ratio of 10∼40 and confined channels of sub-10 nm at both edges. The key protocol involves modulating the critical collapse pressure by reducing the bending stiffness of MXene layers, thereby triggering the tube collapse of pre-formed nanoscrolls into edge-closed nanoribbons upon solvent evaporation. The resulting nanoribbons exhibit an enhanced polarization electric field, leading to a higher surface proton concentration and enhanced proton transport rate compared to nanoscrolls and nanosheets. As a result, these MXene nanoribbons provide an efficient platform for anchoring single-atom Pt, achieving a low overpotential of 23 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and a Tafel slope of 25 mV dec −1 in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), outperforming the most reported electrocatalysts.

10.1002/adma.75598.title: A Retinal Matrix Stiffening Model Reveals FAK-Dependent Mechanotransduction in Pericytes Underlies Vascular Destabilization
10.1002/adma.75598.abstract: ABSTRACT Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear. We define design parameters for an iPSC-derived microphysiological system (MPS) comprising pericyte-endothelial capillary networks embedded in a dynamically stiffening hydrogel engineered to reproduce matrix stiffening in a controlled, human-relevant context. Microrheology of Ins2 Akita mouse retinas revealed increased storage modulus in perivascular regions at a diabetic timepoint coincident with reduced pericyte coverage and vascular remodeling, establishing a stiffness magnitude used to inform the design of the MPS. In the MPS, progressive matrix stiffening alone, in the absence of hyperglycemic exposure, was sufficient to induce analogous vascular defects and to suppress pericyte expression of NOTCH3 , HEY1 , JAG1 , and N-cadherin in a focal adhesion kinase (FAK)-dependent manner. Inhibition of FAK restored pericyte signaling and vascular integrity in stiffened conditions without altering soft controls, identifying a FAK-dependent mechanotransduction as a druggable target. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of human diabetic retinas validated enrichment of focal-adhesion components and alterations in Notch-pathway transcripts in pericytes. These findings establish a human MPS showing matrix stiffening as a key regulator of pericyte-mediated vascular stabilization and nominate it and FAK-dependent mechanotransduction as targets to prevent DR pathogenesis.
authors: Emily Warren, Alex Wu, Lucas Ramirez, Yaqing Huang, Connor Amelung, Sophia Saxonhouse, Sharon Gerecht

10.1002/adma.75606.title: Anchored Fluoro-Shielded Solvation for Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75606.abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for solid-state lithium metal batteries owing to their favorable overall electrochemical properties. However, conventional PVDF-based polymer electrolytes suffer from uneven solvation distribution, discontinuous ion-transport pathways, and unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces caused by residual solvents and porous PVDF frameworks. Herein, we report an anchored fluoro-shielded solvation strategy to construct a high-performance PVDF-based polymer electrolyte. By integrating polyanionic anchoring sites with fluorinated shielding segments, the optimized electrolyte enables spatially distributed anion-rich solvation pathways, homogeneous Li + transport, and robust LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The polymer electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.26×10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.69, an oxidative onset potential of 5.27 V, and a critical current density of 6.4 mA cm −2 . Spectroscopic and interfacial analyses reveal that the anchored fluoro-shielded solvation structure promotes LiF-rich SEI formation and suppresses solvent decomposition. Consequently, Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 batteries retain 80.2% capacity after 2000 cycles under high-voltage and high-rate conditions of 4.5 V and 5 C. This work highlights anchored fluoro-shielded solvation as an effective molecular design principle for advanced polymer electrolytes toward practical high-voltage and high-rate solid-state Li metal batteries.
authors: Kaihua Wen, Tengsheng Chi, Junyao You, Lei Mao, Xinxin Zhu, Yan-Bing He, Zaiping Guo, Shilin Zhang

10.1002/adma.75570.title: Suprasilica Nanosieves for Selective Capture of Aromatics Over Cyclic Aliphatics in Hydrocarbon Feedstocks
10.1002/adma.75570.abstract: ABSTRACT Separating aromatic from cyclic aliphatic hydrocarbons remains a major challenge, as conventional distillation is both energy-intensive and poorly selective. Here, we report supramolecular silica nanosieves (suprasilica) that integrate organic molecular recognition sites directly into robust inorganic matrices. A hexasila-ureido-trianglamine (Δ-Si 6 ) is co-condensed within the silica matrix through a self-assembly sol-gel approach at controlled loadings to produce suprasilica sieves ( Δ-SiN x ). In vapor sorption, Δ-SiN x reject cyclic aliphatic hydrocarbons while displaying high aromatic uptake, achieving benchmark ideal selectivity for benzene over cyclohexane (23.5, uptake 9.4 mmol g − 1 ) on Δ-SiN20 and for toluene over methylcyclohexane (6.3, uptake 6.3 mmol g − 1 ) on Δ-SiN10 . The selectivity was further confirmed by Dynamic Column Breakthrough experiments, which demonstrated efficient separation under dynamic conditions. Importantly, the Δ-SiN x retain their molecular discrimination in the binary liquid phase, showing strong preferential uptake while preserving aromatic selectivity in neat naphtha and in diluted crude oil. Metadynamics simulations indicate that the selectivity is kinetic in origin, benzene passing the macrocyclic apertures with a modest barrier while cyclohexane is excluded. These suprasilica nanosieves deliver benchmark separation performance and provide a scalable, energy-efficient strategy for hydrocarbon purification.

10.1002/adma.75473.title: Over 95% Optical Reflectance From Structurally Modulated All-Biopolymer Multilayers
10.1002/adma.75473.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable photonics aims to replace conventional optical materials with environmentally benign alternatives, yet its development is fundamentally constrained by the narrow intrinsic refractive-index variability of biopolymers. Here we show that a dense-porous periodic architecture yields nearly perfect optical reflection using only polysaccharides. By exploiting the difference in skeletal rigidity between amorphous pectin and crystalline cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), we form alternating dense, high-refractive-index pectin layers and porous, low-refractive-index CNF layers through a combination of electrodeposition with solvent exchange. This dense-porous periodic architecture yields reflectivities exceeding 97% in the visible range and 95% in the near-infrared-a range unprecedented for biopolymer-based optical materials. Moreover, the strategy is simple, scalable, and highly versatile, enabling free spectral design across the visible and near-infrared regions, broadband metallic-like reflection, and planar patterning within a single fabrication process. Combined with the low thermal conductivity arising from porous layers and the coexistence of visible transparency and near-infrared reflection, the resulting films show potential as transparent thermal-management materials. This work establishes a new materials design principle for biodegradable, polysaccharide-based photonic systems and advances the field of sustainable photonics.
authors: Takaaki Kasuga, Ami Mizui, Shun Ishioka, Yintong Huang, Yuto Kaku, Tsuguyuki Saito, Tatsuya Namba, Yohsuke Goi, Hirotaka Koga, Masaya Nogi

10.1002/adma.75582.title: Ultra-Long Helical CNFs 3D-Networks as High-Conductivity Current Collectors for Efficient Sodium Deposition
10.1002/adma.75582.abstract: ABSTRACT Aluminum (Al) current collectors are crucial for sodium metal batteries (SMBs), yet sodium (Na) dendrite suppression and uniform Na deposition remain challenges. Surface modification could significantly optimize Na deposition behavior. Herein, a 20 nm copper (Cu) layer is designed to confine NiY diatomic catalyst (DAC) for Al surface modification via magnetron sputtering and heat treatment. The adjacent NiY atoms, with low single-point energy (-228.05 eV), minimum segregation energy (−0.67 eV), and maximum aggregation energy (5.84 eV), synergistically stabilize diatomic dispersion in the Cu nanolayer. Benefiting from the tailored acetylene adsorption energy (−1.16 eV) and favorable formation energies of C 2 H (−13.58 eV) and C 2 (−11.44 eV), NiY-DAC exhibits excellent catalytic activity, in-situ growth ultra-long helical CNFs 3D-networks with a thickness of 46.3 µm on Al current collectors, enabling efficient Na storage and remarkable inhibition Na dendrite formation. The modified current collector delivers outstanding electrochemical performance. The coulombic efficiency is up to 99.49% over 3000 h of half-cells at 1.0 mA cm −2 /1.0 mAh cm −2 with a low overpotential (3.1 mV), and the CNFs-Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 full-cells achieve stable cycling over 1500 cycles at 10.0 C. This diatomic catalyst confinement strategy provides new insight into designing high-performance carbon-modified current collectors.
authors: Yuwen Zhao, Zhijie Zhou, Qingshuo Yang, Yuefang Chen, Guoping Liu, Huan Yang, Yifang Zhang, Mengmeng Zhang, Zhenyang Yu, Zhijia Zhang, Jianmin Ma, Yong Jiang

10.1002/adma.75605.title: Flexible High-Speed Low-Noise Organic Photodiode Arrays for Dynamic Near-Infrared Imaging
10.1002/adma.75605.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photodiodes (OPDs) hold significant promise for next-generation IoT optical sensing and low-power imaging applications. However, widespread application of OPD in flexible and dynamic imaging has been constrained by high dark current, poor stability, and the lack of a cost-effective imaging system. In this work, we present an integrated solution through tailoring pseudo-planar heterojunction (PPHJ) OPD arrays and a customized, rapidly accessible imaging system, the dynamic organic photonics imaging system (DOIS). The resulting PPHJ OPD exhibited a high responsivity (0.6 A W −1 at 868 nm), low dark current (1.5 × 10 −8 A cm −2 at −1 V) and fast response time (480 ns), benefiting from optimal vertical phase separation and donor-acceptor interface morphology. Moreover, flexible photodetector exhibits superior mechanical stability, photostability and storage stability. Crucially, a pixel-shifting strategy was incorporated into conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) based machine learning algorithms to capture dynamic images and enhance resolution by leveraging sub-pixel information sampling. This work demonstrates a significant potential for the extensive application of organic photovoltaic materials in image sensing and flexible electronics.
authors: Tingting Guo, Yu Zhu, Zhe Zhang, Ruiman Han, Hanzhe Shi, Haoyu Li, Wenkai Zhao, Jing Zhang, Mengfan Li, Chen Geng, Wangqiao Chen, Guankui Long, Guanghui Li, Zhaoyang Yao, Yanfang Wang, Yongsheng Chen

10.1002/adma.75587.title: Crystallinity-Governed Liquid Wettability and Mobility on Solid Surface
10.1002/adma.75587.abstract: ABSTRACT Control over liquid wettability and droplet mobility is essential for several emerging applications including open microfluidics, anti-icing, self-cleaning, and heat transfer. Existing strategies generally rely on permanent chemical modification or continuous external stimuli to regulate droplet spreading, pinning, and sliding. Here, we report a unified approach for reconfiguring wettability states and droplet mobility by regulating crystalline packing of a semicrystalline polymer. A phase-transitioning polymer, poly(octadecyl acrylate) (PODAc), was incorporated into a porous polymeric coating, where melting and subsequent cooling pathways determine the extent of alkyl-chain crystallization and interfacial polar functionality. Cooling in air or underwater generates reversibly switchable hydrophilic ( θ W ∼ 85°), hydrophobic ( θ W ∼ 104°), and amphiphobic slippery states across liquids with surface tensions of 22-72 mN m −1 . These distinct regimes enable programmable droplet spreading, pinning, and low-friction transport without post-synthetic chemical treatment or sustained external stimulation. Furthermore, reconfigurable wettability patterns enable guided liquid transport through spatially selective complete wetting or customized contact line frictional force.
authors: Sumit Sarkar, Jaysri Das, Vedant Phad, Debasmita Sarkar, Pritam Giri, Samiran Morang, Sarajit Naskar, Debdas Dhabal, Uttam Manna

10.1002/adma.75573.title: Additives and Relaxation Fluidize Molecular Transport Within Covalent Adaptable Networks
10.1002/adma.75573.abstract: ABSTRACT Incorporating dynamic covalent bonds into polymer networks could offer stimuli-responsive control over molecular transport, often requiring additives to facilitate bond rearrangement. Here super-resolution localization microscopy was employed to examine fluorescent probe transport in unhydrated, elastic networks containing thiol-thioester dynamic covalent chemistry (DCC). In static, DCC-free networks, displacement distributions revealed frequent trapping and slow, anomalous, and heterogeneous diffusion. Introducing a dynamic catalyst additive markedly increased mobile fraction and produced diffusivity that was more fluid-like. These effects were observed with several classes of fluorescent probes, two distinct additives, and for networks with or without DCC. Experiments with a photo-releasable catalyst (NPPOC-TMG) separated additive effects from those of activated exchange. Catalyst release conferred additional fluidization of the network. Importantly, these changes were not accompanied by macroscopic plasticization, suggesting that small additive concentrations can strongly affect transport in confining environments. Spatial analysis further indicated that transport enhancement was primarily due to restructuring of an initially heterogeneous network rather than local bond exchange near the diffusing probes. Additive incorporation and post-cure exchange likely reduced defects and homogenized the crosslink density. In sum, these results demonstrate how DCC modulates transport, emphasize the importance of the activation method, and highlight its potential in separation and controlled-release systems.
authors: Ian Wyllie, Zachary Mora, Christopher N. Bowman, Daniel K. Schwartz

10.1002/adma.75612.title: Ultra-Broad-Temperature Mechanoluminescence Enabled by Intrinsic Lattice Disorder
10.1002/adma.75612.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanoluminescent (ML) materials convert mechanical stimuli into light through carrier excitation and radiative recombination, enabling external-power-free stress sensing and visualization. The strict energy matching required for carrier release, transport, and recombination restricts ML to narrow thermal windows. Their application at extreme temperatures, however, is constrained by discrete defect levels arising from relatively uniform local atomic environments. Here, we use intrinsic lattice disorder to engineer a quasi-continuous trap landscape in Sr 3 Gd 2 (Ge 3 O 9 ) 2 :Mn 2+ . Diverse local crystal-field environments, together with dynamically generated defects, create energetically adjacent traps that support a trap-relay process. Charge carriers are continuously redistributed across this trap manifold, sustaining stable ML over an ultrabroad temperature range from 133 to 433 K. We further demonstrate a human-machine interaction system based on this material under simulated extreme-temperature conditions. These results establish intrinsic lattice disorder as a strategy for broadening the thermal operating window of ML materials and provide a general design principle for thermally robust, energy-storing luminescent materials for extreme environments.
authors: Jingyi Gao, Xiaohui Zhao, Jiaqi Wang, Xinyi Jiang, Xu Wu, Yongfa Kong, Yi Zhang, Li Wu, Jingjun Xu

10.1002/adma.75611.title: Sulfur Locking and Chlorination Synergistically Enable Efficient Charge Transport and Low Nonradiative Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75611.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient charge transport while maintaining low nonradiative energy loss remains a key challenge in the molecular design of small-molecule acceptors (SMAs) for organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a stepwise molecular engineering strategy based on sulfur locking and chlorination to regulate intermolecular packing and excited-state properties simultaneously. Sulfur locking modifies molecular conformation and intermolecular packing, leading to enhanced exciton diffusion and charge transport. Subsequent chlorination further strengthens intermolecular interactions through additional Cl···S contacts, resulting in tighter π-π stacking and improved crystalline ordering. Binary OSCs based on D18:Qx2Ph-SCl achieve an efficiency of 20.0% with a high open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.951 V, while maintaining a low nonradiative energy loss of ∼0.19 eV. Owing to its intrinsically lower reorganization energy and weaker electron-phonon coupling than L8-BO, Qx2Ph-SCl further serves as an effective third component in ternary OSCs, reducing nonradiative recombination and increasing the V OC . As a result, the ternary device delivers an efficiency of 21.3%. This work demonstrates that stepwise sulfur locking and chlorination provide an effective molecular design strategy for simultaneously optimizing charge transport and voltage loss in high-performance OSCs.
authors: Jinjin Wang, Han Tian, Jiehao Fu, Yintao Yang, Lunbi Wu, Guoli Wang, Jiarui Lu, Hanjian Lai, Jun Zhang, Sha Liu, Zhanxiang Chen, Jianqi Zhang, Wei Zhang, Gang Li, Chuluo Yang, Zhenghui Luo

10.1002/adma.75634.title: PASS-Derived O/S Donor Field-Directed Competitive-Cooperative Fe/Co Phase Evolution for Cross-Band Microwave Absorption
10.1002/adma.75634.abstract: ABSTRACT Fe/Co bimetallic regulation enables high-performance microwave absorbers, yet the role of intrinsic coordination disparity in precursor conversion, nonequilibrium phase evolution, and cross-band loss redistribution remains unclear. We design a poly(arylene sulfide sulfone) (PASS)-predefined O/S heterogeneous donor-field strategy to direct competitive-cooperative nonequilibrium phase evolution in Fe/Co systems. Covalently embedded sulfone-O and thioether-S sites, with PASS's rigid backbone, create a molecularly preorganized donor field that amplifies non-equivalent Fe/Co coordination, promoting competitive bonding, differentiated phase pathways, and electronic-state reconstruction during confined pyrolysis. Fe/Co regulation thus reshapes local phases, O/S chemical environments, and interfacial charge states via Fe─O/Co─S coordination preferences, generating multiphase heterostructures, amorphous/crystalline interfaces, defects, and lattice strain while balancing dielectric polarization, conductive transport, magnetic response, and impedance matching. The resulting CFC absorber achieves cross-band absorption in low-frequency 5G and high-frequency radar bands. CFC-4 exhibits −73.83 dB at 6.23 GHz (3.20 mm) and −76.59 dB at 16.98 GHz (1.31 mm), with a maximum EAB of 5.03 GHz. CFC-4∼6 (1-5 mm) show >90% cumulative effective absorption over 2-18 GHz. Finite-element simulations reveal a maximum RCS reduction of 42.5 dB on PEC. This work establishes O/S donor-field engineering as a viable route to amplify Fe/Co coordination differentiation for efficient cross-band microwave absorption.
authors: Rui Zhang, Yonggang Yan, Gang Zhang

10.1002/adma.75630.title: Scalable Gigapascal Strength Bamboo Veneers via Nanocellulose Reinforcement
10.1002/adma.75630.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon neutrality demands materials that deliver both performance and low environmental impact. Carbon fiber and glass fiber rely on fossil feedstocks and energy-intensive processing, while nature bamboo the ecological marvel is limited by inefficient load transfer within their heterogeneous cell walls. Here we show that this limitation can be overcome by reprogramming the bamboo cell wall through supramolecular nano-reinforcement. Cellulose nanocrystals infiltrate the cell wall and promote the reorganization of the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network within the aligned cellulose framework converting structural discontinuities into a continuous load-bearing scaffold. This enhances interfibrillar stress transfer and homogenizes mechanical response across scales. The resulting material achieves a tensile strength of 0.98 GPa and a Young's modulus of 52.7 GPa, with specific strength rivaling many synthetic fiber materials. These gains are achieved with up to two orders of magnitude lower carbon intensity than that of carbon fiber. This work demonstrates a scalable route to transform abundant biomass into high-performance structural materials, decoupling mechanical performance from carbon intensity.

10.1002/adma.75618.title: Unlocking the Potential of Magnesium-Based Hydrogen Storage Composites via Advanced Thermodynamic and Kinetic Tuning Strategies
10.1002/adma.75618.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of efficient and safe solid-state hydrogen storage technologies is pivotal for the transition toward sustainable clean energy. Magnesium is a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high gravimetric (7.6 wt.% for MgH 2 ) and volumetric storage capacity (110 kg m −3 ), abundance, and excellent reversibility. However, the practical application of Mg-based materials is hindered by their high thermodynamic stability (ΔH = −74.7 kJ mol −1 H 2 ) and sluggish sorption kinetics. Here, we overview the latest advances in Mg-based composites for high hydrogen storage performance. We discuss key material modification strategies, including catalysis, nanostructuring, alloying, and external field assistance to tune the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of Mg-based materials. We stress the emerging role of machine learning in accelerating material design, performance prediction, and optimization. We also critically assess the techno-economic viability of Mg-based hydrogen storage within integrated hydrogen value chains. This assessment considers how storage connects with hydrogen production, transport, and end-use applications. Finally, we outline challenges and future research directions, aiming to guide the rational design of next-generation Mg-based hydrogen storage materials and systems toward commercial applications.

10.1002/adma.75577.title: Transforming Pathological H2S Into a Photodynamic Amplifier: In Vivo Formation of Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 Heterojunction for Microenvironment-Adaptive Periodontitis Treatment
10.1002/adma.75577.abstract: ABSTRACT Current periodontitis management is hindered by the inability to effectively reverse the dysbiotic microenvironment of persistent infection and restore immune homeostasis. Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) presents a promising non-invasive antibacterial strategy, its clinical efficacy remains limited by poor microenvironmental selectivity and insufficient immunomodulatory capacity. Herein, we engineer a microenvironment-responsive “trash-to-treasure” PDT strategy based on Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 nanosheet-assembled microspheres. This platform actively scavenges excess hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) within the periodontal pocket, triggering an in situ transformation into Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 @Bi 2 S 3 heterojunctions. This H 2 S-triggered conversion neutralizes the pro-inflammatory gasotransmitter and establishes an S-scheme heterojunction with enhanced photocatalytic activity. The resulting reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress, together with targeted disruption of bacterial iron metabolism, enables highly efficient photodynamic eradication of major periodontopathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis . Moreover, Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 -mediated scavenging of pathological H 2 S alleviates inflammatory responses in human gingival fibroblasts and reactivates macrophage respiratory burst for intracellular bacterial clearance. In vivo evaluations in a rat periodontitis model demonstrate effective inflammation resolution, suppression of alveolar bone loss, and robust tissue regeneration. This work introduces an intelligent therapeutic strategy that hijacks pathological H 2 S as a photodynamic amplifier, establishing a microenvironment-adaptive PDT paradigm for periodontal infection.
authors: Danyang Wang, Ying Wang, Zhibang Li, Xinwei Liu, Kai Li, Yi Chen, Junkun Feng, Baojin Ma, Wenjun Wang, Jianhua Li, Shaohua Ge

10.1002/adma.75575.title: Nanoscale Thermal Imaging of Dislocation-Mediated Heat Transport
10.1002/adma.75575.abstract: ABSTRACT Dislocations are widely used to tailor lattice thermal conductivity in semiconductors and thermoelectrics, yet the local thermal resistance of individual buried dislocations and their spatial extent remain experimentally unresolved. Here, operando scanning transmission electron microscopy-electron energy-loss spectroscopy thermometry, atomic-resolution imaging, vibrational spectroscopy, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics are combined to map heat transport across a dislocation array within a 5°SrTiO 3 low-angle grain boundary. The effective thermal conductance of the dislocation array is estimated to be ∼35.4 MW m − 2 K − 1 using the bulk reference conductivity, corresponding to a Kapitza length of ∼339 nm. Nanoscale temperature maps reveal a spatially heterogeneous resistance landscape: reconstructed dislocation cores act as sharp thermal bottlenecks over ∼2.14-5.17 nm, with steeper local temperature gradients than inter-core regions, whereas inter-core regions show weaker but more extended modulation over ∼8.34-11.57 nm. Correlative structural and vibrational analyses show that Ti─O bond distortion, Ti valence change, P4 optical-phonon blueshift, and reduced local-bulk phonon density-of-states overlap create a core-specific vibrational environment. These results uncover the underlying mechanism whereby atomic-scale core reconstruction generates nanoscale localized thermal resistance, and offer quantitative descriptors for defect-structure-guided thermal design.
authors: Ruilin Mao, Bingyao Liu, Jiaxin Liu, Xiaoyue Gao, Junping Luo, Fachen Liu, Ruochen Shi, Jiade Li, Jinlong Du, Peng Gao

10.1002/adma.75563.title: Orthogonal Passivation of Polar Facets for Efficient InSb Quantum Dot SWIR Photodetectors
10.1002/adma.75563.abstract: ABSTRACT Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) offer a heavy-metal-free route to short-wave infrared (SWIR) photodetection, but their performance still lags behind lead- and mercury-based CQD systems, and the surface chemistry that limits their performance is not well understood. Here, we identify two independent oxide-derived trap pathways on the polar terminations of zincblende InSb: oxidation of the In-terminated {111}A and Sb-terminated {111}B facets creates chemically distinct mid-gap states, each of which degrades carrier transport. Density functional theory calculations show that metal halides bind strongly to Sb-terminated facets, but weakly to In-terminated facets, while thiolates show the opposite preference; this asymmetry leaves single-ligand passivation incomplete. Exploiting this orthogonality, we develop a facet-specific exchange that passivates both terminations and removes their surface oxides in a single step. The resulting CQD films show a fivefold reduction in hole-trap density and a sixfold improvement in hole mobility relative to thiol-only controls. The photodetectors achieve 50% external quantum efficiency under 1 V reverse bias at 1390 nm, to the best of our knowledge, the highest reported for InSb CQD photodetectors in the 1300-1500 nm range, along with a 580 ns fall time and 95% photocurrent retention after 100 h of continuous operation.
authors: Sile Hu, Yangning Zhang, Filip Dinic, Lizhou Fan, Benjamin Rehl, Oleksandr Voznyy, Sjoerd Hoogland, Edward H. Sargent

10.1002/adma.75622.title: Planar Focusing of Anisotropic Plasmon Polaritons in MoOCl2/Au
10.1002/adma.75622.abstract: ABSTRACT Hyperbolic polaritons offer a promising approach for subwavelength light confinement and manipulation. While extensively explored across mid-infrared to terahertz bands, achieving long-distance focusing at visible frequencies remains challenging due to the trade-off between long propagation and strong compression. In this work, we demonstrate planar focusing of anisotropic plasmon polaritons with an extended focal length in a MoOCl 2 /Au heterostructure. By integrating an Au metastructure with the natural hyperbolic material MoOCl 2 , we convert surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) into surface plasmon hyperbolic polaritons (SPHPs), enabling excitation and focusing of the low-momentum hybrid anisotropic polariton in the heterostructure. Furthermore, by optimizing the thickness of the MoOCl 2 layer, we synergistically enhance both the propagation distance and the field compression. Using transmission-mode scanning near-field optical microscopy (SNOM) and quantitative methods, we demonstrate a focal length of 2.5λ and a focal spot with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of λ /5 under 633 nm excitation, accompanied by a threefold energy enhancement. This visible-frequency long-focus system offers significant potential for noncontact nanoscale probing, integrated photonics, and optical interconnects. The proposed heterostructure engineering approach provides a versatile design paradigm for coupling hyperbolic polaritons with multiple plasmonic excitations, paving the way for advanced photonic applications.
authors: Jianqiao Zhao, Yuxin Zhang, Xiaotian Xue, Haodong Zhong, Tongzhou Xu, Yaolong Li, Jingbo Sun, Weipeng Wang, Ji Zhou, Shufeng Wang, Zhengjun Zhang

10.1002/adma.75591.title: Hydro-Gated Photonic Actuators With Programmable Color and Shape
10.1002/adma.75591.abstract: ABSTRACT Structural color actuators integrating visual readout with motion are prized for biomimicry, yet typically operate in a coupled, color-gradient mode with limited freedom. Here we report a photonic liquid crystal network that decouples these responses via a scattering-gated mechanism. The material hides its structural color in the dry state but, upon water uptake, simultaneously switches on vivid coloration and executes programmable three-dimensional deformation. Crucially, we achieve stimulus-selective control: ethanol turns on color without motion, while heat induces motion without color. This independent, on-demand manipulation of optical and mechanical outputs offers a transformative platform for multi-responsive soft robotics, adaptive camouflage, and smart displays.
authors: Yujian Liu, Shimin Shao, Hao Mi, Xiang Shang, Meng Wang, Shuai Huang, Zhiyang Liu, Hong Yang

10.1002/adma.202513813.title: Engineering Topological Phases in Two-Dimensional Materials: A Path from Preparation to Device Applications
10.1002/adma.202513813.abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to their topologically protected edge or surface states, rapid electronic transport, and highly tunable physical properties, two-dimensional topological materials (2D TMs) have garnered significant attention in condensed matter physics and materials science, and are regarded as potential candidates for quantum computing. Since the first observation of the quantum Hall effect, fundamental research on the physics of TMs has made remarkable progress. To better utilize the unique properties of TMs, the importance of material fabrication and phase engineering of topological states has become increasingly prominent. This review systematically discusses phase engineering in 2D TMs, from their growth to device applications. First, various topological phases and related 2D materials are introduced briefly. Next, the growth methods for 2D TMs are summarized. It then discusses progress and limitations in growth, driven by the requirements of characterization and application. Furthermore, the general approaches for modulating topological phases are reviewed, alongside the current applications in electronic devices. Finally, the review outlines future directions and challenges in phase engineering of 2D topological materials, aiming to promote the transition of 2D TMs from fundamental physics research to phase-engineered material platforms.

10.1002/adma.75100.title: Electrostimulus Phase-Transition Mediated Robust Adhesive Hydrogels
10.1002/adma.75100.abstract: ABSTRACT Adhesive hydrogels are crucial for interfacing wearable electronics with substrates, yet the inherent trade-off between interfacial adhesion and cohesive strength always limits their application performance. Here, we present an adhesive hydrogel based on lignin-mediated catechol chemistry and salt hydrate phase-transition, which achieves synergistic enhancement of interfacial adhesion and cohesive strength upon 1 V electrostimulated crystallization. The hydrogel is soft and exhibits mild adhesion to various substrates in amorphous state. Electrostimulus-induced phase-transition realizes a significant increment of cohesive strength and boosts interfacial adhesion by up to 8-40 times (exceeding 3000 J m −2 ) on skin. The adhesion-enhancement mechanisms on different substrates are elucidated via multi-scale experimental designs and molecular simulations. When the hydrogel is applied as the adhesive layer, the assembled elastomer sensing devices inherit the electrostimulus adhesion-enhancement and shape-memory properties, significantly improving signal transmission stability and motion-interference resistance. This study offers a simple and versatile strategy for stimuli-enhanced adhesives, deepens the understanding of phase-transition regulated adhesion behaviors, and supports the development of large-area flexible devices for intelligent robotics and human-computer interactions.
authors: Jinlai Shen, Minkun Cai, Xiong Yi, Pang Zhu, Yong Qian, Xueqing Qiu

10.1002/adma.75620.title: High-Entropy Complementary d-Band Decoupling of Redox Kinetics for Bidirectional Catalysis in Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/adma.75620.abstract: ABSTRACT The reversible conversion of sulfur and Li 2 S in lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single-component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi-step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high-entropy complementary d-band center model, extending the classical d-band center theory to multi-metal systems. The complementary d-band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi-metal sites collaboratively construct a “highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption” closed-loop pathway, with the d-p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high-entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li-S batteries.
authors: Di Wang, Zihan Dong, Shiyi Liu, Hailong Yan, Fangqing Liu, Yi Huang, Zhipeng Sun, Le Huang, Zaiping Guo

10.1002/adma.75589.title: Structure-Encoded Magnetic Anisotropy in Super-Tough Magnetoelastic Aramid-Silk-Magnetite Fibers
10.1002/adma.75589.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic anisotropy is essential for controlling magnetic responses in soft matter, yet it is conventionally imposed using external magnetic fields. Here, we show that magnetic anisotropy can instead be intrinsically encoded and continuously tuned through hierarchical structural organization, establishing a route by which anisotropic dipolar interactions, rather than conventional shape effects, dominate the magnetic energy landscape. This mechanism is achieved by engineering composite nanofibrils in which magnetite nanoparticles are grown in situ within an aligned aramid-silk matrix, inspired by biomineralization in chiton teeth. The resulting aramid-silk-magnetite fibers combine high strength and modulus with exceptional toughness up to 820 MJ m − 3 , while exhibiting tunable magnetic anisotropy spanning axial to radial easy-axis configurations through structural relaxation. Quantitative analysis reveals that collective dipolar coupling dominates magnetic anisotropy by orders of magnitude over demagnetization-field contributions, identifying nanoparticle interaction networks as the primary origin of anisotropy. This built-in anisotropy enables strain-mediated reconfiguration of magnetic properties, giving rise to magnetoelastic coupling that scales with fiber modulus and reflects the available structural mobility for magnetic reorientation. By amplifying structure-defined anisotropy under mechanical loading, we further demonstrate strain-controlled magnetic torque for actuation. These findings establish a structural design principle for programming magnetic anisotropy in mechanically robust magnetoelastic materials.
authors: Tiantian Ren, Shouhua Feng, Ming Yang

10.1002/adma.75632.title: Non-Selective Suppression of Cation and Anion Crosstalk from an Anode Perspective
10.1002/adma.75632.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode-centric mechanism utilizing a Na-rich nanoalloy (Na x Sn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the Na x Sn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na 2 O-rich solid electrolyte interphase that non-selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF 2 ||Na x Sn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||Na x Sn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g −1 at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na-rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high-energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode-cathode coupling.

10.1002/adma.74990.title: Regulating Phase Evolution and Crystallization Dynamics Enables Low Open-Circuit Voltage Deficit in Wide-Bandgap Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.74990.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide-bandgap kesterite Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 (CZTS) is a promising top-cell candidate for tandem photovoltaics owing to its earth-abundant composition and low-cost solution processability. However, its progress is hindered by a large open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) deficit. A key origin lies in the defects generated during sulfurization. For solution-processed CZTS absorbers, an intermediate-phase pathway involving Cu 2 SnS 3 and other intermediate phases alters the local chemical environment and crystallization behavior, leading to substantial defects and carrier recombination. Here, we develop a bilayer composition-modulated sulfurization (BCMS) strategy using a pre-stabilized Cu-rich bottom layer and a Cu-poor upper layer to regulate Cu redistribution during sulfurization. The BCMS strategy suppresses Cu 2 SnS 3 and favors the direct transformation pathway, while transforming the crystallization from surface-dominated growth to a more synchronized process across the film. The regulation of phase evolution and crystallization suppresses bulk and interface defects, reducing carrier recombination. As a result, a power conversion efficiency of 11.05% with a V OC of 747.64 mV is achieved, representing the lowest V OC deficit reported for solution-processed wide-bandgap (>1.5 eV) CZTS solar cells. The coordinated regulation of phase evolution and crystallization dynamics highlights pathway engineering as an effective strategy for defects and voltage-loss management in kesterite materials, with implications for other chalcogenide semiconductors.

10.1002/adma.75628.title: A Noninvasive Approach to Study Localized Forces in 3D Epithelia
10.1002/adma.75628.abstract: ABSTRACT Epithelial tissue integrity and remodeling rely on mechanical coupling between cytoskeletal organization and adhesion complexes, but their orchestration in three-dimensional (3D) epithelia remains unresolved. Here, we introduced a noninvasive strategy to locally probe forces within 3D epithelial tissues. We engineered elastic polyacrylamide (PAAm) microbeads with cell-like size and mechanical properties, enabling their integration into tissues. PAAm microbeads were spontaneously engulfed by the tissue, establishing an intrinsic interface. This allowed bead deformation to be directly correlated with local cytoskeletal architecture and adhesion organization, visualized through high-resolution imaging and quantitative 3D computational reconstruction. Using this approach, we demonstrated that localized mechanical perturbations trigger cytoskeletal remodeling while preserving tissue polarity. We further identified extracellular matrix composition as a key determinant of bead-tissue interactions. At the bead-cell interface, cells assembled tension-bearing focal adhesions and actin stress fibers. Quantitative analysis of bead deformation revealed sub-cellular scale patterns of cell-bead interaction forces, which correlated with the localization of cytoskeletal elements. Our findings extend previous traction force microscopy observations to 3D, revealing coordinated, spatially heterogeneous forces specifically at the cell-bead interface. Taken together, this enabled us to dissect the interplay between cellular processes and tissue mechanics in a noninvasive way in 3D model systems.
authors: Niels Gouirand, Muhamet Ibrahimi, Claire Valotteau, Brice Lecouffe, André Le Bivic, Dominique Massey-Harroche, Felix Rico, Matthias Merkel, Delphine Delacour, Elsa Bazellières

10.1002/adma.75623.title: Buried CdSe Sacrificial Layer Driving Phase Evolution and Crystallization Kinetics Enables 14.78%-Efficient DMF-Based Kesterite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75623.abstract: ABSTRACT During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early-stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth-dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of N,N -dimethylformamide (DMF)-derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in-situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early-stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu 2 SnSe 3 -related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear-side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface-dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd 2+ partially substitutes Zn 2+ sites, reducing defect-assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF-derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se-containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.
authors: Letu Siqin, Yuan Li, Ningyu Ren, Yaqing Cui, Shuyu Li, Ruijian Liu, Hongmei Luan, Chengjun Zhu

10.1002/adma.75498.title: Coordination Bridges in Confined-Water Domains Enable Partially Desolvated Zn2+ Transport in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75498.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs), owing to their intrinsic safety and cost competitiveness, are attracting significant interest as next-generation energy storage system (ESS) technologies. However, their commercialization is severely hindered by poor cycle stability, primarily originating from dendritic Zn growth and parasitic hydrogen evolution. To address these challenges simultaneously, we design and integrate a multifunctional polymeric protective layer incorporating amide and imidazolium functional groups. The zincophilic amide groups facilitate ion transport by providing stable Zn 2+ binding sites, whereas the hygroscopic imidazolium groups establish a confined-water domain that regulates local solvation dynamics. Within this domain, water molecules transiently stabilize Zn 2+ and act as a coordination bridge during ion migration, yet their mobility toward the electrode surface is restricted. This dual functionality increases the Zn 2+ single-ion conductivity 6.55-fold and reduces the hydrogen evolution rate by 79.1%. Consequently, Zn//Zn symmetric cells exhibit markedly extended cycling lifetimes of up to 2200 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . When applied to Zn-I 2 full cells, the protective layer enables stable operation over 4000 cycles with >85% capacity retention, even under a practical areal capacity of 3.6 mAh cm −2 . These findings highlight a robust interfacial strategy to realize long-duration, high-capacity aqueous ZIBs for grid-scale energy storage.
authors: Jin Seong Cha, Dongmin Jeon, Kyungmi Kim, Yuna Hwang, Eun Jeong Yoon, Donghee Gueon, Young-Woo Choi, Chan-Woo Lee, Jung Hoon Yang

10.1002/adma.75024.title: Spin Transport Across Interfaces With the Non-Collinear Antiferromagnet Mn 3 Sn
10.1002/adma.75024.abstract: ABSTRACT Non-collinear antiferromagnets such as are promising materials for ultrafast spintronic applications due to their peculiar electronic structure and efficient spin-dependent transport phenomena. Here, we investigate magnetic ordering and ultrafast spin transport in c -axis oriented thin films and -based heterostructures with Pt and . Temperature-dependent magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements confirm thermally activated switching of the cluster octupole moment near the Néel temperature, while preserving predominantly in-plane magnetic order. In heterostructures, however, pronounced room-temperature ferromagnetic signatures are observed, including enhanced Kerr rotation and out-of-plane magnetization. Systematic magnetometry studies reveal the formation of an intermixed interfacial phase upon annealing. Ultrafast transport measurements using a sample with optimized interfaces show that optical excitation of generates predominantly anomalous Nernst currents, with no detectable evidence of efficient spin-current injection into Pt. In contrast, exhibits a significant inverse spin Hall conversion when driven by spin currents injected from , reaching approximately of the efficiency of Pt-based reference structures. The conversion efficiency is found to be independent of the relative orientation between ferromagnetic magnetization and antiferromagnetic octupole moment. Our results emphasize the importance of interface engineering for spintronic devices.

10.1002/adma.75602.title: Design of Heteroatomic Active Sites for Electrochemical COx Reduction Toward Multicarbon Products
10.1002/adma.75602.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical CO 2 and CO reduction (CO x RR) to value-added multicarbon (C2+) products offers a promising route for sustainable carbon recycling and renewable fuel generation. Although Cu catalysts exhibit unique activity, these single-metal sites are constrained by linear scaling relations of intermediate adsorption energies, which limits further improvements in selectivity and energy efficiency. Introducing heteroatoms to regulate active-site coordination provides an effective approach to transcend these limitations. This review describes recent advances in the theoretical design, controllable fabrication, and mechanistic investigation of heteroatomic active sites for CO x RR toward C2+ products. Theoretical identification for high-performance sites through descriptor-based modeling, data-driven screening, and dynamic simulations is first discussed. Then, the precision synthesis strategies for constructing atomically dispersed, long-range-ordered, and interfacial-confined heteroatomic structures are systematically summarized. Subsequently, mechanistic insights into the promoting effect of heteroatoms, driven by synergistic electronic and geometric modulation, are highlighted, followed by an analysis of future research directions and the key challenges for the industrial implementation of heteroatomic catalysts for CO x RR. This review provides an integrated perspective linking active-site design to catalytic performance, offering guidance for the development of next-generation heteroatomic electrocatalysts for efficient CO x RR toward the sustainable production of high-value chemicals.
authors: Shuying Li, Yachao Zeng, Zhi-Jian Zhao, Peng Zhang, Jinlong Gong

10.1002/adma.75675.title: Twistsonics: Engineering Acoustic Topological Textures in Moiré Sound Lattices
10.1002/adma.75675.abstract: ABSTRACT Moiré superlattices formed by twisting periodic systems provide a powerful platform for emergent topological phenomena, but their use for programming real-space topology in acoustic wave fields remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a phase-controlled spoof surface acoustic wave platform for constructing moiré topological textures in the acoustic particle-velocity field. On a perforated acoustic metasurface, two twisted skyrmion lattices are synthesized and superposed, yielding acoustic skyrmion bags with controllable topological numbers and geometries. The twist angle and rotation center control the scale and configuration of the bags, enabling deterministic reshaping of the composite texture. We further introduce controlled defects to assess the defect tolerance of the moiré skyrmion bags. The skyrmion bags retain their composite topology over a finite range of defect fractions, and comparison with an untwisted single-layer skyrmion lattice suggests enhanced stability of the enclosed skyrmion cluster relative to the single-layer reference at higher defect fractions. The same programmable platform also supports transitions from skyrmion lattices to meron lattices and enables twist-induced meron clusters. These findings establish acoustic moiré superlattices as a reconfigurable platform for engineering robust real-space topological textures, with potential applications in topology-guided acoustic manipulation and information encoding.
authors: Wen-Yu Wang, Shuai Liu, Xiang-Yuan Xu, Qing Tong, Hao Ge, Yijie Shen, Ming-Hui Lu

10.1002/adma.75653.title: Rigid Double-Spiro-Grid Polymer Regulates Donor Fibrillar Pre-Assembly and Acceptor Interdiffusion in Layer-by-Layer Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75653.abstract: ABSTRACT Layer-by-layer (LBL) fabrication of organic solar cells (OSCs) decouples donor and acceptor deposition, which, however, induces difficulties in controlling donor crystallization and acceptor interdiffusion. Here, we introduce NPSG, a fully conjugated double-spiro-grid polymer, to regulate donor fibrillar pre-assembly before acceptor deposition. Morphological results reveal that NPSG shifts D18 assembly from loosely associated aggregates toward pronounced fibrillar pre-assemblies in solution. Molecular dynamics simulations further suggest that the rigid NPSG backbone provides multiple noncovalent interaction sites that favor anisotropic association between D18 chain segments. During film formation, these fibrillar precursors evolve into a coherent and solvent-resistant donor framework, which moderates L8-BO interdiffusion and promotes a vertically graded, double fibrillar heterojunction. The resulting morphology facilitates interfacial charge transfer, improves the balance of electron and hole transport, and suppresses nongeminate recombination. Consequently, the optimized D18+NPSG/L8-BO devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.2%, with a certified value of 20.7%. This strategy also improves device reproducibility, processing tolerance, applicability across different donor/acceptor systems, and operational stability under maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking. These findings establish donor-underlayer pre-assembly regulation as an effective strategy for efficient and robust sequentially processed OSCs.

10.1002/adma.75641.title: Surface-Coordinated Gas-Solid Polymerization Enables Quasi-2D Polyphenylacetylene Single-Crystalline Nanoribbons
10.1002/adma.75641.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular-weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long-range order. Here, we report a gas-solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi-2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single-crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuO x surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination-assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π-stacking-driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer-scale PPA single-crystalline nanoribbons with left-handed cis-transoidal helical chains and long-range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended-chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper-bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 10 9 g mol − 1 . The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W − 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 10 1 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade-off between molecular-weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi-2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.
authors: Qian Cai, Wenting Hong, Wei Liu

10.1002/adma.75017.title: Interface-Confined Cationic Polarization Enables Rapid and Reversible Polyiodide Conversion for High-Rate Zinc-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/adma.75017.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-iodine (Zn-I 2 ) batteries are promising for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their application is limited by sluggish polyiodide redox kinetics and severe shuttle effect. Many cathode-regulation strategies improve iodine chemistry through physical confinement and polar adsorption. However, simultaneously suppressing polyiodide shuttling and enabling rapid iodine conversion remains challenging, particularly under high-rate where fast interfacial redox kinetics are required. Here, interface-confined cationic polarization is established by integrating π-delocalized guanidinium cations (Gdm + ) into iodine cathodes, where cation-π interactions with Ketjen Black (KB) sp 2 carbon domains confine Gdm + on the KB surface. The delocalized positive charge of interface-confined Gdm + electrostatically enriches polyiodides within the cathode, while its delocalized π-electron system polarizes the electron cloud of iodine species and promotes interfacial charge transfer, enabling reversible polyiodide conversion without irreversible trapping. The optimized I 2 cathode delivers 100 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh-rate of 50 A g −1 (∼237 C) and sustains 40 000 cycles with only 0.002% decay per cycle. A 1.0 Ah pouch cell retains 82.6% capacity after 1200 cycles. This work demonstrates interface-confined cationic polarization as an effective strategy for regulating polyiodide redox chemistry, offering a new route toward high-rate and long-life Zn-I 2 batteries.
authors: Jie Feng, Xinyang Li, Xiaofeng Cui, Teng Deng, Yiru Zhao, Dandan Yin, Lanya Zhao, Kai Xi, Zaiping Guo, Hongyang Zhao, Shujiang Ding

10.1002/adma.75633.title: Tailored Cationic Visible-Light-Active Interfaces for Sustainable, Biodegradable Nanofibers With Dual-Mode Antimicrobial Activity and Robust Electrostatic Particle Capture
10.1002/adma.75633.abstract: ABSTRACT The accumulation of microplastics originating from single-use personal protective equipment presents a growing environmental concern. Developing biodegradable fibrous alternatives is essential, but integrating robust antimicrobial efficacy with stable electrostatic capture while maintaining degradability remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a surface co-functionalization strategy addressing these challenges through covalent immobilization of sodium copper chlorophyllin (SCC) and quaternary ammonium compounds (QAC). Beyond simple dual functionalization, this molecular design induces intramolecular charge separation, suppressing electron-hole recombination in SCC and thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species generation under visible light. Simultaneously, QAC introduce permanent cationic surface charges that enable contact-mediated microbial inactivation and humidity-resistant electrostatic particle capture. Demonstrated on biodegradable silk nanofibers as a model substrate, the functionalized fibers exhibit potent antibacterial and antiviral activity under both dark and illuminated conditions, together with high nanoparticle capture efficiency. Importantly, the fibers retain intrinsic biodegradability, undergoing near-complete degradation under enzymatic conditions and substantial decomposition in soil environments. This work establishes a versatile surface functionalization platform applicable to diverse fibrous substrates, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional microplastic-generating protective materials.
authors: Dong Uk Lee, Jae Hak Shin, Seung Yeon Lee, In Ho Kim, Jiho Choi, Joon Young Park, Sang Bok Kim, Jeong Sang Son, Sang Hun Kim, Jae Hee Jung, Dong Yun Choi

10.1002/adma.75593.title: Heterostructure Design in Two-Dimensional Perovskites by Sequential Recrystallization
10.1002/adma.75593.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost-efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow. Here, we demonstrate a versatile one-pot synthesis to fabricate a large variety of 2D perovskite heterostructures based on different halides and/or metal cations. Exploiting sequential crystallization of different 2D perovskites and tuning the composition and injection events of the materials, enables the design of diverse heterostructure architectures, including multiple heterojunctions. We obtain heterostructures with high crystalline quality, multicolor emission, and optical coupling between the different heterostructure regions. We foresee that the design freedom of our method will stimulate the development of novel optoelectronic devices where electronic band engineering is crucial.
