10.1002/adma.75053.title: Versatile Soluble Iron Oxide-Based Monolayers With Ultrahigh Two-Dimensional State Stability
10.1002/adma.75053.abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to the quantum confinement effect, atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) materials exhibit many exceptional physical properties that are closely related to their atomically thin structure, rendering them extraordinary application potential across diverse fields. However, maintaining their 2D state stability in versatile systems has been a challenge for their practical applications. Here, we report a facile coordination-substitution strategy to synthesize iron oxide-based (FeO-NHR, NHR = primary amine) monolayers with large lateral dimensions and high crystallinity. Benefiting from sufficient and tunable coordinated functional groups, the FeO-NHR monolayers feature good solubility in low-polarity solvents along with ultra-high 2D state stability. By changing the coordination with oxygen-rich organic ligands, the as-obtained FeO-NHR monolayers exhibit good water solubility and biocompatibility, and show superior antibacterial activity under light irradiation in the presence of hydrogen peroxide. Our findings provide a robust FeO-based 2D platform with tailorable solubility and ultra-high 2D state stability, offering new insights for the rational design of other reliable solution-processable 2D materials.
authors: Chuying Dai, Ping He, Shengpeng Xia, Haotian Bai, Youquan Liu, Peilin Yang, Bo Guan, Yue Zeng, Yue Liu, Lingxiang Hou, Zike Wang, Xueping Cui, Shu Wang, Jian Zheng

10.1002/adma.75097.title: Injectable Bioadhesive Ultrasonic Sensor for Continuous and Wireless On-Demand Pressure Monitoring in Acute Compartment Syndrome
10.1002/adma.75097.abstract: ABSTRACT Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) is a severe orthopedic emergency caused by limb injuries and elevated intra-compartmental pressure (ICP), which can lead to permanent disability. Clinical practice has long pursued continuous and on-demand ICP monitoring across the risk window for accurate ACS management. Existing probe manometry imposes pain and infection risk, particularly during prolonged wired indwelling or repeated punctures. Implantable electronic sensors enable wireless monitoring, but face biocompatibility and stability challenges from the mismatched human-machine interface. Here, we present an injectable, bioadhesive ultrasonic sensor (metagel sensor) that enables continuous and wireless on-demand monitoring of intracompartmental pressure across the post-njury clinical window. The ultrasonic modulation properties of the metastructural hydrogel encode pressure signals into reflected ultrasonic waves as measurable bandgap shifts, enabling fully passive wireless readout. The metagel exhibited substantial biodegradation over 14 weeks in rats. In a porcine model, we demonstrated the capability of the metagel sensor in continuous acute-phase ICP monitoring and repeated wireless on-demand interrogation over 10 days. Simultaneously decoupled signals related to respiration and pulse offer additional physiological information relevant to ACS assessment.
authors: Lejie Qin, Huanyan Liu, Zhangqi Pan, Bo Gao, Yue Lian, Na Li, Yuan Feng, Yibo Huang, Haonan Wang, Ye Tian, Yuchen Zhou, Ligang Cui, Hanchuan Tang, Jianfeng Zang

10.1002/adma.75135.title: Enhanced Interfacial Contact Enables Stable MA-free Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75135.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite rapid efficiency gains in perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells (P/Si TSCs), state-of-the-art devices continue to rely heavily on methylammonium (MA)-containing wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, where MA facilitates crystallization but intrinsically accelerates thermal degradation and halide segregation. Achieving efficient, thick (>700 nm), MA-free WBG perovskites on textured silicon remains an unresolved challenge. Here, a coordination network coupled with π-π stacking work is designed to synchronize kinetics in MA-free FACs-based perovskite and promote conformal integration with textured silicon. A compact heterocyclic molecule simultaneously forms hydrogen-bonds with FA cations and coordinates with the Pb-I framework, while engaging in π-π stacking with underlying self-assembled monolayers. This multi-interaction synergy regulates nucleation and drives vertical crystal growth, yielding void-free buried interfaces and columnar grains spanning the full film thickness. The reconstructed interface exhibits reduced trap density and favorable energy-level alignment, enabling efficient hole extraction and suppressing electron back-transport and mixed-halide segregation. Consequently, the 1.68 eV MA-free perovskite device achieves an efficiency of 24.04%. Monolithic P/Si TSCs reach 33.04% efficiency, maintaining >90% initial performance after 1600 h of maximum power point tracking. This work establishes a generalizable strategy to decoupling crystallization control from MA incorporation, enabling durable and high-performance tandem photovoltaics.
authors: Jiyao Wei, Biao Li, Yu Tong, Weihua Ning, Yong Wang, Deren Yang, Xuegong Yu

10.1002/adma.74884.title: Binder Engineering for Phosphoric Acid Distribution and Retention in High-Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Cathodes
10.1002/adma.74884.abstract: ABSTRACT High-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT-PEMFCs) offer compelling advantages for energy conversion, including simplified water and thermal management and high tolerance to fuel impurities. In these systems, phosphoric acid (PA) serves as the primary proton conductor, enabling anhydrous proton transport. However, cathode performance and durability remain constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics and the challenge of controlling PA distribution and retention. Uneven acid distribution, manifesting as local flooding that blocks gas pathways and covers active sites or local depletion that disrupts proton-conducting networks, causes severe mass-transport losses and performance decay. Concurrently, gradual PA migration and loss during operation progressively degrade proton conduction pathways, accelerating voltage decay. Recent studies have established cathode binder engineering as an effective strategy to regulate both PA distribution and retention. This review systematically examines the design of cathode binder systems-encompassing polymer binder optimization and functional additive integration-and the characterization and diagnostic frameworks for evaluating their efficacy in PA management. We further integrate advanced PA characterization techniques with a comprehensive electrochemical performance evaluation framework. By establishing explicit connections among binder design, PA distribution and retention behavior, and device-level performance assessment, this review provides an instructive guide for the rational development of high-performance, durable HT-PEMFC cathodes.
authors: Pengyu Song, Xiaotao Liu, Junwen Zhou, Lu Wang, Bo Wang

10.1002/adma.75011.title: Geometry-Mediated Microgel Structure-Mechanics for Intestinal Region-Specific Probiotic Delivery
10.1002/adma.75011.abstract: ABSTRACT The physiological efficacy of functional food ingredients, particularly probiotics is highly dependent on their spatial localization within the intestine. The non-specific delivery of probiotics severely restricts their therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we developed a sustainable, food-grade microgel delivery platform assembled from corncob nanocellulose building blocks with distinct geometries for programmable intestinal probiotic release. Owing to their distinct topological structures and mechanical properties, spherical nanocellulose-based microgels (CNSM) were found to disintegrate in the ileum, while rod-like nanocellulose-based microgels (CNRM) retained intact until reaching the colon, where they subsequently ruptured. Molecular dynamics simulations supported the superior structural stability of CNRM against osmotic swelling, revealing a structure-mechanics driven mechanism for the controlled release pattern. Both microgels significantly enhanced probiotic survival, as well as nanocoating-mediated mucoadhesion and colonization. To maximize functionality, bile salt hydrolase-producing L. plantarum WCFS1 and immunomodulatory L. rhamnosus GG were embedded into CNSM and CNRM, respectively. Consequently, ileum-targeted WCFS1@CNSM significantly ameliorated hypercholesterolemia, accompanied by increased fecal cholesterol excretion and potential modulation of the gut-liver signaling axis whereas colon-targeted LGG@CNRM profoundly alleviated DSS-induced colitis through epithelial barrier restoration and inflammation suppression. This work provides a region-specific delivery strategy for next-generation probiotic therapeutics.
authors: Shanan Chen, Wei Shang, Qimeng Wang, Jasper Landman, Yoav D. Livney, Yuemiao Zhang, Caroline Thum, Shangwu Chen, Zhengyuan Zhai, Xiangyu Liu, Zhaoxiang Ma, Wenxuan Di, Yuan Li

10.1002/adma.75098.title: A Single Quasi-Vertical van der Waals Heterostructure Memristor as Opto-Reconfigurable Artificial Intelligence Hardware
10.1002/adma.75098.abstract: ABSTRACT The explosive advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has driven vast amounts of unstructured data that directly emerges at sensory interaction interfaces. Memristors with superior computing ability are among the most promising computing blocks. However, conventional vertical Metal/Resistive layer/Metal (V-MRM) memristors tend to generate intense electric fields, suffer from limited sensory response, inflexible, and rigid functional modes, as well as long-standing variability and overshoot issues. Here, we present an unconventional two-terminal quasi-vertical (QV) van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) memristor as opto-reconfigurable hardware. Unlike the V-MRM memristor with a strong, rigid vertical electric field, this QV-vdWH memristor realizes a significantly softened, tunable electric field, enabling parametric configurable and wavelength-dependent reconfigurable modes across nonvolatile/volatile memory, neurons, synapses, and optical perception. Moreover, the light-memristive switching-vdWH coupling triggers a super-additive synergistic enhancement of memristive performance (> 100-fold) and photoresponse (> 3000-fold). Meanwhile, the long-standing variability and overshoot issues are overcome, yielding ultra-uniform memristive behavior with even a single-valued distribution. Leveraging the opto-reconfigurability, high-accuracy object tracking, and human motion recognition (∼96.8%) are successfully performed. Breaking through the inherent functional limitation of the conventional V-MRM memristive structure, the QV-vdWH memristor provides a flexible, opto-reconfigurable hardware platform for emerging computing paradigms, and AI applications.
authors: Yesheng Li, Changxu Yin, Xiaolin Zhang, Gaoli Luo, Yi Wang, Wenkai Zhou, Yao Xiong, Jun He

10.1002/adma.75099.title: Engineered Extracellular Vesicle Revitalizing Macrophage Energy Metabolism for Aged Wound Repair
10.1002/adma.75099.abstract: ABSTRACT One major obstacle for aged wound healing is the abnormal senescence of macrophages in chronic wounds which causes immunosenescence. Tissue homeostasis depends on regulation of metabolism in accumulating senescent cells (SnCs) with aging, and cell activation for aged tissue repair requires sufficient energy. Therapeutic advancements are potential by employing metabolic strategies for intervention. First, a disorder of arginine-oxidative phosphorylation metabolism in aging skin was found, which may be the main culprit of aging. Engineered EVs (4-octyl itaconate (4OI)-EVs) which possess naturally abundance of mitochondrial proteins have been developed here. Our findings demonstrate that 4OI-engineered EV (4OI-EV) may accelerate the repair of aged mouse skin and diabetic mouse skin, reduce cellular senescence, and recover cell dysfunctions. After 4OI-EV therapy, metabolism has been notably altered, with decreased glycolysis and increased arginine-oxidative phosphorylation axis through enhanced argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) level. We demonstrate how 4OI-EV partially restores macrophages senescence by reversing mitochondrial dysfunctions and mitophagy suppressions via ASS1 which may be identified as a potential effective target for alleviating skin aging.
authors: Jiayi Ding, Jie Li, Tongyao Ji, Mengjie Huang, Peiyao Liu, Kun Zhang, Jian Li, Ji Ma, Xiaoxiao Chen, Fengkai Qiu, Minjiang Chen, Gaofeng Shu, Weiqian Chen, Jiansong Ji

10.1002/adma.75130.title: Stepped-Dimensional 2D/3D Tin-Based Perovskites for High-Efficiency Light-Emitting Diodes
10.1002/adma.75130.abstract: ABSTRACT Tin (Sn)-based perovskite near-infrared (NIR) light-emitting diodes (LEDs) show great potential for applications in night vision, biomedical sensing, and optical communications. However, their performance remains limited by uncontrolled crystallization and the facile oxidation of Sn 2+ . Here, we demonstrate a versatile buried-interlayer strategy to effectively regulate the crystallization and suppress the Sn 2+ oxidation by constructing a two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) heterodimensional structure. We reveal that strong interactions between the buried ligand layer, the perovskite precursor, and the underlying hole-transport layer promote rapid nucleation, retard crystal growth, and induce a vertical dimensional gradient, leading to reduced defect density and enhanced radiative recombination. As a result, NIR Sn-based perovskite LEDs achieve a record external quantum efficiency of 13.7% with a radiance of 103 W sr −1 m −2 . Furthermore, the buried-interlayer strategy enables dual-functional Sn-based perovskite devices capable of both efficient light emission and photodetection, which are successfully integrated into a compact heart-pulse monitoring system. Our work suggests a synergistic crystallization and dimensional-regulation strategy for achieving high-performance Sn-based perovskite optoelectronic devices.
authors: Pengpeng Teng, Zheng Jiang, Yuhan Zhou, Yangyu Liu, Wenxiao Niu, Chunping Pu, Quan Liu, Xianrong Li, Fan Pu, Yiran Zhang, Qipan Yu, Xingjiao Feng, Dongxu Jin, Yuxuan Wei, Wenhao Zheng, Zhibo Yan, Haifeng Zhao, Sai Bai, Yatao Zou, Weidong Xu, Wing Chung Tsoi, Tao Yu, Jie Yang, Xiaodong Shen, Chunxiong Bao

10.1002/adma.75133.title: Programmable Doping-Enabled Engineering of Hydrogel Iontronics for Tailored Soft Ionic Devices
10.1002/adma.75133.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft ionic conductors with tunable mechanical properties and biological signal compatibility are essential for facilitating seamless abiotic-biotic interfaces. However, the lack of precise, scalable control over the intrinsic transport performance of these materials critically restricts their broader deployment in advanced biotechnology. In this work, we present a programmable doping strategy, inspired by conventional semiconductor manufacturing paradigms, aimed at creating high-performance hydrogel iontronic devices. By systematically modulating polyelectrolyte concentrations and strategically integrating lignosulfonate sodium, we meticulously tailor the semiconducting characteristics of hydrogel heterojunctions. The resulting programmable hydrogels exhibit exceptional operational tunability, successfully functioning as robust ionic diodes, logic circuits, pnp-type transistors, and synthetic synapses. This scalable method establishes a highly adaptable framework for tailored soft ionic conductors, broadening their potential applications in complex signal transmission and neuromorphic computing.
authors: Ye Rao, Yanbing Li, Shuihong Zhu, Lianfei Huang, Senxuan Tang, Jia Yi, Tianqi Fu, Zhehao Han, Youhui Lin, Huanghao Yang

10.1002/adma.75629.title: Discovery of Small-Molecule Cryoprotectants Using Pretrained Language Model Representations
10.1002/adma.75629.abstract: ABSTRACT Cryopreservation supports cell therapy, transfusion medicine, and tissue banking, but cryoprotectant selection remains constrained by empirical screening, toxicity, and ice recrystallization. We used pretrained language models as SMILES sequence encoders to prioritize small-molecule cryoprotectants for experimental testing. Hierarchical representations were coupled to descriptor reconstruction, gated fusion, and downstream prediction of normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels. Splat-cooling measurements assessed candidate ice recrystallization inhibition, followed by compatibility and cryopreservation experiments in red blood cells, human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells and rat abdominal aortas. Selected additives improved recovery or preservation endpoints within the tested formulations. This representation-based screening workflow connects molecular property prediction with experimental cryobiology across ice, cellular, and tissue endpoints.

10.1002/adma.75626.title: Bismuth-Mediated Zinc Extraction-Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single-Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
10.1002/adma.75626.abstract: ABSTRACT Fe single-atom catalysts with Fe-N 4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi-mediated Fe-adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe-N 4 moieties on ZIF-8-derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe-N-pC d catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half-wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi-solid-state Zn-air battery using Fe-N-pC d as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at −40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe-N 4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH-bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect-modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d-band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe-*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential-limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring-template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

10.1002/adma.75661.title: High-Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging
10.1002/adma.75661.abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurface-enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high-throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade-off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction-enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high-quality-factor resonances. By embedding bound-state-in-the-continuum metapixels within a bandgap-engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three-dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal-to-noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single-shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral-spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one-to-one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single-pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real-time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.

10.1002/adma.75543.title: Quantum Saturation of the Electro-Optic Effect
10.1002/adma.75543.abstract: ABSTRACT Future quantum computing architectures require electro-optic materials that maintain a strong, stable performance at cryogenic temperatures. In conventional electro-optic materials, large electro-optic coefficients are often confined to narrow temperature windows near structural phase transitions, where small changes in temperature lead to large changes in the electro-optic response. Using thermodynamic analysis, phase-field simulations, experimental growth, and cryogenic optical measurements, we show that quantum fluctuations can be harnessed to overcome this trade-off. By tuning the ferroelectric phase boundaries down to 0 K, quantum fluctuations induce a saturation regime in which a large electro-optic response becomes nearly temperature-independent below 25 K. We demonstrate that the phase boundaries can be tuned through either strain in BaTiO 3 or through chemical composition in Ba 1- x Ca x TiO 3 , leading to a large, temperature-insensitive, cryogenic electro-optic response, r eff = 2850 pm V −1 (experiment) and r 51 = 2900 pm V −1 (theory) for BaTiO 3 on GdScO 3 and r 51 = 1898 pm V −1 (theory) for Ba 0.77 Ca 0.23 TiO 3 . These values exceed the room temperature performance of bulk BaTiO 3 r 51 = 1600 pm V −1 and surpass the cryogenic performance of BaTiO 3 -on-Si, r eff = 200 pm V −1 , by over an order of magnitude. These findings establish a general design principle for engineering high-performance electro-optic materials for cryogenic applications.

10.1002/adma.75646.title: Preserving Polymorphic Crystalline Structures in Bulk Heterojunctions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75646.abstract: ABSTRACT The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non-halogenated mixed-solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS 2 ) and o-xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high-performance acceptor BTP-eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat-film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide-angle x-ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing-incidence wide-angle x-ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single-crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non-radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II-based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm 2 active area) fabricated by slot-die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution-processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single-crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.

10.1002/adma.75658.title: Sustainable Soft Electronic Devices by High-Performance Recyclable Elastomers and Conductors
10.1002/adma.75658.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft electronics have driven emerging advancements, which are expected to have wide-range and large-scale applications in health management, electronic skins, soft robotics, and interactive human-machine interfaces. However, existing strategies mainly focus on isolated components, and system-level soft electronic devices combining sustainable fabrication, robust performance, and versatile integrated functions have rarely been explored. Herein, we develop a recyclable soft electronic system enabled with multifunctional poly thioctic acid (TA) elastomer and high-performance elastic metallic conductors. The multifunctional TA elastomer exhibits an exceptional combination of stretchability (435% strain), fracture energy (5.5 kJ/m 2 ), apparent adhesion energy on Cu (10.7 kJ/m 2 ), and thermal conductivity (0.69 W/m·K). These properties enable robust mechanical and electronic interfacing with different electronic components for sustainable soft circuits, while also endowing the electronic systems with outstanding self-healing and recycling capabilities. Furthermore, by integrating with printable and recyclable elastic conductors based on eutectic liquid metals, the sustainable soft electronic systems can fully restore circuit functionality after complete mechanical rupture with the selfhealing capability of the composite elastomer and the elastic conductor. The system can be reprocessed to achieve full functionality restoration. The materials strategy developed in this study renders a promising solution for the development of soft and sustainable electronic devices.

10.1002/adma.75604.title: Ultralow Loading Iridium Doped Hollandite Manganese Oxide Nanowires for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction
10.1002/adma.75604.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow-loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, <16 µgIr cm − 2 ) integrated within a hollandite MnO 2 framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm − 2 from 580 mV (undoped α-MnO 2 ) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrO x . Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP-MS dissolution measurements with x-ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH- and potential-dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir-efficient mixed-metal oxide catalysts.

10.1002/adma.75664.title: Pd Single-Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self-Decoupled Temperature-Humidity Dual-Mode Sensors
10.1002/adma.75664.abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high-fidelity multi-modal temperature-humidity sensing without inter-channel cross-talk and computational post-processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron-ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self-decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single-atom anchoring and heterogeneous-nucleation-driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus-response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra-fast quasi-2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy-driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross-talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low-temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi-modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed-loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on-demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next-generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

10.1002/adma.75650.title: Upcycling Piezoelectric Single-Crystal Debris Into High-Performance Flexible 0-3 Composites
10.1002/adma.75650.abstract: ABSTRACT High-value piezoelectric single-crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor-based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off-cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling-to-device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 -PbTiO 3 (PMN-PT) single-crystal debris into high-performance flexible 0-3 piezoelectric composites and energy harvesters through material-structure-mechanics co-design. A ball-milling-based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)-assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi-1-3-like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single-crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a d 33 of 118.5 pC N −1 while retaining mechanical flexibility, placing it among the highest-performing flexible 0-3 piezoelectric composites. Comparative experiments and finite-element simulations reveal that single-crystal-derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP-induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm − 2 . This work establishes a scalable upcycling pathway for reutilizing high-value functional crystal waste in flexible self-powered electromechanical systems.

10.1002/adma.75682.title: Ion-Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision
10.1002/adma.75682.abstract: ABSTRACT A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single-channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion-electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual-channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic-light-guided closed-loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This “single device enabled, distinguishable dual-channel readouts” principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

10.1002/adma.75619.title: Rate Capability of Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Oxide Cathodes: Charge-Discharge Kinetics, Multiscale Bottlenecks, and Dynamic Rate-Determining Steps
10.1002/adma.75619.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g −1 through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next-generation high-energy-density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast-charging applications. This review deconstructs rate-limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge-transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate-determining step (RDS) shifts from electron-transfer to ion-diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density ( j 0 ) and the limiting current density ( j d ). Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often-overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high-rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross-study C-rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high-rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.

10.1002/adma.75654.title: pH-Responsive Synthetic Cells for Programmable In Situ Protein Synthesis and Release
10.1002/adma.75654.abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid membrane-bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell-like compartments for on-demand biomolecule production. However, most cell-free gene expression systems in synthetic cells are regulated by user-imposed cues rather than signals associated with environmental or physiological states. Here, we present an acidity-transducing synthetic cell that converts external pH changes into nucleic acid information to drive in situ protein synthesis. The system integrates gramicidin A proton channels for pH sensing, triplex-forming single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that releases a trigger ssDNA upon acidification, and a toehold switch RNA that activates translation in response to the released trigger ssDNA. This work further reveals that tuning the annealing length between the pH-responsive and trigger ssDNAs controls the trigger-release pH, which is critical for enabling acid-triggered protein synthesis. The synthetic cells retain their pH-responsive activity when embedded in alginate hydrogels, creating acidity-responsive materials that synthesize proteins in situ rather than release preloaded cargo. Cell-penetrating peptide tagging further enables selective protein release and target-specific binding. This work establishes a molecular transduction strategy for programming synthetic cell materials to sense environmentally relevant acidity and generates functional biomolecules on demand.

10.1002/adma.75647.title: Fluoride-Mediated Host-Activator Engineering in Homogeneous Lithium Glass Scintillators for Thermal-Neutron Detection and Imaging
10.1002/adma.75647.abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous lithium-aluminosilicate-glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride-mediated host-activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce 3+ -activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F − preferentially coordinates with Li + and Mg 2+ , preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter-tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host-network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect-mediated trapping, modulates medium-range Ce-centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce-concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO 2 (twice that of GS20). After 6 Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron −1 , an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak-to-trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6 Li-enriched glass scintillator, achieving single-digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3 He proportional counters and high-performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof-of-concept two-dimensional thermal-neutron imaging with a system-level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position-sensitive neutron imaging.

10.1002/adma.75683.title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10 H -Pyrido[1,2- a ]-5-indolium Salts
10.1002/adma.75683.abstract: ABSTRACT Next-generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent-free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation-caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion-π + interactions. Specifically, a rigid N-doped fluorene (10 H -pyrido[1,2- a ]-5-indolium, PIn + ) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent-free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

10.1002/adma.75635.title: Dynamic, Wet-Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
10.1002/adma.75635.abstract: ABSTRACT Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self-repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial-based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet-adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid-covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff-base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine-containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self-healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane-derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host-graft integration, and cartilage-like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet-adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial-cartilage interface healing in fluid-rich joint environments.

10.1002/adma.75643.title: Skunk Cabbage-Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence
10.1002/adma.75643.abstract: ABSTRACT Near-infrared (NIR)-responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade-offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra-fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR-responsive actuators by integrating aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus-structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra-low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi-donor-π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor-acceptor interactions and molecular motion-facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat-transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.

10.1002/adma.75649.title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial- and Mesenchymal-Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC-Derived Intestinal Organoids
10.1002/adma.75649.abstract: ABSTRACT Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill-defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG- and Matrigel-cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation-associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM-remodelling and integrin-associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2-positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

10.1002/adma.75668.title: A Dual-Locked and H 2 S-NO Tandem-Activatable NIR-II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics
10.1002/adma.75668.abstract: ABSTRACT Dual-locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual-locked systems only restricted to enzyme-responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker-responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near-infrared (NIR-II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual-locked and gas tandem-activatable NIR-II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water-dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid-responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN-NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible-NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN-NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H 2 S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR-II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN-NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type-I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR-II fluorescence imaging-guided efficient photo-elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual-locked and H 2 S-NO tandem-activatable nanoagents with gas-responsive and NIR-II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

10.1002/adma.75670.title: Sensitive, Broadband, and Stable Short-Wave Infrared Photodetection and Imaging in Mixed-Dimensional Organic/Inorganic Heterostructures
10.1002/adma.75670.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional short-wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed-dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier-collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices’ performance. Herein, a type-II band-aligned PTF/WSe 2 mixed-dimensional heterostructure is reported for high-performance broadband SWIR photodetection via heterostructure synergy and rational Schottky barrier engineering. The Cr/ p -WSe 2 /PTF configuration (∼ 0.28 eV barrier) achieves superior performance, while Cr/ n -WSe 2 /PTF suffers from a higher barrier (∼ 1.18 eV). The optimized device achieves broad spectral photoresponsivity (∼ 10 3 A/W, 1060-1470 nm) and exceptional performance at 1310 nm: ultrahigh photoresponsivity ( R = 2894 A/W), robust specific detectivity ( D * = 1.0×10 12 Jones), and excellent long-term ambient stability. Versus standalone PTF, it delivers 17-fold higher photoresponsivity and 96% lower bias voltage. High-resolution SWIR image-pattern reconstruction, together with concurrent performance improvements after six months of controlled storage, validates this PTF/WSe 2 mixed-dimensional heterostructure's potential for advancing next-generation high-performance SWIR detectors.

10.1002/adma.75659.title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ-Formed Ceramic-Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation
10.1002/adma.75659.abstract: ABSTRACT Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water-rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross-linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual-mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm − 3 ) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame-inhibiting SO 2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic-carbon hybrid barrier. Post-test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO 4 ) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically “weld” B 2 O 3 to carbon. This trend in BO 4 fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high-performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi-stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next-generation battery safety materials.

10.1002/adma.74306.title: Soft-Rigid Liquid Metal-SiC Hybrid Fillers Enable Superior Nonlinear Conductivity and Electric Field Regulation of Composite Dielectrics
10.1002/adma.74306.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonlinear dielectrics with superior electric field regulation capabilities are essential for advanced power equipment. However, traditional nonlinear dielectric materials depend on an electrical percolation mechanism, requiring high concentrations of nonlinear conductive filler that degrade insulation and mechanical properties. Herein, we propose a synergistic strategy using a hybrid filler of soft liquid metal and rigid silicon carbide particles (LM-SiCp) to develop insulating nonlinear composite dielectrics. The unique LM-SiCp structure enables a favorable network of potential barriers at low fields and steep exponential current growth at high fields, yielding an excellent “low onset, high gain” nonlinear behavior. The resulting composites exhibit an impressive nonlinear coefficient of ∼7.55 and a markedly reduced threshold field strength from 4.81 to 3.41 kV/mm. It also achieves improved toughness (2.29 MJ/m 3 ), thermal conductivity (0.36 W/mK), high breakdown strength (∼33.4 kV/mm), and low dielectric loss (<0.03), which ensure the stable performance of the composite dielectric under practical engineering conditions. This strategy offers a novel design concept for high-performance composite dielectrics capable of effective electric field modulation in power equipment.

10.1002/adma.74547.title: Direct Observation of Propagating Spin Waves in a Spin Hall Nano-Oscillator
10.1002/adma.74547.abstract: ABSTRACT Constriction-based spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) show great promise for application as highly tunable microwave sources with straightforward scalability toward large coupled networks. However, details of the magnetization dynamics within SHNOs have thus far not been addressed experimentally, due to the minute time and length scales involved. In this work, we present direct imaging of the magnetization dynamics within a single CoFeB-based SHNO using time-resolved scanning transmission x-ray microscopy (TR-STXM). Our measurements reveal that the magnon amplitude is strongest at the two constriction edges, with a pronounced asymmetry favoring one edge, and that the emitted spin waves (SWs) exhibit strongly anisotropic propagation. Micromagnetic simulations suggest that grain boundaries and the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) play a key role in both effects. Furthermore, the magnetodynamics changed during measurement, indicating that the CoFeB/MgO interface may be more susceptible to x-ray-induced modifications than previously recognized, challenging its presumed radiation hardness.

10.1002/adma.74548.title: A Scalable, Robust, and Bioinspired Liquid Diode for Ultrafast Unidirectional Absorption
10.1002/adma.74548.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient management of biofluids on body surfaces is essential for advanced medical protection and healthcare. While conventional designs often rely solely on unidirectional penetration, our previously established model of a microfiber-covered porous substrate leverages synergistic interplay between lateral capillary forces and vertical permeation to enhance absorption kinetics by over 150-fold. However, scalable fabrication and mechanical robustness of such a structure remain challenging. Here, we present a semi-continuous manufacturing strategy based on electrostatic flocking combined with non-solvent-induced phase separation to produce a trilayered composite consisting of a micro-fiber array, a porous adhesive interlayer, and a fibrous support (MA-PA-FS). We systematically elucidate the role of each layer in guiding rapid liquid absorption and enhancing structural integrity. The optimized MA-PA-FS composite achieves ultrafast unidirectional water absorption (5 µL in 9.3 ms)-three orders of magnitude faster than a porous control surface (90.0 s)-and also effectively absorbs viscous biological fluids such as fresh porcine blood. Besides exceptional liquid absorption, the material exhibits high moisture permeability and strong mechanical durability. This study provides a scientific foundation for designing scalable, high-performance biofluid-handling interfaces, with promising potential in medical textiles, protective gear, and related health technologies.

10.1002/adma.74812.title: Self-Feeding Living Materials Enabled by Cell Responsive Glycogen Nanoparticles as Metabolic Batteries
10.1002/adma.74812.abstract: ABSTRACT Scaling engineered living materials to clinically relevant dimensions is limited by diffusion-dependent depletion of oxygen and nutrients, which rapidly induces metabolic failure. We introduce glycogen as a nutritional nanoparticle that provides cell-mediated, autonomous nutrient release to support long-term survival under extreme metabolic stress. We demonstrate that human mesenchymal stromal cells (hMSCs) survive for weeks in anoxia and serum deprivation when provided extracellular glycogen. Contrary to long-held assumptions, hMSCs secrete glycogen-degrading enzymes, enabling cell-density-controlled extracellular glycogenolysis and sustained release of glucose and metabolic intermediates, positioning glycogen as the first-of-its-kind metabolic battery. This cell-responsive process maintains metabolic activity, limits glycolytic acidosis, and enhances pro-angiogenic signaling. To translate this mechanism into a versatile materials platform, we engineered core-shell dextran-tyramine microcapsules that stably encapsulate glycogen while permitting diffusion of enzymes and degradation products. Integrated into centimeter-scale GelMA constructs, these microcapsules maintained hMSC viability and function for at least 1 month under anoxia. In vivo, glycogen-loaded implants promote deep cellular infiltration, enhanced matrix remodeling, increased M2 macrophage polarization, and orchestrated accelerated vascularization. This work establishes the novel concept of glycogen-based nutritional nanoparticles as metabolic batteries to endow engineered tissues with autonomous self-feeding capacity, enabling scalable and functional living materials for regenerative medicine and related technologies.
