10.1002/adma.75700.title: Polymer-Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template-Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single-Crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3
10.1002/adma.75700.abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer-directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template-free synthesis of mesoporous single-crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3 (MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn 2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single-crystalline MnBO 2 OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 . As an anode active material for lithium-ion batteries, MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , more than twice that of bulk Mn 2 OBO 3 . Notably, this polymer-directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single-crystalline materials for energy storage.

10.1002/adma.75688.title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π-Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro-Crosslinking-Network for Flexible Polymer Light-Emitting Diodes
10.1002/adma.75688.abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π-conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic-deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft-micro-crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p - n FπCPs (P X -OXI 1-X -HDI) films with a recoverable-deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three-dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro-crosslinked network formed by oxime-urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro-crosslinked p - n FπCPs free-standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X -OXI 1-X -HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro-crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle-deformation-stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro-crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long-term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

10.1002/adma.75645.title: Determining Composition-Structure-Property Relationships in Quaternary Perovskitoids Through Megalibraries
10.1002/adma.75645.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how composition governs structure and function is essential for designing functional materials, however, establishing these relationships remains prohibitively slow for materials with massive and tunable compositional spaces, such as Bi and Sb-based perovskitoids. Here, a novel megalibrary-based synthetic methodology has been developed and used to rapidly identify and characterize quaternary perovskite derivatives across an expansive compositional space. Parylene templates were used to synthesize one million compositionally distinct, positionally encoded Cs 3 Sb 2−x Bi x Br 9−y I y microcrystals on 2 × 2 cm 2 chips with 20 µm periodicity. These megalibraries enabled the systematic investigation of structural and optoelectronic evolution across this compositional space using micro-area x-ray diffraction, position-resolved absorbance spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and confocal fluorescence microscopy. An unusual non-monotonic bandgap shift was observed with increasing Br content, reaching a minimum at 33% Br. This behavior is attributed to the formation of halide-segregated heterostructures, consisting of low-dimensional, I-rich shells surrounding Br-rich layered cores. Phase separation was most pronounced in Sb-rich compositions, which were found to stabilize heterostructure formation. This study demonstrates how megalibraries enable the simultaneous evaluation of key optoelectronic parameters, including bandgap and phase purity, revealing complex, composition-dependent structure-function relationships in perovskitoids and providing a versatile platform for accelerating the discovery of optoelectronic-relevant materials.

10.1002/aenm.71681.title: Pore-Stitching Engineering of Biomass-Derived Hard Carbon for Enhanced Sodium-Ion Storage
10.1002/aenm.71681.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass-derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising and cost-effective anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Prior to carbonization, biomass precursors are commonly subjected to acid/alkali purification to remove metallic and non-metallic impurities. However, the accompanying ionic etching process often generates abundant through-pores and disrupts the carbon framework, leading to increased irreversible capacity loss. Herein, we propose a “pore stitching” strategy using hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a functional reconstruction precursor. The hydroxyl-rich HEC is proposed to interact with oxygen-containing sites in the demineralized precursor and to be retained within accessible pore regions during mixing and drying. During subsequent carbonization, HEC-derived carbon contributes to the reconstruction of the disrupted carbon framework, resulting in reduced open surface exposure and a redistributed micro/ultramicroporous architecture while preserving favorable Na + storage domains. Consequently, the optimized HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 375.3 mAh g − 1 at 20 mA g − 1 . A 700 mAh pouch cell pairing this HC with sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 , NFPP) delivers 150 Wh kg − 1 based on the combined active-material mass of both electrodes and retains 97.8% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a viable route for converting impurity-rich agricultural waste into high-performance HC anodes for practical sodium-ion energy storage.
authors: Xueting Shen, Guiyu Liu, Wenjun Shi, Cheng Wang, Xuhui Li, Hongzhi Wang, Chengyu Yang, Yulin Cao, Lijie Ci, Hua Cheng, Zhouguang Lu

10.1002/aenm.71695.title: Dual Descriptor-Guided Design of Hydrated Eutectic Electrolytes for Stable Zinc Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71695.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise large-scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen-bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H 2 O activity and regulate Zn 2+ desolvation through hydrogen-bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol-based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen-bond network formation and Zn 2+ coordination. A series of C 2 -C 6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen-bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C 4 , EOD = 0.022 Å −3 , MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery-enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm −2 with 1 mAh cm −2 , and the Zn||I 2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.
authors: Qian Li, Chen Zhang, Yida Hu, Xueer Xu, Mingyue Zhu, Yu Zhong, Jiangping Tu, Changdong Gu

10.1002/aenm.71700.title: Jahn-Teller Distortion of MnO6 Octahedra Enhances Piezoelectric Polarization and Lattice Oxygen Activation of BaTiO3 for Efficient Piezo-PEC Water Splitting
10.1002/aenm.71700.abstract: ABSTRACT Piezo-photoelectrochemical (Piezo-PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water-splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn-Teller effect-driven strategy to regulate the local B-site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO 3 for efficient Piezo-PEC water splitting. By introducing Mn 3+ ions with asymmetric e g orbital occupancy (t 2g 3 e g 1 ), a local MnO 6 octahedral coordination environment is constructed and pronounced Jahn-Teller distortion is induced. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn-Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non-centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn 3+ strengthens Ti─O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water-splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) toward the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), thus accelerating reaction kinetics. Under coupled ultrasonic vibration and illumination, the optimized BTMO-6 photoanode delivers a high photocurrent density of 2.18 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE and exhibits a piezoelectric coefficient (d 33 ) of 52.3 pm V −1 . This work reveals that Jahn-Teller distortion simultaneously enhances piezo-polarization and tunes reaction pathways, offering new insights for robust Piezo-PEC water-splitting systems.
authors: Tianyu Jia, Mengnan Ruan, Chengyi Wang, Li Zhou, Zhifeng Liu

10.1002/aenm.71693.title: Nickel-Free Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Self-Assembled Monolayers: A Pathway to Efficient and Recyclable Devices
10.1002/aenm.71693.abstract: ABSTRACT High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel-containing hole-selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross-contamination during end-of-life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel-free hole-selective interface material based on phenyl-substituted phosphonic-acid carbazole self-assembled monolayers (Ph-nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure-property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph-5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried-interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me-4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph-5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel-free interface enables a closed-loop recycling route unavailable to nickel-based devices, with recycled-ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life-cycle and techno-economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity-related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.
authors: Yanxue Wang, Roman Kučera, Sinuhé Perea-Puente, Mykhailo Sytnyk, Andrew Hainer, Zijian Peng, Savannah Bennett, Juan S. Rocha-Ortiz, Albert These, Hakan U Dag, Qi Fan, Anastasia Barabash, Zhenni Wu, Chaohui Li, Jens Hauch, Olga Kasian, Christoph J. Brabec, Ian Marius Peters

10.1002/aenm.71692.title: Photoelectrochemical Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion: Cocatalyst Design Principles and Mechanistic Insights from Electrocatalysis
10.1002/aenm.71692.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO 3 RR) offers a solar-driven route to NH 3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value-added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO 3 RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO 3 RR research has produced an extensive library of high-performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO 3 RR, spanning light-absorber engineering, photoelectrode-cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO 3 RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge-transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH 3 synthesis.
authors: Seongi Lee, Wonjin Jeong, Wan Jae Dong

10.1002/aenm.71688.title: Gravity-Differential Modulated Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Continuous and Stable Energy Harvesting From Disordered Vibrations
10.1002/aenm.71688.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self-powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity-differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM-TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity-driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM-TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher-frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double-sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM-TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long-term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM-TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self-powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yuhe Wu, Menghe Gao, Yinxi Da, Miaoze Min, Yijia Dong, Qiang Tang, Cheng Xu

10.1002/aenm.71690.title: Molecular Architecture of Non-Fullerene Acceptors Balances Homo- and Hetero-Intermolecular Interactions to Enhance Thermal Stability of Organic Photovoltaics
10.1002/aenm.71690.abstract: ABSTRACT High-efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor-acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo- and hetero-intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well-known indacenodithieno[3,2- b ]thiophene-based (ITIC-series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene-based (IEICO-series) acceptors, and state-of-the-art Y-series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo-interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine-tune their hetero-interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo-interactions while minimizing hetero-interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature-reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo- and hetero-interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.
authors: Jianhua Han, Han Xu, Anirudh Sharma, Sri Harish Kumar Paleti, Nicolas Ramos, Jaime Martin, Derya Baran

10.1002/aenm.71652.title: Local Atomic Disorder-Driven Deep Relaxor State for Ultrahigh Dielectric Energy Storage With High Thermal Stability
10.1002/aenm.71652.abstract: ABSTRACT Lead-free dielectric ceramic capacitors are indispensable for advanced high-power electronic pulse systems owing to their exceptional power density and rapid charge-discharge kinetics. However, the simultaneous realization of ultrahigh recoverable energy density ( W rec ) and high efficiency ( η ), especially with robust thermal stability, remains challenging. Here, we propose a local structural design strategy focused on implementing atomic-scale disorder within relaxor ferroelectrics to achieve a deep relaxor state across a wide temperature window. Atomic-scale structure characterizations reveal that this local chemical/structural disorder induces ultrafine, highly active polar nanoregions, fostering an optimized polarization response while remaining resilient against thermal fluctuations. Consequently, the designed ceramics exhibit superior energy-storage performance, characterized by a large W rec of 13.1 J cm −3 and ultrahigh η of 93%, leading to a high figure of merit up to 187.1. Notably, exceptional performance stability across diverse operating conditions is bestowed, with η remaining above 90% at temperatures up to 200°C. This study thus provides a robust paradigm for designing dielectric capacitors that deliver both high energy-storage performance and reliability in harsh working environments.
authors: Bing Xie, Yuhang Hu, Wenqiang Xiang, Zhiyong Liu, Kun Guo, Haibo Zhang, Huajie Luo, Tianyu Li

10.1002/aenm.71686.title: Ni-MOFs Mediated Ni2+/4+ Balancing and Enhanced Metal-Oxygen Covalency Unlocks Fast and Stable Sodium Storage in High-Entropy Layered Cathode
10.1002/aenm.71686.abstract: ABSTRACT O3-type cathodes suffer from heterogeneous metal distribution and insufficient active nickel content, limiting specific capacity, cyclic stability, and electrochemical kinetics. Herein, Ni-based metal-organic frameworks (Ni-MOFs) are applied as precursors to enable atomic-level control over regulated active nickel content and metal-oxygen bonds in high-entropy NaTMO 2 cathodes. It is found that the introduction of Ni-MOFs can accelerate the crystallization and purity of O3-type structures. Ni-MOFs-derived high-entropy cathode (M-HEO) exhibits an optimized electrochemically active Ni 2+ , which can balance the capacity depth and structural stability, contrasting with excessive Ni 2+ in normal high-entropy oxide or insufficient Ni 2+ in commercial oxide. Concurrently, enhanced transition metal-oxygen covalency, especially Ni-O covalency, could form a robust metal-oxygen network with an ultrafast Na + transport path and suppress lattice degradation. The reinforced covalent Ni-O-TM network enables a highly reversible phase transition with a small volume change, as well as the modified, thinner double-layer cathode-electrolyte interface, together with fast Na + ion transport kinetics. As a result, M-HEO delivers a higher discharge capacity of ∼130 mAh g −1 with an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.6% under 0.1C and stable cyclic property under 1C and 2C.
authors: Shengkui Zhong, Bo Yang, Jishu Zeng, Xingyu Luo, Jiequn Liu, Zejun Jiang, Yanfang Wang, Fangping Wang, Xueling Hu, Huijue Luo, Yan Su, Zongkang Sun, Zhuokui Zhong, Shibao Tang, Renzong Hu, Wei Li, Fanbo Meng

10.1002/aenm.71691.title: Counter-Halide-Directed Ion-Pair Passivation Enables High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71691.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (PVSK) are key top-cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics but remain limited by severe open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) losses and photoinduced halide segregation. Since iodide- and bromide-related defects coexist at the surface and bulk of Br/I mixed-halide WBG PVSK, the counter-halide identity in ammonium passivators may critically influence defect passivation effectiveness. Moreover, while deprotonation of ammonium passivator has emerged as an important factor governing interfacial stability, its discussion has focused mainly on organic cation structure, leaving the counter-halide's role in regulating deprotonation-driven side reactions largely unexplored. Here, we establish a counter-halide-directed ion-pair passivation strategy using 4-fluorobenzylammonium halides (FBz-Cl, FBz-Br, and FBz-I). Density functional theory calculations combined with optoelectronic and interfacial characterizations reveal that the counter-halide simultaneously governs defect-binding affinity, nonradiative recombination, energy-level alignment, and deprotonation-driven degradation. Among the passivators, FBz-Br achieves the optimal balance of strong defect passivation, favorable band alignment with C 60 , and enhanced stability. Consequently, FBz-Br-treated PVSK exhibits suppressed nonradiative recombination and reduced V OC deficit, delivering a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.89% with improved resistance to moisture, thermal, and light-induced degradation. Integrated with Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) bottom cells, the optimized WBG PVSK enables PVSK/CIGS tandem solar cells with PCEs of 29.51% in four-terminal and 25.65% in two-terminal configurations.
authors: Huyen Tran, Dong Gyu Lee, Ahreum Lee, Inchan Hwang, Van Hung Tran, Jun Hyeok Choi, Junseop Byeon, Yu Jin Kim, Sang Hwan Nam, Jihye Gwak, Seung Kyu Ahn, Sungjun Hong, Kihwan Kim, Bong Joo Kang, Minwoo Park, SeJin Ahn, Tae Kyung Lee, Inyoung Jeong

10.1002/aenm.71694.title: Calendering-Dependent Electrochemical and Cost-Energy Tradeoffs in Layered - Olivine Blend Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71694.abstract: ABSTRACT Blended cathodes comprised of layered oxide and olivine materials, such as LiNi 0.9 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (NMC) and LiMn 0.7 Fe 0.3 PO 4 (LMFP), are appealing due to their reduced cost and enhanced safety, rate capability, and cyclability compared to high-Ni layered oxides. However, while these blends are often discussed in terms of particle-level properties, the effect of processing conditions, such as calendering, has received less attention, despite their strong influence on electrode microstructure due to the differences in morphology, surface characteristics, and crystallographic density. We investigate here systematically NMC, NMC/LMFP with 70/30 wt.%, and NMC/LMFP with 50/50 wt.% cathodes under uncalendered, moderately-calendered, and hard-calendered conditions, employing state-of-charge-dependent rate analysis, full-cell cycling, electrode-level transport characterization, and cathode-level cost-energy evaluation. NMC tolerates calendering, maintaining rate capability, while showing improved capacity retention over 500 cycles. In contrast, NMC/LMFP blends show a narrower, composition-dependent calendering limit. The 70/30 blend retains its rate-capability benefit under no-to-moderate calendering, whereas the 50/50 blend is strongly penalized by densification. Hard calendering induces transport-limited behavior in the blends, eliminating rate benefits and degrading cyclability. Stabilizing the NMC with Nb incorporation further improves cyclability and energy retention of the 70/30 blend, demonstrating a pathway to combine microstructure-enabled rate capability with improved durability and favorable cathode-level cost-energy balance.
authors: Huyen T. K. Nguyen, Arumugam Manthiram

10.1002/aenm.71677.title: Unlocking Three-Dimensional Electron and Ion Transport in High-Loading and Dense Lithium-Ion Battery Electrodes Assisted via Porous Graphene Networks
10.1002/aenm.71677.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient electron and ion transport in high-loading, densely packed electrodes remains a major challenge for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries. Increasing mass loading extends transport pathways for both charge carriers, while electrode densification by roll pressing, essential for maximizing gravimetric and volumetric energy density and minimizing electrolyte content, further restricts ion transport in low-porosity electrodes. Here, graphene mesosponge (GMS) is introduced as a functional conductive additive that tailors electrode microstructure through its sponge-like mesoporous framework. High-loading electrodes based on Co-free, pure-Ni layered oxides containing only 1 wt.% GMS exhibit enhanced electronic and ionic conductivity, delivering high reversible capacity with reduced polarization. The deformable mesoporous framework of GMS also buffers compressive stress during roll pressing, enabling practical electrode densities above 3.5 g cm −3 without inducing cracking of the active material particles. Digital-twin analysis reveals that the porous GMS architecture forms a three-dimensional electron- and ion-transport network, with electrolyte retained within its mesopores facilitating ion transport and resulting in superior rate capability compared with electrodes containing single-walled carbon nanotubes. These results demonstrate that GMS is a transformative conductive additive for simultaneously improving energy and power densities in practical lithium-ion batteries through rational microstructural design of dense composite electrodes.
authors: Yosuke Ugata, Rei Matsumoto, Sera Sato, Jaejin Lim, Yong Min Lee, Hiroshi Ueda, Atsuo Omaru, Kosuke Ishii, Naoaki Yabuuchi

10.1002/aenm.71685.title: Catalytic Activity Matching Governs Scaffold-Coating Competition in Silicon Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71685.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon scaffolds are widely used to accommodate lithiation-induced volume changes of silicon (Si) nanoparticles and maintain electrode integrity, yet whether increasing scaffold rigidity provides sufficient mechanical benefit to offset its cost in surface coating quality remains unexamined. The scaffold template and the native SiO x on Si surfaces compete for the same finite carbon source, so that scaffold wall thickness and coating uniformity are inversely coupled rather than independently tunable. We formalize this coupling as catalytic activity matching and probe it using MgSO 4 and CaSO 4 whisker templates, whose activity contrast is quantified by density functional theory and H 2 temperature-programmed reduction. The high-activity MgSO 4 template diverts carbon flux toward the scaffold, leaving nonuniform Si coatings, whereas the moderate-activity CaSO 4 template yields a compliant scaffold with uniform coatings. The uniform coating governs solid electrolyte interphase quality, while the compliant scaffold reduces peak lithiation stress to only 53.4% of its rigid counterpart. The matched CaSO 4 system delivers 91.0% initial Coulombic efficiency and enables full cells up to 510 Wh kg −1 (based on the combined mass of active materials). Matching rather than maximizing template catalytic activity is thus established as a general design principle for balancing scaffold formation and Si-surface protection in template-catalyzed CVD.
authors: Yin Yang, Henglong Ren, Maoxin Cai, Xinlong Ma, Yongfeng Li

10.1002/aenm.71683.title: Macromolecular Design of Bipolar Donor-Acceptor Polymer Cathodes for Fast and Durable Aluminum Dual-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71683.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum dual-ion batteries (ADIBs) are promising for sustainable electrochemical energy storage, yet organic cathodes rarely combine efficient bipolar redox utilization, rapid charge transport, long-term durability, and operation at high mass loadings. Here, four phenothiazine-anthraquinone donor-acceptor polymers are constructed by varying chain architecture, D-A connectivity, and backbone rigidity to elucidate how macromolecular structure regulates bipolar charge storage. The resulting structure-transport relationships reveal that open crosslinked networks improve ion accessibility, whereas direct D-A conjugation within rigid backbones promotes orbital delocalization and charge transfer. These complementary structural features activate both p-type phenothiazine and n-type anthraquinone redox centers, enabling reversible co-storage of AlCl 4 − and AlCl 2+ . Accordingly, the optimized PTZAQ-C3 delivers a reversible capacity of 243 mAh g −1 , excellent rate capability (122 mAh g −1 at 50.0 A g −1 ), and exceptional cycling stability up to 90,000 cycles. PTZAQ-C3 also maintains 200 mAh g −1 at −30°C and reaches an areal capacity of 10.08 mAh cm −2 at a mass loading of 50.4 mg cm −2 . These findings highlight macromolecular design as a general strategy for developing high-performance bipolar organic cathodes for aluminum dual-ion and related multicarrier batteries.
authors: Wenyan Ma, Chong Zhang, Ran Zhou, Xiaoxiao Zhang, Can Liu, Zikang Deng, Ziming Tu, Xunliang Hu, Jia-Xing Jiang

10.1002/aenm.71680.title: Upcycling Strategy for Mixed Spent Batteries to Enable NMC622 & Graphite Full Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71680.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of lithium-ion batteries is intensifying pressure on critical-material supply chains while generating increasing volumes of complex battery waste. However, existing recycling technologies struggle to process mixed feedstocks efficiently and often recover products with limited added value. Here, we advance beyond cathode-focused hydrometallurgical recycling by integrating composition-adjustable cathode resynthesis with the purification and surface modification of co-recovered graphite, followed by full-pouch-cell validation and unified process-level assessment. Mixed low-nickel cathodes are upgraded to high-performance LiNi 0.6 Mn 0.2 Co 0.2 O 2 (NMC622) with improved lithium-ion transport and cycling stability. Meanwhile, a closed-loop graphite upcycling process produces battery-grade anodes with enhanced interfacial kinetics and durability. Full pouch cells assembled entirely from the upcycled materials exhibit fewer side reactions and approximately twice the cycle life of cells using commercial counterparts, retaining 70% of their capacity after 2590 cycles. Techno-economic and life-cycle analyses further indicate >95% recycled-material utilization, 22.9% higher profitability, and reductions of 27.0% in greenhouse-gas emissions and 29.4% in energy consumption relative to the reference recycling route. These findings establish mixed battery waste as a viable feedstock for producing high-value battery materials and demonstrate a pathway from conventional resource recovery toward value-added remanufacturing for circular, resilient, and low-carbon battery supply chains.
authors: Zeyi Yao, Jiahui Hou, Zifei Meng, Xiaotu Ma, Jinzhao Fu, Zexin Wang, Zhenzhen Yang, Jianguo Wen, Maksim Sultanov, Hari Adhikari, Yihao Shen, Geoffrey A. Tompsett, Yan Wang

10.1002/aenm.71654.title: Integrated d-p Orbital Coupling Within High-Entropy Oxide/Halloysite Accelerates Sulfur Reduction Kinetics in Sodium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71654.abstract: ABSTRACT The sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttle effect remains a major obstacle to achieving the high theoretical capacity of room-temperature sodium-sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries. Herein, the high-entropy oxide/halloysite nanotube hybrid host (HEO/HNT) is developed by integrating multicomponent catalytic sites with a naturally abundant 1D clay scaffold for efficient sulfur conversion. The hollow tubular structure of HNT enables uniform HEO anchoring and effective confinement of sulfur species, while the robust Si─O and Al─OH framework enhances cathode stability during long-term cycling. Density functional theory calculations reveal that interfacial coupling between the metal 3d orbitals of HEO and the Al/Si 3p orbitals of HNT induces extended orbital delocalization, thereby strengthening NaPSs adsorption and lowering the free energy barriers for stepwise polysulfide conversion. In situ and ex situ characterizations further verify accelerated NaPSs reduction kinetics and suppressed shuttling. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the S@HEO/HNT cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 1225 mAh g −1 after 450 cycles at 1 C and maintains 478 mAh g −1 over 2500 cycles at 10 C, corresponding to an ultralow capacity fading of 0.008% per cycle. This study bridges high-entropy oxide with naturally abundant clay substrates, offering a scalable route toward durable, high-rate RT Na-S batteries.
authors: Guangming Cao, Heng Zhang, Youcun Bai, Yingying Song, Lang Qiu, Xiang-Long Huang, Tao Song, Wei Sun, Chang Ming Li

10.1002/aenm.71687.title: Chloride-Mediated Photoelectrochemical Selective Oxidation of Polyols Coupled With Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/aenm.71687.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting coupled with the oxidation of polyols into high-value-added chemicals is of practical significance for the upgrading of biomass and polyester plastics. However, the current polyols selective oxidation reactions suffer from harsh reaction conditions (strong basic electrolyte) and high costs of noble metal-based catalyst via the reactive oxygen species-mediated pathway. Herein, we for the first time demonstrate a chlorine radicals-mediated route toward polyols oxidation under neutral conditions. As proof-of-concept, NiCo-LDH-decorated TiO 2 has been developed to promote the oxidation of ethylene glycol (EG) to glycolic acid (GA), achieving a GA production rate of 8.7 µmol cm -2 h -1 with a selectivity of 76.2% in NaCl electrolyte under irradiation, which is the highest value reported to date in PEC system. Mechanistic studies reveal that the key chlorine radicals facilitate C─H bond cleavage to form chlorinated intermediates for GA production. Additionally, we successfully coupled PEC PET-derived EG valorization with H 2 generation from seawater, attaining GA and H 2 productivity of 30.6 and 93.9 µmol cm -2 , respectively. This work offers a novel perspective on polyols oxidation reaction pathway modulation and demonstrates a solar-to-chemical conversion approach for integrating low-value carbon sources recycling and PEC synthesis.
authors: Lan Luo, Shanshan Zhang, Xiaomei Zhang, Yutong Cai, Wangsong Chen, Wenjing Dai, Haisong Feng, Zhen Yin, Zhenhua Li, Mingfei Shao

10.1002/aenm.71682.title: In Situ Formation of a Hybrid Alloy-Fluoride Interphase for Stable High-Capacity Phosphorus Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71682.abstract: ABSTRACT Phosphorus-based anodes are promising candidates for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries owing to their high theoretical capacity. However, their practical application is severely limited by drastic volume variation and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry. Achieving both mechanical robustness and rapid ion transport within the SEI remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, trace SbF 3 is doped into the phosphorus-carbon (P/C) composites through a facile ball-milling. Taking advantage of the SbF 3 preferential reduction over phosphorus, a hybrid interphase enriched with Li 3 Sb and LiF is in situ formed during initial lithiation. The hybrid interphase effectively suppresses the dissolution and shuttling of polyphosphides, which also integrates fast ionic/electronic transport with enhanced mechanical rigidity, thereby accelerating reaction kinetics. The synergetic effect endows the P/C-SbF 3 anode with a high retained capacity of 970.10 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g −1 and a superior rate capability of 893.84 mAh g −1 at 15 A g −1 . When paired with an NCM811 cathode, the full cell retains 80.25% of its capacity after 400 cycles at 1 C. The single-layer pouch full cell further confirms the practical feasibility. This work highlights in situ formed hybrid interphase engineering for overcoming the stability-transport trade-off in high-capacity alloying anodes.
authors: Gengchang Lai, Qiuyan Li, Xiaoxiao Feng, Huijuan Ma, Chao Peng, Paul K. Chu, Xue-Feng Yu, Jiahong Wang

10.1002/aenm.71684.title: Janus Ag Nanoskin-Armored Polyimide Bilayer Separator Enables Efficient Li-Nucleation Regulation for Dendrite-Free Lithium Metal Battery
10.1002/aenm.71684.abstract: ABSTRACT Uncontrolled lithium (Li) dendrite growth has been regarded as the most critical obstacle for the widespread adoption of Li metal batteries (LMBs), stemming from the preferential nucleation of Li ions (Li + ) at low-energy-barrier sites that trigger heterogeneous deposition. Therefore, it is pivotal yet significantly challenging to effectively control Li nucleation and deposition in LMBs. Here, we engineer a Janus Ag nanoskin-armored polyimide (Ag@PI/PI) bilayer separator by in situ growth Ag nanoparticles on the surface of PI nanofiber and integrating a high-strength PI nanofiber membrane as the dorsal substrate. Specifically, the Ag nanoskin acts as a three-dimensional lithiophilic host to seize Li and induce sequential Li nucleation, thereby preventing Li dendrite formation. As a result, the Ag@PI/PI-Li||Cu cell exhibits a low overpotential of 31.0 mV, high Coulombic efficiency of 98.9%, and prolonged Sand's time of 26.3 h. Significantly, the Ag@PI/PI separator delivers a high Li + transference number (0.70) and exceptional cycling stability (1600 h) in a Li||Li cell. Moreover, the Ag@PI/PI-based Li||NCM523 cell achieves a remarkable specific capacity of 108.32 mAh g −1 at 5 C while retaining a satisfying capacity retention of 88.7% at 1 C. These results underscore the viability of this universal and efficient Ag nanoskin-armored strategy for high-security LMBs applications.
authors: Pengpeng Li, Xinluo Li, Qingsong Zhang, Yisong Zhou, Junyi Han, Nianyu Yue, Jiameng Li, Jiaji Yue, Guohua Sun, Nanjun Chen

10.1002/aenm.71678.title: Medium-Concentration Electrolytes Balance Hydrogen-Bond Disruption and Ion-Ion Interactions for Wide-Temperature Aqueous Trivalent Indium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71678.abstract: ABSTRACT It is desirable to develop aqueous batteries that can operate efficiently across wide temperature ranges; however, it remains a grand challenge to simultaneously suppress electrolyte freezing at low temperatures and water-induced side reactions at elevated temperatures. Herein, we demonstrate that a medium-concentration chloride electrolyte can effectively regulate the electrolyte solvation structures, leading to high-efficiency and wide-temperature aqueous trivalent indium metal batteries. Specifically, the increment of salt concentration progressively disrupts the hydrogen-bonding network of water and reconstructs the In 3+ solvation structure toward chloride-rich complexes, achieving a balanced effect at the medium concentration (10 m) of the studied range (5, 10, and 15 m). The optimized 1 m InCl 3 + 10 m LiCl electrolyte shows the best anti-freezing property at −70°C with sufficient ionic conductivity of 1.42 mS cm −1 , and it further mitigates the In 3+ hydrolysis tendency and water-related side reactions at elevated temperatures (+65°C). Consequently, in metal anode exhibits a highly reversible plating behavior with high Coulombic efficiencies of 99%-99.95% over a wide temperature range from −70 to +65°C. Rather than simply maximizing the electrolyte concentration, our work demonstrates that balancing hydrogen-bond disruption and chloride-rich ion coordination is the key to achieving wide-temperature stability in aqueous trivalent electrolytes.

10.1002/aenm.71464.title: Field-Regulated Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Enhanced Energy Conversion
10.1002/aenm.71464.abstract: ABSTRACT Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) provide a versatile platform for distributed mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing. However, their practical deployment remains constrained by insufficient surface charge density, high output impedance, impedance mismatch, and environmental instability, particularly under low-frequency and low-intensity mechanical excitation. To move beyond purely mechanically driven contact electrification, optical, thermal, magnetic, and electric fields have recently been introduced into TENG systems to regulate interfacial charge generation, separation, transport, and retention. Unlike reviews centered on the simple structural integration or output superposition of otherwise independent energy-harvesting units, this review focuses on mechanistic external-field coupling and adopts field-assisted charge modulation as a unifying framework for analyzing multifield-coupled TENGs. Starting from Maxwell's displacement current, the fundamental working mechanism of conventional TENGs and the key parameters governing their output performance are discussed. Coupling mechanisms involving localized surface plasmon resonance, photon-generated carriers, pyroelectric effects and heat-excitation effects, magnetic nanomaterials, magnetically assisted structures, charge injection, and charge pumping are then highlighted. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities in unified theoretical modeling, field-responsive materials, system-level integration, power management, and long-term reliability are discussed. By linking external-field coupling mechanisms with materials design and device architecture, this review provides guidance for developing high-output, adaptive, and multifunctional self-powered systems.
authors: Wenyi Tu, Endian Cui, Danni Yang, Qian Yang, Pengfan Wu, Xiaojing Mu, Fayang Wang

10.1002/aenm.71473.title: Cellulose Materials Integrate Ion Transport, Interfacial Chemistry, and Structural Stability in Zinc Battery Systems
10.1002/aenm.71473.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable zinc batteries offer a promising route toward safe, low-cost, and sustainable energy storage, but their practical application is hindered by nonuniform ion transport, parasitic interfacial reactions, and progressive structural degradation. Cellulose is attractive because its oxygen-containing functional groups, hierarchical fibrous structure, and processable networks can be tailored for zinc anodes, electrolytes, separators, cathodes, and flexible devices. This Review discusses recent advances in cellulose-based materials for mild aqueous zinc-ion batteries and alkaline zinc-air batteries, focusing on how chemical modification, nanoscale organization, pore structure, and wet-state mechanics affect ion conduction, electrode/electrolyte contact, and structural retention. Particular attention is given to the evidence supporting proposed mechanisms and to the distinct reaction environments of the two systems, including Zn 2+ transport and plating/stripping in mild electrolytes, and OH − transport, zincate redistribution, ZnO evolution, and air-electrode processes in alkaline cells. The Review also examines performance trade-offs, component contributions in multicomponent systems, and the limits of comparisons across different testing conditions. By linking cellulose chemistry and architecture with chemistry-specific battery requirements, it provides practical guidance for material selection, mechanism verification, and device-oriented design, while identifying chemical durability, dimensional stability, feedstock consistency, standardized evaluation, and scalable manufacturing as priorities for future development.
authors: Tengshuai Li, Yi Chen, Yonghui Xie, Yang Lu, Kehui Cen, Keliang Wang, Manhui Wei, Bin Liang, Dengyu Chen, Hengwei Wang

10.1002/aenm.71484.title: Empowering Triboelectric Nanogenerators With Origami and Kirigami Mechanics: From Metamaterials to Self-Powered Systems
10.1002/aenm.71484.abstract: ABSTRACT Origami- and Kirigami-inspired structures have emerged as transformative strategies for enhancing the performance and versatility of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Their folding mechanisms facilitate efficient for contact-separation TENGs, as well as their geometric patterns provide essential stretchability for complex interfaces. This review emphasizes that the core mechanism of these architectures lies in their ability to bridge mechanical deformation and electrical output of TENGs. On this basis, we summarize the representative origami and kirigami configurations and their mechanical characteristics. More importantly, we propose a general design framework to clarify how these structural strategies adapt to different operating conditions by leveraging their inherent mechanical characteristics. Typical applications include blue energy harvesting, vibration and biomechanical energy harvesting for micro/nano energy systems, self-powered sensing for environmental and health monitoring, tactile sensing, and wearable electronics that benefit from the stretchability and deformability of kirigami structures. Finally, the current challenges and outline emerging opportunities toward deeper functional integration and scalable implementation of origami- and kirigami-inspired TENGs are concluded.
authors: Hanlin Sun, Xiaocheng Sun, Zhihao Zhao, Jie Wang

10.1002/aenm.71489.title: Mechanistic Insights Into Entropy Regulation in Sodium/Potassium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71489.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) and potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) have emerged as significant contenders for large-scale energy storage technology due to their substantial resource reserves and cost effectiveness. However, their large-scale development is hindered by several key challenges, including the structural degradation of electrode materials during cycling, slow kinetics, and instability at the electrode-electrolyte interface. Entropy-regulation strategies, particularly medium-to-high-entropy designs, represent an emerging paradigm in materials design. The integration of multiple components, with the aim of leveraging their synergistic effects, presents a novel approach to address the aforementioned challenges in a systematic manner. It has been demonstrated that, owing to its elevated configurational entropy, this strategy accomplishes two objectives: first, it provides thermodynamic stabilization of the crystal structure, and second, it suppresses undesirable phase transitions. Additionally, it induces kinetic effects that result in slow diffusion, thereby effectively delaying element migration and side reactions. Concurrently, entropy regulation fosters the establishment of a stable interfacial film at the electrode-electrolyte interface, thereby enhancing interfacial ionic transport efficiency and chemical stability. This paper systematically reviews the mechanistic insights and research progress of entropy-regulation strategies in cathode materials, anode materials, and interface engineering for SIBs and PIBs, and outlines future directions for this field.
authors: Rufeng Ye, Junlong Zheng, Yanhong Feng, Qinjian Ou, Yanyan Meng, Xinze Zhang, Zhengyang Qin, Yang Luo, Longchao Zhuo, Xijun Liu

10.1002/aenm.71510.title: Toward Scalable Water Electrolysis Catalysts: Mechanistic Insights, Structure-Activity Relationships and Multiscale Design
10.1002/aenm.71510.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly active catalysts have substantially advanced water electrolysis for green hydrogen production and decarbonized energy systems. However, large-scale deployment remains hindered by the challenge of simultaneously achieving high catalytic activity, long-term durability, and scalable manufacturability. Despite remarkable progress in developing non-noble electrocatalysts, most materials remain confined to lab-scale demonstrations owing to complex synthesis routes and non-industrial evaluation conditions, inducing a significant gap between catalyst discovery and practical implementation. This review summarizes recent progress in bridging laboratory innovation and scalable manufacturing for water electrolysis electrocatalysts. Fundamental reaction mechanisms, scalable synthesis strategies, structure-activity relationships, and multiscale design principles are systematically discussed, spanning atomic-level regulation of intrinsic activity and active site density to macroscopic architectures engineering for optimized mass transport and operational stability. Finally, the prevailing challenges and future trajectories for sustainable catalyst manufacturing and industrial deployment are presented.
