By introducing 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl trifluoromethanesulfonate to undergo synergistic decomposition with fluoroethylene carbonate, this formulation enables the in situ construction of the dual-layer gradient interphase. This unique SEI efficiently facilitates desolvation and accelerates Na + transport, while achieving even Na plating after cycling. Consequently, the designed electrolyte delivers outstanding electrochemical performance, enabling Na || sodium vanadium phosphate full cells to exhibit long cycle-life of 5500 cycles at 20 C and 97.5% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 25 C. This work highlights the critical role of gradient SEI engineering and offers an insightful design principle for developing next-generation QSSMBs.
authors: Yi Li, Shangming He, Weiliang Li, Shilin Zhang, Kai Wan, Mingbao Huang, Weiyuan Huang, Zhiyong Fu, Zhenxing Liang, Xiaoru Chen

10.1002/aenm.71519.title: Proton Flux Engineering for Selective CO2 Electroreduction
10.1002/aenm.71519.abstract: ABSTRACT The carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) is central to carbon valorization and renewable electricity storage, yet its selectivity, efficiency, and durability depend on coordinating proton availability with electron transfer at dynamic electrochemical interfaces. Despite advances in catalysts, electrolytes, hydrogen evolution suppression, and devices, proton effects are described by isolated descriptors, such as pH, water activity, buffer capacity, cation identity, hydrophobicity, ionomer chemistry, and local alkalinity. This fragmentation obscures how protons regulate initiation, *COOH formation, *CO/formate branching, *CO coverage, C─C coupling, hydrogen evolution, and high-flux decay. A proton-centered perspective is needed to link atomic proton-transfer events with interfacial microenvironments and device operation. This review establishes proton regulation as a mechanistic framework for CO 2 RR by examining proton sources, transport pathways, interfacial accessibility, hydrogen-bond-network reorganization, local electric fields, and proton-coupled electron-transfer timing. By integrating molecular mechanisms, microenvironment modulation, in situ characterization, and gas-diffusion or membrane-electrode architectures, we organize dispersed observations into a source-transport-utilization framework. This framework shows how proton location, dose, and temporal availability define kinetic boundaries between hydrogen evolution, one-carbon (C 1 ) products, and multicarbon (C 2+ ) pathways, while governing stability under practical fluxes. Proton regulation guides selective, scalable, and durable CO 2 electroconversion.
authors: Rongjing Miao, Guoqing Zhang, Jialu Liu, Zihang Li, Xiayan Zhang, Shengwei Kong, Mingyu Sun, Jia Wang, Ming Ma, Zixu Sun, Xinjian Shi

10.1002/aenm.71541.title: Enhanced Figure-of-Merit Energy Harvesting in [001]-Oriented PMN-PZT Ceramics Via Synergistic Multi-Scale Engineering
10.1002/aenm.71541.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing piezoelectric materials with a high figure-of-merit (FOM = d 33 × g 33 /tan δ ) is crucial for advanced energy-harvesting technologies. Here, a high FOM is achieved in [001]-oriented Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 -PbZrO 3 -PbTiO 3 (PMN-PZT) textured ceramics by synergistically integrating grain orientation, defect engineering, and morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) design. The textured ceramic exhibits exceptional properties (piezoelectric charge coefficient d 33 = 1120 pC·N −1 , piezoelectric voltage coefficient g 33 = 62 × 10 −3 V·m·N −1 , and an ultralow dielectric loss tan δ = 0.23%). Atomic-scale analysis reveals that the [001] intrinsic anisotropy and mixed rhombohedral-tetragonal domains facilitate polarization rotation to boost d 33 and g 33 , while Mn doping-induced defect dipoles suppress dielectric loss. Consequently, an ultrahigh FOM of 30,180 × 10 −12 m 2 ·N −1 is realized. Furthermore, a cantilever energy harvester utilizing this textured ceramic delivers an outstanding power density of 0.72 µW·mm −3 , which is 78 times higher than that of commercial soft PZT. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high-FOM piezoelectric materials for high performance energy harvesting applications.
authors: Mingyang Tang, Xin Liu, Wei Bai, Zihan Tan, Yike Wang, Yuxin Wang, Yewen Zhang, Zhuo Xu, Linlang Bai, Liwei Geng, Yongke Yan

10.1002/aenm.71521.title: Redox-Buffering PEAI-CeOx Passivation Suppresses Thermo-Mechanical Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells Under Rapid Thermal Cycling (Adv. Energy Mater. 38/2026)
authors: George Kwesi Asare, Minwoo Lee, Joshua Sraku Adu, Ram Datt, Wing Chung Tsoi, Trystan Watson, Xiaojing Hao, Juhong Oh, Chang Eun Song, Behrang H. Hamadani, Jae Sung Yun, Helen Hejin Park

10.1002/aenm.71520.title: Dual-Diol Synergized Electrolyte for Wide-Temperature Hydrogel Zn-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71520.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) feature low cost, superior safety, and eco-friendliness, promising extensive prospects for next-generation electrochemical energy storage. Nevertheless, inferior interfacial stability, uncontrollable Zn dendrite formation, and poor temperature tolerance severely hinder their practical exploitation in flexible electronic devices. Herein, glycerol (Gly) and ethylene glycol (EG) are incorporated into a polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogel matrix via a facile one-pot route to fabricate a wide-temperature-tolerant PAM-based composite hydrogel electrolyte (PAM/Gly/EG). Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two diols, the hydroxyl-rich structure reconstructs the intrinsic hydrogen bond network of confined water, while coordination interactions modulate the solvation configuration of Zn 2+ , thereby fundamentally restraining Zn dendrite propagation and parasitic hydrogen evolution. The resultant Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers a long stable lifespan over 3000 h at 1 mA·cm −2 , and sustains steady cycling for 500 h at −20°C and 300 h at 50°C. This synergistic diol modification strategy affords a feasible avenue for structural optimization and practical deployment of wide-temperature flexible AZIBs.
authors: Qianwen Xue, Dinghao Xu, Rui Hu, Tongshan Zhao, Tao Zhong, Zixuan Zhou, Yuange Wang, Qianyu Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71540.title: Strain Engineering in High-Entropy Electrocatalysts: Mechanisms, Strategies and Water Splitting Applications
10.1002/aenm.71540.abstract: ABSTRACT Strain engineering has emerged as an effective strategy for tailoring the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of materials at the atomic scale. For electrochemical water splitting, the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction are largely limited by scaling relationships and nonoptimized adsorption energetics of key intermediates. High-entropy materials, featuring multiprincipal-element compositions and pronounced lattice distortion, offer a unique platform for strain-mediated catalytic regulation. Their intrinsic microstrain fields, derived from atomic size mismatch together with sluggish diffusion and cocktail effects, enable tunable electronic structures and abundant metastable active sites. This review summarizes recent advances in strain engineering of high-entropy materials for water splitting. Fundamental concepts of strain and its influence on d-band centers, adsorption energetics, and reaction kinetics are first introduced. This is followed by a discussion of strain modulation strategies, including doping, solid solution alloying, and defect engineering. Special emphasis is placed on the distinct behavior of high-entropy materials compared with conventional alloys, particularly their nonlinear electronic hybridization and multisite synergy. Finally, key challenges involving strain quantification, operando evolution, and strain-entropy coupling are highlighted, providing guidance for the rational design of next-generation water-splitting catalysts.

10.1002/aenm.71531.title: Experimentally Determined Spatiotemporal Charge Carrier Dynamics for the Development of Particulate Photocatalysts
10.1002/aenm.71531.abstract: ABSTRACT Particulate photocatalysts have generated interest for the low-cost implementation of various photocatalytic processes, including the production of solar fuels as clean energy sources. With light absorption, charge generation, charge transport, and interfacial charge transfer all constrained in individual particles, complex photophysical and photochemical processes occur on a wide range of timescales within spatially defined volumes. The allure of deciphering the charge carrier dynamics to build a fundamental picture of photocatalysis in different materials has motivated the development of state-of-the-art spatiotemporal measurement techniques. Monitoring charge carrier dynamics on relevant time and length scales is a challenging experimental task. Many experimental barriers have been overcome in recent years, providing some guidance for future directions for material development. This review delves into the underlying origins of spatial heterogeneity in charge carrier dynamics, introduces charge carrier transport phenomena, and details the recent examples of spatiotemporal investigation of charge carrier dynamics in particulate photocatalysts. These new experimental capabilities pave the way for a more comprehensive description of photocatalytic processes, guiding the optimization of photocatalytic materials.

10.1002/aenm.71552.title: Holistic Top-to-Bottom Film Restructuring to Achieve Highly Stable Unencapsulated Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71552.abstract: ABSTRACT While perovskites have emerged as frontrunners in optoelectronics due to their exceptional properties, their performance remains bottlenecked by film imperfections such as interfacial defects, non-uniform crystallization, and band alignment mismatches. Conventional treatments often fail to simultaneously address issues at the top surface, the bulk, and the buried interface. In this work, we introduce a holistic top-to-bottom restructuring strategy using a facile vapor-phase post-treatment. This approach induces a gradient-distributed 2D perovskite phase that extends from the surface into the bulk while uniquely healing structural voids and chemical inhomogeneities at the buried interface. This synergistic restructuring optimizes the energy band structure for accelerated carrier extraction and passivates defects throughout the entire film depth. As a result, our unencapsulated n-i-p solar cells demonstrate exceptional environmental resilience, maintaining over 90% of their initial efficiency after 2,800 h of high-humidity exposure. This study establishes a new benchmark for stability and provides a robust pathway for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Zhengyan Jiang, Jiayun Sun, Zhixian Zhang, Peide Zhu, Wenjun Liu, Biao Zhou, Hong Zhang, Baomin Xu, Wallace C. H. Choy

10.1002/aenm.71535.title: Elucidating the Suppression of High-Voltage Degradation in O3-type NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2: A Voltage-Switching Strategy for Na-ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71535.abstract: ABSTRACT Elevating depth-of-charge (DoC) enhances the energy density of layered oxide cathodes for sodium-ion batteries; however, such high-DoC cycling inevitably triggers severe structural and interfacial degradation. In practice, battery management systems commonly adapt voltage-derating strategies dynamically according to battery state of health, achieving a favorable trade-off between energy density and cycle life. Nevertheless, a critical yet overlooked question remains: how high-DoC-induced damaged regions evolve when reverted to moderate-DoC cycling. Here, using NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM111) as a prototype, a voltage-switching strategy is employed to elucidate the dynamic and long-term behavior of these damaged regions. During high-DoC cycling (charging to 4.3 V), the rapid capacity fading is driven by pronounced formation of bulk defects and interfacial disordered spinel phases. However, upon switching these cells to moderate-DoC cycling (charging to 4.0 V), these pre-existing damaged regions become stabilized: their rapid propagation is suppressed, and they no longer accelerate degradation in surrounding intact regions. This enables degraded NFM111 to deliver capacity retention comparable to that of cells cycled solely under moderate-DoC conditions. This work presents a dynamic and evolving picture of high-DoC degradation and subsequent moderate-DoC stabilization in NFM111 cathodes, providing mechanistic insights into voltage-derating process and the lifetime prolongation of compromised cells.
authors: Xiangjie Li, Xilong Chen, Jie Cui, Ziyong Li, Fanbo Meng, Gui Chen, Youyuan Zeng, Xiaoyun Gao, Min Zhu, Renzong Hu

10.1002/aenm.71515.title: Volatilization-Kinetics-Dictated Crystallization Enabling Efficient Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells for Near-Space Environment
10.1002/aenm.71515.abstract: ABSTRACT The remarkable progress in metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has propelled perovskite/silicon tandem architectures as a transformative solution in photovoltaics, enabling efficiencies beyond single-junction limits while offering high specific power and radiation resistance for challenging environments, including near-space and aerospace applications. Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites on textured silicon, however, encounter hurdles in controlled crystallization and halide phase stability, leading to recombination losses and reduced performance. This work investigates additive engineering using volatile alkylammonium chlorides with tailored alkyl chain lengths to fine-tune volatilization kinetics. By strategically slowing down the volatilization rate, the additive promotes homogeneous nucleation and retards grain growth, which is critical for achieving uniform perovskite coverage over the intricate topography of textured silicon substrates.​ An optimized additive promotes dense, oriented films with suppressed segregation, culminating in tandem solar cells boasting a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 31.1% and stability exceeding 1000 h. First-ever flight test measurements and calibrations of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells were conducted under near-space conditions at altitudes reaching 37.29 km. These advancements may contribute to the development of robust tandem devices for various application settings.
authors: Minchao Liu, Bin Jiao, Hua Kong, Fei Wang, Yixin Li, Shasha Li, Yang Yuan, Yufei Gong, Yiyang Wang, Wenzhu Liu, Yanchu Yang, Guoning Xu

10.1002/aenm.71514.title: Clean Tin Oxide via Volatile Additive Engineering for High-performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/aenm.71514.abstract: ABSTRACT SnO 2 is a benchmark electron transport material for perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, SnO 2 films from the conventional chemical bath deposition (CBD) are limited by impurities and defects that accelerate non-radiative recombination and compromise device stability. Here, we present a volatile additive engineering strategy using pyruvic acid (PA) as a dual-functional nucleation promoter and surface modulator during SnO 2 deposition. Owing to its volatility (sublimation at 145°C), PA can be effectively removed during annealing, resulting in cleaner SnO 2 surfaces with reduced residual groups. This is accompanied by a decrease in oxygen-related defect densities in the SnO 2 layer. This improvement leads to enhanced charge recombination and improved thermal stability at the buried interface. Consequently, PA-engineered PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.17%, together with improved device stability, retaining >80% of their initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation, 1000 h at 65°C, and 30 days under 30% relative humidity. Furthermore, this approach is compatible with large-area fabrication, yielding efficiencies of 24.83% for 1 cm 2 lab-scale cells and 20.21% for 30 cm × 30 cm industrial-scale solar modules. These results suggest that controlling additive volatility improves CBD-SnO 2 quality and offers a promising route for stable, scalable perovskite solar cells.
authors: Xin Wang, Ziang Pan, Jingyao Feng, Lifei Chen, Yuchen Song, Wenkai Liao, Peng Huang, Yifan Li, Jianguang Xu, Feng Wang, Xiaoming Zhao

10.1002/aenm.71533.title: Enabling Low-Temperature Fast-Charging Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries: A Synergistic Design of Electrolyte Solvation and Current Collector Interface
10.1002/aenm.71533.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) promise ultrahigh energy density (>350 Wh kg −1 ) and low cost, yet their operation under low-temperature and fast-charging conditions is critically hindered by limited sodium inventory and sluggish interfacial kinetics. This conflict creates a “stability paradox”: the pursuit of high energy density amplifies interfacial instability, leading to inhomogeneous sodium deposition and rapid capacity decay. This review systematically analyzes AFSMB failure mechanisms under extreme conditions and demonstrates that overcoming these bottlenecks requires integrated co-design across four synergistic domains: (1) engineering electrolyte solvation structures (weakly solvating, high-concentration, and high-entropy designs) to lower the desolvation barrier and stabilize the solid-electrolyte interphase; (2) tailoring current collector interfaces with sodiophilic coatings or three-dimensional architectures to guide uniform sodium deposition; (3) incorporating rational pre-sodiation strategies to compensate irreversible sodium loss; and (4) leveraging artificial intelligence and molecular simulations for data-driven electrolyte screening. We critically assess the trade-offs of each strategy and provide a forward-looking perspective on reversible sodium compensation, multi-scale AI platforms, and full-cell integration. This review offers a roadmap for developing practical, wide-temperature-range, high-energy-density AFSMBs, with recent pouch cells already demonstrating >200 Wh kg −1 and stable cycling from −40°C to 60°C.
authors: Dongni Zhao, Yong Pang, Xiaoling Cui, Li Wang, Shiyou Li, Xiangming He

10.1002/aenm.71530.title: Redox-Mediated Electrified Method for Green and Low-Cost Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Materials Recycling
10.1002/aenm.71530.abstract: ABSTRACT After 30 years of commercialization and mass production, lithium-ion batteries have generated massive waste streams, especially with their expanding use in electric vehicles. Recycling spent batteries and valorizing useful components are therefore increasingly urgent for sustainable development. However, conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical methods are limited by high energy consumption or large chemical input, creating demand for greener and more efficient recycling technologies. Here, using LiCoO 2 as an example, we report a closed-loop electrified chemical process based on redox-targeting reactions to recover valuable species from spent battery materials using only electricity and water. Complementary reductive leaching of LiCoO 2 and oxidative leaching of LiFePO 4 were performed with anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonate as a regenerative redox mediator to sequentially break down LiCoO 2 and achieve efficient separation of Co 2+ and Li + in the form of Co(OH) 2 and LiOH. This cost-effective and environmentally friendly method was also extended to the recycling of LiNi x Mn y Co z O 2 with a high recovery rate of Li + and transition metal species. It is anticipated that the electrified chemical recycling method demonstrated here would provide a credible solution to the valorization of battery waste and contribute to the sustainable development of lithium-ion batteries.
authors: Songpeng Huang, Yongfeng Zhi, Zhiyu Wang, Mengqi Gao, Saikiran Reddy, Shiqiang Huang, Manohar Salla, Hang Zhang, Feifei Zhang, Xun Wang, Qing Wang

10.1002/aenm.71534.title: Chelation Compensation Strategy for High-Performance Iron-Based Redox Flow Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71534.abstract: ABSTRACT Iron-based redox flow batteries (IRFBs) are compelling candidates for cost-effective grid-scale energy storage, benefiting from high safety, low cost, and the natural abundance of iron-based active species. However, heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and kinetic deactivation lead to capacity decay and energy efficiency reduction, which limits the long-term cycle stability of IRFBs. Chelation compensation is employed to regulate metal-ion redox species through multidentate ligand design. Their coordination environment, solvation structure, and interfacial reactivity are thereby optimized, leading to improved energy efficiency and cycling stability. This review summarizes the major degradation mechanisms of IRFBs and highlights recent progress in chelation-modified systems constructed with representative chelating functional groups. Particular attention is given to the influence of chelation on heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and reaction kinetics. Finally, current challenges and future directions in ligand design, electrolyte compatibility, mechanistic understanding, and practical implementation are discussed, offering guidance for the development of high-performance chelation-modified IRFBs for large-scale energy storage.
authors: Fan Yang, Shangkun Wang, Yanqin Zhao, Yingqiao Jiang, Ningning Zhao, Bin Li, Xiaojian Feng, Jing Zhu, Lei Dai, Ling Wang, Zhangxing He

10.1002/aenm.71537.title: Integrating Machine Learning and High-Throughput Calculations for the Rational Design of Photocatalytic 2D-COFs on Overall Water Splitting
10.1002/aenm.71537.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D-COFs) with tunable structures offer a promising platform for photocatalytic overall water splitting (OWS) under visible-light. However, it is challenging to quickly find photocatalytic OWS materials from the massive amounts of 2D-COFs and then achieve precise synthesis. In this work, we constructed 11 934 hcb-type 2D-COFs by assembling 28 building blocks and 9 linkages. The machine learning (ML) and high-throughput computation (HTC) were integrated to predict feasible photocatalytic OWS hcb-type 2D-COFs. Through training 10 initial algorithms and optimizing the hyperparameters of top 4 algorithms in terms of performance, the ETR model for predicting the band-edge levels with R 2 of 0.97 and 0.99 was developed, and the KNR and RFR models were built for predicting Δ G *H and Δ G *OH with R 2 of 0.99 and 0.83, respectively. 2581 2D-COFs (21.63% of dataset) are screened to be potential structures for visible-light-driven water splitting. After applying the optimal ML models on all assembled 2D-COFs, a list of high-frequency building blocks and linkages is suggested as a set of suitable candidates for the first time. Then TBTZ_FBN0_Imine (TBTZ-FBN0-COF) was assembled and experimentally synthesized. Its OWS activity verified our ML-HTC paradigm, which provides the researchers recommendation to construct photocatalytic OWS 2D-COFs.
authors: Rui Zhang, Zhao-Di Yang, Xiaoyu Chu, Guiling Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71551.title: Interface Engineering via Ceria Coating Reconciles Ion Transport and Lithium Compatibility in Composite Polymer Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71551.abstract: ABSTRACT Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) exhibit considerable potential for solid−state lithium−metal batteries (SLBs). However, incompatibilities between the various components in the electrolyte continue to hinder the full realization of its performance and practical applications. In this work, a multifunctional ceria interfacial layer is proposed to achieve uniform dispersion of ceramic fillers and facilitated interfacial transport of lithium ions in CPEs. At the same time, the physical barrier provided by this multifunctional interface layer prevents direct contact between the ceramic filler and the lithium metal, thereby avoiding potentially harmful side reactions that could further lead to a performance deterioration in battery cycling. Owing to the introduction of this multifunctional interface layer, the CPE exhibits high ionic conductivity (0.772 mS cm −1 ) and Li-ion transference number (0.626), with a wide electrochemical window (5.03 V). Furthermore, the Li|CPE|Li symmetric cell exhibits a lithium deposition/stripping capacity exceeding 1500 h at room temperature, indicating the CPE's excellent ability to suppress interfacial side reactions. Li|CPE|NCM811 cells retained a capacity of 77% after 350 cycles, whilst pouch cells retained 76% after 300 stable cycles at room temperature and 0.5 C. The method of optimizing ceramic fillers offers new insights into the design of novel composite solid-state electrolytes for SLBs.
authors: Quanzhi Lin, Senlin Liao, Weixian Wang, Qi Zeng, Yajie Yang

10.1002/aenm.71532.title: Unraveling Spatial Electrochemical Heterogeneity and Additive-Mediated Regulation in Scale-up Aqueous Zinc-Ion Pouch-Type Cells
10.1002/aenm.71532.abstract: ABSTRACT Scaling aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) to pouch-type configurations amplifies electric-field and Zn 2+ flux heterogeneities, causing non-uniform Zn deposition. Here, β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and Tween 80 (Tw80) are systematically investigated to decouple bulk transport and interfacial kinetic regulation in scale-up pouch-type cells. β-CD increases ionic conductivity (3.44 to 5.95 mS cm − 1 ) and the Zn 2+ transference number (0.16 to 0.47), promoting uniform bulk ion flux and extending symmetric pouch-type cell lifespan beyond 1000 h at 1 mA cm − 2 . Conversely, Tw80 operates via interfacial adsorption to regulate local reaction kinetics, achieving stable cycling for >600 h. Spatially resolved analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and in situ thermal imaging reveal that β-CD suppresses macroscopic heterogeneity across near-tab, central, and edge regions by stabilizing bulk solvation, whereas Tw80 mitigates localized interfacial instability. In practical Zn||V 2 O 5 pouch-type full cells, β-CD delivers superior long-term capacity retention, while Tw80 excels under high-rate conditions. This work identifies spatial electrochemical heterogeneity as a primary scaling limit and offers general design principles connecting additive chemistry, transport kinetics, and format-dependent deposition for practical AZIBs.
authors: Nhat Anh Thieu, Wei Li, Shanshan Zhang, Chanho Kim, Guang Yang, Liam Collins, Derrick Banerjee, Konstantinos A. Sierros, Xiaolin Li, Xingbo Liu

10.1002/aenm.71516.title: Highly Efficient and Cost-Effective Single-Atom Catalysts for Lithium-Sulfur Batteries Exceeding 540 Wh kg −1
10.1002/aenm.71516.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the high theoretical energy density (2600 Wh kg −1 ) of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, their practical application in low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles is severely hindered by sluggish reaction kinetics and the severe shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides, making it difficult to meet the stringent demands for high-rate capability and high energy density. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a promising strategy to accelerate polysulfide conversion kinetics. However, conventional SACs often face challenges such as high preparation costs, complex synthetic processes, and catalyst poisoning due to excessively strong binding with sulfur species. To address these technical and economic limitations, this work focuses on developing cost-effective and efficient materials for large-scale energy storage. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ), a low-cost, easily scalable material with abundant nitrogen coordination sites, was selected as the substrate to prepare an atomically dispersed SAC (Mn-CN). Benefiting from the unique half-filled 3d electronic configuration of the Mn atom, the catalyst directly establishes a robust “Mn-S and Li-N” dual-coordination mechanism. This specific interaction effectively activates the Li─S bond and substantially lowers the thermodynamic energy barriers, thereby improving the redox kinetics of polysulfide conversion. Consequently, the assembled Li-S batteries maintain a reversible capacity of 658 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 4 C and exhibit stable long cycling performance. Furthermore, the assembled 14 Ah-level pouch cell achieves an initial energy density of 547 Wh kg −1 and over 30 stable cycles. This work provides a practical approach for preparing cost-effective and efficient single-atom catalysts, supporting the industrial application of high-energy-density Li-S batteries.

10.1002/aenm.71304.title: Electrochemically Driven Refrigeration Based on Dissolution-Crystallization Cycle of Redox-Active Salts
authors: Yifan Zhang, Pei Liu, Yilin Zeng, Xuan Cai, Linfeng Wang, Huaiyu Ke, Xue Long, Hua Jiang, Wendong Yang, Zuoxuan Gan, Jiabao Sun, Jia Li, Jiangjiang Duan

10.1002/aenm.71352.title: Wide-Stable Dynamics Enabling Ultra-High Power Density in Compact Magneto-Mechano-Electric Energy Harvesters for Self-Powered Smart Grid Monitoring
10.1002/aenm.71352.abstract: ABSTRACT Cantilever-structured magneto-mechano-electric energy harvesters (MME-EHs) are considered as one of promising candidates for powering Internet of Things (IoT) devices by capturing ambient magnetic fields. However, conventional MME-EHs with volumes comparable to button cell batteries (≤1 cm 3 ) face a critical challenge in overcoming the output power density bottleneck to meet advancing IoT demands under weak excitations. In this work, we overcome this limitation by proposing a wide-stable energy harvesting strategy. Unlike conventional bistable systems that struggle to sustain high-energy interwell oscillations under weak excitations, or monostable systems restricted by steep potential wells, our design leverages nonlinear dynamics to engineer a broadened and flattened potential well that facilitates large-amplitude intrawell motion even under weak fields. This strategy significantly enhances magneto-mechanical coupling efficiency, enabling a compact MME-EH (effective volume 0.968 cm 3 ) to generate 0.89 mW output power under a weak magnetic field of 1 Oe at 50 Hz, representing an 89% enhancement over the original MME-EH. The output power density reaches 0.92 mW cm −3 Oe −2 , revealing a 26% improvement compared to state-of-the-art performance. Its potential for practical application is validated via a self-powered wireless sensor network (WSN) for grid monitoring and fire alarms, paving the way for maintenance-free, wide-area distributed WSNs.

10.1002/aenm.71634.title: Anion-Driven Solvent Degradation Networks in High-Concentration Battery Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71634.abstract: ABSTRACT High-concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion-mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion-mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride () and fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open-ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro-organic species. These results provide a molecular-level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion-solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.
authors: Esra Ulgey Akgun, Brett M. Savoie

10.1002/aenm.71701.title: Near-Micron Single-Crystalline Mn-Rich Cathodes With Exceptional Cycling Stability
10.1002/aenm.71701.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high-energy-density and long-term cycling stability in Mn-redox-based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni- and Co-free Li-ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn-redox cathodes using near-micron single-crystalline δ-phase cation-disordered rocksalt (δ-DRX), derived from Mn-rich DRX, delivering ≈640 Wh kg −1 with ≈97% capacity retention over 400 cycles. The very high energy density and cycle life were achieved by using a high Mn content, to suppress oxygen redox activity, and careful control of the synthesis parameters to tune single crystal particle size. Using high-throughput automated electron microscopy, we identify interparticle compositional heterogeneity present in the early stage of phase-pure DRX formation as the origin of orthorhombic LiMnO 2 impurity formation during cooling, a finding that rationalizes the long high-temperature dwell times required and the associated particle coarsening in conventional synthesis. We demonstrate that an accelerated cooling strategy kinetically suppresses localized impurity formation, reducing long high-temperature exposure, and enables downsizing of single-crystalline Mn-rich DRX particles to the near-micron regime (D50 = 1.5 µm). This work provides a mechanistic basis for particle-size control in Mn-rich DRX synthesis, and presents δ-DRX as a stable, sustainable, high-performance, Ni- and Co-free cathode material.
authors: Eunryeol Lee, Tucker Holstun, Tara Mishra, Maciej Moździerz, Shilong Wang, Yanbao Fu, Peter Ercius, Alexander Pattison, Satoshi Hiroi, Koji Ohara, Vincent Battaglia, Haegyeom Kim, Akira Miura, Gerbrand Ceder

10.1002/aenm.71711.title: Interfacial Dipole Reorganization Enables Ultrafast Sodium Storage in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71711.abstract: ABSTRACT As a promising cathode material for large-scale sodium-ion energy storage, Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) still suffers from sluggish Na + kinetics and insufficient electronic conductivity. Herein, we propose a bulk-to-interface coupling framework in which substitution-induced electronic regulation propagates from the crystal lattice to the cathode surface, thereby reorganizing the adjacent electrolyte environment. This strategy is implemented by introducing Ni 2 + with high crystal-field stabilization energy into NFPP. Ni 2+ substitution modulates the local electronic structure, strengthens Fe─O d-p hybridization, and promotes medium-range structural ordering. The resulting surface charge redistribution reshapes the interfacial electrostatic potential, suppresses solvent polarization and Na-ClO 4 association, and facilitates interfacial Na + exchange. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 118 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 74% of its capacity after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A pouch cell with a cathode areal capacity of 0.5 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates its feasibility in a full-cell configuration. This work extends substitution chemistry beyond bulk transport optimization toward the deliberate regulation of electrode-electrolyte interactions.
authors: Yuhang Xin, Hexiao Zhang, Kunyu Zhao, Yingshuai Wang, Qingbo Zhou, Yonghao Liu, Runqing Ou, Qianchen Wang, Hongcai Gao

10.1002/aenm.71699.title: Stress Regulation through Precursor Chemistry: From Synthesis to Cycling Stability in O3-Type Layered Oxide Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71699.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium-ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid-state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low-melting-point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid-like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM-A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM-O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM-A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM-A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM-O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.
authors: Qian Li, Changyan Hu, Huan Yang, Haoyu Li, Waiqiao Li, Ruoyang Wang, Guanlin Lv, Peidong Li, Zhenguo Wu, Xiaodong Guo

10.1002/aenm.71709.title: Efficient Cascade Abiotic Synthesis of Sugar From CO2
10.1002/aenm.71709.abstract: ABSTRACT The capability of producing sugar compounds from carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), ideally based on abiotic systems, suggests an artificial, scalable strategy to provide potential solutions for both food and environmental issues. In this work, we report an inorganic, abiotic pathway for the synthesis of sugar from CO 2 without any enzymatic or biological components, comprising several electrocatalytic-catalytic cascade reactions. CO 2 is first electrochemically reduced to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) on a Cu catalyst, and then oxidized to ethylene glycol by hydrogen peroxide in situ generated from the O 2 reduction. Ethylene glycol is further oxidized into glycolaldehyde on a platinum catalyst, and the overall CO 2 -to-glycolaldehyde Faradaic efficiency (FE) reaches ≈ 15.9%. Finally, the as-formed glycolaldehyde is coupled into C 6+ sugar compounds (i.e., higher-carbon carbohydrates products) via the Formose reaction, obviating the need to use biochemical/enzymatic reactions or any additional carbon-based molecules. Using this cascade reaction, we demonstrated an efficient CO 2 -to-sugar production rate of 2.1 g per day with a total carbon selectivity of 25.9%, featuring an attractive approach for producing sugars from CO 2 by renewable electricity.
authors: Ruilin Wei, Yuhang Huang, Lu Song, Maoyin Wang, Haoran Ma, Ximeng Lv, Boyu Hou, Jun Wen, Shuya Hao, Gengfeng Zheng

10.1002/aenm.71569.title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Development of Coking- and Sulfur-Resistant Nanostructured NiGa Alloy-Based Anodes for Solid Oxide Fuel Cells
10.1002/aenm.71569.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) that directly convert natural gas into electricity are promising high-efficiency energy-conversion devices, yet conventional Ni-based anodes suffer from severe carbon deposition and sulfur poisoning, leading to rapid electrode deactivation. Although binary alloying effectively regulates surface reaction pathways and improves anode stability, its development largely relies on experience-driven trial-and-error screening. Here, we propose a rational screening framework that integrates microkinetic analysis with deep neural networks to identify the Ni-Ga alloy from a vast binary alloy chemical space. Density functional theory confirms that such a Ni-Ga alloy combines efficient methane activation with intrinsic resistance to carbon deposition. Guided by these predictions, we further construct a nanocomposite electrode with Gd 0.1 Ce 0.9 O 1.95 (GDC)-encapsulated Ni-Ga alloys (NiGa-GDC). Benefiting from alloy-induced electronic structure modulation and a nanocomposite electrode architecture, the NiGa-GDC nanocomposite anode exhibits exceptional electrochemical performance and coking resistance. In nearly dry methane fuel (3% H 2 O), a corresponding electrolyte-supported single cell achieves both high peak power density and durable operation, far outperforming the counterpart Ni-GDC nanocomposite anode. Moreover, the NiGa-GDC anode demonstrates remarkable resistance to sulfur poisoning. This study provides a new strategy for developing highly active and durable nickel-based nanocomposite anodes for the direct utilization of natural gas.
authors: Haipeng Zhang, Hao Wang, Chenghui Lin, Zhiyi Chen, Jiaqi Qian, Zixiang Cheng, Dewu Long, Chengzhi Guan, Na Ai, San Ping Jiang, Dong Tian, Zijing Lin, Kongfa Chen, Jiujun Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71715.title: Disrupting Solvent Self-Association via Dipole-Dipole Interactions for Improved Performance of Perovskite Solar Cell
10.1002/aenm.71715.abstract: ABSTRACT High-quality perovskite films demand strongly coordinating solvents (SCS, e.g., DMSO, NMP) for crystal growth regulation, yet such solvents often leave residue and induce notorious voids. Prior work elucidated the voids distribution along the vertical direction but cannot explain their lateral dimensions and spatial patterning. Here, we find that the hundreds-of-nanometer lateral dimension and clustered morphology of buried voids originate from the self-association of SCS. The tailored-made 1-bromo-4-dimethylphosphoryl-benzene (BPPO) with inherently weak intermolecular interaction is introduced, which mainly exists in a monomeric form and can efficiently modify the buried interface by constructing dipole-dipole interactions with SCS. The self-association is disrupted, enabling uniform SCS distribution rather than forming big cluster, which accelerates the escape and ultimately eliminates voids at the buried interface. Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on BPPO show an efficiency increase from 25.2% to 27.2% (certified efficiency of 27.0%, aperture area of 0.0712 cm 2 ), with improved stability under ISOS-D-2 and ISOS-L-2 protocols. Furthermore, the BPPO-modified perovskite solar module (PSMs, aperture area of 17.4 cm 2 ) achieved an efficiency of 24.2%, demonstrating its excellent scalability.
authors: Yuqi Du, Wenxiang Xiang, Jiahui Li, Shanwen Wang, Jing Chen, Zhaokui Wang, Geping Qu, Zong-Xiang Xu, Xiangqian Shen, Liyuan Han, Yanbo Wang

10.1002/aenm.71697.title: Electrochemical and Mechanical Understanding of Extruded and Solvent-Cast Solid Polymer Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71697.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on Poly(ethylene oxide)-Lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PEO-LiTFSI) are promising materials for solid-state batteries. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted on their electrochemical and mechanical properties, with SPEs prepared via two processing methods: extrusion and solvent casting. The effects of Al 2 O 3 addition and membrane thickness on SPE performance and cyclability were investigated. Electrochemical characterization showed that extrusion enhanced SPE properties by shortening polymer chains, while the presence of Al 2 O 3 improved membrane stability. Thicker membranes exhibited larger polarization gradients, slower ion diffusion, and lower Sand times, leading to reduced electrochemical performance. Mechanical properties, including yield stress, storage modulus, and fracture toughness, were assessed using rheology and dynamic mechanical analysis. Extruded SPEs displayed higher stiffness and greater resistance to dendrite formation than solvent-cast membranes. Monotonic crack growth tests indicated that the presence of Al 2 O 3 increased fracture toughness, enhancing crack resistance and potentially extending cycle life. Overall, membranes produced via extrusion, containing Al 2 O 3 , and optimized for reduced thickness, combined superior electrochemical properties, making them strong candidates for solid-state battery applications, as demonstrated by their incorporation in multilayer cells.
authors: Elene Sasieta-Barrutia, June Blanco, Laida Otaegui, Aizeti Burgoa, Mikel Isasi, Michel Armand, Rikardo Hernandez, Aitor Villaverde, Maria C. Morant-Miñana

10.1002/aenm.71712.title: Selective Interfacial Coupling in Polymer Electrolytes Stabilizes High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes for > 500 Wh Kg−1 Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71712.abstract: ABSTRACT The interfacial chemistry of high-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is strongly governed by electronic coupling between electrolyte components and cathode surfaces. However, current strategies generally regulate coupling as an overall interaction-strength issue, overlooking the distinct contributions of individual electrolyte species and thereby limiting precise interfacial control. Here, we propose a selective interfacial coupling strategy by constructing an interfacial architecture comprising a coupling center and a weak-coupling environment. Specifically, 2-cyanoethyl acrylate (CA) acts as the coupling center, while a highly fluorinated acrylate (DFA) creates the weak-coupling environment. Their synergy reconstructs the interfacial molecular organization, suppresses undesirable coupling from non-target species, and preserves favorable CA-cathode interactions. Multiscale calculations and operando spectroscopy reveal the reconstructed interfacial structure and its dynamic evolution. The resulting enlarged Ni 3d-O 2p band-center separation stabilizes the TM-O electronic structure, suppressing lattice oxygen release, cation mixing, and transition-metal dissolution. Consequently, Li||Ni90 cells retain 78% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.7 V, while a 5 Ah pouch cell delivers 529.4 Wh kg −1 at 4.6 V. This work establishes selective interfacial coupling as an effective strategy for regulating high-voltage interfaces.
authors: Zixuan Wang, Zunbin Mao, Lu Wei, Zhuo Li, Xin Guo

10.1002/aenm.71704.title: Coupling Interfacial Defect Regulation With Lattice Relaxation in FACsPbI3 Perovskite
10.1002/aenm.71704.abstract: ABSTRACT FACsPbI 3 perovskites, free of volatile methylammonium and mixed halides, are among promising absorbers for efficient optoelectronics owing to their favourable bandgap and intrinsic stability. However, the structurally soft lattice makes their surfaces prone to distortion and defect generation, creating a heterogeneous interfacial energy landscape that promotes non-radiative recombination and ion migration. Here, we report an interfacial regulation strategy that stabilizes the surface/interface configuration of FACsPbI 3 through a defect-lattice coupling mechanism. Introducing morpholinium chloride at the FACsPbI 3 interface/surface enables coordination with undercoordinated lattice sites, thereby relieving local lattice strain, stabilizing surface Pb-I octahedral network, and reducing the density of defect states. This coupling between interfacial chemistry and lattice energetics increases vacancy formation energies, homogenizes the interfacial electronic environment, and suppresses defect-assisted recombination and ion migration. The resulting perovskite solar cells yield an efficiency of 26.67% with a 16.1 cm 2 -aperture mini-module reaching an efficiency of 22.79%. Moreover, the devices exhibit enhanced stability, retaining 95.8% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of continuous operation. This work reveals a defect-lattice coupling paradigm that links interfacial chemistry, lattice energetics, and ion migration kinetics, offering a general route toward stable and high-efficiency soft ionic semiconductors.
authors: Hongshen Xie, Hanguang Fu, Tianchi Zhang, Yehui Wen, Wenbin Han, Biao Li, Xuegong Yu, Deren Yang, Yong Wang

10.1002/aenm.71707.title: Asymmetric C-C Coupling Driven by Heterostructured Ag-Bi Electrocatalyst Enables Selective CO2 Reduction to Ethanol for Microbial Growth
10.1002/aenm.71707.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (eCO 2 RR) coupled with microbial fermentation offers a promising route for carbon valorization, but faces dual challenges from toxic C 1 byproducts (e.g. formate) and poor long-term catalytic stability. Herein, we present a heterostructured Ag-Bi electrocatalyst (Ag 1.65 @Bi 2 O 3 ) with interfacial synergy that drives asymmetric C-C coupling, enabling highly selective conversion of CO 2 to ethanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 87.00% and stable operation for 324 h at -0.9 V vs RHE. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further reveal an asymmetric coupling pathway between *CO and *CHO intermediates, thereby reducing the C-C coupling energy barrier for ethanol production. The obtained liquid stream exhibits no formate toxicity and can be directly utilized by Saccharomyces cerevisiae in an integrated electrochemical-microbial system for yeast production with a yield of 1.05 ± 0.04 g L −1 , which is 35% higher than that of the single fermentation system. This study provides a paradigm for realizing a coupling system of eCO 2 RR and microbial fermentation.
authors: Zexin Xu, Miao Liu, Yanfeng Shi, Fei Li, Jin Liu, Yuanhong Xu

10.1002/aenm.71716.title: Ligand Electronics and Metal-Site Acidity Enable High-Voltage MOF Electrolytes for Quasi-Solid-State Lithium-Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71716.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-metal batteries (LMBs) coupled with Ni-rich cathodes offer high energy density for next-generation energy storage. Their practical implementation, however, is limited by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial degradation under high voltage. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) would regulate ion solvation and stabilize electrode-electrolyte interfaces in quasi-solid-state electrolytes, yet the molecular origins of their oxidation stability remain unclear. Here, we identify ligand electronics and metal-site acidity as key descriptors for high-voltage-stable MOF electrolytes. Electron-withdrawing ligands lower the HOMO energy levels of MOFs, while hard Lewis-acidic Al sites further enhance oxidation resistance. Guided by this principle, we design a perfluorinated Al-based MOF, Al-FBDC, featuring a high oxidation onset potential of 4.82 V (vs. Li + /Li). Incorporating Al-FBDC into a composite cathode reconstructs the local electrolyte environment at particle-level interfaces, thereby suppressing parasitic reactions and cathode degradation under high-voltage operation. As a result, Li||Al-FBDC@NCM quasi-solid-state cells deliver excellent long-term cycling stability and rate performance, retaining 82% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C over 3.0-4.5 V, while maintaining robust performance even at 4.6 and 4.8 V cut-off voltages and with controlled electrolyte loading. This work identifies a general design principle for high-voltage-stable MOF electrolytes and offers a practical route toward high-energy-density LMBs.
authors: Yuzhu Tian, Yifei Xu, Kang Liang, Tianqi Deng, Wei Zhao, Qinghe Wang, Yurong Ren, Hao Bin Wu

10.1002/aenm.71713.title: Engineering Advanced Electrocatalysts for Energy-Saving Zinc−Air Hybrid Batteries: Concurrent Energy Storage Coupled With Chemical Upgrading
10.1002/aenm.71713.abstract: ABSTRACT Additive-assisted zinc−air hybrid batteries (ZAHBs) that couple favorable additive oxidation with oxygen reduction represent ideal energy storage candidates, distinguished by high theoretical energy density, reduced charging voltage, and functionality for electrochemical upgrading of organics or wastewater. Herein, a critical overview of ZAHBs is provided, commencing with the fundamental electrochemistry (including advantages, working mechanisms, cell configurations, and evaluation parameters) and the selection criteria for small-molecule additives (including theoretical potential, solubility, stability, toxicity, and volatility). We then summarize recent progress in three categories of ZAHBs (i.e., wastewater-purified, value-added, and redox-mediated), discussing alternative anodic oxidation reactions (e.g., alcohol, urea, hydrazine, and iodine oxidation) coupled with cathodic oxygen reduction, along with the underlying catalytic mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on catalyst design strategies spanning electronic (ligand engineering, heteroatom doping, electron delocalization, orbital hybridization, and built-in electric field), geometric (defect engineering, curvature engineering, and nano-confinement effect), and interfacial (high-energy interface, heterostructure, interfacial microenvironment, and core-shell structure) modulations. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future perspectives for advancing ZAHBs. This review offers valuable guidance for the rational design and practical deployment of next-generation energy devices.
authors: Xian-Wei Lv, Tao Meng, Mengyue Zhang, Xiaodong Meng, Zhongli Wang, Xuhuan Yan, Zhong-Yong Yuan, Jianxin Geng

10.1002/aenm.71719.title: High-Energy and Long-Life Na3V2(PO4)2F3 Cathodes via Multielement V-Site Modulation of Local M-O/F Bonding
10.1002/aenm.71719.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage, but their energy density still lags behind lithium-ion systems. Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF) is an attractive high-voltage polyanionic cathode, but fluorine loss generates low-voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 impurities that lower energy density and aggravate lattice deformation during cycling. Here, we report a multielement V-site charge modulation strategy, realized in Na 3-δ V 1.9 Zr 0.02 Ti 0.02 Cr 0.02 Fe 0.02 Al 0.02 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (ME-NVPF). The deliberate combination of high-valence Zr 4+ , Ti 4+ , and same-valence Cr 3+ , Fe 3+ , Al 3+ cations creates a heterogeneous M-O/F bonding network with multi-directional electrostatic interactions enhancing lattice-F retention that completely eliminates NVP impurities, lowers the Na + migration barrier, and reduces unit-cell volume variation to merely 2.87%. Consequently, ME-NVPF delivers a record-high energy density of 477 Wh kg −1 , sustains 11 000 cycles, operates across −40 to 80°C, and is further validated in 600 mAh-level pouch cells. This work establishes multielement compositional regulation as an effective strategy for designing high-energy, long-life, and all-temperature polyanionic cathodes.
authors: Zhichao Li, Fuqiang Li, Mushun Chen, Yanyu Sun, Shouyu Sun, Zifei Shi, Cheng Yang, Yu Liu

10.1002/aenm.71698.title: Site-Selectively Engineered MoS2/ReS2 Heterostructures for High-Performance Supercapacitors
10.1002/aenm.71698.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered MoS 2 holds great potential for supercapacitors; however, its intrinsically low electrical conductivity, sluggish electrochemical kinetics, and susceptibility to Mo dissolution severely hamper its electrochemical performance. Here, we propose a selective-doping-coupled heterostructure engineering strategy, in which atomic Fe preferentially incorporates into the MoS 2 domain, while the local structure of the ReS 2 component remains largely preserved, forming an Fe-doped MoS 2 /ReS 2 (Fe-MRS) heterostructure. Theoretical and experimental results reveal the formation of a built-in electric field at the Fe-MRS interface, driving electron transfer from ReS 2 to Fe-doped MoS 2 , reconfiguring the Mo-S electronic structure, while simultaneously strengthening Mo─S bonds and suppressing Mo dissolution. Moreover, Fe incorporation is energetically favored at octahedrally coordinated Mo sites within the MoS 2 domain, modulating the local electronic environment of the MoS 2 domain and thereby facilitating coupled electron/ion transport. Consequently, the Fe-MRS electrode delivers high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability with a capacitance retention of 97.0% over 5000 cycles. Moreover, asymmetric supercapacitors assembled with the Fe-MRS anode achieve a high energy density of 55.2 Wh kg −1 at 1000 W kg −1 , maintaining good structural and mechanical robustness. This work offers clear guidance for leveraging selective doping to engineer heterostructures with enhanced electron-ion coupling for advanced electrochemical energy storage systems.
authors: Haodong Bi, Huilin Zhang, Jisong Hu, Ling Kang, Yusuke Yamauchi, Bin Ding, Shude Liu

10.1002/aenm.71714.title: Machine Learning in Liquid Electrolyte Design for Rechargeable Batteries: Addressing Fundamental Challenges
10.1002/aenm.71714.abstract: ABSTRACT Designing high-performance liquid electrolytes for rechargeable batteries requires simultaneously achieving fast ionic transport, a wide electrochemical window, and interphase stability, yet these objectives are intrinsically coupled and often involve competing trade-offs. Electrolyte optimization remains a formidable challenge for conventional trial-and-error approaches. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) are transforming electrolyte research into a data-driven and increasingly autonomous paradigm for accelerated materials discovery. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on how ML methodologies are tailored to address the fundamental challenges of liquid electrolyte design. We first introduce the physicochemical foundations of liquid electrolytes alongside key ML workflows, emphasizing dataset construction and feature representation tailored to electrolyte chemistry. We then examine ML strategies for predicting and optimizing ionic transport, electrochemical window, interphase regulation, and multi-objective optimization, highlighting representative advances and practical design principles for rational electrolyte development. Finally, we discuss current challenges, including data quality, model generalizability, and interpretability, as well as future opportunities for developing mechanism-informed and transferable ML frameworks. By bridging machine learning with electrolyte science, this review aims to facilitate the rational design of next-generation liquid electrolytes and accelerate the development of high-performance rechargeable batteries.
authors: Qianqian Liu, Chaojie Wang, Zeyi Zhang, Ming Xiao, Xiaokai Hao, Kunzhe Wang, Liguang Wang

10.1002/aenm.71708.title: Covalently Locked Donor-Acceptor Block Copolymer Nanoparticles Enable Efficient, Stable and Reproducible Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/aenm.71708.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all-conjugated donor-acceptor block copolymer, PBDB-T- b -PYT, in which covalent linkage between PBDB-T and PYT segments constrains nanoscale donor-acceptor organization and promotes intramolecular charge transfer. Compared with nanoparticles prepared from a physical PBDB-T:PYT blend, PBDB-T- b -PYT nanoparticles exhibit stronger photoluminescence quenching, more persistent charge-associated transient absorption features, and improved photoelectrochemical charge extraction. As a result, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rates exceeding 120 mmol cm −2 g −1 h −1 (>450 µmol h −1 ) are achieved with low Pt loading (<3 wt.%). PBDB-T- b -PYT NPs retained 95% of the initial HER rate after 96 h of photocatalysis. Conversely, NPs prepared from physically mixed PBDB-T and PYT show lower activity and faster deactivation, consistent with morphology-driven losses. PBDB-T- b -PYT also maintains high performance across polymer batches, improving reproducibility. These results establish all-conjugated donor-acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.
authors: Alexandre Holmes, Qiaonan Chen, Rafael Bicudo Ribeiro, Leandro R. Franco, Soumi Roy, Linnea Lind, Xiaoman Bi, Mateus Bergami, Mathis Mortensen Brette, Lunjie Zeng, Eva Olsson, Bo Albinsson, Márcio T. do N. Varella, C. Moyses Araujo, Ergang Wang

10.1002/aenm.71722.title: Synergy Between Controllable Sulfur Defect and NiS Cocatalyst Enabling Efficient Photoredox Coupling Catalysis
10.1002/aenm.71722.abstract: ABSTRACT Semiconductor-based photoredox coupling of selective oxidation of vanillyl alcohol (VOL) to vanillin (VAL) with H 2 evolution provides a sustainable alternative to conventional industrial VAL synthesis processes, yet its performance is often hindered by rapid charge recombination and insufficient active sites. Herein, we report a facile one-pot hydrothermal strategy to construct NiS-decorated Zn 3 In 2 S 6 (ZIS) nanoflowers with controllable sulfur vacancies (V S ) for efficient co-production of VAL and H 2 . Moderate concentrations of V S regulate the surface electronic structure and act as oxidation active sites to optimize VOL adsorption. Meanwhile, uniformly dispersed NiS cocatalysts serve as efficient electron relays and reduction active sites, accelerating charge migration and promoting H 2 generation. Benefiting from the interfacial synergy between V S and NiS, the optimal 1%NiS-ZIS-V S2 catalyst delivers an 18-fold enhancement in both VAL and H 2 production rates relative to pristine ZIS, together with excellent stability and broad substrate versatility. This work highlights the critical role of defect-cocatalyst synergy in designing advanced cooperative photoredox catalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis.
authors: Chang-Long Tan, Bo Shen, Xiang Lan, Ming-Yu Qi, Zi-Rong Tang, Yi-Jun Xu

10.1002/aenm.71564.title: Advanced Energy Materials at 15: Advancing the Energy Transition From Fundamental Insights to Practical Technologies
10.1002/aenm.71564.abstract: ABSTRACT This Special Issue commemorates the fifteenth anniversary of Advanced Energy Materials and reflects the evolution of energy materials research from fundamental discovery toward practical technologies. Assembled in conjunction with the 2025 Wiley Forum Spring Meeting, the collection brings together 28 Research Articles and 10 Reviews spanning photovoltaics and optoelectronics, electrochemical energy storage and conversion, flexible and distributed energy technologies, and data-driven materials discovery. Collectively, these contributions demonstrate how advances in materials chemistry, defect and interface control, multiscale characterization, scalable manufacturing, and predictive computation are enabling more efficient, stable, and deployable energy systems. The breadth of the collection underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and of evaluating innovations under realistic technological constraints. The Special Issue is dedicated to the memory of Professor Taiho Park, whose scientific vision, leadership, and service left a lasting legacy in the field. Sincere appreciation is extended to all contributing authors, reviewers, and the editorial team whose efforts made this anniversary collection possible.

10.1002/aenm.202506803.title: Smart Exploration of Perovskite Photovoltaics: From AI Driven Discovery to Autonomous Laboratories
10.1002/aenm.202506803.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite solar cells have been developed as a front runner in next generation photovoltaic technology. However, such rapid development is hampered by complex relationships among material compositions, process routes, device architectures, and environmental conditions. The fabrication system is strongly coupled with many variables, which implies that existing empirical optimization methods are less capable to explore design space in high dimensions. Additionally, perovskite materials have sensitive intrinsic properties to environmental factors hence facilitating reproducible optimization across the composition space is notoriously difficult. Now, in this coupled system, artificial intelligence and machine learning have driven progress toward the understanding of the nonlinear composition-process-property relationships. But their predictive reliability is limited by patchy data and low reproducibility in manual experiments. Therefore, controlling lab environments and generating reproducible data with help from autonomous laboratories is paramount to accelerate predictive design. This review highlights recent progress in data driven materials discovery and closed loop experiments in perovskite research. We also report that AI guided process optimization is capable of identifying reproducible manufacturing windows. In parallel, robotic manipulation, high throughput synthesis with in situ monitoring and autonomous characterization are enabling systematic exploration of the multi-dimensional process space.
authors: Wenning Chen, Zheyu Zhang, Kelvian T. Mularso, Bonghyun Jo, Hyun Suk Jung

10.1002/aenm.202506810.title: Multiscale Perspectives on Perovskite Instability: From Atomistic Deformation to Device Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.202506810.abstract: ABSTRACT This review elucidates where the operational instability of perovskite-based optoelectronic devices originates from by comprehensively exploring degradation phenomena from atomistic interactions to device scale. At thermodynamic equilibrium, the intrinsic stability of halide perovskites is reasonably good when considering the balance of intramolecular Asite covalent bonds, intermolecular A-X hydrogen bonds, and mixed ionic-covalent B-X bonding. Under operation, however, photoexcited or injected carriers become localized via trapping at surface and ionic defects and/or polaron formation in the soft Pb-halide framework, which induce Coulombic force to distort the crystal lattice and change atom-to-atom distances. Such effects lower ion migration barriers, enhance lattice distortion, and accelerate atmospheric reactions with ambient species, leading to quick degradation of perovskite crystals. In terms of device-level stability, holerich conditions and interfacial charge accumulation in heterostructured architectures are identified as particularly detrimental, directly linking carrier localization to device-level degradation. Based on these insights, we discuss composition engineering toward favorable large-polaron formation, defect passivation to suppress trap-assisted localization, and interfacial engineering within the heterostructured device. At the end, we propose advanced operation protocols that effectively relieve charge accumulation as key routes to realize durable perovskite optoelectronic devices.

10.1002/aenm.71046.title: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Energy Materials: Architectures, Training Strategies, and Applications
10.1002/aenm.71046.abstract: ABSTRACT Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) provide a practical route to bridge first-principles accuracy with the spatiotemporal scales required for modeling complex energy materials. By learning potential-energy surfaces from density functional theory (DFT) data, MLIPs enable atomistic simulations up to 10 4 -10 6 atoms over nanosecond timescales, thereby extending access to phenomena inaccessible to ab initio molecular dynamics. This review presents a phenomenon-oriented synthesis of MLIP development, spanning descriptor-based models, Gaussian process frameworks with uncertainty quantification, equivariant graph neural networks, and foundation models trained on large-scale datasets. We assess how architectural choices, training strategies (including active learning and multi-fidelity approaches), and dataset design influence accuracy, transferability, and computational efficiency across representative energy systems. Applications in solid-state electrolytes, battery electrodes, electrocatalysts, perovskite photovoltaics, and high-entropy materials are discussed with both performance metrics and methodological rationale. While MLIPs capture qualitative trends and relative property variations, absolute predictions remain sensitive to DFT functional choices, dataset representativeness, and treatment of long-range interactions. We address a structured validation framework linking model fidelity to experimentally relevant observables and system complexity. Also, we outline emerging directions including generative inverse design, autonomous discovery workflows, and foundation-model fine-tuning, highlighting opportunities and limitations for predictive deployment in energy materials research.
