10.1002/aenm.71726.title: Using MIS Thermally Stimulated Currents for Degradation Dependent Energetic Landscape Evaluation in Triple Cation Mixed Halide Perovskites
10.1002/aenm.71726.abstract: ABSTRACT For perovskite solar cells (PSCs), despite the remarkable advancements in power conversion efficiency and environmental stability, degradation under operational conditions remains a barrier between research and commercialization. Understanding and monitoring the underlying physics of electronic band gap states during degradation as a result of ambient conditions is essential for further improvements in device stability. Here, advanced defect spectroscopy utilizing thermally stimulated currents (TSC) coupled to a metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) structure is used to determine the energetic landscape of band gap states in relevant state-of-the-art triple cation mixed halide (TCMH) perovskite samples to demonstrate the capabilities of this method. MIS TSC is used to resolve the electrical effect of degradation induced by ambient conditions and natural illumination. Coupling these findings to optoelectronic and structural analysis of individual perovskite layers and functional PSCs, a correlation between material degradation, device performance and trap state evolution can be obtained. We find that with aging under ambient conditions and exposure to light, in TCMH the electron trap density is reduced, while the density of detected hole states increases. For this unexpected behavior, we propose a change of trap type and polarity during degradation.
authors: L. Leander Schaberg, Young Un Jin, Witchaya Arpavate, Yueming Wang, Roland Schmechel, Thomas Kirchartz, Doru C. Lupascu, Niels Benson

10.1002/aenm.71728.title: Reaction-Driven Coupled Transport-Nanostructure Evolution in SnSb Anodes for High-Energy All-Solid-State Li-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71728.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state Li-ion batteries (ASSLIBs) require high-performance anodes exhibiting high capacity, high rate capability, and long-term cycling stability; however, existing anodes suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, particle pulverization, and unstable electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Herein, a SnSb anode overcoming these limitations via reaction-driven coupled transport-nanostructure evolution during electrochemical cycling is reported. The transport evolution originates from the reaction-driven formation of continuous mixed ionic-electronic conducting pathways and nanostructure evolution arises from repeated conversion and recombination reactions that induce stabilized nanocrystallization. This coupled evolution dynamically reconstructs mixed-conducting pathways during lithiation-delithiation, suppresses particle agglomeration, preserves intimate contact with the Li 6 PS 5 Cl solid electrolyte (SE), and lowers interfacial resistance, enabling rapid and highly reversible electrochemical reactions. A SnSb|NCM811 full cell delivers an areal capacity of 28.97 mAh cm −2 at an ultrahigh cathode loading of 200 mg cm −2 and maintains ultrafast rate capability over 1000 cycles at 10 C. Using an optimized 30-µm-thick SE sheet, the full cell is projected to achieve gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 355.7 Wh kg −1 and 1017.4 Wh L −1 , respectively. Pouch-cell demonstrations highlight the potential of SnSb for high-energy density ASSLIB applications and establish reaction-driven coupled transport-nanostructure evolution as an effective design principle for next-generation ASSLIB anodes.
authors: Je-Hyeon Han, Deok-Gyu Kim, Jung-Woon Yoo, Jeong-Myeong Yoon, Young-Han Lee, Do-Hyeon Kim, Pugalenthiyar Thondaiman, Chul-Ho Lee, Jeong-Hee Choi, Ki-Joon Jeon, Cheol-Min Park

10.1002/aenm.71717.title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self-Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few-Layer Nanosheets Grown From High-Curvature Micro-Interface for Fuel Cell
10.1002/aenm.71717.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self-supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low-resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self-supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro-interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self-supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few-layer iCOF nanosheets at high-curvature micro-interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation-driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere-like morphologies in previously reported micro-interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil-in-water microemulsion interface using weakly surface-active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As-prepared iCOF few-layer nanosheets (1.3-1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self-supporting iCOF PEM (3.2-15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF-based membranes.
authors: Huimin Zhao, Bo Pang, Zihao Fan, Tianyu Liang, Xinran Li, Wanting Chen, Xuemei Wu, Fujun Cui, Gaohong He

10.1002/aenm.71724.title: Synergistic Proton Transport Regulation and Interfacial Anion Adsorption Engineering in ZIF-8-Derived PtCu Electrocatalysts for High-Performance Light and Heavy-Duty PEM Fuel Cells
10.1002/aenm.71724.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering catalyst-ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT-PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework-8-derived 3D-hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D-hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton-conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half-cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin-type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec − 1 , delivering 0.75 A mg Pt −1 at 0.90 V IR-free under H 2 -O 2 operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm − 2 at 0.70 V under light- and heavy-duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress-test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst-ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass-transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high-performance LT-PEMFC.
authors: Mayank U. Singh, Riya M. Robert, Nikhil S. Samudre, Sailaja Krishnamurty, Sreekumar Kurungot

10.1002/aenm.71721.title: Dual Anion-Involved Interfacial Chemistry Enables Ultra-Stable PEO-Based Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries by Suppressing NMP-Induced Side Reactions
10.1002/aenm.71721.abstract: ABSTRACT The incorporation of solvent N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) into polyethylene oxide (PEO) weakens EO-Li + interaction and boosts Li + transport via strong Li + affinity, but free NMP inevitably reacts with Li metal, undermining interface stability. Herein, we report a dual-anion coordination strategy that repurposes the residual NMP from a “side-reaction source” into a “functional component”. LiDFOB and LiNO 3 are introduced as dual-salt additives into an NMP-containing PEO/LiTFSI system. Leveraging the preferential coordination of DFOB- and NO 3 - with Li + , an anion-enriched solvation sheath is constructed, which strengthens the Li + -NMP interactions. The modified coordination environment facilitates the preferential formation of a kinetically stable, anion-derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively mitigating interfacial side reactions between the NMP and Li metal. As a result, the obtained electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.69 × 10 −4 S cm −1 and stable cycling over 1200 h at room temperature. The assembled Li/LFP cell exhibits a high capacity retention of 93% after 2000 cycles. Even at room temperate and 0°C, the assembled Li/LFP cell maintains stable and efficient cycling. This work establishes a universal solvent structure tailoring strategy to regulate reactive solvent molecules, opening a fresh avenue for high-performance PEO-based solid-state lithium metal batteries.
authors: Weiya Li, Hongkai Hu, Kang Dong, Jiahao Geng, Mengqiu Li, Die Lai, TianTian Dong, Chi Zhang, Yongcheng Jin

10.1002/aenm.71720.title: Electric Double Layer-Driven Surface Reconstruction Enables Cooperative Zn(002)/(101) Growth for High-Utilization Zinc Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71720.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc batteries are limited by the mismatch between dynamic interfacial chemistry and anisotropic Zn crystallization. Here, imidazolidinyl urea (IDU) is used to couple electric double layer (EDL) reconstruction with Zn surface reorganization. IDU preferentially enriches at the Zn/electrolyte interface, displaces interfacial water, and interacts strongly with Zn(100). In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, quartz crystal microbalance, and neutron reflectivity reveal transient removal and reconstruction of surface Zn rather than simple molecular adsorption. The reconstructed interface suppresses Zn(100) and promotes cooperative Zn(002)/(101) evolution, enabling compact deposition with favorable kinetics. Meanwhile, the water-deficient EDL and hybrid organic-inorganic interphase inhibit parasitic reactions and stabilize the interfacial environment. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 6000 h at 4 mA cm −2 and 2 mAh cm −2 , while Zn||Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 3000 cycles. Stable operation is further maintained at −10°C and under high Zn utilization. Zn||CVO full cells retain 75% capacity after 650 cycles at an N/P ratio of 2.9, and a 21 mAh pouch cell preserves 84% capacity after 400 cycles. This work links EDL reconstruction with crystallographic evolution to enable highly reversible and practically relevant Zn metal anodes.
authors: Yuao Wang, Tiantian Wang, Kangcheng Shen, Fengbao Qin, Mingrui Liao, Jian Ren Lu, Ke Ye, Dianxue Cao, Kai Zhu

10.1002/aenm.71723.title: Tailoring Crystal Facets Enables Scalable Synthesis of Highly Dispersed Single Crystal NCM90
10.1002/aenm.71723.abstract: ABSTRACT The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high-valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi 0.90 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (SC-NCM90) in low-cost. The surface substitution of Ni 2+/3+ by W 6+ /Mo 6+ facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo-doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li + -migration and endowing the Mo 6+ -doped SC-NCM90 with the capacity of 111.0 mAh g −1 at 5C, achieving the desired fast charging for SC-NCM90. W-doping facilitates the growth of both (003) and (104) planes, benefiting the particle segregation, as (003) plane inhibits ionic fusion. W- and Mo-doped SC-NCM90 deliver markedly improved cycling life and safety performance than polycrystalline NCM90. This work establishes the strategy of high-valence elemental surface doping as a dual-functional paradigm that simultaneously manipulates crystal facet evolution for suppressing particle agglomeration and fortifies transition metal (TM)─O bonding for stabilizing interface, producing highly dispersed SC-NCM90 with faster charging capability and durability.
authors: Xiaolei Li, Hongjian Zhu, Feng Gao, Xiaohang Liu, Hao Huang, Wei Xu, Xue Wang, Philipp Kurzhals, Qiaobao Zhang, Weidong Zhou

10.1002/aenm.71461.title: Chemomechanically Adaptive MXene-Si-Ag Dual-Seed Interlayer Enabling Low-Pressure Sulfide all-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71461.abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) promise high safety and energy density; however, sustaining stable operation under low stack pressure remains challenging due to chemo-mechanical instability at solid-solid interfaces. Here, we report a chemomechanically adaptive MXene-Si-Ag hybrid interlayer that stabilizes Li metal-based anode interfaces in sulfide ASSBs. A mechanically compliant MXene framework maintains intimate contact with the sulfide solid electrolyte and accommodates interfacial stress evolution, while immobile Si and mobile Ag function as complementary lithiophilic seeds. Si provides persistent interfacial anchoring and continuous ionic pathways owing to its negligible solubility in Li, whereas Ag dynamically redistributes along Li flux to regulate nucleation and interfacial reaction kinetics. This immobile-mobile dual-seed synergy homogenizes Li transport without requiring strict spatial overlap of the seeds. When paired with high-loading NCM811 cathodes, the interlayer enables an areal capacity of 4.56 mAh cm −2 with 84.5% capacity retention over 500 cycles at 1C under 40 MPa. Notably, stable cycling is preserved even under ultralow stack pressure (0.21 MPa), delivering an initial Coulombic efficiency of 82.7% and 72.4% capacity retention after 200 cycles. This work demonstrates that coupling mechanical adaptability with dynamic lithiophilic regulation provides a practical pathway toward pressure-tolerant, high-energy sulfide ASSBs.

10.1002/aenm.71735.title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin Film Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71735.abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth-abundant, non-toxic, and bandgap-tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one-step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium-source switching driven two-step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea-based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film serving as a primary light-harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate-based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as-deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep-level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE-Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one-step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high-quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion-exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.
authors: Junwei Chen, Chenlong Gao, Fang Wu, Congrui Liu, Pengfei Wang, Zhihui Yang, Xiang Li, Tao Chen, Rongfeng Tang

10.1002/aenm.71710.title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71710.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high-voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid-flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS − readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li + , constructing an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H 2 O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO 2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm −2 )/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates-for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF 6 -based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

10.1002/aenm.71725.title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71725.abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble-metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid-etching-assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh-loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal-support interaction to establish a highly electron-deficient, rigid Ir-O-Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g −1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31-fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mg Ir cm −2 , it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial-relevant 1 A cm −2 . Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation-prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum-mechanical origin: strong metal-support interaction-induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d-band center to -3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity-stability trade-off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial-grade acidic water electrolysis.
authors: Fenghua Zheng, Mengjie Liu, Guiru Zhang, Xiaoxuan Xu, Huiyuan Li, Xiaojing Cheng, Liuxuan Luo, Xiaohui Yan, Shuiyun Shen, Junliang Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71727.title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost-Effective Lithium Carbonate-Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71727.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC-derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid-Ni cathode, LiNi 0.65 Co 0.05 Mn 0.30 O 2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC-induced defects that span length scales, from atomic-scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen-deficient atmosphere from evolving CO 2 . Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65-LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all-LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor-specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low-cost, high-performance Ni-based layered oxide cathodes.
authors: Jaesub Kwon, Innyoung Kim, Jong-Heon Lim, Doun Lee, Youngsu Lee, Kyoung Eun Lee, Hoyeon Shin, Young Jin Lim, Siyeong Park, Seok Mun Kang, Jaesang Yoon, Youngki Kim, Jihyun Kim, Eugene Kim, Younghyun Kim, Kyu-Young Park, Docheon Ahn, Yong-Tae Kim

10.1002/aenm.71729.title: Oxyhalide-Derived Nb-O-Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen-Related Degradation and Facilitating Li+ Transport in High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71729.abstract: ABSTRACT High-voltage Ni-rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni-O configurations and Li + transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li + transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide-enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb-O-Cl framework on LiNi 0.83 Co 0.07 Mn 0.10 O 2 cathodes (denoted as C-NCM). Derived from a mixed-anion LiNbOCl 4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb-O-Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb-containing near-surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni-O electronic environment and mediates interface-crossing Li + transport. Nb-O/Nb-O-Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni-O configurations and mitigated oxygen-related irreversible evolution, while the Cl-containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li + migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C-NCM exhibits reduced sulfide-derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide-electrolyte interface design from passive oxide-barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed-anion interfacial chemistry.
authors: Kangzhe Yu, Zhan Wang, Xiao Huang, Lei Su, Leijie Zhang, Bingbing Tian, Musheng Wu, Chuying OuYang

10.1002/aenm.71718.title: Axial Cl-Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single-Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc-Air Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71718.abstract: ABSTRACT Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M-N 4 . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single-atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF-8-derived ion exchange and gas-phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M-N 4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half-wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge-discharge cycling in zinc-air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge-type adsorption of O 2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.
authors: Zehao Tan, Peng Shen, Yangge Guo, Enping Wang, Jiabin You, Aiming Wu, Xiaojing Cheng, Jiewei Yin, Shuiyun Shen, Liuxuan Luo, Junliang Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71731.title: Charge-State-Controlled Surface Modifiers for High-Voltage and Stable Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71731.abstract: ABSTRACT For wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskites, quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) surface reconstruction using bulky-cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium-based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low-dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic-spacer charge-state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs 0.2 FA 0.8 PbI 1.8 Br 1.2 wide-bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N -methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge-neutralized ammonium-sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden-Popper-like quasi-2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap-mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide-ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO-treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO-treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS-L-1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge-neutralized organic spacer for quasi-2D surface reconstruction in wide-bandgap mixed-halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.
authors: Subin Yu, Wooyeon Kim, In Choi, Bonkee Koo, Min Jae Ko

10.1002/aenm.71734.title: Operando Electro-Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport-Mechanical-Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71734.abstract: ABSTRACT Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self-assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene- block -poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time-resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport-mechanical-morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self-assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.
authors: Martino Airoldi, Mercedes Fernandez, Irune Villaluenga

10.1002/aenm.71738.title: Atomically Dispersed Fe-Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two-Electron Li2C2O4 Pathway for Reversible Li-CO2 Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71738.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-carbon dioxide (Li-CO 2 ) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high-energy storage with CO 2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two-electron conversion toward Li 2 C 2 O 4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual-atom Fe-N-Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N-doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe 1 -Mo 1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe 1 -Mo 1 /ICPs) to promote a reversible two-electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N-doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter-site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe-N-Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor-acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li 2 C 2 O 4 . Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li 2 C 2 O 4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual-atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.
authors: Xuelian Li, Yuan Liu, Qianqian Zhang, Gaimei Guo, Yiming Liu, Kai Hou, Lili Gao, Kai Qi, Jianli Cheng, Bin Wang, Jiancheng Wang

10.1002/aenm.71748.title: Mineral Particle Suspensions in Carbonate Electrolyte Enable LiF-Rich Interphases for Durable Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71748.abstract: ABSTRACT The solid electrolyte interphase in lithium metal batteries determines cycling stability but often suffers from the incomplete decomposition of fluorinated components. Herein, we demonstrate that suspending LiF and Li 2 O particles in a carbonate-based electrolyte promotes the defluorination of fluoroethylene carbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate. These particles preferentially adsorb fluorinated electrolyte species and induce electronic polarization, thereby modulating their redox reactivity and facilitating interfacial decomposition toward LiF. The generated LiF, together with the trace dissolution and interfacial reprecipitation of suspended LiF particles, continuously enriches the electrode surface with LiF-rich inorganic species. This process results in the formation of a bilayer interphase on both the lithium metal anode and LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 cathode, featuring a flexible inner layer and a dense LiF-rich outer layer. The resulting interphase suppresses lithium dendrites, mitigates parasitic reactions, and enables 2400 h of stable cycling in symmetric cells and 85.6% capacity retention after 400 cycles in full cells. By introducing suspended LiF/Li 2 O particles to regulate the interfacial decomposition of fluorinated electrolyte species, this work provides an effective electrolyte-design strategy for constructing robust interphases in lithium metal batteries.
authors: Hongmei Liang, Lisha Mou, Jin Leng, Aiping Wang, Li Wang, Yongsheng Han, Xiangming He

10.1002/aenm.71740.title: Helical Keratin-Derived Aqueous Binders for High-Performance Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71740.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next-generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass-derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α-helical protein (α-HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α -helical structure of α-HP in the α-HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N- and O-containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium-sulfur batteries employing the α-HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long-term cycling stability. The α-HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g −1 and retains 487.9 mAh g −1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium-sulfur battery applications.
authors: Bingzhong Chen, Hao Chen, Xuqi Lin, Kunwei Huang, Yuhao Liang, Cheng Yan, Shanqing Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71736.title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li2Ta2OCl10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm−1)
10.1002/aenm.71736.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium-metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy-density limits of conventional lithium-ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo-mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast-ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 , synthesized via a simple low-temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta 2 OCl 10 ] 2− dimers and exhibits a room-temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm − 1 . Ball milling dramatically enhances Li + transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm −1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid-like Li + sublattice. Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89-3.70 V vs. Li x In and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li-M-O-Cl family as a fertile design space for next-generation solid electrolytes.

10.1002/aenm.71737.title: Trash to Treasure: PFAS-Functionalized MOFs for Boosted Piezocatalytic H2 Production
10.1002/aenm.71737.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) hold broad prospects in piezocatalysis because of their high surface area, porosity, and tunable structures, yet pristine MOFs frequently suffer from poor piezocatalytic response. Herein, this study pioneers a novel strategy using pollutant perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) as a functional additive to post-synthetically modify MOF-808(Hf), fabricating MOF-808(Hf)-F for piezocatalytic hydrogen production. PFHxA modification remarkably enhances the polarity of MOF-808(Hf) (dipole moment from 8.90 to 12.58 D) and piezoelectricity (d 33 from 63.70 to 234.30 pm V −1 ), boosting electron-hole separation verified by electrochemical and in situ photoluminescence characterizations. Consequently, MOF-808(Hf)-F achieves an excellent piezocatalytic H 2 evolution rate of 2811.4 µmol g −1 h −1 , 10.5-fold higher than the pristine counterpart and superior to that of numerous reported MOF-based piezocatalysts. In addition, MOF-808(Hf) achieves a PFHxA removal efficiency of approximately 40.1% from water. This work realizes simultaneous per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal and efficient energy production, with excellent universality for Hf-based MOFs with unsaturated metal sites.

10.1002/aenm.71749.title: 16.52% Efficiency All-Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells via Al-Doped ZnO/SnO2 Electron Transport Bilayer for Improved Interfacial Energy-Level Alignment
10.1002/aenm.71749.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial energy-level misalignment in all-inorganic perovskite solar cells generally causes inefficient charge extraction. Here, we propose an Al-doped ZnO (AZO)/SnO 2 electron transport bilayer to improve energy-level alignment in CsPbI 2 Br-based PSCs. By this approach, we achieved a champion efficiency of 16.52%, which is the highest reported value for all-inorganic CsPbI 2 Br PSCs without doping or passivation of the perovskite, along with a high V OC of 1.33 V. AZO-based devices substantially outperform ZnO-based controls, delivering a PCE of 16.52% versus 15.21%, with suppressed dark current, reduced trap density, lower non-radiative recombination, and smaller hysteresis. The AZO device retains 80% of its initial efficiency after 662 h of continuous illumination, compared with only 312 h for the ZnO counterpart. Al 3+ substitution for Zn 2+ elevates the ZnO conduction band minimum, establishing a favorable cascade alignment among SnO 2 /AZO/perovskite that lowers the electron extraction barrier and blocks hole backflow. Al doping also suppresses oxygen vacancies, reducing interfacial trap-state density and enhancing perovskite crystallinity. Efficient charge extraction further suppresses Ag electrode degradation and corrosion, contributing to long-term stability. This work establishes a rational interfacial engineering approach using an AZO/SnO 2 bilayer for efficient and stable all-inorganic perovskite solar cells.
authors: Haoxuan Guo, Zhiqiang Ming, Changqian Li, Xiangyang Yuan, Ruoyuan Xie, Junhui Ran, Xiao Wang, Yongbo Yuan, Bin Yang

10.1002/aenm.71746.title: Resolving the Structural Origin of Lattice Oxygen Release across Scales in Practical Lithium-Manganese-Rich Electrodes
10.1002/aenm.71746.abstract: ABSTRACT Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high-energy-density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary-particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X-ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O 2 evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium-manganese-rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary-particle size are employed as a model system, and their O 2 evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn-reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode- or particle-scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium-intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O 2 evolution matches after frontal-facet area normalization, identifying frontal-facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O 2 evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.

10.1002/aenm.71751.title: Regioisomerism-Guided Molecular Passivation for 26.05%-Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71751.abstract: ABSTRACT Defect-mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism-guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well-defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI 2 ) precursor solution during two-step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho-, meta-, and para-fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2-fluoroaniline (2-FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2-FA facilitates high-quality α-FAPbI 3 films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n-i-p PSCs. Moreover, the 2-FA-containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism-guided design works universally across n-i-p and p-i-n architectures, irrespective of one-step or two-step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.

10.1002/aenm.71760.title: Adaptive Ferroic Bi-Sb Hybrid Iodides for Multi-Modal Energy Harvesting and Phototronics
10.1002/aenm.71760.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic-inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice-charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition-driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6-diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non-centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI 5 (HBI) and HDASbI 5 (HSI) together with a lower-symmetry non-centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi 0.5 Sb 0.5 I 5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable-temperature crystallography and 1 H NMR, multi-perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi-dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb-rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure-dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine-vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI-HSI-HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1-fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.
authors: Shresth Gupta, Sanuja Kumar Khuntia, Nilotpal Deka, Manotosh Pramanik, Bipul Pal, Ramamoorthy Boomishankar, Priya Mahadevan, Sayan Bhattacharyya

10.1002/aenm.71758.title: Suppressing Photooxidation and Iodine Migration in HTL-Free Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells via a Tailor-Made Redox Guard
10.1002/aenm.71758.abstract: ABSTRACT Hole transport layer-free carbon-based perovskite solar cells (HTL-free C-PSCs) suffer rapid performance decay under operational stressors, driven by iodine migration and photogenerated superoxide radicals (O 2 •− ). To break this photo-oxidation-iodine migration vicious cycle, we design a multifunctional molecular stabilizer, tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)tetrathiafulvalene (4B-TTF). This tailor-made “molecular guard” works via two synergistic mechanisms: its reversible TTF core acts as a charge-transfer mediator, reducing I 2 to I − and scavenging O 2 •− , while four peripheral benzoic acid groups anchor to undercoordinated Pb 2+ sites, passivating grain-boundary defects. Incorporating 4B-TTF into MAPbI 3 -based devices yields a champion power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.96%, vs. 17.58% for the control, by suppressing non-radiative recombination. Unencapsulated devices retain 96.4% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under ambient storage and 93.5% after 120 h under harsh UV-oxygen exposure; encapsulated devices retain 90.32% after 700 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1-sun illumination at 55°C in nitrogen. The strategy is further validated in Cs 0.17 FA 0.83 PbI 3 systems, delivering a state-of-the-art PCE of 20.70%. This work provides a unified molecular-level strategy to concurrently address ionic, radical, and defect-related degradation, bridging the performance gap between low-cost HTL-free devices and conventional high-cost architectures.

10.1002/aenm.71756.title: Simultaneous Optimization of Thermoelectric Transport and Mechanical Performance in Full-Zintl CaCd2Sb2/Mg3Sb2 Thermoelectric Modules
10.1002/aenm.71756.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving both high thermoelectric performance and robust mechanical strength remains a key pursuit for the practical deployment of thermoelectric applications. Herein, a solid-solution approach is employed in CaCd 2 Sb 2 via alloying with EuMg 2 Sb 2 , achieving a synergistic optimization of electrical and phonon transport and mechanical performance. The incorporation of EuMg 2 Sb 2 facilitates band degeneracy, thereby substantially improving the electrical transport properties. Together with the reduced thermal conductivity, the optimized composition exhibits a peak zT of ∼ 1.4 at 750 K and an average zT of ∼ 0.81 between 300 and 750 K. Furthermore, solid-solution strengthening markedly enhances the mechanical properties, thereby ensuring mechanical integrity for reliable device integration. Leveraging transient liquid phase bonding, a 2 × 2 full-Zintl module combining this optimized p-type material with Mg 3 Sb 2 -based n-type legs achieves a conversion efficiency of ∼ 11% at a temperature difference of 422 K. This work highlights the viability of Zintl phases toward high-efficiency thermoelectric modules.
authors: Kejia Liu, Ruihuan Cheng, Yujie Huang, Xiaofang Li, Wenhua Xue, Haiqi Li, Huajian Wu, Yuxin Sun, Jinsuo Hu, Dongyi Shen, Xiaodong Wang, Chen Chen, Yue Chen

10.1002/aenm.71759.title: Bifunctional Additive Enabled Thermoresponsive Electrolytes With Dual-Mode Manipulation Toward Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71759.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high-rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO 3 additive into a high-volume-fraction vinylene carbonate-based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE-N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO 3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li + and forms a Li 3 N/LiN x O y solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE-N undergoes a rapid liquid-to-solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO 3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE-N exhibits high-rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE-N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high-rate performance.
authors: Xue Yang, Xiao Hang Guo, Ming Hui Zhang, Yu Hao Huang, Yong Li, Bao Ning Zhu, Hua Jun Tian, Le Yu

10.1002/aenm.71459.title: Electron Spin-State Regulation Unlocks Structural Robustness and Stable Sodium Storage in Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 Cathode
10.1002/aenm.71459.abstract: ABSTRACT The low-cost, structurally robust Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) polyanionic cathode for sodium-ion batteries is constrained by electronic insulation and sluggish Na + transport. Herein, a spin-state-engineered cathode, Na 4 Fe 2.94 Mo 0.03 Co 0.03 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (MC-NFPP), is developed to modulate the local electronic structure of Fe, thereby unlocking additional unpaired electrons to simultaneously enhance intrinsic charge transport and lattice stability. The high-valence Mo 6+ weakens the local ligand field via the inductive effect, while Co 2+ promotes spin reconfiguration through magnetic exchange interactions. This design induces a profound electronic reconfiguration, driving the transition of Fe from an intermediate-spin (IS) to a high-spin (HS) state (with the HS-Fe 2+ fraction rising from 65.0% to 79.2%), which concurrently narrows the bandgap and lowers the Na + migration barrier. Meanwhile, the increased fraction of flexible HS-state FeO 6 octahedra activates a spin-regulated structural breathing effect, enabling rapid relaxation of distorted [P 2 O 7 ] units and markedly reducing unit cell volume fluctuation from 5.78% to 3.89%, thus ensuring robust structural resilience. Consequently, MC-NFPP achieves a high reversible capacity of 89.2 mAh g −1 at 30 C and retains 96.8% capacity after 1200 cycles in full cells. This spin-state regulation effectively overcomes the intrinsic kinetic and structural bottlenecks of polyanionic cathodes, providing a viable pathway for their practical deployment.

10.1002/aenm.71761.title: Redirecting Bond Cleavage in Sacrificial Prelithiation via Dual-Side Separator Engineering for Anode-Free Lithium Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71761.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst-induced bond-cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual-side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC 1-x /NC-0.3Co coating redirects Li 2 C 2 O 4 decomposition from high-barrier Li-O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li + utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi-PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li + desolvation and drives the in-situ construction of a LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm −2 , DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode-free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC 1-x /NC-0.3Co-LCO/PE/PSSLi-PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg −1 and 1005.2 Wh L −1 , a power output of 989.1 W kg −1 , retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non-invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high-energy AFLMBs.
authors: Junyu Zhang, Xiangrui Tian, Jiawen Tang, Yunsong Li, Wenzhuo Tan, Peiwen Fan, Tongshuai Wang, Yisheng Hu, Chunwei Li, Ahu Shao, Jiacheng Liu, Xin Wang, Wei Gao, Yue Ma

10.1002/aenm.71752.title: Chloride-Mediated Activation of Aluminum-Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
10.1002/aenm.71752.abstract: ABSTRACT Gallium-based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite-free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co-design of an aluminum-alloyed gallium-indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride-rich water-in-ionic-liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium-assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl-rich mixed Al-Ga-O shell susceptible to [GaCl 4 ] − -mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential-resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI-based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI-derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride-dominated electrode-electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g − 1 . Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm −3 normalized to the active-electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide-mediated oxide-displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte-design strategy for oxide-passivated liquid-metal and post-lithium anodes.
authors: Adit Gupta, Yufei Zhang, Jae Uk Choi, Pooi See Lee

10.1002/aenm.71757.title: Homogenizing Fullerene Contacts by Supramolecular Host-Guest Assembly for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71757.abstract: ABSTRACT Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high-performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long-term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host-guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene-based ETLs. The [6,6]-phenyl-C 61 -butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)-TPC host-guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal-driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high-stability optoelectronic devices.
authors: Jian Lin, Haonan Wang, Xinyi Liu, Yiheng Shi, Junjie Qian, Guocan Chen, Mengyao Song, Shuang Yang, Yu Hou

10.1002/aenm.71755.title: Molecularly Induced Carrier-Polarity Regulation Enables Efficient Methylammonium-Free Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71755.abstract: ABSTRACT Methylammonium (MA)-free wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites are attractive top-cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, defect-related donor-state contributions can shift the perovskite Fermi level away from the valence-band maximum (VBM), creating an unfavorable energetic mismatch with the hole-selective Poly-4PACZ/perovskite contact and contributing to voltage and fill-factor losses in perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure. Here, we introduce 4-(piperidin-4-yl)benzoic acid hydrochloride (PBAC) as a spatially organized molecular additive that regulates the carrier polarity of MA-free WBG perovskites while passivating defects. PBAC shifts the Fermi level toward the VBM and reduces the Fermi-level offset at the Poly-4PACZ/perovskite interface. This carrier-polarity regulation improves energetic compatibility at the hole-selective contact, facilitating hole extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination. Defect passivation and strain relaxation further inhibit halide migration and stabilize the mixed-halide lattice. As a result, MA-free WBG perovskite solar cells with bandgaps of 1.66 and 1.77 eV achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 24.66% and 20.74%, respectively. The unencapsulated PBAC-treated 1.66 eV device retains 86% of its initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous AM 1.5G operation in ambient air. These results establish molecularly induced carrier-polarity regulation as an effective strategy for reducing interfacial losses in MA-free WBG perovskite solar cells.
authors: Yaqing Li, Qi Huang, Hong Liu, Yu Su, Kongxiang Wang, Xiang Li, Jiahan Wang, Haiting Zhou, Guoping Huang, Yuanzhi Wang, Zhongtao Duan, Jian Mao, Junhao Chu, Fengxian Xie

10.1002/aenm.71610.title: Descriptor-Guided Stabilization of Reconstructed Active Phases for High-Activity and Durable CO2-to-Formate Conversion
10.1002/aenm.71610.abstract: ABSTRACT Sn oxides are promising CO 2 RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over-reduce active oxide-derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working-state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor-guided framework that links dynamic Sn-oxide reconstruction with electronic-structure evolution and formate-producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working-state active phase. Electronic-structure analysis shows that the optimal Sn x O y /Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge-polarization redistribution and Sn 5 s /5 p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5 p coupling, and Sn 5 s lone-pair activation, which exhibits a volcano-type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed Sn x O y /Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO 2 is designed to stabilize the favorable Sn x O y /Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO − partial current density of 438.0 mA cm −2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO 2 . This work provides a descriptor-guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO 2 RR.
authors: Huan Li, Yong Zhang, Jinchao Xu, Chunning Zhao, Yumin Wang, Gang Chen, Yahui Cheng, Ruiting Hao, Xiang Wan, Weichao Wang

10.1002/aenm.71566.title: A Goldilocks-Inspired Amphiphilic Additive Orchestrates Interfacial Microenvironment Homeostasis for Stable 1.2 Ah Zinc Pouch Cells
10.1002/aenm.71566.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional additives addressing zinc anode interfac ial instability face inherent trade-offs among surface adsorption, solvation control, and pH buffering. Inspired by the “Goldilocks effect” of the clinical antihypertensive drug lisinopril (LNPL), we propose a biomimetic amphiphilic electrolyte additive strategy to achieve interfacial microenvironment homeostasis. Systematic investigations reveal that long-term zinc stability is governed by a homeostatic balance among multiple competing interfacial regulatory processes, rather than maximizing each individual function independently. At the homeostatic equilibrium achieved with 1 mM, LNPL preferentially adsorbs on the zinc surface to suppress contact with H 2 O and SO 4 2− , adaptively buffers local pH fluctuations through reversible proton exchange, and simultaneously modulates the Zn 2+ solvation environment by reducing coordinated water. Furthermore, LNPL induces a ZnO/ZnS/organic-rich hybrid SEI that suppresses side reactions, homogenizes Zn 2+ flux, and inhibits dendrite growth. Consequently, the Zn||Zn cell exhibits stable cycling for over 6600 h, and the Zn||Cu cell achieves an average coulombic efficiency of 99.85% over 3000 cycles. Meanwhile, the Zn||I 2 full cell achieves over 20 000 cycles with 98.3% capacity retention, while the pouch cell delivers 1.2 Ah with 84.6% retention after 200 cycles. This work establishes a Goldilocks-inspired design principle for multifunctional electrolyte additives in aqueous metal batteries.
authors: Di Wang, Shunyao Li, Menghan Lin, Jun Zheng, Ming Zhang, Wei Xia, Yanli Zhang, Yueying Lin, Zhongrong Shen, Hao Luo

10.1002/aenm.71568.title: Li─P─F─O Bonding Topology Governs Oxygen Redox and Interfacial Stability in High-Rate LRMO-Based All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71568.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-rich manganese-based oxides (LRMO) derive high capacity from lattice-oxygen redox, but oxygen release at high voltage oxidizes solid electrolytes and drives rapid interfacial resistance growth. Nanosizing improves solid-state kinetics yet exposes more under-coordinated surface oxygen, aggravating interfacial degradation. Here, density functional theory screening identifies phosphate as the most effective oxyanion motif for stabilizing surface oxygen. Guided by this insight, a Li─P─F─O bonding topology is constructed through a one-step mechanochemical reaction between LRMO and LiPO 2 F 2 . This process simultaneously refines the particles, introduces near-surface fluorine, and forms a conformal amorphous interphase featuring P─O, P─F, and Li─F bonding environments. P-O coordination stabilizes surface oxygen, delocalizes oxidation holes, and suppresses O─O coupling, while near-surface fluorine widens the Li layers and facilitates Li + transport. Together, these effects suppress oxygen loss, electrolyte oxidation, impedance growth, and interfacial contact failure. The modified cathode delivers 248.5 mAh g −1 at 25°C and 268 mAh g −1 at 60°C (0.1 C), retains 85% capacity after 2000 cycles at 10 C, and operates up to 16 000 cycles. A high-loading lithium-metal pouch cell achieves 212 mAh g −1 with specific energy of 277 Wh kg −1 . This work demonstrates bonding-topology regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox in solid-state batteries.
authors: Ling Huang, Shilin Zhang, Zhongqin Dai, Wenjun Song, Yanming Cui, Shiwei Chen, Jie Zhang, Miaoyi Zhao, Yifei Yuan, Jun Jin, Yan Lu, Zhaoyin Wen

10.1002/aenm.71589.title: Fused Triphenylamine-Terminated Self-Assembled Hole-Transporting Monolayers for Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71589.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional self-assembled hole-transporting monolayers (SAMs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) suffer molecular aggregation, uneven coverage on rough FTO substrates, and insufficient interfacial defect passivation. The design and application of novel SAMs have become an important approach to enhancing device efficiency and stability. Herein, two asymmetric π-extended SAMs, named T-4PACz and FT-4PACz, based on 4PACz skeleton with a triphenylamine terminal, were designed. FT-4PACz, featuring a fused triphenylamine terminal, suppresses aggregation via moderate π-π stacking and adopts a parallel orientation on FTO, enhancing interfacial bonding and shortening carrier transport paths. Its exposed central nitrogen lone-pair electrons strongly coordinate with Pb 2+ , passivating defects and regulating perovskite crystallization into dense, pinhole-free films. Optimized HOMO alignment further reduces the hole-injection barrier. Consequently, the champion inverted PSCs based on FT-4PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.76%, significantly outperforming those based on T-4PACz (25.09%) and 4PACz (24.28%). The devices retain >90% of their initial efficiency after 1020 h at 85 °C in N 2 . This work provides a rational molecular design strategy for high-performance, stable SAMs for PSCs.
authors: Liwen Zhang, Mingyuan Han, Botong Li, Hanqing Yang, Zheng Zou, Shuangwei Lv, Xuepeng Liu, Zhipeng Shao, Zedong Lin, Wenyong Feng, Changqing Lin, Shuzhang Yang, Yanlei Li, Yong Ding

10.1002/aenm.71581.title: Phase-Change Enabled Bilayer Meta-Fabrics for High-Performance Thermal Rectification
10.1002/aenm.71581.abstract: ABSTRACT Adaptive thermal-management materials capable of direction-dependent heat transport are highly desirable for building-envelope and other moderate-temperature applications, yet scalable and flexible thermal rectifiers remain limited. Here, we report a polyester-based phase-change thermal diode meta-fabric (TDMF) fabricated via continuous modified rotary jet spinning (M-RJS), with potential compatibility for textile-scale processing. The TDMF comprises a hot-pressed reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-integrated dense conductive layer (DCL) and an ultra-porous fluffy insulating layer (FIL), coupling structural asymmetry with phase-change-induced thermal nonlinearity. An optimized configuration containing 80 wt.% phase-change material in the DCL achieves a maximum material-level thermal rectification ratio of ∼2.1 at Δ T = 45 K, where PCM-assisted thermal switching becomes pronounced. The rGO-enabled conductive network promotes forward heat transfer and PCM activation, whereas the porous FIL suppresses reverse heat transport through reduced interfacial contact and increased thermal resistance. The meta-fabric also exhibits high flexibility and moisture permeability. A low-temperature orientation test shows a ∼1.9°C surface-temperature difference between opposite bilayer orientations, while building-envelope analogue tests show differences up to ∼2.7°C under controlled irradiation. This work establishes a scalable fibrous platform for directional thermal management, particularly relevant to building-envelope and other moderate-temperature applications using the current PCM formulation design.
authors: Zubair Ashraf, Atif Nazir, Ali Usman, Mulin Qin, Sadia Noreen, Haiwei Han, Kaihang Jia, Akbar Bashir, Waseem Aftab, Yonggang Wang, Zhenghui Shen, Ruqiang Zou

10.1002/aenm.71563.title: Earth-Abundant Oxides Promoting High-Performance Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 Thermoelectrics via a Metathesis Strategy
10.1002/aenm.71563.abstract: ABSTRACT The bright promise of Mg 3 (Sb,Bi) 2 as a next-generation near-room-temperature thermoelectric material is challenged both by the need for reliable and economical synthesis and by performance degradation from detrimental Mg-vacancy defects at grain boundaries and within grains. Here, we reveal that Earth-abundant oxides (Fe 2 O 3 , ZrO 2 and TiO 2 ) can unlock superior thermoelectric performance in Mg 3 (Sb,Bi) 2 via a simple metathesis strategy. Incorporation of the oxides (at only 1-3 mol%) in Mg-excess Mg 3 (Sb,Bi) 2 powders during spark-plasma sintering initiates “Mg-oxide” reduction reactions; the subsequent “transition metal-Mg 3 (Sb,Bi) 2 ” reactions release a source of additional Mg, whose global diffusion refills cationic vacancies in the bulk matrix, enabling markedly enhanced power factors and figures of merit. Our fabricated 8-pair Mg 3 Sb 0.75 Bi 1.25 /MgAgSb device attained remarkable conversion efficiency and output power density of 11.7% and 1.0 W cm −2 at a temperature gradient (Δ T ) of 315 K. Notably, a Mg 3 Sb 0.5 Bi 1.5 /Bi 0.5 Sb 1.5 Te 3 module demonstrated maximum cooling Δ T s competitive with state-of-the-art Bi 2 Te 3 coolers at 200-373 K. The proposed metathesis strategy not only offers an eco-friendly and cost-effective route to defect engineering, promoting applications of Mg 3 (Sb,Bi) 2 TEs, but also provides key insights into the structure-property relationships and thermoelectric performance optimization of other Mg-based TEs and Zintl phases.
