10.1002/aenm.71585.title: A Universal Synthesis of PtPd-Based High-Entropy Sub-Nanoribbons for Oxygen Reduction Electrocatalysis
10.1002/aenm.71585.abstract: ABSTRACT PtPd-based high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with sub-nano-thick ribbon morphology are a class of promising catalysts for electrochemical reactions; however, a lack of a general synthetic method that allows extensive compositional modulation for probing untold catalytic powers. Herein, we report a universal strategy for constructing PtPd-based sub-nanoribbons (SNRs) with tunable alloy elements for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). In this synthetic method, a ligand collection is organized to balance the large differences in redox potentials of multiple metal precursors and enforce ribbon-like anisotropic growth. By diversifying composition, SNRs can be tuned from low-entropy alloys to HEAs. For acidic ORR, the catalytic performance of SNRs improves as entropy increases, wherein the high-entropy PtPdNiFeGa SNRs exhibit optimal catalytic activity and superior stability. Our theoretical investigations suggest that more bonding states are formed in the HEAs, which is conducive to creating new active sites with greater electron accumulation near the Fermi level for low-barrier electron transfer, besides resulting in a denser crystal structure with robust catalytic stability. When equipped in the membrane electrode assembly, the PtPdNiFeGa SNRs deliver a remarkable mass activity (MA = 0.79 A/mg Pt at 0.9 V) and stability (MA retention = 82% after 30 000 cycles), outperforming most of the reported PtPd-based catalysts.
authors: Lu Tao, Hongtian Mi, Jia Shi, Kaiyi Cui, Qiang Gu, Wenjun Dong

10.1002/aenm.71567.title: 3D Printed Ordered Porous Architectures of Functional Metal Tellurides for Ultra High Mass-Loaded Ammonium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71567.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous ammonium-ion (NH 4 + ) batteries (AAIBs) have recently emerged as promising alternatives for next-generation energy storage, owing to the unique hydrogen-bond-assisted diffusion of NH 4 + ions within the host lattice framework. However, research on electrode materials remains limited, and a considerable gap persists between laboratory scale and practical applications due to the low mass loadings (1-5 mg cm −2 ) of conventional electrodes. This work introduces an ultrahigh mass-loading integrated 3D-printed porous conductive electrode of functional metal tellurides, Bi 2-x Sb x Te 3 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1.5) as an efficient anode for AAIBs. To address the limited ion diffusion associated with ultrahigh mass-loading electrodes, Bi 2-x Sb x Te 3 is integrated with a 3D-printed porous titanium alloy (Ti 6 Al 4 V) substrate fabricated via the Selective Laser Melting (SLM) technique. Such an interconnected porous framework provides efficient mass-transport pathways even at very high mass-loading levels. The designed 3D-printed Bi 2 Te 3 anode with a mass loading of 40 mg cm −2 achieves an impressive areal capacity of 9 mAh cm −2 at 2 mA cm −2 , while still retaining an exceptional specific capacity of 224 mAh g −1 . To improve the cyclic stability, smaller Sb 3+ ions are incorporated into the Bi 2 Te 3 lattice to strengthen the M─Te (M═Bi/Sb) bonds, which consequently mitigates volume fluctuations during cycling. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of 3D-printed Bi 2-x Sb x Te 3 anodes for advancing AAIB technology.
authors: Puja De, Petr Lazar, Michal Otyepka, Jakub Mesicek, Jiri Hajnys, Martin Pumera

10.1002/aenm.71586.title: Decoding the Low-Voltage Plateau in Hard Carbon Negative Electrodes: From Sodium-Storage Models to Quantitative Active-Site Design
10.1002/aenm.71586.abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon (HC) is the leading anode candidate for sodium-ion batteries, but its practical optimization remains constrained by an unresolved question: which structural motifs actually store Na + at low potential? Early voltage-profile assignments separated sloping capacity from plateau capacity and attributed them to adsorption, intercalation, or pore filling. However, recent evidence indicates that these assignments are often sample-dependent and may overinterpret individual characterization signatures. This Review re-examines HC anodes from the perspective of site-resolved Na storage. We first compare the evolution of sodium-storage models and clarify what each model explains, where it fails, and why apparently contradictory conclusions have emerged. We then focus on the low-voltage plateau, discussing monolayer Na accumulation, quasi-metallic Na cluster formation, closed-pore filling, and the remaining pore-volume paradox. Particular attention is given to the strengths and limitations of WAXS/XRD, SAXS, XPS, Raman, NMR, titration, and theoretical simulations for assigning Na storage states. Finally, we connect mechanistic understanding to active-site design, including defects, heteroatoms, pores, metal-assisted motifs, and surface functional groups, emphasizing which design rules are established and which remain speculative. HC design must move beyond qualitative structure-performance correlations toward quantitative active-site identification, closed-pore metrology, and full-cell-relevant optimization of plateau capacity, initial Coulombic efficiency, and scalability.
authors: Haoyang Peng, Shuaiqi Wang, Wei-Jing Chen, Hanjian Lai, Long Kong, Xiaodong Lin, Min Jie Wang, Yonghui Deng, Alexandru Vlad, Pan Xu

10.1002/aenm.71587.title: In Situ Reconstructed Cu-Bi Interfacial Sites Enable Cooperative CO 2 and Nitrate Activation for Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis
10.1002/aenm.71587.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical urea synthesis via co-reduction of CO 2 and nitrate (NO 3 − ) offers a sustainable route for C─N bond formation but remains challenged by poor selectivity and competing side reactions. Here, we report a dual-metal interfacial engineering strategy that enables C─N coupling by favoring a key NO─M 1 ─NO─CO─M 2 configuration. Using CuBi 2 O 4 as a model precursor, in situ electroreduction induces reconstruction into an electron-enriched and low-coordinated Cu─Bi interfacial structure. Operando Raman and surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, reveal that these reconstructed dual-metal interfaces enable cooperative adsorption of NO 3 − and CO 2 , favoring a spatially confined NO─Cu─NO─CO─Bi configuration. This proposed configuration lowers the overall activation barrier and converts the traditionally endergonic C─N coupling into an exergonic N─C─N coupling process, thereby redirecting the reaction pathway toward urea formation while suppressing nitrite and CO byproducts. As a result, the catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 32.7% at −0.4 V vs. RHE with a high yield rate of 2955.3 mg h −1 g −1 at −0.6 V vs. RHE under large current densities. This work provides insights into a generalizable interfacial-site design for modulating reaction pathways in electrosynthetic C─N coupling systems.

10.1002/aenm.71642.title: Recyclable Triboelectric Nanogenerators Enabled by Biodegradable Pollen-Paper Nanoarchitectonics for Sustainable Energy Harvesting (Adv. Energy Mater. 40/2026)
authors: Chenchen Zhou, Zihao Guo, Jun Hao Mo, Licong Yang, Hailu Wang, Daru Seto Bagus Anugrah, Munho Kim, Dan Sun, Nam-Joon Cho

10.1002/aenm.71588.title: Solar Salt Thermal Storage Enhancement Through Defect Engineering
10.1002/aenm.71588.abstract: ABSTRACT Molten salts nanofluids-based thermal energy storage systems offer a viable solution for the advancing of concentrated solar power (CSP) systems and grid peak shaving. However, further enhancement of the thermal energy storage performance of molten salts nanofluids is facing a bottleneck. Here, we report a novel defect-engineering method that can overcome this obstacle by incorporating the oxygen vacancy (Vo) into silica nanoparticles dispersed in solar salts. By integrating experiments, DFT-based charge analysis, MD simulations, and techno-economic analysis, solar salt thermal storage enhancement through defect engineering is systematically investigated from microscale to system level. Unlike SiO 2 nanoparticles without V O , V O -engineered SiO 2 nanoparticles induce strong Coulombic interactions with molten salt ions, which can reorganize the molten salt ions into an exceptionally dense and thick compressed layer. This unique structure triples the specific heat capacity enhancement achievable with conventional nanoparticle doping, yielding a maximum increase of 56.6%. Concurrently, the thermal conductivity, dispersibility, and viscosity have also been significantly improved. System-level analysis reveals that these integrated thermophysical enhancements directly reduce the levelized cost of electricity and increase the annual energy generation of CSP system. The established oxygen vacancy engineering provides a novel approach to underpin the potential of molten salts nanofluids-based thermal energy storage.
authors: Chang Ji, Xueming Yang, Qiyang Cui, Xudong Zhang, Jianfei Xie, Bingyang Cao

10.1002/aenm.71582.title: Process-Oriented Interphase Regulation in Lithium Metal Batteries with Non-Aqueous Liquid Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71582.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are promising candidates for high-energy-density energy storage systems. However, their practical applications are severely hindered by interfacial instability and uncontrolled lithium deposition, which lead to dendrite growth, low Coulombic efficiency, and rapid capacity decay. In this review, we systematically analyze interfacial processes in LMBs with non-aqueous liquid electrolytes from a process-oriented perspective. We employ a six-step kinetic framework involving ion transport, desolvation, interphase transport, charge transfer, nucleation, and morphological evolution. We first discuss the fundamental structure and dynamic evolution of electrode-electrolyte interphases, followed by an overview of advanced characterization techniques across multiple length and time scales. Furthermore, recent strategies for regulating interfacial stability are critically summarized, including electrolyte additives, artificial protective layers, and solvation regulation designs. Instead of categorizing these strategies solely by materials, we emphasize their roles in regulating key kinetic steps and clarify the underlying mechanisms within the six-step process. Finally, we highlight current challenges and future directions toward practical LMBs, including full-cell and pouch-cell validation, high energy density, cost reduction, and manufacturing compatibility. This work aims to provide a unified framework for understanding, characterizing, and regulating interfacial stability in lithium metal batteries.

10.1002/aenm.71583.title: Copper-Governed Divergence of Lithium Deposition Modes in Anode-Free Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71583.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) maximize energy density by eliminating anode host materials, but their lifetime is governed by Li deposition on the current collector (CC)-a heterogeneous nucleation and growth process. Current research mainly focuses on electrolyte or artificial interphase engineering, whereas how the CC's physical structure dictates initial deposition behavior remains unclear. Here, we show that the microstructure of Cu foils induces two distinct Li deposition modes: localized nucleation-selective growth (LS) and distributed nucleation-competitive coalescence (DCC). Using HLCu and nmCu as model interfaces, we elucidate the evolution pathways of these modes. By integrating AFM, iSCAT, ToF-SIMS and operando EIS-DRT, we reveal mode-specific differences in nucleation sites, interfacial kinetics, and the coupling between morphology, mechanical response, and side reactions. The LS mode generates loose, non-uniform Li deposits with strong gas evolution, whereas the DCC mode enables dense, continuous, and kinetically stable Li layers. This work demonstrates that the CC is not a passive substrate but a critical component that determines the deposition mode and performance degradation. Optimizing the physical structure of the CC interface offers a key strategy-beyond electrolyte and interphase design-for long-life AFLMBs.
authors: Sida Huo, Li Wang, Yue Wang, Yihui Bai, Meng Li, Ming Fang, Jingyi Qiu, Shuaiguo Yang, Wendong Xue, Xiangming He

10.1002/aenm.71572.title: Generalizable Mechanism-Anchored Health Management for Lithium-Ion Batteries Across Complex Degradation Trajectories
10.1002/aenm.71572.abstract: ABSTRACT Complex degradation trajectories compromise the lifetime reliability and operational safety of lithium-ion batteries in advanced energy-storage systems. Aging pathways induced by temperature, rate, and voltage-abuse stresses are often entangled in conventional health-estimation models, limiting transferable degradation representation and future-trajectory updating under distribution shifts. Here, a generalizable, mechanism-anchored health-management framework is developed for lithium-ion batteries under heterogeneous aging conditions. Using aging-condition identification as a proxy task, we identify a degradation-sensitive 3.3-3.4 V charging window in LiFePO 4 /graphite cells, where statistically selected features are linked to incremental-capacity fingerprints. These electrochemically anchored features are integrated with a condition-aware soft mixture-of-experts model to disentangle heterogeneous feature-state-of-health (SOH) relationships with and without condition labels during inference. Cross-dataset continual learning enables adaptation to an unseen data source while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Finally, data-driven SOH observations are assimilated into a physics-inspired parametric degradation model through an adaptive unscented Kalman filter, converting pointwise health estimates into online-updatable degradation trajectories. The framework achieves robust SOH estimation across multi-stress aging conditions and stable 100-300-step look-ahead trajectory prediction, establishing an interpretable route from electrochemical fingerprints to trajectory-level battery prognostics.
authors: Yuanzhe Tao, Yonggang Hu, Zhifeng He, Meifang Ding, Yufan Peng, Shijun Tang, Huiyan Zhang, Ke Zhang, Ying Lin, Wenhao Wu, Yanting Jin, Wenhua Zuo, Jinding Liang, Zhengliang Gong, Yiming Wei, Yong Yang

10.1002/aenm.71590.title: All-In-One Sensing Supercapacitor With Shared Configuration and Decoupled Performance
10.1002/aenm.71590.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrated energy-storage sensing devices promote greatly the miniaturization and integration of wearable electronic devices. However, they still face long-lasting challenges of tailored semi-integrated configuration or highly-coupled sensing and energy storage functions. Herein, an unprecedented all-in-one sensing supercapacitor (ASS) is proposed for independent and synchronous strain sensing and self-powering. The ASS features a shared configuration, endows it with several key features, including reversible changes of ion-transport paths and resistance in porous electrolyte, robust electron transport in the dense electrode, and stable interface resistance in the chain-entangled interfaces. These guarantee reliable sensing and charge-discharge processes under compression. Consequently, the ASS exhibits satisfactory electrochemical performance, including low interface-resistance, high areal-capacitance (37.9 mF cm −2 ), and good stability (98.8% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles), which can be well maintained under wide compressive strains of 0%∼80% and 5000 cyclic compression-release. Furthermore, good sensing characteristics are also achieved with wide detection ranges up to 80% compressive strain and superior durability (>7000 cycles). The ASS also shows minimal mutual interference in synchronous sensing-powering mode over harsh conditions, highlighting its great multi-scenario applications. These findings open up a new perspective for highly efficient all-in-one energy-storage sensing devices toward practical wearable applications.
authors: Weiqian Feng, Zhiyin Lin, Zeyu Jiang, Jingbo Xie, Qijun Tan, Yueyue Zhen, Liyong Tian, Ningbo Yi, Yancheng Wu, Feng Gan, Yangfan Zhang, Xiaosong Zhou, Xuliang Fan, Zhi Chang

10.1002/aenm.71575.title: Monolithic Host-Separator Continuum Decouples Polyiodide Confinement and Reversibility in Lithium-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71575.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-iodine batteries are hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect, where conventional mitigation strategies face a fundamental trade-off between active material confinement and redox reversibility. Herein, we report a monolithic host-separator continuum that address this dilemma through spatially organized compartmentalization. The architecture integrates an oxidized sulfonated lignin-functionalized graphene aerogel (GA@SOL) core with an encapsulating sulfonated cellulose polymer (SCP) shell via sequential infiltration and freeze-drying, minimizing the interfacial discontinuities inherent in stacked configurations. Within the conductive scaffold, iodine adsorption spontaneously generates a mixed-valence iodine species (I − /I 2 /I 3 − ) via balanced Lewis acid-base interactions, establishing a redox-active environment that preserves electronic connectivity without compromising reaction kinetics. Concurrently, the sulfonate-rich SCP shell establishes an electrostatic Donnan barrier that selectively repels polyiodide anions while facilitating Li + transport. The resulting GA@SOL-I 2 @SCP cathode delivers 252 mAh g −1 at 1 C with 89.6% retention over 1500 cycles, a Li + transference number of 0.63, and mitigated self-discharge (76.1% capacity retention after 120 h). Operando spectroscopy and in situ impedance monitoring confirm sustained polyiodide accessibility and suppressed anode corrosion. This work demonstrates that structural continuity and mixed-valence-enabled charge transport can decouple confinement from kinetic penalty, offering a design framework for conversion-type energy storage systems plagued by soluble intermediates.
authors: Changyong Song, Yanfu Tong, Shaofen Bai, Xun Dong, Jixian Cao, Congyue Sun, Pengyun Liu, Xiaoning Wang, Qingzhong Xue, Wei Xing, Xuejin Li, Zifeng Yan

10.1002/aenm.71555.title: Competing Charge Separation Pathways Govern Charge Generation in Organic Photovoltaic Blends: Insights From Transient Electron Spin Resonance
10.1002/aenm.71555.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding charge generation in organic photovoltaics remains a central challenge despite recent efficiency gains. Here, competing charge separation pathways in donor:acceptor blends are identified by directly probing photoinduced spin states using transient electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy, enabling distinction between charge-transfer states and separated charges. The results reveal that, across fullerene and non-fullerene acceptor blends, charge generation proceeds via two pathways: a fast pathway forming separated charges on timescales faster than spin mixing, and a slower pathway mediated by spin-polarized interfacial charge-transfer (CT) states. Modeling of the time-dependent evolution of spin polarization across blends and temperatures quantifies the relative contributions of these charge separation pathways and resolves subsequent charge dynamics, governed by a balance of dissociation, re-encounter, and spin-selective recombination via CT states. Analysis of CT-state ESR spectra provides a link between charge separation dynamics and morphology by identifying interfacial donor:acceptor geometries associated with the slower charge separation pathway. The results show that higher-performing blends, particularly PM6:Y6, are characterized by dominance of the faster charge separation pathway and dynamic interconversion between CT states and separated charges. These findings emphasize the importance of balancing fast charge separation with efficient re-dissociation of CT states for achieving high performance in organic photovoltaic materials.
authors: Jack M. S. Palmer, Claudia E. Tait

10.1002/aenm.71578.title: Self-Sustaining Water-Electricity Co-Supply Via a Wirtz-Pump-Driven Triboelectric Nanogenerator
10.1002/aenm.71578.abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneously securing clean water and reliable electricity remains a formidable global challenge, particularly in infrastructure-deficient off-grid regions. However, existing co-supply strategies are hindered by decoupled operating mechanisms and limited energy density. Here, we present a Wirtz-pump-driven triboelectric nanogenerator (WP-TENG) that enables both water conveyance and electricity generation within a self-sustaining platform. Powered by ambient water flow, the Wirtz pump leverages the air-lock effect to lift fluid as segmented liquid columns, thereby inducing periodic liquid-solid triboelectrification along the pipe wall. Crucially, the electrical output is boosted due to the dynamic evolution of the interfacial electric double layers within the inner-outer electrode configuration. Through systematic parameter optimization and modular integration, the WP-TENG achieves a volumetric flow rate of 200 mL·min −1 and a hydraulic head of 0.82 m, while delivering peak outputs of 920 V and 940 µA, exceeding those of reported liquid-solid TENGs under comparable conditions. Moreover, the platform powers an electrochemical disinfection module, enabling sustained 5-log microbial inactivation within 10 min during prolonged operation. This work establishes a self-sustaining platform for decentralized water-electricity co-supply and offers a scalable route toward water-energy resilience in resource-constrained environments.
authors: Hengfei Zhang, Ying Zhang, Yichen Zhang, Hui Ding, Dan Tan, Zhuoyang Lu, Xiangyang Liu, Zhiming Lin, Maogang He, Zhong Lin Wang

10.1002/aenm.71558.title: Biodegradable and Closed-Loop Recyclable Hyaluronic Acid/Alginate Gel Electrolyte for Ultra-Durable Zinc-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71558.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogel electrolytes are promising candidates for flexible energy storage, yet most rely on petroleum-derived polymers, raising significant sustainability and environmental concerns. Herein, we report a bio-based, biodegradable, and closed-loop recyclable hyaluronic acid (HA)/sodium alginate (SA) hydrogel electrolyte with zinc sulfate (denoted as ZHS) for zinc-iodine batteries. Leveraging abundant hydrophilic groups (─OH, ─CONH─, and ─COOH) in these natural polysaccharides, ZHS simultaneously addresses the environmental burden of synthetic gels and the electrochemical challenges of Zn-I 2 batteries. Competitive hydrogen bonding between HA/SA and H 2 O molecules, coupled with dynamic water redistribution along polymer chains, yields a uniform and robust dual-network architecture. This network provides homogeneous pathways for rapid Zn 2+ transport and suppresses dendrite nucleation, while abundant polar adsorption sites immobilize polyiodides (I 3 − and I 5 − ) through ion-dipole interactions, alleviating shuttle effects. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2,600 h, and Zn||I 2 full cells achieve remarkable durability exceeding 35,000 cycles. Notably, the ZHS hydrogel demonstrates excellent biocompatibility and can be readily biodegraded under ambient conditions. Furthermore, cycled ZHS can be regenerated through simple aqueous dissolution and re-casting, supporting stable operation for an additional 21,000 cycles. This work pioneers a sustainable pathway toward environmentally benign, high-performance gel electrolytes for zinc-iodine batteries.
authors: Jiahao Li, Yifan Peng, Xi Liu, Xincang Yu, Ziying Lin, Boyin Hu, Meng Xu, Tianxu Cai, Tianyi Zhang, Peng Wen, Yongbiao Mu, Jing Li

10.1002/aenm.71594.title: Recent Progress Toward Practical Aqueous Zn-I2 Batteries: From Lab to Practical
10.1002/aenm.71594.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-iodine (Zn-I 2 ) batteries are considered promising energy storage systems due to their low cost, high theoretical energy density, intrinsic safety and strong environmental adaptability. However, their practical application remains hindered by several challenges. At the I 2 cathode, soluble polyiodides are readily generated during charge and discharge, leading to severe shuttle effects, active material loss and self-discharge. At the Zn anode, dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, corrosion and by-product formation compromise coulombic efficiency and cycling stability. Moreover, these challenges are intensified under high I 2 loading and in pouch cell configurations. Accordingly, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in physical confinement, chemical adsorption, supramolecular regulation, catalytic conversion, interfacial engineering and electrolyte engineering to address the associated limitations. On this basis, particular attention is devoted to the practical energy density and the underlying degradation mechanisms of aqueous Zn-I 2 batteries under high iodine loading and pouch cell conditions, aiming to provide guidance for the rational design and practical application of durable aqueous Zn-I 2 batteries with high energy density.
authors: Wenjing Li, Yang-Feng Cui, Haobin Song, Mingyue Wang, Han Sheng Wong, Cong Huang, Nan Zhao, Caiyan Yu, Dong Yan, Hui Ying Yang

10.1002/aenm.71592.title: Beyond Oxygen Evolution: Anodic High-Value Conversion for Energy-Saving Hydrogen and Chemical Co-Production
10.1002/aenm.71592.abstract: ABSTRACT Water electrolysis offers a scalable route to green hydrogen, but its anodic half-reaction is still constrained by the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a sluggish four-electron process that consumes voltage while yielding low-value O 2 . Anodic high-value conversion (AHVC) replaces this value-losing step with product-forming oxidation, enabling hydrogen evolution to be coupled with upgrading of oxygenated organics, nitrogen-containing molecules, pollutants, and polymer or waste-derived streams. Yet the promise of AHVC is not established by lower oxidation potential alone. Useful co-production requires selective bond transformation, suppression of overoxidation and OER re-entry, controlled intermediate fate, limited crossover, and recoverable product streams at relevant current densities. This Review develops a value-retention framework for AHVC. We discuss the thermodynamic and kinetic origins of alternative anodic reactions, compare major substrate families and their product windows, and examine how working phases, interfacial adsorption, reactive oxygen species, and local microenvironments steer molecular pathways. Device translation is then considered through full-cell metrics, membrane transport, product recovery, durability, and techno-economic boundaries. By connecting molecular selectivity with electrolyzer operation, AHVC is framed as a route to energy-saving hydrogen and value-added chemical co-production, rather than a simple OER substitute.
authors: Lingbin Xie, Jiali Du, Yanzhou Jin, Longlu Wang, Shujuan Liu, Qiang Zhao

10.1002/aenm.71554.title: Multi-modal Operando Analysis of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries: A Comparative Study on the Influence of Electrolyte Composition
10.1002/aenm.71554.abstract: ABSTRACT The effect of electrolytes on battery cell performance is multifaceted, and it is difficult to isolate their impact on individual processes. Operando analysis of batteries is a powerful tool to investigate battery degradation mechanisms. By combining different techniques on the same cell a wider perspective can be opened and enables easier cross-correlation. Here, we introduce a fully laboratory-based multimodal operando platform that synchronizes EIS/DRT, Raman spectroscopy, UV-vis reflectance spectroscopy, temperature monitoring, and galvanostatic cycling in one sealed Li-S cell. The platform is demonstrated over an extended observation window of up to 20 cycles to compare electrolyte-dependent polysulfide speciation, transport limitations, and resistance evolution. The experimental design is optimized for reproducible mechanistic characterization and is not intended as a benchmark of practical cell performance or long-term cycle life.
authors: Oliver Löhmann, Pouya Partovi-Azar, Mirco Ruttert, Sebastian Risse

10.1002/aenm.71591.title: Kinetic Isotope Effects in CO2 Reduction: Insights Into Reaction Mechanisms
10.1002/aenm.71591.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical and photochemical carbon dioxide reduction reactions (CO 2 RR) represent pivotal strategies for converting CO 2 into valuable chemicals, yet their multistep pathways and transient intermediates complicate the identification of the rate-determining step (RDS). Kinetic isotope effects (KIEs) provide bond-sensitive evidence by revealing how isotopic substitution changes reaction rates. This Perspective critically examines the application of KIEs to investigate CO 2 activation, C─H bond formation, C─C coupling, water activation, and interfacial hydrogen transfer. Across these processes, normal, inverse, and near-unity KIEs, when combined with spectroscopy and theoretical calculations, help distinguish competing elementary steps and reaction pathways. Isotope-dependent product abundances further differentiate Langmuir-Hinshelwood and Eley-Rideal hydrogen transfer pathways and reveal how catalyst structure and interfacial environments regulate reaction pathways and selectivity. Finally, we discuss advances in isotope-resolved operando detection, broader application of isotope analysis, and closer integration with theoretical calculations as opportunities to strengthen mechanistic analysis of CO 2 RR.
authors: Xuemei Diao, Yiyang Li, Xiaowei Zhang, Xiubing Huang, Peng Wang

10.1002/aenm.71570.title: Cross-Scale Orchestration of Sublayer Axially N-Bridged Fe Single Atoms Within Diffusion-Oriented Matrix for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
10.1002/aenm.71570.abstract: ABSTRACT Symmetry perturbation of planar FeN 4 moieties in Fe─N─C single-atom catalysts holds great promise for elevating oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, yet atomically precise coordination engineering of thermodynamically stable configurations with efficient O 2 mass-transport integration remains challenging. Herein, a nitrogen-mediated thermal activation strategy is proposed to construct a sublayer-engineered Fe-N 5 single-atom catalyst, termed FeN 5 -ANDCL, featuring an axially N-bridged dual-carbon-layer architecture integrated into a hollow carbon framework. The elaborately engineered FeN 5 -ANDCL enables cross-scale structural orchestration, wherein the atomic-scale axial N-bridged sublayer steers cross-layer charge transfer and triggers Fe d z 2 -O 2 p orbitals rehybridization, thereby elevating electron occupancy of antibonding states to weaken *OH adsorption, while the hollow carbon framework ameliorates O 2 diffusion resistance and streamlines transport pathways to achieve efficient mass-transport. The unique configuration endows FeN 5 -ANDCL with exceptional ORR activity, attaining a high half-wave potential of 0.927 V vs. RHE in alkaline media. When deployed in zinc-air batteries, it delivers a peak power density of 307.3 mW cm −2 and remarkable cycling stability sustained for 1400 h. Collectively, this work establishes sublayer engineering for precise coordination regulation of single-atom catalysts and demonstrates a cross-scale orchestration principle that couples local electronic-structure optimization with macroscopic transport regulation for efficient electrocatalysis.
authors: Jingshuai Li, Yongsheng Xu, Pengcheng Zhao, Liu Yang, Zhongwei Chen

10.1002/aenm.71576.title: Mechanically Robust Sulfide Electrolyte Membrane Featuring In Situ Dendrite Depletion for High-Stability All-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71576.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite their high ionic conductivities, sulfide solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) must reconcile ionic conductivity with mechanical integrity for ultrathin membrane fabrication when integrated into all-solid-state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs). This study reports a controllable 30 µm sandwich-structured sulfide SSE membrane, fabricated by hot-calendaring two Li 5.3 PS 4.3 ClBr 0.7 (LPSClBr) membranes with a poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) electrospun scaffold embedded with KH-792-modified Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 (LATP@KH) nanoparticles. PVDF-HFP network accommodates electrode volume changes, while LATP@KH nanofillers serve as fast-ion-conducting bridges and fill grain boundaries to suppress lithium nucleation. First-principles calculations reveal LATP's high density of states at Fermi level (57.10), enabling a Ti 4+ /Ti 3+ redox reaction that in situ depletes infiltrating dendrites. The membrane achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.75 mS cm −1 and a critical current density of 1.0 mA cm −2 . Li symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2000 h at 0.2 mA cm −2 . LiIn||NCM811 full cells deliver 166.15 mAh g −1 at 0.2C (99.8% retention after 300 cycles) and exhibit negligible decay over 1000 cycles at 1C with ∼100% Coulombic efficiency. This work establishes a fast-ion-conductor-modified polymer-fiber composite architecture for mechanical reinforcement, in situ dendrite depletion and fast ion transport, offering a key design strategy for reliable ASSLMBs.
authors: Yongtao Zhao, Rong Hao, Jianwei Qiu, Qianqian Fu, Jiaxuan Feng, Ning Liu, Pengchao Si

10.1002/aenm.71574.title: Rigid Symmetric Aromatic Dithiourea Passivation with Strong Intrinsic Dipole for 21.72%-Efficient SnO2-Based Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71574.abstract: ABSTRACT CsPbI 3-x Br x inorganic perovskite solar cells (IPSCs) exhibit excellent intrinsic thermal stability and optoelectronic properties, showing great potential for tandem and space photovoltaics. Nevertheless, iodide oxidation and migration induce undercoordinated Pb 2 + defects that act as non-radiative recombination centers and deteriorate device performance. Herein, we rationally designed a rigid symmetric aromatic molecule, N,N''-1,4-phenylene bisthiourea (1,4-PBTU), as an effective top-surface passivator. Its strong intrinsic dipole stabilizes iodide ions against oxidation, while hydrogen bonding suppresses iodide migration. Dual thiourea moieties offer four coordination sites for robust multidentate chelation with undercoordinated Pb 2 + , greatly lowering defect density. The rigid backbone inhibits molecular migration and desorption for long-term passivation. Furthermore, hydrophobic phenyl skeletons coupled with bisthiourea redox centers realize dual-mode protection of the perovskite via physical isolation and chemical reduction. Consequently, the optimized SnO 2 -based CsPbI 3-x Br x IPSCs deliver a champion efficiency of 21.72%, the highest value among SnO 2 -based counterparts to date. Unencapsulated devices retain over 95% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under N 2 , and still maintain above 90% after 800 h at 65°C. Impressively, 1,4-PBTU also exhibits superior performance to traditional organic ammonium passivators. This work offers a universal guideline for designing rigid conjugated polydentate passivators with strong intrinsic dipoles.
authors: Hongjun Wu, Xiuhua Chen, Min Cui, Simin Ma, Yuanyuan Gai, Hang Yang, Yachao Du, Zongdeng Wu, Chen Li, Shaoyuan Li, Wenhui Ma, Wenhua Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71557.title: Dual-Functional Organic Molecular Layers for Decoupled Interface Engineering Enabling 50 000-Cycle Aqueous Zinc-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71557.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (ZIBs) are promising for grid-scale energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety and high theoretical capacity. However, their development is hindered by the coupled degradation at both electrodes: uncontrollable zinc dendrites growth at the Zn anode and polyiodide shuttling at the iodine cathode. Herein, we develop a decoupled interface engineering strategy based on a low-cost organic molecule, 2,5-di-tert-butylhydroquinone (DBHQ), which exhibits potential-coordinated functionality. At the anode side during charging, the DBHQ layer creates a hydrophobic yet zincophilic interface to guide uniform Zn deposition and suppress hydrogen evolution, enabling a Zn//Zn cell to stably cycle for 6500 h at 1 mAh cm −2 . During discharging at the cathode side, such a layer acts as an efficient polyiodide trapper via strong physical adsorption. The synergistic effect in the DBHQ@Zn//DBHQ@I 2 full cell achieves an exceptional cycling stability of 50 000 cycles with 90.89% capacity retention at 4 A g −1 , and an areal capacity of 2.74 mAh cm −2 for the pouch cell at a low negative-to-positive (N/P) ratio of 4.04. This work establishes dual-functional molecular layers as a versatile platform for stabilizing complex electrode interfaces, offering a new paradigm for addressing interdependent failure mechanisms in aqueous batteries.
authors: Weijun Zhou, Kejie Bao, Hongli Chen, Xingdong Ding, Ming Yang, Minfeng Chen, Dingtao Ma, Limin Lu

10.1002/aenm.71556.title: Composite Polymer Electrolytes With Hierarchical Confinement of Anions and Solvents for Stable Solid-State Li Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71556.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state lithium-metal batteries leveraging solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) represent a promising technological pathway. Among these, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based SPEs are particularly noteworthy, yet they face a fundamental dilemma: electrode/electrolyte interfacial degradation from solvent-dominated Li + coordination versus constrained Li + transport under solvent-deficient conditions. To resolve this paradox, a 3D porous few-layered MoS 2 was synthesized and employed as the filler in PVDF-based SPEs. The fillers concurrently weaken Li + coordination with both FSI − and solvent through targeted dipole interactions, thereby enhancing Li + migration rate and inducing structural reorganization to anion-dominated Li + solvation. The optimized PVDF-based electrolyte demonstrates record-breaking ionic conductivity (1.13 mS cm −1 ), Li + transference number (0.68), and exceptional compatibility with lithium metal anodes under solvent-lean conditions. The LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||Li cell demonstrates exceptional cycling stability, achieving a record-high capacity retention of 90.5% after 1500 cycles at 2 C. Furthermore, practical applicability is confirmed through a 54 mAh pouch cell configuration. The ultra-stable interfacial characteristics establish new performance benchmarks, demonstrating a viable pathway toward practical solid-state batteries with minimal solvent dependence.
authors: Dengfeng Yu, Haocheng Yuan, Peipei Ding, Yue Li, Qian Wu, Hongcai He, Yaoyu Ren, Ce-Wen Nan

10.1002/aenm.71584.title: Chemical Bonding Interface Enables Lithium Batteries to Operate Under Near-Vacuum Conditions
10.1002/aenm.71584.abstract: ABSTRACT The reliance on high stack pressure in lithium metal batteries (LMBs) conflicts with the requirements of lightweight design and low-pressure operating environments, motivating the development of pressure-independent battery designs. Here, a chemical bonding interfacial prototype is proposed to substitute the physical contact interface, thereby liberating LMBs from high stacking pressures. This chemical bonding interface is constructed via strong interactions between the carbonyl groups of poly(ε-caprolactone) segments and Li metal, manifesting as Li─O bonding interfaces. Benefiting from Li─O bonding, the PPE electrolyte exhibits a high adhesion energy of 22.44 J m −2 and a high lap shear strength of 0.31 MPa, sustaining intimate electrode-electrolyte contact without external stack pressure. In addition, the Li─O bonding interface significantly reduces the thickness of the electric double layer, achieving a 120% increase in capacitance (0.20 µF cm −2 ), thus promoting efficient transport (t Li+ = 0.7) and uniform deposition of Li + . As a result, the Li||Cu half-cell equipped with PPE electrolyte achieves a superior coulombic efficiency of 99.78%. A pouch cell equipped with PPE electrolyte and NCM cathode demonstrates high capacity retention of 90.12% after 40 cycles at −0.1 MPa (relative to standard atmospheric pressure). This discovery offers novel insights into material and structural design for pressure-insensitive batteries intended for high-altitude aerospace applications.
authors: Rongrong Guo, Songmei Li, Xiaoyun Xu, Wenqiang Zhang, Yixin Luo, Jinyan Zhong, Jingyi Qiu, Shubin Yang, Bin Li, Xiangbiao Liao

10.1002/aenm.71517.title: Recyclable Triboelectric Nanogenerators Enabled by Biodegradable Pollen-Paper Nanoarchitectonics for Sustainable Energy Harvesting
10.1002/aenm.71517.abstract: ABSTRACT Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising devices for harvesting ambient mechanical energy, however, their development is hindered by low power output, limited energy conversion efficiency, and reliance on synthetic polymers. Here, we report a pollen-based recyclable TENG (PRTENG) achieving a power density of 5.07 W m −2 , rivaling synthetic polymeric TENGs. The seamless integration of bleached pollen paper with PEDOT:PSS and poly(vinyl alcohol) via strong hydrogen-bonding networks exhibits a 21% increase in maximum stress and 82-fold toughness enhancement alongside robust durability of over 100 000 contact-separation cycles. Moreover, when integrated into footwear, the PRTENG effectively converts human motion into electrical energy. Critically, water-assisted disassembly enables complete component recovery for reassembly with negligible performance loss, while the recovered substrates can biodegrade within 12 days. Overall, this study provides a sustainable approach to engineer fully flexible, recyclable, and eco-friendly TENGs for deployment in wearable electronics, decentralized sensing networks, and next-generation sustainable IoT infrastructures.
authors: Chenchen Zhou, Zihao Guo, Jun Hao Mo, Licong Yang, Hailu Wang, Daru Seto Bagus Anugrah, Munho Kim, Dan Sun, Nam-Joon Cho

10.1002/aenm.71706.title: Dynamic Hydrogen-Bond Network Accelerates Lattice Oxygen Regeneration for High-Current-Density Seawater Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71706.abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis for green H 2 production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH − at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release-regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade-off between activity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that yttrium (Y) and carboxylate co-doping reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network of NiFe oxyhydroxide, dynamically accelerating OH − delivery and enabling rapid regeneration of lattice oxygen. This catalyst maintains a high LOM contribution (51.7%-54%) while achieving exceptional durability and Cl − resistance. In situ Raman, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) analyses confirm rapid peroxide intermediate formation, lattice oxygen participation, and negligible chlorine evolution. The anion-exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer delivers 1000 mA cm −2 at 1.79 V and operates stably for 800 h in alkaline seawater. This work establishes interfacial hydrogen-bonding engineering as a generalizable strategy to break the activity-stability trade-off for robust seawater electrolysis.
authors: Wanli Bao, Sijia Xin, Anqiang Deng, Yongtao Tan, Hailong Wang, Ning Yan, Xiaoyu Yan

10.1002/aenm.71778.title: Solvent-Free Metal-Organic Framework-Based Porous Liquid Electrolyte for Ultrahigh-Temperature (180°C) Zn Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71778.abstract: ABSTRACT Zn metal batteries capable of withstanding ultrahigh temperatures are urgently needed across diverse fields, yet their development is hindered by the poor thermal adaptability of conventional electrolytes. Herein, we develop an innovative electrolyte paradigm represented by a metal-organic framework (MOF)-based porous liquid electrolyte (PLE) without active organic or H 2 O solvents, which enables long-term operation of Zn metal batteries at 180°C for the first time. Modeled on UiO-66, PLE combines permanent microporosity with liquid fluidity, offering non-flammability, thermal stability, and anode compatibility. The permanent micropores of the UiO-66 skeleton provide ordered nanoconfined ion transport channels, while flexible grafted polymeric chains offer coordination-dissociation hopping sites, and ultimately suppress dendrite growth even at high temperatures. Zn||Zn symmetric cells deliver ultra-long cycling lifespans of 10 000 h at 25°C, 4000 h at 120°C, 2100 h at 150°C, and 600 h at 180°C, far surpassing state-of-the-art Zn battery electrolytes. Zn||V 2 O 5 batteries deliver stable performance across 25−180°C. Moreover, the pore structure of PLE effectively adsorbs polyiodides and polysulfides, enabling high-temperature Zn||I 2 batteries and, remarkably, extending to Li||S (80°C) and Li||V 2 O 5 batteries (180°C). This work enriches the design philosophy of functional electrolytes and breaks the long-standing temperature barrier of metal batteries.
authors: Chunkun Song, Yaodong Huo, Duanduan Li, Yongqi Wang, Qiyue Zhao, Tuotuo Ma, Xiaojun Gu, Yuliang Gao

10.1002/aenm.71732.title: Machine Learning-Driven Vapor Passivation Enables Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71732.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution-based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor-based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor-assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial-and-error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first-principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor-assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation- π interaction between Pb 2+ and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data-driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor-assisted passivation materials.
authors: Yu Su, Kongxiang Wang, Wenru Lv, Zhongtao Duan, Hong Liu, Yaqing Li, Xiang Li, Qi Huang, Ziyang Song, Hong Zhang, Jian Mao, Junhao Chu, Fengxian Xie

10.1002/aenm.71747.title: Sustainable Biomass-Based Fiber Materials as Structural and Functional Scaffolds for Advanced Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71747.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass-based fiber materials, including cellulose, chitosan, bacterial cellulose, and their derivatives, have emerged as a distinctive class of structural and functional scaffolds, effectively bridging renewable materials chemistry with advanced energy storage technologies. This review systematically elucidates their hierarchical structural characteristics, classifications, and the intrinsic structural-function-application relationships that underpin their versatility. Furthermore, the critical roles of these materials as key components-including solid-state/liquid electrolytes, separators, electrodes, and binders-in various metal battery systems, particularly lithium- and zinc-based batteries, are comprehensively summarized. The discussion further highlights how the rational architectural design of biomass-derived fibrous materials can significantly enhance ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, and mechanical integrity. By improving these fundamental properties, such materials provide effective strategies for addressing major challenges, including dendrite formation and cycling instability. Finally, the current challenges and future research perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on precise molecular-level design, scalable fabrication technologies, and standardized evaluation protocols, all of which are essential for advancing the development of next-generation green and sustainable energy storage devices.
authors: Yifei Yan, Ziqing Ruan, Shukai Wu, Leixin Yang, Hongyao Wang, Nuo Xu, Jingwen Gao, Long Jiao, Yaping Kong, Yun Zheng, Jiujun Zhang, Bowen Cheng

10.1002/aenm.71753.title: Mixed-Antisolvent Engineering for Crystallization and Defect Regulation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71753.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains critically dependent on the quality of the perovskite absorber, which is largely established during the antisolvent-assisted crystallization process. Single-antisolvent engineering, however, is often constrained by the fixed physicochemical properties of the chosen solvent, leaving limited flexibility to balance solvent extraction, crystallization modulation, and defect suppression. Herein, we report a physicochemical-property-assisted binary-antisolvent engineering for high-efficiency inverted PSCs. A series of binary antisolvent combinations were screened by considering key solvent properties, among which the carbon disulfide/anisole (CS 2 :ANI) system delivered the best device performance. Comprehensive chemical, structural, and optical characterizations reveal that the CS 2 :ANI system enables a more coordinated crystallization process by regulating solvent removal and modifying the precursor environment through interactions between CS 2 -derived C═N-containing species and the Pb-I framework. The resulting perovskite films exhibit compact morphology, reduced residual stress, and suppressed defect-assisted nonradiative recombination. The optimized inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.73% and a steady-state output efficiency of 26.43%.
authors: Feiyang Lei, Xinyi Mei, Zhuang Xie, Qiuyan Cao, Dexin Zhang, Minghui Cheng, Xinhong Zhu, Dong Zhang, Yuwei Duan, Qiang Peng

10.1002/aenm.71765.title: Diagnosing the Role of Mn Additives in Aqueous Zn/MnO2 Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71765.abstract: ABSTRACT Manganese dioxides are pervasive as cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries; however, their energy storage mechanism has proven to be complex. Increasing evidence suggests that Mn dissolution contributes to cathode capacity via a reversible dissolution-redeposition process, in addition to capacity from Zn 2+ /H + (de)intercalation. Understanding the role played by Mn 2+ in the electrolyte, particularly when introduced as an electrolyte additive, is important for diagnosing cathode degradation. Using operando X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, we track Mn 2+ in operating cells to gain insights into the complexity of the MnO 2 cathode. While some suppression of cathode dissolution by the additive cannot be excluded, our measurements suggest that Mn 2+ electrolyte additives improve cycling performance by supplying extra redox-active Mn during charge, rather than solely by suppressing Mn dissolution, thereby compensating for cathode degradation. Benefiting from operando XRF, we propose that a potential contributor to capacity fading is the incomplete dissolution of the MnO 2 cathode and incomplete redeposition of Mn 2+ from the electrolyte, and that this fading does not appear to be mitigated by using Mn 2+ additives. These findings underscore the necessity of directly tracking Mn 2+ evolution, and that improving reversibility requires addressing both the dissolution of MnO 2 and the redeposition of Mn 2+ .
authors: Zixuan Li, Katarzyna Sowa, Tomasz Kołodziej, Yi Yuan, Hewen Chen, Lijiang Song, Pawel Wróbel, Didier Wermeille, Paul Thompson, Paweł Korecki, Peter G. Bruce, Alex W. Robertson

10.1002/aenm.71783.title: High-Density Energy Storage in Si-Integrated Dielectric Multilayers Through Interfacial Polarization and ML-Guided Structural Optimization
10.1002/aenm.71783.abstract: ABSTRACT Epitaxial dielectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for better energy storage performance than bulks and polymers, yet their reported recoverable energy density ( W rec ) commonly excludes the substrate, which limits its relevance to practical device-level energy storage. Here, we develop a Si-integrated BZT//S-BZT multilayer capacitor to address this issue and simultaneously enhance polarization and breakdown strength ( E b ). By directly integrating the oxide multilayer on Si-based substrates, the contribution of the substrate to the effective device volume is substantially reduced, enabling a realistic energy density ( W rec-real ) of 105.51 J/cm 3 , exceeding that of the overwhelming majority of comparable systems. The BZT and S-BZT sublayers exhibit small lattice mismatch but pronounced dielectric contrast, which induces strong interfacial polarization ( P inter ) without introducing interfacial structural perturbation. Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire theory and phase-field simulations consistently verify the interface-induced polarization enhancement and agree well with the experimental observations. To further improve E b , machine learning was employed to establish the relationship between the multilayer structural parameters and E b and to identify the optimal starting-layer thickness. Experimental results closely reproduce the predicted trend, leading to an optimized Big-Mac- n architecture with a high W rec of 131.21 J/cm 3 and an E b of 6.5 MV/cm. The multilayer also exhibits excellent fatigue, frequency, and temperature stability, together with ultrafast discharge capability. This work establishes a data-driven interface-engineering strategy for reliable, Si-integrated dielectric energy-storage capacitors.
authors: Jun Yang, Hongyu Yang, Zixiong Sun

10.1002/aenm.71762.title: Operando Mapping of Population Phase Separation and Lithium-Plating Dynamics in Graphite Electrode Using Optical Microscopy and Microstructure Modeling
10.1002/aenm.71762.abstract: ABSTRACT The fast-charging capability of phase-separating graphite electrodes is largely constrained by heterogeneous reaction kinetics and sluggish mass transport at both the particle and electrode scales, which increase the risk of parasitic lithium plating and associated safety concerns. A deeper mechanistic understanding of the interplay among phase-separation dynamics, electrode microstructure, and lithium-plating propensity is therefore essential for guiding the rational design of advanced electrode architectures and fast-charging protocols. Here, we combine operando optical microscopy with three-dimensional microstructure-resolved phase-field modeling to resolve the interplay between phase separation and lithium plating. Microscopy captures stages evolution, phase mode transitions and structural dynamics across the particle population and at the single-particle level, which is driven by the slow interfacial reactions. Non-equilibrium phase-field simulations elucidate the kinetic control mechanisms governing phase transitions as the current varies. Importantly, a new mechanism of lithium plating associated with interfacial ohmic resistance is identified. Based on these insights, we evaluate particle-size-distribution design and use thermal activation as a mechanistic probe to resolve how temperature alters phase-separation pathways and lithium-plating behavior. These results may serve as a foundation for improving the physical understanding and driving optimization of fast charging protocols for lithium-ion batteries.
authors: Heng Huang, Yang Li, Xuekun Lu, Xinyu Liu, Yubai Li, Huanyue Zhang, Zhifu Zhou, Wei-Tao Wu, Lei Wei, Chengzhi Hu, Linsong Gao, Yongchen Song

10.1002/aenm.71763.title: Redefining Decoupled Water Electrolysis as an Integrated Hydrogen-Carrier Platform
10.1002/aenm.71763.abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop. By using a proton-coupled redox mediator to decouple hydrogen and oxygen evolution in time and space, DWE stores hydrogen equivalents in a charged mediator phase and releases H 2 electrochemically or catalytically at the point of use. This architecture shifts part of hydrogen logistics from pressure- or temperature-intensive processes toward ambient-condition electrochemical operation. DWE can therefore be viewed not merely as an alternative electrolyzer architecture, but as an integrated hydrogen-carrier platform. Within this broader framework, this Perspective focuses primarily on solution-phase proton-coupled mediators because their charged inventories can function as transportable liquid-phase carriers. Although current solution-phase DWE mediators remain disadvantaged in gravimetric capacity relative to ammonia and liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs), their system-level value lies in ambient-condition storage, low-temperature on-site H 2 release, independent scaling of power (electrolyzer stack) and energy capacity (mediator inventory), and flexible coupling to intermittent renewable electricity. We therefore propose carrier-relevant benchmarks including full-system capacity, storage-and-release efficiency, mediator retention, gas quality, delivered cost, and closed-loop logistics.
authors: Junghye Lee, Kwang Min Kim, Seongbin Ga, Hyeonmyeong Oh, Jungki Ryu

10.1002/aenm.71779.title: Locally Competitive Coordination Electrolyte for High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries With Ni-Rich Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71779.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy-dense cathode such as Ni-rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni-rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co-solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm − 2 ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah − 1 ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm − 2 ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah-level anode-free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.
authors: Jianqi Sun, Juliane Fiates, Kohei Shimokawa, Qingsong Weng, Heng Wang, Zhuangnan Li, Su Jin Heo, Hooman Abbasi, Minfei Fei, Tianhao Wu, Yaogang Li, Hongzhi Wang, James A Dawson, Michael De Volder

10.1002/aenm.71780.title: Constructing an Adaptive Flexible Interphase on Halide Electrolytes by Lewis-Acid-Induced Polymerization for High-Voltage All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71780.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) combining halide solid electrolytes (HSEs) with high-nickel layered oxide cathodes offer great promise for high energy density, yet they suffer from severe interfacial issues such as oxidative decomposition, mechanical degradation, and chemical incompatibility with sulfide electrolytes. Herein, we report a Lewis-acid-induced surface-softening strategy that constructs a nanoscale adaptive flexible interphase (AFI) via in situ polymerization of acrylonitrile (AN) on a representative halide electrolyte, Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC). The resulting AFI layer concurrently provides ionic conductivity, excellent oxidation stability (>4.8 V), and favorable viscoelasticity, thereby synergistically enhancing the electrochemical, chemical, and mechanical stability of the interface without compromising bulk ion transport. When paired with a single-crystal ultrahigh-nickel cathode LiNi 0.94 Co 0.05 Mn 0.01 O 2 (Ni94), the surface-softened LIC (S-LIC) enables ASSLBs delivering specific capacities of 223.8 and 209.5 mAh g −1 at 2 C and 4 C, respectively, retaining over 85% of the initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 C, and operate stably for more than 9000 cycles at 10 C. Even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.8 V, a capacity retention of 81% is achieved after 800 cycles at 2 C. This work provides a broadly applicable and efficient interfacial engineering route for high-voltage halide-based ASSLBs.
authors: Guo Tang, Yicheng Deng, Gengzhong Lin, Benchi Li, Kean Chen, Hui Li, Jiangfeng Qian, Yongjin Fang, Yuliang Cao, Xinping Ai

10.1002/aenm.71781.title: Directing Hole Utilization Through Self-Reconstructed Crystallinity Differentiation for Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
10.1002/aenm.71781.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is limited not simply by light absorption, but by inefficient hole routing and utilization at the semiconductor-electrolyte interface, together with severe defect-mediated recombination. Here, a self-reconstructed crystallinity-differentiated interface is developed to program hole utilization in photoanodes. A one-step hydrothermal synthesis creates an interlocked architecture in which highly crystalline In 2 S 3 pyramids are coupled with a disordered mixed-anion nanosheet domain, generating a spatially polarized reaction field for directed hole accumulation and transfer. This reconstructed interface lowers the work function, redistributes the local coordination environment around In sites, and induces a spatially heterogeneous photovoltage landscape that promotes interfacial charge separation. Mild Ar annealing further serves as a defect-selective activation step, suppressing recombination-active defects while preserving the beneficial interfacial polarization, thereby accelerating charge injection and oxygen evolution kinetics. The optimized photoanode reaches 8.74 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE , establishing interlocked crystallinity-differentiated architecture engineering combined with defect-selective activation as an effective strategy for sulfide photoanodes.
authors: Tianyun Liu, Linxing Meng, Dongniu Wang, Yuyang Kang, Yutao Xing, Xuefei Liu, Zhenhao He, Liang Li

10.1002/aenm.71784.title: Chemical Rounding Suppresses Morphology-Induced Interfacial Losses in Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71784.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface texturing in crystalline silicon solar cells imposes a fundamental trade-off in perovskite-silicon tandems: micrometer-scale pyramids enable efficient light trapping but limit the conformal deposition of thin perovskite films with sub-micrometer thickness, whereas reduced texture heights improve compatibility at the expense of optical performance and interfacial quality of the tandem device. Here, we address this challenge by combining precisely controlled submicron texturing with an ozone-assisted chemical rounding treatment. The resulting silicon substrates feature smoothly rounded, symmetric submicron textures that suppress micro-terrace formation and partial epitaxy at the amorphous silicon/crystalline silicon interface, while promoting more spatially uniform optoelectronic properties in the subsequently integrated top-cell stack. The morphology-engineered texture yields a monolithic perovskite-silicon tandem device with a power conversion efficiency of 33.25%, demonstrating that multiscale morphological control provides a powerful pathway to simultaneously improve the optical performance and interfacial quality of tandem solar cells.
authors: Nan Sun, Binbin Xu, Gaosheng Huang, Yuehui Li, Karsten Bittkau, Eunseo Noh, Sercan Aslan, Andreas Lambertz, Sang Il Seok, Michael Saliba, Christoph J. Brabec, Thomas Kirchartz, Kaining Ding

10.1002/aenm.71730.title: Coprecipitation-Enabled Scalable Synthesis of High-Energy Density Polyanion-Integrated Disordered Rocksalt Cathodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71730.abstract: ABSTRACT Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt- and nickel-free high-energy density lithium-ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries that have been predominantly developed via mechanochemical routes. A prominent example is polyanion-integrated DRX (DRXPS) cathodes, which rank among the best DRX cathodes reported to date in terms of reversible energy density, but have thus far been synthesized only mechanochemically via low-temperature ball milling. Here we demonstrate a coprecipitation-enabled solid-state synthesis of a DRXPS cathode, Li 1.67 Mn 1.5 P 0.17 O 4 , translating a mechanochemical route into a scalable process that is compatible with established cathode manufacturing infrastructure. The workflow programs precursor chemistry via coprecipitation of Mn 2 + with HPO 4 2 − and OH − , followed by a eutectic lithium-salt-assisted solid-state reaction, enabling low-thermal-budget DRXPS formation (450°C, 30 min) in air. The reduced thermal budget suppresses particle coarsening and yields a mixed micro-/nanoscale particle morphology, thereby eliminating the need for post-synthesis particle pulverization. The resulting cathodes deliver 324 mAh g −1 (935 Wh kg −1 ), demonstrating that high-energy density DRXPS can be realized within a manufacturing-compatible workflow. This work establishes a direct pathway toward scalable production of metastable high-energy density DRXPS cathodes and identifies precursor engineering as the key enabler.
authors: Hsi Chen, Yung-An Chen, Chen Chang, Frances M. Ross, Yimeng Huang, Ju Li
