10.1002/aenm.71776.title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr-O-Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
10.1002/aenm.71776.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling lattice-oxygen reactivity in transition-metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars-van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM 1 -O-TM 2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox-active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden-Popper LaSrFeO 4 (A 2 BO 4 ) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A-O-B motifs (i.e., La-O-Fe and Sr-O-Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A-O-B configuration could convert redox-inert A-site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO 4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO 3, with an Fe-O-Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35-fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A-O-B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B-O-B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.
authors: Qian Yang, Haoyu Yan, Chuande Huang, Zhe Song, Yumei Zhou, Jiahui He, Zhen Wang, Mingyu Shao, Teng Zong, Yuxuan Cui, Bo Jiang, Yanyan Zhu, Xiaodong Wang

10.1002/aenm.71775.title: Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal-Enhanced High-Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
10.1002/aenm.71775.abstract: ABSTRACT High-entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal-oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual-pathway activation, enabled by the high-entropy rock-salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O 1−x can accelerate interfacial charge-transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH * deprotonation. Under Xe-lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol −1 , and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm −2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long-term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm −2 . These findings underscore the potential of Fe-doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.
authors: Diming Yang, Kangqiang Li, Shiming Wu, Yeshuang Wang, Yuxi Xie, Jin Chen, Ju Tang, Fan Zhang, Zhaoyu Ma, Junying Zhang, Guo Chen

10.1002/aenm.71796.title: Strengthening TMP-Derived Phosphate SEI via Sn Scaffold and BF4− Interphase Chemistry for Ultra-Stable, High-Rate Zn Metal Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71796.abstract: ABSTRACT While dynamic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction and solvation engineering have transformed aqueous zinc-ion batteries, translating these approaches to Organic electrolytes (OE) remains a challenging endeavor due to fundamentally different interfacial environments, solvation thermodynamics, and anion decomposition pathways. Despite providing superior thermodynamic stabilization to Zn anode, OE exhibits low ionic conductivity, thereby limiting operational current densities. Herein, we report the first demonstration of Sn(BF 4 ) 2 /H 2 O (SFB) additive integration in a non-flammable trimethyl phosphate (TMP)-ethanol (EtOH) (2:1 v/v) OE to architect a gradient SEI interphase on Zn anodes. The multifunctional integration of SFB facilitates the formation of a Sn-coated Zn surface, a BF 4 1− -derived SEI@Zn, and H 2 O molecules as a proton source, collectively contributing to enhanced capacity. This strategic solvent-salt-metal synergy enables bi-layered interfacial engineering within a single electrolyte system, significantly improving the reversibility and stability of the Zn anode. Consequently, SFB enables a robust SEI, achieving exceptional Zn anode durability (7000 h), high-rate capability (10 mA cm −2 ), and a high Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8%. Full cells with SFB outperform controls in coin and pouch configurations. Given the rarity of additive(s) in OEs, this study offers a new path to boost stability and lifespan of non-aqueous Zn batteries.
authors: Ahmad Naveed, Xinyu Zhao, Rong-Hao Wang, Minfeng Jiang, Hao Shen, Yangyang Wan, Zhongti Sun, Huijun Yang, Teng Li, Yang-Feng Cui, Li-Feng Chen, Yunjian Liu

10.1002/aenm.71785.title: Chemical Coordination and Pore Confinement Enabling a Bifunctional Interface for Accelerated Desolvation and Oriented Deposition Toward Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71785.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries show great potential for large-scale energy storage; however, dendrites formation and corrosion on zinc anodes significantly hinder their practical applications. Uneven Zn deposition leads to dendrite growth, while H 2 O molecules in solvated Zn 2+ ions exacerbate surface corrosion and the hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, we propose a Schiff-base-covalently-grafted UiO-66-NH 2 metal-organic framework to construct a bifunctional interface for stable zinc metal anodes. Specifically, the chemical chelation between Schiff base and Zn 2+ accelerates desolvation and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed Zn 2+ -chelated sites and the well-defined confined pore channels of UiO-66-NH 2 scaffold guide a homogeneous Zn 2+ flux and promote Zn(002)-oriented deposition. As a result, this bifunctional interface enables Zn plating/stripping with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% over 2000 cycles at 5 mA cm −2 /1 mAh cm −2 . Furthermore, it achieves a capacity retention of over 90% after 4000 charge-discharge cycles in a Zn||MnO 2 full cell. This work is expected to open a new avenue for interfacial chemical regulation toward stabilizing zinc metal anodes.
authors: Miao Wang, Yuchu Tao, Liucheng Cao, Yubing Qiu, Kai Qi, Zheng-Long Xu, Bao Yu Xia

10.1002/aenm.71794.title: N-Heterocyclic Molecular Additives Enable Solvation and Interfacial Chemistry Regulation for High-Stability, High-Rate, and High-Capacity Lithium Metal Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71794.abstract: ABSTRACT Most electrolyte additives enable long-term Li plating/stripping at <3 mA cm − 2 , non-applicable to practical Li-metal batteries (LMBs) operating at ≥5 mA cm − 2 and ≥ 5 mAh cm − 2 . Here, we report an interaction chemistry that enables simultaneous solvation and interfacial regulation by exploring a novel N-heterocyclic molecule (i.e., TPTC)-comprising an N-heterocyclic core and four pyridine units-as an efficient additive for achieving ultra-stable Li-metal anodes under practical conditions. Electron-rich N atoms in TPTC serve as ion-dipole interaction sites, inducing competitive coordination that weakens Li + solvation and enhances Li + migration in the bulk electrolyte, which homogenizes Li + concentration near the interface, favoring high-rate Li deposition. TPTC also adsorbs on Li surface to construct a protective layer with a low interfacial de-solvation barrier, which-together with low-barrier Li + transport through heterocyclic cavities-facilitates uniform Li deposition. Meanwhile, electron-deficient C-H sites in pyridine weakly interact with TFSI − , forming an anion-rich interfacial region that in situ decomposes into an inorganic-rich interphase, affording high-flux Li + transport. This synergy allows stable Li plating/stripping at 10 mA cm −2 /10 mAh cm −2 for 3000 h. Paired with a high-loading LiFePO 4 cathode (∼15 mg cm −2 ) and thin Li (∼100 µm), the cell maintains 87.8% capacity after 400 cycles.
authors: Fujie Liu, Linglin Xia, Tingting Zhao, Juying Zhou, Jianfang Lu, Cong Liu

10.1002/aenm.71733.title: Surpassing Metal-Centric E-Waste Recycling: Unveiling Graphite in Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries Towards Electrocatalytic Upcycling
10.1002/aenm.71733.abstract: ABSTRACT With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. The study revealed an interesting pattern, wherein the graphite in BM complemented their impurity flaws by delivering an excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Defects, surface activation, structural variation, and metal-graphite synergism arising from prolonged cycle life served as a serendipitous finding of upcycling BM for OER, despite being loaded with impurities and/or degradation byproducts. Further, among these BM sets, direct upcycling of select graphite-containing BM via mechanochemical functionalisation aided downsized derivatives delivering an overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , while functionalized graphite via bioleaching BM recorded an overpotential of 249 mV, an epoch-making record in graphite upcycling. By correlating the overall insights using advanced material, electrochemical characterisation studies, and life cycle analysis, the current study unlocks spent graphite benefits for achieving sustainable energy solutions and beyond.
authors: Akshay Kumar K. Padinjareveetil, Kwok Kiong Chan, Jacob Balagot, Martin Gonson Rajan Nadar, Joseph Jegan Roy, Jun Ji Nicholas Lim, Madhavi Srinivasan

10.1002/aenm.71786.title: Decoupled Dual-Stream Seawater Electrolysis Toward Cost-Effective Green Hydrogen Production
10.1002/aenm.71786.abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean, as a vast natural reservoir of ionic minerals, provides a promising approach to offset the high cost of hydrogen production from electrocatalytic water splitting. However, the complex ionic environment of seawater compels us to separate out scaling-prone ions via cost-effective membrane separation technology, and further separately electrolyze diluted and concentrated seawater to produce H 2 and high value-added marine chemical products. We herein apply electrodialysis to separate out divalent cations and produce twofold concentrated seawater and fresh seawater. A decoupled dual-stream seawater electrolysis (DDSE) strategy is designed. The fresh seawater is routed into an alkaline/AEM water electrolyzer to sustain stable H 2 evolution. The concentrated seawater is fed into a home-made electrolyzer to produce NaClO and high-purity Mg(OH) 2 . A scalable non-noble metal-based electrode (50 cm × 50 cm) was designed and fabricated with high activity and stability when applied in the chlorine evolution reaction. System-level evaluation validates the feasibility of the DDSE strategy. Through rigorous techno-economic analysis, the unit price of H 2 production is reduced to $0.39 kgH 2 −1 (DOE 2030 target: $1 kgH 2 −1 ), and the Global Warming Potential can be reduced up to 6.83%. This proposed DDSE strategy offers a new approach for cost-effective green hydrogen production with comprehensive seawater valorization.
authors: Zhan Zhao, Shiyu Qin, Tong Li, Huiying Yang, Zizhen Li, Kelei Huang, Zisheng Zhang, Xiangchao Meng

10.1002/aenm.71793.title: Zwitterionic Thermoplastic Polyurethane-Based Quasi-Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium Metal Batteries With Machine-Learning-Assisted Mechanistic Insights
10.1002/aenm.71793.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a quasi-solid-state electrolyte based on zwitterionic thermoplastic polyurethane (QS-Z-TPU) for lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional quasi-solid polymer electrolytes that mainly serve as passive liquid-electrolyte reservoirs, QS-Z-TPU is designed as an active ion-regulating matrix via phosphorylcholine-derived zwitterionic groups in the TPU framework. The resulting electrolyte combines the elasticity and film-forming capability of TPU with dual-site ion regulation, where phosphate sites coordinate Li + while quaternary ammonium and urethane N-H groups immobilize TFSI − anions. This design enhances electrolyte affinity while suppressing destructive swelling due to ionic crosslinking. QS-Z-TPU exhibits high ionic conductivity, a wide electrochemical stability window, and an enhanced Li + transference number. Machine-learning-assisted molecular modeling further reveals that the zwitterionic oligomer stabilizes separated LiTFSI configurations through cooperative Li + coordination and TFSI − association, substantially reducing the energetic penalty for ion-pair separation. This regulated ion environment promotes uniform Li + flux at the lithium metal interface and facilitates the formation of a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, QS-Z-TPU enables stable Li plating/stripping and improves the cycling stability and rate capability of LFP|Li full cells, further validated in flexible pouch-cell demonstrations. These findings highlight zwitterionic molecular engineering as an effective strategy for interface-stabilizing quasi-solid electrolytes.
authors: Hongbin Na, Kyeonghyeon Nam, Yonghyuk Lee, Sung-Kon Kim

10.1002/aenm.71787.title: Versatile Acetyl-Functionalized Phenothiazine Self-Assembled Monolayers for Efficient Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71787.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of versatile, stable, and cost-effective hole-transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next-generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine-based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for perovskite and organic solar cells. By systematically tuning the substituents, including unsubstituted phenothiazine (PTZ), dibromo-PTZ (PTZ-diBr), and diacetyl-PTZ (PTZ-diACE), we achieve control over interfacial energetics and surface properties. The dual coordination sites of carbonyl groups and sulfur in PTZ-diACE provide Lewis basic sites that coordinate undercoordinated Pb 2 + ions, facilitating passivation at the buried HTL/perovskite interface. Additionally, polar acetyl groups induce interfacial dipoles that reinforce the built-in electric field, promoting efficient hole extraction. Among the series, PTZ-diACE exhibits superior film formation, a deeper HOMO level, and stronger interfacial interactions, resulting in enhanced charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells employing PTZ-diACE achieve a power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.5% with excellent operational stability, retaining 93% of its initial efficiency after 500 h under the ISOS-D-2I protocol. These advantages extend to organic solar cells, where PTZ-diACE delivers a PCE of 20.4% in D18:L8BO devices and demonstrates compatibility across multiple active layers. This study demonstrates phenothiazine-based SAMs as HTLs and provides design guidelines for efficient, stable interfacial materials.
authors: Qurrotun Ayuni Khoirun Nisa, Rahmatia Fitri Binti Nasrun, Dong Hwan Son, Joo Hyun Kim

10.1002/aenm.71782.title: Asymmetric Cooperative Solvation Structure Enables Entropy-Enthalpy Compensation for Ultralow Temperature Sodium-Metal and Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells
10.1002/aenm.71782.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-metal batteries are promising for low-temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME-rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na + and anions (PF 6 − /BF 4 − ), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE-rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy-entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic-rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na + migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled-up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.
authors: Yuanlong Feng, Mingshan Wang, Xinyu Tan, Peihao Zhu, Enzhi Li, Dongling Wu, Guozhong Cao, Xing Li

10.1002/aenm.71791.title: Light-Induced Ce-Ov-Ni Motifs Enable Hydrogen-Poisoning-Resistant Photothermal NH3 Decomposition
10.1002/aenm.71791.abstract: ABSTRACT NH 3 is an attractive hydrogen carrier, but efficient H 2 release is hindered by N-H bond cleavage and hydrogen poisoning. Herein, we develop Ni nanoparticle-supported CeO 2 (Ni/CeO 2 ) for low-temperature photothermal NH 3 decomposition. Light irradiation is accompanied by the dynamic generation of oxygen vacancies on CeO 2 , which couple with adjacent Ni sites to form Ce-Ov-Ni motifs, indicating that illumination can regulate the catalyst surface state beyond its thermal contribution. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that these interfaces create differentiated local environments for NH 3 activation and product evolution. Oxygen-vacancy-associated sites favor NH 3 adsorption, N-H bond activation, and N-containing intermediates, whereas adjacent Ni sites accommodate H migration and recombination. Moreover, vacancy-induced electronic modulation weakens H 2 adsorption on Ni, thereby facilitating H 2 release. Such site differentiation and facilitated hydrogen removal reduce the competitive occupation of active sites by N- and H-containing species and contribute to the resistance to hydrogen poisoning. Under photothermal conditions, 10 wt.% Ni/CeO 2 achieves 96.3% NH 3 conversion at 450°C, versus 42.5% under thermal catalysis, and maintains >95% conversion at a GHSV of 18,000 mL·gcat −1 ·h −1 . It delivers 20.09 mmol·gcat −1 ·min −1 H 2 with 50 h stability. This work demonstrates light-induced oxygen-vacancy-metal interfaces for efficient, hydrogen-poisoning-resistant NH 3 -to-H 2 conversion.
authors: Yue Zhu, Jianping Sheng, Chenyu Du, Ye He, Chaowei Yuan, Yanjuan Sun, Fan Dong

10.1002/aenm.71438.title: Multifunctional Matrix-Activated Electrodes Enabling Efficient Proton Transport and Durable Low-Pt Operation for High-Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
10.1002/aenm.71438.abstract: ABSTRACT Phosphoric acid (PA)-related challenges, including PA loss, redistribution, and flooding, critically limit the performance and long-term durability of high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT-PEMFCs) based on PA-doped membrane electrode assemblies. Although these issues can be partially mitigated using proton-conducting additives and hydrophobic polytetrafluoroethylene, practical commercialization remains impeded by restricted high-temperature operability and the requirement for high Pt loadings. To address these challenges, here we report a cerium hydrogen phosphate (CeHP)-integrated multifunctional matrix-activated electrode (MME) that stabilizes PA-containing electrode microenvironments and preserve electrochemical pathways under severe high-temperature operation above 200°C, where acid evaporation, dehydration, and migration become increasingly pronounced. This integrated matrix combines high-temperature proton-conduction, radical scavenging, and structural reinforcement of the porous catalyst layer, consequently alleviating the degradation at such high temperature. As a result, the optimized MME delivers a 38% increase in peak power density and a 62% reduction in voltage decay rate at 240°C, while requiring only 40% of the Pt loading of a Celtec commercial HT-PEMFC electrode (0.4 vs. 1.0 mg Pt cm −2 per electrode). These results establish multifunctional catalyst-layer matrix engineering as an effective strategy for enabling durable, low-Pt HT-PEMFC operation in acid-doped polymer electrochemical systems under harsh high-temperature conditions.
authors: Gyeongseok Gwak, Sunjin Park, Joonbyum Kim, Hena Lee, Jihyeon Ok, Chae Young Lee, JunHwa Kwon, Jong Geun Seong, Sung Pil Yoon, Suk-Woo Nam, Hansung Kim, Katie Heeyum Lim, So Young Lee

10.1002/aenm.71609.title: Water-Mediated Proton Facilitation for Stable Acidic CO2 Electrocatalysis
10.1002/aenm.71609.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical CO 2 conversion in acid can, in principle, maximize carbon efficiency but is typically undermined by facile hydrogen evolution. Moreover, operating at high current density often triggers a sharp local pH increase that propagates into the bulk electrolyte, causing an overall pH shift that erodes nominally “acidic CO 2 reduction” toward neutral/alkaline conditions. To address these limitations, we incorporated Ce species with high proton affinity into the surface of porous Cu nanosheet, constructing proton-mitigating Cu─O─Ce active sites. Beyond conventional C─C coupling driven by local * CO accumulation, Cu─O─Ce motifs accelerate * CO formation and its protonation, thereby enabling downhill proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) toward and beyond * CO─ * CHO dimerization. This strategy demonstrates efficient multi-carbon generation under retentive pH conditions minimizing the collateral deficiencies of acidic CO 2 reduction. Facilitating kinetically suppressed C─C coupling at a relatively low current density offers a strategic catalyst design that maintains a stable bulk pH compared to high current density operations, thereby maximizing the in situ generation of CO 2 within the acidic media.
authors: Jeong Hyun Hwang, Yoonjun Cho, Yoojin Lee, Hyo Sang Jeon, Man Ho Han, Zhonghao Wang, WooJean Kim, Kug-Seung Lee, Hyung-Suk Oh, He Li, Sunghyun Cho, Jeong Woo Han, Haotian Wang, Jong Hyeok Park

10.1002/aenm.71614.title: Interfacial Electronic Modulation of Vacancy-Stabilized Pt Sites in Mo-NiSeO4/NiSe2 Heterostructures for Industrial Alkaline Water Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71614.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing bifunctional electrocatalysts that combine high activity, long-term durability, and practical device compatibility remains a major challenge for alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, we report a heterostructure catalyst of a conductive Co 2 P nanowire scaffold integrated with a Mo-regulated NiSeO 4 /NiSe 2 heterophase shell, and atomically dispersed Pt species stabilized at O/Se-coordinated vacancy sites (Pt,Mo-NiSeO 4 /NiSe 2 @Co 2 P) grown on nickel foam via sequential electrodeposition, controlled selenization, and galvanic replacement. Benefiting from synergistic electronic modulation and heterointerface engineering, the catalyst requires only 24 and 98 mV to deliver 10 and 100 mA cm −2 for the hydrogen evolution reaction, and 242 and 330 mV for the oxygen evolution reaction, in 1.0 M KOH, with excellent durability. Operando Raman spectroscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal dynamic surface evolution during electrocatalysis and confirm the atomic dispersion of Pt. When assembled in a two-electrode electrolyzer, the catalyst achieves cell voltages of 1.47 V at 10 mA cm −2 and 1.65 V at 100 mA cm −2 in 30 wt.% KOH. Furthermore, an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer delivers 1.55 V at 0.3 A cm −2 and 1.76 V at 1.0 A cm −2 at 70 °C, demonstrating its promise for practical alkaline hydrogen production.
authors: Thokchom Anjali Devi, Abhisek Majumdar, Sidra Saleem, Do Hwan Kim, Bollu Manoj, Duy Thanh Tran, Nam Hoon Kim, Joong Hee Lee

10.1002/aenm.71598.title: Inside-Out Joule Heating Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane to Near-Stoichiometric Syngas Over LDH-Derived NiCo Catalysts
10.1002/aenm.71598.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrifying endothermic reactions offers a promising route toward sustainable chemical manufacturing, yet its practical implementation is constrained by inefficient outside-in heat delivery. Herein, we report a Joule-heating catalyst, NiCo/(Ni,Co)O-AlO x /Ti, derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs) rooted onto a Ti scaffold. This monolithic architecture establishes intimate electrical-thermal coupling and creates an inside-out thermal field that generates heat directly at the catalytic interface, shortening the heat-transfer pathway and mitigating reaction-induced catalyst-surface cooling. Experimentally validated multiphysics simulations resolve the resulting inverted temperature field and reduced source-to-surface temperature drop compared with outside-in furnace heating. Guided by this thermal design principle, the optimized Ni:Co = 2:1 catalyst achieves a high rate of 6.65 mmol·g Ni(Co) −1 ·s −1 with a near-unity H 2 /CO ratio, together with stable operation over 200 h and markedly suppressed carbon accumulation. Co-incorporation enriches vacancy-associated defect sites in the oxide lattice, promoting CO 2 activation through carbonate intermediates and reducing the energy barrier for carbonate-mediated carbon removal. These findings demonstrate how interfacial heat-delivery engineering can be coupled with defect-modulated catalyst design to advance electrified endothermic catalysis.
authors: Jinghao Li, Shuaiyu Chen, Jiaqi Li, Xianyong Li, Zhengpeng Qin, Gaowu Qin, Song Li

10.1002/aenm.71600.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Regulated and Rheologically Adaptive Interphase for Corrosion-Suppressed Dense Zinc Deposition in Long-Lasting 4 Ah Zinc Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71600.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical implementation of ampere-hour-scale aqueous zinc metal batteries is severely hindered by hydrogen evolution corrosion and dendritic growth under high-current operation. Although regulating electrode-electrolyte interphase water via hydrogen bonding has been recognized as an effective strategy to suppress parasitic reactions, achieving dense, and uniform zinc deposition at high current densities remains a critical challenge due to interfacial instability and stress accumulation. Here, we construct a hydrogen-bond-network-regulated ionic liquid layer coupled with a rheologically adaptive polydimethylsiloxane gel to establish a water-poor and mechanically resilient interphase. The modified hydrogen-bond network modulates the interfacial water environment, thereby contributing to suppressing corrosion. Simultaneously, the polydimethylsiloxane gel layer provides a hydrophobic barrier against water penetration and dynamically accommodates interfacial stress, enabling dense and uniform zinc deposition under high-rate conditions. As a result, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit exceptional cycling stability exceeding 1800 h at 50 and 25 mAh cm − 2 . More importantly, a 4 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling for 300 cycles with a cumulative capacity exceeding 1200 Ah. This work establishes a rational interphase engineering strategy for achieving durable, high-capacity aqueous zinc metal batteries under practical high-current conditions.
authors: Guowei Gao, Conghao Yu, Boxin Li, Yuhao Guan, Jingxuan Bi, Zhenkai Zhou, Xin Yu, Wei Ai

10.1002/aenm.71603.title: Moist-Electric Wallpaper With Engineered Unidirectional Moisture Transport for Indoor Energy Harvesting and Humidity Management
10.1002/aenm.71603.abstract: ABSTRACT Moist-electric generators (MEGs) convert ambient humidity into electricity, but their inherently low power output makes outdoor deployment as a general energy source impractical. Indoor environments, where humidity is stable and low-power electronics demand only microwatt-to-milliwatt supplies, present a more realistic opportunity-and wallpaper, with its large continuously exposed surface area and seamless architectural integration, is the most compelling platform to realize it. Here we report the first wallpaper-type MEG, enabled by a peripheral-absorption, center-evaporation architecture that achieves engineered unidirectional moisture transport on a single paper sheet. Glycerol at the periphery captures atmospheric moisture; polyvinylpyrrolidone in the intermediate region acts as a bound-water sink whose reduced porosity and lowered water activity drive inward transport through Laplace pressure and chemical potential gradients; and a wax-treated center exploits the phase-selective behavior of hydrophobic pores-blocking liquid while transmitting vapor-to confine evaporation without a solid seal. A concealed through-hole interconnection strategy enables modular scaling with no visible wiring. A single unit delivers ∼0.34 V and ∼2.2 µW/cm 2 at 80% RH with stable output over 90 min. A 1596-unit array powers a wireless keyboard and simultaneously reduces indoor humidity from 38% to 32%, transforming passive wall surfaces into self-powered, climate-responsive interfaces.
authors: Guangya Yuan, Yang Gao, Seokheun Choi

10.1002/aenm.71607.title: Siloxane-Mediated Dual Cross-Linking for Thermally Resilient and Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71607.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of perovskite solar cells (PerSCs) is still limited by their intrinsic instability, particularly under dynamic temperature fluctuations in outdoor conditions. In this study, we present a series of dual cross-linking agents to improve the efficiency and temperature endurance of PerSCs. Specifically, 3-(trichlorosilyl)propyl methacrylate (MPTCl) with multiple functional groups is applied to modify the upper interface of the perovskite. The ─C═O group exhibits strong interactions with the undercoordinated Pb 2+ on the perovskite surface, helping to stabilize structures and reduce interfacial charge recombination. The C═C bond of the methacrylate group undergoes in situ polymerization/cross-linking, while the trichlorosilyl group undergoes hydrolysis and subsequent condensation under humid conditions, enabling MPTCl to form a Si─O─Si cross-linked network. This cross-linked interfacial layer improves interfacial structural stability and enhances resistance to moisture- and heat-induced degradation. Consequently, the optimal PerSCs achieved a high power conversion efficiency of 26.22% and demonstrated enhanced thermal durability under simulated thermal cycling conditions, retaining 82.4% of their initial efficiency after 250 cycles. This work proposes a dual cross-linking strategy that provides an effective route for simultaneously improving the efficiency and thermal resilience of PerSCs, offering valuable insights into the development of durable perovskite photovoltaic technologies.
authors: Zongzhi Yang, Jiana Zheng, Jiayao Li, Kelei Wang, Ziyue Zhang, Runnan Yu, Zhan'ao Tan

10.1002/aenm.71611.title: CO2-Free Formaldehyde Electro-Reforming Fuel Cell
10.1002/aenm.71611.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional electrochemical synthesis is often hampered by steep energy demands and catalyst degradation, limiting both efficiency and durability. Here we introduce a hybrid alkali/acid formaldehyde-to-hydrogen fuel cell (h-A/AFHFC) that transcends these limitations by coupling alkaline formaldehyde oxidation conversion with acidic oxygen reduction. A columnar branched AgCu catalyst drives the h-A/AFHFC to a striking 2.0 V output and peak power density of 482 mW cm −2 , maintaining robust operation for over 110 h. Beyond electricity, the device leverages the exceptionally low oxidation potential of formaldehyde and its single-electron dehydrogenation pathway to co-produce hydrogen and formate in a *CO-free, CO 2 -free electrochemical process, reformulating the role of fuel cells. Each kilogram of hydrogen is inherently paired with 46.0 kg of formate and 33.2 kWh of electricity, offering a rare convergence of clean energy and high-value chemical synthesis. This strategy extends to gaseous formaldehyde and diverse aldehydes, enabling integrated energy-chemical platforms for sustainability.
authors: Kai Chen, Zhiwen Lu, Fen Hu, Yingyi Zeng, Junxiang Chen, Svetlana Štrbac, Lazar Rakočević, Zhenhai Wen

10.1002/aenm.71615.title: Complex Makes It Powerful: From Unidirectional to Bidirectional via Synergistic Volatile Solid Additives Enabling 20.16% Efficient and Stable Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71615.abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional volatile solid additives (VSAs) often regulate only the donor or acceptor phase, limiting synergistic microstructure optimization. Here, we report two halogenated nitrobenzene-based additives, 3,5-dichloronitrobenzene (DCNB) and 3,5-dibromonitrobenzene (DBNB), that enable bidirectional regulation of both components. Owing to their anisotropic electrostatic potential and large dipole moments, they simultaneously promote ordered crystallization of donor D18 and enhanced packing of acceptor L8-BO. Characterizations confirm improved molecular ordering and optimized phase separation, forming a favorable interpenetrating network. Consequently, D18:L8-BO devices with DCNB and DBNB achieve power conversion efficiencies of 20.16% and 19.80%, respectively, versus 17.87% for the control. The 20.16% efficiency ranks among the highest for binary OSCs processed with volatile solid additives. Charge dynamics and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal enhanced exciton dissociation, suppressed recombination, and accelerated interfacial hole transfer. This strategy also shows broad universality across multiple D-A systems, retaining >90% initial efficiency after 1000 h. This work unveils a bidirectional synergistic regulation mechanism and offers new insights into morphology engineering for stable, high-efficiency OSCs.
authors: Jichu Wu, Pengyuan Su, Yu Wang, Zhaoshuang Liu, Haoran Zhang, Yingshuang Bi, Xinming Zheng, Guangliu Ran, Haiyang Li, Wenkai Zhang, Jing Zhang, Hairui Liu, Donghong Yu, Chuanlang Zhan

10.1002/aenm.71616.title: Electrolyte Microenvironment and Alloy Interface Synergy Enables Wide-Temperature Aqueous Aluminum-Ion Batteries From −30 to 50°C
10.1002/aenm.71616.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum-ion batteries (AAIBs) have attracted interest due to the high abundance, low cost, and high theoretical capacity of aluminum. However, their development is hindered by limited electrolyte stability, severe corrosion and passivation of the Al anode, and sluggish Al 3+ diffusion kinetics, particularly under temperature extremes. Herein, an electrolyte-anode coupled strategy is developed by combining a hydrated eutectic electrolyte with an electrodeposited Al-Zn alloy anode. The optimized electrolyte, denoted as AETH30, is composed of Al(ClO 4 ) 3 ·9H 2 O, ethylene glycol (EG), triethyl phosphate (TEP), and H 2 O at a molar ratio of 1:6:4:30. EG and TEP reorganize the hydrogen-bond network and establish a dynamic mixed Al 3+ solvation environment, reducing water-dominated coordination and suppressing parasitic reactions. Electrolyte-derived interfacial species improve surface stability, while the Al-Zn alloy lowers interfacial resistance and facilitates reversible plating/stripping. Benefiting from the complementary regulation of the electrolyte microenvironment and alloy-anode interface, the Al-Zn || AETH30 || PANI full cell retains 88.81 mAh g −1 after 1700 cycles at 25°C. It also maintains capacities of 53.96 and 81.47 mAh g −1 after 850 cycles at −30°C and 1000 cycles at 50°C, respectively. This work demonstrates an electrolyte microenvironment and alloy interface synergy strategy for durable AAIBs capable of wide-temperature operation.
authors: Zhen Zhang, Guode Chen, Zhenxun Tang, Jing Yang, Du Yuan, Jun Li, Zhicong Shi, Carlos Ponce de León, Dmitry Bavykin, Chuan Wu, Jia Hong Pan

10.1002/aenm.71638.title: Resolving the Electro-Mechanical Trade-Off at the Buried Interface of Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71638.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole-based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are essential in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) due to superior electrical properties, yet their inherent rigidity imposes severe mechanical stress on the perovskite layer. Herein, we construct an interfacial architecture featuring discontinuous metal-oxide islands to circumvent this fundamental electro-mechanical trade-off at the buried contact. Specifically, this discontinuous topography imparts macroscopic structural flexibility to the interface by functioning as localized strain-relaxation zones, enabling strain-relaxed perovskite films with reduced defect density. Meanwhile, the modified interface maintains unimpeded hole-selective pathways and optimal energy level alignment. Consequently, the corresponding PSC yields a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.92% (certified 26.60%) with enhanced long-term stability. This strategy establishes a rational design principle for synergistic electro-mechanical management, paving the way for high-efficiency and stable photovoltaic devices.
authors: Ying Chen, Xiaosong Qiu, Dejian Yu, Gang Wang, Na Han, Shengwen Li, Yulin Wang, Ruifeng Zheng, Shi Chen, Ying Li, Guichuan Xing

10.1002/aenm.71612.title: Materials-Property Classification of Interlayers for Stabilizing Lithium Metal Interfaces in Sulfide-Based All-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71612.abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs) promise high energy density by using lithium metal anodes, but their practical implementation is limited by severe interfacial instability. At the lithium metal/sulfide electrolyte interface, coupled chemical, electrochemical, and mechanical degradation accelerates impedance growth and cell failure. Interlayer strategies are promising for stabilizing sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries because they can mitigate interfacial degradation, improve contact stability, and regulate ion/electron transport at critical electrode-electrolyte interfaces. However, their mechanisms have largely been interpreted based on phenomenological observations and empirical performance improvements, rather than through intrinsic material property-mechanism relationships, highlighting the need for a material property-driven design framework. Here, we categorize interlayer strategies into metal, polymer, ceramic, and composite systems and reinterpret their functions from an electro-chemo-mechanical perspective. We discuss how stiffness, ductility, fracture toughness, electronic conductivity, electrochemical stability, chemical stability, lithiophilicity, and Li-ion transport govern interfacial behavior during assembly, plating, stripping, and long-term cycling. By correlating representative interlayer systems with their electro-chemo-mechanical properties, this perspective clarifies the relationship between material characteristics and interfacial stabilization behavior in sulfide-based ASSLMBs. This property-driven framework is expected to provide practical criteria for screening unexplored interlayer materials and guiding the rational design of stable lithium metal/sulfide electrolyte interfaces.
authors: Jeonghun Lee, Minseok Ko, Jaekyung Sung

10.1002/aenm.71799.title: Decoupling Oxygen Reduction From Hydrogen Oxidation on Platinum via Phosphorus Coordination for Reversal-Tolerant and Durable PEM Fuel Cells
10.1002/aenm.71799.abstract: ABSTRACT During the start-up/shut-down (SU/SD) processes of proton-exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), anode reversal generates an excessively high voltage that accelerates corrosion of the cathode Pt/C catalyst. Conventional approaches focus on blocking the delivery of oxygen or electrons to the anode, but fail to address the intrinsic activity coupling of Pt/C for both hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Here, we report a strategy that can selectively tailor the catalytic function of Pt nanoparticles. We used phosphorus to modulate the electronic structure of low-loading Pt clusters on a carbon support, forming a Pt/P-BP catalyst. The P-coordination downshifts the d -band center of Pt cluster, as evidenced by in situ ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, thereby widening the activity gap between HOR and ORR. Specifically, compared to Pt/C, Pt/P-BP enhances HOR mass activity by fivefold while substantially suppressing ORR, transforming Pt from a bifunctional catalyst into a highly selective HOR catalyst. Consequently, Pt/P-BP achieves a 10.8-fold higher HOR/ORR selectivity than Pt/C. In SU/SD experiments, the Pt/P-BP anode significantly reduces carbon corrosion of the cathode catalyst layer, maintaining the fuel cell performance better than Pt/C. This work paves a new avenue toward durable PEMFCs and inspires the selectivity design for electrocatalysts.
authors: Shuang Li, Ahui Hao, Dandan Liu, Xin Wan, Qian Niu, Weihao Liu, Zhao Zhang, Xiaofang Liu, Jianglan Shui

10.1002/aenm.71797.title: Relay Catalysis on Phase-Separated Janus-CuCo Alloys for Efficient Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction at Industrial Low Concentration
10.1002/aenm.71797.abstract: ABSTRACT Earth-abundant Cu and Co are attractive electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO 3 − RR); however, conventional solid-solution alloys with single-phase active sites lack effective intermediate spillover, impeding the hydrogenation of multiple reaction intermediates and limiting NH 3 selectivity under dilute nitrate conditions. Here we report phase-separated yet electronically coupled Janus-CuCo alloys synthesized via a time-charge regulated electrochemical reduction strategy, forming metallic Cu/Co domains with a well-defined interphase electronic structure. This Janus architecture enables relay catalysis, in which Cu domains activate NO 3 − , intermediates migrate to Cu−Co interfaces for hydrogenation, and adjacent Co domains promote subsequent NH 3 formation. In situ characterizations reveal pronounced Cu-Co synergy, where Co sites regulate *H-mediated hydrogenation while the balanced surface coverage of *H and *NO 3 − optimizes NH 3 selectivity and yield. Consequently, the optimized Janus Cu−Co catalyst, Janus-Cu 70 Co 30 /NOMC, achieves a peak NH 3 Faradaic efficiency (FE NH3 ) of 95.5% at −500 mA cm −2 and delivers a FE NH3 of 93.1% with an NH 3 yield rate of 4.2 mg h −1 mg cat −1 at −0.4 V vs RHE in an MEA flow cell under low nitrate concentrations. These findings establish phase separation with electronic coupling, enabled by electrochemical time-charge control, as an effective design principle for efficient multistep NO 3 − RR electrocatalysis.
authors: Mazhar Hayat, Enyang Sun, Min Wang, Qamir Iqbal, Wenwen Zhou, Yan Yan, Minghui He, Yu-Cheng Huang, Yujuan Zhang, Yi Fu, Muhammad Akmal, Ying-Rui Lu, Tuoping Hu, Yuxuan Lu, Yu Ding, Huili Chen, Siming Li, Yawei Li

10.1002/aenm.71446.title: Hard Carbon Networks for Mitigating Graphite Lattice Strain Under Extreme-Low-Temperature Fast Charging
10.1002/aenm.71446.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-temperature fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is primarily constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics and mechanical degradation of graphite anodes. Here, a kinetic-structural coordination strategy based on a 15 wt.% hard carbon (HC) percolating network embedded within the graphite matrix is proposed. This HC network functions as an ionic flux redistributor, effectively suppressing the high-strain phase transition to stage 1 (LiC 6 ) and reducing lattice strain, thereby protecting the graphite from mechanical pulverization. Moreover, the coordinated lithiation promotes the formation of a robust, LiF-rich inorganic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which facilitates fast desolvation and prevents interfacial delamination. As a result, NCM523‖Graphite/HC pouch cells deliver 2250 cycles at −20°C under a 4C rate with 88% capacity retention, and maintain stable operation at 8C and −40°C. This network doping approach thus provides a scalable design principle for all-climate, high-power batteries intended for electric vehicle applications.

10.1002/aenm.71792.title: Synergistic Fluoride and Polymer-Regulated Interfacial Engineering of NiFe-LDH Anodes for Ampere-Scale Natural Seawater Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71792.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride-induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride-management, defect-engineering, and polymer-interfacial-protection strategy for NiFe-LDH anodes, enabling kilo-hour-scale operation at ampere-level current densities in natural seawater. A custom-designed microwave-assisted method produces fluoride-protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F-NiFe-LDH MW /NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation-deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F-NiFeZn vac -LDH MW @CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial-scale current density of 1000 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining stage-resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F − regulation and the evolving cation-defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe-LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl − access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F − undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.
authors: Xiang Li, Nafeesa Sarfraz, Yi Ding, Imran Mahmood Khan, Shahid Iqbal, Muhammad Sajjad, Sanghyuk Wooh, Ibrahim Khan

10.1002/aenm.71803.title: Engineering Energy-Storage Interfaces With Atomic and Molecular Layer Deposition: From Surface Chemistry to Process Design
10.1002/aenm.71803.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance and lifetime of energy-storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self-limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy-storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry-process-structure-function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge-transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li-based and beyond-Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post-deposition characterization, and full-cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.

10.1002/aenm.71805.title: Non-Stoichiometric Molybdenum Oxides Enable Phase-Stable Proton Storage
10.1002/aenm.71805.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium-ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H + often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non-stoichiometric tunnel-structured molybdenum oxide, Mo 5 O 14 , as a highly reversible proton-storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H 3 O + intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo 5 O 14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g −1 at 1.5 A g −1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g −1 even at 300 A g −1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg −1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg −1 , and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro-cell array demonstrates rapid-charge capability, powering a red light-emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high-rate charging.
authors: Yongqi Lu, Jianxiong Gao, Bowen Jin, Zhilong Wang, Mingliang Zuo, Yu Wu, Shimeng Zhang, Yanlan Ren, Qijing Zhao, Mingfei Shao

10.1002/aenm.71750.title: Fast Dynamic Re-Equilibration of Chloroaluminate Speciation Enables a Stable Electrode-Electrolyte Interface in Aluminum Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71750.abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl 3 /EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re-equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane-enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode-electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl 4 − /Al 2 Cl 7 − conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl 3 /EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g −1 at 200 mA g −1 after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long-life aluminum-ion batteries.
authors: Jingshan Chai, Canfu Zhang, Zhifei Mao, Amirhossein Mirtaleb, Li Xie, Ruigang Wang

10.1002/aenm.71810.title: Spatial-Decoupled Synergy between Asymmetric Ni-N3 Sites and Ni Nanoparticles Extending the Air-Tolerant Poisoning Limit of MgH2 Hydrogen Storage
10.1002/aenm.71810.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state MgH 2 holds immense promise for high-capacity hydrogen storage, yet its practical deployment is severely hindered by extreme atmospheric susceptibility and an elusive activated dehydrogenation mechanism. Herein, we report a armor like architectural design featuring asymmetric Ni-N 3 sites and nanoparticles (NPs) co-decorated within a flexible nitrogen-doped graphene (NG). Driven by the electronic synergy between the Ni-N 3 sites and the highly active Ni NPs, the NG achieves robust encapsulation of MgH 2 , providing a rigid size-exclusion barrier against ambient O 2 /H 2 O infiltration. Concurrently, strong electronic interactions between MgH 2 and Ni species optimize the MgH 2 electronic structure, which further reduces its reactivity toward O 2 /H 2 O, enabling the MgH 2 to preserve its full capacity even after a 28-day cumulative air exposure. Furthermore, the encapsulated Ni NPs undergo an in situ reaction to form Mg 2 Ni nanorivets, which serve as high-flux interfacial hydrogen pumps, while creating a vital spatial buffer during dynamic cycling, thereby achieving 95% capacity retention over 360 cycles at 300°C. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the electronic hybridization induced by the asymmetric Ni-N 3 sites, Ni NPs, and Mg 2 Ni nanorivets destabilizes Mg-H bonds. This multi-scale engineering of environmental isolation, electronic modulation, and structural riveting presents a robust blueprint for air-tolerant, fast-kinetics solid-state hydrogen storage.
authors: Jie Tian, Mingzi Sun, Yuyang Zhao, Junming Huang, Wenfeng Li, Yangfan Lu, Qian Li, Zhenhui Ma, Bolong Huang, Hu Liu

10.1002/aenm.71804.title: Synergistic Anion Regulation Inducing Fluoride-Rich SEI and Defect-Rich MnO2 for Stable Dual Electrode-Free Zn-MnO2 Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71804.abstract: ABSTRACT Dual electrode-free (DEF) Zn─MnO 2 batteries based on dissolution-deposition chemistry are promising candidates for large-scale energy storage due to their lightweight architecture and high theoretical capacity (616 mAh g −1 ). However, poor interfacial reversibility and the accumulation of “dead manganese” significantly limit their lifespan. Here, we demonstrate a stable DEF battery enabled by an anion-regulation strategy using a hybrid electrolyte (E-OA) comprising trifluoromethanesulfonate (OTf − ) and acetate (Ac − ) ions. At the anode, OTf − facilitates the formation of a fluoride-rich solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively suppressing dendrite growth and the hydrogen evolution reaction. At the cathode, the synergistic anionic environment elevates the MnO 2 nucleation overpotential, shifting the electrocrystallization pathway to an instantaneous nucleation mode. The kinetically driven growth process traps abundant structural defects, identified as proton-compensated manganese vacancies (Ruetschi defects). These vacancies lower the thermodynamic energy barrier for Mn─O bond cleavage, thereby ensuring highly reversible dissolution. Consequently, the E-OA-based DEF battery achieves exceptional stability for over 7500 cycles at 0.5 mAh cm −2 and sustains 600 cycles at 2 mAh cm −2 (10 mA cm −2 ), demonstrating superior rate capability and versatility in both flow and gel battery configurations. This work provides a transformative strategy for high-energy aqueous batteries via tailored anion chemistry and kinetics-driven defect engineering.
authors: Zheng Li, Yong Xu, Hao Liu, Liuzhang Ouyang, Renzong Hu, Jun Liu, Lichun Yang, Min Zhu

10.1002/aenm.71816.title: Stress-Regulated Li Plating in Hybrid Ag-Carbon/Carbon Nanofiber Anodes for Durable All-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71816.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with Li-metal or Li-metal-free anodes enable high energy density, yet high-loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag-carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short-circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag-C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag-C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag-Li alloy-assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase-field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag-Li alloying within the Ag-C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag-C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high-loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm −2 ). Furthermore, stable pouch-cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high-energy-density ASSBs.
authors: Junhee Kang, Tae Young Lee, Jeongvin Park, Hong Rim Shin, Dong Seok Kim, Jieun Lee, Hun-Gi Jung, Jeong-Hee Choi, Jong-Won Lee

10.1002/aenm.71790.title: Rethinking Battery Safety: Unveiling Aluminum Propellant-Like Reactions During Thermal Runaway and Developing Protective Solutions
10.1002/aenm.71790.abstract: ABSTRACT Battery safety remains a critical challenge in the large-scale deployment of lithium-ion batteries. While thermal runaway is typically attributed to exothermic reactions involving electrode materials and electrolytes, the contribution of current collectors has been largely overlooked. Here, we demonstrate that the conventionally presumed inert aluminum (Al) current collector engages in intense exothermic reactions with various cathode materials at temperatures exceeding 600°C. This reactivity is catalyzed by fluorides, which disrupt the Al passivation layer, resembling combustion mechanisms observed in Al-based rocket propellants. The specific heat release from Al oxidation (−22 to −33 kJ g −1 ) is nearly twice that of the electrolyte (−12 to −16 kJ g −1 ). Considering that the Al mass is approximately half that of the electrolyte, its theoretical thermal contribution during thermal runaway is comparable to that of the electrolyte. Employing fluorine-free electrolytes can suppress the propellant-like reaction. Together with flame-retardant strategies, the total heat release during thermal runaway can be further reduced, with the measured peak temperatures around pouch cells being effectively suppressed below 400°C. This work uncovers a pervasive yet previously underappreciated high-energy reaction in batteries and offers new design strategies for improving thermal safety.
authors: Yangfan Lin, Jiahao Chen, Yuqi Liu, Lei Liu, Chuanyu Hou, Han Zhang, Li Wang, Xiangming He, Jianhui Wang

10.1002/aenm.71809.title: Super-Toughness Self-Healing Composite Solid Electrolyte With Structured Interfacial Reconstruction Enabling Fast Ion Transport and Stable Interface for High-Performance Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71809.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-metal batteries are widely regarded as a key direction for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density. However, LiNi 0 . 8 Co 0 . 1 Mn 0 . 1 O 2 ||Li battery systems face severe challenges in practical application, including lithium dendrite growth, interfacial side reactions and structural degradation of high-nickel cathodes. Here, we proposed a versatile modification strategy combining in-situ interfacial transformation with polymer phase regulation to fabricate self-healing solid polymer electrolyte with fast ion transport and stable interface. This strategy not only constructs fast ion channels and suppresses hydrofluoric acid production by in-situ converting Li 2 CO 3 on the Li 6.4 La 3 Zr 1.4 Ta 0.6 O 12 surface into Li 2 PO 3 F interfacial layer, but also induces the transition of PVDF from α-phase to high polarity β-phase using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid to promote lithium salt dissolution and reduce Li + migration resistance. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.13 V), high room-temperature ionic conductivity (1.694 mS cm − 1 ), excellent thermal stability (200°C), high elongation at break (422.6%), and superior cycling stability (89.4% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C). A non-destructive monitoring method based on d p /|d Q | and d T /|d Q | differential signals has been developed to track electrochemical-mechanical-thermal responses during battery operation. This work provides an effective strategy for designing solid polymer electrolytes with high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability.
authors: Feng Zou, Zhihong Yao, Bo Peng, Shixin Liu, Runwei Mo

10.1002/aenm.71798.title: Unlocking Wide-Temperature Battery States via Noninvasive Nonlinear Ultrasound
10.1002/aenm.71798.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are central to modern energy storage, yet evaluating their internal states under extreme thermal fluctuations remains a critical challenge. Here we present a non-destructive evaluation framework that leverages the quasi-static component (QSC) of nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves. By integrating an operando electro-acoustic-thermal platform, we isolate temperature-induced artefacts from intrinsic acoustic signals. This statistical compensation enables the precise, simultaneous prediction of state of charge (SOC) and state of charge relative to nominal capacity (SOC N ) across a wide temperature span (−10°C to 40°C). Furthermore, in situ multidimensional characterization maps these ultrasonic signatures to temperature-dependent mechanics and irreversible capacity fade mechanisms. Ultimately, this unified framework provides a scalable, quantitative diagnostic tool for reliable energy systems operating under extreme environments.
authors: Xiaolei Lin, Xiaofeng Li, Xianlin Cao, Jiyu Liu, Xinyi Yuan, Jinshan Wen, Yancheng You, Mingxi Deng, Weibin Li

10.1002/aenm.71812.title: Synergistically Modulating Electronic Structure and Interfacial Wettability of MnF2/NF−CNF Toward Enhanced Oxygen Reduction in Zinc−Air Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71812.abstract: ABSTRACT Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple-phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF 2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF 2 /NF−CNF). The unique interconnected fibrous and hierarchical porous architecture, together with tailored MnF 2 embedding and N/F doping, achieves an optimal balance between activity and wettability regulation. Excellent ORR performance with a high half-wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE and limiting current density of 6.34 mA cm −2 is achieved, outperforming Pt/C and most previously reported Mn-based/heteroatom-doped systems. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal surface N dopants as active sites, with MnF 2 modulating p-orbital configuration, refining ORR pathways. Meanwhile, surface F dopants, in synergy with the porous architecture, regulate wettability, equilibrate electrolyte/oxygen transport, and substantially extend triple-phase reaction interfaces. The assembled ZAB delivers an exceptional peak power density of 181.5 mW cm −2 with high specific capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability. This work deciphers the regulatory mechanism balancing catalytic activity and interfacial wettability, proving a versatile strategy for developing advanced ORR electrocatalysts in ZABs.
authors: Junhao Zhang, Chuan Xie, Hanzhen Li, Lipeng Wang, Yuanjun Liu, Xiangjun Zheng, Zhongyao Duan, Xingmei Guo, Qinghong Kong, Shenglin Xiong

10.1002/aenm.71764.title: Ionomer-Free Iridium Anodes With Low Loading for Zero-Gap Electrolyzers via Direct Atomic Layer Deposition
10.1002/aenm.71764.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer-free catalyst layers based on custom-made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using as counter-reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/ and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 . The PEMWE cell-level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst-coated membrane anode despite lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low-loading ALD-made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 . Plasma-enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower-activity . Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer-bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.
authors: Peter M. Piechulla, Iris Blommestein, Anne van Gerven, Henri Pelzer, Ezgi Demiröz, Jonas Englhard, Mingliang Chen, Julien Bachmann, J. Ruud van Ommen

10.1002/aenm.71808.title: ZrO2 Clusters Enabling Room-Temperature Hydrogen Absorption and Low-Temperature Desorption of Commercial Mg Powder for Reversible Hydrogen Storage
10.1002/aenm.71808.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium-based hydrogen storage materials exhibit great application potential, but high operating temperature and slow kinetics hinder their large-scale utilization. Here, the amorphous-carbon-stabilized Mg particles decorated with sub-2 nm ZrO 2 nanoclusters are reported, which were in situ fabricated via ball milling of commercial Mg powder, acetone (ACE), and zirconium acetylacetonate (Zr(acac) 4 ). The optimized Mg-ACE-1 wt.% Zr composite achieves rapid hydrogen absorption of 4.25 wt.% at 30°C within 60 min and exhibits high cycling stability with nearly no H 2 capacity fading after 40 cycles at 300°C under 30 bar H 2 . Notably, the Mg-ACE-1 wt.% Zr sample enables reversible hydrogenation at room temperature and dehydrogenation at high temperature, achieving better energy efficiency than conventional thermally driven MgH 2 and showing promise for coupling with renewable hydrogen production. Interfacial characterizations and DFT calculations confirm that the in situ formed ZrO 2 /Mg interface accelerates H 2 adsorption, dissociation, and diffusion.
authors: Mengdan Guan, Qijun Pei, Haoran Guo, Hong Wen, Zibo Cheng, Jia Zheng, Yong Pei, Wei Xie, Hujun Cao, Ping Chen

10.1002/aenm.71826.title: Non-Planar Chlorine-Coordinated Activation of Triatomic Ruthenium Sites for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
10.1002/aenm.71826.abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru-based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement-pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine-doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru 3 ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru 3 ON 6 Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru 3 ClNC delivers a high alkaline half-wave potential ( E 1/2 ) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc-air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru 3 ON 6 Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non-planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d -band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate-determining step of Ru 3 NC and OH * desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept for Ru-based catalysts to overcome the thermodynamic limitations and thereby improve the ORR activity.
authors: Luoluo Qi, Lina Li, Jingqi Guan

10.1002/aenm.71788.title: Rational Terminal-Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71788.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy-level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active-layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S-SMA and AS-SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8-BO with a weaker electron-withdrawing 2-(3-ethyl-4-oxothiazolidin-2-ylidene)malononitrile (CN-Rh) unit. This terminal-group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8-BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid-to-solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S-SMA, asymmetric AS-SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8-BO:AS-SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal-group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy-level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high-performance ternary organic solar cells.
authors: Yongchao Hu, Jinrong Shi, Zhenyu Chen, Shanshan Qin, Jinfeng Ge, Hongchen Rong, Pengfei Ding, Tao Zhang, Deping Qian, Kangqiao Ma, Kang Wang, Ziyi Ge

10.1002/aenm.71814.title: Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71814.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer-anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray-coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm −2 . The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.
authors: Zheng Wang, Xin Shen, Feng Jiang, Yun-Fei Du, Nai-Lu Shen, Ke-Feng Ren, Tao Wang, Zhi Zhu, Yiren Zhong, He Liu, Xinyan Liu, Hong-Jie Peng, Yuping Wu, Xin-Bing Cheng

10.1002/aenm.71739.title: Dual Suppression of Triplet Exciton and Energetic Disorder via Organic Room-Temperature Phosphorescent Additive to Reduce Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71739.abstract: ABSTRACT Non-radiative energy loss originating from triplet exciton generation and intrinsic energetic disorder severely restricts the efficiency breakthrough of organic solar cells (OSCs). To address this dual bottleneck, herein, two benzodiimide-based solid additives with distinct photophysical properties, namely fluorescent HPmDI and room-temperature phosphorescent (RTP) BrPmDI, are developed to simultaneously suppress triplet exciton dissipation and mitigate energetic disorder for high-efficiency OSCs. Both additives construct favorable intermolecular interactions with the D18 donor and L8-BO acceptor, optimizing active layer molecular packing, enhancing film crystallinity, and reducing Urbach energy to alleviate intrinsic energetic disorder. Benefiting from the unique long-lived triplet exciton characteristics of organic RTP BrPmDI, an efficient Dexter energy transfer (DET) pathway is additionally enabled, which effectively inhibits non-radiative decay channels, including intersystem crossing and charge recombination-induced triplet exciton formation. Consequently, the optimized D18:L8-BO-based OSCs modified with BrPmDI achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.52% with a low non-radiative energy loss of 0.217 eV, far outperforming the pristine device (19.01% and 0.226 eV) and HPmDI-modified device (19.70% and 0.219 eV). This work reveals the dual regulatory mechanism of organic RTP additives on triplet exciton dynamics and energetic disorder, providing a facile strategy for the design of high-efficiency additive materials toward low-energy-loss and high-performance OSCs.
authors: Qingqiu Zhu, Junhong Liang, Xiaosong Qiu, Liangliang Chen, Yiyun Zeng, Mingxuan Yang, Zixun Chen, Wentao Miao, Ming Wan, Yao Wu, Renqiang Yang, Xunchang Wang

10.1002/aenm.71703.title: Fully Roll-to-Roll Coated Large-Area Perovskite Solar Modules on Indium-Free Microgroove Substrates
10.1002/aenm.71703.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low-cost, low-carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll-to-roll coated, large-area back-contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm 2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm 2 . The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll-to-roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS-compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x-ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real-world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.
authors: Nathan S. Hill, Freddie White, Sophia Baker, Timothy Thornber, Farshad Jafarzadeh, Jazib Ali, George Koutsourakis, Lavanya Malarkannan, James Blakesley, Jessica M. Walker, Trevor McArdle, Roderick C.I Mackenzie, David G. Lidzey, Dumitru Sirbu

10.1002/aenm.71819.title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO2-to-Formate Electrosynthesis
10.1002/aenm.71819.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton-coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high-rate CO 2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic-and-gap-confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)-modified Bi (Bi-PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst-electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near-surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen-bond environment, while slow-growth proton-transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton-delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to * OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential-dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate-related pathway response. Bi-PDMS-30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm − 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface-deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion-water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO 2 -to-formate electrosynthesis.
authors: Jifeng Wu, Xiao Ma, Tingsong Li, Miao Hu, Xiangyun T. Xiao, Abdulrahman Allangawi, Moyu Yi, Magnus Rueping, Wan-Lu Li, Huabin Zhang, Kuo-Wei Huang

10.1002/aenm.71800.title: Synergistic Crystallization Regulation and Defect Suppression via Dual-Site Molecular Coordination for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71800.abstract: ABSTRACT Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long-term stability. Herein, (1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual-site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH 3 + ) and electron-rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl-modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non-radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy-level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp-heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80.52% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85°C and 800 h at 85°C, 85% relative humidity, respectively. This work demonstrates a practical molecular-interaction strategy for efficient and durable inverted PSCs based on multifunctional, dual-site passivation and crystallization regulation.
