For example, a used Nafion membrane from a 200 h lifespan PEM fuel cell achieves a hydrogen storage capacity of 2.05 wt.% at 150°C and 5 MPa, along with excellent cycling stability and rapid kinetics. This performance is comparable to that of specially engineered hydrogen storage materials, highlighting its practical potential. The service-evolved hydrogen storage functionality provides a sustainable and high-value route for managing EoL electrochemical membranes.
authors: Xuan Zhang, Bingru Liu, Yao Pang, Dandan Liu, Zhihui Wu, Xiaofang Liu, Zhao Zhang, Jianglan Shui

10.1002/adfm.78047.title: Engineering Solvation Sheath and Gradient Interphase via Pull-Expulsion Dynamics for Low-Temperature Quasi-Solid-State Sodium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78047.abstract: ABSTRACT Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) hold particular promise for solid-state sodium metal batteries (SSMBs) owing to their inherent flexibility and processability. However, their practical implementation is severely constrained by sluggish ion transport kinetics and exacerbated dendrite growth at low temperatures. To tackle these issues, we propose a coordination-driven pull-expulsion dynamics strategy that employs poly(vinylene carbonate) (PVC) and residual monomer to address the aforementioned multifaceted bottlenecks simultaneously. The highly polar C─O groups in PVC chains actively extract Na + from the solvent-separated ion pair solvation sheath, transforming them into contact ion pairs and aggregate structures, while residual VC monomers with low hindrance expel solvents and relax the solvation sheath. These concerted dynamics reduce solvent coordination around Na + , promote anion participation, and form a robust polymer-rich gradient interphase, yielding a high ionic conductivity of 2.31 mS cm −1 at 25°C. As a result, at −30°C, the Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 ||Na full cell achieves outstanding cycling stability (1000 cycles with 97% capacity retention at 3.8 V, and 93.3% retention even at 4.2 V after 300 cycles), and a remarkable rate capability of 20 C. This study provides crucial design guidance for durable SSMBs in extreme-environment applications.
authors: Wanting Wu, Ying Xiao, Gang He, Ruxue Ruan, Xinyu Wang, Yu Yang, Yiming Fang, Shimou Chen

10.1002/adfm.78049.title: Polarization Switching of Layer-Degenerate Valley Trions in Even-Layered MoSe2
10.1002/adfm.78049.abstract: ABSTRACT The valley-coupled tightly bound electrons and holes in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) lead to a rich spectrum of valley many-body complexes with intricate fine structures. Introducing layer degrees of freedom in multilayer systems offers additional control over valley polarization and coherence of excitonic complexes via layer-valley coupling. In this study, we investigate the layer degenerate states in even-layer MoSe 2 , in contrast to odd-layer with non-degeneracy. Through photoluminescence (PL) and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy, we reveal that even-layer MoSe 2 predominantly forms robust trions at room temperature, unlike the excitons in odd-layer. We identify a novel interlayer trion in even-layer: the layer degenerate valley trion, characterized by a larger binding energy than intralayer trions in odd-layer. Our dynamical analysis uncovers a direct formation process with faster time for these trions, driven by strong interlayer coupling within a layer degenerate valley. Additionally, we demonstrate switching between layer-degenerate and non-degenerate trions with valley polarization ranging from 0% to 25%, enabled by electrically tunable layer degeneracy and Berry curvature. These findings provide insights into the role of layer degeneracy in many-body complex formation and open new avenues for quantum information modulation.
authors: Wenwei Chen, Qianqian Mo, Junfeng Tu, Shichao Yang, Qiuyan Wang, Junbin Lin, Xingzhi Wang, Jingying Zheng, Jiajie Pei, Hongbing Zhan, Yuerui Lu

10.1002/adfm.78053.title: Electrocapillary Metal Expulsion in Ga-Bi-Sn-Pb Liquid Alloy System
10.1002/adfm.78053.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocapillary metal expulsion has recently emerged as a promising low-temperature approach for separating metals from liquid alloys. However, prior studies have been largely limited to binary and ternary systems in aqueous electrolytes, where selectivity is primarily governed by intrinsic surface-energy differences of the constituent solute metals. Here, we extend this framework to a multicomponent quaternary Ga-Bi-Sn-Pb liquid alloy and demonstrate that electrolyte composition provides an additional parameter for controlling expulsion behavior. Under cathodic polarization of the liquid metal-electrolyte interface, electrocapillary charging reduces interfacial tension and promotes surface over-enrichment (supersaturation), leading to interfacial instability and the expulsion of solute metals as nanoparticles. The expulsion sequence is governed by the combined effects of surface energy and excess Gibbs free energy, following the order Bi → Pb → Sn → Ga in non-aqueous electrolytes. In contrast, aqueous electrolytes enable selective suppression of Pb expulsion and cation-dependent control over Bi and Sn separation. By exploiting this electrolyte-dependent behavior, two protocols are established: a single-electrolyte approach for rapid preconcentration and a stepwise electrolyte-switching strategy for high-purity separation, yielding Bi (>98 wt.%), Sn (∼88-92 wt.%), and Pb (>95 wt.%). This work establishes electrocapillary refining as a low-temperature tunable platform for selective metal recovery from multicomponent liquid alloys.

10.1002/adfm.78056.title: Natural Light Emission via Quantized Anderson Localized States in 2D Amorphous Semiconductor Heterojunctions
10.1002/adfm.78056.abstract: ABSTRACT Nowadays, the full-spectrum artificial lighting technology that approaches the solar spectrum has become an important issue in the field of lighting. Yet, to date, the development of full-spectrum white-light-emitting diodes (WLEDs) remains hindered by the fixed band gaps of conventional semiconductors and the synthetic challenges of certain specific-color phosphors, resulting in poor spectral tenability and far deviation from the solar spectrum. Herein, based on first-principles calculations, we propose a new conceptual scheme to potentially achieve full-spectrum white light emission via two-dimensional (2D) amorphous heterojunction (a-SiC/a-MoS 2 ), which intrinsically emits broadband white light closely matching the D65 standard source. We further reveal that the underlying mechanism of full-spectrum emission stems from two aspects: firstly, the quantum confinement effects in 2D amorphous heterojunctions lead to the formation of a series of discrete and strongly localized Anderson tail states in their bandgaps; secondly, the disordered structure breaks the orbital symmetry, which fully enables transitions of these states that maybe forbidden in crystalline counterparts. Thus, the combined effect of the two not only allows for sufficient transition energy levels, but also modulates the spectral distribution. Our work opens a new approach for full-spectrum artificial lighting, with promising implications for the advancement of high-quality lighting.
authors: Yanhao Song, Wenqi Xiong, Chongze Wang, Yangyang Guo, Liying Zhang, Rui Zhu, Liangliang Liu, Xue Li, Xiaowei Huang, Peng Lv, Jun-Hyung Cho, Chang Liu, Zhenyu Zhang, Yu Jia

10.1002/adfm.78058.title: Wood-Derived Separators: Cost-Centric Material Design for Zinc-Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78058.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-metal batteries (AZMBs) are regarded as a promising solution for grid-scale energy storage owing to intrinsic safety, high energy density, and low cost. Yet, their commercialization remains limited by an unexpected bottleneck: a lack of decisive cost advantage over commercialized lithium-ion batteries. Here, we reveal that the separator-rather than the electrode materials-dominates the cell-level cost of AZMBs, accounting for half of the total cost in practical pouch cells. To overcome this constraint, we introduce a wood-derived separator that synergistically integrates cost reduction with performance optimization. By delignifying and sulfonating natural wood, the resulting wood-derived separator preserves vertically aligned, low-tortuosity microchannels that homogenize/stabilize Zn 2+ flux and suppress concentration polarization on zinc metal surface, while sulfonate functionalities promote [Zn(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+ desolvation and inhibit hydrogen evolution. Consequently, zinc-metal half-cells exhibit dendrite-free cycling over 750 h under harsh conditions (DOD: 50%, 10 mA cm −2 /5 mAh cm −2 ), while full Zn-I 2 cells deliver 6300 stable cycles at 1 A g −1 with a capacity retention of 91.8%. Notably, this strategy substantially cuts separator costs relative to commercial glass fiber (CGF) separators and potentially lowers the total battery cost by approximately half based on projected component-level cost analysis, offering a cost-effective route to boost AZMB competitiveness.
authors: Lichen Jin, Changlai Wang, Lei Zhang, Derek Ho, Haibo Hu

10.1002/adfm.78061.title: Beyond Conventional Assessments: An Automated Framework for OSC Film Quality Evaluation via Asymmetric Attention Networks and Energy-Entropy Characterization
10.1002/adfm.78061.abstract: ABSTRACT As organic solar cell efficiency exceeds 20%, precise nanoscale morphology regulation is a bottleneck. Conventional AFM-based morphological analysis commonly uses R q , yet this statistical metric often averages out sparse but disruptive topological defects, such as nanoscale pin-holes and islands, beneath a flat baseline. These deceptive morphologies induce high-density trap states and severe leakage pathways, causing films with identical R q values to exhibit drastically divergent device performances. To address this challenge, we propose an automated AFM surface-defect analysis framework. Under this framework, we first developed an asymmetric attention network, Asym-FLAANet, for high-precision pixel-level segmentation of complex topological defects in atomic force microscopy images, achieving a test-set Intersection over Union of 0.898. Second, utilizing the segmented masks, we construct the Energy-Entropy Defect Characterization Function (EEDCF). By non-linearly coupling microscopic morphological energy and macroscopic systemic disorder, EEDCF achieves multi-dimensional quantification of intrinsic film quality and builds a precise bridge between film morphology and optoelectronic performance. EEDCF scores demonstrate a high positive correlation with device efficiency, yielding a Pearson coefficient of 0.897 and achieving precise quantification of film quality that traditional metrics fail to capture. We integrated this system into an App as a digital tool to assist in screening high-performance optoelectronic devices.
authors: Yin Wang, Qian Kang, Jianqiu Wang, KaiJie Yuan, Jianhui Hou

10.1002/adfm.78064.title: In-Plane Organic Ferroelectric Memtransistor Arrays for Temporal Optoelectronic Processing
10.1002/adfm.78064.abstract: ABSTRACT Encoding temporal optical information in solid-state hardware requires devices that can locally integrate light sensing, nonvolatile memory, and tunable relaxation dynamics. However, existing optoelectronic memristive architectures still face two key limitations: sneak-path interference in dense arrays and limited control over the photoresponse dynamics of persistent-photoconductive materials. Here, we report an in-plane organic ferroelectric optoelectronic memtransistor array based on a diisopropylammonium bromide (DIPAB)/In 2 O 3 heterostructure. The in-plane polarization of DIPAB nonvolatilely modulates carrier transport and interfacial barriers, while the out-of-plane bottom gate independently regulates the ultrathin In 2 O 3 channel. This orthogonal field configuration decouples ferroelectric memory from gate control, enabling intrinsic selection without disturbing stored states. The monolithic transistor-memristor architecture suppresses sneak-path currents in a 32 × 32 addressable array with a 91.3% device yield. Coupling ferroelectric polarization with persistent photoconductivity further produces programmable self-driven photoresponses and gate-tunable relaxation dynamics. Dynamic handwritten-digit demonstrations show photoresponsivity-weighted temporal encoding for recognition and early prediction, establishing a scalable memtransistor platform for temporal optoelectronic information processing.
authors: Chenxu Sheng, Jiawen Chen, Shuwei Zhang, Shoaib Awan, Weiao Chen, Dacheng Xia, Lele Shan, Xu Zhu, Ye Lu, Zhi-Jun Qiu, Chunxiao Cong, Shisheng Xiong, Ran Liu, Laigui Hu

10.1002/adfm.78070.title: Logic-Gating Self-Erasing Encryption Specialty Paper by Temporal Coupling of Fluorescence and Phosphorescence
10.1002/adfm.78070.abstract: ABSTRACT Temporally coupled intelligent fluorescence and phosphorescence signals provide a promising strategy for constructing complex logic-gating technologies that enhance information encryption security. Herein, a logic-gated self-erasing encryption specialty paper (LGSEP) was developed by embedding pH-responsive atomically precise gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) into a room-temperature phosphorescent cellulose nanofiber matrix. The phosphorescent cellulose nanofibers emitted green or blue phosphorescence through regulation of the chromophore molecular structure, with a visible afterglow duration of up to 11 s and a maximum phosphorescence quantum yield of 21.08%. These properties could be attributed to the rigid cellulose microenvironment, which effectively suppresses nonradiative transitions. Ingeniously, the fluorescence of the AuNCs gradually decreased from red emission to complete quenching as the pH shifted from acidic to alkaline conditions. Meanwhile, the fluorescence color of the specialty paper could be tuned from blue to purple or red by adjusting the volume ratio of phosphorescent materials to AuNCs from 1:1 to 1:6, while the phosphorescence color remained unchanged. By leveraging the intelligent response and color adjustability of the system, combinations of AND, NOT, OR, XOR, and NOR logic-gate operations were implemented, enabling rapid logical information encoding. This work provides a strategy for the development of special paper with self-erasing encryption technology of logic gates.
authors: Hongli Dai, Hui Liu, Lei Wang, Xueying Xie, Guoguo Chang, Hongxiang Zhu, Hui He

10.1002/adfm.78072.title: Intermetallic Bond Mediated Singlet Oxygen Generation System for Emerging Pollutants Detoxification in Carbon-Neutral Water Purification
10.1002/adfm.78072.abstract: ABSTRACT Mineralization-driven advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) effectively remove emerging pollutants but often require substantial energy input and generate considerable carbon emissions, conflicting with carbon-neutrality goals. Here, we develop a transformation-focused AOP based on cobalt-doped lanthanum oxycarbonate (Co-LC), which activates peroxymonosulfate (PMS) to selectively generate singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ). Experimental and theoretical results reveal that Co-La bonding interactions reconfigure the local electronic environment, stabilize high-valent O* intermediates, and lower the energy barrier for 1 O 2 formation. The Co-LC/PMS system exhibits a transformation rate 49.23 times that of pristine LC and selectively destroys the carcinogenic amino and naphthalene moieties of 1-naphthylamine. Ecotoxicological assays using Chlorella vulgaris confirm complete elimination of biological risks, with physiological indicators returning to baseline levels after treatment. A continuous-flow packed-bed reactor maintained >94% removal efficiency for 37 days and increased the BOD 5 /COD ratio of real wastewater from 0.25 to 0.50. Life-cycle assessment further shows 85.6% lower CO 2 emissions and reduced operating costs compared with the Co 3 O 4 /PMS system. This study establishes a low-carbon detoxification strategy that prioritizes toxicity elimination over complete mineralization for sustainable water purification.
authors: Jing Li, Pengfei Wang, Huaizhu Wang, Wuxuan Tu, Zhengkun Yu, Ligang Wang, Weigao Zhao, Zhong Jin, Sihui Zhan

10.1002/adfm.78073.title: Extraordinary Thermal Radiation Suppression Enables High-Entropy Oxide Ceramics for Ultrahigh-Temperature Protection up to 2000 K
10.1002/adfm.78073.abstract: ABSTRACT The escalating energy crisis and the demand for thermal protection under extreme environments require materials that effectively suppress heat transport while maintaining long-term thermal stability. However, thermal insulation ceramics inherently suffer from the dual challenge of simultaneously inhibiting lattice heat transfer and radiative heat transfer. Here, we establish a synergistic regulation of solid-state and radiative heat transfer through rare-earth site compositional screening and entropy engineering. This principle informs the development of a physics-informed constrained random forest model for predicting wavelength-dependent infrared radiation properties in the RE 3 TaO 7 system, facilitating efficient screening of candidate compositions. High-throughput screening of 504 structural variants has led to the identification of 21 candidates with a representative high-entropy ceramic of (Nd 0.2 Sm 0.2 Gd 0.2 Dy 0.2 Y 0.2 ) 3 TaO 7 that exhibits ultralow near-infrared transmittance (< 1% over 0.78-2.5 µm), high broadband emissivity (> 0.9 over 2.5-14 µm) and low radiative thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m −1 K −1 at 1273 K. This work makes progress in high-entropy thermal-protective ceramics for extreme environments and establishes a general framework for advanced thermal insulation materials.
authors: Enyu Xie, Shuqi Wang, Qiancheng Zhao, Zijian Peng, Jingran Guo, Guoliang Chen, Yongchun Zou, Qingyuan Zhao, Zhiyun Ye, Jingchi Mu, Junteng Yao, Xiang Xu, Jiahu Ouyang, Dechang Jia, Yu Zhou, Yaming Wang

10.1002/adfm.78074.title: A Self-Powered and Rechargeable Multimodal Hydrogel Sensor with Decoupled Oxygen and Temperature Sensing
10.1002/adfm.78074.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable self-powered sensors capable of monitoring multiple physiological signals are highly desirable for next-generation healthcare electronics, yet achieving decoupled multi-signal sensing within a single compact system remains challenging. Here, we report a self-powered, rechargeable multimodal soft sensor (SRMS sensor) based on a multilayered zinc-air battery design for decoupled O 2 and temperature monitoring. The SRMS sensor utilizes a potassium polyacrylate/polyacrylamide hydrogel as the polyelectrolyte, and employs a Co 3 O 4 /graphene-coated nickel foam cathode for O 2 concentration monitoring, as well as a Zn-electrodeposited graphite film anode for temperature sensing. It is demonstrated that the sensor can be used for contactless temperature-sensing, thermal imaging, and information input through sensor-array integration. During the respiratory gas monitoring, the SRMS sensor shows decoupled negative and positive responses of relative current change upon O 2 and temperature stimuli. The SRMS sensor also successfully distinguishes different respiratory states, identifies sleep-related respiratory disturbance events, and monitors skin-temperature variations during sleep. This work provides a novel strategy for constructing multimodal self-powered soft sensors with decoupled sensing capability, which shows promising applications in wearable healthcare monitoring and contactless information interaction.
authors: Jiamin Wu, Xiangke Wang, Bo Liu, Runing Cao, Gengsheng Weng

10.1002/adfm.78077.title: Trans-Reflective Dichroic Display-Integrated Colorful Semi-Transparent Organic Photovoltaic Glass
10.1002/adfm.78077.abstract: ABSTRACT Display-integrated organic photovoltaic (OPV) glass merges building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) and display technologies, integrating power generation, visualization and aesthetics. To holistically assess the performance of colorful semi-transparent OPV glass, particularly the trade-off among power conversion efficiency (PCE), transmission (T), and color purity (CP), we first introduce a comprehensive figure of merit (FoM = PCE×T MAX ×CP) and demonstrate an optimized antisymmetric metal-dielectric-metal-dielectric color filter designed to enhance these parameters simultaneously. By depositing a top dielectric layer with a thickness of λ /4 n , we achieve optical field truncation at the dielectric-metal interface, enhance the reflection of non-resonance wavelength. This results in significantly improved transmission, color purity at the target wavelength, external quantum efficiency, and overall FoM. The resulting double-sided heterochromatic Janus structure also enables trans-reflective dual-mode display functionality, achieving record FoM values of 4.71%, 2.04%, and 2.29% for blue, green, and red semi-transparent OPVs, respectively, which are among the highest reported to date for such devices. Additionally, the fabricated photovoltaic glasses exhibit exceptional ultraviolet blocking (94.2%) and near-infrared rejection (99.0%), along with improved thermal insulation (reducing temperature rise by 1.6°C). This work advances multifunctional BIPV glass with photoprotection, energy harvesting, aesthetic coloring, and self-powered dichroic display.
authors: Ruiqi Tian, Ningning Liang, Yiming Chen, Tianci Zhao, Xinghao Guo, Tianrui Zhai, Jianhui Hou

10.1002/adfm.78080.title: Exciton Dissociation Strategy-Guided Design of High-Sensitivity COF-Based Gas Sensors
10.1002/adfm.78080.abstract: ABSTRACT Exciton binding energy acts as a key modulator of the optoelectronic performance of semiconductor devices. Nevertheless, dedicated research addressing its impacts on gas sensing reactions for photoexcited semiconductor gas sensors is rarely reported. To uncover the intrinsic correlation between exciton effects and gas-solid interfacial reactions, we rationally design Ni coordinated donor-acceptor (D-A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs), which effectively promote spatial charge rearrangement, weaken the strong Coulombic interaction of Frenkel excitons, and reduce the exciton binding energy ( E b ). This modification not only enhances NO 2 adsorption at Ni active sites but also enables the directional, rapid migration of photogenerated election toward target NO 2 molecules. As a result, the fabricated COF-based micro-electromechanical-system (MEMS) sensor achieves a high sensitivity of 52 to 10 ppm NO 2 and an ultralow limit of detection of 84 ppt, representing a state-of-the-art performance among the reported COF/MOF-based gas-sensing devices. Encouragingly, we also verify that this exciton engineering strategy enables versatile modulation of gas sensing kinetics, with broad applicability extending to metal sulfides, graphitic carbon nitride polymers, metal halides, metal oxides, and so on. As a proof-of-concept, we built a wireless robotic platform integrating MEMS sensors and AI algorithm, achieving 98.35% mixed-gas discrimination accuracy for next-generation hazardous gas detection technology.
authors: Hongtao Jiang, Duo Zhang, Xueyu Wang, Tingting Zhou, Wang Li, Yu Gong, Pengjia Qi, Yang Chen, Ying Xu, Shuao Wang, Tong Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78086.title: Space-Confined Kinetic Growth of Thick 2D Perovskite Single Crystals for High-Performance X-Ray Detection
10.1002/adfm.78086.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) perovskites have emerged as promising scintillators for ultrafast X-ray imaging due to their unique quantum confinement effects. However, their intrinsic thermodynamic growth habits, driven by highly anisotropic chemical bond strengths, typically restrict crystals to thin, plate-like morphologies, which limits their X-ray stopping power and overall light yield. Here, we report a space-confined kinetic manipulation strategy to circumvent the conventional thermodynamic thickness limitations, enabling the growth of macroscopically thick phenethylammonium lead bromide single crystals (PEA 2 PbBr 4 SCs). By reallocating chemical potential gradients and maintaining a stable metastable window, we successfully accelerated longitudinal growth along the ( 00l ) facets, achieving crystals with thicknesses exceeding 3.2 mm and a low lateral-to-longitudinal aspect ratio (<3). The resulting SCs exhibit exceptional structural quality, and the enhanced X-ray attenuation in these thick SCs leads to a superior light yield of 37 500 photons MeV −1 , doubling that of the thin counterparts (0.6 mm, 15 224 photons MeV −1 ). This work provides a robust pathway for synthesizing thick 2D perovskite SCs for high-performance radiation detection and imaging without compromising their inherent exciton confinement advantages.
authors: Jiaxin Wen, Yuhao Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Mengling Xia

10.1002/adfm.78088.title: Mechanically Powered Piezoelectric Pulsed-Field System for Tumor Ablation
10.1002/adfm.78088.abstract: ABSTRACT Pulsed electric-field tumor ablation enables localized treatment but depends on bulky, costly high-voltage equipment, limiting use to specialized settings. Here, we developed a portable, mechanically powered piezoelectric pulsed-field (MPPF) system based on an ultra-low-cost commercial piezoelectric igniter. Through mechano-electrical transduction, charge accumulation and pulse modulation, discrete thumb actuations were converted into kilovolts-level, microsecond exponential-decay pulses without batteries or an external power supply. Coupled with a microneedle electrode array, the system generated tissue electric fields exceeding irreversible electroporation (IRE) thresholds. Compared with repeated-dose chemotherapy, MPPF monotherapy outperformed dacarbazine in mouse B16F10 melanoma and performed comparably to docetaxel in 4T1 breast tumors. A single treatment combining MPPF with intratumoral Ca 2 + produced greater tumor growth inhibition than the corresponding multicycle chemotherapy regimens in both models, with macroscopic tumor disappearance by day 2 in >80% of mice. Complete local regression persisted at the study endpoint in 17% and 50% of mice with B16F10 and 4T1 tumors, respectively, with 100% survival in both groups. This treatment was also associated with increased intratumoral CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell infiltration, increased serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), and reduced interleukin-10 (IL-10) levels. This ultra-low-cost (<2 US dollars) platform enables mechanically powered high-voltage tumor ablation, with potential applicability to decentralized cancer treatment in resource-limited settings.
authors: Jingwen Hu, Linyu You, Huan Yu, Dongmei Cun, Rafael V. Davalos, Dengning Xia

10.1002/adfm.78089.title: Chiral Supramolecular Electrolyte Engineering Enables Ultra-Long-Cycling Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78089.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) is severely hampered by unregulated dendrite growth and parasitic hydrogen evolution reaction at Zn anodes. Electrolyte additive engineering affords a promising strategy. Herein, a bio-derived composite additive is fabricated via intermolecular proton transfer between chitosan and L-ascorbic acid, yielding chiral supramolecular associations supported by a rigid macromolecular backbone. Simulations and experiments verify a dual-regulation mechanism: the chiral configuration enables stereoselective adsorption on Zn anodes, forming a protective interphase with ultralow lattice mismatch ( δ < 20%) with the Zn (101) facet, which thermodynamically favors selective nucleation and simultaneously suppresses interfacial side reactions. Meanwhile, the chiral supramolecular associations form continuous polar channels, facilitating Zn 2+ desolvation by partially displacing coordinated water and reconstructing the hydrogen-bonding network of the electrolyte, thereby inhibiting dendrite growth. Furthermore, the strong binding affinity between Zn 2+ and chiral polar groups further facilitates uniform Zn deposition kinetics. Consequently, Zn//Zn symmetric cells achieve an ultralong cycling lifespan exceeding 4900 h at 1.0 mA cm −2 , along with the Zn//Cu asymmetric cells showing exceptional reversibility, and both Zn//NH 4 V 4 O 10 and Zn//I 2 full cells deliver exceptional cycling stability. This chirality-driven crystal facet engineering strategy provides valuable insights for constructing advanced AZIBs.
authors: Geng Liu, Li Li, Haochang Li, Jinmei Tian, Xiaopeng Yang, Cuihua An, Linrui Hou, Changzhou Yuan

10.1002/adfm.78090.title: Interfacial Electric Field From a Dual-Ion-Mediated Enables Nitrile Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78090.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrile-based solvents are regarded as promising candidates for high-voltage batteries owing to their exceptional anodic stability. However, their application in Li metal batteries (LMBs) is hindered by severe corrosion of the Li anode by nitriles, which fail to form stable interfacial layers. Herein, we propose a dual-ion-mediated interfacial electric field strategy by incorporating 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([EMIm] + BF 4 − ) into succinonitrile (SN)-based electrolyte. The cation-induced interfacial electrostatic field excludes free nitrile molecules from the anode region, preventing SN from attacking the Li metal, while simultaneously homogenizing Li + flux to suppress dendrite growth. Meanwhile, the preferential adsorption of anions (FSI − /BF 4 − ) and partial nitrile species on the positively charged cathode facilitates the construction of an inorganic-rich cathode electrolyte interphase originating from anions and solvents. Such interphase effectively suppresses interfacial side reactions including self-discharging, transition metal dissolution, and cathode structure degradation. As a result, the optimized electrolyte enables a 4.5 V-charged 2 Ah Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cell to maintain stable cycling for over 120 cycles with 95.2% capacity retention. Remarkably, the corresponding pouch cell withstands nail penetration without ignition or explosion. This work presents an electrostatic field regulation strategy that decouples electrolyte safety from Li compatibility, paving the way for practical high-voltage LMBs utilizing nitrile-based electrolytes.
authors: Mingming Fang, Can Yang, Jinmin Wang, Zijun Wei, Yongzhen Zhu, Keyu Tao, Yurong Ren

10.1002/adfm.78095.title: Ultrafast and Stress-Adaptive Magnesium Conversion in Hollow NiS2@N-Doped Carbon Cathodes via Interfacial Ni─N Bonding Modulation
10.1002/adfm.78095.abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion-type nickel sulfide (NiS 2 ) is a compelling cathode for rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) owing to high theoretical capacity, yet suffers from severe volume changes, polysulfide shuttling, metal dissolution, and sluggish kinetics caused by strong Ni─S bonds. To overcome these challenges, the interfacial optimization and bond regulation are of crucial importance. Herein, nitrogen-doped carbon (NC)-armored NiS 2 hollow microspheres (NiS 2 @NC) is designed with interfacial Ni─N bonding modulation. The introduced Ni─N bonds elongate and weaken adjacent Ni─S bonds, significantly lowering the conversion energy barrier and accelerating Mg 2 + storage kinetics. The synergistic effect of chemical anchoring (Ni─N bonds) and physical confinement (NC coating) suppress side reactions and shuttle effects, stabilizing the cathode-electrolyte interface (CEI) and electrode structure. The unique hollow structure further promotes rapid Mg 2+ diffusion and accommodates the volume variation. Experimental and calculation results confirm that NiS 2 @NC material possesses excellent stress-adaptive ability, mitigating volume fluctuations and preserving structural integrity. As a result, the NiS 2 @NC cathode delivers a high specific capacity (392 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 ), excellent long-term cyclability (capacity retention of 92.8% after 3200 cycles at 5 A g −1 ), and superior rate capability. This interfacial bonding engineering strategy provides a universal pathway for designing high-performance and robust conversion-type electrodes in RMBs.
authors: Yiyi Wang, Zhenfeng Guan, Lingxiao Luo, Guiyang Gao, Li Xia, Hongfei Zheng, Jiajia Han, Jie Lin, Laisen Wang, Baihua Qu, Dong-Liang Peng, Qingshui Xie

10.1002/adfm.78096.title: Spatiotemporally Hierarchical Regulation of Zinc Anode Interface via a Multifunctional Additive for High-Durability Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78096.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of aqueous zinc-ion batteries is severely hindered by spatiotemporally complex interfacial instabilities at the zinc anode, which cannot be sufficiently addressed by conventional single-function additives. Here, we present a novel “spatiotemporally hierarchical regulation” strategy that achieves precise, full-lifecycle intervention in Zn 2+ deposition through a rationally designed multifunctional additive, (3-amino-3-carboxypropyl) dimethylsulfonium chloride (ACDC). Distinct from conventional single-function additives, ACDC integrates coordinating and electrostatic functionalities within a unified molecular framework, allowing relay-type regulation across the bulk electrolyte, electric double layer, and electrode interface. This synergistic, multi-tiered regulation fundamentally reshapes the Zn deposition pathway, enabling stable Zn plating/stripping cycling for over 2100 h at 5 mA cm −2 . Full cells deliver high-rate capability, suppressed self-discharge (93% capacity retention after 24 h), and prolonged cycling durability. Meanwhile, the pouch cells exhibit a capacity retention of 84.6% after 100 cycles. Beyond performance enhancement, this work establishes a general molecular design paradigm for spatiotemporal regulation of electrochemical interfaces, offering insights into electrolyte engineering for high-safety, long-lifespan aqueous energy storage systems.

10.1002/adfm.78097.title: Interlayer Metal-Ligand Coordination in Covalent Organic Frameworks: A Structural Strategy for Enhanced Nitrate Reduction Electrocatalysis
10.1002/adfm.78097.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient multielectron electrocatalysis in layered covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is frequently limited by weak cross-plane charge delivery to pore-confined active sites. Herein, we report the construction of two metal-bridged COFs (Py1-COF-Cu and Py2-COF-Cu) by incorporating nitrogen-containing heterocycles to facilitate interlayer Cu─N coordination. This design generates continuous linear coordination chains within the 1D channels while maintaining high intrinsic porosity. Synchrotron XANES confirms the Cu─N coordination environment, and DFT reveals realigned frontier-orbital energetics together with pronounced redistribution of electron density along the interlayer direction. Among them, the optimized Py2-COF-Cu serves as a highly active cathode catalyst for the electroreduction of nitrate to ammonia in neutral media. It delivers a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 87.8% and a peak NH 3 yield rate of 4964.6 µmol h −1 mg −1 at -1.0 V vs. RHE, comparable to leading Cu-based NO 3 RR catalysts. This interlayer coordination motif provides a structural lever to couple ordered porosity with effective cross-plane charge transport for demanding multielectron reactions.
authors: Mingqing Shan, Jinhao Guo, Zhixin Zhang, Jie Zhou, Lin Li, Longyu Cheng, Xiuyang Zou, Siyu Guo

10.1002/adfm.78100.title: Integrated Molecular-Structural Design of “Mille-Feuille” Triboelectric Sensors for Self-Powered Tactile Perception and Material Recognition
10.1002/adfm.78100.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving human-skin-like multidimensional tactile perception in self-powered electronics remains fundamentally constrained by the intrinsic trade-offs among sensitivity, mechanical compliance, and electrical output. To overcome these bottlenecks, a biomimetic “mille-feuille” triboelectric sensor is engineered via hierarchical nanofibrous membranes, transitioning conventional 2D interfacial contact into 3D volumetric nesting to significantly increase the effective contact area. Incorporating a zwitterionic polymer poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (PSBMA) into the triboelectric matrix enables multiscale enhancement of dielectric polarization, charge trapping, interfacial contact, and mechanical robustness. This integrated design concurrently improves surface charge density and contact area, culminating in a remarkable 2.16-fold enhancement in triboelectric performance compared to pristine counterparts. The sensor exhibits an ultra-low detection limit (1.21 Pa), a broad working range (2.45-100 kPa), fast response and recovery times (35 and 29 ms), and excellent durability over 10 000 cycles. Beyond conventional motion monitoring, integrating this sensor with a robotic gripper and a convolutional neural network (CNN) enables active material cognition. The system demonstrated accurate recognition and sorting of geometrically identical objects, reaching 100% test accuracy under current dataset and sorting of geometrically identical objects based on their material-dependent tactile responses during physical interaction. This work provides a robust material-algorithm synergistic paradigm for intelligent robotics and tactile sensing applications.
authors: Chunyan Li, Wenlong Pang, Zhiguang Li, Shanshan Shao, Luping Yao, Lei Dai, Yun Wu, Dan Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78101.title: Neighboring Copper Atoms Enhance Valence-Adaptive Catalysis of Cobalt for Boosted Polysulfide Redox Kinetics
10.1002/adfm.78101.abstract: ABSTRACT Reversible polysulfide redox kinetics critically govern the capacity, rate capability, and cycle life of sodium-sulfur (Na-S) batteries. Here we report a single-atom catalyst featuring S-bridged Cu-Co dual sites anchored on N-doped Ti 3 C 2 S 2 MXene. The sulfur cathode delivers a high specific capacity of 573.8 mAh g −1 at 5.0 A g −1 with an ultralow capacity decay of ≈0.0037% per cycle over 15,000 cycles. Experimental and DFT calculations reveal that Co serves as the valence-adaptive catalytic center, donating electrons to sulfur species during discharge and accepting them during charge, corresponding to the Co 1.32+ ↔ Co 1.58+ valence transition. Neighboring Cu atoms amplify this behavior by modulating the electronic structure of Co, as evidenced by a larger Co valence fluctuation in CuCo-NSM (Δ = 0.26) than in Co-NSM (Δ = 0.18). Additionally, the Cu-Co dual sites accelerate sodium-ion diffusion and facilitate the reverse polysulfide conversion (Na 2 S→Na 2 S 2 ) during charge. The synergistic valence-adaptive catalysis arising from the Cu-Co dual-metal sites significantly promotes the kinetics of polysulfide conversion, offering a feasible atomic-level design strategy for high-performance metal-sulfur batteries.
authors: Ronghui Liu, Ya Gao, Yuxuan Gao, Hongfei Gu, Zhen Fang, Zhimei Sun, Jianbo Wu, Wei Zhou, Lin Guo

10.1002/adfm.78102.title: A Quasi-1D TiS3/2H-MoTe2 van der Waals Heterostructure for Intelligent Sensing With Decoupled Perception and Memory Functions
10.1002/adfm.78102.abstract: ABSTRACT The relentless demand for real-time, high-dimensional optical information processing is fundamentally hindered by the physical separation of sensing, storage, and computing in conventional architectures, which incurs prohibitive energy and latency overheads. Here, we break this paradigm by constructing a quasi-one-dimensional TiS 3 /2H-MoTe 2 van der Waals heterostructure that intrinsically decouples and synergistically couples two distinct physical mechanisms of anisotropic carrier transport for polarization-sensitive perception and ion migration/trapping for nonvolatile memory. This TiS 3 /2H-MoTe 2 heterostructure simultaneously delivers self-powered, near-infrared polarization-senstive photodetection with comparable performance (a dichroic ratio of 7.14, responsivity of 198 mA/W, detectivity of 6.9 × 10 11 Jones, and a fast 61/67 µs response at 1064 nm), alongside robust memristive switching behavior (ON/OFF ratio exceeding 10 5 and retention >2300 s). The versatility is governed by decoupled driving forces of transient photogenerated carrier dynamics and persistent electric-field-driven ion and hole migration, enabling physically independent yet co-located perception and memory channels. Beyond functional synergy, this platform executes a complete bioinspired cognitive chain, from threshold-triggered nociception and injury-induced sensitization to real-time skylight-polarization navigation, all within a single device. Our work transcends post-processing compensation and functional additivity, establishing an intrinsic, intelligent paradigm for in-sensor computing with immediate implications for edge AI, autonomous systems, and neuromorphic electronics.
authors: Peng Guo, Lijian Li, Tao He, Yalin Zhai, Peng Wan, Daning Shi, Mingming Jiang

10.1002/adfm.78104.title: Asymmetric Interfacial Potential Barrier Driven Photovoltaic Effect Enhancement in 2H-Stacked Bilayer MoS2
10.1002/adfm.78104.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional photovoltaic-type devices operate by artificially stacked heterostructures with atomically thin p-n junctions or non-centrosymmetric layers, in which photogenerated carriers are separated under built-in or internal electric fields. However, their photocurrent conversion efficiency is restricted by small electric field strength and large carrier recombination, which poses a major limitation with the requirement of specific 2D materials. Herein, large-area centrosymmetric 2H-stacked bilayer MoS 2 with low defect density was synthesized by slow-kinetic chemical vapor deposition and showed a remarkable photovoltaic response (0.13 mA/W at 520 nm) with a small vertical barrier of 23.2 mV. The local energy levels and doping effects derived from Raman spectroscopy and Kelvin probe force microscopy revealed the resulting sharp slope of interfacial band bending, which explains the efficient separation of photogenerated carriers by precise work function differences. A higher asymmetric barrier of 139.6 mV resulted in enhanced photocurrents in the 405-1064 nm and achieved a maximum responsivity of 0.51 mA/W at 520 nm as well as a consistent six-fold enhancement at 638 nm (0.04 to 0.24 mA/W). Our research reveals an enhanced physical mechanism with low-defect-density centrosymmetric 2D materials as photovoltaic-type layers by tuning interfacial barriers for optoelectronic devices.
authors: Cheng Li, Jing Liu, Hua Zhang, Luwei Zou, Xilong Zhou, Jialong Li, Zhihui Chen, Xiao Wang, Weigao Xu, Zheng Peng, Xiaolong Chen, Yu Zhou

10.1002/adfm.78106.title: Boosting Graphite Anode Performance in Potassium-Ion Batteries With Synergistic Six-Membered Cyclic Ether Electrolytes
10.1002/adfm.78106.abstract: ABSTRACT Graphite anode offers high theoretical capacity and low potassium storage potential, making it attractive for practical potassium-ion batteries (PIBs). Ether-based electrolytes have been widely explored in graphite anodes because of their capability in robust solid-electrolyte interphases (SEIs) formation, yet several challenges remain, including solvent co-intercalation and poor oxidation stability. Compared to widely studied five-membered cyclic ethers, the six-membered counterparts possess advantages in improving the physical properties of electrolytes and formulating weak solvating structures that are beneficial for building stable interfaces. By hybridizing two six-membered cyclic ethers, 1,3,5-trioxane and 1,3-dioxane, a thin, uniform, and inorganic-rich SEI has been constructed. Consequently, the graphite anode delivers exceptional rate capability, realizing over 230 mAh g −1 at 2 C and 150 mAh g −1 at 6 C with outstanding cycling stability. Meanwhile, the formulated electrolyte demonstrates decent stability with 3.83 V-class Prussian blue analogue cathodes, allowing the fabrication of high-voltage full cells. This work enriches ether-based electrolyte chemistry for advanced PIB development.
authors: Danni Wang, Xuyun Guo, Xiaoqiong Du, Dengyun Zhai, Valeria Nicolosi, Biao Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78109.title: Enhanced Ferroelectric Phase Formation via Local Structure Modification in the Pre-Crystalline State of Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Thin Films
10.1002/adfm.78109.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide is one of the most promising materials for non-volatile memory applications due to its stability at small size scales and compatibility with robust fabrication techniques. However, the manufacture of phase-pure ferroelectric hafnia remains an elusive challenge due to its sensitivity to synthesis and integration factors. This work reports on the use of argon plasma atomic layer annealing during atomic layer deposition growth as a route to enhance formation of the ferroelectric phase in hafnium zirconium oxide thin films. The introduction and the lengthening of the duration of atomic layer annealing enhance the ferroelectric properties of the films that form after a rapid thermal anneal. This is observed through Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and corroborated via scanning transmission electron microscopy, polarization measurements, and piezoresponse force microscopy. Qualitative analysis of the extended X-ray absorption fine structure region reveals a change in the second-nearest-neighbor environment of the absorbing species in the amorphous deposit as atomic layer annealing duration varies. This change in the local structure creates a more favorable environment for ferroelectric phase crystallization, positioning atomic layer annealing as a processing route to facilitate hafnia-based films with increased ferroelectric phase concentrations and virtually no polarization wake-up.

10.1002/adfm.78120.title: Synergy of Bulk Flexible Motif Buffer With Surface Engineering Enabling Mechanochemical Durability for Single-Crystalline Ni-Rich Layered Oxides
10.1002/adfm.78120.abstract: ABSTRACT The high specific capacity and cost efficiency of Ni-rich layered oxides render them promising cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Nevertheless, the intrinsic chemicophysical instability of Ni-rich layered oxides severely limits their application at scale. Herein, a motif buffer strategy coupled with surface engineering is proposed to improve the electrochemical performance of single-crystalline LiNi 0.83 Co 0.07 Mn 0.10 O 2 (MS-SC-NCM). The introduced Nb 5+ without d electrons in the transition metal site imparts NbO 6 octahedron motifs the capacity to buffer the local structural distortion derived from the Jahn-Teller effect in Ni 3+ -O 6 octahedrons. In addition, the tenacious Nb-O bonds with superior bond energy limit the anisotropic volume change of MS-SC-NCM and alleviate the irreversible lattice oxygen loss, thereby inhibiting the heterogeneous stress accumulation and uncontrollable structural degradation effectively. Furthermore, the constructed fast ion conductor Li 3 NbO 4 on the surface of MS-SC-NCM accelerates the Li + diffusion kinetics at the electrode-electrolyte interface and suppresses interfacial parasitic reactions. As a result, MS-SC-NCM displays excellent cyclic performance both in coin cell and pouch cell with the capacity retention of 91.54% after 150 cycles and 92.5% after 300 cycles, respectively. This work provides valuable insights for designing advanced electrode materials for next-generation LIBs.
authors: Chenrui Zeng, Ruixin Zheng, Yan Huang, Yang Zhang, Haoruo Xiao, Chaozhu Shu

10.1002/adfm.78124.title: Shear-Oxidation Regulated Liquid Metals: From High-Fidelity Patterning to Intelligent Wearable Interfaces
10.1002/adfm.78124.abstract: ABSTRACT Gallium-based liquid metals (LMs), due to their extremely high surface tension, are incompatible with conventional manufacturing processes, thereby hindering high-precision patterning and becoming a serious bottleneck for their application in flexible electronic devices. Here, we present a facile shear-oxidation modulation strategy and introduce a mass-evolution-derived effective oxide-state descriptor (Φ ox ) for quantitatively evaluating shear-conditioned liquid-metal systems. Under ambient shear, the native gallium oxide skin is continuously ruptured and incorporated into the liquid metal matrix, forming an oxide-enriched metastable microstructure. This structure enhances flow resistance, induces pronounced shear-thinning behavior, and produces a yield-like threshold, thereby suppressing surface-tension-driven relaxation. Guided by Φ ox -based state selection, we demonstrate that a representative low-Φ ox state enables stable direct writing of low-interference interconnects, whereas a representative high-Φ ox state supports blade coating combined with laser patterning for fabricating high-fidelity features and robust strain-sensing units. Further integration of these state-partitioned LM states into interference-resistant wearable gloves yields reliable multi-channel motion signals, enabling 100% gesture-recognition accuracy with a lightweight Transformer model and supporting real-time robotic-hand control. These findings highlight oxide-state engineering as a route to balance fluidity, pattern stability, and electrical functionality in Ga-based LMs, providing a foundation for scalable flexible electronics and human-machine interfaces.
authors: Jinkun Hu, Qi Wang, Dingyu Nie, Huasheng Bi, Yichuan Mao, Peiming Lei, Hongwei Sheng, Wei Lan

10.1002/adfm.78146.title: Dual-Dimensional Compositional Engineering Driven Synergistic Color Switching and Emission Enhancement in Mn(II)-Based Metal Halides
10.1002/adfm.78146.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-dimensional Mn-based organic-inorganic metal halides (OIMHs) have attracted considerable interest for optoelectronic applications owing to their unique d-d electronic transitions, environmental friendliness, and structural tunability. Nevertheless, achieving simultaneous control over emission color and intensity within a single precursor system remains challenging. Herein, we propose a dual-dimensional compositional engineering strategy based on the same precursor (C 6 H 14 ClN) to synergistically tune the luminescence properties of Mn-based OIMHs via a combined computational-experimental approach. By simply varying the molar ratio of the organic amine salt to MnCl 2 and further adding raw materials to the as-obtained products, we achieve reversible switching between (C 6 H 14 N)MnCl 3 and (C 6 H 14 N) 3 MnCl 5 , accompanied by a transition in dimensionality from 1D) to 0D), a change in Mn 2+ coordination number from 5 to 4, and a corresponding emission color shift from red to green. Moreover, substituting Cl − with Br − optimizes the Mn···Mn distance, reducing energy transfer between Mn 2+ ions. This effect effectively suppresses non-radiative recombination induced by the heavy-atom effect, thereby significantly enhancing the green emission intensity of (C 6 H 14 N) 3 MnBr 5 . This work not only elucidates the composition-structure-luminescence relationship in low-dimensional Mn(II)-based OIMHs, but also provides clear compositional engineering guidelines for designing next-generation high-performance and emission color-tunable metal halides.

10.1002/adfm.78151.title: Efficient Methylamine Electrosynthesis Enabled by Coupling Heterometallic MOF Catalyst With Integrated Reaction System
10.1002/adfm.78151.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical C-N coupling offers a sustainable pathway for organonitrogen synthesis but faces kinetic challenges in reactant activation and C-N coupling for target product generation. Herein, we report a heterometallic metal-organic framework (MOF), Cu-MIL-125, as a high-performance catalyst for selective methylamine synthesis from co-electrolysis of CO 2 and NO 3 − . In situ spectroscopic experiments and theoretical calculations unravel that the constructed heterometallic Cu-Ti sites on Cu-MIL-125 synergistically promote key * HCHO/ * NH 2 OH intermediate generation and boost their C-N coupling and hydrogenation energetics, while simultaneously facilitating reactant accumulation and side reaction suppression. Moreover, by integrating plasma-assisted nitrogen fixation, cathodic methylamine electrosynthesis coupled with anodic glycerol oxidation in a zero-gap MEA electrolyzer, we achieve an unprecedented Faradaic efficiency of 86.28% with a methylamine yield rate of 132.02 mmol h −1 g −1 , representing one of the best performances thus far. Our strategy establishes a scalable, economically viable, and carbon-neutral paradigm for the decentralized synthesis of organonitrogen chemicals.
authors: Chenguang Yin, Changrong Hao, Shiyao Shang, Hu Zhang, Dongwei Ma, Ke Chu

10.1002/adfm.78155.title: Molecular Design of 1D Iron-Based MOF for High-Performance Oxygen Evolution Reaction
10.1002/adfm.78155.abstract: ABSTRACT We designed a series of one-dimensional metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) on nickel-iron foam (NiFe foam) surfaces via molecular tailoring and assembly to achieve enhanced electrocatalytic performance. Molecular tailoring was accomplished by introducing secondary metal ions (Ni or CoNi) and substituting bulky ligands in [Fe(Htpim) 2 (HOBA) 2 ·2(H 2 O)] n ( Fe-MOF-L ; Htpim = 2,4,5-tri(4-pyridyl)-imidazole; H 2 OBA = 4,4′-oxybisbenzoic acid) with compact acetate ligands, yielding MFe-MOF-L (M═Ni or CoNi) and [Fe(Htpim) 2 (CH 3 COO) 2 ] n ( Fe-MOF) . The morphology of MOFs was tuned by varying the NiFe foam thickness and controlling reaction conditions. Synergistic etching of the substrate coupled with in situ generation of compact CH 3 COO − ligands enabled the formation of ultrafine hierarchical nanostructures. The Fe-MOF@4 mm NiFe foam catalyst exhibited ultralow overpotentials of 194, 201, and 208 mV at 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, the catalyst demonstrated excellent stability, sustaining consistent activity for 180 h in 1.0 M KOH and 150 h in alkaline natural seawater at 1000 mA cm −2 , with negligible degradation. Both experimental analyses and theoretical calculations revealed that ligand exchange to introduce compact CH 3 COO − ligands in Fe-MOF represents the most efficient approach to achieve milestone performance in MOF-based oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysis.
authors: Jiangyan Dang, Muhammad Rafiq, Wenjuan Xu, Dan Xie, Xiaoying Zhang, Wenliang Li, Jingping Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78029.title: Shallow Trap States Control Electrical Performance of Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor Thin-Film Transistors
10.1002/adfm.78029.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of n -type amorphous oxide semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) is controlled by the electronic states near the conduction band mobility edge. Here, the full subgap density of states (DoS) of amorphous InGaZnO (a-IGZO) TFTs, used in display panels and dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) development, is measured by ultrabroadband photoconduction (UP-DoS) microscopy to within 0.1 eV of the mobility edge. The measured subgap DoS for 25 TFT processing conditions accurately predicts each transfer curve, showing how shallow defect states are electron traps that rigidly tune subthreshold swing, threshold voltage, and drift mobility. For a set of TFTs, the subthreshold transfer characteristics can be simulated independently by the experimental shallow-defect DoS, with no adjustable parameters. The full transfer curve is simulated by introducing a single parameter: the conduction band tail energy. Additionally, each simulation reveals how the shallow trap density controls subthreshold behavior and can be directly extracted from transfer curves. Finally, a systematic In-enrichment study, combined with DFT+U DoS simulations, enables identification of vacancy-cation coordination environments for experimentally observed subgap peaks. The dominant trap controlling conventional a-IGZO TFT performance is centered at 0.32 eV below the conduction band mobility edge and is attributed to a Ga-Ga-In oxygen-vacancy defect.

10.1002/adfm.78048.title: Oxygen-Vacancy-Mediated Coupling of Oxide-Path and Lattice-Oxygen Mechanisms in CoFeMo Oxyhydroxide for Efficient and Stable Water Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.78048.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and stable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts must accelerate O─O bond formation while avoiding sustained lattice degradation. However, lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) often causes structural instability due to excessive consumption of lattice oxygen, whereas oxide-path mechanism (OPM) requires geometrically and electronically matched dual-site structural units, which are difficult to maintain during dynamic OER reconstruction. Here, we report an oxygen-vacancy-rich CoFeMo oxyhydroxide in which oxygen vacancies mediate dynamic OPM-LOM cooperation. Density functional theory calculations show that oxygen vacancies reshape the local coordination, charge distribution, and spin polarization around Fe/Co sites, which stabilizes the M─O─O─M intermediate required for direct O─O coupling. Electrochemical activation of a (CoFe)MoO 4 precursor yields a reconstructed oxyhydroxide containing abundant oxygen vacancies and trace residual Mo. The catalyst delivers an overpotential of 226 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and sustains 1 A cm −2 operation for over 1000 h at 1.78 V in an anion-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope-labeling differential electrochemical mass spectrometry, and electrolyte-dependent stability tests support a self-regulated vacancy cycle, in which OPM serves as the dominant O─O coupling route, while moderate LOM participation regenerates oxygen-vacancy motifs required for sustained OPM operation. These findings highlight defect-pathway coupling as a useful strategy for designing durable OER electrocatalysts.
authors: Feng Gao, Jiaqing He, Biao Wang, Xuguang Sun, Wanting Bu, Zhi Huang, Ye Wang, Chuan Liu, Yifei Sun, Mengye Wang

10.1002/adfm.78067.title: Sustainable Stabilization of Perovskite Solar Cells Using Multifunctional Ammonium Alginate for over 26% Efficiency
10.1002/adfm.78067.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite solar cells have emerged as a revolutionary photovoltaic technology due to their exceptional optoelectronic properties and low-cost fabrication processes. However, the commercialization is significantly hindered by insufficient operational stability. The inherent ionic character of the perovskite lattice renders it susceptible to degradation under thermal and environmental stresses, primarily initiated by the loss of volatile organic cations and ion migration. Although defect passivation strategies have been extensively explored, a solution that effectively addresses the thermodynamic instability of the organic cation lattice site remains highly desirable. Herein, we first introduced ammonium alginate, a benign biopolymer, as a multifunctional stabilizer, which are proposed to suppress the deprotonation of formamidinium cations, thereby anchoring the A-site, while the carboxylate groups can efficiently passivate undercoordinated Pb 2+ ions, reducing defect states. The synergistic effect, combined with the induced preferential crystallographic orientation and suppressed ion migration, significantly enhanced the device's photovoltaic performance-increasing the power conversion efficiency from 24.05% to 26.12%, with the fill factor improved from 80.2% to 85.1%. Meanwhile, the devices have also exhibited an exceptional thermal and ambient stability, retaining over 80% of their initial efficiency under accelerated thermal aging and ambient exposure.

10.1002/adfm.77807.title: Field-Free Switching of Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Devices via Symmetry Breaking: An Overview and Outlook
10.1002/adfm.77807.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-orbit torque (SOT) technology stands at the forefront of next-generation non-volatile memory and logic computing, promising superior endurance and ultrafast dynamics compared to conventional spin-transfer torque (STT) architectures. However, the persistent requirement of an external magnetic field for deterministic switching of perpendicular magnetization severely impedes high-density integration and commercial viability. This review systematically evaluates the evolutionary trajectory of symmetry-breaking strategies developed to overcome this bottleneck. The analysis progresses from early macroscopic structural engineering, such as wedged geometries and lateral asymmetries, to mesoscopic built-in effective fields driven by interfacial exchange coupling and chiral spin textures. Crucially, we identify a defining paradigm shift in the field: the transition from complex geometric modifications toward intrinsic material-level innovations, including low-symmetry crystals, vertical composition gradients (VCG), and synergistic dual-torque (STT-SOT) architectures. By resolving the trade-offs among switching efficiency, thermal stability, and structural complexity, these intrinsic and hybrid approaches offer a practical roadmap for integrating scalable, all-electrical SOT-MRAM with standard CMOS back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes. Finally, we establish a dual-track strategic roadmap: while long-term breakthroughs require parallel exploration of new exotic physics, we underscore the importance of focusing on mass production and foundry scalability at the current stage.
authors: Rundong Zhu, Sheng Wang, Zihan Deng, Kaixun Han, Guoxin Li, Xiaohang Li, Fangliang Gao, Xinman Chen, Shuti Li

10.1002/adfm.77999.title: Single-Crystal Perovskite High-Energy Radiation Detectors: From Bulk Crystals to Micro/Nano Integration
10.1002/adfm.77999.abstract: ABSTRACT High-energy radiation detection has various applications in medical imaging, industrial testing, and other fields. However, detectors made from traditional semiconductor materials struggle to meet the demands of modern applications, such as flexible wearable devices and low-cost, miniaturized detectors. To address this issue, single-crystal perovskite materials have been applied in the manufacturing of high-energy radiation detectors, owing to their enhanced optoelectronic properties and low-cost integration method. However, no review specifically discusses the relationship between crystal dimensionality, crystallinity, morphology modulation, and the performance of high-energy radiation detectors. In this review, we first systematically overview the relationship between crystal dimensionality, crystallinity, morphology modulation, and device performance in high-energy radiation detection. Then, the working mechanism and performance parameters of high-energy radiation detectors are thoroughly discussed. Furthermore, the fabrication techniques for bulk and micro/nano single-crystal perovskite are highlighted, and the influence of the nucleation and crystallization process on the fabrication of single crystals is also discussed. Moreover, the advances in high-energy radiation detectors based on single-crystal perovskite are systematically reviewed. Finally, the remaining challenges and future research prospects are presented. A detailed review of the development of perovskite single-crystal high-energy radiation detectors will inspire more researchers to join this field and highlight directions for the future.
authors: Kaixin Dong, Shasha Zhang, Yicheng Sun, Mengru Zhang, Junjie Liu, Dan Li, Zhonghao Wei, Yanlin Song, Yingjie Zhao

10.1002/adfm.78012.title: Covalent Organic Framework Polyamide Nanocomposite Membranes: From Chemical and Structural Regulation to Efficient Water Separation
10.1002/adfm.78012.abstract: ABSTRACT Membrane-based desalination and wastewater reclamation play an important role in addressing the global freshwater crisis. However, state-of-the-art polyamide (PA) composite membranes still suffer from inherent limitations, including the trade-off between permeability and selectivity, insufficient retention of small neutral solutes, susceptibility to fouling, and poor chemical stability. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), with their ordered crystalline structure, tunable pore function, and chemical stability, offer unprecedented opportunities for molecular-level regulation of PA membranes. Introducing COF nanomaterials into PA layers enables the construction of ordered transport channels for rapid water permeation and selective solute sieving. COF fillers also act as interfacial modifiers to regulate monomer diffusion and PA crosslinking during interfacial polymerization, reshaping membrane physicochemical properties. These synergistic effects simultaneously improve water permeance, solute rejection, fouling resistance, and structural stability. Given the rapid advancement of COF nanomaterials, this review summarizes progress in COF-based PA nanocomposite membranes for water separation, focusing on COF structural design, incorporation strategies, regulatory mechanisms, and the relationship between membrane structure and separation performance. Critical challenges in interfacial chemistry, scalable fabrication, and long-term stability are discussed, and future research directions toward practical applications are proposed. This review underscores the potential of COF-based PA nanocomposite membranes for efficient and sustainable water purification.
authors: Zhenxiang Pan, Adhithya Patabendige, Jian Sun, Jiang Zhan, Bizhen Zeng, Gang Han

10.1002/adfm.78038.title: Advances in Energy-Driven Atomic-Scale Post-Engineering of Nanomaterials
10.1002/adfm.78038.abstract: ABSTRACT Wet-chemical atomic-scale post-engineering can tailor nanomaterial atomic configurations and upgrade device performance, yet existing reviews only list discrete modification routes without unified energy-centered mechanisms, restricting industrial popularization. This work innovatively classifies all driving forces into chemical potential difference, thermodynamic bonding energy difference, and externally input energy. Around composition modulation, surface engineering, structural reconstruction, and interfacial assembly, the energy-driven rules of each regulation method are elaborated explicitly: chemical potential dominates lattice doping, bonding energies control surface modification, thermodynamic and external field energies induce crystal reconstruction, and weak interactions realize hierarchical nanoassembly. A complete energy mechanism system is built to unify scattered modification strategies. This work further analyzes practical prospects in catalysis, biomedicine, theranostics, and quantum devices, and systematically summarizes the critical obstacles hindering lab-to-industry translation, providing solid theoretical support for the basic research and large-scale industrialization of nanomaterial atomic post-engineering.
authors: Yujia Gao, Naiwen Liu, Wenxia Xu, Suping Li, Bin Li, Lei Wang, Jianping Lai

10.1002/adfm.78039.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission Luminogens (AIEgens): From Intrinsic Therapeutic Effect to Sensitization of Conventional Antitumor Modalities
10.1002/adfm.78039.abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional cancer treatment methods, such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, are often limited by poor treatment efficacy, poor targeting, and adverse side effects, as well as intrinsic or acquired drug resistance, which are mainly caused by the complex and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. The development of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizers provides a promising strategy to address these challenges. In addition to being high-performance imaging agents, AIE luminogens (AIEgens) have inherent phototherapeutic capabilities, including photodynamic and photothermal effects, which can directly achieve tumor ablation. More importantly, they can act as multifunctional sensitizers to enhance the efficacy of traditional anti-cancer treatments, reverse drug resistance, alleviate tumor hypoxia, and reshape the immune microenvironment. This review summarizes the basic mechanisms and rational design of AIEgens, emphasizing their transformation from independent therapeutic agents to synergistic sensitizers for combined treatment. By combining imaging guidance, intrinsic therapy, and enhanced treatment sensitivity technologies, the AIEgens-based system provides a new model for precise, efficient, and safe integrated tumor diagnosis and treatment, which has profound significance for future clinical applications.
authors: Wentao Wang, Yuxin Deng, Ziying Tang, Qicheng Zhang, Ying Xu, Yan Lin, Ben Zhong Tang, Ming Zhang
