With electron accumulation in metal 3d states recognized as the electronic component of space charge storage, the remaining question is how the compensating Li + is accommodated within the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). In situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy tracks the reversible formation of the SEI, and ex situ analyses identify organic polymers as the main components for Li + storage. In situ electron paramagnetic resonance with spin trapping captures reversible carbon-chain radical evolution associated with Li + accommodation. Together, these findings reveal a radical bearing polymeric SEI that undergoes Fe-catalyzed dynamic reconstruction and serves as the ionic component of space charge storage. This work links coordination confined interface design with radical mediated SEI chemistry, establishing an active ionic reservoir for fast interfacial Li + storage.

10.1002/adfm.79044.title: Differential Adaptation between Active Sites and Charge-Transport Networks in Covalent Organic Frameworks for H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.79044.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts for H 2 O 2 production. However, optimizing their electronic structure to enhance oxygen activation, charge separation, and transport remains challenging. Herein, a dual-dimensional COF platform was constructed by integrating diazine isomers, pyridazine (Dz) and pyrazine (Pz), with tunable linkage chemistries (sp 2 c-, mix-, and imi-linked), enabling decoupled regulation and systematic investigation of active-site electronic environments and framework charge-transport behavior. Experiments and theoretical calculations revealed that N -heterocyclic isomers primarily govern O 2 activation configurations and oxygen reduction reaction pathways, whereas linkage chemistry mainly regulates framework charge transport. More importantly, a previously unrecognized differential adaptation mechanism is revealed: in the intrinsically asymmetric Dz systems, highly conjugated sp 2 c linkages further enhance electron delocalization and transport, maximizing photocatalytic performance and enabling sp 2 c-COF-Dz to achieve the highest H 2 O 2 production rate (9270 µmol h −1 g −1 ); in contrast, in the Pz systems, mixed-linkage architectures generate localized electron-density gradients that compensate for insufficient site polarization by disrupting electronic symmetry, resulting in higher activity than the sp 2 c-linked COF. These findings uncover a matching relationship between active-site electronic structures and linkage-mediated charge transport behavior, providing a site-framework matching principle for the rational design of high-performance COF photocatalysts.

10.1002/adfm.79008.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Polarity-Switchable Photoelectrochemical Platform Based on B-Eu 2 O 3 Nanospindle and Dual-Amplified Rod-Shaped DNA Walker
10.1002/adfm.79008.abstract: ABSTRACT This work first reports the synthesis of boron-doped europium oxide (B-Eu 2 O 3 ) nanospindle by carbonization of B-doped Eu-based metal organic framework (Eu-MOF), as a high-performance polarity-switchable material with efficient charge transport. Based on B-Eu 2 O 3 nanospindle and target-triggered dual rod-shaped DNA walker signal amplification, a novel polarity-switchable photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensing platform is constructed for retinol binding protein 4 (RBP4) detection, using machine learning for the effective classification of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The fabricated PEC biosensor based on B-Eu 2 O 3 nanospindle and dual-amplified rod-shaped DNA walker for RBP4 detection shows high selectivity and sensitivity with a detection limit of 0.49 fg/mL. This developed B-Eu 2 O 3 nanospindle-based PEC platform for RBP4 assay in serum effectually differentiates T2DM from healthy persons. Moreover, the machine learning model is applied to explore the potential pattern hidden in data of the established technology, and the accuracy of T2DM classification can acquire 100%. The integrated detection platform combining B-Eu 2 O 3 nanospindle-based PEC biosensor with machine learning offers a new avenue for biomarker monitoring.

10.1002/adfm.79041.title: Plant Crude Polysaccharide-Enabled Hydrogel Electrodes for Long-Term Stable EMG Recording
10.1002/adfm.79041.abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels with high conductivity, flexibility, skin compatibility, and long-term stability are essential for reliable bioelectrical signal recording in flexible bioelectronic interfaces for wearable health monitoring and human-machine interaction. However, additive-based enhancement often disrupts the intrinsic hydrogel network, leading to trade-offs among conductivity, flexibility, biocompatibility, and long-term stability. To address this challenge, we propose a conductive hydrogel formation strategy based on the endogenous synergy of plant-derived polysaccharides. As a representative system, we constructed a gelatin/PCA-Na hydrogel incorporating safflower crude polysaccharides, which was denoted as GPP. Plant-derived polysaccharide systems contain abundant hydrophilic groups and active components, including phenolic and ketone groups, which introduce multiple hydrogen bonds and non-covalent interactions into the hydrogel network. As a result, GPP exhibits strong overall performance, with an adhesion strength of 50.1 kPa and a conductivity of 6.3 S m −1 . Moreover, it enables repeated EMG recordings during 7-day continuous wear, with the signal-to-noise ratio remaining above 30 dB, indicating stable skin contact and reliable signal output. In addition, the endogenous synergy mechanism was extended to Prunella vulgaris crude polysaccharides. Overall, this work provides a plant-derived endogenous synergy route toward safe, comfortable, and long-term wearable bioelectronic interfaces.

10.1002/adfm.78949.title: Neuromorphic Devices for Extreme Environments: State-Variable Reliability and Stabilization Strategies
10.1002/adfm.78949.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices are increasingly considered for edge-intelligence systems operating in spaceborne, aerospace, nuclear, cryogenic, and other harsh environments, where local decision-making is constrained by limited power, communication bandwidth, and latency. Reliable operation in these environments requires more than the preservation of basic electrical functionality because neuromorphic computation is physically encoded in material and interfacial state variables. Environmental stress can reshape these variables and alter analog modulation, plasticity, memory retention, threshold dynamics, and readout stability. This review discusses neuromorphic devices for extreme environments from the perspective of state-variable reliability and stabilization. Radiation, temperature extremes, and vacuum or low-pressure conditions are examined as major stressors that perturb defect generation, ionic and electronic transport, interfacial chemistry, switching pathways, and signal readout. Emerging space-relevant factors, including microgravity-assisted fabrication and mechanical loading, are also considered with respect to device formation, structural integrity, and long-term reliability. Stabilization strategies are organized across material-level design, environmental boundary control, and programming or readout compensation. By connecting device-level degradation to neuromorphic metrics, array operation, soft-error response, and inference accuracy, this review provides a framework for evaluating and designing reliable neuromorphic hardware under realistic environmental constraints.

10.1002/adfm.79022.title: Hard-Acid High-Entropy Stabilized Chloride Octahedra for Halide Solid Electrolytes at High-Voltage of 4.8 V
10.1002/adfm.79022.abstract: ABSTRACT Halide solid-state electrolytes (HSSEs) are promising candidates for high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). However, the instability of the metal-chloride (M-Cl) octahedra remains a major obstacle to their operation under ultrahigh-voltage conditions. In chloride electrolytes such as Li 3 InCl 6 , the elongated weak M-Cl bond can trigger structural degradation and induce Cl − oxidation during the charging process. Herein, guided by the strong hard acid-hard base interaction between metal cations and Cl − (hard base), a hard-acid high-entropy halide electrolyte, Li 2.5 In 0.5 Y 0.1 Al 0.1 Zr 0.1 Ta 0.2 Cl 6 , is developed through the synergistic incorporation of multiple hard-acid cations. Structural and electronic analyses reveal that the hard-acid high-entropy strategy can stabilize M-Cl octahedra and chloride electronic states, thereby suppressing chloride oxidation and enhancing stability at 4.8 V. Meanwhile, the modified framework creates a more favorable Li + migration pathway, enabling a high ionic conductivity of 2.38 mS cm −1 . When paired with an ultrahigh-nickel NCM955 cathode, the resulting ASSLB exhibits outstanding electrochemical performance, retaining over 80% of its capacity after 1400 cycles at 10 C and 4.8 V while maintaining stable operation at -20°C. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of hard-acid high-entropy engineering in simultaneously enhancing oxidative stability and Li + transport, providing a new crystal-chemistry design strategy for ultrahigh-voltage halide solid electrolytes.

10.1002/adfm.79023.title: Rest-Pulse Interphase Reconstruction Enables Capacity Recovery in Aged Lithium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79023.abstract: ABSTRACT To address capacity loss associated with inactive Li-related species and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth, we developed a Rest-Pulse (RP) protocol for aged LiFePO 4 /graphite diagnostic pouch cells. The protocol combines a 12 h discharged-state rest with a short voltage pulse. The rest step partially dissolves and restructures the graphite-side SEI, reducing interfacial blocking. Quantitative ex situ 7 Li solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) shows a pronounced decrease in NMR-detectable residual metallic Li after RP treatment. Atomistic molecular-dynamics simulations further indicate that the pulse produces a short-range, field-dependent directional bias of isolated Li-rich domains within the porous interphase rather than long-range migration. The RP protocol achieves a 99.3% average Coulombic efficiency and ∼10% absolute capacity recovery, exceeding the recovery obtained from rest alone (∼6%). A coupled recovery process occurs involving SEI reconstruction, improved interfacial kinetics, and changes in inactive Li-related inventory. The RP protocol provides a proof-of-concept route for non-destructive capacity recovery, although larger-format validation and chemistry-specific optimization are still required.

10.1002/adfm.78951.title: Surface Energy Anisotropy Mediated Grain Rotation Yields Strong Texture in Low Symmetry Intermetallic Compounds
10.1002/adfm.78951.abstract: ABSTRACT Sub-100 nm grains and strong deformation texture in low-symmetry intermetallic compounds (LSICs) cannot be achieved by conventional mechanisms like slip, twinning, and dissolution-precipitation. Using Nd 2 Fe 14 B as a model LSIC, a novel texture formation mechanism driven by grain surface energy anisotropy (GSEA) is proposed. Ab-initio calculations revealed a size-dependent driving force for grain rotation, in which GSEA dominates below ∼45 nm, while GSEA and elastic strain energy anisotropy co-operate between ∼45 and ∼892 nm. In this mechanism, platelet nanograins induced by GSEA undergo orientation-convergent Jeffery orbit rotation in the strain flow, and texture initially forms, which is strengthened by the GSEA-driven reduction of high-energy grain boundaries. A low-temperature and low-strain-rate deformation process is adopted to suppress grain growth and activate diffusion creep, maintaining the GSEA-dominant size regime and enabling continuous strain flow to realize ultrastrong texture within sub-100 nm grains. Precession electron diffraction, atom probe tomography, and transmission electron microscopy confirm three texture evolution stages: (i) formation of platelets, (ii) platelet alignment, and (iii) texture strengthening. An Nd 2 Fe 14 B magnet with ∼75 nm grain thickness and 99.6% c-axis texture is achieved through this GSEA-based mechanism. This work establishes a generalizable texture mechanism for nanocrystalline LSICs and provides a scalable route for ultrahigh-performance intermetallic materials.

10.1002/adfm.79005.title: Atomic-Scale Regulation of Spin Polarization in High-Entropy Frameworks for Efficient Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Wave Attenuation
10.1002/adfm.79005.abstract: ABSTRACT High-performance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption in the low-frequency S and C bands (2-8 GHz) remains challenging due to fundamental constraints like the Snoek limit and difficulty in achieving proper impedance matching, which conventional ferromagnetic materials cannot overcome through extrinsic morphology engineering alone. Here, an electronic-structure-driven strategy is reported to design a series of (Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Cr)Se 2 high-entropy selenides (HESe) that translate atomic-scale orbital regulation into enhanced macroscopic EMW absorption. By integrating magnetic elements (Fe, Co, and Ni) with trivalent chromium, the distinctive t 2g 3 e g 0 electron configuration of the Cr (III) ion generates high spin polarization and strengthened spin-orbit coupling, which increases the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant (K) and shifts magnetic resonance toward the low-frequency region without compromising saturation magnetization. Moreover, controlled introduction of Se vacancies further modulates the dielectric environment by inducing lattice distortion and interfacial polarization, thereby optimizing impedance matching. As a result, the vacancy-engineered pentanary material (HESe-V r ) exhibits a minimum reflection loss of −50.13 dB at 2.92 GHz with an effective bandwidth spanning the S and C bands. This work demonstrates that d-orbital electron configuration engineering in high-entropy compounds provides a viable route for tailoring intrinsic electromagnetic responses, offering a new paradigm for the rational design of next-generation EMW absorbing materials.

10.1002/adfm.78935.title: Unveiling the Interfacial and Bulk-Structural Failures of TiS 2 Anodes Under Deep Sodiation
10.1002/adfm.78935.abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) suffer from severe capacity degradation during deep sodiation, yet the fundamental failure mechanisms remain elusive. Using titanium disulfide (TiS 2 ) as a model anode, we unravel the interfacial and bulk-structural failures triggered by extending the discharge cutoff voltage to 0.01 V. Specifically, the interfacial failure is driven by the massive precipitation of highly reactive metallic Ti, which aggressively reacts with the electrolyte to form inactive Ti-O compounds, irreversibly consuming active Ti and preventing Ti-S bond reconstruction. Meanwhile, the bulk-structural degradation originates from severe accumulation of internal stress, leading to the irreversible disintegration of the layered framework. To circumvent these coupled challenges, we propose a robust carbon-sphere encapsulation strategy, confining TiS 2 nanosheets within dense spherical carbon matrices (TiS 2 @C). This dual-functional architecture effectively redistributes localized stress to mechanically buffer severe volume expansion and physically isolates the precipitated active Ti from the electrolyte, thereby suppressing the detrimental parasitic oxidation. Consequently, the TiS 2 @C composite unlocks its full conversion capacity, achieving exceptional long-term stability with a 98.5% capacity retention over 1800 cycles within an expanded 0.01-3.0 V window. This work elucidates the intrinsic degradation mechanisms of TMDs at extreme sodiation and establishes a highly effective structural engineering paradigm.

10.1002/adfm.79010.title: Understanding Repulsion-Governed Adsorption Mechanism for Efficient Surface Passivation in Blade-Coated Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79010.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface passivation of perovskite thin-films via adsorption of amine-based derivatives plays an important role in minimizing nonradiative recombination. In this work, we developed a novel and efficient amine-based surface passivation molecule, cystamine dihydrochloride (CH), which possesses a characteristic symmetric structure and exhibits an anomalous passivation mechanism. It is found that the electron-rich sulfur atoms in central disulfide moiety of CH experience strong short-range repulsion with surface iodides of perovskites. Consequently, contrary to the conventional attraction-driven-based passivation mechanism, the presence of S-I repulsion dictates a unique binding geometry that drives preferential coordination of the two terminal amine groups with undercoordinated Pb 2+ while displacing sulfur atoms away from the surface. This repulsion-induced interfacial reconstruction effectively suppresses the formation of deep-trap Pb-Pb dimers and thereby significantly suppresses nonradiative recombination. Eventually, the blade-coated PSCs with CH-passivated achieve a champion efficiency of 26.15% compared to 23.64% of the control devices, along with markedly improved operational stability. This work provides new insight into repulsion-mediated interfacial passivation for high-efficiency and stable perovskite solar cells.

10.1002/adfm.79057.title: A Bidirectional Molecular Barrier for Efficient and Stable Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79057.abstract: ABSTRACT The inward diffusion of Ag electrodes and outward migration of perovskite constituents trigger a vicious degradation cycle in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), severely limiting device longevity. Herein, 2,5-dimercapto-1,3,4-thiadiazole (DMTD) is introduced as a bidirectional ionic barrier layer to simultaneously stabilize the Ag electrode and the perovskite lattice. The -SH groups strongly coordinate with Ag + to establish a molecular barrier against Ag migration, while the -N-N- groups bind Pb 2+ to passivate defects and reinforce the crystal structure. This synergistic bidirectional inhibition effectively prevents interfacial reactions between perovskite species and Ag + , thereby breaking the chain of mutually reinforced degradation. As a result, DMTD-modified devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.13% and exhibit outstanding stability, retaining 87.68% of their initial PCE after 3000 h of storage at 25°C (15% ± 5% RH), and 80.87% after 1000 h under continuous heating at 85°C.

10.1002/adfm.79030.title: Cross-Phase Impurity-Interphase Regulation for Suppressing Thermally Accelerated Failure in Ni-Rich Pouch Lithium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79030.abstract: ABSTRACT Practical LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||graphite pouch cells suffer rapid degradation under thermal stress because liquid-phase impurity reactions, electrode interphase failure, and cathode-anode cross-talk are tightly coupled. However, most strategies are designed to address either impurity chemistry or interphase chemistry, leaving the amplified cross-talk between electrolyte degradation and electrode failure unresolved. Here, we propose a cross-phase impurity-interphase regulation strategy using p-Phenylenebis(dimethylvinylsilane) (PDVS) for LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||graphite pouch cells. The vinyl-dimethylsilyl groups endow PDVS with synchronized liquid-phase scavenging and solid-phase interphase-forming capability. In the liquid phase, PDVS acts as an impurity scavenger, lowering HF from 90.88 ppm to 29.44 ppm while reducing residual H 2 O from 10.65 to 8.45 ppm, thereby suppressing LiPF 6 hydrolysis and reducing the accumulation of corrosive by-products. At the solid interfaces, PDVS preferentially participates in interfacial reactions to construct Si-containing cathode-electrolyte interphase and solid-electrolyte interphase on the Ni-rich cathode and graphite anode, mitigating electrolyte decomposition, gas evolution, transition-metal crossover, and resistance growth. Consequently, 2 Ah LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||graphite pouch cells retain 92.81% capacity after 304 cycles at 45°C, show reduced swelling during 60°C storage, and maintain 86.5% capacity after over 1620 cycles at 25°C. This work establishes cross-phase impurity-interphase regulation as a manufacturing-compatible electrolyte design principle for thermally durable Ni-rich pouch cells.

10.1002/adfm.79004.title: Anion Co-Intercalation in Conductive 2D MOFs via π-d Hybridization for High-Performance Magnesium Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79004.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) are a promising post-lithium battery technology due to abundant magnesium reserves, high volumetric capacity, and dendrite-free Mg anodes. However, the strong electrostatic interaction between Mg 2+ and inorganic cathode lattices causes high diffusion barriers and sluggish kinetics. To circumvent this, two-dimensional conductive metal-organic frameworks (2D c-MOFs), featuring favorable electronic transport characteristics arising from π-d hybridization and structural tunability, have attracted widespread attention. This work systematically investigates the electrochemical performance of M 3 (HITP) 2 (M = Co, Ni, Cu; HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene) as cathodes for RMBs and reveals the decisive role of the metal center in Mg storage. All three materials achieve synergistic dual-ion storage through heteroatomic N coordination with Mg 2+ coupled with anion intercalation. Among them, Ni 3 (HITP) 2 demonstrates superior overall performance, arising from its characteristic Ni 2+ d 8 electronic configuration, which facilitates the formation of a stable Ni-N coordination environment and effective π-d conjugation. It retains approximately 201 mAh g −1 after 1100 cycles at 1.0 A g −1 , corresponding to a high-capacity retention of 98.0%. This study elucidates how different metal centers regulate Mg storage in 2D c-MOFs, providing molecular-level guidance for designing high-performance organic cathodes for multivalent-ion batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79073.title: Bio-Inspired Nucleotide Electrolyte Engineering Enables Highly Reversible Zinc Anodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79073.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage but suffer from Zn dendrite growth, water-induced parasitic reactions, and interfacial instability. Herein, inspired by natural nucleotide architectures, we introduce disodium inosinate (IMP) as a green multifunctional electrolyte additive to regulate Zn electrochemistry. Its naturally preorganized nucleotide framework integrates chemically differentiated phosphate, hydroxyl-rich ribose, and O/N-containing heterocyclic regions, which exhibit distinct interaction preferences toward Zn 2 + , water molecules, and the Zn surface under different local electrochemical environments. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that IMP participates in Zn 2+ solvation and regulates the local water environment, while preferential multisite adsorption at the Zn interface homogenizes Zn 2+ flux and promotes Zn(002)-preferred deposition, enabling dense and dendrite-suppressed Zn growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells achieve stable cycling for over 2000 h at 5 mA cm −2 and 2.5 mAh cm −2 , while Zn||Cu cells maintain an average Coulombic efficiency above 99.8% over 3500 cycles. Zn||NVO full cells retain 87.3% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 , and pouch cells demonstrate stable cycling for 300 cycles. This work highlights how the intrinsic chemical differentiation of a naturally preorganized nucleotide architecture can translate into distinct molecular interactions across different electrochemical environments, providing a bio-inspired strategy for sustainable aqueous electrolyte design.

10.1002/adfm.78899.title: Unraveling the Origins of C-Rate Dependent Capacity Decay in Fe-Mn-Based Prussian Blue Cathodes for Sodium Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78899.abstract: ABSTRACT Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), especially low-cost Mn-doped Fe-based PBAs, demonstrate significant potential for power-type sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), owing to their open framework and high theoretical capacity (∼170 mAh g −1 ). However, their capacity decay mechanisms, particularly under rapid charge/discharge conditions, remain insufficiently understood, hindering their practical implementation in high-power energy storage systems. Here, we systematically investigate the failure mechanisms of Mn-doped Fe-based PBAs through multiple in/ex situ characterizations of Mn-doped Fe-PBA cathodes cycled under various current densities. Our analysis reveals that there are several pathways induce electrode degradation at high rate: (1) transition metal dissolution that disrupts redox-active sites, (2) mechanical degradation that impairs electrode kinetics under high-rate conditions, (3) severe and rapid Na dendrite growth, and (4) interfacial side reactions that generate a thick cathode-electrolyte interphase layer. Rather than viewing transition metal dissolution and mechanical degradation as isolated degradation pathways, this study reveals that capacity collapse at 10 C is fundamentally driven by the intrinsic kinetic mismatch and mechanical failure, offering key insights for the design of durable, high-power PBA-based SIBs.

10.1002/adfm.79046.title: Organic-Inorganic Hybrid Nanofiller Enables In situ Thermal Conductive Network toward Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79046.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PVSCs) have long faced challenges in long-term thermal stability due to their low thermal conductivity and the volatile nature of frequently incorporated additives. Herein, we report a versatile strategy that uses organic-inorganic hybrid filler, composed of 3-methacryloxypropyltris(trimethylsiloxy)silane (MPTMS)-modified Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles, to construct an in situ thermal conduction network in perovskite. The surface modifier, MPTMS, of the hybrid filler has multiple functionalities in regulating the chemical interactions, perovskite crystallization, and intermolecular compatibility. Specifically, it's carbonyl moiety coordinates with Pb 2 + in perovskite to passivate defects and stabilize the α-phase, while its hydrolyzed groups enhance Al 2 O 3 -perovskite compatibility for the formation of uniform thermal conductive pathways. The resultant PVSC achieves 27.05% efficiency and retains 96% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum-power-point tracking at 65°C under illumination. This work synergistically optimizes the thermal behavior and crystallization stability in perovskite, offering a viable way to improve the thermal stability of PVSCs via complementary hybridization of organic and inorganic functional species.

10.1002/adfm.78984.title: Spatially Integrated Intercalation-Conversion Hybrid Cathode for Durable, High-Capacity Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78984.abstract: ABSTRACT The fundamental trade-off between structural stability and high capacity remains a key challenge in Li-ion battery cathode design, especially in cost-sensitive, large-scale applications. Here, we present a spatially integrated intercalation-conversion hybrid cathode that combines LiFePO 4 and sulfur-based materials within a monolayer architecture. This earth-abundant composition synchronizes Li-ion intercalation with the solid-liquid sulfur conversion reaction: LiFePO 4 serves as a mechanically robust Li host and a chemical regulator that suppresses polysulfide shuttles, while sulfur-based materials provide high specific capacity. By rationally tailoring the cathode composition and electrolyte solvation chemistry, we reveal how electrolyte-cathode synergistic interactions govern active material utilization, interfacial kinetics, and long-term stability. The optimized Li-metal battery delivers stable cycling over 3000 cycles with a low-capacity decay rate of 0.016% per cycle at 5 C and also demonstrates stable cycling under practical asymmetric cycling protocols. This work provides a new design principle for hybrid cathodes, offering a scalable pathway toward ultra-durable and high-capacity Li-metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79077.title: Intrinsically Spin-Exchange-Field-Modulated Two-Dimensional Sensor with Platinum Single Atoms for High-Performance Hydrogen Peroxide Monitoring
10.1002/adfm.79077.abstract: ABSTRACT Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer broad prospects in catalysis and sensing due to their maximum atom efficiency and tunable coordination. However, the performance of Pt-based SACs in electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) sensing remains kinetically limited. To overcome this, we propose a magnetic engineering strategy that introduces Fe/Co atoms adjacent to Pt sites. Through in situ pyrolysis, magnetized Pt SACs (mag-Pt SACs) were stably anchored on a 2D electrode. This approach uses the intrinsic magnetic moments of Fe/Co to induce local spin polarization, thereby modulating the electronic structure of Pt without an external field. Compared to PtN 4 and Fe-Co diatomic catalysts, the mag-Pt SACs-modified electrode exhibited significantly enhanced sensitivity-by 1.80- and 2.14-fold, respectively. Mechanistic studies reveal that the induced spin polarization generates a net magnetic moment and unpaired electrons at Pt, which optimizes the d -band center and weakens the over-strong adsorption of reaction intermediates, thus lowering the H 2 O 2 reduction barrier and boosting sensing kinetics. Based on this spin-polarization enhancement, the mag-Pt SACs biosensor achieved highly sensitive and selective real-time monitoring of H 2 O 2 fluctuations from MSB/VK3-stimulated cancer cells. This work introduces spin behavior into electrocatalytic kinetics, providing a new paradigm for designing high-performance SAC-based electrochemical sensors.

10.1002/adfm.79006.title: Decoupling the Conductivity-Seebeck Trade-Off in N-Type MXene/Conjugated Polyelectrolyte Thermoelectric Bilayers
10.1002/adfm.79006.abstract: ABSTRACT To decouple the Seebeck coefficient from electrical conductivity in metallic thermoelectric (TE) systems, we investigated bilayer heterostructures of MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ) and conjugated polymers with anionic (-SO 3- Na + , CPE-Na), neutral (CP), and cationic (-N + (CH 3 ) 3 Br-, CPE-Br) side chains. Strong electrostatic anchoring between the cationic ammonium side chains and electronegative MXene terminations induces a previously unreported Coulombic trap-induced filtering mechanism, distinct from conventional energy filtering. The resulting localized potential wells selectively trap low-energy carriers to enhance the Seebeck coefficient, while concurrent lattice stiffening suppresses electron-phonon scattering and preserves high-energy carrier transport. This decoupling raises Hall mobility from 1.01 to 5.40 cm 2 V −1 s −1 and the Seebeck coefficient from -8.6 to -19.0 µV K −1 while maintaining a metallic conductivity of 5291.9 S cm −1 . The optimized MXene/CPE-Br film, processed with a halogen-free solvent, achieves a record power factor of 190.5 µW m −1 K −2 and a peak figure of merit ( zT ) of 0.0279. Strong interfacial adhesion further imparts good electromechanical durability under repeated bending to a flexible TE generator, providing an effective strategy to address the transport limitations of n-type MXene-based TE materials.

10.1002/adfm.79039.title: Interfacial Regulation and Phosphate-Siloxane Hybrid Networks Enable Regenerated Cellulose Aerogels for Multi-Scenario Transport Packaging
10.1002/adfm.79039.abstract: ABSTRACT A large barrier to replacing petroleum-derived foams in transport packaging is the difficulty of simultaneously achieving high mechanical resilience, fire safety, and environmental durability in sustainable aerogels. Here, a regenerated cellulose (RC) aerogel is designed via interfacial regulation and hybrid crosslinking: phytic acid (PA) enables phosphate-assisted crosslinking between RC and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), while sodium lignosulfonate (SLS) stabilizes the foamed precursor. Subsequent hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (HTMS) chemical vapor deposition constructs a robust hydrophobic siloxane-containing surface layer, yielding the silanized aerogel (S-RPPS). S-RPPS exhibits durable hydrophobicity with water contact angles of 140.7° (outer surface) and 137.2° (cross-section), enabling rapid underwater compression-rebound cycling without structural disintegration. It also delivers strong fire safety and thermal insulation, showing no ignition under a 600°C open flame and maintaining a surface temperature below 143.2°C within 3 min. Mechanically, S-RPPS remains stable after 500 compression cycles at 80% strain (stress loss rate ≈ 6.6% and strain loss rate ≈ 8.1%), retains > 90% oil sorption capacity after 100 squeeze-regeneration cycles, and maintains performance after one-month exposure to harsh media. Overall, this work establishes a scalable strategy for multifunctional biomass aerogels targeting flame-retardant thermal insulation and pollutant adsorption, aiming to mitigate fire hazards and leakage-induced contamination during transport packaging.

10.1002/adfm.79068.title: Near-Unity Photoluminescent Copper(I) Halide Hybrids with Multifunctionality in WLEDs, X-Ray Scintillation and Information Encryption
10.1002/adfm.79068.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic-inorganic copper-based halides have become a current research hotspot due to their excellent optical properties, structural diversity, favorable stability, and low toxicity. Herein, we report a low-cost, large-scale synthesized All-in-One (AIO) structural copper(I) halide hybrid material, Cu 6 I 8 (bu-ted) 2 (bu-ted = 1-butyl-1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octan-1-ium bromide), which generates broadband green-yellow emission (530 nm) via self-trapped excitons (STEs), with excellent photoluminescent quantum yield (99.38% ± 0.41%) and thermal stability (decomposition temperature reaches 295°C). Its multifunctionality has been demonstrated in high-performance white LEDs (R a = 91.5), ultrasensitive X-ray imaging scintillators (detection limit: 366.5 nGy air /s, resolution reaches 20 lp/mm), and information encryption labels via reversible emission shifts (Δ λ em = 85 nm) triggered by dichloromethane vapor/solution with rapid KI-enabled resetting. This work further demonstrates the excellent properties of AIO-type copper(I) halide hybrid materials and their commercialization potential for multifunctional applications.

10.1002/adfm.79052.title: Optical Transduction of Magnetically Controlled Spin-Selective Oxygen Evolution at a Ferrimagnetic Heterointerface
10.1002/adfm.79052.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-dependent pathways play a critical role in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), yet direct and dynamic probing of spin-selective catalysis remains challenging. Here we report an optical transduction strategy that provides a real-time, chemically responsive readout of magnetically controlled spin-selective OER. A ferrimagnetic Fe 3 O 4 /CoFe 2 O 4 heterointerface is engineered to establish a spin-selective charge transport pathway, where interfacial magnetic coupling enables efficient field-induced domain alignment under an external magnetic field. Electrochemical measurements and spin-resolved calculations suggest that interfacial spin polarization favors triplet-related oxygen evolution. Coupling this process to luminol electrochemiluminescence (ECL) translates changes in OER-derived oxygen-precursor availability into a reversible and peak-selective optical signal through oxygen-derived reactive species. The pronounced reverse-scan enhancement provides a chemically amplified optical output of the magnetically regulated catalytic state, enabling dynamic optical transduction of spin-dependent electrocatalysis. This work establishes a general framework for coupling spin-dependent electrocatalysis with a chemically responsive optical readout, providing new opportunities for probing and controlling interfacial reactions through spin polarization.

10.1002/adfm.79035.title: Arginine-Induced Catalytic Microenvironment Engineering of ZrMOFs Enables Broad-Spectrum Hydrolase Nanozymes for Biofilm Eradication
10.1002/adfm.79035.abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial biofilms are protected by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix primarily composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides, rendering them highly resistant to conventional antimicrobial treatments. Although natural hydrolases efficiently degrade individual EPS components, their narrow substrate scope, poor stability, and high cost restrict effective biofilm eradication. Here, we report a catalytic microenvironment engineering strategy that enables broad-spectrum hydrolase nanozymes through arginine-directed modulation of Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (ZrMOFs). Systematic amino acid-directed defect engineering afforded a series of amino acid-coordinated ZrMOFs, among which arginine-coordinated ZrMOF (Arg-ZrMOF) exhibited the highest hydrolase-like catalytic efficiency ( k cat /K m = 1437.5 M −1 s −1 ). The enhanced catalytic performance originated from the engineered catalytic microenvironment, characterized by increased surface hydrophilicity, enhanced formation of nucleophilic Zr-OH species, and strengthened electrostatic interactions with negatively charged substrates. Arg-ZrMOF efficiently hydrolyzed phosphodiester, peptide, and glycosidic bonds, enabling concerted degradation of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides within the EPS matrix. This expanded hydrolytic substrate scope enabled superior inhibition and eradication of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, outperforming the benchmark enzyme DNase I while retaining over 80% catalytic activity after 60 reuse cycles and excellent storage stability for more than 100 days. Furthermore, a spray-on Arg-ZrMOF formulation enabled effective biofilm removal from stainless-steel, plastic, and glass surfaces, demonstrating its practical applicability for surface biofilm control. This work establishes catalytic microenvironment engineering as a versatile strategy for constructing hydrolase nanozymes capable of broad biomacromolecular degradation and practical biofilm eradication.

10.1002/adfm.79045.title: Programming Multi-Timescale Carrier Dynamics in Circularly Polarized Light Photodetectors for Polarization Neuromorphic Vision
10.1002/adfm.79045.abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable recognition of complex scenes remains challenging because physically distinct objects can exhibit similar appearances in conventional intensity images, while dynamically changing environments require continuous temporal information processing. Although circularly polarized light (CPL) provides an additional optical dimension for distinguishing surface reflection properties, integrating efficient polarization perception with multi-timescale synaptic plasticity in a single material platform remains difficult because these functionalities require fundamentally different carrier dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that donor-acceptor composition engineering in chiral bulk-heterojunction diodes enables programmable carrier dynamics across multiple timescales. By regulating the balance between carrier transport and trapping, the devices evolve from volatile through quasi-nonvolatile to nonvolatile synaptic plasticity while preserving efficient CPL photodetection. The optimized composition delivers a photocurrent dissymmetry factor of −0.026, whereas complementary volatile and nonvolatile devices enable cooperative temporal information processing. As a proof of concept, a polarization neuromorphic vision system combining RGB-CPL multidimensional perception and multi-timescale memory improves static recognition accuracy by 15% and dynamic recognition accuracy by up to 12% compared with conventional systems. This work establishes donor-acceptor composition engineering as a strategy for coordinating optical perception and temporal computation, opening opportunities for polarization-aware neuromorphic vision and intelligent optoelectronics.

10.1002/adfm.79090.title: Chemical Equilibrium Modulated Crystallization of 2D Perovskite Single Crystals for High-Performance and Robust Dual-Mode Photonic Detection
10.1002/adfm.79090.abstract: ABSTRACT 2D perovskites, characterized by distinctive quantum-well structure and high exciton binding energy, offer unprecedented opportunities for photonic detection. However, synergistically driving efficient carrier extraction and rapid radiative recombination within monolithic single crystals (SC) remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, a room-temperature chemical equilibrium-modulated crystallization strategy is demonstrated to synthesize centimeter-scale 2D (PA) 2 PbBr 4 (PPB) SCs. The use of a hygroscopic acid-base reactive agent precisely regulates the solvent evaporation kinetics, suppressing stochastic nucleation and yielding high-quality SCs with suppressed light scattering. Consequently, planar PPB photodetectors (PDs) exhibit a notable and robust UV response, featuring a large on/off ratio of 2.77 × 10 4 , a wide linear dynamic range of 159 dB, and an ultra-low limit of detection of 3.5 nW cm −2 . Simultaneously, the intense exciton confinement endows the PPB SCs with strong radioluminescence and robust radiation stability. Both SCs and flexible film scintillators demonstrate excellent practical x-ray imaging capabilities. Crucially, the absence of grain boundaries inherently mitigates internal light scattering, enabling SC scintillators to achieve an impressive spatial resolution up to 26.5 lp mm −1 , representing one of the highest values among the reported metal halide SC scintillators. This work establishes a kinetically control for high-quality SCs synthesis and provides valuable insights for high-performance and robust dual-mode photonic detection.

10.1002/adfm.78938.title: Zr-Al-C MAX Phases Stabilized by Carbon Vacancies
10.1002/adfm.78938.abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme service environments demand the engineering of innovative high-performance materials, with high purity as a critical design requirement. Zirconium-based MAX phases are touted for their radiation tolerance, favorable neutronics, and liquid metal compatibility. Accordingly, they are proposed as highly promising candidates to replace corrosion-sensitive zircalloy coatings for accident-tolerant fuels in Gen-III/Gen-IV nuclear reactors. However, their potential has never materialized due to their poor synthesizability and thus low purity. The inevitable and poorly understood competing formation of ZrC during synthesis severely compromises their thermomechanical integrity and radiation response. This work combines complementary insights into theoretical phase stability and experimental synthesizability of and . Carbon vacancies are predicted to adversely affect stability, whereas moderate (5-10 at.%) carbon deficiency improves stability. Reactive spark plasma sintering /Al/C powder mixtures of varying stoichiometry validated these trends: only forms substantially when using stoichiometric or carbon-excessive feedstocks, whereas formation is highly sensitive to carbon-deficient feedstocks: carbon-stoichiometric or -excessive (25 at.%) feedstocks do not yield appreciable quantities of . Defect engineering thus emerges as a powerful alternative strategy for enhancing MAX phase stability and synthesizability without compromising their chemical integrity, opening new avenues for their design and application.

10.1002/adfm.79048.title: Engineering the Ir─O─Ni Interface Bonds in Ir@Ni-MOF to Accelerate Li 2 O 2 Formation and Decomposition for High-Reversibility Li-O 2 Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79048.abstract: ABSTRACT Aprotic lithium-oxygen (Li-O 2 ) batteries have attracted considerable interest due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy density, yet their practical application is severely limited by slow cathode reaction kinetics and large voltage hysteresis. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy to construct ultrafine Ir nanoparticles anchored on Ni-based metal-organic framework (Ir@Ni-MOF) as an efficient bifunctional cathode catalyst for Li-O 2 batteries. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal the formation of interfacial Ir─O─Ni chemical bonds, inducing significant charge redistribution and downshifting the d-band center of Ir@Ni-MOF. This electronic modulation weakens the adsorption affinity toward the LiO 2 intermediate, thereby enhancing a solution-mediated discharge pathway to form nanosheet-like Li 2 O 2 with intimate interface contact and rapid charge/mass transfer, which facilitates reversible decomposition during charging. As a result, the Ir@Ni-MOF cathode delivers a remarkably low overpotential of 0.76 V, an extended cycling stability over 400 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , outperforming most reported MOF-based and noble-metal catalysts. This work provides a promising avenue for designing high-performance Li-O 2 batteries and beyond through precise electronic structure engineering.

10.1002/adfm.78978.title: Critical Coupling in Semi-Trasparent Fano Resonators for Photothermal Converters
10.1002/adfm.78978.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient photothermal conversion and localized thermal field modulation are powerful design axes for next-generation energy, electronic, and biomedical materials. Conventional photothermal platforms typically rely on opaque broadband absorbers, enforcing a fundamental trade-off precluding simultaneous optical transparency and high thermal performance. Here, we report a semi-transparent Fano nano-cavity resonator, fabricated via lithography-free deposition, that overcomes this limitation by operating under a critically coupled, resonant interaction regime. By harnessing asymmetric Fano interference between a continuous lossy background and a discrete cavity mode, the resonator suppresses reflection to achieve a zero-reflectance () state. Under this coupling condition, the system reaches a balanced 50%-50% optical transmission absorption, respectively. Under continuous-wave laser excitation, this optimal energy partition drives extreme, spatially confined temperature rises exceeding 500 within seconds, with an internal photothermal efficiency of 50%. Its functional versatility is demonstrated across diverse applications, including rapid phase-transition defrosting and localized biothermal tissue cauterization, along with the proof of concept of an optical scalpel.

10.1002/adfm.77606.title: Low-Cost, Energy-Saving, Room-Temperature Synthesis of Ductile Thermoelectric Semiconductors
10.1002/adfm.77606.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible thermoelectric has recently attracted great attention in wearable technologies. Ag 2 (Se,S)-based ductile materials are promising candidates for flexible thermoelectric applications. However, conventional melting methods with high-temperature routes (>1000°C), which are commonly employed for the synthesis of these materials, are energy-intensive and limited in achieving precise control over composition and homogeneity. In this work, a simple chemical reaction route was employed to synthesize Ag 2 (Se,S)-based materials at room temperature, enabling highly homogeneous distribution and good chemical stoichiometric control. Among the S-substituted compositions, Ag 2 Se 0.7 S 0.3 exhibited the best thermoelectric performance, and excess Ag was subsequently incorporated to regulate carrier transport. Although the Ag-excess bulk sample achieved a zT value of 0.54 at 340 K due to reduced thermal conductivity, its power factor remained limited. Hot-rolling deformation was therefore introduced to promote an anisotropic microstructure with grain alignment, which facilitates carrier transport and increases carrier mobility. The optimized Ag 2.05 Se 0.7 S 0.3 film achieved a maximum power factor of 13.88 µW cm −1 K −2 at 340 K. Furthermore, a six-leg in-plane thermoelectric device fabricated from this material delivered a normalized maximum power density of 0.44 W m − 1 under Δ T = 37.4 K, demonstrating the potential of this cost-effective and energy-saving room-temperature synthesis strategy for flexible thermoelectric applications.

10.1002/adfm.78872.title: From Carrier Behavior to Cathode Design: Toward High-Performance Aluminum Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78872.abstract: ABSTRACT This review systematically summarizes recent advances in cathode materials for aluminum batteries (ABs), emphasizing the critical influence of carrier properties on electrode performance. Focusing on carrier properties, including ionic size, valence, charge density, and coordination environment, we analyze their transport kinetics, interfacial reactions, and energy storage mechanisms across different cathode systems, including Al 3+ , AlCl 4 − , AlCl 2 + , as well as the synergistic behavior of multiple carriers. We identify intrinsic carrier characteristics, solvation/desolvation dynamics, and the electrode/electrolyte interface as the primary factors governing battery performance. Furthermore, the review delineates the constraints of cathode materials in achieving high capacity, fast kinetics, and long-term cycling stability. An integrated framework for understanding carrier behavior and energy storage mechanisms is established, accompanied by a systematic classification of cathode materials, including inorganic, Prussian blue, and organic compounds, together with their corresponding optimization strategies. Finally, universal design principles for structural engineering, electronic structure modulation, defect/doping, and interface engineering are proposed. More importantly, this review establishes a carrier-centered framework that systematically links carrier chemistry, charge storage mechanisms, and cathode design principles, thereby providing a unified mechanistic perspective for the rational development of next-generation high-performance ABs.

10.1002/adfm.79049.title: Fluorocarbon Surfactant-Derived Ultrathin Porous Carbon Interface Layer for Stable Zn Anode
10.1002/adfm.79049.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by parasitic hydrogen evolution, dendritic growth, and low Zn utilization. Here, we report an ultrathin (∼5.5 nm) fluorine/oxygen co-doped porous carbon interface layer constructed on Cu foil via controlled pyrolysis of a fluorocarbon surfactant precursor. This nanoscale interface confines Zn deposition behavior at the Cu interface region, effectively regulating nucleation and growth. The F/O dopants induce localized electronic modulation and hydrophobicity to suppress water-induced side reactions, while the porous framework facilitates rapid Zn 2+ migration and accelerates the desolvation kinetics. As a result, Zn preferentially deposits beneath the interface layer, leading to dense and uniform metal growth with minimal dead Zn formation. Benefiting from this interfacial confinement effect, the optimized electrode, with a low Zn loading of 5 mAh cm −2 , delivers exceptional reversibility and cycling stability (>1500 cycles at 5 mA cm −2 with 40% depth of discharge). When paired with a MnO 2 cathode, the full cell achieves 88.2% capacity retention after 800 cycles at 1 A g −1 . This work highlights a scalable strategy to engineer ultrathin functional interfaces on current collectors and provides new insights into regulating metal deposition via interfacial confinement for high-efficiency metal-based batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79062.title: Electrically Programmable Light-Thermal Regulation With Two-Dimensional Liquid Crystals
10.1002/adfm.79062.abstract: ABSTRACT Smart agriculture concerns the precise regulation of light and thermal environments to improve energy efficiency and optimize plant growth. However, current approaches predominantly rely on energy-intensive active systems or static technologies that cannot adapt to the evolving spectral and thermal demands of plants. Here, we report a two-dimensional inorganic liquid crystal system in which a frequency-controlled electric field dynamically reorients nanosheets, enabling dynamic control of both light availability and ambient temperature. The electro-optic response of α−zirconium phosphate nanosheets is extended into the visible-near-infrared region through collective reorientation of the nanosheets, increasing the Kerr coefficient by an order of magnitude to 9.49 × 10 −4 m V −2 . The enhanced response enables broadband spectral programmability within a single device, allowing simultaneous modulation of the spectral composition of light and the thermal flux. The resulting smart window exhibits continuous full-color optical tunability and achieves temperature regulation of up to 12-19°C under solar irradiation while operating at low power consumption. When implemented in a plant cultivation system, the platform alleviates heat stress, reduces water evaporation, and enables programmable control of plant morphology and nutrient accumulation. This work demonstrates a materials-based strategy for integrated light and thermal management in intelligent agricultural systems.

10.1002/adfm.78943.title: Insulating-Passivating Interfaces for Narrow-Bandgap Tin-Lead Perovskites Enable High-Photovoltage in Single- and Double-Junction Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78943.abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing non-radiative charge-carrier recombination at both p- and n-side interfaces of the perovskite layer is crucial for realizing high-voltage single- and multi-junction solar cells. Herein, it is demonstrated that co-depositing a mixture of ethane-1,2-diammonium iodide and different oleyl-based amphiphiles renders a passivator-insulator modification at the perovskite-C 60 interface, which suppresses n-side contact losses in narrow-bandgap (∼1.26 eV) Sn-Pb perovskite solar cells. Interestingly, a cationic oleyl-based amphiphile introduced concurrently with the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate hole-transport-layer, deposited from an aqueous dispersion in 1-propanol, also reduces the p-side energy loss by providing a substrate for high-quality perovskite films and limiting the contact between the doped hole-transport-layer and the perovskite layer atop. This double-sided interface modification strategy enables open-circuit voltage ( V oc ) values of up to 0.91 V-over 91% of the detailed-balance limit-for 22.6% efficient single-junction Sn-Pb perovskite solar cells. Monolithic all-perovskite tandem solar cells show V oc and efficiency values of up to 2.16 V and 26.1%, respectively. The results demonstrate that insulating-passivating interface modifications between the perovskite and charge transport layers represent an effective strategy for reducing energy losses in emerging perovskite solar cell technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79020.title: Second Coordination Shell Engineering Tunes Fe 3d Orbital Occupancy for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
10.1002/adfm.79020.abstract: ABSTRACT Second coordination shell (SCS) engineering offers a powerful strategy for fine-tuning the intrinsic activity of Fe-N-C single-atom catalysts, yet achieving targeted SCS regulation remains a formidable synthetic challenge. Herein, we propose a rational precursor-engineering approach driven by the steric hindrance of pyrazole-borate ligands to precisely construct Fe─N 4 sites with tunable boron SCS doping levels. The optimized FeN 4 B 3 /NC catalyst exhibits an exceptional half-wave potential of 0.92 V for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in alkaline media and a specific energy density of 967.03 Wh kg Zn −1 in a zinc-air battery. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that second-shell boron coordination induces ligand-field asymmetry around the Fe center, leading to an occupancy transition of -to- in the Fe 3 orbital. This reconfiguration of Fe 3d electron distribution fine-tunes the adsorption energetics by forcing electron injection into the Fe─O σ∗ anti-bonding orbital, which generates enhanced Pauli repulsion to weaken the * OH binding affinity and accelerate its desorption. This work demonstrates the pivotal role of the SCS environment in intrinsic activity modulation but also provides an orbital-level design principle for high-performance single-atom catalysts.

10.1002/adfm.78989.title: Neuromorphic Computing with Interfacial Dynamics in Electrolytic Memristive Synapse
10.1002/adfm.78989.abstract: ABSTRACT Brain-inspired computing demands devices that operate at biological voltages and embody biological principles. Existing liquid-based memristors offer ion-mediated computation yet exceed physiological levels and require rigid matrices. Here, we report a hydrogel-confined electrolytic memristive synapse (EMS) that leverages reversible Ag/AgCl interfacial electrochemistry for synaptic modulation and reservoir-state encoding at only 100 mV. The device exhibits chloride-ion-dependent memristive hysteresis and emulates fundamental synaptic learning rules. Such dynamics provide the short-term memory and nonlinearity used in a simulated reservoir-computing framework, achieving 95.05% accuracy in handwritten-digit classification and exhibiting good performance under noise and mechanical deformation. The device conformability and the design flexibility of the electrochemical interface offer new opportunities toward bio-integrated systems, promising for adaptive human-machine computing architectures.

10.1002/adfm.79058.title: γ-Ray Controlled Topological Evolution of Binders for Stable and Activated Li─S Battery Cathodes
10.1002/adfm.79058.abstract: ABSTRACT γ-ray irradiation facilitates controllable, clean, and reagent-free cross-linking of polymer networks without side reactions. Leveraging these merits, we precisely tune the irradiation dose to engineer a three-dimensional (3D) poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) binder network for lithium-sulfur (Li─S) batteries. By integrating multiscale synchrotron radiation X-ray characterization techniques, we elucidate how the γ-ray irradiation dose governs the 3D network structure and consequently regulates sulfur cathode stability and sulfur reaction kinetics without using catalysts. The optimal dose of 3 kGy yields a favorable PVA binder network featuring a dense framework, favorable connectivity, and homogeneous spatial distribution. The interpenetrating structure composed of binder, sulfur, and conductive agent leads to coupling of the mechanical architecture with the electron-conductive network, accompanied by high-flux lithium-ion diffusion, thereby relieving cathode volume variation and promoting sulfur interconversion kinetics. This resulting sulfur cathode delivers a capacity decay rate of only 0.045% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. Moreover, a 1.23 Ah-level pouch cell fabricated with the 3 kGy dose-enabled PVA (3-PVA) binder achieves an energy density of 390.2 Wh kg −1 . This study highlights γ-ray irradiation as a clean and controllable strategy to engineer binder topological structure, disclosing dose-dependent structure-property relationships that govern electrode mechanics and electrochemistry.

10.1002/adfm.79024.title: H 2 O 2 -Stimulus-Responsive NIR-II Imaging Employing an Organic Radical as Resonance Energy Transfer Acceptor for High-Security Information Encryption
10.1002/adfm.79024.abstract: ABSTRACT Optical information encryption technology has emerged as a crucial strategy for ensuring data security. In particular, the integration of second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) fluorescence imaging and chemical stimulus-triggered decryption presents a promising approach for constructing high-security optical encryption systems. Nevertheless, no related encryption materials have been reported due to the absence of efficient strategies for modulating NIR-II fluorescence. To overcome these limitations, an organic radical composite MPTCar 2+ -MPTCar •+ -CB[8] was rationally designed to modulate the NIR-II fluorescence of NaYF 4 :3%Nd rare-earth nanoparticles (RENPs) through resonance energy transfer (RET), facilitating the fabrication of the high-security encryption material named RENPs-MPT +• . This material only generated a fluorescence signal under specific NIR-II imaging conditions after the H 2 O 2 -triggered conversion of the radical back to the parent compound. These dual-security mechanisms endowed the encryption material with a high-level security. Moreover, the combination of this material with permanently fluorescent RENPs-MPT 2+ allowed for the introduction of deceptive pseudo-information to further enhance encryption security, offering an innovative model for the development of high-performance advanced optical encryption technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79051.title: Adaptive Interfacial Recognition Through Proton-Coupled Force Reconfiguration in MOF@COF Composites
10.1002/adfm.79051.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving dynamic, in situ switchable molecular recognition in porous composites remains challenging due to the difficulty of precisely modulating interfacial noncovalent interactions at the atomic level. Here, we demonstrated that proton-coupled interfacial force reconstruction served as a general and efficient regulatory strategy to control adsorption-desorption behaviors in a metal-organic framework (MOFs)-based covalent organic framework (COF) composite, NH 2 -UiO-66@COF-TpDBA (NU@FC). Reversible protonation-deprotonation at carboxyl sites induced precise redistribution of the interfacial noncovalent force field, thereby endowing switchable molecular capture and markedly improving the utilization efficiency of interfacial active sites, constructing a stimuli-responsive adsorption platform featuring molecular capture and release. This atomic-scale regulation, coupled with solvent- triggered microenvironment modulation, allowed adaptive recognition of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) under diverse environments. Combined with the mechanically reinforced sheath-tube-protected solid-phase microextraction device (STP-SPME), this proton-responsive interfacial regulation strategy was extended to an in situ, low-cost, anti-interference sample pretreatment system, achieving reliable identification and efficient extraction of trace organic pollutants from complex environmental matrices. Beyond device-level performance, this study established proton-coupled force reconstruction as a general design principle for constructing intelligently responsive MOF-COF composites, bridging atomic-scale interfacial modulation with expansive environmental analysis.

10.1002/adfm.79047.title: In Situ Interfacial Assembly of Dynamic Semi-Interpenetrating Biopolymer Networks for Robust and Mechanically Adaptive Droplet Interfaces
10.1002/adfm.79047.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust yet rapidly adaptive interfacial films are difficult to construct from naturally derived polymers because of their limited structural programmability. Herein, we report an in situ stepwise interfacial assembly strategy that transforms β-sheet-rich silk fibroin (SF) and rhamnolipid-modified chitosan (CS-RL) into a strong, dynamic oil-water interfacial network. The resulting interfacial film rapidly transforms from a spherical droplet geometry to distorted tubular shape within seconds without rupture, and exhibiting markedly enhanced dilational rheological properties. Abundant β-sheet provides rigid hydrophobic nanodomains, while flexible SF chains and positively charged CS-RL form a semi-interpenetrating network through electrostatic attractions. Additionally, the hydrophobic interactions between β-sheet domains and CS-RL create load-bearing reinforcing nodes and dynamic polymer junctions, enabling coherent network remodeling and efficient stress dissipation under deformation. This unique interfacial network contributes to stable interface and controllable interfacial releasing and transportation. Emulsions stabilized by this network remain stable after 15 months and show pH-responsive drug release even under acidic conditions. The network also enables reversible transport of 200 nm nanoplastics across both oil-water and oil-oil interfaces. This work establishes a molecular-topological design principle for creating strong, adaptive, and functional natural-polymer interfacial films, offering broad opportunities for advanced soft matter systems with programmable properties.

10.1002/adfm.79009.title: Spatiotemporally Programmable Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy Activation Disarms the Senescence-Immunity Axis for Targeted Intervertebral Disc Regeneration
10.1002/adfm.79009.abstract: ABSTRACT Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) causes low back pain, yet the causal link between nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence and immune dysregulation remains unclear. Here, we identify that senescent NPCs drive M1 polarization through chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) dysfunction-dependent NLRP3 inflammasome activation and GSDMD-mediated HMGB1 secretion, establishing HMGB1 as the core upstream effector of the senescence-immunity axis. To intercept this cascade, we engineer a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogel (TA@HA-PD-EVs AR7 ) with differential release kinetics, rapidly releasing tannic acid (TA) for on-demand antioxidant preconditioning and sustainably delivering AR7-loaded EVs for CMA reactivation, enabling a functional sequential intervention. This system degrades NLRP3, blocks HMGB1 release, suppresses NPC senescence and SASP, and restores extracellular matrix homeostasis. Leveraging intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM1) as a surface-enriched receptor on senescent NPCs, we construct senescence-targeted EVs for source-specific HMGB1 blockade. In a rat puncture model, the targeted hydrogel preserves disc height and MRI signal, reduces M1 macrophage infiltration, and attenuates NPC senescence without systemic toxicity. Notably, senescence-targeted delivery alone achieves efficacy equivalent to dual targeting, confirming HMGB1 as the dominant driver. This work transforms CMA into an actionable checkpoint and provides a precision hydrogel platform that spatiotemporally disrupts the senescence-immunity vicious cycle, offering a paradigm for IVDD.

10.1002/adfm.78462.title: Spatially Decoupled Electron and Lithium Storage at Fe/Solid Electrolyte Interphase Interfaces
10.1002/adfm.78462.abstract: ABSTRACT Extra lithium storage in transition-metal nanoparticles remains debated because interfacial reactions are difficult to distinguish. Using Fe/C as a model anode, we combine in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and magnetometry to resolve two concurrent storage processes. Magnetometry identifies electron accumulation in Fe 3d orbitals at Fe/Li 2 O rich interfaces, consistent with space charge storage. Furthermore, EPR reveals a reversible, potential-dependent radical formation within the polymeric solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) after its initial formation. Density functional theory supports Fe-catalyzed ring opening of carbonate solvents and chain-radical intermediates that undergo polymerization and reconstruction. These results show that the dynamic organic SEI participates in reversible charge storage alongside inorganic Fe/Li 2 O interfaces. Thus, the traditionally believed inactive Fe-dominated materials deliver a reversible capacity of 554 mAh g −1 at 2 A g −1 , leading to an energy density of 100 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 100 W kg −1 in an asymmetric lithium ion capacitor with activated carbon as the cathode. These findings extend established interfacial storage concepts to radical-mediated charge storage within a dynamically reconstructed SEI.
authors: Hongling Duan, Xiaoling Teng, Bin Wang, Yi Wan, Xiangkun Li, Yujie Xu, Yuqi Li, Hengjun Liu, Zhiqiang Zhao, Pawin Iamprasertkun, Lijun Yang, Nuria Tapia-Ruiz, Qiang Li, Mingbo Wu, Han Hu

10.1002/adfm.78645.title: Drop-on-Demand Printed Negative Dielectric Anisotropy Liquid Crystal Droplets for Adaptive Complex Beam Manipulation and Assessment
10.1002/adfm.78645.abstract: ABSTRACT Adaptive manipulation of vectorial optical fields is important for optical metrology, imaging, and structured light-related applications, yet existing approaches often rely on bulky or sequentially operated systems. Here we demonstrate an inkjet-printed negative dielectric anisotropy nematic liquid crystal droplet platform that unifies adaptive complex beam generation and full-vectorial optical field sensing within a single printed architecture. For complex beam generation, electric-field-driven director reconfiguration in the droplets produces tunable birefringence and wavelength-dependent polarization textures, including skyrmionic-like optical fields. For adaptive full-vectorial optical field sensing, the same droplet array enables spectral and polarization retrieval through wavelength-dependent intensity patterns and division-of-wavefront polarimetry, while also functioning as a microlens array for Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensing to reconstruct phase. These results establish negative dielectric anisotropy liquid crystal droplets as a scalable soft-matter photonic system for adaptive beam manipulation and multidimensional optical field characterization.
