10.1002/adfm.78290.title: Support-Geometry-Directed Multidimensional Pore Networks Enable High-Performance Low-Pt Fuel Cells
10.1002/adfm.78290.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen transport in cathode catalyst layers remains a major barrier to high-performance low-Pt fuel cells, yet the pore-network features governing transport across length scales are poorly defined. Here we show that carbon-support geometry can direct the formation of accessible multidimensional pore networks in catalyst layers, thereby regulating oxygen transport under high-current operation. Thermolabile mixed-ligand zeolitic imidazolate frameworks were used as precursors to generate carbon supports with controlled particle size and surface concavity. Using these model supports, we establish how support geometry governs particle packing and catalyst-layer architecture. Combined focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy and N 2 sorption analyses reveal that the optimal catalyst layer exhibits a porosity of 58.2%, an open-pore ratio of 99.6%, and a continuous pore-size distribution spanning sub-35 to 900 nm. This interconnected pore network lowers oxygen-transport resistance and improves the accessibility of the triple-phase boundary. Consequently, membrane electrode assemblies deliver a peak power density of 1.30 W cm −2 under H 2 -air at 0.05 mg Pt cm −2 , outperforming commercial Pt/C and surpassing many reported Pt-based catalysts operated at higher loadings. Results identify multiscale pore network architecture as a key descriptor governing oxygen transport and provide a support-geometry-based strategy for designing transport-efficient low-Pt fuel-cell electrodes beyond conventional active-site optimization.
authors: Xianchun Chen, Xiaotao Liu, Hongxin Yang, Pengyu Song, Zhaojing Ni, Jianke Jiang, Lin Zeng, Bo Wang, Lu Wang

10.1002/adfm.78292.title: Implanting Redox Dual Sites on Crystalline Carbon Nitride for High-Efficiency Photocatalytic Selective Oxidative Coupling of Benzylamine into N-benzylidenebenzylamine
10.1002/adfm.78292.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient photocatalysis over polymeric carbon nitride (PCN) for value-added chemical synthesis is challenged by rapid charge carrier recombination and sluggish surface redox reaction kinetics. Herein, crystalline carbon nitride (CCN) introduced with Co single atoms and cyano groups (Co-CCN) was successfully synthesized through a molten-salt method for photocatalytic selective oxidative coupling of benzylamine (BA) into N-benzylidenebenzylamine (NBBA). In comparison to PCN and CCN, the obtained Co-CCN exhibits much higher photocatalytic performance, with both BA conversion and NBBA selectivity reaching 99%. Moreover, the NBBA yield, reaching 24.75 mmol g −1 h −1 , encouragingly outperforms almost all the reported PCN-based photocatalysts. Spectral characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the electron-deficient Co-N 4 sites act as oxidation sites, promoting hole accumulation and facilitating the adsorption and activation of BA, while the strongly electron-withdrawing cyano (-C≡N) groups act as efficient electron-extraction sites, enhancing charge separation and promoting O 2 absorption and activation, which synergistically contributes to the excellent photocatalytic activity. This study demonstrates a guidable strategy to the rational and cooperative modulation of molecular and electronic structures for efficient photocatalysis toward selective oxidative coupling of BA into NBBA, and also deepens the understanding of active sites engineering in photocatalytic organic transformation.
authors: Ruizhe Wang, Yiqing Wang, Ta Thi Thuy Nga, Bo Kou, Kaini Zhang, Binglan Wu, Ming Cao, Yufei Xu, Zhi Lin, Daming Zhao, Dong Liu, Chung-Li Dong, Shaohua Shen

10.1002/adfm.78296.title: Photo-Degradable Polyester Networks and Multi-Photon Printed Objects Based on Cyclic Ketene Acetals
10.1002/adfm.78296.abstract: ABSTRACT Radical ring-opening polymerization (RROP) of cyclic ketene acetals (CKAs) constitutes a powerful avenue to biodegradable polyesters via radical polymerization. CKA-based degradable polymers have been established mainly as linear polymers, while networks from CKA-based RROP remain scarce despite their potential as degradable materials. Herein, a photoreversible RROP-polyester network based on poly(2-methylene-1,3,6-trioxocane) (PMTC) is introduced. Photoreversibility is achieved by decorating the PMTC chains with pendant pyrene chalcone (PyChal) moieties. Photoinduced [2+2] cycloaddition ( λ max = 440 nm) of the PyChal moieties affords covalent cross-links, while irradiation at λ max = 345 nm allows for network reversion as underpinned by an in-depth solution assessment of the photochemistry. The reversible nature of the photochemistry enables repeatable gel-sol transitions as shown by variations in their storage and loss modulus (resulting in G ’ changes of up to 9 kPa). Importantly, the photoreactive CKA-based polymer can be employed in light-driven multi-photon printing (MPP) without the need for any initiators, allowing the fabrication of pre-determined spatially confined architectures as evidenced by ToF-SIMS. The MPP structures can be degraded by expore to UV irradiation and alkaline conditions. We thus establish a degradable PCKA-based resist with reversible photochemistry for modular soft matter manufacturing.
authors: Till Meissner, Julian Fanelli, Vinh Xuan Truong, Rob Jones, Jens Gaitzsch, Christopher Barner-Kowollik

10.1002/adfm.78297.title: Multimodal Anti-/Deicing on Laser-Structured Polymer Surface via Photothermal Retention and Post-Abrasion Redeposition
10.1002/adfm.78297.abstract: ABSTRACT Multimodal deicing remains challenging because surfaces that perform well initially often lose essential functionality after service abrasion. Here, we establish a multimodal deicing strategy based on Ni-decorated laser-induced graphene (LIG) hierarchical surfaces. This surface integrates excellent superhydrophobicity, enhanced abrasion tolerance, anti-icing capability, and multimodal deicing performance, exhibiting a water contact angle of 162.6 ± 0.7°, an icing delay time of 224.8 ± 21.4 s, and photothermal, electrothermal, and magnetothermal deicing times of 63.2 ± 5.0 s, 56.2 ± 6.0 s, and 83.0 ± 12.3 s, respectively. The surface operates across three service states. In the initial state, the intact hierarchical architecture supports efficient multimodal deicing. After abrasion within the defined redeposition window, the retained LIG framework preserves daytime photothermal deicing, maintaining essential deicing capability despite the deterioration of electrothermal and magnetothermal functions. When all-day anti-/deicing operation is required again, secondary electrodeposition reconstructs the Ni-rich functional layer within this window, re-establishes the electrothermal and magnetothermal pathways, and enables multimodal deicing again. This surface can be prepared through a simple, scalable, and patternable route compatible with curved and large-area substrates. This work demonstrates multimodal deicing through photothermal function retention and post-abrasion redeposition, offering practical strategies for deicing interfaces under service abrasion.

10.1002/adfm.78306.title: Time-Varying Mosaic Metasurface Architecture Enabling Programmable Multi-Tone Pseudo-Doppler Spectral Engineering
10.1002/adfm.78306.abstract: ABSTRACT The pseudo-Doppler effect, an artificial frequency shift produced by time-varying phase modulation of stationary structures, offers a promising route for electromagnetic (EM) wave manipulation. However, existing time-modulated metasurfaces are predominantly spatially uniform and single-channel, limiting pseudo-Doppler generation to one frequency component per aperture and yielding symmetric harmonic spectra. Here, a time-varying mosaic metasurface (TVMM) is proposed to realize a programmable multi-tone pseudo-Doppler effect. By partitioning the aperture into independently and continuously modulated spatial channels, each assigned a distinct linear phase-ramp frequency, the TVMM enables simultaneous generation of multiple controllable pseudo-Doppler components. An X-band varactor-loaded prototype is designed, fabricated, and experimentally characterized, exhibiting continuous reflection-phase tunability approaching 300° over 9.1-10.9 GHz and robust response under oblique incidence. The multi-tone spectral states are validated using direct spectral analysis and an inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR)-based visualization protocol, in which pseudo-Doppler frequencies are linearly mapped into spatial displacements. Complex aircraft-scattering simulations and anechoic-chamber experiments consistently verify single-tone, uniform/nonuniform multi-tone, and dense-cluster pseudo-Doppler spectral states. This mosaic time-varying architecture establishes a general strategy for programmable EM spectral engineering, with potential applications in adaptive sensing, dynamic scattering control, and radar-signature management.
authors: Fan Wu, Chang Ding, Huilin Mu, Zhuoluo Wang, Mengxiao Zhao, Zhaotang Liu, Shulei Zhang, Ya Fan, Jiafu Wang

10.1002/adfm.78309.title: Simultaneously Improving the Stability and Singlet Oxygen Formation via Interlayer Confinement Effects for Efficient and Sustainable Water Purification
10.1002/adfm.78309.abstract: ABSTRACT Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are highly promising for Fenton-like catalytic degradation of refractory organic contaminants in waters. Nevertheless, surface-exposed single-atom sites on carbon supports are prone to premature deactivation and limit the utilization of short-lived reactive oxygen species in peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation processes, resulting in an inherent trade-off between catalytic activity and stability. Herein, we report an interlayer confinement strategy to precisely anchor Fe-N 4 monatomic sites within the interlayers of two-dimensional graphitic carbon nitride (SA-Fe inter -CN). Benefiting from the interlayer confinement effect, SA-Fe inter -CN exhibited significantly enhanced PMS activation performance compared with the surface-supported counterpart (SA-Fe sur -CN), achieving a high apparent reaction rate constant of 3.317 min −1 and maintaining 100% degradation efficiency after eight consecutive cycles, demonstrating excellent stability. Theoretical simulations revealed that the interlayer confinement effect strengthens metal-support interactions and lowers the energy barrier for singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) formation, thereby promoting 1 O 2 generation and utilization. The SA-Fe inter -CN/PMS system also showed strong resistance to interference in complex water matrices and real wastewater. Life cycle assessment and long-term continuous-flow operation further confirmed its practical applicability. This work resolves the long-standing activity-stability trade-off of SACs in advanced oxidation processes via the interlayer confinement effect, offering a robust strategy for efficient and sustainable wastewater treatment.
authors: Zhuoran Mei, Chen Liu, Huinan Che, Bin Liu, Yanhui Ao

10.1002/adfm.78315.title: Atomic Ni─O─Zn Bridge Engineering Enables Efficient C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.78315.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical co-reduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − is a promising route for sustainable urea synthesis, but its efficiency is limited by kinetic mismatch between CO 2 RR and NO 3 RR, and unfavorable adsorption-migration of *CO for C─N coupling. Herein, we design a nickel single-atom catalyst anchored on ZnO (Ni SA /ZnO) to coordinate CO 2 RR and NO 3 RR kinetics by promoting C─N coupling for efficient urea electrosynthesis. At −0.8 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, Ni SA /ZnO achieves urea yield rate of 41.38 mmol h −1 g cat −1 and Faradaic efficiency of 31.47%. In situ spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations collectively reveal the formation of atomically defined Ni─O─Zn interfacial bridges, inducing charge redistribution and intrinsic electronic gradient across adjacent metal sites. This electronic heterogeneity enables spatially differentiated reaction pathways, with Ni sites favoring for CO 2 activation toward *CO formation, while neighboring Zn sites facilitate NO 3 − reduction to *NH 2 . Meanwhile, DFT calculations suggest that the interfacial electronic gradient thermodynamically drives *CO migration from Ni to Zn sites, which co-localizes the key intermediates with a lowered barrier for subsequent C─N coupling. This work demonstrates that atomic-scale interfacial bridge engineering can overcome kinetic bottlenecks in sustainable urea electrosynthesis, providing a general principle for regulating intermediate spillover and coupling in multistep electrocatalysis.
authors: Yucheng Zhou, Jiaju Yang, Hua Zou, Guoshuai Liu, Shijie You

10.1002/adfm.78320.title: Ultraviolet-Induced Band Engineering in Black Phosphorus/Gallium Nitride Heterojunction Toward High-Performance Broadband Photodetection
10.1002/adfm.78320.abstract: ABSTRACT Broadband photodetectors that combine ultraviolet sensitivity with visible and near-infrared response are important for multispectral optoelectronic sensing. However, the performance of these photodetectors is often limited by weak interfacial carrier separation and inefficient gain formation. Here, we demonstrate a mixed-dimensional van der Waals heterojunction photodetector integrating two-dimensional black phosphorus (bP) with three-dimensional n-type gallium nitride (n-GaN), enabling broadband photodetection from 255 to 1800 nm. We reveal an ultraviolet-induced interfacial band engineering, in which two cooperative photogain pathways regulate both carrier lifetime and carrier transit time. Under ultraviolet illumination, hole trapping within GaN and charge accumulation at the bP/GaN interface simultaneously prolong the electron lifetime and shorten the tunneling transit time, producing a high photoconductive gain. By contrast, visible and near-infrared photons are mainly absorbed by narrow-bandgap bP, enabling broadband response through direct photocarrier generation. This wavelength-dependent carriergeneration and transport mechanism enables a responsivity of 145.67 A W −1 and a detectivity of 1.32 × 10 12 Jones under 365 nm illumination while enabling multispectral detection across the ultraviolet-to-infrared range. These results establish a wavelength-dependent band engineering strategy in mixed-dimensional van der Waals heterojunctions and provide a promising platform for high-performance broadband photodetection and multispectral perception.
authors: Zhenyu Liu, Shi Fang, Zhixiang Gao, Zhanpeng Su, Yang Kang, Muhammad Hunain Memon, Junxing Qiu, Reza Taheri Ghahrizjani, Yuchen Du, Yiguo Yan, Jiayao Li, Haochen Zhang, Xutao Zhang, Guofeng Yang, Jinshui Miao, Xiao Gong, Renjie Zhou, Yong Yan, Haiding Sun

10.1002/adfm.78334.title: Synergistic Crystallization Control and Defect Passivation via Bifunctional Hydrogen-Bonding Networks in Methylammonium-Free Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78334.abstract: ABSTRACT Methylammonium (MA)-free Cs X FA 1-X PbI 3 perovskite solar cells (PSCs), despite their commercial promise stemming from enhanced stability, face the dual challenge of controlling crystallization and achieving stable defect passivation. Here, we introduce 4-hydroxybenzamidine hydrochloride (4OHFACl) as a bifunctional additive to address these challenges. The amidinium and hydroxyl groups in 4OHFACl form hydrogen-bonding with I − and [PbI 6 ] 4− in perovskite precursors, regulating the colloidal properties of the precursor solution to optimize nucleation and crystallization kinetics. This enables a synergistic process of rapid nucleation followed by slow crystal growth, yielding high-quality perovskite films with enlarged grains and low residual strain. Owing to its higher pKa, the amidinium group also provides stable defect passivation, effectively suppressing non-radiative recombination. Consequently, 4OHFACl-modified PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.16% along with enhanced operational stability, retaining 90% of their original efficiency after 900 h of continuous illumination. Moreover, this approach exhibits excellent scalability, enabling a 66 cm 2 (aperture area) perovskite solar module to attain a champion PCE of 21.15%, underscoring its potential for practical large-area fabrication. This work demonstrates a new strategy to couple precursor coordination chemistry with defect passivation, enabling concurrent control of crystallization kinetics and defect energetics for stable perovskite solar cells.
authors: Yu Chen, Qingshun Dong, Shiqi Rong, Peng Xu, Yongfu Liang, Jiazhen Wei, Yufa Li, Mingyan Wu, Hao Xian, Yantao Shi, Zhiyuan Xu, Young Sun, Shengye Jin, Wenming Tian, Yuanmin Du

10.1002/adfm.78336.title: Orientation-Programmed Effective Fields in FeCo@N-rGO Magnetic Chains for Multifunctional Electromagnetic Materials
10.1002/adfm.78336.abstract: ABSTRACT Anisotropic microwave absorbers offer designable performance for next-generation electronic devices, yet the underlying orientation-performance mechanism remains unclear, and heat accumulation and short-circuit risks persist. Here, chain-like FeCo@N-rGO/silicone composites with controlled 0°, 45°, and 90° orientations are fabricated by interfacial adsorption-carbonization and magnetic-field-assisted hot pressing. The ultrathin N-rGO shell amplifies interfacial and dipolar polarization, enabling effective absorption at 25 wt.% in paraffin and 35 wt.% in silicone, lower than most reported magnetic metal absorbers with comparable absorption intensity. The 45° orientation delivers an ultrawide absorption bandwidth of 7.7 GHz with a minimum reflection loss of −49.84 dB, whereas the 90° orientation covers low-frequency 5G bands. An effective-field mechanism is established, revealing that orientation regulates depolarization and shape-anisotropy fields, thereby decoupling polarization, magnetic resonance, conduction, and eddy-current losses. The oriented composites further achieve an in-plane thermal conductivity of 4.07 W·m −1 ·K −1 and an insulating resistivity of 8.7 × 10 11 Ω·cm, establishing an orientation-field-loss design principle for multifunctional anisotropic electromagnetic materials.

10.1002/adfm.78338.title: Desert Plant Inspired Hierarchical Nanofibrous Membranes for Integrated Solar Desalination and Heavy Metal Remediation
10.1002/adfm.78338.abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater scarcity is a global challenge, increasingly compounded by heavy metal contamination of water systems. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation has emerged as a compelling solution owing to its energy efficiency and environmental benignity. Inspired by a desert plant − Alhagi camelorum , we develop a biomass-based composite nanofibrous membrane to facilitate the capture of heavy metals in contaminated water and solar-driven water evaporation. Following the electrospinning of cellulose, chitosan, and an indium-based metal-organic framework (MIL-68(In)), the in situ growth of copper oxide (CuO) nanoflowers is realized on the nanofiber network. The hierarchical porous network − assembled from interwoven nanofibers decorated with roughened nanoflowers − enables exceptional broadband light trapping. Meanwhile, the CuO nanoflowers serve as a catalytic interface, activating interfacial water molecules through efficient charge transfer that lowers the dissociation energy barrier, thereby enabling rapid and stable vapor generation. Under one-sun irradiation (1 kW m − 2 ), the membrane achieves an evaporation rate of 2.80 kg m − 2 h − 1 and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 98.95%. Density functional theory calculations elucidate the atomistic and electronic mechanisms underpinning this exceptional performance. This biomass-derived photothermal membrane simultaneously combines the capture of heavy metals and water purification, representing a meaningful advance in water purification and resource recovery.
authors: Yuqiong He, Ronggang Luo, Shengbo Ge, Kaixin Jiang, Kirsten Dyer, Xiaojian Zhou, Ben Bin Xu, Xuehua Zhang, Guanben Du, Kaimeng Xu

10.1002/adfm.78339.title: Ladder-Type Polymer Enables Dual-Directional Phonon Bridging in Thermally Conductive h-BN/TOCNF Film
10.1002/adfm.78339.abstract: ABSTRACT The persistent trade-off between preserving the intrinsic thermal conductivity of fillers and minimizing interfacial thermal resistance remains a critical bottleneck in polymer-based thermal interface materials (TIMs). Herein, we address this challenge through a “dual-directional bridging” strategy using poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), a rigid ladder-type conjugated polymer, as an interfacial mediator. Unlike conventional modifiers, BBL features an extended superplane architecture that concurrently establishes maximized π - π interlocking with the hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) basal plane and weaves dense hydrogen-bonding networks with the TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofiber (TOCNF) matrix. Combined spectroscopic analyses and solvent-corrected DFT calculations support π -associated coupling between BBL and h-BN together with hydrogen-bonding interactions between BBL and TOCNF, increasing the calculated interfacial binding energy from 0.85 to 2.86 eV under an aqueous environment. Crucially, this creates a continuous “dual-directional phonon bridge” that substantially mitigates interfacial thermal resistance and localized phonon scattering, all without disrupting the intrinsic h-BN lattice. Consequently, the BBL@h-BN/TOCNF film achieves in-plane and through-plane thermal conductivities of 8.78 and 1.18 W m −1 K −1 , outperforming standard commercial thermal silicone grease and demonstrating superior heat extraction in simulated high-power CPU cooling. Overall, this work establishes a rational structural paradigm to unlock the macroscopic thermo-mechanical potential of two-dimensional (2D) composites for next-generation electronics.
authors: Xian Wu, Zhixu Zhang, Jupeng Chen, Chen Wang, Yiwen Chen, Xinbo Zhang, Bo Yuan, Mengzhu Zhao, Yiqing Li, Guigan Fang, Hongqi Dai, Chen Su, Xiu Wang, Jianchun Jiang

10.1002/adfm.78359.title: Programmable Tensegrity-Inspired Metamaterials With Compression-Torsion Coupling and Tunable Energy Dissipation
10.1002/adfm.78359.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical metamaterials with programmable deformation, tunable energy dissipation, and reusable impact-mitigation capability are highly desirable for adaptive protective systems and multifunctional mechanical devices. However, achieving stable compression-torsion coupling together with post-fabrication programmability and recoverable energy dissipation remains challenging. Here, we develop a tensegrity-inspired mechanical metamaterial based on the structural duality between Kresling origami and three-strut tensegrity structure. Through discrete hole-position switching, the metamaterial enables programmable configuration switching, stiffness regulation, and configuration-dependent compression-torsion coupling within a single physical architecture. Within the investigated design space, the structural configuration strongly influences the accessible energy-dissipation range, whereas elastic-member stiffness regulates its magnitude. The three-strut tensegrity unit cell exhibits recoverable deformation, stable cyclic response, and pronounced torsional output. Multicell assemblies further translate unit-cell-level programmability into collective deformation pathways, enabling staged deformation, graded energy dissipation, and chirality-dependent Poisson's ratio responses. Dynamic impact experiments demonstrate reduced peak transmitted forces, suppressed rebound, and repeatable impact-mitigation behavior at the unit-cell level. This work establishes a programmable tensegrity-inspired metamaterial platform for regulating nonlinear mechanical responses and provides a design strategy for adaptive impact mitigation, soft robotics, and reusable energy-dissipating systems.

10.1002/adfm.78372.title: Amino-Acid-Assisted Interfacial Polymerization Enables Reaction-Diffusion of COF Membranes for High-Performance Desalination
10.1002/adfm.78372.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes hold significant promise for energy-efficient desalination, yet achieving precise control over their crystallization and selective-layer architecture remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an amino-acid-assisted interfacial polymerization (AAIP) strategy that regulates reaction-diffusion dynamics to enable the fabrication of highly crystalline, ultramicroporous membranes. L-cysteine serves as a bifunctional molecular modulator, through cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen-bond interactions to sequester isophthalic dihydrazide (IPH) monomers, thereby regulating monomer transport toward the reaction interface. The resulting reaction-diffusion-controlled growth facilitates the emergence of Turing-patterned surface structure and promotes an ordered ABC-stacked framework with high crystallinity. The resulting Tp-IPH-Cys 20% membrane exhibits a refined ultramicroporous architecture. When tested with 2000 ppm NaCl feed solution under an operating pressure of 15 bar, the Tp-IPH-Cys 20% membrane delivers a NaCl rejection rate of 98.1% and a water permeance of 1.0 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 , outperforming conventional COF membranes while demonstrating exceptional durability under both acidic exposure and 104 h of continuous hydraulic stress. More broadly, this work establishes amino-acid-directed reaction-diffusion engineering as a versatile strategy for controlling the evolution of crystalline porous membranes, offering new pathways for mitigating the permeability-selectivity trade-off in advanced separation materials.
authors: Zeyu Yang, Guishan Hu, Tiantian Liu, Junke Qiu, Gaojing Du, Jiaqi Li, Junyong Zhu, Miaomiao Tian, Yatao Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78382.title: Interfacial Superspreading-Induced Underoil Adhesive via Adaptive Displacement and Assembly
10.1002/adfm.78382.abstract: ABSTRACT Robust underoil adhesives are critical for maintaining the safety and sealing performance of oil infrastructure, but oil's low surface energy and high viscosity hinder strong adhesion by trapping an interfacial oil layer. We report an interfacial superspreading-induced (ISI) adhesive formed by self-adaptive assembly of an emulsion precursor at the oil-solid interface. It superspreads on oily substrates within 180 ms and crosslinks in 20 s. The ISI adhesive achieves underoil adhesion strengths up to 11.37 ± 0.50 MPa and adheres effectively to various substrates in emulsion, water, and air. Confocal microscopy and in situ Raman spectroscopy show that the precursor displaces the retained oil layer, allowing direct substrate contact. This strategy offers a versatile solution for emergency repair of subsea pipelines and oil tank sealing under challenging conditions.
authors: Shaofan He, Maolin Sun, Jiajian Zhang, Longge Bai, Jiankai Sun, Che Wu, Kai Wang, Jianying Huang, Weilong Cai, Dezhao Hao, Yuekun Lai

10.1002/adfm.78442.title: A Magneto-Mechanically Activated Nerve Guidance Conduit Promotes Peripheral Nerve Regeneration via TIMP1-Mediated Membrane Tension Transfer
10.1002/adfm.78442.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite architectural advances, current nerve guidance conduits inadequately replicate the mechanoactive microenvironment required for functional neural regeneration. While membrane tension is increasingly recognized as an important biomechanical regulator of axonal extension and glial behavior, its therapeutic exploitation in peripheral nerve repair remains limited. Whether and how membrane tension-related cues are relayed from support cells to neurons also remains unclear. Here, we developed a magneto-mechanical augmentation strategy by functionalizing mesenchymal stem cells with superparamagnetic Fe 3 O 4 @polydopamine nanoparticles (FP@MSCs) and incorporating these cells into an aligned PCL/GelMA conduit. Under static magnetic stimulation, FP@MSCs showed increased membrane tension, cytoskeletal remodeling, and accelerated differentiation toward a Schwann cell-like phenotype. Mechanistically, transcriptomic profiling and protein-protein interaction mapping pointed to TIMP1 as a candidate paracrine mediator, which subsequently activated the ITGB1/CD63-FAK axis in recipient NE-4C cells. Further analyses, including atomic force microscopy and osmotic perturbation, indicated that elevated membrane tension drove TIMP1 secretion, which subsequently amplified membrane tension in NE-4C and promoted neuronal differentiation. In a rat 15 mm sciatic nerve gap model, the magneto-mechanically activated conduit promoted motor, sensory and histological recovery. Together, these findings support a TIMP1-dependent intercellular mechanotransductive pathway and suggest a magneto-mechanical strategy for enhancing the regenerative performance of nerve guidance conduits.

authors: Zhengqin Wang, Hua-Lu Zhuang, Jincheng Yu, Hezhang Li, Yilin Jiang, Jun Pei, Zhanran Han, Lu Chen, Chen Chen, Su-Wei Zhang, Chao Wang, Yuzuru Miyazaki, Jing-Feng Li

10.1002/adfm.78264.title: Anion Exchange Membrane in Water Electrolysis: From Material Research to Integrated Component Operation
10.1002/adfm.78264.abstract: ABSTRACT Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM-WE) has attracted increasing interest because it combines the compact device architecture of membrane-based electrolyzers with the potential to utilize platinum-group-metal-free catalysts. Despite rapid advances in anion exchange membrane (AEM) hydroxide conductivity and alkaline stability, with some AEMs demonstrating over 8000 h stability and conductivities approaching 300 mS cm −1 , these material-level advances have not translated proportionally into device operation. Consequently, long-term electrolyzer lifetimes remain far below those of proton-exchange membrane systems. In this perspective, we argue that the AEM should be considered not merely as a hydroxide-conducting separator, but as a functional component of the membrane electrode assembly, influencing water transport, interfacial compatibility, gas crossover, and failure mechanisms. We first discuss why the conductivity and alkaline-soaking stability of AEM alone are insufficient predictors of practical performance. We then examine coupled challenges including interfacial effects, oxidative degradation near the anode, chemical-mechanical degradation, and the limitations of current evaluation methods. Finally, we outline how future progress may depend on integrating membrane chemistry with scalable fabrication, greener synthesis, and more consistent benchmarking protocols. We hope this perspective helps situate current membrane research within a broader device-level context and highlights key questions for the next stage of AEM-WE development.
authors: Liqiang Yin, Rong Ren, Licheng Sun

10.1002/adfm.79129.title: Balanced Cr 3+ and RE 3+ Luminescence in a Novel Non-Concentration-Quenching Cs 2 RbCrF 6 : High-Efficiency Wide-Coverage NIR Phosphors Toward Solvent Extraction Monitoring
10.1002/adfm.79129.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving wide-coverage near-infrared (NIR) luminescence spanning from NIR-I to NIR-II regions in Cr 3+ -sensitized rare-earth-ion (RE 3+ ) phosphor systems without sacrificing the Cr 3+ emission intensity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a novel double-perovskite-structured Cs 2 RbScF 6 host with large interionic separation was first discovered, which enables successful full substitution of Sc 3+ by Cr 3+ without concentration quenching. The resulting Cs 2 RbCrF 6 phosphor exhibits broadband NIR emission centered at 775 nm with a full width at half maximum of ∼118 nm, and high internal/external quantum efficiencies of 84.2%/32.1%. More importantly, this Cr-rich host serves as an effective sensitizing platform for RE 3+ ions (i.e., Yb 3+ , Nd 3+ , Er 3+ ), extending the spectral coverage from 650 to 1600 nm via efficient Cr 3+ →RE 3+ energy transfer, while remarkably retaining substantial Cr 3+ emission intensity. This balanced coexistence of intense broadband Cr 3+ and multiple RE 3+ characteristic emissions enables a genuinely wide-coverage NIR luminescence profile spanning 650-1600 nm. Finally, a prototype NIR phosphor-converted LEDs device was fabricated and innovatively demonstrated practical utility for quantitatively monitoring various RE 3+ concentrations and detecting aqueous-phase entrainment in the organic phase during solvent extraction. This work provides a rational design strategy for developing high-efficiency wide-coverage NIR phosphors and offers a new broadband NIR light source for real-time monitoring of RE solvent extraction processes.

10.1002/adfm.79218.title: Fully Exposed Confined Pt-Ru Sites in Gas-Liquid Separation Channels Synergistically Boost Multi-Scenario Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
10.1002/adfm.79218.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of highly efficient and stable hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts is crucial for the large-scale production of clean hydrogen energy. Herein, PtRu composite nanomaterials confined to TiO 2 nanotube arrays were prepared by anodic oxidation-hydrothermal method, which integrated multifunctional active sites such as single-atom Pt, single-atom Ru, Pt clusters; Through synergistic effects, the material maintains remarkable HER activity with very low noble-metal loadings, and significantly surpasses commercial Pt/C and PtRu/C catalysts in diverse applications. In situ infrared and Raman spectroscopy observed the interfacial adsorption of H 2 O and [H] formation on Pt/Ru sites, unveiling their co-participation, while DFT calculations further clarified the synergy of multiple active sites in H 2 O adsorption, activation, dissociation, and [H] production. Meanwhile, by creating a state of enrichment in the hollow tubes and wall pores, the hollow structure promotes the active sites exposure and confined metal sites, while the abundant pores on the nanotube walls provide dynamic fluid channels for the timely release of hydrogen, forming gas-liquid separation channels with the electrolyte and promoting matter exchange. This study combines surface-rich supports and multi-functional sites to boost noble metal utilization, and establishes gas-liquid separation channels to promotes matter exchange, offering a strategy for ultra-low noble metal HER electrocatalysts.

10.1002/adfm.79174.title: Electron Localization at In-on-Li Antisites Enables High-Current-Density Compatibility of Chloride Solid Electrolytes with Lithium Metal
10.1002/adfm.79174.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-metal all-solid-state batteries offer a pathway toward high-specific-energy storage but remain limited by instability at the solid-state electrolyte (SSE)/Li interface. Fluorinated chloride solid electrolytes exhibit improved kinetic stability toward Li metal at low current densities (≤0.2 mA cm −2 ), but become increasingly susceptible to electron injection at high current densities (≥1 mA cm −2 ), leading to sustained reductive decomposition and interfacial degradation. Here, we develop LiCl-deficient Li 3-x InCl 5.2-x F 0.8 solid electrolytes to regulate interfacial electron transport. LiCl deficiency generates Li vacancies preferentially at 4 g sites and lowers the barrier for In migration into these vacancies, thereby forming In-on-Li antisites. These antisite-centered defect environments serve as electron-localization centers that trap injected electrons, suppress long-range electronic transport, and inhibit the reduction of In 3+ to metallic In. This electron-localization mechanism promotes a self-passivating interphase and markedly improves high-current-density compatibility with Li metal. The optimized Li 2.76 InCl 4.96 F 0.8 composition exhibits an ionic conductivity of 1.24 mS cm −1 , stable Li plating/stripping at 1.0-1.5 mA cm −2 , and durable full-cell cycling with LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 (NCM622) cathodes at 1 mA cm −2 . These findings establish LiCl-deficiency-induced electron localization as an atomic-scale electronic regulation strategy for enabling high-current-density compatibility between chloride solid electrolytes and Li-metal anodes, thereby advancing the development of high-specific-energy all-solid-state lithium-metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79061.title: Tantalum-Palladium Ultrathin Resistance Hydrogen Sensor
10.1002/adfm.79061.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen sensors play a pivotal role in tomorrow's hydrogen economy, yet today's sensors cannot fulfill all needs. We rationally design resistive thin-film hydrogen sensors based on tantalum alloys. The heart of the sensor is a tantalum-based layer, that gradually absorbs hydrogen when exposed to hydrogen, which in turn results in a measurable change of the resistance. In situ x-ray diffraction and x-ray and neutron reflectometry show that nanoconfinement efficiently suppresses unwanted phase transitions present in bulk when the material is exposed to hydrogen and enables completely elastic expansion, yielding a stable, hysteresis-free and long-life sensor. Additionally, alloying is used to maximize the sensitivity of the sensor. The resulting sensor, combining a 5 nm sensing layer with a 4 nm adhesion layer, a 5 nm capping layer, and polymer protective layers, enables a low-cost, reversible hydrogen sensor with a hysteresis-free sensing range from ppb to 100% in anaerobic conditions at room temperature and sub-second response-times.

10.1002/adfm.79158.title: Pre-Embedded Intramolecular Donor-Acceptor Engineering in Isoreticular Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.79158.abstract: ABSTRACT Modulating intrinsic molecular dipoles via donor-acceptor ( D - A ) skeleton engineering is an effective strategy for promoting charge dynamics in organic photocatalysts. However, conventional intermolecular D - A covalent organic frameworks (COFs) suffer from weak electronic coupling and uncontrollable dipole strength, with elusive structure-dipole-activity relationships. Herein, two isoreticular imine-linked COFs are fabricated via pre-embedded intramolecular D - A engineering. Unlike conventional intermolecular D - A COFs assembled from independent donor and acceptor monomers, the donor and acceptor units are covalently locked within a single C 3 -symmetric building block. Periodic integration of the pre-embedded intramolecular D - A motif endows CR-COF-7 with improved crystalline ordering, accessible porosity, and enhanced framework polarization. Periodic calculations reveal an electrostatic potential step of 0.220 eV across the CR-COF-7 layer and a 0.76 eV reduction in work function, favoring electron transfer to platinum (Pt). Complementary spectroscopic and photoelectrochemical measurements support the notion of facilitated exciton conversion and enhanced utilization of photogenerated charges. Consequently, CR-COF-7 exhibits a photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 12.09 mmol g −1 h −1 , approximately 150-fold higher than that of CR-COF-8, and outperforms an intermolecular D - A COF control. This work reveals the dipole regulation mechanism of intramolecular D - A modification and provides a general design principle for high-efficiency COF-based solar photocatalysts.

10.1002/adfm.79195.title: Synergistic Surface Reconstruction to Suppresses Interfacial Losses in Inverted Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adfm.79195.abstract: ABSTRACT Inverted perovskite solar cells have become a leading photovoltaic architecture with considerable promise for scalable manufacturing, yet the resulting top surface often contains residual precursor species, heterogeneous defect terminations, and unfavorable energetics that intensify nonradiative recombination at the interface. Here, we introduce a surface reconstruction strategy based on piperazinium iodide (PipI) and piperazinium bromide (PipBr). The two salts share a bifunctional piperazinium scaffold while providing distinct I − and Br − counterions, enabling coordinated regulation of surface binding and the local halide environment. These structural and electronic changes decrease trap-assisted nonradiative recombination and improve charge transfer across the perovskite/C 60 interface. Notably, the perovskite films are fabricated through an antisolvent-free process, eliminating the additional antisolvent dripping step and thereby simplifying film processing and improving its compatibility with large-area fabrication. The optimized inverted perovskite solar cell achieves a power conversion efficiency of 25.68% over an active area of 0.09 cm 2 , with an open-circuit voltage of 1.154 V and a fill factor of 86.54%. The strategy is further transferred to a 4 cm 2 mini-module, delivering an efficiency of 22.78%. These results provide an effective molecular design method for low-loss and scalable electron-selective interfaces in antisolvent-free perovskite photovoltaics.

10.1002/adfm.79159.title: Customizing Electronic-Physical Dual-Shield Interlayers via d-p Orbital Hybridization for Ultra-Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
10.1002/adfm.79159.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising protective interlayers to mitigate Zn dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions, yet their aqueous vulnerability and unresolved electronic mechanisms hamper practical application. Herein, we propose an electronic structure engineering strategy via d-p orbital hybridization to customize the Zn anode interphase. Using UiO-66 derivatives (-NH 2 , -COOH, and -F 4 ) as models, theoretical calculations reveal that strengthening the substituents’ electron-withdrawing capability deepens d-p orbital coupling and shifts the π* d-band center toward the Fermi level, thus inducing intense spatial charge polarization and enhancing Zn 2+ affinity. Experimentally, the highly fluorinated UiO-66-F 4 achieves the highest Zn 2+ adsorption, drives selective SO 4 2− exclusion, accelerates desolvation, and enables rapid ion transport. Synergizing with inherent physical hydrophobicity, this unique electronic-physical dual-shield of the UiO-66-F 4 interlayer effectively averts H 2 O-induced side reactions and ensures highly reversible Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the Zn@UiO-66-F 4 anode delivers a 3600 h lifespan at 5 mA cm −2 and sustains 560 h under a stringent 90% depth of discharge, outperforming most MOF-modified anodes. Furthermore, flexible full cells exhibit impressive cycling stability and reliably power wearable systems even under severe deformation. Overall, this work establishes d-p orbital hybridization regulation as a powerful paradigm for customizing advanced functional interlayers toward ultra-stable Zn metal anodes.

10.1002/adfm.79117.title: Structural Locking Strategy in Copper(I) Iodide Cluster-Based Scintillator for High-Fidelity Conformal X-Ray Imaging
10.1002/adfm.79117.abstract: ABSTRACT Conformal scintillators have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation high-fidelity X-ray imaging, owing to their superior geometric adaptability. However, realizing such imaging remains challenging because high-performance scintillators typically suffer from insufficient processing stability, whereas conventional flexible scintillator films fail to faithfully reproduce microscopic surface topographies. Herein, we report a structural locking strategy for constructing a copper halide cluster scintillator, (PyEA) 4 Cu 4 I 4 (PyEA = Pyridin-3-yl acetate). Dense hydrogen bonds, π-π interactions, and metal/halide to ligand charge transfer processes lock both intermolecular and intramolecular architectures, endowing (PyEA) 4 Cu 4 I 4 with a near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield, a high X-ray light yield of 34000 photons MeV −1 , and superior water stability. Leveraging these characteristics, we explored a water-driven adaptive reconstruction strategy by blending (PyEA) 4 Cu 4 I 4 with a hydrophilic polymer matrix, enabling the film to dynamically conform to irregular surfaces and achieve high-fidelity conformal X-ray imaging. This work establishes a general paradigm for translating water-stable scintillators into adaptive conformal imaging platforms, opening new opportunities for high-fidelity X-ray imaging of complex three-dimensional objects.

10.1002/adfm.79147.title: Strengthened D-p Orbital Hybridization Via Interlayer Coupling Enables Sulfur Redox Kinetics in Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79147.abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent wide bandgap and large d-p band center energy difference (Δε d-p ) of δ-MnO 2 significantly impede electron transport and ion diffusion, limiting its catalytic efficiency in lithium-sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we report an interlayer coupling strategy that intercalates cetyltrimethylammonium (CTA + ) cations into birnessite (δ-MnO 2 ) to simultaneously modulate the Mn 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization and expand the Li + diffusion channels. Synchrotron X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the strong electrostatic interaction between CTA + and the MnO 2 host layers narrows the d-p band center energy difference (Δε d-p ) from 1.458 to 1.145 eV, substantially enhancing Mn 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization. This optimized d-p matching renders the Mn d-band more compatible with the S 2p orbitals of polysulfides, synergistically optimize adsorption energies and conversion barriers. Meanwhile, the CTA + expanded interlayer afford ordered Li + diffusion channels with a high Li + transference number and uniform Li deposition. Consequently, the Li─S batteries deliver a remarkable capacity of 819.07 mAh g − 1 at 3.0 C and sustain 850 cycles at 1.0 C with an capacity decay of only 0.05% per cycle. Significantly, the Li─S pouch cell equipped with a Bir(CTAB)-separator delivers a high energy density of 305.25 Wh kg −1 .

10.1002/adfm.79211.title: Pollen-Derived Paper for Sustainable Droplet Energy Harvesting
10.1002/adfm.79211.abstract: ABSTRACT Harvesting electricity from raindrops offers a promising route toward distributed self-powered electronics, but conventional devices rely predominantly on non-renewable synthetic polymers and metals. Here, we report a pollen-derived droplet energy harvester (PDEH) fabricated from abundant sunflower pollen. Defatting and mild de-esterification convert rigid pollen grains into processable microgels that form free-standing paper. Functionalization produces dielectric and conductive layers for an ultrathin multilayer device containing only 24 wt.% non-renewable solid materials. The incorporated constituents of a 3 × 3 cm 2 device cost approximately US$0.003, excluding processing consumables. Optimizing dielectric-layer thickness and surface fluorination yields 16.8 V from a single 37 µL tap-water droplet, with an energy-conversion efficiency of 1.26% and a maximum instantaneous power density of 63 mW m −2 . The approximately 70 µm-thick, 0.191 g device conforms to flat, curved, and irregular surfaces and maintains stable electrical output over 14 days of operation. A ten-unit PDEH array harvests simulated rainfall to charge a 10 µF capacitor to 2 V, subsequently powering a commercial electronic clock. These findings establish pollen-derived functional paper as a low-cost platform for droplet energy harvesting and demonstrate its potential for renewable-material-based, distributed self-powered electronic systems that combine renewable feedstocks, mechanical conformability, and energy storage for practical applications.

10.1002/adfm.79111.title: Entropy-Driven Design of an Adaptive Gel for All-Stage Inflammatory Regulation in Diabetic Peri-Implantitis
10.1002/adfm.79111.abstract: ABSTRACT Diabetic peri-implantitis (DPI) is characterized by persistent and dysregulated inflammation in a hostile microenvironment, where conventional therapies fail to achieve long-term control. Increasing evidence indicates that the key pathological feature lies not only in excessive inflammatory activation, but in the failure of inflammation resolution. Here, we propose an all-stage inflammatory regulation strategy targeting the full progression of DPI, including initiation, propagation, and resolution. An adaptive composite gel (CGCI) was developed by integrating predominantly amorphous copper-doped bioactive glass with a boron-modified poly(vinyl alcohol) hydrogel. The system forms a shear-thinning and self-healing network, enabling injectability and effective biological sealing. The amorphous bioactive glass mediates rapid Cu ion release for early antibacterial intervention, while the hydrogel provides sustained interleukin-10 delivery to promote macrophage-mediated efferocytosis and vascular/lymphatic remodeling. To enable programmable delivery, structural entropy was operationalized within a model to quantitatively describe degradable hydrogel network evolution and establish a predictive framework linking structure to release kinetics. Guided by this model, CGCI achieves stage-specific therapeutic delivery aligned with inflammation dynamics. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals coordinated macrophage-endothelial interactions, and in DPI beagle model, CGCI enables effective all-stage inflammatory regulation and tissue regeneration.

10.1002/adfm.79164.title: Interfacial Evolution, Failure Mechanisms, and Multiscale Stabilization Strategies for Silicon Anodes in Sulfide-Based All-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79164.abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes offer exceptionally high theoretical capacity and low lithiation potential, making them attractive for high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries using sulfide solid-state electrolytes. However, Si undergoes substantial structural reconstruction and volume variation during cycling, while deeply lithiated Li x Si strongly reduces sulfide solid-state electrolytes. The resulting interphase growth, loss of active lithium, particle fracture, interfacial delamination, contact loss, and heterogeneous ionic/electronic transport produce tightly coupled electrochemical-chemical-mechanical degradation. This Review summarizes the alloying-type Li-storage mechanism and room-temperature phase evolution of Si, emphasizing low-potential interfacial instability, volume-strain-induced fracture, solid-solid contact loss, and pressure-dependent failure. Stabilization strategies based on structural regulation, carbon hybridization, conductive-network construction, prelithiation, Li-Si alloying, elemental doping, surface modification, protective interlayers, functional binders, electrode processing, and pressure management are critically assessed. Advanced characterization and modeling methods are discussed for resolving interfacial reactions and failure pathways. Future progress requires chemically stable and mechanically compliant interfaces, low-pressure architectures, controllable prelithiation, scalable manufacturing, artificial-intelligence-assisted design, standardized full-cell evaluation, and coordinated optimization of transport, stress accommodation, Li inventory, and manufacturability.

10.1002/adfm.79150.title: Fiber-Inspired Quantum-Dot Micropillar Pixel Architecture for Micro-LED Displays
10.1002/adfm.79150.abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum-dot (QD) color conversion pixels with partitioned black matrix (BM) enable low-crosstalk color generation for Micro-LED displays, yet conventional structures face an inherent trade-off, the crosstalk-suppressing BM induces parasitic absorption and reduces conversion efficiency. Inspired by the light-confining core-shell structure of optical fibers, we propose a novel reflective QD micropillar pixel architecture for high-efficiency, crosstalk-suppressed full-color Micro-LED displays. Vertically aligned QD micropillar pixel array is fabricated via in situ photolithography, followed by sidewall deposition of a highly reflective aluminum (Al) cladding layer via evaporation. Unlike conventional planar color conversion layers, where the optical path is inherently constrained by film thickness, the vertically aligned three-dimensional (3D) micropillar fundamentally extends the interaction length between excitation light and QDs. By further enabling metal-mirror multiple reflections of excitation light within the micropillar, this design substantially prolongs the optical path and fosters secondary excitation, leading to a marked improvement in color conversion efficiency (CCE). Furthermore, the Al cladding forms a lateral photon-recycling microcavity, mitigating BM absorption and optical crosstalk. Breaking the efficiency and crosstalk trade-off, our device achieves green CCE of 27.15%, red CCE of 28.6%, and an ultra-wide color gamut of 131.54% NTSC, promising for near-eye full-color Micro-LED light engines.

10.1002/adfm.79166.title: Morphology-Dictated Interfacial Stacking of TiO 2 Nanosheets Delivers Robust Tribofilms under Extreme Pressure
10.1002/adfm.79166.abstract: ABSTRACT Under extreme pressure (EP), lubricating base oils with low viscosity frequently suffer from film rupture, leading to severe adhesive wear and lubrication failure. Although nano-additives can reinforce the sliding interface, how their morphology dictates stacking behavior and tribofilm formation remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate anatase TiO 2 nanosheets (ANS) and nanoparticles (ANP) to reveal how additive morphology governs tribological performance. We found that ANS reduced the friction coefficient (COF) by 56% and wear by 88% compared to base oil, while boosting EP load capacity by 6.8 times. Under applied normal load, the ANS physically reorient and stack into a dense, continuous tribofilm that effectively shields surface asperities. Conversely, ANP form an island-like, loosely packed tribofilm with poor load capacity. Beyond physical shielding, ANS exert a mechanical polishing effect that drives iron wear debris to react with oil hydrocarbons. This tribochemical process builds a Fe-rich reinforced structure, drastically improving the hardness and stability of the tribofilm. Ultimately, this work provides a morphology-driven engineering pathway for designing robust lubricants operating under extreme conditions.

10.1002/adfm.79136.title: Synergistic Weakening of Magnetoelastic Coupling and Enhancement of Exchange Interactions Enable High-Temperature Zero Thermal Expansion in a Lightweight and Hard Monoboride Ferromagnet
10.1002/adfm.79136.abstract: ABSTRACT Severe thermal expansion at high temperatures can induce internal stress accumulation and interfacial failure, leading to dimensional instability in structural and functional components. Yet, high-temperature zero thermal expansion (ZTE) alloys, which are of technological importance, remain rare. In this work, we developed a lightweight ferromagnetic MnB-based alloy by isostructural alloying, which exhibits a stable high-temperature ZTE ( α l = 1.95 × 10 −6 K −1 , 595-705 K; α l = −1.99 × 10 −6 K −1 , 705-815 K) and high hardness of 16.5 GPa. The incorporation of Fe simultaneously weakens the magnetoelastic coupling strength and increases the Curie temperature ( T C ), leading to this rare Invar effect. First-principles calculations further elucidate the underlying physical mechanism. The introduction of Fe modifies the electronic density of states and reduces the bonding strength associated with negative thermal expansion (NTE), thereby softening the strong NTE and enabling ZTE behavior. Meanwhile, ferromagnetic Fe brings about strong Mn-Fe exchange interactions, resulting in an overall increase in exchange interaction strength and an elevated T C . Additionally, the strong covalent bonding between B atoms provides the fundamental origin of the outstanding mechanical hardness. Our work thus not only proposes a high-temperature ZTE alloy system but also deepens the understanding of thermal expansion behavior in magnetic NTE/ZTE materials.

10.1002/adfm.79180.title: A miRNA Nanoprodrug Hydrogel for Multistage Regulation of Burn Wound Repair
10.1002/adfm.79180.abstract: ABSTRACT Burn wound repair requires not only rapid wound closure but also coordinated regulation of the evolving pathological processes across distinct healing stages to minimize scar formation. However, many existing wound dressings address only isolated aspects of healing and are often limited by burst release, short local retention, and insufficient intracellular delivery. Here, we report ATMP@Gel, a GelMA hydrogel incorporating an activatable tetrahedral miR-146a-5p nanoprodrug (ATMP), for multistage regulation of burn wound repair. The tetrahedral nanoframework improves miRNA stability and cellular uptake, while the hydrogel matrix prolongs local delivery; RNase H-responsive activation further contributes to increasing the functionally available intracellular pool of miR-146a-5p. ATMP@Gel attenuates excessive inflammation and oxidative stress during early repair, shifts the macrophage marker profile toward a reparative state, and suppresses fibroblast overactivation and profibrotic remodeling at later stages of healing. In a murine full-thickness burn model, ATMP@Gel accelerates wound closure and promotes angiogenesis, re-epithelialization, restoration of skin appendage structures, and more normal-like collagen architecture, while reducing residual scar area and scar-associated fibrosis. Together, these findings demonstrate a miRNA nanoprodrug hydrogel strategy that integrates sustained local delivery with responsive intracellular regulation to coordinate multiple pathological processes throughout burn wound healing.

10.1002/adfm.79151.title: Low-Flicker-Noise MoS 2 Transistors Enabled by High- κ Rare-Earth Oxychlorides for Mixed-Signal Electronics
10.1002/adfm.79151.abstract: ABSTRACT The trade-off between gate dielectric constant and interface quality limits two-dimensional (2D) analog and mixed-signal electronics because trap-mediated 1/ f noise from amorphous oxides degrades signal fidelity. Here, single-crystalline rare-earth oxychlorides (REOCl; LaOCl and GdOCl) are employed as Cl-terminated crystalline high- κ dielectrics that form atomically abrupt van der Waals interfaces with MoS 2 . MoS 2 /REOCl transistors exhibit near-thermal-limit switching, with minimum one-decade-averaged subthreshold swings of 65.7 and 63.2 mV dec −1 for LaOCl and GdOCl, with ultralow hysteresis and suppressed low-frequency noise. Carrier-number-fluctuation analysis of two independently measured devices per dielectric yields effective noise-derived interface trap densities of 1.15-1.94 × 10 10 cm −2 eV −1 , approaching the hexagonal boron nitride regime while retaining high- κ electrostatic coupling. Channel-area-scaled normalized 1/ f noise remains up to two orders of magnitude below amorphous SiO 2 /Al 2 O 3 /HfO 2 controls, with on-state S I / I D 2 reaching ∼10 −10 Hz −1 . A Samsung 28 nm high- κ /metal-gate reference process design kit sensitivity analysis, with only the flicker-noise coefficient varied, indicates reduced voltage-controlled oscillator phase noise and phase-locked-loop jitter and an effective-number-of-bits improvement of up to 1.45 bits in passive noise-shaping successive-approximation-register analog-to-digital converters. These results establish REOCl as a trap-poor high- κ dielectric platform for low-noise 2D electronics and illustrate the mixed-signal relevance of reduced transistor flicker noise.

10.1002/adfm.79131.title: Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Framework-Directed Facet Orientation Reconstruction in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79131.abstract: ABSTRACT Crystallographic orientation engineering is critical for suppressing defect formation, relieving lattice strain, and promoting charge transport in metal halide perovskites, yet the selective regulation of facet competition during solution crystallization remains challenging. Here, we introduce a vinylene-linked covalent organic framework, TBD-COF, as a structurally robust crystallization regulator for high-performance PSCs. The ordered porous skeleton of TBD-COF, together with its embedded pyridinic nitrogen atoms, provides spatially distributed interaction sites for coordinating with perovskite precursors and modulating the nucleation and crystal growth processes. Notably, TBD-COF incorporation redirects the crystallization pathway from conventional (001)-dominated growth toward an enhanced fraction of (012)-oriented crystalline domains. This orientation regulation alleviates disordered grain packing and lattice-strain accumulation, thereby suppressing defect-assisted nonradiative recombination and facilitating carrier transport. Consequently, the optimized devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.01% with a remarkable fill factor of 88.72%, representing one of the highest values reported for COF-incorporated PSCs. Moreover, the TBD-COF-modified devices retain 89% of their initial PCE after 1000 h under the ISOS-L-2 protocol.

10.1002/adfm.79144.title: Programming Neuromorphic Plasticity Through Ionic and Electronic Coupling in Organic Electrochemical Transistors
10.1002/adfm.79144.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) encode the history of ionic motion as persistent changes in channel conductance, providing a material basis for neuromorphic plasticity. Yet memory lifetime is determined not simply by electrochemical doping, but by how the programmed ionic and electronic state relaxes or stabilizes after stimulation. This Review establishes a mechanistic framework that classifies OECT responses as rapidly relaxing, metastably confined, or persistently stabilized states. We show how semiconductor chemistry and morphology, electrolyte composition and ion identity, interfacial interactions, and device architecture collectively govern ion injection, transport, confinement, and release. These processes are connected to temporal processing, selective consolidation, and persistent synaptic weight storage. We further assess the coupled tradeoffs among programming speed, retention, reversibility, update linearity, and endurance. Rather than maximizing retention alone, we identify function matched and reversible stabilization, together with its decoupling from programming kinetics and weight update characteristics, as a central design principle for neuromorphic OECTs.

10.1002/adfm.79059.title: Layered Organic-MXene Heterostructures for High-Capacity and Long-Life Aqueous Sodium-Ion Storage in Seawater-Based Hybrid Electrolytes
10.1002/adfm.79059.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous sodium-ion batteries (ASIBs) are attractive for large-scale storage due to intrinsic safety and low cost. However, their practical applications are often limited by sluggish kinetics and the dependence on purified electrolytes. Here, we report a layered organic-MXene heterostructured anode by direct thermal polymerization of a conjugated naphthalene-based polyimide (NPI) in the presence of multilayer Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene, forming a tightly coupled 2D architecture (NPI@MXene). NPI provides reversible imide-carbonyl redox sites, while MXene facilitates electron transport and interfacial ion-transfer kinetics, thereby reducing polarization and accelerating Na + storage. Benefiting from the reversible carbonyl conversion, enhanced pseudocapacitive behavior, and improved Na + diffusion kinetics, the optimized NPI@MXene anode delivers a specific capacity of 124.5 mAh g − 1 at 1.00 A g − 1 and shows excellent durability with 100.0% retention over 65 000 cycles at 15.0 A g − 1 . For practical operation, seawater is used to prepare a 1.00 M sodium acetate electrolyte with the most favorable interfacial kinetics among the tested seawater-based electrolytes. The assembled NPI@MXene//Cu-PBA full cell operated stably over the 0-1.60 V range and maintained its performance for 15 000 cycles.

10.1002/adfm.79185.title: Erosion Sequential Deposition with Halogen-Free Solvent Enables Organic Solar Cells With 21.05% Efficiency and 83.19% Fill Factor
10.1002/adfm.79185.abstract: ABSTRACT Halogen-free solvent processed organic solar cells (OSCs) usually show much lower power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) if compared with halogenated solvents, especially for sequential deposition (SD) process. Herein, erosion-SD processing with halogen-free solvents was demonstrated, in which an eroded material was pre-inserted into a donor (D18) bottom layer. Subsequent deposition of acceptor (L8-BO) solution swells the bottom layer more easily, enabling deeper acceptor penetration and optimizing vertical phase separation. Judicious selections of eroded materials and halogen-free solvents open chances to re-organize SD morphology. With toluene:CS2/toluene as halogen-free solvents and partially removable polymer acceptor PYDT as eroded material, OSCs based on D18:PYDT/L8-BO achieved a remarkable PCE of 21.05% (certified 20.71%), greatly higher than 20.53% achieved with chloroform/chloroform solvent system. Moreover, the erosion-SD processed 300 and 500 nm thick active layers exhibited superior PCEs of 19.64% and 18.75%, respectively, showing promising ability to re-organize morphology toward halogen-free solution printing.

10.1002/adfm.79179.title: Manipulating Covalency to Activate Dual-Interface Kinetics for Efficient Solar Water Splitting
10.1002/adfm.79179.abstract: ABSTRACT Interface engineering plays a crucial role in improving the performance of semiconductor-based solar energy devices. Nevertheless, conventional interface modulation strategies still suffer from limited charge separation efficiency and sluggish surface reaction kinetics, restricting further performance improvement. Distinct from traditional interface regulation, we herein propose a novel covalency manipulation strategy to construct a dual-interface kinetics-activated BiVO 4 /CoPi-F/FeOOH photoanode for efficient photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. The optimized photoanode reaches a high photocurrent density of 6.72 mA/cm 2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and exhibits remarkable stability during 24 h of continuous operation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations combined with in situ experimental analysis reveal that the introduced CoPi-F modulates the hole transfer pathways and promotes the separation of photogenerated charge carriers by forming electron-rich species. At the CoPi-F/FeOOH interface, the strengthened adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates facilitates surface reaction kinetics. Moreover, this universal covalency modulation strategy can be adapted to other configurations such as BiVO 4 /CoPi-F/NiOOH for prominent PEC performance enhancement. This work demonstrates the distinct superiority of the proposed covalency manipulation strategy over existing methods, providing a useful guideline for the rational design of covalency-tuned photoanodes and advancing the development of efficient solar-driven water splitting technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79148.title: Bioinspired Hierarchical Woven Fabrics With Capture Ridges and Patterned Drainage for Efficient Fog Harvesting
10.1002/adfm.79148.abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater scarcity has emerged as a critical bottleneck restricting sustainable development, while fog harvesting represents a promising strategy to alleviate this global water crisis. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art fog-harvesting materials remain constrained by the lack of effective coupling between rapid droplet capture and directional liquid transport, resulting in unsatisfactory collection efficiency over long-term operation. Here, through precise modulation of fabric surface chemistry, macroscopic woven architecture, and asymmetric wettability, a bioinspired hierarchical Janus woven fabric is designed that synergistically integrates two biofunctional structures: beetle-mimicking topographic ridges on the capture side for ultrafast fog droplet nucleation and interception, and leaf-vein-like hierarchical drainage channels on the opposite side for low-resistance directional liquid delivery. Leveraging this multiscale synergistic enhancement, the as-prepared fabric achieves an exceptional fog harvesting rate of 3663.9 mg cm −2 h −1 , surpassing that of most fabrics. Furthermore, the resulting fabric exhibits excellent long-term operational stability in fog collection, as well as robust environmental durability against prolonged ultraviolet irradiation, acidic, alkaline, and high-salinity aqueous conditions. This study establishes a universal design paradigm based on woven fabrics that achieves seamless synergy between efficient fog interception and directional liquid transport. It provides a viable technical route for large-scale freshwater production in water-deficient fog-prone regions.

10.1002/adfm.79168.title: Modulating the Spin Structure of LiFeO 2 by Cr Substitution for Oxygen Electrocatalysis
10.1002/adfm.79168.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are crucial for renewable energy technologies like fuel cells and metal-air batteries, yet their performance is limited by sluggish kinetics. Addressing the need for efficient catalysts, a series of Cr-doped LiFeO 2 (LiFe 1-x Cr x O 2 , x = 0.00 to 1.00) have been synthesized via a sol-gel method for ORR and OER catalysis. Among these, LiFe 0.25 Cr 0.75 O 2 exhibits superior bifunctional oxygen electrocatalytic activity (0.74 V and 1.58 V vs. RHE to reach 25 µA cm oxide −2 for ORR and OER). In LiFe 1-x Cr x O 2 , a structural transformation from a fcc to a layered hexagonal phase has been observed with Cr increasing, enhancing cation ordering and ion transport capability. Cr doping also modulates the spin state of Fe active sites, reducing the effective magnetic moment and e g orbital occupancy, thereby strengthening Fe-O bonding. Following a “dual-metal competitive bonding” mechanism, the strengthened Fe─O bond weakens the coordination with adjacent metal sites, shifting the adsorption configuration from bridging to atop M 1 O 1 , thereby promoting OOH desorption. Furthermore, this study innovatively introduces the total bonding energy of dual-metal dioxygen atoms (B ICOHP ) as a novel OER activity factor, providing new theoretical insights and experimental guidance for designing spin-regulated transition metal oxide catalysts.

10.1002/adfm.79121.title: Modulation of Hydroxy Functionalities in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Oxygen Reduction Reaction
10.1002/adfm.79121.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal-free catalysts are gaining increasing interest for the electrochemical oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their lower cost and functionality-dependent catalytic performance. However, controlled functionalization and establishing a clear functional-to-property relationship in Metal-free heteroatom-doped carbon-based electrocatalysts (CMFEs) is a daunting challenge. It's also vague how much functional group (heteroatom) incorporation in CMFEs is required to achieve optimal ORR activity. Here, we utilize a hydroxy-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) as a predesignable, highly functionalizable platform for establishing a clear functional-property correlation for the electrochemical ORR reaction. We observe that the incorporation of hydroxy functionalities into imine COF is highly beneficial in enhancing the ORR activity with an increase in onset potential (E onset )and half-wave potential (E 1/2 ). Control over the number of hydroxy (-OH) functionalities is highly essential for achieving optimal ORR activity. Among the various synthesized COFs, dihydroxy-functionalized DATB-COF displays the highest onset potential (0.96 V vs. RHE) and a half-wave potential (E 1/2 ) value (0.71 V vs. RHE). Hydroxy functional group incorporation generates multiple catalytically active centers (C O and C N ) in COFs and makes ORR reaction kinetics more favorable by facilitating the formation of *OOH reaction intermediates.

10.1002/adfm.77764.title: Tough Hydrophobic Ionogel Fibers via Molecularly Engineered Phase Separation for Multi-Scenario Sensing
10.1002/adfm.77764.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly stretchable gel fibers are increasingly critical given the growing miniaturization and adaptivity demands within flexible wearable devices. Current fiber-based iontronics, however, exclusively rely on hydrogels with limited environmental tolerance. Moreover, most existing gel systems exhibit insufficient strength and toughness to meet fiber processing requirements. Inspired by the composite architecture of natural biomaterials (e.g., spider silk and human skin), we develop tough hydrophobic ionogel fibers (IGFs) through molecularly engineered polymerization-induced phase separation. This strategy embeds rigid hydrogen-bonded polyacrylamide-rich nanophases within an elastic matrix, endowing IGFs with an exceptional toughness of 24.6 MJ/m 3 and a fracture strength of 4.5 MPa whilst retaining high stretchability of ∼900%. Crucially, the continuous soft phase establishes efficient ion channels, enhancing conductivity while overcoming the mechanics-conductivity trade-off in traditional gel systems. The incorporated fluoropolymer segments further confer outstanding underwater adhesion and self-healing capabilities. As strain sensors, IGFs exhibit high sensitivity (GF = 11.5) and perform well under extreme conditions including high (100°C) or low (−40°C) temperatures, vacuum (1.325 kPa), high humidity (98%RH), and even underwater environments. This work addresses the scarcity of robust flexible sensors for harsh-environment applications, thereby substantially broadening their operational scenarios.

10.1002/adfm.77813.title: Human-Skin-Inspired Structural Decoupling for Constructing Ultra-Stable and Infrared Stealth MXene/PFOTS Coatings
10.1002/adfm.77813.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing multifunctional materials that integrate exceptional infrared (IR) stealth with long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Inspired by the synergistic function of human skin hair and sweat glands, we report a hydrophobic, highly conductive, and anti-oxidant IR stealth material (P-MXene). Perfluorooctyl long chains are covalently grafted onto MXene surfaces to form “molecular hairs”, creating a robust hydrophobic boundary layer via steric hindrance that passivates reactive -OH groups without disrupting high-density conductive pathways. Consequently, P-MXene maintains a high electrical conductivity of 2074.58 S cm − 1 even after 40 days of accelerated oxidation, while its water contact angle increases to 135.6 ° alongside an ultra-low IR emissivity of 0.125. Leveraging a continuous coating process, large-scale fabrication of flexible P-MXene fabrics (3 m × 0.5 m) was successfully achieved. The resulting fabrics exhibit excellent spatial uniformity (2.2-2.8 µm thickness, 22-27 Ω surface resistance) and remarkable mechanical durability, showing less than 5% resistance change after 5,000 bending cycles. Furthermore, the covalent grafting ensures robust wearability, retaining high hydrophobicity and IR stealth performance after 40 washing cycles and 100 severe friction cycles, demonstrating great potential for large-area flexible wearables.

10.1002/adfm.76779.title: Optical Signature of Moiré Superlattices Formed by Twisted SrTiO3 Membranes
authors: T. A. M. Ragib Shahriar, Fumikazu Murakami, Xing He, Konnor Koons, Xinyan Li, Bumseop Kim, Shihan Qin, Varun Harbola, Jochen Mannhart, Yimo Han, Ruijuan Xu, Shengxi Huang, Andrew M. Rappe, Hanyu Zhu

10.1002/adfm.77221.title: Interface Induced Ferroelectricity in Designed CeO2, HfO2, ZrO2 and YSZ Based Superlattice Heterostructures
authors: Pralay Paul, Sajid Husain, Shashank Chaturvedi, Levi Brown, Pushpendra Gupta, Shashank Kumar Ojha, Casey Kerr, Sreehari Puthan Purayil, Sumit Goswami, Dhiman Biswas, Ben Summers, Yiwei Ju, Deeksha Gupta, Ashish Omar, Horst Hahn, Xiaoqing Pan, Umesh V. Waghmare, Alisa Javadi, Ramamoorthy Ramesh, Thirumalai Venkatesan

10.1002/adfm.79013.title: Flexible Neuromorphic Softness Sensory System
10.1002/adfm.79013.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate softness sensing remains a challenge for artificial tactile systems, as conventional force-based sensing misses key deformation cues. Biological perception instead uses active, displacement-controlled exploration. Here we report a biomimetic neuromorphic tactile system that integrates iontronic softness sensing, spike-based signal encoding and organic synaptic processing to enable softness sensory system. Displacement-controlled operation of a hemispherical pressure sensor produces more discriminative temporal deformation signals than simple pressure sensors. Machine learning reveals interpretable temporal features and confirms high classification accuracy. The signals are encoded into spikes and processed by an organic synaptic device, enabling in-sensor classification without digital post-processing. Synaptic outputs demonstrate that material softness can be inferred directly from the excitatory postsynaptic current without complex post-processing. This work establishes a sensor-to-synapse neuromorphic framework for softness perception.

10.1002/adfm.79145.title: Spatially Programmed Ferritin Nanocage Vaccine Enables DC-Biased Delivery and Enhanced Antigen Cross-Presentation
10.1002/adfm.79145.abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer vaccines can induce durable antitumor immunity, yet their therapeutic efficacy remains limited by inefficient lymphatic trafficking, insufficient dendritic cell (DC) engagement, and suboptimal antigen presentation. Here, we developed Fe@DCpep-Fn-OVA, a spatially engineered ferritin nanocage vaccine integrating multivalent antigen display, DC-biased delivery, and an intrananocage functional module within a single protein scaffold. The ferritin shell was genetically programmed to display the OVA 257-264 epitope (SIINFEKL) and a DC-engaging peptide (DCpep), whereas an iron-mineralized catalytic component was confined within the internal cavity. This orthogonal shell-cavity architecture enables coordinated extracellular immune cell recognition and intracellular immune regulation. Following subcutaneous administration, Fe@DCpep-Fn-OVA exhibited enhanced accumulation in draining lymph nodes (dLNs) and increased association with CD11c + DCs. The cavity-confined iron component retained acid-responsive peroxidase-like activity and provided localized intracellular regulatory cues, promoting DC maturation, H-2K b /SIINFEKL presentation, and antigen-specific CD8 + T cell activation. In therapeutic subcutaneous and intravenous B16-F10-OVA lung-colonization models, Fe@DCpep-Fn-OVA effectively inhibited tumor growth and lung colonization, outperforming OVA plus Poly(I:C). Moreover, prophylactic immunization induced durable CD8 + memory T cell responses and protected mice against lung colonization upon tumor challenge. These findings establish ferritin shell-cavity compartmentalization as a programmable strategy for next-generation cancer vaccination.

10.1002/adfm.79146.title: Electron Reservoir Enabled Oxygen Vacancies Engineering for Charge Transport and Defect-Mediated Relaxation
10.1002/adfm.79146.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen vacancy (V o ) engineering is crucial for regulating electronic structures and charge responses in functional materials, yet V o induced localized states can enhance charge localization and limit the participation of charge carriers in charge-response processes, resulting in insufficient charge supply for defect-mediated electronic responses. Developing a strategy that alleviates charge-supply limitation while preserving the electronic modulation enabled by localized defect states remains challenging.
