To address this challenge, we investigate electronic compensation of V o related states using Mo 2 C MXene/MoO 3-x heterostructures constructed through an in situ redox method, in which Mo 2 C MXene serves as the electron donating component and tunable V o in MoO 3-x acts as defect-state regulation centers. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experimental results reveal that electron compensation from Mo 2 C MXene promotes defect-mediated charge response and dielectric relaxation, thereby alleviating charge supply limitations associated with localized vacancy states and enabling systematic modulation of defect electronic structures. This defect-state regulation is further demonstrated in electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption, achieving an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 7.28 GHz and a minimum reflection loss (RL min ) of −51.49 dB. This work provides insight into defect state-mediated charge regulation and provides a perspective for defect engineering toward tailoring of electronic and charge response behavior.

10.1002/adfm.79094.title: Carbene-Mediated Cross-linking of Aromatic Dielectric Polymers for Capacitive Energy Storage at 250°C
10.1002/adfm.79094.abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable energy storage in electrostatic capacitors requires dielectric materials that can withstand extreme thermal and electrical stresses, a demand that exceeds the capabilities of many commercial polymers. Cross-linking offers a promising route to improved thermal and electrical robustness, but existing strategies often depend on polymer-specific reactive groups, harsh activation conditions, or byproducts that limit broader adoption. Herein, we report a post-polymerization cross-linking strategy based on carbene-mediated C-H insertion, enabled by a stepwise thermal activation protocol. Using commercial fluorinated polyimide (FPI) and the commercial bis-diazirine cross-linker BondLynx Gen-1 (CX-1) as a model system, this approach yields free-standing cross-linked films with a high cross-linking efficiency of 95.8% at only 2 wt.% CX-1, despite the exclusive presence of aromatic/ sp 2 C-H bonds in the polymer backbone. The resulting cross-linked FPI films exhibit outstanding capacitive energy storage performance, along with excellent spatial uniformity and long-term durability. A maximum discharged energy density of 4.4 J cm −3 is achieved at 250°C, which is among the highest values reported for state-of-the-art polymer films under comparable conditions. This work establishes thermally activated carbene cross-linking as a versatile route for transforming commercial aromatic polymers into thermally resilient electrostatic energy storage materials.

10.1002/adfm.79070.title: Exceptional Electro-Optic Coefficient Unlocked via Polarization Swaying in KNbO 3 Thin Films
10.1002/adfm.79070.abstract: ABSTRACT The electro-optic effect powers microwave-to-optical quantum transducers, photonic quantum computing switches, and high-speed optical interconnects. A larger electro-optic coefficient directly reduces the drive voltage and device footprint of electro-optic modulators, making the search for materials with large coefficients a central challenge in photonics. Here, guided by phase-field modeling, we engineer an electro-optic coefficient of 43 000 pm V −1 in monoclinic KNbO 3 thin films, the largest ever measured in any material, exceeding industry-standard LiNbO 3 by 1000×. This exceptional response arises from electric field-driven “lateral swaying” of the ferroelectric polarization vector between symmetry-equivalent monoclinic variants, which reorients the optical index ellipsoid far beyond the conventional Pockels response that relies on a linear coupling between field and polarization. The ultralow coercive fields of the monoclinic phase (∼1 kV cm −1 ) place this giant response within reach of standard drive electronics, enabling drive voltages orders of magnitude below the current state-of-the-art. The response is stable to within 1% − 2% over hours, robust under thermal and electrical cycling, and demonstrated up to 1 MHz, establishing low-symmetry ferroelectric phases as an unexploited design space for next-generation energy-efficient electro-optic modulators for classical and quantum photonic integrated circuits.

10.1002/adfm.79192.title: Highly Crystalline Co Nanoparticles With Uniform Surface CoO x Nanoislands Derived From a Co-N 2 O 2 Precursor for Selective CO 2 Conversion
10.1002/adfm.79192.abstract: ABSTRACT Converting CO 2 into useful chemicals is a cornerstone of sustainable chemistry; among viable routes, the reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction supplies CO for subsequent fuel and olefin synthesis, yet achieving simultaneously high CO selectivity, fast CO 2 activation, and stability with non-noble metals remains elusive. Here, we employ a pure H 2 torrent to rapidly reduce a Co-salophen framework, forging a core-shell Co@CoO x -C catalyst consisting of a highly crystalline metallic Co core and a defect-rich CoO x shell capable of dynamic reconstruction under redox conditions. The metallic Co core dissociates H 2 , driving hydrogen spillover to the metal-oxide interface, where CO 2 is efficiently activated, resulting in selective CO formation at the highly active Co/CoO x boundary. Rapid CO desorption from coordinatively saturated CoO x sites suppresses further hydrogenation, affording >99% CO selectivity and a CO formation rate of 254.0 mmol g cat −1 h −1 at 500°C maintained for >100 h. These findings demonstrate that engineering dynamic Co/CoO x interfaces via H 2 torrent reduction overcomes the intrinsic selectivity limitations of cobalt-based RWGS catalysts and highlight defect-rich core-shell structures derived from H 2 -reduced metal-salophen precursors as a versatile platform for next-generation CO 2 conversion technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79193.title: Chiral Peptide Glass-Templated MAPbBr 3 Nanocrystals: Enhanced Circularly Polarized Luminescence Performance and Stability for Chiral Optoelectronic Applications
10.1002/adfm.79193.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) with strong circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) hold enormous potential for applicating in chiral optoelectronic fields, including 3D displays, chiral sensing, anti-counterfeiting, and information storage. Nevertheless, the weak luminescence asymmetry and insufficient stability of CPL-active perovskite NCs have severely hampered their practical applications. Herein, through a solvent-induced in situ crystallization method, the MAPbBr 3 NCs were successfully embedded into the network of blue-emitting chiral peptide glass (L/D-Zn-Car). The L-Zn-Car chiral peptide glass acts as both a chiral template and a protective matrix, offering a confined chiral microenvironment for the nucleation and growth of MAPbBr 3 NCs. Theoretical calculations combined with experimental evidences collectively confirm the strong coordination interactions between MAPbBr 3 NCs and L-Zn-Car matrix, which not only facilitate efficient chirality transfer but also effectively suppress surface trap states. The optimized MAPbBr 3 @L-Zn-Car chiral glass exhibits excellent CPL performance, featuring high luminescence asymmetry (g lum : 2.14 × 10 −2 ), remarkable photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY: 76%), and superior stability. Furthermore, the chiral light-emitting diode (LED) fabricated based on MAPbBr 3 @L/D-Zn-Car achieves high luminous efficiency (68.5 lm/W) and prominent CPL characteristics. This work establishes a feasible strategy for the rational design of high-performance CPL-active perovskite materials and broadens their application prospects in chiral optoelectronic fields.

10.1002/adfm.79153.title: Large-Scale Sulfur Quantum Dots Production Coupled With Hydrogen Evolution Via Electrochemical-Chemical Tandem Synthesis
10.1002/adfm.79153.abstract: ABSTRACT Production of value-added chemicals and materials through electrochemical processes represents a game-changing synthetic route, yet its scalability has not been demonstrated. Here, we report a tandem electrochemical-chemical process that converts aqueous sulfide feedstocks into sulfur quantum dots (SQDs) while co-producing hydrogen. Based on cost-effective, commercially available Ni 3 FeMo 0.1 powders, a heterostructured Ni 3 FeMo 0.1 @NiTe 2 catalyst is developed, which drives the electrochemical sulfide-to-polysulfide oxidation reaction at current densities up to 1.0 A cm −2 with a voltage of only 1.07 V in natural seawater electrolyte at 80°C, and achieves stable operation for over 290 h in the membrane electrode assembly while maintaining excellent performance in four-cell electrolyzer stacks with a SQD yield rate of 142 mg cm −2 day −1 . Operando spectroscopy investigations and density functional theory calculations reveal that multi-metal electronic delocalization around Ni, Fe and Mo active centers confines sulfidation to the catalyst surface and stabilizes a higher surface sulfur coverage, thereby lowering the energy barrier to the rate-determining step while suppressing bulk NiS formation. The resulting SQDs exhibit excitation-dependent photoluminescence tunable across the violet-to-blue region. This work demonstrates surface-reconstruction engineering as a rational catalyst-design principle for coupled electrosynthesis of nanomaterials and green hydrogen, and moreover, it showcases scale-up synthesis of SQDs with tunable photoluminescence.

10.1002/adfm.79175.title: Sterically Engineered Molecular Alloying for Kinetic Regulation of Acceptor Crystallization Achieves 20.73% Efficiency in Ternary Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79175.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over crystallization kinetics and multi-scale morphological evolution is crucial for achieving high-performance organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a molecular alloying strategy by introducing a sterically hindered acceptor, L8-Ph, into the L8-BO matrix to construct a homogeneous alloy phase and regulate acceptor crystallization behavior. In situ kinetic analysis reveals that L8-Ph increases the nucleation barrier and effectively modulates the crystallization process, prolonging the Stage II crystallization duration from 0.17 s in the binary system to 0.23 s in the ternary blend. The moderated crystallization suppresses uncontrolled aggregation while preserving sufficient molecular order, leading to a refined fibrillar network with enhanced crystalline coherence and a more balanced vertical phase separation. These morphological improvements promote charge transport and reduce bimolecular recombination and trap-assisted losses. Consequently, the D18:L8-BO:L8-Ph ternary device delivers a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.73%, outperforming the D18:L8-BO binary control device with PCE of 19.77%, with a high fill factor of 82.95%. This work establishes sterically hindered acceptor alloying as an effective route to regulate non-equilibrium crystallization and guide morphology evolution toward high-efficiency organic photovoltaic devices.

10.1002/adfm.79154.title: Counter-Anion-Engineered Solid-State Polymer Electrolytes for Vertically Stacked Artificial Synapses With Configurable Plasticity
10.1002/adfm.79154.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic hardware requires artificial synapses (ASs) with configurable plasticity to support diverse signal-processing functions while employing device architectures that minimize interconnect complexity among functional components. Electrolyte-gated synaptic transistors enable low-voltage conductance modulation, tunable synaptic plasticity, and mechanical flexibility through ion-mediated operation. However, the use of gel or liquid electrolytes often compromises mechanical robustness and processability. Here, we report ASs based on solid-state cationic polyurethane (cPU) gate dielectrics, in which Li + mobility is regulated by the counter-anion of the cPU. Compact Br − counter-anions suppress Li + transport and redistribution, thereby enabling long-term synaptic plasticity. In contrast, bulky BPh 4 − counter-anions weaken Li + coordination and facilitate Li + transport through anion exchange with Tf 2 N − , resulting in short-term synaptic plasticity. The counter-anion-dependent Li + transport mechanism is validated by first-principles calculations and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We further integrate these counter-anion-engineered devices into vertically stacked, array-level architectures that implement reconfigurable AND/OR logic and in-memory computing via multiply-accumulate operations. This strategy establishes a foundation for future neuromorphic hardware by engineering solid-state ion dynamics to achieve configurable plasticity, vertical integration, and multifunctional array-level operation.

10.1002/adfm.79215.title: Neuromorphic Devices Enhanced by Resonant Photonic Structures
10.1002/adfm.79215.abstract: ABSTRACT Optoelectronic neuromorphic visual sensors have garnered considerable interest owing to their ability to both detect light and perform synaptic computations within a single device. This in-sensor integration reduces the energy-intensive data transfer between separate sensing and processing hardware, presenting an energy-efficient pathway toward bio-inspired machine vision. However, limited optical absorption in ultrathin photoactive layers can hinder their practical deployment in artificial vision systems. This review examines how resonant photonic structures address this challenge by serving as an additional geometric design dimension that complements active-material engineering. Recent advancements are organized into three architecture families: plasmonic structures (nanoparticles and periodic patterns), multilayer interference architectures (Fabry-Pérot resonators, distributed Bragg reflectors, and Tamm-plasmon structures), and nanowire arrays. Depending on the device configuration, photonic geometry and material optical properties jointly control optical field enhancement within the active layer, wavelength selectivity, and polarization sensitivity, whereas multilevel storage relies on material- and interface-level switching mechanisms. This structural engineering supports filter-free, energy-efficient, and multispectral in-sensor computing for next-generation artificial vision applications.

10.1002/adfm.78818.title: Lone-Pair-Induced Lattice Distortion in Lead-Free Hybrid Perovskites for High-Performance Nanogenerators
10.1002/adfm.78818.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high piezoelectric performance in lead-free halide perovskites remains challenging because substituting lead typically compromises piezoelectricity through reduced lattice distortion and introduces stability concerns. Here, a lead-free two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper hybrid perovskite, (ATHP) 2 SnCl 4 (ATHP = 4-aminotetrahydropyran), is developed with strongly distorted [SnCl6] 4 − octahedra and enhanced lattice asymmetry relative to its lead-based analogue. First-principles calculations reveal pronounced Sn 5s-Cl 3p hybridization and an anisotropic Sn 2+ lone-pair lobe, producing stereochemical activity and structural polarization. Cooperative interactions between the lone pair and uniformly oriented [ATHP] + cations stabilize the layered structure, yielding an experimental spontaneous polarization of 8.3 µC.cm −2 , and a d 33 of 65.7 pC.N −1 in the optimized composite. The piezoelectric nanogenerator (PENG) delivers a milliwatt-level power density of 2.34 mW.cm −2 , among the highest reported for lead-free hybrid-perovskite PENGs and competitive with lead-based systems. The device maintains 65% of its voltage and 25% of its current density at −90°C, corresponding to ∼3.5- and ∼12-fold higher retention than pure poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)), while retaining 76.8% and 71.3%, respectively, at 90% relative humidity. Cryogenic operation is demonstrated by continuously powering an electronic watch for over 15 min at −50°C. These findings establish a lone-pair-engineering route to stable, flexible, high-efficiency lead-free perovskite PENGs for extreme environments.

10.1002/adfm.79172.title: An Integrated All-Solar-Powered Evaporator-Electrolyzer Coupled System Through Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Network Modulation for Freshwater and Green Hydrogen Co-Production
10.1002/adfm.79172.abstract: ABSTRACT Distributed solar-driven interfacial evaporation coupled with water electrolysis offers a sustainable route to simultaneously address water scarcity and energy crises. However, reliable integrated system design and disruption of high-energy barrier imposed by strong hydrogen bonds remain key challenges. To solve these problems, an integrated solar-driven coupling system was designed based on the unified TiN/TiO 2 (N-TiO 2 ) platform, while two separate modules were developed based on photothermal Ag 2 @N-TiO 2 evaporator and Ni 4 Co 1 @N-TiO 2 electrocatalyst, achieving synchronous production and adjustment of freshwater and green hydrogen according to the target application scenario. Using active N-TiO 2 sites for water molecule adsorption and activation, Ag 2 @N-TiO 2 and Ni 4 Co 1 @N-TiO 2 heterostructures can break hydrogen bonding networks and weaken H-O-H bonds through strong interfacial interactions. Notably, quasi-in situ Raman captures the release of low-barrier “weakly hydrogen-bonded water” from Ag 2 @N-TiO 2 interface, which reduces the vaporization latent heat for effective evaporation. Meanwhile, the Ni 4 Co 1 @N-TiO 2 interface promotes the release of active hydrogen (H * ) to accelerate the Volmer step, thereby optimizing the hydrogen production kinetics. The integrated device achieves a high evaporation rate of 2.425 kg m −2 h −1 under 1 kW m −2 and a low HER overpotential of 113 mV at 100 mA cm −2 , which offers a reliable strategy for sustainable seawater desalination and green hydrogen co-production.

10.1002/adfm.79127.title: Bioinspired Repurposing of Lisinopril: A Clinical ACE Inhibitor as a Trace Dual-Functional Additive for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79127.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) is critically hindered by rampant dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions, originating from unregulated Zn 2 + solvation chemistry and unstable electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Inspired by the zinc-targeting molecular recognition mechanism of angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, we repurpose clinical drug lisinopril (LIS) as a trace multifunctional electrolyte additive for high-performance AZIBs. The multidentate and amphiphilic structure of LIS orchestrates a synergistic dual-regulation mechanism: LIS spontaneously adsorbs and in situ assembles into a robust gradient organic-inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase that homogenizes Zn 2+ flux and establishes a water-depleted electric double layer by its hydrophobic moieties; meanwhile LIS alters the [Zn(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+ solvation shell, disrupts the native hydrogen-bond network, and buffers interfacial pH fluctuations at the anode interface. Consequently, trace LIS enables highly reversible Zn plating/stripping, with Zn||Cu cells delivering an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.78% over 1500 cycles and Zn||Zn cells operating for 2400 h at 4 mA cm −2 /4 mAh cm −2 . Remarkably, the LIS-containing full cells retain 77.25% of their capacity after 10 000 cycles, and pouch cells maintain 74.46% capacity after 600 cycles. This work illustrates that pharmaceutical molecules with inherent Zn-binding motifs can be converted into function-oriented electrolyte additives to achieve durable AZIBs.

10.1002/adfm.79162.title: Molecular Bridges for 2D Nanomaterials
10.1002/adfm.79162.abstract: ABSTRACT The exceptional electronic, optical, and chemical properties of nanomaterials are often compromised when individual building blocks are assembled into macroscopic devices, where poorly defined interfaces govern charge transport, mechanical integrity, and functional performance. Cross-linking has emerged as a powerful strategy for engineering these interfaces by introducing molecular bridges that couple neighboring nanostructures and control their structural and electronic interactions. Although this concept has been explored in nanoparticle assemblies, its translation to 2D materials remains in its early stages. In this perspective, we propose molecular cross-linking as a unifying framework for interfacial engineering across nanomaterial systems, highlighting how linker chemistry governs spacing between nanomaterials, charge transport, mechanical behavior, and chemical functionality. By comparing molecular bridging strategies in metal nanoparticles, quantum dots, transition-metal dichalcogenides, graphene oxide, and MXenes, we review how different binding motifs and types of linkers give rise to distinct structure-property relationships. Building on our recent demonstration of hydrogen-bonded diamine bridging in Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes, we propose molecular junction engineering as a general design principle for 2D materials. We envision that a programmable molecular interface will enable next-generation hybrid materials with tunable charge-transport characteristics, mechanics, and chemical functionality, extending far beyond MXenes to a broad class of molecularly engineered 2D systems.

10.1002/adfm.79170.title: Ionic Microenvironment Regulator Enables Enhanced Anion Trapping in Cationic Poly(Ionic Liquid) Solid Electrolyte for Low-Temperature Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79170.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the considerable promise of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) for enabling high-energy-density and intrinsically safe lithium metal batteries, their practical deployment in cold environments remains hindered by sluggish Li + transport at sub-zero temperatures. Herein, methyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (TMS) is introduced as an ionic microenvironment regulator into a cationic poly(ionic liquid) solid electrolyte, enabling enhanced Li + transport under extreme low-temperature conditions. Notably, TMS not only enhances lithium salt dissociation but also induces an anion-trapping effect by modulating the local charge distribution of the polycationic backbone, thereby facilitating uniform lithium deposition. As a result, the optimized cationic poly(ionic liquid) solid electrolyte (PIL-TMS 1 ) enables stable cryogenic operation of high-voltage Li||PIL-TMS 1 ||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 and Li||PIL-TMS 1 ||LiFePO 4 batteries, delivering capacity retentions of 89.8% after 500 cycles and 80.1% after 800 cycles at −15°C, respectively. This work presents an effective strategy for designing low-temperature solid-state lithium metal batteries through additive-regulated anion trapping and accelerated Li + transport.

10.1002/adfm.79118.title: Switching the Spin at the B-Site: How a Low-to-High Fe 3+ Spin-State Transition Selectively Drives CO 2 Reduction in Perovskite Oxides
10.1002/adfm.79118.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) co-electrolyze CO 2 and H 2 O to syngas with high thermodynamic efficiency, but the cathode must do more than catalyze two reductions: it must selectively activate CO 2 in the presence of competing H 2 O. Here we report that B-site doping of LaCaFeO 3 perovskite with Co, Ni, or Cu resolves this competition by switching Fe 3+ from a low-spin (t 2g 5 e g 0 ) to a high-spin (t 2g 3 e g 2 ) configuration. The dopant induces lattice contraction, which elongates Fe─O bonds, reduces the crystal-field splitting energy, and triggers the spin-state switch. This switch reconstructs the electronic structure of Fe-O-M (M = Cu, Co, Ni) bridge sites, the genuine active centers for CO 2 activation. The reconstructed bridge asymmetrically polarizes adsorbed CO 2 , selectively weakening one C─O bond and steering the cleavage toward CO production. The consequence is a pronounced shift in selectivity: the CO faradaic efficiency rises from 32% to over 90%, the co-electrolysis current density increases by up to 228%, and the CO/H 2 ratio becomes tunable from 0.14 to 11.8. By establishing a mechanistic pathway from lattice distortion through spin-state transition to catalytic selectivity, this study identifies spin-state engineering as a design dimension that operates beyond the explanatory reach of conventional geometric descriptors.

10.1002/adfm.79124.title: Functional Separator Coatings for Lithium/Sodium Metal Batteries: Bridging Academic Research and Industrial Prospects
10.1002/adfm.79124.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium/sodium metal batteries (LSMBs) are promising candidates for next-generation high-energy-density storage, yet their practical deployment remains constrained by dendrite formation, unstable electrode-electrolyte interfaces, and safety risks. Functional separator coatings offer an attractive strategy for stabilizing metal anodes because they are compatible with existing battery manufacturing and can be readily integrated into cell designs. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution from conventional polyolefin-based separators to advanced functional architectures. The physicochemical mechanisms through which functional coatings regulate ion transport, homogenize metal deposition, suppress dendrite growth, and improve thermal stability are critically reviewed. Representative coating materials, including ceramics, polymers, carbonaceous materials, metal-organic frameworks, and hybrid systems, are discussed in terms of their structure-function relationships, advantages, and limitations. The scalability of different coating strategies is evaluated in terms of coating thickness, line speed/throughput, material utilization, equipment requirements, and process continuity, thereby facilitating the selection of appropriate fabrication routes for distinct application scenarios. Finally, key challenges and future directions are outlined to guide rational separator design and practical manufacturing. This review aims to provide mechanistic insights and design principles for translating functional coated separators toward commercially viable metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79229.title: Bioinspired Stable Superhydrophobic Hierarchical Luminescence Textiles via Electrospinning and Electrospraying Synergism
10.1002/adfm.79229.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive photoluminescent textiles hold great promise for emergency signaling in extreme environments, yet preventing the loss or quenching of luminescent particles under water, ice, and abrasion remains a major challenge. Inspired by the transparent skin protection mechanism of Aequorea victoria , we propose a periodic electrospinning- electrospraying synergistic strategy to fabricate a bioinspired superhydrophobic electrospun luminescence film (ELF) with a unique hierarchical “skeleton-and-flesh” composite structure. The transparent “skin” air cushion protective layer, endowed with stable superhydrophobicity, enables the ELF to persistently luminesce for over 180 s in both dark air and underwater environments. White and colored luminescence yarns are obtained via high-temperature twisting and can be applied to patterned embroidery, encrypted optical messaging, and underwater warning displays. The woven centimeter-scale textile exhibits significantly enhanced superhydrophobic stability, withstanding >120 min washing, 20 abrasion cycles, and anti-icing at −28°C, showing potential for protective clothing in extreme cold wild environments. A proof-of-concept for a rescue experiment of a trapped underwater diver has been successfully demonstrated. This bioinspired strategy opens a new pathway for passive and durable optical signaling in harsh environments.

10.1002/adfm.79097.title: SP94-Functionalized Corosolic Acid Liposomes Enhance Tumor Delivery and Immunomodulatory Remodeling Against Hepatocellular Carcinoma
10.1002/adfm.79097.abstract: ABSTRACT The combination of arsenic trioxide (ATO) and all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) achieves synergistic efficacy in acute promyelocytic leukemia, with recent studies revealing its therapeutic potential against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Nonetheless, its application is constrained by inconsistent pharmacokinetics, dense stroma, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Herein, an SP94 peptide-functionalized, cholesterol-free corosolic acid (CA) liposomes (S-CALP) was developed to co-deliver arsenic precipitate and a lipophilic all-trans retinoic acid derivative (RAD) at an optimal 5:1 synergistic molar ratio. S-CALP prevented premature leakage under neutral physiological conditions, while triggering an acidity-responsive arsenic burst and intracellular RAD release upon internalization. Notably, substituting cholesterol with CA endowed S-CALP with superior membrane fusion capability, enabling enhanced intratumoral accumulation. Together with SP94 functionalization, S-CALP significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation and angiogenesis. In vivo, S-CALP achieved a tumor inhibition rate of 82%, extended median survival to 67.5 days, and effectively remodeled the TME by increasing anti-tumor immune cell infiltration and reducing immunosuppressive cell populations. Interestingly, unmodified CALP outperformed SP94-modified cholesterol liposomes (S-LP), highlighting its superior antitumor efficacy and translational potential. Overall, this cholesterol-free liposome, featuring highly efficient co-delivery, improved tumor accumulation, and TME remodeling capacities, provides a promising strategy for synergistic chemo-immunomodulatory therapy of HCC.

10.1002/adfm.79251.title: Lattice Bromine-Induced Pinning Effect Stabilizes Spinel Co 3 O 4 for Durable Bromine Radical-Mediated Propylene Oxide Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.79251.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical oxidation of propylene to propylene oxide (PO) using renewable electricity is a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial processes. However, this route is challenged by the high C═C activation barrier, competing oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and poor catalyst stability under high anodic potentials. Here, we report a bromine-doped Co 3 O 4 nanosheet array supported on carbon paper (Br-Co 3 O 4 /CP) that enables an efficient and stable bromine radical-mediated propylene oxidation reaction (BrPOR). Lattice Br induces a pinning effect that enhances Co─O covalency, stabilizes the spinel Co 3 O 4 structure, and suppresses detrimental surface reconstruction to CoOOH. Consequently, Br-Co 3 O 4 /CP delivers a PO Faradaic efficiency of 77.5% and a PO yield of 2.89 mmol h −1 at 200 mA cm −2 , while maintaining nearly 80% of its initial efficiency over 80 h. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations reveal that Br doping lowers the water dissociation barrier, enhances propylene adsorption, and stabilizes Co─O bonds, thereby achieving efficient and durable BrPOR. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of lattice doping and pinning effects in stabilizing oxide catalysts for robust electrochemical oxidation reactions, offering a viable pathway toward industrial-scale PO electrosynthesis.

10.1002/adfm.79197.title: Ultra-Thin Tow-Based Discontinuous Composites-Material Overview and Aspirations
10.1002/adfm.79197.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultra-thin Tow-Based Discontinuous Composites (µt-TBDC) are emerging as a transformative alternative to conventional continuous-fiber composites, offering the potential to overcome longstanding limitations in manufacturability, waste, and design flexibility. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of µt-TBDCs, spanning manufacturing, forming, mechanical characterization, and multi-scale modelling. Experimental results demonstrate that reducing tow thickness fundamentally alters the material response, enabling µt-TBDCs to achieve stiffness, strength, and notched performance comparable to quasi-isotropic laminates, while delivering enhanced compressive strength, fatigue resistance, and significantly improved energy absorption in tearing. These gains are attributed to a transition towards stable, interface and fibre dominated-controlled failure mechanisms, combined with reduced mesostructural variability arising from the increased number of tows through the thickness and reduced tow wavinesss. Analytical and numerical modelling approaches are reviewed, highlighting the effectiveness of simplified methods for predicting average behavior and the necessity of stochastic frameworks to capture strength and variability. Crucially, µt-TBDCs enable a broad and tunable design space, where fibre properties, tow thickness, and architecture act as independent design variables rather than fixed constraints. By linking material architecture, processing, and structural performance, this work positions µt-TBDCs as a paradigm shift in composite design, with significant implications for the future of high-performance lightweight structures.

10.1002/adfm.78501.title: In Situ Formed Co(OH)F Enabling Electronic and Atomic-Level Structure Optimization in Medium-Entropy Fluoride Cathodes for Zinc Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78501.abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt-based cathodes have attracted considerable attention in aqueous zinc batteries, however, their application remains impeded by intrinsic trade-off between high electrochemical activity and long-term cycling stability. Herein, an entropy-regulated fluoride cathode is proposed to overcome the limitations via co-engineering electronic and atomic structures. Specifically, x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and first-principle calculations collectively demonstrate that Co(OH)F is formed in situ within the fluoride matrix during electrochemical cycling and induces electron reconstruction. Concurrently, the generated Co(OH)F shortens Co─F bond length within the entropy-regulated fluoride, reinforcing atomic-level structural integrity and enabling excellent cycling performance. Moreover, a hollow architecture is integrated to homogenize flux and electric field distributions, ensuring sufficient accessibility of active sites while mitigating interfacial degradation. Consequently, the assembled zinc battery exhibits a high specific capacity of 252.3 mAh·g −1 and superior cycling stability (92.4% capacity retention after 25 000 cycles at 10 A·g −1 and 90.8% capacity retention after 50 000 cycles at 20 A·g −1 ). This work demonstrates a synergistic approach that simultaneously achieves high redox activity and structural robustness in cobalt-based cathodes for zinc batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79242.title: Industrial-Grade Recyclable Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Dynamic Thermoset Composites
10.1002/adfm.79242.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic thermoset resins (DR), defined as thermosets containing dynamic covalent bonds, present a promising solution for addressing the challenge of closed-loop recycling in carbon fiber reinforced thermoset (CFRP) composites. However, achieving large-scale preparation of DR-based CFRP and ensuring their compatibility with industrial equipment and production remain significant challenges. To address this issue, this work presents a full-chain process solution, encompassing the molecular structure design, prepreg and product manufacturing, and recycling stages. Specifically, we successfully synthesize an industrial-grade DR (IDR) with adjustable viscosity through the construction of a physically interpenetrating network between polyethersulfone chains and a polyester-based dynamic covalent network. Large-scale production of CF/IDR prepreg is achieved by existing industrial coating and roller impregnation techniques. Subsequently, CF/IDR prepregs are processed utilizing established industrial cutting, lamination, and autoclave curing to produce a large-scale aircraft panel (1 m × 2 m), that reveals a reliable buckling performance with a strain of −3133 µε. Notably, the panel exhibits solvent-assisted recyclability, owing to the dynamic reversible reaction of the IDR network, which enables complete recovery of both the resin and CF bundles. Moreover, the dynamic performance of the IDR network imparts reshapability and repairability to the panel. Therefore, this work demonstrates the feasibility of employing dynamic resin-based CFRP in industrial applications.

10.1002/adfm.78816.title: From Steric Liability to Structural Asset: Non-Benzylic Cation-π Anchoring Unlocks Hierarchical Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Ultra-Tough Recyclable Aromatic Polyurethane Elastomers
10.1002/adfm.78816.abstract: ABSTRACT Aromatic polyurethane elastomers offer intrinsic mechanical advantages, yet their bulky backbones are widely regarded as a steric liability that precludes the formation of ordered hydrogen-bond networks essential for high toughness. This long-standing conflict has consequently forced the field to rely on aliphatic precursors. To address this, we introduce thiabicyclononane-pyridinium ionic crosslinkers to engage the aromatic hard segments through cation-π interactions. This strategy effectively transforms the inherent steric hindrance of benzene rings from an impediment into a potent driving force for assembling dense, hierarchical hydrogen-bonded networks. The resulting elastomer (MA-S) exhibits exceptional mechanical integration, featuring a high tensile strength of 60.3 MPa, an ultra-high toughness of 283 MJ m −3 , outstanding impact resistance and a fracture energy of 198 kJ m −2 . These properties stem from the synergistic energy dissipation of hydrogen bonds, dynamic covalent bonds, and cation-π interactions. In addition, these multiple dynamic bonds endow the material with remarkable mechanical property retention (>95%) after multiple thermo-compression cycles. Furthermore, the aromatic-rich architecture enables robust π-π interfacial integration with carbon fibers, demonstrating a viable route toward closed-loop recyclable structural composites. Consequently, this work establishes a versatile molecular design paradigm for creating sustainable, high-performance polyurethanes that successfully reconcile mechanical robustness with dynamic recyclability.

10.1002/adfm.79108.title: Molecular Bridging Enables Uniform and Solvent-Resilient Buried Contacts for Efficient and Stable Perovskite/TOPCon Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79108.abstract: ABSTRACT Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable high-performance inverted perovskite solar cells and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, but polar solvents can partially disrupt preformed SAMs and produce nonuniform buried contacts, a challenge amplified on silicon substrates. Here, 3-(9H-carbazol-9-yl)propan-1-aminium iodide (CzPA) is introduced as a molecular bridge at the SAM/perovskite buried interface. The carbazole unit promotes π-π interactions with the SAM, improving monolayer retention during solvent exposure, while the terminal ammonium group interacts with iodide-containing precursor species to regulate interfacial nucleation. Furthermore, the iodide ions can effectively passivate the iodide vacancies at the buried interface. The reconstructed interface accelerates early-stage nucleation, promotes orientationally ordered crystal growth, and reduces residual tensile stress, thereby yielding a more p-type heterojunction and effectively suppressing non-radiative recombination. CzPA-modified wide-bandgap inverted single-junction cells deliver a PCE of 23.79%. Applied to perovskite/tunnel oxide passivating contact (TOPCon) tandems, this strategy improves perovskite continuity in pyramid valleys, enabling 1 cm 2 devices with a PCE of 33.4%. Unencapsulated tandems retain 88% of their initial PCE after 800 h of one-sun maximum-power-point tracking and 90% of their post-burn-in PCE after 737 h at 85°C, underscoring the robustness of the reconstructed buried interface.

10.1002/adfm.78630.title: Oxygen Reduction Reaction in Seawater as Electrolyte: From Mechanism and Electrocatalyst Design to System Integration
10.1002/adfm.78630.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in seawater as the electrolyte combines resource accessibility with significant application potential, providing important opportunities for chemical production and the development of electrochemical energy technologies. However, the multi-ion synergistic failures induced by Cl − , Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ , and other species in seawater severely restrict catalyst performance. Based on this, this review summarizes the latest research advances in ORR in seawater and simulated seawater systems. Starting from the reaction mechanisms, the 2e − and 4e − reaction pathways and the inhibitory effects of key ions on ORR are elucidated. Subsequently, electrocatalyst design strategies for enhancing activity, regulating selectivity, and improving stability are summarized, followed by an overview of the integration and application advances of ORR in seawater for H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis and energy devices. Finally, the engineering challenges and techno-economic issues facing seawater-based ORR systems are analyzed, and future development directions involving multidimensional synergistic advancements are proposed. This review aims to provide theoretical insights and engineering guidance for the design of high-performance electrocatalysts for ORR in seawater and the construction of practical application systems.
authors: Jingran Sun, Yuxin Liu, Yuxin Zhang, Guiru Sun, Xihan Wang, Junfeng Qin, Qingguo Meng, Jingqi Chi, Xiaobin Liu, Lei Wang

10.1002/adfm.79137.title: Mo2C-Mediated Surface Reconstruction in MoNi4@Mo2C Heterostructure for Efficient Electrocatalytic Urea Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.79137.abstract: ABSTRACT Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) offers an energy-saving route for H 2 production, yet rational regulation of surface reconstruction in Ni-based UOR electrocatalysts remains challenging. Herein, we report a MoNi 4 @Mo 2 C heterostructure and demonstrate its Mo 2 C-mediated reconstruction of surface Ni species toward NiOOH-containing active species during UOR. As a result, MoNi 4 @Mo 2 C requires only 1.26 V vs. RHE to reach 10 mA cm −2 and delivers 199.3 mA cm −2 at 1.30 V vs. RHE, outperforming MoNi 4 , Mo 2 C, and most reported Ni-based UOR electrocatalysts. Electrochemical measurements reveal the dynamic generation, consumption, and regeneration of high-valent Ni species during UOR. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms the potential-dependent formation of NiOOH-containing active species, while electrochemical impedance measurements demonstrate accelerated charge-transfer kinetics. When assembled in a two-electrode electrolyzer, MoNi 4 @Mo 2 C||Pt/C delivers 112.3 mA cm −2 at 1.40 V and lowers the cell voltage by 210 mV at 100 mA cm −2 relative to conventional water electrolysis. This work highlights the importance of Mo 2 C-mediated surface reconstruction in regulating active Ni species for UOR and offers insights into the rational design of Ni-Mo-based heterostructures for efficient urea electrolysis.
authors: Li-Qiu An, Xiao-Li Wang, Wen-Li Li, Kui Li, Yujie Song, Xing Lu

10.1002/adfm.79110.title: Microneedle-Integrated Catalytic Nanosweepers Enable Enrichment-Driven Clearance of Cell-Free DNA for Psoriasis Management
10.1002/adfm.79110.abstract: ABSTRACT Aberrant extracellular cell-free DNA (cfDNA) accumulation sustains chronic inflammation in psoriasis by activating the cGAS-STING pathway and amplifying oxidative stress. However, existing therapies primarily target downstream cytokines and fail to eliminate the upstream nucleic acid trigger. Here, we engineer a microneedle-integrated catalytic nanosweeper for localized and sustained catalytic cfDNA clearance within psoriatic lesions. The nanosweeper is constructed by embedding polycyanidin-coated cerium oxide nanozymes (PCeN) into positively charged aminated mesoporous bioactive glass nanoparticles (AMBN), forming an enrichment-enabled catalytic nanointerface. The AMBN framework electrostatically concentrates cfDNA at the nanoparticle interface and confined PCeN subsequently cleaves the phosphodiester backbone of cfDNA via phosphatase-like activity while restoring redox homeostasis through superoxide dismutase- and catalase-mimetic functions. This spatially coupled enrichment-catalysis mechanism converts transient nucleic acid sequestration into sustained catalytic cleavage, effectively disrupting the inflammation-oxidative stress feedback loop. Integrated into dissolvable microneedles, the platform achieves efficient intradermal delivery and catalytic confinement within hyperkeratotic lesions, resulting in suppression of the cfDNA-cGAS-STING axis, immune reprogramming, and epidermal normalization in imiquimod-induced psoriasis mice. Overall, this study provides a catalytic nanomaterial-based approach for regulating nucleic acid-driven inflammation and may offer a potential strategy for the treatment of psoriasis and other cfDNA-associated inflammatory skin disorders.
authors: Di Liu, Jingxian Gao, Xin Yang, Xueling Wu, Qian Lu, Lu Han

10.1002/adfm.79249.title: A Nanozyme-Enabled Peritoneum-Biomimetic Nano-Hydrogel for Macrophage-Targeted ROS-STING Modulation in Postoperative Adhesion-Free Healing
10.1002/adfm.79249.abstract: ABSTRACT Postoperative abdominal adhesion, characterized by its high prevalence, therapeutic intractability, and severe secondary complications, remains an intricate pathological condition following surgery. Here, using a peritoneal adhesion model integrated with multi-omics analyses, we identify ROS-driven activation of the cGAS-STING pathway as a central mechanism underlying macrophage activation and adhesion formation. To address this, black phosphorus nanosheets functionalized with Cu 2+ and NH 2 -PEG-polyinosinic acid (BPNS@Cu@PI) are engineered as a peritoneal macrophage-specific nanozyme to scavenge ROS. Furthermore, a silk fibroin-based Janus hydrogel with an MMP-responsive porous layer and a dense barrier layer (MMP-JSF) is constructed to mitigate copper-associated impairment of tissue repair. In vitro, this nano-hydrogel system enables targeted delivery, redox regulation, mitochondrial homeostasis restoration, cGAS-STING pathway inhibition, inflammation suppression, and wound healing promotion. In a 7-day rat model, the BPNS@Cu@PI demonstrated significant efficacy in inhibiting adhesions, with the accompanying MMP-JSF further enhancing therapeutic outcomes for tissue healing. Mechanistically, in a 3-day model, the platform not only inhibited adhesions but also exhibited robust therapeutic effects in suppressing the ROS-STING pathway and restoring mitochondrial function, as evidenced by both pathological and transcriptome analysis. Collectively, this work establishes a pathway-specific nano-hydrogel strategy for adhesion-free healing with translational potential.
authors: Yuan Chen, Mingyi Li, Jia Chen, Zhaojie Wang, Rui Zhao, Weiting Lu, Zhirong Zhao, Fan Yang, Weiliang Tian, Weiming Zhu, Qian Huang

10.1002/adfm.79219.title: Highly Stable Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Enabled by PGMA Anchoring Layer for Silicon-Based Anode
10.1002/adfm.79219.abstract: ABSTRACT The cycling stability of silicon-based anodes is severely compromised by the large volume changes of active particles during (de)lithiation, which disrupt the electrode structure due to insufficient interfacial bonding. Here, by leveraging the initiated chemical vapor deposition (iCVD) technique, we construct a poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) anchoring interlayer on SiO x particles. This interfacial design replaces weak physical interactions with robust covalent bindings: the epoxy groups in PGMA undergo ring-opening reactions with the poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) binder. This covalent linkage maintains direct contact between SiO x particles and the binding network during volume expansion, while enabling the conductive matrix to recover upon contraction, thereby effectively preventing particle isolation and pore formation. Consequently, the PGMA-modified electrode exhibits significantly enhanced interfacial adhesion and structural robustness, spatially confining solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth and mitigating continuous electrolyte depletion. As a result, the proposed strategy delivers improved cycling stability, retaining 95.0% of its capacity after 300 cycles with alleviated polarization. This study offers new perspectives for designing high-performance silicon-based anodes by overcoming a key limitation in electrode structural stability, namely the weak interaction between silicon particles and the binder.
authors: Yueyuan Tang, Yutong Liu, Zijin Xu, Kunchen Xie, Yitao Liu, Jiayao Qian, Jun Cao, Mingze Xu, Tianqi Wu, Xueyi Lu, Xia Lu, Luyi Yang, Guoyu Qian, Qiang Liu

10.1002/adfm.79130.title: Van der Waals Grain Boundary and Entropy Engineering Realize Broad-Temperature High Thermoelectric Performance in SnTe
10.1002/adfm.79130.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high conversion efficiency in thermoelectric materials requires excellent performance over a broad temperature range. In this work, the high thermoelectric performance of SnTe-based materials is extended from a single temperature point to a wide temperature range of approximately 200 K. Elemental doping and Sn vacancy engineering modulate the electronic structure and promote band convergence, thereby enhancing electrical transport properties. Meanwhile, abundant Sn vacancies aggregate at grain boundaries to form ordered van der Waals gaps, which enhance phonon scattering while maintaining favorable electrical transport. Additionally, multi-element doping induces lattice softening and increases configurational entropy, resulting in strong lattice distortion that further intensifies phonon scattering. These effects collectively enable the synergistic optimization of electrical and thermal performance. The lattice thermal conductivity is substantially reduced, and a peak ZT value of 1.4 (823 K) and a high average ZT of ∼1.3 (623-823 K) is achieved in Sn 0.61 Sb 0.10 Pb 0.15 Mn 0.09 Te. The single-stage module based on optimized SnTe achieves a conversion efficiency of 8%. This synergistic approach to modifying the lattice and grain boundaries provides a new perspective for optimizing the thermoelectric performance of materials in the medium- to high-temperature range.
authors: Shuhuan Yang, Zhangyujie Liu, Jianrui Wang, Hongwei Ming, Moran Wang, Yitao Lu, Binbin Jiang, Baohai Jia, Hai-Feng Li, Jiaqing He

10.1002/adfm.79019.title: In Situ Constructed Exogenous-Payload-Free Hydrogel for Electrochemical Therapy of Diabetic Burn Infection
10.1002/adfm.79019.abstract: ABSTRACT Diabetic wounds remain a critical clinical challenge due to their hostile microenvironment featured by high infection risk, persistent inflammation, etc . Herein, we innovatively constructed an exogenous-payload-free hydrogel via in situ photopolymerization for electrochemical therapy (ECT) of diabetic burn wounds, which utilized (3-acrylamidopropyl)trimethylammonium chloride as monomer and hydroxypropyltrimethyl ammonium chloride chitosan as biomass scaffold. Cationic quaternary ammonium groups on the hydrogel backbone first captured bacteria through electrostatic attraction. The platinum electrodes embedded within hydrogel generated therapeutic agents under a mild 2.0 V: counter Cl − within the hydrogel matrix was oxidized at the anode into reactive chlorine species for sterilization, while water in the hydrogel was electrolyzed to produce H 2 at the cathode to downregulate pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-1β. Meanwhile, the electric field accelerated fibroblast migration and angiogenesis by activating the PI3K/AKT and VEGF pathways. By harnessing the hydrogel's own structural components as the sole therapeutic resources, this work established an exogenous-payload-free strategy for multifunctional ECT toward diabetic wound healing.
authors: Aihui Wang, Xingyu Liu, Yaxuan Lin, Ziqi Ling, Weifeng Chen, Liqian Zheng, Rimei Huang, Shenghai Zhang, Fei Lv, Mingli Zhong, Shichen Ji, Hong Liang, Xing-Can Shen, Bang-Ping Jiang, Yu Liu

10.1002/adfm.79226.title: Dual Redox-Active Iron-Based Metal-Organic Network for Digital-Analog Memristors
10.1002/adfm.79226.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular memristors have shown great potential for digital memory and analog computing applications. However, developing molecular active layers with controllable structures and stable electrical properties remains challenging. Here, we employ a triphenylamine centered three armed terpyridine ligand (TPA-(TPy) 3 ) to construct a two-dimensional (2D) iron based metal-organic network (Fe-MON) film through interfacial coordination assembly. The three-armed molecular topology promotes lateral network growth, enabling the formation of continuous and robust Fe-MON films. In contrast, the structurally analogous two-armed ligand (TPA-(TPy) 2 ) fails to generate continuous networks, resulting in inferior device stability. The resulting Al/Fe-MON/ITO memristors exhibit reliable digital resistive switching characteristics with narrow ON/OFF voltage distributions, good retention, and endurance. Moreover, the synergistic redox activity of triphenylamine and Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ centers enables continuous conductance modulation under pulse stimulation, achieving 64 distinguishable multilevel conductance states. By integrating these conductance states into a convolutional neural network (CNN), the system achieves 96.57% accuracy in flower image recognition. This work demonstrates the capability of 2D metal-organic network films for digital-analog dual-mode memristors.
authors: Jiaxuan Pan, Qiongshan Zhang, Qing Yan, Lei Zhao, Hao Wang, Bin Zhang, Fuzhen Xuan

10.1002/adfm.79214.title: Ionic Nano-Engineering of Wood Cell Walls for High-Performance Marine Energy Harvesting
10.1002/adfm.79214.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanofluidic systems hold great promise for water treatment and blue energy harvesting. However, fabricating natural-based nanofluidic materials that simultaneously deliver tunable channel orientation, high charge density, and robust mechanical at scale remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate a wood nanofluidic platform enabled by ionic nano-engineering of the wood cell wall, involving ionized cell-wall scaffold reconstruction and in situ nanopolymer polymerization. Periodate oxidation followed by Schiff-base coupling grafts positively charged ─NH 2 functionalities onto the cellulose skeleton, converting oxidized wood from negatively charged (ζ = −16.5 mV) to positively charged (ζ = +33.5 mV). Subsequent in situ nano-polymerization rebuilds a 3D gel network within the cell wall, enriching charge density while creating additional nanochannels and interconnecting previously isolated pores. This strategy of structure regulation, interface modification, and functional assembly that overcomes the intrinsic “fiber-aligned transport” limitation of wood. As a result, the obtained cationic wood membrane (C-WM) and anionic wood membrane (A-WM) deliver tensile strengths of 11.7 and 13.1 MPa, respectively, and exhibit high ionic conductivities of 2.24 × 10 −3 and 1.65 × 10 −3 S cm −1 in dilute electrolytes. This sustainable wood ionic membranes offering an appealing strategy for developing high-performance and environmentally blue energy conversion systems.

10.1002/adfm.79225.title: Atomic-Scale Cation Partitioning Links Reaction-Product Chemistry to Molten-Silicate Passivation in Rare-Earth Tantalates
10.1002/adfm.79225.abstract: ABSTRACT Molten silicates can be immobilized by protective reaction products or continue to penetrate oxide ceramics, but the structural features that distinguish these pathways remain unclear. Here we examine CMAS reactions with RETa 3 O 9 and connect crystallographic cation partitioning in corrosion products with passivation across rare-earth chemistry, melt composition, and multicomponent design. EuTa 3 O 9 forms a durable bilayer comprising a dense AX 2 O 6 barrier and a cation-sequestering B 2 Y 2 O 7 layer; a related consumption-barrier architecture persists in Fe-rich lunar- and Martian-regolith analogue melts. Across 11 RETa 3 O 9 compositions, rare-earth size acts as a structural descriptor for access to AX 2 O 6 -, B2Y2O 7 -, and CZO 4 -containing reaction pathways. Using this relationship as a design constraint, Eu-centred high-entropy RETa 3 O 9 compositions retain resistance to bulk penetration while reducing thermal conductivity. HEC-2 forms an 84.4 µm reaction layer after 100 h at 1300°C and exhibits an 8.3% lower calculated effective thermal conductivity than EuTa 3 O 9 at 1200°C. These results link reaction-product chemistry to mechanism-constrained composition design for high-temperature protective ceramics.
authors: Zeyu Chen, Yiling Huang, Fan Peng, Wei Zheng, Xuemei Song, Yaran Niu, Yi Zeng

10.1002/adfm.79254.title: Programmable Organic Light-Emitting Transistors Enabled by Floating-Gate Charge Storage
10.1002/adfm.79254.abstract: ABSTRACT Display technologies for high-resolution smartphones, wearable screens and near-eye VR/AR microdisplays increasingly require compact pixel architectures with high aperture ratios. Organic light-emitting transistors (OLETs) improve functional integration by combining transistor switching and electroluminescence within a single device. However, conventional OLETs still define emission states through instantaneous electrical bias, leaving state storage separated from light emission. The absence of memory-emission co-location limits intrinsic state programmability in OLET-based pixel devices. Here, we report programmable organic light-emitting transistors (P-OLETs) based on a floating-gate architecture, in which charge storage enables reversible charge trapping and release, producing programmable switching behavior and tunable electroluminescence. The stored charge modulates channel transport and light emission, allowing electrical programming to define persistently retained optical states. Optimized P-OLETs exhibit a large memory window of 27.07 V, stable luminance retention over 5000 s, and reliable endurance over 100 program/erase cycles. Floating-gate charge storage shifts OLET operation from bias-defined emission toward charge-state defined emission and establishes a memory-emission integrated device architecture. This work introduces programmable state-retentive emission as a compact operating concept for programmable optoelectronics and reconfigurable display systems.
authors: Jiatong Liu, Zeyi Yan, Pusen Zhang, Xiwei Zheng, Xiteng Li, Zhouying Wu, Jun Han, Meili Xu, Hong Meng

10.1002/adfm.78993.title: From Coacervates to Ordered Lattices: Sequence-Guided Condensation of Polyelectrolyte Complexes Through Designed Coiled-Coil Peptides
10.1002/adfm.78993.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrostatic complexation of oppositely charged biomacromolecules produces a spectrum of condensed phases, from liquid coacervates to ordered solids. Yet the underlying amino acid sequence-level rules remain poorly understood. Here, we utilize computationally designed coiled-coil peptide “bundlemers” as a programmable platform to systematically investigate these principles. This study demonstrates that precise control over the material phase formed through electrostatic complexation is achieved through subtle amino acid sequence modifications. By tuning coiled coil terminal motifs and surface charge distribution, bundlemer-polypeptide complexation can span liquid coacervates, soft solids, or solid precipitates. Specifically, bundlemer coiled coil nanoparticles with +24 charge were complexed with different lengths of polyanionic polypeptide. Nanoparticles with a mixed charge character containing both acidic and basic amino acids produced coacervate phases. When the bundlemers displayed only basic amino acids making a single charge-type +24 nanoparticle, solid precipitates with specific hexagonal lattice symmetry were formed. When the charge character was flipped with negatively charged bundlemers and positively charged polypeptide, similar hexagonally packed complexes were formed. This work establishes a robust framework for programming the self-assembly of polyelectrolyte-based soft matter, offering a sequence-guided pathway from disordered liquid condensates to precisely defined, ordered nanomaterials.
authors: Weiran Xie, Tianren Zhang, Wenjun Peng, Bin Wang, Darrin J Pochan

10.1002/adfm.79274.title: Ultralow Electric and Photonic Noise MoS2 Transistors for Noise-Limited Multistate Readout
10.1002/adfm.79274.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) semiconductors offer a compelling route toward co-integrated logic, memory, and optoelectronic sensing. However, their performance is often constrained by defect-mediated contact resistance, and its impact on low-frequency noise (LFN) and signal resolution remains under-quantified. Here we demonstrate antimony (Sb)-contact monolayer MoS 2 transistors that simultaneously deliver ultralow 1/ f noise and high phototransistor gain, offering high photonic resolution. Sb contacts exhibit reduced contact-limited transport and lower contact-related carrier fluctuations than Au-contact reference devices, leading to near-ohmic-like injections and a reduced LFN. Furthermore, under illumination, the devices exhibit high photogating-enabled responsivity (1.33 × 10 5 A/W) and detectivity (7.50 × 10 15 Jones) under the measurement conditions used in this work without a discernible illumination-induced excess noise. Leveraging the exceptional ultralow-noise and high-gain characteristics of the Sb-contact MoS 2 transistors, we provide an LFN-to-photonic-resolution metric that translates fluctuation-induced noise into information fidelity. This work translates contact engineering of vdW semiconductors into a direct lever for information-fidelity-limited 2D logic and optoelectronics.
authors: Youngchan Cho, Jinhyeok Pyo, Min Wook Kang, Youngmin Han, Hyunjun Ahn, Sanghyuk Lee, Sohyeon Park, Jueun Lee, Sangwan Kim, Jaehong Park, Jaehong Min, Hosu Park, Seojun Hwang, David Radermacher, Saeroonter Oh, Sung-Tae Lee, Hocheon Yoo, Youngho Kang, Sangyeon Pak, Wonjun Shin

10.1002/adfm.79236.title: Substoichiometric [4+3] Strategy for Constructing Subvalent COFs with Acrylonitrile Unit Toward Solar-Driven H2O2 Production from Seawater
10.1002/adfm.79236.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid charge carrier recombination and limited active site availability remain major challenges for photocatalytic production of H 2 O 2 in water, particularly in seawater. Herein, we propose a substoichiometric [4+3] strategy to construct a subvalent covalent organic framework (TAQ-COF) functionalized with acrylonitrile and benzoxadiazole moieties and the off-stoichiometry of the polymerization reaction preserves two unreacted aldehyde groups per node. The resulting TAQ-COF exhibits outstanding visible-light-driven H 2 O 2 production in pure water without any sacrificial agent, retains approximately 93% of its activity in seawater, and demonstrates excellent recyclability and antibacterial performance. Both theoretical and experimental evidence demonstrate that the enhanced local electron density surrounding the benzoxadiazole moieties in TAQ-COF creates a favorable microenvironment for the proton-coupled reduction of O 2 . Owing to its strong electron-withdrawing effect and conjugated structure, the acrylonitrile unit markedly extends the lifetime of photogenerated charge carriers from 1.50 to 17.94 ns. Moreover, the enhanced surface hydrophilicity of TAQ-COF sample promotes interfacial water enrichment, thereby favoring the proton-coupled oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The synergy of these features endows TAQ-COF with outstanding catalytic activity in the two-electron ORR pathway. This work demonstrates that synergistic functionalization with acrylonitrile units in a substoichiometric COF yields robust photocatalysts.
authors: Guilin Li, Jia He, Zikun Zhang, Ting Song, Zehui Zhang, Yizheng Chen

10.1002/adfm.79266.title: Loop Corrected Virtual Tactile Interaction: From Haptic Sensing to Feedback Based on Integrated Glove Interface
10.1002/adfm.79266.abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced tactile interfaces, regarding sensing and feedback functions, have revolutionized tactile interaction in virtual reality. These two build a bridge facilitating communication between the physical and virtual world, but were developed independently. A glove interface integrated with sensing and feedback is proposed for loop-corrected virtual tactile interaction. It consists of an iontronic tactile sensor and micro-discharge electrotactile feedback, which are integrated on the opisthenar and palm side of the textile glove, respectively. Iontronic sensor is modified with various sized micro pyramid and its springback hysteresis is reduced to 5.82% for dynamic pressure monitoring. Meanwhile, the electrotactile feedback is optimized with ideal micro-gap discharge contributing to a safe current (about 40 µA) on the skin, supporting frequent electrostimulation for hierarchical feedback. In this loop-corrected system, the iontronic tactile sensor can provide various pressure data originating from joint bending, consisting the data source for controlling the virtual hand, while the monitored virtual operation state is informed in the physical world by electrotactile feedback, and then the hand gesture is corrected according to feedback of various degrees to adjust the virtual counterpart. Thus, closed-loop tactile interaction is accomplished, and this loop-corrected glove interface is promising for realizing complicated but precise manipulation tasks in VR-based human-machine cooperation.
authors: Yuxiang Shi, Chong Feng, Zhiyuan Xu, Yuning Liang, Xinyang Liu, Xinyi Yuan, Jun Luo, Jun Zhang, Yong Qin, Guozhen Shen

10.1002/adfm.79074.title: Rational Construction of Multicomponent Electrocatalyst via Cluster-Nanoparticle Synergy for Enhanced Hydrogen Production Coupled With Hydrazine Oxidation at Large Current Densities
10.1002/adfm.79074.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrazine-assisted water electrolysis enables low-energy-consumption hydrogen production while simultaneously facilitating the harmless treatment of hydrazine-containing pollutants. Herein, a hydrothermal and air-annealing strategy was employed to simultaneously anchor Ru nanoclusters and Pt nanoparticles on NiO nanowires, thereby constructing a bifunctional Pt-Ru/NiO catalyst with synergistic dual-sites for the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This study reveals that the incorporation of Pt and Ru effectively tailors the electronic configuration, optimizing the free energy of hydrogen adsorption/desorption and N 2 H 4 dehydrogenation kinetics, thus endowing the catalyst with outstanding HER and HzOR electrocatalytic activity. To attain the current density of 1000 mA cm − 2 , Pt-Ru/NiO merely requires working potentials of 0.158 V for HER and 0.157 V for HzOR, respectively. Impressively, with Pt-Ru/NiO functioning as cathode and anode, the assembled full hydrazine electrolyzer yields 200 mA cm − 2 at an extremely low cell voltage of just 0.057 V, with stable operation sustained for more than 100 h. This work provides a design framework for cluster-particle dual-site synergistic systems and offers a new pathway for hydrazine-assisted high-efficiency electrolytic hydrogen production technology.
authors: Jingyan Duan, Zhongge Luo, Xueqin Ni, Huachuan Sun, Mingpeng Chen, Tong Zhou, Zongwei Wang, Boxue Wang, Dequan Li, Qingjie Lu, Bin Xiao, Yuxiao Zhang, Xuefei Xu, Dingsheng Wang, Qingju Liu

10.1002/adfm.79221.title: Moderate Li-N Coordination Between Dibromopyrazine and Polysulfides Enables High-Rate Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79221.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries are promising candidates for high-energy storage, yet their practical application is limited by poor rate capability. To date, the conversion of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) remains a major challenge due to the high energy barrier of the liquid-solid conversion from Li 2 S 4 to Li 2 S. Herein, to overcome this barrier, dibromopyrazine (DBP) was identified through screening as an effective electrolyte additive owing to its unique Br─C═N functionality, which weakens Li-S bonding via moderate Li-N coordination through the electron-withdrawing effect of Br, thereby enabling effective LiPSs anchoring without impeding conversion. In the electrolyte containing 0.04 M DBP, the interaction favors Li 2 S 4 formation at 2.3 V and promotes three-dimensional (3D) Li 2 S deposition. Consequently, the Li-S coin cells deliver a high capacity of 785 mAh g −1 at the high rate of 6 C and a low capacity decay rate of 0.09% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. A 2 Ah pouch cell also demonstrates stable cycling over 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work highlights a coordination-modulated moderate-interaction strategy for accelerating LiPSs conversion in Li-S batteries.
authors: Zhonghui Sun, Handing Liu, Xin Chao, Zhenghui Li, Ziyang Xie, Qisen Wang, Chaoxin Wu, Ruohan Jiang, Runjing Xu, Jiayun Zhang, Jinyu Yang, Ziyue Li, Dalin Sun, Fei Wang, Fang Fang

10.1002/adfm.79284.title: Manipulating Spectral Location in a Cr3+-Activated Broadband Garnet Phosphor Toward Highly Efficient NIR Pc-LEDs
10.1002/adfm.79284.abstract: ABSTRACT Near-infrared phosphor-converted light-emitting diodes (NIR pc-LEDs) are highly attractive due to compact, low-cost, and portable characteristics. Despite the discovery of several efficient and thermostable NIR garnet phosphors, the output power and photoelectric conversion efficiency of the fabricated NIR pc-LEDs remain severely limited, hindering their practical deployment. Herein, we address this challenge by a single-site substitution design of Ge 4+ for Si 4+ in a garnet host Y 2 MgAl 4 SiO 12 (YMASi). The newly developed Y 2 MgAl 4 GeO 12 (YMAGe):Cr 3+ phosphor demonstrates a substantially red-shifted broadband NIR emission (90 nm shift, peaking at 809 nm) with an ultra-broad full-width at half maximum (FWHM) of 152 nm, along with good thermal stability (82%@423 K). Remarkably, this substitution simultaneously enhances the internal and external quantum efficiencies by factors of 1.8 and 2.1, respectively. Combining atomic-resolution imaging with spectroscopic analysis, we unravel the origin of the spectral redshift and the underlying mechanism for the luminescent enhancement. Benefiting from these outstanding properties, driven by 100 mA, a prototype NIR light source fabricated with YMAGe:Cr 3+ achieves a high output power of 51.6 mW and photoelectric conversion efficiency of 22.7%, thereby demonstrating strong potential for multifunctional applications including night vision, biological imaging, non-destructive testing, and plant growth lighting.
authors: Yiting Huang, Hong Yuan, Yuxin Liu, Yuanbiao Li, Xiaoshuang Tang, Yuncang Yang, Jiale Dong, Xiongwei Dai, Wei Qian, Bo Wang, Jing Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79224.title: Dual-Site Engineering of a Noble-Metal-Free Z-Scheme Heterojunction for Radical-Kinetics-Steered Selective C-C Coupling
10.1002/adfm.79224.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective photocatalytic C─C homocoupling of amines remains challenging due to uncontrollable radical kinetics and over-oxidation. Herein, we construct a noble-metal-free Z-scheme Cr-TiO 2 @N-C/CdS heterojunction photocatalyst that decouples thermodynamic and kinetic control through a dual-site strategy. The incorporation of N-doped carbon buffer layer not only resolves the intrinsic work function mismatch between Cr-TiO 2 and CdS for efficient Z-scheme charge transfer, but also facilitates rational control over the sequential arrangement of interfaces, thereby precisely regulating the coupling sites. Thermodynamically, Cr-induced impurity levels near the valence band edge of TiO 2 moderate hole oxidation potential, preventing over-oxidation of benzylamine. Kinetically, at the CdS surface, strong electronic interactions between surface three-coordinated Cd atoms and the Ph( • CH)NH 2 radical impede further oxidation to imine, maintaining a high local radical concentration and exclusively driving C─C coupling. Consequently, under blue light, this heterojunction selectively converts benzylamine to the corresponding diamine (∼80% selectivity and an apparent quantum yield of 2.78%) with simultaneous high-rate hydrogen evolution through a concerted proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. This selectivity is broadly applicable to other benzylamine derivatives and benzyl alcohol systems. This work demonstrates that coordinated regulation of redox and surface reaction sites provides a robust strategy for achieving controllable radical dynamics and selective C─C bond synthesis.

10.1002/adfm.79209.title: Thermodynamic Suppression of Deprotonation in Succinonitrile-Based Electrolyte for Durable Solid-State Sodium-Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79209.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state sodium-metal batteries (SSMBs) offer a low-cost, safe, and high-energy-density energy-storage technology. While succinonitrile (SN) is widely adopted in solid and gel electrolytes for its high dielectric constant, exceptional oxidative stability, and robust cathode compatibility, its practical application is limited by parasitic reactions with Na metal, including deprotonation and polymerization. Herein, we demonstrated a thermodynamic suppression strategy of deprotonation that substantially inhibits parasitic reactions in SN-based electrolytes for durable SSMBs. By utilizing an acrylonitrile (AN) based polymer as the host framework, we establish an optimized interaction with free SN that thermodynamically disfavors the parasitic decomposition, effectively stabilizing the α-hydrogens of the methylene groups against deprotonation. The rationally designed electrolyte exhibits high ionic conductivity of 2.17 mS cm −1 and exceptional compatibility with Na metal, enabling stable cycling of Na | Na symmetric cells for 6200 h. Na | Vanadium phosphate sodium full cells retain 95.6% capacity after 5000 cycles at 1.0 C, 93.4% after 10000 cycles at 2.0 C, and pouch cells with an ultra-high cathode loading of 20 mg cm −2 demonstrate stable performance. This work establishes thermodynamic suppression of deprotonation as a foundational design principle for high-energy-density and long-lifespan SSMBs.
authors: Shangming He, Mingbao Huang, Yi Li, Kai Wan, Zhiyong Fu, Zhenxing Liang, Xiaoru Chen

10.1002/adfm.79228.title: A Multifunctional Smart Window for Adaptive Solar, Thermal, and Electromagnetic Management in Buildings
10.1002/adfm.79228.abstract: ABSTRACT Smart windows could reduce building energy demand, but most regulate only one or two spectral bands and do not address the increasingly complex electromagnetic environments of modern buildings. Here we report a multifunctional window that combines electrochemical switching with low-frequency mechanical reorientation to control visible, near-infrared, long-wave infrared, and microwave responses. A transparent Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene electrode ( T 550 nm > 60%, R s ≈ 40 Ω/sq) and a PEDOT:PSS layer enable electrochemical regulation of glare and solar heat gain through coupled visible-near-infrared optical switching. Reorientation of a Janus interface switches the outward long-wave emissivity ( ε LWIR ) between ∼0.83 and ∼0.38 for cooling- and heating-oriented operation. The device also shows reversible X-band shielding modulation from 15.5 to 20.2 dB. Comparative chamber tests, climate-resolved building simulations and carbon accounting suggest reduced annual HVAC demand and associated CO 2 emissions in representative climates.
authors: Runcheng Hao, Kaige Wang, Ruizhe Wang, Zhen Tang, Kerui Li, Hongzhi Wang, Hengda Sun, Gang Wang, Meifang Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79210.title: Beyond Primary Nucleation: Molecular Basis of Peptide Crystal Secondary Nucleation at Soft Interface
10.1002/adfm.79210.abstract: ABSTRACT The formation of peptide 2D crystals with well-organized molecular arrays by primary nucleation mechanism have provided an efficient way to incorporate biofunctions into the underlying single layer graphene and MoS 2 , leading to broad applications for biosensing, biomedicine and bioelectronics. Further realizing a high-level architecture of peptide 3D crystals coupling with the underlying nanomaterials would expand its applications for the next-generation bionanodevices, while facing a big challenge. A layer-by-layer stacking of 3D peptide assemblies through secondary nucleation (SN) mechanism at soft interface provides an available strategy while its molecular basis has been rarely explored. We utilized time-resolved 3-dimensional atomic force microscopy (3D-AFM) to directly observe SN and growth mechanism of stacked peptide 3D crystals on highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG). Moreover, the formation details of peptide 3D crystals including nucleation sites, growth dynamics, molecular-resolution nanostructures, phase transitions, and cross-seeding growth were discovered. Such non-traditional methodology in engineering peptide 3D crystals would bring new prospects for nanoscience and nanotechnology.
authors: Linhao Sun, Abilesh Kumar, Ayhan Yurtsever

10.1002/adfm.78353.title: Solvent-Solvent Interaction Regulation Enables a Practical Ultra-Low-Temperature Electrolyte for Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78353.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrolytes encounter critical challenges at low temperatures (LT), such as solvent crystallization and sluggish Na + transport kinetics. While most studies have primarily focused on low-viscosity ethers or highly fluorinated solvents for LT performance, their practical applications remain limited by inadequate stability and environmental and safety concerns. In this work, a low-cost, highly safe electrolyte for LT applications was designed based on sodium-ion pouch cells. Through methyl substitution at α-H, the polarity of ethyl butyrate was enhanced, promoting interactions with propylene carbonate to construct a highly stable electrolyte with low solvation energy barriers. It exhibits an ultra-low freezing point (−130°C) and superior kinetics, demonstrating excellent electrochemical performance in Ah-scale pouch cells, including: a discharge capacity retention of nearly 70% at −60°C; maintaining 90% of initial capacity after 200 cycles of continuous discharge at 1C and −30°C; and a fast-charge/discharge capacity retention of over 90% at 10C and 25°C. Furthermore, systematic analysis of sodium plating behavior on anodes at LT revealed that the electrolyte has significant advantages in suppressing sodium plating. Finally, successful engineering-scale validation was conducted in a 5 Ah pouch cell, providing a safe, reliable, and practical electrolyte design strategy for LT sodium-ion batteries.
authors: Guangcong Zeng, Xu Yang, Yong Yi, Zilong Li, Ji Qi, Heshan Yang, Wen Liu, Qian Cheng, Baohua Li, Guobing Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79186.title: Organic Ligand-Functionalized CoN2-C-N2Ni Dual-Atom for Tailored Proton and Non-Proton Transfer in Hydrogen Evolution and Triiodide Reduction
10.1002/adfm.79186.abstract: ABSTRACT Regulating the sustained transport and local concentration of reactive intermediates is essential for accelerating kinetics; however, constructing effective pathways for transferring both protonic and non-protonic intermediates remains challenging. Herein, we present organic ligand-functionalized interfacial engineering by anchoring trimesic acid (TMA) to MXene-supported Co/Ni dual-atom sites (TMA-CoNi DA -MXene) to establish carboxyl-mediated proton and non-proton transport channels. By leveraging continuous π-π stacking and deprotonated ─COO − groups in aromatic frameworks, TMA-CoNi DA -MXene facilitated the capture and delivery of I * /H * intermediates toward Co/Ni dual active sites, while also mitigating localized excessive accumulation of I * /H * .
