By exploiting the expanded interlayer spacing, stabilized CoN 2 -C-N 2 Ni centers, and tailored transport pathways, TMA-CoNi DA -MXene achieved a photoconversion efficiency of 8.62% as a counter electrode in iodine-based solar cells and attained 10 mA cm −2 with an overpotential of only 71 mV in the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work provides insightful perspectives on integrating carboxylated organic ligands to jointly transfer protonic and non-protonic intermediates and offers new approaches for organic-inorganic interfacial design in other complex systems.
authors: Rou Feng, Menglong Sun, Zechang Liu, Tianxiang Yang, Jiaoe Dang, Zhiguo Wang, Haijiang Yang, Weidong Tian, Sining Yun

10.1002/adfm.79189.title: Insights into Local Framework Conformations of pH-Tunable Electro-Optic-Catalytic β-Cyclodextrin-Synthetic Polymer System: Selective Dual-Mode Sensing and Electrocatalysis of Amino Acids
10.1002/adfm.79189.abstract: ABSTRACT In polymeric system, local framework conformations provide an effective route to generate supramolecular architectures from identical structural units; herein, pH-tunable realization in electro-optic-catalytic semisynthetic-polymers for dual-mode fluorogenic-electrochemical amino acid sensing/ electrocatalysis is reported. Initially, synthetic fluorescent electroactive conducting polymers (FECPs) were synthesized using N , N -dimethylacrylamide and cis -butenedioic acid through polymerization in an aqueous medium. The optimized FECP3 was modified with β -cyclodextrin to rigidify the matrix and fix the orientation of ─C(═O)N/ ─C(═O)OH groups, inducing local framework conformations. Combined computational and pH-dependent spectroscopic-electrochemical studies confirmed two local framework conformations in all the β -cyclodextrin/FECP3 (LFCFECPs). In optimum LFCFECP2, coexistence of LFCFECP2-A and LFCFECP2-B was validated by the excitation-dependent emission profile and cathodic peaks of C═N + →C • ─N in cyclic voltammogram of LFCFECP2-A-/ LFCFECP2-B-modified glassy-carbon electrode (LFCFECP2-A|GCE/ LFCFECP2-B|GCE). LFCFECP2-A and LFCFECP2-B exhibited pH-selective dual-mode sensing, enabling fluorogenic-electrochemical detection of Tyrosine and Tryptophan in aqueous solution/ cow milk/ soybean extract at pH 6.0 and 8.0, respectively, with rapid response, low detection limits, and high reproducibility. Compared to LFCFECP2-A|GCE/ LFCFECP2-B|GCE, LFCFECP2-A/ LFCFECP2-B film working-electrode (WE) displayed a higher electroactive surface area. Therefore, LFCFECP2-A and LFCFECP2-B films (WEs) were employed for efficient electrocatalytic conversions of Tyrosine and Tryptophan to Dopaquinone and 3 a -hydroxyhexahydropyrrolo[2,3- b ]indole-2-carboxylic acid with 95.35 and 92.31% conversion efficiencies, respectively.
authors: Shrestha Roy, Preetam Nandy, Deepak Chowdhury, Nadira Hassan, Saikat Sarkar, Suman Kalyan Samanta, Mincheol Chang, Mostafizur Rahaman, Narendra Nath Ghosh, Pijush Kanti Chattopadhyay, Dilip K. Maiti, Nayan Ranjan Singha

10.1002/adfm.79279.title: Ordered Cu─Pd Intermetallic Alloy With Complementary Facets Enables Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis via Accelerated C─N
10.1002/adfm.79279.abstract: ABSTRACT CO 2 and nitrate are widespread contaminants. Co-electrolysis of them to produce urea enables eco-friendly pollution treatment and agricultural support, while bare Cu suffers low selectivity, quick deactivation and dominant hydrogen evolution reaction competition. Herein, we synthesize long-range ordered concave CuPd intermetallics (f-CuPd) by liquid reduction and gradient annealing. Characterizations confirm annealing converts disordered face-centered cubic d-CuPd to ordered body-centered cubic phase. Fully ordered f-CuPd exposes complementary (211) and (001) facets with evenly mixed Cu and Pd without segregation. Its ordered atomic arrangement induces Pd to Cu charge transfer and restrains Cu surface oxidation. Electrochemical measurements reveal exceptional electrocatalytic activity toward urea synthesis, attaining a urea production rate of 74.78 mmol h −1 g cat −1 and steady catalytic activity throughout 28 h of uninterrupted electrolysis. In situ spectra track the reaction and prove the ordered structure adjusts interfacial water to generate active hydrogen and avoid competitive adsorption of CO 2 and nitrate intermediates. Density functional theory calculations uncover a unique synergistic effect between two crystal facets. The (211) facet drives efficient CO 2 activation to form * CO intermediates, while the adjacent (001) facet facilitates nitrate reduction and C─N coupling with substantially reduced kinetic barriers. Reaction intermediates migrate across distinct crystal facets, driving highly efficient urea formation.
authors: Ruidong Wang, Jing Tao, Chaochen Wang, Jianhua Shen, Yihua Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79235.title: Engineering Ni 0/δ+ -Co σ+ Pairs to Facilitate Interfacial Water Restructuring and Promote Volmer-Heyrovsky-Dominated Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.79235.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal phosphide alloy materials exhibit application potential in alkaline water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. However, interfacial H 2 O structure, along with protons kinetic behavior at the interface in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) remain elusive. Herein, we report a site-substitution-electronic modulation strategy to construct P-bridged Ni 0/δ+ -Co σ+ pairs in Ni mesh (NM) supported NiCoP (NiCoP-NM), wherein Co substitution at Ni sites modulates the electronic structure and generates an electron-rich Ni center. The experiment and theoretical studies reveal that the Ni 0/δ+ -Co σ+ pairs redistribute the electron spin orientation at Ni sites, strengthening H* binding, and increasing surface H* coverage, which accelerates Heyrovsky kinetics by facilitating H 2 release. Additional, Ni 0/δ+ -Co σ+ pairs reorganize the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network and increase K + concentration in closest ion plane, leading to stronger H 2 O adsorption (−1.52 vs. −0.96 eV on NiP-NM) and a lower H 2 O dissociation barrier (1.59 vs. 1.64 eV on NiP-NM), thereby facilitating Volmer kinetics via boosting H 2 O activation. Consequently, NiCoP-NM achieves outstanding HER performance with an overpotential of only 86.75 mV at 100 mA cm −2 , along with stability over 1000 h. This work offers a new strategy for designing metal phosphide alloys that tailor interfacial water structure and proton dynamics for advanced electrosynthesis.

10.1002/adfm.79165.title: Neuron Mitochondria Targeted “Zipper Peptide” Delivery for VHL-Inhibiting Therapy in Parkinson's Disease
10.1002/adfm.79165.abstract: ABSTRACT Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) emerges as a promising target for neuroprotective treatment in Parkinson's disease (PD), but the challenging druggability hampers therapeutic development. Herein, we report a leucine zipper-inspired peptide design for VHL-targeting therapy, in which spontaneous formation of α-helical structure yields high affinity and biostability, and a symmetrical hetero-charge distribution on the α-helix is easier to zip peptide into nanogel, followed by complexing with lipids and T7 peptide for dopaminergic neuron-targeted mitochondria therapy. After systemic administration, the peptide-lipid nanocomplex could reach dopaminergic neurons within 2 h, and release the VHL-inhibiting peptide upon acidic pH to effectively disrupt VHL/Dishevelled-2 (DVL-2) interaction. Downstream β-catenin and hexokinase 2 (HK2) proteins are elevated, promoting mitochondrial homeostasis, metabolic activity, and energy production for neuronal protection. The VHL-targeting peptide therapy effectively ameliorates neurodegenerative pathologies and motor/coordination deficits in both MPTP-induced injury and α-synuclein overexpression PD models. Collectively, this study provides an innovative peptide drug design and a dopaminergic neuron-targeting strategy for the neuroprotective treatment of PD.

10.1002/adfm.79187.title: Engineering Acidic CO 2 Electroreduction for Efficient and Durable Formic Acid Production
10.1002/adfm.79187.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical synthesis of formic acid (HCOOH) via the carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic electrolytes can circumvent the severe CO 2 loss in alkaline and neutral conditions. However, simultaneously attaining high HCOOH production efficiency and durable long-term operation in acidic CO 2 RR remains a critical bottleneck impeding the technology's practical deployment. Herein, we first discuss the core challenges faced by acidic CO 2 RR to HCOOH, most notably the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, serious catalyst deactivation, and the inherent trade-off between product selectivity and carbon utilization efficiency. Then, key strategies to improve CO 2 to HCOOH conversion efficiency are systematically summarized, with a focus on stabilization of key reaction intermediates and rational engineering of the catalytic microenvironment. Additionally, effective approaches to enhance catalyst durability, as well as the design of advanced electrolyzer configurations tailored for acidic CO 2 RR systems, are elaborated. We end the review by outlining the existing challenges and future directions for accelerating the industrialization of acidic CO 2 RR to HCOOH.

10.1002/adfm.79222.title: High-Voltage Electrospinning-Assisted Defect Engineering in Oxide-Derived Cu Nanowires Enables Selective CO 2 Electroreduction Toward C 2+ Products
10.1002/adfm.79222.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical CO 2 reduction toward multicarbon (C 2+ ) products remains challenging because conventional Cu catalysts lack the ability to simultaneously optimize intermediate stabilization, proton transfer, and C─C coupling kinetics. Here we report a high-voltage electrospinning-assisted defect engineering strategy to regulate the electronic structure of Cu catalysts for selective C 2+ electrosynthesis. Defect-rich CuO nanowire precursors were fabricated by high-voltage electrospinning and subsequently reconstructed into oxide-derived Cu (OD-Cu) nanowires enriched with abundant electronically perturbed Cu sites. The resulting OD-Cu nanowires exhibit substantially enhanced C 2+ selectivity compared with conventional Cu catalysts. Mechanistic studies reveal that high-voltage electrospinning-assisted defects reorganize the reorganization of the interfacial water configuration and proton-transfer dynamics while strengthening Cu─ * CO π-backbonding interactions, thereby optimizing * CO stabilization and promoting hydrogen-assisted C─C coupling. This work establishes a direct correlation between high-voltage electrospinning-assisted defect regulation, electronic structure modulation and multicarbon formation kinetics, providing a general strategy for designing efficient Cu catalysts for selective C 2+ electrosynthesis.

10.1002/adfm.79259.title: Multifunctional Interface Modifier Enables High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79259.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide-bandgap (WBG, ≥1.68 eV) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) represent promising top-cell candidates for monolithic perovskite tandem photovoltaics. However, fast crystallization kinetics of perovskite precursors and incomplete surface coverage of hole-transporting self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) commonly degrade perovskite film quality and introduce detrimental defects at the buried interface. Herein, we report a buried-interface engineering strategy using a rationally designed dioxaboranaphthoanthracene-based modifier, which exhibits preferential accumulation at the perovskite buried interface. The results support additional interfacial coverage associated with DOBNA-3PA enrichment, while modulation of perovskite crystallization kinetics enlarges grain size and reduces residual strain, contributing to improved interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the inverted 1.68 eV PSC delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.55% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.281 V and a fill factor of 85.39%, alongside a negligible hysteresis index of 1.37%. The device retains 94% of its initial efficiency after 1800 h of storage in ambient air (40-45% relative humidity) under ISOS-D-1 testing protocols. Notably, this strategy exhibits outstanding generalizability across different perovskite bandgaps, enabling PCEs of 26.44% and 21.04% for 1.54 and 1.78 eV PSCs. This work establishes a dual-function modifier strategy for improving both perovskite bulk crystallization and buried interface modification, offering a generalizable pathway toward highly efficient and stable WBG PSCs.

10.1002/adfm.79160.title: Microfluidic Architecting of Patchy MXene Core-Shell Particles for Ultralow-Loading Photothermal Shape-Memory Actuation
10.1002/adfm.79160.abstract: ABSTRACT Shape memory polymers capable of remote actuation are promising for soft robotics, adaptive structures, and biomedical devices, yet efficient photothermal actuation remains limited by particle aggregation, localized thermal hotspots, and poor energy utilization. Here, we introduce a microfluidic architecture-engineering strategy that transforms MXene nanosheets into spatially distributed patchy core-shell particles for efficient near-infrared (NIR)-triggered actuation at ultralow loadings. Flow-focusing microfluidics assembles Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets into 7-10 nm patchy shells around polymeric cores, suppressing restacking while maximizing accessible photothermal interfaces. Incorporated into poly(L-lactic acid), these particles enable the composite to reach its glass-transition temperature within 10 s under NIR irradiation (850 nm, 1.8 W cm −2 ) at MXene loading of only 0.0024 wt%, resulting in ≈95% shape recovery within 25 s. In contrast, composites containing directly dispersed MXene exhibit localized heating and achieve only ≈63% recovery after 150 s. Combining Monte Carlo photon transport and finite-element thermal simulations, we show that the patchy-shell architecture enhances photon harvesting and volumetric heat generation by spatially distributing photothermal interfaces throughout the material. This work establishes architecture-controlled photothermal transport as a design principle for next-generation smart composites and demonstrates microfluidic engineering of functional particle architectures as a scalable route toward high-performance remotely actuated materials.

10.1002/adfm.79216.title: Coordination-Based Regulation of Integrated Photoanodes for Boosted Water Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.79216.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy-related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. Moreover, n-type semiconductors as photoanodes exhibit sluggish water oxidation kinetics. Coordination-based regulation between semiconductors and cocatalysts as a form of interface optimization in integrated photoanodes has been proved an effective strategy to optimize charge transfer and water oxidation processes. Herein, recent critical headway on improving the efficiency of semiconductor-based photoanodes for water oxidation via coordination-based regulation is reviewed. In particular, this review aims to clarify how coordination-based regulation achieves performance enhancement through the joint modulation of surface states and spin-electronic states. The mechanism of coordination-based regulation in integrated photoanodes on charge transfer and water oxidation kinetics prioritization scheme is demonstrated in detail. These benefits of coordination-based regulation for efficient and stable water splitting devices will show huge advantages in the future.

10.1002/adfm.79188.title: Bifunctional Carbon-Sensitized Hollow Heterojunctions for Dual-Mode Sensing of Emerging Contaminant 6-PPD
10.1002/adfm.79188.abstract: ABSTRACT N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6-PPD), a ubiquitous rubber tire antioxidant, poses a severe threat to ecological safety due to its pronounced ecotoxicity. This work achieves the unprecedented dual-mode photoelectrochemical and electrochemical (PEC-EC) sensing of 6-PPD through a dual-mode platform endowed with bifunctional catalytic signal amplification. Integrating a novel hollow Bi@BiOBr/CdLa 2 S 4 heterojunction with multiwalled carbon nanotubes, this dual-mode platform delivers highly stable, efficiently amplified signals. It demonstrates exceptional sensing performance with remarkably broad linear ranges from 1 to 10000 nM for PEC and 1 to 20000 nM for EC. By coupling Kelvin probe force microscopy and density functional theory with comprehensive characterizations, the intrinsic sensing mechanisms, specifically the charge transfer pathways and catalytic adsorption preferences, are systematically elucidated. Crucially, this dual-signal cross-validation ensures reliable quantification in complex real-world matrices, and portable on-site analysis is achieved via smartphone Bluetooth integration. Ultimately, by synergizing advanced heterojunction engineering with a dual-mode sensing strategy, this work establishes a robust and highly efficient methodology for emerging contaminant monitoring with exceptional application prospects.

10.1002/adfm.78860.title: Scalable Interfacial Engineering of Covalently Interlocked Hierarchical CNT/Phase Change Composite for Multifunctional Thermal Management and EMI Shielding
10.1002/adfm.78860.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon nanotube (CNT)-based hierarchical architectures offer a promising platform for engineering multifunctional materials with synergistic thermal, electrical, and optical properties. However, weak interfacial coupling between CNTs and growth substrates compromises structural robustness, hindering practical implementation. Here, a scalable dual-silanization-assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy is developed to construct a covalently bonded organosilica interlayer, thereby creating a robust interlocked CF@CNTs hierarchical architecture. Experiments and density functional theory calculations reveal that interlayer enhances charge transfer and interfacial binding strength, suppressing CNT detachment. Leveraging this robust architecture, we fabricated a multifunctional phase change composite (PCC) that effectively resolves the inherent trade-off between latent heat storage and thermal/electrical transport. The resulting PCC maintains a high latent heat of 210.17 J·g −1 while delivering a thermal conductivity of 0.760 W·m −1 ·K −1 and an electrical conductivity of 802.56 S·m −1 . Consequently, it lowers electronic device operating temperatures by 9°C, achieves an average total shielding effectiveness of 41.51 dB·mm −1 , and reaches a photothermal conversion efficiency of 93.36%. Notably, this interfacial engineering strategy is readily extendable to 0D, 1D, 2D, and 3D substrates, enabling scalable integration of CNT-based architectures. This work establishes interfacial coupling engineering as a versatile design principle for constructing robust CNT-based architectures, opening new opportunities for multifunctional materials.

10.1002/adfm.79033.title: Sacrificing Initial Active Area for Superior Structural and Interfacial Stability in MoSe 2 /C Anodes for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79033.abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion-type materials for all-solid-state lithium batteries face low conductivity, sluggish kinetics, severe volume expansion, and unstable interfaces. Herein, a MoSe 2 /C composite is fabricated via a wet-chemical synthesis approach combined with shell engineering. Density functional theory calculations show that the carbon skeleton enhances conductivity, improves Li + adsorption, and lowers the diffusion barrier. In situ and finite element analyses confirm that the hollow carbon mitigates volume expansion and redistributes stress. Distribution of relaxation times analysis reveals that stress buffering suppresses interfacial degradation and enhances Li + migration. Pseudocapacitive analysis shows a slightly higher contribution for pristine MoSe 2 due to face-to-face stacking versus point-contact packing in MoSe 2 /C, which sacrifices some initial active area. However, the carbon skeleton accelerates the kinetics of the remaining active regions and provides excellent stress buffering and interfacial stability. Consequently, the MoSe 2 /C anode exhibits rate capability and long-term cycling performance in both half-cells (11 000 cycles at 3 A g −1 ) and full-cells (200 cycles at 0.1 C). This work proposes a counterintuitive strategy of “trading part of the initial active area in exchange for superior structural and interfacial stability,” offering a rational design paradigm for conversion-type materials.

10.1002/adfm.79106.title: Two-Dimensional Few-Layer Selenides: From Materials to Applications
10.1002/adfm.79106.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) few-layer selenides attract much attention due to their unique electronic structures and layer-dependent properties, which differ markedly from those of bulk layered selenides. Especially some transition metal diselenides, which undergo a transition from an indirect bandgap to a direct bandgap with reduced layer number, can meet the specific requirements of high-performance optoelectronic devices. However, the stable, controllable, and large-scale synthesis of few-layer selenides remains a key bottleneck limiting their development. Furthermore, employing strategies such as edge engineering, heterostructure construction, and phase engineering to regulate their properties is equally important for maximizing their application value. Herein, the structural characteristics and layer-dependent properties of various 2D few-layer selenides are systematically introduced. Both top-down and bottom-up synthesis methods are emphasized. The relationship between the properties of 2D few-layer selenides and their applications in energy storage, electronics, optoelectronics, thermoelectricity, and catalysis is revealed. Recent developments and potential directions for future research are discussed. This comprehensive review is expected to advance theoretical research on 2D few-layer selenides and provide insightful guidance for their future functionalization and large-scale applications.

10.1002/adfm.79183.title: Energy-Autonomous Janus Nanofibrous Textile for Sustainable Bi-Directional Thermal Management and Self-Powered Wearable Electronics
10.1002/adfm.79183.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving energy autonomy and zero-energy bidirectional personal thermal management (PTM) in wearable electronics remains a formidable challenge. Here, we fabricate an energy-autonomous Janus PS@PT textile via a multifunctional synergistic filler strategy, integrating alkyl-chain-modified silica and photothermal nanoparticles into poly(vinylidene fluoride- co -hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP), denoted as PS and PT, respectively. This strategy yields synergistic effects: the fillers act as PTM enhancers for adaptive regulation, as dielectric modifiers increasing the β -phase content, and as charge trap centers strengthening interfacial polarization, raising the dielectric constant to 1.27 times that of pristine PVDF-HFP. Under 1000 W/m 2 irradiation, the PS layer achieves radiative cooling of ∼2.7°C (net cooling power 97.1 W/m 2 ) with 95.3% solar reflectance and 92.2% MIR emissivity, while the PT layer delivers solar heating of ∼12.9°C (net heating power 260.43 W/m 2 ) with 49.9% solar absorptance. Significantly, the functional fillers substantially optimize the dielectric properties and charge-trapping capability, effectively suppressing high-temperature performance degradation. At 85°C, the output voltages of PT and PS show enhancements of 159.7% and 144.9% relative to room-temperature values. This work establishes a new paradigm for synergistically enhancing PTM capability and stable triboelectric output in a single device, offering a promising pathway toward multifunctional integration in smart textiles.

10.1002/adfm.79133.title: High-Pressure and High-Temperature Co-Engineering of Dislocations and Chemical Short-Range Order Mitigates the Strength-Ductility-Corrosion Trade-Off in CoCrNi Medium-Entropy Alloy
10.1002/adfm.79133.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional processing makes it difficult to develop chemical short-range order (CSRO) while retaining a high dislocation density in CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy. Annealing promotes local ordering but accelerates dislocation recovery, whereas deformation introduces dislocations without producing a comparable ordered state. Here, high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) treatment at 5 GPa and 600°C for 2 h yields 1.3 ± 0.3 nm CSRO domains (projected area fraction, 26.9 ± 3.2%) and a dislocation density of (6.8 ± 0.3) × 10 13 m −2 without appreciable grain-size change. First-principles calculations show that pressure favors the ordered configuration through a negative ordering volume and raises vacancy formation enthalpy, limiting recovery. This architecture raises yield strength from 326 to 537 MPa and ultimate tensile strength from 800 to 880 MPa while retaining ∼72% elongation. Dislocations dominate the initial strengthening, while nanotwinning, microband formation, and deformation-induced phase transformation develop within the HPHT-induced dislocation-CSRO architecture. The same architecture also accelerates Cr-dominated primary passivation in 0.1 m H 2 SO 4 , reducing passive current density from 9.55 to 1.50 µA/cm 2 . Surface-sensitive analyses reveal a higher oxide-like Cr 3+ /hydroxide-like Cr 3+ ratio and faster development of interconnected Cr─O-rich regions. These results establish a pressure-regulated defect-engineering route integrating strengthening, sustained plasticity, and improved primary passivation.

10.1002/adfm.79256.title: A Precursor Doping Source Layer Engineering to Suppress Antisite Defects Enabling High Efficiency in Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 Solar Cell
10.1002/adfm.79256.abstract: ABSTRACT Pure-sulfide kesterite Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 (CZTS) is an attractive photovoltaic absorber, but its efficiency is largely constrained by antisite defects (e.g., Cu Zn ) and the associated band-tail-induced carrier losses. Here, we develop a precursor doping source layer (PDSL) engineering, in which an ultrathin CdS layer deposited on the porous CZTS precursor surface serves as an active Cd dopant during sulfurization. Different from conventional Cd cation doping, this localized PDSL targeted releases dopant during CZTS absorber formation, enabling Cd incorporation to be coupled with thermodynamics of phase evolution and kinetics of grain coalescence. Such reaction-coupled Cd delivery stabilizes Zn-site occupation and weakens Cu/Zn interchange, thereby mitigating Cu Zn -dominated defect responses and disorder-induced band tails. As a result, trap-assisted recombination and energetic fluctuations are reduced, leading to improved carrier transport and collection. The obtained pure-sulfide CZTS/ZTO photovoltaic device delivers an efficiency of 12.23% and a large-area (1.00 cm 2 ) efficiency of 10.31%, reaching the leading level of efficiency reported for non-alloyed pure-sulfide kesterite thin-film solar cells. This work highlights PDSL design as an effective approach for overcoming defect-limited performance in kesterite photovoltaics.

10.1002/adfm.79139.title: Unleashing Multi-Electron Storage in Synergistic Dual-Active-Center Bridged Covalent Organic Polymer Cathode for High-Capacity and Long-Life Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79139.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of aqueous zinc-ion batteries is hindered by the scarcity of advanced cathode materials. Covalent organic polymers (COPs) have garnered substantial interest due to their tunable structures. However, simultaneously achieving high capacity and structural stability remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we propose an active dual-unit bridging strategy to construct an extended conjugated framework, enabling high specific capacity and structural stability. This bridging design integrates six-electron-storage hexaazatrinaphthalene (HAT) and redox-active 2,5-dihydroxy-1,4-benzoquinone (DHBQ) units, departing from the disadvantage that conventional strategies only rely on inactive linkers. Theoretical calculations and spectroscopic analyses elucidate a cascaded Zn 2+ storage pathway characterized by the preferential reaction of HAT sites, followed by subsequent participation of the benzoquinone moieties. Electrochemical evaluations of the HAT-DHBQ cathode reveal a high initial capacity of 316.2 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , along with impressive cycling stability, as evidenced by maintaining discharge capacities of 190.3 mAh g −1 and 147.0 mAh g −1 after 10 000 cycles at 1.0 A g −1 and 5.0 A g −1 , corresponding to low-capacity attenuation rates of 0.0029% and 0.0030% per cycle, respectively. By synergistically integrating multi-electron-storage units through an active-bridging strategy, this work establishes a promising molecular design paradigm for high-performance organic active materials in aqueous multivalent-ion secondary batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78770.title: Decoupling Li + Transport in Self-Healing Polymer Dual-Salt Electrolytes for Room Temperature Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78770.abstract: ABSTRACT Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) stand as leading candidates for advancing high-energy-density lithium metal batteries toward next-generation applications. However, the inherent crystallinity of conventional polymer matrices severely limits ionic conductivity (IC) and Li + transference number (t Li + ), while imposing large interfacial resistance and uncontrollable lithium dendrite growth-critical bottlenecks hindering practical room-temperature application. Herein, we report a dual-salt incorporation strategy within a self-curing polymer framework to overcome these challenges. The anion-anion interactions of the dual-salt system within the polymer network immobilize the anions, thereby liberating a greater number Li + ions. Additionally, the salt-polymer interactions alter the polymer energy levels, cooperatively enhancing the IC to 2.23 mS cm −1 and the t Li + to 0.55. The electrolyte sustains stable Li||Li symmetric cycling for over 2000 h. When integrated with a LiFePO 4 cathode, the full cell delivers 133 mAh g 1 at 1C with 75% capacity retention over 700 cycles, while the NMC811||Li cell achieves 135 mAh g −1 , retaining 72% of its initial capacity over 250 cycles. Additionally, the electrolyte exhibits inherent flame retardancy and uniform Li + plating-stripping, effectively suppressing dendrite penetration. This design strategy provides a viable route to ambient-temperature, self-curing GPEs that enhance battery safety and suppress dead lithium.

10.1002/adfm.77698.title: A Biodegradable and Tough Piezoelectric Silk Fibroin Fiber
10.1002/adfm.77698.abstract: ABSTRACT Biodegradable piezoelectric implants are optimal platforms for transient biosensing and therapeutics. However, limited piezoelectric properties and toughness impede the deployment of biodegradable piezoelectric implants in dynamic tissues and organs. In this study, we have developed silk fibroin (SF) fibers with high piezoelectricity and toughness via a microfluidic spinning method and post-treatment via dynamic salting-out (DSO). The optimized SF-DSO fibers exhibited remarkable mechanical properties (fracture strain: 45.58%, toughness: 115.03 MJ/m 3 ) and enhanced piezoelectric performance ( d 33, eff = 26.51 pC/N). Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and two-dimensional wide-angle X-ray scattering (2D-WAXS) analyses revealed increased β-sheet content and molecular alignment, correlating with improved properties. The fibers also showed excellent cytocompatibility and biodegradability, confirmed by in vitro and in vivo evaluations. Piezoelectric films based on SF-DSO fibers provided stable electrical outputs and were successfully used for in vivo applications, including respiratory monitoring, muscle motion detection, and ultrasound-driven energy harvesting in rats. The regenerated SF-DSO fibers prepared in this study offer a promising option for next-generation biodegradable piezoelectric implants.

10.1002/adfm.78387.title: Room-Temperature Spontaneous Topological (Anti)Merons Induced by Magnetoelastic Coupling
10.1002/adfm.78387.abstract: ABSTRACT Topologically protected magnetic (anti)merons have garnered widespread attention owing to their promising potential use as long-range information carriers in spintronic devices. However, (anti)merons usually emerge only within a narrow temperature range below room temperature and/or under an external magnetic field, hindering the development of such applications. Here, we report the direct observation of spontaneous isolated (anti)meron pairs and (anti)meron chains without the need for external magnetic fields over a wide temperature range across room temperature (313-80 K) in a Fe 2 P-type Mn-Fe-P-Si material with easy-plane magnetic anisotropy. Spontaneous isolated (anti)meron pairs are induced by a magnetoelastic transition from a paramagnetic to ferromagnetic state and subsequently evolve into (anti)meron chains upon cooling. These spontaneous (anti)merons exhibit distinct processes of creation, movement, and annihilation in response to variations in temperature and magnetic field, demonstrating their controllability. Through a combination of first-principles calculations, neutron powder diffraction, and micromagnetic simulations, we reveal that easy-plane magnetic anisotropy plays a pivotal role in the spontaneous generation and stabilization of topological (anti)merons in this system. Our findings provide an alternative way to generate spontaneous topological spin textures utilizing easy-plane magnetic anisotropy and magnetoelastic transition, and establish magnetoelastic coupling materials as a versatile platform for future spintronics devices.

10.1002/adfm.78260.title: Melt-Intercalated Montmorillonite Composite Electrolytes Enabling Interlayer-Interface Dual Conduction Networks for Stable Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78260.abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish ion transport kinetics within solid-state electrolytes and the consequent heterogeneous lithium deposition represent core bottlenecks impeding high-energy-density lithium metal batteries. Such uneven deposition originates from restricted ion transport networks and fragile contact at electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Constructing long-range continuous fast ion transport networks effectively regulates microscopic ion flux, enabling uniform lithium plating/stripping. Herein, we propose an innovative solvent-free melt coordination intercalation strategy, combined with electrospinning and in-situ thermal polymerization, to construct composite solid electrolytes featuring dual-ion conduction channels using 2D layered montmorillonite as the functional skeleton. The highly conductive interlayer confinement transport channels of montmorillonite and the continuous montmorillonite/polymer amorphous interfaces synergistically constitute interconnected “interlayer-interface” dual-conduction networks for Li + . Consequently, the resulting electrolyte exhibits a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 1.6 mS·cm −1 and an outstanding Li + transference number of 0.68. Meanwhile, uniform ion transmission across the electrode/electrolyte interface is guaranteed. The Li||Li symmetric cells demonstrate long stable cycling of over 6000 h at 0.1 ‍mA·cm −1 . Furthermore, LiFePO 4 ||Li full cells retain ∼70% of their initial capacity after 3000 cycles at 2 C rate. This work simultaneously achieves efficient ion transport and enhanced interfacial stability, providing a promising avenue for high-performance solid-state lithium metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78381.title: A Redox-Responsive Nano-Immune Coupling Strategy Enables Synergistic Pathogen Eradication and Host Resistance Activation Against Bacterial Wilt
10.1002/adfm.78381.abstract: ABSTRACT Here, we develop a redox-responsive nano-immune coupling strategy for synergistic control of tomato bacterial wilt. The CuO@MON nanocomposite consists of copper oxide nanoparticles embedded within glutathione-responsive mesoporous organosilica (MON), enabling selective disassembly in the thiol-rich bacterial microenvironment. Under in vitro conditions, Ralstonia solanacearum was treated with CuO@MON at concentrations ranging from 0 to 500 mg/L for 24 h, with CuO, MON, and zhongshengmycin as controls. CuO@MON exhibited concentration-dependent antibacterial activity and higher efficacy than CuO alone, with an EC 50 value of 96.96 mg/L. Mechanistic analyses showed that CuO@MON enhanced intracellular ROS generation (2.054 ± 0.098-fold increase), promoted glutathione depletion, and induced membrane damage and genomic DNA degradation in R. solanacearum . In tomato plants, CuO@MON treatment (250 mg/L) reduced stem colonization by R. solanacearum by 84.0% after 4 days of inoculation compared with infected controls, while zhongshengmycin achieved a 94.9% reduction as a conventional positive control. Moreover, CuO@MON enhanced defense-related responses, increasing PR-1 expression from 400 ± 96-fold to 533 ± 140-fold and PR-5 expression from 340 ± 50-fold to 807 ± 121-fold relative to healthy controls. Collectively, CuO@MON integrates pathogen suppression with host defense activation, providing a nano-immune coupling strategy for sustainable bacterial disease management.

10.1002/adfm.78384.title: A Self-Assembled Zincophobic/Zincophilic Bilayer Interphase from a Hydrated Eutectic Electrolyte for Dendrite-Free Zn Metal Anodes
10.1002/adfm.78384.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Zn batteries are promising for safe and low-cost large-scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is hindered by severe Zn anode instability arising from coupled hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and dendritic electrodeposition, particularly under temperature extremes. Here we report a solvation-interphase coupled strategy enabled by a hydrated eutectic electrolyte formulated from zinc trifluoromethanesulfonate (Zn(OTf) 2 ), ethylene glycol (EG), and an SnF 2 additive (optimized as ZOTF-16/SF30), which delivers stable Zn electrochemistry over an exceptionally wide temperature window from −40°C to 60°C. Spectroscopic and physicochemical analyses reveal that EG confines H 2 O within a reinforced hydrogen-bond network and reconstructs the Zn 2+ coordination environment, thereby suppressing active-water reactivity and mitigating hydrogen evolution and corrosion. Concurrently, SnF 2 programs interfacial chemistry to generate an in situ zincophobic/zincophilic bilayer interphase, wherein the zincophobic component blocks water penetration and parasitic reactions while the zincophilic component homogenizes Zn 2+ flux and nucleation, enforcing uniform Zn deposition and dendrite-free growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit ultrastable cycling for over 2400 h at 1 mA cm −2 . Moreover, Zn||I 2 full cells deliver remarkable long-term durability over 120 000 cycles, sustaining extended lifetimes at 60°C and −40°C. This work establishes a practical electrolyte-interphase co-design blueprint for climate-resilient aqueous Zn batteries, highlighting hydrated eutectic chemistry as a versatile platform for stabilizing reactive metal anodes.

10.1002/adfm.78380.title: Breaking the Diffusion-Limited Aggregation for Ordered Zn Deposition via Interfacial Structure-Directing Engineering
10.1002/adfm.78380.abstract: ABSTRACT Uncontrolled dendrite growth during zinc plating/stripping hinders the practical application of aqueous zinc metal batteries in energy storage systems. In this study, the classical diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) theory was employed to understand the mechanisms of zinc dendritic growth fundamentally and then to guide the design of interfacial structure-directing engineering. [EMIm]EtSO 4 ionic liquid as a structure-directing agent was developed to successfully overcome the disordered Zn dendrite growth following the rules of “random motion” and “contact-stick”. Comprehensive characterizations suggest that EMIm + cations guide the interfacial ordering process by building a buffer layer and a hydrophobic barrier on the Zn anode, while EtSO 4 − anions orchestrate the reconstruction of the Zn 2+ solvation structure. This synergistic regulation transforms zinc deposition morphology from stochastic fractal growth to highly ordered epitaxial growth. As a result, the zinc anode achieves 99.3% Coulombic efficiency at 1 mA cm −2 and stable cycling over 2000 h. It further endows the Zn||NVO battery with significantly improved stability and anti freezing performance (−40°C). This work demonstrates an interfacial engineering strategy that effectively suppresses DLA-type dendritic growth, providing a new perspective for high-performance aqueous zinc batteries.
authors: Qiong Sun, Weijia Zhang, Min Cheng, Xuexue Li, Mengyao Shi, Tianjiang Sun, Zhanliang Tao

10.1002/adfm.78302.title: High-Yield Aerosol CVD Synthesis of High-Quality Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes via Control of Nanotube Structure
10.1002/adfm.78302.abstract: ABSTRACT Aerosol chemical vapor deposition (CVD), a variant of floating catalyst CVD, enables one-step, solvent-free, and scalable production of high-quality single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) films for next-generation electronics, photonics, and optoelectronics. However, simultaneously achieving high production yield and superior film conductivity remains an unsolved challenge, as conventional approaches to boost yield inevitably promote nanotube bundling and degrade performance. Here, the mechanistic origin of this yield-performance trade-off is investigated through precise control of nanotube structural parameters during synthesis. Systematic investigation identifies nanotube diameter as the most influential structural parameter for balancing production yield and film conductivity within the broad parameter space explored: large-diameter SWCNTs not only form lower-resistance junctions but also tend to suppress bundling during aerosol-state growth, thereby indirectly enhancing film conductivity while simultaneously facilitating higher yield. Bundle length and crystallinity also contribute positively, although their influence is less pronounced. Consequently, SWCNT-predominant films (>55%) comprising large-diameter nanotubes (∼2.4 nm) are synthesized, achieving an unprecedented yield-to-sheet-resistance ratio at 90% transparency of 4.7 mm 2 L −1 (Ω □ −1 ) −1 after doping-an order of magnitude higher than previously reported values for SWCNT films. This work establishes fundamental structure-property-yield relationships and provides a rational design strategy for scalable production of high-performance SWCNT films.

10.1002/adfm.78142.title: Embedded Direct Ink Writing of Thermoset and Elastomeric Polymers via Frontal Polymerization
10.1002/adfm.78142.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct ink writing (DIW) using frontal ring-opening metathesis polymerization (FROMP) enables rapid, energy-efficient fabrication of thermoset and elastomeric architectures through a self-propagating exothermic curing reaction. However, FP-DIW is constrained by stringent rheological requirements, feature-size limits from front quenching, and the need for the reaction front to track the nozzle. Here, we overcome these constraints by leveraging embedded 3D printing to implement FP-DIW with delayed solidification, thereby decoupling shape retention and solidification from ink chemistry and rheology. A yield-stress support medium stabilizes low-viscosity inks, suppresses gravitational and capillary instabilities, mitigates quenching at small diameters, and enables complex overlapping and mechanically interlinked features to fuse after deposition. Two thermal initiation strategies are introduced: volumetric dielectric heating via microwaves and surface heating at the support-bath boundary. Dicyclopentadiene (DCPD), cyclooctadiene (COD), and mixed formulations provide tunable mechanical properties with glass transition temperatures from -50°C to 160°C. The approach enables lattices, springs, mechanically interlocked structures, and multimaterial architectures, substantially expanding the accessible material, feature-size, and geometric design space compared with FP-DIW in air.

10.1002/adfm.78383.title: NIR-Responsive CaMoO4/Mo3N2 Heterojunction Modified Biomimetic Periosteum: Synergistic Anti-Infection and Promotion of Bone Defect Repair
10.1002/adfm.78383.abstract: ABSTRACT Treating infected bone defects remains a formidable clinical challenge due to robust bacterial antioxidant resistance and severe microenvironmental deterioration. Herein, an antibacterial biomimetic periosteum (ABP) is rationally engineered by in situ anchoring ultrasmall CaMoO 4 /Mo 3 N 2 heterojunctions onto a porous bioactive glass fiber membrane (CMO/MN) via a sol-gel electrospinning and nitridation strategy. These hierarchical ABPs transform passive bone implants into active metabolic modulators. Under near-infrared irradiation, the CaMoO 4 /Mo 3 N 2 engine initiates localized hyperthermia alongside a sophisticated multienzyme cascade. Specifically, peroxidase-like activity generates a wide range of highly toxic reactive oxygen species, while intrinsic glutathione oxidase and L-cysteine oxidase activities persistently deplete bacterial antioxidants, effectively dismantling fundamental oxidative defenses. In addition, catalase-like activity continuously decomposes endogenous H 2 O 2 into O 2 , mitigating localized tissue hypoxia and inflammatory oxidative stress. Furthermore, this biomimetic three-dimensional fiber network achieves a powerful osteogenic induction effect by continuously releasing therapeutic calcium ions and silicate ions. In vitro experiments have confirmed the excellent biocompatibility of ABPs and their ability to promote the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, while simultaneously exhibiting potent bactericidal activity against bacteria. Consistently, ABPs have also demonstrated superior therapeutic performance in the treatment of both uncomplicated bone defects and infection-compromised bone defects.

10.1002/adfm.78303.title: Oligoethylene Glycol Side-Chain Engineering of Y6-Derived Nonfullerene Acceptors for Thermally Induced Spontaneous Pseudo-Planar Heterojunction Organic Photodetectors
10.1002/adfm.78303.abstract: ABSTRACT Dark current density ( J D ) fundamentally limits the noise characteristics and detectivity of organic photodetectors (OPDs), arising primarily from reverse-bias carrier injection and trap-mediated leakage pathways in donor-acceptor (D-A) bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) active layers. Although pseudo-planar heterojunction ( p -PHJ) architectures effectively suppress these losses, their implementation often requires complex layer engineering or controlled processing conditions. Here, we report two Y6-derived nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs), YTEG-4F and YTEG-4Cl, bearing hydrophilic oligoethylene glycol (OEG) side chains that induce thermally driven spontaneous vertical phase separation within the D-A BHJ layer. This molecular modification enables p-PHJ formation, suppressing reverse-bias carrier injection and leakage pathways, thereby reducing J D . In contrast to the thermally annealed PM6:Y6 device, which exhibits an increased J D of 6.64 × 10 −7 A cm −2 , the PM6:YTEG-4F and PM6:YTEG-4Cl devices achieve low J D s of 2.76 × 10 −9 and 3.24 × 10 −9 A cm −2 , corresponding to approximately 260-fold and 210-fold reductions after thermal annealing, respectively. Consequently, shot-noise-limited detectivities ( D sh *) of 1.17 × 10 13 and 9.74 × 10 12 Jones are achieved at −0.5 V for PM6:YTEG-4F and PM6:YTEG-4Cl p -PHJ OPDs, respectively. This work demonstrates that OEG side-chain engineering of NFAs provides a broadly applicable molecular strategy for inducing p -PHJ architectures and regulating J D toward high-performance OPDs.

10.1002/adfm.78140.title: Bio-Inspired Spatial Encoding in Cellulose-Based Electroluminescent Textiles for Real-Time Gas Leak Localization
10.1002/adfm.78140.abstract: ABSTRACT Spatially resolved electroluminescent (EL) textiles are highly desirable for flexible hazard detection, yet conventional systems limit real-time localization of dynamic stimuli. Inspired by insect olfaction, where spatial information emerges from distributed sensing and spatiotemporal signal differences, we report a cellulose-based EL sensing textile for real-time gas leak localization via material-architecture-governed spatial encoding. Plant-derived cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) serve as fundamental building blocks, organizing functional components through blending or surface modification and being assembled via wet-spinning into continuous fibers with hierarchical porosity, flexibility, and volumetric stimulus accessibility essential for rapid gas sensing. Conductive fibers are fabricated through in situ polymerization of polyaniline (PANI) on CNF surfaces, enabling reversible, gas-responsive electrical modulation with detection limits of 1 ppm for HCl and 3.6 ppm for NH 3 . Coaxial electroluminescent fibers comprising a PANI@CNF conductive core and ZnS-embedded CNF shell provide stable light emission over 100 h of continuous operation. Intersections between these fibers form self-defined units that translate localized gas exposure into spatiotemporally resolved EL patterns, mapping propagation pathways with a naked-eye detection threshold of 100 ppm, while maintaining stable emission after washing and bending. This work establishes a bio-inspired, architecture-driven strategy for smart textiles, highlighting cellulose-based nanocomposites as key components for next-generation smart technologies.
authors: Yuying Kong, Xiaoting Zhao, Hui Mao, Zihuan Zhang, Junqi Gao, Jiamin Liu, Wen-Jun Wang, Tiffany Abitbol, Xuan Yang

10.1002/adfm.78343.title: Suture-Inspired Interlocking Metamaterials for Energy-Efficient Morphing
10.1002/adfm.78343.abstract: ABSTRACT Morphing metamaterials enable programmable shape changes for soft robotics and wearable systems, but intrinsic softness limits load-bearing capacity and robustness. Architected particle assemblies connect discrete rigid particles with tendons, enabling compliance and active assembly into stiff, load-bearing configurations. However, they require continuous energy input or external confinement to maintain morphed states, reducing efficiency and reliability. Here, we introduce a bistable interlocking joint inspired by natural sutures for architected particle-based metamaterials that enable “move-and-hold” functionality. Once assembled, these joints allow structures to retain their configuration without sustained actuation while achieving load-bearing capacity exceeding 60 times their own weight. To achieve this, we first develop computational algorithms to tessellate arbitrary 3D surfaces into particles with interlocking joints. Experiments and FEM simulations reveal how joint geometry influences interlocking strength, actuation force, and bending performance. Tendon-driven assemblies demonstrate low-force morphing, stable load-bearing capacity without continuous energy input or external confinement, and adaptability to complex 3D geometries. As applications, we showcase a proof-of-concept foldable impact-attenuation helmet that combines compact folded volume with impact attenuation under tested conditions, and further extend the concept to reconfigurable wearable devices, highlighting the potential of particle-based architectures for protective and rehabilitation applications.
authors: Yu Chen, Xudong Yang, Junwei Li, Tianyu Chen, Yuzhe Wang, Yifan Wang

10.1002/adfm.78232.title: Self-Trapped Exciton Regulation in a Copper-Iodide Hybrid for Flexible X-Ray Scintillation Imaging and Optical Encryption
10.1002/adfm.78232.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling self-trapped excitons (STEs) provides a promising strategy for achieving tunable photoluminescence (PL) in metal halides, but realizing multiple STEs in a single-component system remains challenging. Herein, we report a Cu(I) halide hybrid scintillator, [(C 4 H 16 N 3 )·H 2 PO 2 ]CuI 3 , exhibiting excitation-dependent dual emission, reversible thermochromic luminescence, and superior x-ray scintillation performance. This emission behavior originates from two competing STEs whose relative populations are modulated by the excitation wavelength, temperature, and local lattice distortion. The high-energy cyan and low-energy yellow emissions originate from two distinct STE configurations associated with different local distortions and Cu···Cu interactions, enabling temperature-dependent color tuning through STE population redistribution. The high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) also endow [(C 4 H 16 N 3 )·H 2 PO 2 ]CuI 3 with strong radioluminescence, an estimated light yield of 34 353 photons MeV −1 , and a low detection limit of 371 nGy air s −1 . Incorporating the crystals into a SEBS matrix produces a large-area and highly flexible [(C 4 H 16 N 3 )·H 2 PO 2 ]CuI 3 @SEBS composite scintillation film for x-ray imaging, achieving a spatial resolution of 14.25 lp·mm −1 . The abundant photophysical properties highlight the multiple optoelectronic applications of [(C 4 H 16 N 3 )·H 2 PO 2 ]CuI 3 in x-ray imaging, anti-counterfeiting, and secure communication.
authors: Chenyang Zhang, Yuexiao Pan, Hongzhou Lian, Jun Lin, Wenxia Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78395.title: Boosting Energy Storage of AgNbO3-Based Capacitors by Constructing Low-Atomic-Displacement Region and M2-M3 Two-Phase Coexistence Strategy
10.1002/adfm.78395.abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric capacitors with excellent energy-storage performance are highly desirable for next-generation advanced high/pulsed power capacitors that require miniaturization and integration. However, the low energy-storage density arising from insufficient breakdown strength (BDS), inadequate maximum polarization ( P max ), and large remanent polarization ( P r ), remains a critical challenge for the practical application of dielectric capacitors. Herein, we propose a strategy to synergistically incorporate the M 2 -M 3 two-phase coexistence and low-atomic-displacement (LAD) region into the AgNbO 3 system, thereby achieving high BDS, large P max and extremely low P r simultaneously. Ultrahigh U rec ∼ 17.1 J·cm −3 , excellent η ∼ 89% are achieved in the (Ag 1-3 x Eu x )(Nb 0.7 Ta 0.3 )O 3 (Eu x ANT) multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) at x = 0.03, representing a breakthrough in the overall energy-storage performance of lead-free antiferroelectric (AFE) capacitors. This study not only develops a promising high-performance lead-free energy-storage dielectric, but also offers a novel microstructural design strategy for the synergistic optimization of multiple energy-storage parameters to improve the energy storage performance of AFE system.
authors: Jiaze Li, Ting Tang, Enqi Li, Yongjian Liu, Qi Wang, Bo-Ping Zhang, Li-Feng Zhu

10.1002/adfm.78385.title: Striated Core-Sheath Fibers for Constructing Breathable Intelligent Fabrics With Multiple X-Ray Shielding and Strain-Pressure Sensing
10.1002/adfm.78385.abstract: ABSTRACT The extensive use of medical X-rays increases chronic radiation exposure risks for medical staff and patients. Traditional lead-based materials present low shielding efficiency at 20-100 keV, along with high weight, stiffness, poor flexibility, toxicity, and single functionality, limiting their wearable applications. Herein, hierarchical striated Bi 2 O 3 /WC/TPU@MXene/TPU (BWMT) core-sheath fibers are fabricated via coaxial wet-spinning. The tightly bonded core-sheath structure maintains superior radiation shielding and mechanical performances, delivering a high strain sensing range (296%) and ultrahigh sensitivity (2.9 × 10 4 ). The striated sheath enables a sensitive piezoresistive response (10.67 kPa −1 ) after helical twisting. Woven BWMT multilayer fabrics achieve 51.84%-94.23% X-ray attenuation at 20-100 keV, while possessing low density (1.06 g cm −3 ), superior stretchability (>800%), air permeability (>37 mm s −1 ), waterproofness, and thermal conductivity. This multifunctional fabric integrates radiation shielding and wearable sensing, promising advanced clinical protective wearable devices.
authors: Shasha Wang, Liqi Zhou, Wenxin Li, Fengkai Zhou, Jian Zhang, Mengqi Shan, Ruolan Deng, Leqian Wei, Wei Li, Zeyu Wang, Meiqi Hu, Guoping Guan, Fujun Wang, Lu Wang, Jifu Mao

10.1002/adfm.78388.title: Halogen-Regulated Luminescent Silver(I) Halide Complexes and the Gel Scintillation Screen for X-Ray Imaging
10.1002/adfm.78388.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide scintillators have attracted continuously increasing interest for low-dose and high-resolution X-ray imaging, yet typical luminescent silver halides suffer from severe hygroscopicity and exciton quenching caused by Ag-Ag cluster aggregation. To address these challenges, we design and report mononuclear five-coordinate silver(I) halide complexes (dppb) 2 AgX·DMSO (X = I, Br, Cl) with 1,2-Bis(diphenylphosphino)benzene (dppb) ligand. Halogen substitution enables tunable broadband emission, while the chloride analogue achieves efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and a high PLQY of 76%. The chloride analogue possesses more rigid AgClP 4 coordination environment compared with its bromide and iodide counterparts, enabling restricts excited-state relaxation, suppresses non-radiative decay, and preserves favorable singlet-triplet energetics and spin-orbit coupling. Meanwhile, the chloride analogue shows superior scintillation with a high light yield of 26631 photons/MeV, and a detection limit of 304.67 nGy air s −1 . Furthermore, a high spatial resolution of 20.2 lp mm −1 for X-ray imaging is achieved based on the transparent Ag-Cl composite gel scintillator screen. This work not only provides a promising design principle for achieving high scintillation in TADF-type Ag(I) halide complexes by halogen regulation, but also provide a new platform for Ag(I) halide complexes in X-ray imaging.
authors: Xuefei He, Kai Han, Lihan Chen, Liang Li, Yongsheng Sun, Maxim Molokeev, Binbin Su, Zhiguo Xia

10.1002/adfm.78351.title: Heavy-Atom-Engineered Conjugated Polymer Enables Thermosensitized Synergistic Cancer Phototherapy
10.1002/adfm.78351.abstract: ABSTRACT Conjugated polymer-based phototheranostics have attracted considerable attention for cancer treatment owing to their excellent photothermal properties and biocompatibility. However, integrating efficient photodynamic activity into conjugated polymer systems without compromising their intrinsic photothermal performance remains a major challenge. Here, we report structurally engineered selenophene-doped polypyrrole nanoplatforms (Ppy-PSe NPs) for imaging-guided synergistic phototherapy. Incorporation of selenium-containing heterocycles into the conjugated polypyrrole framework introduces a pronounced heavy-atom effect, which promotes intersystem crossing and substantially enhances reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation while preserving broadband near-infrared (NIR) absorption and efficient photothermal conversion. Upon NIR laser irradiation, Ppy-PSe induces severe oxidative stress, lysosomal disruption, cytoskeletal collapse, and apoptotic cell death. Mechanistically, ROS-mediated suppression of HSP90 disrupts the oncogenic JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis, thereby reprogramming tumor thermotolerance and sensitizing malignant cells to photothermal injury. In vivo, Ppy-PSe exhibits favorable biosafety, efficient tumor accumulation, and robust photoacoustic imaging capability for real-time therapeutic guidance. Notably, NIR-triggered treatment achieves complete tumor eradication in a lymphoma xenograft model, particularly under NIR-II irradiation. This work establishes a multifunctional conjugated polymer nanoplatform that integrates ROS amplification, thermo-sensitization reprogramming, and imaging-guided synergistic phototherapy for precision cancer treatment.
authors: Xiangmei Wen, Meng Chen, Xueyan Yao, Jiaying Ji, Zijun Xu, Fengyi Du, Suwan Liu, Jiang Lin, Chenyao Wu, Wei Feng, Jun Qian

10.1002/adfm.78390.title: Decoupling Electrolytes Enable 5 Ah Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Pouch Cells
10.1002/adfm.78390.abstract: ABSTRACT Fast-charging lithium (Li)-ion batteries (LIBs) require electrolytes enabling rapid ion transport and desolvation. Conventional solvents strongly coordinate with lithium ions (Li + ), leading to high desolvation energy barriers and organic-rich interphases limiting rate capability. Here, we propose a descriptor-guided strategy for designing decoupling electrolytes to overcome sluggish Li + desolvation and poor interphase transport kinetics, enabling fast-charging LIBs. A solvent screening descriptor (decoupling coefficient (D c )) is introduced based on the ratio of molecular volume to Li + affinity, which captures solvent electronic and steric effects. Among evaluated solvents, propyl acetate (PA), possessing a high D c , is identified as a suitable solvent to formulate decoupling electrolytes, which lowers the desolvation energy barrier, promotes anion participation, and fosters an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Consequently, the PA-based decoupling electrolytes enable exceptional fast-charging LIBs. Li||graphite (Gr) cells deliver a capacity of 190.1 mA h g −1 at 6 C with 80% capacity retention after 2000 cycles. Furthermore, industrial-scale 5-Ah Gr||LiFePO 4 pouch cells, with a high cathode mass loading of 34 mg cm −2 , achieve an initial capacity of 4.29 Ah and retain 70% capacity over 600 cycles at 2 C. Even at 4 C, an impressive capacity of 4 Ah (138.9 Wh kg −1 ) can also be achieved.
authors: Fang Li, Cong Tian, Zhongqiang Wang, Xin Cheng, Huang Xiao, Jian Gao, Congying Song, Guoxing Li

10.1002/adfm.78031.title: Pressure-Assisted Dimensional Transformation of 2D Hydrogenated Borophene into 0D Boron Quantum Dots
10.1002/adfm.78031.abstract: ABSTRACT Borophene is a monoelemental two-dimensional (2D) material whose electron-deficient bonding renders free-standing monolayers intrinsically unstable, raising the question of how borophene can be converted into stable boron nanostructures. Borophene's structural stability and electronic properties are strongly influenced by vacancy configurations and defect engineering, while hydrogenation offers an additional pathway for stabilization and property tuning. Here, we introduce a solvent-free solid-state route that transforms hydrogenated borophene (HB) into either B 2 O 3 nanoplatelets or boron quantum dots (BQDs) via thermal dehydrogenation. Cleavage of B─H bonds releases hydrogen gas, whose escape under flowing N 2 facilitates structural reconstruction and leads to the formation of B 2 O 3 nanoplatelets. In sealed conditions, hydrogen accumulation generates internal pressure that drives fragmentation of the boron framework into BQDs. The resulting materials exhibit distinct photoluminescence (PL) behavior that correlates with their structural evolution, in agreement with first-principles calculations of band-gap changes. This work establishes solvent-free, pressure-assisted dimensional engineering of boron nanostructures and provides a new strategy for controlling the structural and optoelectronic properties of boron-based materials.
authors: Ozden Gunes Yildiz, Ramin Yazdaanpanah, Yongfeng Guo, Pouriya Naziri, Sachin Kulkarni, Martina Mercurio, Maria Cristina Larciprete, Ilaria Fratoddi, Paul Simon, Wan-Lu Li, Koray Aydin, Umut Aydemir

10.1002/adfm.77853.title: Mechanical Programming of PEGDA-β-CD Polyrotaxane-Based Hydrogels via Host-Guest Molecular Recognition
10.1002/adfm.77853.abstract: ABSTRACT Polyrotaxane-based hydrogels with mechanically interlocked structures offer unique opportunities for designing biomaterials with tunable mechanical properties in tissue engineering. However, the polyrotaxane structure based on poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) and β -cyclodextrin ( β -CD) is considered negligible in the aqueous phase, limiting its integration into well-defined hydrogel networks. Here, we report a series of hydrogels constructed from poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA)- β -CD polyrotaxanes and gelatin (Gel), loaded with curcumin as a therapeutic model. We demonstrate that the increasing number of threaded β -CD units on PEGDA chains induced an evolution of gel microstructure from disordered porous to ordered laminar morphology, thereby transforming the mechanical behavior from highly elastic, low-dissipated (13.53%) to high-damping states (46.56%), accompanied by enhanced toughness and modulus. Notably, low threading density variants exhibited desirable elasticity and recovery suitable for skin wound dressings, while higher threading densities enabled mimicking of highly dissipative biological tissues. In vivo studies further demonstrated the excellent wound healing performance of these hydrogels, due to their suitable mechanical properties and anti-inflammatory properties. In summary, this study highlights the critical role of polyrotaxane threading density in coupling supramolecular structure with mechanical and biological functions, providing a versatile strategy for advanced tissue engineering materials.
authors: Shiyi Chen, Xudan Xing, Haopu Su, Dominik Voll, Xiaohe Xu, Jiafeng Wan, Tongtong Cui, Christian W. Schmitt, Stefan Bräse, Peng Li, Patrick Théato

10.1002/adfm.78165.title: Myogenic Fusogen-Engineered Lipid Nanoparticles Enhance mRNA Delivery in Skeletal Muscle
10.1002/adfm.78165.abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as powerful vehicles for mRNA therapeutics, yet efficient delivery to skeletal muscle remains challenging. Here, we engineer LNPs by integrating Myomaker, a muscle-specific fusogen, onto their surface to enhance skeletal muscle delivery. Optimized Myomaker-LNP (Mymk-LNP) formulations demonstrated high fusogen integration, uniform size, and efficient mRNA encapsulation. Mymk-LNPs exhibited selective in vitro transfection in differentiating myocytes while minimizing uptake in myoblasts and fibroblasts. Systemic and local administration of Mymk-LNPs in vivo led to significantly increased mRNA delivery to skeletal muscle, particularly in models with muscles undergoing fusion, such as developing muscles in neonatal mice and chemically injured muscles in adult mice. Furthermore, Mymk-LNPs mediated efficient Cre mRNA-mediated DNA recombination in injured skeletal muscle as quantified by activation of a Cre-dependent tdTomato reporter. These findings highlight the potential of fusogen-engineered LNPs as a targeted and effective platform for delivery of mRNA therapeutics to muscle.

10.1002/adfm.78305.title: Ultrasound-Actuated Tissue Remodeling Integrates Living Bacterial Sonosensitization for Enhanced Tumor Therapy
10.1002/adfm.78305.abstract: ABSTRACT Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) is a promising non-invasive modality for treating deep-seated tumors, yet its efficacy remains constrained by the poor tumor accumulation of conventional sonosensitizers. To address this, we developed a bacteria-based SDT strategy employing Rhodopseudomonas palustris (R.P) as a self-propelled, living sonosensitizer that leverages inherent hypoxia tropism and active motility. Our results suggest that bacteriochlorophyll embedded in the bacterial membrane could act as an effective sonosensitizer, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon ultrasound stimulation and contributing to tumor cell killing via sonochemical effects. Notably, ultrasound also exerts a mechanical effect, inducing approximately 1.35-fold dilation of tumor vessels. Molecular dynamics simulations indicate that periodic ultrasound forces may cause reversible deformation of cell membranes, characterized by transient expansion of intermolecular spacing and rapid structural stretching. This ultrasound-mediated tissue remodeling might enhance tumor permeability, potentially facilitate deeper bacterial infiltration, and contributing to the improved efficacy of SDT. Together, these results present a bacteria-based SDT approach that integrates living therapeutics with self-propulsion and physical actuation, offering a potential strategy to expand the therapeutic scope of ultrasound in cancer treatment.

10.1002/adfm.78365.title: Decoupling the Size and Loading Effects in Silver Nanoparticles for Efficient Paired Carbon Dioxide and Formaldehyde Electrolysis
10.1002/adfm.78365.abstract: ABSTRACT Successful integration of silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) towards highly selective electrochemical CO 2 reduction to carbon monoxide (CO) is often hindered by size-dependent selectivity trade-offs in Ag NPs and by inefficient full-cell operation. Here, we systematically investigate ligand-mediated colloidal synthesis of (quasi) monodisperse Ag NPs (6-15 nm) and evaluate them in a gas-diffusion-electrode-based flow-cell architecture, revealing a pronounced size-dependent activity volcano. By incorporating a non-catalytic carbon support, we demonstrate that an optimized Ag-to-carbon (Ag/C) loading, specifically 20% with 10 nm Ag NPs, achieves nearly 100% Faradaic Efficiency (FE) for CO at −100 mA·cm −2 , significantly outperforming other particle sizes and a commercial Ag catalyst at similar loadings. In situ Raman spectroscopy reveals a substantial role of Ag/C interactions in enhancing the affinity toward the * COOH intermediates, thereby promoting high CO 2 -to-CO selectivity. Post-electrolysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further indicates the electronic and chemical structural stability of the optimized Ag/C, which retains the metallic Ag 0 state. Finally, we demonstrate the bifunctional nature of Ag/C electrodes by pairing CO 2 and formaldehyde electrolysis, enabling simultaneous CO generation at the cathode and formate (HCOO − ) with hydrogen (H 2 ) at the anode at reduced cell potentials. This work highlights an energy-efficient paired electrosynthesis strategy supporting the progress toward a circular carbon economy.
