10.1002/adfm.78310.title: Resonant Levels and Optimized Thermoelectric Performance in Cr-Filled ZrCoBi0.8Sn0.2
10.1002/adfm.78310.abstract: ABSTRACT Vacancy-filling strategy not only expands the Heusler family but also efficiently optimizes their thermoelectric performance. In this work, Cr atoms with 6 valence electrons are filled into the vacant 4d site of ZrCoBi 0.8 Sn 0.2 , preserving its semiconducting behavior. A small amount of Cr filling does not alter the carrier concentration of ZrCoCr x Bi 0.8 Sn 0.2 but introduces resonant levels within the bandgap, significantly enhancing the density of states effective mass from 13 m e ( x = 0) to 20 m e ( x = 0.04). As a result, the room-temperature Seebeck coefficient increases by ∼43% in the ZrCoCr 0.04 Bi 0.8 Sn 0.2 sample. Meanwhile, partial filling of the 4d site induces mass and strain fluctuations, substantially reducing the lattice thermal conductivity. At 950 K, the lattice thermal conductivity of ZrCoCr 0.02 Bi 0.8 Sn 0.2 decreases to 1.65 W m −1 K −1 , among the lowest values reported to date for p-type ZrCoBi- and ZrCoSb-based half-Heusler alloys. Consequently, a thermoelectric figure of merit zT of ∼1.0 is achieved in p-type ZrCoCr 0.02 Bi 0.8 Sn 0.2 at 950 K, representing an improvement of ∼47% relative to the pristine ZrCoBi 0.8 Sn 0.2 . This work not only illustrates the promise of the vacancy-filling strategy for advancing Heusler thermoelectrics, but also offers valuable insight into the regulation of material properties through vacancy filling.
authors: Haojin An, Zhiwei Chen, Zirui Dong, Yifei Huang, Wen Li, Jun Luo

10.1002/adfm.78391.title: A Polyoxoniobate-Based Molecular Heterojunction Orchestrates Heat and Vapor Transport for Efficient Solar Evaporation
10.1002/adfm.78391.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient solar-driven interfacial evaporation requires precise coordination of heat and mass transport, yet achieving such synergy within conventional molecular systems remains challenging. Here, we address this limitation using an atomically precise polyoxoniobate (PONb)-based molecular heterojunction, [Te 5 Cu 0.2 Nb 15 O 57 H 5.6 ][(CuL) 7 (OH)]·21H 2 O (PONb-CuL, L = 2,2′-bipyridine), in which hydrophilic PONb clusters are covalently integrated with photothermal organocopper CuL units. This Janus molecular architecture couples broadband solar absorption with interfacial water-cluster regulation within a single framework. Under one-sun irradiation, a two-dimensional PONb-CuL evaporator delivers an evaporation rate of 2.87 kg m −2 h −1 . Incorporation into a three-dimensional aerogel architecture further boosts the evaporation rate to 5.34 kg m −2 h −1 , affording a freshwater yield of 29.25 L m −2 under outdoor operation. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the PONb domain promotes hydrogen-bonded water-cluster formation, whereas the organocopper domain reduces the energy barrier for interfacial water transport and vapor escape. This work introduces polyoxometalate-based molecular heterojunction engineering as a strategy for orchestrating coupled heat and mass transport, offering critical insights into the rational design of efficient solar-to-vapor conversion systems.
authors: Peiqi Zhang, Xiang Ma, Tong Li, Yunwei Ye, Huixue Lei, Zhong Li, Shou-Tian Zheng

10.1002/adfm.78354.title: Chemical-Gradient-Induced Marangoni Flows Boost Solar-Brine Desalination and Enable Concurrent Power Generation
10.1002/adfm.78354.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers decentralised freshwater production with concurrent electricity generation, yet capillary-driven water supply imposes a kinetic ceiling in high-flux or high-salinity conditions, where boundary-layer buildup drives salt accumulation and performance decay. Here we establish a dual-driving transport regime that couples capillary flow with chemically induced Marangoni convection in low-tortuosity, vertically aligned channels. A longitudinal gradient of oxygen-containing functional groups, introduced into a graphene-oxide aerogel by thermal-gradient reduction, generates a persistent surface-tension disparity that sustains Marangoni microcirculation, continuously refreshing the evaporation interface by displacing concentrated boundary layers into the bulk. A miniaturised evaporator achieves 540 kg m − 3 h − 1 (2.7 kg m − 2 h − 1 ) in 20 wt% NaCl under 1-sun illumination, sustaining stable operation for 12 h without observable salt accumulation, while simultaneously delivering a short-circuit current of 25 µA and an open-circuit voltage of 0.7 V. Series-integrated devices directly power an LED. These results demonstrate that chemical-gradient programming can recruit Marangoni convection as a robust co-driver to surpass capillary-limited transport, offering a generalizable strategy for high-flux brine desalination with concurrent energy harvesting.
authors: Jingjing Zhang, Peng Cui, Hanwei Cai, Hanzhi Li, Yiwen Huang, Lei Ma, Luyang Wang, Kan Zhang, Jung Kyu Kim

10.1002/adfm.78398.title: Comprehensive Insights Into Electrolyte and Electrode-Electrolyte Interface for Aqueous Lithium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78398.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous lithium-ion batteries (ALIBs) stand out as promising grid-scale energy storage candidates, leveraging aqueous electrolytes to address the safety hazards and environmental concerns of traditional nonaqueous batteries. Their development, however, has long been constrained by the narrow electrochemical stability window of water, which limits cell voltage and promotes parasitic reactions. This review summarizes recent progress in ALIBs from the synergistic perspectives of electrolyte regulation, interfacial reaction mechanisms, and cell-level engineering considerations in relation to practical metrics, including energy density and long-term cycling durability. Particular emphasis is placed on the control of Li + solvation environments and the formation of functional interphases, which collectively suppress water-induced side reactions and expand the accessible operating window. By integrating these tightly linked aspects, this review delineates the mechanistic foundations and design principles that redefine the effective stability boundary of aqueous batteries and support the continued evolution of ALIBs toward scalable, high-energy, and durable technologies.
authors: Canfu Zhang, Wenlong Liang, Jiayue Peng, Saisai Qiu, Shijie Cheng, Jia Xie

10.1002/adfm.78319.title: Antisolvent Engineering Enabled Stretchable and Transparent Thermogalvanic Hydrogels with High Thermoelectric Properties
10.1002/adfm.78319.abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic thermogalvanic hydrogels with high ionic thermopower are promising for wearable power supply. However, due to the presence of solid network, their ionic conductivities are still low, limiting their power densities. Herein, a facile and effective enhancement strategy on ionic conductivities and thus ionic thermoelectric properties of PVA(poly(vinyl alcohol))/CMC(carboxymethyl cellulose) hydrogels is proposed through antisolvent engineering. An antisolvent (ethanol) of PVA is introduced into PVA/CMC precursor solution prior to the hydrogel formation, which can change the conformation of PVA and CMC molecular chains as well as hydrogen bond network of prepared hydrogel. It can decrease PVA crystalline domains, and present higher water content and more sub-micron porous structure through freeze-thaw cycles to form stretchable and transparent hydrogel with faster ionic transport. This PVA/CMC hydrogel with antisolvent engineering presents the high ionic conductivity of 57.9 mS cm −1 and elongation at beak of 256%, which are 3.75 and 1.8 times higher than pristine hydrogel, respectively. This boosts its P max /∆ T 2 to a high value of 0.67 mW m −2 K −2 , higher than that of most PVA hydrogels. During this configuration with 27 hydrogels, it can output a high voltage of 718.1 mV under 10 K temperature difference, which is potential for wearable power supply.
authors: Zhuo Liu, Xinyue Hu, Fan Xu, Haijie Zhao, Junxiang Tang, Xinyi Chen, Xiang Wei, Yangfan Song, Jin Yan, Hongwei Chen

10.1002/adfm.78399.title: Accelerating Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution via Interface-To-Surface Proton Transfer Relays on Ru-RuO2−δ Heterostructure
10.1002/adfm.78399.abstract: ABSTRACT Ru has been investigated as a promissing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalyst in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). However, its excessive oxophilicity blocks active sites and over-structures interfacial water, limiting alkaline HER kinetics. In this work, we report a Ru-RuO 2−δ heterostructure that overcomes these kinetic bottlenecks via an engineered interface-to-surface proton transfer relay. This architecture promotes a more flexible interfacial water network that facilitates Grotthuss-type proton transport, coupled with facilitated hydrogen spillover from high-affinity Ru clusters to low-affinity RuO 2−δ surfaces. By decoupling proton delivery from surface binding, the Ru-RuO 2−δ achieves an intrinsic activity 26-fold higher than pristine Ru, requiring ultra-low overpotentials of only 15 ± 4 and 165 ± 6 mV at 10 and 1000 mA cm −2 , respectively. Notably, the catalyst demonstrates long-term durability under high-current-density operation (> 470 h at 1 A cm −2 ) with a degradation rate 2,000-fold lower than commercial Pt/C. In a practical AEMWE, it delivers 1 A cm −2 at a cell voltage of 1.67 ± 0.02 V (45.1 ± 0.5 kWh kg H2 −1 ), meeting the U.S. DOE energy-consumption target. Beyond providing a high-performance alternative to platinum, this work introduces a design principle for accelerating electrocatalytic kinetics through the engineering of interface-to-surface transport relays.
authors: Jiaxi Zhang, Chunying Xi, Jun Ke, Yuanhua Tu, Longhai Zhang, Xinqi Li, Xiaoli Zhang, Chengzhi Zhong, Li Du, Yuwei Zhang, Zhiming Cui

10.1002/adfm.78357.title: Machine Learning-Driven Design of Electrolytes and Interfaces for Solid-State Lithium Batteries: Progress and Outlook
10.1002/adfm.78357.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state lithium batteries are a leading candidate for next-generation high-energy-density and high-safety batteries but suffer from inherent trade-offs among ionic conductivity, electrochemical stability, and mechanical strength in solid-state electrolytes, as well as complex electrode-electrolyte interfacial coupling involving side reactions, space-charge layers, and mechanical mismatch. Traditional trial-and-error experiments and isolated first-principles calculations struggle to address such high-dimensional, multiscale problems. Recently, machine learning has offered a new route to this challenge, enabled by breakthroughs in machine-learning potentials (MLIPs) that approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy while extending atomistic simulations to tens of thousands of atoms and nanosecond timescales, allowing direct observation of ion transport pathways and interfacial dynamic evolution. Concurrently, models such as graph neural networks have significantly improved the efficiency of high-throughput screening for candidate materials, while the integration of active learning, Bayesian optimization, and automated experimental platforms is fostering a closed-loop “prediction-validation-optimization” research paradigm. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in machine learning for solid-state lithium batteries, covering methodological foundations, bulk material design, interface engineering, and closed-loop R&D (research and development) pathways. It highlights that machine learning has evolved from merely improving screening efficiency to a pivotal hub iteratively integrating material discovery, interface analysis, and experimental optimization.
authors: Jihan Wu, Huiqun Wang, Chen Wang, Hao Chen, Jiajia Han, Li Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78361.title: Robust SEI and Uniform Na Deposition Enabled by Sodiophilic Interface for Durable Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries Across Ambient and Subzero Conditions
10.1002/adfm.78361.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) are regarded as promising next-generation energy storage device because of their exceptionally high energy density and low cost. However, their practical application is still hindered by uncontrolled sodium dendrites growth and unstable solid electrolyte interface (SEI) formation. To address these challenges, a sodiophilic Ag interface was in situ constructed on the copper foil current collector to regulate the uniform Na deposition and promote a stable SEI formation. Combined theoretical calculations and experimental analysis revealed that the Ag interface enables uniform Na deposition by enhancing sodiophilicity and homogenizing the electric field, while also promoting the decomposition of NaPF 6 to form a robust and thin SEI. Consequently, the Ag─Cu||Na asymmetric cells exhibited stable cycling for over 1100 cycles with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.87% at 1 mA cm −2 . Moreover, AFSMBs paired with Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cathode delivered a capacity retention of 70% after 500 cycles at 2C. Furthermore, the AFSMBs also maintained stable cycling over 150 cycles at −20°C under 0.05C. These results demonstrate the significant potential of introducing a sodiophilic interfacial layer to regulate uniform sodium deposition and promote stable SEI formation, thereby enabling high-performance anode-free sodium metal batteries across ambient and subzero conditions.
authors: Qiongqiong Lu, Guangtong Sun, Wenjia Zhang, Luyang Sun, Nina Pei, Zhiyuan Zhu, Pengfei Yue, Guoshang Zhang, Bo Song, Kexing Song

10.1002/adfm.78285.title: Lantern-Inspired Electroosmotic Actuator Enabling High Force and Large Quasi-Static Displacement for Haptic Displays and Pulse Sensing
10.1002/adfm.78285.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft actuators capable of delivering substantial force under large quasi-static displacement are essential for controllable human-machine interactions with realistic tactile sensations and wearable health monitoring. However, achieving such performance within lightweight architectures remains challenging due to inherent trade-offs between force, displacement, and device size. Here, we propose a lantern-inspired electroosmotic actuator (LIEA) that delivers excellent quasi-static mechanical output. The lantern-like folded membrane structure enables large deformation and high force output by minimizing parasitic elastic restoring forces. In addition, Au modification of the glass-fiber membrane strengthens the electric field across the membrane, enhancing electroosmotic transport and further improving actuation performance. Owing to this synergistic design, the LIEA achieves comparable displacement at less than 10% of the driving voltage typically required by conventional electroosmotic actuators. We demonstrate a 3 × 3 LIEA array for static pattern and dynamic shape generation, and validate its positional cueing capability using a 2 × 2 subarray in human subjects. Moreover, a pulse sensing patch is developed, in which tunable quasi-static loading provided by the LIEA optimizes arterial pulse acquisition and enables the extraction of multi-dimensional pulse features. Collectively, these results showcase the LIEA as a promising platform for applications ranging from haptic displays to active-sensing healthcare.
authors: Chao Ren, Yaru Zhao, Junchi Teng, Kangkang Dong, Jiani Xu, Zeyuan Cao, Xiongying Ye

10.1002/adfm.78318.title: Stabilization of Zinc Anodes in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries: From Challenges and Strategies to a Bibliometric Perspective
10.1002/adfm.78318.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising candidates for large-scale electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical viability remains fundamentally constrained by coupled failure processes at the metallic zinc anode, including uncontrolled dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, and interfacial corrosion that are systematically underestimated under the idealized testing conditions prevalent in the literature. Unlike existing reviews that evaluate stabilization strategies solely by reported cycling metrics, this work critically assesses three major directions (current collector design, artificial solid electrolyte interphase construction, and electrolyte engineering) by the physical and chemical variables each regulates, including nucleation overpotential, Zn 2+ flux distribution, desolvation barrier, interfacial water activity, and protective-layer mechanical integrity. Bibliometric analysis further reveals publication trends, institutional contributors, and underexplored research hotspots over the past decade. Finally, forward-looking perspectives are proposed spanning mechanism-constrained AI-assisted descriptor design, multimodal operando decoupling of dendrite and corrosion contributions, failure-mode identification under extreme and mass-transport-limited conditions, and ion-economy design at the full-cell scale. Together, these contributions aim to reframe the evaluation standards of the AZIB field and provide a systematic, mechanism-to-application reference for the rational design of highly stable and reversible zinc anodes.
authors: Jianqiang Huang, Zhijin Ju, Tao Yang, Xufen Ding, Lirong Chen, Yuanfeng Wu, Fei Ru, Gongxun Lu, Ouwei Sheng, Jie Xu, Yanshuai Li, Chao Zheng, Shun Wang, Chengbin Jin, Yifei Yuan

10.1002/adfm.78327.title: Triboiontronics for High-Reliability Sensing: Long-Term Maintenance of Asymmetric Electrical Double Layers
10.1002/adfm.78327.abstract: ABSTRACT Triboiontronic devices achieve mechanical-to-electrical signal conversion by dynamically regulating ion migration and the electrical double layer (EDL), offering advantages in flexible sensing and bionic perception. Devices featuring direct electrode-hydrogel contact exhibit high charge transfer densities, but the current output of existing devices decays rapidly with the number of cycles. This current output decay hinders high-reliability sensing applications. Here, an asymmetric Au/PET-carbon cloth electrode system was constructed. By leveraging the abundant oxygen-containing functional groups and porous structure on the surface of the carbon cloth to achieve strong adsorption of Li + , a significantly asymmetric EDL structure was formed and sustained over the long term between the upper and lower electrodes. Leveraging the Hofmeister salting-out effect of Li + , the pore structure and ionic conductivity of the ionic hydrogel were precisely controlled, increasing mobile ions and enhancing the interfacial contact area to synergistically amplify EDL density. Consequently, the device maintained a stable current output (∼60 µA) over 1000 cycles without significant decay. This study allows the expansion of devices based on similar mechanisms from “attenuated energy harvesting” to the field of “highly stable sensing applications,” providing a new theoretical basis and technical pathway for the design of highly reliable, high-current-output triboiontronic sensors.
authors: Jiahao Fang, Xinyue Xiong, Yao Chen, Xiaobo Pu, Peng Wang, Sixuan Wu, Linjin Ye, Yong Zhang, Fanghan Ming, Xiaoqin Liao, Qi-Chang He, Tingting Yang

10.1002/adfm.78325.title: Strain-Engineered Zener Tunneling Diodes Enable Energy-Efficient Neuromorphic Edge Vision
10.1002/adfm.78325.abstract: ABSTRACT Machine vision systems face severe bandwidth-latency bottlenecks and high power consumption due to massive unstructured data transfer. Edge computing via sensor-level nonlinear computation offers a promising pathway to reduce data volume. However, existing breakdown-based neuromorphic photodiodes typically rely on high-bias avalanche processes, resulting in substantial operating power consumption. Here, we propose a strain-engineered Zener tunneling diode (S-ZCD) based on a stretched graphene/silicon heterojunction, where tensile strain opens an effective graphene bandgap and enables controllable cross-bandgap quantum tunneling. The S-ZCD realizes a light-modulated breakdown process along the carrier transport pathway, exhibiting ultrasharp nonlinear switching characteristics with a subthreshold swing of 10-35 mV dec −1 , a minimum breakdown threshold voltage of 0.59 V and ultra-low operating power consumption of ∼0.1 nW at room-temperature. Furthermore, the coupled optical-electrical regulation enables adaptive nonlinear preprocessing for edge vision applications, including fixed-step filtering and bias-programmable feature extraction. The S-ZCD suppresses redundant background information, maintains >90% recognition accuracy while reducing inference energy consumption by ∼43%, and enables device-characteristic-guided array-level contour-extraction validation.
authors: Jiabin Ren, Xianghong Zhang, Yang Wang, Shuiyuan Wang, Chunsen Liu, Peng Zhou

10.1002/adfm.78328.title: Tellurium-Induced Phase-Orbital Coupling Enables High-Mobility p-Type Tin Oxide Transistor
10.1002/adfm.78328.abstract: ABSTRACT P-type oxide semiconductors are intrinsically limited by the spatially localized O 2p orbitals at the valence band edge, which cause a large hole effective mass and sluggish carrier transport. Overcoming this long-standing limitation demands not only defect passivation but, more fundamentally, reconstruction of the valence band topology and transport pathways. Here, we demonstrate a tellurium-induced phase-orbital coupling strategy in tin oxide (SnO x :Te) thin films that simultaneously delocalizes the valence states and establishes high-mobility transport networks. Specifically, Te incorporation enhances Sn 5s-O 2p hybridization, enhancing valence-band dispersion and thereby reducing the hole effective mass. Concurrently, the stabilization of semimetallic Sn nanodomains creates an embedded heterophase network that activates highly efficient transport pathways. Moreover, Te-mediated suppression of oxygen-vacancy formation mitigates ionized impurity scattering, enabling stable hole conduction. As a result, the SnO x :Te thin-film transistors exhibit a high field-effect mobility of ∼62 cm 2 V −1 s −1 with improved operational stability. The transistor arrays show excellent uniformity, and complementary inverters based on these p-type transistors deliver a voltage gain of 59.5 and a minimum static power consumption of 11.82 pW. The phase-orbital coupling mechanism established here extends beyond SnO x , offering a generalizable route to activate dispersive valence states and transcend the intrinsic transport limitations of oxide semiconductors.
authors: Yu Song, Xianglong Zhang, Rui He, Runtong Guo, Xuefang Yan, Lin Tang, Weimin Pan, Ruohao Hong, Xingqiang Liu, Xuming Zou, Benjamin Iñiguez, You Meng, Denis Flandre, Jean-Pierre Raskin, Wei-Qing Huang, Lei Liao, Guoli Li

10.1002/adfm.78373.title: Concentration-Driven Energy-Bridge Synergistic Sensitized High-Efficiency Rare-Earth NIR Emitters Enable Colorful High-Fidelity Hyperspectral Imaging
10.1002/adfm.78373.abstract: ABSTRACT Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) combines imaging and spectroscopy for diverse applications in agriculture, industry, and medicine. However, current broadband and visible light based HSI systems suffer from limited spectral range, poor environment-resistant capabilities and severe emission overlap. Here, we propose a innovative HSI approach based on narrow-band near-infrared (NIR, 900-1700 nm) rare-earth luminescent materials. First, through concentration triggered multi-site synergistic sensitization strategy, we developed high-efficiency narrow-band NIR emitters, LaZnGa 11 O 19 : (RE = Yb, Er, Nd, Tm and Ho), achieving FWHM of 28 nm and 50% external quantum efficiency. Subsequently, we integrated as-developed emitters with HSI technology to construct a novel narrow-band NIR-enhanced HSI system. Compared to wide-band emitters, its theoretical signal isolation in dual-channel mode significantly improved from 1.84 dB and 0.14 dB to 14.62 dB and 9.08 dB, effectively extending the spectral range of imaging systems while avoiding signal crosstalk between multiple wavelength signals. Furthermore, when applied to real-world image information scenarios, the as-constructed system achieves isolation of 11.8 dB (channel to background) and 10.2 dB (channel-to-channel) close to theoretical values, demonstrating the feasibility of narrow-band NIR-enhanced HSI approach. These results provide unique ideas and inspirations for the design of high-performance NIR luminescent materials as well as advanced imaging applications.
authors: Rongyi Kuang, Meng Gao, Binchang Wu, Huiwang Lian, Lin Huang, Bo-Mei Liu, Jing Wang

10.1002/adfm.78324.title: Molecular Engineering of Redox-Induced Conformational Entropy in Polyviologens for Organic Thermogalvanic Cells
10.1002/adfm.78324.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermogalvanic cells are attractive for harvesting low-grade thermal energy because of their strong thermoelectrochemical response and simple architecture. Because the redox entropy change directly governs their Seebeck coefficient, engineering redox entropy offers an effective strategy for enhancing thermoelectric performance. Herein, redox-induced conformational entropy engineering is introduced as a molecular strategy for organic redox-active polymers. Ortho- xylylene-linked polyviologen ( o- PV), meta- PV, and para- PV ( p- PV) are synthesized to modulate steric constraints and conformational reorganization during the viologen redox process. Electrochemical and spectroscopic results indicate that o- PV undergoes the most pronounced conformational reorganization upon reduction and exhibits the largest conformational entropy change, consistent with its sterically constrained architecture. Consequently, o- PV exhibits the greatest Seebeck-coefficient magnitude of −1.87 mV K −1 , whereas p- PV displays the lowest response. This structure-entropy relationship guides the development and subsequent integration of an end-capped o- PV derivative into a poly(acrylamide) hydrogel thermocell, which achieves a Seebeck coefficient of −2.25 mV K −1 and a normalized maximum power density of 0.88 mW m −2 K −2 . A hydrogel-based thermoelectric generator demonstrates scalable voltage output, stable operation, and effective low-grade human body heat harvesting. These findings establish conformational entropy engineering as a strategy for tuning redox thermodynamics and advancing high-performance organic thermogalvanic materials for sustainable heat-to-electricity conversion.
authors: Yung-Chieh Liao, Hayaki Ogata, Yu Sakai, Chun-Chen Hung, Shao-Huan Hong, Takeo Suga, Hiroyuki Nishide, Cheng-Liang Liu

10.1002/adfm.78363.title: Hybrid Topology Enables 3D-Printable Liquid Crystal Network with Synergistic Mechanical Robustness and Energy-Dissipation
10.1002/adfm.78363.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid crystal networks (LCNs), characterized by their unique dynamic mechanical properties derived from LC mesogens, have emerged as one of the most promising materials for ubiquitous vibration and impact protection. Additive manufacturing further expands their potential by enabling the fabrication of lightweight and customizable architectures with tailored energy-dissipation properties. However, the requirements of photocurable groups inherently constrains network topology, hindering synergistic enhancement in energy dissipation and mechanical robustness, a fundamental challenge for energy-dissipative polymers. Here, we propose a topology-engineering strategy to access hybrid-topology liquid crystal network (HT-LCN) that integrates LC mesogens, linear polymer chains, dangling chains, and crystalline domains within a single printable network, enabling multiple energy-dissipation mechanisms while preserving structural robustness. As a result, HT-LCNs exhibit an ultrawide effective damping temperature range (∼200°C), exceptional toughness (68 MJ m − 3 ), and the highest impact absorption reported for 3D-printable polymeric matrix materials (179 MJ m − 3 @4000 s − 1 ). Furthermore, HT-LCN-based architectures show more than 200% higher specific energy dissipation than conventional printed systems, paving the way for designing and engineering robust 3D printable energy-dissipation devices.
authors: Zhijun Yang, Xiao Wang, Zhenyi Liang, Jiayin Zhou, Shuhan Zhang, Huan Liang, Yang Yang, Mingrui Wu, Enjian He, Yixuan Wang, Qiulin Chen, Guoli Wang, Yen Wei, Yan Ji

10.1002/adfm.78362.title: Ion-Coordination “Rails” in a Hydrogel Interphase Enable Stable Aluminum Plating/Stripping
10.1002/adfm.78362.abstract: ABSTRACT The promise of aqueous aluminum-metal batteries for safe and low-cost energy storage is challenged by poor reversibility of the Al anode, primarily due to interfacial heterogeneity. Here we report an ex situ Zn 2+ -coordinated hydrogel interphase (SA/Gel@Zn) on Al foil. Zn 2+ -carboxylate coordination generates regulated ionic nodes within the hydrogel network that act as ion-transport “rails”, homogenizing interfacial Al 3+ flux and enabling uniform nucleation and even Al plating/stripping. Meanwhile, the conformal and mechanically compliant gel interphase reduces direct water access and stabilizes the interfacial electric double layer, thereby markedly suppressing hydrogen-evolution corrosion and lowering charge-transfer resistance. Consequently, SA/Gel@Zn increases the Al 3+ transference number (0.48 to 0.83), eliminates dendritic protrusions, and delivers ultralong symmetric-cell durability up to 5500 h at 0.05 mA cm −2 and 2300 h at 0.10 mA cm −2 , together with improved coulombic efficiency. The SA/Gel@Zn-Al//α-MoO 3 full battery delivers stable cycling for over 150 cycles at 200 mA g − 1 with an average coulombic efficiency higher than 99% and the initial discharge specific capacity reaches 248.8 mAh g − 1 . This work presents a scalable, transport-active hydrogel SEI strategy to stabilize Al anodes in aqueous electrolytes.
authors: Zibo Chen, Jiebin Zheng, Zheng Li, Guoxuan Li, Xinyi Li, Hao Cheng, Hailin Yu, Wei Zhang, Zhongliang Tian

10.1002/adfm.78313.title: ROS-Responsive Doxorubicin Prodrug-Manganese Nanoplatform Synergistically Activates cGAS-STING to Suppress Uveal Melanoma Growth and Metastasis
10.1002/adfm.78313.abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor-derived DNA released during chemo- or radiotherapy serves as a damage-associated molecular pattern that activates antitumor immunity through the cGAS-STING pathway. However, conventional chemotherapy is limited by insufficient tumoricidal efficacy and systemic toxicity, restricting effective activation of innate immune within a tolerable therapeutic window. Here, we report a ROS-responsive nanomedicine (NPDM) for coordinated chemotherapy and cGAS-STING activation. NPDM is constructed via the co-self-assembly of a lipidic doxorubicin (DOX) prodrug (C16-SS-DOX) and a manganese-polyphenol coordination polymer (HSSD-Mn). NPDM exhibits high stability during systemic circulation while selectively releasing DOX and Mn 2 + within the ROS-rich tumor microenvironment. Released DOX induces tumor DNA damage and DAMPs generation, whereas Mn 2 + acts as an endogenous cofactor to amplify cGAS-STING activation, thereby enhancing antigen-presenting cell function and downstream antitumor immune responses. As a result, NPDM effectively suppresses tumor growth and elicits potent systemic immune activation. Notably, NPDM significantly sensitizes tumors to immune checkpoint blockade, and its combination with αPD-L1 produces strong synergistic inhibition of both orthotopic and abscopal tumors. Collectively, this work constructs a novel nanoplatform integrating dual functions of “precise chemotherapeutic delivery” and “targeted activation of the cGAS-STING pathway”, providing a promising chemo-immunotherapy strategy for uveal melanoma and other immunologically “cold” tumors.
authors: Xiaoqin Zheng, Ke Yan, Tao Tao, Qinghe Zhang, Ya Deng, Chun Xu, Haihua Xiao, Dongsheng Tang, Kun Shang, Gang Tan

10.1002/adfm.78316.title: Ground-State Charge-Transfer Doping in Donor-Acceptor Semiconducting Polymers
10.1002/adfm.78316.abstract: ABSTRACT Conjugated polymers are at the heart of numerous current and emerging technologies. Doping, a process by which charge carriers are introduced, is crucial to their functionality and performance. Despite a significant historical context, doping processes based on ground-state charge-transfer (CT) complex formation, mediated by the supramolecular hybridization between the frontier molecular orbitals of distinct molecular species, remain rare and are consequently poorly understood. In this context, there are no clear demonstrations of this alternative doping phenomenon in contemporary donor-acceptor conjugated polymers. Here, we use diketopyrrolopyrrole-based donor-acceptor semiconducting polymers and a π -conjugated penta- t -butylpentacyanopentabenzo[25]annulene “cyanostar” macrocycle to demonstrate the first examples of features that control ground-state CT complex formation in these contemporary conjugated polymer frameworks. Using complementary experimental techniques, we articulate how subtle molecular, electronic, and solid-state features impact the supramolecular hybridization of the frontier molecular orbitals and impact the resultant (opto)electronic, magnetic, and transport properties. These studies demonstrate that the admixture between distinct π -conjugated materials can have dramatic outcomes on solid-state electronic properties and performance through modification of the density of states. These results and associated mechanistic insight will enable completely new co-design rules for organic semiconductors and emerging molecular dopants that offer new functionality and precise property control.
authors: Tanner L. Smith, Akshay N. Shah, Tanya A. Balandin, Michel De Keersmaecker, Paramasivam Mahalingam, Debapriya Gupta, Siqi Yu, Eui Hyun Suh, Pushkar Dalal, Erin L. Ratcliff, Scott P. O. Danielsen, Tse Nga Ng, Amar H. Flood, Jason D. Azoulay

10.1002/adfm.78311.title: Architecture-Driven Functional Coupling in Vertically Aligned Nanocomposites
10.1002/adfm.78311.abstract: ABSTRACT Vertically aligned nanocomposites (VANs) are self-assembled thin-film architectures in which phase distribution, interfacial density, and strain fields are defined concurrently during growth. Nanoscale vertical alignment and coherent interfaces generate anisotropic confinement and directional connectivity, thereby modifying ionic, electronic, optical, and magnetic responses across oxide, oxide-metal, oxide-nitride, and oxide-alloy systems. This review examines how growth kinetics, elastic mismatch, and interfacial energetics control pillar morphology, defect distribution, and transport anisotropy in VAN platforms. Studies spanning electrochemical electrodes, dielectric materials, and magneto-optical systems demonstrate enhanced oxygen exchange kinetics, anisotropic permittivity, strain-stabilized phases, and coupled magnetic-optical behavior arising from architectural control. By correlating structural parameters with functional outputs, the literature establishes VANs as a versatile strategy for engineering coupled phenomena in complex oxides. Emerging design guidelines and open challenges are discussed to outline future directions for energy conversion and nanoelectronic applications.
authors: Md Shatil Islam-Shanto, Javier Zamudio-García, Abraham Sánchez-Caballero, David Marrero-López, Vincenzo Esposito

10.1002/adfm.78171.title: Two-Photon Laser Writing of Sub-Diffraction Three-Dimensional Luminescent Perovskite Architecture Embedded in Non-Luminescent Perovskite
10.1002/adfm.78171.abstract: ABSTRACT As emerging high-performance optoelectronic materials, metal halide perovskites display outstanding advantages in micro-nano optoelectronic integration. However, high-precision multidimensional processing and on-demand dynamic modulation of the luminescent properties of perovskites remain urgent challenges. In this work, we present a femtosecond laser two-photon-induced in situ phase transition strategy that enables the precise construction of highly luminescent multidimensional perovskite heterostructures within non-emissive perovskite single crystals. We systematically investigate the regulatory effects of key laser parameters, including energy density and pulse repetition rate, on the phase transition process, and successfully fabricate patterns with sub-diffraction-limit resolution. Moreover, by incorporating artificial intelligence algorithms, we accomplish point-by-point writing of multilayer anti-counterfeiting information at various depth planes, converting conventional 2D planar tags into 3D stereoscopic anti-counterfeiting architectures. This two-photon laser processing strategy based on in situ phase transition provides a new route for the high-precision 3D integration of perovskite-based optoelectronic devices.

10.1002/adfm.78322.title: Synergistic Anion-π Interaction With an Electron-Deficient Porphyrin Stabilizes Perovskite for High-Performance Printable Carbon-Electrode Mesoscopic Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78322.abstract: ABSTRACT The power conversion efficiency (PCE) of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has progressed rapidly, but operational stability under light and thermal stresses remains a critical challenge, largely due to the migration of weakly bound iodide ions at the lattice terminations. Here, we introduce an electron-deficient macrocycle, 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(4-nitrophenyl)porphyrin (TNPP), as a terminal ion stabilizer in printable carbon-electrode mesoscopic PSCs (p-MPSCs). The strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups create an electropositive cavity in TNPP, enabling synergistic anion-π and hydrogen-bonding interactions with the perovskite lattice. This dual interaction mechanism anchors terminal iodide ions and A-site cations, effectively suppressing ion migration and subsequent perovskite decomposition under environmental stressors. Consequently, TNPP-modified devices achieve a champion PCE of 21.38% alongside exceptional stability. They retain > 95% of their initial PCE after 2000 h in ambient air (50%-70% RH), > 90% after 1040 h at 85°C under inert atmosphere, and > 95% after 1200 h of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) at 55°C under continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a potent molecular design strategy for stabilizing the perovskite lattice through synergistic non-covalent interactions.
authors: Chuanzhou Han, Junwei Xiang, Yongming Ma, Yanjie Cheng, Minghao Xia, Qian Yue, Song Shen, Siqi Jiang, Li-Ming Yang, Yang Zhou, Jiale Liu, Anyi Mei, Hongwei Han

10.1002/adfm.78326.title: Electric-Field-Triggered Sulfonate Interfacial Regulation Enables High-Selectivity Electrochemical Direct Lithium Extraction via Dynamic Ion Sieving
10.1002/adfm.78326.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical direct lithium extraction emerges as a promising route toward sustainable lithium supply, yet pervasive interference from Na + and Mg 2+ incurs formidable kinetic barriers. Herein, we construct field-responsive H 1.6 Mn 1.6 O 4 @poly (3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-polystyrenesulfonate (HMO@PEDOT:PSS) sulfonate interfaces and establish a dynamic ion sieving mechanism for selective lithium recovery. Synergistically integrated conductive PEDOT framework and sulfonate functional moieties endow the heterointerfaces with instantaneous electric field-triggered responsiveness. The field-sensitive-sulfonate sites dynamically regulate interfacial cation affinity, enabling prominent selective separation of Li + against Na + and Mg 2+ in harsh brine media. Profiting from real-time interfacial modulation, the as-fabricated electrode achieves superior lithium extraction performance and drastically enhanced magnesium rejection, having an exceptional separation factor of 458.9 while preserving a high of 1069.4. Alternating electric field actuates reversible conformational evolution of sulfonate groups, alleviating impurity ion entrapment and reviving blocked Li + migration pathways. Theoretical calculations unveil field-induced thermodynamic inversion, converting strong Mg 2+ adsorption into electrostatic repulsion to facilitate impurity expulsion. In situ spectroscopic characterizations further corroborate dynamically tunable sulfonate-cation coordination behavior. This work sheds light on triggered sulfonate-cation interfacial engineering to boost high-performance electrochemical lithium extraction via dynamic ion sieving.
authors: Fei Zhang, Lu Yu, Rui Zhang, Rongping Yun, Xu Xiang

10.1002/adfm.78402.title: Dynamic Piezoelectric Polarization Directs Reaction Pathways in CO2 Reduction Over Pt/Cu2O@BaTiO3 Dual-Site Heterostructures
10.1002/adfm.78402.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and selective CO 2 conversion under mild conditions remains challenging because rapid interfacial charge recombination and poorly controlled carbon-conversion pathways often limit both catalytic activity and product selectivity. Here, we report a Pt/Cu 2 O@BaTiO 3 (Pt/Cu 2 O@BTO) dual-site heterostructure in which Pt and Cu 2 O are spatially separated on piezoelectric BaTiO 3 nanorods to establish differentiated interfaces for CO 2 reduction and H 2 O oxidation. Under coupled mechanical stimulation and light irradiation, stress-induced piezoelectric polarization synergistically enhances interfacial charge separation while promoting CO 2 adsorption and activation at Pt-related reduction sites. Benefiting from the piezo-photocatalytic coupling, Pt/Cu 2 O@BTO achieved a CO production rate of 146.7 µmol g −1 h −1 and a CO selectivity of 95.8%. In situ FTIR spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that the dynamic piezoelectric polarization not only accelerates charge transport and CO 2 activation, but also redirects the subsequent evolution of key *CO intermediates by making CO desorption more competitive than further hydrogenation. This work demonstrates that dynamic interfacial polarization can simultaneously regulate charge-transfer behavior and reaction pathways in CO 2 reduction, providing a strategy for selective carbon conversion in multi-field catalytic systems.
authors: Chunlai Dong, Xiuli Zhang, Yi Wang, Feng Ru Fan

10.1002/adfm.78329.title: Balancing the Activity-Adsorption Trade-Off in Biomass Valorization via Electron-Reconstructed High-Entropy Oxides
10.1002/adfm.78329.abstract: ABSTRACT The directional anchoring of heteroatoms into a high-entropy oxides (HEOs) platform offers substantial scientific and technological promise, yet achieving atomic-level control over such doping remains challenging and rarely demonstrated. Here, we precisely anchor B atoms into an HEO framework (BS-HEO), possessing a distinct O-Mn-B coordination unit in which Mn acts as an electronic hub that triggers an electron-siphoning effect, thereby redistributing the interfacial electron configuration. Theory and experiments confirm that the electron-reconstructed surface enables the optimization of the balance between intrinsic activity and adsorption toward 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) within the potential window (1.40-1.45 V vs. RHE), consequently enhancing interfacial mass transport efficiency. As a result, when the carbon balance is taken into consideration, the BS-HEO catalyst delivers impressive HMFOR performance at 1.42 V versus RHE, achieving 96.0% selectivity for 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and 99.1% faradaic efficiency (F.E.), which surpasses most previously reported benchmarks. This work not only demonstrates precise B anchoring into a HEO but also introduces a new strategy for tailoring and identifying active sites in high-entropy materials for high-performance electrosynthesis.

10.1002/adfm.78369.title: Cartilage-Mimicking Hybrid Avascular Hydrogel Scaffold for Stable Auricular Cartilage Regeneration in Microtia Reconstruction
10.1002/adfm.78369.abstract: ABSTRACT A major challenge in auricular reconstruction is the endochondral ossification of engineered cartilage after subcutaneous implantation. To overcome this, we developed a functionally tailored, hybrid hydrogel scaffold that integrates anti-angiogenic therapy with biomimetic architecture to stabilize the chondrogenic phenotype. The core consists of a DLP-printed, bevacizumab-eluting pNAGA-GT hydrogel framework with 200-µm resolution, exhibiting a compressive modulus of 5.35 MPa and a tensile modulus of 0.34 MPa, providing robust mechanical support. Sustained bevacizumab release suppresses local angiogenic activity and is accompanied by increased TIMP3 and reduced MMP9/MMP13 expression, thereby contributing to cartilage matrix preservation and reduced ossification. Encapsulating this core, a visible-light-crosslinked GelMA-Tyr hydrogel creates a soft (∼15 kPa), degradable (60-day) microenvironment that spatially organizes chondrocytes and perichondrium-derived stem/progenitor cells (PSPCs) into a cartilage-mimetic construct, thereby preserving cell viability and chondrogenic function. This dual-phase design enables the generation of stable, multilayered ectopic cartilage, offering a clinically translatable strategy for microtia reconstruction.
authors: Boqing Zhang, Yu Liu, Hairui Li, Wilson Adrian Wijaya, Li Wang, Fengqin Song, Jingting Huang, Sijie Li, Wenzhao Wang, Zhenyu Zhang, Zhengyong Li, Ying Cen, Changchun Zhou, Xingdong Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78367.title: Decoupled Temperature-Pressure Sensing via Hierarchical Porous Sponge for Thermo-Tactile Perception
10.1002/adfm.78367.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise and crosstalk-free discrimination of pressure and temperature remains a fundamental challenge in artificial sensory systems due to the intrinsic coupling of mechanical and thermal transduction. Herein, we present a flexible, high-fidelity dual-modal sensor based on an ultralight hierarchically porous conductive sponge. The engineered porous architecture synergistically integrates piezoresistive and thermoelectric effects within a single carbon nanomaterial, achieving physical decoupling between resistance-type pressure signals and voltage-type temperature outputs, effectively suppressing dual-modal interference. Owing to its compressibility, conductive network, and thermal insulation, the sensor delivers a pressure sensitivity of 4.43 kPa −1 , a detection limit of 25 Pa, a response time of 91 ms, and durability over 20 000 cycles, alongside a Seebeck coefficient of 9.96 µV K −1 and a temperature resolution of 0.5 K. As a proof of concept, it enables real-time Morse code communication and physiological monitoring. Moreover, a 3 × 3 sensor array integrated with machine learning demonstrates robust tactile-thermal fusion perception, highlighting its potential as a multifunctional sensing platform. This work presents a material-driven strategy to overcome multimodal signal interference, significantly promoting sensory perception in complex environments.
authors: Jiachen Dong, Bo Xu, Hongyu Mi, Xin Zhao, Yuqing Zhai, Yongqi Zhu, Zhiyu Wang, Xinqin Liao

10.1002/adfm.78409.title: Self-Electrostatic Interlock of β-Chitin/MXenes/Ni Fiber-Based Films for Multifunctional Electromagnetic Interference Shielding
10.1002/adfm.78409.abstract: ABSTRACT MXenes have emerged as promising electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials because of their metal-like electrical conductivity, excellent processability, and lightweight nature. However, their limited absorption coefficient and poor mechanical properties restrict further optimization of shielding performance and their ability to meet service requirements in harsh electromagnetic environments. Herein, squid-pen-derived β-chitin/Ti 3 C 2 T x /Ni fiber films are fabricated via magnetic-field-induced assembly and self-electrostatic interlocking. Ni nanoparticles assemble into textile-like magnetic fibers, enhancing magnetic coupling and the absorption coefficient of MXenes. By integrating electropositive β-chitin with electronegative Ti 3 C 2 T x , the films achieve improved mechanical properties (tensile strength of 18.90 ± 2.08 MPa and fracture strain of 8.45 ± 0.08%) together with an excellent EMI shielding effectiveness of 75.1 dB, blocking more than 99.999997% of incident electromagnetic waves. Moreover, the β-chitin/Ti 3 C 2 T x /Ni fiber films integrate Joule heating, photoresponsive heating, and triboelectricity, enabling the design of a “semi-intelligent warm glove” for wearable applications. Therefore, this work provides a versatile strategy for developing high-performance smart films integrating EMI shielding with multiple functions for intelligent wearable applications.
authors: Tong Wang, Fei Pan, Yongpeng Wu, Yuqing Zhu, Chunhua Sun, Pengxu Chen, Xiang Li, Wei Lu

10.1002/adfm.78332.title: Perovskite Quantum Dot/AIEgen Hybrids With Exceptional Photostability and Near-Unity Luminance Efficiency
10.1002/adfm.78332.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite quantum dots (QDs) and aggregation-induced-emission luminogens (AIEgens) are both widely investigated luminescent materials, yet both materials suffer from poor photostability and nonradiative recombination loss. Herein, we report on a hybrid luminescent system that combines CsPbBr 3 QDs with an AIEgen molecule (TBBA) to overcome these intrinsic drawbacks. The resulting CsPbBr 3- TBBA hybrid exhibits exceptional photostability and an almost unity PLQY. The intense absorption of CsPbBr 3 QDs enabled them to function as optical antennas, efficiently transferring their excitons to the AIEgens in 43.1 ps with near-unity yield. This rapid extraction of the excitation energy from CsPbBr 3 QDs and avoidance of ultraviolet photon absorption in AIEgens effectively solved the photostability issues for these two individuals, resulting in remarkable photostability (effective half-life of 1800 days under outdoor solar illumination). Additionally, strong restriction of intramolecular motions for AIEgens grafted onto the QD surface led to near-unity photoluminescence efficiency, with minimized reabsorption loss, which was leveraged to demonstrate efficient large-area luminescent solar concentrator devices. This work introduces a general strategy for constructing hybrid luminescent materials that unify high photostability and near-unity emission efficiency through interfacial coupling between inorganic and organic components.
authors: Shan He, Meng Liu, Lei Wang, Guijie Liang, Jianwei Sun, Ryan T. K. Kwok, Dan Ding, Huilin Xie, Jianquan Zhang, Jacky W. Y. Lam, Kaifeng Wu, Ben Zhong Tang

10.1002/adfm.78333.title: Ion Pathways Optimized via Interlayer Channels in Bimetallic Hydroxides Enable Ultra-Stable Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78333.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) from electrospinning offer robust mechanical frameworks but often require complex post-treatments and suffer from low room-temperature ionic conductivity and sluggish Li + transport, hindering the development of solid-state batteries. Here, we propose a surface-grown protective fiber strategy: growing CoMn-layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets on polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers to anchor residual propylene carbonate (PC) molecules, forming a composite SPE (LDH@PAN SPE) with interfacial stabilization. Abundant LDH hydroxyl groups immobilize PC via hydrogen bonding, while metal sites electrostatically interact with the lithium salt anions (TFSI − ), promoting Li salt dissociation and optimizing [Li(PC) x ] + solvation. Additionally, hydrogen bonding between PAN cyano-groups and LDH creates continuous radial Li + pathways. The LDH@PAN SPE achieves high ionic conductivity (1.36 mS cm −1 ), Li + transference number (0.80 at 20°C), and a 4.9 V window. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle for 1600 h at 0.2 mA cm −2 with a critical current density of 1.8 mA cm −2 . LiFePO 4 ||Li full cells deliver excellent rate capability (110.2 mAh g −1 at 5 C) and long-term cycling (81.3% retention after 1100 cycles at 1 C) at room temperature, alongside flexibility and flame retardancy. This work offers a new interfacial engineering and ion-transport strategy for high-performance solid-state lithium metal batteries.
authors: Xueyu Wang, Keyu Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Weihua Zhang, Daying Guo, Guoyong Fang, Xi'an Chen, Huile Jin, Shun Wang

10.1002/adfm.78092.title: CO2-to-CO Conversion in a Gas-Fed, Zero-Gap, PEM Electrolyzer Enabled by Polycations and Nitrogen-Doped Carbon-Supported Cobalt Nanoparticles
10.1002/adfm.78092.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (ECO 2 R) into value-added chemicals is challenging due to the high overpotential of reaction intermediates, the instability of adsorbed species in the absence of mobile cations, and requiring acidic aqueous electrolyte feed to prevent salt precipitation. A gas-fed, zero-gap proton exchange membrane (PEM) ECO 2 R setup utilizing hydrogen (H 2 ) as anodic feed and nitrogen-doped carbon-supported cobalt nanoparticles (Co/N-C) as catalyst may be a solution to these problems but is observed to be ineffective at suppressing the H 2 evolution reaction (HER). Immobilizing poly-diallyldimethyl ammonium (PDDA + ) cations with finely milled Co/N-C results in a change of selectivity from HER toward coordinating CO 2 intermediates on active sites. Optimizing Co loading at 1.20 wt.% for Co/N-C delivers a peak faradaic efficiency toward carbon monoxide production (FE CO ) of 65% and sustains 5 h electrolysis with FE CO above 50% under a constant current density of 100 mA cm −2 . The effects of acid-wash, cobalt content, mass loading, and PDDA + on the gas-diffusion electrode and secondary particle size in catalyst ink are optimized to improve FE CO against a prohibitively low pH environment. These results highlight the intrinsic properties of PDDA + on Co/N-C electrocatalyst for a modular, humidified gas-fed, zero-gap PEM CO 2 electrolyzer technology.
authors: Yuen Leong Chow, Hsi-Wen Wu, Aimin Li, Yalou Guo, Duhong Chen, Jie Zhang, Paul A. Webley

10.1002/adfm.78377.title: Advances in Electrospun Stimuli-Responsive Smart Fibers: A Review
10.1002/adfm.78377.abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid evolution of flexible electronics and biomedical systems, stimuli-responsive smart fibers have emerged as important functional materials. Electrospinning serves as a versatile fabrication route for micro/nanofibers, enabling tunable fiber morphologies, high porosity, and large specific surface areas to regulate the structure-property relationships of stimuli-responsive smart fibers. This review systematically summarizes the fundamentals, structural design strategies, fabrication technologies, and applications of electrospun stimuli-responsive smart fibers. The response mechanisms underlying seven typical stimuli, including temperature, light, pH, humidity, force, magnetism, and electricity, are first discussed. Subsequently, material selection, electrospinning strategies, and structural design approaches are discussed, highlighting how architecture and interfacial regulation govern response speed, sensitivity, and cycling stability. Furthermore, recent advances in five core application domains, including optical responses, wettability switching, shape-morphing actuation, energy harvesting/storage, and signal transduction, are summarized. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed, with emphasis on multi-stimulus coupling, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted fabrication, and green scalable production. Overall, this review provides comprehensive theoretical guidance for the development and industrial translation of high-performance intelligent fiber materials.
authors: Jingjing Lei, Jingge Ju, Zongjie Li, Lu Gao, Zhongxiang Lei, Yanfei Chen, Yongcheng Wang, Zijia Yan, Weimin Kang

10.1002/adfm.78364.title: AI-Enabled Organoid Chips for Modeling and Decoding Nerve-Tumor Interactions
10.1002/adfm.78364.abstract: ABSTRACT The nervous system is emerging as a central regulator of tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. However, the dynamic mechanisms linking neural activity to malignant, immune, and barrier states remain difficult to dissect in vivo. Animal models capture key aspects of cancer neuroscience, but poorly control human-specific multicellular interfaces, neural activity, secreted signals, and real-time readouts. AI-enabled organoid chip platforms offer a complementary route to reconstruct and interrogate the nerve-tumor interface by integrating human-derived organoids, microfluidic control, sensing, and computational modeling. Here we review advances in nerve-tumor organoids and integrate relevant progress in microfluidics, in situ functional sensing, and AI-driven modeling. These systems can enable controlled studies of perineural invasion, nerve-mediated immune regulation, trans-barrier drug responses, and longitudinal functional states. Key challenges include model standardization, long-term stability, multimodal data interpretation, and clinical translation. AI-enabled organoid chip platforms could help shift cancer neuroscience from descriptive observation towards perturbable, human-relevant and data-rich systems for mechanism discovery and precision therapy assessment.
authors: Junlei Han, Fanwei Meng, Jiemeng Ding, Jun Chen, Li Wang, Chaoyang Shi

10.1002/adfm.78206.title: Micro-Area Interface Regulation for Electromagnetic Responses: Mechanisms, Architectures, and Functional Integration
10.1002/adfm.78206.abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid evolution of communication technologies, the integration density of modern electronic devices has increased dramatically. This progress has, however, exacerbated electromagnetic pollution across various application scenarios, creating an urgent demand for high-performance electromagnetic (EM) absorption materials. As the fundamental “building block” that governs the intrinsic properties of functional materials, micro-area interfaces hold tremendous potential for optimizing microwave absorption performance. Tailored micro-area interfaces can trigger a cascade of beneficial effects, including enhanced interface polarization, optimized hierarchical structure, amplified magnetic coupling, facilitated conductive network, and precise modulation of electronic state, all of which contribute to stronger attenuation and absorption of incident microwaves. This paper outlines a dual-dimensional regulation strategy to maximize the microwave energy response of absorption materials: interface topology reconstruction for assembling-pattern materials, and surface interface modification for supported-pattern materials. This approach enables precise tuning of component compatibility, defect configuration, and charge transfer efficiency at the micro-area interfaces, unlocking full absorption potential. We further review current advances in multifunctional and intelligent EM absorption devices enabled by micro-area interface engineering. Finally, the existing challenges in interface visualization/stability, along with corresponding possible solutions, are presented, and the future development direction is also outlined.
authors: Jinxu Li, Xinmin Yu, Kangli Yin, Mingyue Yuan, Xinsong Xu, Ge Ma, Ke Pei, Wenbin You, Han-Wen Cheng, Renchao Che

10.1002/adfm.78379.title: Triggering Interfacial Magnetoelectric Coupling at Layered Oxide Cathodes for High-Rate Na-Ion Storage
10.1002/adfm.78379.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered oxide cathodes have been recognized as prospective cathode materials for Na-ion batteries (NIBs) owing to their high energy density and low cost. However, the cycling stability and rate capability are hindered by sluggish Na + diffusion kinetics and severe interfacial side reactions. Herein, a ferromagnetic layer is constructed at the interface between layered oxide cathodes and electrolyte, triggering a remarkable magnetoelectric effect to achieve high-rate Na + storage. First, a uniform ion distribution across the cathode-electrolyte interface is promoted, and interfacial ion accumulation is mitigated, as Na + ions are subjected during cycling to a Lorentz force generated by the combined tangential and normal magnetic components. Second, an interfacial electric field is formed between the ferromagnetic modification layer and the layered oxide cathode due to their different work function, significantly boosting the charge diffusion kinetics during the reversible reaction. Third, the magnetoelectric effect guides the nucleation and growth of the cathode-electrolyte interface, promoting a thin, uniform, and NaF-rich layer that enhances interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the exceptional rate (up to 20 C) and cycling capabilities (78.2% retention after 1000 cycles) are achieved, highlighting the effectiveness and significance of regulating interfacial charge transport by activating the interfacial magnetoelectric coupling effect.
authors: Ren Huang, Haolin Zhang, Dong Yan, Yibing Zhang, Caiyan Yu, Wei-Kong Pang, Zhenxiang Cheng, Peng Lv, Hui Ying Yang, Ying Bai

10.1002/adfm.78059.title: Synergistic Coordination and Interface of Carbon Nanomaterials with Metal-Organic Frameworks for Pharmaceutical Wastewater Remediation: Path to Scalable, Circular, and Industrially Viable Solutions
10.1002/adfm.78059.abstract: ABSTRACT Global pharmaceutical consumption, projected to exceed $1.5 trillion by 2030, threatens aquatic ecosystems and public health. This review demonstrates that integrating metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with carbon nanomaterials (CNMs) into MOF@CNM heterostructures delivers a breakthrough in water remediation via synergistic metal-oxygen-carbon (M-O-C) electronic coupling. A meta-analysis of >50 studies indicates that metal node structure (42%), carbon dimensionality (22%), and pharmaceutical class (14%) dictate 78% of performance variance. d 0 metal nodes favor polar antibiotic binding, whereas d 9 nodes drive π-complexation with hydrophobic drugs. However, these interactions also depend on node accessibility, linker chemistry, drug speciation, and solution pH. Furthermore, CNMs extend charge carrier lifetimes from 2-4 ns to 8-15 ns via π-π orbital hybridization, enhancing adsorption 3.4-fold and photocatalysis 4.7-fold. However, matrix interference drops removal efficiency from 98% in pure water to 48% in raw wastewater. Meta-regression identifies carbon functionalization as the strongest synergy driver (coefficient = +1.95, p < 0.001), favouring in situ growth over postsynthetic assembly at an optimal 15-25 wt% carbon loading. To bridge the laboratory-to-scale gap and combat the 10 million annual deaths from antimicrobial resistance projected by 2050, future design must prioritize pharmaceutical properties (polarity, lipophilicity , p K a ), anti-fouling heterostructures, continuous-flow reactors, and >90% material circularity.

10.1002/adfm.79128.title: Elementally Biocompatible Flexible Optoelectronic Platforms With Intrinsic UV Dose Integration and Transient Sensing-Computing Capability
10.1002/adfm.79128.abstract: ABSTRACT Excessive UV exposure is a major cause of skin damage, yet practical wearable UV monitoring systems require not only mechanical compliance but also long-term biological and environmental compatibility. Here, we report an elementally biocompatible flexible optoelectronic transistor (EBOT) platform in which all functional components are constructed from physiologically relevant elements. Zn-Mg-based oxides serve as the semiconductor and dielectric layers, Mg acts the electrode, and biodegradable poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-4-hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB) provides a flexible substrate and encapsulation layer. A low-temperature, all-hard-mask fabrication strategy enables device and circuit patterning without photolithography, preserving the compatibility of the constituent materials. Post-fabrication supercritical-fluid treatment further optimizes the device characteristics, improving the on/off ratio, responsivity and detectivity by 48.1%, 7.5% and 16.8%, respectively. Rather than eliminating persistent photoconductivity, we harness defect-mediated carrier trapping and relaxation as an intrinsic temporal integration mechanism, allowing a single device to simultaneously encode UV dose and exposure history without additional memory components. The EBOT platform exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and mechanical durability over 1,000 bending cycles. Furthermore, vertically integrated sensing-computing architectures are demonstrated by stacking photodetection and logic functionalities, providing a pathway toward highly integrated transient bioelectronic systems. This work establishes an elementally compatible strategy for developing flexible and environmentally transient optoelectronic platforms.
authors: Xiaozheng Jia, Ruixuan Ma, Yulin Cai, Lei Li, Buke Shen, Zehao Chen, Ziyan Guo, Xiaoqing Bao, Kuan-Chang Chang

10.1002/adfm.79161.title: LiTFSI-Regulated Free-Standing Conductive Polymer Hydrogels for Flexible Supercapacitors
10.1002/adfm.79161.abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of flexible and wearable electronics necessitates energy-storage materials that reconcile high electrochemical performance with robust mechanical deformability and environmental adaptability. Here, we design a free-standing conductive hydrogel electrode by integrating poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) into a polyacrylamide/poly(vinyl alcohol) (PAAm/PVA) double-network scaffold, using lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) as an ionic modulator. The dual-network PAAm/PVA skeleton provides robust deformable support, while LiTFSI incorporation is associated with changes in PEDOT chain conformation, intermolecular packing, and nanoscale organization. These structural changes accompany the improved electrical and electrochemical performance of the PEDOT:PSS-PAAm/PVA-LiTFSI (PPLi) hydrogel. The optimized PPLi hydrogel exhibits high conductivity (28.4 S cm −1 on average, 33.2 S cm −1 at maximum), high specific capacitance (202.5 F g −1 ), excellent stretchability (∼506%), and excellent anti-freezing capacity down to −40°C. The assembled all-hydrogel symmetric supercapacitor delivers superior energy output, outstanding capacitance retention of 98.8% over 10 000 cycles, and stable output under twisting, folding, and 100% tensile strain. The device retains 85% capacitance at −40°C and powers wearable electronics when integrated into flexible wristbands. This work provides a mild and scalable strategy for coupling three-dimensional free-standing architectures with ionic regulation to develop conductive polymer hydrogel electrodes with high mechanical robustness and electrochemical efficiency for wearable energy-storage applications.
authors: Lekun Liu, Qing Chen, Liang Xu, Yongguang Wang, Liang Zhang, Xiang Lin, Min Gong, Fengxian Gao, Dongrui Wang

10.1002/adfm.79265.title: Medium-Entropy Hydroxides Enable Bridge-Bound NO Stabilization and Hydrogen Spillover for Nitrite-to-Ammonia Electroreduction
10.1002/adfm.79265.abstract: ABSTRACT Electroreduction of nitrite provides a route to couple aqueous nitrite remediation with ammonia synthesis, but high selectivity requires coordinated nitrite deoxygenation and surface-hydrogen delivery. Here, we report ultrathin NiFeCoCu medium-entropy layered double hydroxide (ME-LDH) nanosheets that promote selective nitrite-to-ammonia conversion by coupling charge-polarized bridge-bound * NO stabilization with hydrogen-spillover-assisted hydrogenation. In neutral K 2 SO 4 electrolyte containing nitrite, the catalyst delivers NH 4 + Faradaic efficiencies above 90% from −0.5 to −0.9 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), reaches a max i mum Faradaic efficiency of 99%, and achieves an NH 4 + yield rate of 7417 µg·h −1 ·cm −2 . Quasi-in situ x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), in situ Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, isotope-resolved spectroscopy, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), kinetic isotope effect (KIE) analysis, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) collectively support dynamic charge redistribution, bridge-bound * NO formation, and rapid generation and consumption of surface active hydrogen, consistent with hydrogen-spillover-assisted hydrogenation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal the preferential stabilization of bridge-bound * NO at multimetal sites and the thermodynamically unfavorable accumulation of isolated H on the fully hydroxylated surface, providing theoretical support for the proposed adsorption-hydrogen-transfer pathway. These findings highlight adsorption-spillover coupling as a promising design strategy for entropy-engineered hydroxides in nitrogen-cycle electrocatalysis.
authors: Jingyi Huang, Xing'an Dong, Qian Liu, Chen Yang, Tianyao Ren, Weidong Dai, Xian Shi, Wendong Zhang, Peng Yu, Fan Dong

10.1002/adfm.79194.title: Native Wood Polyphenol-Driven Construction of Self-Grown Photothermal Interfaces for Salt-Resistant Solar Evaporation
10.1002/adfm.79194.abstract: ABSTRACT Wood-based solar evaporators offer aligned water-transport channels, low thermal conductivity, and renewability. However, most designs rely on externally deposited photothermal components that may compromise interfacial stability and obstruct transport pathways. Here, an endogenous construction strategy is developed by leveraging native polyphenols in eucalyptus wood to create a Janus evaporator with a self-grown Fe-polyphenol (FeP) photothermal interface. Top-protected bottom delignification selectively preserves polyphenolic sites in the top region as Fe coordination anchors while reconstructing the bottom region into a vertically porous, thermally insulating scaffold. Subsequent ascorbic acid (AA)-assisted interfacial evolution enables in situ formation of the FeP interface. The hydrated FeP/AA-delignified eucalyptus wood (FeP/AA-DEW) exhibits an AM1.5G-weighted solar absorptance of 82.05 ± 2.47% and a steady evaporation rate of 2.83 kg m −2 h −1 under standardized 1-sun conditions. Boundary-dependent experiments show that the high evaporation flux arises from absorbed solar energy, reduced equivalent evaporation enthalpy, and environmental heat exchange. The evaporator maintains 2.56 ± 0.04 kg m −2 h −1 in 20 wt.% NaCl, stable operation over 14 d, and 12.10 kg m −2 cumulative water loss during 8 h of outdoor operation. This work provides a native-chemistry-driven route for durable biomass-based solar evaporation.
authors: Qi Gao, Jie Wu, Dawei Pan, Wenji Yu, Yahui Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79248.title: Dynamic Solvation Perturbation Enables Fast-Exchange Interfacial Water Regulation for Stable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79248.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial instability remains the major barrier for practical aqueous zinc batteries. Conventional electrolyte design mainly focuses on reducing water coordination number in the Zn 2+ solvation shell. However, this static criterion often neglects ligand-exchange kinetics and can still leave highly reactive water at the interface. Herein, we propose a dynamic solvation perturbation (DSP) strategy to regulate Zn 2+ solvation through transient solvent coordination. Descriptor-guided screening identifies methyl acetate (MA) as an optimal modulator with balanced Zn 2+ coordination and water regulation. MA forms a fast-exchange mixed solvation sheath, shortens water residence time, and passivates residual water via dynamic solvation-shell rearrangement. Additionally, MA exhibits facet-selective adsorption on Zn anode, which suppresses direct water attack and promotes uniform Zn nucleation. As a result, the DSP-regulated electrolyte enables the Zn anode to achieve long-term cycling life over 8000 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . Remarkably, stable cycling is maintained for more than 2000 h at 32% DOD and more than 1000 h at 80% DOD. In addition, the Zn||V 2 O 5 pouch-cell with the MA-containing electrolyte exhibits approximately 80% capacity retention over 300 cycles at 0.1 A g −1 , highlighting its potential for practical applications.
authors: Qian Xiang, Zhibo Liu, Xiaoling Zhang, Ying Sun, Yong Guo, Yongming Jin, Jixi Guo, Dianzeng Jia, Xingchao Wang

10.1002/adfm.79258.title: Dedicated Convection Window Design for Activating Internal Self-Generation Convection to Accumulate Vapor Diffusion
10.1002/adfm.79258.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar-driven interfacial evaporation technology offers a groundbreaking approach to water treatment. However, the relentless pursuit of high energy efficiency has encountered a bottleneck in vapor generation, necessitating consideration of vapor diffusion. To tackle these limitations, this work establishes a comprehensive liquid-liquid-vapor transport kinetics framework, which couples water transport, vapor generation, vapor diffusion, and thermal management. This system optimizes water transport while minimizing thermal losses by tailoring the pore architecture. More importantly, we design dedicated convection windows for activating internal self-generation convection to accelerate vapor dissipation. This system delivered a superior evaporation rate of 4.93 kg m −2 h −1 , exceeding the conventional designs (2.9 kg m −2 h −1 ) while achieving energy efficiency of 89.6% (considering both environmental heat gain and convective heat gain). This enhancement stems from the efficient vapor generation and release process, driven by the synergistic interplay of water transport, thermal management, and convection control. Outdoor experiments demonstrate that the optimized array system achieves a water production rate of approximately 1.95 kg m −2 h −1 without any detectable contamination. This illustrates that this strategy can be used for maximizing the performance of 3D evaporators.
authors: Jun Guo, Jun Hou, Ning Xu, Wenxin Lu, Wei Ding, Guoxiang You, Jun Wu, Lingzhan Miao, Yanhui Ao

10.1002/adfm.79263.title: Deformation-Robust Multimodal Electronic Skin Enabled by Conformal Surface Plasmons for Cross-Medium Robotic Perception
10.1002/adfm.79263.abstract: ABSTRACT Electronic skins (e-skins) generally transduce contact mechanics but cannot interrogate materials concealed by packaging, limiting robotic perception to accessible surfaces. A multimodal cross-medium e-skin is developed by co-designing a five-channel piezoresistive network and a conformal surface-plasmon (CSP) waveguide within a shared flexible interdigitated-electrode architecture. The piezoresistive channel maps grasp pressure over 0-140 kPa with response and recovery times below 50 ms, whereas the CSP channel confines microwaves to a subwavelength near field for phase-based pre-touch sensing and frequency-resolved electromagnetic fingerprinting. Strong field localization preserves transmission fingerprints under bending and twisting up to 80° and enables interrogation through glass, plastic, and paper containers. Coupled with a support vector machine, these fingerprints discriminate 16 sample classes with 99.4% test accuracy and 99.7% leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy. When integrated with a dexterous robotic hand, the platform unifies grasp-pressure mapping, proximity perception, and nondestructive recognition of hidden contents. This shared-architecture strategy transforms conformal plasmonic waveguides into deformation-tolerant functional sensing interfaces and extends e-skin beyond contact-limited tactile sensing toward cross-medium robotic perception.
authors: Yongze Li, He Gao, Lang Yuan, Ting Cui, Minglu Zhu, Jian He, Tao Chen

10.1002/adfm.79250.title: High-Entropy Platinum-Group Metal Phosphide Atomic Layers With Controlled Phosphorization for Electrocatalytic Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.79250.abstract: ABSTRACT High-entropy phosphides (HEP), derived from high-entropy alloys (HEA), combine multimetallic active sites with phosphorus-induced structural and electronic modulation, yet remain difficult to construct at the atomic-layer scale. Here, a two-step phosphorization and epitaxial-growth strategy is developed to synthesize Pd@PdP@HEP nanocrystals with surface-confined PdPtIrRhRuP HEP atomic layers. This design is further supported by density functional theory (DFT) formation-energy calculations, which indicate that P preferentially occupies surface and near-surface sites. Controlled phosphorization of Pd cubic seeds enables systematic regulation of P incorporation, lattice expansion, and structural disorder, while subsequent multimetallic growth produces compositionally complex surface layers. Electron microscopy and synchrotron-based X-ray absorption spectroscopy confirm the formation of P-enriched HEP atomic layers and reveal strong electronic coupling between P and neighboring metal atoms. The optimized Pd@PdP@HEP catalyst exhibits higher alkaline hydrogen-evolution activity than commercial Pt/C and the unphosphorized Pd@HEA counterpart, while maintaining excellent durability. DFT calculations show that P-induced surface reconstruction and charge redistribution downshift the d-band center, bring the hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔG H* ) closer to thermoneutrality, and shift the hydroxyl adsorption free energy (ΔG OH* ) toward more positive values. These effects create a balanced adsorption environment, contribute to enhanced alkaline hydrogen-evolution kinetics, and provide an effective strategy for engineering nonmetal-modified high-entropy catalysts.
