10.1002/adfm.78287.title: Distributed Haptic Chips With Materials’ Multifunctionalities for Dual-Way Tactile Communication Enabled Terrain Recognition and Reconstruction in Robotic Teleoperation
10.1002/adfm.78287.abstract: ABSTRACT Current robotic teleoperations rely on vision-based detection and feedback of the operation environment. Establishing dual-way tactile sensing and feedback remains challenging for improving comprehensive status awareness. Here, with the aid of laser induced graphene and silicone materials, we present a haptic chip capable of providing multi-dimensional and multi-modal tactile sensing and feedback for both the master side and slave side in a teleoperation system. A triboelectric and piezoresistive sensing array with three-dimensional dynamic and static tactile sensing. The space of triboelectrification is re-used as pneumatic haptic feedback at the master side, and the laser induced graphene layer of the piezoresistive sensor also can be used as a thermal heater. Moreover, a piezoelectric chip is also integrated to offer high-frequency tactile sensing and feedback. Multiple haptic chips can implement a distributed tactile communication network. A hexapod with haptic chips allows the basic identification of territory, attitude, and texture during walking and climbing. Meanwhile, they can then be selectively regenerated at the haptic chip array of the master side directly, and control commands can be sent out by the haptic chip as well. Overall, the haptic chip-based tactile communication system acts as a complementary control interface to the vision system, which possesses advantages for the teleoperation of robots in special tasks.
authors: Minglu Zhu, Junyi Chen, Xinyu Wang, Ke Chen, Kuihan Chen, Chang Li, Zhongyi Lin, Yongze Li, Tao Chen, Jian He

10.1002/adfm.78263.title: Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion-Resistant Alloys: Mechanisms and Design Strategies
10.1002/adfm.78263.abstract: ABSTRACT Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) is a widespread degradation challenge threatening metallic infrastructure in marine and industrial environments. Conventional materials-based mitigation approaches act primarily as external barriers and do not directly control the coupled microbial, electrochemical, and microstructural processes that govern long-term damage. Unlike previous reviews organized primarily by microbial taxa or protection technologies, this review establishes a mechanism-oriented framework that maps distinct MIC pathways to guide the rational design of MIC-resistant alloys. The fundamental MIC mechanisms, including metabolite-induced corrosion, oxygen concentration cells, and extracellular electron transfer, are outlined to establish the basis for bespoke materials design. Three interrelated design strategies are proposed: (i) microbial-level inhibition through antibacterial alloying; (ii) interfacial regulation through passive film engineering to regulate charge transfer; and (iii) microstructure-integrated design, including nanoprecipitates, multiphase structures, and multicomponent alloys, to achieve synergistic antibacterial, mechanical and corrosion-resistant performance. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward durable and adaptive MIC-resistant materials are discussed, providing guidance for bridging mechanistic understanding and engineering applications.
authors: Jiaqi Li, Miaomiao Cui, Hang Yu, Di Wang, Enze Zhou, Jiahang Li, Yu Wu, Tingyue Gu, Fuhui Wang, Arjan Mol, Dake Xu

10.1002/adfm.79293.title: How the Porous Transport Layer Dictates Membrane Electrode Assembly Performance of IrO2 Catalysts
10.1002/adfm.79293.abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing the use of precious metals is essential for the commercialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). The Schottky contact formed between the catalyst layer and Ti porous transport layer (PTL) at the anode significantly degrades cell performance and necessitates high Ir loading or Pt coating. IrO 2 catalysts with various crystallite sizes (1.7-11.0 nm) were synthesized, and their membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performance was evaluated at a low Ir loading of 0.3 mg Ir cm −2 using Pt-coated Ti PTL and bare Ti PTL. The MEA performance exhibited opposite trends depending on the type of PTL, primarily due to variation in the work function, which is determined by the surface oxygen configuration of the IrO 2 catalyst. Smaller crystallites exhibited a larger work function, resulting in a greater performance discrepancy between the two PTL types. To overcome the suboptimal performance of IrO 2 , we utilized the crystalline 7.1 nm-sized IrO 2 as an electron pathway and deposited highly active amorphous IrO x on its surface. This mixed-phase Ir oxide exhibited good cell performance and durability even with a bare Ti PTL. This study highlights that the Schottky contact problem of IrO 2 catalysts can be overcome through surface engineering, enabling low Ir use for PEMWE.
authors: Hyeseong Jeon, Seunghee Han, Jonghyeon Park, Sujin Park, Wonjae Lee, Jihan Kim, Hyunjoo Lee

10.1002/adfm.79286.title: Topological Insulator-Supported Organic π-Dimers Enable Heterogeneous conPET Photocatalysis for Inert C-X Bond Functionalization
10.1002/adfm.79286.abstract: ABSTRACT The photocatalytic activation of inert aryl halides remains a central challenge in organic synthesis due to their high reduction potentials and limited accessibility by conventional visible-light photocatalysts. Herein, we report a heterogeneous photoredox system based on a topological insulator-supported organic π -dimer, Sb 2 Te 3 @Rubrene 2 2+ , which enables reduction photocatalysis via a consecutive photoinduced electron transfer (conPET) mechanism. Rubrene radical cations self-assemble into stable π -bonded dimers on the Sb 2 Te 3 surface, forming a closed-shell dicationic photosensitizer that undergoes one-electron reduction upon reductive quenching to generate [Sb 2 Te 3 @Rubrene 2 2 ] •- . This intermediate can be further photoexcited to achieve highly negative reduction potentials, enabling the activation of inert C─Br, C─Cl, and even C─F bonds. The resulting carbon-centered radicals can be selectively trapped to afford dehalogenation, C─H, and C─B coupling products with broad substrate scope and high chemoselectivity. This work demonstrates a new strategy for stabilizing reactive organic intermediates through topological interfaces and establishes a heterogeneous conPET platform for reduction photocatalysis.
authors: Jing-Han Li, Cong Ling, Shuai Chen, Hao-Yang Ding, Hong-Bao Li, Ru-Xin Tian, An-Wu Xu

10.1002/adfm.79290.title: Photomultiplication-Type Broadband Organic Photodetectors With an ON/OFF Current Ratio Exceeding 79 000 Enabled by Self-Assembled Ultra-Thin Layer
10.1002/adfm.79290.abstract: ABSTRACT Photomultiplication type broadband organic photodetectors (PM-BOPDs) were fabricated by employing one wide bandgap polymer P3HT and one narrow bandgap non-fullerene acceptor BTPSe-Ph4F with a weight ratio of 100:2 as active layers. Plenty of isolated electron traps will be formed in the active layers due to the rather low BTPSe-Ph4F content, leading to poor electron transport channels and efficient hole transport channels in the P3HT:BTPSe-Ph4F (100:2, w/w) active layers. Photogenerated electrons will be trapped in the isolated BTPSe-Ph4F; the trapped electrons near the Al electrode will induce interfacial band bending for hole tunneling injection from the external circuit. The dark current density of PM-BOPDs can be further suppressed by ∼2 orders of magnitude by employing a 3-BPIC-F self-assembled ultra-thin layer to replace PEDOT:PSS. The optimal PM-BOPDs display an external quantum efficiency of 2970%, an on/off current ratio of 79 020, and specific detectivity of 1.16 × 10 13 Jones at a frequency of 90 Hz at 625 nm light under −10 V bias, indicating strong weak-light sensitivity of PM-BOPDs. The optimized PM-BOPD was employed for photoplethysmography (PPG) monitoring. PPG signals were successfully recorded during rest and exercise, and their characteristics were analyzed to extract heart rate information and identify characteristic pulse wave features.

10.1002/adfm.79282.title: Dipole-Regulated Fullerene Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Wide-Bandgap Solar Cells and All-Perovskite Tandems
10.1002/adfm.79282.abstract: ABSTRACT Endohedral metallofullerenes offer intrinsic cage-confined dipoles and structural compatibility with fullerene electron-transport layers, making them attractive for regulating perovskite interfaces. However, the encapsulated metal ion cannot directly coordinate with surface defects, while the outer carbon cage lacks specific anchoring sites, leading to disordered adsorption configurations, electrostatic heterogeneity, and nonuniform coupling with C 60 . Here, we employ 1-pyreneboronic acid (PyBA) as a molecular director to regulate Gd@C 82 at the wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite/C 60 interface. The boronic acid group anchors to the perovskite surface and passivates undercoordinated Pb-related defects, while the pyrene framework associates with the Gd@C 82 cage and stabilizes favorable molecular configurations. This dual interaction enhances the dipolar character and spatial organization of Gd@C 82 , homogenizes the interfacial potential, and strengthens electronic coupling with C 60 , thereby accelerating electron extraction and suppressing nonradiative recombination. The optimized WBG cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 20.23%, enabling monolithic all-perovskite tandem devices with 28.44% efficiency. The modified WBG devices retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1451 h of maximum-power-point tracking and 1563 h under damp-heat conditions, while the tandem devices retain over 80% after 531 h of operation. This work establishes molecularly directed endohedral metallofullerenes as a strategy for coordinating surface chemistry and interfacial electrostatics.
authors: Cheng Gong, Yuqing Pan, Ke Li, Zipei Wan, Liang Xu, Zijie He, Ting Yang, Yuxin Zhou, Cong Zhang, Haiyun Li

10.1002/adfm.79261.title: Halogen-Engineered Nitrogen-Doped Carbon for Dual Nonradical Peroxymonosulfate Activation in Water Purification
10.1002/adfm.79261.abstract: ABSTRACT Peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based advanced oxidation processes are attractive for water purification but are often limited by short-lived radicals that are easily quenched in complex matrices. Here we report a halogen-modulation strategy to engineer the interfacial microenvironment of nitrogen-doped carbon (N-C) for robust, metal-free PMS activation. A family of halogen-doped carbons (NX-C; X = F, Cl, Br, and I) is synthesized via molten-salt-assisted conversion of ZIF-8, among which bromine-doped N-C (NBr-C) exhibits a lattice-strained, hierarchically porous framework with highly polarized graphitic-N sites. NBr-C delivers a 134-fold enhancement in the phenol degradation rate constant ( k obs = 2.55 min −1 ) and 70.5% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 5 min. Mechanistic experiments combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Br doping steers PMS activation away from short-lived radicals toward dual nonradical pathways: singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) oxidation and a catalyst-mediated direct electron-transfer process. The NBr-C/PMS system maintains nearly complete pollutant removal over pH 3-11, in the presence of common inorganic anions and natural organic matter, in real waters, and under continuous-flow operation. This work establishes halogen-regulated interfacial microenvironment engineering as a powerful principle for designing robust, metal-free PMS activators operating through selective nonradical pathways.
authors: Guoliang Li, Liying Wang, Rui Lv, Congyun Zhang, Zongshan Zhao

10.1002/adfm.79270.title: Harnessing Synergistic Photophysical Processes in Phosphorescent Carbon Dots for Multifunctional Neuromorphic Vision
10.1002/adfm.79270.abstract: ABSTRACT Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials hold immense potential for neuromorphic vision, yet achieving system-level cognitive capabilities within a single material remains challenging. Here, we design a carbon dots (CDs)-epoxy composite wherein hydrogen-bond-mediated interfacial assembly between electron-donating CDs surface groups and electron-accepting epoxy moieties deliberately generates interfacial exciplexes. This engineered interface achieves a minimized singlet-triplet energy gap and enhanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC), enabling efficient intersystem crossing (ISC) into a long-lived triplet reservoir that emits green phosphorescence (∼468 ms). We obtain multiple neuromorphic functions by exploiting the exciplex kinetics. Ultraviolet (UV)-dose-dependent triplet filling enables optical learning and noisy pattern capture. The cooperative effect in densely populated exciplex networks establishes an intensity-gated threshold for spontaneous physical noise reduction at the sensory terminal. Alternating UV-induced hydrogen-bond strengthening and near infrared-induced photothermal relaxation bidirectionally modulate exciplex populations, realizing all-optical plasticity with high symmetry (AR = 0.33) that supports a fully connected neural network achieving >95% recognition accuracy on noisy digits. The millisecond-lived triplet reservoir further transcribes dynamic motion trajectories into static 2D afterglow patterns, enabling contactless trajectory recognition and real-time control without high-speed cameras. This work provides a unified material strategy integrating sensing, memory, and computation within a single neuromorphic visual terminal.
authors: Zihan Ying, Yi Zhang, Jiahao Fan, Mengqi Li, Siqi Liu, Jun Zhang, Fangjian Xing, Cihui Liu, Dan Zhu, Yingchun Cheng, Yunsong Di, Chaofeng Gao, Xiangxing Xu, Zhixing Gan

10.1002/adfm.79056.title: Solvent-Free Roll-Pressed Sandwiched Li Anode With Dual-Sided Cu Nanowire Networks for High-Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79056.abstract: ABSTRACT Li metal anodes are promising for next-generation high-energy batteries, but their practical use is hindered by dendritic Li growth, unstable interfaces, and large volume fluctuations. Herein, we report a bidirectional sandwich-structured Li metal anode (SLA) fabricated through a solvent-free rolling and pressing strategy. The SLA integrates an ultrathin Li layer with thermally stable 3D Cu nanowire networks on both sides, forming a lightweight, flexible, and mechanically robust electrode. The interconnected Cu nanowire framework provides continuous electron pathways, homogenizes current distribution, and accommodates Li volume changes, thereby guiding uniform Li deposition and stripping within the electrode interior. Benefiting from this design, the SLA achieves a high Coulombic efficiency of 98.73% over 250 cycles at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 , while symmetric cells operate stably for over 1350 h with low polarization. Full cells paired with high-loading NCM811 cathodes deliver excellent cycling stability and rate capability. For a 4-layer stacked pouch cell, the SLA-based system delivers a gravimetric energy density of 279.11 Wh kg −1 and a volumetric energy density of 470.52 Wh L −1 , outperforming the PLA counterpart. This work provides a simple strategy for advancing stable Li metal anodes and high-energy-density Li metal batteries.
authors: Jianyu Chen, Zhaoci Guo, Xudong Chen, Zhao Ge, Yuwei Huang, Yu Zhang, Zhen Shen, Yizhou Wang, Yanwen Ma, Jin Zhao

10.1002/adfm.79173.title: Ultralow-Bias-Switchable Dual-Mode Retinomorphic Device for Adaptive Extreme-Exposure Image Restoration and Event-Driven Light Source Positioning
10.1002/adfm.79173.abstract: ABSTRACT Safe operation of autonomous driving vision systems requires integrated photodetection and processing capabilities. However, existing vision systems remain constrained by separated architectures and limited adaptability to complex lighting environments. Here, we report a TiO 2 /ZnIn 2 S 4 heterostructure dual-mode optoelectronic device, enabling on-demand switching between photodetection and optoelectronic synaptic functions under an ultralow bias of 1 mV. The type-I heterojunction integrates highly ordered TiO 2 nanotube arrays for directional carrier transport, oxygen vacancies for carrier trapping, and layered ZnIn 2 S 4 nanosheets for enhanced light harvesting and interfacial carrier transfer, enabling bias-dependent carrier separation and release. As a result, the device exhibits efficient photodetection and tunable synaptic dynamics, enabling adaptive exposure compensation and dynamic image restoration for both overexposed and underexposed visual scenes. When configured into bioinspired spheroidal vision arrays, it further supports wide-field detection, targeted localization, and early warning of potential hazards. This device highlights a promising approach for adaptive machine vision toward intelligent perception in autonomous driving scenarios.
authors: Linglong Wu, Ruotao Yu, Jiaxin Chen, Wentao Xu

10.1002/adfm.79273.title: Super-Toughness Self-Healing Bimetallic MOF-based Composite Solid Electrolyte with Nanoconfined Ion Channels and Dynamic Crosslinking for High-Performance Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79273.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state lithium metal batteries are considered ideal candidates for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density and safety. However, NCM811||Li battery systems face severe issues in practical application, such as interface failure between the cathode and anode, lithium dendrite growth, and the insufficient stability of conventional electrolytes. Here, we proposed a synergistic modification strategy combined with nanoconfined polymerization and interface dynamic crosslinking to fabricate self-healing bimetallic MOF-based composite solid electrolyte with enhanced ionic conduction and interface stability. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits high room-temperature ionic conductivity (12.63×10 −4 S cm − 1 ), extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.14 V), excellent elongation at break (270%), high puncture resistance (5.28 N), superior thermal stability (200 °C), and outstanding cycling stability (94.77% retention over 150 cycles at 0.1 C), which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. Even under high mass loadings of 9.24 mg cm − 2 and 20.38 mg cm − 2 for the cathode, the capacity retention rates can still reach 90.88% and 86.35% after 150 and 100 cycles, respectively, demonstrating practical potential under high-loading conditions. This strategy reconstructs the Li + transport, interface stability, and recyclability of composite solid electrolytes at the molecular level, paving the way for the development of next-generation high-performance solid-state batteries.
authors: Bo Peng, Feng Zou, Zhihong Yao, Shixin Liu, Runwei Mo

10.1002/adfm.79271.title: Fatigue-Resistant Biaxially Stretchable Micro-Origami Structured Electrodes
10.1002/adfm.79271.abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable electrodes are essential for next generation wearable electronics, but simultaneously achieving high conductivity, large stretchability, and long-term reliability remains challenging. This work proposes a micro-origami structured electrode (MOSE) that mitigates the conflicts between stretchability, conductivity and fatigue resistance. By prefabricating valley creases of origami pattern on an EcoFlex substrate, the Platinum (Pt) film/EcoFlex substrate bilayer undergoes bending deformation along the creases upon release of biaxial pre-stretch, forming regular and controllable micro-origami structures. Benefiting from the surface metal film, the initial conductivity reaches 19600 S·cm −1 . Furthermore, the micro-origami structure enables the electrode to withstand biaxial tensile strains over 80%, and the high regularity of the origami structure provides excellent fatigue resistance (after 10000 cycles at 50% strain, the sheet resistance remains below 20 Ω/sq). Based on this electrode, a capacitive pressure sensor with high signal repeatability is fabricated. Utilizing the anisotropy of the micro-origami structure, handwriting signal classification using one single small pressure sensor (approximately 2 cm 2 ) instead of large-area sensor array is achieved, with an accuracy of 96%. The proposed MOSE provides a design route for metal-film-based stretchable electrodes.
authors: Yifei Huang, Yujun Deng, Peiyun Yi, Linfa Peng

10.1002/adfm.79213.title: In Situ Electric Tuning―An Emerging STM Tactic for Probing Exotic Quantum Materials
10.1002/adfm.79213.abstract: ABSTRACT In situ electric tuning (ISET) integrated with scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS) has established itself as a highly effective methodology for controlling quantum electronic states in low-dimensional materials. This approach combines the sub-atomic spatial resolution and meV-resolved spectroscopic capability of STM with the reversible and continuously tunable carrier modulation of field-effect device architectures. To date, this approach has been applied to numerous systems, including graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures, correlated electron systems, and moiré superlattice systems hosting emergent quantum phases. Herein, we systematically summarize the state-of-the-art experimental implementations, including global electrostatic gating, tip-induced local gating, tip-induced voltage pulse, and in-plane electric tuning, accompanied with distinct physics under each configuration. We then highlight key representative advances in resolving gate-dependent band renormalization, correlated insulating states, charge ordering, symmetry breaking, and electrically driven metastable phases at the nanoscale. We discuss practical limitations, such as restricted carrier-density ranges, tip-induced perturbations, dielectric reliability, and challenges in decoupling electric effects from current injection and Joule heating. Looking forward, we outline future directions in device engineering, including programmable local electrostatics, scalable architectures, and integrated platforms for operando studies, highlighting their potential to enable deterministic control of emergent quantum phases in functional materials.
authors: Pin Lyu, Yizhou Zhao, Yixuan Han, Yang Wang, Ying Liu, Jiong Lu, Yanpeng Liu

10.1002/adfm.79227.title: Current-Controlled Inactive Aluminum Loss: Quantification, Mechanism, and Mitigation via Stack Pressure for Long-Cycle Al-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79227.abstract: ABSTRACT Aluminum-ion batteries are a promising energy storage technology for high resource abundance, safety, and cost-effectiveness advantages, but practical implementation is hindered by two degradation mechanisms in Al metal anode: electrically isolated metallic aluminum (iAl 0 ) and electrochemical side-reaction products (iSEI Al 3+ ). Precise quantification of these inactive species and relationships with cycling reversibility have rarely been established, limiting rational anode design. Here, we develop a basic titration gas chromatography technology to accurately quantify iAl 0 and iSEI Al 3+ , revealing a current density-dependent Al loss mechanism: iSEI Al 3+ loss dominates at low current, while metallic iAl 0 loss prevails at high current. We discover that an inorganic-dominated interphase favors significant suppression of inactive Al formation. Applying an optimal stack pressure strategy (780 kPa) constructs tip-localized stack pressure/electric field, effectively reducing inactive Al loss by 81.99% and prolonging battery cycling life by ≥500%. These advancements offer fundamental theory and techniques for Al anode reaction mechanism research and provide design principles for high-performance aluminum-ion battery.
authors: Yaoyao Liu, Yushuang Yang, Haichen Huang, Haoying Qi, Xianglin Yin, Xingmin Yu, Shuhua Wang, Jian-Jun Wang, Yuanhua Sang, Peihua Zhu, Hong Liu, Weijia Zhou, Hao Chen

10.1002/adfm.77623.title: High-Entropy Perovskites for Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Progress, Challenges, and Prospects
10.1002/adfm.77623.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical energy storage and conversion systems powered by renewables underpin the clean energy transition, yet sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) severely limits energy efficiency, driving demand for efficient OER catalysts. Perovskites stand out for adjustable electronic structures and strong catalytic activity. High-entropy perovskites (HEPs), with multiple principal lattice elements, gain stable phases from configurational entropy and favorable electronic states via multicomponent synergy, promising OER performance. However, their vast compositional range renders trial-and-error development ineffective, hindering structure-activity analysis and targeted catalyst design. Covering oxide and halide HEPs, this review summarizes advances in HEP OER catalysts over four aspects: synthetic routes, performance regulation, mechanistic analysis via computation, and AI-driven rational design (covering material screening, descriptor mining, and activity prediction). Unlike prior reviews covering separate high-entropy oxides, standard perovskites, or general AI catalysis, this work builds a closed logical loop for HEPs spanning synthesis, experiment, mechanism, and rational design. An outlook on AI-assisted HEP electrocatalysis is offered to inform the development of advanced OER catalytic systems.

10.1002/adfm.78435.title: Reconstruction of Coal Gangue-Derived Porous Carbon/Silica-Alumina for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
10.1002/adfm.78435.abstract: ABSTRACT High-value utilization of industrial coal gangue (CG) solid waste presents formidable environmental and technical challenges, especially in tailoring charge transport to realize high-performance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption whilst retaining its native structural and chemical attributes. Herein, we propose a carbon ash reconstruction strategy that confines nanoscale SiAl within porous carbon (PC) and tailors component contents to regulate charge behaviors, thereby achieving electromagnetic performance inversion. Specifically, alkali melting coupled with acid picking activates the inert SiAl phase, refining its particle size from 328.35 to 25.78 nm, and enabling homogeneous dispersion within PC while maintaining structural integrity. Furthermore, the dielectric discrepancy between PC and SiAl, together with gelation-induced interface bridge-oxygen bonding (C─O─Al and C─O─Si), enhances interfacial polarization and reduces electron migration barriers. Notably, reconstructed CG exhibits a remarkable performance inversion of microwave absorption capacity, expanding the effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) from 0 to 5.05 GHz at an ultrathin thickness of 1.5 mm. This work elucidates the reconstruction strategy roles in spatial confinement, interfacial chemistry, and electronic modulation in solid waste utilization, providing a theoretical foundation and scalable pathway for sustainable materials engineering.
