10.1002/adfm.79295.title: Modulation of Surface-Associated Transport in (Bi 1-x Sb x ) 2 Te 3 via Battery- Inspired Solid-State Iontronic Gating
10.1002/adfm.79295.abstract: ABSTRACT Topological insulators (TIs) possess unique topological surface states (TSS) with strong spin-momentum locking. This leads to a large net surface spin accumulation when a surface charge current flows, thereby efficiently exerting a strong spin-orbit torque (SOT) on an adjacent ferromagnet. However, the effectiveness of TSS transport is largely constrained by the Fermi-level (E F ) position set by composition during growth and can hardly be adjusted afterward. In this work, we investigate the effectiveness of solid-state iontronic gating for modulating the relative contributions of bulk-like and surface-associated transport in (Bi 1-x Sb x ) 2 Te 3 (BST) at technologically relevant gate biases (V g < 2 V). In a battery-inspired device geometry, a 7 QL-thick BST is interfaced with a solid-state electrolyte and an anode-like Li-ion reservoir, thereby making the cathode-like BST gate-tunable. Using magnetotransport measurements together with phenomenological two-carrier/weak anti-localization (WAL) analyses, we track gate-dependent transport signatures consistent with a valve-like modulation of surface-associated transport fingerprints, with the strongest WAL-associated coherent transport signatures emerging near the transport-defined carrier compensation regime. Our findings suggest that this battery-like three-terminal device geometry can be a promising strategy for low-voltage reconfigurable spintronic applications such as tunable SOT, directional spin information processing, or quantum information channel allocation.

10.1002/adfm.79176.title: Functional Surface Self-Assembly on Nitinol Biliary Stents for Enhanced Anti-Fouling and Low-Friction Behavior
10.1002/adfm.79176.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitinol (NiTi) stents are widely used for biliary decompression, but their biofluid-exposed metallic surfaces remain susceptible to mechanical irritation, bacterial colonization, sludge deposition, and inflammation-associated restenosis. Inspired by the dynamic, low-adhesion interfacial function of the native glycocalyx, we developed a self-assembled slippery liquid-infused porous surface (SASLIPS) for NiTi biliary stents. The modified surface formed a continuous liquid-infused architecture, exhibited water sliding angles <0.5°, and reduced adhesion under the tested conditions. SASLIPS decreased the coefficient of friction (COF) from 0.69 (NiTi) to 0.09 (SASLIPS), reduced biliary sludge accretion, inhibited 96.98% of E. coli adhesion and biofilm formation, and attenuated inflammatory responses, while preserving macroscopic thermally induced shape recovery. Molecular dynamics simulations supported favorable interactions between perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) and perfluorodecalin (PFD) and showed that the PFD-rich interfacial region reduced water and cholesterol access to the modeled substrate. In a porcine study with independent 1- and 6-month cohorts, SASLIPS-coatedstents showed 89.92% lower sludge-associated autofluorescence than bare NiTi stents at 1 month and no gross evidence of luminal obstruction at the 6-month retrieval. This work established a liquid-infused fluorinated surface strategy for engineering anti-fouling, anti-inflammatory, and mechanically compatible biliary stents, and offered a materials-driven solution to persistent interfacial failure in biofluid-rich implant environments.

10.1002/adfm.79156.title: Lignin Eutectogel Smart Skins for Integrated Fast Communication, Cervical Posture Monitoring and Warning
10.1002/adfm.79156.abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels underpin multifunctional electronic skins, yet unifying sustainable processing, long-term interfacial adhesion, and robust performance across extreme temperatures remains a central materials challenge for wearable sensing applications. This study presents a long-term storable lignin eutectogel (LS/PAM/DES) synthesized via a facile one pot method. The eutectogel demonstrates remarkable stretchability, relatively high ionic conductivity, and reliable strain sensing performance. It remains soft and highly stretchable even at −20°C environment, and retains most of its mass, ionic conductivity, and tensile deformability but a more pronounced decrease in tensile strength after one month of ambient exposure, indicating its promise as a non-volatile hydrogel alternative. The eutectogel can accurately capture motion signals from various body regions and enables rapid information input through a T9-style keyboard interface. When integrated with a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based classification framework, it enables automated recognition of predefined posture classes under the present controlled conditions. Moreover, an integrated device based on this eutectogel effectively evaluates sustained neck-posture deviations beyond preset angular and temporal thresholds and activates corresponding visual warnings. This work demonstrates the proof-of-concept feasibility of wearable sensing, gesture-based communication, cervical-posture monitoring, and threshold-based posture-deviation warning using the LS/PAM/DES eutectogel.

10.1002/adfm.79314.title: Scalable Fabrication of Thermally Reconfigurable Ge Metasurfaces Using Stencil Lithography for Mid-Infrared Molecular Fingerprinting
10.1002/adfm.79314.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface-enhanced infrared absorbance spectroscopy (SEIRAS) enables sensitive, label-free molecular detection on compact platforms, but practical deployment is hindered by low-throughput fabrication and limited bandwidth of photonic resonators. Here, we present a scalable stencil lithography approach for fabricating large-area Ge pillar metasurface arrays supporting polarization-insensitive Mie resonances. We leverage a combined geometric and thermal resonance tuning approach where geometric scaling yields discrete resonances spanning the 950-1700 cm − 1 molecular fingerprint region and thermal modulation of Ge's refractive index enables post-fabrication dynamic tuning of these discrete resonances at a rate of ∼0.18 cm − 1 K − 1 across 300-500 K. This combined resonance sweeping enables controlled molecular-photonic mode alignment at the same location, a critical requirement for SEIRAS. We reconstructed PMMA thin-film vibrational signatures across 1100-1215 cm − 1 and detected polystyrene microparticles, resolving modes near 1450 and 1492 cm − 1 . This platform combines scalable fabrication, broad spectral coverage, and dynamic resonance tuning for mid-IR molecular fingerprinting with potential applications in polymer and microplastic detection.

10.1002/adfm.79316.title: Helical Conductive Pathways Bridge Polarization Centers at Hollow-Confined Metal/N-C Interfaces to Form a Coherent Electromagnetic Loss Network
10.1002/adfm.79316.abstract: ABSTRACT Lightweight microwave absorbers are needed for electromagnetic interference mitigation, wireless communication protection, and radar scattering control. Carbon metal heterostructures integrate conductive networks, interfacial polarization, and cooperative magnetic dissipation; however, dense shell stacking can induce premature reflection and surface current accumulation, causing dielectric loss to depend excessively on conductive loss. Helical configurations are introduced to extend tortuous conductive pathways, and cavity-enabled spatial decoupling is integrated with helical-pathway reconnection through a scaffold-guided growth-reconstruction-conversion strategy. The hollow space separates the helical CNC backbone from the surrounding CoNi/N-doped carbon domains, reducing compact conductive stacking and facilitating microwave entry. The helical pathway reconnects distributed metal/N-C polarization centers and extends induced current pathways, while its chiral topology may provide a geometric basis for potential cross-polarization-related interactions. Under microwave excitation, these centers form an impedance-compatible coherent electromagnetic loss network that couples wave entry with volumetric dissipation. At their respective matching thicknesses, the optimized absorber achieves a minimum reflection loss of −54.80 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 6.29 GHz. Complete Ku-band and near complete X-band coverage are obtained at optimized thicknesses, and simulations show reduced radar scattering. This work provides a design principle for broadband microwave absorbers and other wave functional heterostructures.

10.1002/adfm.79269.title: Aryl-Sulfonate-Functionalized V 2 CT x /SPEEK Membranes Regulate Cation and Water Transport in Zinc-Ferricyanide Flow Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79269.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc-ferricyanide flow batteries offer low-cost energy storage, but osmotic water redistribution and the conductivity-selectivity trade-off of sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) membranes limit operation at high electrolyte concentrations. Here, an aryl-sulfonate-functionalized V 2 CT x /SPEEK interface is engineered to promote cation conduction while limiting ferricyanide crossover and electrolyte redistribution. Tetramethylammonium hydroxide-assisted redispersion provides thin V 2 C-SO 3 nanosheets for incorporation into SPEEK. Compared with the unfunctionalized V 2 CT x /SPEEK control, the resulting membrane exhibits higher ionic conductivity, lower swelling and ferricyanide permeability, and reduced electrolyte redistribution during cycling. With a 0.8 M K 3 [Fe(CN) 6 ] catholyte, the optimized membrane retains 81.4% of its initial capacity after 390 cycles and delivers an energy efficiency of 88.9% at cycle 390. At 0.1 M, the cell operates for 7,000 cycles with a capacity-decay rate of 0.0013% per cycle. The peak power density increases from 691.3 mW cm − 2 for pristine SPEEK to 822.9 mW cm − 2 . These results demonstrate that aryl-sulfonate functionalization improves the balance between cation transport, dimensional stability, and electrolyte retention in zinc-ferricyanide flow batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79283.title: A Monolithic Quantum-Dot/AlGaN Phototransistor Breaking the UV-NIR Sensitivity Trade-off for Ultrasensitive Dual-Band Detection
10.1002/adfm.79283.abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneous detection of solar-blind ultraviolet (UVC) and second near-infrared (NIR-II) light is highly desirable for advanced optoelectronic functions like all-weather vision. However, monolithic integration of these two bands is hindered by a fundamental material incompatibility, imposing a fundamental trade-off between UVC and NIR sensitivity. Here, a monolithic dual-band phototransistor is demonstrated​ by integrating a PbS colloidal quantum dot (CQD) NIR-II sensitizer with a polarization-engineered AlGaN/AlN UVC channel. A built-in virtual photogate, arising from strong polarization fields, enables ultrahigh photogating gain in both bands without compromising speed or spectral purity. The device achieves record room-temperature performance: a responsivity of 7.9 × 10 6 A/W and a specific detectivity of 1.5 × 10 18 Jones at 260 nm, together with 1.1 × 10 3 A/W and 2.0 × 10 14 Jones at 1550 nm. An ultralow optical crosstalk below −30 dB and ambient stability exceeding 200 days are demonstrated. The detector successfully performs dual-band imaging and optical communication under nanowatt-level illumination. This work presents a versatile materials platform for high-performance, multispectral optoelectronics.

10.1002/adfm.79280.title: A Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework-Based DNase I Delivery System for Targeted Suppression of the cGAS-STING Pathway in Acute Lung Injury
10.1002/adfm.79280.abstract: ABSTRACT In sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI), mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) released from damaged lung cells is recognized by the cytosolic DNA sensor cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS), leading to aberrant activation of the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway. This signaling cascade amplifies inflammation and oxidative stress, ultimately resulting in severe pulmonary dysfunction and high mortality. Here, we present a hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF-101)-based delivery system for DNase I that enables enzymatic clearance of cytosolic DNA and targeted suppression of the cGAS-STING pathway in ALI. Following efficient pulmonary delivery and macrophage internalization, this DNase I@HOF-101 platform effectively clears intracellular mtDNA, thereby attenuating inflammatory responses and alleviating acute lung injury. Moreover, the system exhibits desirable biocompatibility, minimal cytotoxicity, and enhanced enzymatic stability, highlighting its potential as a nanotherapeutic strategy for cGAS-STING-mediated inflammatory diseases.

10.1002/adfm.79294.title: Thermally Robust Piezoelectric KNN/Polyimide Separator for Regulating Lithium Deposition in Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79294.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-metal batteries offer exceptionally high theoretical energy density but are hindered by dendrite-induced short circuits and the limited thermal stability of conventional separators. Here, we report a thermally robust piezoelectric composite separator composed of highly fluorinated polyimide and potassium sodium niobate (KNN), fabricated through an electrospinning/imidization strategy. Molecular dipole engineering, preferential through-thickness polarization, and ceramic-polymer electromechanical coupling collectively enable regulation of the local interfacial electric field, homogenized Li + flux, and suppressed lithium dendrite growth during cycling. Meanwhile, the rigid polyimide framework endows the separator with excellent thermal tolerance and structural integrity at elevated temperatures. Consequently, LiFePO 4 ||Li cells retain 88.5% of their initial capacity after 1900 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates an electromechanically active separator that integrates intrinsic thermal stability with interfacial regulation, providing a potential strategy for improving the durability of lithium-metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79268.title: Wood-MOF Thermoelectrics for Heat and Power Harvesting
10.1002/adfm.79268.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoelectric materials and devices enable to harvest heat energy from the environment, which offers a promising solution for addressing the critical issue of conventional fossil fuels for energy supply. However, sustainable development of low-grade heat conversion to electricity is limited by materials and technologies. Herein, inspired by the conduction of water molecules and ions in trees, natural wood is chemically modified and synthesized to a nanostructured wood/metal-organic framework (wood/MOF) gradient, in which it enables the driving of the ions movements through charged nanochannels for enhancing the generation of the thermally generated voltage. This has resulted in a 1200% increased differential thermal voltage of wood/MOF gradient compared to that of natural wood due to the thermophoretic mobility difference between the negative and positive ions. An electric double layer is formed among cellulose nanofibrils with a distance of approximately 4.8-7 nm enabling a favorable ionic regulation performance and a continuous output voltage of about 1.2 V, which has demonstrated its potential as a low-grade heat and power harvesting system for heat-to-electricity conversion. Coupling with its long-term durability and low environmental impact advantages, this research provides insights into an innovative “wood-sunlight-thermal energy” tripartite system for clean electricity generation, which enables large-scale production from such sustainable materials.

10.1002/adfm.79302.title: Techno-Economically Viable Glycine Electrosynthesis From CO 2 -Derived Oxalic Acid Via Enhanced Oxime Adsorption on Atomically Dispersed Copper
10.1002/adfm.79302.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical C─N coupling offers a promising strategy for producing value-added chemicals, particularly glycine. The N-pathway (glyoxylic acid and nitrate) for glycine electrosynthesis is hindered by multiple electron-transfer processes, which may increase energy consumption. Alternatively, the C-pathway (oxalic acid and hydroxylamine) offers the potential for achieving a higher FE (Faradaic efficiency) at industrially relevant current densities, but requires optimized adsorption of the key oxime intermediate. Here, we fabricate a SnO 2 catalyst incorporating atomically dispersed Cu (Cu-SnO 2 ) for selective glycine synthesis, reaching a maximum glycine FE of 73.1% and a maximum partial current density of 106.3 mA cm −2 . The Cu-SnO 2 catalyst maintains catalytic performance over 24 h. In a flow cell, the Cu-SnO 2 catalyst achieves a maximum FE Glycine of 58.1% and exhibits sustained catalytic performance over 72 h. Furthermore, we construct a cascade electrocatalytic system for glycine synthesis using CO 2 -derived oxalic acid. A prospective technoeconomic analysis indicates that the proposed C-pathway has the potential to achieve economic viability under specific operating and economic conditions. Control experiments, in situ ATR-SEIRAS and theoretical calculations suggest that SnO 2 facilitates the conversion of oxalic acid to oxime, while atomically dispersed Cu sites may promote oxime adsorption and its subsequent hydrogenation.

10.1002/adfm.79298.title: Flame Retardant Lithium Composites With Synergistic Suppression of Lithium Dendrites and Smoke Toxicity for High Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79298.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are regarded as the promising next-generation high energy density storage, but their commercialization is hindered by uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and the persistent risk of thermal runaway. Herein, a multifunctional artificial interface membrane is designed through electrospinning combined with in situ metal-organic framework (MOF) growth, aiming to construct a highly safe lithium metal anode. The uniformly dispersed MOF nanoparticles in the membrane generate uniform Li + flux through their inherent cage window structure, effectively inhibiting excessive Li dendrite formation and thereby stabilizing the lithium metal anode with improved cycling stability. Notably, the membrane exhibits strong adsorption and catalytic ability for hazardous CO gases released during thermal runaway, enabling valid conversion of CO to CO 2 . Importantly, the ignition time of the as-prepared Li metal composite anode is significantly prolonged, providing a valuable time window for battery fire accident response and personnel rescue. This work demonstrates a multifunctionally flame retardant interface protective layer design method through integrated interfacial and rational material structure engineering. It leads to a new strategy for synergistic suppression of Li dendrites and smoke toxicity in future safe LMBs.

10.1002/adfm.78871.title: Correction to “Revisiting Cobalt Dopability in GeTe System to Design Modulation-Doped Thermoelectrics”

10.1002/adfm.79181.title: Unlocking Thermoelectric Performance in Cu 2 SnSe 3 Through Controlled Structural Ordering
10.1002/adfm.79181.abstract: ABSTRACT Diamond-like semiconductors offer a versatile platform for the design of highly efficient energy-converting materials, owing to their tunable electronic structures and high charge carrier mobility. A thorough understanding and precise control of their structural complexity and defect chemistry are, however, essential for optimizing their transport properties. Here, we demonstrate that both the spatial arrangement of tetrahedral motifs and the polymorphic landscape of the diamond-like semiconductor Cu 2 SnSe 3 can be precisely controlled through post-synthesis annealing. Electron diffraction combined with precession-assisted electron diffraction tomography reveals that structural disorder at the sub-µm length scale, arising from the coexistence of monoclinic and cubic structures, promotes charge carrier trapping within the induced localized states. The degree of localization plays a key role in shaping the temperature dependence of the electronic properties, which evolve from amorphous-like hopping conduction to conventional valence-band transport as the annealing temperature increases from 573 to 947 K. Optimum hole mobility and thermoelectric performance are achieved once a single crystallographic phase is obtained by annealing above 873 K. These findings showcase the detrimental influence of local structural disorder on charge carrier transport, providing an additional degree of freedom for tailoring functional properties in crystalline semiconductors.

10.1002/adfm.79321.title: A Multicomponent Body-Centered Cubic Superconducting Alloy with Exceptional Mechanical Robustness at 4.2 Kelvin
10.1002/adfm.79321.abstract: ABSTRACT The ductile-to-brittle transition poses a persistent challenge for body-centered cubic (BCC) structure superconducting alloys at liquid helium temperature (4.2 K), where intrinsic brittleness frequently leads to premature material failure and severely restricts their application in extreme environments. Here we present a BCC multicomponent V-Nb-Ti-Mo superconducting alloy that achieves a high fracture elongation of ∼16% while maintaining pronounced strain-hardening capacity of ∼620 MPa at 4.2 K. This exceptional ultra-cryogenic ductility surpasses that of nearly all reported superconducting materials, and even BCC structured alloys. The rarely reported nanoscale orthorhombic martensitic transformation and the local chemical fluctuations with V-enriched nanoclusters considerably promote the strain-hardening capacity. Unlike traditional BCC alloys dominated by screw dislocations, a high density of non-screw dislocations also formed to facilitate elongation. Plenty of kink bands, which are generally difficult to form at 4.2 K, delay the fracture process. This study not only offers a viable solution to the long-standing cryogenic brittleness problem of BCC structure alloys, but also introduces a superconducting material with superior mechanical reliability for extreme-condition applications.
authors: Zitang Zhang, Hengcheng Zhang, Tao Yang, Jingyi Xiao, Jixun Zhang, Kai Zhao, Yiping Lu

10.1002/adfm.78680.title: Correction to “Controlling Nuclei Growth and Phase Transition of CsFA-Based Perovskite During Slot-Die Coating via Solvent Engineering for High-Performance Solar Cells and Modules”

10.1002/adfm.79281.title: Chiral Au@Semiconductor Yolk-Shell Nanostructures with Tailored Chiroptical Properties and Chirality-Dependent Photocatalysis
10.1002/adfm.79281.abstract: ABSTRACT The spatial configuration of chiral metal-semiconductor hybrid nanostructures directly determines the coupling efficiency between chiral plasmonic metals and semiconductors, which in turn affects their key physical and chemical properties and applications in diverse scenarios. However, precise spatial control of complex chiral hybrid nanostructures with increased structural and compositional diversity remains a significant challenge. Herein, we develop a general bottom-up synthetic strategy for the construction of chiral Au@semiconductor yolk-shell nanostructures. By using chiral Au@Cu 2 O nanostructures with tunable geometric parameters as a chiral core, a finely controlled redox-coupled ion exchange process is employed to realize the transition from a Cu 2 O shell to other semiconductors, including Cu 7 S 4 , Cu 2-x Se, CdS, and CuFeS 2 , to form chiral Au@semiconductor yolk-shell structures. More importantly, intriguing shell-dependent chiroptical activities were experimentally observed and further elucidated by the theoretical simulations. The controllable integration of chiral plasmonic nanostructures with semiconductor components further allows applications in chirality-dependent photocatalysis. The insights gained from this work provide an important knowledge framework for understanding the coupling of the semiconductor shell with the chiral plasmonic core that underpins the design of multifunctional chiral hybrid plasmonic nanomaterials toward catalysis and photonics.
authors: Guizeng Yang, Xinhui Wang, Binbin Zhang, Zheng Wang, Xuehao Sun, Sujing Zhang, Yunlong Tao, Bintao Tang, Lichao Sun, Shunping Zhang, Qingfeng Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79272.title: Dual-Axial Nitrogen Coordination-Induced Mn Charge Localization at Fe-Mn Dual-Atom Sites for Enhanced Sulfur Redox Kinetics
10.1002/adfm.79272.abstract: ABSTRACT The optimization of coordination environments for heteronuclear dual-atom catalysts (DACs) has been a formidable challenge in lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, arising from complex electronic coupling induced by inherent inter-metallic-site charge transfer at heteronuclear sites. Herein, an Fe-Mn dual-atom catalyst (FeMn-(N ax ) 2 DAC/NC) with dual-axial nitrogen coordination anchored on nitrogen-doped carbon is rationally constructed to achieve the directional electronic modulation of active sites. The axial nitrogen ligand reconfigures the electronic distribution of Fe-Mn heteronuclear sites, inducing Fe-to-Mn charge transfer and further charge localization on the Mn center. The electronic effect precisely modulates Mn d-orbital energy levels, reinforcing the d-p orbital hybridization between active sites and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs). The FeMn-(N ax ) 2 DAC/NC strengthens the chemical adsorption of LiPSs to suppress the shuttle effect, and further bidirectionally accelerates the rate-determining steps of sulfur redox: the solid-to-solid conversion from Li 2 S 2 to Li 2 S and the oxidative dissociation of Li 2 S. Consequently, the resultant sulfur cathodes deliver a discharge capacity of 682 mAh g − 1 at 5 C and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.047% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 3 C. This work offers a novel strategy for optimizing the redox kinetics of sulfur cathodes in Li-S batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79312.title: Trieffect Dense Organic-Derived Coating Enabling Synergistic Bulk Stability and Interfacial Reactivity for Superb Zn-Mn Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79312.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of aqueous Zn-MnO 2 batteries is hindered by sluggish Zn 2+ diffusion kinetics, severe Mn dissolution, and “dead” MnO 2 accumulation in Mn 2+ -containg electrolytes, leading to inferior rate capability and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we designed an organic-modified MnO 2 uniformly encapsulated by 1,4-dihydroxybenzene (HQ) to simultaneously regulate bulk stability and interfacial reactivity of HQ-MnO 2 hybrid (denoted as H-MnO 2 ) via a facile solvent-free ball milling method. In/ex situ characterization and theoretical calculation results reveal that the dense HQ-derived coating with Mn─O─C interfacial bonds significantly boost charge diffusion kinetics and improves the structural robustness of H-MnO 2 . Furthermore, the redox-catalytic HQ-derived layer with C═O/C─OH couples efficiently promotes selective H + insertion ability as well as boosts cathodic Mn 2+ /MnO 2 conversion to prevent irreversible ZnMn 2 O 4 and “dead” MnO 2 accumulation simultaneously. As a result, the Zn//H-MnO 2 battery exhibits an outstanding capacity of 575 mAh g −1 , superior rate performance, and ultra-long lifespan over 15 000 cycles. Moreover, 192.5 Wh kg H-MnO2 −1 pouch cell with practical high-mass loading maintained 100% capacity retention after 130 cycles, demonstrating the effectiveness of trieffect-integrated organic interfacial engineering for high-energy and durable Zn-MnO 2 systems.

10.1002/adfm.79310.title: Understanding the Multi-Electron Conversion Mechanism and High Performance of NbCl 5 Cathodes in All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79310.abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion-type cathodes are promising candidates for high-energy all-solid-state lithium batteries due to their high capacities enabled by multi-electron redox chemistry. However, their practical application is severely hindered by large voltage hysteresis and rapid capacity decay arising from sluggish Li-ion transport and structural degradation during conversion reactions. Herein, we develop a high-valent NbCl 5 cathode with continuous electronic pathways, enabling highly reversible four-electron conversion with ultralow discharge-charge overpotentials. The NbCl 5 cathode delivers a reversible capacity of 281 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 70% of its initial capacity at 1.0 C after 2000 cycles. Notably, it exhibits minimal voltage hysteresis across four electrochemical plateaus (0.08, 0.03, 0.03, and 0.01 V, respectively), achieving an energy efficiency of 98.9%, which surpasses reported conversion-type and most layered oxide intercalation cathodes. We revealed that conversion-induced interfaces between crystalline LiCl and low-valent niobium chloride nanodomains facilitate Li-ion migration within the cathode bulk and across the cathode/solid electrolyte interface. Meanwhile, the internal framework remains structurally stable during prolonged conversion reactions, as evidenced by only a slight increase in porosity from 2.48% to 3.55% after 200 cycles. This chemo-mechanical synergy accelerates Li-ion transport and maintains intimate interfacial contact, thereby enabling ultralow voltage hysteresis and durable cycling performance.

10.1002/adfm.79190.title: In Situ and Dynamic Reconfiguration of Nonlinear Optical Absorption by Carbon Nanotube Optical Fiber
10.1002/adfm.79190.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanomaterial-based nonlinear optical absorbers, such as saturable absorbers and optical limiters, have been widely employed for laser intensity manipulation. However, their nonlinear absorption regimes are typically constrained by static nonlinear responses within specific spectral regions. Tuning the operational regime generally necessitates material functionalization or complex post-treatments. Consequently, reconfiguring the nonlinear absorption regime in a monolithic device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in situ manipulation of the nonlinear interaction strength using an optical fiber-integrated single-walled carbon nanotube absorber, which exhibits reconfigurable nonlinear optical absorption. Our monolithic device enables dynamic onset tuning of optical limiting within a designated spectral excitation energy range, in addition to supporting saturable absorption operation. Furthermore, leveraging the tunable nonlinear optical response of a saturable absorber, we realize a passively mode-locked fiber laser with an unprecedented tuning range of 10 GHz and a side-mode-suppression ratio exceeding 30 dB, surpassing other nanomaterial saturable absorber-based GHz light sources. Our device fabrication strategy features a simple configuration and low cost compared to static nonlinear optical absorbers, and it can be readily extended to other types of nonlinear optical nanomaterial absorbers. This approach may find immediate applications in flexible light intensity control, optical signal processing, and intelligent physical systems requiring dynamic nonlinear activation functions.

10.1002/adfm.79350.title: Time-Domain Regulation of Electrolyte Microenvironments Enables 30 mA cm − 2 Stable Lithium Plating/Stripping for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79350.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of high-voltage lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is severely hindered by interfacial instability and structural degradation, fundamentally originating from “time-domain mismatch” between rapid parasitic reactions and sluggish interface passivation. Herein, we propose a time-domain responsive in situ gel polymer electrolyte (SiNCO-GPE) to dynamically regulate the electrolyte microenvironment. The (trimethylsilyl)isocyanate (SiNCO) acts as a “scavenging cage” to eliminate trace water and hydrogen fluoride, while its reaction products subsequently participate in interfacial evolution. The in situ polymerized poly(vinylene carbonate) integrated with poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) electrospun fiber skeleton creates a F-O co-coordination environment to facilitate fast Li + transport. The electroactive isocyanate group in SiNCO, together with lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate and fluoroethylene carbonate, decomposes preferentially to rapidly construct a robust B/N/F-rich interphase layer during initial cycling on both the anode and cathode, while the Si-containing scavenging products are dynamically incorporated into the interphase layers during prolonged cycling to accommodate mechanical stress. The SiNCO-GPE enables exceptional Li plating/stripping stability for over 4000 h at 1 mA cm − 2 and withstands an ultrahigh current density of 30 mA cm − 2 over 70 h, while the Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cell delivers an outstanding capacity retention of 90.5% after 500 cycles at 4.7 V, offering new insights into the development of durable high-voltage LMBs.

10.1002/adfm.79291.title: cis/trans -Through-Space Charge-Transfer Isomers Enabled by Acceptor Fusion for High-Efficiency Thermally-Activated Delayed Fluorescence and Circularly Polarized Emission
10.1002/adfm.79291.abstract: ABSTRACT Multi-π-stacked through-space charge-transfer (TSCT) emitters have shown great potential for developing efficient thermally-activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) toward organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) applications. New design paradigms are highly demanded for constructing multi-π-stacked TSCT-TADF emitters, especially the chiral ones with chiroptical activity. Herein, by fusing the acceptors of two single π-stacked TSCT units, cis / trans isomeric multi-π-stacked TSCT emitters ( cis -2D/A and trans -2D/A ) are developed. The trans isomer exhibits intrinsic chirality and exists as a pair of enantiomers, ( R , R )- trans -2D/A and ( S , S )- trans -2D/A . In doped films, cis -2D/A and trans -2D/A exhibit green TADF with largely accelerated radiative decay, and ( R , R )/( S , S )- trans -2D/A display circularly polarized emission. OLEDs based on cis -2D/A and trans -2D/A show maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max ) of around 27.0% and largely suppressed efficiency roll-offs. The devices based on ( R , R )/( S , S )- trans -2D/A further exhibit circularly polarized electroluminescence with electroluminescence dissymmetry factors at around ±1.2 × 10 −3 . Narrowband OLEDs employing cis -2D/A and trans -2D/A as sensitizers show high EQE max up to 37.0% and EQEs at 1000 cd m −2 up to 30.2%. The devices employing ( R , R )/( S , S )- trans -2D /A as chiral sensitizers further exhibit circularly polarized narrowband electroluminescence with electroluminescence dissymmetry factors at around ±2.3 × 10 −3 , which rank among the most efficient circularly polarized narrowband OLEDs reported so far.

10.1002/adfm.79300.title: Nanoimprint-Enhanced Organic Heterojunction Phototransistors for Bipolar Optical Encoding in Reservoir Computing
10.1002/adfm.79300.abstract: ABSTRACT Optoelectronic reservoirs require transient states with sufficient electrical contrast and diverse temporal dynamics. However, weak optical-to-electrical transduction reduces the resolvability of reservoir states, whereas unipolar photoresponses restrict how successive optical inputs modulate the residual device state. Here, we report a nanoimprint-enhanced PDVT-10/F 16 -CuPc heterojunction organic phototransistor that combines amplified photocurrent output with wavelength-dependent bipolar dynamics. Periodic nanostructures introduced into the PDVT-10 layer enhance broadband optical absorption and photocurrent generation, enabling a minimum detectable irradiance of 0.65 µW cm −2 at 430 nm. Meanwhile, the heterojunction generates wavelength-dependent photocurrent transients with opposite polarities and distinct relaxation behaviors, enabling bipolar optical encoding in which binary 0 and 1 inputs are represented by optical pulses at two wavelengths that drive the photocurrent state in opposite directions. Consequently, successive inputs can selectively reinforce, offset, or reverse the residual photocurrent state, yielding more distinguishable and history-dependent reservoir trajectories. This bipolar encoding improves reservoir-state distinguishability by expanding the accessible photocurrent range and reducing state overlap under fluctuations, increasing nine-class human action-recognition accuracy from 77.04% to 83.3%. Combining two bipolar reservoir groups further increases recognition accuracy to 90.0%. This work establishes a compact device paradigm that unifies weak-light sensitivity with temporal dynamics, advancing hardware-efficient processing of complex temporal information.

10.1002/adfm.79344.title: Crown-Ether-Based Covalent Organic Network Membranes for Hydration-Governed Li + /Mg 2+ Separation
10.1002/adfm.79344.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective Li + /Mg 2+ separation remains a central challenge for sustainable lithium extraction because ion transport in confined aqueous environments is governed by coupled steric and hydration effects rather than ionic size alone. Here, we report a crown-ether-based covalent organic network membrane for hydration-governed mono/divalent ion sieving. Unlike conventional crown-ether materials that rely on cavity-specific host-guest recognition, the conformational flexibility and steric hindrance of dibenzo-18-crown-6 induce locally ordered yet globally disordered packing, transforming the nominal ∼3 nm intrinsic cavity into sub-nanometer transport channels with an effective aperture of ∼0.9 nm. Structural analyses reveal that the exposed ether oxygen atoms of crown-ethers reconstruct oxygen-rich confined hydration interfaces that regulate hydrated-ion partitioning and migration. Thus, the membrane exhibits high mono/divalent ion discrimination, delivering a Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of ∼3900 together with high Li + flux, and also demonstrating efficient K + /Mg 2+ and Cs + /Sr 2+ separation with selectivities of ∼3140 and ∼840, respectively. Spectroscopic studies, density functional theory calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal a dual physical-thermodynamic blockade mechanism, where steric confinement suppresses hydrated divalent ions and hydration-mediated thermodynamic compensation facilitates monovalent ion transport. The membrane maintains robust performance under concentrated and Mg-rich conditions, highlighting the potential of engineered transport architectures for lithium extraction and precise ionic separations.

10.1002/adfm.79299.title: Meso-Substituent Engineering Tunes Co-OOH Binding in Cobalt Porphyrins for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.79299.abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt porphyrins are prototypical molecular catalysts for two-electron oxygen reduction to H 2 O 2 because of their well-defined CoN 4 active sites and synthetically tunable ligand frameworks. However, conventional phenyl-substituted cobalt porphyrins generally exhibit limited H 2 O 2 selectivity due to excessively strong Co-OOH chemisorption, which can favor O─O bond activation and the competing four-electron oxygen reduction pathway. Herein, we establish a meso-substituent engineering strategy to regulate Co-OOH interaction in cobalt porphyrins without altering the primary CoN 4 coordination motif. By progressively replacing meso-phenyl groups with thienyl and bithienyl substituents, the optimized CoT 2 TP catalyst achieves a H 2 O 2 Faradaic efficiency of 98.4% together with a H 2 O 2 production rate of 74.96 mg cm −2 h −1 at 120 mA cm −2 . In situ attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals a continuous blue shift of the O─O stretching vibration of adsorbed *OOH with increasing thiophene incorporation, indicating weakened Co-OOH chemisorption and facilitated Co─OOH bond cleavage. Density functional theory calculations further show that bithienyl substitution shifts the Co d-band center away from the Fermi level and optimizes the *OOH adsorption strength. This work establishes remote meso-substituent regulation of Co-OOH binding as a molecular design strategy for selective H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis.

10.1002/adfm.79318.title: Rigid π-Bridge Conformational Locked Crosslinker for Non-Destructive Direct Photopatterning of Colloidal Quantum Dot
10.1002/adfm.79318.abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are promising emitters for next-generation displays, yet direct photolithography often causes severe photophysical degradation that compromises device performance. Although molecular rigidification can alleviate photodamage, it usually reduces crosslinker solubility, limiting compatibility with octane-dispersed QDs. Here, we propose a conformation-locked π-bridge design that simultaneously enhances molecular rigidity and solubility. Using fluorinated phenyl (F1) and biphenyl (F2) π-bridge crosslinkers as model systems, we reveal how conformational regulation governs QD photopatterning. The conformation-locked F2 suppresses molecular torsion while maintaining excellent octane solubility, enabling high-fidelity photopatterning with a resolution of 12,700 PPI. Meanwhile, the extended π-conjugation increases its molar extinction coefficient to 77,598 L mol −1 cm −1 , reducing the required UV exposure dose to 2 mJ cm −2 . As a result, patterned QDs retain over 95% of their photoluminescence quantum yield and 97% of their fluorescence lifetime. QLEDs fabricated from F2-patterned QDs exhibit an external quantum efficiency of 24.40% and a maximum luminance of 237,692 cd m −2 , with both performance metrics essentially preserved after patterning. Furthermore, the enhanced exciton binding energy significantly improves operational stability, extending the device lifetime (T 95 ) from 421 h to 2,324 h at 1,000 cd m −2 . This work provides a general strategy for low-dose, non-destructive, high-resolution QD photolithography.

10.1002/adfm.79331.title: Self-Assembled Supramolecular Host-Guest Composite Enables Interfacial Regulation Toward Dendrite-Free Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79331.abstract: ABSTRACT The instability of zinc anodes during reversible deposition and dissolution in the aqueous electrolyte constitutes a critical bottleneck limiting the lifespan of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Herein, we utilize a straightforward and supramolecular self-assembly approach involving 4-sulfocalix[6]arene (SCA[6]) and N,N’-dimethyl-9,9’-biacridinium dinitrate (LCG), driven by cooperative host-guest recognition and electrostatic forces. The spontaneous interfacial assembly of these components enables the construction of a protective interphase on zinc anodes and functions as a “molecular switch” to regulate the Zn 2 + solvation structure, facilitate ion transport, and accommodate volumetric fluctuations during cycling. Consequently, the LCG/SCA[6]-modified interface effectively mitigates corrosion and dendrite growth, thereby significantly enhancing the electrochemical stability and cycling performance of AZIBs. As a result, the (LCG/SCA[6]) 2 -Zn symmetric cell can maintain stable operation for over 3800 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . The (LCG/SCA[6]) 2 -Zn||I 2 coin cell retains a specific capacity of 200.50 mAh g −1 with a capacity retention rate of 87.25% at 2 A g −1 even after 14 000 cycles. Considering the low cost and simplicity of LCG/SCA[6] film fabrication, this supramolecular composite presents a promising strategy for enhancing the stability of zinc anodes.

10.1002/adfm.79289.title: Dynamically Modulated Ultralong Organic Phosphorescent Materials: Achieving Wide-Range Lifetime Tunability for Multicolor Data Storage
10.1002/adfm.79289.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultralong organic phosphorescence (UOP) materials have attracted growing research attention in the field of optical information storage, anti-counterfeiting, and data encryption owing to their unique long-lived emission characteristics. However, the widespread application of UOP-based information storage is currently constrained by two main limitations: the dominant binary (on/off) encoding mode with limited information capacity, and the lack of high-precision, facile data-writing approaches compatible with scalable fabrication. In this work, we develop a time-resolved information storage strategy based on widely and precisely tunable UOP lifetimes, which is realized by rationally controlling the polymerization degree of the polymer host. Combining with digital processing (DLP) 3D printing method, the photosensitive materials 3-TBAOF@HEA:AA and 4-TBAOF@HEA:AA are designed and developed with tunable UOP lifetimes from 4.6 to 1577.50 ms. Leveraging this tunability of broad lifetime, we demonstrate time-dependent information storage including multicolor information display and direct photopatterning on flexible 2D thin films. The 3D-printable UOP system with precisely controllable phosphorescence lifetimes provides a viable material platform for constructing high-level data security storage devices.

10.1002/adfm.79341.title: Constructing Fast Sensing-Monitoring System via Spillover-Free Hydrogen Reaction Path
10.1002/adfm.79341.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen (H 2 ) leakage monitoring is paramount for the safety of hydrogen fuel cells. However, traditional metal-sensitized oxide semiconductor sensors often suffer from sluggish response caused by the limited hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we explore a spillover-free hydrogen response strategy via constructing a disordered 3LiPdPt-sensitized interface on ZnO supports (3LiPdPt/ZnO) for ultrafast and low-concentration H 2 detection. We find the introduction of Li + can collapse the regular PdPt interface and induce stable amorphization even at high temperature. The resultant 3LiPdPt/ZnO sensor can achieve ultrafast response (<4 s) to 3-200 ppm H 2 , superior hydrogen response (13-50 ppm of H 2 ) and excellent long-term stability. In-situ experiments confirm that the disordered 3LiPdPt interface can bypass the hydrogen spillover limitation to realize a direct reaction between activated hydrogen and oxygen species. This path fundamentally eliminates the reliance on long-range hydrogen diffusion and thus improves the sensing response speed reactive. Moreover, we demonstrate an autonomous monitoring system by equipping the sensors on fuel cell electric vehicle devices for dual-mode (continuous/intermittent) H 2 leakage assessment. Therefore, our proposed strategy reveals a fundamental understanding of the hydrogen sensing mechanism and may create a new path for highly effective H 2 detection.

10.1002/adfm.79223.title: Revealing the Intrinsic Ion Species, Diffusion Paths, Governing Factors for Charge Carriers of Cement-Based Structural Capacitors (CSCs)
10.1002/adfm.79223.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrated structural/functional rechargeable CSCs combine the load-bearing properties of construction with electrochemical energy storage, thereby expanding the functional capabilities of modern buildings by providing distributed and adaptive energy storage. However, many fundamental scientific issues-including the dominant ionic species, ion diffusion pathways, and the key factors governing charge-carrier transport-remain unclear, hindering the rational design of CSCs. In this work, we first employ a unidirectional charging method to identify Na + and K + as the dominant charge carriers in CSCs. Subsequently, a novel Zn-based cement structural capacitor (Zn-CSC) is designed, in which Zn-containing species serve as a tracer to qualitatively reveal the direction and spatial pathways of field-assisted ion transport through the interconnected porous network of the cement matrix. Furthermore, the fundamental factors governing charge-carrier behavior are investigated: (1) the concentration of charge carriers in the cement pore solution is positively correlated with the energy-storage performance of CSCs; (2) a reduction in the water content of the cement electrolyte hinders the transport of Na + and K + ions, leading to diminished energy-storage capability; and (3) the solidified, percolating 3D micro-/nanoporous network formed within the cement electrolyte serves as the critical pathway for efficient charge-carrier transport.

10.1002/adfm.79327.title: Lattice-Level Negative Thermal Expansion Enables Thermomechanical Self-Compensation in High-Rate Lithium Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79327.abstract: ABSTRACT Localized Joule heating in high-rate lithium metal batteries often induces severe thermomechanical failure of polymer separators and accelerates thermal runaway in cells with Ni-rich NCM cathode. Here we report a multiscale separator design strategy that translates lattice-level negative thermal expansion into macroscopic thermomechanical self-compensation. In this design, Cu 2 P 2 O 7 is coupled with the PVDF-HFP matrix through a PDA mediated interface. Temperature-dependent structural analysis and thermal-response tests demonstrate the anisotropic lattice contraction of Cu 2 P 2 O 7 , which relieves the thermally induced deformation of PVDF-HFP through PDA mediated interfacial interactions. The amine-rich PDA layer further suppresses corrosive hydrofluoric acid during the cycling, improving interfacial durability. The resulting composite membrane maintains complete dimensional stability up to 200°C while preserving high ionic conductivity and a uniform Li + flux. As a result, Li||Li symmetric cells with the self-compensating separator operate for more than 3000 h at 1 mA cm −2 . When paired with Ni-rich NCM811 cathodes, full cells maintain 1000 stable cycles at 5 C and deliver 135 mAh g −1 at 60°C after 100 cycles. This work demonstrates a solid-state negative thermal expansion strategy for active separator protection, providing a materials route for mitigating thermomechanical failure in high-power lithium metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79275.title: Localized Nicotinamide Riboside Delivery Through a Reversible Affinity Hydrogel Promotes Myocardial Restoration
10.1002/adfm.79275.abstract: ABSTRACT Myocardial infarction (MI), a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, is characterized by acute ischemic injury followed by mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, redox imbalance, and adverse cardiac remodeling. NAD + -a vital coenzyme-is rapidly perturbed after MI and represents a potential metabolic target for supporting myocardial recovery. However, existing biomaterial formulations have limited efficacy because of their insufficient loading and local delivery of NAD + and other small hydrophilic molecules to the myocardium. Herein, we present an injectable, on-heart adhesive hydrogel capable of efficiently loading and gradually releasing nicotinamide riboside (NR), a precursor of NAD + , to restore NAD + levels in infarcted cardiac tissue. Phenylboronate-modified chitosan forms reversible yet high-affinity interactions with NR, enabling controlled delivery; while the hydrogel network is engineered from crosslinking with gallol-modified chitosan that provides tissue adhesion and facilitates in situ gelation upon injection. In a murine MI model, hydrogel-mediated NR delivery increased NAD + availability and improved cardiac function and electrophysiology. Benefits included reduced injury, improved redox and metabolic function, and preserved cardiac structure. Mechanistically, NR protection converged on the SIRT1-p65 axis, limiting ferroptotic and inflammatory injury while preserving mitochondrial function. Thus, the hydrogel provides a cardiac-adhesive platform for NR delivery, restoring NAD + homeostasis and promoting recovery after MI.

10.1002/adfm.79301.title: Morphology-Engineered ZIF Nanosheet Membranes With 4-Membered-Ring Apertures for Propylene/Propane Separation
10.1002/adfm.79301.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise hydrocarbon separations remain a major challenge for membrane technologies because molecular discrimination is often limited by poor control over pore accessibility and transport pathways in conventional mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). Here, we report a morphology-engineering strategy that transforms the intrinsic pore anisotropy of ZIF nanoparticles into selectively exposed 4-membered-ring apertures within two-dimensional (2D) nanosheets, which are subsequently assembled into highly oriented 2D ZIF MMMs. The pore system is reactivated through a soft chemical activation that removes residual surfactants while preserving structural integrity and solution processability. A shear-flow-induced pre-alignment process directs the in-plane orientation of 2D ZIF nanosheets within the polymer matrix, aligning the aperture channels parallel to the gas transport direction to maximize hydrocarbon molecular recognition. Multiscale characterization and simulations reveal a direct structure-transport relationship linking nanosheet orientation, aperture-specific diffusion, and macroscopic separation behavior. The resulting 2D ZIF-8 nanosheet MMMs exhibit enhanced mechanical robustness together with outstanding hydrocarbon separation performance, delivering a 332% increase in C 3 H 6 permeability and a 274% improvement in selectivity relative to the pure polymer membrane. This work provides a general strategy for programming pore accessibility and orientation in 2D MOF MMMs for precise molecular separations.

10.1002/adfm.79317.title: Cascade Catalysis of Zn/Nb Single-Atom Sites for Wide-Temperature Li-S Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79317.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-sulfur batteries are considered promising next-generation energy-storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density. However, their practical applications are severely hindered by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttling, which are significantly aggravated under extreme-temperature conditions. To address this issue, a novel cascade catalysis strategy is developed to regulate the multistep sulfur redox process through embedding the Nb-N 4 and Zn-N 4 dual single-atom sites within N, P co-doped carbon fibers (Zn/Nb-NPMCFs). In conjunction with theoretical analysis, it is clarified that Nb single-atom site preferentially adsorbs soluble LiPSs through forming an Nb-S bond and catalyzes their conversion, whereas Zn single-atom site facilitates subsequent Li 2 S-related redox conversion. With the cascade catalysis effect enabling accelerated sulfur conversion and suppressed LiPSs shuttling, the assembled Li-S batteries with Zn/Nb-NPMCFs as free-standing sulfur hosts deliver good electrochemical performance over a wide temperature range, retaining 651.8 and 401.1 mAh g −1 under 50°C and −20°C at 0.5 C, even after 500 cycles, respectively. This work provides a guideline for improving multistep sulfur redox kinetics in Li-S batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78880.title: Carbon Dioxide Synergized Photo-Reforming for Efficient Valorization of Bio-Polyols With a Dynamic Carbon Balance
10.1002/adfm.78880.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic upgrading of biomass-derived feedstocks into value-added chemicals is promising for carbon neutrality but limited by low carbon utilization and CO 2 emissions from over-oxidation. Herein, we establish a “self-feeding” photocatalytic system coupling glycerol oxidation with concurrent CO 2 photoreduction to seamlessly close the carbon loop, enabling a truly dynamic and emission-free biomass valorization strategy. This design uses defect-engineered metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with atomically anchored Cu sites to synergistically activate glycerol and O 2 and introduce CO 2 to steer the evolution of reactive oxygen species, thereby tempering hydroxyl radicals (•OH) for selective oxidative cleavage. Under illumination, CO 2 coordination with in situ formed Cu I sites facilitates CO 2 photoreduction and dictates chemo-selective C-C scission via decarbonylation to avoid over-oxidation. By kinetically matching CO 2 release with in situ reduction, the system channels liberated carbon exclusively into value-added C 1 products, achieving both carbon yield and selectivity approaching ∼100%. Benchmark production rates reach 2875 µmol g −1 h −1 for CO and 1185 µmol g −1 h −1 for HCOOH (corresponding to ∼3.0 carbons per glycerol molecule), culminating in a strictly zero-CO 2 -emission process. This work resolves the classic trade-off between oxidation depth and carbon retention and reframes CO 2 as a functional reaction modulator, charting a viable paradigm for carbon-neutral chemical synthesis.

10.1002/adfm.78431.title: The Electron Sink Effect Driven by Work Function Gradient for Enhanced Interface Polarization and Broadband Microwave Absorption in Conductive Heterostructures
10.1002/adfm.78431.abstract: ABSTRACT The traditional development of magnetic alloy-based microwave absorbers has relied on trial-and-error, lacking systematic control over interfacial electronic behavior, which often leads to poor impedance matching, single loss mechanisms, and limited bandwidth. To address these issues, this work proposes a DFT-guided design strategy for conductive heterogeneous interfaces. The work function analysis reveals a gradient energy level alignment among FeSiAl, Fe 3 C, Fe, and CNTs. A difference exceeding 0.4 eV drives spontaneous electron migration from low-work-function components (FeSiAl, Fe 3 C, Fe) to CNTs, forming localized electron-rich regions, referred to as the “electron sink” effect. This electron accumulation induces intense interfacial polarization relaxation under alternating electromagnetic fields, providing a work-function-gradient-driven mechanism for enhanced dielectric loss. Using alkaline etching activation and in situ CVD, a hierarchical all-conductive FeSiAl@CNT-Fe 3 C/Fe heterostructure was constructed. Leveraging the synergy of electron-sink-enhanced interface polarization, optimized conduction loss, and magnetic loss, the composite achieves a minimum reflection loss of −76.53 dB at 1.55 mm and an effective absorption bandwidth of 6.06 GHz at 1.72 mm, with a density only 18% of FeSiAl, demonstrating the “thin, lightweight, broadband, strong” advantages. This strategy was further validated in the CoNi alloy system, pioneering a rational design pathway for high-performance electromagnetic protection materials beyond traditional trial-and-error.
authors: Ruping Yang, Peikun Wu, Xin Yan, Ya Ning, Zhenpeng Huo, Shujuan Tan, Guangbin Ji

10.1002/adfm.78426.title: Plasma-Tailored Vertical Graphene Sheath Boosts Sodium-Storage Kinetics in Starch-Derived Hard Carbon Anodes
10.1002/adfm.78426.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite its promise as a viable anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), hard carbon (HC) remains plagued by the simultaneous realization of high capacity, high initial-Coulombic-efficiency (ICE), and superior rate-capability-a bottleneck rooted in microstructural disorder and deficient electronic transport. Herein, a synergistic dual-engineering strategy is reported to circumvent this trilemma. Our approach combines ZnAc 2 -molecular-templating during electrospinning with subsequent vertical graphene (VG) growth via plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). The sacrificial template generates a dense network of closed nanopores, dramatically increasing Na + plateau storage, while the conformal VG sheath establishes an uninterrupted conductive highway that shortens electron pathways. This design boosts closed pore volume by 1.75 times and electronic conductivity by 4.19 times. As a result, the VG-reinforced AC anode achieves an ultrahigh reversible capacity of 440.6 mAh g −1 , ICE of 92.24%, and high-rate performance (323.6 mAh g −1 at 0.8 A g −1 ). Beyond electrode engineering, the intrinsic flexibility and surface functionality of the electrospun membrane enable a “three-in-one” full-cell architecture, where a single fibrous membrane acts as the anode, separator, and cathode host simultaneously. This integrated device delivers an energy density of 325 Wh kg −1 and a high-power output of 1794 W kg −1 , underscoring the potential of coupling chemical activation with nanocarbon-grafting for next-generation SIBs.
authors: Yunxuan Zhang, Ying Xue, Yuanrong Dai, Shengda Tang, Yanjie Qi, Peng-Ju Liang, Jun Jin, Rui Wang, Yansheng Gong, Weiwei Zhou, Xinhui Xia, Huanwen Wang

10.1002/adfm.77583.title: Nitro-Functionalized PDOL Gel Electrolytes with Regulated Li+ Coordination for Li─S Batteries
10.1002/adfm.77583.abstract: ABSTRACT Rational design of lithium-ion coordination architectures within gel polymer electrolytes remains challenging for simultaneously improving ionic transport and interfacial stability in lithium-sulfur batteries. Herein, we report an in situ copolymerization strategy of 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) with π -conjugated nitroaromatic R-glycidyl nosylate (R-GN). The π -conjugated structure promotes electron-density delocalization onto the nitro group, reducing N═O bond polarity compared with conventional nitrate additives. The resulting PDOL@R-GN electrolyte builds a multidimensional lithium-ion coordination network through electronic modulation and spatial effects, enabling preferential Li + transport and a high Li + transference number ( = 0.66) at 25°C. It also promotes a gradient solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) with F- and N-rich components, improving interfacial robustness and ionic transport. Pouch-cell feasibility was demonstrated using a 3 Ah pouch cell, delivering 392 Wh kg −1 under high sulfur loading (8 mg cm −2 ), and lean electrolyte (E/S = 3 g electrolyt e g s −1 ), while retaining 811 mAh g −1 after 40 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 95.0%. This work provides insights into the molecular-level design of multifunctional electrolytes for high-energy-density batteries.
authors: Yunzhen Ye, Qingchen Wei, Mengxian Pei, Baochun Wang, Zhengyi Fan, Jianhao Lu, Weikun Wang, Yaqin Huang

10.1002/adfm.78466.title: Sapphire Surface Reconstruction for Uniform Monolayer, Bilayer 2-inch WSe2 Wafers
10.1002/adfm.78466.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) p-type WSe 2 has remarkable potential to resolve the intrinsic performance mismatch between p-type and n-type materials for next-generation integrated electronics. However, a scalable chemical vapor deposition (CVD) strategy for wafer-scale, layer-tunable, high-quality p-type WSe 2 is still lacking. Here, we realize 2-inch monolayer and bilayer WSe 2 via Al 2 O 3 interface passivation engineering. By investigating the Al 2 O 3 interfacial structure variations of Se-terminated and Al-terminated sapphire, we found that Se-passivated Al 2 O 3 achieves superior lattice matching and strong interfacial coupling with WSe 2 , enabling alkaline-etching-dependent separation. In contrast, Al-passivated WSe 2 facilitates efficient water-assisted PMMA transfer of WSe 2 owing to weak interfacial interaction with sapphire. Top-gate transistors reveal Se-passivated WSe 2 is intrinsically p-type, while Al-passivated WSe 2 displays n-type due to ALD-doping. The electrical performance of bilayer WSe 2 outperforms monolayers, with excellent uniformity. Back-gate transistors of Al-passivated WSe 2 present tunable ambipolar transport with switchable n/p-type conduction. Pristine bilayer WSe 2 exhibits a hole mobility of 13.73 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , while ALD-doped WSe 2 realized an electron mobility up to 60.17 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Moreover, WSe 2 /MoS 2 complementary inverters exhibit reliable switching behavior. This study develops a feasible approach to grow wafer-scale WSe 2 , offering a reliable material preparation scheme for large-scale fabrication of 2D-based logic devices.
authors: Xin Lu, Ding Lu, Keyan Chen, Yangxiu Chen, Ling Wang, Haijuan Wu, Chao Tan, Xin Hao, Guohua Hu, Zegao Wang

10.1002/adfm.78468.title: Coupling Grain Architecture Control With Oxygen-Vacancy Suppression in Ultra-Large Single- and Quasi-Single-Crystal Ni-Rich Cathodes
10.1002/adfm.78468.abstract: ABSTRACT Single-crystalline Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes exhibit superior cycling and thermal stability over conventional polycrystalline counterparts by eliminating grain-boundary-associated degradation. However, the extended Li + diffusion length in single crystals limits practical particle sizes to only a few micrometers, creating a fundamental trade-off between electrode density and electrochemical performance. Here, we report a practical synthesis strategy for ultra-large (≈15 µm) single-crystalline and quasi-single-crystalline LiNi 0.95 Co 0.04 Mn 0.01 O 2 cathodes that deliver an exceptional rate capacity of 170 mA h g −1 at 5 C despite their unprecedented particle size. Using these grain-engineered architectures, we identify oxygen transport during high-temperature synthesis as a previously overlooked factor governing defect formation in ultra-large Ni-rich cathodes. In single-crystal particles, sluggish oxygen diffusion through the ordered bulk lattice produces a pronounced oxygen-deficient structural state, accompanied by severe cation disorder. In contrast, internal grain boundaries in quasi-single-crystal particles act as rapid oxygen-transport channels, enabling efficient oxygen redistribution during sintering and thereby suppressing oxygen vacancy formation and cation mixing while preserving structural integrity. Consequently, ultra-large quasi-single-crystal cathodes simultaneously achieve high electrode density, fast reaction kinetics, excellent thermal stability, and long-term cycling durability. This work identifies grain-boundary-assisted oxygen transport as a key design consideration for defect control in ultra-large, highly Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes.
authors: Soon-Kie Hong, Gawon Song, Seung Weon Jeong, Seung Hyun Choi, Junsung Park, Byunghyun Yun, Junho Jung, Chaeyeon Kwak, Jaeuk Ha, Chanhyun Baik, Sangheon Lee, Kyu Tae Lee

10.1002/adfm.78281.title: NaYF4: Er3+ Nanoparticles-Graphene Photodetector for High-Responsivity 1.5 µm Narrowband Imaging and Multi-Wavelength Sensing
10.1002/adfm.78281.abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon-based photodetection in the 1.5 µm spectral window is important for next-generation photonic systems, enabling critical applications in optical communication, LiDAR, and atmospheric gas sensing. Although erbium-based upconversion photodetectors (UPDs) offer advantages in cost-effective fabrication and stable spectral selectivity, their deployment is fundamentally limited by compromised responsivity, slow response times, and complex multilayer architectures that hinder scalability. Here, we report a UPD that synergistically integrates high-efficiency Er-based nanoparticles (ENPs) with an engineered graphene photogating architecture. Fabricated on SiO 2 /p+-Si substrates, the optimized device achieves unparalleled performance metrics: a record-high responsivity of 59.5 A/W at 1 V bias, millisecond-scale response dynamics, and narrowband 1.5 µm detection. This exceptional performance originates from two synergistic mechanisms: the ENPs' high upconversion quantum yield (2.1%) and a substantial photoconductive gain (∼10 7 ) from the graphene photogating, increasing responsivity by a factor of 5 over conventional designs. Additionally, leveraging the intrinsic narrowband response of ENPs, we demonstrate a dual-channel wavelength-selective structure capable of effectively discriminating signals within the 1.5 µm band from those below 1.1 µm. This permits simultaneous multi-wavelength detection, as demonstrated via spatially-resolved imaging at 633 and 1523 nm. Combined with its fabrication simplicity and scalability, this work represents a significant leap forward for high-performance UPDs.
authors: Jinhua Wu, Hao Sun, Zhang Liang, Ying Cui, Shipeng Yao, Yongzhuo Li, Zhangyu Hou, Cun-Zheng Ning

10.1002/adfm.78423.title: Stacking-Engineered Tunable Altermagnetism in Topological FeSe Bilayer Systems
10.1002/adfm.78423.abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnetism and topological insulators represent two of the most transformative frontiers in modern condensed matter physics, spintronics, and quantum information science. Bringing these two paradigms together opens a largely unexplored route toward fundamentally new quantum phenomena. Here, we predict a topological altermagnetic phase in bilayer tetragonal Fe-based superconductors and reveal it as a highly tunable platform for valley-polarized anomalous Hall and quantum anomalous Hall physics. Based on first-principles calculations, we show that the characteristic spin-splitting and valley polarization can be effectively tuned via applied strain. Moreover, increasing the in-plane uniaxial strain can induce a topological phase transition from topological insulator phase to quantum anomalous Hall insulator phase. These findings reveal a powerful route for controlling altermagnetism and topology while identifying a realistic material platform for its experimental realization and technological exploitation.
authors: Jie Li, Shifang Li, Mengyang Zhang, Pan Zhou, Jianxin Zhong, Ruqian Wu
