This article systematically reviews the latest research progress of memristors in intelligent perception and neuromorphic systems for next-generation HCI. First, starting from the material system, performance regulation, and application adaptation are analyzed. Second, the strategy of memristors in device design and integration architecture is discussed. Furthermore, the biomimetic perception system based on memristors is emphasized, demonstrating its integration capability at the hardware level of brain-inspired perception information processing. Finally, it systematically summarizes the research achievements of memristors in the field of HCI applications and discusses the key challenges currently faced. Looking forward, this review suggests that memristors are expected to provide a solid foundation for building high-performance, low-power, and biocompatible next-generation HCI systems.
authors: Jinlong He, Bo Yang, Bai Sun, Qi Chen, Chuncai Kong, Zelin Cao, Kaikai Gao, Mengna Wang, Longhui Fu, Kun Wang, Teng Wu, Songling Wang, Ye Tang, Jinyou Shao

10.1002/adfm.78493.title: Entropy-Driven Local Polarization Engineering for Superior Energy Storage Performance
10.1002/adfm.78493.abstract: ABSTRACT Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) with high recoverable energy storage density ( W rec ) and high efficiency ( η ) are essential electronic components in advanced electronic devices and pulsed power systems. However, achieving both high W rec and η remains a long-standing challenge. Here, guided by phase-field simulations, we propose a strategy of entropy-driven local polarization fluctuations to realize excellent energy storage performance by judiciously introducing foreign ions with different ferroelectric activities. We validate this by fabricating high-quality MLCCs and achieve a high W rec of 23.5 J cm −3 and an ultra-high η of 95.1% simultaneously. Atomic-scale structural analysis reveals local polarization fluctuations where ultra-weak polarity regions coexist with short-range polarity regions. This unique configuration has good flexibility and enables easy polarization switching and fast recovery, thereby achieving high polarization and near-zero hysteresis. This approach offers a new paradigm for designing high-performance capacitors.
authors: Xiaoyan Dong, Zhipeng Wang, Ke Xu, Houbing Huang, Xiang Lv, Jiagang Wu

10.1002/adfm.78452.title: Tailoring the Orientation of Electron-Delocalized Conjugated Structures in Polyimide Dielectrics for High-Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
10.1002/adfm.78452.abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric polymers for high-temperature capacitive energy storage require both high thermal stability and electrical insulation. Although the rigid conjugated structure of polyimide affords a high glass transition temperature, making it a promising candidate, it also introduces compromised electrical insulation through electron delocalization. Here, we propose and demonstrate that regulating the spatial orientation of localized π-containing/electron-delocalized conjugated structures in polyimide can effectively break the trade-off between thermal stability and electrical insulation. The out-of-plane orientation of localized conjugated structures reduces the spatial connectivity of short-range electron-delocalization sites along the electric-field direction, thereby suppressing continuous carrier migration. Consequently, under high temperature and elevated electric field, the out-of-plane-oriented semi-aromatic polyimide exhibits an electrical conductivity reduced by over an order of magnitude compared to its in-plane-oriented counterpart. It achieves a high discharge energy density ( U e ) of 7.16 J cm − 3 with a charge-discharge efficiency ( η ) exceeding 90% at 200°C, surpassing its in-plane-oriented analogue ( U e = 3.44 J cm − 3 , η = 90%). Furthermore, analysis of the dual gas-phase and condensed-phase mechanism demonstrates the exceptional breakdown self-healing ability of the designed polymer, highlighting the promise of the out-of-plane conjugation orientation for high-performance polymer capacitors operating at elevated temperatures.
authors: Yuting Wan, Shuotong Wang, Hang Luo, Fan Wang, Deng Hu, Guanghu He, Yiqi Zhu, Dou Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78252.title: Highly Stable Composite Solid Electrolytes Based on Caffeic Acid Molecular Bridges for Long Lifespan Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78252.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state lithium metal batteries are promising next generation energy storage devices and composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) with high ionic conductivity and mechanical stability have attracted widespread attention. However, the slow ion transport kinetics at the heterogeneous interface between ceramic fillers and polymer matrices severely limits the performance of CSEs. This work reports a facile surface modification using biogenic caffeic acid (CA) to functionalize LLZTO. CA monomers anchor on LLZTO via Lewis acid-base interactions and react with surface lithium carbonate, during which in-situ polymerization evolves to form a uniform 5 nm poly(caffeic acid) (PCA) coating. After incorporating PCA@LLZTO into the PEO matrix, hydrogen bonding between PCA polar groups and PEO chains promotes filler dispersion and reduces interfacial resistance. The PCA@LLZTO/PEO CSE exhibits significantly enhanced ionic conductivity of 2.19 × 10 −4 S cm −1 , a reliable Li + transference number of 0.64, excellent mechanical robustness and superior Li metal compatibility, along with a stable electrochemical window of 5.1 V and long-term stable cycling over 3200 h in Li||Li symmetric cells. This superior performance stems from the sequential reactions of PCA that homogenize Li + distribution, suppress Li dendrites, and stabilize the electrolyte/electrode interface, presenting a green strategy for practical solid-state lithium metal batteries.
authors: Kan Zhao, Lin Li, Bo Wang, He Cao, Xiaohan Shi, Shixue Dou, Hua Yuan, Yang Zuo, Fuyi Jiang, Wei Du, Fushan Li, Wenbao Liu, Tianyi Ma, Xiaoyu Zhang

10.1002/adfm.77914.title: Reversible Tuning of Multiple Molecular Kinking for Stem Cell Regulation In Vivo
10.1002/adfm.77914.abstract: ABSTRACT In the native extracellular matrix, collagen fibrils regulate stem cell fate and tissue regeneration by modulating the number of serial kinks via intramolecular kinking and unkinking, which affects integrin ligation. However, biomimetic materials composed solely of multi-kink-bearing molecules for dynamic regulation of ligand exposure remain limited. In this study, we designed materials composed solely of liganded multiple kink-bearing molecules with a tunable number of kink points (mono-kink, tri-kink, and penta-kink molecules), including flexible linkers and densely packed via intermolecular interactions, are designed. Near-infrared-upconverted ultraviolet light and visible light induce multiple kinking and unkinking of liganded multiple kink-bearing molecules conjugated to upconversion nanoparticle-coated materials, inducing kinked and unkinked states, respectively. Tri-kinking and unkinking mediate the effective regulation of ligand masking and exposure, respectively, by modulating intermolecular interactions, while mono-kink and penta-kink molecules continuously expose the ligands regardless of their kinking/unkinking state. Tri-unkinking cyclically stimulates integrin ligation and focal adhesion-mediated stem cell mechanotransduction and differentiation in vivo, which are inhibited by tri-kinking. This study presents a newly developed reversibly switchable multi-kink molecule-conjugated surface for dynamic regulation of ligand exposure and stem cell responses, providing a useful modality for regulating cell-material interactions and stem cell fate in vivo.
authors: Kanghyeon Kim, Jeongah Shin, Chowon Kim, Honghwan Choi, Dahee Kim, Sungkyu Lee, Choongmo Kang, Hyunsik Hong, Taehoon Ha, Nayeon Kang, Jungyeon Rhi, Ramar Thangam, Yuri Kim, Jeongyun Heo, Cheol Hwan Kwak, Jangsun Hwang, Daun Jeong, Rasoul Moradi, Sunghoon Hur, Hyun-Cheol Song, Hyun-Do Jung, Min Jae Lee, Rongqin Huang, Pooyan Makvandi, Yun Suk Huh, Ji Hye Choi, Wenguo Cui, Sehoon Kim, Heemin Kang

10.1002/adfm.78411.title: Amorphous ZrOx-Mediated *OH Enrichment Enables Dynamic Oxygen Replenishment for Stable Acidic Water Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.78411.abstract: ABSTRACT While triggering the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) represents an efficient approach to enhancing the intrinsic activity of iridium-based catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), the irreversible lattice oxygen loss and subsequent Ir dissolution induce structural collapse, constituting the fundamental activity-stability trade-off. To address this challenge, we propose an amorphous support-mediated *OH enrichment strategy that dynamically replenishes oxygen vacancies (O v ) to stabilize and optimize the LOM pathway. This concept is exemplified by engineering IrO x nanoparticles supported on amorphous zirconia (ZrO x ). In addition to anchoring Ir sites and mitigating their over-oxidation-induced dissolution, the ZrO x support efficiently facilitates water dissociation, leading to the in situ accumulation of reactive *OH intermediates. This enrichment process dynamically replenishes the O v generated during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), thereby accelerating the LOM rate-determining step and simultaneously preserving the catalyst's structural integrity and boosting the intrinsic activity, as evidenced by in situ spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations. In PEMWE tests, the catalyst achieves a low voltage of 1.75 V at 2 A cm −2 and demonstrates stable operation for 1000 h. This work establishes a new design principle for developing highly efficient and durable Ir-based OER catalysts for PEMWE applications.
authors: Yuqing Cheng, Yibo Wang, Zhaoping Shi, Ziang Wang, Ming Yang, Minhua Shao, Meiling Xiao, Changpeng Liu, Wei Xing

10.1002/adfm.78257.title: Thermal Stability of High-Entropy Oxide Thin Films: From Stability Mechanisms to Materials Design
10.1002/adfm.78257.abstract: ABSTRACT High-entropy oxide (HEO) thin films, as an important branch of high-entropy material systems, have shown broad application prospects in energy, catalysis, protective coatings, and other fields, owing to their unique compositional design strategy and potentially excellent multifunctionality. Thermal stability is a core factor determining their high-temperature service performance and reliability, and has become a key research focus and challenge in this field. This paper reviews recent progress in the thermal stability of HEO thin films, focusing on material-system classification, major influencing factors, and underlying mechanisms. It highlights key processes, including phase evolution, elemental segregation, grain growth, and interfacial reactions, and examines how the four core effects regulate thermal stability. The review also outlines potential applications of HEO thin films in high-temperature and multifunctional environments. Current studies show that HEO thin films generally offer superior structural stability compared with conventional oxide films; however, long-term thermal cycling reliability and accurate performance prediction under extreme conditions remain important challenges. Future research should integrate high-throughput experimentation and machine learning to optimize compositional space, and further explore material composition optimization, defect engineering, and stability under coupled multi-field conditions, thereby promoting the practical application of HEO thin films in high-temperature functional devices.
authors: Xian Li, Jiali Yang, Ke Liu, Daoyun Zhu, Xin-Gui Tang, Zhongfei Mu, Fugen Wu

10.1002/adfm.78335.title: Broadband Convolutional Processing Perception-Memory-Computation InSe Neuromorphic Vision Device for High-Accuracy Recognition of Color Images
10.1002/adfm.78335.abstract: ABSTRACT Broadband convolution processing is critical for accurate color image recognition. However, current broadband convolution processing involves a photoresponse matrix based on continuous-voltage modulation devices, resulting in high energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate an InSe neuromorphic device that integrates broadband convolutional processing with perception, memory, and computation functions to realize high-accuracy recognition of color images with the potential for low latency and reduced energy consumption. A photoresponse matrix was constructed using voltage pulses for broadband convolutional processing. The device's broadband perception capability originates from the moderate bandgap of approximately 1.3 eV in InSe, while its memory function is attributed to the ferroelectric polarization effect of Pb(Zr 0.2 Ti 0.8 )O 3 (PZT). Analog computation is realized via bias-dependent, continued nonvolatile positive and negative photoconductive responses. Moreover, the multiband non-volatile photocurrent matrixes generated by the InSe neuromorphic devices are used for broadband convolution processing of color images. Furthermore, combining the multifunctional InSe neuromorphic device with a convolutional neural network achieves 97.4% recognition accuracy for color “S”, “D”, “U” letter images after only ten training epochs. The proposed work is promising to set the stage for next-generation intelligent machine vision systems in imminent embodied artificial intelligence humanoid robots.
authors: Jing Chen, Zhen-Hua Wang, Min Jin, Ping Li, Tiantian Wei, Jianguo Hu, Guanhua Dun, Hengji Li, Zonghao Wang, Shanbin Liu, Xiao-Ming Wu, Hong Liu, Tian-Ling Ren, Lin Han

10.1002/adfm.78410.title: Wearable Electrochemical Sweat Sensors Beyond Snapshots With Long-Term Stability
10.1002/adfm.78410.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable sweat electrochemical sensors enable continuous and noninvasive monitoring of electrolytes, metabolites, and stress-related biomarkers for personalized healthcare. However, the translation of these platforms from proof-of-concept prototypes to reliable clinical tools is hindered by a critical bottleneck of long-term operational stability. In realistic wearable scenarios, complex biofouling, fluctuating microenvironments, and dynamic physical deformations collectively trigger degradation pathways that severely compromise signal fidelity. In this review, we establish a stability-centered framework to systematically untangle the multi-dimensional failure mechanisms across four primary sensing modalities, including ion-selective potentiometric, enzymatic, nanozyme-based, and affinity-based sensors. State-of-the-art mitigation strategies are then discussed, encompassing materials engineering, device architecture, and computational calibration. Furthermore, critical challenges and prospects encompassing AI-driven material discovery, continuous sampling, and edge-computing-assisted analytics are introduced, serving as a timely resource to accelerate the translation of wearable electrochemical sensors into reliable platforms for comprehensive health management.
authors: Min Wang, Changxin Li, Hepeng Yang, Zhuojun Yan, Zhifeng Liu, Sisi He

10.1002/adfm.78414.title: Phototunable Nonreciprocal Cilia-Like Self-Oscillator
10.1002/adfm.78414.abstract: ABSTRACT Natural cilia generate non-reciprocal beating through coordinated deformation and recovery, enabling sensing, propulsion, transport, and feeding. Synthetic cilia-like actuators have been widely explored, yet combining self-sustained oscillation, non-reciprocal motion, multimode tunability, and adaptive behavior in fluidic environments remains a daunting challenge. Here we report a phototunable nonreciprocal cilia-like self-oscillator (PNCSO) that address this challenge. PNCSOs are based on light-driven high-degree-of-freedom deformation of self-winding liquid crystal elastomer fibers, which can generate multiple non-reciprocal oscillation modes through coupled 3D deformation and dynamic stiffness modulation. PNCSOs enable real-time tuning of oscillatory motion through multiple optical inputs. Interestingly, two adjacent PNCSOs can communicate with each other, and give rise to synchronized, collective motion through compliant coupling. In addition, their self-sustained non-reciprocal oscillation enables active manipulation of small objects in viscous aqueous environments. This work establishes an effective strategy for constructing adaptive and functional artificial ciliary systems for soft robotic and future microfluidic applications.
authors: Zhiming Hu, Kai Liu, Tonghui Zhao, Jiao Wang, Xin Shen, Jiu-an Lv

10.1002/adfm.78455.title: Vectorial Slip-Touch Perception Enabled by Sliding-Gated Charge Carrier Dynamics
10.1002/adfm.78455.abstract: ABSTRACT High-dimensional tactile perception is essential for dexterous robotic manipulation, but is severely constrained by the hardware-stacking of pixelated arrays or the computational latency of inverse-problem algorithms. To overcome these bottlenecks, we report a monolithic, array-free robotic skin (SG-skin) driven by sliding-gated carrier dynamics, achieving high-fidelity, vectorial slip-touch perception. Specifically, leveraging a localized triboelectric field acting as a moving gate, the SG-skin triggers reversible microscopic p -to- n inversion and directional carrier transport within a continuous semiconductor film, deterministically translating macroscopic mechanical stimuli into vectorial electrical signatures. Supported by an analytical model that validates in-sensor signal decoupling, a minimalist four-electrode design augmented by a computationally lightweight machine learning framework concurrently resolves sliding speed, omnidirectional trajectory (1° precision), material type, and touch localization. Ultimately, our SG-skin maps complex tactile stimuli into deterministic commands, enabling agile human-machine interaction and advanced closed-loop robotic control. By breaking the longstanding dependency on complex sensor arrays or resource-intensive computations, this sliding-gated strategy translates microscale charge carrier dynamics into macroscopic intelligent perception, providing a scalable and robust material foundation for next-generation embodied intelligence.
authors: Chongxiang Pan, Hongxiang Xue, Hao Sun, Zi Hao Guo, Jing Wang, Yutong Song, Fuchun Sun, Zhong Lin Wang, Xiong Pu

10.1002/adfm.78458.title: Nitrogen Configuration-Driven Modulation of Built-in Electric Field Toward Synchronously Boosted Anti-Corrosion and Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
10.1002/adfm.78458.abstract: ABSTRACT Built-in electric field (BIEF) engineering has emerged as a promising strategy for regulating interface electron structure and tailoring multifunctional performance; however, constructing strong BIEF to achieve multifunctionality remains a challenge. Herein, an intensified-BIEF strategy through nitrogen configuration regulation is proposed in CoNi/Mo 2 C@N-doped carbon (NC) composites to simultaneously enhance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption and anti-corrosion. By tailoring pyrolysis temperature, the nitrogen configuration and electronic structure of the NC matrix are systematically regulated, enlarging the work function difference and strengthening BIEF at the CoNi/NC and NC/Mo 2 C heterointerfaces. The intensified BIEF induces directional charge migration, generating oriented interface dipole arrays that enhance the dipole-array polarization relaxation and boost conductive loss. Meanwhile, the strong BIEF facilitates electron accumulation at the CoNi surface, suppressing charge delocalization that inhibits anodic dissolution and promotes passivation. The optimized CoNi/Mo 2 C@NC achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 6 GHz at a thickness of 1.8 mm. Meanwhile, compared with commercial absorbers, the corrosion potential is increased by 94.9%, while the corrosion current is reduced by 74.5%, demonstrating exceptional durability and ultralow corrosion kinetics in marine environments. This work reveals the mechanistic role of strong BIEF in simultaneously optimizing EMW absorption and anti-corrosion, and provides a novel strategy for designing multifunctional materials.
authors: Bo Huang, Chen Li, Fang Ye, Jingchao Wang, Yuchen Cao, Yi An, Wenjing Zhang, Xiaomeng Fan

10.1002/adfm.78415.title: Minimizing the Trade-off Between Voltage and Current in Organic Solar Cells via an Anthracene-Based Non-Fullerene Equalizer
10.1002/adfm.78415.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic solar cells are among the most advanced thin-film photovoltaic technologies due to their lightweight, thin, and flexible characteristics. However, an inherent trade-off between open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) and short-circuit current density ( J SC ) exists, fundamentally stemming from the balance between charge generation and recombination. To address this challenge, we developed a two-dimensional extension molecule based on the A-D-A′-D-A non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) framework by replacing the central core with anthracene and introducing halogen-free end groups, yielding a novel molecule named QxAt. This molecule combines high crystallinity with a complementary absorption spectrum to commonly used NFAs. When incorporated as a voltage-current balancer into the PM6:BTP-eC9 system, the active layer morphology was largely preserved, while molecular packing was modestly optimized, contributing to more efficient exciton dissociation and charge collection, improved hole and electron mobilities, and effective suppression of charge recombination, ultimately enabling a moderate improvement in J SC . More importantly, QxAt significantly increased the electroluminescence quantum efficiency, effectively suppressing non-radiative recombination and reducing energy loss, which in turn elevated V OC . Consequently, the PCE was markedly improved from 18.9% to 20.1%, achieving a synergistic optimization of both V OC and J SC . This work provides a molecular design strategy to mitigate the voltage-current trade-off for high-efficiency organic photovoltaics.
authors: Lijun Hu, Haoran Hu, Dingqin Hu, Huanyan Jiang, Menglong He, Xianyong Zhou, Chang Liu, Xingzhu Wang, Duu-Jong Lee, Hanjian Lai

10.1002/adfm.78418.title: Multivalued Logic and Encryption Based on Anti-Ambipolar Transistor Dynamic Controlled by Light and Temperature
10.1002/adfm.78418.abstract: ABSTRACT Anti-ambipolar transistors (AATs) show great potential to improve the performance of ternary logic circuits and the areal computing density. Beyond developing the environmental adaptability of AATs, exploring the synergistic modulation mechanisms and modulating 1/2 state through external environment signals offers new insights for the specific-application of multivalued logic devices. In this study, reconfigurable organic AATs are developed, constructed from an asymmetric p-n heterojunction architecture. The dynamic carrier's distribution near the vertical interface with gate voltage changing resulted in the channel current non-monotonic behavior. The light-induced photocarrier generation and thermally enhanced charge transfer enabled light-temperature antagonistic operations on the dynamic control of 1/2 state. The specific pair of optical intensity and temperature could be set as the independent “key” to activate the encrypted 1/2 state, a portable decryption framework based on the puzzle-style optical encoding and thermal decoding strategy is implemented in encrypted binary images that enhance the information security confidentiality in specified environment.
authors: Diandian Chen, Jingwen Wang, Chuan Qian, Yanran Mao, Wenjian Wu, Yangkang Chen, Dongsheng Tang, Jia Sun

10.1002/adfm.77723.title: Active Learning for Data-Efficient Optimization of Entangled Granular Metamaterials
10.1002/adfm.77723.abstract: ABSTRACT Entangled granular materials derive exceptional macroscopic rigidity from topological interlocking of their constituents. However, rationally designing particle geometries to maximize this effect remains a formidable challenge due to the immense configuration space and the prohibitive computational cost of discrete element simulations. Here, we present a data-efficient and uncertainty-aware design framework for autonomous discovery of optimal particle geometries that substantially enhance macroscopic yield strength beyond conventional heuristic shape families. A Semi-Supervised Graph Wasserstein Autoencoder embeds discrete particle topologies into a continuous latent manifold, while Langevin-based stochastic optimization explores the structure-property landscape. By explicitly penalizing epistemic uncertainty through a Lower Confidence Bound acquisition strategy, the framework robustly avoids spurious optima under extreme data scarcity. The discovered low-aspect-ratio particle geometries achieve quasi-cohesive behavior, high yield strength, and self-supporting capability typically associated with slender fibers. Compression and angle-of-repose experiments on 3D-printed assemblies confirm high simulation fidelity and validate geometry enhanced, interlocking-dominated load-bearing architectures.
authors: Peng Wang, Gaoyan Shi, Xin Bian, Yu Guo

10.1002/adfm.78417.title: Ultra-Selective Molecular-Sieving Gas Separation Membranes Enabled by Light-Heat Dual Crosslinking of Polyimide for Helium Extraction From Natural Gas
10.1002/adfm.78417.abstract: ABSTRACT Helium extraction from natural gas demands ultra-high He/CH 4 selectivity (>1000), yet this benchmark remains largely unmet by polymeric membranes due to the permeability-selectivity trade-off and the challenge of constructing sub-4 Å sieving channels. Here, we report an orthogonal light-heat dual-crosslinking strategy to program the free-volume topology of polyimide membranes. A photoreactive precursor (6FCC-X) was synthesized via a click reaction by incorporating photosensitive units (C═C─S) and varying amounts of thermally labile─COOH groups into the backbone. UV irradiation first triggers [2+2] cycloaddition to construct a dense and uniform super-crosslinked network, which defines the primary molecular-sieving framework. Subsequent thermal decarboxylation generated rigid biphenyl linkages that are proposed to function as molecular-strut-like structural motifs, enhancing chain rigidity, improving micropore connectivity, and refining sub-4 Å sieving constrictions. This sequential topology programming decouples helium transport from methane exclusion, which enables the optimized 6FCC-3-CR membrane to achieve a He permeability of 33.9 Barrer and an exceptional He/CH 4 selectivity of 3767, outperforming most reported polymer-based membranes and rivaling advanced carbon molecular sieve membranes. This work establishes a molecular-strut-mediated topology-programming principle for polymer molecular sieves, offering a general route to reconcile fast transport with precise molecular exclusion.
authors: Mingwei Cai, Fuhui Liang, Fudong Deng, Baisheng Liang, Shiyang Zhang, Yonggang Min

10.1002/adfm.77950.title: Robust Adaptive Interphases via Dual Regulation of Solvation and Molecular Armor for Long-Life Ni-Rich Quasi-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/adfm.77950.abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of nickel-rich lithium metal batteries is significantly impeded by the trade-off between ion transport efficiency and electrode/electrolyte interfacial stability. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a 9-µm-thick composite quasi-solid electrolyte MLZPE based on a molecular-armor-mediated solvation engineering strategy. MLZPE features a three-dimensional interpenetrating network in which nanosuperacid ZrO 2 -SO 4 2− preferentially interacts with ethylene carbonate to weaken Li + -solvent coordination, thereby increasing the Li + transference number to 0.698 and raising the ionic conductivity to 0.107 mS/cm. Simultaneously, in-situ polymerized poly(N, N'-methylene bisacrylamide) (PMBA) forms a dense passivation layer that chemically anchors onto the superacid surface, suppressing electrolyte decomposition. Together with poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (P(VDF-HFP)), PMBA promotes the formation of interphases enriched with LiF and Li 3 N. in-situ impedance spectroscopy reveals that these interphases undergo reversible reconstruction during cycling, indicating adaptive and self-healing characteristics. As a result, the NCM83||Li quasi-solid-state cell achieves 92.6% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. This work demonstrates a synergistic design that concurrently achieves rapid ion transport and durable interfacial stability, providing a viable route to high-energy, long-cycle-life nickel-rich quasi-solid-state batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79171.title: Non-Precious Metal Catalysts for Acidic Oxygen Evolution in Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis: Degradation Challenges and Regulation Strategies
10.1002/adfm.79171.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is a promising technology for green hydrogen production, but its large-scale application is still limited by the high cost and limited supply of Ir-based anode catalysts. Non-precious metal catalysts provide abundant and structurally tunable alternatives, yet they generally suffer from poor stability under acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions. Their high activity often relies on reactive metal centers, oxygen defects, reconstructed surfaces, or flexible coordination environments, which may also increase the risk of structural damage and material loss, causing degradation of the catalyst and lower activity. This Review discusses the thermodynamic basis of catalyst instability and the primary catalyst degradation processes under operation, including proton- and potential-driven metal dissolution, interfacial water-assisted corrosion and oxygen-sublattice depletion, as well as degradation amplification effect induced by dynamic operation. The coupling among these degradation processes and their dependence on operating conditions are further elaborated. The degradation risks associated with the adsorbate evolution, lattice oxygen, oxide path, and mixed OER pathways are then compared. Based on these challenges, stability-oriented strategies are summarized as intrinsic structure tuning, heterointerfacial engineering, proton/water microenvironment modulation, and dissolution-redeposition regulation. Finally, recent advances in both half-cell measurements and practical PEMWE devices are reviewed, and future research priorities are outlined with respect to standardized testing protocols, quantitative material tracking, rational catalyst design, and scalable device development.
authors: Jie Yin, Dongsheng Cai, Yanji Bao, Tianfei Chu, Kuo Liu

10.1002/adfm.79277.title: Bifurcation-Driven Additive Redistribution from Bulk Doping Enables In-Situ Modulation of Interfaces Toward >26% Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79277.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfaces in perovskite solar cells govern crystallization kinetics, interfacial energetics, defect formation, charge transport dynamics, and nonradiative recombination of charge carriers, thereby critically determining device efficiency and operational stability. Here, we report an in situ dual-interface engineering strategy using a multifunctional additive, maleimido propionic acid hydrazide hydrochloride (MPAH.HCl), incorporated directly into the perovskite precursor. During film formation, MPAH.HCl undergoes spontaneous bifurcation-driven bidirectional segregation, with Cl − preferentially enriching at the buried interface and MPAH + accumulating at the near top surface. At the buried interface, Cl − modulates crystallization dynamics, promotes grain growth, passivates deep-level defects, and improves energy-level alignment. Simultaneously, surface-segregated MPAH + effectively passivates dominant vacancy (V I , V Pb , V FA ) and antisite (Pb I , I Pb , I FA ) defects. This synergistic dual-interface modulation suppresses nonradiative recombination while facilitating efficient charge extraction and transport. As a result, optimized inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a fill factor of 86.6% (vs. 80.6% for the control), with a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.10% for 0.09 cm 2 , and 24.28% for 1 cm 2 devices. Furthermore, enhanced crystallinity and stabilized interfacial chemistry significantly improve device stability under ambient, thermal, and operational stress conditions. This work introduces bifurcation additive segregation as an effective strategy for simultaneous buried and top-interface optimization, enabling highly efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Himangshu Baishya, Ramkrishna Das Adhikari, Swastik Laha, Mayur Jagdishbhai Patel, Deepak Yadav, Diganta Bhattacharyya, Kalishankar Bhattacharyya, Parameswar Krishnan Iyer

10.1002/adfm.77445.title: Simultaneous Enhancement of Performance and Stability in Dual-Gate a-IGZO Thin-Film Transistors via Single-Step Laser Annealing for Capacitor-Less DRAM
authors: Sihyeon Kwon, Junil Kim, Geuntae Park, Minseok Kim, Woohyun Hwang, Wanki Kim, Daewon Ha, Byeongmoon Lee, Jae Eun Jang, Hyuk-Jun Kwon

10.1002/adfm.79378.title: A p-Type Ladder-Polymer Photoelectrochemical Transistor Enabling Integrated Optical Sensing and Adaptive Computing
10.1002/adfm.79378.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of optical sensing, signal amplification, memory, and computation in compact devices is important for artificial visual systems, neuromorphic electronics, and robotics. Organic photoelectrochemical transistors (OPECTs) offer a promising platform, as their photonic-ionic-electronic coupling enables low-voltage operation and intrinsic amplification. However, most single-component OPECTs rely on n -type mixed ionic-electronic conductors, while high-performing p -type devices remain scarce. Advancing p -type photoactive materials is crucial for complementary circuits with reconfigurable responses. We report a high-performance p -type OPECT based on the ladder-type organic conductor, PBBT-Me, serving as both light-sensitive channel and gate electrode. Under illumination, the device achieves a photocurrent of ∼640 µA, and a photoinduced transconductance modulation ratio of 35, combining strong photoresponse with transistor amplification. The effect arises from light-induced gate potential modulation that enhances electrochemical channel doping and increases drain current. Beyond photodetection, the OPECT emulates optical synaptic functions such as short-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and rehearsal learning, enabling neuromorphic preprocessing for digit recognition. A complementary, light-controlled inverter operates as a voltage-to-voltage photoamplifier with gain of 120 V/V, supporting optically switchable OR/NOR logic. Integration with robotic platforms further demonstrates light-controlled gestures and motion, establishing p -type ladder-polymer OPECTs as versatile building blocks for compact optoelectronic and neuromorphic systems.
authors: Zhongliang Zhou, Han-Yan Wu, Meera Stephen, Xuechao Xing, Qiang He, Shuai Chen, Nripan Mathews, Simone Fabiano, Wei Lin Leong

10.1002/adfm.79352.title: Endocytosed pH-Sensitive Nanoparticles Orchestrate Mitochondrial Bioenergetics and Calcium Signaling to Boost NSC-Mediated Alzheimer's Therapy
10.1002/adfm.79352.abstract: ABSTRACT Neural stem cell (NSC) transplantation holds great potential for Alzheimer's disease (AD) therapy; however, its efficacy is severely compromised by the oxidative microenvironment, which impairs mitochondrial function and promotes aberrant glial differentiation. To overcome this barrier, lysosome-responsive EGCG-lysine nanoparticles (EL NPs) were developed. Upon endo-lysosomal disassembly, EL NPs release active components that scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) and restore mitochondrial bioenergetics via AMPK signaling. This metabolic rescue activates a Ca 2 + -dependent MAPK pathway, driving commitment to the GABAergic neuronal lineage. Under oxidative stress, EL NPs enhanced neuronal differentiation efficiency by 2.5-3.0-fold compared with spontaneous differentiation while suppressing astroglial activation. In an AD mouse model, transplantation of EL NP-loaded NSCs promoted in situ neurogenesis, attenuated neuroinflammation, and restored cognitive performance to ∼89%-90% of wild-type levels. These results present a translatable strategy to augment NSC-based repair by modulating intracellular responses to oxidative stress and promoting neuronal differentiation.
authors: Zhong Zhuang, Dongshuang Wang, Zhichao Feng, Qihao Yan, Aijun Hao, Xiancheng Ai, Congcong Zhang, Zanmei Zhou, Hong Liu, Chunhui Sun, Wenjuan Zhou, Baojin Ma

10.1002/adfm.78930.title: Bidentate Pb2+ Chelation Enables Unified PbI2 Crystallization Control for Process-Agnostic Perovskite Fabrication and High-Performance Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78930.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of perovskite solar cells depends on how the absorber crystallizes. PbI 2 nucleates unevenly and grows without order. The resulting films carry iodide-rich aggregates, nonuniform grains, and a high density of grain-boundary defects that degrade device performance. Existing strategies for controlling crystallization are typically designed for a single deposition route and rarely work in another. We report that bathocuproine (BCP), a phenanthroline derivative, can be added to the precursor to control how the perovskite crystallizes. Its two pyridyl N sites chelate Pb 2+ through several coordination motifs, and the five-membered chelate is the most stable. Chelation changes the nucleation and growth kinetics of PbI 2 . We tested BCP in three deposition routes: two-step spin coating, solvent-free co-evaporation of PbI 2 and BCP, and solvent-assisted vacuum flash evaporation. In all three, the films came out more uniform. Residual PbI 2 dropped, grain-boundary traps were passivated, and stability improved. The higher crystallinity and reduced nonradiative recombination translate into better single-junction devices. On pyramid-textured silicon, BCP forms conformal, dense perovskite layers with few vertical boundaries or voids. The best perovskite/silicon tandem reached a TÜV NORD-certified steady-state efficiency of 32.22% with negligible hysteresis, and held its performance under MPPT tracking in the ISOS-L-2 protocol.
authors: Wenhao Chen, Shengxing Zhou, Hao Zhang, Jiale Cao, Chuankun Ma, Yihua Chen, Ligang Yuan, Junhong Duan, Weiqin Liu

10.1002/adfm.79191.title: Selenium-Integrated Cyanine Dye With Enhanced Photophysical Properties for Optoacoustic-Guided Cancer Imaging and Therapy
10.1002/adfm.79191.abstract: ABSTRACT Near-infrared (NIR) cyanine dyes demonstrate considerable promise in medical applications, notably in cancer diagnosis, due to their favourable fluorescence properties and biocompatibility. However, these dyes generally have low photostability and tend to aggregate in aqueous solution, which can constrain their usefulness for prolonged in vivo imaging and phototherapy applications. Here, we report the synthesis of a selenium-integrated NIR cyanine dye, Se-Cyn, designed to modulate its electronic and photophysical properties. Se-Cyn demonstrates high photostability, molar absorptivity, photothermal conversion efficiency (PCE), and sustained optoacoustic (OptA) contrast under prolonged irradiation. Se-Cyn nanoparticles (NPs) outperform the indocyanine green (ICG) NPs, exhibiting PCE of 59% and a 1.36-fold higher OptA generation efficiency. Additionally, nano-formulated Se-Cyn NPs show excellent aqueous stability and improved bioavailability, supporting its suitability for biological applications. Furthermore, Se-Cyn NPs accumulate in tumors following systemic administration, enabling effective OptA tumor imaging. Together with their strong photodynamic and photothermal properties, these NPs show considerable potential for cancer theranostics.

10.1002/adfm.79163.title: Covalently Anchored, LiF-Reinforced Rigid-Flexible Interphase for Stable Nano-Si Anodes
10.1002/adfm.79163.abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon-based materials are ideal alternatives to conventional graphite anodes in lithium-ion batteries due to their exceptionally high theoretical capacity. However, the dramatic volume changes of silicon during lithiation/delithiation cause pulverization of active particles and repeated fracture and reformation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, severely hindering practical applications. Here, a covalent anchoring in situ crystallization (CAIC) strategy is proposed to construct a multifunctional modification layer composed of triglyme (G3) and nano-sized LiF on the nano-silicon surface (denoted as nSi@G3-LiF). This unique architecture provides multiple synergistic effects: high-modulus LiF and flexible ether-chain network buffer volume expansion and dissipate mechanical stress; abundant oxygen coordination sites enable rapid Li + transport; and LiF nanocrystals induce a dense, inorganic-rich SEI layer that effectively suppresses parasitic reactions. Consequently, the nSi@G3-LiF electrode achieves a remarkably high initial Coulombic efficiency of 91.3%, outstanding rate capability (1754, 1631, and 1301 mAh g −1 at 2, 3, and 5 A g −1 , respectively), and superior long-term cycling stability, retaining 1465 mAh g −1 after 900 cycles at 2 A g −1 . This work presents an effective strategy for regulating interfacial mechanics and kinetics through chemical bonding coupled with in situ crystallization reinforcement, offering new insights into interfacial design for silicon-based anodes.
authors: Heyang Shen, Benchi Li, Jing Wang, Huiqian Xiong, Hui Li, Yongjin Fang, Yuliang Cao, Qinghua Chen, Xinping Ai

10.1002/adfm.79252.title: Isomorphic Cu-Doped Ag Nanoclusters for Water-Modulated Conversion of Propargylic Alcohols and CO2 to Cyclic Carbonates or α-Hydroxy Ketones
10.1002/adfm.79252.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing a single catalytic system capable of producing distinct high-value products from the same feedstock under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a heterogeneous catalyst based on a copper-doped silver nanocluster (Ag 3 Cu 2 /CNT) engineered via isomorphic doping. Its unique structure features fully exposed Ag─Cu dual sites, with its core innovation lying in the highly efficient catalysis of the water-modulated conversion of propargylic alcohols and CO 2 , selectively yielding cyclic carbonates (98%) under anhydrous conditions or α-hydroxy ketones (96.8%) with added water, both with record turnover numbers (>19 000) at gram scale. Crucially, through atomic-precision paired comparison with an isostructural Ag 5 /CNT, we directly attribute the superior performance to synergistic Ag─Cu sites, where Cu preferentially anchors the alkyne group. Combined spectroscopic, intermediate-trapping, and computational studies reveal that water modulates the reaction pathway, while the instability of the undoped Ag 5 cluster stems from dynamic Ag─S bond cleavage. This work establishes a scalable catalytic platform and provides a general design strategy-isomorphic heteroatom doping coupled with site exposure-for constructing predictable, tunable, and stable heterogeneous cluster catalysts.
authors: Lin Li, Ying Lv, Haifeng Li, Yao Qin, Bingbing Wen, Yang Wang, Changhui Hou, Dongsheng Song, Haizhu Yu, Hongting Sheng, Manzhou Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79325.title: Giant Electrobending with Superior Thermal Stability in (K,Na)NbO3 Based Lead-Free Piezoceramics: Insights from Polarization Configuration
10.1002/adfm.79325.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrobending in lead-free piezoceramics has recently achieved remarkable attention, but the intrinsic coupling between electrobending and polarization configuration remains inadequately understood -leading to temperature instability that plagues practical applications. Herein, combining finite element analysis, density functional theory calculations, phase-field simulations, in situ property measurements and atomic-scale scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), we revealed that polarization configuration with enhanced switchability can promote inconsistent transverse shrinkage between the upper and lower surfaces of ceramics under an external electric field and leads to enhanced electrobending. By designing multiscale flexible polarization configuration, we achieved a giant apparent unipolar electrostrain (S uni ∼2.2%, d 33 * ∼11 000 pm/V @ 2 kV/mm) with exceptional temperature stability (∼10% variation over the range of −40°C-160 °C) in (K,Na)NbO 3 -based ceramics, which outperforms the state-of-the-art lead-free piezoceramics. In addition, this ceramic also exhibits excellent comprehensive piezoelectric properties, with a small-signal d 33 of ∼500 pC/N and T c of ∼240°C. This study advances the understanding of electrobending, which could provide valuable insights for the rational design of next-generation lead-free piezoceramics with excellent comprehensive performances.
authors: Tongxin Wei, Jinzhu Zou, Zhongna Yan, Miao Song, Xuefan Zhou, Kechou Zhou, Dou Zhang, Shujun Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79253.title: Harnessing Defect Engineered Multiferroic Catalysts for Cascade Responsive Microwave and Sonodynamic Therapy in Osteomyelitis
10.1002/adfm.79253.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient multi physics energy conversion, particularly the transformation of microwave and ultrasound energy into localized heat and reactive oxygen species, offers great potential for non-invasive biomedical therapy. However, conventional single modal catalysts suffer from inefficient energy coupling and rapid charge recombination. Here, we develop a defect engineered multi field responsive catalytic platform by integrating manganese doped bismuth ferrite nanocatalysts with Rehmannia Polygonati derived extracellular vesicles in an injectable hydrogel. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Mn doping induces defect dipoles to regulate the electronic structure of bismuth ferrite, suppress leakage currents, and enhance dielectric loss and piezoelectric responses. This enables sequential thermo piezocatalytic energy conversion, where microwave irradiation generates localized heating to reduce catalytic barriers and subsequent ultrasound stimulation promotes piezoelectric charge separation for efficient reactive oxygen species production. The synergistic catalytic process effectively eradicates deep seated biofilms in chronic osteomyelitis. Meanwhile, hydrogel degradation releases extracellular vesicles to regulate macrophage polarization and promote bone regeneration. This work establishes a defect engineered multi physics energy conversion platform for efficient microwave and ultrasound driven heat and reactive oxygen species generation, providing a promising strategy for complex deep tissue infection treatment.
authors: Xuxu Chen, Jing Ren, Quanheng Yu, Ziwei Zhao, Shichang Liu, Xinhua Yin, Liang Yan, Ming Yang

10.1002/adfm.79330.title: Ultra-Tough and Ultralow-Hysteresis Liquid Crystalline Nanocomposite Stretchable Ionogels Constructed by Attapulgite Nanorods Assisted Mixed-Ionic Liquids-Induced Phase Separation
10.1002/adfm.79330.abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional stretchable ionogels suffer from the trade-off between mechanical toughness and elastic recoverability, severely hindering their practical applications in durable and resilient flexible ionotronics. Here, an ultra-tough and ultralow-hysteresis liquid crystalline nanocomposite stretchable poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) ionogel is realized by using the mixed-ionic liquids-induced phase separation method with attapulgite nanorods as the junction points. The as-prepared ionogels achieve ultrahigh toughness of 87.28 MJ/m 3 , extraordinary tensile strength of 13.58 MPa, high stretchability of 2320%, and ultralow-hysteresis (5.9%-8.7%), outperforming most reported stretchable ionogels. Importantly, the nanocomposite ionogels display strong birefringence with the integration of bright structural colors and mechano-chromic performances. Moreover, the ionogel exhibits excellent ionic conductivity (up to 1.1 mS/cm), good reprocessability, and favorable healability. The application of these resilient ionogels as high-performance flexible sensor for temperature/motion detecting and electrophysiological monitoring are further demonstrated, showing record high temperature sensitivity (up to 2237.8%/°C), high strain sensitivity (up to 6.69) over a wide range of detection from 1% to 700%, fast response time (83 ms), and excellent durability (3000 cycles). This ionogel demonstrates significant potential for application soft robotics, optical display electronics, and motion/temperature monitoring.
authors: Qingshang Peng, Jiali Zhang, Jiaxin Tong, Xinru Liu, Yanmin Wang, Hongzan Song

10.1002/adfm.79322.title: Mitoxyperiosis-Driven Immunotherapy Enabled by Photothermal Ru-Doped MXene/MoS2 Nanozymes for Systemic Immunity Against Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
10.1002/adfm.79322.abstract: ABSTRACT The immune-privileged oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) microenvironment and low vaccine immunogenicity hinder lymphocyte recruitment, driving recurrence and lymph node metastasis and highlighting the need for better therapies. Herein, we report a 1T/2H-enriched Ru-doped MXene/MoS 2 (RMT) heterostructure engineered for synergistic photothermal-enhanced nanozyme catalysis and mitoxyperiosis-based therapy to boost immunotherapeutic efficacy. Ru incorporation and MoS 2 phase engineering generate abundant active sites and optimize electronic structures, enabling enhanced catalytic activity. Under TME conditions (acidic pH, elevated glutathione, and H 2 O 2 ), RMT exhibits catalase- and peroxidase-like activities, decomposing H 2 O 2 into O 2 and hydroxyl radicals (•OH), thereby amplifying oxidative stress and alleviating hypoxia. The strong near-infrared (NIR) absorption of MXene enables efficient photothermal conversion, further accelerating catalytic reactions. The generated reactive oxygen species (ROS) induce mitochondrial dysfunction and membrane disruption, triggering mitoxyperiosis. Notably, rapid thermal suppression of mitochondrial apoptosis combined with sustained mitophagy induction enables precise regulation of mitochondrial activity. In vivo, RMT achieves deep tumor penetration and extensive tumor ablation, resulting in significant regression. Moreover, this combined therapy induces immunogenic cell death (ICD), promotes dendritic cell maturation, and activates systemic antitumor immune responses. Overall, RMT provides a versatile platform for integrating nanozyme catalysis, photothermal therapy, and mitochondrial targeting to overcome immunosuppressive OSCC.
authors: Thi My Hue Huynh, Ngoc-Tri Tran, Yun-Hsuan Chang, Hoi Man Iao, Wan-Chi Pan, Hui-Wen Lien, Tsu-Chin Chou, Wen-Hsuan Chiang, Dai-Cheng Dong, Fei-Ting Hsu, Ya-Wen Chen, Kaptan Rajput, Hsin-Yi Tiffany Chen, Shang-Hsiu Hu

10.1002/adfm.79334.title: Screening-Effect-Driven Growth of Large-Area High-Quality COF Films with Wavelength-Dependent Photochromism
10.1002/adfm.79334.abstract: ABSTRACT Competing heterogeneous and homogeneous nucleation severely restricts scalable, high-yield synthesis of high-quality covalent organic framework (COF) films, as bulk homogeneous nucleation generates particulate impurities and cuts film yield below 5% with exorbitant fabrication costs. Here we propose a screening-effect-mediated nucleation control strategy to fully suppress homogeneous nucleation by overlapping monomer depletion layers around substrate nuclei, implemented via a custom batch micro-slit reactor that tunes inter-substrate distance, polymerization kinetics, and surface wettability to achieve exclusive heterogeneous film growth. This approach affords high-crystallinity COF films with ∼90% intrinsic yield and minimal particle contamination, applicable to 12 COF structures and capable of fabricating >1 m 2 films at drastically reduced costs (6.0-27.5 USD/m 2 ). The impurity-free films display pronounced wavelength-dependent photochromism from selective 350-500 nm absorption, enabling high-resolution optical patterning for anti-counterfeiting and sensing. This work provides a scalable, low-cost route for COF membrane production and establishes a universal kinetic framework to decouple dual nucleation processes in 2D crystalline porous materials.
authors: Furui Luo, Mengfan Xu, Xinping Cao, Jun Zhang, Lili Zhao, Ying Chu, Shengnan Guo, Xueying Wang, Ying-yan Hu, Yongping Zhu, Song Wang

10.1002/adfm.79368.title: High-Loading Ag Single Atoms Anchored on MoS2 Nanosheet Aggregates Enable Synergistic Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electroconversion
10.1002/adfm.79368.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR) to ammonia (NH 3 ) offers a sustainable route for coupling nitrate (NO 3 − ) remediation with NH 3 synthesis. However, its efficiency is often limited by the insufficient NO 3 − activation, incomplete hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates, and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we report a catalyst consisting of Ag single atoms anchored on flower-like MoS 2 nanosheet aggregates (Ag-MoS 2 NAs) for efficient NO 3 − -to-NH 3 conversion. Ag-MoS 2 NAs feature a high loading of isolated Ag sites while preserving atomic dispersion, providing abundant NO 3 − activation centers. During NO 3 − -to-NH 3 conversion, Ag sites promote NO 3 − adsorption and initial deoxygenation steps, whereas MoS 2 provides active hydrogen species for the subsequent hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates. The integration of these complementary functions enables efficient NO 3 − activation and subsequent hydrogenation, thereby enhancing NH 3 production and achieving a Faradaic efficiency of up to 95%. As a result, the Ag-MoS 2 NAs maintain stable operation for over 200 h at current densities exceeding 400 mA cm −2 , achieving an NH 3 yield rate of 30.6 mg h −1 cm −2 . This work demonstrates that integrating NO 3 − activation sites with hydrogenation functionalities in a single catalyst can effectively promote NH 3 production from NO 3 − under industrially relevant conditions.
authors: Ming-Xuan Shi, Ying-Ying Meng, Ying-Xue Shi, Ze-Nong Zhang, Shu-Ni Li, Xuan Ai, Yu Chen

10.1002/adfm.79308.title: Suppressing Side Reaction via Fluorinated Core-Shell Electrolyte for Durable 4.8 V Li-Rich Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79308.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-rich Mn-based cathode materials with high energy density hold promise for enabling > 500 Wh kg −1 batteries; however, the reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated at high voltages trigger electrolyte decomposition and gas evolution, posing severe interfacial stability challenges and safety risks. Herein, a “side-reaction inhibition” strategy is proposed by employing a bulky, ROS-stable diluent to modulate core-shell solvation structures and shield highly reactive solvents, effectively suppressing interfacial side reactions. As a result, a 2.5 Ah pouch cell with an ultrahigh areal capacity of 9.6 mAh cm −2 achieves 502.7 Wh kg −1 and delivers a capacity retention of 89.85% after 50 cycles at 0.1 C, while significantly suppressing gas evolution. This work provides novel insights into electrolyte design for high-voltage lithium metal batteries through targeted mitigation of reactive oxygen species side effects.
authors: Kaiwen Shi, Donglei Zhao, Haoxiang Sun, Haixia Li, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan, Yong Lu, Jun Chen

10.1002/adfm.79360.title: Dynamic Supramolecular Cryptomaterials for Compositional Encoding and Mechanical Decryption
10.1002/adfm.79360.abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced cryptomaterials capable of storing concealed information and selectively revealing it through dynamic pathways are desirable for next-generation cryptography. However, simultaneously achieving high-dimensional information encoding, scalable material fabrication, and secure yet equipment-free decryption remains an unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a class of dynamic supramolecular cryptomaterials (DSCs) that couple compositional encoding with mechanical decryption, establishing a fundamentally different cryptographic paradigm. Multi-component functionalized colloids are embedded within polymer matrices via dynamic supramolecular interactions, producing visually indistinguishable precursor materials in which the encoded information is completely concealed. Upon prescribed oscillatory shearing stimulus, transient supramolecular networks are selectively activated, driving a disorder-to-order transition and leading to highly ordered superstructures with formulation-specific optical fingerprints, jointly governed by material composition and the mechanical activation. By independently programming composition, including the colloids and polymer, the DSCs enable continuous structural-color regulation across 410-753 nm while simultaneously tailoring color saturation and brightness. The multidimensional compositional space provides exceptional information density, with each pixel capable of encoding up to 393 identities. This work establishes a general materials design strategy that transforms composition from a passive formulation parameter into an active information carrier and introduces mechanically programmable supramolecular cryptomaterials as a scalable platform for high-security information encryption and advanced anti-counterfeiting.
authors: Zhen Hu, Xingduo Chen, Jing Wang, Xiujuan Zhang, Junsong Wu, Luyao Xu, Lianbin Zhang, Jintao Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79342.title: Ultramicropore Tightening in Carbon Molecular Sieve Membranes Enables Entropy-Dominated Propylene/Propane Separation
10.1002/adfm.79342.abstract: ABSTRACT Membrane-based propylene/propane separation demands molecular discrimination at the sub-ångström scale. Carbon molecular sieve (CMS) membranes offer rigid molecular-sieving ultramicropores which exploit the subtle differences in molecular size and configuration between planar C 3 H 6 and three-dimensional C 3 H 8 . However, precisely tailoring these ultramicropores while retaining rapid transport remains challenging. Here, fluorinated copolyimide precursors with tunable concentrations of bulky ─C(CF 3 ) 2 ─ units enable composition-controlled ultramicropore tightening. Increasing the concentration of these units raises precursor free volume and enhances volatile evolution during pyrolysis. Regulating precursor composition and pyrolysis temperature produces CMS structures with tighter ultramicropores and preserved transport accessible microporosity. After 65 days of stabilization, the optimized membrane achieves a mixed-gas C 3 H 6 permeability of 55.8 Barrer and a C 3 H 6 /C 3 H 8 selectivity of 68.6 under an equimolar feed at 60 psia and 35°C, surpassing the reported mixed-gas upper bound. Selectivity remains close to 70 over 35-55°C and feed pressures of 60-180 psia. Sorption-diffusion analysis identifies diffusivity selectivity as the principal contributor to separation. The enhanced apparent entropic selectivity is consistent with greater configurational restrictions on three-dimensional C 3 H 8 than on planar C 3 H 6 . These findings demonstrate ultramicropore tightening in CMS membranes as a means of leveraging configurational entropy for challenging sub-ångström molecular separations.
authors: Yuqing Lu, Zhongyun Liu, Yong Wang

10.1002/adfm.79346.title: Bioinspired Helical Hydrogel Scaffold with Janus Wettability for Magnetically and Thermally Responsive Tricuspid Valve Repair
10.1002/adfm.79346.abstract: ABSTRACT Tricuspid valve insufficiency and restricted opening remain clinical challenges in structural heart disease interventions, often requiring invasive repair or replacement. Inspired by natural organisms such as the nautilus, jellyfish, and lotus leaf, we propose a bioinspired helical hydrogel scaffold featuring a Janus wettability interface for magnetically and thermally responsive tricuspid valve repair. The scaffold comprises a spiral architecture and a trilayer hydrogel system, integrating a hydrophobic PDMS/CNT/Fe 3 O 4 surface for blood-facing anti-thrombotic performance and a hydrophilic P(HEMA-co-AAm) surface for enhanced tissue adhesion. The magnetic responsiveness endowed by Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles enables remote, non-contact clamping under external fields, while the incorporation of a thermoresponsive P(NiPAAm-bis-AA) hydrogel ensures in situ mechanical anchoring and dynamic adhesion at physiological temperature. In vitro mechanical and actuation tests, ex vivo porcine heart simulations, and in vivo biocompatibility assessments demonstrated the scaffold's reliable fixation, fatigue resistance, blood compatibility, and stable integration under cardiac-mimicking conditions. This work presents a minimally invasive, suture-free solution with high translational potential for tricuspid valve repair, and offers a modular platform for expanding intelligent hydrogel devices to other cardiac and interventional applications.

10.1002/adfm.79371.title: Synergistic Passivation of Deep and Shallow Defects Enables High-Efficiency and Stable Low-Bromine 1.68 eV Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79371.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance and operational stability of wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are critically limited by voltage loss induced by non-radiative recombination and halide phase segregation. Deep-level defects act as dominant recombination centers for voltage loss, while shallow-level halide vacancies trigger ion migration and halide vacancies trigger ion migration and phase segregation. Herein, we characterize deep-level and shallow-level defects via deep-level transient spectroscopy and photoluminescence measurements, and introduce a high-dipole zwitterionic additive, pyridinium propyl sulfobetaine (PPS), to simultaneously passivate these defects. PPS strongly coordinates with Pb 2+ ions to modulate perovskite crystallization, thereby improving film crystallinity and reducing PbI 2 residues. Preferentially accumulating at the bottom interface, PPS passivates deep-level defects through pyridinium and sulfonate functional groups to suppress non-radiative recombination, while remedying shallow-level defects to retard ion migration and boost photostability. The resulting reduction in defect density further suggests that these defects are likely enriched at the bottom interface. Enabled by an anti-solvent-free process, the 1.68 eV WBG PSC (8% bromine content) delivers an efficiency of 22.29%, (vs. 20.05% for the control) and retains 92.9% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking. This work demonstrates a synergistic defect passivation strategy for high-performance and stable WBG perovskite.

10.1002/adfm.79309.title: Programming of Hierarchical Noncovalent Interactions Enables Thermoplastic Elastomers With Ultrahigh Mechanical Strength and Dynamic Stability
10.1002/adfm.79309.abstract: ABSTRACT Noncovalent thermoplastic elastomers face a persistent trade-off between stability and processability; strategies relying on increasing interaction density are reaching diminishing returns. Here, we report a hierarchical programming strategy for noncovalent interactions that moves beyond the parallel superposition of multiple weak bonds. Guided by multiscale simulations, we predict and design a thermoplastic elastomer in which strong naphthalene π-π stacking acts as primary directional anchors, templating the ordered assembly of a secondary hydrogen-bond network through conformational confinement and producing a synergistic response larger than simple additivity. The linear polymer system achieves an ultrahigh tensile strength of 99.6 MPa and a stress-relaxation activation energy of 153.5 kJ mol − 1 , comparable to values typically reported for covalent adaptable networks. Using computational chemical calculations and characterization, we clarify how the layered division of labor between interactions governs macroscopic stability. The resulting elastomers are reprocessable and tolerate harsh conditions, offering a generalizable design principle for noncovalent materials.

10.1002/adfm.79285.title: Targeting ALOX15 with a ROS-Responsive Lipid Nanoparticle for the Treatment of Allergic Conjunctivitis and Its Comorbidity Dry Eye Disease
10.1002/adfm.79285.abstract: ABSTRACT Allergic conjunctivitis (AC) and its frequent comorbidity, dry eye disease (DED), represent prevalent ocular surface inflammatory disorders, significantly impairing patients’ visual quality. Arachidonic acid 15-lipoxygenase (ALOX15) emerges as a common pathogenic factor, mediating inflammatory responses and lipid peroxidation in both conditions. Here, a therapeutic strategy is designed based on reactive oxygen species-responsive lipid nanoparticles loaded with siALOX15-5 (rLNP@siALOX15-5). This strategy enhances ocular penetration and sustains silencing of ALOX15, alleviating the symptoms of AC by executing a dual mechanism. It simultaneously suppresses multiple signaling pathways involved in the inflammatory response, particularly cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction and chemokine signaling pathway, while potently inhibiting lipid peroxidation and enhancing antioxidant defenses. In an autoimmune-related DED mice model, rLNP@siALOX15-5 alleviates clinical symptoms and restores ocular surface homeostasis. Moreover, in the AC and DED comorbid model, it outperforms cyclosporine A and TobraDex monotherapies, achieving effects comparable to their combination. These studies not only validate the value of ALOX15 as a common therapeutic target for both AC and DED but also establish rLNP@siALOX15-5 as an effective strategy for treating these two associated ocular surface diseases through its dual-regulatory mechanism.

10.1002/adfm.79313.title: V-Shaped Linkers Modulate Covalent Organic Frameworks' Interlayer Spacing for Efficient Iodine Capture
10.1002/adfm.79313.abstract: ABSTRACT Significantly enlarging and precisely regulating the interlayer spacing of two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) is both meaningful and challenging. Capitalizing on the weak conjugation effects inherent in flexible monomer assembly, this study proposes an interlayer regulation strategy for constructing 2D flexible COFs using dual-flexible monomers. By introducing nonlinear V-shaped linkers, we elucidated the core structure-property relationship of “angle-packing-spacing” and established a novel assembly method for synthesizing highly crystalline 2D nonlinear COFs (NLCOFs). Crucially, the V-shaped topology effectively suppresses interlayer π-π stacking interactions, thereby enabling controllable expansion and precise tuning of COF interlayer spacing within the range of 4.2 Å to 4.5 Å. Moreover, fine-tuning the included angle of linkers allows NLCOFs' structural optimization, allowing control over the adsorption and transport properties toward guest molecules such as iodine vapor and iodomethane. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of flexible crystalline COFs and establishes a potentially generalizable strategy for interlayer engineering.

10.1002/adfm.79335.title: Metal Nanoparticle Sensitized Molecular Triplets for Efficient Photon Upconversion
10.1002/adfm.79335.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal nanoparticles have recently been explored as sensitizers for molecular triplet generation via charge transfer and recombination. A key feature of metals is their gapless band structure with a wide range of electronic states available for charge transfer, potentially relaxing energy alignment constraints in semiconductor sensitizers. Here we show efficient triplet generation in metal (Au or Pt) nanoparticle-Rhodamine B (RhB) hybrids after exciting RhB, followed by hole transfer from singlet 1 RhB * to the metal and charge recombination to form triplet 3 RhB * , revealed by ultrafast time-resolved spectroscopy. Hole transfer from 1 RhB * to the Fermi level of the metal leads to products with insufficient energy to sensitize 3 RhB * thermodynamically. This contrasts with the high triplet generation yield and suggests the possibility of hole transfer to electronic states below the Fermi level, inducing a transition from inverted to normal Marcus regime that is thermodynamically and kinetically favorable for triplet generation. We show efficient phosphorescence emission, singlet oxygen generation, antibacterial applications, and triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion sensitized by nontoxic metal nanoparticles, which is crucial for practical application. The gapless band structure, low toxicity, and high stability of metal nanoparticles make them promising for mediating molecular triplet generation for a variety of applications.

10.1002/adfm.79324.title: Breaking the Gain-Speed Trade-Off in Phototransistors With Sub-10 nm Single-Crystalline Organic-Inorganic van der Waals Heterojunctions at the Exciton-Diffusion Limit
10.1002/adfm.79324.abstract: ABSTRACT Phototransistors offer intrinsic gate-controlled gain amplification, providing much higher responsivity than photodiodes, but this advantage is generally limited by the gain-speed trade-off: high gain typically relies on long-lived trapped carriers, which inevitably slows the photoresponse. Although low-dimensional semiconductors and hybrid heterojunctions have improved responsivity and detectivity, they still predominantly operate through slow, trap-mediated gain, leaving the trade-off unresolved. Here, sub-10 nm organic-inorganic single-crystalline van der Waals heterojunctions are introduced to decouple gain from slow carrier trapping. Specifically, a bilayer molecular crystal (C 6 -DPA) is integrated onto a monolayer MoS 2 channel. Reducing the heterojunction thickness to the exciton diffusion limit, localized Frenkel excitons in C 6 -DPA efficiently undergo interfacial charge separation and transfer across the type-II interface, while the separated charges rapidly modulate the MoS 2 channel conductance through the field effect. Gain therefore arises from efficient channel gating rather than prolonged trapped-carrier circulation. The resulting phototransistors achieve a responsivity of 1.07 × 10 5 A W −1 , rise/decay times of 771.2/809.8 µs, and a specific detectivity of 2.19 × 10 15 Jones under their respective optimized operating conditions. These results demonstrate that the gain-speed trade-off in phototransistors arises primarily from trap-mediated gain mechanisms and can be mitigated through exciton-engineered ultrathin single-crystalline organic-inorganic van der Waals heterojunctions.

10.1002/adfm.79326.title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Ion Transport Pathways by a Shape Memory Separator for Safer Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79326.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal safety is a key challenge for high-energy lithium metal batteries. Conventional separators deform under overheating while sustaining ion transport, accelerating thermal runaway. Herein, we report an aramid-supported shape memory separator that converts temperature rise into reconstruction of ion transport pathways. A covalently crosslinked PETMP-TMPTA-IBOA network is photopolymerized within a porous aramid scaffold. At normal operating temperatures, the interconnected pore structure affords an ionic conductivity of 0.29 mS cm −1 and enables stable Li plating/stripping for over 3000 h. At 140°C, the shape memory network undergoes thermomechanical rearrangement, constricting the percolating pores and increasing the ionic resistance by one order of magnitude. Meanwhile, the aramid scaffold preserves dimensional integrity up to 175°C and maintains electrode isolation after ionic shutdown. The separator is compatible with high-energy NCM811 and Li-rich Mn-based oxide cathodes. In particular, a Li-rich cathode with high mass loading of 16 mg cm −2 cycles stably for 100 cycles at 0.5 C, delivers nearly 250 mAh g −1 at 60°C, and remains operable up to 125°C. This work establishes thermomechanical reconstruction of ion transport pathways as a general design principle for intrinsically self-protective lithium metal batteries that reconcile high energy operation with autonomous overheating protection.

10.1002/adfm.79292.title: State-Instructive Apoptotic Body-Mimetic Nanoparticles Reprogram Macrophages to Establish Antigen-Specific Immune Tolerance in Celiac Disease
10.1002/adfm.79292.abstract: ABSTRACT Celiac disease is an antigen-driven autoimmune enteropathy characterized by a breakdown of gluten tolerance, yet current antigen-delivering nanotherapies primarily focus on optimizing nanoparticle properties while overlooking the immunological state of antigen presenting cells (APCs). Here, we engineered apoptotic body-mimetic gliadin nanoparticles (ABM-G NPs) by incorporating phosphatidylserine (PS), an endogenous “eat-me” signal, into a PLGA-based gliadin delivery platform. ABM-G NPs enhanced macrophage efferocytosis through PS-dependent recognition, inducing a tolerogenic macrophage program characterized by metabolic remodeling and epigenetic reprogramming. Mechanistically, ABM-G NPs promoted glycolytic flux and lactate accumulation, leading to H3K9 lactylation-mediated activation of immune-regulatory and metabolic genes, including Mrc1 and Hk1 . In gluten-induced mouse models of celiac disease, ABM-G NPs suppressed gliadin-specific immune responses, promoted regulatory T cell expansion, and alleviated intestinal inflammation. This study establishes a state-instructive biomaterial strategy that couples apoptotic mimicry with antigen delivery to achieve antigen-specific immune tolerance.

10.1002/adfm.79307.title: Polar Topologies in Lead-Free Oxide Antiferroelectric Ceramics
10.1002/adfm.79307.abstract: ABSTRACT Polar topological structures have emerged as an important frontier in ferroic materials because of their unusual polarization textures and potential functionalities. However, their existence and formation mechanism in antiferroelectrics remain largely elusive owing to the intrinsic self-compensating antipolar ordering. Here, diverse polar topologies are revealed in CaTiO 3 -doped NaNbO 3 antiferroelectric ceramics using atomic-resolution integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy. Continuous dipole rotation is directly observed at different domain walls, giving rise to topological vortex configurations at uncharged inclined 90° domain walls, antivortex configurations at charged inclined 90° domain walls, alternating vortex-antivortex arrays at vertical 90° domain walls, and periodically arranged center-convergent and center-divergent polarization textures at charged 180° domain walls. Phase-field simulations reveal that these topological structures originate from the diffusive superposition of different antipolar variants at domain walls, which is driven by the intrinsic competition between bulk and gradient energies. These results establish a direct relationship between domain walls, charge state, and polar topologies, and demonstrate that modulated antiferroelectrics provide a platform for exploring intrinsic polar topologies states and may open new avenues for optimizing dielectric energy-storage performance and electromechanical responses in lead-free antiferroelectric materials.

10.1002/adfm.79304.title: Self-Adaptive Gradient Interphase Enables Durable Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79304.abstract: ABSTRACT Garnet-type solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) enable safe, high-energy solid-state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) but suffer from poor interfacial contact and lithium dendrite penetration. Here, we report a machine learning -guided interfacial strategy that constructs a self-adaptive graded interphase from a B 105 M 40 composite interlayer (BiOCl: Mg 3 N 2 = 105:40). The interphase features a lithiophilic LiMg phase at the bottom to ensure intimate Li/LLZTO contact, a porous Li 3 Bi phase to accommodate lithium plating/stripping, and Li 3 N/Li 3 OCl phases that enable fast ionic transport and dendrite suppression. The self-adaptive gradient interphase maintains stable contact with lithium metal during cycling. As a result, B 105 M 40 -Li||LLZTO||B 105 M 40 -Li symmetric cells exhibit a high critical current density of 15 mA cm −2 and stable cycling over 5000 h at 14 mA cm −2 . Full cells retain 93.7% capacity after 1000 cycles with LiFePO 4 cathodes at 2.0 C, while those paired with high-voltage LiNbO 3 @LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathodes exhibit cycling for over 1000 cycles at 1.0 C. Moreover, the strategy is applicable to sulfide SSEs, offering a universal interfacial design for long-life SSLMBs.

10.1002/adfm.79184.title: Two-Dimensional Magnetic Materials From Ferromagnetism to Altermagnetism: Fabrication, Symmetry, Evidence, and Device Readiness
10.1002/adfm.79184.abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically thin magnets are governed by composition, thickness, stacking, strain, defects, substrates, ferroic order, and interfaces. This Review organizes two-dimensional (2D) magnetism using net magnetization and momentum-space spin splitting or spin-polarization patterns as primary coordinates, supplemented by sublattice structure and the symmetry relations between opposite-spin sublattices. Ferromagnets generally carry a net moment; ferrimagnets can be fully compensated. Conventional antiferromagnets may retain spin-degenerate bands, while altermagnets permit nonrelativistic alternating spin splitting under dimension-specific symmetry constraints. M1-M4 reporting classes introduced here distinguish layer-resolved atomically thin forms, non-layer-resolved thin flakes or films, bulk benchmarks, and theoretical candidates or design routes; the evidence category and ordering-temperature provenance are reported independently. Current experimental support for altermagnetism comes mainly from M2 thin-film and M3 bulk benchmarks, leaving a fully verified atomically thin M1 altermagnetic phase as an open experimental goal. Most proposed monolayer and few-layer systems therefore fall within M4, and contested cases clarify the measurements needed for phase assignment. Device readiness is compared qualitatively using operating temperature, readout, switching, domain control, stability, scalability, interface sensitivity, and integration difficulty. Reliable phase assignment and device assessment require complementary measurements from the same material form under matched conditions, ideally on the same specimen or in situ.

10.1002/adfm.79038.title: Aging- and Moisture-Resistant Pectin-Based Aerogels: A Breakthrough in Bio-Based Thermal Superinsulation
10.1002/adfm.79038.abstract: ABSTRACT Bio-based aerogels are a compelling class of sustainable materials, with some of them distinguished by their exceptional thermal superinsulating performance, i.e. conductivity lower than that of air. However, their practical use is limited by poor stability in humid environment. Pectin/polyurea aerogels were developed to address this issue. Pectin was combined with polyurea precursors to explore how polyurea chemistry affects thermal performance at 25°C and high relative humidity (RH). ATR-FTIR and NMR analyses confirmed the formation of a conformal polyurea network coating pectin nanofibrils. All aerogels displayed high specific surface areas (350-520 m 2 g −1 ) and exceptionally low thermal conductivity, 0.015-0.018 W m −1 K −1 . Among the formulations tested, the aerogel based on pectin/rigid aliphatic polyurea network demonstrated superior performance, maintaining a stable thermal conductivity of 0.015 W m −1 K −1 in 80% RH for nearly 300 days (duration of test). In addition to thermal superinsulation, this optimized formulation showed high mechanical strength, good flame retardancy, and effective acoustic reflectivity.
