10.1002/adfm.79380.title: Boosting N-Type Ferrous/Ferric Thermocells by a Ternary Electrolyte Leveraging Dual-Ligand Coordination
10.1002/adfm.79380.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermocells (TECs) offer a promising route for directly converting low-grade heat into electricity, while n-type TECs historically lag behind their p-type counterparts due to their sluggish reaction kinetics and thermodynamic limitations. Herein, a ternary electrolyte with synergistic coordination effect is proposed to uniquely address these challenges within the ferrous/ferric n-type TECs. In this electrolyte, 15-crown-5 selectively encapsulates Fe 3+ while p-toluenesulfonic acid provides additional coordination sites, effectively suppressing detrimental hydrolysis and enhancing the electrochemical reversibility that is often compromised by the crown ether used alone. Such selective and synergistic coordination directly enlarges entropy change and facilitates charge transfer, significantly contributing to the overall thermoelectrochemical performance. The resulting TECs based on the optimized ternary electrolyte exhibit a notably enhanced thermopower of −2.41 mV K −1 and a markedly increased normalized power density of 1.348 mW m −2 K −2 , representing one of the highest values reported for n-type TECs. The substantial enhancement in both thermopower and power density facilitates an excellent match with the classic p-type ferricyanide/ferrocyanide TECs, and a device integrated with 14 p-n TEC pairs is further demonstrated, showing high potential toward practical low-grade heat harvesting applications.
authors: Yinglu Liu, Yuanqian Bi, Zhixi Xu, Jie Lai, Yang Huang, Ze Chen, Wenjun Meng, Guangming Chen, Zhuoxin Liu

10.1002/adfm.79357.title: Radial Interface Sequence Coordination Regulates Impedance Matching and Interface Polarization for Microwave Attenuation
10.1002/adfm.79357.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly conductive carbon fibers are promising for ultra-thin microwave absorption (MA), but the significant impedance mismatch limits microwave incidence and subsequent energy dissipation. Conventional interface engineering largely optimizes component composition and loading, whereas the role of radial interface order remains unclear. In this work, the interface sequence is treated as a new structural variable. ZIF-67 and MIL-88B nanolayers with tunable electromagnetic (EM) responses were synthesized in situ on carbon fibers. First, the impedance mismatch characteristics of carbon fibers were improved by adjusting the heat treatment temperature and shell loading. Furthermore, the EM response properties of the materials were finely tuned by reversing the growth order of ZIF-67 and MIL-88B on the surface. The optimized CFC-9-2 achieved minimum reflection loss (RL) of −70.81 dB and effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 4.85 GHz at a thickness of 1.58 mm. Further simulations of far-field conditions and near-field Wi-Fi radiation tests demonstrate attenuation in representative environments. The results demonstrate that the spatial sequence of interfaces serves as a key structural parameter for regulating the transmission and dissipation of electromagnetic energy.
authors: Yijie Liu, Yanling Weng, KunPeng Li, Zhenyu Cheng, Yi Yan, Yucheng Wang, Lvtong Duan, Hainian Liu, Jiaqi Tao, Zhengjun Yao, Jintang Zhou

10.1002/adfm.79345.title: Dynamic Wafer Curvature Engineering Toward Ultraflat and Highly Uniform 8-Inch GaN Heteroepitaxy
10.1002/adfm.79345.abstract: ABSTRACT Large-area GaN heteroepitaxy is essential for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic systems, yet simultaneously achieving low wafer bow and high epitaxial uniformity remains challenging due to the dynamic evolution of thermo-mechanical stress during growth and cooling. Here, we develop a dynamic wafer curvature engineering strategy based on a thermal-cycling stress-loading (TCSL) layer to regulate curvature evolution throughout epitaxy and suppress residual bow after cooling. The TCSL layer consists of a hydrogen-rich SiO 2 film deposited on the backside of sapphire substrates, where hydrogen-driven viscoelastic relaxation and dehydrogenation-induced network densification generate asymmetric stress evolution. Applying this strategy to AlGaN/GaN HEMT epitaxy, we realize ultraflat and highly uniform 8-inch wafers on 1-mm-thick sapphire substrates, achieving a bow of 7.4 µm, a warp of 17.2 µm, and relative standard deviations of 0.82%, 1.2%, and 1.8% for epitaxial thickness, Al composition, and sheet resistance, respectively. The AlGaN/GaN heterostructure preserves high crystalline and interfacial quality, enabling a high-quality two-dimensional electron gas with a sheet density of 7.0 × 10 12 cm −2 and an electron mobility of 2040 cm 2 /V·s. This work establishes a scalable approach for simultaneous control of wafer flatness and epitaxial uniformity in large-area GaN heteroepitaxy, paving the way toward highly integrated GaN-based electronic and optoelectronic technologies.
authors: Xingcheng Yu, Shuangshuang Kang, Zhaoying Chen, Yan Wang, Zexing Yuan, Chaofan Ma, Tai Li, Xin Rong, Ding Wang, Fang Liu, Ping Wang, Yao Chen, Shiping Guo, Ye Yuan, Shangfeng Liu, Rencun Tao, Bo Shen, Xinqiang Wang

10.1002/adfm.79364.title: Closed-Pore Engineering Couples Sodium Confinement and Interfacial Stabilization for Dendrite-Resistant Hard Carbon Anodes
10.1002/adfm.79364.abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon, a leading anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), suffers from nonuniform sodium deposition, which causes dendrite growth and compromises safety and cycle life. Here, we report a closed-pore engineering strategy based on cobalt-doped hard carbon (CoHC) that couples internal sodium-cluster confinement with interfacial stabilization. Internally, the closed nanopores redirect sodium storage from surface accumulation to deep pore filling, thereby inhibiting the growth of quasi-metallic sodium clusters and dendrite propagation. Externally, the closed-pore architecture regulates interfacial chemistry, leading to a thin, uniform, inorganic-rich solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) with reduced charge-transfer resistance. In situ electrochemical tests confirm stable interfaces and suppressed dendrite growth in both Na||CoHC half cells and CoHC||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) full cells, whereas severe dendritic deposition occurs on pristine hard carbon (HC) under identical current density. The CoHC anode delivers superior cycling stability with a capacity retention of 95% after 500 cycles, significantly outperforming HC. This work paves the way for dendrite-resistant, safer, and longer-lasting sodium-ion batteries.
authors: Fuchen Zhou, Runyi Zhou, Yongyao Xia, Qian Yu

10.1002/adfm.79356.title: Atomically Sharp but Three-Dimensionally Rough Ferroelectric Domain Walls in BiFeO3 Nano-islands
10.1002/adfm.79356.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric domain walls (DWs) have attracted extensive interest because of their emergent physical properties and potential functionalities in nanoelectronic devices. Although DWs are traditionally proposed to be atomically sharp interfaces, experimental observations frequently report apparent broadening, roughness, and even complex three-dimension, suggesting structural variations beyond the conventional 2D picture. However, direct experimental characterization of such 3D structures remains challenging because of the intrinsic limitations of projection-based imaging. Here, we employ energy-filtered multislice electron ptychography with ∼2 nm depth resolution to directly resolve the 3D morphology of ferroelectric DWs in BiFeO 3 nano-islands grown on SrTiO 3 substrates. We reveal that domain walls can exhibit irregular 3D morphologies while remaining intrinsically atomically sharp, with widths confined to approximately one unit cell. The apparent broadening observed in conventional imaging is shown to originate predominantly from depth-dependent structural variations rather than from a genuine increase in wall width. Furthermore, depth-resolved strain analysis demonstrates that interfacial strain gradients and dislocations play an important role in stabilizing and modulating 3D domain-wall configurations. Our findings uncover the 3D nature of ferroelectric domain walls and provide a structural foundation for understanding domain-wall functionalities.
authors: Zelin Wang, Lisha Liu, Kun Xu, Zehao Dong, Shaoxuan Zheng, Jing-Feng Li, Zhen Chen, Jing Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79365.title: Fluctuation-Enhanced True Random Number Generators and Physical Unclonable Functions in a Synaptic Hybrid Ferro-Ionic Tunnel Diode
10.1002/adfm.79365.abstract: ABSTRACT Secure edge hardware demands compact device platforms that can integrate low-power information processing with hardware-level security. However, this convergence of computation and security remains challenging because accurate analog operation and stochastic security functionality rely on fundamentally different device characteristics. Here we demonstrate that transient fluctuations in a synaptic hybrid ferro-ionic tunnel diode (HTD) can be harnessed as an in materia physical resource for unified hardware security, enabling both true random number generators (TRNGs) and physical unclonable functions (PUFs) within the same device platform. To achieve this functional separation, low-frequency noise is introduced as a new degree of freedom for hardware security, serving either as a direct stochastic source or as a guide to the optimal operation condition. Therefore, the HTD supports both static identity and dynamic randomness in distinct operating regimes, while separating information processing in the conductance domain from security generation in the fluctuation domain. In the TRNG mode, the tunneling regime activates shot noise-dominant fluctuations that provide a broadband entropy source with enhanced thermal stability for TRNG operation. In the PUF mode, voltage-driven stochastic switching produces device-specific power spectral density fingerprints, overcoming the limited dimensionality of conventional conductance-based fingerprints.
authors: Sangwan Kim, Hosu Park, Jeong-Han Kim, Seojun Hwang, Jiwon You, Youngchan Cho, Been Kwak, David Radermacher, Jaekyoung Park, Cheol-Woong Yang, Suraj S. Cheema, Daewoong Kwon, Wonjun Shin

10.1002/adfm.79323.title: Ultrasensitive and Wide-Range Ionic Pressure Sensors Toward Intelligent Assessment of Traditional Chinese Medicine Pulse and Oral Occlusal Health
10.1002/adfm.79323.abstract: ABSTRACT Pulse monitoring and tooth occlusion detection are two key scenarios for non-invasive monitoring of cardiovascular and oral health. Traditional pressure sensors suffer from a trade-off between sensitivity and measurement range. Their rigid structure and poor surface fit hinder the accurate acquisition of weak pulse signals and the detection of wide-range occlusal pressure. Here, a high-performance capacitive ionic pressure sensor was realized based on the electric double-layer (EDL) effect, featuring both ultra-high sensitivity (73224 kPa − 1 ) and a wide detection range (0.01-1100 kPa). Compared with most reported ionic pressure sensors, our sensor achieves competitive ultra-high peak sensitivity at low pressure while maintaining an exceptionally broad detection range. Drawing on pulse-diagnosis principles of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), this sensor accurately captures wrist pulse signals at the “Cun, Guan and Chi” acupoints. Integrating machine-learning techniques, the occlusal-pressure monitoring prototype achieves automatic classification of ten distinct occlusal-pressure patterns acquired from dental phantom models. Such a cutting-edge design for the ionic pressure sensor and its application in monitoring of both cardiovascular and oral health are rarely reported in the literature. These findings lay a foundation for the development of adaptive flexible monitoring systems for personalized medicine and intelligent physiological monitoring technology.
authors: Hongliang Ma, Zhe Zhang, Shulin Guo, Tengfei Ma, Kai Hu, Ruibing Yao, Xutao Fan, Wendong Zhang, Jun Zhang, Xuge Fan

10.1002/adfm.79359.title: Radiation-Resistant Piperazine-Tröger's-Base Porous Organic Polymer for Efficient Chemical Immobilization of Methyl Iodide With Low Leakage
10.1002/adfm.79359.abstract: ABSTRACT Preventing secondary release after capture remains a critical challenge in the management of radioactive methyl iodide (CH 3 I) from nuclear off-gas. Here, a metal-free porous organic polymer, TBPOF-PZ, was developed by covalently integrating piperazine-derived tertiary amines and Tröger's-base bridgehead nitrogen centers into a thermally stable porous architecture. TBPOF-PZ achieves a high total CH 3 I uptake of 4.35 g g −1 , while 1.60 g g −1 remains irreversibly retained after thermal desorption. Spectroscopic analysis, density functional theory, and pyrohydrolytic combustion-ion chromatography collectively clarify the chemical immobilization mechanism. TBPOF-PZ exhibits excellent CH 3 I retention performance in multicomponent fixed-bed breakthrough experiments using a simulated realistic gas mixture. Importantly, no obvious deterioration in performance is observed after exposure to an NO x -containing atmosphere or 240 kGy γ-irradiation. In addition, CH 3 I-loaded TBPOF-PZ effectively retains iodide under both high-temperature conditions and prolonged storage. These results establish a covalent porous-polymer strategy for integrating efficient capture, durable chemical fixation, and leakage resistance under demanding nuclear off-gas conditions.
authors: Yinhui Li, Tengfei Shi, Zhizheng Wang, Qingkuan Meng, Yongzheng Wang, Qingxin Liang, Zhihao Bian, Junwei You, Heping Ma

10.1002/adfm.79386.title: Guiding Morphology Evolution via Solid-State Relaxation for Highly Reproducible and Robust Organic Photovoltaics
10.1002/adfm.79386.abstract: ABSTRACT Poor device reproducibility and insufficient processing robustness hinder organic photovoltaics (OPVs) industrialization, primarily due to poor morphological reproducibility of the active layer. Here, we establish a direct correlation between the morphology evolution pathway and morphological reproducibility. When evolution is governed by solid-state relaxation, the active layer converges into energetically similar low-energy metastable ensembles, yielding highly reproducible morphologies. In contrast, rapid quenching traps the active layer in a broad distribution of low-energy metastable states, leading to poor morphological reproducibility. This principle is validated through two independent approaches: molecular structure design and additive engineering. Chemically, acceptor dimerization (PM6:DY2) shifts evolution from quenching- to relaxation-dominated, reducing the coefficient of variation ( CV , a reproducibility measure) from 2.14% to 1.19% and increasing the performance figure of merit ( P-FOM , a robustness measure) from 0.925 to 0.944. Physically, replacing the additive 1,2,4-TCB with 1,3,5-TIB delays the evolution of PM6:L8-BO to the relaxation stage, achieving 19.59% PCE while achieving a record-low CV of 0.86% (reduced from 1.55%) and increasing P-FOM from 0.935 to 0.955. These findings establish a general principle: solid-state relaxation-dominated evolution leads to morphological convergence and device performance consistency, providing a theoretical basis for rational design toward high reproducibility and robustness in OPVs.
authors: Xingpeng Liu, Longjing Wan, Ruikai Yu, Zemin He, Yutong Zhang, Xiao Yang, Chuanhao Zhao, Rui Zhou, Zirui Liu, Jingming Xin, Chunpeng Song, Bin Tang, Wancheng Yu, Zhi-Guo Zhang, Qiuju Liang, Jiangang Liu

10.1002/adfm.79377.title: Breaking the Limits of Piezo-Photocatalysis: Pd-O d-p Orbital Hybridization Mediated Charge Reconstruction and Polarization Enhancement
10.1002/adfm.79377.abstract: ABSTRACT Piezo-photocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy to suppress charge recombination in conventional photocatalysis for the removal of refractory organic pollutants and green hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production. Nevertheless, sulfide-based piezo-photocatalysts still suffer from weak piezoelectric response and ambiguous coupling mechanisms between atomic orbitals and polarization. Herein, we designed Pd-doped and lattice oxygen-modified Zn 3 In 2 S 6 piezo-photocatalyst (Zn 3 In 2 S 6 -Pd-350) by regulating d-p orbital hybridization at Pd sites to achieve efficient piezo-photocatalytic performance. Lattice oxygen occupies sulfur vacancies and converts Pd-S into Pd-O coordination, enabling strong Pd 4d-O 2p orbital hybridization. The σ* and π* antibonding orbitals act as electron acceptors to accelerate charge separation. The charge asymmetry induced by Pd and lattice oxygen enhanced piezoelectric properties of catalyst, resulting in a 156% increase of the piezoelectric coefficient. Zn 3 In 2 S 6 -Pd-350 achieved 100% degradation of 2,4-DCP and H 2 O 2 yield of 327.9 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 , accompanied by •OH, •O 2 − and 1 O 2 synergistic oxidation. Calculations confirm that single-atom Pd replacing Zn is the active center with optimal Pd-S 1 O 3 coordination, and external strain further enhances O 2 /H 2 O adsorption. This work establishes an atomic-level design strategy via orbital engineering, reveals the essential synergy among orbital hybridization, charge distribution and piezoelectric polarization, and provides a feasible route for chlorophenol wastewater remediation and low-carbon H 2 O 2 synthesis.
authors: Meng Dai, Yi Ren, Shumeng Qin, Hongsheng Li, Ziye Zheng, Lihui Xiao, Dong Zhai, Xiaoge Wu, Shu-guang Wang, Zuoli He

10.1002/adfm.79379.title: Multi-Site Contact Schottky Junctions with Improved Light Adsorption Enable Efficient Carrier Transport for Photoelectrocatalytic Water Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.79379.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) water splitting enables sustainable solar-to-hydrogen conversion, yet bismuth tungstate (Bi 2 WO 6 ) photoanodes suffer from severe charge recombination. Herein, we rationally design a novel multi-site contact Schottky junction with modulated interfacial electronic structure and multi-site charge transport channels by integrating 2D Fe-doped Bi 2 WO 6 (Fe-BWO) nanosheets with 3D RuCu co-doped WC (RuCu-WC) dodecahedra. The polyhedral scaffold forms multiple discrete yet intimate contact points at its vertices and edges, constructing abundant parallel electron extraction channels. The introduction of Fe broaden the light harvesting efficiency endowing with an improved interfacial carrier density. Driven by the large work function difference, a strong interfacial built-in electric field is established, which unidirectionally drives photogenerated electrons from band-narrowed Fe-BWO into the interconnected 3D RuCu-WC conductive network while spatially confining photogenerated holes on the Fe-BWO basal plane to drive the water oxidation reaction. The optimized photoanode delivers an exceptional photocurrent density of 7.40 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) with 66.1% charge transfer efficiency. The assembled PEC water splitting cell achieves a remarkable photocurrent density of 6.39 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V and a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency of 5.59%. This work provides a generalizable strategy for enhancing charge separation in semiconductor-based energy conversion systems.
authors: Qingqing Liu, Liyun Cao, Jianfeng Huang, Xingang Kong, Liangliang Feng, Faliang Luo, Haijun Ma, Dewei Chu, Yijun Liu, Junle Dong, Yongqiang Feng

10.1002/adfm.77680.title: MOF-Based Materials for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction: From Mechanism Foundation to Catalyst Design
10.1002/adfm.77680.abstract: ABSTRACT Currently, hydrogen energy, as a clean energy carrier, plays a crucial role in future energy development. Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is one of the essential half reactions in electrochemical water splitting for hydrogen production. However, HER under alkaline condition suffers from sluggish kinetics due to its complex reaction mechanism. Consequently, developing highly active, stable, and cost-effective HER catalysts in alkaline media and understanding its underlying reaction mechanisms are indispensable for advancing the hydrogen energy economy. Metal-organic framework (MOF) and their derivatives have emerged as a prominent class of alkaline HER catalysts, owing to their structural tunability, compositional diversity and coordination environment adjustability. Herein, we systematically review the recent research progress of MOF-based materials for alkaline HER. First, the fundamental mechanisms of alkaline HER are summarized, including the classical hydrogen binding energy theory, bifunctional theory, and emerging insights related to the interfacial water structure and hydrogen-bond networks at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Furthermore, the latest research on MOF-based alkaline HER catalysts is categorized by heterostructure engineering, alloys, and doping strategies, with focus on illustrating the intrinsic relationship among the electrocatalytic performance, intermediate behaviors and interfacial microenvironment. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives, particularly, artificial intelligence-assisted catalyst design are outlined.

10.1002/adfm.79383.title: Interfacial Hydrophilization-Assisted Buried-Interface Reconstruction for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79383.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole-based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) stand out as competitive hole-transport materials for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), benefiting from their low-temperature processing and robust operational stability. Nevertheless, intrinsic SAM aggregation and surface hydrophobicity hinder perovskite precursor wetting, trigger uneven buried-interface nucleation, and worsen interfacial contact, limiting device performance improvement. Herein, two fluorinated phosphonic-acid molecules, namely FPA-Ph and FPA-Py, are utilized to reconstruct the buried SAM/perovskite interface. Both modifiers improve the wettability of the SAM surface and modulate the local interfacial environment via interactions with the SAM and perovskite components. Relative to FPA-Ph, the extra pyridinic-N sites in FPA-Py further boost surface wettability and strengthen Pb 2+ coordination, concurrently generating a smoother and more homogeneous SAM layer. These synergistic effects promote the formation of compact perovskite films, favorable interfacial energetics, and optimized carrier dynamics. Consequently, FPA-Py-modified PSCs deliver a champion efficiency of 26.53% while possessing exceptional operational stability against high humidity, elevated temperature, and continuous illumination. This work demonstrates hydrophilization-assisted molecular post-treatment as an effective approach to buried-interface reconstruction and provides rational molecular-design guidance for the scalable fabrication of inverted PSCs.
authors: Zerui Wu, Shiji Zhang, Yuhua Gao, Xueming Hong, Hongbing Li, Jia Yang, Bairu Liu, Kai Huang, Piao Zhang, Yonghua Tang, Hongxing Li, Gang Liu, Yanling Wang, Fei Guo, Lili Ke

10.1002/adfm.79410.title: A Superelastic Xylan-Stabilized Liquid Metal Aerogel for Wearable Energy Harvesting and Personal Thermal Management
10.1002/adfm.79410.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of wearable electronics places higher demands on materials with mechanical flexibility, sustainable energy supply, and thermal management. However, incorporating conductive fillers such as liquid metal (LM) into soft porous materials may introduce additional heat-transfer pathways and complicate thermal management. Here, a molecular and structural engineering strategy is reported to integrate triboelectric energy harvesting with thermal insulation in a superelastic aerogel. Industrial xylan is converted into carboxymethyl xylan (CMX) through ball-milling pretreatment and etherification, enabling stable dispersion of LM micro/nanodroplets. Subsequently, by synergistically integrating directional freezing and foaming, an aerogel with a unique interconnected perforated-bubble structure is constructed. During 1000 compression cycles at a maximum strain of 60%, the aerogel exhibits progressively stabilized cyclic behavior, with residual strains of 8.7% and 11.5% in the transverse and longitudinal directions, respectively. The aerogel-based triboelectric nanogenerator delivers an output voltage of 112 V, while the aerogel architecture maintains low transverse and longitudinal effective thermal conductivities of 35.8 and 39.5 mW m −1 K −1 , respectively. This work provides a structural design strategy for integrating triboelectric energy harvesting, mechanical resilience, and thermal insulation within a multifunctional soft aerogel.
authors: Qiang Liu, Yin Yan, Mingguo Ma, Mingfei Li, Feng Peng, Jing Bian

10.1002/adfm.79332.title: Electric-Field-Coupled Heterointerface Engineering via Li/F Co-Doping for Enhanced Rate Capability and Interfacial Stability of Fe/Mn-Based Layered Sodium Cathodes
10.1002/adfm.79332.abstract: ABSTRACT P2-type Fe/Mn-based layered oxide materials have long been plagued by structural degradation, air sensitivity, and interfacial instability, which severely restrict their application in sodium-ion batteries. Herein, we propose an in situ modification strategy integrating bulk Li/F co-doping with a surface heterojunction coating and successfully synthesize Na 0.67 Fe 0.35 Mn 0.5 Li 0.15 O 1.93 F 0.07 (LMO@NFMLOF). IDPC-STEM reveals the heterogeneous structure comprising distinct inner and outer regions. DFT calculations confirm the presence of a built-in electric field at the heterointerface. The experimental results demonstrate that bulk Li/F co-doping enhances crystal stability, while the built-in electric field generated by the surface heterojunction accelerates Na + kinetic processes, and the coating further improves air and interfacial stability. Consequently, the LMO@NFMLOF cathode delivers a discharge capacity of 110 mAh g − 1 after 200 cycles at 2C. Remarkably, it maintains a discharge capacity of 85.6 mAh g − 1 after 300 cycles at 5C, demonstrating outstanding rate capability and cycling stability. This synergistic bulk-surface optimization provides a new approach for designing high-rate layered oxide cathodes.
authors: Yihan Li, Zixiang Guo, Anrui Feng, Yuanyuan Yang, Runze Liu, Na Chen, Anqi Li, Xue Qin, Lijuan Zhang, Zezhong Lin

10.1002/adfm.79358.title: Recyclable Lignin-Based Thermadapt Shape Memory Polymers With Near-Infrared Light Response
10.1002/adfm.79358.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have been designed to address the recycling challenges associated with thermosets, while preserving their mechanical properties. However, producing biobased CANs with intelligent response capabilities remains challenging. We report the preparation of lignin-polypentadecalactone-based CANs with a high biomass content (86.2-96.4 wt%). In lignin-PPDL CANs, acetoacetate-modified lignin serves dual roles as the hard segment and crosslinker, while the polypentadecalactone (PPDL) soft segment exhibits a semi-crystalline nature. Crosslinking between the soft PPDL and hard lignin segments is achieved via vinylogous urethane chemistry, resulting in CANs with markedly enhanced mechanical properties and recyclability. When applied to shape memory systems, the semi-crystalline polymer domains act as reversible molecular switches, while dynamic bond exchange enables topological rearrangement, allowing reconfiguration of the permanent shape, characteristic of thermadapt shape memory polymers. Leveraging the photothermal conversion capability of lignin, we successfully developed near-infrared (NIR) light-responsive shape memory CANs. These innovative materials hold promising prospects for applications in intelligent materials, given their unique combination of mechanical strength, shape memory capabilities, and responsiveness to NIR light. Furthermore, the approach of tailoring the new material based on the specific properties of the raw material in this study offers a novel avenue for designing high-performance multifunctional CANs.
authors: Jian Liu, Yanfan Yang, Görkem Eylül Kaya, Huixing Cao, Joost Brancart, Niko Van den Brande, Lin Dai, Chuanling Si, Katrien V. Bernaerts

10.1002/adfm.79305.title: External Field Driven Oxygen Reduction Reaction: From Catalytic Chemistry, Mechanistic Characterization to Device Applications
10.1002/adfm.79305.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) serves as the cornerstone of next-generation energy conversion technologies, including zinc-air batteries, electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide, and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, its intrinsically sluggish kinetics remains a critical bottleneck limiting device performance. This review work systematically examines the recent frontier advances in the development of advanced ORR electrocatalysts, aiming to construct a cross-scale framework spanning from atomic-level design to macroscopic device integration. First, this review focuses on atomic-level catalyst design strategies, elaborating how approaches such as Cheteroatom coordination, construction of heteronuclear dual-atom sites, and coupling of single atoms with clusters/nanoparticles can break the symmetry limitations of conventional M-N 4 configurations. Second, the mechanism of enhanced external field coupling and how the external fields (light and magnetism, etc.) synergistically accelerate the ORR process are explored. Finally, this review summarizes the integration and application outcomes of advanced catalysts in zinc-air batteries, electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide, and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Despite significant progress, the commercialization of these catalysts still faces the challenge of balancing activity and stability. Future research should focus on electrode mass transport engineering, multi-field coupling integration, and data-driven research paradigms to promote the practical application of high-performance ORR electrocatalysts.

10.1002/adfm.79311.title: Heteroengineering-Induced Electronic Reconstruction for Ammonium-Ion Energy Storage
10.1002/adfm.79311.abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonium-ion supercapacitor (AISC) emerges as a promising energy storage system owing to its safety, low cost, and sustainability. However, the large tetrahedral geometry of NH 4 + , compared with the spherical structure of metallic charge carriers, leads to an inefficient intercalation chemistry, resulting in unsatisfied capacity. Here, we introduce local heteroengineering on the VO 2 (B) surface to modulate its electronic structure, which enables an integrated electronic reconstruction behavior: (i) electrons spontaneously transfer to the higher-energy V t 2g orbital, enhancing the intrinsic conductivity; (ii) adaptive electron redistribution at the heterointerface generates a reversible built-in electric field (BIEF), offering extra coulombic driving force for NH 4 + (de)intercalation. This electronic adjustment accordingly reduces the NH 4 + diffusion energy barriers in host materials and promotes NH 4 + intercalation efficiency. As a result, the VO 2 @VS heterogenous electrode delivers 214.7 mAh g −1 (556.3 F g −1 ) at 1 A g −1 , reaching 2/3 theoretical capacity of vanadium dioxides (323 mAh g −1 ), and retains 107.2 mAh g −1 (275 F g −1 ) at a high current density of 10 A g −1 . This study explores the electronic structural evolution induced by rational heteroengineering, providing new pathways for advancing efficient ammonium-ion energy storage systems.
authors: Ji-Chi Liu, Nuo Xu, Liberty L. Mguni, Kexin Wang, Lanxiang Ma, Ying Sun, Hui Li, Lingfeng Zhu, Yali Yao, Xu Han, Zi-Hang Huang, Tianyi Ma

10.1002/adfm.78895.title: The Effect of Hydrophilic Headgroup Chemistry on Peptoid-Directed Mineralization of CaCO 3
10.1002/adfm.78895.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineered mineralization of calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) provides one strategy for CO 2 capture removal. Developing additives to accelerate the process or control resulting polymorphs would enhance underground reservoir security and advance development of CaCO 3 -based building materials. Peptoids - sequence-specific poly-N-substituted glycines - have been shown to accelerate CaCO 3 nucleation and growth, select for metastable polymorphs, and induce unusual morphologies, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate control of these phenomena by using amphiphilic di-block peptoids with carboxyl (-COOH) and amine (-NH 2 ) rich hydrophilic blocks. We demonstrate that -COOH-functionalized peptoids free in solution drive rapid crystallization of calcite directly from amorphous precursors, bypassing the metastable vaterite phase observed in control experiments. Systematically increasing the number of -COOH groups progressively tunes calcite morphology from perfect rhombohedra to truncated structures to spindle-shaped mesocrystals. In contrast, -NH 2 -bearing peptoids preferentially stabilize vaterite. When assembled into crystalline nanosheets exposing the hydrophilic block, only -COOH-rich peptoid sheets nucleate crystals, unequivocally identifying carboxyl moieties as the key templating group for calcite formation. These findings provide chemical insights into controls of amphiphilic peptoids over CaCO 3 formation, establishing a platform for design of peptoids to control crystallization and advancing CO 2 sequestration and sustainable materials synthesis through carbonate mineralization.

10.1002/adfm.79372.title: Bridging Local Anionic Polarity to Macroscopic State Separability: Molecular Design for Tailored Polaron Kinetics in Organic Synaptic Transistors
10.1002/adfm.79372.abstract: ABSTRACT Rational modulation over carrier dynamics in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors is fundamental to modern neuromorphic hardware, yet molecularly regulating the relaxation kinetics of polarons to dictate high-dimensional state space remains an elusive goal. Here, we demonstrate that the anionic polarity index (API), a quantitative metric defining localized charge density, functions as a predictive descriptor bridging microscopic polaron kinetics to macroscopic state space evolution in electrolyte-gated organic synaptic transistors (EGOSTs). Rather than acting as passive counterions, high-API anions concentrate their local electrostatic potential, establishing robust non-covalent interactions with the oxidized polymer matrix. This electrostatic confinement elevates the energy barrier for anion back-diffusion, retarding polaron relaxation kinetics without sacrificing electrochemical doping efficiency. By translating this local charge localization into macro-scale transport control, we decouple dynamic range from fading memory, enabling precise tuning of the relaxation time constant and significantly expanding accessible reservoir state space. Consequently, the resulting physical reservoir achieves superior phase-space separability, yielding a 91.2% classification accuracy in MNIST benchmark simulations and maintaining 89.2% accuracy under fourfold feature compression. This study establishes a generalizable molecular design strategy that quantitatively connects local electrostatic confinement to high-dimensional state evolution in organic physical reservoirs.
authors: Myeongjin An, Meng Qiang Li, Donghwa Lee, Junho Sung, Jinglong Pang, Jaewon Lee, Eunho Lee

10.1002/adfm.79349.title: NiN4C-Coordination Stabilized Cobalt-Based Single Cluster Catalyst with High Active Site Density: Rationally Designed Atomic Architecture Boosts Oxygen Reduction Activity
10.1002/adfm.79349.abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of single-cluster catalysts (SCCs) for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is hindered by difficulties in achieving atomic precision, high site-density and resistance to aggregation during synthesis and operation. To address these challenges, we report a NiN 4 C-coordinated cobalt-based SCC which is synthesized via a gradient pyrolysis-driven stepwise anchoring strategy that enables the sequential thermal anchoring of Ni and Co species. Well-defined NiN 4 C moieties are anchored on the carbon support at the lower pyrolysis temperature; these sites subsequently capture cobalt oxide fragments at a higher pyrolysis temperature, leading to the formation of a NiN 4 C-site coordinated stable Co 3 O 5 NiN 4 C ensemble. Advanced in situ spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry and density functional theory calculations infer its electrochemical transformation into an active Co 3 O 1 NiN 4 C phase prior to the onset of ORR. The triangular Co 3 motif facilitates side-on adsorption, elongating the O-O bond and lowering the dissociation energy barrier for the rate-determining step. Consequently, the catalyst delivers exceptional ORR performance, achieving a half-wave potential of 0.923 V vs. RHE, an active-site density of 4.16 × 10 20 sites g −1 , and a peak power density of 247.3 mW cm −2 in Zinc-air batteries. This work provides an effective strategy for designing stable, efficient oxygen electrocatalysts by precisely engineered cluster architecture.
authors: Xinbo Qiu, Yuqing Xin, Tianxiang Chen, Xiaoyu Wu, Zehong Yuan, Eduardo Villalobos-Portillo, Carlo Marini, Peng Diao, Jing Peng

10.1002/adfm.79393.title: Guest Donor With High Electrostatic Potential Enables Low-Energy-Loss Ternary All-Polymer Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79393.abstract: ABSTRACT In ternary all-polymer organic solar cells (all-PSCs), while the short-circuit current density ( J SC ) and fill factor (FF) are enhanced, further device efficiency improvement is constrained by the large energy loss. Here, a wide-bandgap guest donor PTO2 with deeper energy level is introduced into the PM6:PYIT system to resolve this issue. Theoretical calculations indicate that PTO2 exhibits a more negative electrostatic potential (ESP), enabling the formation of a strong intermolecular electric field when paired with the acceptor that displays a positive surface ESP, thereby facilitating efficient exciton dissociation. Experimentally, PTO2 endows complementary light absorption, optimizes the vertical composition distribution, balances the crystallization kinetics, and promotes tighter π - π stacking. Meanwhile, PTO2 can effectively enhance the built-in electric field and reduce charge generation/recombination associated energy loss. Consequently, the ternary device achieves an optimal efficiency of 19.12% with an enhanced open circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.963 V without sacrificing J SC and FF compared to PM6:PYIT. This work highlights the crucial role of ESP modulation and provides a novel matching approach for high-performance ternary all-PSCs.
authors: Yongjie Cui, Anxu Cheng, Wenzhao Xiong, Zhibo Wang, Shenbo Zhu, Zaifei Ma, Huawei Hu

10.1002/adfm.79400.title: Mast Cell-Targeted Gas Therapeutic Strategy: Intelligent H2S-Donor Nano-Stabilizer for the Long-Term Treatment of Allergic Diseases In Vivo
10.1002/adfm.79400.abstract: ABSTRACT Allergic diseases driven by dysregulated mast cell activation remain a major clinical challenge due to the repeated long-term dosing and severe side effects of current small-molecule stabilizers. Gas therapy offers a promising alternative owing to its high biocompatibility, minimal toxicity, and stimulus-responsive release. Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), an endogenous gas mediator involved in inflammatory regulation, has not yet been explored for the treatment of allergic inflammation. Herein, a mast cell-targeted H 2 S gas therapeutic strategy was developed for the long-term treatment of allergic diseases. Biodegradable mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles incorporating tetrasulfide bridges were rationally designed, loaded with sodium cromoglicate, and surface-modified with hyaluronic acid (HA) to construct the nano-stabilizer ( S MSNs@SC@HA ). HA coating enabled mast cell targeting and prevented premature drug leakage. Intracellular glutathione triggered sustained (>24 h) H 2 S release via tetrasulfide bond cleavage, suppressing mast cell degranulation through antioxidative effects and AMP-activated kinase (AMPK) activation, while simultaneously inducing carrier degradation and controlled drug release. This system represents the first H 2 S-donating nanoplatform for targeted mast cell delivery, achieving synergistic anti-allergic efficacy. In vivo studies in passive cutaneous anaphylaxis and allergic asthma models demonstrated high therapeutic efficacy, prolonged treatment duration, and negligible inflammatory side effects, highlighting its strong potential for clinical translation.
authors: Qian Shen, Chan Fu, Xiaoyu Song, Yangyang Pu, Yao Wang, Xiang Che, Apeng Chen, Man Tian, Lin Li, Changmin Yu

10.1002/adfm.79402.title: A Particle-Level Dual-Polymer Interphase for Coupled Interfacial and Contact Stabilization of Zinc Metal Powder Anodes in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79402.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc metal powder (ZnMP) anodes offer a practical strategy for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). However, the curved and discontinuous ZnMP surfaces enlarge the Zn/electrolyte interface, accelerating hydrogen evolution and surface corrosion. Point contacts and limited electronic pathways further cause nonuniform current distribution and Zn 2+ flux, leading to uneven Zn deposition and contact loss. Here, a dual-polymer interphase composed of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) on ZnMP (C/P@ZnMP) is reported. The CMC matrix regulates the local aqueous environment and suppresses water-related interfacial degradation, while PAA provides abundant carboxyl/carboxylate sites with relatively high Zn 2+ affinity. Their integration balances PAA-derived Zn 2+ affinity with CMC-mediated interfacial stabilization and limits byproduct accumulation. The hydrophilic C/P interphase improves electrolyte infiltration into the particulate ZnMP electrode, helping alleviate electrical contact loss within the powder framework. C/P@ZnMP enables stable Zn plating/stripping for over 1500 h at 2 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . The C/P@ZnMP‖V 2 O 5 coin cell retains 85.5% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g −1 , and the 4 × 3 cm 2 C/P@ZnMP‖V 2 O 5 pouch cell retains 89.2% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 , demonstrating the potential of dual-polymer interphase engineering for practical ZnMP-based AZIBs.

10.1002/adfm.79412.title: Amorphous-Nanocrystalline Silicate-Superalloy Heterointerfaces Combining High-Temperature Electrical Insulation with Large-Strain Tolerance
10.1002/adfm.79412.abstract: ABSTRACT The key bottleneck in in situ monitoring of nickel-based superalloy hot-section components is the lack of a reliable insulating interface for oxidative and thermomechanical extremes. Conventional ceramic insulating layers and multilayer architectures remain constrained by complex processing, interfacial mismatch, limited strain tolerance, and brittle failure. Here, we report a directly printable amorphous-nanocrystalline silicate coating that enables a robust multifunctional interface on nickel-based superalloys without additional bonding or transition layers. During annealing, the printed silicate layer densifies, locally crystallizes, and wets the superalloy surface, producing an amorphous-nanocrystalline coating with a mechanically interlocked interface. The amorphous matrix ensures electrical insulation and oxygen-barrier performance, while dispersed nanocrystals promote strain redistribution and crack-path deflection. The integrated structure allows the coating to maintain stable insulation at 1100°C, achieve an adhesion strength of 90.5 N, substantially suppress high-temperature oxidation, and remain structurally intact under strains exceeding 18,000 µε. Integrated Pt thin-film strain sensors achieve stable strain monitoring at 1100°C, and turbine-blade demonstration further validates the printable insulating interface for conformal integration and accurate high-temperature sensing. The printable single-coating strategy provides a multilayer-free interfacial platform for robust high-temperature sensing on superalloy components.
authors: Lida Xu, Shilong Jia, Yuelong Li, Ning Wang, Rui Liang, Qinnan Chen, Daoheng Sun

10.1002/adfm.79390.title: Photovoltaic-Hydrovoltaic Synergistic Luminescent Solar Concentrators for Weather-Adaptive Energy Harvesting and Self-Powered Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79390.abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent solar concentrators (LSCs) present an aesthetically viable pathway for building-integrated photovoltaics, yet their practical deployment remains constrained by luminophore defect-induced photoluminescence losses and diminished functionality under rainy conditions. To overcome these limitations, photovoltaic-hydrovoltaic synergistic LSCs (PHS-LSCs) for energy harvesting under both sunny and rainy conditions are proposed based on defect-passivated perovskite-poly(vinylidene fluoride) composite films laminated with fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP). The incorporation of tetraethylenepentamine acetate enables multisite in situ passivation of surface defects in perovskite luminophores, thereby affording the PHS-LSCs a competitive external optical efficiency of 8.8% ± 0.3%. During rainy conditions, the perovskite-poly(vinylidene fluoride) composite film significantly improves hydrovoltaic performance of PHS-LSCs via enhancing electrostatically induced charge density through dipolar reorientation in the high-polar-phase perovskite-poly(vinylidene fluoride) dielectric interlayer, yielding an output voltage of 310 V and an instantaneous power of 58.3 ± 4.2 mW (67.5% improvement compared with pristine FEP-based devices). The dual-mode energy output is used to power low-consumption sensors, demonstrating a weather-adaptive energy-harvesting platform for smart buildings and intelligent agriculture.
authors: Pengfei Xia, Shujiao Chen, Yuchen Hu, Erdong Zhang, Chunyang Tian, Haotian Guo, Kaijie Chen, Shuhong Xu, Chunlei Wang

10.1002/adfm.79387.title: A Cationic Redox-Active Interface Couples Nitrate Enrichment With Hydroxylamine Release for Cyclohexanone Oxime Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.79387.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis of cyclohexanone oxime (CYCO), a key nylon-6 precursor, is limited by the poor selectivity of nitrate reduction toward hydroxylamine because surface-bound NH 2 OH can be over-reduced to NH 3 before coupling with cyclohexanone. Herein, we construct a thionine acetate (Th) modified Cu 2 O interface (Th/Cu 2 O) that integrates electrostatic steering with redox-mediated electron transfer. Under weakly acidic conditions, protonated Th creates a positively charged interfacial microenvironment that enriches NO 3 − , stabilizes early reduction intermediates, and promotes the release of protonated NH 2 OH (NH 3 OH + ) from the inner Helmholtz layer. Concurrently, the redox activity of Th facilitates electron delivery to Cu active sites and favors the NH 2 OH-forming pathway over further reduction to NH 3 . At −0.35 V vs. RHE, Th/Cu 2 O achieves a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 82.14% for NH 2 OH, with nearly 100% selectivity toward CYCO. In a membrane-separated flow cell operated at 1.2 A, the CYCO production rate reaches 57.63 g h −1 g cat. −1 , demonstrating the industrial potential of Th/Cu 2 O for gram-scale CYCO synthesis. In situ characterization, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations collectively connect interfacial charge regulation, mass transport, and reaction energetics, establishing a molecular-level interfacial strategy for universal oxime electrochemical synthesis.
authors: Ziyuan Xiu, Dian Ling, Hao Yu, Ying Liu, Hao Zhu, Qiao Lu, Dongzhi Chen

10.1002/adfm.79278.title: Multifunctional Borate Additive Enables Defect Passivation and Crystallization Control Toward High-Performance n-i-p Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79278.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) represent one of the most promising next-generation photovoltaic technologies, owing to their exceptional optical absorption coefficient, tunable bandgap, long carrier diffusion length and low-cost solution processability. However, the performance of PSCs remains constrained by the crystalline quality and high defect density of perovskite thin films. Herein, we report a multifunctional molecular additive, potassium [(tert-butoxycarbonylamino) methyl] trifluoroborate (denoted as ER). Theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations reveal that the hydroxyl groups generated via -BF 3 − hydrolysis and carbonyl oxygen atoms in ER strongly coordinate with undercoordinated Pb 2+ ions. Meanwhile, the tert-butoxycarbonylamino (-NH-Boc) group effectively suppresses iodide migration by anchoring I − through hydrogen bonding. Notably, ER molecules can capture ambient moisture, converting humidity from a detrimental environmental factor into “chemical fuel” that drives in situ defect passivation through a self-catalyzed molecular transformation process. As a result, the optimized n-i-p structured PSCs with ER achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.63%. Moreover, the unencapsulated device maintains 93.84% of its initial PCE after for 1778 h of aging under ISOS-D-1 conditions. This work provides an effective strategy for synergistically regulating perovskite crystallization and defect passivation via molecular engineering, thereby promoting the development of high-performance and long-term stable PSCs.
authors: Yujie Liu, Jiacheng Pi, Jiafan Zhang, Yang Cao, Haoyi Zhang, Kai Wang, Danyang Qi, Jiarong Wu, Nan Li, Jianzhong Liu, Jinjun Wu, Xingyu Gao, Yucheng Liu, Shengzhong (Frank) Liu, Jiangshan Feng

10.1002/adfm.79384.title: Adaptive Lubrication and Antiwear Enabled by Synergy Between Friction-Induced In Situ Tribo-Click Reaction and Gel Confinement of Reaction Products
10.1002/adfm.79384.abstract: ABSTRACT Friction and wear cause massive energy dissipation and mechanical failure, driving the demand for advanced lubrication. Here, we report a facile gel-confined in situ tribo-click platform triggered by interfacial friction. Azide and alkyne precursors are incorporated into supramolecular gel lubricants; reciprocal sliding on copper releases catalytic Cu(I) ions to initiate on-site Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reactions, producing lubricious triazole adducts. The 3D supramolecular network physically traps base oil and tribo-products via molecular confinement and anchoring, facilitating dense, durable tribofilms. This system exhibits intrinsic adaptive behavior: harsher frictional stimuli accelerate tribo-click conversion and yield more lubricating species. Through systematic characterization, we show that, unlike conventional liquid-oil systems, the gel network suppresses product diffusion and leaching, drastically improving tribofilm thickness and long-term stability. By synergizing tribocatalytic click chemistry with the spatial confinement of low-molecular-weight gelators (LMWGs), this work establishes a high-performance self-adaptive lubrication paradigm in friction control.
authors: Weijian Liu, Luyao Bao, Hao-Zhe Xu, Ao Xie, Ming Zhang, Yijing Liang, Xin-Gang Wang, Meirong Cai, Feng Zhou, Weimin Liu

10.1002/adfm.79385.title: Regulating Liquid-Phase Mass Transport via Electric Field-Pore Size Synergy in Separator for Long-Life Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79385.abstract: ABSTRACT The separator critically dictates liquid-phase mass transport in aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), while it is poorly regulated in conventional commercial separators due to inappropriate pore structure and heterogeneous surface charge. Herein, we engineer a multifunctional separator (PTT-GF-D) that integrates ordered nanoporous channels with highly negatively charged surface to synchronously regulate ion flux and interfacial electric fields. This design effectively optimizes liquid-phase mass transport, thereby promoting homogeneous multi-site nucleation, accelerating Zn 2+ desolvation, and mitigating Zn 2+ concentration polarization. Consequently, the symmetric cells achieve exceptional reversibility, stably operating for 3300 h under 1 mA cm −2 , 1 mAh cm −2 and maintaining robust stability over 1000 h even under harsh conditions of 10 mA cm −2 , 10 mAh cm −2 . The as-fabricated Zn||MnO 2 full cell delivers a specific capacity of 130 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 , preserving 96.2% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles. A large-sized pouch cell is also demonstrated, which can operate at 5 mA cm −2 for 100 cycles without noticeable decay. This study establishes the critical synergy of pore architecture and surface charge engineering in separators to control liquid-phase mass transport, offering a promising strategy for developing high-performance and practical AZIBs.
authors: Qingyi Lu, Kaiming Xue, Yupeng Xing, Sihan Zheng, Bo Tang, Xiaotao Sun, Cuiping Han, Ze Chen, Guangming Chen, Zhuoxin Liu

10.1002/adfm.79406.title: Interfacial Locking Strategy by Porous Low-Dimensional Structure for High-Efficiency and Stable Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79406.abstract: ABSTRACT In p-i-n inverted perovskite solar cells, the photochemical instability and interfacial diffusion of small-molecule electron transport layers (e.g., PCBM) are critical bottlenecks limiting long-term operational stability. Herein, we introduce a bis-pyridine bidentate ligand to reconstruct the three-dimensional perovskite surface into a discontinuous, porous low-dimensional phase. Unlike conventional continuous capping layers that impede charge transport, this unique porous architecture achieves simultaneous protection and extraction. The chemically robust low-dimensional framework, anchored via bidentate coordination, encapsulates the intrinsically fragile perovskite surface and provides steric hindrance against small-molecule diffusion. Meanwhile, its discontinuous porosity enables PCBM to penetrate and form an interpenetrating network with the underlying perovskite, dramatically expanding the effective interfacial contact area for carrier extraction without introducing transport resistance. This “porous interfacial locking” strategy fundamentally resolves the passivation-extraction dilemma inherent in traditional interface engineering. Consequently, champion devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.06% with enhanced open-circuit voltage and fill factor, while unencapsulated devices retain over 95% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h of continuous maximum power point tracking. This work establishes discontinuous porous locking as a viable design principle for achieving simultaneous high efficiency and stability in perovskite optoelectronics.
authors: Mengyao Guo, Ziyu Wang, Jinling Zhang, Qihang Sun, Xiyue Wang, Xinyu Yuan, Minghao Wu, Shen Li, Yidan Ren, Yanlin Song, Ziqiu Ren

10.1002/adfm.79347.title: Architectural Tuning of Bouligand Electrospun Laminates Enables Coupled Mechanical Robustness and Electromechanical Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79347.abstract: ABSTRACT Nature provides design principles that enable multifunctional materials to combine mechanical resilience with specialized functionality. Translating hierarchical biological architectures into compliant synthetic systems capable of integrated sensing and human-machine interfacing, however, remains largely unexplored. Here, we analyze the helicoidal Bouligand organization of the blue crab (Callinectes sapidus) exoskeleton and translate this principle into biodegradable electrospun poly(L-lactide-co-ε-caprolactone) (PLCL) laminates with embedded carbon nanotube (CNT) sensing layers. By varying the angular rotation between fiber layers while maintaining identical composition, we isolate the influence of laminate architecture on mechanical and electromechanical performance. A 20° interlayer rotation provides the most balanced mechanical response, increasing Young's modulus more than threefold and tensile strength by almost 40% relative to randomly stacked laminates. Despite being around 100 µm thick, the laminates withstand out-of-plane deformations exceeding 55 to 73 times their thickness before failure, while the embedded CNT network enables real-time detection of structural damage. After textile integration, laminates function as wearable sensors for touch, strain, temperature, and weight, with laminate architecture producing over an order of magnitude variation in electrical output. As a proof-of-concept human-machine interface, the laminates enable real-time signal visualization and synchronized robotic hand actuation, demonstrating a scalable strategy for smart materials and bioinspired structural electronics.
authors: Piotr K. Szewczyk, Daniel P. Ura, Michał Kopacz, Katarzyna Marszalik, Urszula Stachewicz

10.1002/adfm.79395.title: Electronic Structure Engineering Enables Dynamic Interfacial Adaptation of Zinc Anodes
10.1002/adfm.79395.abstract: ABSTRACT In aqueous zinc-ion batteries, Zn plating/stripping is accompanied by continuous evolution of the local electric field, solvation structure, and interfacial chemical environment. Therefore, conventional electrolyte additives that rely on fixed adsorption or static interfacial layer construction are insufficient for sustained interfacial regulation. Herein, we propose an electronic structure regulation strategy that endows electrolyte additives with dynamic interfacial adaptability through molecular engineering. Using pyrrolidone derivatives as model molecules, we demonstrate that vinyl functionalization strengthens π-electron delocalization and enhances the polarization response of N -vinyl-2-pyrrolidone (NVP). Such electronically adaptive behavior allows NVP to respond to the evolving local interfacial environment via electronic redistribution, thereby adaptively modulating the Zn/electrolyte interface while simultaneously optimizing interfacial Zn 2+ solvation, water distribution, and Zn deposition behavior. Consequently, the ZSO+NVP electrolyte enables a Zn//Zn symmetric cell to operate stably for over 4000 h at 10 mA cm −2 , while the Zn//NH 4 V 4 O 10 full cell delivers 92.6% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 2 A g −1 . This work reveals the critical role of additive electronic responsiveness in stabilizing dynamic Zn/electrolyte interfaces.
authors: Jiaming Li, Qin Xiang, Fengle Bai, Zhuofan Chen, Tianli Li, Congcong Cai, Chaoqun Shang, Weifeng Huang, Hanhao Liang, Pu Hu

10.1002/adfm.79319.title: Intrinsic-Decoupled Biomimetic Two-Dimensional Sensing Enabled by Positive-Negative Dielectric Heterostructures for Pressure Visualization
10.1002/adfm.79319.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible tactile sensors capable of simultaneously emulating the multidirectional perception of human skin and realizing intrinsic force decoupling remain a critical challenge for advanced robotics and intelligent human-machine interfaces. Inspired by the hierarchical architecture of epidermal cells, we present a two-dimensional force sensor (TDFS) featuring a biomimetic heterostructure that enables structural separation of normal and tangential force components. Force discrimination is enabled by engineering a negative-permittivity composite with a gradient-modulus architecture that mechanically reduces the overlap between deformation fields induced by normal and tangential loading. Additionally, benefiting from this structural design and a differential capacitive scheme, the TDFS exhibits reduced inter-axis coupling within the calibrated loading range and a high angular resolution of 1.5° ranging from 20 to 30 N. The TDFS device provides monotonic normal and tangential responses over 0-30 N, exhibiting high detection sensitivity. Through optimization of the parameters, a separate normal device fabricated with Ni 0.9 achieves a peak normal sensitivity of −892.933 N − 1 within the 27-30 N loading range. A customized readout circuit was further developed to enable stable signal acquisition from the negative-capacitance sensing system. The synergistic design facilitates directional force perception and provides a reliable and scalable solution for next-generation multidimensional electronic skins.
authors: Jingjing Li, Peng Li, Yuanhang Xu, Fujing Xie, Kaiqi Guo, Feihong Ran, Chen Rong, Han Wang, Yufen Wu, Jin Yang, Wei Wei

10.1002/adfm.79404.title: Multistage Thermally Responsive Aerogel for Full-Cycle Thermal Protection in Battery Modules to Prevent Thermal Runaway Propagation
10.1002/adfm.79404.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal runaway propagation (TRP) remains a critical safety challenge for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, traditional thermal protection materials cannot address the coupled hazards of heat, flames, and explosion-induced mechanical impact during TR. Herein, a multistage thermal response aerogel strategy for full-cycle TR protection was designed. During the controllable stage, the aerogel releases water vapor, which not only reduces the theoretical oxygen mole fraction to 4.07% but also enables early warning through changes in local humidity. During the uncontrollable stage, Co-BDC-assisted decomposition sustains the evolution of flame-retardant gases, enabling prolonged flame suppression. Meanwhile, an in situ ceramization reaction is triggered, generating a dense ceramic layer on the aerogel surface. Together with sustained gas-phase flame suppression, this condensed-phase ceramic barrier effectively suppresses flame propagation. The sandwich-like porous structure of the aerogel creates a tortuous heat-transfer pathway, suppressing heat transfer. Furthermore, in situ ceramization enhances the compressive strength of the aerogel from 1.25 to 4.5 MPa, enabling resistance against explosion-induced mechanical impact during TR. TRP experiments conducted on different battery modules confirmed that the aerogel effectively suppresses TRP. This study demonstrates a strategy for thermal protection materials that is tailored to the stages of TR, ensuring the operational safety of battery modules.

10.1002/adfm.79336.title: Orbital Engineering through Strain-Induced Spin-Orbit-Lattice Coupling in Sr 2 FeReO 6 Double Perovskites
10.1002/adfm.79336.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferromagnetic 3 d -5 d double perovskites exhibit appealing physical properties due to their unique electronic band structures, which result from the hybridization of 3 d and 5 d orbitals. Sr 2 FeReO 6 (SFRO) exhibits half-metallicity, a high Curie temperature (∼400 K), and spin-orbit-lattice coupling, making it a promising candidate for spintronic applications. Here, we demonstrate that epitaxial strain modulates the oxygen-octahedral tilt configuration and the associated Re 5 d orbital polarization in SFRO thin films, leading to pronounced changes in magnetic anisotropy and electronic transport. Atomic-resolution STEM analysis and first-principles calculation reveal distinct octahedral configurations under compressive and tensile strain, accompanied by an orbital-dependent reorganization of the Fe-O-Re hopping network. The resulting redistribution of Re t 2g states near the Fermi level (E F ), further supported by X-ray linear dichroism, is associated with a reversal of the magnetic easy axis from in-plane to out-of-plane. Under tensile strain, the reconstructed low-energy electronic states are accompanied by suppressed optical conductivity and semiconducting-like transport, in contrast to the metallic-like behavior under compressive strain. These findings establish epitaxial strain as an effective means of controlling coupled lattice, orbital, magnetic, and electronic degrees of freedom in 3 d -5 d double perovskites.

10.1002/adfm.79297.title: Strain Rate Triggered Network Locking in Shear-Stiffening Gel/Wood Fibres Composites for Adaptive Impact Protection
10.1002/adfm.79297.abstract: ABSTRACT Lightweight structural materials capable of simultaneously sustaining mechanical load-bearing and dissipating extreme impact energy remain a long-standing challenge, as conventional systems are constrained by the intrinsic trade-off between stiffness and toughness under dynamic loading. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a strain rate triggered network locking strategy that enables adaptive mechanical reconfiguration in poplar fibres (PFs) and shear stiffening gel (SSG) composites (PSCs). PSCs are constructed by integrating PFs networks with SSG, forming a hierarchical interpenetrating architecture in which interfacial interactions and dynamic bonding jointly govern the mechanical response. Under low strain rate loading, PSCs enabled efficient stress distribution, achieving a flexural strength of 58.88 MPa with a balanced toughness. Under high strain rate loading, PSCs reached an energy absorption per unit thickness of 2.04 J·mm −1 and a force per unit thickness of 377.80 N·mm −1 . Notably, a steel projectile impacting at 153.4 m·s −1 rebounded, further demonstrating its potential as a scalable biobased adaptive impact-resistant panel. This strain-rate adaptive design principle provides a general pathway for structural materials, enabling them to simultaneously achieve static load-bearing capacity and dynamic impact protection, and offers a scalable route for the development of biobased adaptive impact-resistant panels.

10.1002/adfm.79440.title: Targeted Lipid-Polymer Nanoparticles Enable Gene-Encoded TRIM21 Degraders for Programmable Protein Degradation
10.1002/adfm.79440.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise and reversible control of endogenous protein abundance in vivo remains a formidable challenge, particularly for targets refractory to small-molecule or traditional genetic perturbation. Here, we report a gene-encoded, programmable protein-degradation nanoplatform enabled by targeted lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles. Through the systematic engineering of poly(β-amino ester) nanocarriers and their integration with cationic lipids and a transferrin-receptor targeting ligand, we achieve highly efficient cytosolic delivery of plasmids encoding degradation-competent E3-ligase fusion proteins. These plasmid payloads drive the intracellular expression of programmable degraders, triggering the ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated elimination of endogenous proteins without requiring modification of endogenous target genes or direct delivery of preformed antibodies or recombinant proteins. Based on the findings, this nanoplatform supports the selective depletion of diverse protein classes, including cytosolic enzymes, membrane-associated immune checkpoints, and aggregation-prone neuronal proteins, yielding high on-target potency with minimal off-target transcriptional perturbation. Crucially, systemic administration yielded proof-of-concept tumor- and brain-targeted gene delivery, target-protein depletion in preclinical models, and encouraging therapeutic signals in selected cancer and neurodegeneration models. By unifying advanced nanomaterial engineering with gene-encoded degradation, this study addresses key in vivo delivery challenges of conventional Trim-Away technology, establishing a highly adaptable blueprint for next-generation protein-degradation therapeutics.

10.1002/adfm.79381.title: State-Dependent Noncovalent Cohesion Enables Durable and Recoverable All-Biomass Photothermal Coatings
10.1002/adfm.79381.abstract: ABSTRACT Balancing service durability with practical material recovery remains challenging for functional coatings because permanent network fixation can hinder reuse. An all-biomass photothermal coating with state-dependent noncovalent cohesion is reported, fabricated by organizing lignocellulosic nanofibers (LCNF), biochar (BC), and carnauba wax through a bioinspired “jet-to-net” spray process. Lignin-retaining LCNF forms an entangled capture scaffold with hydroxyl and aromatic interaction sites, while BC supplies photothermal absorption and roughness and carnauba wax establishes a low-polarity interface. Pareto analysis identifies a composition that balances water repellency, mechanical retention, and photothermal response. Molecular calculations further reveal distributed hydrogen-bonding, aromatic, and wax-mediated dispersion interactions that strengthen collectively after solvent evaporation but weaken in solvent. Accordingly, the coating retains 90.2% of its mass after 100 sand-impact cycles, yet redisperses within 10 s and undergoes ten stripping-recovery-respraying cycles with stripping recovery above 97% in each cycle. As a representative functional validation, the coating heats by 25.83°C under 0.5 sun at −10°C and delays complete freezing to 732 s while reducing ice adhesion. This work illustrates a material design strategy combining structural complementarity, composition control, and reversible interactions for service stability with practical recovery and reuse in application scenarios where both are required.

10.1002/adfm.79338.title: BDNF-Regulated Molecular-to-Material Transduction in an Ion-Electronic Memristive Biointerface for Modeling Addiction-Related Neuroplasticity
10.1002/adfm.79338.abstract: ABSTRACT Addiction-related memories are associated with dysregulated neurotrophic signaling and maladaptive synaptic plasticity. However, it still remains challenging in translating such disease-relevant molecular regulation into history-dependent and programmable material states. Herein, a brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-regulated ion-electronic memristive biointerface is developed by integrating a recognition module comprising a BDNF-responsive aptamer and a tropomyosin receptor kinase B Fc chimera (TrkB-Fc) with a photoactive sodium alginate (SA)/WO 3 composite. Under 365 nm illumination, BDNF-dependent interfacial regulation produces concentration- and history-dependent conductance dynamics associated with W 6+ /W 5+ mixed-valence evolution. The device exhibits synaptic-like responses, including paired-pulse facilitation, learning-forgetting-relearning-like dynamics, and reversible potentiation/depression-like conductance modulation. These device-state changes show functional correspondence with BDNF-enhanced ΔFosB expression and morphine-conditioned place preference, whereas ANA-12 attenuates device-state persistence and behavioral reinstatement in the respective experiments. Experimentally measured volatile responses are further used to construct reservoir states, while experimentally characterized nonvolatile conductance states provide a device-informed basis for differential-conductance readout-weight representation in a software-executed classification workflow, achieving a held-out Fashion-MNIST accuracy of 93.9%. Therefore, this work establishes a molecular-to-material transduction framework that converts neurotrophic regulation into programmable ion-electronic states and links biomolecular recognition, adaptive material dynamics, addiction-related neuroplasticity, and proof-of-concept neuromorphic information processing.

10.1002/adfm.79396.title: Acoustic Levitation Engineered Au-InSe Schottky Junctions for Single-Molecule SERS Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79396.abstract: ABSTRACT Detecting single molecules with high sensitivity and specificity is of great scientific and practical interest. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is an ultrasensitive molecular detection technique for single-molecule detection. However, the fabrication of ultrasensitive single-molecule SERS substrates remains a key goal. Herein, we report an acoustic levitation assisted containerless strategy to construct InSe-Au Schottky junctions with robust interfacial bonding, achieving single-molecule detection of zeptomolar level and an EF of 10 10 . The controllable acoustic radiation pressure inside the levitated droplet induced robust interfacial coupling of InSe-Au Schottky junctions, which was verified by HAADF-STEM etc. The bianalyte Poisson-binomial statistical model confirmed single molecule origin of Raman signals. Linear relationship between detection probability and ultralow Rhodamine B (RhB) concentration was established. Single molecule SERS mapping directly visualized molecular adsorption sites, identifying strongly bonded junction interface as critical signal enhancement region. The enhancement mechanism is primarily attributed to chemical enhancement, wherein the built-in electric field facilitates multiple photoinduced charge-transfer pathways, while the localized surface plasmon resonance of Au couples with out-of-plane dipole of InSe to enhance light harvesting. This strategy is material-generalizable, as demonstrated by WSe 2 /GaSe-Au systems with attomolar limits. This work provides new insights into engineering strongly bonded heterojunctions for single-molecule sensing devices.

10.1002/adfm.79416.title: Water-Resistant Tin Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots in Transparent Glass Matrix
10.1002/adfm.79416.abstract: ABSTRACT Tin (Sn)-based halide perovskites are regarded as environmentally friendly alternatives to toxic Pb-based counterparts, but their practical use is severely limited by the facile oxidation of Sn 2+ to Sn 4+ , which leads to lattice distortion, phase instability, and structural degradation. Herein, we demonstrate a glass-stabilization strategy for Sn-based perovskite quantum dots (QDs) by overcoming the oxidation issue of Sn 2+ through a nanoporous-template-assisted spatial-chemical confinement strategy. Vacuum chemical vapor deposition enables the in situ formation of CsSnBr 3 QDs within the nanoscale pores of a silicate glass template, while subsequent densification seals the pores and provides physical isolation from the external environment, yielding dense and environmentally stable lead-free perovskite QD glass. Moreover, the CsSnBr 3 QD glass exhibits excellent long-term environmental stability, retaining about 70% and 75% of its initial photoluminescence intensity after 120 days in water and air, respectively. This work provides a robust and facile route to overcome the intrinsic instability of Sn-based halide perovskites, opening a new pathway toward durable lead-free optoelectronic materials.about

10.1002/adfm.79423.title: Hydration-Induced Environmentally-Adaptive Thermal Management with Microphase Separated Hydrogel
10.1002/adfm.79423.abstract: ABSTRACT The heat stress associated with extreme weather has paved the way for the rapid development of passive cooling techniques, but they are unable to tolerate fluctuating thermal and hydric environments, and their cooling power is more than halved under harsh conditions. Reliable multimodal thermal management techniques to couple with dynamic weather conditions are highly sought-after. Herein, we develop a phase-separated hydrogel via water-induced microphase separation of waterborne polyurethane with the assistance of a hygroscopic layered network for hierarchical structure engineering. The obtained hydrogel undergoes hydration-induced structural evolution from a compact solid monolith to a layered porous architecture, delivering a solar modulation capacity of ∼0.8 together with a high mid-infrared emissivity of ∼0.95. Such optical features enable the hydrogel to achieve dynamic thermal regulation with a 9°C temperature span and sub-ambient radiative cooling (∼6°C) under direct solar radiation. Additionally, via in situ incorporation of a light absorber or hygroscopic agent, the hydrogel is endowed with dual-mode solar heating/cooling functionality and synergistic dehumidification-cooling performance, respectively. Furthermore, the manufacturing process for the as-proposed hydrogel is green, sustainable, and scalable, which permits industrial-size hydrogels with combinations of stability, durability, sustainability, and processability. This work provides a promising candidate to meet the need for integrated thermoregulatory systems for environment-specific adaptation.

10.1002/adfm.78483.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Soft Sensors: From Material Design to Motion Recognition
10.1002/adfm.78483.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of soft electronics provides reliable performance under deformation, excellent adaptability to irregular surfaces, and superior comfort for wear. Their deployments offer solutions to address the challenges of harsh signal acquisition conditions, poor wearing experience, insufficient continuous tracking, and low accuracy in traditional motion recognition. Recently, extensive research has been conducted on enhancing materials, structures, and multimodal sensor systems or networks for information extraction. However, motions typically produce large streams of data that require labor-intensive processing steps to extract and interpret. The rising artificial intelligence has demonstrated high efficiency and accuracy in processing multi-dimensional data. Using machine learning (ML) algorithms to analyze data from wearable sensors has shown significant progress, enabling smart and intelligent sensing applications. This review examines the working mechanisms, materials, and structures of soft sensors for motion recognition and discusses how their physical design shapes signal quality and algorithm selection. The applications of soft sensors aided by ML algorithms in various motion recognition tasks are reviewed, including smart healthcare monitoring, intelligent soft robotics, and human-machine interaction. Finally, the review discusses the challenges and future development of ML-assisted soft sensors, focusing on how long-term reliability, system integration, material and structural design can be improved by ML strategies.

10.1002/adfm.78553.title: Tailoring Spin-Polarized Ferrimagnetic Domains in CeCu-Fe3O4 Breaks the Adsorption-Activation Dilemma in Biomass Valorization
10.1002/adfm.78553.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to high-value chemicals such as 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) remains highly challenging because of the difficulty in simultaneously optimizing HMF adsorption and lowering the activation barrier for the rate-determining aldehyde-to-carboxylate conversion. Herein, we exhibit a spin-engineered Ce and Cu co-doped inverse spinel iron oxide (CeCu-Fe 3 O 4 ) featuring regulated electronic structure, abundant oxygen vacancies, and tunable ferrimagnetic spin polarization. The catalyst achieves 97.6% HMF conversion, 98.3% FDCA selectivity, and 98.2% Faradaic efficiency with sustained 100 h stability in the HMF electro-oxidation process, outperforming most reported non-noble-metal electrocatalysts. Through systematic experimental characterization and theoretical calculations, we reveal that Ce/Cu co-doping induces a coordinated reconstruction of the electronic and magnetic landscape in Fe 3 O 4 , manifested by enhanced spin-dependent electronic polarization and the formation of oxygen-vacancy-associated unpaired electron centers that strongly couple with Fe d orbitals. This coupled electronic and magnetic reconstruction modulates the interfacial interaction between the catalyst surface and HMF molecules, thereby regulating adsorption behavior and facilitating subsequent charge-transfer processes. This work highlights that tailoring spin-polarized magnetic domains through Ce/Cu co-doping effectively overcomes the adsorption-activation bottleneck in HMF electro-oxidation, providing a targeted strategy for designing state-of-the-art electrocatalysts for biomass valorization.
