10.1002/adfm.78621.title: Machine-Learning-Powered Screening of CuNi@FeO Electrocatalyst for Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion in Industrial Wastewater Concentrate
10.1002/adfm.78621.abstract: ABSTRACT High-pressure reverse osmosis concentrates (HPROC) generated from coal chemical zero-liquid-discharge processes accumulate nitrate in high-salinity matrices that deteriorate downstream salt recovery and nitrogen management. This necessitates selective nitrate conversion before evaporation-crystallization. Electrocatalytic reduction offers a promising route to convert nitrate into ammonia, yet electrocatalyst design remains largely empirical, complicating the development of manufacturable electrodes for practical applications. Herein we developed a literature-informed interpretable machine learning (ML) framework to screen the CuNi@FeO electrocatalyst toward highly selective nitrate-to-ammonia conversion under high-salinity conditions. The self-supporting CuNi@FeO was fabricated by spontaneous deposition on sacrificial iron foam and it could realize spatially and energetically nitrate activation, hydrogen supply, and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) suppression, accounting for a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 98.74% and an ammonia yield of 19.56 mg h −1 cm −2 at −1.0 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). Operando spectroscopy and theoretical calculations revealed a synergistic multisite pathway involving the sequential *NO 3 →*N→*NH x conversion. The membrane-electrode assembly reactor could sustain 200 mA cm −2 for over 100 h and ammonia FE of 91.46% at cell voltage of 2.5 V during treatment of real industrial wastewater concentrate. This work establishes a paradigm shift to ML-powered screening of electrocatalyst toward scalable nitrate valorization from industrial concentrates.

10.1002/adfm.78822.title: Perspectives of Biomaterial-Based Sustainable Integrated Micro- and Nanophotonics
10.1002/adfm.78822.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomolecular photonics is emerging as a pathway toward sustainable alternatives to fully semiconductor-based devices, leveraging the unique optical properties and solution processability of proteins, nucleic acids, and other biogenic molecules. This review covers recent advances in nano- and microscale biophotonic devices, spanning biopolymer waveguides (with optical losses down to 0.24 dB cm −1 ), bio-organic LEDs and lasers (luminous efficiencies up to 130 lm W −1 ; lifetimes >3600 h), biohybrid photovoltaics (PCE up to ∼20%), photodetectors, and optoelectronic memristors. We critically examine interfacial engineering challenges, such as stability, charge separation, and hybrid integration with semiconductor solid-state platforms, as the central bottleneck to be overcome in translating laboratory breakthroughs into consumer-grade photonic integrated circuits. We argue that, while biomaterial-based devices generally trail their inorganic counterparts in efficiency and lifetime, the unique biocompatibility, specificity, and broadband tunability of biogenic molecules provide decisive advantages in well-defined niches: implantable and wearable diagnostics, point-of-care biosensors, and emerging quantum bio-photonic platforms. Moreover, clear evidence indicates that inexpensive, stable, and easy-to-handle biopolymers and composites, available for large-scale production from biomass, can become essential for building, improving, and stabilizing waveguide and photovoltaic structures. By bridging molecular biology and photonic engineering, biomaterials offer a pathway toward scalable, biocompatible, and energy-efficient photonic technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79433.title: Wulff-Guided (002)/(103) Faceted Step-Terrace Microtopography Enables Rapid and Reversible Zn Deposition
10.1002/adfm.79433.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling Zn crystallographic orientation provides an effective pathway to stabilize Zn metal anodes. However, conventional single-textured Zn anodes face an intrinsic trade-off between interfacial stability and deposition kinetics. Herein, we develop an ion co-driven Wulff-guided crystal growth strategy to construct a step-terrace Zn microtopography consisting of (002) terraces and (103) step facets. The Zn 2+ concentration regulates Zn growth kinetics, while preferential adsorption of H + /SO 4 2− selectively modifies facet dependent surface energies to reshape the Wulff construction. The (002)/(103) step-terrace interface exhibits synergistic advantages. The (002) terraces enhance interfacial stability through HER suppression, while the (103) steps and activated (002) terrace edges accelerate Zn nucleation and interfacial kinetics. This ordered step-terrace architecture enables spiral Zn growth, leading to uniform and dendrite free Zn deposition. Consequently, the step-terrace Zn anode maintains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.80% for 2000 h and enables stable Zn plating/stripping for 500 h at 5 mA cm −2 with 50% depth of discharge. Full cells retain 313.0 mAh g −1 after 8000 cycles at 10 A g −1 , corresponding to a decay rate of 0.0022% per cycle. This work establishes a Wulff-guided step-terrace interface paradigm for long-life aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79427.title: Dopant-Enhanced Inhibitory Negative Photoconductance and Hetero-interfacial Switchable Synaptic Response in CsPbI 3 Perovskite
10.1002/adfm.79427.abstract: ABSTRACT All-inorganic halide perovskites, particularly CsPbI 3 , are excellent candidates for neuromorphic devices owing to their unique defect-tolerant electronic structure and mixed ionic-electronic transport. Here, we demonstrate that the inherent synaptic plasticity of CsPbI 3 can be modulated by cationic doping and heterojunction engineering. By introducing transition metal dopants (Cu, Mn and Zn) into the perovskite lattice, we modify the trap-state density and charge-carrier dynamics. CsPbI 3 naturally exhibits negative photoconductance (NPC) due to its defect-mediated charge dynamics and Mn-doping increases this effect manifold. First-principles calculations reveal that Mn-substitution creates highly localized states within the bandgap, significantly amplifying light-activated charge trapping kinetics. This manifests as a robust negative photoconductance, enhancing biomimetic inhibitory responses with a high paired-pulse depression index of 188%. Also, we show that the polarity of the optical synaptic response is not merely a bulk property but can be inverted via interfacial charge-transfer at the CsPbI 3 /ZnO heterostructure. This transition from inhibitory to excitatory behavior underscores the role of material interfaces in controlling synaptic polarity. These findings establish a materials-based strategy for developing CMOS-compatible, dual-mode neuromorphic architectures on monolithic substrates.

10.1002/adfm.79392.title: Material Coupling in Hybrid Neuromorphic Devices: From Fundamentals to System-Level Applications
10.1002/adfm.79392.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices aim to integrate sensing, memory, and processing by emulating adaptive biological functions. Emerging semiconductor materials, including organic semiconductors, metal oxides, two-dimensional materials, and metal halide perovskites, provide complementary physical properties, but each platform also faces intrinsic limitations in stability, charge transport, optical response, ionic/defect control, or scalable integration. Hybrid materials coupling effectively addresses these challenges by creating heterogeneous interfaces where charge transfer and storage, energy-level alignment, defect modulation, photogating, and ion migration can be deliberately combined. In this review, we discuss recent progress in hybrid neuromorphic devices based on emerging semiconductor materials from a material-interface-device-system perspective. We first outline the material characteristics that enable neuromorphic operation in each platform. Hybrid neuromorphic devices were then classified into intra-family and inter-family hybridization strategies, highlighting how heterointerface design governs charge transport, charge storage, optical response, and ion- or defect-mediated dynamics, thereby shaping synaptic plasticity and learning while enabling adaptive sensing, optoelectronic memory, and in-sensor computing. We also discuss remaining challenges in process compatibility, interface stability and reproducibility, coupled interfacial mechanism analysis, and array-level reliability.

10.1002/adfm.79212.title: High-Entropy Materials for Gas Sensing in Extreme Environments: Mechanisms, Performance Regulation, and Design Strategies
10.1002/adfm.79212.abstract: ABSTRACT Gas sensors are increasingly required for distributed and unattended applications, where low power consumption, reliable calibration, and environmental robustness are as important as sensitivity. Temperature extremes, high humidity, chemically aggressive atmospheres, and coexisting gases can perturb adsorption/desorption, surface-reaction kinetics, carrier transport, interfacial barriers, and long-term baseline stability. This Review critically assesses high-entropy materials (HEMs) as compositionally tunable platforms for gas sensing under such conditions. Structurally validated high-entropy oxides and alloys, together with emerging high-entropy-derived or compositionally complex MXene-, MOF-, carbonaceous, and non-oxide systems, provide diverse design spaces for regulating local coordination, defect chemistry, active sites, and interfacial electronic structure. An application-oriented framework is established to link HEM design with gas-sensing mechanisms, evidence-based evaluation, and extreme-environment operation. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing high-entropy-design-related contributions from conventional multicomponent, element-specific, defect-mediated, and interfacial effects. Performance and reliability are considered across high-temperature, high-humidity/marine, low-temperature/cold-chain, and corrosive/poisoning environments, with material stability and sensing-signal stability evaluated separately. Environment-specific criteria are discussed for thermal and humidity cycling, mixed-gas interference, recovery completeness, long-term drift, and multi-stressor operation. Overall, this Review advances mission-oriented strategies for reliable and environment-tolerant high-entropy gas sensors.

10.1002/adfm.78915.title: Ag-Se Synergistic Diffusion for Highly Homogeneous Elemental Distribution and Significantly Improved ACZTSSe Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78915.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of Cu 2 ZnSn(S x Se 1−x ) 4 (CZTSSe) solar cells is primarily limited by an inability to control the selenization process, where non-uniform selenium distribution leads to profound Cu-Zn cation disorder and associated performance losses. Compositional engineering, such as in (Ag x Cu 1−x ) 2 ZnSn(S x Se 1−x ) 4 (ACZTSSe), can mitigate some defects; however, it fails to address the root cause: mastering the reaction kinetics to achieve elemental homogeneity. Herein, we introduce a self-sacrificing Ag 2 Se layer on Mo substrates that enables a bottom-up, cooperative Ag-Se diffusion pathway during grain growth. The rapid migration of Ag atoms modifies the local chemical environment, thereby acting as a kinetic driver that dramatically enhances the selenium diffusion flux. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm a 28.6% increase in the selenium diffusion coefficient ( D Se ), demonstrating that this kinetic enhancement activates the cooperative Ag-Se diffusion mechanism, thereby achieving a macroscopic improvement in material homogeneity. The resultant absorber exhibits an unprecedented, near-linear elemental distribution, which effectively suppresses Cu-related antisite defects (e.g., Cu Zn and Cu Sn ). This superior homogeneity minimizes bulk recombination and facilitates efficient carrier transport, thereby providing a fundamental basis for the enhancement of photoelectric properties. Consequently, the champion device treated with 65 nm Ag 2 Se (ASe 65) achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.36% (certified as 13.91%), primarily due to a remarkable enhancement in short-circuit current density ( J sc ) and fill factor (FF). This work not only provides a foundational understanding of cooperative diffusion chemistry, but also establishes a novel paradigm for manipulating reaction kinetics in solid-state energy materials.

10.1002/adfm.79177.title: Cross-Component Coupling in Rechargeable Zinc-Air Batteries: From Reaction Competition to Device Reversibility
10.1002/adfm.79177.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of renewable energy and electrified systems is increasing the demand for safe, low-cost, and resource-sustainable energy storage. Rechargeable zinc-air batteries are promising because they combine abundant Zn, aqueous electrolytes, and an air-fed oxygen electrode, yet their long-term reversibility is constrained by coupled oxygen reactions, Zn chemistry, species transport, interfacial evolution, and finite material inventories. This review develops an operating-state-resolved framework linking reaction-pathway competition during discharge, charge, and rest with shared-electrolyte transport, electrode reversibility, cross-component coupling, inventory retention, and device reversibility. An evidence hierarchy distinguishes direct operando or component-resolved observations from correlation, mechanistic inference, and cross-system analogy, while practical evaluation is considered under explicit load, Zn utilization, electrolyte inventory, gas environment, cumulative output, maintenance, and failure boundaries. These elements are further integrated into reaction-selectivity-oriented cross-component co-design. The resulting framework specifies the evidence needed to attribute failure, compares cycling claims within declared load and inventory boundaries, and identifies conditions under which air-electrode, electrolyte, and Zn-interface modifications can remain compatible.

10.1002/adfm.79461.title: Formulating the Dual-Function Separator-Enabled Homogenizing Ion Flux in Nonflammable Phosphate toward High Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79461.abstract: ABSTRACT The high-energy lithium metal battery employing a nonflammable phosphate electrolyte is an attractive strategy to resolve the notorious safety trouble. Unfortunately, the sluggish ion dissociation and transport kinetics, strong interaction of Li + -phosphates, and uncontrollable secondary reaction between the electrode and electrolyte interfaces severely impedes the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries. Herein, the dual-function separators with fast ion dissociation and transport capability are designed to enable the homogeneous and efficient ion flux in nonflammable phosphate electrolyte. By virtue of the regulating effect of the designed dual-function separator, the homogeneous distribution of the ion field and electric field are constructed, thus reducing the concentration polarization among nonflammable phosphate electrolyte and weakening the parasitic reaction of the metallic lithium anode and nickel-rich cathode with the electrolyte. The Li||Li symmetrical cells exhibit remarkable cycling stability of above 1000 h at 2 mA cm −2 . Moreover, the Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) battery exhibits above 90% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 1C. Furthermore, stable bidirectional electrode-electrolyte interfaces are also realized after cycling. This approach holds great promise for regulating the ion flux in nonflammable electrolyte, and would encourage more separator engineering design to optimize ionic transport behavior.

10.1002/adfm.79469.title: Bioinspired Compartmentalized Sponge Integrating Active Biological Filtration and Redox Intervention for Hemostasis and Diabetic Wound Regeneration
10.1002/adfm.79469.abstract: ABSTRACT Effective management of severe hemorrhages and chronic diabetic wounds requires navigating a contradictory fluidic challenge: efficiently clearing hazardous exudates and pathogens without depleting critical regenerative factors. Conventional dressings rely on non-selective bulk absorption, inadvertently drawing away essential cellular components along with waste fluids. Herein, we report a compartmentalized sponge that resolves this dilemma through a structurally and electrochemically programmable biological filtration strategy. By embedding a selective membrane between an outward-facing random-pore layer and a tissue-facing aligned-pore layer, the architecture drives directional outward translocation of plasma and micro-scale pathogens. Concurrently, it physically traps vital regenerative components, like red blood cells and platelets, thereby accelerating localized coagulation at the tissue interface. To actively address microbial threats, Nb 2 C/CeO 2 (NbCe) heterojunctions are integrated into the matrix. The NbCe energy band structure matches the biological redox potential (BRP) of bacterial respiratory chains, triggering spontaneous interfacial electron efflux that effectively disrupts the microbial electron transport chain (ETC). Synergizing precise physical size-exclusion with targeted thermodynamic biocatalysis, this sponge reduces hemostasis time and blood loss by ∼80% versus commercial Celox, achieving a 95.1% wound closure rate by day 15. This active-separation platform offers a programmable biomaterials strategy for full-process tissue repair.

10.1002/adfm.79445.title: Liquid Metal Spheres Achieving Stable Residual SEI for Dendrite-Free Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79445.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium dendrite growth represents the primary factor hindering the commercialization of high-energy-density lithium metal batteries, as it gives rise to safety hazards and low Coulombic efficiency. Surface morphology of deposited lithium is particularly affected by solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and current collectors. Herein, we propose a current collector coated by spherical GaIn liquid metal nanoparticles encapsulated in a carbon layer (GaIn@C), which are spontaneously formed by the physical properties of liquid metal. This three-dimensional spherical GaIn@C layer shows remarkable structure stability and avoids the tip effect during deposition of lithium, thus maintaining a stable residual SEI (rSEI) and dendrite-free morphology over the repeated plating/stripping processes. The dendrite-free lithium deposition behavior on GaIn@C layer was revealed via multiphysics simulation, ex-situ deposition observation, in situ optical experiments, and in situ impedance analysis. Uniform deposition process of lithium half-cell achieves a cycle life of up to 3500 h at an areal deposition capacity of 5 mAh cm −2 . Anode-free full cell maintains specific capacity of 172.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles at 1C, with capacity retention of 99.9% and energy density of pouch battery exceed 410 Wh kg −1 . This study presents a general synthetic strategy for the construction of a current collector with stable residual SEI in dendrite-free lithium metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79466.title: Solvent Toughened Glass Gel Electrolyte for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79466.abstract: ABSTRACT In situ polymerization electrolytes hold great promise for high-energy-density lithium-metal batteries but often require additional separators due to their limited mechanical strength. Here, inspired by “glassy gels”, we developed a free-standing glass gel electrolyte by introducing tributylmethylphosphonium dimethyl phosphate ([P 4441 ] [DMP]) into a poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) matrix. Strong non-covalent interactions between [P 4441 ] [DMP] and PAA chains generate a tough and homogeneous network while enabling efficient ion transport. The resulting glass gel electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.59, a tensile strength of 30 MPa, and an elongation of up to 700%. The solvent-toughened scaffold effectively confines the liquid electrolyte and mitigates parasitic reactions with Li metal. Consequently, Li||Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling for 1900 h at 3 mA cm −2 with an areal capacity of 3 mAh cm −2 . Li//NCM811 cells retain 90% of their capacity after 420 cycles, while Li//LiCoO 2 cells exhibit stable cycling for over 290 cycles at 1 C with a cutoff voltage of 4.6 V. This work provides a robust strategy for designing free-standing electrolytes for high-energy-density lithium-metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79431.title: A Thermodynamic-Decoupling-Empowered Defect Engineering Guide: Uncovering the Substantial Yet Overlooked Stress Role in Electrode Potential Regulation
10.1002/adfm.79431.abstract: ABSTRACT Defect chemistry for improving electrochemical potential and structural stability traditionally relies on chemical bonding and charge compensation. However, it reaches a bottleneck when the beneficial defect concentration saturates under the formation-energy constraint, because defect-induced lattice stress generally dissipates through volume expansion, obscuring its electrochemical contribution. Herein, we establish a defect-engineering guide that thermodynamically decouples formation energy to extract an unprecedented stress dimension alongside traditional defect concentrations. Crucially, we develop a stepwise process driven by quantitative ligand-field and stress descriptors to simultaneously screen both dimensions to their limits. We elucidate how universally expansive electrodes like silicon can maintain structural stability while suppressing passive stress release to mitigate expansion. Furthermore, targeting the extreme archetype of non-expansive Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 electrodes, we uncover how confined stress can be transformed into a thermodynamic gain to lower their potentials. Among the 612 dual-doping configurations, the optimal La-Zr doping maximizes both the defect concentration and the strain energy, reducing the lithiation potential from 1.55 to 1.00 V (vs. Li/Li + ) while preserving intrinsic the zero-strain characteristic. This work proposes a defect-engineering guide rooted in a four-quadrant panorama of thermodynamically decoupled concentration and stress dimensions, breaking optimization bottlenecks by harnessing stress upon formation-energy-constrained defect saturation to expand the boundaries of defect chemistry.

10.1002/adfm.79435.title: Bottom-Stack Shear Transfer in Thin-Film Flexoelectric Measurements
10.1002/adfm.79435.abstract: ABSTRACT Bending-based measurements are widely used to probe flexoelectricity in ferroelectric thin films, but the measured response is often shaped by mechanical boundary conditions beyond the intrinsic flexoelectric coefficient. Here we show that the conducting bottom stack acts as a hidden electromechanical boundary condition in mica-supported BaTiO 3 (BTO) capacitors. Dynamic bending measurements reveal opposite bottom-layer-thickness dependences for two-dimensional and oxide electrodes, while a BTO(001)/LSMO(001)/MoS 2 /mica hybrid exhibits an intermediate response at the same nominal BTO orientation as the MoS 2 -supported films. Interface-resolved first-principles calculations show that the hybrid retains a stiff BTO/LSMO contact above substantially more compliant LSMO/MoS 2 and MoS 2 /mica junctions. A reduced shear-transfer model combines the local interface stiffnesses into an effective interfacial-path stiffness, and finite-element simulations confirm progressive suppression of interfacial slip with increasing tangential stiffness. These results identify the complete bottom-stack shear-transfer pathway as a mechanical control of bending-induced polarization and piezoelectric admixture in ferroelectric thin-film flexoelectric measurements.

10.1002/adfm.78634.title: Support-Mediated Electronic Modulation of Ru Sites with Interfacial Water Network Reconstruction Toward High-Efficiency Water Electrolysis
10.1002/adfm.78634.abstract: ABSTRACT Rational regulation of the electronic environment of active sites is an effective strategy for improving water electrolysis kinetics. Herein, we report a P-modified Ru-doped NiMoO 4 nanoarray (Ru/P-NMO) as a highly efficient bifunctional catalyst for overall water splitting. Experimental analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that phosphorus incorporation drives electron redistribution around Ru and tunes its d-band center, thereby optimizing the adsorption energy of H 2 O and HER/OER intermediates. In situ Raman spectroscopy further shows a reorganization of the interfacial hydrogen-bond network toward weakly hydrogen-bonded water configurations, favoring interfacial water activation. As a result, Ru/P-NMO exhibits outstanding HER and OER activities, requiring overpotentials of 11 and 231 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 , respectively. In a two-electrode system, Ru/P-NMO delivers 10 mA cm −2 at a cell voltage of 1.51 V and maintains long-term durability for 2000 h at 400 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the Ru/P-NMO-based AEMWE achieves 1.0 and 2.0 A cm −2 at only 1.813 and 2.076 V, respectively, and exhibits stable operation at ampere-level current density. This work provides a viable strategy for designing Ru-based electrocatalysts toward energy-efficient hydrogen production.
authors: Huyen Thi Dao, Saleem Sidra, Quoc Hao Nguyen, Trieu Vu Tran, Sang-Kyung Kim, Do Hwan Kim, Jinsoo Kim

10.1002/adfm.78420.title: Electrical-Programming-Free Neural Crossbars Enabled by Photochemical Weight Patterning
10.1002/adfm.78420.abstract: ABSTRACT Hardware neural networks based on crossbar architectures require reliable implementation of multilevel synaptic weights, yet conventional electrical programming often suffers from programming interference, device variability, and write-verify overhead. Here, we present electrical-programming-free neural crossbars enabled by photochemical weight patterning using photoresponsive PEDOT:PSS devices. Ultraviolet/ozone (UVO) and ultraviolet-only (UV) irradiation provide fully optical bidirectional conductance modulation, allowing programming and erasing of synaptic weights without electrical assistance. The flexible crossbar array exhibits eight well-resolved conductance states with low device-to-device variation (4.7%), stable retention, repeatable programming/erasing endurance, and mechanical robustness over 2000 bending cycles. Through mask-assisted parallel photochemical weight patterning, trained weights are directly transferred into a 25 × 4 flexible hardware neural network for fingerprint identification, achieving a hardware accuracy of 86.67%, comparable to the software model accuracy of 89.0%. The platform further supports optical reset and reprogramming for reconfigurable user registration while enabling complete removal of the PEDOT:PSS active layer through water dissolution for substrate recovery. These results establish photochemical weight patterning as a scalable strategy for electrical-programming-free, flexible, and reconfigurable neuromorphic hardware.

10.1002/adfm.79408.title: Emerging Heterojunction Memristors: Structural Design, Switching Mechanisms, and Advanced Computing Applications
10.1002/adfm.79408.abstract: ABSTRACT The relentless demand for data-intensive computing has exposed the fundamental bottlenecks of the conventional von Neumann architecture, driving the search for alternative processing paradigms. Memristors have emerged as compelling building blocks for next-generation in-memory and neuromorphic computing. Within this domain, heterojunction-based memristors stand out as highly promising candidates, leveraging interfacial engineering to deliver exceptional device performance and multifunctional capabilities. This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of recent advancements in heterojunction memristors. We systematically examine the material systems, structural classifications, and fabrication strategies that underpin these devices, followed by an in-depth analysis of their underlying resistive switching (RS) mechanisms. Furthermore, we highlight their transformative potential across diverse application domains, spanning data storage, artificial synapses, neuromorphic biomimetic sensory perception, and advanced logic circuits. Finally, we address the prevailing technical challenges and propose viable strategies, offering a strategic roadmap for the rational design of high-performance heterojunction memristors to power the future of neuromorphic hardware.

10.1002/adfm.78999.title: Record Enhancement of Curie Temperature in an Efficient Luminescent Hybrid Metal Halide Ferroelastic
10.1002/adfm.78999.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelastic materials with intrinsically switchable spontaneous strain hold great promise for actuators, shape-memory systems, and energy-harvesting technologies. However, enhancing the Curie temperature ( T c ) and multifunctionality remain long-standing challenges in hybrid ferroelastics, as the former critically governs the operational temperature window while the latter paves the way for novel functionalities. Here, we present an organic-inorganic hybrid ferroelastic (4-FPD) 2 KInCl 6 :Sb (4-FPD = 4-fluoropiperidinium), which showcases remarkable multifunctionality combining a high T c of 417 K with efficient red-light emission. By implementing a fluorination strategy on the parent (piperidinium) 2 KInCl 6 ( T c = 263 K), we achieved a record enhancement of 154 K in T c for hybrid metal halide ferroelastics, far exceeding the reported enhancements induced by the isotope effect and other techniques. Moreover, strikingly, isovalent Sb 3+ doping into the inorganic framework introduces highly efficient radiative recombination centers within the lattice, which boosts the photoluminescence quantum yield of (4-FPD) 2 KInCl 6 from 2.09% to 85.63% without compromising the intrinsic ferroelastic properties. This study offers an effective route for performance optimization and multifunctional design of hybrid ferroelastics.

10.1002/adfm.79420.title: Supramolecular Assembly-Driven Photofluorochromism Enables Time-Encoded Transient Encryption
10.1002/adfm.79420.abstract: ABSTRACT Stimuli-responsive luminescent materials offer dynamic optical outputs for advanced information security, yet achieving programmable fluorescence color evolution in water using a single optical input remains challenging. We developed a water-soluble zwitterionic monomer, 2-(pent-4-en-1-yl)isoquinolin-2-ium-5-sulfonate (IQIS), that exhibits pronounced photofluorochromism under ultraviolet (UV) irradiation. Its fluorescence evolves from blue to green, accompanied by an increase in the overall fluorescence quantum yield from 3.5% to 17.3%. Mechanistic studies reveal that IQIS is weakly pre-associated in water, while UV irradiation promotes the growth, densification, and packing reorganization of these loose molecular clusters. The resulting long-wavelength emission exhibits distinct aggregation-dependent photophysical characteristics and is consistent with an aggregate-associated excited state with enhanced intermolecular charge-transfer character. By programming the kinetics of this supramolecular reorganization in different polymeric architectures, high-resolution grayscale patterns with time-evolving optical outputs can be generated. Under continuous UV irradiation, the same light used for fluorescence readout simultaneously drives the optical evolution, causing initially visible information to progressively fade and ultimately disappear without an additional stimulus. This single-input, self-evolving behavior enables a “Snapchat-like” transient encryption mode and provides a strategy for spatiotemporal information encoding based on kinetically programmed supramolecular photofluorochromism.

10.1002/adfm.79429.title: Disorder Engineering for Continuous Excited-State Tuning in Hybrid Glass Scintillators
10.1002/adfm.79429.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional scintillators rely on crystalline lattices that lock luminescent centers into discrete, fixed configurations, fundamentally restricting the dynamic regulation of emission pathways. Here, we establish a strategy for tuning excited-state behavior in hybrid glass scintillators by harnessing structural disorder as an active design parameter for regulating local Mn coupling environments. Through non-stoichiometric engineering of hybrid organic-inorganic (methyl(triphenyl)phosphonium) 2 MnBr 4 (MTP 2 MnBr 4 ) glasses, continuously distributed Mn-Mn coupling environments are established within a single amorphous phase, spanning from isolated Mn monomers to exchange-coupled pairs. This disorder-mediated coupling landscape reconstructs the excited-state hierarchy and facilitates excited-state energy redistribution, producing continuously tunable luminescence from green to orange-red under both UV and X-ray excitation. The optimized glass achieves a light yield of 43 825 photons MeV −1 and spatial resolution of 13.6 lp mm −1 , rivaling commercial standards. Leveraging the composition-dependent emission contrast, flexible glass-core fibers are fabricated for quantitative ratiometric X-ray dosimetry, with potential for wearable radiation monitoring. This work establishes disorder engineering as a general strategy for reconstructing local excited-state configurations beyond the constraints of crystalline symmetry.

10.1002/adfm.79452.title: Fluorine-Rich Lewis Acidic MOF as Ion Modulator to Enable Dendrite-Free Li Plating for Ah-Level Li-Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79452.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal stands as the most promising anode material to drive the development of next-generation energy storage systems owing to its unparalleled theoretical gravimetric capacity. However, the naturally formed solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is inadequate to suppress the uncontrolled growth of lithium dendrites, posing the safety concerns for lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we propose a F-rich Lewis acid metal-organic framework (F-mof) as an anion captor and a cation accelerator to mitigate the concentration polarization and expedite the lithium ion transport at anode-electrolyte interface. The lithiophilic nature of F-mof with a 3D open framework facilitates the uniform lithium deposition and mitigates the electrode volume change during extended cycling. This strong Lewis acid-modified Li anode enables Li||Li symmetric cells to achieve an extended cycle life of 2000 h at a high capacity of 2 mAh cm −2 . The modified LMBs with LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cathodes demonstrate the prolonged 700 cycles at 1 C. The NCM811-pouch cells with a thick cathode (30 mg cm −2 ) achieve a high energy density of 300 Wh kg −1 based on entire pouch weight. Moreover, this work uses a conversion-type FeF 3 cathode to assemble multilayer pouch cell, achieving a high capacity of 600 mAh for fluoride conversion reaction batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78588.title: Work Function-Guided Tandem Ohmic-PN Heterojunctions on Nanoporous Scaffolds for Industrial Oxygen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.78588.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing robust non-precious electrocatalysts for oxygen evolution reaction is essential for widespread use of alkaline water electrolysis. However, the intrinsic trade-off between structural durability and catalytic activity under harsh industrial conditions remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a synergistic tandem Ohmic-PN heterojunction architecture monolithically integrated on a nanoporous Ni scaffold, enabling work function-guided interfacial electronic-state engineering to break this dilemma. Specifically, the sequential np-Ni/NiS Ohmic contact and NiS/NiFe LDH PN junction establish a dual-interface kinetic modulation. The Ohmic interface facilitates low-resistance charge extraction, while the NiS/NiFe LDH PN junction promotes interfacial charge redistribution, accompanied by changes in the electronic state and local coordination environment of the NiFe LDH layer. The 3D bicontinuous nanoporous framework simultaneously confers a super-hydrophilic and underwater aerophobic surface that promote rapid micro-bubble detachment. As a result, the electrode requires an overpotential of only 343 mV to deliver 1000 mA cm −2 in 1.0 m KOH. Under industrial conditions, the electrolyzer not only sustains for 572 h under 500 mA cm −2 , but also exhibits exceptional resilience against start-stop voltage reversals and dynamic power fluctuations. This work offers a general strategy that bridges atomic-level interfacial engineering with macroscopic mass transport for scalable and sustainable hydrogen production.

10.1002/adfm.79467.title: Ultrasonically Engineered Low-Coordination Mn Sites in Fe-MOF Promote Charge Separation for Sacrificial-Agent-Free Photocatalytic N 2 Reduction
10.1002/adfm.79467.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction involves complex proton-coupled multi-electron transfer processes, which bring about abundant reaction pathways and thus result in poorly controllable product selectivity. Benefiting from their unique electronic configuration and unsaturated coordination environment, single-atom photocatalysts can effectively regulate the reaction pathways of photoreductive N 2 activation and reduction, thereby improving the selectivity and NH 3 productivity of target ammonia products. Herein, an acetate-modified ultrasonication method is developed to construct atomically dispersed, coordinatively unsaturated Mn-N sites on Fe-based metal-organic frameworks (FeMOFs). Distinct from traditional carbon-based single-atom catalysts, these Mn─N sites are fabricated via a mild wet-chemistry approach without high-temperature treatment. The optimized U-FeMnMOF(Fe:Mn = 1:3) achieves a high NH 3 productivity of 1823.1 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 , 21.2 times that of pure FeMOF. Characterizations and DFT results verify that Mn─N sites not only activate N 2 and optimize hydrogen adsorption, but also work as a charge transfer mediator to form a direct Z-scheme heterojunction. This study presents a feasible strategy to synthesize non-carbon M─N single-atom catalysts for efficient PNRR.

10.1002/adfm.79421.title: Laminar Boundary Layer Mass Transport-Guided Machine Learning for Precision Density Regulation of Horizontal Carbon Nanotube Arrays
10.1002/adfm.79421.abstract: ABSTRACT Horizontally aligned carbon nanotube (HACNT) arrays are essential building blocks for next-generation carbon electronics. However, precise control over the density of HACNT remains a formidable bottleneck due to the complex, nonlinear coupling of multi-physical parameters. To address this challenge, we propose a machine learning (ML) workflow that incorporates boundary layer fluid dynamics (BLFD). Conventional high-dimensional growth parameters are condensed into a concise feature space dominated by two physics-informed descriptors: mass transfer coefficient ( K m ) and residence time ( t ). This kinetics-informed feature set significantly improves HACNT density prediction, increasing the coefficient of determination (R²) from 0.68 to 0.84. Consequently, 4200 virtual screenings map a global kinetic phase diagram, revealing an extremely narrow growth window for high-density HACNT that demands sufficient yet moderate carbon precursor supply combined with appropriate t . Subsequent validation experiments confirm the reliability of BLFD-informed ML model in HACNT density prediction and identifies the failure mechanisms, and demonstrates the capability to guide targeted growth of array with 120 tubes/µm. By uncovering the underlying kinetic mechanisms rather than merely fitting data, this BLFD-ML fusion framework would contribute to the HACNT synthetic paradigm shifting from empirical trial-and-error to a rational design process governed by fluid dynamics and reaction kinetics.

10.1002/adfm.79443.title: Supramolecularly Anchored Skeleton-Intrinsic Phase-Change Monoliths Enabling Passive Thermal Homeostasis of Outdoor Electronics
10.1002/adfm.79443.abstract: ABSTRACT Mitigating extreme temperature fluctuations is critical for maintaining data integrity and preventing failure in outdoor electronics. However, durable passive thermal homeostasis for such electronics under fluctuating outdoor conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a skeleton-intrinsic phase-change monolith (SPCM) fabricated through supramolecular anchoring. A noncovalent supramolecular network robustly confines molten phase-change domains within a load-bearing skeleton, combining a high latent-heat capacity of 125 J g −1 with an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.027 W m −1 K −1 . The monolith retains 99% of its mass after 100 thermal cycles and remains leak-free under 50% compressive strain. By integrating thermal insulation, latent-heat buffering, and radiative heat dissipation, SPCM protects electronic devices against external thermal shocks. An SPCM-packaged electronic device exhibits a temperature variation of less than 1.5°C when exposed to a 120°C heat source, compared with approximately 25°C for an unprotected device. The monolith also largely retains its phase-change behavior, thermal insulation performance, and spectral selectivity after thermal cycling and environmental exposure, demonstrating stability under the tested harsh conditions. This work establishes a supramolecular skeleton-engineering strategy for passive thermal management of electronics in fluctuating outdoor environments.

10.1002/adfm.79397.title: Biomimetic Hybrid-Membrane Nanoreactor for Deep-Seated Photodynamic Immunotherapy of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via Dual Catalysis-Enhanced ROS Amplification and cGAS-STING Activation
10.1002/adfm.79397.abstract: ABSTRACT Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is promising against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its efficacy against deep-seated HCC is severely restricted by limited light penetration, intratumoral hypoxia, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity. Here, we developed a highly integrated biomimetic self-oxygenating nanoreactor UCNP@MnO x -Hyp@HRM (denoted UMHM). Coated with a Hepa1-6 tumor cell/red blood cell fused hybrid membrane, UMHM achieves homologous tumor targeting and immune evasion, ensuring effective nanoparticle accumulation in deep-seated tumors. The manganese oxide shell catalyzes H 2 O 2 decomposition for in situ oxygen generation to mitigate hypoxia and improve upconversion nanoparticle-mediated PDT outcomes, while PDT/CDT synergistically amplifies oxidative stress and induces immunogenic cell death (ICD). Crucially, cytoplasmic double-stranded DNA released by ICD acts synergistically with Mn 2 + to activate the cGAS-STING pathway. In concert with ICD, this signaling pathway facilitates dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte recruitment, as well as remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In vivo, UMHM achieved an 86.4% tumor growth inhibition rate in a large-volume subcutaneous HCC model and effectively suppressed tumor progression in an orthotopic HCC model. Furthermore, UMHM induced a marked abscopal effect, inhibiting the growth of distant tumors and lung metastases. This study provides a novel and multifunctional synergistic strategy for photodynamic immunotherapy of deep-seated solid tumors.

10.1002/adfm.79407.title: Dichloro-Functionalized Urea Additive for Crystal Regulation in Stable Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adfm.79407.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing passivators that deliver multi-mechanistic synergistic effects constitutes a highly efficacious strategy for crystallization regulation, while simultaneously serving as a critical approach to bolster the long-term operational stability of perovskite solar cells. In this work, a series of amine-derived functional additives was rationally engineered and systematically evaluated via molecular design strategy to precisely regulate both the substitution pattern and the chlorine atoms count. Notably, the dichloro-substituted derivative 1-(3,4-dichlorophenyl)-3-(pyridin-4-yl)urea (DCLPU) demonstrates exceptional coordination passivation capability, an effect predominantly ascribed to the significantly enhanced electronegativity of its carbonyl group. This modification markedly reduces the perovskite crystallization rate and directs the preferential orientation of the perovskite (100) crystal facet. Furthermore, DCLPU suppresses non-radiative recombination losses and weakens electron-phonon coupling via energy level modulation. Consequently, the inverted device incorporating DCLPU attained a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.32% (certified: 26.91%), alongside a corresponding module efficiency of 22.50%. These devices further exhibited outstanding thermal stability, ultraviolet resistance, and sustained operational durability. This work delineates a robust and practicable paradigm for advancing high-efficiency, stable perovskite photovoltaic technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79373.title: Manganese Nanoparticles Coupled with Adjacent Single-Atom Nanozymes for Concerted Synergistic Amplification of the cGAS-STING Pathway and Glioblastoma Immunotherapy
10.1002/adfm.79373.abstract: ABSTRACT Glioblastoma is a highly aggressive brain tumor whose profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) compromises the efficacy of conventional therapies and immunotherapy, while insufficient activation and inefficient agonist delivery limit antitumor potential of the cGAS-STING pathway. Herein, we design a manganese nanoparticle/adjacent single-atom nanozyme loaded with potent STING agonist diABZI, which is further camouflaged with homologous glioma cell membranes (Mn AC/SA -D@M) to enable efficient blood-brain barrier penetration and precise GBM targeting. The electronic coupling between Mn 10 ACs and neighboring Mn single-atom sites optimizes the d-electron density and charge distribution of Mn-N 4 catalytic centers, thereby drastically enhancing peroxidase-like activity and facilitating tumor-specific hydroxyl radical generation and glutathione depletion. Such robust catalytic oxidative stress triggers ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, accompanied by mitochondrial damage and subsequent cytoplasmic release of mitochondrial DNA, which potently activates the cGAS-STING pathway. Meanwhile, released manganese ions (Mn 2+ ) and co-delivered diABZI sustain and amplify STING signaling, boosting the secretion of type I interferons and proinflammatory cytokines. This integrated cascade promotes dendritic cell maturation, repolarizes tumor-associated macrophages to antitumor M1 phenotype, and augments cytotoxic T-cell infiltration. Consequently, the immunosuppressive TME of glioblastoma is reversed, leading to enhanced antitumor immunotherapy in orthotopic tumor models, patient-derived organoids, and postoperative tumor recurrence settings.

10.1002/adfm.79459.title: A Water-Repellent-Zincophilic Molecular Strategy for Concurrent Solvation and Interfacial Regulation toward Highly Reversible Zinc Anodes
10.1002/adfm.79459.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are promising for grid-scale energy storage but suffer from severe anode issues, including dendrite growth and water-induced side reactions. Herein, an organic molecule, N,N,N’,N’-Tetrakis(2-hydroxyethyl)adipamide (THEA), is used to implement a “water-repellent-zincophilic” strategy for synergistically regulating both the electrolyte and the electrode interface. Its flexible hydrophobic backbone and multiple zincophilic hydroxyl groups enable multi-site functionality. In the electrolyte, THEA coordinates with Zn 2+ to reconstruct the primary solvation sheath, displacing water, and reducing its activity. At the anode interface, it chemically adsorbs to form an organic interfacial layer. This layer effectively repels water to mitigate parasitic reactions while guiding Zn 2+ flux toward the dense (002) plane deposition. Consequently, cells employing THEA achieve exceptional stability: Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 5550 h (0.5 mA cm −2 , 0.5 mAh cm −2 ); Zn||β-MnO 2 cells retain 81.3% capacity after 1000 cycles (1 A g −1 ) and 60.5% capacity after 3000 cycles at 2 A g −1 . Furthermore, THEA effectively suppresses ice crystallization at subzero temperatures, enabling stable Zn anode operation at −8°C. This work integrates solvation control with interfacial engineering, offering an effective pathway toward durable, high-performance aqueous zinc batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79458.title: Bioinspired Homologous Gradient Interphase Sustains Phase-Change Buffering and Radiative Cooling Under Thermal Shocks
10.1002/adfm.79458.abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling phase-change buffering with passive radiative cooling offers complementary continuous and transient regulation for personal thermal management (PTM). In fibrous systems, however, repeated phase transitions drive molecular rearrangement and thermomechanical stress accumulation, causing fiber deformation, pore collapse, and irreversible deterioration of radiative cooling performance. Herein, inspired by graded stress transfer in mussel byssus, we develop a homologous gradient interphase strategy to construct a core-gradient interphase-shell fibrous membrane (Ho-GIFM) for durable PTM. During coaxial electrospinning, homologous polyethylene glycol-based polyurethanes interdiffuse and entangle across the interface, while in situ UV crosslinking stabilizes the interphase. This structure redistributes phase-change-induced strain and constrains long-range chain rearrangement, preserving phase-change functionality and porous fiber networks. Ho-GIFM exhibits a broad solid-solid phase-transition window (30.2-51.5°C) with a competitive melting enthalpy (60.2 J g −1 ). Notably, after 100 alternating thermal shocks between −40 and 80°C, Ho-GIFM retains 99.0% of its initial solar reflectance versus only 74.5% for the heterogeneous counterpart, together with 99.9% mid-infrared emissivity retention. Furthermore, it delivers a calculated daytime net radiative cooling power of 101.9 W m −2 and achieves an average synthetic-skin temperature reduction of 14.9°C. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for durable PTM and multicomponent functional fibers.

10.1002/adfm.78308.title: Mechanism-Guided Inverse Electrolyte Design for Advanced Metal-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78308.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of new electrolytes for metal-ion batteries is currently constrained by the inefficiency of trial-and-error exploration across vast chemical spaces. Here, we establish a comprehensive framework for chemical descriptor-based inverse electrolyte design that maps target electrolyte properties back to molecular, polymeric, and lattice-level building blocks. By extracting fundamental chemical descriptors, we decompose electrolyte performance into electrochemical stability, ionic transport, electronic leakage, thermal safety, and lifecycle constraints, challenging classical frontier-orbital (highest occupied molecular orbital/lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) criteria for electrochemical stability by accounting for the electron/hole addition perturbations and the critical role of interfacial effects. Addressing ion transport, we unify optimization strategies across phases, linking solvation structures in liquids and lattice defects in solids to minimize impedance via atomic-level ion transport control. We decouple the origins of electronic leakage, distinguishing between structural-defect-induced pathways and parasitic redox transport. On safety, we trace thermal runaway to molecular thermodynamics. Integrating lifecycle constraints, we analyse how manufacturing defects and abuse conditions compromise these theoretical designs. Furthermore, to address the data-scarcity bottleneck in data-driven discovery, we propose the “Minimum Information for Electrolyte Studies and Cells” (MIESC) checklist and advocate systematic reporting of negative results to establish robust decision boundaries. This work thus provides a roadmap for rationally designing next-generation electrolytes.

10.1002/adfm.79438.title: Synergistic Modulation of Interfacial Energetics and Crystallization Kinetics for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79438.abstract: ABSTRACT The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term stability of polycrystalline perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are fundamentally limited by bulk non-radiative recombination and mismatched interfacial energy levels. To address these bottlenecks, we introduced 4,4’-(2,1,3-benzothiadiazole-4,7-diyl)dibenzoic acid (BTBA) as a twisted molecular additive for regulating crystallization kinetics and interfacial energetics. With dual carboxylic acid groups and a rigid, non-coplanar benzothiadiazole-based backbone, BTBA coordinates with Pb-based precursor during film formation, which retards the crystallization kinetics and yields films with enlarged grains. In addition, residual BTBA at the perovskite surface passivates undercoordinated Pb 2+ defects and regulates the surface work function, which improves the energy-level alignment with C 60 and facilitates charge extraction. The resulting PSCs achieved a champion PCE of 27.16% (certified 27.14%) with a fill factor (FF) of 86.73%. Furthermore, the unencapsulated devices exhibited improved stability, retaining over 90% of their initial PCEs after 1200 h of maximum-power-point tracking (MPPT) under continuous 1-sun illumination and after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C.

10.1002/adfm.79463.title: Molecular Confinement-Driven Programmable Multicolor Metal-AIEgen Frameworks Combined With Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Sensitivity of Lateral Flow Immunoassay
10.1002/adfm.79463.abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent metal-organic framework (MOF)-based sensing platforms have emerged as promising tools for bioanalysis. However, their limited optical outputs and insufficient information encoding capacity remain major challenges in complex matrices detection. Here, we develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-interpretable sensing platform by integrating programmable multicolor aggregation-induced emission metal frameworks (MAFs) with dual-hue lateral flow immunoassay (DH-LFIA) for intelligent detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ). A highly emissive MAF was constructed using an AIE-active ligand (TCPE) and Hf 4+ nodes. Additionally, donor-acceptor interactions between TCPE and incorporated rhodamine B (RhB) enabled programmable multicolor emission through the Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) mechanism. The optimized MAFR-6 probe was subsequently incorporated into the LFIA, achieving a detection limit of 10 CFU/mL for P. aeruginosa . Moreover, an inner filter effect (IFE)-driven DH-LFIA platform was established to convert bacterial concentrations into visible color transitions, providing a highly sensitive with a 100-fold improvement over conventional gold nanoparticles-based lateral flow immunoassay (AuNPs-LFIA). Furthermore, integration with a convolutional neural network (CNN) enabled autonomous interpretation of color-coded signals and achieved 100% classification accuracy for P. aeruginosa in human blood, overcoming the limitations of subjective visual analysis. Collectively, this study provides a new strategy for advancing pathogen detection toward automation, precision, and intelligence.

10.1002/adfm.79340.title: Applications of Atomic Catalyst Platforms in Electrochemical Oxygen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.79340.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is cornerstone reaction used for sustainable energy-related devices. However, its sluggish reaction kinetics, stemming from the complex four-electron transfer mechanism, pose a critical bottleneck, which drives the pursuit of high-efficiency catalytic materials. Atomic catalysts are currently regarded as highly compelling electrocatalytic platforms for tackling this challenge, garnering tremendous research attention originating from their definite active sites, high metal-atom usage, and exceptional selectivity. This review outlines the recent advances of atomic catalysts for OER electrocatalysis. To begin with, the microstructure regulation of atomic catalysts is systematically presented from three aspects: metal centers, support carriers, and metal-support interaction. Furthermore, OER mechanisms are summarized, and the electrocatalytic OER behaviors of atom-dispersed systems, namely single-atom catalysts (SACs), dual-atom catalysts (DACs), multi-atom catalysts (MACs), and atomic array catalysts (AACs), are elaborated. The intrinsic structure-activity correlation is comprehensively analyzed with illustrative examples. Following that, the application potentials of atomic catalysts in OER-relevant electrochemical energy devices exemplified by water electrolyzers and metal-air batteries are discussed. In the final section, the existing bottlenecks and prospective research orientations for atomic catalysts toward OER are proposed.

10.1002/adfm.79403.title: Low-Temperature Construction of Self-Strengthening, Reusable, Ultralight Mullite Fiber Composites with Fish-Scale-Like Adaptive Boron-Rich Layers
10.1002/adfm.79403.abstract: ABSTRACT Reusable thermal protection materials are prone to structural damage accumulation and performance degradation under cyclic thermomechanical loading. Overcoming the conventional “cycling equals damage” paradigm is a critical challenge for long-term service. Here, we exploit low-temperature ceramization of a boron-rich precursor at 600°C to in situ construct a fish-scale-like adaptive ceramic reinforcement layer (ACRL) on mullite fiber surfaces and junctions. The composite exhibits remarkable thermomechanical-cycling-induced strengthening (TMCIS) during cyclic compression at 420°C, with the average modulus nearly tripling after 100 cycles. In situ SEM reveals that thermomechanical coupling drives local displacement of adjacent fiber segments and node reconstruction; the ACRL of viscous softening acts as a dynamic “high-temperature solder” that bridges fiber contacts and reconfigures the load-transfer network, enabling a service-induced strengthening mechanism. After 50 cycles (totaling 25 h) at 420°C, the mass loss per cycle is only 0.07%. Furthermore, the material simultaneously achieves a low density (0.29-0.35 g/cm 3 ), high compressive strength (1.60 MPa), and low thermal conductivity (0.062 W/(m·K)), realizing a synergy of lightweight, load-bearing, and thermal insulation. This work converts cyclic loading from a damage source into a driving force for structural strengthening, establishing a new adaptive paradigm for long-life reusable thermal protection materials.

10.1002/adfm.79262.title: Efficient Magnetization Switching Driven by Orbital Torque in Light 3 d Transition-Metal Nitrides
10.1002/adfm.79262.abstract: ABSTRACT The orbital Hall effect (OHE) in light transition metals offers a promising route to generate orbital torques for efficient magnetization control, providing an alternative to the conventional spin Hall effect approaches that rely on heavy metals. We demonstrate perpendicular magnetization switching in [Co/Pt] multilayers driven by the OHE in a light 3 d transition metal nitride, VN, with a (111)-textured face-centered cubic structure. Second harmonic Hall measurements reveal a large torque efficiency of ~ -0.41 in the VN(7.5 nm)/[Co(0.35 nm)/Pt(0.3 nm)], which significantly surpasses those in the control samples with Co, Py, and CoFeB ferromagnets, suggesting strong conversion of orbital current originating from VN into spin current in the [Co/Pt] ferromagnet. Full switching by an in-plane charge current is achieved in the presence of an in-plane magnetic field, while partial field-free switching occurs without it. The critical current density for switching is found to be comparable to that of a W-based spin-orbit torque device. First-principles calculations predict a large orbital Hall conductivity in VN, with a small spin Hall conductivity around the Fermi energy. Our results highlight the potential of combining light 3 d transition metal nitrides and Co/Pt ferromagnetic multilayers with (111)-texture to maximize the magnetization switching efficiency of orbitronic devices.

10.1002/adfm.79470.title: Rational Design of Non-Centrosymmetric Sn(II)-Based Chalcogenides Exhibiting Superior Infrared Nonlinear Optical Performances
10.1002/adfm.79470.abstract: ABSTRACT Non-centrosymmetric Sn(II)-based chalcogenides hold great promise as infrared (IR) nonlinear optical (NLO) materials; however, their rational design and synthesis remain a substantial challenge due to the facile oxidation of Sn(II) to Sn(IV). Herein, by synergistically assembling Sn(II)/Pb(II) cations with GeS 4 tetrahedra and MX 6 (M═Pb, Sn, Na; X═Cl, Br) octahedral groups, two new Sn(II)-chalcogenide IR NLO crystals, [Sn 0.5 Br 3 ][Sn 3 GeS 4 ] and [Na 0.5 Sn 0.25 Br 3 ][Sn 3 GeS 4 ], were successfully synthesized using a unique quenching-reannealing method. Notably, they achieved 10- and 2-4-fold enhancements in the SHG effect and birefringence, respectively, compared with their isostructural homolog, [Pb 0.5 Cl 3 ][Pb 3 GeS 4 ] (0.6 × AgGaS 2 , ∆n = 0.030). This unusual property disparity originates from the difference in stereochemical activity of lone pair electrons between Sn and Pb cations. Furthermore, owing to the property-modulating effect of strongly electropositive Na + cations, [Na 0.5 Sn 0.25 Br 3 ][Sn 3 GeS 4 ] exhibits a well-balanced set of optical properties, including strong SHG effect (6.4 × AgGaS 2 ), moderate birefringence (0.074), wide optical transparency range (0.47-12.5 µm), indicating it is a potential IR NLO materials. This work opens an avenue for the design of Sn (II)-based IR NLO materials and the synthesis of metastable chalcogenides.

10.1002/adfm.79437.title: In Situ X-Ray Scattering Reveals the Nucleation, Growth, and Self-Assembly of CsBr Nanocrystals in a Heterogeneous Medium
10.1002/adfm.79437.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how nanocrystals form is central to the rational synthesis of nanomaterials, yet the formation mechanisms of ionic nanocrystals remain poorly resolved. Here, we use synchrotron-based in situ small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering to track the formation and assembly of CsBr nanocrystals in solution. We find that the precursors spontaneously organize into dense clusters before reaction, generating a heterogeneous reaction medium that dictates the subsequent formation pathway. Following injection of Cs-oleate, these clusters act as metastable precursor reservoirs that regulate precursor availability, thereby sustaining extended nucleation and promoting effective size focusing. At later stages, the same clusters function as depletants that drive the self-assembly of CsBr nanocrystals into face-centered cubic superlattices. These superlattices then undergo partial disassembly through Ostwald ripening, governed by the interplay between structural ordering and kinetic evolution. Together, our results identify multiple roles of precursor clusters during nanocrystal formation and assembly and provide mechanistic insights into ionic nanocrystal synthesis in heterogeneous media.

10.1002/adfm.79471.title: Domain-Pinned Ferroelectric-Like Fields Drive Deep Zn 2+ Intercalation in Bi 2 TeO 5
10.1002/adfm.79471.abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional MnO 2 - and V 2 O 5 -based frameworks remain among the most widely studied cathode systems for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), yet persistent structural instability and sluggish Zn 2+ transport often result in severe polarization and capacity degradation during cycling. Herein, we report a domain-pinned cathode platform based on Cr-doped oxygen-vacancy Bi 2 TeO 5 (Cr-OvBTO). The synergistic combination of Cr/Ov engineering and the stereochemically active lone-pair electrons of Bi 3+ and Te 4+ reconstructs localized ferroelectric-like fields associated with electrostatic heterogeneity and built-in potential gradients. Consequently, a more stabilized local electrostatic environment is established, thereby enhancing lattice stability during cycling. Contact potential difference mapping and migration-barrier calculations reveal a 77 mV built-in potential gradient and a substantially reduced Zn 2+ migration barrier from 0.75 to 0.34 eV, consistent with improved Zn 2+ transport kinetics. As a result, Cr-OvBTO delivers reversible deep-intercalation behavior (∼360 mA h g −1 ) together with stable high-rate cycling performance, retaining ∼77% capacity over 2000 cycles at 2 A g −1 . More importantly, this work demonstrates that domain-pinned ferroelectric-like fields can transform deep Zn 2+ intercalation from a kinetically constrained process into a reversible and sustainable transport pathway.

10.1002/adfm.79389.title: Functional Siloxane Cross-Linking Nodes in Thermoset Polymer Networks Enhance Mechanical Robustness and High-Temperature Electrical Insulation
10.1002/adfm.79389.abstract: ABSTRACT In next-generation power electronics and electrical systems, thermoset insulating polymers are required to simultaneously provide mechanical support and electrical insulation under extreme electrothermal conditions. However, conventional epoxy resins suffer from an inherent trade-off between mechanical robustness and high-temperature insulation. Herein, a nodal engineering strategy is proposed to construct multifunctional thermoset networks based on cyclic siloxane cross-linking nodes. The siloxane nodes facilitate localized stress relaxation and homogenize the cross-linked network, thereby enabling efficient energy dissipation while maintaining structural integrity and mechanical robustness. Meanwhile, the intensified local network constraints and homogenized chain distribution effectively decouple inter-chain charge transport from thermally activated segmental motion. In addition, the nodal platform is further functionalized via highly efficient hydrosilylation. Fluorinated moieties are grafted onto the siloxane nodes to create localized energetic traps that suppress intra-chain charge transport. Consequently, the resulting network simultaneously improves mechanical robustness and electrical insulation, significantly improving breakdown strength (295.09 kV mm −1 at 120°C, 92.27% increase), tensile strength (75.61 MPa, 29.85% increase), and fracture toughness (2.82 MPa m 1/2 , 57.54% increase). This study provides a new route for constructing high-performance multifunctional polymer networks, showcasing the immense potential of functional siloxane cross-linking nodes for high-reliability insulation in extreme environments.

10.1002/adfm.78652.title: Bio-Inspired Rigid-Flexible Synergistic Nanofibrous Textiles for Mechanically Robust Radiative Cooling
10.1002/adfm.78652.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) textiles offer an efficient pathway for personal thermal management. However, the inherent conflict between optical performance and mechanical robustness remains a formidable challenge. Although elastomer-based electrospun nonwovens serve as a potential solution, they typically necessitate high nano-filler loading for sufficient reflectance, which inevitably weakens interfacial bonding, leading to performance degradation and even structural failure during cyclic deformation. Herein, inspired by spider silk, we propose a filler-free biomimetic rigid-flexible synergy strategy regulated by dynamic hydrogen bonding. Via coaxial electrospinning, a robust TPU@PVDF-HFP film (RTPF) comprising a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) core and a polyvinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene (PVDF-HFP) sheath is engineered. The RTPF demonstrates outstanding mechanical strength (10.17 MPa) and elongation (301.34%), exhibiting superior mechanical and spectral stability with a mere 10.53% residual strain and 1.58% degradation after 1000 cycles at 30% strain. Attributed to high solar reflectance (96.2%) and long-wave infrared emittance (92.5%), the RTPF achieves an average/maximum temperature reduction of 21.3/25.4°C on uncovered heated-pad under 950 W·m − 2 irradiation. Remarkably, it exhibits exceptional stability against rigorous washing and extreme environments (high/low temperatures and acid/alkali conditions). This bioinspired design achieves a synergistic enhancement of optical performance and mechanical robustness, paving the way for long-term wearable cooling materials.

10.1002/adfm.79260.title: Closed-Loop Recycling of Gallium-Based Liquid Metals for Sustainable Soft Electronics
10.1002/adfm.79260.abstract: ABSTRACT Gallium-based room-temperature liquid metals (RTLMs) are widely used in soft electronics, yet their high fluidity and oxide-mediated adhesion can generate persistent residues, complicating recovery and reuse. Here, we establish a Stage-State-guided closed-loop recycling framework for externally accessible Ga-based RTLM residues, in which contamination morphology (Stage) and LM-substrate interfacial condition (State) are independently classified to guide cleaning and recovery. A carbonate-surfactant cleanser (CSC) provides complementary interfacial regulation: the alkaline component promotes oxide-regulated LM retraction, whereas the surfactant enhances interfacial mobility and de-adhesion; strongly oxidized residues are further addressed through a particle-assisted removal mode. The same CSC chemical system and Stage-State decision framework were validated for both EGaIn and Galinstan across representative substrate-interface states without alloy-specific chemical reformulation. A single CSC batch retained comparable functional performance over 20 consecutive reuse cycles, while recovered EGaIn maintained electrical functionality under strains up to 500% and continuous electrical responses over 5000 deformation cycles. A YOLOv11-based vision module provides stage recognition, with true-positive rates of 0.96, 0.97, and 0.83 for Stages I-III, respectively, and practical recognition under variable illumination. Recovered LM was demonstrated in a soft-electronic device, supporting a practical material-level framework for cleaning, recovery, and reuse of externally accessible Ga-based liquid metals.

10.1002/adfm.79418.title: Challenge-Routed Reconfiguration in Multidimensional Black Phosphorus Physical Unclonable Functions for Replay-Resistant Hardware Authentication
10.1002/adfm.79418.abstract: ABSTRACT Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) provide hardware-level authentication by converting uncontrollable physical variations into device-specific challenge-response pairs. However, conventional PUFs often rely on fixed responses, making exposed responses vulnerable to reuse and replay, while expansion of the challenge space may require additional devices or increased readout complexity. Here, roll-printed black phosphorus (BP) is introduced as a self-active multimodal entropy source that intrinsically combines infrared emission, electrical conduction, and strong in-plane anisotropy. Random variations in layered position, thickness, orientation, overlap, and connectivity generate spatial, spectral, orientation, and percolation disorder. Four polarization-resolved photoluminescence (PL) intensities and the PL full width at half maximum (FWHM) form a 125-bit optical authentication response pool, while the electrical PUF provides conductance-rank-based routing rules for challenge-dependent response assembly. Across the optical response channels, the mean inter-Hamming distance (HD) reaches 0.500 for FWHM, the mean intra-HD reaches 0 for PL-YY, the mean bit uniformity reaches 0.500 for PL-XX, and the mean Shannon entropy reaches 0.985 for PL-YX. Challenge-routed responses exhibit a mean inter-challenge Hamming distance of 0.472, which has been unattainable in conventional PUFs with fixed responses. Server-issued electrical challenges generate session-specific response arrangements, enabling replayed responses from previous sessions to be rejected and establishing replay-resistant, multi-session hardware authentication.

10.1002/adfm.79419.title: High-Contrast, Dynamic Visible-Infrared Regulator for Adaptive Multispectral and Multipixelated Camouflage
10.1002/adfm.79419.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic regulation of optical properties in visible (VIS) and infrared (IR) simultaneously is vital for camouflage, energy harvesting, information display, and thermal management. However, current approaches cannot achieve high-contrast, versatile modulation of visible colors and infrared emissivity concurrently, essential for emerging applications like adaptive camouflage in multiple scenarios. To address this challenge, here we develop a novel dynamic VIS-IR regulator based on the reversible metal electrodeposition (RMED) technology, whose reconfigurable nanoscale metallic layer, combined with judiciously designed photonic electrodes, permits real-time, precise control of excitation/annihilation of asymmetric lossy Fabry-Pérot resonances. As a result of this strategy, our regulator shows unprecedented performance, which can not only generate diverse structural colors with a large color gamut (∼33% sRGB area) and high color switching contrast (up to 83%), but also realize broadband, large-contrast IR emissivity modulation of Δ ε 3-14 µm ∼0.68. We further demonstrate a highly-programmable multipixelated device, where each pixel can be controlled independently, enabling spatially adaptive multispectral camouflage and information display for the first time. This work offers a remarkably designable, exactly controllable, and highly scalable platform for multispectral dynamic optical regulation, with wide-ranging applications in adaptive camouflage systems, information encryption and optical skin.

10.1002/adfm.79448.title: Glutamine-Modified Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles Deliver FGF18-mRNA to Alleviate Cartilage Degeneration in Osteoarthritis
10.1002/adfm.79448.abstract: ABSTRACT Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by articular cartilage breakdown, metabolic disorder, and pain. Current therapies provide only symptomatic relief, while cartilage has limited intrinsic repair capacity. Here, we developed glutamine-modified ionizable lipid nanoparticles (GLNP) for intra-articular delivery of FGF18 mRNA. GLNP showed uniform particle size and a favorable polydispersity index, enabling complete RNA encapsulation and protection against degradation. Compared with unmodified lipid nanoparticles (LNP), GLNP achieved efficient lysosomal escape, deep cartilage penetration, and enhanced chondrocyte uptake. In vitro, GLNP-mediated FGF18 mRNA delivery increased anabolic marker expression and reduced catabolic and senescence markers in chondrocytes, while glutamine release further enhanced metabolic synergy. In a surgically induced OA mouse model, intra-articular GLNP-FGF18 improved gait parameters and attenuated cartilage degeneration. It also suppressed synovial inflammation, reduced osteophyte formation, and preserved cartilage matrix integrity in both early and delayed intervention settings. Mechanistically, the therapeutic effect was associated with PRG4 upregulation, PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling modulation, and autophagy restoration. Overall, GLNP-FGF18 mRNA reversed chondrocyte catabolic and senescent phenotypes and restored joint homeostasis by combining cartilage penetration, chondrocyte affinity, and metabolic regulation, offering a promising synergistic gene therapy for OA.

10.1002/adfm.79455.title: Water Rolls Off, Current Flows: The Rise of Conductive Superhydrophobic Textiles
10.1002/adfm.79455.abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive superhydrophobic textiles uniquely combine electrical conductivity with extreme water repellency, enabling humidity-resistant wearable electronics, smart protective clothing, and self-powered systems. This review systematically examines the design principles, fabrication strategies, and multifunctional applications of these materials, with a focus on the core interfacial coupling mechanism-water rolls off, current flows-that governs their performance. Key application domains are critically analyzed, with emphasis on how superhydrophobic protection enhances device stability under humid, sweaty, or rainy conditions. The review identifies fundamental bottlenecks-conductive network failure under deformation, poor durability of hydrophobic interfaces, and inherent trade-offs between conductivity and water repellency-that currently limit practical deployment. A structured translation roadmap from laboratory design to scalable manufacturing is presented, incorporating the development workflow of discovery, design, fabrication, testing, validation, qualification, scaling, deployment, impact, and sustainability. Future directions, including stretchable self-healing architectures, artificial intelligence (AI)-guided inverse design, fluorine-free sustainable manufacturing, and self-powered wireless textile systems, are discussed with technical specificity. This review provides a unified framework connecting materials chemistry, textile engineering, and device physics, guiding researchers and engineers toward transforming these materials from laboratory prototypes to real-world products that enhance human safety, comfort, and connectivity.

10.1002/adfm.79424.title: Programming Film-Formation Kinetics via Photoinduced Acceptor Oligomerization for Efficient and Stable Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79424.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over the solution-to-solid transition is essential for high-performance organic solar cells (OSCs), yet the rapid crystallization of Y-series acceptors severely narrows the morphology-optimization window. Here, we develop a photoresponsive thioctic acid-functionalized acceptor, L8-TA, whose photoinduced pre-oligomerization was systematically optimized to generate Oli-L8-TA prior to film formation. When used as a low-content third component in D18:L8-BO, Oli-L8-TA regulates host crystallization through favorable compatibility with L8-BO and steric confinement from the oligomeric structure, extending the crystallization window from 152 to 273 ms while enhancing molecular ordering. The optimized blend microstructure exhibits a favorable vertical phase distribution, contributing to improved charge transport and reduced recombination. Consequently, ternary devices achieve a PCE of 20.12% with a fill factor (FF) of 81.31%. Device stability is also enhanced, with extrapolated T 80 lifetimes extended from 490 to 905 h under continuous illumination and from 448 to 750 h at 65°C. These results demonstrate that photoinduced pre-oligomerization provides a direct molecular-state handle for programming host crystallization kinetics and optimizing active-layer morphology during the solution-to-solid transition in OSCs.

10.1002/adfm.77791.title: Ultrasmall-Bandgap Tellurium Nanowire-Based Photothermal Superhydrophobic Coating With Biomimetic 3D Thermal Network for Energy-Autonomous Anti-/De-Icing
10.1002/adfm.77791.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient anti-/de-icing coatings are urgently needed for outdoor infrastructures in cold climates. Here, we report a photothermal superhydrophobic coating based on ultrasmall-bandgap tellurium nanowires (TeNWs, E g = 0.43 eV) synthesized via a surfactant-assisted solid-solid-solid growth strategy. The composite, integrating TeNWs with fluorinated diatomite, constructs a continuous three-dimensional thermal conduction network that synergistically enhances light absorption, heat transfer, and water repellency. The optimized coating achieves an exceptional solar-thermal conversion efficiency of 92.02%, owing to strong electron-phonon coupling (λ = 2.47) enabled by bandgap engineering, as revealed by first-principles simulations. This biomimetic 3D network further yields a high thermal conductivity of 0.857 Wm −1 K −1 , a 306% enhancement over the matrix.
