Under harsh conditions (−20°C, 70% RH), it delays ice formation for 480 ± 32 s, maintains an ultralow ice adhesion strength of 17.4 ± 2.6 kPa, and under one-sun irradiation, rapidly raises the surface temperature to 89.6°C to achieve complete de-icing within 283 ± 23 s. Practical tests on aluminum cables, aircraft wings, and wind-turbine blades demonstrate its versatility and durability. This work establishes a design paradigm integrating semiconductor photophysics with biomimetic engineering for scalable, high-efficiency photothermal anti-/de-icing materials.

10.1002/adfm.78929.title: Pre-Calcination-Governed Spatial Architecture Engineering of MOF-Derived Magnetic Carbon Nanohybrids for Effective Microwave Absorption
10.1002/adfm.78929.abstract: ABSTRACT Precisely steering the spatial distribution of functional units in MOF-derived carbon-based hybrids remains a formidable challenge for microwave absorption. Here we reveal that pre-calcination can govern the intermediate chemistry and final spatial architectures of an identical ZIF-8@PBA precursor, yielding two structurally distinct nanohybrids (Fe 3 C−N−C and Fe 3 C−N−CNTs). Pre-calcination at 200°C preserves the ZIF-8@PBA framework to spatially confine Fe species enabling uniform Fe 3 C dispersion during subsequent pyrolysis, forming Fe 3 C−N−C; whereas pre-calcination at 400°C decomposes the framework into Fe 3 O 4 /ZnO intermediates that convert to surface-exposed Fe 3 C with localized enrichment, catalyzing carbon nanotubes (CNTs) growth to yield Fe 3 C−N−CNTs. The Fe 3 C−N−C architecture simultaneously enhances polarization relaxation, ferromagnetic resonance, and impedance matching, thus delivering a minimum reflection loss (RL min ) of −73.60 dB and an ultrawide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 9.29 GHz at 3.32 mm, superior to its pervious cournterparts. In comparison, The Fe 3 C−N−CNTs shifts to a dielectric-dominated regime, yielding an RL min of −65.71 dB, and an EAB of 7.79 GHz at 2.04 mm. These findings reveal that nanoscale spatial arrangements govern the attenuation-impedance balance in microwave absorbers. This work establishes a new mechanistic paradigm for designing high-performance microwave absorbers and functional materials by tailoring spatial architectures.
authors: Na Chen, Bing-Bing Han, Xiaoning Song, Boyou Hou, Kang-Jun Wang, Xiao-Guang San, Ye-Tang Pan

10.1002/adfm.79343.title: Integrated Multiband Smart Windows From UV to LWIR Based on Molecularly Engineered Thermochromic Hydrogels
10.1002/adfm.79343.abstract: ABSTRACT Smart windows offer energy-saving potential for buildings, while challenges remain in achieving multi-band design across ultraviolet-visible-near infrared-long wavelength infrared (UV-VIS-NIR-LWIR). Here we present a smart window integrating a thermochromic poly (EEEA-co-NIPAM) (PEN) hydrogel with an anti-UV layer and an indium tin oxide layer, enabling dynamic VIS-NIR solar modulation alongside UV shielding and low LWIR emissivity ( ɛ LWIR ). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that 2-(2-ethoxyethoxy) ethyl acrylate (EEEA) comonomer strengthens the polymer network and forms favorable hydrogen-bonding interactions with N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAM), promoting rapid dehydration-driven chain collapse above a reduced lower critical solution temperature, and accelerating the optical response during heating. The produced window achieves a solar modulation (Δ Т sol ) of 42.7%, nearly complete UV shielding ( T UV = 0.1%), and low indoor-facing ɛ LWIR = 0.31, with stable performance after 100-h UV exposure and 100 thermal cycles. Outdoor tests demonstrate a 7.7°C cooling effect compared with ordinary glass, while EnergyPlus simulations demonstrate up to 62.6% savings in building heating/cooling energy in Singapore, San Francisco, and Brisbane. This work provides an effective multiband strategy for smart windows together with an in-depth understanding of thermochromic hydrogel, and is expected to inspire future efforts toward spectrally selective, energy-efficient building glazing.
authors: Jiashuo Sun, Yutong Tan, Congyuan Wei, Zhenhui Hu, Rui Zhu, Yu Zhao, Yueyue Guan, Ruifeng Zhang, Hengshan Wei, Ran Tao, Wang Zhang, Jingting Luo, Guofa Cai, Xi Chen, Yi Long, Yongsheng Yang, Jinqing Peng, Yujie Ke

10.1002/adfm.79456.title: Activating Selenium for Atomic-Level Defect Passivation and Band Engineering Enables High-Efficiency Bulk Heterojunction CuInS2 Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79456.abstract: ABSTRACT Copper indium sulfide (CuInS 2 ) stands out as a promising candidate for next-generation photovoltaics due to its exceptional stability, high absorption coefficient, and eco-friendly composition. However, realizing high-quality CuInS 2 absorbers typically demands high-temperature processing, which not only limits substrate compatibility but also invites interfacial degradation from elemental interdiffusion. Here, we overcome this challenge by introducing a low-temperature selenium ion activation (LTSA) strategy that enables near-surface atomic-level defect passivation and band-structure modulation in solution-processed CuInS 2 absorbers. Beyond conventional passivation, LTSA orchestrates three synergistic effects: (i) selenium ion diffusion tailors a favorable band alignment; (ii) atomic substitution effectively passivates critical deep-level defects (such as In Cu and V S ) through robust chemical bonding; and (iii) interfacial charge transport is markedly enhanced while carrier recombination is suppressed. These combined benefits yield CuInS 2 solar cells on transparent conducting oxide substrates with a record-competitive power conversion efficiency of 11.43% and the highest fill factor of 66.88% reported to date. By establishing LTSA as a low-temperature route for near-surface atomic-level defect passivation and structural reconstruction, this work unlocks new pathways toward high-performance, cost-effective inorganic photovoltaics.
authors: Junwei Chen, Congrui Liu, Chengwu Ruan, Chenlong Gao, Yichao Wang, Pengfei Wang, Zhihui Yang, Fang Wu, Yan Zhang, Jun Xu, Rongfeng Tang

10.1002/adfm.79451.title: Printable Architected Porous Ceramic Metamaterials Enabling Electromagnetic-Thermal Coupling
10.1002/adfm.79451.abstract: ABSTRACT The coupled demands for electromagnetic interference mitigation and thermal management in aerospace and advanced electronic systems necessitate lightweight materials that integrate broadband microwave absorption with effective thermal insulation under extreme operating conditions. Conventional electromagnetic absorbers and thermal barriers are typically monofunctional, whereas metamaterials, despite their architectural versatility, often exhibit limited thermal protection. Here we introduce a printable porous Silicon-Boron Oxycarbide (SiBOC) ceramic metamaterial that combines structural precision, multifunctionality, and high-temperature resilience. By dispersing hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) into a UV-curable SiBOC pre-ceramic polymer, we achieve a resin system that simultaneously supports high loading, porosity, and digital light processing printability. During heat treatment, HGMs act as both structural stabilizers and catalytic reservoirs, yielding a hierarchical SiBOC@Graphene@HGM architecture. This unique configuration enhances dielectric loss, promotes multi-scattering, and suppresses heat conduction. Consequently, the porous SiBOC ceramic metamaterial achieves an ultrabroad effective absorption bandwidth of 35.58 GHz (within 2-40 GHz, at the incident angle of 50°) with a minimum reflection loss of −59.71 dB, along with low thermal conductivity (0.208 W·m −1 ·K −1 ) and light density (0.313 g cm −3 ). This strategy establishes a generalizable paradigm for multifunctional ceramic metamaterials, bridging electromagnetic and thermal protection for next-generation extreme-environment applications.
authors: Yuyao Sun, Yekun Liu, Zhen Yu, Ruoxi Xiao, Jiaxin Huang, Guoxuan Xu, Zhaofan He, Ruizhe Xing, Zhilong Yu, Jie Kong

10.1002/adfm.79405.title: Dual-Alloy Exsolution in Fe-Based Perovskite Anodes for High-Performance Direct Ammonia Solid Oxide Fuel Cells
10.1002/adfm.79405.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct ammonia solid oxide fuel cells (DA-SOFCs) offer an integrated route for carbon-free power generation by coupling in situ ammonia decomposition with electrochemical hydrogen oxidation. However, anode catalysts must simultaneously achieve rapid NH 3 decomposition, efficient electrochemical charge transfer, and long-term resistance to nitridation and particle coarsening. Here, we report an Fe-based perovskite multi-doped with Co and Ni, La 0.6 Sr 0.2 Ba 0.2 Mn 0.2 Fe 0.6 Co 0.1 Ni 0.1 O 3 (P-LSBMFCN), as a precursor for dual-alloy exsolved DA-SOFC anodes. Upon H 2 reduction, P-LSBMFCN transforms into a Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) layered oxide decorated with highly dispersed FeCo and FeNi alloy nanoparticles (R-LSBMFCN). Co and Ni multi-doping directs the reduction-induced nucleation and alloying pathway, reducing the average nanoparticle size from 129.3 nm for the Fe-only reference to 48.3 nm for R-LSBMFCN while increasing nanoparticle density. The resulting dual-alloy architecture provides abundant accessible active sites and electronically tuned metal surfaces, accelerating NH 3 activation, NH x intermediate conversion, and N recombination/desorption. Consequently, R-LSBMFCN exhibits the lowest apparent activation energy, nearly complete NH 3 conversion at high temperature, and maximum power densities of 1.638 and 1.386 W cm −2 under H 2 and NH 3 at 800°C, respectively, with stable operation for 200 h under NH 3 . This work demonstrates multi-doping-induced dual-alloy exsolution as an effective strategy for durable DA-SOFC anodes.
authors: Jungseub Ha, Sehun Choi, Sanghwa Jeong, Minguk Kwak, Daehwan Kim, Jongcheol Gang, Taeyeol Jeon, Sujin Kim, Yongju Yun, Won Bae Kim

10.1002/adfm.79475.title: A Self-Reinforcing Hydrogel Orchestrates Dynamic Microenvironment Reprogramming for High-Quality Diabetic Skin Regeneration
10.1002/adfm.79475.abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, oxidative stress, hypoxia, impaired angiogenesis, and pathological fibrosis. Herein, a self-reinforcing hydrogel dressing (RNPP) is developed by integrating copper peroxide (CuO 2 )/manganese dioxide (MnO 2 ) hybrid nanozymes and ginsenoside Rg1 (Rg1) into a sodium polyacrylate/polymetformin matrix for wound microenvironment regulation and high-quality diabetic wound healing. RNPP rapidly promotes hemostasis, absorbs exudate, and maintains a moist protective interface. CuO 2 /MnO 2 nanozymes provide non-antibiotic antibacterial activity through Cu 2+ release while scavenging excessive reactive oxygen species and converting endogenous H 2 O 2 into oxygen, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and hypoxia, promoting pro-regenerative macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and re-epithelialization. Meanwhile, released Cu 2+ dynamically coordinates with polymetformin, reducing free Cu 2+ toxicity while reinforcing the hydrogel network. Sustained Rg1 release further modulates the transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) axis and suppresses myofibroblast overactivation, thereby attenuating fibrotic signaling and promoting organized collagen remodeling. These effects suggest a favorable microenvironment for improved tissue remodeling. Consequently, RNPP accelerates tissue repair in diabetic and MRSA-infected wounds while favoring regenerative tissue remodeling, providing a multifunctional material strategy for chronic wound management.
authors: Yi Zhang, Hening Liu, Yuanbo Zhu, Yue Yin, Zixuan Wang, Weijie Shu, Yubing Lu, Ye Ding, Zihan Wang, Cong Fu, Ziwei Yan, Yi Hou, Yunxiang Kang, Zhencheng Gao, Bei Lv, Guangda Zhu, Lu Tang, Wei Wang

10.1002/adfm.79401.title: Multifunctional Phase Engineering Expands the Carrier Concentration Optimization Window for High-Performance Mg3(Bi, Sb)2 Thermoelectrics
10.1002/adfm.79401.abstract: ABSTRACT The optimization of thermoelectric materials is fundamentally limited by the narrow carrier concentration ( n H ) window, which limits n H as an effective degree of freedom for enhancing performance. Here, we demonstrate that the introduction of a multifunctional phase overcomes this inherent limitation in Mg 3 (Bi, Sb) 2 . Specifically, the work-function difference between NbC and the Mg 3 (Bi, Sb) 2 matrix drives interfacial electron transfer, establishing an elevated n H regime. NbC-induced grain growth suppresses grain-boundary scattering, thereby improving carrier mobility and significantly boosting electrical conductivity beyond the conventional n H optimization window. Meanwhile, interfacial charge redistribution and magnetic interactions associated with NbC modulate energy-dependent carrier scattering, increasing the scattering factor and enabling the Seebeck coefficient to be maintained or even enhanced under high n H . Consequently, the optimized composites achieve an outstanding average power factor of 3.1 mW m −1 K −2 over 300-573 K, along with a maximum zT of ∼1.3 at 523 K and an average zT of ∼1.1. Furthermore, the fabricated single-leg device achieved a conversion efficiency of ∼5.5% under a temperature difference of 282 K. This work breaks the conventional paradigm that restricts thermoelectric performance optimizing solely within the optimal n H regime, highlighting the pivotal role of multifunctional phase engineering in unlocking new performance frontiers.
authors: Haiping Guo, Lifeng Jiang, Xinghui Wang, Jingyi Xiao, Huijun Kang, Zongning Chen, Enyu Guo, Tongmin Wang

10.1002/adfm.79426.title: In Situ Constructed Fluorosulfided Interface With Metallic Mo Sites for Robust Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79426.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) are acclaimed for their low-cost, sustainability, and high energy density. However, achieving highly reversible Na plating/stripping on bare current collectors (CCs) and robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is challenging. Herein, we present a robust fluorosulfided SEI (FS-SEI) layer with metallic Mo active sites through in situ electrochemical transformation of 2D MoS 2 coating on the Cu CCs. Specifically, the ingenious 2D MoS 2 holds short ion transport pathways and large contact active areas during battery operation. Furthermore, MoS 2 can in situ convert into metallic Mo and Na 2 S, while catalyzing the dissolution of NaPF 6 to generate NaF. The in situ formed FS-SEI film possesses excellent sodiophilicity, high Na + diffusion, and good electron-blocking capability, which effectively guides a homogeneous distribution of Na + flux, accelerates the electrochemical reaction kinetics, and blocks side reactions between electrolyte and electrodes. Benefiting from these advantages, the MoS 2 @Cu half cells achieve average Coulombic efficiency of 99.85% over 350 cycles at 10 mA cm −2 and 10 mAh cm −2 . When paired with Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cathodes, the AFSMBs exhibit excellent rate capability and cycling stability (>97.0% retention). This work offers insights into engineering a stable in situ SEI via 2D sodiophilic architectures, paving the way for developing energy-dense and durable AFSMBs.
authors: Di Zhou, Meng Zhang, Yijia Zhang, Bangning Cheng, Sung-Soo Kim, Zhengqing Ye, Kai Liu, Ying Jiang, Lianqi Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79409.title: Ion Migration in Metal Halide X-Ray Detectors: Mechanism, Impact, and Suppression
10.1002/adfm.79409.abstract: ABSTRACT In recent years, metal halides (MHs) and their derivatives have emerged as promising candidates for x-ray detection. These materials offer distinct advantages, including high x-ray absorption efficiency, tunable bandgaps, low costs, and facile processing. While the performance of MHs-based devices has improved rapidly, ion migration under high operating bias voltages remains a critical bottleneck. This phenomenon leads to severe degradation issues, such as elevated dark currents, electrode corrosion, baseline drift, and reduced carrier collection efficiency. Therefore, a systematic review of ion migration in MHs-based x-ray detectors is of crucial importance for breaking through the bottlenecks in their performance and stability, as well as advancing their practical applications. This review starts with the microscopic mechanisms of ion migration, detailing its origins, pathways, driving forces, and electrical characterization methods. Subsequently, based on energy band analysis, we elucidate the impact of ion migration on device performance. We then categorize existing suppression strategies into four main approaches: enhancing lattice interactions, minimizing migration channels, blocking transport pathways, and designing self-powered detectors. Finally, the review discusses current challenges and outlines future development directions for stable MHs-based x-ray detectors.
authors: Haoran Deng, Youkui Xu, Zhiwen Jin

10.1002/adfm.79333.title: Digitally Printed Eco-Friendly Electronic Devices
10.1002/adfm.79333.abstract: ABSTRACT The sustainable life cycle of electronics is one of the major challenges of modern society. Moreover, the manufacturing of conventional electronics significantly impacts the environment due to the extensive consumption of raw materials, energy, and the release of harmful byproducts. In this regard, manufacturing of electronics using eco-friendly materials through digital printing routes represents a promising and sustainable solution. This review discusses the state-of-the-art research in this field, exploring various digital printing techniques such as inkjet, electro-hydro-dynamic jet, aerosol-jet, and extrusion printing techniques, focusing on resource efficient manufacturing with minimal material wastage and their environmental impacts. Various eco-friendly ink formulation strategies are discussed together with their practical application. Additionally, the review addresses various end-of-life management strategies such as repair, recycling, and biodegradation. Finally, major challenges associated with digital printing of eco-friendly electronics to compete with conventional electronics are explored and future perspectives in this emerging area are outlined.
authors: Nitheesh M. Nair, Mikel Rincón-Iglesias, Cristian Mendes-Felipe, Fatemeh Etehadi, Senentxu Lanceros-Méndez, Gerardo Hernandez-Sosa

10.1002/adfm.79454.title: C-H Arylation-Constructed Non-Fully-Fused Dimeric Acceptors for o-Xylene Processed Organic Solar Cells With 20.17% Efficiency
10.1002/adfm.79454.abstract: ABSTRACT Although organic solar cells (OSCs) have made significant progress in photovoltaic performance, their practical applications still face challenges, such as the complex material synthesis and involvement of Stille coupling reaction with organotin reagents of fused-ring electron acceptors, and using halogenated toxic solvents in device fabrication. Here, we develop two non-fully-fused dimeric acceptors (named dNA-C6 and dNA-C12) with varying alkyl linker lengths using organotin-free C-H activation approach, which present the advantages of environmental friendliness and easy synthesis. When introducing dNA-C6 and dNA-C12 into PM6:BTP-eC9 system, these OSCs achieve higher power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 19.07% and 18.74%, respectively, compared to their parental monomer based device (18.44%), while the dNA-C6 based OSC obtains both superior PCE and device stability. Moreover, dNA-C6 is also introduced into D18:BTP-eC9 host to verify its universality in boosting photovoltaic performance, and the relevant device processed with halogen-free o -xylene offers a further improved PCE of 20.17%, ranking among the highest values in the reported non-fully-conjugated dimeric acceptors and halogen-free solvent processed OSCs. This work develops organotin-free synthesized non-fully-fused dimeric acceptors by integrating eco-friendly chemistry for preparing green solvent processed OSCs with high PCE and device stability.
authors: Hua Tan, Guanchen Dong, Wenjing Zhou, Shaoqiang Wang, Yang Qiu, Hairui Bai, Manjun Xiao, Jianhua Chen, Wenyan Su, Weiguo Zhu, Junting Yu, Qunping Fan

10.1002/adfm.79453.title: Preiodization Unlocks an Orbital-Regulated Cascade Redox Chemistry for High-Capacity Zinc-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79453.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc-iodine (Zn-I 2 ) batteries are considered as competitive candidates for large-scale energy storage devices due to their high safety and low cost, but slow iodine conversion kinetics and limited theoretical capacity have always hindered their commercial application. In this work, the preiodization strategy successfully activates the iodine redox conversion of VS 2 catalytic electrodes (I-VS 2 /I 2 ) and achieves a cascade of I 0 /I − redox and Zn 2+ intercalation/deintercalation reactions. Theoretical and experimental analyses indicate that preiodization optimizes the V─I orbital coupling strength and electron exchange by effectively regulating the bonding and antibonding states occupation, which promotes the iodine redox conversion and inhibits polyiodide formation. Moreover, the cascade of I 0 /I − redox conversion and Zn 2+ intercalation/deintercalation reactions contributes to exceeding the theoretical capacity limitation of conventional Zn-I 2 batteries. Consequently, high-capacity (372 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 ) and cycling-stable (86% capacity retention after 4000 cycles) Zn-I 2 batteries were acquired. The work offers an essential inspiration for investigating in depth the orbital electronic structure-catalytic performance relationship.
authors: Wentao Qu, Jian Zhu, Yongwen Tan, Limin Wang, Zhongwen Zhang, Hongcheng He, Ming Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79490.title: Tailoring Covalent Organic Frameworks as Functionalized Molecular Traps to Enable Sulfur Conversion and Li + Desolvation for Durable Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79490.abstract: ABSTRACT Suppressing polysulfid shuttling and enhancing Li + desolvation kinetics are crucial for high-performance lithium-sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we propose an elaborate molecular trap design strategy based on functional-group decoupling and synergistic enhancement in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to resolve the aforementioned issues. A cyano-containing COF (CN-COF) and its amidoxime derivative (COF-AO) serve as cooperative dual-sided separator coatings. CN-COF contributes a well-ordered porous structure for confining sulfur species; its C≡N sites interact with polysulfides to reduce the reaction energy barrier of sulfur conversion. On the anode side, ─NH 2 /─OH groups in COF-AO promote Li + desolvation and modulate Li + transport by capturing solvent molecules via hydrogen bonding, which suppresses parasitic reactions and ensures rapid Li + migration. Besides, the regular topological structure and size-exclusion effect of COF restrict migration of large-sized solvent molecules and polysulfides, enabling homogeneous Li + flux and smooth Li deposition. Benefiting from these advantages, Li||Li symmetrical cells achieve stable cycling for 7000 h at 5 mA cm −2 /5 mAh cm −2 . The Li─S battery delivers an initial capacity of 820 mAh g −1 with an ultralow decay rate of 0.024% per cycle over 900 cycles at 5 C.The pouch cell exhibits a high initial capacity of 1020 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C and stable operation for 150 cycles.

10.1002/adfm.77841.title: Optimizing Vanadium Single-Atom Nanozyme via Cluster-Mediated Charge Orchestration for Modulating Immune Homeostasis in Intracerebral Hemorrhage
10.1002/adfm.77841.abstract: ABSTRACT Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) triggers excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and persistent neuroinflammation, which synergistically drive progressive neuronal damage and poor neurological functional recovery, severely restricting patient prognosis. Artificial enzymes are hailed for their robustness and economy, yet their catalytic ceiling is often set by an inability to finely sculpt the electronic landscape of active centers. Here, we present V AC -V SA /NC, a single-atom nanozyme (SAN) in which vanadium (V) atomic clusters (AC) orchestrate proximal V single atoms (SA), thereby regulating the local charge distribution and igniting a potent ROS for detoxification. Density functional theory calculations revealed that electrons flowing from V AC to V SA active sites drain electron density around the V SA center, reshape the local charge distribution, and promote a rapid ROS detoxification cascade. To realize targeted blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration for ICH treatment, we fabricated V AC -V SA /NC@M by coating with M1 microglial membranes. In vivo fluorescence imaging confirms that the V AC -V SA /NC@M efficiently crosses the BBB and precisely accumulates at hemorrhagic inflammatory lesions. In vitro and in vivo experimental results combined with single-cell sequencing analysis demonstrate that V AC -V SA /NC@M effectively converts proinflammatory M1 microglia into an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, terminates the self-amplifying neuroinflammatory cascade, and inhibits progressive neuronal death.

10.1002/adfm.79497.title: Snake-Scale-Inspired Serrated Structures With Frictional Anisotropy for Tunable Bidirectional Shear-Force Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79497.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible tactile sensors are essential components of intelligent robotics, wearable healthcare systems, and human-machine interfaces. However, most existing tactile sensors have limited capability to discriminate the direction of tangential forces, restricting multidimensional tactile perception under complex loading conditions. Herein, inspired by the serrated unidirectional compliant architecture of snake ventral scales, we develop a bioinspired serrated anisotropic tactile sensor (BSATS) for normal-pressure sensing and bidirectional shear-force discrimination. Moreover, modulation of the serration angle enables effective tuning of the sensing sensitivity and detection range, establishing a direct structure-property relationship for adaptable tactile sensing. Finite element analysis elucidates the direction-dependent deformation and contact-area evolution of the serrated friction-anisotropic structure under normal and bidirectional shear loading, revealing the underlying angle-dependent anisotropic sensing mechanism. The optimized BSATS exhibits a high pressure sensitivity of 1.832 kPa −1 , a rapid response time of 50 ms, and robust durability over 2000 loading-unloading cycles, while reliably distinguishing oppositely directed shear forces. The BSATS further demonstrates versatile functionality in wearable physiological monitoring, human-motion tracking, surface-texture recognition, and real-time robotic grasp-state perception. This work establishes bioinspired friction anisotropy as an effective structural strategy for tunable multidimensional tactile sensing in wearable healthcare and intelligent robotics.
authors: Qinggang Guo, Yumin Li, Long Zheng, Luquan Ren

10.1002/adfm.79157.title: Building-Block Design of Nonflammable Quasi-Solid Electrolytes for Ampere-Hour-Scale Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79157.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a competitive technology for large-scale energy storage; however, their commercial viability remains severely hindered by the inherent flammability and high volatility of liquid electrolytes (LEs). Herein, we propose a modular assembly strategy inspired by the building-block principle to architect a quasi-solid electrolyte (QSE). By synergistically integrating vinylene carbonate (VC) and 2,2,3,4,4,4-hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA) monomers, we modulate the electron density distribution within the polymer matrix. The resulting PVH QSE lowers the Na + desolvation barrier and provides continuous ion migration pathways, thereby achieving exceptional ionic conductivity of 5.60 mS cm −1 and a sodium-ion transference number of 0.58. Furthermore, the spatially locked polymer architecture drives the formation of ion-solvent aggregates and a robust NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, synergistically suppressing solvent decomposition and eradicating sodium dendrite growth. Consequently, the Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells exhibit an outstanding capacity retention of 94.9% after 3000 cycles alongside superior temperature adaptability. To demonstrate practical feasibility, the hard carbon||NaNi 0.33 Fe 0.33 Mn 0.33 O 2 pouch cells maintain stable cycling over 200 cycles. Crucially, nail penetration and accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) tests verify the exceptional safety of the pouch cells. By linking molecular microenvironment regulation to macroscopic battery safety, this work illuminates a viable pathway toward the commercialization of intrinsically safe SIBs.
authors: Qichong Yuan, Xuelian Fu, Xinye Mai, Guilong Wang, Yongcong Huang, Wen Luo, Hongzhi Wang, Mingwei Liu, Xuhui Li, Yujie Yan, Yun Yan, Xingqun Liao, Chaopu Tan, Yonghong Deng, Yingzhi Li, Zhouguang Lu

10.1002/adfm.79457.title: Precursor Size Governs Thermally Activated Solid State Conversion Into the Redox Active Framework Formation in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7
10.1002/adfm.79457.abstract: ABSTRACT Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 is an attractive Fe-based polyanionic cathode for low-cost sodium-ion batteries, but scalable synthesis remains constrained by the trade-off between precursor homogeneity and process compatibility. Soluble Fe salts enable intimate mixing, whereas Fe (II)-phosphate precursors avoid nitrate/oxalate burdens but react as insoluble domains. Here we identify precursor defined solid state reaction length as the key variable governing NFPP formation from Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 . Reaction-diffusion simulations predict that oversized Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 domains retain under converted interiors, while low submicrometre domains enter a conversion-saturated regime. Experiments using size-controlled precursors confirm that this length scale regulates competing NaFePO 4 and Na 2 FeP 2 O 7 formation, Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ local chemistry and Na + transport kinetics. A CV precursor captures most of the kinetic and electrochemical benefit of stronger refinement, delivering 104.1 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and 61.8 mAh g −1 at 20 C, together with stable long-term and full-cell operation. These findings establish reaction length scale control as a practical design rule for phosphate compatible NFPP synthesis.
authors: Yuanhang Wang, Hangxin Niu, Dongdong Li, Wei Han

10.1002/adfm.79447.title: Low-Melting-Point Alloys for Printable Rear Electrodes in Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells: A Review
10.1002/adfm.79447.abstract: ABSTRACT Noble-metal rear electrodes deposited by high-vacuum thermal evaporation impose a major bottleneck for the development of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and organic solar cells (OSCs), owing to high material costs, unstable interfaces, and poor manufacturability. Low-melting-point alloys (LMPAs) represent a versatile alternative rear-electrode candidate that supports direct patterning under low-temperature, vacuum-free conditions. Upon ambient air exposure, LMPAs spontaneously develop an in-situ surface oxide layer, which can mitigate Schottky-barrier effects to facilitate efficient charge extraction and suppress ion/atom migration to improve device stability. In addition, the intrinsic mechanical compliance and self-healing capacity of LMPAs render them particularly promising for flexible and stretchable photovoltaic devices. This timely review first introduces fundamental properties of LMPAs and their unique merits for photovoltaic applications. Recent advances in LMPA rear electrodes for OSCs and PSCs are reviewed, with focused emphasis on fabrication strategies for finely patterned LMPA electrodes. We thoroughly discuss the critical functions of the in-situ oxide layer, alongside the mechanical advantages of LMPAs for bendable and stretchable devices. Design principles and performance trade-offs are then summarized. Finally, remaining challenges and future research opportunities for LMPA-electrode-based solar cells are highlighted.
authors: Junjie Liu, Yanzhi Tang, Xinwei Li, Yanchun Liu, Guoge Zhang, Nianqing Fu

10.1002/adfm.79415.title: Electrolyte-Enabled Suppression of Static Corrosion for Long-Cycle Calendar Life in Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79415.abstract: ABSTRACT The calendar life of lithium (Li) metal batteries is commonly evaluated through cycling performance, implicitly assuming that storage-induced degradation follows the same interfacial processes. However, this work reveals that Li metal undergoes continuous non-Faradaic interfacial corrosion under open-circuit conditions, defining a distinct degradation pathway governing calendar aging, distinct from cycling-induced failure. To quantify this process, we introduce a kinetically defined descriptor based on the degradation rate constant (λ), enabling direct evaluation of time-dependent capacity loss during storage. This framework treats calendar aging as a corrosion-driven kinetic process rather than an extrapolation of cycling behavior. We further show that static corrosion can be actively regulated via electrolyte design. Based on the degradation rate constants derived from capacity decay fitting, the LiNO 3 -15C5-CsBr electrolyte projects a 2.7-fold extension in storage lifetime at 100% SOC and a 3.4-fold extension at 0% SOC versus the baseline electrolyte. Mechanistically, Cs + -mediated electrostatic shielding, Br − -induced interfacial polishing, and NO 3 − -derived inorganic passivation cooperatively stabilize the Li interface, suppress corrosion kinetics, and reduce irreversible Li loss, leading to a marked decrease in λ. These findings establish static corrosion as a distinct degradation mode in Li metal batteries and provide a quantitative framework for evaluating and regulating calendar aging beyond cycling metrics.
authors: Zengwu Wei, Haichao Li, Yixiao Kong, Li Liu, Danning Yu, Min Zhou, Mingjiong Zhou, Xing Xin, Yongyao Xia

10.1002/adfm.79494.title: Optimized Small Polaron Hopping Enhances the Conductivity Barrier of Polyanionic Frameworks
10.1002/adfm.79494.abstract: ABSTRACT The low intrinsic electronic conductivity of polyanionic cathodes, caused by electronic localization of isolated anionic groups, restricts the fast-charging performance of sodium-ion batteries. To address this challenge, we strategically introduce low-valence Cs + into Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (P 2 O 7 ) (NFPP) to enhance small polaron hopping and electronic conductivity. The Cs + triggers a charge-compensation effect that pre-stabilizes Fe 3+ species and establishes an Fe 3+ reservoir in NFPP. This configuration creates a built-in electric field that introduces electron-relaying states above the valence-band maximum, significantly lowering the small-polaron hopping barrier between Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ couples. Crucially, Hall-effect measurements directly validate this mechanism, revealing enhanced carrier mobility and concentration that overcompensate for conventional doping strategies with reduced carrier mobility trade-off due to carrier scattering from doped foreign ions. Consequently, the optimized NFPP-Cs cathode overcomes carrier transport bottlenecks and hence enhances charge storage kinetics, achieving an 80% state-of-charge in just 7.9 min at 5 C and achieving full charge in 58 s at 50 C with a high specific capacity of 81.0 mAh g −1 . Distribution of relaxation times analysis further substantiates that this charge-compensation-driven small polaron hopping constitutes the core mechanism for the enhanced electrochemical reaction kinetics. This work provides a compelling paradigm for designing polyanionic frameworks with enhanced reaction kinetics.
authors: Cong Liu, Yumeng Jiang, Zhi Zhang, Huanyi Liao, Zhaopei Liu, Anan Guo, Yanan Zhang, Zhongxi Li, Yuan Yuan, Jinsong Wu, Yihua Gao

10.1002/adfm.79367.title: Conformational Restriction Unlocks Record Birefringence in Sulfonate Ultraviolet NLO Crystals
10.1002/adfm.79367.abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing second-harmonic generation (SHG), birefringence, and bandgap simultaneously within a single material remains a formidable challenge due to their intrinsic mutual trade-offs. Herein, we propose a conformational restriction strategy that replaces a flexible monocyclic cation with a rigid polycyclic analogue, which affords two organic ionic sulfonate crystals, [C 5 H 6 NO][SO 3 (C 7 H 5 O 3 )]·2H 2 O ( HPSA ) and [C 12 H 9 N 2 ][SO 3 (C 7 H 5 O 3 )] ( OPSA ). HPSA adopts a highly ordered centrosymmetric (CS) crystal structure, Pbca , stabilized by strong and directional hydrogen bonds. Whereas OPSA crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric (NCS) space group P 2 1 arising from steric hindrance and weak, asymmetric supramolecular interactions, thereby endowing OPSA with a stable SHG response (1.1 × KDP), with no observable intensity degradation upon heating up to 533 K. Both compounds possess wide bandgaps and pronounced optical anisotropy, notably OPSA with record-high birefringence ( Δ n = 0.93@546 nm) among all known NLO crystals containing π-conjugated groups with bandgap exceeding 3.1 eV. Moreover, OPSA achieves single-phase white light with an ultrabroad dual-band spectrum spanning 400-800 nm, enabling a prototype white-light-emitting diode with a color rendering index of 87, CIE chromaticity coordinates of (0.31, 0.32), and correlated color temperature of 7185 K. This work expands the structural diversity of sulfonate-based materials and establishes a rational design strategy for multifunctional optical crystals.
authors: Jiajing Wu, Yu-Mei Zhang, Zhen-Cheng Wu, Wen-Dong Yao, Sheng-Ping Guo

10.1002/adfm.79493.title: Lanthanide-Doped Hybrid Metal Halide Glasses with Multidimensional Luminescence for X-Ray Imaging and Photonic Authentication
10.1002/adfm.79493.abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid metal-halide glasses combine optical homogeneity and processability for scintillators, yet most reported systems rely on a single emissive center and conventional radiation-to-light conversion. Here, we report lanthanide (Ln)-doped BTP 2 MnCl 4 (BTP + = Butyltriphenylphosphonium) hybrid glasses prepared by one-step melt-quenching, demonstrating expanded emission channels while preserving optical transparency and the amorphous state. Eu 3+ is selected as a secondary emitter for its spectroscopic complementarity with Mn 2+ . The glasses integrate broadband green Mn 2+ emission with narrow red Eu 3+ lines, whose relative contributions are regulated by Eu 3+ content and excitation wavelength. Distinct thermal responses provide additional temperature modulation, while spectroscopic and time-resolved measurements support Mn 2+ →Eu 3+ energy transfer. As scintillators, the glasses achieve a light yield of 18 843 photons MeV −1 , a detection limit of 26.7 nGy air s −1 , and an imaging resolution of 28.5 lp mm −1 , with stable radioluminescence under repeated and prolonged irradiation. Beyond conventional imaging, the composition-, excitation-, and temperature-dependent spectral responses enable photonic barcodes for sequential multilevel authentication. Furthermore, the successful preparation of Ln- and Sb-based glasses further demonstrates the generalizability of this glass-forming strategy. These results extend hybrid metal-halide glasses beyond conventional scintillation media toward spectrally addressable multifunctional materials, providing a route to integrate x-ray imaging with multidimensional optical information processing.
authors: Shilin Jin, Xiaoai Cao, Luyao Wei, Zhiqiong Wu, Daqin Chen

10.1002/adfm.79474.title: Rational Design of Vis-to-NIR Light Driven Photocatalytic System With Bidirectional Transfer of Charge and Energy for Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.79474.abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of photocatalytic systems capable of utilizing the full solar spectrum while maintaining efficient charge separation remains a persistent challenge in sustainable hydrogen production. Herein, we combine up-conversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) with near-infrared absorbing ability and visible-light driven covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalyst together to construct a hybrid heterostructure for Vis-to-NIR light driven hydrogen production. In this system, UCNPs convert NIR light into ultraviolet and visible light for the utilization of TpPa-1-COF, while an effective heterojunction formed between UCNPs and TpPa-1-COF benefiting the separation of photogenerated charge carriers. As a result, PNGF(15%)@TpPa-1-COF composites achieve an exceptional high hydrogen evolution rate of 126.9 mmol g −1 h −1 , which is 28 times enhancement over pristine TpPa-1-COF. The contribution of UCNPs in facilitating the separation of charge carriers of TpPa-1-COF was confirmed by measurements of femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (fs-TAS) and various characterizations. The results of control experiments demonstrate that energy band matching between COFs and UCNPs is crucial for the formation of the bidirectional transfer of photogenerated electrons and energy within the photocatalytic system. This provides an innovative strategy for developing an efficient photocatalytic heterojunction system to broaden the utilization of solar light and achieve effective separation of photogenerated charge carriers.
authors: Xiaoyu Chu, Yu-Han Liu, Zhi-Hao Zhao, Xiaomin Song, Guixin Yang, Lu-Hua Shao, Feng-Ming Zhang, Ya-Qian Lan

10.1002/adfm.79432.title: Architected Bio-Based Iontronic Skin With Dual-Mode Pressure and Strain Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79432.abstract: ABSTRACT Human skin encodes pressure and stretch through the motion of ions, a principle soft iontronics reproduce but rarely on sustainable terms. Additive manufacturing has lifted ionogels from cast slabs into architected sensors, yet this progress rests on fossil-derived acrylates, because plant-based networks expel the polar ionic liquids that carry charge. Here we print an ionogel whose matrix exceeds 80% bio-based carbon while stably hosting a hydrophobic imidazolium ionic liquid, resolving a long-standing compatibility barrier. A single monomer ratio tunes stiffness 30 fold (9 to 0.3 MPa) and nearly doubles ionic conductivity to 0.53 mS cm −1 . Printed as gyroid lattices, the material senses pressure capacitively and strain resistively through separable channels: near-incompressibility pins the gauge factor near 2 irrespective of geometry, whereas the lattice amplifies low-pressure sensitivity eightfold and accelerates the strain response 4.6-fold. On the body, both modes track joint motion with complementary signatures. Chemistry and printed architecture thus act as independent levers for renewable iontronic skin.
authors: Maksims Jurinovs, Madara Veseta, Fevzihan Basarir, Beatrise Silava, Eduards Bakis, Krisjanis Smits, Olesja Starkova, Jaana Vapaavuori, Sergejs Gaidukovs

10.1002/adfm.79182.title: Core-Shell Solvation Structure Engineering Enables Practical Lithium Metal Batteries With 475 Wh Kg −1
10.1002/adfm.79182.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) offer extremely high theoretical energy densities, but face significant challenges in terms of electrolyte compatibility and interface stability. Existing low-concentration electrolytes struggle to form a robust solid-electrolyte interface to maintain stable cycling. Here, we designed a low-concentration electrolyte based on a functionally partitioned core-shell solvation strategy. Methyl sulfone, possessing a relatively high donor number, dominates the primary Li + coordination domain, while fluoroethylene carbonate, with a low donor number and low viscosity, primarily regulates the outer solvation environment and interfacial chemistry. This design facilitates rapid desolvation, high ionic conductivity (4.42 mS cm −1 ), and an exceptionally high Li + transference number (0.74). The core-shell structure induces a gradient SEI, promoting uniform lithium deposition. Consequently, the LiFePO 4 (LFP)||Li cell achieved capacity retention of 85.9% after 5000 cycles at 1 C, along with cycling stability from −10°C to 50°C. Practical application was further confirmed by stable cycling of NCM811||Li pouch cells (200 cycles, 95.7%) and NCM811||graphite pouch cells (650 cycles, 88.5%). Furthermore, a 2.2 Ah NCM811||Li pouch cell achieves a gravimetric energy density of 475 Wh kg −1 . This work presents a scalable approach to engineering solvation chemistries for high-voltage and high-energy-density LMBs.

10.1002/adfm.79422.title: A Bioinspired Photon-Gated Phase-Change Textile for Two-Stage Heat-Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
10.1002/adfm.79422.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet-spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase-change material (mPCM)-integrated radiative-cooling meta-fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO 4 ) photon-regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent-heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric-window emission, and phase-change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta-fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric-window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny-day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three-day cement-panel measurements further yielded an average peak-temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy-balance analysis and climate-scale modelling further indicate promising cooling-energy and carbon-reduction potential in hot and cooling-dominated regions. These results establish wet-spun radiative cooling/phase-change material meta-fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.

10.1002/adfm.79488.title: First-Principles Insights Into Fe 2 O 3 /In 2 S 3 Heterojunction and Its Application in Dispersion-Managed Fiber Lasers
10.1002/adfm.79488.abstract: ABSTRACT Heterostructure materials have garnered substantial interest across optics, medicine, optoelectronics, and electromagnetics due to their ability to combine advantageous characteristics from multiple constituent phases. Notably, Fe 2 O 3 /In 2 S 3 heterojunctions have demonstrated enhancement mechanisms for both photogenerated charge carrier separation and nonlinear optical response. However, their optoelectronic properties from a theoretical perspective and their potential in ultrafast photonics have not been extensively explored. Herein, robust S─O covalent-bonded Fe 2 O 3 /In 2 S 3 heterojunctions were successfully synthesized via heat treatment technology. First-principles calculations were conducted to examine thermal stability, electronic band structures, density of states distributions, electron localization functions, and dielectric responses, thereby establishing a fundamental understanding of intrinsic material properties while informing future optoelectronic implementations. By employing the Fe 2 O 3 /In 2 S 3 heterojunction in a fiber cavity with negative dispersion, passive mode-locking operation was realized, delivering a pulse width of 300 fs. Moreover, the incorporation of the Fe 2 O 3 /In 2 S 3 heterojunction into a net positive dispersion fiber cavity resulted in the achievement of mode-locked operation with a pulse duration of 123 fs. Compared with previous studies, these lasers show improved performance. This work advances the understanding of Fe 2 O 3 /In 2 S 3 structure-property relationships from a theoretical perspective and highlights their potential as promising nonlinear optical materials for advanced optoelectronic devices from an experimental standpoint.

10.1002/adfm.79449.title: Superior Capacitive Energy Storage in Lead-Free Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 -based Relaxors via High-Entropy Design
10.1002/adfm.79449.abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric capacitors are attractive for the high/pulsed power electronic systems owing to their ultrafast charging/discharging capability. Yet, the simultaneous achievement of high recoverable energy density ( W rec ) and efficiency ( η ) in lead-free relaxor ferroelectric (RFE) ceramics still remains a major challenge. Here, a high-entropy engineering in Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 -based RFE ceramics was proposed to construct heterogenous local structures, demonstrating an ultrahigh W rec of 13.7 J cm −3 and a high η of 86% under 780 kV cm −1 . Atomic-scale microstructure, along with the three-dimensional polar structure derived from neutron total scattering, revealed that the diversified A-site atoms increase the local chemical heterogeneity and lattice distortion of AO 12 cages, facilitating the formation of strong local clusters distributed in the matrix with weak polarity, thereby yielding enhanced relaxor behavior, reduced polarization hysteresis, and retained high polarization after applying an electric field. Moreover, the promoted insulating performance and significant reduced grain size result in a high endurance for external electric field. This work elucidates the roles of A-site atoms in the high-entropy effect, local lattice distortion, atomic polar displacement and energy storage properties, offering insights for the design of complex ferroelectrics with high-performance.

10.1002/adfm.79481.title: Analog-Tunable Nonvolatile Memristors with Self-Compliance Behavior via a MoS x -Interlayer Strategy for Neuromorphic Recognition and Zero-Trust Image Encryption
10.1002/adfm.79481.abstract: ABSTRACT The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfO x memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self-protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfO x /MoS x /HfO x trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self-compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero-trust XOR-based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near-optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoS x interlayer modification strategy to optimize high-performance artificial synapses on oxide memristors, enabling co-integration of neuromorphic computing and hardware security.

10.1002/adfm.79506.title: One-Component Carbon Dot Photoinitiator Enables High-Fidelity Digital Light Processing 3D Printing With Improved Mechanical Resistance
10.1002/adfm.79506.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient photoinitiators ( PIs ) from biomass for high-fidelity, robust, and bio-safe digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a unique one-component carbon dot-based PI ( CD - PO ), capable of high-fidelity DLP printing, is developed by grafting photocleavable diphenylacylphosphine oxide moieties onto the surface of CD s derived from renewable furfural. The nanostructured CD - PO effectively generates radicals to initiate the photopolymerization of acrylate monomers during DLP printing. Compared to conventional diphenyl(2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphine oxide ( TPO ) used in DLP printing, CD - PO achieves three breakthroughs: 1) CD - PO enables micron-scale printing precision by optimizing the photocuring depth; 2) CD - PO enhances mechanical resistance, as approved by the increased storage modulus at T g , with the resulting polymer network exhibiting a nano-composition reinforcement effect that leads to a toughness approximately 4.6 times that of the network photocured with petroleum-based TPO ; 3) The reduced migration of CD - PO components improves biological safety. The combined effectiveness of CD - PO in initiating photopolymerization, controlling curing depth, and reinforcing mechanical toughness ultimately enables high-fidelity DLP 3D-printing of diverse photoresins with structural complexity. In addition, CD - PO maintains high photoreactivity under aerobic conditions at low UV-LED intensity. This study demonstrates a robust strategy for designing one-component PI s incorporating biomass-derived components, further highlighting the versatility of biomass in photopolymerization-driven applications.

10.1002/adfm.79014.title: Universal Water-Based Hydrophilization of Non-Wettable Surfaces
10.1002/adfm.79014.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite water's central role as a universal solvent, many technologically and biologically relevant surfaces, including natural substrates, polymers, and electronic materials, present low-energy interfaces that resist aqueous wetting. We introduce here a universal, all-aqueous hydrophilization strategy based on regenerated silk fibroin (SF) pretreatment that renders diverse natural, living, and artificial substrates compatible with aqueous processing. Brief immersion or spraying with ultra-dilute (0.001−0.1 w/v%) SF solutions rapidly (5 s−5 min) induces surface wetting while preserving native morphology and function. This approach enables conformal coating and direct micro-patterning of a large library of water-dispersible materials across two- and three-dimensional hierarchically structured surfaces. The versatility of the method is demonstrated through aqueous coating of hydrophobic surfaces, including plants, vegetables, skin, feathers, hair, and synthetic substrates, as well as through direct patterning of deformable and wireless sensors on living systems. Leveraging the inherently benign properties of SF, including its edibility, biocompatibility, and aqueous processability, this approach yields a simple and scalable method for sustainable surface engineering with broad relevance to manufacturing, healthcare, food technology, and bioelectronics.

10.1002/adfm.79505.title: Oxygen-Rich Carbon Quantum Dots Enable Multiscale Synergistic Regulation for Ultralong-Life Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79505.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) is now threatened by irreversible parasitic processes at the Zn anode. Here we report a molecular-scale interfacial engineering strategy using oxygen-rich carbon quantum dots (o-CQDs, 38.83 wt% oxygen) that spontaneously self-assemble into a 2D ion-transport network in ZnSO 4 electrolyte. This architecture enables multiscale synergistic regulation. First, o-CQDs induce reconstitution of the primary solvation sheath into a stable [Zn(H 2 O) 4 (o-CQDs)] 2+ complex, reducing the desolvation barrier from 23.6 to 17.8 kJ mol −1 . Furthermore, the continuous 2D network elevates the Zn 2+ transference number from 0.51 to 0.85 and ionic conductivity enhanced from 40 to 93 mS cm −1 . At the electrode interface, a protective electric double layer promotes preferential Zn(002) deposition while effectively excluding reactive water species. Thus, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells achieve a long cycling life (>10 000 h) and high average Coulombic efficiency (99.6%). Full cells employing the commercial activated carbon as cathode retain >96.1% capacity after 100 000 cycles. More importantly, it can work in a wide temperature range from −10°C to 60°C, with obvious self-healing capability. This work establishes a synergistic regulation method by using a functional carbonic additive to optimize interfacial engineering to achieve durable zinc-based energy storage devices.

10.1002/adfm.79394.title: Hydrogel-Based Method for High-Resolution Measurements of Contact Mechanics in Rapid Biological Adhesives: A Case Study in Cuttlefish Tentacle Strikes
10.1002/adfm.79394.abstract: ABSTRACT Cuttlefish and squid attach to various substrates in their environment remarkably well using arms and extensible tentacles lined with arrays of suckers. Each sucker has a stiff internal ring with terminal teeth and microstructured rim. Previous studies have measured attachment forces of amputated suckers; however, in vivo investigations are lacking given the short time scales of attachment (milliseconds) and complex array geometries. To address this, we present a novel framework using a cross-linked and plasticized gelatin hydrogel mimicking the non-linear mechanical properties of prey tissues, high-speed videography to locate sucker contact points, and optical coherence tomography for 3D reconstruction of sucker imprints. Comparing in vivo imprints to ex vivo indentations with predefined loads allowed us to correlate imprint shape with normal, contact forces at the sucker rim. We show that cross-linking significantly increased the relaxation time of the hydrogel, essential for long-term imprint retention, while plasticization may have reduced self-healing by interfering with hydrogen-bond reformation. Such properties enabled observations of sucker attachment in vivo, which indicated that sucker arrays function probabilistically and that aiming and alignment are achieved through large numbers of high-safety-factor suckers. Our hydrogel provides a new approach to study biological small-scale attachment mechanisms in vivo.

10.1002/adfm.79484.title: Carbon-Shell-Confined Functional Silica Xerogels for Concurrent Lithium Dual-Mode Optical Detection and Seawater Recovery
10.1002/adfm.79484.abstract: ABSTRACT Rational material designs for lithium extraction from unconventional dilute resources have attracted attention to meet the rising demand. Here, a new multifunctional composite is developed that not only extracts lithium but also enables its concurrent optical detection. The material design integrates silica xerogel confined within hollow carbon spheres as a high-surface-area matrix, heteroatom-doped CDs as a fluorescence tag, and a covalently attached benzophenone-derived ligand as the lithium-binding site. This design also demonstrates an alternative detection paradigm in which a non-fluorogenic receptor coupled with matrix-confined CDs is used for optical signal transduction. In the presence of major seawater ions (Na + , Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ , K + ), the composite demonstrates selective dual-mode detection: naked-eye colorimetric and turn-on red luminescence with ultra-high sensitivity (LOD: 1.5 nM). The turn-on emission arises from disruption of the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) process upon Li + binding, which restores the intrinsic emission of the CDs. The flexible benzophenone-derived ligand enhances Li + binding stability, as supported by density functional theory (DFT) investigations. The adsorbent exhibits high lithium uptake (110 mg g −1 ), fast adsorption kinetics, and good recyclability, meeting key requirements for direct lithium extraction (DLE). Real seawater-system testing for lithium quantification and extraction highlights its potential for advancing integrated lithium detection-extraction technologies.

10.1002/adfm.79436.title: Separator-Mediated Pre-Desolvation Regulation via Oxygen-Doped Carbon Nitride for Efficient Sodium Storage in Hard Carbon
10.1002/adfm.79436.abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon (HC) is a highly promising anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its practical reversibility is still limited by uncontrolled electrolyte reduction at the HC/electrolyte interface. Herein, we developed a separator-mediated pre-desolvation regulation strategy via oxygen-doped carbon nitride (CNOI) modified separator that enables concurrent interfacial passivation and rapid Na + transport. The CNOI with abundant polar N/O sites electrostatically interacts with Na + and preconditions its local solvation environment before interfacial charge transfer. As a result, the Na + flux across the separator becomes more homogeneous, and the interfacial desolvation barrier is reduced, thereby promoting the in situ formation of a thin, ion-conductive SEI. Accordingly, HC|Na half-cells with the CNOI-modified separator exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 93.0%, sustain a capacity of 297.7 mAh g −1 after 600 cycles at 1 C, and deliver 247.3 mAh g −1 even at an elevated rate of 15 C. It also realizes remarkable low-temperature adaptability, delivering a capacity of 163.5 mAh g −1 at 0.5 C even at −40°C. This work establishes separator-driven pre-desolvation regulation as a transferable interfacial engineering strategy for high-performance HC anodes of practical sodium-ion batteries.

10.1002/adfm.79491.title: Bioinspired Microcone-Array-Based Eutectogel Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Self-Powered Dual-Modal Sensing and Human-Machine Interfaces
10.1002/adfm.79491.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible wearable sensors currently face challenges in terms of self-powering and human-machine interaction (HMI) capabilities. In order to cope with these challenges, through the utilization of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):lignosulfonate (PEDOT:LS) as a dynamic physical crosslinker, N-acryloylsemicarbazide-acrylic acid/PEDOT:LS (NAP) eutectogel is developed via multiple-crosslinking and direct deep eutectic solvent (DES) solvation strategies. A stable composite network is constructed within the eutectogel, which endows the gel with excellent stretchability (1559%), self-adhesiveness (244.8 kPa), self-healing, anti-freezing, and anti-drying capabilities. Therefore, the reliable monitoring of human motions and electrophysiological signals is ensured. Furthermore, a microcone-array-based single-electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (M-TENG) mimicking the setal structures of ant legs is designed, utilizing the NAP eutectogel as the back electrode. Favorable electrical outputs (196 V, 16.3 µA, and 452.2 mW/m 2 ) are delivered by the M-TENG, through which self-powered and dual-modal motion monitoring can be achieved. Finally, through the integration of the M-TENG onto a flexible fabric substrate, a wearable human-machine interface touch panel is constructed. Through this interactive system equipped with a password authentication mechanism, the secure remote control of a hexapod robot model is successfully achieved, demonstrating the potential of the system in unmanned search and rescue scenarios.

10.1002/adfm.79444.title: Highly Efficient and Stable Roll-to-Roll Coated Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Antisolvent Vapor-Assisted Crystallization
10.1002/adfm.79444.abstract: ABSTRACT A key challenge in roll-to-roll (R2R) perovskite solar cell (PSC) manufacturing is translating crystallization-control methods developed for laboratory-scale spin coating to scalable processes. Liquid antisolvent baths suffer from process drift due to contamination and generate substantial solvent waste, while gas-assisted quenching induces rapid nucleation with limited control over grain growth. Here, antisolvent vapor-assisted crystallization (AVAC) is demonstrated as a scalable strategy for controlling perovskite crystallization during R2R slot-die coating under ambient conditions. By regulating antisolvent vapor partial pressure within the coating zone, AVAC controls host-solvent extraction, limits moisture exposure, and promotes grain growth. One-step R2R coating of Cs 0 . 12 FA 0 . 88 PbI 3 films using AVAC produces pinhole-free, α-phase films with grain sizes exceeding 500 nm. Corresponding PSCs with evaporated gold electrodes achieve champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 18.3%, and 15.2% for fully R2R-processed PSCs with a carbon electrode. The latter retain 97% of their initial PCE after more than 550 h of maximum power point tracking under 1000 W m − 2 illumination in an inert atmosphere at 38°C ± 2°C and < 1% relative humidity. This performance ranks among the highest reported for R2R-processed PSCs. Technical challenges associated with antisolvent properties for AVAC are discussed and suitable candidates for R2R manufacturing are identified.

10.1002/adfm.79499.title: Dual-Interface Management Modulated by Functional Cationic Ligands Enables Robust and Efficient Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adfm.79499.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the effectiveness of surface passivation, simultaneous optimization of buried interface and top surface in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains challenging due to incompatible additive functions and uncontrolled crystallization kinetics. Here, we present a dual-interface regulation strategy that deploys phenyltrimethylammonium chloride (THPA) treatment on the top surface and 5-amino-1-pentanol (5-APT) treatment at the buried interface of the perovskite film. This approach achieves multiple collaborative regulation effects of dual interfaces: (i) THPA reduces trap density at the top surface of perovskites and promotes n-type character. (ii) 5-APT forms hydrogen and ionic bonds with the substrate, enhancing bottom crystallinity via cation exchange with FA + /Cs + and facilitating hole extraction. Besides, in-situ photoluminescence reveals that 5-APT retards the crystallization process, promoting grain merging and yielding uniformly sized grains. As a result, the optimized PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.24% with excellent stability. This straightforward strategy transcends conventional spacer cation engineering, bridging the efficiency-stability divide and providing a generalizable paradigm for interface passivation in perovskite optoelectronics.
authors: Dengxue Li, Hongyan Li, Yaochang Fei, Ting Hu, Wangping Sheng, Yiwang Chen

10.1002/adfm.79374.title: A Sustainable Fully Fluorine-Free Interfacial Chemistry for Reversible Anode-Free Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79374.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free lithium metal batteries promise high energy density. However, fluorinated electrolytes raise sustainability concerns. Herein, we develop a fully fluorine-free interfacial strategy by coupling a cross-linked vinylene carbonate-N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) on Cu current collectors with a fluorine-free electrolyte to regulate both lithium deposition and subsequent SEI formation. This combination offers an alternative to interfacial stabilization using fluorinated SEI-forming components or alloy-forming interlayers. The ASEI possesses strong Li-ASEI interactions and enhanced lithiophilicity, thereby enabling homogeneous and compact Li deposition with reduced growth overpotential. Furthermore, the ASEI induces the formation of a conformal, mechanically robust, inorganic-rich SEI containing Li 2 O and Li 3 N, leading to improved interfacial stability and the reversibility of Li plating/stripping. Consequently, the ASEI-modified current collector delivers markedly improved full-cell performance. The prelithiated LFP||ASEI-Cu full cell achieves stable cycling over 350 cycles with a capacity retention of 84.5% at 25°C, while the prelithiated NCM811||ASEI-Cu full cell delivers a reversible capacity of 146.8 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles with a capacity retention of 86.6% at 25°C. This work demonstrates the potential of fluorine-free interfacial engineering for anode-free lithium metal batteries, while further improvements in lithium-inventory retention and high-current-density operation remain necessary for practical implementation.
authors: Xuzhi Duan, Zihuan Min, Lingxi Zhou, Weijian Xu, Jiahui He, Wanqi Zhang, Songxin Lu, Kaicheng Zhang, Sikai Xiao, Lidong Tian, Qiuyu Zhang, Lei Tian

10.1002/adfm.79500.title: Ultra-Sensitive Reconfigurable SERS Platform Enabled by Tunable Plasmonic Nanogaps
10.1002/adfm.79500.abstract: ABSTRACT Plasmonic nanogaps that generate intense electromagnetic hot spots are crucial for surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing, particularly at the single-molecule level. However, plasmonic nanogaps in conventional SERS platforms are usually fixed, posing significant challenges for precise and ultra-sensitive molecular detection. Here, we propose a stretchable SERS platform, on which plasmonic nanogaps can be modulated stepwise, to sequentially control the trapping and deposition of target molecules, which are subsequently detected by significantly enhanced Raman signals. Functionalized with monodisperse silver nanoparticles, the platform enables reversible and precise bidirectional tuning of plasmonic nanogaps from nearly 400 nm down to sub-5 nm, endowing the SERS sensor with excellent sensitivity, robust reconfigurability, and broad detection versatility. SERS measurements on various small-molecule analytes achieve the lowest detectable concentrations of 10 −14 m (rhodamine 6G, R6G), 10 −12 m (4-Mercaptopyridine, 4-MPY), and 10 −5 m (urea and sodium lactate). The dual-analyte measurement confirms the single-molecule SERS detection capability. Meanwhile, large biomolecules (hemoglobin, Hb) detection down to a limit of 10 pg/mL further validates the reliability and universality of the developed SERS sensor. Our scheme paves the road for ultrasensitive detection of arbitrary molecules with robust reconfigurability.
authors: Jiaye Du, Ruirui Ren, Fengguang Shen, Jiajun Li, Leilei Hou, Jingjing Wei, Xiuying Liu, Ming Kang, Lei Zhou, Feifei Liu

10.1002/adfm.77762.title: Synergistic Photothermal and Superhydrophobic Metasurface for Passive Radiative Cooling and Anti-/Deicing
10.1002/adfm.77762.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling offers a sustainable pathway for building thermal regulation without energy input, however, the sub-ambient surface temperatures inevitably promote ice nucleation and accretion in cold climates, creating a fundamental seasonal conflict. In this work, we address this seasonal limitation by hierarchically engineering a synergistic photothermal and superhydrophobic metasurface (SFPS film) that delivers efficient radiative cooling in summer while enabling anti-icing and de-icing in winter. The SFPS film integrates self-assembled hollow glass bead/nano-SiO 2 supraballs for Mie scattering, a PDMS matrix with pyramidal microstructures for emissivity enhancement, and SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 nanospheres with superhydrophobic coating for photothermal conversion and water repellency. The SFPS film exhibits a solar reflectivity of 88%, which is lower than the 97% of the Pyramid-PDMS/Supraballs film due to absorption by the SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 , while maintaining an atmospheric window emissivity of 96%, enabling sub-ambient cooling of 4°C-6°C under outdoor summer conditions. In winter, the durable superhydrophobic surface together with the photothermal effect synergistically delays freezing by a factor of 4.6 and cuts melting time by 51% compared to bare glass, while also reducing ice adhesion strength to ∼25 kPa. This multifunctional metasurface offers a promising pathway toward all-season passive thermal management for buildings, transportation, and outdoor infrastructure.

10.1002/adfm.77738.title: Biomimetic Polymer Membrane for Precise Ion Separation in Selective Electrodialysis
10.1002/adfm.77738.abstract: ABSTRACT Electric-driven membranes featuring precise ion transport are extensively employed in energy and environmental science. Although separation performance has been significantly improved, the structural requirements for treating high-salinity salt-lake brines via selective electrodialysis (S-ED) remain ambiguous. Herein, we exploit the differential reactivity of carboxyl and aldehyde groups in D-glucuronic acid toward the abundant amino groups of polyethyleneimine. Combined with the monomer sustained-release effect of the porous TpPa interlayer, this approach enables the construction of a biomimetic separation layer that possesses a dense surface and continuous internal Li + -conducting channels. These continuous pathways, rich in carboxyl moieties, enlarge the activation free-energy barrier difference for Li + and Mg 2+ transport from 4.03 to 4.94 kJ·mol −1 . Such energetic differentiation emulates biological ion channels, wherein carboxyl groups selectively promote Li + transit while imposing a pronounced energetic penalty on heavily hydrated Mg 2+ . Consequently, the membrane exhibits cell-membrane-mimetic selectivity, delivering a Li + /Mg 2+ perm-selectivity of 22.7 and a Li flux of 4.88 × 10 −8 mol·cm −2 ·s −1 , outperforming the current upper-bound benchmark. Notably, the step-current S-ED process attains 78.45% Li + recovery from a simulated brine containing 106.74 g/L Mg 2+ and a Mg/Li mass ratio of 31.58. This work provides new insights into S-ED membrane fabrication and process design for practical scalability.

10.1002/adfm.79511.title: Ion-Modulated All-Van Der Waals Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Tunnel Junctions With Multilevel Switching
10.1002/adfm.79511.abstract: ABSTRACT Advancing van der Waals (vdW) spintronics requires hardware for multistate storage and in-memory processing. All-vdW spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs) that simultaneously achieve field-free operation and multilevel switching have remained elusive. Here, we report an ion-modulated all-vdW SOT-MTJ with a stack structure of WTe 2 /Fe 3 GaTe 2 /WSe 2 /Fe 3 GaTe 2 /CuInP 2 S 6 (CIPS). We then apply pulsed currents along the crystallographic a -axis of WTe 2 , which produce field-free deterministic SOT switching with ultralow critical current density of 2-5 × 10 6 A/cm 2 at 300 K, and excite resistance changes at the MTJ. The SOT efficiency of WTe 2 is ∼0.35. The CIPS ion modulator enables localized Cu + migration and accumulation at the interface under a lateral electric field, thereby destroying the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of the adjacent reference layer and inducing an intermediate resistance state in the MTJ. These ion-modulated devices exhibit tunneling magnetoresistance ranging from 0.2% to 5%. This work addresses the integration challenges of all-vdW SOT-MTJs and demonstrates multilevel switching controlled by a solid-state ion source in this architecture, generating three distinct nonvolatile resistance levels that serve as ternary connection weights in a neural network for image recognition. These results establish a scalable platform for low-current switching, multilevel storage, and image recognition, promising energy-efficient in-memory computing.
