10.1002/adfm.77850.title: Flexible Mechanical Metamaterials With Unusual Dual-Plateau Negative Poisson's Ratio Responses Under Large Deformation
10.1002/adfm.77850.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible mechanical metamaterials with stable negative Poisson's ratios hold great promise for applications in flexible electronics. Nevertheless, most existing stretchable auxetic designs rely on single or strongly coupled deformation modes, which confine their mechanical responses to only one stable state and restrict their functional versatility. A dual-plateau Poisson's ratio characteristic that enables strain-switchable and bi-stable Poisson's ratio states has rarely been reported in previous studies. This work introduces a new class of flexible mechanical metamaterials based on rotating soft network structures (RSNSs), where deformable network units replace the rigid plate units in traditional rotating rigid structures. Owing to a unique multi-stage deformation mechanism, the proposed RSNS metamaterials exhibit an unusual strain-switchable dual-plateau negative Poisson's ratio response under large tensile deformation. The dual-plateau Poisson's ratio characteristic is accurately captured by FEA simulations and can be systematically tuned through rational design of structural geometries. The RSNS metamaterials can be constructed by modular assembly of discrete rotating units using physical pin-based hinges or by one-step fabrication employing a living-hinge design. Finally, a class of RSNS-based stretchable luminescent devices is demonstrated, exhibiting strain-controlled optical information switching performance, with each stable working state sustained over a finite continuous strain range.

10.1002/adfm.77909.title: Pore-Surface Charge Engineered Anion-Pillared MOFs With Tailored Electronegative Narrow Windows for Simultaneous Thermodynamic and Kinetic Separation of MTO Products
10.1002/adfm.77909.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of separable adsorbents for the efficient separation of ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) and propylene (C 3 H 6 ) from methanol-to-olefin (MTO) products is regarded as a sustainable approach to supply vital industrial feedstocks, thus holding critical significance. Herein, we synthesized a new material SIFSIX-DPU-Cu using 1,3-di(pyridin-4-yl) urea (DPU) ligand for the separation of MTO products (C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures), and which features the scarcely explored characters concurrently integrating rich F-containing [Cu 4 (μ 3 -F) 4 ] 2+ cation clusters and SiF 6 2− anion pillars. By constructing continuous electronegative pore surfaces with rich active sites and dumbbell-shaped pores, the material can preferentially adsorb C 3 H 6 rather than C 2 H 4 and exhibit significantly high C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 adsorption selectivity. The dynamic breakthrough experiment on equimolar C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures shows that following one separation cycle at 298 K, SIFSIX-DPU-Cu enables to separate and produce 38.3 L kg −1 C 2 H 4 (purity ≥ 99.95%) and 46.2 L kg −1 C 3 H 6 (purity ≥ 99.5%) simultaneously. Experimental results based on single crystal analysis together with simulations reveal an uncommon simultaneous thermodynamic and kinetic separation mechanism in which the narrow pore window and enlarged F-rich cavity synergistically generate restricted binding sites, leading to significant selectivity in the competitive adsorption of C 3 H 6 over C 2 H 4 .

10.1002/adfm.78164.title: Reconfigurable Noise-Spectroscopy Physical Unclonable Function in Floating-Body Charge-Trap-Flash Transistors
10.1002/adfm.78164.abstract: ABSTRACT Resource-constrained edge and Internet-of-Things devices require hardware roots of trust that are compact, reconfigurable and compatible with large-scale manufacturing. However, many physical unclonable functions (PUFs) rely on fixed post-fabrication variability, limiting their adaptability once challenge-response information is exposed. Here we report a reconfigurable noise-spectroscopy PUF (NS-PUF) implemented in a floating-body charge-trap-flash (FB-CTF) transistor that builds on technologically mature silicon transistor. In this device, low-frequency noise (LFN) acts as a spectrally amplified entropy source: minute process-induced variations in defects, electrostatics and body relaxation are transformed into multidimensional power spectral density fingerprints rather than a single scalar electrical shift. The CTF gate stack provides a nonvolatile internal state that remaps these spectral fingerprints under the same external read condition. This co-integrated architecture supports two security modes: (1) Multiple cells can generate conventional bitmap-type PUF responses through relative PSD ordering, while (2) a single addressed transistor, or a small number of devices, can be authenticated directly by matching enrolled PSD phenotypes for dynamic PUF verification. Thus, authentication can be scaled not only by increasing array size or bit-string length, but also by exploiting the spectral depth of individual reconfigurable transistors. The proposed reconfigurable NS-PUF demonstrates that LFN, once treated as an undesirable noise source, and mature charge-trap memory functionality can be repurposed within commercially established transistor technologies as adaptive security primitives, providing a scalable route toward reconfigurable PUFs for future edge and IoT systems.

10.1002/adfm.79255.title: A Nonlinear Organic Low-Frequency Sound Sensor Based on Electrochemical Coupling in a Solidified Gel Membrane
10.1002/adfm.79255.abstract: ABSTRACT Measuring low-frequency or infrasound acoustic signals plays a crucial role in the monitoring of natural disasters, structural health, and predictive maintenance of critical energy structures. Smart sound sensing systems often consist of linear sound sensors coupled to a separate processing unit, nonlinearly transforming the signal to solve the given task. However, nonlinear sensors have seen increased scientific interest in fields like reservoir computing, with the goal of minimizing power consumption by implementing the signal processing in the sensor itself. Here, the use of an organic electrochemical transistor based on conductive polymeric fibers embedded inside a free-standing solidified gel membrane as a robust, highly sensitive, and nonlinear low-frequency sound sensor is demonstrated. The slow dynamics of the device allow sensing in the low-frequency and infrasound regime with a cutoff-frequency at around with power consumptions below . Our work further demonstrates that the introduction of a gating mechanism increases sensitivity, nonlinearity, and stability compared to a previously introduced linear two-terminal sensors. As a demonstration, we show that a three-terminal device contains sufficient information to classify spoken digits from ten classes, using in-software reservoir computing.
authors: Maarten Mittmann, Carsten Habenicht, Andreas Hofacker, Richard Kantelberg, Stefan Jacob, Karl Leo, Hans Kleemann

10.1002/adfm.79537.title: Intrinsically Self-Assembled SrFeOx Topotactic Phase Transition Memristor
10.1002/adfm.79537.abstract: ABSTRACT Topotactic phase-transition (TPT) oxide memristors contain ordered 1D oxygen-vacancy channels (OVCs) that enable anisotropic oxygen-ion migration and reversible brownmillerite/perovskite transition, offering a materials platform for neuromorphic computing. However, the lack of spatially predefined oxygen-ion migration sites in conventional TPT films promotes stochastic perovskite SrFeO 3 conductive filament (CF) growth, compromising the response stability and state distinguishability required for reliable temporal signal processing. Here, a single-component self-assembled SrFeO x memristor with alternating vertical and horizontal superlattice-like OVC regions is reported. Structural characterization, density functional theory calculations, and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations indicate that this intrinsic self-assembled architecture directs oxygen-ion migration through vertical channels while horizontal regions restrict stray out-of-plane transport, promoting localized CF growth. The device combines forming-free bipolar switching, an ON/OFF ratio of ∼4.4 × 10 3 , low cycle-to-cycle (C2C) variation with CV(V SET )/CV(V RESET ) of 3.2%/0.6%, 16-state retention over 10 4 s, and endurance up to 10 7 pulse cycles. Reproducible device-to-device (D2D) switching is obtained across 32 cells, with D2D CV(V SET )/CV(V RESET ) values of 10.1%/5.9%. Finally, the device's short-term memory transforms temporal inputs into distinguishable states that a fixed linear readout decodes with 84.59% accuracy on a temporal classification task. This work highlights intrinsic OVC-orientation engineering as a materials-level strategy toward reliable single-component TPT memristors.
authors: Runqing Zhang, Kai Huang, Dunbao Chen, Weiming Cheng, Rui Su, Xiangshui Miao, Lei Ye

10.1002/adfm.79523.title: Ordered Macroporous Prussian Blue Analogues for Rechargeable Na-Cl2 Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79523.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable Na-Cl 2 batteries have emerged as a promising alternative and supplement for lithium-ion batteries due to their ultra-high energy density. Nevertheless, developing satisfactory cathode materials to facilitate the complex solid, liquid, and gas three-phase conversion process during charge-discharge cycling remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a three-dimensional ordered macroporous Prussian blue analog (3DOM PBA) fabricated via a stepwise vacuum impregnation template strategy, which can serve as an ideal cathode material for rechargeable Na-Cl 2 batteries. The hierarchically ordered porous structure arranging from micropores to macropores can provide appropriated channels for ions transfer, Cl 2 storage, and NaCl crystal deposition. Moreover, customizable metal site doping not only optimize the electronic and ionic conductivity but also provide efficient adsorption and in-situ catalytic conversion sites for Cl 2 /Cl − , thereby effectively increasing the reversible reaction kinetics and long-term cycling stability. As a result, the assembled Na-Cl 2 battery delivers a reversible capacity of 2000 mAh g − 1 and stable cycling life of 2500 cycles at 15 000 mA g − 1 , which can still maintain reversible charge-discharge behavior even at 30 000 mA g − 1 , much superior to the reported results. This study provides new insights for developing high-performance electrode materials for rechargeable Na-Cl 2 batteries.
authors: Xiang Yu, Boman Li, Lingling Ling, Zhenyang Meng, Ziming Qiu, Yuanhang Xu, Shaopeng Deng, Xiuyun Zhang, Shouyin Cai, Hsiao-Chien Chen, Yecan Pi, Zheng Liu, Huan Pang

10.1002/adfm.79482.title: Electrically Reconfigurable Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect in Centrosymmetric Dirac Semimetal SrIrO3 at Room Temperature
10.1002/adfm.79482.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-charge interconversion mediated by spin-orbit interaction represents a central concept in modern spintronics. The efficiency of spin-charge interconversion is conventionally estimated from the Berry curvature of Bloch states within the linear-response regime. Besides the linear regime, recent studies have uncovered nonlinear spin-charge conversion arising from higher-order electric-field terms in noncentrosymmetric materials with nontrivial spin textures. Hence, harnessing and controlling such nonlinear responses promise opportunities for designable and reconfigurable nonlinear spintronic devices. Here, we report the nonlinear planar Hall effect in topological semimetal SrIrO 3 (001) thin film, enabled by inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface. Furthermore, systematic transport measurements reveal robust second-order electrical transport that can be dynamically and reversibly tuned by ionic-liquid gating. This tunability originates from gating-induced structural reconstruction, valence-state modulation, and oxygen-vacancy formation, which modify the interfacial inversion-symmetry breaking and consequently reshape the band structure. These findings establish an effective electrical route for controlling nonlinear planar Hall responses through ionic engineering of spin texture in momentum space and provide a promising platform for reconfigurable nonlinear spintronic applications.
authors: Taiyu An, Mingfang Zhang, Jifan Hu

10.1002/adfm.79529.title: Molecular Polarization Engineering Homogenizes Interfacial Potential for Long-Life Wide-Temperature Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79529.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium dendrite formation in solid-state lithium metal batteries originates not only from mechanical failure but also from spatially heterogeneous interfacial electrostatic fields that induce localized Li + accumulation. However, existing electrolyte designs mainly regulate mechanical strength or chemical interfacial reactions, while dynamic regulation of interfacial electrostatic disorder remains unexplored. Here, we introduce an interfacial potential homogenization enabled by polarization-mediated regulation. A molecularly entangled PEO/polyurethane/MOF-177 electrolyte is constructed, where polar polymer networks and MOF polarization domains cooperatively redistribute local electric-field fluctuations. This electrostatic regulation homogenizes Li + flux, lowers migration barriers, and suppresses preferential lithium nucleation. Consequently, CPEZ exhibits an ionic conductivity of 1.9 × 10 −3 S cm −1 and a Li + transference number of 0.71, both measured at 60°C. The Li/CPEZ/Li cell cycles stably for 9000 h at 0.1 mAh cm −2 . The Li/CPEZ/LFP retains 90 % capacity after 5000 at 1 C, while Li/CPEZ/LFP retains 85% capacity after 500 cycles at 100°C and cycles stably for 150 cycles at −15°C. This work establishes electrostatic regulation via polar interactions as a transferable design principle for durable, wide-temperature solid-state lithium metal batteries.
authors: Dajiang Tang, Yiwen Zhang, Xiaoyang Du, Cai-jun Zheng, Yongbing Tang, Silu Tao

10.1002/adfm.79487.title: Freeform 3D Printing of Omnidirectionally Deformable Conductors via Newtonian Liquid Metal Droplet-Mediated Stress Relaxation
10.1002/adfm.79487.abstract: ABSTRACT Next-generation soft robotics and shape-morphing electronics demand materials that possess intrinsic softness yet processable into freeform 3D architectures. However, direct-write 3D printing of soft elastomers suffers from a rheological trade-off, where high yield stress required for printability increases stiffness. This work presents a ternary silicone elastomer ink that breaks this limitation by incorporating liquid metal (LM) as a Newtonian liquid filler. The fluidic LM droplets act as stress buffers, accelerating stress relaxation during flow without compromising post-curing compliance. Additionally, they induce an excluded-volume effect that increases the effective local concentration of the dispersed multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), thereby enhancing the percolating conductive network. This strategy enables support-free 3D printing, achieving maximum bridging spans of 32 mm and a peak resolution of 124 µm independently. The composite exhibits high stretchability (446% elongation), a bulk conductivity of 7.08 S/m, and electrical stability under large deformation (∆R/R 0 = 0.51 at 100% strain). The versatility of this platform was further validated through reconfigurable 3D circuits, demonstrating that in addition to functioning as compliant conductors, the printed structures can also serve as robust load-bearing structural elements. By reconciling printability, softness, and deformation-tolerant electrical conductivity, this work establishes a general approach for freeform 3D soft electronics.
authors: Tianqi Pang, Yaxin Zhang, Yuhan Jiang, Xinying Li, Miao Yu, Xiang Lin, Fengxian Gao, Min Gong, Dongrui Wang, Liang Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79517.title: Wireless Electrical Stimulation via Piezoelectric Nanogenerator for Parkinson's Disease Therapy Through Activating Calcium Channels and Mitigating Oxidative Damage
10.1002/adfm.79517.abstract: ABSTRACT The primary pathological hallmarks of Parkinson's disease (PD) comprise the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and abnormal accumulation of α-synuclein, accompanied by severe oxidative damage due to excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). Clinical electrical stimulation therapies pose invasive risks from long-term electrode implantation with neuroinflammation side effects, while antioxidant drugs for scavenging brain ROS also fail to meet clinical demands due to poor blood-brain barrier permeability and short half-lives. Herein, we report a brain-targeted piezoelectric nanogenerator (PEL) for wireless electrotherapy for PD. Under ultrasonic stimulation, the piezoelectrically induced output current generated by the PEL promotes voltage-gated calcium channel-mediated calcium influx, upregulating tyrosine hydroxylase expression to promote dopamine synthesis. Concurrently, acting as a piezoelectric catalyst, the PEL rapidly decomposes water to continuously release hydrogen, which scavenges excess ROS and mitigates oxidative damage. In the mouse model of PD, the ultrasound-responsive PEL nanogenerator alleviated the symptoms of the disease without causing obvious toxicity. This synergistic approach targeting ion channels and hydrogen therapy may inspire the development of other minimally invasive therapeutic strategies for PD.

10.1002/adfm.79460.title: Spatially Programmed 3D-Bioprinted Tumor-Stromal Assembloids Reveal Progressive Microenvironmental Remodeling and Phase-Dependent Drug Responses in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
10.1002/adfm.79460.abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular csarcinoma (HCC) progression is driven by dynamic interactions between cancer cells and stromal fibroblasts that evolve with spatial proximity and physical association. However, conventional co-culture models either combine these populations from the outset or maintain them in permanent separation, limiting compartment-specific analysis of their progressive interaction. Here, we develop a distance-programmed tumor-stromal assembloid platform in which tumor and stromal microtissues are bioprinted at defined surface-to-surface separations. We engineer a collagen-alginate hybrid bioink that restrains spreading, promotes cell-cell cohesion, and preserves discrete tumor and stromal compartments throughout assembly, while interface angle and neck length quantify structural integration, which TGF-β1 accelerates. Compartment-specific tracking resolves a graded E-cadherin-to-N-cadherin transition within the tumor compartment together with progressive activation and spatial expansion of the stromal compartment. Paracrine signaling, fibroblast activation, matrix remodeling, and drug-resistance programs predominate at distinct phases, producing phase-dependent responses to pathway-specific inhibition combined with doxorubicin. Modular repetition of these units extends assembly across a large spatial field, yielding an interconnected centimeter-scale array with high viability. This platform couples compartment-resolved analysis of tumor-stromal remodeling with a scalable route to macroscale tumor tissues.

10.1002/adfm.79519.title: Grape Cluster Inspired Biomimetic Composite Solid Electrolyte for High-Voltage and Long-Life Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79519.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state lithium metal batteries suffer from poor interfacial stability and dendrite growth, primarily limited by the ion transport kinetics and mechanical properties of composite solid electrolytes (CSE). Inspired by the hierarchical grape cluster, we design a biomimetic electrolyte via electrospinning PAN fiber “pedicel” integrated with mesoporous SiO 2 -SO 3 Li “grape berry” fillers, followed by in-situ polymerization. This structure establishes long-range Li + conduction channels and a robust physical barrier, delivering a high Li + transference number of 0.65, ionic conductivity of 1.44 × 10 −3 S cm −1 at 25°C, and a modulus of 520 MPa. Benefiting from these advantages, the assembled LFP|Li and NCM811|Li cells achieve 88.8% capacity retention after 1000 cycles and 94.3% after 300 cycles, respectively. Moreover, a high-loading pouch cell realizes an energy density of 414.9 Wh kg −1 /797.8 Wh L −1 and withstands harsh abuse tests. Mechanistically, DFT and phase-field simulations reveal the dual Li + pathways and TFSI − immobilization enabled by the -SO 3 Li groups. Notably, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework decouples interface activation-aging kinetics and predicts long-term impedance evolution. This work provides a biomimetic paradigm and data-driven methods for the design and interface analysis of high-performance CSE.

10.1002/adfm.79549.title: A Fluorinated 3D Interphase With Built-In Si-Gradient Lithiophilicity Enables Spatially Adaptive Li Deposition for Stable Li Metal Anode
10.1002/adfm.79549.abstract: ABSTRACT Li metal anodes, sought after for next-generation high-energy batteries, are severely hindered by dendritic growth and an unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Here, we design a fluorinated 3D artificial SEI with a built-in vertical Si-gradient lithiophilicity (3D F-SiG SEI) via in situ copolymerization of hexafluorobutyl methacrylate and 2,4,6,8-tetramethyl-2,4,6,8-tetraethynylcyclotetrasiloxane. Critically, this crosslinking reaction proceeds exclusively under the catalytic action of the Li metal substrate, ensuring seamless interfacial integration. The resulting porous SEI generates a continuous lithiophilicity gradient that homogenizes Li + flux, enforces “bottom-up” pore-filling deposition, and buffers volume fluctuations. Simultaneously, the F/Si-rich chemistry promotes in situ formation of a stable LiF-enriched Si-based SEI, which reduces the nucleation overpotential and accelerates interfacial kinetics. The modified anode delivers an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% in half cells and ultralong cycling stability over 3500 h in symmetric cells. Full cells paired with LiFePO 4 and high-nickel NCM cathodes exhibit superior capacity retention and rate capability even under high mass loading. This work provides a blueprint for simultaneously engineering interfacial deposition, buffering volume fluctuations, and enhancing air stability in practical Li metal anodes.

10.1002/adfm.79559.title: High-Entropy Sulfides Enable Dual-Pathway Sulfur Conversion in PEO-Based All-Solid-State Li-S Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79559.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) are promising for safe, high-energy storage, but their development is limited by lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) dissolution and shuttle effect in poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolytes, leading to sluggish sulfur conversion and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we report a dual-phase high-entropy sulfide system (HES, FeCoNiCuMoS x ) nanoflowers as a multifunctional sulfur host. Owing to lattice distortion and strong d-p orbital coupling, HES exhibits strong chemical affinity toward LiPSs and accelerates sulfur conversion. Importantly, the dual-phase HES enables a dual-pathway sulfur reduction reaction, in which a restrained LiPSs-mediated “liquid”-phase route sustains kinetics, while a dominant “solid-solid” (S to Li 2 S) pathway fundamentally blocks LiPSs dissolution and shuttling. As a result, the S@HES cathode delivers a high specific capacity of 1319.3 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and maintains remarkable cycling stability with a low capacity decay rate of only 0.0458% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C, along with stable electrochemical performance over the investigated temperature range of 40°C to 60°C. Furthermore, S@HES-based pouch cells exhibit excellent mechanical flexibility and deliver a high initial capacity of 1365.8 mAh g − 1 with stable cycling performance, collectively underscoring the strong potential of this dual-pathway regulation strategy for practical advanced ASSLSBs.

10.1002/adfm.79531.title: Surfactant Induces Uniform and Stable Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79531.abstract: ABSTRACT Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have been extensively studied in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Nevertheless, the aggregation tendency of SAM molecules results in non-uniform deposition and inadequate substrate coverage, thereby severely impeding device performance. Herein, we introduce a multifunctional additive, nonafluorobutane-1-sulfonic acid (PFBS), to actively regulate the growth of SAM layers. Our investigations reveal that PFBS suppresses the self-aggregation of SAM molecules through hydrogen bonding and steric disruption, thus promoting their dispersion in the solution and facilitating the exposure of anchoring groups. The PFBS-modified SAM exhibits improved coverage, robustness, and interfacial energy-level alignment. Furthermore, PFBS effectively passivates interfacial defects, reduces non-radiative recombination, and promotes the growth of high-quality perovskite film. Consequently, the PFBS-optimized PSC with a 1.68 eV bandgap delivers a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24% and significantly enhanced stability. This work presents an additive-induced ordering strategy, providing a scalable route for high-performance PSCs and tandem photovoltaics.

10.1002/adfm.79132.title: Controlling Structure and Stability in Ultrathin Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Multilayers for Hydrogen Gas Barrier Applications
10.1002/adfm.79132.abstract: ABSTRACT Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene is a promising 2D nanofiller for gas barrier composites. However, controlling the composite's nanoscale structure and ensuring its stability in harsh thermal environments remain significant challenges. This study compares the multilayer properties, morphology, and hydrogen (H 2 ) gas barrier performance of two different MXene-based layer-by-layer (LbL) assemblies, demonstrating the influence of polymer content and complementary positively charged assembling species. LbL assembly effectively promotes brick-and-mortar-like multilayer ordering of MXene in nanoscale thin films, but the method requires positively charged species to electrostatically assemble with negatively charged MXene. Using either reduced graphene oxide (rGO) precomplexed with a polycation (rGO-PDDA) or positively charged MXene (f-MXene) functionalized with [3-(2-aminoethylamino)-propyl] trimethoxysilane (AEAPTMS) as the complementary species, the two MXene-based multilayers show strikingly different behaviors at elevated temperatures. Structural and chemical characterization shows that only the rGO-PDDA/MXene multilayer maintains electrostatic bonding, leading to improved stability and performance in harsh conditions. In films as thin as 43 nm, the LbL multilayers retain their performance. The rGO-PDDA/MXene multilayer exhibits low H 2 gas permeability (7.13 ± 0.09 × 10 −11 m 3 ·m·m −2 ·atm −1 ·day −1 ) even at 400°C. This study offers insightful guidelines for the rational design of MXene- or polymer-based composite films for gas barrier applications in extreme temperatures.

10.1002/adfm.79541.title: Staged Orientation-Controlled Epitaxy of Organic Low-Dimensional Heterostructures
10.1002/adfm.79541.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic low-dimensional heterostructures (OLDHs) possess remarkable optoelectronic properties, positioning them as candidates for next-generation optoelectronic integrated systems. While epitaxial self-assembly enables efficient preparation, ensuring precise orientation during heteroepitaxial growth remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, a staged orientation controlled epitaxial growth strategy is developed to obtain OLDHs composed of two 4H-Cyclopenta[2,1-b:3,4-b']dithiophene (CDT)-based cocrystals. Importantly, each epitaxy stage is governed by in-plane molecular spacing matching relationships between multiple crystal-plane combinations, which allows for the controllable relative position and continuously adjustable epitaxy-length of axial/lateral OLDHs by regulating the material ratio ( R = n CB / n CQ ) of the heterogenous components. The fabricated OLDHs exhibit promising functionalities as optical filters and multi-channel optical routing by exploiting energy transfer and photon propagation within the heterostructures. This strategy provides a crucial pathway for controllable epitaxial self-assembly, thereby shedding light on the synthesis methodology of OLDHs.

10.1002/adfm.79504.title: Crystalline Seed Identity Selects Assembly Topology in Silk Fibroin
10.1002/adfm.79504.abstract: ABSTRACT Protein nanofibrils assemble hierarchically, yet directing the mesoscale topology that connects fibrillar growth to network mechanics remains challenging. Here, we show that crystalline seed identity redirects regenerated silk fibroin assembly while retaining a common silk II packing motif. Top-down silk nanocrystals promote core-arm units with dense cores and radiating fibrillar arms, whereas seed-free assembly and length-matched bottom-up nanofibril seeds yield predominantly linear structures. Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy and spectroscopy reveal preorganized, β-sheet-rich fibrillar bundles within the seeds. Time-resolved imaging supports a mechanism in which these scaffolds accommodate multiple local growth regions, followed mainly by arm elongation. Composition-dependent morphologies are consistent with precursor allocation among these regions, linking seed abundance to arm length and assembly-unit density. At matched solids content, core-arm gels enter the flow regime at lower strains than linear gels while retaining substantial modulus recovery after repeated high-strain deformation. Idealized network simulations suggest that multivalent cores preserve global connectivity while shorter reconstruction pathways facilitate reversible bridge exchange. These findings establish crystalline seed interfaces as topology-selecting elements in protein assembly and provide a strategy for constructing thixotropic and injectable protein materials without additional chemical cross-linking.

10.1002/adfm.79496.title: 3D Solar-Driven Interfacial Evaporator Based on Tailored TiO 2 Nanotube Arrays by Wireless Anodizing for Efficient Desalination
10.1002/adfm.79496.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar-driven interfacial evaporation is an energy-efficient desalination strategy. However, the existing solar-driven interfacial evaporators mostly rely on a surface-localized photothermal layer for heat confinement, which limits evaporation exclusively to the top surface. The internal transfer channels and potential evaporation area remain unexplored, restricting water production rates. Here, a wireless anodization with a composite bipolar electrode has been proposed to prepare completely internal anodized porous Ti with TiO 2 nanotube (TNT) arrays, serving for 3D solar-driven interfacial evaporation. By regulating the reaction area and intensity, the TiO 2 nanotubes (TNTs) with tailored size (diameter of 120-170 nm, length of 3-10 µm) have successfully anisotropically grown on the porous Ti substrates, constructing internal interconnected channels. The obtained wireless anodized porous Ti (WAPT) possessed an increased surface area of 7.938 m 2 ·g −1 , as well as solar absorbance >80%, superhydrophilicity (totally wetting within 10 s), and low evaporation enthalpy (451.83 kJ·kg −1 ), making efficient water evaporation with larger evaporation area and lower energy consumption possible. Under one-sun irradiation, the WAPT showed an evaporation rate of 1.68 kg·m −2 ·h −1 with no salt crystallization and could maintain over 30 days. By assembling the WAPTs into a 3D interfacial evaporator, cooperated with wind-driven cold evaporation, the maximum evaporation rate reached 2.412 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . In outdoor conditions (solar intensity of 0.6 kW·m −2 at 12 pm), the water collection rate reached 1.59 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . This work should make possible the development of a high-performance solar-driven interfacial evaporator for various applications.

10.1002/adfm.79477.title: Lanthanide MOF-Perovskite Quantum-Cutting Circularly Polarized Emitters for Vital Sensing and AI-Assisted Emotion Recognition
10.1002/adfm.79477.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely deployed in catalysis, separation and chemical sensing, yet luminescent MOFs, especially those emitting near-infrared (NIR) circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), remain largely underexplored. Here, we address this critical gap through a hierarchical dual-sphere engineering strategy to fabricate luminescent Eu-Yb-BTC MOFs, wherein L-phenylalanine serves as a second-sphere modulator to construct low-symmetry chiral microenvironments surrounding lanthanide centers. Subsequent hybridization with Yb-doped perovskite quantum dots synergistically enhances both quantum-cutting efficiency and CPL performance, yielding a 170% enhancement in the 980 nm Yb 3+ emission, an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 154%, and a luminescence dissymmetry factor of -1.58 × 10 −2 . Leveraging its single-source RED-NIR dual-band CPL output, whose inherent polarization selectivity suppresses stray light and ambient background noise to enable more accurate blood oxygen monitoring, we demonstrate a portable blood oxygen sensor with 15 s response and <1.5% measurement error, and further develop an AI-assisted emotion recognition framework based on dual-channel photoplethysmography signals. This work establishes a versatile design paradigm for high-performance chiral luminescent MOFs, opening new avenues for next-generation wearable biomedical diagnostics and edge-AI-enabled healthcare.

10.1002/adfm.79514.title: Interfacial Charge Dynamics and Polarization Coupling in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystal Tailored PVDF Composite Films for High-Performance Organic Triboelectric Nanogenerator-Based Electromechanical Energy Harvesting
10.1002/adfm.79514.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing soft and conformable materials with enhanced charge generation and retention capabilities remains a critical barrier for next-generation flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Here, we report a polarization-coupled tribo-negative film fabricated by integrating a room-temperature ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (FNLC) material (FNLC-1571) into an electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) mat. In contrast to traditional rigid fillers, the optimally engineered ferroelectric nematic phase (N F ) of FNLC-1571 microdomains assists spontaneous soft polar ordering in the nanofibrous PVDF matrix. This facilitates the integration of dipolar interactions with the fluorinated ends of PVDF, thereby synergistically promoting the crystallization of the electroactive β-phase, enhancing dielectric behavior, modulating surface potential, improving interfacial charge-trapping ability, and increasing contact area for superior charge generation while maintaining mechanical flexibility. When paired with a polyethylenimine (PEI)-coated polyamide-6 (PA-6) tribo-positive counter layer, the optimized 1 wt.% FNLC/PVDF-based TENG delivers stable electrical output under low-amplitude mechanical periodic contact-separation excitation (8N, 10 Hz), with a peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage of ∼395 V, a short-circuit current of ∼40 µA, and a transferred charge of ∼167 nC. Finally, the optimally engineered all-organic TENG assemblies were employed for various practical applications by demonstrating efficient capacitor charging, LED illumination, accurate biomechanical-motion sensing, and real-time IoT-enabled monitoring through wireless interfacing.

10.1002/adfm.79521.title: Glutathione-Responsive Cu Nanoplatform Enables Quantitative CEST MRI for Predicting Cuproptosis Therapeutic Response
10.1002/adfm.79521.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate quantification of glutathione (GSH), a key regulator of intracellular redox homeostasis, and its correlation with the early therapeutic response to cuproptosis-based treatment in animal models are crucial for developing effective glutathione-depletion therapeutics, yet in vivo GSH quantification remains challenging. Here, we developed a GSH-responsive Cu nanoplatform (Cu-CDs) for early and noninvasive assessment of cuproptosis by exploiting the thiol chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signal of glutathione. In vivo studies in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice demonstrated that thiol CEST MRI enabled quantitative detection of GSH as low as 0.39 µmol/g in tumors (R 2 = 0.944). Notably, no correlation was observed between the levels of GSH and the MRI signals (R 2 = 0.302 or 0.117) from the exogenous analog, indicating that assessments using exogenous probes at a single time point were inaccurate. Remarkably, dynamic changes in the thiol CEST signals within only 8 h after administration of the Cu-CDs strongly correlated with the tumor inhibition rate measured (R 2 = 0.993), enabling early prediction of the long-term cuproptosis therapeutic efficacy. Thus, CEST MRI provides a non-invasive and quantitative approach for monitoring GSH in vivo, with potential for assessing therapeutic agent accumulation and predicting early therapeutic response of GSH-related therapies.

10.1002/adfm.79560.title: Beyond Superlattice Order: Full-Composition Li Stoichiometry Screening Identifies Interfacial Spinel Passivation as the Decisive Factor for Durable Cobalt-Free Li-Rich Cathodes
10.1002/adfm.79560.abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt-free Li-rich layered oxides (LRMs) hold great promise for next-generation high-energy batteries, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by irreversible oxygen redox and progressive interfacial degradation. Here, a full-range Li stoichiometry screening across Li 1+0.65 x Ni 0.35 Mn 0.65 O 2+0.65 x (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) was conducted to decouple bulk superlattice evolution from surface chemistry. A structural crossover at x ≈ 0.5 with minimized Li 2 MnO 3 long-range ordering is identified, yet optimal electrochemistry unexpectedly emerges at x = 0.375, governed by a triple synergistic mechanism: finely dispersed Li 2 MnO 3 nanodomains, moderate Li + /Ni 2+ antisite pillars, and-most critically- an in situ coherent spinel passivation interphase spontaneously formed during calcination. The optimized LRM0.375 delivers 227.1 mAh g −1 at 0.1C, 161.8 mAh g −1 at 5C, and an ultralow voltage fade of only 1.33 mV cycle −1 , with its graphite full cell retaining 78.48% capacity after 500 cycles. Operando XRD, RIXS, and DEMS collectively demonstrate that the spinel surface barrier, rather than bulk superlattice ordering alone, governs anionic redox reversibility and cycling durability. This work challenges the superlattice-centered design paradigm and identifies interfacial spinel passivation as a key stability-governing factor within a triple synergistic mechanism, providing targeted stoichiometric guidelines for designing durable anionic-redox cathodes beyond conventional bulk-structure-focused strategies.

10.1002/adfm.79525.title: Ultra-Robust All-Weather Perovskite Memristor Protected by Conformal Parylene Nanoscale Coating
10.1002/adfm.79525.abstract: ABSTRACT Halide perovskites are promising memristive materials for neuromorphic computing, yet their practical deployment in hardware is severely hindered by instability against moisture, oxygen, and reactive metallic ions. Here, we develop an ultra-robust perovskite memristor with all-weather adaptability protected by a ∼100 nm conformal polymeric nanoscale coating. Deposited by low-temperature, solvent-free chemical vapor deposition (CVD) technique, the polymeric Parylene serves as an encapsulation, interfacial passivation, and homogeneous dielectric layer. The memristor exhibits excellent bipolar resistive switching under ambient conditions with high uniformity, an endurance of 1.5 × 10 4 cycles (over 12.5-fold improvement), and a low set voltage of ∼0.27 V. It maintains stable operation under 100% relative humidity, thermal treatment at 348 K, 6-month ambient storage, and 300 bending cycles at 90°, and even passes the stringent IPX7 waterproof standard. A hardware-mapped convolutional neural network leveraging the synaptic properties of these memristors achieves a highly reliable MNIST recognition accuracy of 90%±0.4% across 10 independent test cycles. This work demonstrates that conformal Parylene encapsulation offers a comprehensive solution to the perovskite instability, paving the way for flexible and low-power neuromorphic systems.

10.1002/adfm.79495.title: Regulating Resonance-Related Dynamic Magnetic Response through In Situ MnO Formation in FeCoNiCr 0.4 Mn 0.6 High-Entropy Alloy for Low-Frequency Microwave Absorption
10.1002/adfm.79495.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient microwave absorption in the S-C band requires the strength and frequency distribution of resonance-related magnetic loss to be regulated while sufficient permeability is retained. The key is therefore to balance control of the resonance-related dynamic magnetic response with preservation of the magnetic contribution from the ferromagnetic matrix. Here, FeCoNiCr 0.4 Mn 0.6 high-entropy alloy (HEA) powders were subjected to wet milling and low-temperature annealing to produce anisotropic flakes while enabling controlled in situ oxidation of the intrinsic Mn. The resulting MnO/HEA interfaces were accompanied by changes in the local strain state and magnetic anisotropy environment of the adjacent ferromagnetic matrix, providing a structural basis for the evolution of resonance linewidth and effective damping. At 300°C, limited MnO formation produced a moderate effective damping state while maintaining relatively high permeability and sufficient ferromagnetic-phase contribution, enabling effective absorption over 3.2-4.9 GHz at a thickness of 3.5 mm. At 400°C, further MnO formation increased the fraction of the non-ferromagnetic phase and weakened the microwave magnetic response. These results demonstrate that controlling the oxidation degree of intrinsic alloying elements can balance interfacial regulation, dynamic magnetic relaxation, and ferromagnetic-phase retention, providing a feasible strategy for low-frequency microwave absorption in corrosion-resistant HEAs.

10.1002/adfm.79522.title: Laser-Architected Hierarchical Wood Evaporator for Salt-Resistant Solar Desalination and Dual-Mode Water-Electricity Cogeneration
10.1002/adfm.79522.abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater scarcity and intermittent solar irradiation motivate the development of technologies for freshwater production and electricity generation. However, salt accumulation limits the long-term operation of solar interfacial evaporators. A laser-architected delignified balsa wood evaporator (DBW/LCC) with a 3D cylindrical array and laser-carbonized surfaces is fabricated through delignification, laser engraving, and in situ laser carbonization. The array enhances light trapping and exposes additional sidewall area. Vertically aligned hydrophilic channels sustain capillary water supply and, together with the hydrophobic top surface, establish asymmetric wettability. DBW/LCC achieves an average absorptance of 99.46% over 250-2500 nm. The wetted surface exhibits a valley-plateau temperature difference of ∼1.2°C. Thermo-solutal Marangoni circulation may contribute to brine redistribution. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation for 150 h in 20 wt.% brine without visible salt deposition. Under 1 sun, it achieves a mass-loss rate of 5.09 kg m −2 h −1 normalized to its horizontal projected area, with an apparent evaporation efficiency of 99.85% calculated using an effective enthalpy. Coupled with a thermoelectric module, it generates voltages of 86.3 mV under 1 sun and 79.8 mV at a wind speed of 9.6 m s −1 without illumination. This platform offers a route to decentralized water-electricity cogeneration.

10.1002/adfm.79552.title: Stretchable Antimicrobial Nanomesh Antenna for Robust Epidermal Millimeter-Wave Wireless Communications
10.1002/adfm.79552.abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable millimeter-wave (mmWave) electronics are essential for next-generation wearable wireless systems. However, intrinsically stretchable mmWave devices remain challenging because it is difficult to fabricate metallic structures that simultaneously combine high conductivity, mechanical stretchability, high-resolution patterning, and skin biocompatibility for epidermal wireless operation. To bridge this gap, we report a mmWave nanomesh with low sheet resistance of 0.24 Ω/sq and µm-level patterning precision, and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity for hygienic epidermal deployment. The proposed nanomesh is compatible with the fabrication of mmWave antennas operating above 20 GHz and supports efficient mmWave radiation. Meanwhile, the nanomesh exhibits mechanical robustness and electrical stability even after 1000 cycles of mechanical deformations. On this basis, we realized a stretchable dual-unit nanomesh antenna array with a high realized gain of 6.8 dBi at 24 GHz, and demonstrated the first robust mmWave wireless data transmission based on nanomesh electronics. Beyond electromagnetic performance, the nanomesh antenna exhibits long-lasting and broad-spectrum antibacterial effects, ensuring hygiene and safety by avoiding epidermal bacterial accumulation. Combining high electromagnetic performance, mechanical-electrical stability, and antimicrobial ability, the proposed nanomaterial and mmWave device provide a practical strategy for wearable mmWave wireless electronics.

10.1002/adfm.79398.title: Coordination Geometry Reconstruction Mitigates α-Dihedral Angle Restriction of Polyanionic-Type Cathodes for Ultrafast Sodium Storage
10.1002/adfm.79398.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries have attracted extensive attention for large-scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources. However, the near-coplanar structure geometry of polyanionic-type cathodes causes in-plane stress and electrostatic barriers, which lead to blocked Na + transport kinetics and hinder their practical application. Herein, an α-plane, defined by the transition metal and its coordinating dangling anions, is identified as the critical structural bottleneck for Na + diffusion. By screening and tuning the dangling anions, a coordination geometry reconstruction is achieved that twists the α-plane into α1- and α2-planes. This twisting behavior breaks α-plane restriction and relieves the in-plane stress, thereby lowering the Na + migration barrier. Concurrently, the geometry reconstruction enlarges the Na2-centered polyhedral volume and increases the Na2 site occupancy from 0.56 to 0.62. Thus, the modified cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 130 mAh g −1 and outstanding rate capability, with 80% retention at 30 C and 83 mAh g −1 at 50 C. It also exhibits excellent wide-temperature operability (−40°C to 55°C) and stable full-cell performance. The universality of this strategy is validated on several polyanionic cathodes. This work reveals the α-plane as a tunable structural parameter, offering a geometry-electronic synergy paradigm for high-power polyanionic-type cathodes.

10.1002/adfm.79413.title: Elastic-Invisibility-Enabled Metastructure With Mechanically Programmed Nonlinear Resonators for Vibration Attenuation and Energy Harvesting
10.1002/adfm.79413.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical programming provides a simple way to tune embedded nonlinear resonators without redesigning the host structure. Here, seven magneto-elastic piezoelectric resonators are integrated into elastically reconstructed openings of a host beam. The removed stiffness, mass, and inertia are restored. The dynamics of the intact beam are therefore recovered over the investigated frequency range. Programming is performed by changing only the spacing between repulsive magnets. Each resonator can be set independently. This creates uniform, nonuniform, and graded combinations of monostable and bistable states. Experiments and simulations show marked changes in both vibration attenuation and harvested power. Different programs favor different functions. One configuration reaches 1.82 times the reference attenuation bandwidth. Another reaches 1.57 times the reference harvesting performance. Assuming nine admissible states per resonator, the seven-resonator system spans possible configurations. Model-selected candidates improve both numerical references simultaneously, reaching 1.16 times the attenuation bandwidth and 1.11 times the harvesting metric. The prototype also delivers up to 10.67 of total AC load power near resonance. The result is a structurally integrated platform with programmable nonlinear functionality and largely preserved host dynamics.

10.1002/adfm.79031.title: Breaking the 35% Efficiency Milestone: Material Innovations and Interface Mechanisms in Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79031.abstract: ABSTRACT Crystalline silicon solar cells are approaching their theoretical Auger efficiency limit, necessitating tandem architectures that transcend the Shockley-Queisser constraint and lower the cost of electricity. Monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) have breached the 35% power conversion efficiency barrier, emerging as the leading candidate to disrupt the photovoltaic landscape. However, translating this laboratory success to terawatt-scale deployment requires precise control over charge transport and interfacial recombination at the interconnecting layer (ICL). This review examines the material innovations driving this evolution, grounded in a quantitative loss-budget analysis, with a focus on the ICL and full-dimensional interface engineering. We first examine the evolving ICL paradigm, from defect-mediated transport in amorphous silicon to efficient band-to-band tunneling in polycrystalline silicon junctions, and the enhanced charge extraction enabled by transparent conductive oxides with self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), whose Ohmic contact formation we trace through an anchoring-to-Fermi-level-depinning mechanism. We further dissect breakthroughs mitigating non-radiative losses on textured silicon substrates, where SAMs and passivation strategies overcome steric hindrance and contact resistance, and where the same pyramid texture governs wide-bandgap perovskite crystallization and its process-engineering trade-offs. Finally, we navigate the “efficiency-stability-cost” trilemma, addressing halide-segregation and ion-migration suppression under a standardized stability framework, alongside scalable manufacturing toward industrial translation.

10.1002/adfm.79510.title: Thermally Robust Room-Temperature Interlayer Excitons in a Hybrid van der Waals Heterostructure
10.1002/adfm.79510.abstract: ABSTRACT Having long lifetimes and intrinsic electric dipole moments, interlayer excitons in van der Waals heterostructures are promising quasiparticles for excitonic optoelectronics. However, their practical implementation has been largely hindered by the fact that most interlayer excitons suffer from strongly suppressed radiative recombination and are stable only under cryogenic conditions. Here, we identify a distinct class of interlayer excitons that are simultaneously optically active and robust at room temperature in an atypical van der Waals heterostructure formed by a two-dimensional layered perovskite (PEA) 2 PbBr 4 and monolayer MoS 2 . These interlayer excitons appear as a distinct photoluminescence feature and exhibit a polarization-anisotropic response in a tilted sample geometry, consistent with an out-of-plane component of the optical transition dipole moment. Remarkably, the interlayer exciton emission persists up to 400 K, indicating exceptional thermal robustness. Time-resolved measurements reveal a moderate lifetime enhancement compared to intralayer excitons, indicating a hybrid state that balances partial spatial charge separation with retained electron-hole wavefunction overlap. First-principles calculations support a type-II electronic structure with spatially displaced band-edge states, finite interfacial coupling, and charge redistribution across the interface. Our findings establish (PEA) 2 PbBr 4 /MoS 2 as a promising platform for optically active interlayer excitons under ambient and elevated-temperature conditions.

10.1002/adfm.79508.title: Dynamic Liquid Crystal Elastomer Surfaces: From Bulk Responses to Interfacial Functions
10.1002/adfm.79508.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) combine liquid crystal orientational order with the elasticity of polymer networks and respond to thermal, optical, electrical, chemical, and mechanical stimuli. These responses can change not only the shape of an LCE but also its surface morphology and properties. The resulting surface changes can regulate wetting, adhesion, friction, biological contact, and interactions with light, electromagnetic waves, and sound. This review summarizes recent progress in molecular and network design, alignment programming, surface fabrication, and functional layer integration for LCE surfaces and LCE-driven composite interfaces. The resulting functions are organized into fluid, mechanical, and wave interactions. Guided by the central idea that bulk responses generate deformation while surface states determine interfacial behavior, this review discusses functions controlled by LCE surfaces and examines the conversion of bulk deformation into changes in surface shape and properties. These dynamic surface states enable liquid manipulation, adhesion and friction control, biological and haptic interfaces, optical readout, and wave modulation. Finally, the review discusses challenges and future directions in reliable switching, scalable fabrication, and feedback control. By linking bulk responses to changes in surface and interfacial states, it provides a framework for understanding and designing functional LCE surfaces and LCE-driven composite interfaces.

10.1002/adfm.79561.title: Self-Assembly and Humidity-Adaptive Memristive Behavior of Benzophosphole Nanohoops
10.1002/adfm.79561.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the condensed-state properties of π-conjugated macrocycles via molecular structure remains a fundamental challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Here, we report benzophosphole-embedded nanohoops as a heteroatom-doped platform where spatial configuration ( exo vs. endo ) directly governs molecular conformation, self-assembly, and electronic function. The endo -nanohoop adopts a unique outward-facing conformer that assembles into discrete tetrameric cage-like assemblies stabilized by cooperative P═O···H 2 O interactions, which further evolve into hierarchical hollow nanobowl architectures exhibiting aggregation-induced emission enhancement (AIEE). This differentiation generates distinct hydration microenvironments that correlate with divergent memristive behaviors. The exo -analogues exhibit highly uniform volatile threshold switching arising from transient ion migration dynamics, enabling physical reservoir computing. In contrast, the endo -framework possesses a distinct hydration microenvironment and exhibits robust analog non-volatile memory behavior. Available evidence suggests a possible mechanism in which water acts as structural nodes that bridge Ag clusters and coordinate ion transport with filament stability, thereby enabling non-volatile memristive behavior. Leveraging the humidity-dependent switching characteristics of the exo system, we further demonstrate a humidity-sensitive resistive switching capable of real-time and noise-resistant respiratory monitoring. These findings establish a direct correlation between molecular structure, water confinement, and adaptive electronic functionality, providing a supramolecular strategy for designing intelligent organic memristive materials and sensing-memory integrated hardware.

10.1002/adfm.79478.title: Engineering Intraframework Energy Transfer in Metal-Organic Frameworks for Luminescent Discrimination of Bisphenol Pollutants
10.1002/adfm.79478.abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent sensing relies on the generation, migration, and dissipation of excited-state energy modulated by analytes. However, the contribution of intraframework energy transfer processes to sensing performance remains insufficiently studied. Owing to the highly tunable structures and designable energy transfer pathways, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an ideal platform for dissecting detailed processes. Herein, a series of isostructural lanthanide MOFs were constructed from 2,5-furandicarboxylic / 3,5-pyridinedicarboxylic acid, enabling independent regulation of metal-to-metal and linker-to-linker energy transfer. Direct comparison of chemically integrated frameworks and their physical mixtures using bisphenol pollutants as probes reveals that metal-to-metal energy transfer dominates sensing performance, while linker-to-linker energy transfer contributes marginally. Mechanistic analyses indicate the impacts originate from the different energetic characteristics. Rigid lanthanide energy levels in Eu-Tb systems create an “energy reservoir” that strongly regulate luminescence responses, whereas highly environment-sensitive linker states in mixed-linker systems give rise to self-compensating energy transfer, resulting in a diminished influence. Moreover, the additional energy transfer pathways introduced by chemical integration can partially compensate for analyte-induced excited-state energy loss by releasing the “accumulated energy”, thereby mitigating the overall quenching effect. This work establishes a fundamental relationship between intraframework energy transfer and luminescence recognition performance, providing a general design pattern for sensing materials.

10.1002/adfm.77918.title: Oxygen-Vacancy-Regulated Crystallization and Ferroelectric Phase Stabilization in Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 Thin Films
10.1002/adfm.77918.abstract: ABSTRACT Defect-regulated crystallization pathways govern metastable phase formation in functional oxides, yet the role of oxygen-vacancy-related oxygen deficiency in crystallization and ferroelectric phase stabilization in ultrathin Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 remains unresolved. This work combines atomic-layer-deposition ozone-dose tuning with temperature-resolved in situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering reciprocal-space mapping to track crystallization in 10 nm Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 thin films with systematically varied, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy-inferred relative oxygen-deficiency levels. Vacancy-lean films crystallize at lower temperatures than vacancy-rich films (370°C vs. 400°C) and exhibit a lower comparative apparent activation energy for crystallization (3.6 × 10 2 vs. 4.4 × 10 2 kJ mol −1 ), together with more efficient lateral crystallite growth and a larger strain-free d-spacing consistent with an increased orthorhombic-phase contribution. In contrast, vacancy-rich films show delayed crystallization, suppressed lateral coarsening, and stronger tetragonal-phase retention. The vacancy-lean film achieves a switchable polarization, 2P r , of 19.9 µC cm −2 after annealing at 400°C, within a back-end-of-line-relevant thermal budget; higher annealing temperatures induce partial monoclinic transformation and reduce polarization. These results identify oxygen-deficiency control as a practical route to tune crystallization pathways and low-temperature ferroelectric phase formation in HfO 2 -based thin films.

10.1002/adfm.79588.title: Ultrafast All-Optical Switching with Engineered Wavefronts via Chiral Nonlocal Phase Gradient Metasurfaces
10.1002/adfm.79588.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid-growing demands in high-speed telecommunication and optical computing necessitate the advances in all-optical switching based on high quality (Q) factor photonic nanostructures. However, current all-optical switching approaches cannot simultaneously shape the output wavefront, because combining pixelated phase control with high-Q nanostructures remains extremely challenging. Here, we demonstrate picosecond all-optical switching of the unpolarized incident light with engineered output wavefronts via nonlocal geometric-phase gradient metasurfaces supporting high-Q chiral quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs). The nonlocal geometric-phase gradient metasurfaces enable pixelated wavefront shaping of the transmitted light in both real and momentum spaces, while the high-Q quasi-BIC resonances underpin the resonantly enhanced responses critical for ultrafast optical modulation. Notably, leveraging the chiral-selectivity of the chiral quasi-BICs, the metasurfaces are functionally integrated with circular polarizers, which thereby overcome the inherent constraint of nonlocal geometric-phase gradient metasurfaces on the incident polarization. Our work provides an ultrafast and versatile platform for multi-dimensional optical field manipulation.

10.1002/adfm.79530.title: Compositionally Tuned FeNiMnCuNbAg x High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles With Enhanced ROS Generation and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity
10.1002/adfm.79530.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional antibacterial nanomaterials is of considerable interest in combating antibiotic resistance and marine biofouling. Herein, Ag-containing FeNiMnCuNbAgx high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA-NPs) with tunable composition were synthesized through a non-equilibrium arc-discharge plasma strategy. By introducing Nb to stabilize Ag within the alloy matrix, homogeneous HEA-NPs with adjustable Ag content were successfully obtained. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, efficient photothermal conversion, and strong biofilm-removal capability. In particular, FeNiMnCuNbAg 0.25 HEA-NPs achieved 99.99% elimination of planktonic Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria at a low dosage of 15 µg·mL −1 (15 ppm), while under simulated solar irradiation (1 sun), the biofilm removal efficiency at 50 µg·mL −1 increased from 86% to 98%, demonstrating a pronounced photothermal enhancement effect. Mechanistic investigations combining electron spin resonance (ESR), density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and transcriptomic analysis revealed that the Ag incorporation altered the thermodynamic evolution of oxygen reduction intermediates and modulated reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation behavior. Meanwhile, transcriptomic results indicated that HEA-NP treatment induced redox imbalance, respiratory dysfunction, and translational suppression in the bacterium. These findings highlight the potential of Ag-containing HEA-NPs as multifunctional antibacterial materials for biofilm control and antimicrobial protection in marine-relevant environments.

10.1002/adfm.79464.title: Understanding Multiscale Disorder in Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors1
10.1002/adfm.79464.abstract: ABSTRACT Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors are central to applications across quantum information science, but their performance is constrained by the effects of disorder and electrodynamic inhomogeneities that are not well understood. By combining DC transport, dark-count measurements, and bias-dependent microwave transmission spectroscopy in the presence of controlled nanoscale disorder introduced through helium-ion irradiation, local instabilities and global superfluid response are distinguished. This approach enables controlled tuning of the depairing current, kinetic inductance, microwave dissipation, and mode structure within a single device through systematic variation of the ion fluence. Bias- and temperature-dependent resonance shifts quantify disorder-induced modifications of the superconducting density of states through the nonlinear kinetic inductance, while the emergence of multiple resonant modes reveals the formation of electrodynamically distinct superconducting regions. The combined microwave response, characterized by the resonance frequency and quality factor , provides qualitative fingerprints of perturbation-dependent microwave dissipation under bias current, temperature, perpendicular magnetic field, RF power, and disorder, thereby establishing a multifunctional foundation for disorder engineering of superconducting nanowire detectors and resonators.

10.1002/adfm.79547.title: Ultrawide-Temperature Stable Superelasticity in a Nanoprecipitation-Strengthened NiTi Strain Glass Alloy
10.1002/adfm.79547.abstract: ABSTRACT Superelastic materials exhibiting flag-shaped hysteresis are valued for their high elasticity and damping capacity, which arise from stress-induced martensitic transformation and related phase-transition hysteresis, enabling effective energy absorption and vibration mitigation. However, their widespread use is limited by the narrow operating temperature range and poor functional fatigue. Here, we report an ultrawide temperature range superelasticity spanning from 163 to 373 K, coupled with recoverable strain of 3.5% and exceptionally stable energy dissipation at 183 K. These properties are achieved via a nanoprecipitation-strengthened two-step strain glass transition in the Ti 48.3 Ni 51.7 alloy through aging at 573 K for 2 h. In situ transmission electron microscopy shows B2 to R to B19' nanodomains upon cooling, attributed to aging-induced ultrafine and dispersed Ni 4 Ti 3 nanoprecipitates. These nanoprecipitates not only strengthen the matrix but also stabilize R and B19' nanodomains, enabling stress-induced reversible phase transformation over a wide temperature range. Phase-field simulations confirm that precipitation-induced structural ordering at low temperatures can occur without equilibrium composition in the matrix, maintaining the low transition temperature. This work provides a viable pathway for developing high-performance superelastic alloys with wide-temperature and functional fatigue stability, offering significant potential for applications in extreme environments such as aerospace and deep-sea exploration.

10.1002/adfm.79575.title: Polarization-Sensitive Photodetectors Based on Biaxially Grown Two-Dimensional Organic Charge-Transfer Cocrystals
10.1002/adfm.79575.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic polarization-sensitive photodetectors are promising for simultaneously acquiring light intensity and polarization information, but their development is hindered by the one-dimensional packing of conventional charge-transfer (CT) cocrystals, which limits device integration and anisotropic optoelectronic modulation. Herein, two-dimensional DTP-TCNQ CT cocrystal microplates are fabricated by solution self-assembly using dithieno[3,2-b:2′,3′-d]thiophene (DTP) as the donor and 7,7,8,8-tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ) as the acceptor. Benefiting from strong intermolecular charge-transfer interactions and an anisotropic crystal structure, the cocrystals exhibit broadband optical absorption and pronounced intrinsic optical anisotropy. DTP-TCNQ-based photodetectors achieve a specific detectivity of 2.29 × 10 14 Jones under 532 nm illumination, closely matching the noise-derived value at 1 kHz. Moreover, devices constructed along the [100] and [011] directions show stable polarization-dependent photoresponses, with polarization ratios of 7.40 and 6.61, respectively. Furthermore, time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations indicate that the orientation-dependent response is associated with the alignment of the optical transition dipole moment, which forms angles of 17.8° and 78.5° with the [100] and [011] directions, respectively. This work offers guidance for designing anisotropic CT cocrystals and high-performance organic polarization-sensitive photodetectors with improved integration and functional modulation.

10.1002/adfm.79598.title: Wavelength-Tailored Distributed Bragg Reflector Capping Layers for Highly Efficient and Color-Pure RGB TEOLEDs
10.1002/adfm.79598.abstract: ABSTRACT Color-selective optical management is essential for improving the efficiency and color purity of red, green, and blue (RGB) top-emitting organic light-emitting diodes (TEOLEDs). This study introduces wavelength-tailored distributed Bragg reflector capping layers (DBR-CPLs) as color-specific top-side optical structures for RGB TEOLEDs. Thermally evaporated MoO 3 and LiF are used as alternating high- and low-refractive-index DBR materials, respectively. Unlike conventional single-layer organic CPLs, the proposed MoO 3 /LiF DBR-CPLs provide additional design freedom by enabling independent control of the optical thickness and dyad number for each emission color. Optical simulations and experimental analyses show that the DBR-CPLs induce wavelength-selective reflection, enhance the electric-field intensity, narrow the emission bandwidth, and strengthen cavity resonance through cavity modulation. At 300 cd m −2 , optimized 2-dyad DBR-CPL devices achieve external quantum efficiencies of 24.36%, 35.26%, and 12.01% for blue, green, and red TEOLEDs, corresponding to improvements of 28.82%, 42.12%, and 27.77%, respectively, compared with thickness-optimized NPB-CPL reference devices. In addition, the electroluminescence full width at half maximum decreases to 52, 70, and 66 nm for blue, green, and red emission, respectively, expanding the NTSC color-gamut coverage from 62.5% to 70.4%. These results demonstrate that DBR-CPLs are practical, vacuum-compatible optical structures for realizing efficient and color-pure RGB TEOLED displays.

10.1002/adfm.79543.title: Molecular Conformational Matching Enables Robust Buried Interfaces in Efficient and Temperature-Cycling-Resilient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79543.abstract: ABSTRACT Temperature fluctuations can disrupt the organization of buried self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), weaken interfacial contact, and accelerate device degradation. Here, we develop a co-assembly strategy by incorporating two bisphosphonic acid molecules with distinct linker structures, denoted S1 and S2, into the widely used carbazole-based SAM [4-(3,6-dimethoxy-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl] phosphonic acid (MeO-4PACz). Compared with S1, S2 exhibits improved conformational compatibility with MeO-4PACz. The S2/MeO-4PACz pair also features stronger hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions. In addition, S2 possesses a larger molecular dipole and adsorbs more favorably on indium tin oxide. These molecular attributes promote more continuous and spatially uniform coverage. They also strengthen substrate anchoring and homogenize the interfacial potential distribution. The resulting S2-based co-assembled SAM (Co-SAM) provides favorable energy-level alignment, facilitates hole extraction, and suppresses nonradiative recombination. It also reinforces the buried interface against cyclic thermal stress. Residual stress accumulation is alleviated, interfacial morphology is preserved, and perovskite phase degradation is retarded. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on the S2 Co-SAM achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.01% and retain 92.8% of their initial efficiency after 500 temperature cycles between −40°C and 85°C. Synergistic molecular and interfacial regulation enables efficient and temperature-resilient inverted PSCs.

10.1002/adfm.79391.title: Thermoelastic Wave-Based Logic for Mechanically Cognitive Materials
10.1002/adfm.79391.abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advances in metamaterials and fabrication techniques have revived interest in mechanical computing. Contrary to techniques relying on static deformations of buckling beams or origami-based lattices, the integration of wave scattering and mechanical memory presents a promising path toward efficient, low-latency elastoacoustic computing. This work introduces a novel class of multifunctional mechanical computing circuits that leverage the rich dynamics of phononic and locally resonant materials. These circuits incorporate memory-integrated components, realized here via metamaterial cells infused with shape memory alloys which recall stored elastic profiles and trigger specific actions upon thermal activation. A critical advantage of this realization is its synergistic interaction with incident vibroacoustic loads and the inherited high speed of waves, as opposed to recent adaptations of mechanically intelligent systems that employ innately slower mechanisms such as elastomeric shape changes and snap-through bistabilities. Through a proof-of-concept physical implementation, the efficacy and reconfigurability of the wave-based gates are demonstrated via output probes and measured wavefields. Furthermore, the modular design of the fundamental gates can be used as building blocks to construct complex combinational logic circuits, paving the way for sequential logic in wave-based analog computing systems.

10.1002/adfm.79476.title: Photodetectors Based on Two-Dimensional Materials: From Sensory Health Monitoring to Cognitive Neuromorphic Computing
10.1002/adfm.79476.abstract: ABSTRACT Driven by advances in wearable electronics and artificial intelligence, photodetectors have become central to modern sensing technologies. Two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as promising platforms for advanced optoelectronics, owing to their atomic-scale thickness, widely tunable bandgaps, strong light-matter interactions, and inherent mechanical flexibility. Although sensory health monitoring and cognitive neuromorphic computing are currently evolving as distinct domains, they represent a continuous technological trajectory from passive data acquisition to active in-sensor processing. This review provides a comprehensive overview of 2D material-based photodetectors, bridging flexible healthcare devices and advanced artificial visual systems. First, fundamental photodetection mechanisms, advanced synthesis methods, and device performance enhancement strategies are systematically elucidated. Subsequently, recent progress in flexible photodetectors for health monitoring is summarized. To overcome the power, latency, and data-transfer limitations of conventional von Neumann architectures, neuromorphic optoelectronic devices are further discussed, particularly artificial optical synapses capable of emulating biological perception-memory-processing pipelines for low-power biomimetic vision and in-sensor computing. Finally, future challenges are critically assessed, including scalable manufacturing, long-term stability in biointegrated environments, stretchable devices for suppressing motion artifacts, and multimodal sensory fusion. This review delineates a promising path toward physiological cognitive computing and imperceptible intelligent optoelectronics for precision medicine and edge-AI diagnostics.

10.1002/adfm.79535.title: Janus Electronic State of Supported Metal Oxide Catalysts Governs Removal of Multiple Pollutants
10.1002/adfm.79535.abstract: ABSTRACT Orchestrating adsorption and activation of multiple pollutants at specific sites in environmental catalysis remains challenging. Here, we report a Janus electronic state in the catalysts by dispersing nanosized MnO 2 on hydroxylated TiO 2 , comprising interface-proximal electron-enriched Mn 3+ sites and interface-distal electron-deficient Mn 4+ sites, arising from spatially asymmetric charge distribution induced by strong oxide-support interaction. This structure was elucidated through atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, X-ray absorption spectroscopy probing the interface between nanosized MnO 2 and hydroxylated TiO 2 , complemented by density functional theory calculations. Taking the synergistic catalytic conversion of nitrogen oxide and volatile organic compounds as a model reaction for environmental catalysis, this Janus electronic state catalyst exhibits remarkable molecule-site specificity, channelling nitrogen oxide reduction to electron-enriched Mn 3+ sites and volatile organic compound oxidation to electron-deficient Mn 4+ sites. This work highlights the potential of the Janus electronic state for precise catalysis in removal of multiple pollutants.

10.1002/adfm.79572.title: A Single-Channel Humidity-Pressure Dual-Modal Decoupling Sensor for Assistive Geriatric Rehabilitation
10.1002/adfm.79572.abstract: ABSTRACT Against the background of global population aging and the growing need for elderly care, developing multi-modal sensing platforms with high interference immunity, specifically for complex respiratory dysfunctions, has become a critical demand in the field of precision medicine. However, conventional multimodal sensors suffer from performance limitations and signal crosstalk due to excessive reliance on complex material synthesis and suboptimal structural design. A humidity-pressure dual-modal sensor (HPDS) was designed by integrating polyimide, electrodes, and a heterogeneous conductive elastomer into a sandwich-structured device. The HPDS exhibited good sensitivity over a wide pressure range (0.58-392 kPa), high mechanical stability exceeding 50 000 cycles, and a fast humidity response of 200 ms. An intelligent assistive training scheme combined with a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) was further constructed for respiratory pattern discrimination and physical therapy assistance, achieving an accuracy of 98.9% in classifying the six core respiratory states. This work provided a universal design paradigm for next-generation low-coupling and high-performance AI devices, showing great promise in the development of intelligent healthcare and home-based rehabilitation.

10.1002/adfm.79551.title: A Microenvironment-Feedback Cascaded Hydrogel for Regenerative Repair of Infected Diabetic Wounds
10.1002/adfm.79551.abstract: ABSTRACT Infected diabetic wound repair is hindered by a hostile microenvironment of heavy bacterial burden, persistent oxidative stress, toxin-driven inflammation, and hypoxia. Here we report a microenvironment-feedback cascaded hydrogel, termed HL-10, for infected diabetic wound repair. HL-10 is formed via dynamic Schiff base crosslinking between L-arginine -modified chitosan and aldehyde-functionalized F127, with erythrocyte membrane-hybridized, polymyxin B-modified and perfluorohexane (PFH)-loaded liposomes (Rφ-PLipo-PFH) embedded within the hydrogel network. The chitosan-based network first suppresses bacterial growth and biofilm formation. As the acidic and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-rich conditions trigger matrix degradation, the hydrogel scavenges local ROS and generates nitric oxide to alleviate oxidative stress and inflammation. This degradation process simultaneously exposes the embedded liposomes, which neutralize bacterial toxins and reduce the LPS-induced M1 macrophage phenotype, while the PFH core provides a sustained oxygen supply to counter hypoxia. In a Pseudomonas aeruginosa -infected diabetic model, HL-10 treatment accelerated wound repair and was accompanied by attenuation of AGE-RAGE/PI3K-Akt signaling, restoration of angiogenesis, and improved tissue remodeling, demonstrating a systematic biomaterial approach for managing refractory wounds.

10.1002/adfm.79553.title: Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Logic Circuits Driven by Ion-Mediated Organic Electrochemical Diodes
10.1002/adfm.79553.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of data-intensive computing has exposed the physical limitations of conventional hardware architectures. While accumulative multistate memory devices offer low-power alternatives, incorporating multistate reconfigurability into switching devices enables fully integrated, multifunctional neuromorphic operations across both logic and memory. Herein, we report programmable multistate logic circuits based on organic neuromorphic devices.
