By leveraging the intrinsic learning capability of organic electrochemical diodes (OECDs), multiple logic functions are realized within a single diode-resistor configuration. The channel conductance of each OECD is dynamically modulated by the polarity and frequency of the input voltage, enabling seamless reconfiguration to execute custom logic operations (e.g., AND/OR and XOR/unknown). Furthermore, we demonstrate a functional half-adder by cascading two multistate logic circuits as a proof-of-concept neuromorphic computing architecture. These results establish a promising pathway toward on-chip, learning-based digital circuitry with potential relevance to future neuromorphic computing applications.

10.1002/adfm.79579.title: Environmentally Stable Hydrogel-Based Biomimetic Leaf for Hyperspectral Camouflage
10.1002/adfm.79579.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogel-based hyperspectral camouflage faces a fundamental trade-off: water is essential for replicating the diagnostic absorption bands of vegetation, yet its high mobility inevitably causes dehydration, ice nucleation, and spectral distortion. Inspired by plant polyol-mediated water binding, we report a biomimetic leaf that integrates spectral modulation units (composite dyes and silicon dioxide (SiO 2 ) microspheres) with an ethylene glycol (EG)-water hydrogen-bonding network in a polyacrylamide matrix. EG locks water into a bound state via hydrogen bonds, reducing its activity and suppressing evaporation and ice crystallization. The optimized leaf achieves a spectral angle cosine of 0.995 against natural Pittosporum leaves (400-1000 nm) and a full-range (400-2500nm) correlation coefficient of 0.986 against the mean spectrum. It resists dehydration (25°C/40% RH, 2 h) and rehydrates within 14.5 h (25°C/90% RH), mimicking leaf transpiration-moisture cycles. Furthermore, it remains unfrozen and flexible at −20°C, and maintains mechanical integrity after repeated freeze-thaw cycles (−70 to 25°C). Notably, after 4 h of xenon-lamp aging, its color difference (Δ E = 6.32) is much lower than natural leaves (Δ E = 16.93), indicating superior photostability. Overall, water-state engineering offers a route to balance spectral fidelity and environmental stability in the design of hyperspectral camouflage materials.

10.1002/adfm.79544.title: Confinement-Enabled Epitaxy of Single-Crystal InN Fins Enables Room-Temperature Ohmic Contact to GaN
10.1002/adfm.79544.abstract: ABSTRACT Indium nitride (InN) combines the highest electron mobility and peak carrier velocity among the III-nitrides with an intrinsically degenerate surface accumulation layer, making it an attractive but difficult material for electronic interfaces. Here, we show that geometric confinement increases local adatom supersaturation and enables the growth of single-crystal InN by standard pulsed metal-organic chemical vapor deposition under conditions that otherwise do not support planar InN. This approach yields single-crystal InN fins through selective-area growth and supports versatile AlN/InN and GaN/InN heterostructures. The resulting selectively grown InN fins form abrupt GaN/InN and AlN/InN heterointerfaces and exhibit exceptionally low-resistance, anneal-free ohmic behavior. When integrated as epitaxial contact layers in AlGaN/GaN heterostructure FinFETs, they enable room-temperature contacts that outperform conventional high-temperature alloyed contacts while preserving interface crystallinity. These results establish confinement-enabled InN epitaxy as a route to low-thermal-budget, gate-first GaN processing and highlight a broader strategy for contact engineering and heterogeneous integration in advanced nitride electronics.

10.1002/adfm.79597.title: Spatial Tailoring of Pt Clusters and Co Single Atoms Over TiO 2 Nanosheets Achieves Directed Charge Separation for Boosted Methanol Photoreforming
10.1002/adfm.79597.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient methanol photoreforming requires the coupling of methanol oxidative dehydrogenation and proton reduction, yet these half-reactions demand distinct active-site configurations. Here, acid-etching-assisted dual-site engineering enables the synergistic integration of Pt clusters (Pt C ) and Co single atoms (Co SA ) on TiO 2 nanosheets (TNS). Experimental results and theoretical calculations reveal that the electronic interaction between Pt C and Co SA upshifts the d-band center of Co SA to enhance the adsorption and activation of methanol-derived intermediates, while downshifting the d-band center of Pt C to weaken proton adsorption and facilitate H 2 desorption. Furthermore, compared with isolated Pt single atoms (Pt SA ), Pt C reduces the proton migration energy barrier and apparent activation energy, thereby facilitating efficient H 2 evolution. More importantly, the nanosheet structure of TNS accelerates the migration of holes toward Co SA and electrons toward Pt C , effectively suppressing charge recombination and establishing a directional redox pathway. Consequently, spatial tailoring of the reactive active sites enables Pt C Co SA /TNS to deliver an H 2 evolution rate of 117.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , approximately 2 times that of Pt SA Co SA /TNS, together with an apparent quantum yield of 66.4% at 365 nm. This work provides a novel strategy for the controlled fabrication of active sites on photocatalysts and efficient methanol photoreforming.

10.1002/adfm.79526.title: Non-Invasive Optical Inspection of Thermally Driven Interface State Evolution at Buried Metal-MoS 2 Contacts
10.1002/adfm.79526.abstract: ABSTRACT Van der Waals (vdW) metal contacts to two-dimensional semiconductors promise efficient carrier extraction alongside long photocarrier lifetimes, yet how the buried interface evolves under back-end-of-line thermal budgets remains difficult to track. Here, annealing-dependent transient reflection spectroscopy is established as a device-free optical readout of interface state evolution for transferred vdW Au, graphene-buffered Au, and deposited semimetal Sb contacts on multilayer MoS 2 up to 400°C, correlated with cross-sectional electron microscopy, photoelectron spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations. As the Au-S separation contracts from 3.47 Å to 2.16 Å (into the bonding range) two distinct optical signatures emerge: reduction of the early-time excitonic response from the first annealing step, consistent with strengthening extraction, and a picosecond capture channel that appears at 200°C, following thermally activated chemisorption whose hybridization-induced gap states straddle the pinned Fermi level. At matched separation, the Sb interface forms comparable gap states that lie occupied below its Fermi level, explaining its nearly invariant response, whereas graphene delays the transformation by holding the metal away from the semiconductor. These results frame contact selection as a navigable trade-off between carrier extraction and photocarrier lifetime and identify interlayer engineering and semimetal contacts as complementary routes to thermally robust 2D interfaces.

10.1002/adfm.79532.title: Dual-Anion Mutual-Facilitation Effect Directs Surface Reconstruction for Reversible Anion Redox in Cobalt-Free Li-Rich Mn-Based Cathodes
10.1002/adfm.79532.abstract: ABSTRACT Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LLOs) offer high energy density through coupled cationic and anionic redox, but suffer from irreversible oxygen loss, voltage decay, and surface reconstruction. Here, we develop a mutual-assisted F/S dual-anion doping strategy to regulate anion incorporation and near-surface evolution. Density functional theory calculations show that F alleviates S-induced lattice strain, stabilizes the local charge environment, and lowers the barrier for S penetration. The resulting cathode features a depth-dependent architecture with lattice-incorporated F/S species, regulated oxygen vacancies, a spinel-like reconstructed region and a sulfate/sulfite-derived interphase, while retaining the layered bulk. Multiscale spectroscopy and operando analyses reveal enhanced Mn/Ni redox and reversible lattice-oxygen activity, suppressing oxygen release, lattice breathing, electrolyte decomposition, and phase propagation. The optimized cathode retains 84.4% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a voltage-decay rate of 1.093 mV per cycle, and 88.63% after 1000 cycles at 5 C. Post-cycling analyses and multiphysics simulations further link this durability to reduced transition-metal dissolution, homogenized Li + transport, and mitigated stress localization. This work demonstrates dual-anion doping as an effective route to coordinate defect chemistry, redox activity and interfacial reconstruction in high-capacity cathodes.

10.1002/adfm.79538.title: Trap-Mediated Photonic Synapses Based on Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 /ZnO x Heterojunctions for Audiovisual Physical Reservoir Computing
10.1002/adfm.79538.abstract: ABSTRACT Emulating biological sensory processing in hardware requires synaptic devices with tunable dynamics and multimodal integration capability. However, heterogeneous physical signals are difficult to encode uniformly in a single synaptic device. Herein, we construct an optically programmable photonic synapse (CZH-PS) based on Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 /ZnO x (defect-type) heterostructure, where abundant oxygen vacancy (Ov) deep traps in ZnO x dominate the synaptic plasticity. Photoexcited electrons injected from the perovskite into ZnO x are stored in Ov trap states and thermally released, producing a persistent photocurrent whose decay kinetics are optically tunable. This mechanism underpins a rich repertoire of synaptic behaviors, including short-term/long-term memory (STM/LTM), Ebbinghaus forgetting, and the habituation/sensitization of the Aplysia gill-withdrawal reflex under dual-wavelength programming. Moreover, the nonlinear, history-dependent excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) serves as a physical reservoir for temporal information processing. With 4-bit optical pulse coding, a reservoir computing system is constructed that achieves recognition accuracies of 91.7% and 95.0% for letter and audio classification tasks, respectively. These results establish trap-mediated photonic synapses as a versatile hardware platform for bimodal bio-inspired computing.

10.1002/adfm.79516.title: Crack-Defect Landscapes Enable Multimodal Memristive Switching in WS 2 Mono-Bilayers
10.1002/adfm.79516.abstract: ABSTRACT While nano or micro cracks are often unavoidable during the scalable growth of 2D materials, their role and interactions with vacancies in facilitating variable memristive switching are generally overlooked in device applications. Addressing device-to-device and cyclic variability in 2D memristor demands a mechanistic understanding of vacancy dynamics and their conduction pathways. We unveil how point defects and intergranular cracks modulate dynamic memristor behavior in mono-bilayer WS 2 lateral devices associated with varied sulfur vacancy concentrations, ranging from nearly pristine to ∼10 14 cm −2 , as confirmed by aberration-corrected electron microscopic and spectroscopic investigations. The crack boundaries act as preferential sites for vacancy migration and charged species, facilitating resistive switching in polycrystalline like WS 2 mono-bilayers. The observed conductance switching originate from Schottky barrier modulation at the WS 2 metal interface and the redistribution of vacancies within the channel. To enhance the device performance, controlled thermal annealing in distinct environments has been performed. The devices exhibited distinguishable switching for 800 cycles with consistent resistance ratios followed by onset of toggling state and later collapsing to trap state. These findings establish a direct correlation between atomic-scale defects and memristive performance, providing fundamental insights into vacancy-crack interactions that govern charge transport and stability in 2D materials.

10.1002/adfm.79605.title: Robust Ambient-Pressure-Dried MXene Aerogels via Multiscale Structural Engineering
10.1002/adfm.79605.abstract: ABSTRACT Ambient pressure drying is a promising route to scale up MXene aerogels, but it is limited by severe capillary collapse during solvent evaporation. Here, robust ambient-pressure-dried MXene aerogels are fabricated via multiscale structural engineering. At the molecular scale, ethanol acts as both a low-surface-tension solvent and a poor solvent inducing MXene phase separation, revealing its role in stabilizing wet gels beyond reducing surface tension. This process increases the contact between oxygen-containing groups on MXene and hydroxyl groups of TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofiber (TOCNF), leading to a dense hydrogen-bonding network. More importantly, the phase separation degree serves as a microstructural descriptor linking ethanol-induced structural evolution to mechanical reinforcement, providing a basis for optimizing capillary-resistant aerogels. Macroscopically, polydopamine-modified loofah acts as a reinforcing framework to form a reinforced concrete-like architecture with the MXene/TOCNF matrix. The molecular hydrogen bonding network and the macroscopic skeleton jointly preserve an intact porous structure after drying. The resulting aerogel exhibits a Young's modulus of 0.57 MPa, an electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of 74.6 dB, excellent infrared stealth performance, and a rapid Joule heating response. This work clarifies the hidden role of ethanol in ambient pressure drying and establishes a microstructure-guided design principle for robust multifunctional MXene aerogels.

10.1002/adfm.79155.title: 4D Insights into Anisotropic Fracture Behavior in Crossed-Lamellar Mollusk Shells
10.1002/adfm.79155.abstract: ABSTRACT Crossed-lamellar mollusk shells are among the toughest natural ceramic composites. This is achieved through their hierarchical architecture consisting of multiple orthogonally oriented macro-layers, each composed of sheet-like lamellae assembled from progressively finer mineral building blocks. Despite this pronounced structural anisotropy, its role in governing direction-dependent fracture remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine systematic in situ synchrotron X-ray micro-computed tomography enabled by a custom miniature four-point bending device, and post-fracture mechanical characterization, to directly visualize and compare four-dimensional (4D) time-resolved fracture evolution in longitudinal and transversal shell specimens, which are oriented parallel and perpendicular to the shell major axis, respectively. The results reveal two distinct fracture pathways dictated by the crossed-lamellar architecture. Longitudinal loading promotes sequential channel cracking, crack arrest at the macro-layer interface, interface-initiated back-running cracks, macro-layer delamination, and multiscale crack bridging. In contrast, transversal loading suppresses extensive channel cracking and instead develops distributed intra-lamellar fracture and corrugated crack paths, enabling prolonged damage accumulation, resulting in significantly higher bending strength and fracture energy. These findings establish a direct link between structural anisotropy and direction-dependent fracture evolution in crossed-lamellar shells, providing new mechanistic insights into this biological ceramic composite and providing design insights for the production of damage-tolerant synthetic structural materials.

10.1002/adfm.79581.title: Asymmetric π-Extended B/N MR-TADF Emitters Enabling Deep-Blue OLEDs with Suppressed Efficiency Roll-Off, Anti-Quenching and High Horizontal Dipole Orientation
10.1002/adfm.79581.abstract: ABSTRACT Narrowband deep-blue multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters are crucial for high-color-gamut organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), whereas their practical applications are severely restricted by efficiency roll-off and aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ). Herein, a twisted-planar-twisted (TPT) MR-TADF emitter named A-BFCz is synthesized via an asymmetric π-extension molecular-design strategy. The asymmetric π-extended conjugation can retain the locally excited (LE) character of the singlet state and accelerate reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) kinetics via potentially accessible high-lying RISC pathways, resulting in narrowband deep-blue emission with a full width at half-maximum (FWHM) of 17 nm, a fast RISC rate constant approaching 10 6 s −1 , and a near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Meanwhile, the dual twisted peripheral substituents on the TPT backbone are beneficial to solid-state packing behavior by spatially separating adjacent molecules and thus suppressing undesired intermolecular π-π stacking interactions. In addition, the centrally located B-N-fused rigid scaffold maintains a well-preserved planar configuration, leading to a horizontal dipole ratio of 99%. Consequently, the non-sensitized deep-blue OLEDs based on A-BFCz achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 42.8%. This work paves the way for the design and optimization of high-efficiency narrowband deep-blue MR-TADF luminescent materials.

10.1002/adfm.79557.title: Synergistic Defect−Disorder Engineering in RuO 2 Nanosheets for Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis
10.1002/adfm.79557.abstract: ABSTRACT The regulation of defect structures and crystal disorder has attracted tremendous research interest due to its high efficacy in developing high-performance electrocatalysts for diverse energy technologies. In this study, we developed a dual defect−disorder engineering strategy to optimize the electrocatalytic performance of atomically thin RuO 2 nanosheets by controlling their stacking structure and degree of amorphization. The self-assembly of exfoliated RuO 2 nanosheets with intermediate-sized Sr 2+ ions enabled the simultaneous optimization of the defect concentration and surface area in the restacked RuO 2 nanosheets. Through the synergistic combination of this approach with calcination-induced amorphization, the Sr 2+ -restacked RuO 2 nanosheets calcined at 250°C showed outstanding electrocatalyst activity toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), delivering a low overpotential of 12 mV in alkaline electrolyte. The benefit of the amorphization approach was more pronounced in alkaline media than in acidic one, underscoring the pH-dependent impact of disorder introduction on the HER mechanism through modulation of the Volmer step barrier. In situ spectroscopic investigations and density functional theory calculations offered compelling evidence that the combined amorphization and defect-engineering approach effectively promotes interfacial charge-transfer kinetics, H 2 O adsorption, and dynamic activation of the interfacial water network in alkaline media.

10.1002/adfm.79582.title: Benzotriazole-Functionalized g-C 3 N 4 /NH 2 -UiO-66 Heterojunctions Enable Photothermal Self-Healing and Durable Polyurea Protective Coatings
10.1002/adfm.79582.abstract: ABSTRACT Protective polymer coatings for marine and island infrastructures are expected to integrate resistance to mechanical damage, chloride attack, ultraviolet aging and fungal colonization, yet achieving these functions in a single dynamic coating remains challenging. Herein, an Oct-CUPU coating is developed by embedding a benzotriazole-modified g-C 3 N 4 /NH 2 -UiO-66 heterostructure, denoted as Oct-CU, into a disulfide-containing polyurea network. The g-C 3 N 4 /NH 2 -UiO-66 heterointerface provides photothermal conversion and interfacial reinforcement; the benzotriazole moiety improves UV shielding, and the dynamic polyurea matrix supplies reversible hydrogen bonding and disulfide exchange for damage repair. These coupled molecular and interfacial interactions enable localized light-to-heat conversion to activate chain mobility and network reconstruction, while the rod-like heterostructure promotes stress redistribution and improves long-term barrier stability. As a result, the optimized Oct-CUPU coating exhibits rapid NIR-triggered scratch healing and markedly enhanced corrosion-barrier retention. It also maintains improved abrasion tolerance, UV-aging resistance, and mold resistance compared with the unmodified coatings. This work presents a heterostructure-assisted design strategy for adaptive polyurea coatings with integrated self-healing, anticorrosion, anti-aging, and antifouling-related functions, offering potential for durable protection of metallic structures in marine, coastal, and outdoor environments.

10.1002/adfm.79554.title: Lipopolysaccharide-Triggered Self-Assembling Peptide Nanotraps for Coordinated Capture-Killing-Endotoxin Neutralization in Complicated Urinary Tract Infection
10.1002/adfm.79554.abstract: ABSTRACT Complicated urinary tract infections (cUTIs) caused by uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) remain difficult to treat because multidrug resistance and continuous urinary washout jointly limit antibacterial efficacy and local drug retention. Here, a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-responsive supramolecular peptide conjugate, PpIX-GFFVLK-HWKAVNWLKPWT (PFFH), is developed to address this delivery-retention trade-off through pathogen-triggered structural adaptation. PFFH integrates an E. coli LPS-binding motif, a β-sheet-forming self-assembly segment, and a PpIX sonosensitizer. It remains dispersed during delivery but transforms into peribacterial nanofibrous networks upon LPS recognition, promoting bacterial trapping and positioning PpIX near the bacterial interface for localized sonodynamic ROS activity. PFFH retains LPS-responsive assembly and antibacterial activity under urine-mimicking conditions and effectively kills reference and multidrug-resistant UPEC. The same LPS-binding motif also sequesters bacteriolysis-derived endotoxin and attenuates inflammatory activation. In a mouse cUTI model, PFFH shows prolonged retention at infected urinary sites, reduces bacterial burdens, and alleviates inflammatory injury. Thus, PFFH extends LPS-triggered structural adaptation beyond bacterial trapping to resolve the delivery-retention trade-off in cUTIs, while coupling peribacterial sonodynamic activity with endotoxin regulation in a single molecular platform, thereby establishing a disease-adapted supramolecular strategy for drug-resistant cUTIs.

10.1002/adfm.79178.title: Advancing CO 2 Electroreduction Toward Multicarbon Products via Catalyst Engineering and Integrated Paired Electrolysis
10.1002/adfm.79178.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (CO 2 RR) provides a compelling pathway for converting CO 2 into value-added multicarbon (C 2+ ) products using renewable electricity, yet its technological translation remains limited by coupled challenges spanning catalyst chemistry, reaction microenvironments, reactor architecture, and cathode-anode integration. This review develops a multiscale framework that connects molecular-level C-C coupling with device- and process-level performance. Fundamental CO 2 activation, reaction pathways, electrochemical metrics, and structure-activity relationships are critically examined, with particular emphasis on Cu-based catalysts and emerging catalyst-engineering strategies for selective C 2+ synthesis. These catalytic principles are then linked to operando surface states, intermediate coverage, local microenvironments, mass transport, membrane behavior, and electrolyzer configuration under technologically relevant conditions. Beyond cathodic optimization, oxygen evolution and alternative anodic chemistries, including biomass-derived alcohol oxidation and plastic-derived stream valorization, are assessed within integrated paired-electrolysis architectures. Their practical significance is benchmarked through matched current density, full-cell voltage, carbon and electron efficiency, product concentration, crossover, separation, durability, and realistic feed compatibility. This framework exposes critical catalyst-reactor-process trade-offs and defines design principles for scalable, durable, and economically credible CO 2 -to-C 2+ electrosynthesis.

10.1002/adfm.79548.title: Interfacial Stability Engineering of Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer Anodes
10.1002/adfm.79548.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is central to renewable hydrogen production, yet anode durability remains difficult to predict from half-cell catalyst metrics alone. In membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs), acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts must remain active while staying coupled to electron, proton, water and oxygen transport networks. This Review frames PEMWE anode degradation as a multilevel interfacial stability problem. It first defines the near-surface stability window of Ir/Ru active sites through valence evolution, hydroxylation, lattice-oxygen participation, reconstruction and metal dissolution. It then shows how this window is reshaped in MEAs by catalyst-layer percolation, ionomer distribution, pore architecture, porous transport layer (PTL)/catalyst-layer contact, membrane contamination, metal migration and dynamic operating stresses. Layered diagnostic strategies are summarized to trace macroscopic performance decay back to specific interfacial instability pathways. Future directions are discussed in terms of standardized evaluation, realistic operating environments and data-driven materials-interface-device optimization. This interfacial framework provides a basis for designing durable, non-noble-metal PEMWE anodes for practical renewable hydrogen production.

10.1002/adfm.79509.title: A Multifunctional Surface for Microplastic Trapping, SERS-Based Molecular Sensing, and PFAS Breakdown Through Microdroplet Deposition
10.1002/adfm.79509.abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) co-occur in natural and drinking waters, where they persist, accumulate, and pose risks to ecological and human health. Their mitigation demands integrated detection and remediation beyond single-function platforms. Here, we report Ag@TiO 2 nanobrushes (NBs), fabricated entirely by ambient charged microdroplet deposition, as a unified substrate for MP capture, SERS-based sensing, and photocatalytic PFAS degradation. In a two-step electrospray process, 1D Ag nanowire arrays (Ag NBs) were grown over large areas and overcoated with TiO 2 . During overcoating, a Marangoni-type capillary rearrangement drives Ag nanoparticles to the wire periphery, yielding an Ag@TiO 2 architecture with a percolated plasmonic network in a photoactive TiO 2 scaffold. The 3D NB network traps MP beads, while dense electromagnetic 3D hotspots enable SERS detection of Rhodamine 6G (LOD ∼38 fM; EF ∼6 × 10 7 ) and 1 µm polystyrene beads (LOD ∼31.6 ng mL −1 ; EF ∼ 10 5 ) across DI, tap, and simulated seawater. The unmodified substrate drives photocatalytic degradation of perfluorooctanoic acid under ambient sunlight, confirmed by mass spectrometry. This is the first fully electrosprayed platform, integrating MP trapping, femtomolar-level SERS detection, and PFAS photoremediation, thereby demonstrating ambient charged microdroplets as a scalable route to multifunctional nanostructures for water monitoring and remediation.

10.1002/adfm.78170.title: Concentration-Dependent Self-Assembly and Nanoparticle Maturation of Reflectins
10.1002/adfm.78170.abstract: ABSTRACT Cephalopods dynamically modulate coloration for camouflage and communication through iridophores whose Bragg reflector-like ultrastructures contain high-refractive-index proteins known as reflectins. However, the mechanisms linking concentration, conformation, and nanoparticle stabilization in full-length reflectins remain poorly understood. Here, coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of Doryteuthis pealeii reflectin A2 (RfA2) across five concentrations are combined with dynamic light scattering (DLS) and circular dichroism (CD) measurements. The simulations reveal rapid initial protein aggregation followed by slower structural maturation, during which interprotein interaction energy and contact networks continue to evolve. A simulation-derived concentration-dependent crossover separates multi-cluster vs single-cluster regimes and DLS shows larger assemblies at higher experimental concentrations. The simulations further delineate region-specific secondary-structure reorganization and CD demonstrates concentration-sensitive structural changes with a distinct secondary-structure redistribution. Moreover, the simulations predict concentration dependence in the contribution of intermolecular contact network reorganization; the L1, L3, and L5 linker regions supplied many of these contacts, with L3 providing the dominant contribution. Overall, these findings establish a molecular-level framework where concentration governs RfA2 self-assembly and continued conformational and intermolecular reorganization during maturation, providing insight into sequence- and assembly-level principles regarding iridophore optical function and reflectin-based materials design.

10.1002/adfm.79595.title: Correction to “Machine Learning-Driven Molecule Additives for High-Performance Perovskite Solar Cells With Bandgap Universality and Scalability”

10.1002/adfm.79329.title: Mechanical Strain Tunes Proton Chemistry at Oxide-Water Interfaces
10.1002/adfm.79329.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton transfer at oxide-water interfaces controls surface hydroxylation, interfacial charge, and elementary photocatalytic steps, and is usually tuned electrostatically, through pH or applied potential. Whether mechanical strain provides an independent handle, and by what molecular mechanism, has remained unclear. Using Deep Potential molecular dynamics with density-functional-theory accuracy, we study the anatase (101)-water interface under biaxial strain from to . Tension switches the contact layer from molecular to dissociative adsorption, raising the dissociated fraction from 8% to 67%; free-energy surfaces show the proton is released through an intermediate solvent water rather than transferred directly, with tension lowering the barrier and inverting the molecular-dissociated stability. The Wannier centers of the electronic distribution trace this to a rearrangement of valence electron density at both surface reactive sites, which results in -bound water becoming a stronger acid and becoming a stronger base. Analysis of the strain dependence of the dissociation free energy also indicates a reciprocal mechanical effect: water dissociation contributes a compressive interfacial stress that reduces the tensile stress at fixed imposed strain. Strain thus tunes both halves of an interfacial acid-base pair at once, providing a mechanical handle on proton chemistry at oxide-water interfaces.

10.1002/adfm.78265.title: Dual-Dipole Synergy Breaks the Polarization-Breakdown Trade-Off for Ultrahigh Energy Density Flexible Capacitors
10.1002/adfm.78265.abstract: ABSTRACT A fundamental trade-off plagues dielectric capacitors: enhancing maximum polarization typically degrades breakdown strength, severely limiting energy density. Here we present a dual-dipole synergy strategy that resolves this contradiction. In layered perovskite films, we engineer an interlayer dipole driven by charge misalignment between functional layers, working in concert with the intralayer polyhedral dipole. Their synergy simultaneously amplifies polarization and strengthens the relaxor behavior and band gap that govern breakdown strength. Implemented in flexible SrBi 5- x Pr x Ti 4 AlO 18 capacitors, this design breaks the inverse coupling between maximum polarization and breakdown, delivering an ultrahigh energy density of 131.1 J∙cm −3 with 70.5% efficiency, a 179% enhancement over the unengineered counterpart. The capacitor retains excellent stability over 10 6 bending cycles. This work establishes a generalizable design paradigm wherein the vertical interlayer dipole acts as a new degree of freedom to independently tune polarization and breakdown in layered dielectrics, opening a transformative route beyond the classic trade-off.

10.1002/adfm.78701.title: Programmable-Responsive Cell-Resident Polymeric Micelles for Granzyme B-Steered Integrated Anti-PD-L1 Immunotherapy via Membrane Repair Interference
10.1002/adfm.78701.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the clinical promise of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), its therapeutic performance in prostate cancer remains suboptimal due to membrane repair-associated resistance and insufficient immune engagement. Herein, a programmable-responsive cell-resident micelle (PBAM) is engineered to integrate BAPTA (a calcium chelator), anti-PD-L1 antibody, and prochlorperazine (PCZ)/β-cyclodextrin inclusion complexes within a pH/granzyme B (GzmB)-dual-responsive system, enabling spatiotemporally coordinated multidrug release for integrated anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy. PBAM selectively accumulates in tumors and undergoes acid-triggered PCZ release, suppressing PI3K/Akt signaling and reducing endocytic uptake to maintain tumor cell surface anchoring. Upon ICB-mediated immune activation, cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) secrete granzyme and perforin to induce tumor cell apoptosis while triggering GzmB-responsive micellar degradation for BAPTA release, thereby disrupting Ca 2+ -dependent membrane repair and sensitizing tumor cells to CTL-mediated cytotoxicity. This spatiotemporally coordinated cascade reinforces PD-1/PD-L1 blockade to overcome immune resistance, thereby restoring antitumor immunity and enhancing memory-associated T-cell responses, ultimately constraining tumor progression and recurrence.

10.1002/adfm.78783.title: Low-Concentration Hydrated Eutectic Electrolyte Design for High-Performance Aqueous K-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78783.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous K-ion batteries (AKIBs) hold promising potential for large-scale energy storage due to high safety, environmental friendliness, and low cost. However, traditional aqueous electrolytes are limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window (ESW), while water-in-salt electrolytes face challenges such as high cost, low ionic conductivity, and precipitation at low temperatures, which significantly hinder their applications. Herein, we report a class of low-concentration hydrated eutectic electrolyte (2.45 m KFSI-Bds-H 2 O) featuring a wide ESW (3.7 V), reduced viscosity (13.4 mPa·s), improved ionic conductivity (17.5 mS cm −1 ), and excellent non-flammability characteristics to construct high-performance AKIBs. In the designed electrolyte, Bds serves dual roles in regulating hydrogen-bond and solvation structures, wherein it not only disrupts the strong hydrogen-bond network of H 2 O to suppress its decomposition side reactions, but also reconstructs the K + solvation structure. The AKIB delivers a high energy density of 100 Wh kg −1 and superior capacity retention of 75.1% after 2000 cycles, and can perform stably across a broad temperature window of -20°C to 60°C. This work offers a promising strategy for developing low-cost, high-safety, and long-life aqueous batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78741.title: Milliampere-Level p-Type 2D Zero Differential Transconductance-MVL Device via Asymmetric Acceptor Doping
10.1002/adfm.78741.abstract: ABSTRACT The limited performance of p-type devices, which remain significantly inferior to their n-type counterparts, is a critical bottleneck in advancing 2D transition-metal dichalcogenide (2D TMDC)-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Moreover, in the context of high-density integration, multivalued logic (MVL) has emerged as a promising approach to reduce device count and interconnect complexity. However, the development of high-performance p-type devices for MVL applications remains largely unexplored. Here, we report an asymmetric Cl doping-induced high-performance p-type zero-differential transconductance (ZDT)-based MVL device. The facile one-pot asymmetric Cl doping in vertically stacked WSe 2 channels realizes ternary behavior with three distinct states with a flat middle state within a single device. Owing to the significant efficiency of Cl doping, the resulting p-type ZDT-MVL device shows a high on-current of 1.49 mA. In addition, the Cl-doped p-type FET exhibits a low subthreshold swing (SS) of 74.17 mV dec −1 and achieves a high on-current of 2.83 mA within distinct configurations, respectively. This effective strategy not only achieves high-performance p-type characteristics comparable to those of an n-type FET but also enables the realization of the first 2D TMDC-based p-type ZDT-MVL device, thereby providing a viable platform for CMOS-based MVL systems.

10.1002/adfm.78753.title: Decouple and Synergize: D-π Conjugation-Enabled Remote Electronic Tuning of M-O Sites for Enhanced C-H/O-H Cleavage in HMF Electrooxidation
10.1002/adfm.78753.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation reaction (HMFOR) is a green biomass valorization route, yet its scalability is constrained by the intrinsically sluggish hydroxymethyl oxidation on transition-metal-based catalysts, which, unlike aldehyde oxidation, requires concurrent C-H/O-H cleavage and C(sp 3 ) → C(sp 2 ) rehybridization. However, current strategies lack atomic-scale precision to accelerate this kinetics and establish clear structure-performance relationships. Herein, M 3 (HHTP) 2 (M = Co, Cu) with atomically ordered and dispersed metal sites was designed to decouple intrinsic roles of M-O sites in HMFOR. Building on this, bimetallic Co 1.8 Cu 1.2 (HHTP) 2 was constructed, harnessing d-π conjugation for precise bidirectional long-range electronic communication between spatially separated M-O sites: Cu-O kinetically accelerates the sluggish hydroxymethyl oxidation on Co-O, while Co-O reciprocally mitigates Cu-O poisoning from excessive HMF adsorption, establishing a self-sustaining electronic synergy. Meanwhile, differentiated OH − adsorption on the dual sites optimizes the H-bond network, accelerating electrochemical-chemical cycle at Co-O. Ultimately, Co 1.8 Cu 1.2 (HHTP) 2 delivers a 2.7-fold higher 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid yield than Co 3 (HHTP) 2 and enables gram-scale production of 99.4%-pure 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid via 2,5-diformylfuran and 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furancarboxylic acid pathways. This work establishes d-π conjugation as a general strategy to decouple and synergize specific roles of spatially separated sites to overcome the rate-determining step, providing a novel paradigm for rational catalyst design in complex multi-step reactions.

10.1002/adfm.78746.title: Crystalline-Amorphous Heterointerfaces Enable Elastic Peracetic Acid Activation for Resilient Remediation of Hypersaline Wastewater
10.1002/adfm.78746.abstract: ABSTRACT Hypersaline organic wastewater treatment is chronically impeded by mechanistic inhibition and rigid lattice inelasticity. Herein, we design a MnBiCoO x catalyst featuring crystalline-amorphous (C-A) heterointerfaces and propose a synergistic “remote electron pump-localized electronic depot” mechanism for peracetic acid (PAA) activation. This architecture leverages interfacial symmetry breaking and spin polarization to modulate e g orbital occupancy and d-d hybridization, establishing a resilient electronic structure with intrinsic charge-buffering capacity that ensures robust catalytic stability against hypersaline environments. Intriguingly, the presence of chloride ions (Cl − ) induces a counterintuitive 2.58-fold kinetic acceleration, reframing halides as coordination-driven modulatory hubs that promote spin-polarized electron injection into PAA σ* antibonding orbitals. Quantitative contribution analysis identifies singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) as the dominant matrix-tolerant species (65.47%), underscoring a mechanistic shift toward non-radical-mediated pathways. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the d z 2 -mediated σ-bonding overlap, coupled with an upward shift of the d-band center, substantially reduces the activation barrier. Crucially, the MnBiCoO x /PAA system exhibits operational stability for 912 h in hypersaline wastewater, and life cycle assessment (LCA) confirms its exceptional environmental sustainability. This work provides mechanistic insights into rationally designing catalysts with structural resilience and electronic responsiveness for adaptive environmental remediation.

10.1002/adfm.78742.title: Spatial-Color Encoding for Multimodal Optical Encryption via an Electrowetting Display Platform
10.1002/adfm.78742.abstract: ABSTRACT Optical encryption and secure display technologies provide physical-layer protection for visual information, yet most platforms face a trade-off between rapid response and simple optical readout. Here, we report a confined electrowetting display (EWD) platform for optical encryption, featuring mask-free programmable patterning, direct optical readout, and millisecond-scale response. An encoding strategy combining spatial and color coding is proposed, for the first time, for multimodal information encryption. Inkjet-printed conductive micropillars locally enhance the electric field at pixel quarter-edges, inducing deterministic oil-film rupture and directional retraction that define four spatial states, while a vertically stacked cyan-magenta-yellow structure enables subtractive color mixing. As demonstrations, the encrypted patterns are revealed only upon simultaneous application of independent voltage keys. Decryption supports dual-level readout: direct visual recognition of the reconstructed mixed-color pattern, and microscopic decoding of spatial pixel states mapped via a Base64 scheme to retrieve digital and textual information. In addition to a fast switching time of 25 ms, the experimentally demonstrated Base64 mapping corresponds to an estimated areal payload density of 1.77 × 10 8 bits/m 2 . This scalable EWD platform integrates programmable patterning, key-gated access, rapid response, and two-level optical readout, opening a new avenue toward high-speed secure displays and advanced anti-counterfeiting technologies.

10.1002/adfm.78713.title: A Dragon-Fruit-Like Nanoplatform Containing Polydopamine-Wrapped Selenium Quantum Dots Boosts Synergistic Chemo-Photothermal Therapy for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
10.1002/adfm.78713.abstract: ABSTRACT Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a significant clinical challenge due to lack of targetable biomarkers and systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. To address these hurdles, we engineered a bioinspired “dragon-fruit-mimetic” nanoplatform (GemSe@PDA), with selenium quantum dots (SeQDs) and gemcitabine (Gem) uniformly dispersed in polydopamine (PDA) matrix that acts as a functional photothermal carrier. This distinctive structural endows high drug loading capacity, and the PDA matrix degrades under lysosomal acidic conditions (pH ∼5.0), enabling stimuli-responsive release of SeQDs and Gem. GemSe@PDA shows uniform morphology (174.8 nm in diameter) and excellent photothermal capability of raising local temperature to 48.3°C within 10 min. Functionally, the GemSe@PDA nanoplatform integrates three modalities of SeQD-driven apoptosis, PDA-mediated photothermal ablation under 808 nm NIR irradiation, and Gem-induced chemotherapy. Mechanistically, RNA-seq analysis revealed that SeQDs provoke apoptosis by regulating the Akt/caspase-3 signaling pathway, while Gem triggers cell cycle arrest. In vivo studies demonstrated that GemSe@PDA markedly boosts tumor-targeted accumulation and effectively suppresses tumor growth, lowering the tumor weight to merely 15.9% of the control group without systemic toxicity. By combining the structural advantages of a dragon fruit-like design with bioactive SeQDs, this nanoplatform provides a versatile, biocompatible strategy for overcoming the therapeutic problems of TNBC.

10.1002/adfm.78119.title: Physics-Grounded Materials Artificial Intelligence for Reliable Materials Discovery
10.1002/adfm.78119.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming materials discovery, yet conventional data-driven approaches often suffer from limited interpretability, poor extrapolation, and inconsistency with physical laws. Since materials behavior is fundamentally governed by thermodynamics, kinetics, electronic structure, transport processes, and operating environments, the next generation of materials intelligence must move beyond correlation-based prediction toward physics-grounded reasoning. In this Perspective, we systematically discuss Physics-Grounded Materials AI (PhysMat AI) as a unifying perspective for integrating physical knowledge into materials intelligence through five complementary roles: physics as prior knowledge, descriptors, constraints, verifiers, and infrastructure. Using representative examples from catalysis, solid-state electrolytes in solid-state battery, and hydrogen-storage materials, we illustrate how physical principles guide data representation, model reasoning, validation workflows, and knowledge management. We further present how AI agents can leverage these physics-aware components to perform mechanism-guided discovery within physically feasible search spaces. Finally, we outline a developmental roadmap from physics-aware AI to physics-reasoning AI and ultimately physics-autonomous AI. Looking forward, materials intelligence should evolve from predictive models toward autonomous scientific systems capable of integrating physical reasoning, multiscale simulations, experimental validation, and continuous knowledge updating for reliable materials discovery.

10.1002/adfm.78764.title: Liquid-Metal-Printed Ga 2 O 3 Weaves a Spherical Self-Driven Meta-Array With Panoramic Solar-Blind Polarization Compass Function
10.1002/adfm.78764.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-dimensional ultrawide-bandgap oxides underpin the development of integrated solar-blind photodetectors. However, the cumbersome production line and the humdrum photodetection dimension both restrict further application in the field of integrated optoelectronics. Herein, we optimize the liquid-metal-printing process on both planar and curved-surface substrates and synthesize a 2D 8-inch β-Ga 2 O 3 single crystal. The β-Ga 2 O 3 solar-blind photodetector features an excellent ultraviolet-visible rejection ratio (> 10 5 ), prominent anisotropy ratio (4.5), and wide linear dynamic range (∼130 dB). Based on a 2D crossed-printed β-Ga 2 O 3 homojunction, a self-driven solar-blind polarization photodetector with high responsivity (33.3 A/W) and fast response speed (< 2 µs) is exquisitely constructed. Inspired by the skylight polarization pattern in the solar-terrestrial system, we introduce a novel spherical meta-array, working as a panoramic polarization compass to detect solar-blind sources within a complete 720° spatial angle. This work delivers insights into the growth platform for single-crystal Ga 2 O 3 and demonstrates a prospective passive device architecture for solar-blind warning, positioning, and monitoring.

10.1002/adfm.77997.title: Pyrene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks With Diacetylene Linkers for Tandem Adsorption and Photodegradation of Perfluorooctanoic Acid
10.1002/adfm.77997.abstract: ABSTRACT Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are anthropogenic water contaminants that pose severe risks to human health and the environment, and strategies for PFAS remediation are urgently needed. Here, we present a combined experimental and computational study of a tetragonal Py-DEBD framework, as both an adsorbent and a heterogeneous photocatalyst for the degradation of PFOA. Through batch photodegradation experiments, we found that Py-DEBD adsorbed and degraded PFOA, and as the solution pH decreased from 4 to 2, PFOA adsorption capacity and degradation rate increased. For photocatalytic degradation experiments at a pH of 2, over 99% of PFOA was removed from the solution, and 32% defluorination was achieved within 24 h. The solution concentrations of short-chain degradation byproducts initially increased during photodegradation, and several peaked and then decreased with continued irradiation as they were photochemically degraded. Density functional theory simulations demonstrate favorable adsorption of PFOA onto the Py-DEBD and show that photoinduced charge transfer under UV irradiation leads to PFOA oxidation, supporting the decarboxylation-hydroxylation-elimination-hydrolysis (DHEH) mechanism for PFOA photo-oxidative degradation. This work, therefore, uncovers a fundamental strategy for designing metal-free porous materials for adsorption and photocatalytic degradation and opens a promising avenue for the development of photoactive adsorbent materials for contaminant remediation.

10.1002/adfm.78684.title: Synergistic Dual-Photoreaction Crosslinking Enables High Phosphoric Acid Retention in High-Temperature Proton Exchange Membranes
10.1002/adfm.78684.abstract: ABSTRACT Phosphoric acid (PA)-doped high-temperature proton exchange membranes (HT-PEMs) enable anhydrous proton conduction but remain limited by PA migration, excessive swelling, and conductivity decay. Here, anthracenylmethyl groups are introduced into PEEK side chains through partial quaternization of tertiary amine groups. The resulting polymer retains pre-existing benzophenone photoreactive units while incorporating anthracene sites capable of UV-induced [4 + 4] photocycloaddition. The newly formed quaternary ammonium groups enhance polymer-PA interactions. PA is introduced before UV irradiation, allowing a proton-conducting environment to develop within the membrane. Subsequent anthracene [4 + 4] photocycloaddition and benzophenone type II photochemistry cooperatively stabilize the PA-doped structure while generating additional subnanometer free volume and a compact crosslinked surface layer. Among the investigated membranes, PEEK-M70-50%-PA-UV exhibits the most favorable performance, retaining nearly 98% of its PA and 91% of its initial conductivity after 120 h at 80°C and 40% RH. It achieves a proton conductivity of 240 mS cm − 1 and a peak power density of 1150 mW cm − 2 at 160°C, while sustaining non-humidified fuel-cell operation for 210 h. This work establishes synergistic crosslinking through anthracene [4 + 4] photocycloaddition and benzophenone type II photochemistry as an effective strategy for limiting PA loss while preserving rapid proton transport in HT-PEMs.

10.1002/adfm.78725.title: Intratracheal Extracellular Matrix-Mimetic Hydrogel Modulates Immune Homeostasis for Asthma Therapy
10.1002/adfm.78725.abstract: ABSTRACT Glucocorticoids, while central to asthma management, face clinical challenges due to systemic toxicity and acquired resistance, underscoring an urgent demand for novel targeted therapies. Here, a bioinspired hydrogel derived from decellularized lung extracellular matrix (dECM) is engineered for the localized and synchronized co-delivery of methylprednisolone (MP) and resveratrol (RSV). The resulting RML@dECM platform demonstrates excellent biocompatibility and provides sustained release of both agents within the bronchial microenvironment. Therapeutically, the system effectively alleviates asthma pathology via dual immunomodulatory and anti-remodeling actions. Mechanistically, RML@dECM restores pulmonary immune homeostasis by rebalancing Th1/Th2 responses and repolarizing macrophages from a pro-fibrotic M2 toward a protective M1 phenotype, while concurrently inhibiting mucus hypersecretion through modulation of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway. In vivo, RML@dECM surpasses conventional corticosteroid monotherapy, markedly reducing airway hyperresponsiveness, mucus overproduction, and histological damage. Importantly, by confining drug action to the lungs, the platform significantly minimizes systemic exposure and off-target adverse effects. This work presents a synergistic, locally delivered dual-drug hydrogel that addresses core limitations in asthma treatment, offering a promising translational strategy for achieving sustained airway immunomodulation with enhanced safety.

10.1002/adfm.78686.title: Dynamic Matrix Competition Enables Host-to-Guest Reversal for Tailoring Carbon Dots Afterglow From Time-Dependent Color to White Emission
10.1002/adfm.78686.abstract: ABSTRACT Room-temperature afterglow carbon dots (CDs) materials, combining long-lived emission, low toxicity, structural tunability, and ease of processing, hold significant application prospects in information encryption, anti-counterfeiting, lighting, and sensing. However, existing boric acid (BA)-based CDs afterglow systems generally suffer from issues such as single-color emission, limited stimulus-response dimensions, and unclear matrix regulation mechanisms. Herein, a BA/NaOH dual-matrix system was developed, in which CDs afterglow can be precisely regulated by matrix ratio, achieving orange-to-green and orange-to-cyan time-dependent color-changing afterglow, and white afterglow. Through structural characterization of the composites, it was found that with increasing NaOH content, the confinement environment transitioned from a BA-dominated B-O network to a NaOH-dominated borate structure, Na ionic bonds, and a deprotonated CDs surface. The specific regulatory mechanism of NaOH on each emission center in the composites was elucidated as promoting the generation and enhancement of short-wavelength thermally activated delayed fluorescence while suppressing long-wavelength room-temperature phosphorescence. Based on this, a theoretical model of “host-to-guest reversal” based on dynamic matrix competition was proposed. This work provides a new matrix competition regulation strategy for the design of single-component multicolor and white CDs afterglow materials and demonstrates their application potential in multi-level information encryption, anti-counterfeiting patterns, Morse coding, and warning signage.

10.1002/adfm.78767.title: Visible-Light-Triggered Carbene Crosslinking in Dynamic Disulfide Networks for Patternable, Debondable, and Recyclable Smart Adhesives
10.1002/adfm.78767.abstract: ABSTRACT Smart pressure-sensitive adhesives (PSAs) capable of on-demand debonding and recycling are highly desirable for advancing the sustainability of flexible electronics and devices. Here, we report a visible-light-responsive PSA based on a dynamic copolymer composed of α-thioctic acid (TA) and a diazo-functionalized acrylate. The dynamic disulfide backbone imparts intrinsic self-adhesion and closed-loop recyclability, while the diazo moieties enable ultrafast carbene-mediated crosslinking upon blue light (420 nm) irradiation. This rapid crosslinking triggers a synergistic effect within 10 s: it elevates the bulk modulus of the adhesive matrix to facilitate ultrafast interfacial debonding, while the concurrent in situ evolution of N 2 creates a microporous architecture that enables high-resolution surface patterning. Moreover, the resulting hierarchical porosity dramatically accelerates ethanol infiltration, driving rapid removal of the patterned area, thereby enabling selective recyclability of the unexposed polymer. Consequently, this work establishes a versatile and sustainable paradigm for smart adhesives, seamlessly integrating, on-demand debonding and recyclability for next-generation flexible electronics.

10.1002/adfm.78768.title: Soft Confinement Couples Shape Morphing With Persistent Phosphorescence in Liquid Crystal Networks
10.1002/adfm.78768.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological systems regulate molecular functions by coupling local confinement with dynamic structural reconfiguration. Translating this principle to govern excited-state dynamics in soft materials remains challenging, as conventional photophysical stabilization relies on rigid matrices that conflict with macroscopic deformability. Here, we introduce a liquid crystal network-based soft-confinement strategy that reconciles these characteristics. Ordered mesogenic domains establish soft confinement that stabilizes triplet excitons through dispersion-driven π-π interactions while preserving thermally induced network reorganization. Consequently, the material synchronizes microscopic phosphorescence regulation with macroscopic shape morphing under a unified structural transition. The platform enables persistent room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) in seven polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), achieving a triplet lifetime of 5.12 s and a phosphorescence quantum yield of 26.80% under ambient conditions. Theoretical calculations and structural characterization indicate that soft confinement plays the dominant role in exciton stabilization, while long-range order further suppresses oxygen quenching. Additionally, the material exhibits reversible deformation-phosphorescence switching over 200 thermal cycles and can be processed into fibers, films, and microspheres for dynamic photonic writing and time-domain information encryption. This work establishes adaptive soft confinement as a pathway for coupling excited-state regulation with macroscopic mechanical functionality.

10.1002/adfm.77836.title: Gradient-Conductivity Architecture Enables Synchronous Enhancement of Sensitivity and Detection Range in Multifunctional All-Paper Sensors
10.1002/adfm.77836.abstract: ABSTRACT Paper-based sensors offer a sustainable platform for wearable electronics, yet their performance is fundamentally constrained by the intrinsic “contact-jumping” behavior of hierarchical cellulose fibers, which causes abrupt conduction transitions, early current saturation, and an inevitable sensitivity-detection range trade-off. Here, we introduce a stepwise conductivity-gradient, open-circuit-triggered architecture that spatially reprograms pressure-induced electron pathways within cellulose networks. By integrating in situ grown AgNPs on MXene-modified fibers with a pressure-activated MXene interdigitated electrode, the sensor enables cascaded pathway evolution that delays current saturation and establishes a progressively tunable piezoresistive response. Multiscale simulations and interfacial charge analyses reveal strain-induced Ag-MXene polarization and charge delocalization, which expand available conduction channels and lower transport barriers. Benefiting from this gradient-engineered mechanism, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh sensitivity of 1365.87 kPa −1 , a broad detection range of 0.7 Pa-203.2 kPa, a 0.7 Pa detection limit, and excellent durability over 10 000 cycles. The hierarchical network also affords strong EMI shielding and high breathability, enabling stable on-skin operation and multifunctional sensing.

10.1002/adfm.77921.title: Tracking Battery Microstructural Degradation Through Directional Thermal Transport Signatures
10.1002/adfm.77921.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a compact, surface-mounted thin-film sensor that measures a battery cell's three-dimensional anisotropic thermal conductivity in real time, enabling non-invasive tracking of cell state of health. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on voltage or capacity measurements, this technique assesses degradation directly through changes in the cell's internal microstructure. During accelerated degradation cycling, we observe a systematic increase in the anisotropy ratio of in-plane to through-plane thermal conductivity as the battery degrades, consistent with microstructural and compositional evolution of the electrodes. The in-plane thermal conductivity exhibits the highest sensitivity to degradation by detecting anode lithium plating, which introduces an additional pathway for in-plane heat conduction. In contrast, the through-plane thermal conductivity captures particle cracking and the formation of additional interfaces that impede heat flow. This directional thermal transport signature provides a powerful indicator of microstructural and compositional changes within the cell, establishing a foundation for operando battery diagnostics and predictive health modeling.

10.1002/adfm.78732.title: Bioinspired Ultralow-Power Flexible Electro-Optically Configurable Synaptic Transistors: An Integrated Perception-Processing-Tracking Visual Chain
10.1002/adfm.78732.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological visual tracking closely parallels the autonomous navigation that requires motion recognition, typically progressing through a cascade of optical perception, adaptive attention, and real-time tracking. However, most efforts focus on low-level perception and decoupled algorithms, while overlooking the crucial intermediate mechanism of in situ background suppression for salient target separation. Here, inspired by the Nile tilapia visual system, a perception-processing-tracking visual chain architecture based on flexible, electro-optically configurable synaptic transistors is first proposed. Leveraging the sharp absorption edge of quantum dots (QDs), the device achieves prominent RGB-NIR band recognition. Notably, the introduction of a phosphoric acid-mediation strategy significantly enhances the stability of blue-emitting CsPbCl 3 QDs while preserving their excellent optical performance. Combined with a poly(vinylidene fluoride- co -hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) dielectric layer, the system enables efficient cross-modal optoelectronic signal processing. Electric field tuning of photocarrier tunneling assigns an attention score as high as 95.88% to target regions and merely 3.79% to backgrounds, with the score gap widening over time. Assisted by reservoir computing (RC), the device classifies six target motion trajectories with 98.89% accuracy, operating at an ultra-low energy cost of 0.011 fJ per synaptic event with exceptional mechanical flexibility. These attributes open up promising prospects for future autonomous driving applications.

10.1002/adfm.78256.title: Segmental-Incompatibility-Enabled Non-Conjugated Nanodomains for Aggregation-State Regulation of Wide-Temperature Polyimide Energy-Storage Dielectrics
10.1002/adfm.78256.abstract: ABSTRACT Addressing the issues of accelerated charge migration and diminished energy storage performance in polyimide (PI) under a high-temperature electric field, this study proposes an aggregation-state regulation strategy through the construction of non-conjugated nanodomains in PI-based copolymers. By introducing non-conjugated polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) diamine into the PI backbone and leveraging the segmental incompatibility between aromatic PI and PDMS segments, a nanoscale “sea-island” phase-separated structure is generated based on the enthalpy-driven phase separation principle. This tailored heterogeneous structure weakens compact aromatic packing, reduces local electronic coupling between PI-derived segments, and suppresses long-range charge migration while simultaneously introducing deep trapping sites at heterogeneous interfaces, thereby synergistically regulating charge diffusion behavior of the PI-PDMS copolymer. The resultant PI-PDMS film exhibits outstanding performance over a wide-temperature range: a dielectric constant of 4.41 with low loss of <0.015 at 100 Hz, a discharged energy density of 16.2 J/cm 3 with efficiency of > 90% at 950 MV/m and 25°C, and 6.6 J/cm 3 with efficiency of > 90% at 600 MV/m and 200°C. This research establishes a fresh paradigm for the design of high-performance polymer dielectrics through aggregation-state regulation.
