10.1002/adfm.78736.title: Coupling *CO Protonation on Cu Single Atoms With H 2 O Dissociation on Bi Nanoclusters for Synergistic CO 2 -to-Methanol Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.78736.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to methanol (CH 3 OH) represents a promising strategy for mitigating global warming and energy shortages. However, the rational design of high-performance electrocatalysts for selective CO 2 -to-CH 3 OH conversion remains challenging. Herein, we construct a dual-site catalyst featuring Cu single atoms (Cu SAs ) and Bi nanoclusters (Bi NCs ) co-anchored on a hierarchical porous nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) support (Cu SAs Bi NCs /NC). It delivers a high CH 3 OH Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 73.6% with a stability of 120 h in an H-cell, and reaches a CH 3 OH partial current density of 106.6 mA cm −2 with 82% FE in a flow cell. The excellent performance is attributed to a synergistic mechanism: Cu SAs promote the generation and protonation of the key *CO intermediate, while Bi NCs facilitate H 2 O dissociation to supply *H to adjacent Cu sites. Their electronic interaction strengthens *CO adsorption and lowers its protonation barrier at Cu sites, while accelerating H 2 O activation at Bi sites. Furthermore, the confinement effect of the hierarchical pore structure in the NC support facilitates the enrichment of *CO intermediate and stabilizes the catalyst. This work establishes a conceptual framework for developing synergistic electrocatalysts through precise atomic-scale component integration, offering an appealing strategy to boost CH 3 OH production by simultaneously tuning *CO adsorption/protonation and H 2 O dissociation.

10.1002/adfm.78696.title: Reconstructive Polarimetry With Scalable Graphene-Metal Infrared Photodetectors
10.1002/adfm.78696.abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advent of smart photodetectors, where in situ tuning of responsivity enables the reconstruction of light intensity, polarization, and spectrum by a single device, has revolutionized the field of optoelectronics. So far, most such reconstructive detectors were realized with non-scalable technology of van der Waals stacking. Here, we demonstrate the infrared reconstructive polarimetry with photodetectors based on conventional gated graphene-metal junctions. The reconstruction exploits the gate tuning of polarization contrast, which enables the determination of both infrared power and polarization angle from photovoltage measurements at two different gate voltages. The physics enabling the polarimetry lies in polarization-dependent shift of the electron hot spot near the contact, and the gate tuning of photosensitive barrier width. We further show the universality of polarization reconstruction, i.e. its feasibility with different geometries of the junction, and with graphene of different quality, from boron-nitride encapsulated flakes to the scalable chemical vapor deposited films.

10.1002/adfm.78283.title: Hydrogel-Based Optical Fiber: Sensing Mechanism, Biomedical Applications, and Perspectives
10.1002/adfm.78283.abstract: ABSTRACT Optical fibers have been widely applied in biomedical sensing technologies, including health monitoring, disease diagnosis, and minimally invasive surgery. However, traditional silica (SiO 2 )-based rigid fibers face significant challenges in biomedical integration due to their inherent brittleness and limited biocompatibility. In contrast, hydrogel-based optical fibers have garnered increasing attention in optogenetics, implantable photomedicine, and biomedical sensing, due to their excellent biocompatibility, biomimetic mechanical modulus, and immunity to electromagnetic interference. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of hydrogel optical fibers for biomedical sensing, emphasizing their fabrication technologies, sensing mechanisms, biomedical applications, current challenges, and future prospects. First, fundamental characteristics and synthetic strategies are introduced, together with the classification of light-guiding hydrogels. Second, fabrication techniques and sensing mechanisms of hydrogel optical fibers are systematically summarized, focusing on their unique optical modulation modes. Third, a wide range of biomedical sensing applications are highlighted, including the detection of glucose, antibiotics, dopamine, pH, and metal ions. Finally, key challenges and future prospects are discussed, including improving biocompatibility, long-term reliability, sterilization strategies, multimodal integration, and achieving intelligent therapeutic systems. This review aims to inspire further innovations in hydrogel optical fiber-based biomedical sensing, and to facilitate the development of next-generation biomedical sensing platforms for wearable and implantable healthcare devices.

10.1002/adfm.79601.title: Six-Electron-Storage Polynuclear Quinoxaline Derivatives with Multiple S -Propanoic Acid Side-Groups for High-Capacity Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79601.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous organic redox flow batteries are promising for constructing large-scale energy storage systems with inherent safety and eco-friendliness, but restricted by limited capacity and cyclability. Herein, we design and synthesize two types of six-electron-storage triquinoxalinylene derivatives functionalized with six or three S -propionic acid side groups, namely HATN-HSPA or HATN-TSPA, both demonstrating a reversible three-step six-electron storage capability. The extended π -conjugation structure of triquinoxalinylene redox core and rational modification of S -propionic acid groups bring them high electrochemical reversibility and stability. The strong solubilizing effect of hexa-substituted S -propanoic acid groups rendered HATN-HSPA a maximum solubility of 1.26 m (i.e., a charge storage concentration of 7.56 m ) and a theoretical capacity (202.62 Ah L −1 ), which are over three times those of traditional organic active molecules with single- or two-electron storage processes. The flow batteries grounded in nearly saturated HATN-HSPA anolyte achieved a record-breaking capacity of 150 Ah L −1 . The flow batteries grounded in 0.5 m HATN-HSPA anolyte also released high-capacity retention of 98.4% after 600 cycles (or 60 days), with a capacity decrement of 0.0027% cycle −1 (or 0.027% day −1 ). This work presents a multi-electron molecular engineering methodology for developing high-storage and durable multi-electron-storage organic species for scalable and sustainable grid-scale energy storage.

10.1002/adfm.79534.title: Guest-Engineered Intrapore Microenvironments in Resorcinarene-Based Frameworks for Enhanced Iodine Capture
10.1002/adfm.79534.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient iodine capture by metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) requires the spatial integration of accessible pore space and strong binding sites without compromising framework integrity. Herein, we employ host-guest encapsulation to functionalize otherwise underutilized pore space of macrocycle-based MOFs by introducing an organic salt guest, N-(2-trimethylammonioethyl)pyridinium dibromide (PyBr) within the cage-like units of resorcinarene-based uranium-organic frameworks (UOF-1D and UOF-2D). While maintaining the host framework well, such a modification creates a Br − /N + -rich pore microenvironment in as-synthesized PyBr@UOF-1D and PyBr@UOF-2D. The resulting materials exhibit gas-phase iodine uptakes of up to 3.50 g·g −1 , markedly exceeding those of the pristine frameworks, free guests, and physical mixtures. Spectroscopic analyses and calculations show that confinement enriches iodine around guest sites, where Br − polarizes I 2 and promotes polyiodide/polyhalide formation, while N + electrostatically stabilizes the resulting anions. The enhanced capture originates from improved pore utilization through cooperative confinement and guest-derived binding interactions. Its successful application to both 1D and 2D UOFs demonstrates the adaptability of guest-engineered pore microenvironments across distinct architectures, offering a route toward target-specific separations.

10.1002/adfm.79593.title: Thickness-Confined Mo-VO 2 /CNTs Heterogeneous Composite Films for Synergistic Dynamic Infrared Camouflage and Electromagnetic Protection
10.1002/adfm.79593.abstract: ABSTRACT As a typical phase-change material for adaptive infrared (IR) camouflage, the development of VO 2 is constrained by its inherent “extreme-emissivity trap”, with modulation limited to a narrow range of 0.9-0.65, and suffers from intrinsically low free-electron density that precludes coinstantaneous electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding. Here, a multi-modulation strategy via thickness-confined Mo-VO 2 /CNTs composite films is adopted to resolve these issues. By controlling the in-situ growth on flexible CNTs films, Mo-VO 2 with an appropriate thickness can partially allow IR information transmission of CNTs. The high-conductivity CNTs scaffold effectively pulls down the radiative baseline, escaping the “extreme-emissivity trap”, while Mo 6+ -induced band modulation and interfacial charge redistribution optimize the modulation amplitude (Δε) to 0.335 (0.795-0.460). Crucially, the CNTs network provides the massive free-electron reservoir required to overcome shielding deficiency of VO 2 , elevating EMI shielding performance to an exceptional 62-76 dB. Furthermore, leveraging Joule heating effect as a compensatory dimension, the composite films enable active IR camouflage across extreme thermal mismatches (60 C-75°C). This work integrates desirable baseline IR optical modulation with highly efficient electromagnetic protection, redefining the design paradigm of advanced protective materials.

10.1002/adfm.79603.title: A Dual-Functional Inherent Hydroxyl Chainmail on Defective La(OH) 3 for Robust Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation in Extreme Aqueous Matrices
10.1002/adfm.79603.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of carbon-heteroatom bonds promises sustainable chemical synthesis and water remediation, yet practical deployment is challenged by both sluggish proton supply from water dissociation in alkaline media and rapid catalyst poisoning by dissolved organic matter (DOM). Herein, we show that the defective La(OH) 3 nanorods bearing an inherent hydroxyl chainmail circumvent these two bottlenecks simultaneously. The chainmail is proposed to be capable of reconstructing the interfacial hydrogen-bond continuum into a proposed proton-relay highway that accelerates water-dissociation-limited proton delivery, while acting as a proposed biomimetic, multisite hydrogen-bonding shield that sequesters macromolecular DOM to protect active sites from fouling. Demonstrated for the electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination reaction, the catalyst achieves highly effective dechlorination of florfenicol across pH 3.0-13.0 and sustains exceptional stability in high-chemical oxygen demand (COD) matrices (1000 mg L −1 humic acid), outperforming most state-of-the-art catalysts. Continuous-flow treatment of real aquaculture and pharmaceutical effluents confirms sustained dechlorination efficiency and pronounced toxicity abatement. By revealing how this seemingly passive OH − chainmail orchestrates proton transfer and molecular sieving, this work establishes a broadly applicable design paradigm for fouling-resistant electrocatalysts operating in complex aqueous environments.

10.1002/adfm.79576.title: Hydroxyl-Rich Sodium Gluconate Enables Dense SAM Assembly and Enhances Conductivity in NiO x -Based Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79576.abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel oxide (NiO x )/self-assembled monolayer (SAM) composite hole transport layers represent a promising configuration for inverted perovskite solar cells (IPSCs). Nevertheless, the insufficient electrical conductivity of NiO x and the limited number of binding sites on its surface lead to incomplete monolayer coverage, resulting in substantial interfacial charge losses that constrain efficiency improvements. To address these issues, we introduce hydroxyl-rich sodium gluconate (SG) into the NiO x solution. Gluconate anions from SG modulate the electronic properties of NiO x , thereby enhancing its conductivity. Meanwhile, the abundant hydroxyl groups along the SG backbone furnish additional hydrogen-bonding sites for the subsequent adsorption of the SAM, promoting the formation of a compact and well-ordered interfacial molecular layer. This dense SAM not only suppresses leakage currents but also optimizes the energetic cascade at the heterojunction, ultimately enabling the resulting IPSCs to achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.24%. During maximum-power-point operation under ISOS-L-1 protocol, the optimized device preserves 91.6% of the starting output after 1000 h. This work establishes a versatile interfacial engineering approach that overcomes limitations in both SAM assembly and charge transport, offering new opportunities for the development of highly efficient and durable IPSCs.

10.1002/adfm.79363.title: Poisson's Ratio-Driven Control of Myogenic Differentiation and Maturation in Auxetic Metamaterials under Dynamic Mechanical Stimulation
10.1002/adfm.79363.abstract: ABSTRACT Skeletal muscle regeneration requires scaffolds that accommodate the remarkable mechanical heterogeneity of different muscle types while supporting tissue development. Auxetic metamaterials-structures with negative Poisson's ratio that expand laterally when stretched-offer superior mechanical properties including enhanced energy absorption and high yield strain capacity. However, their effects on muscle differentiation under dynamic loading remain unexplored. This study systematically investigated how Poisson's ratio influences skeletal muscle development by designing, fabricating, and mechanically characterizing nine auxetic geometries via melt extrusion printing with a medical-grade poly(L-lactide-co-ε-caprolactone) (PLLA/PCL) copolymer copolymer (PLC). Three geometries with distinct Poisson's ratios (tetrachiral ≈ 0, arrowhead ≈ −0.3, Lozenge ≈ −0.68) were selected for biological evaluation. The auxetic scaffolds were loaded with C2C12 myoblasts encapsulated in fibrin hydrogels and underwent cyclic tensile strain (0%-3%) for 3 h daily over 10 days. Gene expression analysis revealed geometry-dependent differences in differentiation and fiber-type commitment that were associated with distinct Poisson's ratio profiles. By comparing scaffold geometries spanning a broad range of Poisson's ratio values while maintaining similar constituent material and fabrication conditions, this work demonstrates that negative Poisson's ratio and the mechanical environments generated by auxetic architectures may represent important mechanobiological cues for skeletal muscle engineering.

10.1002/adfm.79450.title: Voltage Gated Ion Entry Into Two-dimensional Angstrom-Scale Channels
10.1002/adfm.79450.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological ion channels with angstrom-scale (Å-scale) constrictions regulate key physiological processes by controlling ion flow via stimuli such as voltage gating across cellular membranes. Artificial Å-scale channels can reveal insights into the voltage-gating mechanisms, especially the role of geometrical constrictions on ion entry and dehydration. Here, we investigate voltage-gating in artificial slit-shaped channels with a height ( h ) of one monolayer of graphene, fabricated from layered materials. In the resting state, these channels exhibit selective ion exclusion while permitting flow for water molecules. Under the influence of high voltage, we observe a transition from an insulating to a highly conducting state, facilitating ion permeation beyond a threshold voltage. Our experimental findings unveil non-linear hysteretic current-voltage ( I-V ) characteristics, which we attribute to a confinement-induced ion-entry energy barrier involving ion dehydration and electrostatic effects. The applied voltage can facilitate ion entry by modifying this barrier, potentially through partial dehydration or rearrangement of the hydration shell. Molecular simulations further reveal distinct ion concentrations and mobilities inside the channel during forward and reverse voltage sweeps, demonstrating the influence of the structural organization of confined water on ion transport.

10.1002/adfm.79607.title: Highly Efficient and Stable Flexible Quantum-Dot Light-Emitting Diodes With Excellent Bending Resistance
10.1002/adfm.79607.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (F-QLEDs) hold great promise for future wearable electronics and foldable display applications, yet their efficiency and stability remain inferior to those of their rigid counterparts. Here, we demonstrate very efficient and stable F-QLEDs by using a PET/Ag/IZO substrate and an oxide-layer-free Ga 60 In 40 top electrode. Due to well-matched energy levels and high electrical conductivity of the two electrodes, charge injection balance of F-QLED is significantly improved. As a result, we obtained F-QLEDs with an impressive external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 30.01% and an exceptional T 95 operational lifetime of 20 966 h at 1000 cd/m 2 , which are all the best values ever reported for F-QLEDs. Moreover, benefiting from deformation-tolerant capability of the liquid Ga 60 In 40 , our F-QLEDs can also exhibit negligible efficiency degradation after bending at an ultra-low radius of 1 mm, highlighting their excellent bending resistance. On this basis, we further fabricated high performance large-area F-QLEDs and double-sided emitting F-QLEDs (both with EQEs > 28%), demonstrating the excellent scalability of our device. We believe that the high-performance, bendable, and scalable F-QLEDs demonstrated here will paving the way for practical adoption of F-QLEDs in next-generation wearable and deformable displays.

10.1016/j.actamat.2026.122806.title: Thermodynamics and dynamics of non-compact prismatic dislocation loops simulated using a machine-learning model
10.1016/j.actamat.2026.122806.abstract: We explore how the thermodynamic properties and dynamics of a self-interstitial prismatic dislocation loop are affected by microscopic-scale variations in its geometric configuration, an aspect that rarely received attention in literature. We develop a machine-learning (ML) model to predict the formation energy of an arbitrary geometrically complex configuration of a self-interstitial atom dislocation loop. Trained on atomistic simulation data, the ML model achieves high predictive accuracy across a broad range of configurations, with a typical error in the 1% range. From the ML model, we evaluate the density of configurational microstates as a function of loop's formation energy and derive analytical expressions valid in tractable limiting cases. Using statistical mechanics, we derive the configurational free energy, the average energy, and the thermodynamic entropy of a dislocation loop as a function of temperature. We also simulate the dynamics of self-climb of dislocation loops with various geometries and evaluate their diffusion coefficients and effective activation energy for diffusion. Analysis shows that there is a single universal parameter describing the morphological irregularity of the loop configuration in its ground state. This parameter determines the thermodynamic properties of a loop as well as its dynamics, and simulations illustrate how the properties and mobility of a configurationally complex loop vary as functions of the irregularity parameter.

10.1016/j.actamat.2026.122761.abstract: Stacking-sequence variations in polytypic silicon carbide (SiC) provide a unique platform to isolate the influence of long-range structural order on mechanical behavior while preserving identical local tetrahedral Si-C bonding. However, the mechanistic role of stacking sequence in governing shear instability, strain localization, and fracture in hexagonal SiC remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the tensile deformation behavior along the 〈 1120 〉 direction of 2H, 4H, and 6H SiC using molecular dynamics simulations with a machine-learning interatomic potential (UF3). All polytypes show nearly identical elastic responses up to 6% strain. However, significant differences emerge near failure. To understand these differences, we examine the evolution of shear localization using von Mises strain and non-affine squared displacement. Deformation in all polytypes is governed by shear, while the degree of localization varies significantly. Shear localization severity follows the order 4 H > 6 H > 2 H . This trend mirrors the corresponding increase in Shannon entropy-based local stacking complexity, suggesting that higher local stacking heterogeneity promotes stronger strain localization in hexagonal SiC. In contrast, peak tensile stress follows the order 6 H > 4 H > 2 H and correlates with unstable stacking fault energy and theoretical shear strength obtained from generalized stacking fault energy calculations. These results demonstrate that global hexagonality governs intrinsic shear resistance and attainable peak stress, whereas local stacking complexity controls strain localization and fracture morphology.
